title: Area selection shapes and containment modes in plan and 3D
description:
WHY: SEL-003 (M): area selection shall support rectangle, rotated rectangle and polygon shapes, each with three containment modes: fully inside; partially inside; direction-dependent (left-to-right = fully inside, right-to-left = partially inside). Gap: only the axis-aligned rectangle with the direction mode (views/plan.rs:536-582, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:246-264); no rotated rectangle, no polygon, no explicit modes, no area selection in 3D. SEL-004 (M): select all acts on the active tool's element kind (all kinds with the selection tool), limited to the current view, or to the selection region if one exists; gap: the region clause is impossible because SEL-005 (templates-presets) does not exist, and the tool-to-kind mapping is a hard-coded match (workspace.rs:207-211).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: `SelectionShape { Rect, RotatedRect([DVec2; 4]), Polygon(Vec<DVec2>) }` converted to a geo Polygon, `Containment { FullyInside, PartiallyInside, ByDirection }` (ByDirection resolved by the first drag direction in screen x), and PlanElement::in_shape(&Polygon, fully) (fully: footprint and all segments inside; partially: any segment intersects, any vertex inside, or the shape lies inside the footprint) replacing in_rect. App: Select tool options 'Shape: Rectangle / Rotated rectangle / Polygon' and 'Mode: Fully inside / Partially inside / By direction' in ui/properties.rs tool_modes, persisted in Preferences (defaults Rectangle and By direction = today's behaviour). Plan interaction: rectangle by drag; rotated rectangle by press-drag of the base edge, then a click for the width; polygon by clicks closed with Enter or double-click; Esc cancels; Shift adds to the selection; solid feedback for fully, dashed for partially (as today). 3D: the same shapes in screen space against element meshes projected with the camera (fully: all projected vertices inside; partially: any projected triangle intersects or contains the shape), evaluated once on release from the scene's cached CPU vertices and filtered by is_selectable. SEL-004: Workspace::select_all derives the kind through one ToolKind::kind_tag() mapping (the tool concern element-kind-framework-02 leaves in the app) instead of its local match, limits to the active pane (plan: the elements of that PlanDrawing, which reflects display ranges once plan-views-browser lands; 3D: is_selectable in that pane) and honours `ws.selection_region: Option<SelectionRegion { shape, storeys: Current | All }>` — None until templates-presets adds SEL-005; when Some, only elements partially inside the region on its storeys are selected. Out of scope: drawing and moving the persistent region (SEL-005), area selection in section views, area selection of parts in edit mode.
design: Use geo (Polygon, Intersects, Contains) in place of the hand-written segments_intersect so every shape shares one code path; keep an axis-aligned fast path. Rotated rectangle: base edge a-b, width w = signed distance of the third point from line ab, corners a, b, b + n w, a + n w. ByDirection uses the direction of the first drag edge for all shapes. In 3D, cache projected element hulls when the drag starts (the camera does not move during a drag). Polygon input must not fight click-to-select: it starts only with a press on empty space (or Alt held), stated in the status prompt. Pointers: geometry plan.rs:205-282; views/plan.rs:534-582; views/view3d.rs:140-160; workspace.rs:202-225.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry unit tests for all 9 shape x mode combinations on three walls and a slab: a wall fully inside is selected in every mode; a wall crossing the boundary only in PartiallyInside or with a right-to-left drag; a slab enclosing the whole shape only in PartiallyInside; rotated rectangle and polygon agree with the rectangle for axis-aligned input.
- Regression: with the defaults (Rectangle, By direction) a plan drag selects exactly what today's in_rect path selects (views/plan.rs:536-563) on both samples.
- 3D unit test: with a fixed camera the projected test selects the expected ids in fully and partially modes.
- kittest marquee in the three containment modes in the plan: a left-to-right drag selects only the inside wall, a right-to-left drag also the crossing wall, and mode 'Fully inside' with a right-to-left drag selects only the inside wall; a polygon marquee closed with Enter selects the enclosed elements; a rectangle drag in the 3D pane selects an element.
- select_all unit tests: with the wall tool only walls of the active plan's drawing; with the select tool every kind; a test SelectionRegion limits the result; elements rejected by a pane filter (task 04) are never selected.
- Satisfies SEL-003 and SEL-004 (the region clause through the SelectionRegion hook consumed by templates-presets).
notes:
SRS: SEL-003 SEL-004
SelectionRegion is the hand-over point for SEL-005 in templates-presets.

title: Offer storey re-association after vertical moves; bulk command
description:
WHY: ELM-007 (M): after an element is moved vertically (by dragging, elevating or editing its elevation), the system shall offer to re-associate it with the storey at its new elevation; a bulk command shall re-associate the selected elements with the storeys matching their elevations without moving them. Gap: missing — no vertical move existed, editing Base offset or Elevation offset in the properties panel (ui/properties.rs:314-324, 453-463) triggers no offer, and no bulk command exists (grep re-associat: no hits); storey_at_elevation (crates/archicraft-model/src/storey.rs:124-130) and relink_to_storey (command.rs:419-433) exist. Epic acceptance: paste onto another storey keeps the relative elevation and offers re-association.

WHAT: archicraft-model: `Project::storey_mismatches(ids) -> Vec<(ElementId, StoreyId)>` (base elevation from vertical_extent, matched with storeys.storey_at_elevation; a mismatch when it differs from the home storey) and `Command::ReassociateStoreys { ids }` planned with relink_to_storey per mismatched element (absolute position kept, ELM-005 semantics; NoChange when nothing mismatches). App: a non-modal offer bar (`Workspace.offer: Option<Offer>` rendered above the status line in ui/shell.rs) — 'W-003 now lies on storey 01 First floor. [Re-associate] [Keep]' — raised by `Workspace::offer_reassociation(ids)` after a Command::Transform with a vertical component (task 10 Vertical, Move with dz), after properties edits of base offset or elevation (properties.rs apply path), after a paste onto another storey whose elements reach into a different storey's range (task 13; for example a slab 2.80 m above a 3.00 m storey pasted onto a 2.60 m storey) and after drags: edit-reshape-palette's elevation drag commits Command::Transform with a vertical component and section-view drags (VIEW-032) call the same function, so 'moved vertically by dragging' needs no extra wiring here. Accept executes ReassociateStoreys for the listed ids; any other executed command clears the offer. Bulk action 'Re-associate with storeys by elevation' in the Edit menu and the context menus. Out of scope: vertical arrays assigning home storeys (EDT-004 in drafting-trim-split reuses ReassociateStoreys), dragging in section views (sections-elevations-dims).
design: Matching uses the element's base (bottom of vertical_extent) and storey_at_elevation, which element-kind-framework-01 already moves onto MODEL_TOLERANCE: an element whose base lies on a storey elevation belongs to that storey (unit test pins the boundary). The offer is not modal (UI-005: no unnecessary dialogs) and is cleared by any other executed command so it never refers to stale positions. Pointers: storey.rs:124-130, command.rs:399-433, ui/properties.rs:314-324, 453-463, 602-620, ui/shell.rs status line.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/commands.rs: a ground-floor wall moved up by the storey height reports a mismatch with the first floor; ReassociateStoreys rehomes it there keeping its absolute base and top (a top linked relative to the old home becomes an absolute storey link, as relink_to_storey does) and undo restores; elements already on their matching storey give NoChange; a slab offset edit into the next storey is detected.
- Unit test: Workspace::execute of a Command::Transform with dz issued directly (as a drag caller would, not through the tool) raises the offer; a SetStoreyHeight that moves linked elements does not.
- kittest: a vertical move of a wall by a typed +3.00 m shows the offer naming the first floor and Re-associate changes the home storey (strip shows the first floor) without moving the wall; editing Base offset to 3.0 in the strip shows the offer; the bulk command re-associates two mismatched elements in one undo step.
- kittest paste_onto_other_storey_offers_reassociation: a slab 2.80 m above a 3.00 m ground storey pasted onto a 2.60 m storey keeps offset 2.80 relative to that storey and shows the offer naming the storey above.
- Satisfies ELM-007.
notes: SRS: ELM-007

title: Verify exit criterion: Selection model, part selection (edit mode) and transform commands
description:
WHY: The epic is done only when its exit criterion is demonstrated on the integrated workspace: the part-selection infrastructure of SEL-008, complete picking (SEL-001, SEL-002, SEL-003, SEL-004, SEL-007, VIEW-045), locking feedback (ELM-013), storey re-association (ELM-007), the transform family (EDT-001, EDT-002, EDT-003, EDT-006, EDT-007, EDT-021), cut/copy/paste (EDT-016) and new identities for copies (IFX-011). Later epics (edit-reshape-palette, drafting-trim-split, stair-body-plan, free-form-solids, curtain-walls, ifcx-interop, templates-presets, library-dw-exchange) build on these contracts.

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged branch, walk through the epic acceptance clause by clause against the tests of tasks 01-16, update the rows of every covered requirement in docs/implementation-status.md (status, evidence with file:line, remaining gap) plus the technical-debt list (HOVER_TINT dead code and 'Editing has no UI' items), file beads for anything deferred, and close the epic in beads. No new feature work.
design: Verification only. Commands: cargo test --workspace; cargo test -p archicraft-model --features test-kinds; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --all --check; conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx. Check the provisional shortcuts (Cmd+D, Cmd+Shift+D, Cmd+E, Cmd+Shift+M, Cmd+9, Cmd+X/C/V, Cmd+Shift+V, Alt variant cycling, Enter for edit mode) against commands-and-l10n's registry if it has landed and record any rebinding. Confirm the two-skin edit-mode case with layer-structures (whichever epic landed second owns the real two-skin test). Update docs/implementation-status.md following its existing row format.
acceptance_criteria:
- Epic acceptance: commands.rs tests for Transform{Move,Rotate,Mirror,VerticalMove} with copy variants and undo for every registered kind (a test iterates the registry); kittest: marquee in the three containment modes, Tab cycles candidates, Shift-click toggles, a locked element shows ghost handles and the hover reason; edit mode on a slab selects a single outline node and on a layered wall a single skin, leaves with Esc, and later compound kinds register their PartRef variants without touching selection code (module-layout test); copies get new UUIDs (round-trip test); rotating a wall about a horizontal axis is refused with a message naming the kind (EDT-007 applicability clause: the registry transform hook returns Unsupported; free-form solids and imported elements assert any-axis rotation and objects vertical-axis rotation in their own epics through the same hook); paste onto another storey keeps the relative elevation and offers re-association; zoom to selection works plan to 3D and back.
- Clause map: transform_every_registered_kind (task 03, declared-unsupported transforms refused through the hook); marquee containment kittest (07); Tab cycling and Shift-click in plan (05) and 3D (06); locked_element_shows_ghost_handles (09) and the hover lock reason (05); edit_mode_selects_single_slab_node and edit_mode_selects_single_wall_skin with Esc (08); parts_are_registered_per_kind module-layout test and the SEL-008 part-category test (01, extended in 08); copies_get_new_identities_and_round_trip (03); rotate_wall_about_horizontal_axis_is_refused (12); paste_onto_other_storey_offers_reassociation (13, 14) and the drag-caller offer test (14); copy and multiple-copy for every transform (11, dialog copies in 12); show_selection_round_trip (16) — all present and passing.
- cargo test --workspace (including --features test-kinds where the tests require it), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green; golden files changed only where a blessed diff was reviewed.
- docs/implementation-status.md updated for SEL-001 SEL-002 SEL-003 SEL-004 SEL-007 SEL-008 VIEW-045 ELM-013 ELM-007 EDT-001 EDT-002 EDT-003 EDT-006 EDT-007 EDT-016 EDT-021 IFX-011, with the counts and increment readiness recomputed.
- Deferred clauses have beads or are owned by named epics: 3D two-point vertical move and working-plane transforms (3d-input-navigation), positive any-axis and vertical-axis rotation cases (free-form-solids, ifcx-interop, library-dw-exchange), selection region (templates-presets), view filters (3d-view-restrictions), host copy cascade (host-openings), arrays (drafting-trim-split), real two-skin walls (layer-structures), identities across application updates (element-kind-framework-12 migrations).
- The epic selection-transforms is closed in beads.
notes:
SRS: SEL-001 SEL-002 SEL-003 SEL-004 SEL-007 SEL-008 VIEW-045 ELM-013 ELM-007 EDT-001 EDT-002 EDT-003 EDT-006 EDT-007 EDT-016 EDT-021 IFX-011
Estimate assumes all tests already exist from tasks 01-16; failures reopen the owning task.

title: Align and distribute the selection
description:
WHY: EDT-021 (C): align and distribute commands may align the selection to an edge or line, or distribute it at equal spacing. Gap: missing. With Command::Transform, plan bounds and the point-input service in place this is a thin planner, so it ships with the transform family instead of waiting for could-scope-polish.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/transform.rs: `plan_align(project, ids, line: (DVec2, DVec2), side: Near | Far | Centre) -> Vec<(ElementId, Transform)>` translating each element perpendicular to the line so the near edge, far edge or centre of its plan bounds touches it, and `plan_distribute(project, ids, axis: DVec2) -> Vec<(ElementId, Transform)>` keeping the two extreme elements and spacing the others with equal gaps between their bounds along the axis; both execute as one `Command::TransformEach { moves: Vec<(ElementId, Transform)> }` (one undo step; lock and validation as Command::Transform). App: 'Align to line…' (two points through a PointInput consumer, or an element edge picked through task 05's PlanDrawing::candidates (Hit::Edge); side in the tool options) and 'Distribute horizontally', 'Distribute vertically' and 'Distribute along line…' in Edit > Transform and the context menus. Out of scope: distributing copies along a path (EDT-005), rotational alignment.
design: Bounds come from Project::plan_bounds (task 03). Distribute sorts by bounds start along the axis, gap = (span - sum of sizes) / (n - 1); when the gap would be negative (overlapping elements) it spaces the centres equally instead. TransformEach generalises Transform to per-element transforms and can serve drafting-trim-split's array planner. Pointers: command.rs Transform (task 03), tools/transform.rs (task 10).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: three walls aligned to the line y = 0 with side Near have their lower bounds on y = 0; Centre aligns centres; distributing four slabs along X gives equal gaps within MODEL_TOLERANCE with the outer two unchanged; locked elements are rejected with CommandError::Locked; one undo restores everything.
- kittest: select three walls, 'Distribute horizontally' — equal gaps; 'Align to line…' with two clicks aligns them.
- Satisfies EDT-021.
notes: SRS: EDT-021

title: Draw selection handles, ghosted for locked elements
description:
WHY: ELM-013 (M): individual elements are lockable independently of their layer; a locked element rejects move, delete, resize and parameter changes and shows ghosted handles when selected; on hover the system tells whether the element or its layer causes the lock (hover in task 05, rejections in task 03). Existing (kept): the element lock flag (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:284-285, persisted by the IFCX writer and reader), the Locked toggle (ui/properties.rs:627-647) and command rejections (command.rs:351-385). Gap: no handles exist at all; a locked selection is highlighted like any other (views/plan.rs:309-318), and the strip only says 'The selected elements are locked.' without naming element or layer.

WHAT: Selection handles for every selected element at its node anchors (the Node parts of Kind::part_refs and part_anchor, task 01): in the plan as an overlay after the selection outline, and in 3D as anchors projected at the element's base elevation through the camera and drawn with the egui painter over the 3D image. Editable elements get filled squares in the selection colour; locked ones (Project::lock_cause, task 05) get hollow squares at 40 % alpha with a dashed outline (ghosted). Handles are visual here; dragging them is EDT-009 in edit-reshape-palette, which reuses `HandleStyle` and the handle size constant from this task. The properties strip names the cause: 'W-001 is locked.' or 'On locked layer “Structure”.' next to the Lock toggle (ui/properties.rs:627-671). Out of scope: handle dragging (edit-reshape-palette), handles in section views.
design: HandleStyle { Active, Ghosted } and a 7 px handle size shared with edit-reshape-palette-07's node palette. Ghost colour palette.selection.gamma_multiply(0.4) with a 1 px dashed stroke, so the state is distinguishable without colour (NFR-A11Y-003). In 3D only the anchors of selected elements are projected, every frame (cheap). Pointers: views/plan.rs:299-318; ui/properties.rs:627-671; views/view3d.rs painter section after the image.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest locked_element_shows_ghost_handles: lock a wall and select it — the plan view's test hook PlanViewState.last_handles holds HandleStyle::Ghosted at both wall ends; unlock — HandleStyle::Active; a wall on a locked layer is ghosted too and the strip names the layer.
- Unit tests: a slab's handles are its outline and hole vertices; deselected elements have none; above a cap of 2,000 handles only outlines are drawn (no frame stall on large selections).
- tests/ui.rs selecting_an_element_shows_its_properties and the commands.rs lock tests pass unchanged (lockable independently of the layer stays as is).
- Satisfies the ghosted-handles clause of ELM-013; with tasks 03 and 05 the whole requirement.
notes: SRS: ELM-013

title: Transform tool: move, rotate, mirror and vertical move with preview
description:
WHY: EDT-001 (M): any selection shall be transformable by move (by a vector), rotate (centre, reference direction, then target direction or typed angle), mirror (about an axis defined by two points) and vertical move (by a signed dZ); all defining points use INP-001 and the result is previewed live. Gap: move exists only as a model command with no caller in the app (grep MoveElements: model and tests only); no tool, menu item, shortcut or context-menu entry, no preview. Appendix D.8 requires default shortcuts for move, copy-move, rotate, mirror and vertical move; NFR-PERF-005 requires rubber-band feedback within 50 ms.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/transform.rs in the tools/ module that point-input-snapping-01 creates from views/tools.rs (tools/mod.rs with ToolKind and ToolState, wall.rs, slab.rs): `TransformTool { op: Move | Rotate | Mirror | Vertical, ids, points }` implementing the InputConsumer trait of point-input-snapping-01. Move: base point, destination. Rotate: centre, reference direction point, target direction point or typed angle. Mirror: two axis points. Vertical: typed signed dZ in the tracker (Expect::Distance; two-point input in 3D arrives with 3d-input-navigation's ViewSurface without changes here). Every step has a StepSpec prompt ('Pick the base point', 'Type the height difference'). Preview: the selected elements' existing PlanElement::segments() from the active plan's cached PlanDrawing (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs) transformed by the candidate Transform::affine() — no geometry evaluation per frame; Vertical shows the new base elevation in the tracker. Commit executes Command::Transform{copy: false} on Workspace::editable_subset (task 04) and reports skipped locked elements. Actions in ui/actions.rs: Move, CopyMove (starts Move in the copy variant, completed by task 11), Rotate, Mirror, VerticalMove with provisional shortcuts Cmd+D, Cmd+Shift+D, Cmd+E, Cmd+Shift+M, Cmd+9; an Edit > Transform submenu in ui/shell.rs; plan and 3D context-menu entries; app.rs run() arms; without a selection the actions report 'Select elements first.' The selection follows the moved elements. While the Selection is in edit mode (task 01) the transform actions are disabled with the status message 'Leave edit mode to transform whole elements.' (part transforms belong to edit-reshape-palette and free-form-solids). Out of scope: copy and multiple-copy (11), rotate plus/minus 90, resize and rotate about an axis (12), drag-moving and stretching (edit-reshape-palette), 3D working-plane input (3d-input-navigation).
design: Start from the transform stub consumer in point-input-snapping-01's tests. Rotation angle = angle(target - centre) - angle(reference - centre); a typed angle overrides the third point. The moving elements must not snap to themselves: pass a temporary exclusion set in InputContext for the duration of the tool (not the persistent snap-exclusion flags of point-input-snapping-12), keeping the base point snappable. The tool lives in the workspace tool slot so switching tools cancels it. Shortcuts follow the reference product (Drag Cmd+D, Rotate Cmd+E, Elevate Cmd+9) but avoid Cmd+M, which macOS reserves for minimise; commands-and-l10n moves them into its registry. Pointers: tools/mod.rs ToolState and input/consumer.rs (point-input-snapping-01), ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs:59-77, views/plan.rs:750-779, views/view3d.rs:270-290, app.rs:377.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in tools/transform.rs drive PointInput headlessly: Move with base (0,0) and a typed relative destination yields Transform::Move{(2,1,0)}; Rotate with centre, reference east and typed 30 degrees yields Rotate{30 degrees}; Mirror from two points yields Mirror{a,b}; Vertical with typed 0.5 yields Move{(0,0,0.5)}; Esc drops one step and Backspace one point (Esc ladder of point-input-snapping).
- Preview test: preview outlines equal the transformed PlanElement segments of the selection and no ModelGeometry evaluation happens while previewing (evaluation counter unchanged).
- kittest: select a wall, press the Move shortcut and click two points — the wall moved by the vector with one undo step 'Move 1 element'; Rotate from the Edit menu with a typed 90 rotates it; Mirror flips a slab; in a selection of a locked and a free wall only the free one moves and the status line names the locked one.
- Unit test: with Selection::enter_edit active, the Move, Rotate, Mirror and VerticalMove actions do nothing and report 'Leave edit mode to transform whole elements.'
- actions.rs: shortcuts_are_unique passes; appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts includes Move, CopyMove, Rotate, Mirror and VerticalMove.
- Satisfies EDT-001 for plan views; 3d-input-navigation reuses the consumer through its ViewSurface.
notes:
SRS: EDT-001
Provisional D.8 bindings: Move Cmd+D, Copy-move Cmd+Shift+D, Rotate Cmd+E, Mirror Cmd+Shift+M, Vertical move Cmd+9.

title: Show the selection zoomed in 3D or in its plan
description:
WHY: VIEW-045 (S): the selection shall be kept when switching views; commands shall show the current selection in 3D or in the plan, zoomed to it. Gap: the selection survives view switches (task 04 asserts it), but 'Show in 3D' (views/plan.rs:773-779) opens the first 3D view without zooming, and there is no 'show selection in plan' from 3D (it needs the storey of the selection and a zoom). Epic acceptance: zoom to selection works plan to 3D and back.

Existing by then (reuse, do not re-implement): element-kind-framework-14 extends Request::ZoomTo to { ids, storey } — handle_requests opens or activates the plan of that storey and a pending zoom in PlanViewState is applied on the pane's first laid-out frame. WHAT: `Request::ShowSelection(Target::View3d | Target::Plan)` handled in app.rs: Plan picks the storey of the selection (the active plan if it shows all selected elements, else the home storey with most selected elements, ties to the lower one) and pushes Request::ZoomTo { ids, storey: Some(storey) }; View3d opens or activates the first 3D view and fits model_bounds of the selection (views/view3d.rs:59-72) through a new `pending_zoom: Option<Vec<ElementId>>` in View3dState, applied on the first frame with a valid rect (the 3D counterpart of the plan's pending zoom). Commands 'Show selection in 3D' (replaces 'Show in 3D' in the plan context menu; View menu) and 'Show selection in plan' (3D context menu; View menu). SwitchPlan3d keeps the selection and zooms to it on the target only when the new preference zoom_selection_on_switch is on (default off, so plain switching keeps the camera). Out of scope: section and elevation targets (sections-elevations-dims).
design: Reuse zoom_active (app.rs:354-375) and element-kind-framework-14's ZoomTo { ids, storey } handling; only the 3D pending zoom is new. Pointers: app.rs:291-318, 354-375, 417-425; views/plan.rs:773-779; views/view3d.rs:270-290; workspace.rs Request.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest show_selection_round_trip: select a wall in the first-floor plan, 'Show selection in 3D' — the 3D pane is active and its camera target lies within the wall's bounds; 'Show selection in plan' from the 3D pane — the first-floor plan is active and the wall's bounds lie inside its visible rect; the selection is unchanged throughout.
- Unit tests: the storey choice for a selection spread over two storeys picks the one with more elements; with an empty selection both commands are disabled.
- Satisfies VIEW-045 (with task 04).
notes: SRS: VIEW-045

title: Pick bodies, edges and nodes in plan with hover lock reasons
description:
WHY: SEL-001 (M): the element under the cursor is highlighted before it is clicked and identified in a short info label; Tab cycles through overlapping candidates and a click selects the highlighted one — the plan already does this (views/plan.rs:450-464, 621-632, 669-678). SEL-002 (M): clicking selects by body or surface as well as by edges and nodes; an option limits picking to edges and nodes; Shift-click toggles; Esc or a click on empty space clears; a held modifier selects while a creation tool is active. Existing in the plan (keep and regress): Shift-click toggles (views/plan.rs:510-514), a click on empty space clears (plan.rs:519), Esc clears (plan.rs:701-711, the Esc ladder after point-input-snapping-01), Cmd held selects while a creation tool is active (plan.rs:448). Gap: no edges-and-nodes option, and elements drawn only projected (the default slab below the 1.10 m cut plane) are hit only on their outlines, not by their body (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:237-243, 270-282 test cut polygons only). ELM-013 (M): on hover the system tells whether the element or its layer causes the lock; the hover label shows only name and kind (views/plan.rs:621-632).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: PlanElement gains `footprint: MultiPolygon<f64>` (the element's bodies projected to XY through a `plan_footprint` hook on element-kind-framework-07's GeometryKind registry, defaulting to the union of the body's down-facing outline polygons; walls reuse wall::footprints, slabs outline minus holes, failed elements the fallback box of element-kind-framework-13) and `nodes: Vec<(DVec2, PartRef)>` from Kind::part_refs/part_anchor (task 01); `PlanDrawing::candidates(p, tolerance, mode: PickMode) -> Vec<Candidate { id, hit: Hit::{Node(PartRef), Edge, Body}, distance }>` ordered by hit class (node, edge, body), then cut before projected before overhead, topmost first; pick() stays as a wrapper returning ids. PickMode { BodiesEdgesNodes, EdgesNodesOnly }. App: the selection hover/click path in views/plan.rs (or the select consumer if point-input-snapping moved it) uses candidates() with the existing Tab cycle state; a 'Pick edges and nodes only' toggle in the Select tool options (ui/properties.rs tool_modes) persisted as Preferences.pick_edges_and_nodes_only (serde default false). The info label shows 'W-003 · Wall', a lock line from `Project::lock_cause(&Element) -> Option<LockCause::{Element, Layer { name }, Both { layer }}>` ('Locked' / 'Locked by layer “Structure”' / 'Locked, and layer “Structure” is locked too') and '1/3 · Tab for next' with several candidates; edit_lock_reason (project.rs:212-221) is reimplemented on lock_cause with unchanged messages. Out of scope: 3D (06), area selection (07), part picking in edit mode (08), handles (09).
design: Footprints are computed once per plan build and cached in PlanDrawing (ModelGeometry is incremental after element-kind-framework-10 and plans are cached per storey by element-kind-framework-11). Candidates query an rstar index of segments and nodes per PlanDrawing (rstar 0.12, shared with point-input-snapping-02's SnapIndex; reuse its SnapSource where practical). Pick tolerance stays 4 px (views/plan.rs:444); node tolerance is the snap radius (Appendix D.1: 8 px). Tab keeps cycling selection candidates in the Select tool (plan.rs:669-678, kept by point-input-snapping-01); inside a point-input step Tab cycles snap candidates or moves to the next field (rule of point-input-snapping-03), so the two never compete. Keep the info label clear of the tracker label of drawing tools (offset as in views/plan.rs:625). Overlays stay on the egui painter after plan-renderer's GPU pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry unit tests: a slab below the cut plane is hit at its centre as Hit::Body in BodiesEdgesNodes and not at all in EdgesNodesOnly; a wall end within tolerance is Hit::Node(PartRef::Node{ring:0,index:0}) and preferred over the edge; two overlapping elements give two candidates topmost first; candidates use only cached PlanDrawing data.
- Model unit test: lock_cause returns Element for a locked wall, Layer{name} for a wall on a locked layer, Both{layer} when both apply (the hover names both, since unlocking the element alone would not help) and None otherwise; edit_lock_reason messages and the commands.rs lock tests are unchanged.
- A failed element's fallback box (element-kind-framework-13) is hit as Hit::Body.
- kittest (plan of a seeded fixture from element-kind-framework-03's FixtureBuilder): hovering a locked wall shows a label containing 'Locked', and for a wall on a locked layer the layer name (hover reason); with 'Pick edges and nodes only' a click inside the slab body selects nothing while a click on its edge selects it; Tab with two stacked candidates moves the highlight and a click selects the highlighted one; Shift-click toggles; Cmd-click with the wall tool active selects instead of drawing; Esc and a click on empty space still clear the selection (regression of the existing behaviour).
- Hover over RM-M-sized stand-ins (stand_in(5000)) stays within NFR-PERF-005's 50 ms (timed unit test, release profile).
- Satisfies SEL-001 and SEL-002 for plan views and the hover clause of ELM-013.
notes:
SRS: SEL-001 SEL-002 ELM-013
Appendix D.1: snapping radius 8 px. Open: overhead (dashed) elements are body-pickable by footprint after cut and
projected ones (chosen).

title: Add the Selection model with kind-registered PartRef and EditMode
description:
WHY: SEL-008 (M): compound elements (stairs, railings, curtain walls, segmented beams and columns, free-form solids) shall have an edit mode in which their parts are selectable: segments, faces, edges, vertices, frames, panels, steps. The gap row rates it missing (XL): the selection is a flat HashSet<ElementId> (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:54) and nothing can address a sub-element. Building the addressing now, before the first compound kind exists (stair-body-plan, curtain-walls, members-profiles-adv and free-form-solids all list this epic as a prerequisite), keeps every later kind from rewriting selection code; edit-reshape-palette-01 expects PartRef::Node/Edge in crates/archicraft-model/src/selection.rs for slab outline nodes. The proving cases are slab outline nodes/edges and wall skins.

WHAT: New headless module crates/archicraft-model/src/selection.rs (re-exported from lib.rs): `enum PartRef { Node { ring: u16, index: u32 }, Edge { ring: u16, index: u32 }, Kind(KindPart) }` where Node/Edge are the shared outline addressing (ring 0 = exterior, 1.. = holes; a wall's ends are Node{ring 0, index 0|1}; edge i runs from node i to node i+1) and KindPart is generated by the `kinds!` macro of element-kind-framework-02 from each kind module's associated `type Part` (WallPart::Skin { index: u16 } in kinds/wall.rs, SlabPart without kind-specific variants yet in kinds/slab.rs, and DummyPart in kinds/dummy.rs under the test-kinds feature with one variant per part category SEL-008 names — Segment { index, role }, Face(u32), Edge(u32), Vertex(u32), Frame { u, v }, Panel { u, v }, Step { flight, index } — plus Skin { index } for task 08's two-skin edit-mode test; the dummy reports them only when its parts flag of element-kind-framework-02 is set, each with a label and a sub-rectangle of its footprint as outline). `SelItem { element: ElementId, part: Option<PartRef> }`; `Selection` backed by an IndexSet (insert, remove, toggle, select_only, clear, contains_element, elements(), parts_of(id), len, is_empty, retain_valid(&Project)); `EditMode { element: ElementId }` with Selection::enter_edit(id) / leave_edit() rules (in edit mode only parts of that element are accepted; leaving maps the selection back to the element). The Kind trait (kinds/mod.rs) gains selection-part hooks with no-part defaults: `part_refs(&self) -> Vec<PartRef>` (stable order; deliberately not named parts(), because element-kind-framework-02's `Kind::parts() -> Vec<PartSpec { role, class, label }>` stays the list of IFC child parts that element-kind-framework-07 writes and evaluates), `part_ref_for_role(&self, role: &str) -> Option<PartRef>` (maps a PartSpec/PartGeometry role such as 'Part_1' to its selectable part, None by default; the 3D id buffer of task 06 uses it), `part_label(&self, &PartRef) -> Option<String>` ('node 3', 'edge 2 of hole 1', 'skin 1'), `part_anchor(&self, &PartRef) -> Option<DVec2>` (plan position for handles and labels), `part_outline(&self, &PartRef) -> Option<Vec<DVec2>>` (plan polyline or polygon for highlighting and hit tests) and `validate_part(&self, &PartRef) -> bool`; KindDescriptor gains `part_roles: &'static [&'static str]`. Wall: two end nodes and one skin band today through `Wall::skin_bands() -> Vec<SkinBand { offset, thickness, material }>` (layer-structures later fills it from the layer structure without changing PartRef). Slab: nodes and edges of the exterior ring and every hole. Out of scope: any UI (tasks 04 and 08), node editing commands (edit-reshape-palette), per-part 3D bodies, layer structures (layer-structures), saving selections to IFCX.
design: Hybrid enum on purpose: Node/Edge are shared because every polygon-based kind (slab now; roof, shell, 2D fill, terrain boundary later) addresses outline nodes and edges the same way and edit-reshape-palette's Outline type implements them generically; everything else is kind-specific and registered through the macro, so stairs (Flight{index}, Landing{index}, Step{flight, index}), curtain walls (Frame{u, v}, Panel{u, v}), segmented members (Segment{index, role}) and free-form solids (Face/Edge/Vertex by stable halfedge ids) add variants in their own module. Macro sketch: extend the kinds! entries to `wall: Wall => WallPart`, generating `pub enum KindPart { Wall(WallPart), Slab(SlabPart), #[cfg(feature = "test-kinds")] Dummy(DummyPart) }` with From impls and KindPart::kind(); ElementKind delegates the part hooks (part_refs, part_ref_for_role, part_label, part_anchor, part_outline, validate_part) and returns None for a KindPart of another kind. Stable addressing: indices refer to the parametric definition (outline vertex order, skin order from the exterior face), never to tessellation; commands that reorder (slab mirror reverses rings, task 02) are followed by Selection::retain_valid so stale parts are dropped instead of pointing at the wrong vertex. indexmap is already a dependency of archicraft-model. Pointers: kinds/mod.rs, kinds/wall.rs, kinds/slab.rs and kinds/dummy.rs after element-kind-framework-02 (today crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:129-147 Wall, 178-190 Slab rings), crates/archicraft-model/tests/module_layout.rs (element-kind-framework-02), crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:54.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in selection.rs: insert/remove/toggle/select_only semantics; contains_element is true when any item of the element is present; in edit mode inserting a part of another element or a whole element is rejected (returns false); leave_edit leaves exactly [(element, None)]; iteration order is insertion order.
- element-kind-framework-02's PartSpec parts() and the registry tests stay unchanged (part_refs is a separate hook).
- Kind tests: a slab with a 4-node outline and one 4-node hole reports 8 nodes and 8 edges with the expected (ring, index) addresses; part_outline(Edge{ring:1,index:2}) equals that hole segment; a wall reports Node 0, Node 1 and Kind(WallPart::Skin{index:0}) whose outline equals the free-standing wall footprint within MODEL_TOLERANCE; validate_part rejects out-of-range indices and parts of another kind.
- SEL-008 part categories: a dummy with parts = true reports one part per category (segment, face, edge, vertex, frame, panel, step) plus two skins, each with a non-empty part_label and part_outline and a serde_json round trip, and part_ref_for_role('Part_1') returns its registered part — the addressing expresses every part kind SEL-008 lists before the real compound kinds (stairs, railings, curtain walls, segmented members, free-form solids) exist.
- Module-layout test parts_are_registered_per_kind (feature test-kinds, added to crates/archicraft-model/tests/module_layout.rs of element-kind-framework-02): DummyPart and its role strings occur only in kinds/dummy.rs and the existing Dummy line of kinds/mod.rs, and selection.rs contains no kind names (Wall, Slab, Dummy) outside doc comments — proving that later compound kinds register PartRef variants without touching selection code.
- PartRef, SelItem and Selection derive Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize and Deserialize (journal and clipboard ready); no PartRef variant carries mesh or triangle indices (doc comment plus review item).
- cargo test --workspace, clippy and fmt green; the app still compiles unchanged (the workspace adopts Selection in task 04).
- Satisfies the model half of SEL-008 (part addressing and edit-mode state).
notes:
SRS: SEL-008
Open question: wall ends as PartRef::Node{ring:0,index:0|1} (chosen, so node commands of edit-reshape-palette treat wall
ends and slab vertices alike) versus a WallPart::End variant. Coordination: layer-structures (parallel epic) fills
Wall::skin_bands() from the layer structure; whichever lands second adds the two-skin unit test. edit-reshape-palette-01
adopts PartRef::Node/Edge for its Outline type.
Naming: part_refs()/part_ref_for_role() leave element-kind-framework-02's parts() (PartSpec, IFC child parts) intact;
downstream texts that write parts() for selectable parts (free-form-solids-02, members-profiles-adv-10) mean part_refs().

title: Pick and hover in 3D through a GPU id buffer
description:
WHY: SEL-001 (M): hover highlight, info label and Tab cycling — 3D views have none (views/view3d.rs:166-188 only picks the nearest hit on click). SEL-002 (M): picking by body or surface as well as edges and nodes, and the edges-and-nodes option, apply to 3D as well; Shift-click toggles (view3d.rs:176-180). Technical debt: 3D hover highlighting is dead code — view3d.rs:213 calls build_scene(..., None) and SceneKey omits hover, so the HOVER_TINT path in views/render3d.rs:129-144 never runs. Epic risk: per-frame hover picking is costly; pick on pointer move only, through an id buffer, never by ray casting per frame. SEL-008's edit mode (task 08) needs part-level picking in 3D.

WHAT: views/render3d.rs: Vertex gains `pick: u32` (24-bit element slot, 8-bit part slot) with a slot table SceneData.pick_ids: Vec<(ElementId, Option<PartRef>)> built in build_scene (part slots from the compound children of element-kind-framework-07, ElementGeometry.children keyed by role, mapped to selectable parts through Kind::part_ref_for_role of task 01; 0 = whole element); an id pass renders into a single-sample R32Uint texture with its own depth buffer only when FrameKey changes; on pointer move (never every frame) a block around the cursor is copied into a staging buffer, mapped asynchronously and read in the next frame, giving the nearest non-zero id within about 5 px (thin elements and edges stay pickable). The hover tint moves from vertex colours into views/shader.wgsl (uniforms hover_slot and hover_part), so hover changes never rebuild or re-upload the scene; the hover parameter of build_scene is removed. views/view3d.rs: ws.hover from the id-buffer result; info label 'name · kind' plus task 05's lock line (Project::lock_cause); Tab in the Select tool cycles candidates from a CPU `pick_all(ray) -> Vec<(ElementId, f64)>` sorted by distance, computed on the Tab press only; a click selects the highlighted candidate; with task 05's PickMode::EdgesNodesOnly (Preferences.pick_edges_and_nodes_only) the id pass draws the edge pipeline with ids and faces with id 0. Fallback without a wgpu render state (kittest, software): hover uses the CPU pick on pointer-move events only. Every element in the id pass passes Workspace::is_selectable (task 04). Out of scope: 3D area selection (07), edit-mode part styling (08), clip-plane-aware picking (3d-view-restrictions adds its planes to the id pass).
design: Integer targets cannot be multisampled: render the id pass single-sampled (SAMPLE_COUNT 4 applies to the colour pass only, render3d.rs:19). copy_texture_to_buffer needs bytes_per_row aligned to 256, so copy a 64-texel-wide block and index into it. Map with map_async and poll in the next frame (device.poll with Maintain::Poll) — never block the UI thread. FrameKey includes the hover slot so the colour pass re-renders when hover changes; SceneKey (split into geometry revision and selection by element-kind-framework-11) does not, and the SceneCache blocks are never recomputed for hover. Scale the pixel tolerance by pixels_per_point so it matches the plan's 4 px pick tolerance on high-DPI screens. Compound kinds with more than 255 parts encode part groups and refine with CPU picking on click. Pointers: render3d.rs:60-160 (Vertex, build_scene), 243-330 (pipelines), 501-580 (render); view3d.rs:75-91, 166-215; workspace.rs:43-47.
acceptance_criteria:
- render3d unit tests (no GPU): build_scene assigns unique slots that map back to (ElementId, part) and leaves out hidden-layer and pane-filtered elements; two builds with different hover produce identical vertex buffers.
- A headless wgpu test (skipped when no adapter is available, like the existing render3d tests) renders two boxes and reads back the right id over each and 0 over the background.
- view3d unit tests on the CPU fallback: pick_all returns stacked elements sorted by distance; N frames without pointer motion perform zero picks (counter assertion).
- kittest (fallback path): hovering an element in the 3D pane sets ws.hover and shows the info label; Tab cycles the hovered candidate between a stacked wall and slab; Shift-click toggles; a click on empty space clears.
- Hovering over the stand_in(1000) model causes no scene upload (upload counter constant while hovering).
- Satisfies SEL-001 and SEL-002 for 3D views and removes the HOVER_TINT technical-debt item.
notes:
SRS: SEL-001 SEL-002 SEL-008
Open: tolerance block size (5 x 5 device-independent pixels proposed).

title: Move the workspace selection onto Selection with view filters
description:
WHY: SEL-007 (M): elements on hidden layers or hidden by view filters shall not be selectable; locked elements are selectable but not editable (ELM-013). Existing (kept and extended): plans are generated from visible elements (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:116-118), the 3D pick and select_all filter Project::is_visible (views/view3d.rs:77, workspace.rs:219), prune_selection drops hidden or deleted elements (workspace.rs:153-165), and locked elements are selectable but rejected by commands (command.rs:351-385, workspace.rs:180-200, ui/properties.rs:627-671). Gap: Project::is_visible checks only the layer (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:207-209), so 'hidden by view filters' cannot be honoured; the filters arrive with 3d-view-restrictions (VIEW-040/041/044) and plan-views-browser (display ranges), scheduled in parallel, which need one gate to plug into. SEL-002 (M): Esc or a click on empty space clears the selection — Esc is handled only in views/plan.rs:701-711, so it does not clear the selection while a 3D view is active. VIEW-045 (S): the selection shall be kept when switching views; it is workspace-global today but element-only. The model Selection of task 01 must replace HashSet<ElementId> before any part-aware UI.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs: `selection: Selection` replaces the HashSet; migrate every call site (views/plan.rs, views/view3d.rs SceneKey and build_scene, views/render3d.rs, ui/properties.rs gather/apply, ui/dialogs.rs problems click, ui/browser.rs, app.rs) to contains_element, elements(), toggle and select_only. Add `trait ViewFilter { fn accepts(&self, &Element, &Project) -> bool; fn generation(&self) -> u64 }` with an AcceptAll default stored per pane in PlanViewState and View3dState, and `Workspace::is_selectable(&Element, Pane) -> bool` = layer visible and the pane's filter accepts; picking, area selection, select all and hover use it. prune_selection keeps dropping elements hidden by layer or deleted; an element hidden only in the active pane stays selected (it may be visible in another pane) but is not drawn there. Add `Workspace::editable_subset(ids) -> (Vec<ElementId>, Vec<String>)` (editable ids plus lock reasons) used by delete_selection now and by the transform, resize and cut actions later. Esc: register 'clear the selection' as the workspace rung of the Esc ladder of point-input-snapping-01 for 3D panes too, so Esc in a 3D view with nothing pending clears the selection. Assert the selection survives open_pane and SwitchPlan3d. Selection changes are not undo steps. Out of scope: hover candidates (05, 06), part-selection UI (08), the filters themselves (3d-view-restrictions, plan-views-browser), zoom to selection across views (16).
design: Keep SceneKey's selection as sorted element ids derived from Selection::elements() so GPU scene caching behaves as today (workspace.rs:43-47). The filter's generation lets per-frame caches (snap index, plan candidate index) invalidate cheaply, like point-input-snapping-02's targets generation. Keep Project::is_visible (model-level, layer) separate from Workspace::is_selectable (view-level). Pane-less contexts (problems panel, browser) select by id through the active pane's filter. properties.rs collects the selection in several places (properties.rs:70-75): keep model order through selected_ids(). Pointers: workspace.rs:54, 151-160, 180-225; views/plan.rs:440-530, 701-711; views/view3d.rs:166-215; views/render3d.rs:102-110.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test --workspace, clippy --all-targets and fmt green; all existing kittests pass.
- Workspace unit tests (no egui): a stub ViewFilter rejecting slabs makes plan picking, 3D picking and select_all skip slabs in that pane while another pane still selects them; an element on a hidden layer is pruned after UpdateLayer; a locked element is selectable and not editable; editable_subset splits a mixed selection and names the locked ones.
- kittest: select a wall in the plan, switch to 3D with F3 — the wall is still selected (properties strip shows it); Esc in the 3D pane empties the selection; a click on empty 3D space clears it too.
- No HashSet<ElementId> selection field remains in crates/archicraft-app/src (review item or grep test).
- Satisfies SEL-007 (hidden by layer or by any registered view filter is not selectable; locked selectable but not editable — commands.rs:102-139 still pass), the 3D Esc clause of SEL-002 and the 'kept when switching views' clause of VIEW-045.
notes:
SRS: SEL-007 SEL-002 VIEW-045
Coordination: 3d-view-restrictions implements ViewFilter for hidden/isolated elements, kind and storey-range filters and
region filters (VIEW-044: elements cut by a region stay selectable, so accepts() returns true for them).

title: Copy and multiple-copy variants with modifier switching
description:
WHY: EDT-002 (M): every transform shall have a copy variant (keeps the original) and a multiple-copy variant (every further click places another copy until Esc or double-click); the variants are switchable during the operation with a modifier, and the cursor shows the active variant. Gap: no copy or multiple-copy variant, no modifier switching, no cursor indicator. IFX-011 (M): copies get new identities — provided by Command::Transform{copy: true} (task 03) and exercised here from the UI.

WHAT: TransformTool (task 10) gains `variant: Variant { Single, Copy, Multi }`: a press of the modifier (Alt/Option, provisional) cycles Single, Copy, Multi during any step; the CopyMove action starts Move in Copy. Copy commits one Command::Transform{copy: true} and ends. Multi commits one copy per click relative to the same base (Move: each destination; Rotate: each target direction from the same centre and reference; Mirror: each new axis; Vertical: each typed dZ), keeps the step at 'next destination' and ends on Esc or double-click. Cursor: a glyph next to the crosshair in plan and 3D (none for Single, '+' for Copy, '++' for Multi) through the InputConsumer preview's CursorState, plus the variant name in the status prompt. After Copy the copies are selected; after Multi the last copies. Out of scope: arrays (EDT-004, drafting-trim-split), paste (13).
design: Alt because Shift constrains (INP) and Cmd selects while a creation tool is active (SEL-002); it acts on the key-down edge, not while held, so it works on laptops; commands-and-l10n may rebind it. Draw the glyph with the egui painter at cursor + (14, 14) px, below the tracker label. Pitfall: on macOS Option-modified typing produces special characters — read egui::Modifiers on the key event and swallow the text event of a bare Option press so the tracker does not receive it. Pointers: tools/transform.rs (task 10), views/plan.rs snap marker and label drawing (580-620).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: in Move two modifier presses give Variant::Multi; three clicks in Multi produce three Transform{copy: true} commands relative to the original base; Esc keeps the copies and ends the tool; a double-click ends Multi; Copy commits once and ends; Multi in Rotate places one copy per target direction about the same centre and reference, and in Vertical one copy per typed dZ (every transform has both variants).
- Unit test: the preview's CursorState glyph follows the variant (none, '+', '++').
- kittest: copy-move a wall with Cmd+Shift+D and two clicks — two walls, the copy named W-002 with a new UUID, the original unchanged; Multi with three clicks — four walls and three undo steps, and undo removes only the last copy.
- Satisfies EDT-002 and exercises the copy clause of IFX-011 from the UI.
notes:
SRS: EDT-002 IFX-011
Provisional modifier: a press of Alt/Option cycles the variant.

title: Add the per-kind transform hook: move, rotate, mirror, scale
description:
WHY: EDT-001 (M): any selection shall be transformable by move (by a vector), rotate (centre, reference direction, then target direction or typed angle), mirror (about an axis defined by two points) and vertical move (by a signed dZ). EDT-006 (S): a selection shall be resizable by a target size or a scale factor about a reference point; elements whose parameters cannot be scaled (a wall's thickness) are scaled in position only, and the user is told. EDT-007 (M): free-form solids and imported elements rotate about any 3D axis and objects about the vertical axis; other elements allow only the transforms their parameters can represent, and the system tells the user when a requested transform cannot be applied instead of ignoring it. Today the only geometric operation is the 2D translate (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:257-270); gap rows: EDT-001 L, EDT-006 M, EDT-007 L (all missing). What exists by then (keep and extend, do not re-implement): element-kind-framework-02 turns translate into the per-kind hook `Kind::transform(&PlanTransform) -> Result<(), TransformError>` through which MoveElements plans, with wall rotation, slab mirroring that keeps the exterior ring counter-clockwise and holes clockwise, and `TransformError::Unsupported` for the dummy's mirror. Missing: vertical move, scale with position-only notes, rotation about a 3D axis, declared support per kind, and a refusal that names the kind. Epic risk: mirroring parametric elements must mirror parameters, not meshes.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/transform.rs (replacing element-kind-framework-02's PlanTransform, whose move, rotate and mirror become the first three variants): `enum Transform { Move { delta: DVec3 }, Rotate { center: DVec2, angle: f64 }, Mirror { a: DVec2, b: DVec2 }, Scale { reference: DVec2, factor: DVec2 }, RotateAxis { point: DVec3, axis: DVec3, angle: f64 } }` with Transform::vertical(dz) (= Move with (0, 0, dz)), affine() -> DAffine3, apply_point and a classification (PlanIsometry, PlanReflection, Vertical, UniformPlanScale, NonUniformPlanScale, TiltedRotation); non-finite values, zero or negative scale factors and zero-length axes are rejected before any kind is called. Kind trait: element-kind-framework-02's hook becomes `fn transform(&self, t: &Transform, ctx: &TransformContext) -> Result<Transformed<Self>, TransformError>` with `Transformed { value, notes: Vec<TransformNote> }` (TransformNote::NotScaled { parameter }) and `TransformError::Unsupported { kind_label, reason }` (the existing variant gains label and reason) whose Display names the kind ('Walls can only be rotated about a vertical axis.'); KindDescriptor.transforms: TransformSupport flags declare what the hook accepts (UI pre-check in task 12, agreement test here); MoveElements keeps planning through the hook as Transform::Move, so its behaviour is unchanged. Wall: Move shifts start/end and base_offset by dz (top links keep their storey); Rotate (element-kind-framework-02, kept) rotates start/end about the centre; Mirror reflects start/end and swaps them so the body stays on the mirrored side (ReferenceLine Outside/Inside/Custom keep their meaning); Scale scales start/end and keeps the thickness with a NotScaled note; RotateAxis about a vertical axis equals Rotate, any other axis is Unsupported. Slab: Move shifts outline/holes and offset; Rotate; Mirror keeps element-kind-framework-02's reflection and ring reversal (exterior CCW, holes CW) and gains a documented node index mapping (needed by PartRef::Node, task 01); Scale keeps thickness with a note; tilted rotation Unsupported. Dummy (test-kinds) keeps element-kind-framework-02's refusal of Mirror, now declared in its KindDescriptor.transforms so the registry-driven tests here and in task 03 exercise a declared-unsupported plan transform, implements Move, Rotate, vertical move and Scale, and refuses RotateAxis. Geometry tests in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/transforms.rs. Out of scope: commands and copies (03), UI (10-12), mirror about a 3D plane (EDT-022, 3d-input-navigation), kinds that accept tilted rotation (free-form-solids, imported elements in ifcx-interop), objects (library-dw-exchange).
design: glam DAffine3/DMat3 is already available through archicraft_model::glam. Transform is plain data (Serialize/Deserialize) so commands stay journal-replayable. The refusal is a value carrying the descriptor label, so the message names the kind (EDT-007 acceptance). Parameter mirroring rule per kind: a reflection reverses orientation, so the left side of the reflected direction is the reflection of the right side — walls swap start and end, slabs reverse their rings, later arc edges negate their sweep (curved-geometry) and asymmetric profile anchors flip (profiles-columns-beams); each kind owns its rule and the geometry test enforces it. TransformContext carries the home storey elevation and &StoreyList so a vertical move is validated against linked tops through vertical_extent. Use exact quarter-turn sine/cosine for multiples of 90 degrees so rotate plus/minus 90 (task 12) never drifts and golden files stay stable. Pitfall: negative scale factors would be hidden reflections — mirror is the explicit command. Pointers: kinds/mod.rs, kinds/wall.rs, kinds/slab.rs, kinds/dummy.rs after element-kind-framework-02 (today element.rs:257-270), command.rs:153-166 (MoveElements), validate.rs (validate_wall, validate_slab), geometry evaluate.rs, extrude.rs, mesh.rs check_closed.
acceptance_criteria:
- transform.rs unit tests: affine() maps sample points correctly for every variant; Mirror classifies as PlanReflection, RotateAxis about Z as PlanIsometry and about X as TiltedRotation; Scale (2,2) is UniformPlanScale and (2,1) NonUniformPlanScale; invalid parameters are rejected with an explanatory message.
- Wall tests: rotating (0,0)-(5,0) by 90 degrees about the origin gives (0,0)-(0,5) with thickness and reference line unchanged; Transform::vertical(0.5) adds 0.5 m to base_offset; Scale x2 doubles the length, keeps 0.25 m thickness and returns NotScaled{thickness}; RotateAxis about the X axis returns Unsupported whose message names 'Walls'.
- Slab tests: mirror keeps the orientation invariants (validate_slab passes unchanged) and follows the documented node index mapping; scale keeps thickness with a note; vertical move changes the offset.
- element-kind-framework-02's transform-hook tests (wall rotation, slab mirror orientation, dummy refusal) pass on the new signature.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/transforms.rs iterates KINDS (Dummy under test-kinds): for every plan transform the kind's KindDescriptor.transforms declares (of Move, Rotate, Mirror and vertical move) the evaluated body of the transformed element equals the transformed body of the original as vertex sets within MODEL_TOLERANCE (parameters mirrored, not meshes), and every resulting mesh is closed and outward-oriented (check_closed).
- A unit test asserts that each kind's hook refuses exactly what its KindDescriptor.transforms excludes (wall and slab: every plan transform and vertical move accepted, tilted rotation refused; dummy: Mirror and tilted rotation refused).
- Existing MoveElements tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs pass unchanged.
- Satisfies the model clauses of EDT-001 (all four transforms representable per kind), EDT-006 (position-only scaling with notification data) and EDT-007 (refusal instead of silent ignore, for walls and slabs).
notes:
SRS: EDT-001 EDT-006 EDT-007
Open question: a vertical move of a wall with a storey-linked top keeps the top link (chosen; the wall changes height
and the ELM-007 offer of task 14 follows) versus converting the top to a fixed height. free-form-solids, ifcx-interop
(imported elements) and library-dw-exchange (objects) assert the positive EDT-007 cases through this hook.

title: Add Command::Transform with copy variants and new identities
description:
WHY: EDT-001 needs one undoable command per transform. EDT-002 (M): every transform shall have a copy variant (keeps the original) and a multiple-copy variant. IFX-011 (M): identities remain stable across edits, undo/redo and save/open cycles, and copy, duplicate and array operations create new identities. Gap: only Command::MoveElements exists (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:41-44, 153-166) and there is no copy command; copies need new ElementIds and names via Project::next_element_name (project.rs:270) and counters as in plan_add_elements. ELM-013 (M): a locked element rejects move, delete, resize and parameter changes; plan_update_elements already rejects locked edits (command.rs:362-369) and the transform command must name the locked element. EDT-007's refusal must reach the user as a command error instead of being ignored.

WHAT: command.rs: `Command::Transform { ids: Vec<ElementId>, transform: Transform, copy: bool }` with labels ('Move 3 elements', 'Copy 3 elements', 'Rotate 1 element', 'Mirror …', 'Elevate …', 'Resize …') planned through the Kind transform hook (task 02): copy == false produces ReplaceElement edits through plan_update_elements (lock, validation and NoChange semantics reused); copy == true calls `Project::duplicate(ids, &Transform) -> Result<Duplicate, CommandError>`, which creates random v4 ElementIds, names from the per-kind counters with nth offsets (W-004, W-005), keeps layer, class and position, sets locked = false, and remaps explicit relations of element-kind-framework-08's RelationStore whose both ends are in the set (Edit::InsertRelation with new relation ids; relations to elements outside the set are dropped and derived junctions re-evaluate), yielding InsertElement + SetCounters + InsertRelation edits. New `CommandError::Unsupported(String)` carries the hook's message and is returned atomically when any element refuses. Locked elements yield CommandError::Locked with the element or layer name; copying a locked element is allowed because the original is not edited. MoveElements stays for journal compatibility and is planned as Transform::Move without copy. Helpers for the UI: `Project::plan_bounds(ids) -> Option<(DVec2, DVec2)>` as the union of the per-element Kind::plan_bounds() hook of element-kind-framework-02 (not a second bounds implementation) (rotate plus/minus 90 and resize in task 12, align in task 15) and `Command::preview_notes(&Project) -> Vec<TransformNote>` (the EDT-006 notes without executing). The old-to-new id mapping lives in one `IdRemap` (element and relation ids, applied to element references and relations) in crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs, which task 13's paste and Project::reidentify_all reuse. Out of scope: UI (tasks 10-12), clipboard and Save As re-identification (13), arrays (EDT-004 in drafting-trim-split reuses Project::duplicate), the host cascade (ELM-016, host-openings).
design: Copies are inserted at the end of the element map (drawn on top, matching the reference product). Names use Project::next_element_name(kind, nth) with nth counted per kind within the command. The multiple-copy variant is a sequence of Transform{copy: true} commands, one undo step per placed copy, which keeps each step small and lets undo remove the last copy only; the tool (task 11) groups them visually. Duplicate stays generic so host-openings extends the id set through relations.dependents_of(id) filtered to Host relations (ELM-016) without touching this command; document the hook. NoChange for identity transforms (zero vector, 0 degrees, factor 1). Validate every transformed element with validate_element so a vertical move cannot put a base above a linked top. Pointers: ids.rs (IdRemap), relations.rs (element-kind-framework-08), command.rs:153-166, 320-342 (plan_add_elements counters), 351-385 (lock checks), project.rs:265-312, tests/commands.rs:101-145 (lock tests).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs transform_every_registered_kind (feature test-kinds) iterates KINDS, builds each kind's prototype (Project::prototype(kind, storey) of element-kind-framework-04) and, for Move, Rotate, Mirror and VerticalMove (Transform::vertical) with copy false and true, asserts for every transform the kind's KindDescriptor.transforms declares: execute succeeds; with copy the original is bit-identical and exactly one element with a new id and the next counter name is added; undo restores the exact project (revision normalised); redo reapplies identically; for every transform it excludes (the dummy's Mirror): CommandError::Unsupported naming the kind and an unchanged project.
- Locks: transforming a locked wall returns CommandError::Locked naming W-001; a wall on a locked layer names the layer; copying a locked wall succeeds and the copy is unlocked; every rejection leaves the project unchanged.
- Unsupported: RotateAxis about the X axis on a wall returns CommandError::Unsupported containing 'Walls'; a mixed wall and slab selection is refused atomically.
- IFX-011: copies have UUIDs distinct from every existing id; an identity test runs 20 random transforms with undo/redo and asserts the original ids never change; crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs copies_get_new_identities_and_round_trip saves and reopens a wall and its copy with two distinct node paths and equal parameters except position and name.
- Kept, not re-implemented: the existing identity tests add_undo_redo_keeps_identity (tests/commands.rs), round_trip_restores_the_editable_model and spatial_tree_and_identities (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs) pass unchanged (edit, undo/redo and save/open clauses of IFX-011).
- Relations: two elements joined by an explicit test relation and copied together yield a relation between the copies; copied alone, the copy has none.
- MoveElements tests pass unchanged; history_is_bounded_and_replayable passes with Transform commands in the journal (serde round-trip).
- Satisfies EDT-001 and EDT-002 at model level, the copy clause of IFX-011, the move/resize rejection clause of ELM-013 and the 'tells the user' clause of EDT-007 as a command error.
notes:
SRS: EDT-001 EDT-002 EDT-007 ELM-013 IFX-011
Open question: a mixed selection is refused atomically with a message naming the refusing kinds (chosen) versus applying
the transform to the supporting elements with a report; revisit after the usability test (NFR-USE-001).

title: Selection model, part selection (edit mode) and transform commands
description:
Complete picking (edges and nodes, area shapes and containment modes, view filters, locked ghosting, selection kept across views), introduce the generic part-selection infrastructure of SEL-008 (Selection holds (ElementId, Option<PartRef>), PartRef is an extensible enum registered per kind, an EditMode state enters and leaves with part highlighting) proven on slab outline nodes and wall skins before the first compound element exists, and give EDT its first user-facing commands: move, rotate, mirror and vertical move with copy and multi-copy variants, rotate plus/minus 90 degrees, resize, cut/copy/paste, re-association after vertical moves, applicability messages for transforms a kind cannot represent, align/distribute and new identities for copies. Transforms are planned through the per-kind transform hook of the kind registry, hence the dependency on element-kind-framework.

Risks: Per-frame 3D hover picking is costly: pick on pointer move only, through the id buffer, never by ray casting per frame. Mirroring parametric elements must mirror parameters, not meshes, covered by per-kind transform tests. The PartRef design must serve stairs, segments, grid axes, curtain walls and free-form solids: it is a kind-registered enum with stable addressing (segment index plus role), never mesh indices.
design: archicraft-model: Command::Transform family planned into ReplaceElement edits through per-kind transform(&Isometry) from the kind registry; Project::reidentify for copies; clipboard as serialised elements plus referenced resources (prepares SW-003); PartRef enum and EditMode in a selection module shared with the app. archicraft-app: workspace.rs Selection gains part references; tools/transform.rs steps on the point-input service; cursor variant glyphs; candidates from plan segments and 3D picking through an id buffer in views/render3d.rs (wires the dead HOVER_TINT path); actions for the D.8 transform shortcuts.
acceptance_criteria: commands.rs tests for Transform{Move,Rotate,Mirror,VerticalMove} with copy variants and undo for every registered kind (a test iterates the registry); kittest: marquee in the three containment modes, Tab cycles candidates, Shift-click toggles, a locked element shows ghost handles and the hover reason; edit mode on a slab selects a single outline node and on a layered wall a single skin, leaves with Esc, and later compound kinds register their PartRef variants without touching selection code (module-layout test); copies get new UUIDs (round-trip test); rotating a wall about a horizontal axis is refused with a message naming the kind (EDT-007 applicability clause: the registry transform hook returns Unsupported; free-form solids and imported elements assert any-axis rotation and objects vertical-axis rotation in their own epics through the same hook); paste onto another storey keeps the relative elevation and offers re-association; zoom to selection works plan to 3D and back.
notes: SRS: SEL-001 SEL-002 SEL-003 SEL-004 SEL-007 SEL-008 VIEW-045 ELM-013 ELM-007 EDT-001 EDT-002 EDT-003 EDT-006 EDT-007 EDT-016 EDT-021 IFX-011

title: Rotate by 90 degrees, resize and rotate about an axis
description:
WHY: EDT-003 (S): a single command shall rotate the selection by +90 or -90 degrees about the centre of its bounding box; gap: no command and no bounding-box helper for a selection (PlanElement::bounds is per element). EDT-006 (S): a selection shall be resizable numerically, by a target size or a scale factor, about a chosen reference point; elements whose parameters cannot be scaled (a wall's thickness) are scaled in position only, and the user is told; gap: missing. EDT-007 (M): other elements allow only the transforms their parameters can represent, and the system tells the user when a requested transform cannot be applied instead of ignoring it; epic acceptance: rotating a wall about a horizontal axis is refused with a message naming the kind.

WHAT: Actions RotatePlus90 and RotateMinus90 (Edit > Transform and context menus, no default shortcut) execute Command::Transform{Rotate{center: centre of Project::plan_bounds(selection) (task 03), angle: plus/minus 90 degrees}}. Resize dialog in ui/dialogs.rs ('Resize…'): mode Scale factor (uniform, or X and Y) or Target size (width and depth of the selection bounds with a keep-proportions toggle); reference point from the nine bounds anchors or 'Pick point…' (one PointInput step through a small InputConsumer reusing task 10's infrastructure); before OK it lists Command::preview_notes ('Wall thickness is kept: W-001 and W-002 are scaled in position only.') and after OK the status line repeats them. 'Rotate about axis…' dialog: axis X, Y or Z through the centre of the selection's 3D bounds, or two typed 3D points, plus an angle; executes Transform::RotateAxis; a CommandError::Unsupported is shown as a message naming the kind ('Walls can only be rotated about a vertical axis. Free-form solids and imported elements can be rotated about any axis.'); options excluded by the selection's KindDescriptor.transforms are greyed out with the same explanation as hover text. Both dialogs offer 'Keep original (copy)', executing the transform with copy: true (the copy variant of EDT-002 for dialog transforms; multiple copies of a dialog transform are arrays, EDT-004 in drafting-trim-split). Locked elements are reported through editable_subset (task 04). Out of scope: mirror about a 3D plane (EDT-022) and interactive 3D axis picking (3d-input-navigation), the positive any-axis cases (free-form-solids, ifcx-interop, library-dw-exchange).
design: The nine-anchor picker is a 3 x 3 grid of radio buttons in ui/widgets.rs; Target size converts to per-axis factors (keep-proportions forces equal factors). The Rotate-about-axis dialog stays simple until 3d-input-navigation provides 3D picking; it is the user-facing path that proves the registry hook refuses (and, for free-form solids and imported elements, later accepts) tilted rotations. Follow the 'Add a dialog' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md. Pointers: ui/dialogs.rs, ui/widgets.rs, ui/actions.rs, command.rs Transform (task 03).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: plan_bounds of two walls; RotatePlus90 keeps the bounds centre fixed and maps bounds (w, h) to (h, w); four RotatePlus90 return the exact original coordinates (quarter-turn exactness from task 02).
- Resize tests: factor 2 about the lower-left anchor doubles wall lengths, keeps thicknesses and lists the note; target width 10 m on a 5 m wide selection equals factor 2; a picked reference point at the centre keeps the centre fixed; resizing a locked element is rejected (ELM-013); Resize with 'Keep original (copy)' leaves the original unchanged and adds a scaled copy with a new id.
- kittest rotate_wall_about_horizontal_axis_is_refused: select a wall, open 'Rotate about axis…', choose X and 90 degrees, OK — a message containing 'Walls' appears and the project revision is unchanged.
- kittest: the Resize dialog shows the 'scaled in position only' note for a wall selection before OK.
- Satisfies EDT-003, EDT-006, the applicability clause of EDT-007 for walls and slabs, and the copy variant of EDT-002 for dialog transforms.
notes:
SRS: EDT-003 EDT-006 EDT-007 EDT-002
Open: whether Resize also scales heights (chosen: plan only; heights are reported as kept in the notes).

title: Cut, copy and paste with storey-relative paste and Save As choice
description:
WHY: EDT-016 (M): delete, cut, copy and paste shall be available; paste places at the same position, or at a picked point, and can paste onto another storey at the same relative elevation. Existing (keep and regress): delete (Action::Delete with Del and Backspace, ui/actions.rs:16, app.rs:391 and 487-490, workspace.rs:180-200 honouring locks, Edit menu ui/shell.rs:73, plan and 3D context menus). Gap: cut, copy and paste are missing entirely (no clipboard, no actions). IFX-011 (M): copy, duplicate and array operations create new identities, and Save As shall offer new project (new UUIDs and a new header.id) or copy of this project (identities kept); gap: Save As only asks for a path (app.rs:189-211) and no function re-identifies a Project. D.8 requires default shortcuts for cut, copy and paste. The clipboard payload prepares cross-project paste (SW-003, library-dw-exchange).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/clipboard.rs: `ClipboardPayload { format: 1, elements, relations (explicit, both ends inside), layers, materials (the referenced resources), source_storey, source_storey_elevation, bounds }` serialised with serde_json behind the marker 'archicraft-clipboard/1'; `Project::copy_to_clipboard(ids)`; `Project::paste(payload, PastePlacement::{SamePosition, AtPoint { base, target }, OnStorey { storey }}) -> Result<Command, CommandError>` maps resources by id (unknown ones are added), re-identifies through Project::duplicate's id and name machinery and IdRemap (task 03), keeps each element's offset relative to its home storey when pasting onto another storey (same relative elevation) and plans one command 'Paste 3 elements' (resource inserts, InsertElement, counters). `Project::reidentify_all(&mut self)` assigns new ProjectId, SiteId, BuildingId, StoreyIds, ElementIds, LayerIds, MaterialIds and ViewIds and remaps every reference (element storey, layer and material, TopLink::Storey, the per-kind tool-default slots of element-kind-framework-04, relations of element-kind-framework-08, views) through IdRemap, generalising the fresh-id construction of template.rs:347-374. App: actions Cut, Copy, Paste and PasteAtPoint (Cmd+X, Cmd+C, Cmd+V, Cmd+Shift+V) in the Edit menu and context menus; Cut copies everything and deletes the editable subset (locked elements are reported, not removed); system clipboard through egui (ctx.copy_text, Event::Paste) with an in-process fallback; Paste on the active plan's storey: same position on the source storey, same relative elevation on another storey; PasteAtPoint runs a one-step InputConsumer with an outline preview (base = lower-left of the payload bounds). Save As: after the file picker a modal offers 'New project (new identities)' and 'Copy of this project (keep identities)'; New project calls reidentify_all, clears the undo history with a status notice and restarts the autosave session. Out of scope: multi-window and cross-project paste UI (SW-003), the host cascade (ELM-016, host-openings extends Duplicate), templates (templates-presets reuses reidentify_all), the re-association offer after paste (14).
design: egui turns Cmd+C, Cmd+X and Cmd+V into Event::Copy, Event::Cut and Event::Paste(text) instead of key events, so these actions are matched on those events in app.rs (not consume_shortcut) and only when no text field has focus (works_while_typing false). Keep the payload self-contained and free of file paths so another window or project can paste it (SW-003). Tests use the seeded v5 FixtureBuilder (element-kind-framework-03) for deterministic remaps; production uses random v4 ids. The undo history refers to old ids: clear it after reidentify_all and say so rather than rewriting it. Pointers: app.rs:185-215 (save), template.rs:347-374, ids.rs, workspace.rs:180-200, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs:59-77.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model unit tests: copy plus SamePosition paste yields elements equal to the originals except id and name; OnStorey onto the first floor keeps base_offset/offset relative to the new home storey; AtPoint translates by target - base; a payload with a layer unknown to the project adds that layer; undo of a paste restores the exact project; the payload round-trips through JSON and a payload with another marker is rejected.
- reidentify_all test: every id changes, validate passes, all references resolve, geometry evaluates identical bodies and the writer's header.id changes; roundtrip.rs save_as_new_project_gets_new_identities and save_as_copy_keeps_identities.
- kittest: select a wall, Cmd+C, open the first-floor plan, Cmd+V — a wall on the first floor at the same relative elevation with a new UUID; Cmd+X removes the original and Cmd+V restores it at the same position; the Edit menu shows Cut, Copy, Paste and 'Paste at point'.
- Kept: Delete via Del, Backspace, the Edit menu and both context menus still deletes the editable selection (tests/ui.rs or a new kittest); template.rs every_project_gets_new_identities and the round-trip identity tests pass unchanged.
- actions.rs: Cut, Copy and Paste are in appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts; shortcuts_are_unique passes.
- Satisfies EDT-016 and IFX-011 (copy and Save As clauses; the template clause is met by template.rs; arrays reuse Project::duplicate in drafting-trim-split).
notes:
