SRS: EDT-016 IFX-011
Provisional bindings: Cut Cmd+X, Copy Cmd+C, Paste Cmd+V, Paste at point Cmd+Shift+V.
IFX-011 application-update clause: element-kind-framework-12's format_v1_files_migrate_with_a_report loads a migrated
v1 file equal to the current golden, ids included, so identities survive updates; this task does not re-implement it.

title: Edit mode: enter, highlight and select parts, leave with Esc
description:
WHY: SEL-008 (M): compound elements shall have an edit mode in which their parts are selectable: segments, faces, edges, vertices, frames, panels, steps. Task 01 adds the addressing; this task makes it usable and proves it on the parts that exist before the first compound kind — slab outline nodes and wall skins — so stair-body-plan, curtain-walls, members-profiles-adv and free-form-solids only register their parts. Epic acceptance: edit mode on a slab selects a single outline node and on a layered wall a single skin, and leaves with Esc.

WHAT: Workspace: edit mode through Selection::enter_edit/leave_edit (task 01). Enter: 'Edit parts' in the plan and 3D context menus for a single selected element whose kind reports parts (non-empty Kind::part_refs), the Enter key in the Select tool, or a double-click on a selected element in the plan (the 3D double-click keeps setting the orbit pivot, VIEW-021). Leave: Esc (the top rung of the Esc ladder while in edit mode; the element stays selected), a click on empty space, or picking another element. Plan overlays (views/plan.rs): other elements dimmed; every part drawn from Kind::part_outline and part_anchor — nodes as squares, edges as thin lines, skins as translucent bands; the hovered part tinted and selected parts in the selection colour; part candidates from hit tests on part outlines (node > edge > band), click selects one part, Shift toggles, Tab cycles part candidates. 3D: the id buffer's part slot (task 06) highlights and picks body parts (skins and compound children where the geometry provides per-part bodies; a single-body wall reports skin 0) and a shader uniform dims the other elements. The properties strip shows 'SL-001 · Slab — node 3' (Kind::part_label) and keeps element fields read-only while parts are selected. Whole-element transform actions stay disabled while edit mode is active; task 10 implements that check on Selection's edit-mode state (task 01), so this task needs no transform code (part transforms belong to edit-reshape-palette and free-form-solids). Selection::retain_valid runs after every executed command. Out of scope: node and edge editing commands (edit-reshape-palette), layered skins themselves (layer-structures), part properties.
design: Part hit tests use Kind::part_outline in model coordinates, independent of PlanDrawing, so parts of elements outside the cut range stay editable. Order: node within the snap radius (8 px, D.1) > edge within the pick tolerance > band containment; drawing order band fills < edges < nodes. Dimming multiplies the other elements' overlay colours by 0.4 instead of re-rendering the plan. Esc ladder in edit mode: step-local input state, then leave edit mode, then clear the selection. The Select tool's double-click does nothing today; the drawing tools' double-click (finish) is untouched. Pointers: views/plan.rs:285-318 (outlines), 503-521 (click), 669-678 (Tab), 701-711 (Esc); render3d.rs and shader.wgsl after task 06; ui/properties.rs gather.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest edit_mode_selects_single_slab_node: select a slab, press Enter, click one outline vertex — the selection is exactly [(slab, Some(PartRef::Node{ring:0,index:k}))] and the strip shows 'node'; Esc leaves edit mode and the selection is [(slab, None)].
- kittest edit_mode_selects_single_wall_skin: on a two-skin wall a click on one band selects exactly that skin (uses layer-structures' layered wall if merged; otherwise a test-kinds Dummy element with parts = true and its two DummyPart::Skin parts of task 01, and the real two-skin assertion is added to layer-structures' verification); on today's single-skin wall the click selects Skin{index:0}; Esc leaves edit mode.
- Unit tests: Tab cycles between a node and the edge under the same point; Shift-click toggles parts; entering edit mode on an element without parts reports 'This element has no editable parts.'; retain_valid drops an out-of-range node after UpdateElements removes a vertex.
- The module-layout test of task 01 is extended: crates/archicraft-app/src contains no kind-specific part type names (WallPart, SlabPart, DummyPart) — the UI handles parts only through the Kind hooks.
- Satisfies SEL-008 (edit-mode infrastructure with part selection, proven on slab nodes and wall skins; compound kinds register their parts in their own epics).
notes:
SRS: SEL-008
Enter as the edit-mode key is provisional (commands-and-l10n confirms). Two-skin coordination with layer-structures as
described in the acceptance.

title: Add criterion benches for open, save, evaluate and slice
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-001 (M, partial): performance targets refer to a minimum and a reference hardware class and are measured, not assumed; the gap row notes that no measurement protocol or results file exists, and AS-07 notes there are no benches, no criterion dependency and no harness (Instant::now appears only in the autosave timer). The roadmap moved the harness into increment 1 so every later slice is measured as it lands; perf-tuning-rm-m-l runs AS-07 with RM-M/RM-L on it in increment 4. The benches observe the NFR-PERF-002 (open/save) and NFR-PERF-006 (update after an edit) quantities that other epics own; known limits from the technical debt: whole-model re-evaluation per edit (document.rs:97-103) and O(n^2) footprints (wall.rs:239-246).

WHAT: criterion as a workspace dev-dependency; crates/archicraft-geometry/benches/geometry.rs: `evaluate` (ModelGeometry::evaluate), `plan` (plan_drawing per storey: slice and classification), `slice` (slice_loops on a wall mesh), `edit_then_evaluate` (MoveElements on one wall, then evaluate and plan, the headless part of NFR-PERF-006); crates/archicraft-ifcx/benches/ifcx.rs: `save` (write + compact to_bytes), `save_indented`, `load` (parse + read), `validate`. Bench-model registry in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs: `pub struct BenchModel { pub id: &'static str, pub ci: bool, pub build: fn() -> Project }` and `pub fn bench_models() -> Vec<BenchModel>` returning two_storey_shell and a provisional `tiled_shell(n)` (both `ci: true`; the CI gate of task 18 runs only `ci` models, so later RM-M/RM-L entries set `ci: false`) (two_storey_shell's storeys replicated on an n x n grid, about 1,000 elements) until element-kind-framework's seeded 1,000/5,000/20,000-element stand-ins exist; they are appended there, the single extension point. Bench ids are stable strings (`ifcx/save/two_storey_shell`) because the regression gate (task 18) compares by id. docs/performance/README.md lists the benches and models. Out of scope: the CI gate and results publication (task 18), in-app frame instrumentation (task 17), any tuning.
design: Use criterion 0.5 with `harness = false` [[bench]] entries; disable default features and enable only what is needed (cargo_bench_support; html reports optional) to keep plotters out if cargo-deny objects. Build bench inputs outside the timed closure (iter_batched for edit_then_evaluate so each iteration starts from the same project). tiled_shell: copy the walls and slabs of two_storey_shell with an offset of (i*20 m, j*20 m) through AddElements commands so it stays valid; mark it provisional in its doc comment. Pitfall: ModelGeometry::evaluate uses catch_unwind; benches must assert no problems once outside the timing, otherwise a failing element makes a bench look fast.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo bench -p archicraft-geometry -p archicraft-ifcx -- --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 2 --sample-size 10` runs every bench on every registered bench model and writes reports under target/criterion.
- Benches compile in the existing `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` CI step, so a broken bench fails CI.
- bench_models() returns two_storey_shell and tiled_shell(n), both flagged ci, with element counts asserted in a unit test; tiled_shell evaluates without geometry problems and round-trips through IFCX because it is registered as an EXTRA fixture of crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (task 02) and so passes the generic model, geometry and IFCX checks.
- cargo deny check licenses passes with criterion and its dependencies (default features trimmed if a dependency's licence is not on the allow list).
- docs/performance/README.md lists bench ids, models and how to run them locally.
- Workspace tests, clippy (all targets) and fmt green.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-001
Stand-ins are provisional; RM-M/RM-L replace them in increment 4 (perf-tuning-rm-m-l).

title: Gate benches in CI, publish results and record hardware classes
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-001 (M, partial): performance targets refer to two hardware classes: Minimum (proposal) Apple MacBook Air M1 with 8 GB RAM and a Windows laptop with an Intel Core i5-1135G7 (Iris Xe), 8 GB RAM and a 1920x1080 display; Reference (proposal) Apple MacBook Air M2 with 16 GB RAM and a Windows laptop with an Intel Core Ultra 7 155H (Arc) and 16 GB RAM; Linux is measured on the Windows laptop of each class with the current Ubuntu LTS; all targets are measured on reference hardware unless stated otherwise; the concrete machines are still to be chosen (O-15). Gap: machines not chosen, nothing published (NFR-PORT-006 asks to publish them with every release), no protocol or results file. Epic acceptance: benches publish numbers per CI run and fail on a 20 % regression; results follow docs/performance/<date>-<machine>.md; the classes are documented in docs/technology-choices.md, closing O-15.

WHAT: (1) scripts/bench-gate.py (python3 stdlib) and a `bench` job in ci.yml (ubuntu-24.04, pull requests and pushes to main): check out the merge base in a git worktree and run the benches in smoke mode (`--warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 3 --sample-size 20 --save-baseline base`), then run them on HEAD with `--baseline base`; parse target/criterion/**/change/estimates.json; fail when the lower bound of a bench's mean-change confidence interval exceeds +20 %; write a markdown table (bench id, base, head, change) to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and upload target/criterion as an artefact. A pull-request label `perf-regression-accepted` lets a reviewer accept a justified regression, recorded in the results log. scripts/tests/test_bench_gate.py with canned estimates (+25 %, +15 %, -30 %, missing bench) runs in CI. (2) docs/performance/README.md: the measurement protocol (full-mode benches, perf-feature scripted runs, models, repetitions) and the results convention docs/performance/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<machine-id>.md with a header table (class, CPU, GPU, RAM, display, OS, commit, toolchain) and result tables; machine ids min-mac-m1, min-win-i5, ref-mac-m2, ref-win-u7 (Linux runs as -ubuntu suffix); the first file is a developer-machine run labelled dev-<name>. (3) docs/technology-choices.md: the Hardware row and the GPU section record both classes with the selection criteria for the concrete Windows laptops, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS for Linux, and state that O-15 is closed; README gains a 'System requirements' section that the release checklist publishes with each release (NFR-PORT-006). Out of scope: buying or naming laptop SKUs beyond the criteria (product owner), meeting the targets, RM-M/RM-L.
design: Comparing base and head on the same runner in one job is what makes a 20 % threshold usable on shared runners; never compare against stored numbers from other runs. Criterion's change/estimates.json holds mean.point_estimate and mean.confidence_interval.{lower_bound, upper_bound} as relative changes; gate on lower_bound > 0.20. Keep smoke mode short (whole job under 10 minutes) by running only the bench models flagged `ci` (BenchModel::ci, task 16); full mode is for reference hardware. The SRS O-15 row itself is not edited here; the pull request proposes the resolution text for the SRS owner.
acceptance_criteria:
- The bench job runs on pull requests, shows the comparison table in the job summary and uploads the criterion reports (numbers published per CI run).
- scripts/tests/test_bench_gate.py passes: +25 % with a lower bound above +20 % fails, +15 % passes, -30 % passes, a bench missing in the base is reported but does not fail, the accepted label overrides with a message.
- A scratch commit that doubles the cost of one bench (e.g. evaluating twice) makes the job fail; reverting makes it pass (shown in the pull request).
- docs/performance/README.md holds the protocol, stating that every target is measured on reference hardware unless the target says otherwise and that Linux runs on each class's Windows laptop with the current Ubuntu LTS; one results file docs/performance/<YYYY-MM-DD>-dev-<name>.md follows the naming convention and holds full-mode bench numbers and one scripted perf-feature run (task 17).
- docs/technology-choices.md documents the minimum and reference classes and Linux measurement, and states O-15 is closed; README has the system requirements section, and the hardware placeholder of docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md (task 13) links to it.
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green. Satisfies NFR-PERF-001's hardware and protocol clauses (the measurements against targets are AS-07, increment 4).
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-001
NFR-PORT-006 (publication with every release) is owned elsewhere; this task supplies the text and the checklist item.

title: Run conformance on three OS runners and add the release checklist
description:
WHY: NFR-LEG-002 (M, done) is verified by inspection; its non-text half (no Graphisoft images, library parts or templates) needs a per-release item next to the grep guard of task 01. The epic acceptance requires the headless viewer check of IFX-006 (M) on every golden file on Windows, macOS and Linux, the platforms of NFR-PORT-001..003; files must be platform-independent (NFR-PORT-004, verified by task 06). IFX-006 (b) also requires a manual visual check in the hosted IFC5 viewer (R4) once per release, and the gap row notes there is no release checklist for it. The epic risk on CI time asks for conformance on changed goldens per push and the full matrix nightly.

WHAT: .github/workflows/conformance-matrix.yml: matrix ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest, macos-latest; triggers: nightly schedule, workflow_dispatch, and pull_request with a paths filter on crates/archicraft-model/**, crates/archicraft-geometry/**, crates/archicraft-ifcx/**, conformance/** and the workflow itself; steps: write the reference models (compact, and indented through the `--indented` flag of task 05), run conformance/run.sh with `shell: bash` (Git Bash on Windows) on them and all goldens, upload screenshots per OS. The per-push ubuntu job in ci.yml stays. run.sh is made robust under Git Bash (path conversion, npm ci on Windows, Playwright browser cache per OS). docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md: open every golden and reference model in the hosted IFC5 viewer (R4) and compare tree, geometry and colours with the CI screenshots; confirm the one-hour fuzz run; run the AS-05 manual procedure on the three OSes; publish the minimum and reference hardware with the release notes (NFR-PERF-001, NFR-PORT-006); inspect that no Graphisoft content (text, images, library parts, templates) or Archicad trademark beyond the allowlists of scripts/check-legal.sh entered the product or documentation (NFR-LEG-002); confirm docs/implementation-status.md is current; record results with date, commit and tester. The fuzz, AS-05 and hardware items start as placeholders that tasks 11, 15 and 18 replace with links to the documents they write. Out of scope: automating R4, the AS-01..AS-04 procedures (doors-windows-core, reference-models, release-candidate).
design: Use `defaults: run: shell: bash` at job level so run.sh runs unchanged on Windows; Node 22 via actions/setup-node with the npm cache keyed on conformance/package-lock.json; cache Playwright browsers under ~/.cache/ms-playwright (Linux), ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright (macOS) and %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\ms-playwright (Windows). Avoid third-party path-filter actions: GitHub's native `on.pull_request.paths` is enough because the matrix is its own workflow. Pitfall: the IFC5 clone in run.sh uses git; on Windows runners git is present, but long paths in node_modules may need `git config --system core.longpaths true` in the job.
acceptance_criteria:
- conformance-matrix.yml passes on all three OS runners for both goldens and both reference-model variants (job links in the pull request).
- The nightly schedule is active and a pull request touching crates/archicraft-ifcx triggers the matrix; a docs-only pull request does not.
- run.sh produces identical PASS lines on all three OSes for the same inputs.
- docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md exists, is linked from docs/testing.md and README, and lists the manual R4 check of IFX-006 (b), the NFR-LEG-002 inspection, the status table check and the placeholders for the fuzz run, AS-05 on three OSes and hardware publication (filled by tasks 11, 15 and 18).
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green.
notes:
SRS: IFX-006 NFR-LEG-002
The checklist is also the home of the per-release items other epics add (AS-01..AS-05 procedures, licence gate); release-candidate extends it.

title: Pin the done model requirements with headless regression tests
description:
WHY: The done model requirements of this epic need named headless tests so that a later slice cannot break them unnoticed; today they are covered only partly by crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs (add_undo_redo_keeps_identity, undo_restores_the_exact_project, deleting_a_storey_can_keep_its_elements, history_is_bounded_and_replayable, relinking_keeps_the_absolute_position) and unit tests in storey.rs, project.rs and units.rs. ELM-004 (M): every element has an editable name (Element.name, UpdateElements; the Name field of the UI is pinned in task 20). ELM-010 (M): every element is on exactly one layer and new elements take the tool's default layer. STR-001 (M): ordered storeys with name, signed elevation and positive height, the top storey with a nominal height used by links beyond it, numbered 0 at the ground, positive above and negative below. STR-004 (M): deleting a storey with elements either deletes them or moves them to another storey keeping their absolute position (model half; the count prompt is pinned in task 20). STR-005 (M): every storey operation (insert, delete, rename, change of elevation or height) undoable without clearing the history. STR-008 (M): cut plane 1.10 m above the storey elevation, overridable per storey. STR-013 (M): one site and one building with editable names. UND-001 (M): element edits, storey operations, resource and setting changes undoable and redoable, at least 100 configurable steps (imports do not exist yet; saving is pinned in task 20). UND-002 (M): no operation clears the history within an open project. NFR-MNT-001 (M): every change a command object that can be executed, undone, redone, logged and replayed (command.rs Command, History, JournalEntry, replay). NFR-ACC-002 (M): numeric input accepted with a resolution of at least 0.1 mm or 1/64 inch and stored at full double precision (units.rs parse_length; the write side is task 04). NFR-ACC-005 (M): values rounded only for display according to the unit settings (units.rs format_length/format_angle).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/tests/done_requirements.rs (headless), one test per requirement named after it (e.g. `str_005_every_storey_command_undoes_exactly`); tests that already exist (commands.rs, storey.rs, project.rs, units.rs unit tests) are referenced in the traceability table of docs/testing.md rather than duplicated. This task keeps the existing behaviour and only adds tests (regression net). Out of scope: new behaviour; the application-level clauses (task 20); recording, not fixing, the gap-row observations that are not requirement clauses (a per-storey cut-plane override cannot be cleared from the UI; History::undo drops both stacks when an inverse fails, command.rs:827-833) unless the fix is under an hour.
design: Mirror the helpers of crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs (ground(), wall()); if both files need them, move them to crates/archicraft-model/tests/common/mod.rs. Build every project from template::default_metric_project() or samples so the tests exercise the command layer. For 'every Command variant', keep an explicit list in the test with a compile-time exhaustiveness guard (a match over Command without a wildcard arm) so a new variant forces the test to be extended. Name tests after requirement ids so scripts/status.py (task 19) can grep them.
acceptance_criteria:
- ELM-004: renaming through UpdateElements changes Element.name, undo restores it, an empty name is rejected (validate.rs:244-246).
- ELM-010: AddElements of a wall and of a slab takes the respective tool default layer; validate_element rejects an unknown layer; DeleteLayer reassigns its elements and the tool defaults to the replacement layer, so every element stays on exactly one existing layer.
- STR-001: after inserting storeys below and above, numbering reads -1/0/+1/+2 in elevation order; elevations may be negative; a zero or negative height is rejected; a wall linked beyond the top storey uses the top storey's nominal height.
- STR-004: DeleteStorey with move keeps every moved element's absolute base and top elevation; DeleteStorey with delete removes them; the number of affected elements (project.elements_on(storey).count(), the value the prompt shows) is asserted before deletion.
- STR-005: each of the six storey commands (InsertStorey above and below, DeleteStorey, RenameStorey, SetStoreyElevation, SetStoreyHeight, SetStoreyCutPlane) undoes to the exact start state and redoes to the edited state, and the undo stack only grows.
- STR-008: the default is 1.10 m, a per-storey override wins in cut_plane_height(storey), and SetStoreyCutPlane undoes.
- STR-013: the project has exactly one site and one building; SetSpatialNames renames both and undo restores them.
- UND-001: one command of each category (element edit, storey operation, layer and material resource change, tool defaults, settings, project information, location) undoes and redoes to the exact state; 150 commands followed by 100 undos all succeed with History::new(100) and with the default limit; a limit below 100 is never produced by the preference path (see task 03).
- UND-002: a scripted session executing every Command variant at least once ends with an undo stack holding every successful command (none clears the history).
- NFR-MNT-001: one instance of every Command variant round-trips through serde_json; replaying a recorded session with command::replay yields a project equal to the original; History::journal lists Executed, Undone and Redone entries with the command labels.
- NFR-ACC-002 (extending the units.rs unit test that parses '1234.5678 mm'): parse_length accepts '0.1 mm', '0.0001' (metre) and '1/64"' and returns exactly 1e-4 and 0.0254/64 (within 1e-15); a value such as 1.23456789 m entered and stored keeps all digits.
- NFR-ACC-005: format_length at 3 decimals displays a rounded value while the stored value stays bit-identical; switching the unit settings to mm with 1 decimal changes only the display.
- docs/testing.md traceability table lists every requirement above with at least one test name.
- cargo test --workspace on all three OS runners, clippy and fmt green.
notes:
SRS: ELM-004 ELM-010 STR-001 STR-004 STR-005 STR-008 STR-013 UND-001 UND-002 NFR-MNT-001 NFR-ACC-002 NFR-ACC-005
The application-level clauses of ELM-004, STR-004 and UND-001 and all UI requirements moved to task 20.

title: Regenerate the status table by script and check it per merge
description:
WHY: The roadmap requires docs/implementation-status.md to be enforced per merge: a CI script compares each merged epic's srs_ids with the changed rows, and no done requirement may regress. Today the table was generated once from gap-analysis.json in a workflow scratchpad outside the repository, so it can be neither regenerated nor checked, and evidence paths are absolute paths of one machine. This epic holds 56 done requirements that rely on the check to stay done: ELM-004 ELM-010 IFX-001 IFX-002 IFX-005 IFX-010 IFX-013 IFX-014 IFX-020 IFX-021 IFX-022 IFX-025 IFX-030 IFX-031 IFX-032 IFX-043 IFX-061 IFX-063 IFX-064 IFX-067 IFX-080 IFX-090 LAY-004 LAY-005 NFR-ACC-001 NFR-ACC-002 NFR-ACC-005 NFR-LEG-002 NFR-MNT-001 NFR-MNT-002 NFR-MNT-004 NFR-PORT-004 NFR-PORT-005 NFR-REL-001 NFR-REL-002 NFR-REL-003 NFR-SEC-001 NFR-SEC-004 NFR-USE-004 PRJ-004 PRJ-005 PRJ-010 STR-001 STR-003 STR-004 STR-005 STR-008 STR-013 UI-006 UI-007 UND-001 UND-002 VIEW-002 VIEW-014 WAL-001 XCH-008.

WHAT: (1) docs/status/requirements.json: the per-requirement rows (id, priority, section, status, evidence, gap, remaining_effort, depends_on) imported once from gap-analysis.json with absolute paths rewritten to repository-relative ones; it becomes the source of truth. (2) scripts/status.py (python3 stdlib): `generate` rewrites the counts, per-section and requirement tables of docs/implementation-status.md between `<!-- status:begin -->` / `<!-- status:end -->` markers from the JSON and docs/SRS.md (live IDs and priorities parsed from lines like '- **WAL-003** · M — ', withdrawn ones skipped); `check` verifies the document is in sync, every live SRS ID has exactly one row, every evidence path exists, and every done row names a test or CI guard in its evidence or in the docs/testing.md traceability table (tasks 01, 03, 06, 07, 15, 20); `merge-check --base <sha>` reads `SRS:` lines from the pull-request body and commit messages, requires each listed ID's row to have changed between base and head, and fails if any row moved from done to partial or missing unless a `Regresses: <ID> <reason>` line is present. (3) A `status` job in ci.yml runs check on every push and merge-check on pull requests; the PR template (task 04) carries the SRS line, and docs/testing.md states that an epic's final '-done' pull request lists the epic's srs_ids. (4) scripts/tests/test_status.py. Out of scope: updating rows for other epics (each epic's done task does), editing the SRS.
design: Parse the SRS with a single regex over lines `^- \*\*([A-Z0-9-]+)\*\* · ([MSC])` and treat requirements marked withdrawn as not live (match the convention used in docs/SRS.md; 567 live IDs today). Keep the generated Markdown byte-stable (sorted by section then document order, no timestamps inside the markers) so `check` is a plain regenerate-and-compare. For merge-check in GitHub Actions read the PR body from $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH and the commits with `git log --format=%B base..HEAD`; run it only on pull_request events. Evidence 'paths exist' is checked on the file part of `path:line` tokens; line numbers are not verified (they drift). Pitfall: the per-section table and counts must be derived, never edited, otherwise check flags them.
acceptance_criteria:
- `python3 scripts/status.py generate` on the committed JSON reproduces the current tables of docs/implementation-status.md (diff limited to the one-time marker comments and the relative evidence paths).
- `check` fails on: a live SRS ID without a row, a row for a withdrawn or unknown ID, an evidence path to a missing file, a done row without a test or guard reference, a hand edit inside the markers; it passes on the committed state.
- `merge-check` fails when the pull request lists an ID whose row did not change, and when a done row regresses without a Regresses line; passes otherwise; all cases covered by scripts/tests/test_status.py, which runs in CI.
- The status job is green on the pull request that introduces it, and docs/testing.md documents the workflow for epics (update rows in requirements.json, run generate, list srs_ids in the PR).
- All 56 done rows of this epic reference at least one test name or CI guard step (from tasks 01, 03, 06, 07 and 20; PRJ-004, PRJ-005, NFR-REL-001 and NFR-REL-002 also gain crash_recovery.rs once task 15 lands).
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green.
notes:
SRS: ELM-004 ELM-010 IFX-001 IFX-002 IFX-005 IFX-010 IFX-013 IFX-014 IFX-020 IFX-021 IFX-022 IFX-025 IFX-030 IFX-031 IFX-032 IFX-043 IFX-061 IFX-063 IFX-064 IFX-067 IFX-080 IFX-090 LAY-004 LAY-005 NFR-ACC-001 NFR-ACC-002 NFR-ACC-005 NFR-LEG-002 NFR-MNT-001 NFR-MNT-002 NFR-MNT-004 NFR-PORT-004 NFR-PORT-005 NFR-REL-001 NFR-REL-002 NFR-REL-003 NFR-SEC-001 NFR-SEC-004 NFR-USE-004 PRJ-004 PRJ-005 PRJ-010 STR-001 STR-003 STR-004 STR-005 STR-008 STR-013 UI-006 UI-007 UND-001 UND-002 VIEW-002 VIEW-014 WAL-001 XCH-008
The script supersedes the one-off generation in the planning scratchpad; gap-analysis.json is imported once and not read again.

title: Add repository guards: ignores, line endings, advisories, layering
description:
WHY: The regression net needs a clean working tree and mechanical guards for done requirements that today hold only by inspection. NFR-PORT-004 (M, done): files are platform-independent and a project saved on one platform opens identically on another; the gap row notes there is no .gitattributes guarding the golden files against CRLF conversion. NFR-LEG-002 (M, done): no Graphisoft content and no Archicad trademarks in UI or documentation except nominative references; verified once by a manual grep. NFR-SEC-001 (M, done): the application works fully offline with no account or licence server; NFR-SEC-004 (M, done): network access only after user consent and only to fetch import URIs named in a file (IFX-081); both hold only because no HTTP crate is in the dependency graph, and nothing keeps it that way until ifcx-interop adds the consent-gated fetch. NFR-MNT-002 (M, done): model, geometry evaluation and IFCX serialization run without the UI; NFR-MNT-004 (M, done): the IFCX reader/writer is a separate versioned module and a new IFCX version needs no change to the model or geometry crates; both hold by the Cargo.toml dependency lists, unguarded. Technical debt from docs/implementation-status.md: deny.toml:42 claims advisories are checked although .github/workflows/ci.yml:79 runs `cargo deny check licenses sources bans`. The neighbouring debt bullet (implementation-status.md:151, 'conformance build artefacts are not git-ignored') is a false positive: the tracked conformance/.gitignore already ignores node_modules/, .build/ and .ifc5/, and `git check-ignore` only reported them because it was run on non-existent paths without a trailing slash; this task keeps that file and corrects the bullet.

WHAT: conformance/.gitignore (existing: node_modules/, .build/, .ifc5/) gains test-results/ and playwright-report/ (task 12); the root .gitignore gains fuzz/target/, fuzz/corpus/, fuzz/artifacts/ and fuzz/coverage/ (task 10); docs/implementation-status.md:151 is corrected. New .gitattributes: `*.ifcx -text` (golden files keep their exact bytes on every checkout) and `*.snap text eol=lf` for insta snapshots. scripts/check-layering.sh: runs `cargo tree -e normal --prefix none` for archicraft-model, archicraft-geometry and archicraft-ifcx and fails if egui, eframe, egui_tiles, wgpu, winit or rfd appear, or if archicraft-ifcx appears under the model or geometry crate; a `--from-file` option lets CI run a negative self-test on canned output. scripts/check-legal.sh: `git grep -n -i -E 'graphisoft|archicad'` over tracked files except docs/SRS.md, docs/technology-choices.md and docs/implementation-status.md, with scripts/legal-allowlist.txt for reviewed nominative lines; it also fails on any tracked image, library-part or template file (`git ls-files` for *.png, *.jpg, *.jpeg, *.gif, *.bmp, *.gsm, *.lcf, *.pln, *.pla, *.tpl, *.aat) not listed in scripts/asset-allowlist.txt with its origin and licence (none today), the mechanical half of 'no Graphisoft content (text, images, library parts, templates)'. deny.toml [bans] denies HTTP client crates (reqwest, ureq, hyper, isahc, curl, attohttpc, surf) with a reason naming NFR-SEC-004/IFX-081; deny.toml [advisories] comment corrected. CI: the licences job runs `check advisories licenses sources bans`; a new `guards` job (ubuntu-24.04) runs both scripts and the negative self-test. docs/testing.md is created as the skeleton the later tasks fill (sections: golden files and ARCHICRAFT_BLESS, snapshots, conformance, fixture registry, Appendix D defaults, done-requirement traceability, fuzzing, security review, performance); its traceability table starts with the rows this task guards (NFR-PORT-004, NFR-LEG-002, NFR-SEC-001, NFR-SEC-004, NFR-MNT-002, NFR-MNT-004), each naming the CI guard step as its regression check (input of task 19). Out of scope: the Playwright, fuzz and bench jobs (tasks 12, 10, 18), any crate source change.
design: Keep the scripts POSIX sh so they also run under Git Bash on Windows; CI runs them on ubuntu only. cargo-deny bans syntax: `deny = [{ crate = "reqwest", reason = "..." }]` (cargo-deny >= 0.16; if the pinned action is older, use `name =`). tokio stays allowed (it arrives through rfd for the native dialogs). The layering check uses `cargo tree -p <crate> -e normal` so dev-dependencies (egui_kittest in tests) do not count. For the legal check, exclude kb-scraper/ (already git-ignored) and the three docs that cite the reference product nominatively; every allowlist line carries a comment why it is nominative. The README gets one line on the guards so contributors know why a dependency was refused. Pitfall: `-text` on *.ifcx only stops end-of-line conversion; diffs still work. Do not mark the files `binary`, reviewers need the text diff (task 04 adds readable snapshots on top).
acceptance_criteria:
- `git check-ignore -v conformance/.ifc5/ conformance/node_modules/ conformance/.build/ conformance/test-results/ conformance/playwright-report/ fuzz/target/ fuzz/corpus/` (directory paths with trailing slash) reports every path; running conformance/run.sh on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx leaves `git status` clean; the false technical-debt bullet in docs/implementation-status.md is corrected.
- `git check-attr text -- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/two-storey-shell.ifcx` reports `unset`; golden_files_are_reproduced stays green on windows-latest with core.autocrlf=true (NFR-PORT-004).
- scripts/check-layering.sh exits 0 on the current tree and non-zero on a canned `cargo tree` output that contains egui under archicraft-model; both runs are CI steps (NFR-MNT-002, NFR-MNT-004).
- scripts/check-legal.sh exits 0 on the current tree, non-zero on a scratch line containing a trademark outside the allowlist and non-zero on a scratch tracked *.gsm or *.png file outside scripts/asset-allowlist.txt (NFR-LEG-002).
- deny.toml bans the listed HTTP crates with a reason; `cargo deny check advisories licenses sources bans` is the CI command and is green; adding `ureq` to any crate fails the bans check (NFR-SEC-001, NFR-SEC-004).
- docs/testing.md exists with the section skeleton and traceability rows for NFR-PORT-004, NFR-LEG-002, NFR-SEC-001, NFR-SEC-004, NFR-MNT-002 and NFR-MNT-004 naming their CI guard steps.
- cargo build/test/clippy -D warnings/fmt --check stay green; no crate source changes; golden files unchanged.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-004 NFR-LEG-002 NFR-SEC-001 NFR-SEC-004 NFR-MNT-002 NFR-MNT-004
The HTTP-crate ban is lifted by ifcx-interop together with the consent prompt of IFX-081; that epic must re-inspect NFR-SEC-004 (gap row).

title: Set up cargo-fuzz targets, seed corpus and the nightly fuzz job
description:
WHY: NFR-REL-007 (S, partial): the application shall not crash on any file of the Appendix D.9 fuzzing corpus; malformed input is rejected with a message. NFR-SEC-003 (M, partial) with D.9: every parser of external files (the IFCX reader, and the SET-004 preference import once it exists) is fuzzed for at least one hour per release with a coverage-guided fuzzer, seeded with the R2 examples and ArchiCraft-generated files. Gaps: no fuzz/ directory, cargo-fuzz not set up, no nightly job in .github/workflows, no corpus, no one-hour run; SET-004 does not exist yet. NFR-LEG-003 (S, another epic) requires the buildingSMART examples to be fetched at test time rather than redistributed. The technology choices plan cargo-fuzz on nightly in its own CI job.

WHAT: fuzz/ in cargo-fuzz layout (its own Cargo workspace; root Cargo.toml gets `exclude = ["fuzz"]`) with targets `ifcx_load` (archicraft_ifcx::load on arbitrary bytes; when it returns Ok, evaluate the geometry, save and load again, all without panicking), `ifcx_validate` (validate::parse + validate::validate) and `units_parse` (archicraft_model::units::parse_length and parse_angle on arbitrary UTF-8 with every unit and number format; the typed-input grammar is a parser of user input), plus fuzz/dict/ifcx.dict with IFCX and archicraft:: keys. scripts/fuzz-corpus.sh builds fuzz/corpus/<target>/ from the reference_models example output, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/corrupt (task 08) and the R2 examples (Hello Wall, PCERT, Tekla House, ACCA) fetched from IFC5-development at the commit conformance/run.sh pins; nothing fetched is committed. .github/workflows/fuzz.yml: nightly schedule and workflow_dispatch with a `minutes` input (nightly 10 minutes per target; release run 60), nightly toolchain only in this job, corpus kept with actions/cache, crash artefacts uploaded, job fails on any crash, timeout or OOM. crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fuzz_regressions.rs replays every file in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fuzz-regressions/ through load() on stable in the normal test job. docs/testing.md 'Fuzzing' section: local run, promoting a crash to a regression file (cargo fuzz tmin), release requirement, and the placeholder for a `prefs_import` target when SET-004 lands. Out of scope: fixing findings beyond trivial ones (task 11).
design: cargo-fuzz uses libfuzzer-sys (libFuzzer is Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, allowed by deny.toml; fuzz/ is outside the workspace, so mention it in the licence inventory by hand). Run with `-rss_limit_mb=2048 -timeout=10 -max_len=4194304` so slow or memory-hungry inputs count as findings (denial of service through a crafted file is in scope of NFR-SEC-003). The R2 fetch uses a sparse, blob-filtered clone of the pinned IFC5-development commit (same as conformance/run.sh) and copies only the example .ifcx files into fuzz/corpus; keep the list of example paths in the script. ifcx_load must not call ModelGeometry::evaluate on absurd inputs without the validation the app performs; mirror the app's open path (load, then evaluate) so findings are real. Pitfall: GitHub-hosted runners cap jobs at 6 hours; the release run of 60 minutes per target fits, running targets sequentially. Pitfall: cache the corpus with a restore-keys prefix so a new night starts from yesterday's corpus.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo +nightly fuzz build` builds the three targets on Linux; `cargo +nightly fuzz run ifcx_load -- -runs=100000 -dict=fuzz/dict/ifcx.dict` on the seeded corpus completes (findings, if any, are handed to task 11 as artefacts).
- scripts/fuzz-corpus.sh creates seeds from both goldens, every corrupt fixture, both reference models and the four fetched R2 examples; `git status` is clean afterwards.
- fuzz.yml is scheduled nightly and runnable on demand with a duration input; a crash makes the job fail and uploads the crashing input; the corpus persists between nights.
- tests/fuzz_regressions.rs runs in the stable test job on all three runners over the regression directory, initially seeded with the inputs of malformed_input_is_rejected_without_panicking.
- The main workspace build, cargo deny and clippy are unaffected by fuzz/ (excluded); fuzz/ has its own `cargo +nightly fmt --check` step in fuzz.yml.
- docs/testing.md documents the workflow, the at-least-one-hour-per-release rule and the SET-004 placeholder. Covers the fuzzing infrastructure of NFR-REL-007 and NFR-SEC-003; the first one-hour campaign is task 11.
notes:
SRS: NFR-REL-007 NFR-SEC-003
Appendix D.9: fuzz each parser of external files at least 1 h per release, coverage-guided, seeded with R2 examples and ArchiCraft files. The prefs_import target is added by the epic that implements SET-004.

title: Pin the Appendix D defaults in a table-driven test
description:
WHY: Appendix D fixes the defaults a new project and a fresh installation start with, and several are clauses of done requirements held by this epic: STR-001 (M, done) ordered storeys numbered from the ground storey 0, with D.1 '00 Ground floor' at +-0.000 m and '01 First floor' at +3.000 m, both 3.00 m high; STR-008 (M, done) plan cut plane 1.10 m above the storey elevation; PRJ-004 (M, done) and NFR-REL-002 (M, done) autosave every 5 minutes by default; NFR-REL-003 (M, done) one backup version by default; UND-001 (M, done) at least 100 undo steps; LAY-004 (M, done) a practical template layer set (structure, exterior walls, interior walls, slabs, roof, openings, stairs and railings, terrain, furniture, 2D construction, references). Further D.1/D.2/D.4 values: metre with 3 decimals, decimal degrees with 2 decimals, model tolerance 0.01 mm, repair thresholds 0.1 mm edges and 0.1 degree slivers (validate.rs MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, MIN_CORNER_ANGLE_DEG), tessellation 2 mm chord deviation and at most 10 degrees per segment (hence at least 36 segments per circle), view range from the storey elevation to the next storey (archicraft-geometry plan.rs ViewRange::for_storey), snap radius 8 px, angle increment 45 degrees; wall 0.25 m masonry with the reference line on the exterior face, base offset 0, top linked to home storey + 1 with offset 0; slab 0.20 m reinforced concrete with its top at the storey elevation; the D.4 material intersection priorities (reinforced concrete 900 ... soil 50). The values are scattered over template.rs, project.rs (Tessellation, cut_plane_height), command.rs (DEFAULT_UNDO_LIMIT = 200), validate.rs (MODEL_TOLERANCE = 1e-5) and the app's persistence/prefs.rs, and the existing template test only counts layers and views, so a refactor can change one silently.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/tests/defaults.rs with a table of rows (Appendix D reference, expected value, tolerance, getter on default_metric_project() or a constant), one assertion per row whose message carries the reference, and a D.4 block that maps every template material by name to its group and asserts the group priority. crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/defaults.rs pins the D.1 view range through ViewRange::for_storey on default_metric_project() (cut 1.10 m, bottom 0 = storey elevation, top = storey height = next storey). crates/archicraft-app/tests/defaults.rs (headless, no egui) pins the preference defaults: autosave_minutes 5, backups 1, undo_steps >= 100 and clamped to >= 100 by sanitized(), snap_radius 8.0, angle_increment_deg 45.0. Rows for Appendix D values that do not exist yet are `Pending { owner }` entries naming the owning epic: column, beam, door, window, roof, stair, railing, curtain wall, terrain and grid defaults (D.2), the D.3 stair rule set, snap reference dwell 1.0 s (point-input-snapping), drawing scale 1:100 (plan-renderer, plan-views-browser), so the table mirrors Appendix D completely and owners convert rows into checks. Out of scope: changing any default, the shipped template file's template_contents test (templates-presets).
design: Rows as `struct Row { reference: &'static str, check: fn(&Project) -> Result<(), String> }` built with a small macro so each row is one line; floats compared with 1e-12. Keep the material-to-group map explicit by material name (the template has 25 materials in template.rs:31-258) rather than deriving it from MaterialCategory, because D.4 groups do not map 1:1 to categories (e.g. glass and aluminium share one group). The app test reads Preferences::default() and exercises the private Preferences::sanitized through Preferences::load on a temporary preferences file (prefs.rs:56-110) without constructing ArchiCraftApp. Pending rows are data, not ignored tests: the test prints the pending list so reviewers see what is still open. Pitfall: D.1 'at least 100 undo steps' is a lower bound, not the value 200; assert >= 100 and the clamp, not equality.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test -p archicraft-model --test defaults passes and pins: wall thickness 0.25 m, material Brick (masonry), ReferenceLine::Outside, base offset 0, TopLink::Relative { storeys: 1, offset: 0 }; slab 0.20 m, Reinforced concrete, SlabReference::Top, offset 0; cut plane 1.10 m (STR-008); storeys '00 Ground floor' 0.0/3.0 and '01 First floor' 3.0/3.0 with ground numbered 0 (STR-001); tessellation 0.002 m and 10 degrees and the derived minimum of 36 segments per circle; MIN_EDGE_LENGTH 1e-4 m and MIN_CORNER_ANGLE_DEG 0.1; metre with 3 decimals; degrees with 2 decimals; MODEL_TOLERANCE 1e-5 m; DEFAULT_UNDO_LIMIT >= 100 (UND-001); the eleven template layers equal the LAY-004 list.
- The D.4 block asserts, for every template material, the priority of its group: reinforced concrete 900, concrete 880, structural steel 860, masonry 800, CLT/glulam 760, structural softwood 740, screed 600, natural stone 560, glass/aluminium 500, thermal insulation 400, gypsum board 350, plaster/render 300, tiles 280, membranes 200, air gap 100, soil/gravel 50; a template material without a group fails the test.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/defaults.rs pins the D.1 view range (cut 1.10 m, bottom at the storey elevation, top at the next storey).
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/defaults.rs pins autosave 5 min (PRJ-004, NFR-REL-002), 1 backup (NFR-REL-003), undo >= 100 with the clamp (checked through Preferences::load on a temporary file with undo_steps 5, because sanitized() is private), snap radius 8 px and angle increment 45 degrees.
- Changing any single value makes exactly its row fail with the Appendix D reference in the message (checked by hand once, noted in the pull request).
- Every D.1, D.2 and D.3 row appears in the table; not-yet-existing values are Pending rows naming their owner epic; docs/testing.md explains how to convert one.
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green.
notes:
SRS: STR-001 STR-008 PRJ-004 NFR-REL-002 NFR-REL-003 UND-001 LAY-004
Appendix D.1 snapping: radius 8 px, reference dwell 1.0 s, angle increment 45 degrees (15 selectable). The shipped-template variant of this test belongs to templates-presets (roadmap verification-asset table).

title: Add the format-migration chain and a successor adapter stub
description:
WHY: IFX-090 (M, done): the IFCX reader and writer are versioned; a release writes exactly one IFCX version (ifcx_alpha against Table 5-2) and reads every version earlier releases wrote. IFX-091 (S, missing): when buildingSMART publishes a successor of ifcx_alpha, ArchiCraft shall provide an automatic migration for existing project files; no successor exists, and O-1 decides to stay on the pinned versions for v1 and migrate in an update, so v1 must make that path ready and tested. NFR-MNT-004 (M, done): adopting a new IFCX version requires no change to the domain model or geometry modules. IFX-092 (C, missing): the ArchiCraft schema may be published on ifcx.dev under its own namespace; gap: the archicraft:: declarations exist only in-file. Context owned elsewhere: IFX-062 (archicraft:: FORMAT_VERSION migration on open, newer-version warning; FORMAT_VERSION = 1 in schema.rs:15). Epic acceptance: a FORMAT_VERSION 1 fixture migrates and a mock successor version routes to the adapter stub.

WHAT: (1) crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs: `upgrade(from: u32, project_attr, nodes, report)` applies registered step functions in order up to FORMAT_VERSION (none registered today) and reports 'migrated from format N' as an info problem; reader.rs calls it before reading. A frozen fixture crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/formats/format-1.ifcx (a copy of a golden written at FORMAT_VERSION 1, excluded from ARCHICRAFT_BLESS) must load without warnings forever; a cfg(test) step registry proves a synthetic v1->v2 step runs and its result validates. (2) lib.rs: the version match becomes an adapter table (`struct Adapter { version, read }`); WRITTEN_VERSION unchanged; ReadOutcome gains `source_version` so the app can tell the user a file will be saved in the current version. (3) crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/successor/ behind cargo feature `successor-stub` (off in release builds, enabled in this crate's tests): IFCX_VERSION 'ifcx_successor_mock', a reader that maps the header and delegates to alpha::reader, i.e. the 'copy alpha/' pattern of the extension point. (4) docs/ifcx-evolution.md runbook for a real successor: new adapter module, Table 5-2 pins and bundled schemas (registry.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/schemas), conformance IFC5 commit pin, writer switch, alpha reader kept, migration notice and overwrite confirmation, golden re-bless. (5) IFX-092 readiness: schema.rs exposes `declarations()`; an example `archicraft_schema` writes a standalone schema document; docs list the manual publication steps (namespace, licence of the schema text, versioning with FORMAT_VERSION). The writer keeps declaring in-file (IFX-005, IFX-061 stay satisfied). Out of scope: a real successor, publishing on ifcx.dev.
design: Follow the extension point 'Add a new IFCX version adapter' (docs/implementation-status.md): copy crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha as the template, keep alpha untouched. To let a test resolve a non-bundled import, add `validate::validate_with(file, extra: &[(&str, &IfcxFile)])` (SchemaSet::for_file gains extra sources; registry.rs stays the production list). Migration steps operate on the flattened JSON (IndexMap<String, FlatNode> plus the archicraft::project object) before typed reading, so a step never needs the old Rust types. The successor feature must not be in `default`, and CI builds the crate once with `--features successor-stub` in the test job. Pitfall: the frozen fixture's bytes must never be regenerated; guard it with a test that hashes the file and fails with 'frozen format fixture changed'.
acceptance_criteria:
- format-1.ifcx loads with no warnings into a project with the expected storeys, elements and names, and its ReadOutcome reports source_version 'ifcx_alpha'; the golden bless loop skips tests/formats/.
- With the cfg(test) step registry, a file at format 1 is upgraded by a synthetic v1->v2 step, the step's change is visible in the loaded project and the info problem 'migrated from format 1' is reported.
- With feature successor-stub, a golden whose header.ifcxVersion is rewritten to 'ifcx_successor_mock' routes to the stub (asserted via source_version) and loads to the same project as the original; an unknown version still fails with the message naming the supported versions; save still writes ifcx_alpha only (IFX-090).
- `cargo tree -p archicraft-model` and `-p archicraft-geometry` are unchanged by the stub (NFR-MNT-004; guarded by task 01's script).
- `cargo run -p archicraft-ifcx --example archicraft_schema -- out.ifcx` writes a schema-only IFCX document; a test removes the in-file archicraft:: schemas from a golden, adds an import of that document under a placeholder URI resolved from a test-local registry, and validate() returns no problems (IFX-092 readiness).
- docs/ifcx-evolution.md exists and is linked from the crate docs and docs/testing.md.
- Workspace tests (with and without the feature), clippy and fmt green; golden files unchanged.
notes:
SRS: IFX-090 IFX-091 IFX-092 NFR-MNT-004
O-1: stay on the pinned versions for v1 and migrate in an update. Placeholder schema URI for the readiness test: https://ifcx.dev/@archicraft/archicraft@v1.ifcx (not resolvable; the real namespace is decided at publication).

title: Pin the done IFCX requirements with named regression tests
description:
WHY: This epic holds the done IFCX requirements no other epic extends, and each needs a named test so that a later slice cannot break it unnoticed. IFX-001 (M): ifcx_alpha structure, UTF-8 JSON with header, imports, schemas, data, extension .ifcx (the extension handling of the app is pinned in task 20). IFX-002 (M): header id, ifcxVersion 'ifcx_alpha', dataVersion incremented on every save, author, ISO 8601 UTC timestamp (the dataVersion increment and the author preference live in the app and are pinned in task 20). IFX-005 (M): every attribute key in data declared by an import or in schemas. IFX-010 (M): UUID paths for project, site, building, storey, element, part, type and material; regenerated sub-nodes get v5 UUIDs from owner and role. IFX-013 (M): IfcProject is the only root; header.id derived from the project UUID, unchanged on rename or move. IFX-014 (M): child keys unique, readable, stable, unchanged on rename, form <Kind>_<8 hex>. IFX-020 (M): bsi::ifc::class code and bSDD uri per Table 5-1. IFX-021 (M): bsi::ifc::prop::Name on project, site, building, storey and element; descriptions as bsi::ifc::prop::Description. IFX-022 (S): IsExternal when the position is known. IFX-025 (M): own holes (slab holes) are geometry, not IfcOpeningElement. IFX-030 (M): metres, right-handed, +Z up. IFX-031 (M): row-major usd::xformop with translation in the fourth row, storey transform translates by its elevation, world points within 0.1 mm. IFX-032 (M): closed, 2-manifold, consistently oriented triangle meshes. IFX-043 (M): named material nodes, every part references a named material. IFX-061 (M): every archicraft:: attribute declared in schemas. IFX-063 (M): the standard attributes alone describe geometry and meaning. IFX-064 (M): round-trip fidelity within 0.1 mm. IFX-067 (M): unused resources inside archicraft::project, single root. IFX-080 (M) and XCH-008 (M): open every file the system wrote with full editability. IFX-090 (M): versioned reader/writer, one written version. LAY-005 (M): layer assignment in the ArchiCraft namespace, visibility never affects standard content (gap: no test writes a hidden layer). PRJ-010 (S): project information (name, number, description, client, address, author) editable (Command::SetInfo) and written, name and description on the project node and the rest in archicraft::project (gap: round trips only cover empty info fields). NFR-ACC-001 (M) and NFR-ACC-002 (M): double precision, round-trip precision for parameters. NFR-PORT-004 (M): platform-independent files.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/done_requirements.rs with one test per requirement, named after it (e.g. `ifx_013_header_id_survives_rename`, `lay_005_hidden_layers_do_not_change_standard_content`), using samples::two_storey_shell and small projects built through commands and the shared helpers of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/common/mod.rs (task 02); existing tests in roundtrip.rs that already cover a clause are referenced, not duplicated. docs/testing.md gets the 'Done requirements and their tests' table: one row per done requirement of this epic in the IFCX area with the test names (input of the status check in task 19). If a test exposes a defect, fix it here when it takes under an hour; otherwise file a bug bead and mark the row. Out of scope: new behaviour; model and app requirements (task 07).
design: Reuse the helpers options(), save(), edit() and node_index() from crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/common/mod.rs, which task 02 extracts from roundtrip.rs. For IFX-063 strip keys starting with 'archicraft::' from data[].attributes and schemas, then run validate::validate and compare a projection (class code, Name, number of mesh children per element) of validate::flatten on both files; the reference-viewer check of the stripped file comes for free once task 12 lands. For LAY-005 compare the standard-namespace projection, not bytes (archicraft::project carries the visibility flags). Table 5-1 URIs: derive the expected uri from the class code with the bSDD IFC 4.3 pattern the writer uses (writer.rs class attribute), and assert the pattern rather than duplicating the writer's table. Name tests after the requirement so the status script (task 19) can grep them.
acceptance_criteria:
- done_requirements.rs passes with at least these tests: IFX-001 the output is valid UTF-8 and its top-level object has exactly the members header, imports, schemas and data; IFX-002 header.id equals 'archicraft:project/<project UUID>', ifcxVersion 'ifcx_alpha', dataVersion and author as given in WriteOptions, ISO 8601 UTC timestamp pattern; IFX-005 every data attribute key resolves to a bundled import or an in-file schema; IFX-010 every project, site, building, storey, element and material node path parses as an RFC 9562 UUID (version 4 for objects created in the test), every Body and Axis sub-node path equals writer::sub_node_id(owner, role) (version 5), and the Body sub-node path is unchanged after a wall thickness change; IFX-013 header.id unchanged after renaming the project and saving under another path; IFX-014 child keys match `^[A-Z][A-Za-z]+_[0-9a-f]{8}$`, are unique per parent and unchanged after renaming an element; IFX-020 class code per Table 5-1 (IfcProject, IfcSite, IfcBuilding, IfcBuildingStorey, IfcWall for walls, IfcSlab for slabs, and the IfcFooting/IfcCovering overrides of the IfcClass enum) with the Table 5-1 parent, and uri `https://identifier.buildingsmart.org/uri/buildingsmart/ifc/4.3/class/<Code>`, on every spatial node and element (compound parts do not exist yet; the owners of IFX-016 extend the test); IFX-021 Name everywhere and Description on the project; IFX-022 IsExternal true/false for exterior/interior walls and absent for an undefined slab; IFX-025 the stair hole of two_storey_shell creates no IfcOpeningElement and no Void child; IFX-030 a 5 m wall along +X with height 2.7 m yields mesh extents of 5 m by its thickness by 2.7 m with z up (metres, right-handed, +Y = project north) and true north and survey point round-trip in archicraft::project.location; IFX-031 storey transform row-major with z = elevation and world points within 0.1 mm; IFX-043 every body references a material node with a Name; IFX-061 every archicraft:: key has a value description; IFX-063 a copy with every archicraft:: attribute and schema removed still validates and composes to the same classes, names and mesh counts; IFX-064 regenerated mesh points within 0.1 mm on a project with non-trivial coordinates; IFX-067 an unused material and layer sit in archicraft::project and the tree has one root; IFX-080/XCH-008 every element of a loaded file accepts an UpdateElements command; IFX-090 load dispatches on ifcxVersion and the writer emits only ifcx_alpha; LAY-005 a project with a hidden and a locked layer writes standard-namespace content identical to the all-visible project; PRJ-010 SetInfo changes all six info fields and undo restores them, and all six with non-ASCII text round-trip (name/description on the project node as bsi::ifc::prop::Name/Description, the rest in archicraft::project); NFR-ACC-001 a wall at (9999.99, -9999.99) round-trips its parameters bit-exactly and its exported mesh points lie within 0.01 mm of the model; NFR-PORT-004 output contains no carriage return and no platform path.
- IFX-001 and IFX-032 rows reference container_matches_the_ifcx_json_schema and written_meshes_are_closed_bodies.
- docs/testing.md lists every done IFCX-area requirement of this epic with at least one test name.
- cargo test --workspace (all three OS runners), clippy and fmt green; golden files unchanged.
notes:
SRS: IFX-001 IFX-002 IFX-005 IFX-010 IFX-013 IFX-014 IFX-020 IFX-021 IFX-022 IFX-025 IFX-030 IFX-031 IFX-032 IFX-043 IFX-061 IFX-063 IFX-064 IFX-067 IFX-080 IFX-090 XCH-008 LAY-005 PRJ-010 NFR-ACC-001 NFR-ACC-002 NFR-PORT-004
Observation from the gap rows kept for the record: IFX-032 validity rests on the generator and tests (the writer does not call check_closed); IFX-021 element descriptions do not exist in the model yet.

title: Inject an autosave clock and automate AS-05 crash recovery end to end
description:
WHY: AS-05 (SRS 7.2): force-terminate the application six minutes after the last save, while editing; on restart the user is offered recovery, the recovered model contains everything up to the last autosave, and the original file is intact; it must pass on Windows, macOS and Linux, and the increment-1 exit (roadmap) requires it automated. PRJ-004 (M, done): recovery data at a configurable interval (default 5 minutes) in a location separate from the project file, restore offered at the next start, the project file not overwritten until the user saves. NFR-REL-002 (M, done): at most the work since the last autosave is lost. NFR-REL-001 (M, done) and PRJ-005 (M, done): atomic save with backups. Gap (AS-05 row): the mechanics are unit-tested (autosave.rs:236-273, persistence/mod.rs tests) but there is no end-to-end test that spawns the app, edits, kills it after the interval and restarts, no UI test of the recovery dialog, and the six-minute timing is not exercised because the autosave trigger uses Instant with no injectable clock (app.rs:60, 112, 497-512).

WHAT: (1) crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/autosave.rs: `pub trait Clock: Send + Sync + Debug { fn now(&self) -> Duration }` with `SystemClock` (monotonic since start) and `ManualClock` (shared atomic milliseconds with advance()); ArchiCraftApp stores `Arc<dyn Clock>` and `last_autosave: Duration`; `ArchiCraftApp::with_clock(dirs, prefs, log, open, clock)` (new() uses SystemClock); `Autosaver::wait_idle(timeout)` for tests. (2) In-process kittest tests: with a ManualClock and an edit at t = 0, no autosave at 4:59, an autosave at 5:00, none without further changes, and a 2-minute preference is honoured. (3) crates/archicraft-app/tests/crash_recovery.rs: the parent test re-runs its own test binary as a child process (role chosen by an environment variable, ARCHICRAFT_DATA_DIR pointing to a temp folder). The child builds the real ArchiCraftApp in an egui_kittest harness with a ManualClock, saves a project to house.ifcx through the app's save path, edits at minute 1, advances to minute 5 and waits until the autosave is written, edits again at minute 5.5, advances to minute 6, writes a ready marker and keeps stepping frames. The parent kills it (Child::kill: SIGKILL or TerminateProcess, no destructors run), waits for exit, then starts a fresh ArchiCraftApp on the same data folder and asserts the 'Recover unsaved work' window, clicks Recover, and checks the recovered content, the dirty state and the original file. The test runs in the normal test job on all three OS runners. (4) docs/test-plan/as-05.md: the manual procedure with the windowed binary; this task replaces the AS-05 placeholder of docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md (task 13) with a link to it. The child and parent reuse the harness helpers of crates/archicraft-app/tests/common/mod.rs (task 20). Out of scope: crash reports (NFR-SEC-002), running the windowed binary under a compositor in CI.
design: The kittest harness runs the real ArchiCraftApp (Session lock, Autosaver thread, recovery discovery) without a window or GPU, which is why the spawned child uses it instead of the eframe binary: macOS runners have no usable GPU and Linux runners no display. Re-invoking the test binary: `Command::new(std::env::current_exe()?)` with args `["--exact", "as05_child", "--ignored", "--nocapture"]` and env ARCHICRAFT_AS05_ROLE=child. Session locking uses std File::try_lock (autosave.rs:54, 129); the OS releases the lock when the process dies, which is exactly what find_abandoned relies on; on Windows wait for the child to exit after kill before scanning, or the handle may still be open. Edits are commands executed through app.workspace() (the existing test accessor) so no pointer input is needed. Keep SystemClock the default in production; ManualClock lives in the library (not cfg(test)) because integration tests are a separate crate. Pitfall: ctx.request_repaint_after(30 s) in autosave() is irrelevant under kittest; step frames explicitly after each clock advance.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit/kittest tests prove the trigger with the injected clock: no autosave before 5:00, one at 5:00, none without changes, interval from preferences.
- crash_recovery.rs passes on ubuntu, windows and macos runners: after the kill six virtual minutes after the save, the restarted app shows 'Recover unsaved work'; Recover yields a project that contains the minute-1 edit and not the minute-5.5 edit (everything up to the last autosave); the document is marked unsaved; house.ifcx is byte-identical to the saved file (original intact, PRJ-004, NFR-REL-001); the killed session's folder is consumed or discarded after recovery; autosave files were written only below DataDirs::recovery() and the project folder holds nothing but house.ifcx and its backup (separate location, PRJ-004).
- The child role never runs on its own (the child test is #[ignore] and refuses to run without the role variable).
- The test completes in under 60 seconds and leaves no processes or temp folders behind on any runner.
- docs/test-plan/as-05.md exists and the release checklist links to it instead of the placeholder.
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green. Automates AS-05 and re-verifies PRJ-004, PRJ-005, NFR-REL-001 and NFR-REL-002 end to end.
notes:
SRS: PRJ-004 PRJ-005 NFR-REL-001 NFR-REL-002
Appendix D.1: autosave 5 minutes, 1 backup version.

title: Enforce the D.9 limits before reading and unit-test each one
description:
WHY: NFR-SEC-003 (M, partial): all imported files are untrusted input; parsers enforce the Appendix D.9 limits and no file content is ever executed. D.9: file size at most 2 GB, JSON nesting fewer than 128 levels, IFCX composition depth (children/inherits chains) at most 64, at most 32 imports. Gaps: no unit tests for MAX_FILE_SIZE, MAX_IMPORTS or MAX_COMPOSITION_DEPTH (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:19-23); the 2 GB check in validate::parse runs after the whole file has been read into memory (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:153-160 std::fs::read, and the recovery path app.rs:269-271 does the same). The composition limit is enforced by validate::roots, which stops at depth 64 and reports, but no test proves it on a pathological chain.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx: `pub fn load_path(path: &Path) -> Result<ReadOutcome, Problem>` that checks `metadata().len()` against MAX_FILE_SIZE before reading and reads through `Read::take(MAX_FILE_SIZE as u64 + 1)` so a file growing during the read is still rejected; an internal `read_bounded(reader, declared_len, limit)` makes the check testable with a small limit. app.rs open_path and the recovery path use load_path. New crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/limits.rs. docs/testing.md 'Security review' section states the no-execution property (no eval, no plugin loading, no process spawning in the reader; file content only ever becomes data) and that it is reviewed per release; deny.toml [bans] additionally denies script-engine and dynamic-loading crates (rhai, mlua, rlua, boa_engine, deno_core, v8, wasmtime, wasmer, libloading) with a reason naming NFR-SEC-003, so the 'never executed' clause is guarded mechanically. Out of scope: the preference import of SET-004 (does not exist yet), fuzzing (task 10).
design: Keep validate::parse(bytes) for in-memory callers (tests, fuzz targets) and add the path-based entry point on top; `load(bytes)` stays the core. For the size test, never allocate 2 GB: test read_bounded with limit = 1 KiB and a `CountingReader` wrapper. serde_json's recursion limit of 128 is the JSON nesting limit (technology-choices.md:244); assert the exact boundary in the test because a serde_json upgrade could change it. validate::roots (validate.rs:258-301) memoises depths, so the 100,000-node chain is linear; the chain test guards against a future recursive traversal in the reader. Pitfall: Windows reports metadata().len() for files opened by other processes correctly, but a FIFO or device path has no length; treat a zero/unknown length as 'unknown' and rely on take().
acceptance_criteria:
- limits.rs: 32 imports pass the limit (unknown imports are reported as unresolved, not as the limit error) and 33 are rejected with 'more than 32 imports'; a children chain of depth 64 loads, depth 65 is reported as 'composition is nested too deeply' with the node path, and an inherits chain behaves the same; a chain of 100,000 nodes completes in under a second without stack overflow; JSON nested 127 levels inside an attribute value parses, 128 or more is rejected with a message and no stack overflow.
- Size: read_bounded rejects a declared length above the limit after reading zero bytes (a counting reader proves it), rejects a stream that grows past the limit, and accepts a stream at exactly the limit; MAX_FILE_SIZE, MAX_IMPORTS and MAX_COMPOSITION_DEPTH equal the D.9 values (2 GB, 32, 64).
- app.rs opens and recovers through load_path; an egui_kittest test opening a non-existent or oversized (limit lowered through the internal API) file shows the 'Cannot open the project' message instead of panicking.
- The 'more than 2 GB' message is user-facing English and names the limit.
- docs/testing.md security section exists; deny.toml bans the listed script-engine and dynamic-loading crates, and adding libloading to any crate fails `cargo deny check bans`.
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green. Satisfies the limit clauses of NFR-SEC-003 (fuzzing clause: tasks 10 and 11).
notes:
SRS: NFR-SEC-003
Appendix D.9: size <= 2 GB, JSON nesting < 128, composition depth <= 64, imports <= 32; the nesting limit is serde_json's (technology choices).

title: Offer indented IFCX output as a save preference
description:
WHY: IFX-008 (C, partial): the user may choose between compact JSON (the default) and indented, human-readable JSON when saving. Gap: crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:141 always passes pretty = false to archicraft_ifcx::save, and no preference or save option exists. The gap row names the SET-001 preferences dialog as a dependency; a Preferences window already exists (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:679 preferences_window), so the option can land now. The writer already produces indented output (json.rs to_string with pretty = true), and task 04 proves it round-trips.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs: `indented_ifcx: bool` (serde default false, documented as IFX-008). Document::to_bytes takes the choice from the caller (app.rs save and save-as paths pass ws.prefs.indented_ifcx); autosave stays compact (recovery data, smaller and faster to write, NFR-PERF-009) and the choice is documented. Preferences dialog row 'Indented IFCX (human-readable)' with a hover text that files become larger. crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs gains `--indented` so CI conformance also checks an indented file. Out of scope: a per-save option in the native file dialog (rfd cannot add custom controls portably), indenting autosave files.
design: Follow the 'Add a preference' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md: field with #[serde(default)], clamp not needed for a bool, a row in Dialogs::preferences_window (dialogs.rs:679-750, next to digit grouping), read ws.prefs.indented_ifcx where Document::to_bytes is called (app.rs:214-235). Keep the Document API explicit (`to_bytes(author, indented)`) instead of passing the whole Preferences, so document.rs stays testable without prefs. Pitfall: the IFX-062 overwrite-newer flow re-enters the save path; make sure it forwards the flag too.
acceptance_criteria:
- prefs.rs unit tests: the default is false; a preference file without the field loads with false; true survives save and load.
- document.rs test: with the option on, the bytes contain newlines with two-space indentation, load back to a project equal to the original, and a later compact save is byte-identical to a compact save of the same project (header fields aside).
- egui_kittest test in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the Preferences window shows 'Indented IFCX (human-readable)'; toggling it and pressing OK sets ws.prefs.indented_ifcx.
- The CI conformance job also runs conformance/run.sh on `reference_models --indented` output and passes.
- Autosave output stays compact (unit test on the bytes passed to write_autosave).
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green. Satisfies IFX-008.
notes: SRS: IFX-008

title: Report every skipped or repaired record when reading IFCX
description:
WHY: PRJ-008 (M, partial): when a file is damaged or partly invalid, the system loads all valid parts, then presents a report of every skipped, repaired or placeholder object with the reason, and never omits objects silently (NFR-REL-004). The gap row lists silent drops and defaults in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs: layer records that are not objects (reader.rs:266 `record.as_object()?`), malformed view records (reader.rs:391-405 filter_map with `.ok()?`), a missing or invalid toolDefaults object (reader.rs:390 `.ok()`), project info fields (384-387 unwrap_or_default), counters (406-410 silently 0 or clamped) and element position/locked (720-721). Further silent fallbacks of the same kind: rgb() drops non-numeric colour components (147) and an invalid groundStorey uuid becomes None (389). The load report UI exists (Prompt::LoadReport in app.rs), so every new Problem reaches the user.

WHAT: reader.rs: read_layer reports 'layer record N is not an object; skipped'; the views loop keeps valid views and reports each malformed one with its index and reason; read_tool_defaults handles a missing or non-object toolDefaults with a warning 'tool defaults missing; template defaults used'; present-but-invalid info fields, a missing info object, negative, non-integer or out-of-range counters and missing counters are reported as repaired; element position and locked of the wrong type are reported; an rgb with a non-numeric component is reported and the default colour used; an invalid groundStorey is reported before storey_list picks a ground. Corrupted fixtures under crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/corrupt/ are generated from samples by a test (regenerated under ARCHICRAFT_BLESS like the goldens) and committed, so task 10 can seed the fuzz corpus with them. Out of scope: the referential-integrity repairs of NFR-REL-004 beyond the reader, a redesign of the load-report window.
design: All reporting goes through the existing Report helper (reader.rs:42-66): `report.or(result, default)` already warns with 'a default value is used'; add `report.skipped(what, index, reason)` and `report.repaired(what, reason)` so messages are uniform and greppable. Distinguish absent optional fields that the writer may legitimately omit (none today: the writer writes all six info fields and both counters) from damage; document the rule in the module docs. The corrupt-fixture generator uses the edit() helper of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/common/mod.rs (task 02) on samples::storey_with_walls_and_slab. A missing info object is already reported through report.or (reader.rs:380); keep it and add the field-level reports. Pitfall: a counter clamp that silently changes a value is a repair and must be reported; NameCounters only grows, so clamping to the number of existing elements of that kind is the deterministic repair.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/corrupt.rs: each committed fixture loads successfully and keeps all valid parts: non-object layer (layers[1] = 42; the other layers load), malformed views (one with projection 'fisheye', one a string; the valid view loads), missing toolDefaults (defaults from the template), bad counters (wall -5, slab 'x', counters missing), info.client = 7, element locked = 'yes' and position = 3, material colour ['a', 0, 0], groundStorey 'not-a-uuid'.
- For every fixture, the problems list holds an entry whose path is the affected node (project node or element path) and whose message names the record and whether it was skipped or repaired.
- A generic invariant test counts records per collection (materials, layers, views, storeys, elements) in each fixture and asserts loaded + reported-skipped = present, so no record disappears silently.
- The existing lenient-reading tests (invalid_elements_are_skipped_and_reported, missing_references_are_repaired_and_reported, schema_violations_are_reported) stay green; golden files load with an empty problems list.
- An egui_kittest test opens a corrupted fixture through ArchiCraftApp::open_path and finds the load-report window with at least one entry.
- Workspace tests, clippy and fmt green. Satisfies the 'never omit silently' clause of PRJ-008.
notes:
SRS: PRJ-008
Related but owned elsewhere: NFR-REL-004 referential integrity on open, IFX-083 third-party composition reports (ifcx-interop).

title: Instrument frame time and edit latency behind a perf feature
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-001 (M, partial) demands a measurement protocol on the documented hardware classes; the targets it frames are 3D navigation >= 30 frames/s (NFR-PERF-003), plan pan/zoom >= 30 frames/s (NFR-PERF-004), input feedback within 50 ms (NFR-PERF-005), plan and 3D updated within 200 ms after a single-element edit (NFR-PERF-006), no UI freeze over 1 s (NFR-PERF-007) and autosave blocking at most 200 ms (NFR-PERF-009), all owned by later epics. None can be measured today: the application has no frame or latency instrumentation (AS-07 row). The criterion benches of task 16 cover headless work only; frame time and end-to-end latency need the running app.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app cargo feature `perf` (off by default, no code compiled without it): src/perf.rs with a PerfRecorder (fixed-bucket histograms, no new dependency) recording frame time (start to end of ArchiCraftApp::update plus egui's frame delta), edit latency (Workspace::execute until geometry and the active plan cache match the new revision), pointer-to-feedback latency in the plan view (pointer event to snap result and preview), UI-thread time spent in Autosaver::request, and the longest frame (frames over 1 s logged as warnings). Results: a JSON file perf-<timestamp>.json in the data folder on exit and a summary log line (p50, p95, p99, max per metric); a 'Performance' window in the View menu (feature only). Scripted runs: ARCHICRAFT_PERF_SCRIPT=orbit|pan|zoom|plan-pan drives the active view's camera for a fixed number of frames on the open project and exits writing the results, for the manual protocol on reference hardware. A CI step builds and tests archicraft-app with --features perf on ubuntu. Out of scope: GPU timestamp queries, CI thresholds on frame times (shared runners are too noisy), meeting the targets.
design: Hooks: ArchiCraftApp::update (app.rs, eframe::App) for frame time; Workspace::execute (workspace.rs:123-136) stamps the revision and Document's geometry/plan cache refresh (document.rs:97-103) closes the sample; plan.rs point-input path (around plan.rs:443-490) for pointer-to-feedback; app.rs autosave() around autosaver.request. Use std::time::Instant inside the recorder only; a small macro `perf_span!(recorder, Metric::Edit)` expands to nothing without the feature. Keep histograms in microseconds with logarithmic buckets from 10 us to 10 s. Pitfall: egui only repaints on input; scripted runs must call ctx.request_repaint() every frame, otherwise frame rates measure idle time.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo build -p archicraft-app` without the feature contains no perf code (the module and hooks are behind cfg(feature = "perf")); clippy is clean with and without it.
