- `cargo test -p archicraft-app --features perf`: a kittest test executes a wall move on two_storey_shell and the recorder holds at least one edit-latency sample and frame samples; histogram percentiles are unit-tested on synthetic samples; the JSON output parses and matches the documented shape.
- A scripted run (ARCHICRAFT_PERF_SCRIPT=plan-pan on two_storey_shell) on a developer machine writes perf-<timestamp>.json with p50/p95/p99/max per metric; task 18 turns such a run into the first docs/performance/ results file.
- The CI test job builds and tests with --features perf on ubuntu.
- docs/performance/README.md (created by task 16) gains a section that documents the metrics, their mapping to NFR-PERF-003..007/009 and how to run a scripted measurement.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-001
Measured targets (owned elsewhere): NFR-PERF-003, -004, -005, -006, -007, -009.

title: Run the first one-hour fuzz campaign and fix its findings
description:
WHY: Appendix D.9 requires at least one hour of coverage-guided fuzzing per parser and release; NFR-REL-007 (S) requires no crash on any corpus file with malformed input rejected with a message; NFR-SEC-003 (M) treats every imported file as untrusted. The epic's risk list budgets reader fixes for fuzz findings. Likely hot spots from reading the code: index-based access in the reader (e.g. reader.rs:620 `project.layers[0]` after the default-layer repair), u32 casts of counters and indices, NaN or infinite parameters reaching geometry (caught by catch_unwind in evaluate.rs:69, but not necessarily by the reader), huge outline arrays (time-outs), deep but legal JSON inside attributes walking validate::check_value recursively, and the unit grammar on unusual Unicode.

WHAT: run ifcx_load and ifcx_validate for 60 minutes each and units_parse for 30 minutes on the seeded corpus (fuzz.yml workflow_dispatch or a Linux workstation); triage every crash, time-out (> 10 s) and OOM (> 2 GB RSS); fix root causes in archicraft-ifcx, archicraft-model validate.rs/units.rs or archicraft-geometry; minimise each input with `cargo fuzz tmin` and commit it to crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fuzz-regressions/ (units findings as unit tests in units.rs); rerun ifcx_load for a clean 60 minutes after the fixes; record the campaign in docs/testing.md (date, commit, target, duration, executions, coverage, findings and fixes). Out of scope: new features; findings that need a design change are filed as bug beads with the minimised input attached and the campaign is still recorded.
design: Fix at the boundary: the reader validates and reports (task 08's Report helpers), validate_element rejects invalid parameters, and geometry never sees values the model would reject. Prefer bounded algorithms over larger limits: e.g. cap the number of outline points per slab in validate.rs with a reported error rather than letting triangulation run for minutes. Use `cargo fuzz coverage` once to see which reader branches the corpus misses and add hand-written seeds for them (e.g. a file with every optional field absent). Keep fixes small and each in its own commit referencing the regression file, so a later bisect is easy.
acceptance_criteria:
- A final 60-minute ifcx_load run and a 60-minute ifcx_validate run on the fix commit finish without crash, time-out or OOM (job link or log in the pull request); units_parse runs 30 minutes clean.
- Every finding has a minimised regression input replayed by tests/fuzz_regressions.rs (or a unit test for units findings) that fails before and passes after its fix.
- Malformed inputs found by the campaign produce a Problem with a message, never a panic, when opened through archicraft_ifcx::load (NFR-REL-007).
- The application does not crash either: an egui_kittest test in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs opens every file of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fuzz-regressions/ and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/corrupt/ through ArchiCraftApp::open_path and finds the load report or the 'Cannot open the project' message, with no panic.
- docs/testing.md holds the campaign record, and this task replaces the fuzz placeholder of docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md (task 13) with a link to it as the template for per-release runs.
- Golden files unchanged unless a fix changes output, in which case they are re-blessed and the diff reviewed; workspace tests, clippy and fmt green.
notes:
SRS: NFR-REL-007 NFR-SEC-003
Thresholds used for findings: single input > 10 s or > 2 GB RSS (proposal; record them in docs/testing.md).

title: Regression net, fixture registry, fuzzing, headless viewer, performance harness and status upkeep
description:
Keep the increment-0 behaviour verified from day one and build the verification infrastructure every later epic plugs into: the D.7 fixture registry (crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs with f1..f9 entries that the owning epics fill), IFX-006 (b) through the pinned reference viewer run headless under Playwright on every golden file and all three CI runners, byte determinism with rounded storey elevations and plan coordinates and the optional indented output, cargo-fuzz for the IFCX reader (and the preference importer once it exists) in a nightly job seeded with ArchiCraft files and fetched R2 examples with the D.9 limits unit-tested, a reader that never drops a record silently, the format-evolution path (successor adapter skeleton, schema publication readiness), the AS-05 end-to-end crash-recovery run with an injectable autosave clock, an Appendix D table-driven defaults test, the performance harness (criterion benches for open/save/evaluate/slice, frame and edit-latency instrumentation behind a feature, CI smoke-mode bench run failing on >20 % regressions, docs/performance/<date>-<machine>.md results convention) with the NFR-PERF-001 hardware decision recorded, and docs/implementation-status.md enforced per merge. The task estimates add up to about 22 engineer-days (178 h, 21 tasks after splitting the app regression tests into task 20), above the 15-day epic cap; if the cap holds, the frame/edit-latency instrumentation (task 17), the IFX-092 schema-publication part of task 14 and the IFX-008 preference (task 05, Could) are the second-wave candidates, because no increment-1 exit criterion depends on them; the product owner must confirm the cap or the deferral.

title: Create the D.7 fixture registry with f1..f9 slots and generic checks
description:
WHY: Appendix D.7 defines nine acceptance fixtures: F1 trapezoidal wall 300 mm at the start and 500 mm at the end (KB 303968), F2 layered wall brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm (KB 303787), F3 floating floor (KB 303722), F4 precast double-pitch beam with four segments (KB 303950), F5 precast corbel column (KB 303947), F6 three walls at one node with junction orders 8/8/8 versus 8/8/7 (KB 303922), F7 T-junction with concrete and insulation, then the priorities swapped (KB 303922; 880/400 with the D.4 defaults), F8 slab traced from a curved wall's reference line and core face with zero gaps (KB 669891), F9 sloping-site house with storeys -3..+1 (KB 364093). The increment-1 exit criterion names F1, F2, F6 and F7; owners are junction-engine (F1, F6, F7), layer-structures (F2, F3), members-profiles-adv (F4, F5), curved-geometry (F8) and terrain-and-site/reference-models (F9). Today none exists (implementation-status: F3 partial, the rest absent). One registry lets every owner add a constructor and inherit the generic checks: integrity, geometry evaluation without problems and closed 2-manifold bodies (IFX-032, M, done), and an IFCX round trip in which every element stays editable with its parameters and regenerated geometry equals the stored geometry within 0.1 mm (IFX-064, M, done).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (`pub mod fixtures` in lib.rs, headless): `pub struct Fixture { id, title, source, owner, increment: u8, seeded: bool, build: Option<fn() -> Project> }`, `pub const D7: [Fixture; 9]` (F1..F9, KB sources, owner epic keys, required increment F1/F2/F3/F6/F7 = 1, F8/F9 = 2, F4/F5 = 3, build None), `pub const EXTRA: &[Fixture]` for non-D.7 cases (other epics add ids such as dw-l, dw-t; this task registers `S-shell` = samples::two_storey_shell at increment 0 so the generic checks run on something today), `pub const REQUIRED_INCREMENT: u8 = 0` (raised by the increment-exit verifications), `pub fn all()` and `pub fn check(f: &Fixture) -> Result<Project, String>` (integrity_problems empty, every element passes validate_element, unique ids, two builds equal when `seeded`). Owners add `pub fn f1_trapezoidal_wall() -> Project` etc. in this module, so the paths other epics cite (`fixtures::f1_trapezoidal_wall`) resolve. crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs is the registry test: pins the D.7 table, runs `check` on every built entry and enforces the increment gate. crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/fixtures.rs: every built fixture evaluates without problems and every part passes check_closed. crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/common/mod.rs is extracted from tests/roundtrip.rs (options(), save(), samples(), edit(), node_index() move there; roundtrip.rs keeps every test and uses the module), so tasks 04, 06 and 08 share one helper set instead of each moving it. crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures.rs: every built fixture saves without warnings, validates without problems, loads back equal (revision normalised as in roundtrip.rs) and save-load-save is byte-identical. docs/testing.md section 'Fixture registry'. Out of scope: the fixture constructors themselves (owners), seeded identities (element-kind-framework), fixture golden files (owners decide).
design: Mirror samples.rs: constructors build projects through commands on default_metric_project() so they exercise the command layer. The registry lives in src (not only in tests/) so the geometry and IFCX test crates can iterate it without `#[path]` includes; tests/fixtures.rs remains the registry test the roadmap names, and other epics' tasks that say 'register in crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs' add the constructor to src/fixtures.rs plus any fixture-specific assertion in that test file. Because element ids are random v4 until element-kind-framework's seeded builder exists, two builds are only compared when `seeded` is true; round-trip checks compare the loaded project with the same instance that was saved. Keep constructors free of clocks and randomness other than ids. Pitfall: a fixture that is deliberately invalid (e.g. a degenerate case) does not belong here; put such cases in the owner's own tests. F7 note: the SRS gives 740/420 from the KB and 880/400 with the D.4 defaults; the owner must state which values the fixture uses.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test -p archicraft-model --test fixtures pins the D.7 table: ids F1..F9 in order, the nine KB sources above, owner keys and increments.
- The increment gate (a pure function over a table) is unit-tested with a synthetic table: it fails when an entry at or below REQUIRED_INCREMENT has no constructor and names the fixture id; it passes on D7 with REQUIRED_INCREMENT = 0.
- `check` is unit-tested with a synthetic constructor whose project has a dangling layer reference: the error names the fixture id and the problem.
- The S-shell entry passes the model, geometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/fixtures.rs) and IFCX (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures.rs) generic checks, so IFX-032 and IFX-064 are re-verified on every registered fixture from now on.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/common/mod.rs holds the shared helpers; tests/roundtrip.rs uses it and still runs all of its 16 tests.
- docs/testing.md documents the entry shape (id, title, KB source, owner, increment, seeded, constructor), how to add an entry and how REQUIRED_INCREMENT is raised at an increment exit.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check green; golden files unchanged.
notes:
SRS: IFX-032 IFX-064
Appendix D.7 values as above. Registry ids for non-D.7 cases are lowercase with a hyphen (dw-l, dw-t, dw-near, S-shell) to keep the D.7 ids unambiguous.

title: Round placement coordinates and snapshot indented IFCX with insta
description:
WHY: IFX-007 (S, partial): saving an unchanged model twice yields byte-identical files apart from header.timestamp and header.dataVersion; node order follows the spatial tree, attribute order is stable, coordinates are rounded to 10^-6 m with no exponent notation, so files can be diffed and versioned. Gap: storey elevations in usd::xformop are written unrounded (writer.rs:237-239 translation(z), used at writer.rs:313); only mesh and curve points pass json::round_coordinate. The epic acceptance also names plan coordinates (archicraft:: wall start/end, slab outline and holes), which are written at full precision. NFR-ACC-002 (M, done) states that parameters in the ArchiCraft namespace are written with round-trip precision and only mesh and curve coordinates are rounded (IFX-007); NFR-ACC-001 (M, done) requires double precision with a representation error below 0.01 mm within +-10 km; IFX-031 (M, done) requires every exported point within 0.1 mm of the model. Reviewing changes is the other half of 'diffed and versioned': the golden files are single-line compact JSON whose diffs are unreadable, and the technology choices plan insta snapshots of IFCX reviewed as JSON diffs.

WHAT: writer.rs: every transform written to usd::xformop goes through one helper that rounds the translation row with round_coordinate (storey elevation today, element and type transforms later); archicraft:: plan coordinates and parameters stay at shortest round-trip precision (deterministic and exponent-free via json.rs), and the reading 'IFX-007 coordinates = standard-namespace coordinates; archicraft:: parameters per NFR-ACC-002' is recorded in the json.rs/writer.rs module docs and docs/testing.md. Standard-namespace plan coordinates (the wall Axis basis curves, writer.rs:232) already pass round_coordinate and get a test. New crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/determinism.rs (using the tests/common helpers of task 02): odd storey elevations, two saves with different timestamp/dataVersion, save-load-save of awkward floats, exponent checks in compact and indented output, and the indented round trip. insta becomes a workspace dev-dependency of archicraft-ifcx; snapshot tests write a 'review view' of each sample (indented JSON with mesh points/faceVertexIndices replaced by their count and an FNV-1a hash of the rounded values) into crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/snapshots/. docs/testing.md documents ARCHICRAFT_BLESS for goldens, `cargo insta review` for snapshots, and that both diffs are reviewed in the pull request; .github/pull_request_template.md gets the review checkbox and the `SRS:` line used by task 19. Out of scope: the app-level indented preference (task 05), rounding the model on input.
design: Reuse options()/save()/edit() from crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/common/mod.rs (task 02). Current helpers: json::round_coordinate (json.rs:153) and the exponent-free writer (json.rs:12-150); writer.rs:224 and :232 already round mesh and curve points. Replace translation(z) by `transform(t: DVec3)` building the row-major matrix with the translation in the fourth row (IFX-031) and rounding only that row. The review view is produced in the test from the serde_json::Value: walk data[], replace `usd::usdgeom::mesh` points/faceVertexIndices and basis-curve points by `{"count": n, "fnv": "..."}`, then insta::assert_snapshot!(json::to_string(&view, true)). Pick the insta 1.x release that is at least two weeks old and pin it exactly, as the technology choices do for other crates; licence Apache-2.0 is in deny.toml. Pitfall: round_coordinate maps -0.0 to 0.0 already; keep that so negative zero never appears. Pitfall: re-blessing goldens changes nothing for the current samples (elevations 0 and 3 are exact), so the new behaviour is only visible in determinism.rs; do not bless unnecessarily.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/determinism.rs: a storey at elevation 2.9999999999 is written as 3 in the usd::xformop transform and as 2.9999999999 in archicraft::storey; elevation 1e-7 is written as 0 in the transform; exported mesh points of an element on that storey are within 0.1 mm of the model in world coordinates (IFX-031).
- Two saves of the same project with different timestamp and data_version differ only inside header.timestamp and header.dataVersion; save-load-save of a project with values like 0.1+0.2, 1/3, 1e-7 and 12345.678901234 is byte-identical; neither compact nor indented output contains exponent notation (IFX-007).
- Node order follows the spatial tree: data[] lists project, site, building, then each storey in elevation order followed by its elements and their sub-nodes, then materials, and inserting a storey below the ground keeps that order; the attribute key order of every node is identical across two saves and across a save-load-save cycle (IFX-007).
- The points of every wall Axis curve (standard-namespace plan coordinates) are multiples of 1e-6 m for a wall drawn at odd coordinates such as (1/3, 2/7).
- Indented output (pretty = true) loads to a project equal to the one loaded from compact output, and re-saving it compact reproduces the golden bytes exactly ('the indented option round-trips').
- A wall parameter typed as 1/64 inch keeps all digits in archicraft::wall after save and load (NFR-ACC-002); a point 9,999.99 m from the origin round-trips its parameters bit-exactly (NFR-ACC-001).
- insta snapshots of the review view exist for both samples and pass in CI (CI=true makes insta fail on mismatch); changing a wall thickness produces a readable hunk in the snapshot.
- golden_files_are_reproduced is green (re-blessed only if bytes changed, with the diff reviewed); conformance/run.sh green.
- docs/testing.md and the PR template document the bless/review workflow and the IFX-007 / NFR-ACC-002 reading.
notes:
SRS: IFX-007 NFR-ACC-001 NFR-ACC-002 IFX-031
Open question for the product owner: if IFX-007's 'coordinates' must also cover archicraft:: plan coordinates, the consistent alternative is to snap model coordinates to 1e-6 m at command validation (validate.rs), which changes NFR-ACC-002's 'never rounded'; this task implements the reading that keeps NFR-ACC-002 intact and records it.

title: Pin the done app requirements with egui_kittest regression tests
description:
WHY: The done application requirements of this epic hold by implementation and a few unit tests, but crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs has only four label tests (main_window_has_the_parts_of_ui_001, tool_buttons_and_properties_follow_each_other, edit_menu_undoes_and_redoes, selecting_an_element_shows_its_properties), so a UI refactor can break them unnoticed. UI-006 (M): open views as tabs with next/previous-tab shortcuts (cycle_tab, app.rs:340; Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+Shift+Tab, actions.rs:137-138), a closed view reopens from the project browser. UI-007 (S): two or more views side by side, e.g. plan and 3D, with synchronised selection (gap: reachable only by dragging a tab, no UI test). STR-003 (M): insert above/below, rename and delete in the Storeys dialog and the browser context menu, browser updated immediately. STR-004 (M): the delete prompt shows the number of affected elements and offers delete or move keeping the absolute position (dialogs.rs:204-276). VIEW-002 (M): a plan per storey and one perspective and one parallel 3D view in a new project. VIEW-014 (M): middle-button or two-finger pan, wheel or pinch zoom about the cursor, fit to window and zoom to selection, previous/next zoom with at least 20 steps (camera.rs ZoomHistory, private ZOOM_STEPS = 50). WAL-001 (M): single, chained, rectangle and rotated-rectangle modes (tools.rs WallMode). PRJ-004 (M) and NFR-REL-002 (M): recovery data at a configurable interval in a separate location and recovery offered at the next start. PRJ-005 (M), NFR-REL-001 (M) and NFR-REL-003 (M): atomic save, configurable backups (default 1), backups not listed in the open dialog (persistence/mod.rs save_atomically, backup_path; the filter is inlined in app.rs:198 and 257). NFR-USE-004 (M): no 'are you sure?' when undo is available, except deleting storeys and discarding unsaved changes. NFR-PORT-005 (M): high-DPI and 100-200 % UI scaling (gap: no automated check at 200 %). XCH-008 (M): files opened according to IFX-080. App-level clauses of requirements pinned elsewhere: ELM-004 (editable Name field, properties.rs:586-601), IFX-001 (the .ifcx extension on save, app.rs:204), IFX-002 (dataVersion incremented on every save, author from the preferences, default 'ArchiCraft user'; document.rs to_bytes/saved_to), UND-001 (the history is not cleared by saving), NFR-ACC-005 (property fields show rounded values only).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/tests/done_requirements.rs (egui_kittest, no GPU), one test per requirement named after it; the harness() helper of tests/ui.rs moves to crates/archicraft-app/tests/common/mod.rs (shared with ui.rs and task 15's crash_recovery.rs). Test hooks on ArchiCraftApp follow the existing `workspace()` accessor (app.rs:131): `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn tree_mut()` to build a split layout and `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn prompt_title()` to inspect modal state (integration tests are a separate crate, so cfg(test) items are not visible). The dialog filter and the extension rule of app.rs:198-205 and 257 are extracted into `pub const IFCX_EXTENSIONS: &[&str] = &["ifcx"]` and `pub fn with_ifcx_extension(path)` so they can be unit-tested without a native dialog. Existing tests (persistence/mod.rs atomic_save_keeps_backups and failed_save_leaves_the_original, autosave.rs abandoned_sessions_are_found_and_live_ones_skipped, camera.rs zoom_history and zoom_keeps_point_under_cursor, tools.rs mode tests) are referenced in the docs/testing.md traceability table rather than duplicated. This task keeps the behaviour and adds tests only. Out of scope: new behaviour, a split command or split persistence (UI-004), the AS-05 end-to-end run (task 15).
design: egui_kittest 0.36.2: Harness::builder().with_pixels_per_point(f) for NFR-PORT-005; find widgets by accessible label (AccessKit); key presses through harness.key_press_modifiers. For UI-007 insert a Linear container through the egui_tiles Tree returned by tree_mut() (Tree::new_horizontal or Tiles::insert_horizontal_tile) instead of simulating a drag. For the abandoned session create recovery/session-x/ with write_autosave (persistence/autosave.rs:77) before constructing the app; the lock file is not held, so find_abandoned reports it. Saves through the app call save_to(path) (app.rs:214) with a temp path to avoid the native dialog. ZOOM_STEPS stays private: its test lives in the camera.rs test module. Name tests after requirement ids so scripts/status.py (task 19) can grep them. Pitfall: harness() uses a per-test temp folder keyed by the test name and process id; keep that in tests/common so parallel tests do not share recovery folders.
acceptance_criteria:
- UI-006: Ctrl+Tab activates the next and Ctrl+Shift+Tab the previous tab; a closed plan tab reopens from the project browser.
- UI-007: a Linear split built through tree_mut() shows a plan and a 3D pane side by side; selecting a wall in the plan puts it into ws.selection and the 3D pane's SceneKey selection in the next frame.
- STR-003: the Storeys dialog offers Insert above, Insert below, Rename and Delete; the browser context menu of a storey offers the same four; a storey inserted through either appears in the browser in the next frame.
- STR-004 and NFR-USE-004: deleting a storey with three elements opens the prompt showing '3' with 'Move them' (target storey choice) and 'Delete them'; deleting an element opens no modal and is undone by Ctrl+Z; New with unsaved changes asks to save or discard.
- VIEW-002: a new project's browser lists one plan per storey plus '3D perspective' and '3D parallel'.
- VIEW-014: a middle-button drag pans the plan camera; Ctrl+wheel and a pinch (egui Event::Zoom) zoom keeping the world point under the cursor within 1e-9 m; fit to window and zoom to selection change the camera to contain the model or the selected wall; a camera.rs unit test records 25 zoom steps and walks 20 previous and 20 next steps back to the recorded cameras.
- WAL-001: the four wall mode buttons exist and switch WallMode; chained input creates one wall per segment with shared endpoints, rectangle and rotated rectangle create four walls sharing their corners (references to the tools.rs tests where they exist).
- PRJ-004 and NFR-REL-002: an abandoned session folder created with write_autosave under DataDirs::recovery() makes 'Recover unsaved work' appear at start; the autosave interval comes from ws.prefs.autosave_minutes.
- PRJ-005, NFR-REL-001 and NFR-REL-003: saving twice through the app keeps exactly one .bak with the previous bytes and leaves no temporary file; with prefs.backups = 2 a third save keeps .bak and .bak2; IFCX_EXTENSIONS is exactly ['ifcx'] and the backup paths (house.ifcx.bak, house.ifcx.bak2) do not match it, so backups are not listed by the open dialog.
- IFX-001 and IFX-002: with_ifcx_extension adds .ifcx to a path without extension; two saves through the app write dataVersion n+1 and n+2 and the author equals ws.prefs.author (default 'ArchiCraft user').
- UND-001 and ELM-004: after a save the undo stack is unchanged and Ctrl+Z still undoes the last edit; the properties strip of a single selected wall shows an editable Name field whose commit renames the element through UpdateElements.
- NFR-ACC-005: a wall of thickness 0.123456 m shows '0.123' in the properties strip at 3 decimals, and committing the field without editing the text leaves the stored value bit-identical.
- NFR-PORT-005: the main window parts of UI-001 are present and no panic occurs at pixels_per_point 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 (100-200 %).
- XCH-008: open_path on a saved file yields an editable project with no load problems and an UpdateElements command succeeds on it.
- docs/testing.md traceability table lists every requirement above with at least one test name.
- cargo test --workspace on all three OS runners, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check green.
notes:
SRS: UI-006 UI-007 STR-003 STR-004 VIEW-002 VIEW-014 WAL-001 PRJ-004 PRJ-005 NFR-REL-001 NFR-REL-002 NFR-REL-003 NFR-USE-004 NFR-PORT-005 XCH-008 ELM-004 IFX-001 IFX-002 UND-001 NFR-ACC-005
Split from task 07 (model tests) to keep both within three days. NFR-USE-004 must be re-inspected when the first parametric-dropping conversion (SOL-004, ROF-009, STA-048) adds its one-time notice (gap row).

title: Drive the pinned reference viewer headless with Playwright
description:
WHY: IFX-006 (M, partial): every file written by the system shall (a) load with schema validation enabled and without errors or composition cycles in buildingSMART's reference implementation (src/ifcx-core in R2), and (b) display correctly in the R2 viewer (src/viewer at the pinned commit) and in the hosted IFC5 viewer (R4) with the expected spatial tree, geometry and colours. (a) and the spatial tree of (b) are verified by automated tests on the reference models of Section 7.3 with a headless browser for the viewer; the visual check of (b) is manual once per release. Gap: conformance/check.ts runs the viewer's composition code (compose3) in Node, not the viewer in a headless browser; the conformance job is CI-only. The technology choices name Playwright for this. Every later epic that adds a golden (layer-structures, doors-windows-core, reference-models) relies on this job to cover its new files automatically.

WHAT: conformance/ gains Playwright (@playwright/test pinned exactly, Chromium only) and a viewer harness: conformance/viewer/harness.html plus harness.ts bundled by esbuild from the viewer modules of .ifc5/src/viewer at commit 1a63082ada967c683cfacee2005f8f749c8e1b79, exposing `window.loadIfcx(json)` that runs the viewer's own load path (composition, scene construction and tree) and returns the tree model; imports are served offline by page.route from crates/archicraft-ifcx/schemas for the four ifcx.dev URIs and every other external request is aborted. conformance/viewer.spec.ts: per file, load through the harness, assert the tree project -> site -> building -> storeys -> elements with names and bodies, render a frame, take a canvas screenshot and assert visible geometry (non-background pixel share above a threshold) and that each material diffuseColor of the file appears (within a tolerance under the viewer's lighting). conformance/run.sh runs the existing check.ts step and then `npx playwright test` with the file list; screenshots are written to conformance/test-results/. The ci.yml conformance job (ubuntu) installs Chromium with `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` (cached) and uploads the screenshots. Out of scope: the Windows/macOS matrix and the nightly run (task 13), automating the hosted R4 viewer (manual, release checklist), new golden files (owning epics).
design: Inspect src/viewer at the pinned commit first: if it exposes modules that build the three.js scene from compose3 output and a tree from the composed nodes, import them into the harness instead of the full HTML app; if it only offers a file-input UI, serve its index.html and drive it with page.setInputFiles, then read the tree from the DOM. Either way, the harness must not reimplement viewer logic, otherwise (b) degrades to another Node check. Headless WebGL: launch Chromium with `--use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader` so it renders on runners without a GPU; give the colour check a generous tolerance because of shading. Pin @playwright/test to a release at least two weeks old (technology choices rule) and record it in technology-choices.md's 'not checked yet' list with its licence (Apache-2.0). Pitfall: Playwright's browser download must not happen inside the IFX-004 offline guarantee of the product; it is a CI test tool only, like Node.
acceptance_criteria:
- `conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx` runs (a) ifcx-core with schema validation, (b1) the compose3 tree check in Node and (b2) the viewer in headless Chromium, printing PASS or FAIL per file and step, exit code non-zero on any failure.
- For both goldens the Playwright step reports the expected storey and element counts, finds a non-empty render and every material colour of the file.
- Deliberately broken copies fail the Playwright step with a message naming the node: a storey without usd::xformop, a mesh without diffuseColor, a mesh with an out-of-range index.
- The step runs offline: the test asserts that no request outside localhost and the bundled schema URIs was attempted.
- CI uploads one screenshot per golden as an artefact for the manual release check; the conformance job stays under 5 minutes on ubuntu.
- Playwright output folders are git-ignored (task 01); README of conformance/ documents the three steps. Satisfies the automated clauses of IFX-006 (a and the spatial tree, geometry and colours of b) for every golden file.
notes:
SRS: IFX-006
Section 7.3 reference models RM-S/RM-M/RM-L do not exist yet; the increment-0 goldens are the stand-ins and later goldens are picked up by the glob without changes.

title: Add the profiles dialog with parametric shapes and catalogue picker
description:
WHY: PRF-004 (M): profiles are edited in a profile editor and editing a profile updates every element that uses it; PRF-005 (M): parametric standard shapes defined by their dimensions; PRF-011 (S): a catalogue of standard steel sections, which the gap row turns into a searchable picker (UI-014 asks for incremental search on profile lists). The materials window is the dialog pattern to follow (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:376-478 with material_editor at :765). Tasks 10 and 11 offer profile combos without a way to create profiles.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/profiles.rs and its state in Dialogs: a 'Profiles' window opened by Action::Profiles (Design menu, next to Materials in the menu order) and by 'Edit profiles...' buttons added next to the profile combos of the column and beam fields. List with an incremental search field and usage counts; New (choose a parametric shape, filled with sensible defaults), From catalogue... (family combo plus search over catalogue::search; rows show designation, h x b and area; Add creates Profile::from_catalogue with the material 'Steel'), Duplicate, Rename, Delete (an in-use profile asks for a compatible replacement, as material deletion does). Editor for the selected profile: name, shape kind, dimension fields (widgets::length labelled with names and EN symbols), material, usage checkboxes (Columns, Beams; Walls and Railings disabled with the note 'arrives with PRF-010'), insertion origin (nine bounding-box points or custom x/y), a live preview drawn with the egui painter from archicraft_geometry::section with the origin marker and bounding-box dimensions, derived area, and the catalogue designation (editing a catalogue profile's dimensions clears it with a note). Validation messages from validate_profile appear inline; every accepted change is one UpdateProfile. Out of scope: custom regions (task 15), PRF-006..PRF-010.
design: Follow the 'Add a dialog' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md and the material editor's one-command-per-field-change pattern so undo granularity matches the rest of the application. The preview reuses the body's section generator, so what is shown is what gets swept. Default dimensions for 'New' come from a catalogue row of the matching family where one exists (I: IPE 200, U: UPE 200, L: L 100x10, RHS: HSS 6x4x3/8 in metres, CHS: 168.3 x 8) and simple values otherwise. Pitfalls: per-frame cost of the catalogue search (filter only when the query changes); the dialog must not hold a profile copy across frames that a concurrent undo invalidated (re-read by id every frame, as material_editor does).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: open Profiles, choose From catalogue, type 'ipe 30', IPE 300 is the first row, Add puts 'IPE 300' in the list and the preview shows an area of 53.8 cm2 (within 1 %).
- kittest: changing the height of a parametric I profile used by a column changes the column's evaluated volume (PRF-004 propagation through the UI) and one undo restores it.
- Deleting an in-use profile opens the replacement prompt; the chosen replacement is applied to every user in one undo step; incompatible profiles (missing usage flag) are not offered.
- An invalid dimension (flange >= half the height) shows the message and issues no command; unchecking Columns while a column uses the profile is refused with the UpdateProfile message.
- The search field filters the profile list incrementally; each of the nine parametric shapes can be created by its dimensions.
- Satisfies PRF-005 in the UI, the picker clause of PRF-011 and the parametric part of PRF-004's editor.
notes:
SRS: PRF-004 PRF-005 PRF-011
Also touches UI-014 (incremental search on the profile list).

title: Rebuild the project browser with saved views, folders and menus
description:
WHY: VIEW-003 (M): the project browser lists storeys (highest first), 3D views, sections, elevations and saved views, with folders for saved views; double-click opens an item in a tab and marks it active, single click selects it, a context menu offers rename, delete, settings and 'save as view', and new storeys, sections and elevations appear automatically. VIEW-004 (M): saved views are visually distinguishable from plain viewpoints. Gap row: single click already opens the plan (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/browser.rs:48), there are no saved views or folders, no 'save as view' or 'settings', and 3D views have no context menu. Exists and kept (VIEW-003 partial): storeys listed highest first (storey.rs:134 highest_first), the storey context menu with Open plan, Insert storey above/below, the rename/elevation/height dialog and Delete storey (browser.rs:51-81), the per-frame rebuild from the project that makes new storeys appear automatically, Request::OpenPane marking the opened pane active (app.rs:291-318) and the 3D views list (browser.rs:86-96), which gains a context menu.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/browser.rs rewritten as a tree on egui's CollapsingState: groups Storeys (highest_first), 3D views (plain viewpoints), Saved views (nested folders; saved views with a bookmark icon and the accessible label 'Saved view: <name>') and a Sections and elevations group that appears only when such view kinds exist; a browser selection in Workspace; single click selects, double-click or Enter opens (Request::OpenPane / OpenView) and marks the item active; context menus per item: Open, Rename (inline edit -> RenameStorey, UpdateView, UpdateViewFolder), Delete (storey dialog, DeleteView, DeleteViewFolder with confirmation), Settings (Storeys dialog, or a view settings window with name, projection or storey and the stored sections), Save as view (Request::SaveViewAs), Redefine from current window (saved views, when a pane is active), New folder, Move to folder. Tabs get a context menu through egui_tiles Behavior::on_tab_button with Save as view and Close. Out of scope: drag-and-drop between folders (UI-016, templates-presets), incremental search (UI-014, properties-and-dialogs), section and elevation views themselves (sections-elevations-dims).
design: egui_extras has no tree widget, so the roadmap's 'egui_extras tree' becomes egui::collapsing_header::CollapsingState with ids derived from storey, view and folder ids (stable across frames and renames). Group the tree by ViewKind so a new kind adds a group, not a special case. kittest: double-click as two clicks in consecutive steps within egui's double-click time, or injected PointerButton events; context menus through a secondary-click event. If commands-and-l10n has landed, menu entries are registered commands with string keys (UI-005 is owned there). Pitfalls: inline rename must not trigger single-key tool shortcuts (UI-008); deleting the active view closes its tab through the existing pane pruning.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: storeys appear highest first (label order asserted); the default 3D views and a saved view inside folder 'Presentation' are listed; the saved view carries the 'Saved view:' label that plain viewpoints lack.
- kittest: a single click on a storey selects it without opening a tab (pane count unchanged); a double-click (and Enter on the focused item) opens it in a tab and marks it active.
- kittest: the context menu of a saved view offers Rename, Delete, Settings, Save as view and Redefine; Rename changes the name in one undo step; Delete removes the view; the context menu of a 3D view offers Rename, Delete, Settings and Save as view.
- kittest: the context menu of a storey keeps Insert storey above/below and offers Open, Rename, Delete, Settings (Storeys dialog) and Save as view (creates a saved plan view of that storey); the context menu of a folder offers Rename, Delete and New folder.
- kittest: inserting a storey makes it appear immediately; deleting a folder moves its views to the parent folder.
- Satisfies VIEW-003 (sections and elevations are listed automatically once VIEW-059 adds their view kinds) and the visual distinction of VIEW-004.
notes: SRS: VIEW-003 VIEW-004.

title: Division snap points with one active mode and a scope
description:
WHY: Hovering an edge shall show division snap points of exactly one active mode: half; N equal parts (N = 2…100); a percentage from the nearer end; a repeated fixed distance from the nearer end; or the best equal division nearest a target distance. A scope option limits the points to between nodes, between intersections with other elements, or the whole element (INP-010). Edge midpoints and division points are snap targets (INP-008). Today only the midpoint is offered, hard-coded (tools.rs:240-241), nothing is shown when an edge is hovered, and neither ToolState nor Preferences has division state.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-app/src/input/division.rs: Curve { Segment, Circle, Arc } (shared with guide lines in task 11), DivisionMode { Half, Equal(u8), Percent(f64), Repeated(f64), BestEqualNear(f64) }, DivisionScope { BetweenNodes, BetweenIntersections, WholeElement } and divide(curve, mode, cursor) -> Vec<DVec2>. Resolve the scope on the SnapIndex: BetweenNodes is the hovered edge, BetweenIntersections splits the hovered edge at its intersections with other owners' edges, WholeElement uses the owner's whole chain (a wall reference line, a slab outline or cut ring). Store InputSettings { division, scope } in Preferences (exactly one mode by construction). The nearest edge within the radius becomes Resolved.hovered; its division points are drawn as ticks and offered as Division-level candidates. Add a 'Division' control (mode choice plus its value) to the tool-mode row of the properties strip (ui/properties.rs tool_modes, line 745). Out of scope: arcs on model elements (curved-geometry supplies them as Curve::Arc).
design: 'Nearer end' follows the cursor's projection parameter t on the curve (t < 0.5 measures from the start). Repeated stops before the far end; BestEqualNear uses n = max(1, round(L / target)). Only the hovered edge is divided (at most 100 points), so the per-frame cost stays bounded. Keep the hovered edge while the cursor stays within 1.5 × radius (hysteresis) so the ticks do not flicker between parallel edges. BetweenIntersections reuses the pairwise intersection code of candidates() restricted to the hovered edge. The WholeElement chain is identified by TargetOwner plus ring index, so it survives incremental index updates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-mode tests on a 3.5 m edge: Half gives one point; Equal(4) three points; Percent(25) is measured from the end nearer the cursor; Repeated(1.0) gives three points from the nearer end; BestEqualNear(1.1) gives three equal parts of 1.1667 m; Equal values outside 2..=100 are clamped; circles and arcs are divided by arc length.
- Hover test: with the cursor near an edge but away from its nodes, Resolved.hovered holds that edge and exactly the active mode's division points (Equal(4): three ticks); switching the mode replaces the ticks and never mixes two modes; beyond 1.5 × radius the ticks disappear.
- Scope tests on two_storey_shell: BetweenIntersections on the south exterior wall's reference line splits it where the interior wall's reference line meets it (x = 5); WholeElement on the ground slab divides its whole perimeter; BetweenNodes divides only the hovered edge.
- Precedence test: a division point beats a point on the edge and loses to a real intersection.
- Preferences round trip for mode, value and scope; out-of-range values are sanitised.
- kittest: with the Wall tool active the 'Division' control and its value field are present.
- Satisfies INP-010 and the midpoint/division clause of INP-008.
notes:
SRS: INP-010 INP-008
No Appendix D default exists: initial mode Half, scope BetweenNodes.

title: Verify exit criterion: Profiles, columns and beams
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its exit criterion is demonstrated on the integrated workspace: profiles (PRF-004, PRF-005, PRF-011), columns (COL-001, COL-002, COL-003), beams (BEA-001, BEA-002, BEA-008, BEA-010), the wall and beam reference-line display (WAL-007) and beam and column axes in IFCX (IFX-035) must work together, and the status document must say so.

WHAT: Run the workspace quality gates and the conformance job on all golden files; walk through the exit scenario in the app (place a column with one click and with a rotation click, draw a beam and a beam chain, edit end cuts numerically and by handle in plan and 3D, create IPE/HEA/HEB/HEM/UPE/L/W/C/HSS profiles from the catalogue and all nine parametric shapes, draw a custom two-region profile, check projected and overhead beams in plan); update docs/implementation-status.md rows for PRF-004, PRF-005, PRF-011, COL-001, COL-002, COL-003, BEA-001, BEA-002, BEA-008, WAL-007 (done), BEA-010 (chain clause done, grid-axis clause pending grids: partial) and IFX-035 (walls, beams and columns done, grid lines pending grids: partial) with evidence paths, and the touched rows INP-008 (column and beam axis points), INP-021 (column and beam context providers) and UI-014 (profile list search), and the readiness table for increment 1; close the epic in beads and file follow-up beads for anything left (for example merging arc_segments into drafting-trim-split's tessellate and the handle module with edit-reshape-palette's part handles).
design: Verification only; no new features. Use the integrated main branch after all tasks have merged. Evidence for the status document comes from the tests named in tasks 01-15 (validate.rs and commands.rs profile tests, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs and catalogue.rs, the round-trip suite and golden file, the tools.rs and kittest UI tests, handles.rs tests). If a gate fails, reopen the owning task rather than patching here.
acceptance_criteria:
- D.2 column and beam defaults in the template.
- A column is placed with one click plus an optional rotation click, a beam between two points and as a chain.
- End-cut angles editable numerically and by handle.
- The profile editor produces closed cross-sections for rectangle, circle, hollow sections, I/H, T, L, U/C and Z with area regression tests and a catalogue of IPE/HEA/HEB/HEM/UPE/L/W/C/HSS sections.
- IfcColumn and IfcBeam with Axis basiscurves pass conformance.
- Beams below and above the cut plane are classified projected and overhead with correct angled end cuts.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green on every golden file, including columns-and-beams.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (PRF-004, PRF-005, PRF-011, COL-001, COL-002, COL-003, BEA-001, BEA-002, BEA-008, BEA-010, WAL-007, IFX-035) with evidence and remaining gaps.
- The epic is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for every remaining gap.
notes:
SRS: PRF-004 PRF-005 PRF-011 COL-001 COL-002 COL-003 BEA-001 BEA-002 BEA-008 BEA-010 WAL-007 IFX-035
IFX-035 grid lines and BEA-010 grid axes remain with the grids epic.

title: Render line-type dashes on the GPU and keep overlay strokes above one device pixel
description:
WHY: DSP-004 (M): no line shall be drawn thinner than one device pixel, which includes the on-screen overlays the painter keeps drawing over the GPU plan (hover and selection outlines, reference lines, snap markers, rubber bands, tracker lines), whose widths are logical points (for example HIGHLIGHT_WIDTH 2.6 and the 1.2 pt reference lines in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs) and fall below one device pixel when pixels_per_point < 1. DSP-014 (M): anti-aliasing with correct caps and joins at every zoom level also applies to dashed lines. After plan-renderer-08 dashed model lines (overhead lines with the DASH line type by default, PlanStyle.overhead_line_type of plan-attributes-04) are still drawn by the plan-attributes-07 painter with egui's dashed_line_with_offset, which re-tessellates every frame and restarts the pattern per segment.

WHAT: a line-type buffer next to the pen buffer of plan-renderer-08 (per stroke style: the LineType dash list in mm and its Paper/Model scaling, plan-attributes-01); the stroke fragment shader multiplies coverage by the box-filtered dash pulse evaluated on lyon's advancement, with paper-size patterns resolved at the view's DrawingScale and model-size patterns in metres; dashed strokes move from the painter to the GPU path, so draw_plan keeps model lines only as the no-GPU fallback; one overlay stroke helper in views/plan.rs that floors every overlay width at one device pixel; re-bless the plan-renderer-08 goldens that contain overhead lines. Out of scope: drafting line types and 2D elements (drafting-trim-split), custom line types (SRS Section 8), restyling of overlays.
design: Coverage = edge coverage x dash(advance), with dash() the closed-form box filter of the periodic pulse over fwidth(advance) (the same filtered-pulse technique as the hatches of plan-renderer-09, shared WGSL function). Period in model metres: sum(dashes) mm x 1e-3 x denominator for Paper scaling, sum(dashes) mm x 1e-3 for Model scaling; the denominator comes from the uniform, so a scale change never re-tessellates. lyon's advancement is cumulative along a path, so one path per chained polyline (plan-renderer-03) carries the phase across joins. Zero-length dots get a 0.5 px minimum as in plan-attributes-07. Up to 8 dash entries per line type in the buffer (DSP-008 built-ins need at most 6). Overlay helper: `fn overlay_stroke(width_pt: f32, color: Color32, ppp: f32) -> Stroke { Stroke::new(width_pt.max(1.0 / ppp), color) }`; keep HIGHLIGHT_WIDTH in points.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pixel tests in crates/archicraft-app/tests/plan_pixels.rs: an overhead line with the DASH line type measures a dash period of (dash + gap) mm x 1e-3 x denominator x zoom x ppp within 5 % at 1:50 and 1:100; a model-size line type keeps its model period at both scales.
- The dash phase continues across a polyline corner (the dash lengths measured on both sides of the corner add up to the pattern) and dash ends are butt caps within 0.5 px.
- A pattern whose dashes are shorter than one device pixel renders as a continuous lighter line: 16-px block means vary by less than 5 % under sub-pixel pans (no flicker).
- Changing an element's overhead line type or a line type's dash list re-uploads only the line-type buffer (counter); no re-tessellation.
- Overlay strokes (element_outline, reference_line, draw_snap_marker, rubber bands, tracker) go through one helper whose width is max(width_pt, 1.0 / pixels_per_point); unit test at ppp 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 (DSP-004 for overlays).
- The two_storey_shell goldens of plan-renderer-08 are re-blessed with dashed overhead lines (reviewed diff) and pass on the three CI platforms.
- Satisfies the dashed-line part of DSP-014 and the overlay part of the one-device-pixel clause of DSP-004, and keeps the DSP-008 line types of plan-attributes-07 visible on the GPU path.
notes: SRS: DSP-004 DSP-014. DSP-008 line types (paper- or model-size dash and gap lists) are owned by plan-attributes; this task only renders them on the GPU path.

title: Remember dialog sizes, splitters and panel sizes in preferences
description:
WHY: UI-015 (S): dialogs and panels are resizable and remember their size and splitter positions between sessions. Most dialog windows are resizable (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:91, 282, 380, 487, 632, 643; Preferences at 684 only through egui's default) and the browser and problems panels are resizable (app.rs:816 and 823-825), but size persistence is an untested side effect of eframe's egui-memory persistence (eframe 'persistence' feature in the workspace Cargo.toml, storage dir in persistence/mod.rs:26), the Materials dialog splits with fixed ui.columns(2) (dialogs.rs:387) and the toolbox panel is not resizable (app.rs:820) (gap row UI-015). The epic risk requires layout data to be kept in preferences, not in egui memory side effects.

WHAT: persistence/prefs.rs: `Preferences.sizes: SizeMemory { windows: BTreeMap<String, [f32; 2]>, splitters: BTreeMap<String, f32>, sections: BTreeMap<String, bool> }` (serde default; sanitized: finite, clamped to 120..4000 points). New ui/window.rs with `remembered_window(title, key, &mut SizeMemory)` that seeds default_size from the stored size, makes the window resizable and records the size after show. Every dialog window uses it: ui/dialogs.rs (Storeys, Layers, Materials, Project settings, Settings, Reference levels, Keyboard shortcuts, About ArchiCraft at dialogs.rs:668, Preferences) and the startup windows in app.rs ('Recover unsaved work' at app.rs:637 and 'ArchiCraft crashed last time' at app.rs:681, today resizable(false)); Materials gets a draggable list/detail splitter and the Settings dialog a fields/preview splitter (resizable inner panels), both recorded under splitters; the browser, toolbox (now resizable) and problems panels record their size under splitters too ('panel.<name>'), and the settings dialog sections record their open state. app.rs saves preferences when SizeMemory changed (on dialog close and in on_exit) and ArchiCraftApp overrides eframe::App::persist_egui_memory to return false, so egui memory no longer restores sizes across sessions. Out of scope: tile layout, docking and panel visibility (UI-004, plan-views-browser-14), the main window position (eframe window persistence).
design: Approach: one small helper used by all windows keeps the rule enforceable by a source scan. Read the size from the Window's InnerResponse rect each frame, compare with the stored value and mark prefs dirty only on a change above 1 point; egui keeps the size in its own memory during the session, which is fine - turning off persist_egui_memory only removes the cross-session side effect, and default_size seeds the first frame. Splitters: egui::Panel::left(id).resizable(true).default_size(stored).show_inside(ui) inside the window, reading back the panel response width. Coordinate with plan-views-browser-14: it stores PanelPlacement (visible, side, floating) in Preferences.panels, while sizes stay in SizeMemory, so the two tasks touch disjoint fields whichever lands first. The SearchField of task 12 stays at the top of the Materials list panel when the splitter is introduced. Pitfalls: sizes are logical points (HiDPI must not double them); kittest reads window bounds through AccessKit; the settings dialog splitter must not shrink the preview below a usable size (min 160 points). Pointers: prefs.rs:27-113, app.rs:181-186 and 790-868, every egui::Window::new call site in dialogs.rs and app.rs (637, 681), main.rs NativeOptions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs: SizeMemory JSON round trip; sanitized() drops NaN and clamps out-of-range sizes; a preferences file without 'sizes' loads the defaults.
- Unit test in ui/window.rs: record() stores the window rect size under its key, ignores sizes below the minimum and reports 'changed' only for differences above 1 point.
- kittest dialogs_reopen_at_their_remembered_size: an app built with Preferences whose sizes.windows['Materials'] is [700, 520] opens the Materials dialog with a window 700 ± 2 points wide; the Materials list splitter opens at the stored 260 points; after closing, SizeMemory holds the current sizes.
- kittest every_dialog_is_resizable: each dialog opened through its Action, and the two startup windows, is resizable and has an entry in SizeMemory after it was shown.
- Source-scan test: crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs and src/ui/*.rs create no egui::Window outside ui/window.rs remembered_window (egui::Modal confirmations excepted).
- Test that on_exit writes the recorded sizes through save_prefs and that persist_egui_memory() returns false.
- Satisfies UI-015 for every dialog and panel that exists; the add-a-dialog extension point in docs/implementation-status.md names remembered_window for later dialogs.
notes:
SRS: UI-015
UI-004 (layout, docking, visibility) is owned by plan-views-browser.

title: Properties panel, settings-dialog framework, reference levels and datum display
description:
Generalise the properties strip and settings dialog into a declarative field framework driven by the kind registry: collapsible sections, live preview, one dialog for tool defaults and selections, mixed-state fields for multi-selection, range checks with live dependent values, configurable ID prefixes, position and structural flags, derived values, incremental search and resizable dialogs that remember their size. Also adds named reference levels (project zero, sea level, user levels) with the single vertical datum so every elevation field can display relative to a chosen level while storage stays relative to project zero (STR-007, STR-011).

Risks: egui dialog ergonomics and size persistence; layout data kept in preferences, not in egui memory side effects. Datum conversion errors leaking into storage are prevented by converting only in widgets, asserted by round-trip tests.
design: archicraft-app ui/fields.rs: FieldSpec per kind from the registry (getter, setter, range, unit) rendered by both the strip and the dialog; preview through a small offscreen render3d scene; dialog sizes in preferences; archicraft-model position and structural flags on Element and ID counters per kind. archicraft-model: ReferenceLevel list in ProjectSettings and datum-aware formatting in units.rs used by ui/widgets.rs.
acceptance_criteria: kittest: a mixed selection shows only common fields with mixed markers and 'n selected, m editable'; committing applies to every editable element; every registered kind has a dialog with the four sections and a preview (a test iterates the registry); an invalid value shows its explanation and leaves the model untouched; W-001-style IDs with a configurable prefix; derived values for walls, slabs, columns and beams; lists longer than one screen get a search field; the storey-height default shifts the storeys above. A datum 'sea level +412.000' shows a storey at +3.000 as +415.000 and typing +415.000 stores 3.000 (unit tests on widgets::length); the datum is written once to IFCX and never asked for twice.
notes: SRS: UI-002 UI-003 EDT-017 ELM-001 ELM-005 ELM-012 ELM-017 ELM-019 ELM-020 MEA-003 STR-002 UI-014 UI-015 STR-007 STR-011

title: Add the structural-function flag and round-trip element positions
description:
WHY: ELM-012 (S) requires elements to carry a position (exterior or interior), written as `IsExternal` (IFX-022) and usable by display overrides (DSP-016); ELM-020 (C) lets elements carry a structural function (load-bearing or non-load-bearing), also usable by display overrides. Position exists (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:35-67; Position field in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:493-505; crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:399-411 writes bsi::ifc::prop::IsExternal and archicraft::element.position; reader.rs:720 reads it; template defaults template.rs:332/341), but no round-trip test asserts that IsExternal or the position survive save and load (gap row ELM-012). The structural function is missing entirely (gap row ELM-020: no flag on Element, no UI, no IFCX property). Both flags belong on the element envelope so that later display overrides, selection criteria (templates-presets) and parameter transfer can read them for every kind.

WHAT: archicraft-model: `StructuralFunction { Undefined, LoadBearing, NonLoadBearing }` next to Position in element.rs (ALL, code, from_code, label; Default Undefined), a `structural` field on Element (serde default) and on the DefaultsSlot introduced by element-kind-framework (template default Undefined for wall and slab), carried by Project::prototype, the new_wall/new_slab wrappers and samples.rs; UpdateElements needs no change (whole-element replace). archicraft-ifcx: archicraft::element gains an optional `structuralFunction` member, written only when not Undefined so existing golden bytes stay identical, declared optional in alpha/schema.rs and read leniently (unknown code: warning, Undefined); the defaults-slot schema gets the same optional member, among the slot's common members next to position (after element-kind-framework-12 the slot is {layer, position, ifcClass, predefinedType, parameters}; structuralFunction is an envelope flag, not a kind parameter). archicraft-app: a 'Structural function' combo in the Classification section next to Position (ui/properties.rs classification_fields, using the existing Fields::choice so differing values show 'Mixed'; task 05 moves it into a FieldSpec). Out of scope: display overrides themselves (DSP-016, could-scope-polish), selection by criteria (templates-presets), a standard IFC load-bearing attribute (not declared in the bundled prop@v5a schema).
design: Approach: model the flag exactly like Position (an envelope enum with stable codes), because display overrides and selection criteria will match on codes for any kind; keeping it on Element rather than on the payloads means KindDescriptor needs no change. IFCX: bsi::ifc::prop::LoadBearing is not declared in crates/archicraft-ifcx/schemas/prop@v5a.ifcx (IsExternal is the only declared flag), and IFX-061 forbids undeclared attributes, so the value lives in archicraft::element only; when a future bundled schema declares LoadBearing, write it the way IsExternal is written (writer.rs:399-402). Writing only non-default values keeps the golden data nodes stable; the embedded schema declaration still gains the optional member, so the goldens are re-blessed once (schemas section only). It is an optional addition, so FORMAT_VERSION does not change (migration rule documented in alpha/mod.rs by element-kind-framework-12). Pitfalls: Element is built literally in reader.rs, samples.rs, the tools.rs tests and the ifcx tests; serde(default) on the new field keeps journals and autosave replay of older sessions loading; keep the field order in the archicraft::element JSON (kind, layer, locked, position, then structuralFunction). Pointers: element.rs:35-67 and 268-285, writer.rs:399-411, reader.rs:720, alpha/schema.rs element object, properties.rs:478-506, template.rs:321-344.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs: StructuralFunction code/from_code round-trips for every entry of ALL; Default is Undefined; Position::is_external is unchanged.
- Integration test position_and_structural_function_round_trip in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: three walls (Exterior + LoadBearing, Interior + NonLoadBearing, Undefined + Undefined) and one slab survive save and load with equal position and structural function; the written wall nodes carry bsi::ifc::prop::IsExternal true, false and no IsExternal attribute respectively (ELM-012 / IFX-022 clause asserted for the first time).
- Lenient reading: an archicraft::element with structuralFunction "bogus" loads as Undefined with exactly one warning naming the element; a file without the member loads without any problem.
- Golden files: no data node changes (Undefined is not written), but every file embeds the archicraft:: declarations in its schemas section (alpha/schema.rs declarations()), so the goldens are re-blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 and the reviewed diff is limited to the new optional structuralFunction declarations (archicraft::element and the defaults slot); written_files_validate_without_problems passes with the new optional schema member; conformance/run.sh is green.
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: selecting a wall shows 'Structural function'; picking 'Load-bearing' sets element.structural and one Undo restores Undefined; two selected walls with different values show 'Mixed'.
- Tool-defaults test: setting the wall default to Load-bearing through the strip (wall tool, nothing selected) makes the next wall created through Project::prototype/new_wall load-bearing (ELM-001 path).
- Satisfies ELM-020 and closes the round-trip gap of ELM-012 except their 'usable by display overrides' clauses: both flags become matchable by key and code through the COMMON_FIELDS FieldSpecs of task 05 (the generic hook display-override criteria use, asserted there), and the clauses close when DSP-016 (3d-display-styles-15/16) matches on them; recorded as open in docs/implementation-status.md.
notes:
SRS: ELM-012 ELM-020
Also exercises IFX-022 (IsExternal when the position is known). Open question: write bsi::ifc::prop::LoadBearing once a bundled schema declares it (record in docs/implementation-status.md). Appendix D gives no structural-function default; Undefined is used for every kind.
Cross-epic gap: 3d-display-styles-15 defines OverrideCriteria {kinds, storeys, layers, materials} without position or structural function, so ELM-012/ELM-020 'usable by display overrides' cannot close there as planned; the done task files a follow-up bead on 3d-display-styles-15 to add both criteria (matching the COMMON_FIELDS codes).

title: Store the plan drafting grid in the project settings and IFCX
description:
WHY: The drafting grid shall be configured per view type with one plan grid shared by all storeys, made of an invisible snap grid with X/Y steps and a visible construction grid with main and auxiliary spacing, rotation and local origin (INP-013). Project-level settings are stored in the project file so every user who opens it sees the same values (PRJ-007), which a user preference cannot do. Today the only grid setting is Preferences::snap_step (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:45-46, one value for X and Y), and ProjectSettings holds only units, cut-plane height and tessellation (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:45-52). This is the model and file part of INP-013; it needs no other task, so it can run beside the input service, and task 10 consumes it.

WHAT: archicraft-model: PlanGrid { snap_step: DVec2, snap_enabled: bool, main_spacing: DVec2, auxiliary_spacing: DVec2, rotation: f64, origin: DVec2, visible: bool } as ProjectSettings.plan_grid, with its defaults in ProjectSettings::default (which default_metric_project already uses, crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs:352), validated in check_settings (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:595) and changed through the existing undoable Command::SetSettings. archicraft-ifcx: a planGrid object inside the settings of archicraft::project, declared optional in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs (settings block at line 139), written in writer.rs project_attribute (line 144) and read in reader.rs (settings at lines 325-370), falling back to PlanGrid::default() when absent; FORMAT_VERSION (schema.rs:15) stays 1. Re-bless the golden files and review the diff. Out of scope: snapping, drawing and the dialog (task 10), grids of section views (sections-elevations-dims) and the 3D working-plane grid (3d-input-navigation).
design: Proposed defaults (no Appendix D drafting-grid value exists; the 6.00 m 'Grid' row of D.2 is the structural grid of GRD): snap step 0.05 × 0.05 m (the current preference default, prefs.rs:67), snapping on, main spacing 1.00 m, auxiliary spacing 0.25 m, rotation 0, origin (0, 0), construction grid hidden; setting them in ProjectSettings::default lets the Appendix D defaults test of regression-and-status cover them. IFCX shape: planGrid { snapStep, mainSpacing, auxiliarySpacing (two-element length arrays), snapEnabled, visible (Boolean), rotation (Plane angle), origin (point2) }, using the existing length(), angle(), boolean() and point2() helpers of schema.rs. Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md, except that a missing planGrid is not a problem: read it with object(attr, "planGrid").ok() and fall back to PlanGrid::default() as a whole, using report.or per field only inside a present object. Pitfall: ProjectSettings derives PartialEq and SetSettings rejects an unchanged value as NoChange (command.rs:260-266), so PlanGrid derives PartialEq and keeps its f64 values unrounded; validation bounds: finite, > 0 and at most 1,000 m.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: SetSettings with a changed plan_grid undoes and redoes to the exact project; check_settings rejects zero, negative and non-finite steps and spacings and an auxiliary spacing larger than the main spacing; ProjectSettings::default and default_metric_project carry the defaults listed in the design.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: a project with a non-default PlanGrid (rotation 30°, origin (1, 1), snap step 0.1 × 0.05 m) round-trips exactly; a file without planGrid loads with the defaults and reports no problem (the object is optional); a planGrid with one invalid field reports one problem and falls back to that field's default; written_files_validate_without_problems still passes.
- Golden files are re-blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1, the diff contains only the planGrid object in the settings of archicraft::project, and conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green.
- Satisfies the storage part of INP-013 (one plan grid per project, shared by all storeys, kept in the file per PRJ-007); snapping and drawing follow in task 10.
notes:
SRS: INP-013
Decision: the drafting grid is a project setting (PRJ-007: the same for everyone who opens the file), not a user preference; task 10 retires Preferences::snap_step. Defaults to be confirmed by the template owner.

title: Index snap targets in an incrementally updated rstar tree
description:
WHY: Input feedback (cursor snapping, rubber-band preview, tracker values) shall update within 50 ms of pointer movement (NFR-PERF-005). Today SnapTargets::from_plan rebuilds every node and edge every frame while a drawing tool is active (plan.rs:487-490, listed as technical debt 'Per-frame allocations in the plan view' in docs/implementation-status.md) and snap() scans all nodes and intersects edges pairwise without a spatial index (tools.rs:224-250), unverified for an RM-M storey. The cursor shall snap within a configurable screen radius to element targets (INP-008), and locked elements shall keep providing snap targets while they reject edits (INP-017), which today holds only implicitly because from_plan filters on visibility alone (tools.rs:180).

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs: a SnapIndex holding an rstar RTree of IndexedEdge and an RTree of IndexedPoint, each entry carrying its owner (TargetOwner { Element(ElementId), Guide(u64) }), segment index and source class, built from SnapSource implementations for PlanElement (cut rings through polygon_rings, projected and overhead lines; crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:23-33, 298) and for wall reference lines. Cache one index per storey in Workspace keyed by (storey, project.revision); on a new revision diff per-owner fingerprints and remove or insert only the changed owners, bulk-loading on the first build. The active consumer's pending points live in a small side list, not in the tree. Rewrite snap() on index queries (locate_within_distance for points and edges, pairwise intersections only among the edges within the radius). Filter on Project::is_visible only, so locked elements stay snappable. Add rstar 0.12 to [workspace.dependencies] and to the app crate. Out of scope: new target kinds (03), the exclusion flags (12), 3D targets (3d-input-navigation).
design: rstar: implement RTreeObject with AABB<[f64; 2]> envelopes and PointDistance for IndexedEdge through closest_on_segment (tools.rs:190-199, moved in 01); query with locate_within_distance(point, r²). Fingerprint: a u64 hash over the f64 bits of an owner's segments and reference line; keep HashMap<TargetOwner, (u64, Vec<entry>)> and remove changed entries with RTree::remove (entries derive PartialEq), falling back to bulk_load when more than a quarter of the owners changed. Document::plan() returns a fresh Arc<PlanDrawing> per revision (document.rs:105-121), so fingerprints must come from content, not pointers. Layer visibility changes are commands (UpdateLayer) and therefore bump the revision. Pitfall: keep rstar at 0.12, the version geo 0.33.1 pins (docs/technology-choices.md: 'use the version geo uses (0.12), so we don't compile two copies'). The per-element revisions planned by element-kind-framework can later replace the fingerprints without changing the SnapSource API.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equivalence test: on both storeys of two_storey_shell the indexed snap() returns the same Snap as the brute-force SnapTargets path for 500 seeded cursor positions at three radii.
- Build-count test: a debug counter shows one full build per storey and revision across 200 resolve() calls; after Command::AddElements of one wall exactly one owner is inserted and the new wall's nodes are candidates; undo removes them again.
- Locked-element test: a locked wall's nodes and edges are candidates (INP-017 clause 'locked against editing while they still provide snap targets'); a wall on a hidden layer contributes none.
- Timing tests (#[test], debug profile): 1,000 resolve() calls on two_storey_shell average under 1 ms; a generated storey of 5,000 walls averages under 5 ms per call (loose bounds; the frame-time assertion is task 15).
- Cargo.lock contains a single rstar version (0.12.x, shared with geo).
- Satisfies the snap-index part of NFR-PERF-005, removes the per-frame SnapTargets rebuild (the done task drops the technical-debt entry) and asserts INP-017's locked clause; INP-008's target set is unchanged (completed in 03).
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-005 INP-008 INP-017
The 50 ms frame-time assertion on two_storey_shell is task 15; criterion benches and the CI regression gate belong to regression-and-status.

title: Ship the steel section catalogue with area regression tests
description:
WHY: PRF-011 (S): a catalogue of standard steel sections (for example IPE, HEA, HEB, HEM, UPE, L; W, C, HSS) shall be provided. The gap row asks for catalogue data mapped onto the PRF-005 parametric shapes and a searchable picker (the picker is task 14). The application is fully offline (D-2, D-12), so the data must ship inside the binary. The epic acceptance requires a catalogue of IPE/HEA/HEB/HEM/UPE/L/W/C/HSS sections with area regression tests. Status: missing.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/data/steel-sections.csv (header comment naming the source table per family; columns family, designation, aliases, shape code, dimensions, tabulated area, unit system) with the complete European series IPE 80-600 (18 rows), HEA, HEB and HEM 100-1000 (24 rows each), UPE 80-400 (14) and equal-leg angles L 20x3 to 200x24 per EN 10056-1, and the US series W (at least the W8 to W24 groups), C3 to C15 and HSS rectangular, square and round in common sizes (design wall thickness 0.93 t). Add crates/archicraft-model/src/catalogue.rs: the CSV embedded with include_str! and parsed once (std::sync::OnceLock) into `CatalogueEntry { family: SteelFamily, designation, aliases, shape: ParametricShape, tabulated_area: f64 }` with US inch values converted to metres; `SteelFamily` with label() and region (EN or US); `entries()`, `find(designation)` (aliases such as 'HE 200 B' accepted), `search(query)` (case-insensitive, spaces ignored, prefix ranking) and `Profile::from_catalogue(designation, material) -> Option<Profile>` (name = designation, usage columns and beams, catalogue = Some(designation)). Malformed lines are skipped with tracing::error and caught by a test. Out of scope: the picker UI (14), EN hollow sections (not in PRF-011), sloped-flange geometry for US C channels (approximated with parallel flanges at the tabulated mean thickness).
design: CSV instead of JSON or TOML: no new dependency (manual split on commas), line-based diffs, include_str! keeps the data offline in the binary. Parameter mapping: IPE/HE/UPE use h, b, tw, tf, r directly; HEM uses the actual h (HEM 200 has h = 220 mm); W shapes use d, bf, tw, tf and r = k_des - tf; HSS rectangular uses the design thickness and an outer corner radius of 2 x design thickness (AISC convention), HSS round maps to CircularHollow; L uses t, r1 and r2; C channels use the mean flange thickness. The area test lives in archicraft-geometry because the model crate must not depend on geometry (strict layering, NFR-MNT-002). Data provenance: dimensions are transcribed from the published standard tables (EN 10365, EN 10056-1, ASTM A6/A6M with the AISC dimension tables); do not copy a vendor's or AISC's database file verbatim, record the source per family in the header, and have the product owner confirm the provenance under the licence policy (deny.toml covers crates only). Pitfall: 'HE 200 B' versus 'HEB 200' naming; store the common designation and accept the EN 10365 form as an alias.
acceptance_criteria:
- catalogue_parses_completely: no line is skipped; row counts per family are at least IPE 18, HEA 24, HEB 24, HEM 24, UPE 14, L 20, W 60, C 25, HSS 60; designations and aliases are unique.
- every_catalogue_section_is_valid: each entry's ParametricShape passes validate_profile from task 01.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/catalogue.rs catalogue_areas_match_tabulated_values: Section::area() of every row is within 1 % of the tabulated area for IPE, HEA, HEB, HEM, UPE, W and HSS and within 3 % for L and C (documented approximations); the failure message lists every offender.
- Spot checks within those tolerances: IPE 300 53.8 cm2, HEB 200 78.1 cm2, HEM 200 131 cm2 (h = 220 mm), UPE 200 29.0 cm2, W12X26 7.65 in2, HSS6X4X3/8 6.18 in2.
- search('ipe 2') returns IPE 200, IPE 220, IPE 240 and IPE 270 with IPE 200 first; find('HE 200 B') returns HEB 200; from_catalogue sets the usage flags and the designation.
- The release binary contains the data (no file access at runtime) and cargo test, clippy and fmt are green.
- Satisfies the data clause of PRF-011 (the picker clause follows in task 14).
notes:
SRS: PRF-011 PRF-005
Open question: EN hollow sections (EN 10210/10219 SHS, RHS, CHS), US unequal angles and WT shapes are not in PRF-011's examples and are left out; adding rows later needs no code change.

title: Exclude elements and layers from producing snap targets
description:
WHY: Individual elements, layers or references shall be excludable from producing snap targets without being hidden, and elements locked against editing shall still provide snap targets (INP-017). Today Layer has only visible and locked (crates/archicraft-model/src/layer.rs:8-15), Element only locked (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:275-287), and the snap sources filter on visibility alone.

WHAT: archicraft-model: Element.snap_excluded and Layer.snap_excluded (serde default false) and Project::provides_snaps(&Element) (visible, element not excluded, layer not excluded, independent of locked), changed through the existing UpdateElements and UpdateLayer commands; only_lock_changed (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:362-368) becomes 'only the lock or snap flag changed', so an element-locked element accepts the snap flag like its lock flag, while a layer-locked element keeps rejecting every change (plan_update_elements, command.rs:381-386). The SnapSource of task 02 filters with provides_snaps. archicraft-ifcx: an optional snapExcluded boolean in the archicraft::element common attributes (schema.rs ELEMENT near line 224, writer.rs near line 408, reader.rs near line 721) and in each layers entry of archicraft::project (schema.rs near line 163, writer.rs 172-177, reader.rs near line 282), written only when true so existing golden files stay byte-identical; FORMAT_VERSION stays 1. UI: a 'Snap targets' checkbox beside 'Locked' in ui/properties.rs lock_toggle (627-648) and a 'Snaps' column in the Layers dialog (ui/dialogs.rs:301-320). References: reference elements such as grids and 2D lines are elements and use the element flag; linked reference models (IFX-084, ifcx-interop) are a snap source of their own, so SnapIndex gains set_source_excluded(source, bool), which drops or restores all targets of one source and which ifcx-interop wires to its link dialog. Out of scope: the reference-model source itself (ifcx-interop).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point: declare with optional(...) in schema.rs, write with json! only when true, read with boolean(map, "snapExcluded").unwrap_or(false). Keep Project::is_visible unchanged (drawing and selection, SEL-007); provides_snaps is a separate predicate.
