Both flags are command-driven, so the index's revision-based invalidation of task 02 already picks them up. Decision: the snap flag is an input aid, not an edit of the element, so it follows the existing lock-flag exception; for layer-locked elements the user excludes the layer instead. Pitfall: the Layers grid uses num_columns(5) (dialogs.rs:301); raise it to 6 and add the header.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: toggling snap_excluded on an element and on a layer undoes and redoes to the exact project; a locked element reports provides_snaps true; a hidden one false; toggling snap_excluded on an element-locked wall succeeds, on a wall of a locked layer it fails with the lock reason.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: a project with a flagged element and a flagged layer round-trips with both flags; golden_files_are_reproduced passes without ARCHICRAFT_BLESS (attribute omitted when false); a file without the attribute reads as false.
- Input tests: an excluded element's nodes and edges never appear in candidates(), nor those of an element on an excluded layer; a locked element's do; set_source_excluded on a stub reference source removes all its candidates and restores them when switched back, without a full index rebuild.
- kittest: selecting a wall shows the 'Snap targets' checkbox; the Layers dialog shows the 'Snaps' column.
- Satisfies INP-017 for elements, layers and (through the source switch) references; guide lines are covered by task 11's hide switch, and dropping the marks of excluded owners is tested in task 09.
notes:
SRS: INP-017
Both flags default to false; no Appendix D value.

title: Complete the 2D snap targets, seven-level precedence and cycling
description:
WHY: In 2D and 3D views the cursor shall snap within a configurable screen radius to element nodes and handles, points on edges, edge midpoints and division points, real intersections, perpendicular foot points, tangent points, arc and circle centres and the axis points of columns and beams; the cursor glyph distinguishes at least no snap, on edge, on node, on intersection, perpendicular, tangent and the command states copy, multiple copy, trim target and choose side (INP-008). The cursor shall also snap to polygon centroids (INP-024). With several candidates in range the winner follows a documented, fixed precedence: node, intersection, division point, guide intersection, edge, guide, grid, and a key cycles through the candidates in range just as Tab cycles selection candidates (INP-009). Today SnapKind (tools.rs:120-132) knows Node, Intersection, Midpoint, Perpendicular, Edge and Grid, only the single best candidate is computed, Tab is taken by the field toggle (plan.rs:663-668) and draw_snap_marker (plan.rs:321-356) has no tangent, centroid or command-state glyphs.

WHAT: In input/snap.rs introduce SnapLevel with exactly the seven SRS levels and a SnapKind detail inside each level (Node: element node, handle, centre, axis point, centroid; Intersection; Division; GuideIntersection; Edge: perpendicular foot, tangent point, point on edge; Guide; Grid) plus the pipeline results Typed, Locked, Constrained and Free; candidates(index, cursor, radius, previous, guides) -> Vec<Snap> sorted by (level, rank within level, distance) and deduplicated. PointInput keeps the candidate list and a cycle index; Tab cycles while the active typed field is empty and two or more candidates are in range, otherwise it moves to the next field. SnapSource gains circles and arcs (centre, radius, sweep), centroids, axis points and handles (a node-level detail fed through a handle hook; wall endpoints stay plain nodes, and the handles of selected elements arrive with edit-reshape-palette's tools/handles.rs). In crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs add PlanElement::centroids() (geo::Centroid on the cut polygons) and index centroids of cut polygons and slab outlines. Extend draw_snap_marker in plan.rs with the full glyph set and draw a CursorState overlay (Copy, MultipleCopy, TrimTarget, ChooseSide) taken from Preview::cursor. Out of scope: division modes beyond Half (04), guide producers (08, 09, 11), producers of column/beam axis points (profiles-columns-beams), of handles (edit-reshape-palette) and of arcs (curved-geometry), 3D snapping (INP-016, 3d-input-navigation).
design: Precedence table: Node (element node 0, handle 1, centre 2, axis point 3, centroid 4) < Intersection < Division < GuideIntersection < Edge (perpendicular 0, tangent 1, on edge 2) < Guide < Grid. The SRS fixes seven levels; derived points sit inside the level whose nature they share, and perpendicular and tangent points must outrank the plain nearest point on the same edge, which is always closer to the cursor. Tangent points from p to a circle (c, r): c + r·(cos(θ ± φ), sin(θ ± φ)) with θ the direction from c to p and φ = acos(r / |p − c|); arcs keep only points inside the sweep. Centroids are computed in archicraft-geometry because geo is a dependency there and not of archicraft-app. Deduplicate candidates within 1e-9 model units keeping the best level. Keep the existing square and cross glyphs (plan.rs:324-335) so plan-renderer's golden images are not disturbed. The cycle index is keyed like PlanViewState.pick (plan.rs:454-458). Pitfall: Tab must not reach egui focus navigation; the focus-lock filter (plan.rs:382-394) already captures it while the view has focus.
acceptance_criteria:
- One precedence test places seven competing candidates within the radius (node, intersection, division point, guide intersection, edge point, guide point, grid point; the guides injected as synthetic GuideShape lines) and asserts that candidates() returns them in the SRS order; the module doc carries the same table.
- Target tests: centre and both tangent points from the previous point on a synthetic circle and arc source; the perpendicular foot from the previous point outranks the nearer plain edge point; a centroid snap on the ground slab of two_storey_shell lands at (6.0, 4.5) and on an L-shaped cut polygon at its geo centroid; an axis-point source and a synthetic handle source contribute node-level candidates labelled 'axis point' and 'handle'; a point found both as node and as intersection appears once, at node level.
- Radius regression (INP-008 'configurable screen radius', existing prefs.rs:41-42 and plan.rs:443): InputContext.radius equals snap_radius × model_per_pixel; at a fixed zoom a node 10 px from the cursor is no candidate with the default 8 px and is one with 16 px.
- archicraft-geometry test for PlanElement::centroids() on a rectangle, an L shape and a polygon with a hole.
- Cycling tests: with two candidates in range Tab selects the second and then wraps; leaving the radius resets the cycle; with typed text present, or with a single candidate, Tab moves to the next field instead.
- Glyph test: every SnapKind and CursorState variant is drawn in one kittest frame without panic, the crosshair is drawn for Free, and the tracker label names the snap kind ('tangent', 'centroid', 'perpendicular').
- Satisfies INP-008's 2D target and glyph set (3D through INP-016 in 3d-input-navigation; column/beam and arc producers in their epics), INP-024 and INP-009's precedence and cycling (guide levels get real producers in tasks 09 and 11).
notes:
SRS: INP-008 INP-009 INP-024
Appendix D.1: snap radius 8 px (prefs.rs:65, clamped 2-40). Provisional binding: Tab cycles snap candidates while the active field is empty and two or more candidates are in range (the rule doors-windows-core also uses for host candidates); the final keymap belongs to commands-and-l10n (D.8).

title: Verify exit criterion: Properties panel, settings-dialog framework, reference levels and datum display
description:
WHY: The epic properties-and-dialogs turns the properties strip and settings dialog into the registry-driven field framework every later kind (columns, beams, doors, windows, roofs, stairs) plugs its parameters into, and adds the reference levels and datum display; its exit criterion must be demonstrated on the merged state as a whole. Covered requirements: UI-002, UI-003, EDT-017, ELM-001, ELM-005, ELM-012, ELM-017, ELM-019, ELM-020, MEA-003, STR-002, UI-014, UI-015, STR-007 and STR-011; docs/implementation-status.md must reflect their new status with evidence.

WHAT: Run the complete verification on the merged state of tasks 01-12: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (including the test-kinds registry kittest of the settings dialog, the multi-selection, range, dependent-value, derived-value, storey, size-memory and search kittests, the widgets::length datum unit tests and the IFCX round-trip tests), conformance/run.sh on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx and the freshly written reference models, and a review of any golden diff. If profiles-columns-beams has landed, add or run its kittest that a selected column and beam show Length and Volume; otherwise file a follow-up bead blocked by profiles-columns-beams for that clause. Then update the rows of every covered requirement ID in docs/implementation-status.md (status, file:line evidence, remaining gaps owned elsewhere: DSP-016 for ELM-012/ELM-020, DW-015/STA-009/roofs for MEA-003, stairs for the ELM-017 riser count, later lists for UI-014, third-party import for STR-011), update the architecture summary and the extension points (add a kind: FieldSpecs in the kind module, quantities hook; add a dialog: remembered_window; elevation fields: LengthFormat with a datum; imports: read_datum), remove the closed technical-debt entries, and close the epic in beads (bd close) with a note listing follow-up issues. File these follow-ups: 3d-display-styles-15 (OverrideCriteria gains position and structural function, closing ELM-012/ELM-020 'usable by display overrides'), roofs-08 (ridge and eaves elevation and plane areas as Kind quantities, MEA-003 roofs row), host-openings and solid-kernel-ops (re-assert MEA-003 net volume with real openings and solid operations), layer-structures-11 and components-dw-catalogue (SearchField, UI-014), and profiles-columns-beams for the column and beam Length and Volume kittest if it has not landed. Do not commit or push beyond what the active profile allows; report the commands.
design: Verification is a checklist run on the merged branch, not new code. Status rows cite file:line evidence as docs/implementation-status.md does today; the gap-analysis.json rows for these IDs are the template for the wording. The kittests run without a GPU, so the preview is verified through its painter fallback and PreviewState; one manual run of the app on a GPU checks the offscreen preview and the remembered sizes after a restart, recorded in the closing note.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: a mixed selection shows only common fields with mixed markers and 'n selected, m editable'; committing applies to every editable element; every registered kind has a dialog with the four sections and a preview (a test iterates the registry); an invalid value shows its explanation and leaves the model untouched; W-001-style IDs with a configurable prefix; derived values for walls, slabs, columns and beams; lists longer than one screen get a search field; the storey-height default shifts the storeys above. A datum 'sea level +412.000' shows a storey at +3.000 as +415.000 and typing +415.000 stores 3.000 (unit tests on widgets::length); the datum is written once to IFCX and never asked for twice.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on the golden files (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx) and on the freshly written reference models.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (UI-002 UI-003 EDT-017 ELM-001 ELM-005 ELM-012 ELM-017 ELM-019 ELM-020 MEA-003 STR-002 UI-014 UI-015 STR-007 STR-011) with status, evidence and remaining gap, and the architecture summary, extension points and technical-debt list reflect the FieldSpec framework, quantities, reference levels, SizeMemory and SearchField.
- The epic is closed in beads, with follow-up issues filed for deferred clauses: column/beam derived values if profiles-columns-beams has not landed; position and structural-function criteria on 3d-display-styles-15 (DSP-016); roof quantities through the hook on roofs-08; net volume re-assertion on host-openings and solid-kernel-ops; SearchField adoption on layer-structures-11 and components-dw-catalogue.
notes: SRS: UI-002 UI-003 EDT-017 ELM-001 ELM-005 ELM-012 ELM-017 ELM-019 ELM-020 MEA-003 STR-002 UI-014 UI-015 STR-007 STR-011

title: Keep plan navigation at frame rate with hatches shown
description:
WHY: the last clause of DSP-013 requires that with hatches shown plan navigation meets NFR-PERF-004 (panning and zooming at >= 30 frames/s for any storey of RM-M). RM-M does not exist yet, so the 5,000-element stand-in of element-kind-framework is the provisional load; the renderer has to keep navigation a uniform-only update and avoid drawing what is off screen.

WHAT: per-tile draw ranges (spatial bins of each storey's fill, hatch and stroke buffers with bounds) culled against the viewport in the paint callback; an #[ignore] performance test crates/archicraft-app/tests/plan_perf.rs (run with `cargo test --release -p archicraft-app --test plan_perf -- --ignored`; no benchmark crate, since criterion is not in docs/technology-choices.md) that renders a scripted 300-frame pan/zoom sequence of the stand-in storey with F2-layered walls, hatches and separators headless and reports frame times; a CI smoke test asserting that navigation frames write only uniforms; a measurement of plan regeneration (classification plus tessellation) after a single edit; results recorded in docs/testing.md or in the docs/performance convention of regression-and-status if it exists. Out of scope: the RM-M/RM-L reference models and final acceptance (reference-models, perf-tuning-rm-m-l), incremental per-element re-tessellation (follow-up bead if needed) and 3D performance.
design: Tiles: a 16 m x 16 m grid in model coordinates (proposal); each tile owns contiguous index ranges per pass so a culled frame issues draw_indexed calls for the visible tiles only; strokes and hatch regions spanning tiles are assigned by bounding-box centre and the tile bounds used for culling are expanded by the largest resolved stroke width. Frame timing: wgpu timestamp queries when Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY is available, otherwise wall-clock around queue.submit plus device.poll(Maintain::Wait). Build the load with the seeded stand_in(5000) builder of element-kind-framework and apply the F2 layer structure to its walls so hatches and separators are present. On CI the software adapter is too slow for frame-rate assertions, so CI only checks the structural counters.
acceptance_criteria:
- The performance test exists and on the developer reference machine renders the 5,000-element stand-in storey with hatches at a median >= 60 frames/s and a 99th percentile >= 30 frames/s during pan and zoom (2x margin over NFR-PERF-004); machine, adapter and commit are recorded with the results in the repository docs.
- CI smoke test on the software adapter: 100 navigation frames cause zero vertex/index buffer writes and zero tessellations (counters); only uniform writes happen.
- Culling test: zoomed into one room of the stand-in, the submitted index count drops below 10 % of the full-storey count.
- The regeneration time after one wall edit is measured and reported; if it exceeds 100 ms (half of the NFR-PERF-006 200 ms budget) a follow-up bead for per-element incremental tessellation is filed and linked.
- Satisfies the NFR-PERF-004 clause of DSP-013 on the provisional load; final RM-M acceptance stays with perf-tuning-rm-m-l.
notes: SRS: DSP-013. Covers the NFR-PERF-004 clause of DSP-013. NFR-PERF-004: >= 30 frames/s plan panning and zooming for any storey of RM-M; reference hardware is open (O-15, NFR-PERF-001, decided in regression-and-status). Stand-in numbers are provisional.

title: Add the beam kind across model, geometry and IFCX
description:
WHY: BEA-001 (M): a beam shall be created between two picked points; it has a width and height (or a profile), an anchor point chosen from nine cross-section points, a lateral offset of its axis, a roll angle about its own axis, an elevation relative to the home storey and an inclination set by the end elevations or a pitch angle. BEA-002 (M): each beam end shall have an end cut that is vertical (default), horizontal or at a custom angle, editable numerically and by handle in plan and 3D (numeric editing in task 11, handles in 13). ELM-011 allows IfcBeam, IfcMember or IfcFooting for beams. IFX-035 (S) writes beam axes as basiscurves in an Axis child; it is partial: wall axes already flow through ElementGeometry.axis (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:174) into the Axis child (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:229-235, 382-389), and beams reuse that path unchanged. PRF-004 (M): editing a profile updates every element that uses it, so a profile beam re-evaluates on UpdateProfile through the dirty set of task 06. Appendix D.2: 0.25 x 0.50 m reinforced concrete, top-centre anchor, top at the home storey elevation + 2.80 m. Status: BEA-001 and BEA-002 missing.

WHAT: Model: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/beam.rs with `Beam { start, end, section: CrossSection, material, anchor, lateral_offset, roll, start_elevation, end_elevation, start_cut: BeamCut, end_cut: BeamCut }` and `BeamCut::{Vertical, Horizontal, Angle(f64)}` (angle from vertical in the vertical plane through the axis); Beam::pitch() and with_pitch(angle), which keeps the start elevation and recomputes the end elevation from the plan length. Kind impl: DESCRIPTOR { label 'Beam', code 'beam', name_prefix 'B', default_class IfcBeam, ifc_classes [IfcBeam, IfcMember, IfcFooting], has_tool true, template_defaults Some(D.2 beam slot) }, storey_links() empty (no top link), rehome adds the elevation difference between the old and the new home storey to both elevations so the beam keeps its absolute position, transform, vertical_extent from both elevations and the rolled section bounds, validate (plan length >= MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, |pitch| <= 85 degrees, sizes, cut angle within (-85, 85) degrees, Horizontal rejected when |pitch| < 5 degrees, end planes not crossing at any corner of the rolled section bounds; Anchor::ProfileOrigin normalised to Centre for rectangular sections), profiles() and replace_profile(); Project::new_beam(storey, start, end); the template's D.2 slot (Anchor::TopCentre, both elevations 2.80, vertical cuts, layer 'Structure'). Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/beam.rs (GeometryKind impl plus one registry line) applies the lateral offset along the plan line's left normal, builds frame_for_beam with roll, offsets the section to the anchor, puts the cut planes through the anchor-line ends, sweeps into 'Body' or 'Region_n' parts and returns axis = [anchor-line start, anchor-line end] at their elevations. IFCX: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/beam.rs KindCodec `archicraft::beam` with one codecs! line (start, end, section, material, anchor, lateralOffset, roll, startElevation, endElevation, startCut { kind, angle }, endCut) plus the defaults slot, read leniently. Out of scope: the tool and chains (11), handles (13), BEA-003 compound cuts, BEA-004 joins (cleanup-and-trims), segments, openings and curved beams (BEA-005..007, BEA-009).
design: Elevations are stored for the anchor line (the line the chosen anchor point follows) at the picked end points; the pitch is derived and offered as an editable input (BEA-001 'or a pitch angle'). Frame: d = unit vector from (start, start_elevation) to (end, end_elevation) after the lateral offset; v = normalize(Z - (Z.d) d); u = d x v (the right-hand side when looking from start to end, matching the profile plane convention of task 01); roll rotates (u, v) counter-clockwise about d as seen from the start. Cut normals: Vertical = horizontal part of d (a plumb cut, also on inclined beams), Horizontal = +/-Z pointing away from the body, Angle theta = cos(theta) d_h + sin(theta) Z, mirrored at the start; positive angles lean the top of the end outward. Lateral offset is positive to the left, like DVec2::perp() offsets of wall reference lines. vertical_extent must take the rolled bounding-box corners at both ends so the framework's z-extent queries and plan classification see the true body. Pitfalls: Horizontal on a level beam is a plane parallel to the axis (rejected); beams sharing an end point in a chain (task 11) stay separate bodies until BEA-004.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: adding a beam names it B-001 and undo/redo restore exactly; with_pitch(30 degrees) on a 4 m beam sets end_elevation = start_elevation + 4 tan 30 degrees (1e-12); validation rejects zero length, a Horizontal cut on a level beam, crossing cuts on a 0.30 m long, 0.60 m deep beam with +/-60 degree cuts, a profile without the beams flag and the class IfcColumn; IfcFooting and IfcMember are accepted; DeleteProfile with a replacement re-points the beam; raising the home storey by 0.50 m raises the beam body by 0.50 m (elevations relative to the home storey) and deleting the home storey rehomes the beam without moving it.
- Template test: the beam slot is 0.25 x 0.50 m reinforced concrete, Anchor::TopCentre, elevations 2.80 m, vertical cuts, layer 'Structure'.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs: a 6 m D.2 beam is closed with volume 0.75 m3, its top at 2.80 and bottom at 2.30 relative to the storey; lateral offset 0.10 moves the body 0.10 m to the left of the picked line; roll 90 degrees makes the plan footprint 0.50 m wide; a 30 degree pitch with vertical cuts has vertical end faces and volume = area x plan length / cos 30 degrees; a Horizontal end cut on that beam has an end-face normal of +/-Z; Angle(20 degrees) gives area x centroid length; an IPE 300 beam (catalogue, task 04) is closed with volume area x length; the axis equals the anchor-line ends at their elevations; Anchor::ProfileOrigin on a profile beam puts the profile's insertion origin on the picked line.
- IFCX: a beam round-trips exactly; its node carries IfcBeam, Body or Region_n children and an Axis child with two basiscurves points and a v5 id; the file validates; lenient-reading tests cover an unknown profile and an invalid cut.
- Profile propagation (PRF-004): UpdateProfile changing the IPE beam's profile height changes its evaluated volume; the incremental-versus-full property test covers beams as well as columns.
- Satisfies BEA-001 and BEA-002 in model, geometry and file (tool in 11, handles in 13) and the beam clause of IFX-035.
notes:
SRS: BEA-001 BEA-002 IFX-035 PRF-004
Also touches ELM-011 (beam class set). Appendix D.2: beam 0.25 x 0.50 m reinforced concrete, top-centre anchor, top at home storey + 2.80 m. Open question: whether moving an end point should keep the end elevation or the pitch; decided here to store elevations (BEA-001 names the end elevations first) and to treat the pitch as an input mode.

title: Add derived quantities, absolute elevations and keep-offset relink
description:
WHY: MEA-003 (S): the properties panel shows derived values per element: walls (reference-line length, the length of both faces, net volume after openings and solid operations), slabs (top and bottom area, perimeter, net volume), columns and beams (length, volume); roofs, doors/windows and stairs follow via their own requirements. ELM-005 (M): every element has one home storey, its base is an offset from the home storey's elevation, the absolute elevation is shown as well, and changing the home storey keeps the absolute position (relink) unless the user explicitly chooses to keep the offset. Today derived() (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:541-575) shows wall length, slab area (outline minus holes) and volume only; face lengths, top/bottom area and perimeter are missing; the absolute elevation is not shown anywhere and the Home storey combo always relinks (properties.rs:602-620; gap rows MEA-003, ELM-005). Already in place for ELM-005 and kept: exactly one home storey per element (Element.storey, crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:279-280), new elements take the storey of the plan view they are drawn in (views/plan.rs:523 passes the plan's storey to ToolState::add_point, views/tools.rs:451-458), base offsets relative to the home storey (Wall.base_offset, the slab elevation offset) and relink_to_storey keeping the absolute position (command.rs:419-433, test relinking_keeps_the_absolute_position at tests/commands.rs:292-306).

WHAT: archicraft-geometry: new quantities.rs with `Quantity { key, label, kind: QuantityKind {Length, Area, Volume}, value }` (distinct from the FieldType of task 05) and `ElementGeometry.quantities: Vec<Quantity>` filled during evaluation: walls - reference-line length, exterior and interior face lengths from the resolved footprint (wall.rs Footprint after L/T junctions), net volume of the body (net of openings once host-openings cuts them); slabs - top and bottom area from the up- and down-facing faces of the body, perimeter of outline plus holes, net volume; a generic fallback for every other kind - volume, plus the length of a two-point axis (columns and beams write their axis per IFX-035, so they get length and volume when profiles-columns-beams registers them). archicraft-model: command.rs keep_offset_on_storey(project, element, target) next to relink_to_storey, implemented through the Kind trait's rehome hook (only the home storey changes, base offsets and relative top links are kept, impossible results are rejected with an explanation). archicraft-app: derived rows rendered by ui/fields.rs from geometry.quantities (while typing, from a scratch evaluation of the task 07 draft) plus 'Base elevation' and 'Top elevation' from Project::vertical_extent, formatted with the datum-aware LengthFormat of task 04 (the label names the reference level); the Home storey field gets a 'Keep offset' checkbox (default off, reset after each change). Out of scope: roof (ROF), door/window (DW-015) and stair (STA-009) quantities, which register through the same hook; selection sums (MEA-002); base quantities in IFCX (ifcx-interop).
design: Approach: quantities are part of the evaluated geometry, so they are cached per element by the incremental evaluation of element-kind-framework-10; while typing, this task evaluates the draft working copy of task 07 once per draft change through the per-kind generator (neighbour inputs reused so junction-resolved face lengths stay right), task 09 reuses that scratch geometry for its preview, and the app only formats. Face lengths: today's Footprint is [DVec2; 4] with the exterior and interior edges (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:102); junction-engine replaces it by per-skin polygons, so the face-length computation lives in one function in quantities.rs that junction-engine updates (leave a bead note on junction-engine). Top/bottom area: sum of triangle areas with normal.z above 0.999 / below -0.999 (ready for sloped slabs); perimeter from the validated outline and holes; net volume = TriMesh::signed_volume over all parts (evaluate.rs:46-48), which is net once openings and solid operations cut the body. Keep offset: the rehome hook of element-kind-framework-02 takes the target elevation; add a sibling hook with a default implementation that only changes Element.storey and lets validate_element reject impossible tops. Formatting: format_length/format_area/format_volume (units.rs:283-376) and the datum LengthFormat for elevations. Pitfalls: vertical_extent returns None for an element on a missing storey (show nothing); failed elements have no quantities (NFR-REL-006 fallback); quantities must not enter IFCX golden bytes. Pointers: evaluate.rs:20-48 and 130-188, wall.rs:102 and 232-280, mesh.rs:105-120 and 196-205, command.rs:397-433, properties.rs:541-620.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/quantities.rs or tests/): a free 5.00 x 0.25 m wall has reference length 5.000 and both faces 5.000; two 5.00 m walls in an L junction with exterior reference lines have outer faces 5.000 and inner faces 4.750 as resolved by footprints(); a 4 x 3 m slab, 0.20 m thick, with a 1 x 1 m hole has top area 11.000, bottom area 11.000, perimeter 18.000 and net volume 2.200; the test-kinds Dummy with a two-point axis reports length and volume through the generic path.
- Net volume after openings and solid operations: quantities come from the final evaluated body, so a unit test feeding the quantity function a wall body with a 1.00 x 1.00 m through-hole (a hand-built closed TriMesh) reports the gross volume minus the hole; host-openings and solid-kernel-ops re-assert it with real openings and solid operations (bead notes left on both).
- The incremental_equals_full property test of element-kind-framework-10 is extended to compare the quantities field as well.
- Model tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: relinking a wall from storey 0 to storey 1 keeps its absolute bottom and top (existing test kept); keep_offset_on_storey moves both by the storey elevation difference (3.000) and keeps base_offset; a keep-offset change that would put a storey-linked top below the base is rejected with CommandError::Invalid and an explanation.
- kittest: a selected wall shows Length, Exterior face length, Interior face length, Volume, Base elevation and Top elevation; a selected slab shows Top area, Bottom area, Perimeter and Volume; with reference Sea level and altitude 412 the ground-floor wall's Base elevation reads '+412.000'.
- kittest: changing Home storey to '01 First floor' leaves Base elevation unchanged; with 'Keep offset' checked it changes by +3.000; each change is one undo step and the checkbox is unchecked afterwards.
- ELM-005 regression: relinking_keeps_the_absolute_position passes unchanged; a test asserts that a wall drawn in the plan of '01 First floor' gets that storey as its home storey; a wall on '01 First floor' with base offset -0.500 shows Base elevation +2.500 (negative offsets allowed and shown).
- Satisfies MEA-003 for walls and slabs and, through the generic axis path, for columns and beams as soon as they register; the roofs row is delivered by roofs-08 (ROF-011) through the same quantities hook, doors and windows by DW-015 and stairs by STA-009; satisfies ELM-005 (absolute elevation shown, relink by default, explicit keep-offset choice).
notes:
SRS: MEA-003 ELM-005
profiles-columns-beams is not a prerequisite of this epic: column and beam length and volume come from the generic axis path and are re-asserted by a kittest in that epic (or in a follow-up bead if this epic closes first). DW-015 and STA-009 register their own quantities.
roofs-08 still names properties.rs derived() for ridge and eaves elevation and plane areas (MEA-003 roofs row); once this task replaces derived() by Kind quantities, roofs-08 must register them through the quantities hook - the done task files that follow-up bead.

title: Verify exit criterion: Shared point-input service, snapping, guides and construction grid
description:
WHY: Closes the epic point-input-snapping once its exit criterion holds: every point input goes through the shared PointInput service (INP-001) with complete 2D snapping and precedence (INP-008, INP-009, INP-010, INP-024, INP-017), typed entry (INP-002, INP-003, INP-004, INP-005, INP-022), constraints and locks (INP-006, INP-007, INP-023), inference and persistent guides (INP-011, INP-012), the construction grid (INP-013), the user origin (INP-014), context distances (INP-021), the input-mode preference (INP-020), chain Backspace (UND-003) and the 50 ms feedback budget (NFR-PERF-005).

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged branch, update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence with file:line, gap naming the clauses left to other epics: 3D snapping and guides, the stretch consumer, grid/column/beam context providers), record the INP-009 precedence table, remove the SnapTargets rebuild from the 'Per-frame allocations in the plan view' technical-debt entry (keep the raw-event clones at plan.rs:400 and view3d.rs:127 unless they were fixed), drop the 'Typed-input character whitelist' entry (task 06), update the extension points (tools/ module, InputConsumer, SnapSource, ContextProvider), and close the epic in beads. No new features.

The step/preview API is exercised by two consumers in this epic's tests (the wall tool and a transform stub) so that selection-transforms and 3d-input-navigation plug in without changing it.
