Task estimates sum to about 8,460 minutes (about 17.6 engineer-days at 8 h) against the 15-day epic cap; the roadmap expects capped epics to need a short second wave. Clauses deliberately left to other epics: 3D snapping, guides and working-plane grid (3d-input-navigation), the stretch consumer (edit-reshape-palette), transforms (selection-transforms), grid/column/beam snap and context providers (grids, profiles-columns-beams), arc producers (curved-geometry), measuring and dimensioning consumers (3d-input-navigation, sections-elevations-dims).

title: Add per-view plan display switches and layered-element goldens
description:
WHY: DSP-012 (separator lines can be switched off per view), DSP-017 (a view option shows layered elements in full, as core only or without finish skins) and DSP-019 (a view option switches between true weights and uniform thin lines) all need per-view controls; DSP-018 needs goldens of the layered-element rules. The epic exit requires that the F2 wall shows six skin regions with separator lines in the separator pen that a per-view switch hides, and that the core-only option hides finish skins.

WHAT: PlanViewState carries `options: PlanOptions` (separators, layered display) and `weights: WeightMode`; Document::plan takes the options and caches per (storey, PlanOptions); the View menu gets a checkable "Skin separator lines", a radio group "Full" / "Core only" / "Without finishes" and a radio group "True line weights" / "Thin lines" acting on the active plan view, each also an Action in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs (added to Action::ALL) so it appears in menus and in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog; a status-bar indicator next to the drawing-scale combo when a non-default option is active; goldens of the F2 scenes. Out of scope: persisting the options in saved views (plan-views-browser maps ViewState to ViewDefinition), 3D views and per-element overrides.
design: Document::plan(storey, &PlanOptions) with a cache HashMap<(StoreyId, PlanOptions), (u64, Arc<PlanDrawing>)> bounded like the GPU cache (PlanOptions derives Hash/Eq; keep f64 view-range fields out of the key until plan-views-browser defines how they hash, e.g. by to_bits). Menu items follow the existing View menu in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:78-99 and act on ws.active_pane when it is a plan; view options are view state, not model Commands (not undoable, like zoom and scale). The weight mode goes into the paint-callback uniforms, so it never re-tessellates. Status-bar indicator: a small weak label such as "Core only" or "No separators" so the user always sees when the view deviates from the default (section 4.4 intent of showing active filters).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the View menu has items labelled "Skin separator lines", "Full", "Core only", "Without finishes", "True line weights" and "Thin lines"; switching separators off in the ground-floor plan changes only that view's PlanViewState (the upper storey's view keeps them) and the plan returned for that view has no SkinSeparator strokes; the six new actions are in Action::ALL (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs) and therefore listed with their labels in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:646); shortcuts_are_unique still passes.
- Goldens through the plan-renderer-07 harness pass on the three CI platforms: the free wall of samples::f2_layered_wall() at 1:50 with separators on, separators off, core only, without finishes and thin lines; two collinear F2 walls and two joined concrete walls showing no seam.
- Pixel assertion in the F2 scene: separator lines measure the separator pen's resolved width and colour (not the cut pen's); with the switch off, the pixels at the separator positions equal the neighbouring fill or hatch.
- Pixel assertion in the core-only scene: pixels inside the plaster skins equal the paper background, and the cut outline lies on the core faces.
- Switching the weight mode or the scale re-renders without rebuilding PlanBuffers (counter), while a PlanOptions change rebuilds once.
- Satisfies the per-view switch clauses of DSP-012, DSP-017 and DSP-019 and the layered-element goldens of DSP-018.
notes: SRS: DSP-012 DSP-017 DSP-019 DSP-018. Defaults: separators on, layered Full, true weights. Handoff to plan-views-browser: ViewDefinition should store scale, PlanOptions and WeightMode (note in the pull request).

title: Generate closed cross-sections for parametric and custom profiles
description:
WHY: PRF-005 (M) asks for rectangle, circle, rectangular and circular hollow sections, I/H, T, L, U/C and Z shapes 'defined by their dimensions'; the sweep (task 05), the plan preview, the catalogue area tests (04) and the profile editor (14, 15) all need these as closed polygons with holes. PRF-004 regions carry their own materials; COL-001 needs rectangular and circular column sections and the nine anchor points of a cross-section. IFX-034 (M) tessellates curved geometry with at most 2 mm chordal deviation and 10 degrees per segment (at least 36 segments per circle), user-adjustable per project; ProjectSettings.tessellation exists (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:27-43) but no geometry reads it (technical debt). IFX-038 (M) shares vertices only across smooth edges, so the generator must record which section vertices lie on arcs.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-geometry/src/section.rs (registered in lib.rs): `Section { regions: Vec<SectionRegion> }`, `SectionRegion { outer: SectionLoop, holes: Vec<SectionLoop>, material: MaterialId, role: String }` and `SectionLoop { points: Vec<DVec2>, smooth: Vec<bool> }`. `parametric_section(&ParametricShape, material, &Tessellation) -> Result<Section, GeometryError>` for all nine shapes: root fillets for I/H, T and U/C, root and toe radii for L, outer corner radius for RHS (inner radius = outer - t, clamped at 0), circle and CHS rings, sharp-cornered Z. `profile_section(&Profile, &Tessellation)` dispatches parametric shapes and passes custom regions through (all vertices hard). Section methods: area() (outer minus holes), centroid(), bounds(), nine_point(index) for index 0..9 in row-major order from top-left (task 06's Anchor enum maps onto these indices; it does not exist yet when this task lands), transformed(offset, rotation). `arc_segments(radius, sweep, &Tessellation) -> usize` implements the IFX-034 rule (maximum of the angle rule and the chord rule, at least 1). Loops are closed without a repeated last point, outer CCW, holes CW, cleaned with clean_ring. Out of scope: sweeping (05), the catalogue data (04), anchors as element parameters (06, 07), arc edges in custom profiles (curved-geometry).
design: Build every shape with one small 'rounded path' routine: a shape is a list of corners (point, fillet radius); each filleted corner is replaced by an arc tangent to both adjacent edges, tessellated with arc_segments and evaluated as centre + r * (cos, sin) of start + i * sweep / n (no accumulated rotation, deterministic output). Tangent points and arc interiors are smooth because the surface is tangent-continuous there, so averaging normals across them causes no shading artefact (IFX-038 allows sharing across smooth edges). Orientation conventions, documented in doc comments and shown by the editor preview: U/C opens towards +x (web on the left), L has its heel at bottom-left with legs along +x and +y, T has the flange on top, Z has the top flange towards +x. Circles start at angle 0 so identical diameters tessellate identically. drafting-trim-split will introduce the shared tessellate(curve, settings); arc_segments implements the same rule and carries a doc comment pointing to it so the two can be merged when it lands. Pitfalls: RHS with outer_radius <= thickness has a sharp inner corner; L toe radii apply to both leg tips; triangulate.rs (used by task 05) rejects self-intersections, so validate_ring in the tests guards it; MODEL_TOLERANCE from the framework's tolerance module is the only coincidence constant.
acceptance_criteria:
- Closed-form area tests per shape: rectangle w x h exact; circle and CHS equal the inscribed-polygon area n/2 * r^2 * sin(2 pi / n) for the generated segment count n (1e-12 relative) and lie within 0.6 % of the true area at the default 2 mm / 10 degree settings (36 segments give 0.51 %, so a 0.5 % bound would fail); RHS w*h - (w-2t)(h-2t) - (4-pi)(ro^2 - ri^2) within 0.2 %; I/H 2*b*tf + (h-2tf)*tw + (4-pi)*r^2 within 0.2 %; T, U/C and L (including the toe-radius term) within 0.2 %; Z exact.
- IPE 200 (h 200, b 100, tw 5.6, tf 8.5, r 12 mm) gives 28.48 cm2, within 0.5 % of the EN 10365 tabulated 28.5 cm2.
- Every generated loop passes validate_ring unchanged (orientation, no self-intersection, no edge shorter than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH) and every hole lies inside its outer loop (point_in_ring).
- arc_segments: r = 12 mm over 90 degrees gives 9; a full circle of r = 1 m gives 50 (the 2 mm chord rule dominates); changing ProjectSettings.tessellation changes the counts (IFX-034 adjustable).
- smooth flags are true exactly on arc vertices including the tangent points and false on sharp corners; bounds() equals (-b/2, -h/2)..(b/2, h/2) and equals Profile::bounds() from task 01 for every shape (shared test).
- nine_point returns the 3 x 3 bounding-box points in row-major order from top-left; a custom two-region profile keeps both regions with their materials and roles Region_1, Region_2.
- Satisfies the geometric clause of PRF-005 (closed cross-sections defined by dimensions) and supplies the section side of PRF-004 and COL-001.
notes:
SRS: PRF-005 PRF-004 COL-001
Appendix D.1 / IFX-034 defaults: 2 mm chord deviation, at most 10 degrees per segment.

title: Map pane view state to ViewDefinition: save, redefine and open views
description:
WHY: VIEW-004 (M): saving, redefining (keeping ID and name) and opening a saved view that re-applies its state to the current model; VIEW-012 (S): per-view range overrides must persist per view; LAY-003 (S): a view references a layer combination or stores its own states. Gap rows: camera, zoom and display mode live in transient PlanViewState and View3dState (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:22-32, views/view3d.rs:15-23) and are reset on replace_document (workspace.rs:89-101); Pane::Plan(StoreyId) keys plan state by storey, so a storey can have only one plan view; tab insertion depends on HashMap order (app.rs:302-305, technical debt).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs: Pane {Plan(StoreyId), View(ViewId)} (View covers 3D viewpoints and saved views of any kind), deriving Copy, Hash, Serialize and Deserialize; plan_views keyed by Pane; plan::ui(ui, ws, pane) resolves storey and options from the pane. New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/state.rs: capture(pane) -> ViewDefinition sections (camera, drawing scale, plan options with overrides, 3D display mode, current layer states or a chosen combination) and apply(view) -> pane state plus one SetLayerStates when layers are stored, reporting resolve issues in the status line. Sections the pane cannot produce yet (restrictions, sun) are carried over unchanged on redefine and left None on save-as until 3d-view-restrictions-13 and 3d-display-styles-09 extend capture. Requests SaveViewAs(Pane), RedefineView(ViewId, Pane) and OpenView(ViewId); a 'Save as view' modal (name, folder, layers: current states, a combination, or not stored); Action::SaveViewAs and Action::RedefineView. crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs open_pane inserts into the Tabs container of the most recently active pane (tracked TileId) or the root tabs, replacing the heuristic; tab titles mark saved views; pane pruning (app.rs:770-780) checks views by ViewId. Out of scope: browser (10), rotation (12), underlay (13), layout persistence (14).
design: capture and apply are pure functions over (PlanViewState or View3dState, ViewDefinition) and unit-tested without egui; Camera2d <-> ViewCamera::Plan, Camera3d <-> ViewCamera::Model3d, DisplayMode <-> RenderMode. Drawing scale comes from PlanViewState.drawing_scale (plan-renderer-01); if that epic has not landed, add the plain field here (no UI) so saved views already store and re-apply it. Track the last active tabs container in on_tab_button and open_pane via tree.tiles.parent_of(tile). Pitfalls: Pane must stay Copy + Hash + serde because 14 serialises Tree<Pane>; View3dState holds GPU textures and is still keyed by ViewId and released on close (app.rs:842-849); apply runs from handle_requests after layout so the frame stays consistent; SetLayerStates is skipped when nothing differs (NoChange is silent).
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless app test: save the active plan as 'Mezzanine' with a 2.10 m cut override and a zoom; change camera and override; open the view: camera, scale and override are restored; a wall added after saving appears in the reopened view (live model, not a snapshot).
- 3D: saving a 3D view with an orbit camera and display mode Hidden line, changing both and opening the view restores the camera (target, distance, yaw, pitch, fov) and the mode (ViewStyle.mode); the plain viewpoint it was saved from is unchanged.
- Redefine: after zooming, RedefineView keeps id, name and folder, replaces the camera and is one undo step.
- Layer states: a view storing 'Furniture hidden' re-applies it with one undoable SetLayerStates; a view referencing a combination applies the combination's current states; a missing layer produces a status issue while the other states apply.
- The storey plan and a saved plan view of the same storey are open at once with independent cameras and overrides.
- Tab insertion: with a split layout whose second tab group holds the active pane, opening a new view lands in that group (asserted on the Tree after open_pane).
- Opening a saved view whose storey was deleted shows the issue and opens nothing; New/Open drop state only for panes that no longer resolve.
- capture unit test: redefining a view whose restrictions and sun sections are set keeps both unchanged; save-as leaves them None.
- Existing kittests pass. Satisfies VIEW-004 capture, open and redefine, VIEW-012 persistence per view and the LAY-003 view reference.
notes: SRS: VIEW-004 VIEW-012 LAY-003. Open question: point-input-snapping-07 leaves 'saving the user origin per view' to this epic; VIEW-004 does not list it, so capture leaves it out for now and it can be added later as an optional PlanViewSettings field.

title: Edit multi-selections with common fields, mixed markers and counts
description:
WHY: UI-002 (M): with several elements selected, the panel shows how many are selected and how many of those are editable, marks fields whose values differ and applies an edited field to all editable selected elements. EDT-017 (M): for mixed element kinds only parameters common to all kinds are offered; fields with differing values show a mixed state; committing a value assigns it to every selected editable element, including those that already had it. Gaps: a field is shown if any target has it (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:176-178 and 204-206), so a wall+slab selection still offers Reference line, Base offset and Top; the Locked checkbox has no mixed state (properties.rs:627-647); summary() drops the editable count when it equals the selected count (properties.rs:528-530); no test covers mixed-value editing (gap rows UI-002, EDT-017).

WHAT: ui/fields.rs: the field list for a selection is the intersection of the FieldSpec keys of all target kinds (COMMON_FIELDS included); for Choice fields the options are the intersection of the per-target options and the field is hidden when that intersection is empty (so IFC class offers the classes both kinds allow, IfcFooting with today's class sets, for a wall+slab selection). Mixed markers for every quantity: text fields keep the 'Mixed' hint, combos the 'Mixed' text, checkboxes use the indeterminate state, including Locked. The summary always reads '<n> <kind plural> selected, <m> editable' for n > 1 ('elements' for mixed kinds). A commit applies the value to every editable target, locked targets are counted and left unchanged, and the commit is one UpdateElements (one undo step). Out of scope: range explanations (task 07), summed quantities of a selection (MEA-002).
design: Approach: compute the visible field set once per frame from the targets' KindTags (descriptor.fields): intersection by key, ordered as in the first kind's list; option intersection by FieldValue equality. egui 0.36 Checkbox supports indeterminate(true) and AccessKit then reports Toggled::Mixed, which kittest can query. 'Including those that already had it': UpdateElements skips unchanged elements (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:371-395), which is correct because the resulting state is identical and undo stays exact; the tests assert the outcome, not the edit count. The summary uses descriptor.label with a plural helper (commands-and-l10n may replace it by a plural-aware key). Pitfalls: widgets::choice returns None when the pick equals the common value (widgets.rs:123); in the mixed state current is None, so any pick commits, which is the EDT-017 behaviour, keep it; the lock toggle must keep the rule that only-lock changes are allowed on locked elements (command.rs only_lock_changed) and must not touch layer-locked elements. Pointers: properties.rs:168-217, 508-539 and 627-647; widgets.rs:101-131; command.rs:360-395.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest wall_and_slab_show_only_common_fields: one wall and one slab selected show Thickness, Material, Layer, Position, Structural function and IFC class (options: exactly the intersection of the wall and slab descriptor class sets, IfcFooting with today's sets, which element-kind-framework-05 may extend) and do not show Reference line, Base offset, Top or Reference plane; the summary is '2 elements selected, 2 editable'.
- kittest differing_values_show_mixed_and_commit_to_all: two walls of 0.25 m and 0.30 m show the 'Mixed' hint in Thickness; typing 0.20 and Enter sets both to 0.20; a single Undo restores 0.25 and 0.30.
- kittest commit_includes_elements_that_already_had_the_value: walls of 0.25/0.25/0.30 m, typing 0.25 makes all three 0.25; with differing materials, picking the material one wall already has applies it to all.
- kittest locked_elements_are_counted_not_changed: three walls with one locked show '3 walls selected, 2 editable'; a thickness commit changes two walls and leaves the locked one unchanged; the Locked checkbox is indeterminate (AccessKit toggled state Mixed) and clicking it locks all three in one undo step.
- Unit tests in ui/fields.rs: field-key and option intersections for (wall, slab), (wall, wall) and (wall, Dummy, feature test-kinds) selections.
- Satisfies UI-002 and EDT-017 completely.
notes: SRS: UI-002 EDT-017

title: Persist views, view folders and layer combinations in IFCX
description:
WHY: VIEW-004 (M) and LAY-003 (S) need saved views and layer combinations to survive save and reopen; PRJ-007 and SET-002 (M) list views among the project settings stored in the file; IFX-060 puts views in the archicraft:: namespace; LAY-005 and VIEW-047 (via IFX-068) require that visibility state never changes the standard IFCX content. Today only id, name and projection of 3D views are written (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:183-187, reader.rs:391-427 and :842-848).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: the 'views' record gains kind, storey, projection, saved, folder, camera, scale, layers ({combination} or {states}), plan ({cut, bottom, top, showOverhead, underlay}), restrictions, style and sun, all optional except id, name and kind; new 'viewFolders' and 'layerCombinations' arrays in archicraft::project. writer.rs project_attribute and reader.rs read_project_data: old {id, name, projection} records read as plain 3D viewpoints; dangling references (storey, folder, layer, combination, hidden element) become warning Problems with the value dropped and the view kept (PRJ-008). samples.rs gains a saved plan view with a cut override in a folder, a saved 3D view with camera and style, and a layer combination; goldens are re-blessed and reviewed. Out of scope: app behaviour (09 onward).
design: Keep the existing key order (id, name, projection) for plain 3D viewpoints and append kind and saved, so golden diffs stay small and reviewable; write optional sections only when Some. Same FORMAT_VERSION as 02 if no release happened in between; otherwise bump again with a migration entry. Enumerations derive from the model ALL arrays; ids are UUID strings; parameters at full precision (float_roundtrip). Pitfalls: hidden element lists can be long, write them as plain arrays (no nesting) to respect the D.9 depth limit; the reader resolves folders after reading all folders (parent may come later in the array).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs views_and_layer_combinations_round_trip: Project equality including every optional section with non-trivial values (restrictions, style, sun, underlay), which locks the schema for 3d-view-restrictions and 3d-display-styles.
- per_view_cut_plane_override_round_trips: a saved plan view's PlanRange (cut, bottom, top) and show_overhead survive write and read bit-identically.
- old_view_records_read_as_plain_viewpoints: the frozen previous-version fixtures (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/format-v1/walls-and-slab.ifcx of element-kind-framework-12 and the format-v<N> copy of task 02) read into plain 3D viewpoints with no Problem besides the migration info.
- dangling_view_references_are_reported: a hand-edited file with a missing layer in a combination and a missing storey in a plan view loads with one Problem each and keeps both records.
- visibility_state_never_changes_standard_content: two projects differing only in views, combinations and layer visibility produce identical files once archicraft:: attributes are removed (byte comparison of the stripped JSON; IFX-068, LAY-005).
- The offline validator accepts the declarations (IFX-061) and conformance/run.sh is green on the re-blessed goldens.
- Satisfies VIEW-004 and LAY-003 persistence and the 'views' clause of PRJ-007/SET-002.
notes: SRS: VIEW-004 LAY-003 PRJ-007 SET-002.

title: Edit display range, plan display, remote style and view range in UI
description:
WHY: ELM-008, ELM-009 and ELM-018 settings must be editable on elements and tool defaults through the same panel and dialog (ELM-001, UI-003); VIEW-011 (M) and ELM-008 make the remote-storey style project-wide and configurable; VIEW-010 (M) and VIEW-012 (S) require the cut height and the bottom and top limits to be adjustable per plan view. Gap: the settings dialog's 'Plan display' section is a placeholder (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:715-718), and the Storeys dialog only edits the cut plane (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:151-160). Exists and kept (VIEW-012 partial): the Storeys dialog's per-storey cut-plane field (dialogs.rs:151-160, SetStoreyCutPlane) and the unit-aware widgets::length/choice (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/widgets.rs).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs 'Plan display' section: 'Show on storeys' combo listing only the descriptor's modes; for Custom, up/down values (0..=99) and 'Outline' and 'Cover fill' checkboxes; 'Plan display' combo from the descriptor's options; mixed markers for multi-selection with the intersection of allowed modes; applied through UpdateElements or the tool defaults path. crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs: Project settings dialog section 'Remote storeys' (above and below: pattern, colour, cut fill) through SetSettings; Storeys dialog: view range bottom and top (storeys + offset) next to the cut plane through SetStoreyViewRange. crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs plan status bar: 'View range...' popover for the active plan pane (cut height, bottom, top as storey-relative lengths, absolute elevation shown weak; Reset; 'Apply to storey' issuing one SetStoreyViewRange) and Action::ViewRange in the View menu. If properties-and-dialogs has landed its FieldSpec framework, register these fields there instead of hand-written rows. Out of scope: persisting pane overrides (saved views, 09).
design: Descriptor-driven option lists mean columns, beams, roofs and stairs get correct menus without touching this code. Use ui/widgets.rs length/choice for unit-aware values and the existing draft-and-OK pattern of the project dialog so one OK is one command for the remote style. The popover edits session state only; persistence goes through the storey (Apply to storey) or a saved view. Pitfalls: multi-selection across kinds must offer only modes allowed by every selected kind; popovers must not take focus from typed point input (INP-003); the project settings dialog already issues several commands on OK (technical debt) - add the remote style to the SetSettings payload instead of a new command.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: selecting a wall shows 'Show on storeys' with the six wall modes and no 'Custom'; selecting a slab offers 'Custom' and then shows the up/down and outline/cover controls; choosing 'Cut only' on a wall sets Element.plan_display and the wall's projected lines disappear from the plan.
- kittest: changing 'Remote storeys > Below > Pattern' to Dotted in the Project settings dialog updates ProjectSettings.remote_storey_style in one undo step.
- kittest: the View range popover sets a 2.10 m cut override, a bottom limit of -1.0 m and a top limit at storey +2 on the active plan pane (PlanViewState.options) without a model change (revision unchanged) and the regenerated drawing follows; 'Reset' returns to the storey's values; 'Apply to storey' writes cut plane and limits in one undo step.
- Invalid input (top below the cut plane) is rejected with its explanation shown and leaves both pane state and model unchanged (NFR-REL-005).
- The tool defaults path (nothing selected) edits DefaultsSlot.display_range/plan_display, and a newly drawn wall carries them.
- Satisfies the editing clauses of ELM-008, ELM-009 and ELM-018, the configurable style of VIEW-011 and per-view adjustment of VIEW-010/VIEW-012 (persisted per view by 09).
notes: SRS: ELM-008 ELM-009 ELM-018 VIEW-010 VIEW-011 VIEW-012.

title: Show and enter elevations relative to a chosen reference level
description:
WHY: STR-007 (S) requires that elevations can be entered and displayed relative to project zero, sea level or a user level, and STR-011 (M) that every elevation readout uses the one vertical datum. After task 03 the model can convert, but every elevation in the UI is still a raw project-zero length: the Storeys dialog elevation column (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:129-139, footer 'Elevations are relative to project zero' at 193-199), the project browser storey labels (ui/browser.rs:44-46) and widgets::length (ui/widgets.rs:62-77) know no datum, and the altitude is reachable only from the Project settings dialog (dialogs.rs:553-564). The epic acceptance fixes the example: a datum 'sea level +412.000' shows a storey at +3.000 as +415.000, and typing +415.000 stores 3.000.

WHAT: ui/widgets.rs: `LengthFormat { units, nf, datum: Option<Datum { level_elevation, level_name }> }` passed to widgets::length (existing call sites use LengthFormat::plain), with the pure helpers length_text(value, &fmt) and parse_length_text(text, &fmt) that widgets::length uses and that unit tests exercise without egui; in elevation mode the field shows format_elevation, parses with parse_elevation and names the level in its hover text; a helper elevation_format(&Workspace) builds the format from settings.elevation_reference. Elevation fields switched to datum mode: the Storeys dialog elevation column (header 'Elevation (<level>)', footer naming the level), the browser storey labels and the level rows below. New 'Reference levels' dialog (ui/dialogs.rs, Action::ReferenceLevels in the Project menu): rows Project zero (0, read-only), Sea level (its value is the datum; editing it issues SetLocation, the same value the Project settings dialog edits, so it is never entered twice) and the user levels (name, elevation, delete; 'Add level'), plus a 'Show elevations relative to' combo issuing SetReferenceLevels; the status bar shows the active reference ('Elevations: Sea level') and opens the dialog on click. Out of scope: element elevation readouts (task 08), storey shift defaults (task 10), elevation fields of later kinds (they pass a LengthFormat with a datum), a per-field reference override.
design: Approach: one formatting path. widgets::length already owns parse and format through committed_text (widgets.rs:17-77); an optional datum there means later epics (spot elevations, terrain, roof ridge and eaves, the measure tool) get datum support by passing the field's LengthFormat, and the epic's 'unit tests on widgets::length' run on the pure helpers. Conversion happens only inside the widget: values passed in and out are always project-zero metres. Dialog: a striped Grid like the Storeys dialog; the Sea level row shows the datum as the elevation of project zero above sea level ('+412.000') and writes Location.altitude through Command::SetLocation (command.rs:288-302); user rows issue SetReferenceLevels with the edited list. The Project settings row 'Altitude of project zero' stays but is labelled as the datum and shares the formatter. Pitfalls: the browser label (browser.rs:46) and the storey dialog footer must not hard-code 'project zero'; plan-views-browser-10 rewrites browser.rs, so if it has landed put the label helper into its tree rows; every existing caller of widgets::length must switch to LengthFormat in the same change (compile-time checked); the Project settings dialog keeps a draft and executes SetLocation(draft.location) on OK (dialogs.rs:608-616), so an altitude changed meanwhile through the Sea level row would be restored from the stale draft - issue SetLocation only when the draft's location differs from the value it was opened with. Pointers: widgets.rs:17-77, dialogs.rs:87-202 and 480-626, browser.rs:24-60, shell.rs status_bar, actions.rs (Action enum, ALL, label), app.rs Action handling (around 396-451).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/widgets.rs on the widgets::length helpers: with the datum Sea level and altitude 412.000, length_text(3.0) is "+415.000" and parse_length_text("+415.000") returns Ok(3.0) (|difference| < 1e-9); parse_length_text("415") returns Ok(3.0); plain mode is unchanged ("3.000", no sign); a user level 'Finished floor' at 0.150 shows +2.850; decimal-comma and feet-inches cases; parse errors keep the existing messages.
- kittest: with altitude 412.000 and reference Sea level, the Storeys dialog shows '+415.000' for '01 First floor' and '+412.000' for '00 Ground floor'; typing '+415.500' into the first floor's elevation and pressing Enter leaves storey.elevation == 3.5 (stored relative to project zero) as one undo step.
- kittest: editing the Sea level row in the Reference levels dialog changes Location.altitude, and the Project settings dialog then shows the same altitude without a second entry; adding 'Parapet' at +9.000, renaming and deleting it are each undoable; choosing 'Parapet' as reference changes the browser labels; deleting it falls back to Project zero.
- kittest: with the Project settings dialog open, editing the Sea level row in the Reference levels dialog and then pressing OK in Project settings keeps the new altitude (a stale draft never overwrites the datum).
- Round-trip test (app or model level): switching the reference through all three kinds of level never changes a stored storey elevation or element parameter (projects equal apart from settings).
- The existing Storeys dialog behaviour (rename, cut plane, insert, delete) still works; cargo test for archicraft-app green.
- Satisfies STR-007 for storey elevations and all readouts that exist, and the readout clause of STR-011.
notes:
SRS: STR-007 STR-011
Depends on task 03 (levels, format_elevation, parse_elevation, SetReferenceLevels).

title: Persistent guide lines per plan view
description:
WHY: Persistent guide lines (infinite lines, segments, circles and arcs) shall be placeable in plan and 3D views; they are stored per view, snappable including their division points, excluded from export and from the model, creatable by dragging from the view border onto an edge (which aligns them to it), movable with a numeric offset (also as a copy), deletable individually, by sweep or all at once, and hideable globally (INP-012). Guide input goes through the point-input service like every other point (INP-001), and references shall be excludable from producing snap targets (INP-017): hidden guides snap nowhere. Nothing of this exists today.

WHAT: Add input/guide_set.rs: GuideSet { guides: Vec<PersistentGuide { id: u64, shape: GuideShape }> } in PlanViewState (plan.rs:20-32), one set per plan view (today one plan view per storey: Pane::Plan(StoreyId) and Workspace.plan_views, workspace.rs:56; keyed by the view id once plan-views-browser adds saved views), exposed as a SnapSource with TargetOwner::Guide so guides join the index at Guide and GuideIntersection level and offer division points through divide() of task 04. Creation: (a) a drag starting in a 12-point border strip of the plan view creates a horizontal (top/bottom) or vertical (left/right) infinite line that follows the cursor and, when released within the snap radius of an indexed edge, aligns to that edge; (b) a Guide tool in the palette with modes Line, Segment, Circle and Arc as an InputConsumer, so typed values, locks and snapping apply. Editing with the Guide tool: hover highlights a guide; an 'Offset…' popup takes a typed distance and an 'as copy' option; Delete removes the hovered guide; a drag across guides deletes every crossed guide (sweep); actions 'Delete all guide lines' (in the active view) and 'Show guide lines' in the View menu; the show flag is one session-level Workspace.guides_visible that hides the guides and their snap targets in every view at once (global hide), plan views now and 3D panes later. Guides are app state only: never in Project and never written by archicraft-ifcx. Out of scope: 3D guides (3d-input-navigation reuses GuideSet per 3D pane) and keeping guides across sessions.
design: PersistentGuide ids are u64 counters per view. The global show flag lives in Workspace, not in GuideSet, so the per-pane GuideSets of 3d-input-navigation obey it without extra wiring. The border strip is a Sense::drag region inside the plan rect's margin, drawn as a faint ruler; it must not steal middle-button pans or the Select tool's area selection (plan.rs:536-563): react only when the drag starts inside the strip. Infinite lines contribute a clipped extent (view bounds ± 1 km) to the rstar tree; circles and arcs go to the circle list for centre and tangent snaps. Guide editing reuses GuideShape::project/intersect from task 08. The Offset popup is an egui popup anchored at the guide using widgets::length (ui/widgets.rs). Guide tool registration follows the 'Add a drawing tool' extension point (actions.rs action with a free key, shell.rs toolbox, properties.rs tool_modes).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: a border drag released near the south wall face of two_storey_shell yields a line coincident with that edge (distance below 1e-9 at both ends); guide snapping yields Guide and GuideIntersection candidates at their precedence; a guide segment offers division points (Half and Equal(4)); a circle guide offers centre and tangent points; offset +0.5 moves a guide, offset as copy adds a second one; delete one, sweep (a stroke crossing three guides removes those three) and delete all work; with 'Show guide lines' off no guide is drawn or snappable in any plan view and switching it on restores them all; guides added in the ground-floor plan view are absent from the upper-floor plan view (stored per view); Shift holds the cursor on the nearest persistent guide (INP-006); the project and its revision are untouched by every operation.
- Round-trip test: saving a document whose plan views carry guides gives a file byte-identical to saving it without guides.
- kittest: the Guide tool button exists; the View menu has 'Show guide lines' and 'Delete all guide lines'; typing 0.5 into the Offset popup and pressing Enter moves the hovered guide.
- Satisfies INP-012 for plan views (3D in 3d-input-navigation), the guide clause of INP-001 and the reference clause of INP-017.
notes:
SRS: INP-012 INP-001 INP-017
Open question: whether guides should survive closing the project (saved views of plan-views-browser or a sidecar file); the SRS excludes them from export and from the model, so they never enter the .ifcx.

title: Add the skin-separator pen role to the default attributes and IFCX
description:
WHY: DSP-012 (S): separator lines between the skins of a layered element shall be drawn with their own pen. DSP-001 (M) makes every 2D graphic property a reference to a project-level attribute, so the separator pen is a project pen that the user edits once for all elements. What exists after plan-attributes: PenRole in crates/archicraft-model/src/attributes.rs holds exactly the 14 DSP-005 roles (plan-attributes-01), template::default_attributes() ships one pen per role (plan-attributes-02) and the IFCX schema derives the role enumeration from PenRole::ALL. Missing: a role and a default pen for skin separators; today no pens exist at all (gap analysis DSP-012: no pens, no per-view options).

WHAT: PenRole::SkinSeparator (code, label 'Skin separator line', grouped with the cut-line roles, not screen-only) in attributes.rs; one template pen with that role in crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs (0.13 mm, the structural cut pen's colour) plus entries in the MONO and DARK pen tables where they override cut-line pens; DeleteAttribute (plan-attributes-05) refuses to delete the last SkinSeparator pen unless a replacement is given; IFCX: the role enumeration in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs grows, so FORMAT_VERSION is bumped with a Migration in alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework) that adds the template separator pen to older files, and the reader repairs a same-version file without it by adding the template pen with a warning. Out of scope: resolving and drawing separators (plan-renderer-02, -04, -08), separator pens per layer structure or per skin (follow-up bead), and the Pens dialog (plan-attributes-08 lists roles from PenRole::ALL and needs no change).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md and the plan-attributes-02 pattern: reader fallbacks and the migration both call template::default_attributes(), so the separator pen has one source of truth. If no release has been cut since the FORMAT_VERSION bump of plan-attributes-02, extend that migration step instead of adding a new version (the rule plan-attributes-02 states). Role pens that the plan resolves by role count as in use for the in-use protection of plan-attributes-05; add the guard in the DeleteAttribute plan step, not only in the dialog, so scripted commands cannot remove the last one (NFR-REL-005). Pitfall: keep the pens array order stable (new pen appended after the existing role pens) so the golden diff stays readable.
acceptance_criteria:
- attributes.rs unit tests: PenRole::ALL holds the 14 DSP-005 roles plus SkinSeparator (the plan-attributes-01 test is updated to 15 and says why); SkinSeparator is not screen-only and round-trips through code()/from_code().
- template.rs test: default_metric_project() contains exactly one pen with role SkinSeparator, weight 0.13 mm, lighter than both cut-line pens; every_project_gets_new_identities covers it.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: DeleteAttribute of the only SkinSeparator pen without a replacement is rejected with CommandError::Invalid naming the role; with a replacement it succeeds and undo restores it.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: an edited separator pen (name, colour, weight) survives save and load; a reader test with the separator pen removed from a current-version file loads with the template pen added and one warning.
- Migration test: the frozen previous-format fixture under crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/ loads with one Info migration row, the separator pen present and no warnings.
- Golden files are re-blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 and a reviewed diff (only the pens array and the role enumeration change); written_files_validate_without_problems, golden_files_are_reproduced, container_matches_the_ifcx_json_schema and conformance/run.sh are green.
- Satisfies the 'own pen' data clause of DSP-012: separators have a project-level pen of their own, referenced by role (DSP-001).
notes: SRS: DSP-012. DSP-005 organises pens by roles and lists a minimum set; one extra role does not conflict with it. Proposed default 0.13 mm (the lightest non-hairline DSP-005 weight) so the skins read as one element. Open question: a per-structure or per-skin separator pen (Archicad style) is not required by DSP-012; plan-renderer-done files a follow-up bead.

title: Sweep cross-sections along an axis with planar end cuts
description:
WHY: Columns (COL-001) and beams (BEA-001) are prisms of a cross-section along an axis; COL-003 (M) gives columns horizontal or custom-angle top and bottom cuts and BEA-002 (M) gives each beam end a vertical, horizontal or custom-angle cut. technology-choices.md generates columns and beams by extruding 2D outlines and brings Manifold only for general Booleans (solid-kernel-ops, increment 2), so planar end cuts must not need a Boolean kernel. The existing extrude() (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18) only extrudes vertically between two heights: no inclined axis, roll or angled ends. Every body must stay a closed, consistently oriented 2-manifold mesh without degenerate triangles (IFX-032), with per-face vertices except across smooth edges (IFX-038) and at most 65,535 points (MAX_MESH_POINTS).

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-geometry/src/sweep.rs: `MemberFrame { origin: DVec3, axis: DVec3, u: DVec3, v: DVec3 }` (orthonormal, right-handed; section x along u, y along v), `CutPlane { point: DVec3, normal: DVec3 }`, `sweep(section: &Section, frame: &MemberFrame, start: &CutPlane, end: &CutPlane) -> Result<Vec<SweptRegion>, GeometryError>` returning one closed TriMesh per section region with its material and role. For each section vertex p the lateral line origin + u*p.x + v*p.y + axis*s meets each cut plane at s = n.(Q - P0) / n.axis; the end faces are the section polygon mapped onto each plane (an affine image), triangulated once per region with triangulate.rs and reused for both caps with reversed winding at the start; lateral faces are planar trapezoids built per loop as strips that break at hard vertices and share vertices at smooth ones. Reject a plane within 1 degree of parallel to the axis and any vertex whose length between the planes falls below MIN_HEIGHT ('end cuts cross') with GeometryError::InvalidExtent. Helpers: frame_for_column(position, rotation) (axis +Z) and frame_for_beam(start, end, roll) (v = world Z made perpendicular to the axis, u = axis x v, then rolled about the axis). Out of scope: anchors, offsets and cut-plane construction from element parameters (06, 07), segmented and tapered members (members-profiles-adv), compound cut angles of BEA-003 (the plane API already accepts any normal).
design: This is the 'own convex plane clipper' of the epic design notes specialised to prisms: every lateral edge of a straight prism is parallel to the axis, so clipping the infinite prism by a half-space reduces to one plane-line intersection per section vertex, and the cap is exactly the affine image of the section (validity and triangulation preserved). No triangle clipping, no Booleans, exact volumes. Lateral quads have two parallel sides and are therefore planar; split each into two triangles along the shorter diagonal. Orientation follows the loop orientation from task 03 (outer CCW gives outward normals, holes CW give normals into the hole); assert positive signed_volume in tests. Keep output deterministic: regions in section order, outer loop before holes, strips starting at the first hard vertex. Pitfalls: triangulate() needs CCW outer and CW holes (triangulate.rs); check_closed merges points at the framework tolerance, so caps must not share vertices with lateral faces; frame_for_beam must reject a vertical axis (no defined up direction), which beam validation in task 07 prevents.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in sweep.rs: a 0.30 x 0.30 x 3.00 vertical prism with square cuts passes TriMesh::check_closed, has volume 0.27 m3 (1e-9) and the expected bounds; IPE 200 and CHS 168.3 x 8 swept 5 m horizontally are closed with volume = area x length (1e-9 relative); the RHS hole yields a closed mesh with an inner lateral surface.
- Angled cuts (start tilted 30 degrees about u, end 15 degrees about -u): closed, positive signed volume equal to area x centroid-line length between the planes (exact for planar cuts, 1e-9 relative), no degenerate triangles.
- Inclined axis (30 degree pitch) with plumb cuts: both end faces have horizontal normals (|z| < 1e-12) and the volume equals area x plan length / cos 30 degrees.
- Roll 90 degrees swaps the extents along the frame's u and v; a 360-segment circle stays under MAX_MESH_POINTS.
- IFX-038: a circular prism shares vertices between adjacent lateral quads (2n lateral points) while both caps have their own vertices; a rectangular prism shares no vertex between faces.
- Crossing cut planes and a plane parallel to the axis return GeometryError::InvalidExtent with a message; nothing panics.
- Supplies the geometry of COL-001/COL-003 and BEA-001/BEA-002 bodies without a Boolean kernel.
notes:
SRS: COL-001 COL-003 BEA-001 BEA-002
No Appendix D values; MAX_MESH_POINTS = 65,535 (IFX-038).

title: Verify exit criterion: GPU plan renderer with drawing scale, line weights, hatches, skin separators and golden images
description:
WHY: the epic is finished only when its exit criterion holds as a whole on all three platforms: the drawing scale of VIEW-013, the pen weights of DSP-004 and DSP-019, the anti-aliased strokes of DSP-014, the moire-free hatches with the 3-pixel tone of DSP-013, the seamless regions and separator pen of DSP-012, the layered display option of DSP-017 and the golden images of DSP-018.

WHAT: run the full verification on the merged work of plan-renderer-01 to -13, fix or file anything that fails, update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (DSP-004, DSP-012, DSP-013, DSP-014, DSP-017, DSP-018, DSP-019, VIEW-013) with evidence paths, record the remaining gaps as beads and close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new features; anything not in the exit criterion is filed as a follow-up bead.
design: Checklist: (1) CI green on ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest and macos-latest including plan_golden and plan_pixels; check the job logs show lavapipe and WARP as the adapters. (2) Run the app locally at 100 % and 200 % display scaling on the two_storey_shell and F2 fixtures: change the drawing scale, zoom through the full range, toggle separators, layered display and thin lines, and confirm overlays (snap markers, rubber bands, selection) still draw on top. (3) Confirm the painter fallback still works without a render state (label-based kittest tests). (4) Run the plan_perf test and confirm the recorded numbers. (5) Update the DSP and VIEW rows of docs/implementation-status.md and the technical-debt entries that this epic removes (hard-coded scale label, solid-tone fills, lyon not a dependency).
acceptance_criteria:
- egui_kittest wgpu snapshot tests of fixture plans pass on all three CI platforms within the per-pixel tolerance documented in docs/testing.md, rendered on a software adapter (lavapipe on Linux, WARP on Windows) in CI.
- Cut lines are heavier than projected lines at every zoom and no line is thinner than one device pixel (pixel assertions).
- Hatch spacing below 3 px renders as a tone.
- The hard-coded 'Scale 1:100' label has become a per-view drawing scale in ViewState that zooming never changes (VIEW-013; the ViewDefinition of plan-views-browser persists it).
- The cores of joined same-material walls draw without a seam while the F2 wall shows six skin regions with separator lines in the separator pen that a per-view switch hides.

- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on the golden IFCX files (re-blessed for the separator pen in plan-renderer-12).
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (DSP-004, DSP-012, DSP-013, DSP-014, DSP-017, DSP-018, DSP-019, VIEW-013) with evidence and remaining gaps.
- The epic plan-renderer is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for every deferred item (separator pen per structure, option persistence handoff to plan-views-browser, incremental tessellation if measured necessary, the annotation-size clause of VIEW-013 for sections-elevations-dims, and the product-owner confirmation of the uniform-thin interpretation of DSP-004/DSP-019).
notes: SRS: DSP-004 DSP-012 DSP-013 DSP-014 DSP-017 DSP-018 DSP-019 VIEW-013

title: Model storey display ranges, plan display options and remote style
description:
WHY: ELM-008 (M): every element shall have a storey display range that sets the plan views it is drawn in: home storey only; all storeys it intersects (walls, columns, beams, roofs, stairs, curtain walls); home storey plus one up, one down, or both; all storeys. The element is editable wherever it is displayed, and its outline on other storeys is drawn in a project-wide, configurable style (default dashed, separate settings above and below). ELM-009 (S): slabs, roofs and terrain additionally get a custom range of N storeys up and M down, with outline and cover fill set independently. ELM-018 (M): each kind offers plan display options for its cut, projected and overhead parts, at least projected, projected with overhead and cut only where meaningful. VIEW-011 (M) needs the project-wide remote-storey style; VIEW-010 (M) and VIEW-012 (S) need bottom and top limits of the view range that are adjustable per view (defaults: storey elevation and next storey, Appendix D.1) and projected elements with 'cover fill where defined'. Gap rows: Element has no display range (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:275-287), no plan display option exists, there is no remote style, Material has a cut fill only, and only the cut plane is overridable per storey (crates/archicraft-model/src/storey.rs:22, :307).

WHAT: archicraft-model only. (1) New module crates/archicraft-model/src/display.rs (re-exported in lib.rs): DisplayRange {HomeOnly, Intersecting, HomeAndAbove, HomeAndBelow, HomeAboveAndBelow, All, Custom {up, down, outline, cover_fill}} with a fieldless DisplayRangeMode discriminant, code()/from_code(), and the pure admission rule admits(home_index, storey_index, intersects) -> bool; RemoteSide {Above, Below}; PlanDisplay {ProjectedWithOverhead, Projected, CutOnly} with keeps(PlanClass); RemoteStoreyStyle {above, below: RemoteLine {pattern: LinePattern {Solid, Dashed, Dotted}, color: Option<Rgb>, cut_fill: bool}}. (2) Element envelope gains display_range and plan_display; the framework's DefaultsSlot gains the same two fields, copied by Project::prototype/new_wall/new_slab. (3) KindDescriptor gains display_ranges: &'static [DisplayRangeMode], default_display_range, plan_displays: &'static [PlanDisplay], default_plan_display; wall: every mode except Custom, default Intersecting; slab: every mode except Intersecting, default HomeOnly; both offer all three plan displays with default ProjectedWithOverhead; the test-kinds Dummy offers only Projected; later kinds add Intersecting (columns, beams, roofs, stairs, curtain walls: the ELM-008 parenthesis) and Custom (roofs, terrain: ELM-009) in their own descriptors. (4) validate.rs checks element and default values against the descriptor and Custom up/down <= 99. (5) Storey gains view_range: Option<RangeLimits {bottom, top: RangeLimit {storeys: i32, offset: f64}}> (relative to the plan's storey; defaults {0, 0.0} and {1, 0.0}); PlanRange {cut: Option<f64>, limits: Option<RangeLimits>} as the override type reused by saved views; Project::view_range(storey, &PlanRange) -> Option<AbsoluteViewRange {cut, bottom, top}>; Command::SetStoreyViewRange {storey, cut_plane, range} sets both in one undoable edit (SetStoreyCutPlane stays). (6) ProjectSettings.remote_storey_style; Material.cover_fill: Option<CutFill> (None in template.rs) unless plan-attributes has already introduced a cover-fill reference. Out of scope: plan generation (03, 04), IFCX keys (02), UI (06), saved-view overrides (07).
design: Approach: keep everything pure data plus pure functions so geometry, IFCX and app consume one definition. The admission rule takes indices into StoreyList (storey.rs index_of) and a precomputed 'intersects' flag, because intersection depends on the per-view range that only the plan generator knows. RangeLimit is storey-relative so the range follows storey insertion and elevation edits (like TopLink::Relative); a limit beyond the top storey resolves through the top storey's nominal height, mirroring StoreyList::relative_elevation (storey.rs:108). SetStoreyViewRange plans a SetStoreys snapshot edit exactly like SetStoreyCutPlane (command.rs:68/208, storey.rs:307). Defaults ProjectedWithOverhead and wall Intersecting keep today's plan output (walls topped at home+1 touch but do not intersect the storey above). Pitfalls: every Element literal in tests, samples.rs and reader.rs must set the new fields (use the descriptor defaults helper); Command and Project are serde-serialised for the journal and autosave, so derive Serialize/Deserialize on all new types; keep the colour type Rgb from material.rs; do not let the model depend on geometry (PlanClass is a small enum defined in display.rs).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in display.rs: admits() truth table for every DisplayRange mode x relative storey offsets -2..+2 x intersects true/false (HomeOnly only at offset 0; Intersecting only when intersects; HomeAndAbove at 0/+1; Custom{2,1} at -1..+2; All everywhere); RemoteSide derived from storey indices.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: UpdateElements changing display_range and plan_display executes, undoes and redoes to the identical project; Intersecting on a slab, Custom on a wall and CutOnly on the Dummy kind (feature test-kinds) are rejected with CommandError::Invalid and leave the project unchanged; SetStoreyViewRange undo/redo restores cut plane and limits; a range with top <= cut or bottom >= cut is rejected with an explanation (NFR-REL-005).
- Project::view_range with an empty PlanRange equals today's ViewRange::for_storey for every storey of samples::two_storey_shell (cut 1.10 m above the storey, bottom at the storey elevation, top at the next storey, top storey via its nominal height; Appendix D.1).
- Template test: wall defaults Intersecting + ProjectedWithOverhead, slab defaults HomeOnly + ProjectedWithOverhead, remote style Dashed above and below without cut fill, no material has a cover fill.
- Until 02 lands, the IFCX reader fills descriptor defaults, None and Default for the new fields, so crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs Project equality and the golden files stay unchanged.
- cargo test, clippy and fmt green on the workspace. Data side of ELM-008, ELM-009, ELM-018, VIEW-011 and the per-view range of VIEW-010/VIEW-012 is in place.
notes: SRS: ELM-008 ELM-009 ELM-018 VIEW-010 VIEW-011 VIEW-012. Appendix D.1: cut plane 1.10 m, bottom limit at the storey elevation, top limit at the next storey. Open question: ELM-009 'outline and cover fill set independently' is read as two toggles for remote storeys; if it means separate N/M per part, Custom gains two more counts (additive). Later kinds: profiles-columns-beams, roofs, stair-solver-tool/stair-body-plan, curtain-walls and terrain-and-site register their display ranges through the descriptor fields added here. Module name: 3d-display-styles-01 (increment 3) plans a new crates/archicraft-model/src/display.rs for DisplayStyle; it extends this module instead of creating it, and every type here is re-exported from lib.rs so consumers write archicraft_model::DisplayRange (stair-body-plan-09 already points at display.rs).

title: Add incremental search to long lists and option combos
description:
WHY: UI-014 (S): every list that can exceed one screen (project browser, materials, layer structures, profiles, presets, layers, saved views, components) has an incremental search field. Layers (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:284-299) and Materials (dialogs.rs:383-395) have ad-hoc filters, but the project browser (ui/browser.rs:24-116) and the Storeys dialog (dialogs.rs:87-202) have none, and the option combos of the properties panel (materials, layers, storeys, IFC classes; ui/widgets.rs:101-124) grow with the project (gap row UI-014). Layer structures, profiles, presets, saved views and components arrive with later epics and must reuse one widget instead of inventing their own.

WHAT: New ui/search.rs: `SearchField` (single-line field with a clear button and the accessible label 'Search'; Cmd/Ctrl+F focuses it while its window has focus, Esc clears, Enter picks the first match) and `matches(query, &[&str])` (case- and diacritic-insensitive; every whitespace-separated token must occur in one of the given strings, for example name or code). A list shows the field when it has more than 12 entries or its content would exceed the visible height. Applied to the project browser (storeys and 3D views; the tree of plan-views-browser-10 if it has landed), the Storeys dialog, the Reference levels dialog, the Layers and Materials dialogs (replacing their ad-hoc filters) and widgets::choice (search field at the top of the popup above the threshold, so every FieldSpec Choice gets it). Out of scope: lists that do not exist yet - layer structures (layer-structures), profiles (profiles-columns-beams), presets (templates-presets), saved views (plan-views-browser), components (components-dw-catalogue) - which adopt SearchField in their epics.
design: Approach: one widget and one matcher; the threshold combines an item-count rule and a height rule so short lists stay uncluttered. The query lives in egui temp memory per list id (not persisted). Diacritic folding with a small built-in table for Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A letters, so no new dependency enters deny.toml. Inside a ComboBox popup, show_ui can host the TextEdit; request focus when the popup opens. Cmd/Ctrl+F is not in Appendix D.8; bind it window-locally (not as a global Action) and keep the shortcuts_are_unique test green. Pitfalls: plan-views-browser-10 rewrites browser.rs - whichever task lands second integrates SearchField into the tree; task 11 later wraps the Materials list in a resizable splitter panel, so keep the search field inside the list column. Pointers: dialogs.rs:278-300 and 376-400, browser.rs:24-116, widgets.rs:101-124, actions.rs works_while_typing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in ui/search.rs: 'conc' matches 'Reinforced concrete'; 'beton' matches 'Béton armé'; 'ext wall' matches 'Exterior walls' but 'ext slab' does not; the empty query matches everything; matching uses the code as well as the name.
- kittest: in a project with 40 materials the Material combo of a selected wall shows a 'Search' field; typing 'conc' leaves only materials containing 'conc' and Enter picks the first one (UpdateElements); with 5 materials no search field is shown.
- kittest: the project browser of a project with 15 storeys shows 'Search'; typing '03' narrows the list to the storey whose name contains '03'; Esc restores the full list.
- kittest: the Layers and Materials dialogs still filter by name and code through SearchField, and the Storeys and Reference levels dialogs filter rows above the threshold.
- Single-key tool shortcuts do not fire while a search field has focus (UI-008 rule; existing works_while_typing behaviour asserted for the new field).
- Satisfies UI-014 for every listed list that exists in the product; the remaining lists are recorded in docs/implementation-status.md as owned by their epics.
notes:
SRS: UI-014
Owners of the lists that do not exist yet: plan-views-browser-10 (saved views), profiles-columns-beams-14 (profiles), templates-presets-10/19 (presets), library-dw-exchange-08 (components catalogue) and 3d-display-styles-09 already name UI-014 or a search field; layer-structures-11 (layer structure editor) and components-dw-catalogue do not, so the done task files follow-up bead notes asking them to use SearchField.

title: Add the column kind across model, geometry and IFCX
description:
WHY: COL-001 (M): a column shall have a rectangular (width x depth), circular (diameter) or profile cross-section; a base offset; a fixed height or storey-linked top; an anchor point chosen from nine cross-section points; and a rotation about its axis. COL-003 (M): the top and bottom end cuts shall be horizontal (default) or at a custom angle, editable numerically and by handle (numeric editing in task 10, handles in 13). ELM-011 allows IfcColumn or IfcMember for columns; ELM-006 makes the storey-linked top follow storey changes. IFX-035 (S): column axes are written as usd::usdgeom::basiscurves in an Axis child (the writer already writes ElementGeometry.axis generically, writer.rs:382-389). PRF-004: editing a profile updates every element that uses it. Appendix D.2: 0.30 x 0.30 m reinforced concrete, centre anchor, top linked to home storey + 1. Status: COL-001 and COL-003 missing; IFX-035 partial (walls only). The element-kind-framework registry checks at compile time that every kind has a geometry generator and an IFCX codec, so the kind lands in all three crates at once.

WHAT: Model: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/member.rs (shared with beams) with `CrossSection::{Rectangular { width, height }, Circular { diameter }, Profile(ProfileId)}` (height is the section's y-size: the column's depth in plan) and `Anchor::{TopLeft, TopCentre, TopRight, Left, Centre, Right, BottomLeft, BottomCentre, BottomRight, ProfileOrigin}` with bounds(&Project) and offset(); crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/column.rs with `Column { position, section, material, anchor, rotation, link: VerticalLink, top_cut: ColumnCut, bottom_cut: ColumnCut }` (VerticalLink { base_offset, top: TopLink } is element-kind-framework-02's shared vertical link, also used by curtain walls; TopLink::Fixed gives the fixed height, Storey and Relative the storey-linked top) and `ColumnCut::{Horizontal, Angle(f64)}` (tilt about the column's local x axis). Kind impl: DESCRIPTOR { label 'Column', code 'column', name_prefix 'C', default_class IfcColumn, ifc_classes [IfcColumn, IfcMember], has_tool true, template_defaults Some(D.2 column slot) }, transform, vertical_extent, validate (normalising: Anchor::ProfileOrigin becomes Centre for rectangular and circular sections), profiles() and replace_profile() of task 01, storey_links/rehome/relink/unlink_storey through VerticalLink as for walls; Project::new_column(storey, position, rotation); the template's D.2 slot on layer 'Structure'. Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/column.rs (a GeometryKind impl plus one registry line, element-kind-framework-07) builds the section (rectangle and circle as parametric shapes with the column material, profiles through profile_section), applies the anchor offset and frame_for_column, puts the cut planes through the anchor axis at base and top, sweeps (task 05) into parts named 'Body' (one region) or 'Region_n', and returns axis = [anchor point at the bottom cut, anchor point at the top cut]; dirty_set (element-kind-framework-10) adds every element whose Kind::profiles() contains a profile id recorded in Project.changes by task 01's edits. IFCX: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/column.rs KindCodec `archicraft::column` with one codecs! line (element-kind-framework-06) (position, section { kind, width, height, diameter, profile }, material, anchor, rotation, baseOffset, top, topCut { kind, angle }, bottomCut) plus the defaults slot, read leniently. Out of scope: the tool and properties (10), handles (13), inclination COL-004 and segments COL-005 (members-profiles-adv), joins COL-006 (cleanup-and-trims), plan display beyond generic slicing (08).
design: Column position is the anchor point; the section is translated so the anchor point is the local origin, then rotated about +Z by rotation: u = (cos r, sin r, 0), v = (-sin r, cos r, 0). Cut normals: top = Z rotated by the angle about u, bottom = the negated rotation of -Z; both planes pass through the anchor axis at base_offset and at the resolved top. Stored offsets stay exact as for walls (evaluate.rs:130-134 keeps base_offset rather than subtracting elevations). The column material is used for rectangular and circular sections and kept when a profile is chosen, so switching back keeps it; profile sections take their region materials, and material reassignment of profile regions happens at the profile (task 01). Anchors on circular sections use the bounding box (Centre is the circle centre). Part names: 'Body' when the section has one region, otherwise 'Region_<n>' in profile order, ids from sub_node_id(owner, role) (IFX-010) and named materials on every part (IFX-043). Pitfalls: the codec must write angles in radians with the angle() quantity kind; the defaults-slot schema comes from the codec (framework task 05) and the counters array needs no schema edit (framework migration 1 to 2).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: adding a column names it C-001, undo and redo restore exactly; UpdateElements of rotation, anchor and section works; validation rejects width 0, a diameter above MAX_THICKNESS, a cut angle of 60 degrees or NaN, a missing profile, a profile without the columns flag and the class IfcBeam (CommandError::Invalid with a message); IfcMember is accepted.
- Storey behaviour: raising the upper storey moves the top of a column linked to home + 1 (ELM-006/STR-006 test pattern of storey_changes_move_linked_walls); DeleteProfile with a replacement re-points a profile column and undo restores it.
- Template test (and the Appendix D defaults test if regression-and-status has landed it): the column slot is 0.30 x 0.30 m reinforced concrete, Anchor::Centre, TopLink::Relative { storeys: 1, offset: 0 }, horizontal cuts, layer 'Structure'.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs: the D.2 column on the ground floor is closed with volume 0.27 m3; a 30 degree rotation gives the analytic bounding box; Anchor::BottomLeft puts the section's bottom-left corner on the position; a 0.40 m circular column has 36 segments at the default settings and a volume equal to the inscribed-polygon area x 3 (1e-9 relative), within 0.6 % of pi * 0.2^2 * 3; TopLink::Fixed { height: 2.50 } with base offset 0.20 spans z 0.20 to 2.70 above the storey; Anchor::ProfileOrigin on a profile whose insertion origin is (0.05, 0.10) puts that profile point on the column position; a 20 degree top cut gives area x centroid length; an IPE 300 profile column yields one closed 'Body'; a two-region custom profile column yields Region_1 and Region_2 with their materials; the axis is [(x, y, 0), (x, y, 3)] in storey coordinates.
- Profile propagation (PRF-004): UpdateProfile changing an I-profile's height changes the evaluated volume of the column using it; the framework's incremental-versus-full property test, extended with AddProfile, UpdateProfile and column edits, stays bit-identical.
- IFCX: a column round-trips exactly (every field, floats bit-identical); its node carries bsi::ifc::class IfcColumn, Body or Region_n children inheriting their materials and an Axis child with two usd::usdgeom::basiscurves points and the v5 id sub_node_id(owner, 'Axis'); the file validates; an unknown profile reference loads as the D.2 rectangular section with a warning and an invalid cut angle as horizontal with a warning.
- The framework module-layout tests pass: 'column' appears only in the column modules and one registry line per crate.
- Satisfies COL-001 and COL-003 in model, geometry and file (UI in 10, handles in 13) and the column clause of IFX-035.
notes:
SRS: COL-001 COL-003 IFX-035 PRF-004
Also touches ELM-011 (column class set) and ELM-006 (storey-linked top through VerticalLink). Appendix D.2: column 0.30 x 0.30 m reinforced concrete, centre anchor, top linked to home storey + 1. Open question: the SRS gives no limit for the cut angle; 60 degrees is an assumption that keeps the plane well away from the axis.

title: Plan view range and display ranges, saved views, project browser, layers and layout persistence
description:
Make the plan generator cut and project every element intersecting a storey's view range regardless of home storey, add the per-element storey display range with the remote-storey style, per-view cut-plane and range overrides, per-kind plan display options (projected, with overhead, cut only) and the overhead class switch, so that every later kind (columns, beams, roofs, stairs) gets correct plan output for free; and add the ViewDefinition resource (camera or zoom and rotation, scale, layer states or combination, kind filters, storey range, cut planes, hidden elements, style, sun), folders, redefine and open semantics, the full project browser with context menus, layer combinations, hidden/locked-layer warnings, view rotation, the trace underlay and per-user persistence of the tile layout. The optional sections of ViewDefinition are filled by 3d-view-restrictions and 3d-display-styles.

Risks: Cross-storey evaluation cost relies on the incremental per-element cache of the framework epic. VIEW-004 is a union of many later features; the data model is defined now with optional sections to avoid repeated schema churn. Saved views referencing deleted layers or storeys re-apply tolerantly with a report.
design: archicraft-geometry plan.rs iterates a z-extent index of all elements with PlanOptions per view (range, cut height, overhead on/off) instead of elements_on(storey); archicraft-model DisplayRange on Element, the remote style in ProjectSettings, views.rs (ViewDefinition as a superset of View3d with optional sections for restrictions and styles) and LayerCombination; archicraft-app per-pane ViewState mapped to ViewDefinition, Tree<Pane> serde through egui_tiles persistence in persistence/prefs.rs, ui/browser.rs rewritten on an egui_extras tree with Behavior::tab_ui context menus; the HashMap-order tab insertion heuristic is removed.
acceptance_criteria: Geometry test in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs: a wall on storey n-1 reaching into storey n's range is cut on n and drawn remote-style (regression for the known plan.rs debt); each display-range mode produces the expected drawing on every storey (fixture); the overhead class can be switched off per view; a per-view cut-plane override round-trips; ELM-018 options change the classification per kind in tests; saving, redefining and opening a view re-applies its state to the live model (test); views and layer combinations persist in archicraft::project and round-trip; the browser lists storeys highest first, 3D views and saved views in folders, double-click opens a tab, the context menu offers rename, delete, settings and save-as-view (kittest); a rotated plan view keeps snapping and constraints aligned to the rotated axes; the trace underlay with opacity and offset toggles with one command; placing on a hidden layer warns; the egui_tiles tree is serialised in preferences and restored.
notes: SRS: VIEW-010 VIEW-011 VIEW-012 ELM-008 ELM-009 ELM-018 VIEW-003 VIEW-004 VIEW-060 VIEW-015 LAY-001 LAY-002 LAY-003 UI-004 PRJ-007 SET-002

title: Draw remote-storey elements and pick and snap them where displayed
description:
WHY: VIEW-011 (M): elements shown on storeys other than their home storey are drawn in the project-wide remote-storey style; ELM-008 (M): the outline on other storeys uses that configurable style (default dashed, separate settings above and below) and the element is editable wherever it is displayed. VIEW-010 (M): the overhead class can be switched off and projected elements show their cover fill where defined; ELM-009 (S): the custom range's outline and cover fill are visible independently. Gap rows: nothing draws other storeys' elements, snap targets come from the home storey only (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:164-187) and select-all filters by home storey (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:207-224). Exists and kept: the painter path of draw_plan with heavier cut outlines, projected lines and dashed, lighter overhead lines (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:237-320, Palette at :92) and hover and selection highlighting on PlanDrawing.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draw_plan: remote elements drawn first with RemoteStoreyStyle per side (dashed or dotted via Shape::dashed_line, style colour or a lightened palette.projected, cut fill only when RemoteLine.cut_fill), cover-fill meshes drawn under projected lines in the material's cover-fill colour; PlanViewState.options: PlanOptions passed to ws.doc.plan(storey, &options); Action::ToggleOverhead (View menu checkbox and a status-bar toggle) flips show_overhead of the active plan pane; SnapTargets::from_plan takes wall reference lines from PlanElement.reference_line instead of project.elements_on(storey); Workspace::select_all on a plan pane selects the visible elements of that pane's drawing. Editing a remote element is an ordinary UpdateElements/MoveElements, so locking rules stay as they are. If plan-renderer has landed, add Remote{Above, Below} line classes to its tessellator instead of the painter path. Out of scope: editors and the per-view range popover (06), pane-keyed state (09).
design: Draw order: (underlay, task 13) -> remote -> overhead -> projected with cover -> home cut regions -> reference lines -> highlights. Remote cut outlines use PROJECTED_WIDTH so they never outweigh home cuts (DSP-004); hover and selection highlighting work unchanged because they read PlanDrawing. The plan cache from 03 is keyed by (StoreyId, PlanOptions), so toggling overhead is a cache lookup, not a regeneration after the first time. Pitfalls: toggles must not steal keyboard focus from typed point input (INP-003); SnapTargets is rebuilt per frame today (performance debt), keep it fed from the same drawing the user sees; if point-input-snapping has landed, register remote outlines through its SnapSource (crates/archicraft-app/src/input/) instead of SnapTargets::from_plan. Pointers: plan.rs:237-320 (draw_plan, element_outline), tools.rs:156-187, workspace.rs:205-224, ui/shell.rs:87-99 (View menu checkboxes), ui/actions.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless workspace test on a two-storey fixture with an Intersecting wall spanning both storeys: on the upper plan the wall's reference-line end is a SnapKind::Node target, a click selects the wall, Delete removes it in one undo step (editable wherever displayed); the same wall on a locked layer is drawn but rejected for edits (ELM-013, LAY-001 unchanged).
- Unit test of the style mapping function (no GPU): RemoteLine {Dashed} produces dashed shapes, {Solid} plain segments, cut_fill false produces no fill mesh, Above and Below use their own settings.
- Unit test of the plan shape builder (no GPU): a projected slab whose material has a cover fill yields a filled mesh in the material's cover-fill colour drawn before its projected lines, and none without a cover fill; overhead lines stay dashed in palette.overhead (the existing lighter style); a Custom range with outline off draws the cover on remote storeys but no remote lines.
- kittest: View menu 'Show overhead' toggles the active plan pane's options (state asserted through ArchiCraftApp::workspace) and the regenerated drawing has no overhead lines; the model revision is unchanged.
- select_all on the upper storey includes the remote wall and excludes elements on hidden layers.
- The existing kittests in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs pass.
- Satisfies the drawing part of VIEW-011, ELM-008 (style and editability), the per-view overhead switch and cover-fill drawing of VIEW-010 and the visible ELM-009 toggles.
notes: SRS: VIEW-011 ELM-008 VIEW-010 ELM-009.

title: Give every kind a settings dialog with four sections and live preview
description:
WHY: UI-003 (M): every tool has a full settings dialog with collapsible sections (geometry and positioning, plan display, model and appearance) and a live preview, and the same dialog edits tool defaults and selected elements; ELM-001 (M) requires that defaults and selections share it; ELM-001 itself is done (shared gather/apply path ui/properties.rs:55-131 choosing SetToolDefaults or UpdateElements), and this task keeps that path and extends the dialog to every registered kind. The dialog exists (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:770-791 inside ui/dialogs.rs:628-638) with collapsible sections (properties.rs:713-719 and 738-742), but there is no preview, the 'Plan display' section is a placeholder label (properties.rs:715-718) and only walls and slabs have a dialog (gap row UI-003). The epic acceptance requires a test that iterates the kind registry and finds the four sections and a preview for every kind.

WHAT: ui/properties.rs settings_dialog becomes a two-pane layout: the four collapsible sections 'Geometry and positioning', 'Plan display', 'Model and appearance' and 'Classification' rendered by ui/fields.rs from FieldSpec.section (the derived values of task 08 close the first section), and a preview pane. Plan display section: the kind's PlanDisplay FieldSpecs plus a read-only 'Cut fill' row naming the material's cut fill with an 'Edit material...' button that opens the Materials dialog on that material (plan-views-browser registers its display-range and plan-display fields here). New ui/preview.rs: a scratch evaluation of the draft element (shared with the draft geometry of task 08) (for tool defaults the prototype with its descriptor's placeholder geometry, for a selection the first editable target with pending values) through archicraft-geometry, rendered offscreen with views/render3d.rs (own Viewport, GpuScene and a fixed axonometric Camera3d, released when the dialog closes) when a wgpu render state exists, and otherwise drawn as projected feature edges (TriMesh::feature_edges) with the egui painter, so it is never blank in tests or software rendering; the preview is a labelled widget ('Preview') that re-renders when the draft changes. The dialog title names the subject ('Wall tool defaults', 'Wall W-003', '3 walls'). Out of scope: presets in the dialog (ELM-002, templates-presets), the per-kind plan display options themselves (ELM-018, plan-views-browser), remembered dialog size and splitter (task 11).
design: Approach: reuse the 3D pipeline instead of a second renderer: build a one-element scratch Project (clone storeys, materials and layers; insert the draft element), evaluate it with the per-kind geometry generator of element-kind-framework-07 (evaluate_element today, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:150), call build_scene (views/render3d.rs:102) and render into a small Viewport (render3d.rs:438 ensure_viewport, 501 render) with Camera3d::apply_preset and fit (views/camera.rs:212-233).
