Dialogs::show needs frame.wgpu_render_state(): pass it from app.rs as the views get it (Behavior.render_state, app.rs:720-735 and 836-840) and release the preview viewport on close through the existing released-textures path (app.rs:69, 793-795 and 845-848). kittest builds have no wgpu render state, hence the painter fallback; the registry test therefore checks the fallback path and a PreviewState with a non-empty mesh. Wall junctions do not apply in the preview (single element). Pitfalls: never mutate ws.doc for the preview; rebuild only when (subject, draft key, pending text, project revision) changes; avoid leaking GPU textures when the dialog closes; the section CollapsingHeader ids must be stable per section, not per kind, so open states carry over (task 11 persists them). Pointers: properties.rs:684-791, dialogs.rs:628-638, render3d.rs:77-130 and 195-520, view3d.rs:195-215, camera.rs:102-262, mesh.rs:239.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest every_kind_has_a_settings_dialog (feature test-kinds): for every descriptor in KINDS an element of that kind (Project::prototype where the kind has a defaults slot, otherwise the FixtureBuilder of element-kind-framework-03 or a literal element, as for the Dummy whose template_defaults is None) is added and selected, the dialog is opened with Cmd/Ctrl+T, and 'Geometry and positioning', 'Plan display', 'Model and appearance', 'Classification' and 'Preview' are present; for every descriptor with has_tool the same check runs with its tool active and nothing selected (title '<Kind> tool defaults'); the preview state reports a non-empty mesh in both cases.
- kittest defaults_and_selection_share_the_dialog: with the wall tool active and nothing selected the dialog is titled 'Wall tool defaults' and editing Thickness issues SetToolDefaults; after selecting a wall the same dialog edits the wall through UpdateElements.
- kittest preview_follows_pending_values: typing a new thickness without Enter increments the preview generation and changes the preview bounds while project.revision stays unchanged.
- kittest: 'Edit material...' opens the Materials dialog with the wall's material selected.
- Unit tests in ui/preview.rs: the preview scene of the wall prototype has bounds matching the placeholder geometry and the default height; the painter fallback produces at least one line segment.
- Satisfies UI-003 (four collapsible sections, live preview, one dialog for defaults and selection, every registered kind) and the dialog part of ELM-001.
notes:
SRS: UI-003 ELM-001
Section names follow the epic: the three SRS sections plus Classification.

title: Persist profiles in archicraft::project with a format bump
description:
WHY: PRJ-007 (M) stores profiles in the project file; IFX-060 (M) lists profiles among the data that must be stored in archicraft:: attributes to restore the editable model; IFX-061 (M) requires every archicraft:: attribute to be declared in the file's schemas section; IFX-062 (M) versions the ArchiCraft schema so that older releases flag newer files instead of silently dropping data; IFX-011 keeps identities stable across save and open. PRF-004's resource from task 01 must survive save and open, otherwise columns and beams that reference a profile (tasks 06, 07) lose their cross-section on reopen. Today the writer's project_attribute writes the layers (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:172) and materials (:178) arrays, schema.rs project() declares them, and the reader's read_project_data reads materials leniently (reader.rs:411-455).

WHAT: schema.rs: declare an optional `profiles` array in archicraft::project: object { id, name, origin: point2, usage: object { columns, beams, walls, railings: booleans }, catalogue: optional string, shape: object { kind: enumeration (ParametricShape codes plus 'custom', options taken from the model's ALL array), dimensions: optional object of optional lengths (height, width, web, flange, thickness, diameter, rootRadius, toeRadius, outerRadius), material: optional string, regions: optional array(object { material, outer: array(point2), holes: array(array(point2)) }) } }. writer.rs: profile_record() written after the materials array, always present (empty array when there are none), parameters at full precision (float_roundtrip, NFR-ACC-002). reader.rs: read_profiles() runs each record through validate_profile (task 01): an invalid profile is skipped with an error naming it, a region or parametric material that does not exist is repaired to the first material with a warning (the pattern of reader.rs:435-455), a duplicate id keeps the first record with a warning. Bump FORMAT_VERSION by one and add a no-op step to the framework's migration table (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs, description 'adds profiles, columns and beams'), so older releases open these files with the newer-format warning and refuse silent overwrite; the column and beam codecs of tasks 06 and 07 ride on the same bump. Re-bless the golden files and review the diff. Out of scope: the kind codecs (06, 07), the catalogue (04), any UI.
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md. Profiles live inside archicraft::project, not as nodes: they are authoring data with no counterpart in the pinned ifc@v5a schema, and materials are written as nodes only because IFX-040 requires it. One `dimensions` object with optional members covers all nine parametric shapes, so the schema needs no tagged-union support; the reader checks per shape which members are required and reports missing ones. Declare `profiles` as optional so files written before the bump still validate against the current declarations after migration. Use the existing point2(), length(), boolean(), string() and enumeration() combinators (schema.rs:27-60). Pitfalls: keep member order stable for byte-identical output (IFX-007); layer-structures bumps FORMAT_VERSION for layerStructures in parallel, so whichever epic lands second rebases onto the other's number and adds its own no-op step (rule documented in alpha/mod.rs by element-kind-framework: bump and add a Migration whenever a reader-visible shape changes).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs profiles_round_trip: a project with one profile per ParametricShape variant, a custom profile with two regions of different materials and a hole, and a catalogue-designated profile saves and loads equal (ids, names, origin, usage flags, catalogue designation, dimensions and ring points bit-identical).
- written_files_validate_without_problems stays green, proving every written profile member is declared (IFX-061).
- Lenient-reading tests: a profile with a negative width is skipped with one error naming it; a region with an unknown material loads repaired with one warning; a duplicate profile id is reported and the first record kept.
- FORMAT_VERSION is bumped; migrations_are_contiguous passes; the frozen format fixtures of element-kind-framework load through the migration chain with an Info report and no warnings; newer_format_versions_are_flagged still passes.
- Golden files re-blessed with a reviewed diff limited to formatVersion and an empty profiles array; output_is_deterministic_and_plain and conformance/run.sh on the goldens are green.
- Satisfies the persistence clause of PRF-004 and the profile clause of PRJ-007/IFX-060.
notes:
SRS: PRF-004
Also touches PRJ-007, IFX-060, IFX-061 and IFX-062 (owned elsewhere, kept green). Open question: whether optional additions alone would need a bump; decided yes here because new element kinds follow in tasks 06 and 07 and older readers must flag the file (IFX-062 no-silent-overwrite clause).

title: Place, rotate and reset the user origin
description:
WHY: A user origin shall be placeable and rotatable at any point (for example a building corner) to display and enter coordinates relative to it, and resettable to the project origin; it does not change model coordinates (INP-014). Absolute coordinates are measured from the project origin, the user origin or a marked snap point (INP-004). Today the plan only draws the fixed project-origin marker (plan.rs:191-200) and no relative coordinate display exists.

WHAT: Add a session-level InputFrames { user_origin: Frame2d { origin: DVec2, rotation: f64 } } in Workspace shared by all plan views (one plan frame per view type, like the plan grid of INP-013; the 3D working plane gets its own frame through ViewSurface in 3d-input-navigation). A UserOriginTool consumer on the PointInput service with two steps: the origin point, then a direction point or a typed angle for the X axis (Enter keeps rotation 0). Actions PlaceUserOrigin and ResetUserOrigin in ui/actions.rs, the View menu (ui/shell.rs:78) and the plan context menu; they create no undo step because nothing in the model changes. The tracker's absolute fields, Origin::User entry and the locks of task 08 use the frame; the plan view-control bar (ui/shell.rs:228-242) shows the cursor X/Y relative to it; the marker is drawn with its rotation next to the project-origin marker. Not written to IFCX. Out of scope: a 3D user origin and saving the origin per view (plan-views-browser).
design: Frame2d { origin, rotation } with to_local(p) = R(−rotation)·(p − origin) and its inverse, in input/surface.rs next to SurfaceFrame so the 3D working plane can reuse it. UserOriginTool is a non-palette consumer: Workspace keeps active_consumer: Consumer { Tool, UserOrigin, ... } so ToolKind stays the palette concept and later epics can add transient consumers the same way. The readout uses format_length with the project units. Pitfall: the plan context menu (plan.rs:728-780) selects the hovered element first; put the origin items above the separator and skip the selection side effect while a consumer is active.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: Frame2d to_local/from_local round-trip within 1e-12; with the user origin at (10, 10) rotated by 90°, typed absolute (1, 0) resolves to the model point (10, 11); reset restores the identity; the consumer completes in two steps and Enter on the second step keeps rotation 0; the project revision does not change.
- Tracker test: absolute X/Y in the tracker are relative to the user origin; the polar fields are unaffected.
- kittest: the View menu lists 'Place user origin' and 'Reset user origin'; after placing it through the workspace the view-control bar readout changes.
- Satisfies INP-014 and the user-origin clause of INP-004.
notes:
SRS: INP-014 INP-004
Open question: should the user origin be saved per view or per project (candidate for plan-views-browser's saved views)? Current decision: session state, reset when a document is replaced (workspace.rs replace_document).

title: Warn on hidden/locked layers, sort layers, apply layer combinations
description:
WHY: LAY-001 (M): the system warns when a new element is placed on a hidden or locked layer (gap: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:252-337 and views/plan.rs:522-534 execute AddElements without checking, and crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:320-342 accepts additions to locked layers silently while a hidden-layer element vanishes). LAY-002 (M): the layer manager sorts layers (gap: insertion order only, project.rs:171, command.rs:220-223). LAY-003 (S): layer combinations are storable and applicable with one command. Exists and kept (LAY-001 and LAY-002 partial): named layers with visible and locked flags (crates/archicraft-model/src/layer.rs:7-15), exactly one layer per element (validate.rs), hidden elements neither drawn nor selectable (document.rs plan filter, workspace.rs select_all and prune_selection, view3d.rs pick), locked elements drawn but not editable (command.rs:354-386), and the Layers window with create, rename, delete with reassignment, search and element count (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:280-371, Project::element_count_on_layer at project.rs:263).

WHAT: archicraft-model: Project::placement_warnings(&[Element]) -> Vec<PlacementWarning {element, layer, reason: Hidden | Locked}> and Command::ReorderLayers(Vec<LayerId>) for the manual order. archicraft-app: after a successful AddElements (tools, and paste once it exists) the Workspace shows a warning naming the layer with 'Show layer' or 'Unlock layer' buttons (each one UpdateLayer); the tool prompt warns in advance when the active tool's default layer is hidden or locked. crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs Layers window: sortable by name (ascending/descending), element count, or manual order with up/down buttons (ReorderLayers); a Combinations section to store the current states as a new combination, apply, update from current, rename and delete (commands of 07); a View menu 'Layer combination' submenu and a status-bar combo applying a combination in one command (Action::ApplyLayerCombination). Out of scope: per-view layer states (saved views, 09); search and the other layer-manager functions already exist.
design: Compute the warning from the elements actually added (the command input after success), not only from tool defaults, so presets and paste are covered later without changes. SRS wording is 'warns', so placement is never blocked. Keep the warning visible after prune_selection drops the hidden element (status entry with action buttons, not a transient toast). Name and count sorting is a view of the dialog only; manual order is project data. Pitfalls: Undo of a combination must restore both flags; applying a combination that references a deleted layer skips it with a note (resolve logic of 07).
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: placement_warnings reports Hidden and Locked exactly for elements on such layers; ReorderLayers executes, undoes and redoes; a non-permutation is rejected with Invalid.
- kittest: with the wall tool's default layer hidden, drawing a wall shows a warning naming the layer, and 'Show layer' makes it visible in one undo step; with a locked layer the element is placed and the warning shown.
- kittest: sorting the Layers window by element count orders rows accordingly; manual reordering changes project.layers order and survives save and reopen.
- kittest: storing 'Structure only' and applying it from the View menu sets every layer's visible and locked flags in one undo step; Undo restores the previous states.
- Regression: crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs locked_layer_blocks_edits and deleting_resources_requires_a_replacement and render3d.rs hidden_layers_and_selection pass unchanged.
- Element counts are computed in one pass per revision instead of per row per frame (dialogs.rs:327 debt).
- Satisfies the warning clause of LAY-001, sorting in LAY-002 (their other clauses are already done) and the store/apply UI of LAY-003.
notes: SRS: LAY-001 LAY-002 LAY-003.

title: Persist the tile layout and panel docking per user in preferences
description:
WHY: UI-004 (S): panels are dockable, floatable and hideable, and the layout persists per user. PRJ-007 (M): personal settings such as the panel layout are stored outside the project file and opening a project never changes them; SET-002 (M): project settings are stored in the project file as listed in PRJ-007. Gap rows: the egui_tiles tree is rebuilt by default_tree (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:81-87, :147) on every start and every New/Open, only the problems panel is hideable, and layout persistence is an untested side effect of eframe's egui memory. Exists and kept (PRJ-007/SET-002 partial): project settings are written by project_attribute (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:144-190) with storeys as nodes (writer.rs:298-322) and read by read_project_data (reader.rs:301-431); personal settings (theme, separators, snapping, author, recent files) already live in Preferences (persistence/prefs.rs:27-53) and open_path touches only the recent list (app.rs:160-176). Exists (UI-004 partial): the fixed panels (app.rs:805-828), the Problems toggle (Action::Problems, shell.rs:95-98) and the resizable browser.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs: Preferences.layout: Option<SavedLayout {tree: Tree<Pane>, storey_numbers: BTreeMap<StoreyId, i32>}> and Preferences.panels: PanelLayout {toolbox, browser, properties, problems: PanelPlacement {visible, side, floating}} with serde defaults. crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs: restore on start; on New/Open keep the user's tile structure and remap panes (missing storey -> same storey number, else ground; missing view -> first plain 3D viewpoint, else the tile is removed) instead of default_tree; save when the layout changes (compared once per frame, debounced) and in on_exit; panels drawn per placement (side panels left or right, or an egui::Window when floating). View menu 'Panels' submenu: show/hide each panel (the existing Problems checkbox becomes its entry), dock left or right, float, and 'Reset layout'. A settings-location test covers PRJ-007/SET-002. Out of scope: dialog sizes (UI-015, properties-and-dialogs), shortcut and navigation-scheme storage (commands-and-l10n, 3d-input-navigation), floating tabs (an egui_tiles limitation per docs/technology-choices.md).
design: Pane already derives serde (09) and egui_tiles 0.17.1 enables serde by default, so Tree<Pane> serialises directly; keep the tree id stable (Id::new("archicraft-views")). Store StoreyId plus storey numbers so layouts transfer between projects; ViewIds of plain viewpoints differ per project, hence the fallback to the first viewpoint. Panel and dialog sizes belong to SizeMemory of properties-and-dialogs-11, which also turns persist_egui_memory off; PanelLayout stores only visibility, side and floating, so the two stores never overlap; until that task lands eframe's memory may still restore sizes, but the explicit store is authoritative and tested. Save through save_atomically like the rest of the preferences. Pitfalls: an empty or invalid tree (no root) must fall back to default_tree; floating panels need a Dock button so users cannot lose them; remapping must not mutate the stored layout until the user changes it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test: a Tree<Pane> with a horizontal split and two tab groups serialises inside Preferences to JSON and deserialises equal (egui_tiles' default 'serde' feature).
- App test: starting with a saved layout restores that tree; opening another project keeps the tile structure with remapped panes, and the preferences file is byte-identical before and after the open (opening a project never changes personal settings).
- kittest: hiding the browser and floating the properties panel through the View menu survives a harness restart with the same DataDirs; 'Reset layout' restores the default.
- A corrupt layout entry falls back to the default layout with a log line and never blocks start-up.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs project_settings_live_in_the_file: units, storeys, location, layers, materials, views, view folders, layer combinations, remote style, storey view ranges, tessellation and cut-plane defaults survive save and reopen; a prefs test asserts that none of them appears among the serialised Preferences keys.
- Satisfies UI-004 and PRJ-007/SET-002 for every listed item that exists; layer structures, profiles, presets and stair rule defaults are recorded as owned by layer-structures, profiles-columns-beams, templates-presets and stair-solver-tool, and the personal shortcuts and navigation scheme as owned by commands-and-l10n and 3d-input-navigation.
notes: SRS: UI-004 PRJ-007 SET-002.

title: Add the column tool with one-click and rotated placement
description:
WHY: COL-002 (M): columns shall be placed with one click, with an optional second click for the rotation (placement at grid intersections is GRD-005, grids epic). COL-001 parameters and COL-003 end cuts must be editable numerically. Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for every element tool, including the column tool. The tool state machine knows only walls and slabs (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13-17, moved to crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/ by point-input-snapping-01) and the properties strip only wall and slab fields (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:253-506).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/column.rs (ToolKind::Column and its dispatch in tools/mod.rs; the tool is an InputConsumer of the point-input service) with ColumnMode::{Single, Rotated}. Single: one commit adds Project::new_column(storey, point, default rotation). Rotated: the first commit fixes the position, the second commit or a typed angle (a direction step of the point-input service, with Shift constraints and the angle tracker) sets the rotation. Preview: the column's section outline from archicraft_geometry::section with anchor offset and rotation at the cursor; prompts per step. ui/actions.rs: Action::ToolColumn with shortcut C; ui/shell.rs: toolbox button and Design menu item; workspace.rs select_all mapping (ToolKind::Column to KindTag::Column) and the properties gather() mapping. properties.rs: column fields through the Fields getters (hidden for other kinds): section kind (Rectangular, Circular, Profile), width, depth, diameter, profile (project profiles with the columns flag), anchor as a 3 x 3 grid widget (widgets::anchor_grid, plus 'Profile origin' for profile sections), rotation, base offset, top (reuse the wall TopLink fields), top cut and bottom cut (Horizontal or Angle with an angle field), material (replaced by a 'Materials from profile' note for profile sections); derived rows: cross-section area, height, volume; tool_modes shows Single and Rotated. Out of scope: grid placement (GRD-005), handles (13), profile editing (14).
design: Follow the 'Add a drawing tool' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md, adapted to the point-input InputConsumer (StepSpec with Expect::Point then Expect::Direction for Rotated). Two modes instead of a variable point count keep needed() fixed (1 or 2), which matches the reference product's geometry methods and avoids an ambiguous 'finish after one click' gesture. The anchor grid is nine small toggle buttons with tooltips naming the anchor; it is shared with the beam fields of task 11 (properties.rs member_fields helper). ToolKind to KindTag mapping stays in properties gather() until commands-and-l10n's registry exists. Pitfalls: the preview must use the same section generator as the body so what the user sees matches the result; angle fields use widgets::angle with project angle units (D.1 decimal degrees).
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/column.rs unit tests without egui: Single mode, one commit gives one AddElements whose column sits at the snapped point with the default rotation; Rotated mode, a second commit at 45 degrees gives rotation 45 degrees (1e-12); typing 30 and Enter at the second step gives 30 degrees; Esc after the first click drops only that point (point-input Esc ladder); the preview outline is the rotated 0.30 x 0.30 m square around the cursor for the Centre anchor.
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the toolbox shows 'Column', pressing C selects it, a click in the plan creates C-001 on the active storey with the D.2 defaults; the strip shows width and depth for a rectangular section and diameter for a circular one; setting the top cut to Angle 15 degrees issues exactly one UpdateElements; profiles without the columns flag are not offered.
- actions tests: shortcuts_are_unique and appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts include the column tool.
- Satisfies COL-002 (one click plus optional rotation click) and the numeric editing clauses of COL-001 and COL-003.
notes:
SRS: COL-002 COL-001 COL-003
Appendix D.2 column defaults; D.8 column tool shortcut (C proposed, the concrete key is a UI design deliverable).

title: Add the custom profile editor for regions, holes and origin
description:
WHY: PRF-004 (M): a profile is edited in a profile editor: one or more closed regions, holes allowed, each region with a material; an insertion origin. The epic risk note fixes the scope: user-drawn profiles use the polygon input of the point-input service, while creation from geometry (PRF-006) and stretch zones (PRF-007) belong to members-profiles-adv. After task 14 only parametric profiles can be edited.

WHAT: Extend crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/profiles.rs with a canvas for custom profiles: an egui painter area with its own Camera2d (views/camera.rs) implementing the point-input ViewSurface, and modes New region (polygon through the point-input polygon consumer with snapping to existing region nodes and edges via a ProfileCanvasSource SnapSource, typed lengths and Shift constraints, Enter closes), Add hole (pick a region, then draw), Set origin (click; snaps to nodes, bounding-box points and the centroid) and Select (click a region to change its material, Delete removes the region or hole); grid and fit-to-view. 'Convert to custom' turns a parametric profile into a custom one using the tessellated loops of task 03. Each completed operation issues one UpdateProfile validated by validate_profile, and rejections appear in the status line. Out of scope: arc edges (drafting-trim-split, curved-geometry), PRF-006 creation from geometry, PRF-007 stretch zones, PRF-008 offset parameters, PRF-010 per-edge materials.
design: The canvas is a second ViewSurface implementation, which the point-input design anticipates (surface.rs: to_surface, from_surface, model_per_pixel, frame); region drawing reuses the polygon consumer of the slab tool, so the input behaves exactly like other polygon tools (NFR-USE-002 spirit). The canvas works in profile coordinates (metres) with the profile convention of task 01 (seen from the member start, y up). Pitfalls: snapping targets come only from the edited profile, not from the model; holes must be drawn CW or are re-oriented by validate_profile; converting fillets to polylines loses the smooth flag, so the swept fillets shade faceted (acceptable, stated in the convert tooltip).
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless consumer test without egui: drawing a 0.20 x 0.30 m region, a touching 0.10 x 0.30 m region with another material and a 0.05 x 0.05 m hole in the first issues three UpdateProfile commands; the profile validates and its section area is 0.06 + 0.03 - 0.0025 m2 (1e-12).
- A second region overlapping the first is refused with the validation message and no command.
- kittest: opening the editor for a custom profile, clicking four points and pressing Enter creates a region; a click in Set origin mode moves the insertion origin; selecting a region and choosing another material issues one UpdateProfile; a column using the profile then evaluates to Region_1 and Region_2 parts with those materials.
- Convert to custom on IPE 200 yields a custom profile with the same area (1e-9); its fillet vertices become hard (documented).
- Satisfies the region, hole, material and insertion-origin clauses of PRF-004's profile editor.
notes: SRS: PRF-004

title: Declare kind parameters as FieldSpecs and render them in ui/fields.rs
description:
WHY: UI-002 (M) and UI-003 (M) require one properties panel and one full settings dialog that edit both the active tool's defaults and the selected elements, and ELM-001 (M) requires that tool defaults and selected elements are edited through that same panel and dialog. ELM-001 is done (gap row: ToolDefaults crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:120-149, after element-kind-framework-04 the per-kind DefaultsSlot map; template.rs:321-344; SetToolDefaults command.rs:554-593; the shared gather/apply path ui/properties.rs:55-131 and the settings dialog 770-791), so this task keeps that behaviour and must not regress it while it replaces the hand-written fields. Today the fields are hand-written per kind in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:253-506 (geometry_fields, appearance_fields, classification_fields with ElementKind::Wall/Slab arms and the wall_mut/slab_mut helpers at 220-236), so every kind that registers through element-kind-framework (columns, beams, doors, windows, roofs, stairs) would need new app code, and the numeric limits live separately in crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:183-226, although ELM-017 (M) needs one declared range per numeric parameter that the field and the validator share. Step 10 of the add-a-kind recipe in docs/implementation-status.md ('properties.rs prototype, *_defaults extraction, kind-specific Fields getters/setters') is exactly what the registry should remove.

WHAT: archicraft-model: new module fields.rs with `FieldSpec { key, label, section: Section {Geometry, PlanDisplay, ModelAppearance, Classification}, field_type: FieldType {Length, Elevation, Angle, Count, Bool, Choice, Text}, range: Option<(f64, f64)>, range_message, in_strip: bool, get: fn(&Element, &Project) -> Option<FieldValue>, set: fn(&mut Element, &FieldValue, &Project), options: Option<fn(&Project, &Element) -> Vec<(FieldValue, String)>> }` with FieldValue; COMMON_FIELDS for the envelope (material, layer, IFC class with options from the descriptor, position, structural function); KindDescriptor gains `fields: &'static [FieldSpec]`, filled in kinds/wall.rs (thickness, reference line, offset from exterior face, base offset, top mode, height, top storey, linked storey, top offset) and kinds/slab.rs (thickness, reference plane, elevation offset) with ranges taken from the validate.rs constants. archicraft-app: new ui/fields.rs renders a list of FieldSpecs in strip layout or as dialog sections (widgets::length/angle/choice/text, 'Mixed' via widgets::common), collects edits and returns the working copies; properties.rs keeps gather/apply/summary/lock toggle and the selection-only fields (name, home storey) and delegates to ui/fields.rs; its kind-specific functions and helpers are deleted; the defaults path writes the prototype back through the generic DefaultsSlot of element-kind-framework-04. Labels, field order and section titles stay as today. Out of scope: mixed-kind intersection and counts (task 06), inline range explanations and live values (task 07), derived values (task 08), dialog preview (task 09).
design: Approach: the spec is UI-free data in archicraft-model (NFR-MNT-002: the headless crate has no egui dependency), attached to KindDescriptor so 'adding a kind' stays one module plus one registry line; ui/fields.rs is the only renderer, used by both layouts. A getter returning None hides the field for that element (today's auto-hide behaviour, for example Height only for TopLink::Fixed). fn pointers (not closures) keep descriptors const and 'static. FieldValue: Length(f64), Angle(f64), Count(i64), Bool(bool), Code(&'static str) for enum choices, Storey/Layer/Material ids, Text(String). The wall top-mode logic (properties.rs:331-361) moves into kinds/wall.rs as the setter of 'top_mode' because it needs Project::vertical_extent. If commands-and-l10n has landed, label and range_message are message keys resolved by the app catalogue. Pitfalls: keep the egui Ids per field key (today Id::new("properties").with(layout).with(key)) so focus and typed text survive frames; the custom reference-line default thickness/3 (properties.rs:295, listed debt) becomes 'keep the current reference offset' with a note; option lists for layers, materials and storeys are built once per frame. Pointers: properties.rs:24-236 and 253-506, widgets.rs:62-131, kinds/mod.rs KindDescriptor (element-kind-framework-02), validate.rs:10-23 and 183-226.
acceptance_criteria:
- The existing kittests in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs pass unchanged; the strip still shows Thickness, Reference line, Base offset, Top, Material, Layer, IFC class, Position and Structural function for a wall and Thickness, Reference plane, Elevation offset for a slab.
- Registry tests in crates/archicraft-model: every descriptor in KINDS has at least one Geometry field; keys are unique per kind; a key shared by two kinds or with COMMON_FIELDS has the same field_type and label; every ranged numeric field has a non-empty range_message; every Choice field has options.
- Source-scan test: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs and ui/fields.rs contain no `ElementKind::` pattern and no as_wall/as_slab call (kind knowledge lives in the kind modules).
- Dummy-kind kittest (feature test-kinds): a selected Dummy element shows its descriptor's fields in the strip and in the settings dialog without any app change, and editing one issues UpdateElements.
- Defaults test: with the wall tool active and nothing selected, editing Thickness changes only the wall defaults slot through SetToolDefaults (slab slot unchanged); one undo restores it.
- Satisfies ELM-001 and the 'same panel and dialog for defaults and selection' clauses of UI-002 and UI-003 for every registered kind.
- ELM-001 and UI-002 regression: tool_buttons_and_properties_follow_each_other (tests/ui.rs:66) and selecting_an_element_shows_its_properties (tests/ui.rs:102) pass unchanged, so the strip shows the active tool's defaults with nothing selected and the selection's values otherwise; a wall default edited through a FieldSpec is written to toolDefaults, survives an IFCX round trip and is applied to the next element created through Project::new_element.
- COMMON_FIELDS hook test: 'position' and 'structural_function' are Choice FieldSpecs whose FieldValue codes equal Position::code and StructuralFunction::code; a unit test selects the exterior load-bearing elements of a wall/slab project through the FieldSpec getters alone, the generic matching that DSP-016 criteria and templates-presets selection reuse (ELM-012, ELM-020 'usable by display overrides').
notes:
SRS: UI-002 UI-003 ELM-001 ELM-017
Ranges are declared once here and consumed by task 07. doors-windows-core and plan-views-browser-06 register their fields as FieldSpecs once this has landed (their tasks say so).

title: Commit wall chains as one step, Backspace and press-drag-release
description:
WHY: During multi-step input (wall chains, polylines, railings, stair baselines) Backspace shall remove the last entered point without cancelling the input (UND-003). Today Backspace pops the point (tools.rs:537-543), but in chain mode every click has already executed Command::AddElements (tools.rs:464-477), so the wall stays in the model and the next click draws a second wall from the previous point; Esc (one step back, INP-003) has the same flaw. Click-click input shall be the default and press-drag-release selectable as a user preference (INP-020); today click-click is the only mode (plan.rs:498-534). The epic also gathers snap radius, dwell, angle increment and input mode in the preferences.

WHAT: Wall chain: points accumulate in the step state and the whole chain is committed as one Command::AddElements (one undo step) on Enter, double-click, a click on the first point (closing) or the context menu's Finish; switching tool or storey commits an open chain of two or more points instead of discarding it. The preview draws the pending reference-line polyline and the wall outlines from the tool defaults' thickness and reference-line location. Backspace and Esc on a clean step remove the last point; consecutive walls stay joined as before (WAL-001). Preferences: input_mode: InputMode { ClickClick, DragRelease } (default ClickClick) and an 'Input' group in preferences_window (dialogs.rs:679-745) holding snap radius, angle increment and input mode, plus the tracker and dwell rows of tasks 05 and 09 (whichever of these tasks lands last places its row in the group). plan.rs maps pointer events to PointerEvent { Pressed, Released, Clicked, DoubleClicked } for PointInput::pointer(event, mode): in DragRelease a press commits the step's point and the release commits the next point when the pointer moved beyond the drag threshold, otherwise press and release act as a click; the Select tool's area selection is untouched. Prompts list Backspace and the mode. Out of scope: polylines, railings and stair baselines (their epics implement InputConsumer and inherit Backspace).
design: Decision: commit the chain at its end rather than undoing per-segment commands on Backspace; this keeps History untouched during input, makes the chain one undo step like the slab polygon, and lets Backspace and Esc be pure state changes testable without a project. Rejected alternative: per-segment commits with Workspace::undo on Backspace (couples the tool to History and breaks when the user undoes in between). DragRelease uses response.drag_started_by/drag_stopped_by(PointerButton::Primary) for drawing tools and clicked_by for ClickClick (plan.rs:498-534 today). Deserialize input_mode leniently (deserialize_with mapping unknown strings to ClickClick): an unknown enum value would otherwise fail the whole file, and Preferences::load (prefs.rs:79-89) would fall back to all defaults. Chain wall outlines in the preview use ReferenceLine::face_offsets (element.rs:99) with the tool defaults; junction cleanup appears after the commit, as for rectangles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: a chain of four points followed by Backspace leaves three pending points and no element in the project; Enter then creates exactly two joined walls as one undo step; undo removes both; wall_chain_closes_into_joined_walls and slab_polygon_finishes_on_enter still pass; switching to the Slab tool with three pending chain points creates two walls.
- DragRelease tests: press, move 20 px, release produces two committed points; a press and release without movement equals a click; ClickClick behaviour is unchanged.
- Preferences tests: input_mode round-trips; an unknown value falls back to ClickClick while the other preferences of the same file are kept.
- kittest: the Preferences dialog shows the 'Input' group with 'Input mode', 'Click-click' and 'Press-drag-release'.
- Satisfies UND-003 for wall chains (the other multi-step inputs reuse the consumer API), INP-020, and Esc as one step for chains (INP-003).
notes:
SRS: UND-003 INP-020 INP-003
Appendix D.1: snap radius 8 px, dwell 1.0 s, angle increment 45° (15° selectable) — all rows sit in the 'Input' group with the input mode (SET-001).

title: Add the columns-and-beams sample, golden file and Axis conformance
description:
WHY: IFX-006 (M) requires every written file to load in the reference implementation and display in the viewer, verified automatically on reference models; IFX-035 (S) writes beam and column axes as basiscurves in an Axis child; the epic acceptance requires IfcColumn and IfcBeam with Axis basiscurves to pass conformance. IFX-025 (M) writes holes of profiles as geometry, not as IfcOpeningElement (done for slab holes; kept and regressed here for hollow sections and holed profiles); IFX-017/IFX-043 give multi-material bodies one named part per material. The sample is also the saved-file reference for COL-001/COL-003 (rectangular, hollow-section and top-cut columns), BEA-001/BEA-002 (anchors, roll, pitch and end cuts), PRF-004 (a custom two-region profile with region materials) and PRF-011 (a catalogue IPE 300). conformance/check.ts checks classes, names, mesh bodies and colours (check.ts:68-103) but no Axis child, and no sample contains a column, a beam or a profile.

WHAT: Add samples::columns_and_beams() to crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs, built through commands with the framework's seeded fixture builder (v5 ids from the fixture name): one storey with four D.2 reinforced-concrete columns on a 6.00 x 4.00 m rectangle, two D.2 beams between them, an IPE 300 steel beam from the catalogue (task 04), a CHS 168.3 x 8 column with a 15 degree top cut, an inclined reinforced-concrete beam (pitch 20 degrees) with an Angle start cut and a Horizontal end cut, a glulam beam with a steel flitch plate (custom two-region profile) and an RHS beam rolled 90 degrees. FixtureBuilder gains column() and beam() helpers; register the sample once in samples::catalogue(), the single list read by crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs since element-kind-framework-03, bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/ columns-and-beams.ifcx and review it. Extend conformance/check.ts: every element node carrying an archicraft::wall, archicraft::column or archicraft::beam attribute (by kind, so a column classed IfcMember or a beam classed IfcFooting is still checked) must have an Axis child carrying usd::usdgeom::basiscurves points with at least two points, and no IfcOpeningElement may appear below a column or beam. Add plan_of_columns_and_beams to crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs: the ground-floor plan of the sample at the D.1 cut plane (1.10 m) has a cut region for every column, overhead-only lines for the D.2, IPE, glulam and RHS beams, projected, cut and overhead lines for the inclined beam, and a reference_line for every beam (BEA-008 on the reference model, after task 08). Out of scope: AS-02 (grids), plan golden images (plan-renderer).
design: Follow the 'Add a sample/golden model' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md, with registration through samples::catalogue() instead of two lists: constructor in samples.rs, registration in the example and the round-trip test, ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx --test roundtrip, review, then run conformance. check.ts reads composed attributes, so the Axis test looks for 'usd::usdgeom::basiscurves::points' on a child named Axis, mirroring how meshes are found through 'usd::usdgeom::mesh::points' (check.ts:85). Keep the sample small (11 elements) so the golden diff stays reviewable. Pitfall: golden ids must be deterministic, hence the seeded builder rather than random UUIDs; the catalogue profile carries its designation so the reviewer can check the IPE 300 dimensions in the diff.
acceptance_criteria:
- The round-trip suite covers the new sample: written_files_validate_without_problems, round_trip_restores_the_editable_model, regenerated_geometry_matches_the_stored_geometry (within 0.1 mm, IFX-064), output_is_deterministic_and_plain, written_meshes_are_closed_bodies, spatial_tree_and_identities and golden_files_are_reproduced and catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files all pass.
- plan_of_columns_and_beams passes with the classification above and analytic coordinates within 1e-9.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx passes for every golden file (walls-and-slab, two-storey-shell, compound-parts of element-kind-framework-07 and columns-and-beams) with the extended Axis check; removing the Axis child of one column in a scratch copy makes the check fail (verified once and recorded in the PR description).
- The golden file contains IfcColumn and IfcBeam nodes each with an Axis basiscurves child, Region_1 and Region_2 parts with the glulam and steel materials for the flitch beam, closed hollow-section bodies with inner faces and no IfcOpeningElement (IFX-025).
- If regression-and-status has landed its fixture registry, the sample is registered there under its fixture id.
- Verifies IFX-035 for beams and columns end to end and the persistence of PRF-004/PRF-011 profiles in a reference model.
notes:
SRS: IFX-035 COL-001 COL-003 BEA-001 BEA-002 BEA-008 PRF-004 PRF-011
Also touches IFX-006, IFX-025, IFX-043 (verified, owned elsewhere).

title: Edit column and beam end cuts with handles in plan and 3D
description:
WHY: COL-003 (M): column end cuts are editable numerically and by handle. BEA-002 (M): beam end cuts are editable numerically and by handle in plan and 3D. No handle infrastructure exists (gap rows COL-003 and BEA-002): views/plan.rs:497-563 handles tool points, click and area selection only, and views/view3d.rs:153-190 orbits, pans and picks. edit-reshape-palette builds node and edge handles for outlines in parallel, and this epic does not depend on it, so the end-cut handles are built here as a small, separate module.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-app/src/views/handles.rs: `MemberHandle { element, role: HandleRole::{ColumnTop, ColumnBottom, BeamStart, BeamEnd}, position: DVec3, plane: DragPlane { origin, a, b } }`; member_handles(project, geometry, element) for exactly one selected, unlocked column or beam; pure mapping functions beam_cut_from_plan(handle, cursor) (cursor projected on the horizontal axis direction through the end point: theta = atan(s / dz), dz = vertical distance from the anchor-line end to the far section edge) and cut_angle_from_ray(handle, origin, dir) (ray intersected with the drag plane: axis-horizontal and Z for beams, local v and Z for columns); results within 1 degree of the default snap to Vertical or Horizontal; invalid angles clamp to the last valid one (validate_element). A HandleDrag consumer on the point-input service (press-drag-release or click-click per the input-mode preference, typed angle plus Enter commits, Esc cancels) issues one UpdateElements. views/plan.rs draws beam end handles (diamonds) and the live cut line; views/view3d.rs draws column top and bottom handles and beam end handles through overlay3d (task 12), hit-tests them within the snap radius and drags with Camera3d::ray (views/camera.rs:262), committing on release. Out of scope: generic node and edge handles (edit-reshape-palette), length and elevation handles, BEA-003 compound planes, a plan handle for column cuts (the tilt is invisible in plan and COL-003 names no view).
design: All geometry of the interaction lives in pure functions over model values, so it is tested without egui; the egui code only draws and routes pointer events. Plan mapping for beams follows BEA-002's definition from task 07 (cut angle in the vertical plane through the axis): in plan that angle shows as the horizontal shift of the far section edge, hence theta = atan(s / dz); Horizontal (90 degrees) is reachable in 3D or numerically. The 3D drag plane passes through the handle's end point, so the ray intersection is stable while the camera is still; pick handles before element picking in view3d.rs so a handle click does not change the selection. Path: views/handles.rs stays at this path because members-profiles-adv extends beam_cut_from_plan and the HandleDrag consumer there; it is distinct from edit-reshape-palette's generic crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/handles.rs, which is not a prerequisite of this epic. Coordination: edit-reshape-palette adds part_pick and outline handles in views/plan.rs; whichever lands second moves the common hit-testing into one module (keep the API to member_handles plus HandleDrag).
acceptance_criteria:
- handles.rs unit tests: for a TopCentre-anchored beam with h = 0.50 m, a cursor 0.25 m beyond the end along the axis gives Angle(atan(0.5)) with the documented sign; a cursor within dz * tan(1 degree) gives Vertical; a ray meeting a pitched beam's drag plane horizontally gives Horizontal, the same ray on a level beam clamps to the last valid angle; a column top ray gives a 20 degree tilt about the local x axis.
- Locked elements and multi-selections produce no handles.
- kittest: selecting a beam in plan and dragging its end handle 0.25 m along the axis issues one UpdateElements with the expected angle; typing 15 and Enter during the drag sets 15 degrees; Esc cancels without a command.
- A headless 3D drag through view3d's handle hit test and ray mapping changes a column's top cut to the expected angle in one undo step, and the plan (task 08), 3D view and properties fields show the new cut.
- Satisfies the handle clauses of COL-003 (3D) and BEA-002 (plan and 3D); with tasks 10 and 11 the end cuts are editable numerically and by handle.
notes:
SRS: COL-003 BEA-002
Open question: no plan handle for column cuts (decision above); revisit if users ask for it. The 1 degree snap to the default cut is an assumption.

title: Coordinate locks, constraint directions and guide geometry
description:
WHY: While a constraint modifier is held, the cursor shall be restricted to the nearest allowed direction: horizontal, vertical or a multiple of a configurable angle increment (default 45°), measured from the X axis or from the construction-grid orientation, or alternatively held on the nearest guide (INP-006). A key command shall lock the X coordinate, the Y coordinate or the distance from the previous point; the lock is drawn as a temporary guide and lasts until the point is committed or the lock is released (INP-007), and the angle from the previous point shall be lockable the same way (INP-023). Today constrain() (tools.rs:269-280) measures from the X axis only, the constrained branch returns before snapping (plan.rs:481-486), so nothing snaps along the constrained direction, and no lock exists.

WHAT: Add input/guide.rs: GuideShape { Line { point, dir }, Ray, Segment, Circle { centre, radius }, Arc } with intersect(), project(), distance() and clip(rect) for drawing, plus GuideOrigin { Lock, Constraint, Inference, Persistent } shared by tasks 09 and 11. Add input/locks.rs: Locks { x, y, distance, angle: Option<f64> } toggled by Alt+X, Alt+Y, Alt+D and Alt+A (provisional), taking the typed field value if present, otherwise the current cursor value, expressed in the input frame (the user origin once task 07 is in). Each lock yields a guide: a vertical or horizontal line, a circle around the previous point, a line through the previous point. The PointInput pipeline becomes typed → locks → constraint → snap, where snapping runs along the active lock or constraint guide (guide ∩ indexed edges at intersection level, nodes projected onto the guide, otherwise the free point on the guide). Constraint directions are measured from the X axis or from the frame rotation supplied by the construction grid (task 10), chosen by a preference; with guides in range Shift holds the cursor on the nearest guide. Locks are drawn dashed from Resolved.guides. Add the 15°/45° quick choice next to the angle increment row of the Preferences dialog (dialogs.rs:740-742). Out of scope: inference and persistent guides (09, 11), vertical guides in 3D (3d-input-navigation).
design: Keep constrain() as the pure direction function but return the chosen direction so the caller can build a Ray guide and run candidates_on(index, &guide, cursor, radius, other_guides). Locks are step-local PointInput state, cleared on commit, cancel_step and consumer switch. The Alt modifier is Option on macOS (egui Modifiers::ALT); Option+letter also produces Event::Text on macOS, so ignore Text events carrying Alt when a lock key matched. The angle lock uses the angle units of units.rs (degrees, DMS, gradians). D.1: angle increment 45°, 15° selectable; prefs.rs:43-44 and 105-107 already clamp to 1-90.
acceptance_criteria:
- Guide tests: line–line, line–circle (0, 1 and 2 points) and circle–circle intersections; projection onto lines, circles and arcs; clipping an infinite line to a rectangle.
- Constraint tests: 45° increments from the X axis (the existing constrain test kept); with a frame rotated by 30° the allowed directions are 30°, 75°, 120°…; with Shift held and an edge crossing the constraint line, the cursor snaps to the crossing at intersection level instead of a free constrained point.
- Lock tests: with Alt+X the resolved X equals the lock value for any cursor; with Alt+D the distance to the previous point equals the lock within 1e-12; Alt+A plus Alt+D give the exact point; the same key releases the lock; locks clear on commit and on the first Esc (before the step is cancelled); a typed field value is adopted by the lock; every lock contributes a GuideOrigin::Lock guide to Resolved.guides; a node near the lock line snaps onto the line.
- kittest: holding Shift while drawing shows the constrained preview and the label 'constrained'; after Alt+X the tracker marks the X value as locked until the click commits the point; the Preferences dialog offers 15° and 45°.
- Satisfies INP-007 and INP-023; INP-006 for X-axis directions and lock guides (the grid orientation becomes live with task 10, the nearest inference guide with task 09).
notes:
SRS: INP-006 INP-007 INP-023
Appendix D.1: angle increment 45° (15° selectable). Provisional bindings Alt+X, Alt+Y, Alt+D, Alt+A; confirm with commands-and-l10n (D.8).

title: Shared point-input service, snapping, guides and construction grid
description:
Extract the pipeline inlined in views/plan.rs into one headless PointInput service (typed value → lock → constraint → snap) used by every creation, transform, reshape, measuring and dimensioning step, and complete snapping (full target set, precedence, cycling, division points, inference guides with dwell, centroids, exclusions), locks, Cartesian and absolute entry with user origin, arithmetic, persistent guide lines, live context distances, click-click/drag preference and Backspace.

Risks: The service must serve transforms and 3D without a second rewrite; the step/preview API is defined against EDT-001 and INP-015 use cases up front. Removes the per-frame snap-target rebuild debt.
design: archicraft-app input/ module: a state machine without egui (tested like tools.rs), SnapTargets built from an rstar index (geo) updated incrementally instead of per frame, snap glyph set in plan.rs, guides and user origin in per-view state (guide lines excluded from IFCX), live distances from a generic target provider (walls now, grids/columns/beams when they exist). A ViewSurface trait implemented by the plan view now and by the 3D working plane later. Preferences gain snap radius, dwell, angle increment and input mode. Contour detection (INP-018) is not here: it lives in edit-reshape-palette on the polygon machinery.
acceptance_criteria: AS-04 automated: a closed wall polygon drawn purely by typed polar and relative Cartesian values measures back exactly (0.1 mm, 0.01°); unit tests for the precedence node > intersection > division > guide intersection > edge > guide > grid, Tab cycling, X/Y/distance/angle locks drawn as guides, dwell-marked references producing parallel/perpendicular/bisector guides, all division modes and centroid snaps; Esc cancels one step and Backspace one point; input feedback under 50 ms on two_storey_shell (frame-time assertion); kittest covers typing during input. The step/preview API is exercised by two consumers in this epic's tests (the wall tool and a transform stub) so that selection-transforms and 3d-input-navigation plug in without changing it.
notes: SRS: INP-001 INP-002 INP-003 INP-004 INP-005 INP-006 INP-007 INP-008 INP-009 INP-010 INP-011 INP-012 INP-013 INP-014 INP-017 INP-020 INP-021 INP-022 INP-023 INP-024 UND-003 NFR-PERF-005

title: Typed entry: Cartesian and absolute fields, first point, tracker
description:
WHY: Numeric point entry shall support relative polar coordinates (distance, angle), relative Cartesian coordinates (ΔX, ΔY, ΔZ) and absolute coordinates measured from the project origin, the user origin (INP-014) or a temporarily marked snap point, with a single key switching between polar and Cartesian fields (INP-004). The tracker next to the cursor shall show the live distance and angle from the previous point and, on demand, X, Y and Z in working units; when an element is stretched it shows the resulting total length by default and the length change on demand and accepts either as typed input (INP-002). The first keystroke goes to the active field without focusing it (INP-003), which is impossible for the first point today because typing is gated on is_drawing() (plan.rs:647). Typed lengths keep accepting unit suffixes and imperial fractions in any project unit (INP-005 is done in crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:391-424: keep it and regress it in every new field). Today only Field::Distance/Angle exist (tools.rs:86-118), apply_typed is relative polar only (tools.rs:407-426) and the tracker shows only d and a (tools.rs:428-448).

WHAT: In input/typed.rs introduce FieldSet { Polar { distance, angle }, Cartesian { dx, dy, dz }, Stretch { total, change } }, Reference { Relative, Absolute(Origin { Project, User, Marked }) } and resolve() that completes untyped fields from the cursor (typed ΔX with the cursor's ΔY, typed distance with the cursor's angle). The first point of every step sequence defaults to Absolute(Project) with X/Y fields, later points to Relative; P switches polar/Cartesian and Shift+P relative/absolute (provisional keys). Add input/tracker.rs: tracker lines per field of the active set, an 'X/Y/Z on demand' toggle stored as a tracker-behaviour preference (SET-001) and TrackerMode { Relative, TotalLength { base, dir }, LengthChange { base, dir } } chosen by the consumer's StepSpec, exercised by a StretchStub consumer in the tests. Origin::User and Origin::Marked resolve through InputContext (identity and None here; tasks 07 and 09 supply them). Z shows the surface elevation and ΔZ is display-only in plan views until the 3D working plane exists. Out of scope: arithmetic and field addressing (06), placing the user origin (07), marks (09), the stretch command itself (edit-reshape-palette).
design: Each field holds its text and, once parsed, its f64 value; values are parsed through one TypedInput::value(field) function (parse_length/parse_angle, units.rs:391 and 428, replaced by the expression parser in task 06). Stretch resolution: point = base + dir × total (or base + dir × (base_length + change)), projecting the cursor onto dir for untyped values. Field sets switch with conversion of parsed values only, so the AS-04 values stay exact. Absolute(Project) in plan views is measured in the storey plane (SurfaceFrame origin at the storey elevation). Tracker strings use format_length and format_angle (units.rs:283, 334) with the project units and the preference number format. Add the tracker row to the Preferences dialog next to the snap rows (dialogs.rs:730-742; the 'Input' group once task 14 has landed). Pitfall: typing before the first point must not swallow the single-key shortcuts of an idle tool: captures_keys() is true while the active consumer has points or typed text; with neither, a digit, sign or decimal separator starts the typed text and every other key (V, W, S, F, O) keeps its shortcut; the Select tool never captures. The shortcut filter also looks at the frame's Text events, so '3ft' arriving within one frame is not split into a typed 3 and a Fit command.
acceptance_criteria:
- Typed tests: ΔX 3, ΔY 4 from (1, 1) gives (4, 5); ΔX typed alone takes ΔY from the cursor; P converts the typed polar values into Cartesian fields without rounding (f64 kept beside the text); absolute X/Y before the first point resolve from the project origin; Shift+P toggles relative/absolute; the Cartesian set shows ΔZ (0 in plan views) and a typed ΔZ leaves a plan-view point in the storey plane (planar consumers ignore it; 3d-input-navigation activates it).
- First-point test: with the Wall tool active and no points, the keystrokes '3', Tab, '4', Enter commit the first point (3, 4) through PointInput (no candidates in range, so Tab moves the field).
- Tracker tests: the polar set shows d and a, the Cartesian set ΔX and ΔY, the X/Y/Z preference adds absolute X, Y and Z in working units; StretchStub opens in TotalLength mode, so the tracker shows the resulting total length by default; with base length 4.0 it accepts the typed total 5.0 (point moves by 1.0); Tab switches on demand to the change field, the tracker then shows the length change and accepts the typed change 0.5 (total 4.5).
- INP-005 regression: 3'-4 1/2" typed into the ΔX field of a metric project resolves to 1.0287 m; every existing units.rs test passes unchanged.
- kittest: with the Wall tool active and no point, pressing S still switches to the Slab tool (no typing has started); back on the Wall tool, typing '3ft' leaves the view unfitted (F is captured once typing has started) and the tracker shows '3ft_' in the X field (app.rs asks ws.input.captures_keys()).
- Satisfies INP-004 (the user-origin and marked-point origins are wired by tasks 07 and 09), INP-002 (the real stretch consumer arrives in edit-reshape-palette through TrackerMode), INP-003's first-keystroke clause; INP-005 stays done.
notes:
SRS: INP-002 INP-003 INP-004 INP-005
Appendix D.1: metre with 3 decimals, decimal degrees with 2 decimals. Provisional bindings: P toggles polar/Cartesian, Shift+P relative/absolute; final keys in commands-and-l10n. The X/Y/Z toggle is the 'tracker behaviour' preference of SET-001.

title: Automate AS-04, typing kittest and the 50 ms latency assertion
description:
WHY: The epic's exit criterion requires AS-04 automated (a closed wall polygon drawn purely by typed polar and relative Cartesian values measures back exactly at 0.1 mm and 0.01°), a kittest covering typing during input (INP-003, INP-004) and a frame-time assertion that input feedback (cursor snapping, rubber-band preview, tracker values) updates within 50 ms of pointer movement on two_storey_shell (NFR-PERF-005), all through the shared service (INP-001). docs/implementation-status.md lists AS-04 as partial (relative polar only) and NFR-PERF-005 as unmeasured.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/tests/as04_precision.rs drives PointInput headlessly with the wall chain: the first point typed as absolute (0, 0), then polar 6.000 m at 0°, Cartesian Δ(0, 4.000), polar 3.000 m at 180° and Cartesian Δ(−3.000, −4.000), which closes the chain on the first point; it reads back Wall start/end, length and direction (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:142-150) and formats them with format_length at 4 decimals in metres and format_angle at 2 decimals. crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs gains typing tests that inject egui Text and Key events with the Wall tool active ('3', Tab, '4', Enter for the first point; '2500mm', Enter for the second; the Esc ladder; Tab cycling with two candidates in range; Backspace in a chain). crates/archicraft-app/tests/input_latency.rs opens two_storey_shell, sweeps 2,000 seeded pointer positions over the ground-floor plan while drawing with locks, marks, division points, the construction grid, a persistent guide and context distances active, and asserts the p99 of resolve() under 5 ms in debug; a kittest run of 60 frames with pointer moves while drawing asserts each frame's wall-clock time below 50 ms at p95 (scaled by an ARCHICRAFT_PERF_SLACK environment factor for slow CI runners) and that the snap index was built at most once. Out of scope: the measure tool of the manual AS-04 procedure (3d-input-navigation) and the criterion benches of regression-and-status.
design: Use the harness of tests/ui.rs (Harness::builder().build_eframe with Preferences::default()); inject events through the harness input (egui::Event::Text, Event::Key, Event::PointerMoved) and run_steps between them. For the latency kittest measure Instant::now() around harness.step() after moving the pointer, keeping the plan view hovered and the wall tool with one point so snapping, preview and tracker all run. Debug builds use opt-level 1 for the workspace (Cargo.toml [profile.dev]), so thresholds are generous; the assertion that matters for regressions is the index build counter. The closing Cartesian segment is chosen so all coordinates are exact in binary-friendly decimals and the chain closes within CLOSE_TOLERANCE (tools.rs:338).
acceptance_criteria:
- as04_precision.rs passes: every typed polar length and angle and every Cartesian ΔX/ΔY equals the measured value within 0.05 mm and 0.005°, the formatted strings at 0.1 mm and 0.01° are identical to the typed values (the Cartesian closing segment reads 5.0000 m and −126.87°, the atan2 direction as format_angle prints it without normalisation, units.rs:334-340), and the four walls form a closed, joined chain.
- ui.rs typing tests pass: the typed first point, the typed second point, Esc clearing the typed text and then dropping one point, Tab selecting the second snap candidate, Backspace removing one chain point.
- input_latency.rs passes locally and in CI with the default slack of 1.0; the index build counter stays at 1 for the whole sweep, and the test fails when the per-frame rebuild is forced back in (checked once while developing).
- input_latency.rs prints its measured p99 resolve() time and p95 frame time (eprintln!, visible with --nocapture) so the done task can record them in docs/implementation-status.md.
- Satisfies the test clauses of NFR-PERF-005, INP-001, INP-003 and INP-004 and automates AS-04's typed-input part.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-005 INP-001 INP-003 INP-004
The 3D step of AS-04 (measuring with the measure tool) belongs to 3d-input-navigation; regression-and-status later runs the same sweep as a criterion bench on reference hardware.

title: Show another storey or view as a trace underlay in plan views
description:
WHY: VIEW-015 (S): a plan view can show another storey (or a view) as a faint trace underlay whose opacity is adjustable, which can be offset and rotated and switched off with one command. Gap row: no underlay or trace concept exists in plan.rs or workspace.rs. Decision D-11 removed image underlays only; tracing another storey of the same model stays in scope.

WHAT: PlanViewState.underlay: Option<TraceUnderlay> (model type from 07: source Storey or View, opacity, offset, rotation, enabled). crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draws the source plan (ws.doc.plan(source storey, source options); a saved plan view as source contributes its overrides) before the remote and home layers, colours faded towards the paper by the opacity, transformed by rotation about the project origin and then the offset; the underlay is neither pickable nor snappable. Action::ToggleTrace (View menu and a status-bar toggle) switches it with one command; a 'Trace...' popover sets source (other storeys and saved plan views), opacity (default 0.35), offset X/Y and rotation with unit-aware fields. The settings are captured into and applied from ViewDefinition.plan.underlay (09). Out of scope: snapping to the underlay, image or PDF underlays (D-11), difference highlighting.
design: Reuse draw_plan with a faded Palette variant and a point transform closure; the source plan comes from the Document plan cache, so the underlay costs only drawing. If plan-renderer has landed, add an underlay pass with alpha and the transform as a uniform instead. Pitfalls: the underlay must not feed SnapTargets or picking; fit-to-window ignores the underlay; the default opacity is a UI choice, not an Appendix D value.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test: the underlay transform maps source points by rotation and then offset (exact for 90 degrees and an offset of (1, 2)).
- kittest: ToggleTrace switches the underlay on and off in one action each; changing the opacity updates the pane state; the model revision is unchanged and PlanDrawing::pick at an underlay-only position returns nothing.
- With a saved plan view of the storey below as source, the underlay shows that view's storey with its cut override (Document::plan with the view's PlanOptions).
- A saved plan view re-applies its underlay on open; IFCX persistence of the section is covered by the round-trip test of 08.
- Deleting the source storey disables the underlay with a status note instead of failing; choosing the pane's own storey as source is refused.
- Satisfies VIEW-015.
notes: SRS: VIEW-015. Default opacity 0.35 (UI design choice, not in Appendix D).

title: Range-check fields inline and update dependent values while typing
description:
WHY: ELM-017 (M): numeric parameters are range-checked; invalid values are rejected with an explanation (NFR-REL-005), and dependent values (for example a stair's riser count) update live while editing. Ranges exist in crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:183-226 and rejections reach the status line (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:123-136), but only after a command was attempted; fields commit on Enter or focus loss (ui/widgets.rs:52-57) and derived values refresh only after the command (ui/properties.rs:541-575), so nothing updates while typing (gap row ELM-017). The epic acceptance requires that an invalid value shows its explanation and leaves the model untouched.

WHAT: ui/widgets.rs: committed_text reports `Edited::Pending(T)` each frame while focused with a parsable value that differs from the shown one; widgets::length/angle/count take an optional range with its message and return `Edited::Invalid(message)` for out-of-range pending or committed values, draw the field with the error stroke and keep focus and text on Enter. ui/fields.rs: shows the explanation inline (dialog: a red label below the field; strip: a red label after the field plus the status line), never issues a command for an invalid value, maps a command rejection back to the field that caused it, and keeps a draft (working copies with the pending value) rebuilt only when the pending value changes. Dependent values: FieldSpec gains read-only computed fields (get only, `computed: true`) shown in the Geometry section and evaluated from the draft: walls 'Resulting height' (top minus base for linked tops), slabs 'Top face offset' and 'Bottom face offset' relative to the home storey (named so they do not collide with the absolute 'Base elevation' and 'Top elevation' rows of task 08); kinds with true dependent parameters (the stair riser count of stair-solver-tool) register computed fields the same way. Out of scope: geometric quantities (task 08 reads the same draft), the dialog preview (task 09).
design: Approach: validation happens twice by design: the widget checks the FieldSpec range for instant feedback, and validate_element stays the authority (a value can pass its own range but fail a cross-field rule; that message is shown inline too, mapped via the field key that produced the draft). Pending values: committed_text already keeps the user's text in egui temp data (widgets.rs:24-49); parse it each frame and return Pending when it differs from the shown value. Draft: `Draft { field_key, text, elements }` in the panel state, rebuilt only when key or text change, so typing costs O(1) per frame (NFR-PERF-005 input feedback). Pitfalls: adding an Edited variant breaks exhaustive matches in dialogs.rs (Edited::Unchanged arms) - handle Pending there explicitly; egui's TextEdit drops focus on Enter, so request focus again for an invalid value; Esc must clear the draft; computed fields join the mixed-kind intersection only if both kinds declare them. Pointers: widgets.rs:17-77, properties.rs:168-193 and 541-575, validate.rs:183-226, workspace.rs:123-136.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest invalid_thickness_is_explained_and_not_applied: with a wall selected, typing '0' into Thickness and pressing Enter shows 'Thickness must be between 1 mm and 10 m.' next to the field; project.revision, the wall and the undo history are unchanged; correcting to 0.3 commits one undo step and removes the message.
- kittest dependent_values_update_while_typing: a wall whose top is linked to the storey above (+3.000) shows 'Resulting height 3.000'; typing '0.5' into Top offset without Enter shows '3.500' while project.revision is unchanged; Esc restores '3.000' and clears the draft.
- kittest slab_face_offsets_follow_the_thickness: a slab with reference plane 'Top face' and elevation offset 0 shows 'Bottom face offset -0.200'; typing 0.3 into Thickness without Enter shows -0.300 while project.revision is unchanged.
- Unit test ranges_match_the_validator in crates/archicraft-model: for every numeric FieldSpec with a range, a value at each bound passes validate_element and a value 1e-6 beyond fails with exactly its range_message (one source for UI and validator, NFR-REL-005).
- Unit tests in ui/widgets.rs for the pure range check: inclusive bounds, NaN and infinity rejected, message text passed through.
- Both layouts show the explanation: the strip (label plus status line) and the settings dialog (label below the field), covered by a parametrised kittest.
- Satisfies ELM-017: range check with explanation, model untouched, and live dependent values for every computed field that exists (stairs reuse the mechanism).
notes:
SRS: ELM-017
Uses the ranges declared in task 05. The stair riser count named by ELM-017 arrives with stair-solver-tool as a computed FieldSpec.

title: Add the beam tool with two-point and chain input
description:
WHY: BEA-001 (M): a beam is created between two picked points and its parameters (width/height or profile, anchor, lateral offset, roll, elevation, inclination by end elevations or pitch) must be editable. BEA-002 (M): end cuts editable numerically. BEA-010 (S): beams shall be enterable as chains like walls (along grid axes per GRD-005 in the grids epic). WAL-007 (M) cycles the reference location with a key while drawing walls; the beam tool offers the same key for its anchor so both linear tools behave alike. Appendix D.8 needs a beam tool shortcut. The wall chain exists (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:464-477 today; point-input-snapping-14 commits each wall chain as one AddElements in tools/wall.rs), and BEA-010 asks beams to behave like it.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/beam.rs: ToolKind::Beam with BeamMode::{Single, Chain} as an InputConsumer. Single: two commits add Project::new_beam(storey, a, b). Chain, exactly like the wall chain after point-input-snapping-14: points accumulate in the step state and the whole chain is committed as one Command::AddElements (one undo step) on Enter, a double click, a click on the first point (closing) or the context menu's Finish; switching tool or storey commits an open chain of two or more points; Backspace and Esc on a clean step remove the last point; consecutive beams share end points exactly and keep the default elevations. Preview: the beam's plan footprint (width with anchor column and lateral offset) along the rubber band plus its axis. The R key cycles the anchor column (left, centre, right) within the row of the default anchor and reports 'Beam anchor: top-centre' in the status line, through SetToolDefaults like the wall R key (views/plan.rs:712-720). Action::ToolBeam with shortcut B, toolbox button, Design menu item, select_all mapping. properties.rs beam fields via the shared member_fields helper from task 10: section kind (Rectangular width and height, Profile with the beams flag), anchor grid, lateral offset, roll, start elevation, end elevation, pitch (editable, applied through Beam::with_pitch), start cut and end cut (Vertical, Horizontal, Angle with an angle field), material; derived rows: length, cross-section area, volume. Out of scope: grid-axis placement (GRD-005), junction cleanup between chain beams (BEA-004, cleanup-and-trims), curved beams (BEA-009).
design: Reuse the wall chain state handling of point-input-snapping-14 (one AddElements per chain), but beams carry no reference-line side, so closing a chain needs no orientation fix-up. Chain beams create no junction relations: BEA-004 will detect axis contact the way the junction engine does for walls. The pitch field edits a derived value: on commit it calls Beam::with_pitch and issues one UpdateElements with the new end elevation. Pitfalls: each R press currently records one undo step (WAL-007 gap); task 12 makes consecutive presses coalesce for walls and beams; the preview footprint must include the lateral offset and anchor column so that it matches the body of task 07.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/beam.rs tests: Single mode, two commits create one beam with the snapped end points and the D.2 elevations; Chain mode, four points and Enter create three beams named B-001 to B-003 with beam[i].end equal to beam[i+1].start bit for bit in one AddElements, so one undo removes the whole chain; Backspace before Enter drops the last point; closing on the first point creates the closing beam; switching tool with three pending points commits two beams; R cycles TopCentre to TopRight to TopLeft and back.
- kittest: pressing B selects the tool; a three-segment chain drawn in a plan creates three beams; setting the pitch to 10 degrees in the strip updates the end elevation with one UpdateElements; setting a level beam's end cut to Horizontal shows the validation message and leaves the beam unchanged.
- actions tests include the beam tool shortcut (D.8).
- Satisfies the chain clause of BEA-010, BEA-001 placement and parameter editing including the pitch input, and BEA-002 numeric end-cut editing.
notes:
SRS: BEA-010 BEA-001 BEA-002 WAL-007
Appendix D.2 beam defaults; D.8 beam tool shortcut (B proposed). The grid-axis clause of BEA-010 depends on GRD-001/GRD-005 and stays open until the grids epic.

title: Add reference levels and the single vertical datum to the model
description:
WHY: STR-007 (S): besides storeys the system supports named reference levels (project zero, sea level and user-defined levels); elevations can be entered and displayed relative to any of them, while stored elevations stay relative to project zero. STR-011 (M): the project holds one vertical datum, the altitude of project zero above sea level; every import, elevation readout and IFCX export uses it, and no import requires entering it a second time. Today only Location.altitude exists (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:64-73), edited in the Project settings dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:553-564) and written as bsi::ifc::prop::RefElevation on the site node (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:276-279) and as archicraft::project.location.altitude (writer.rs:167, read back at reader.rs:373); there are no reference levels and nothing converts between levels (gap rows: STR-007 missing, STR-011 partial).

WHAT: archicraft-model: new module levels.rs with `ReferenceLevel { id: LevelId, name: String, elevation: f64 }` (elevation relative to project zero; LevelId added to ids.rs) and `LevelRef { ProjectZero, SeaLevel, User(LevelId) }`; ProjectSettings gains `reference_levels: Vec<ReferenceLevel>` (user levels only) and `elevation_reference: LevelRef` (default ProjectZero); Project gains vertical_datum() (the one accessor of Location.altitude), level_elevation(LevelRef) (0, -altitude, or the user level's elevation), level_name(LevelRef) and levels() (Project zero, Sea level, then the user levels). Command::SetReferenceLevels { levels, reference } (label 'Change reference levels') is validated for unique non-empty names (case-insensitive, 'Project zero' and 'Sea level' reserved), finite elevations within ±10,000 m and an existing reference, and falls back to ProjectZero when the referenced level is deleted in the same command. units.rs: format_elevation(z, level_elevation, units, nf, with_unit) with an explicit sign (+3.000, -0.500, ±0.000) and parse_elevation(text, level_elevation, unit, nf) accepting +, - and ±. archicraft-ifcx: optional settings.referenceLevels [{id, name, elevation}] and settings.elevationReference ('projectZero', 'seaLevel' or a level id) in archicraft::project, written only when there are user levels or the reference is not ProjectZero; a reader helper read_datum() takes location.altitude and cross-checks the site's RefElevation (warning when they differ by more than MODEL_TOLERANCE, the archicraft value wins; RefElevation alone is used when the archicraft member is missing, the path third-party import will take). Out of scope: UI (task 04), EPSG height attributes and georeferencing (IFX-070, terrain-and-site), third-party import (ifcx-interop, which calls read_datum); every later import path (IFX-081/082 third-party files, IFX-084 linked reference models) takes the datum through read_datum, recorded as an extension point by the done task.
design: Approach: store only user levels. Project zero is 0 by definition and sea level is -altitude, so the datum exists exactly once and cannot drift (STR-011 'one vertical datum').
