All conversion is display-side: stored z = shown value + level_elevation(reference); nothing in the model stores a datum-relative value, which is the epic's guard against conversion errors leaking into storage (asserted here and by the widget tests of task 04). A dedicated command instead of SetSettings gives a meaningful undo label and lets the dialog of task 04 apply each row edit immediately; it replaces settings.reference_levels and elevation_reference as one snapshot edit (prefer existing Set* snapshot primitives, per the add-a-command recipe in docs/implementation-status.md). Sign convention follows Appendix D.1 ('±0.000', '+3.000'); NumberFormat keeps separators (units.rs:243-268) and feet-inches values get the sign prefix too. Reader: lenient as everywhere (report.or); an unknown elevationReference becomes ProjectZero with a warning. Pitfalls: ProjectSettings derives PartialEq and SetSettings detects NoChange by comparison, so Vec order matters (keep insertion order); LevelId is a v4 UUID like the other ids; optional additions need no FORMAT_VERSION bump (rule of element-kind-framework-12). SetReferenceLevels produces Edit::SetSettings, which the ChangeLog of element-kind-framework-10 treats as a full invalidation (tessellation): stamp the full invalidation in Edit::apply only when old and new tessellation differ, so level, reference and ID-prefix edits re-evaluate nothing. Pointers: project.rs:45-73, units.rs:281-308 and 391-424, writer.rs:146-190 and 276-279, reader.rs:330-375, alpha/schema.rs:130-215, command.rs:288-302 (SetLocation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/levels.rs: with altitude 412.0, level_elevation(SeaLevel) == -412.0 and level_elevation(ProjectZero) == 0.0; a user level 'Finished floor' at 0.15 returns 0.15; levels() lists Project zero, Sea level, then user levels in insertion order.
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs: format_elevation(3.0, -412.0) with metres and 3 decimals is "+415.000"; format_elevation(0.0, 0.0) is "±0.000"; parse_elevation("+415.000", -412.0) returns 3.0 (|difference| < 1e-9) and parse_elevation("±0", 0.0) returns 0.0; decimal-comma and feet-inches cases; format then parse returns the stored value within display precision for 1,000 pseudo-random elevations (fixed seed).
- Command tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: SetReferenceLevels rejects a duplicate name, 'Sea level' as a user level name, NaN and 20,000 m elevations and an unknown reference, each with CommandError::Invalid and an unchanged project; deleting the referenced level resets the reference to ProjectZero; execute followed by undo restores the starting project.
- One-datum test in crates/archicraft-model/tests: a source scan finds no struct field named altitude, datum or sea_level in crates/archicraft-model/src other than Location.altitude, and levels() derives the Sea level elevation from vertical_datum() instead of storing it.
- IFCX tests in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: user levels and the reference survive save and load; written referenceLevels contain user levels only; the datum value appears in the file exactly as location.altitude and as the site's RefElevation, both taken from vertical_datum(); a file whose RefElevation differs from location.altitude loads with one warning and the archicraft value; a file without an archicraft location but with RefElevation 412 loads with altitude 412 and no prompt or error.
- No golden data node changes (no sample adds a user level and the reference stays ProjectZero, neither is written); the goldens are re-blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 for the new optional referenceLevels/elevationReference declarations in the embedded schemas section and the reviewed diff is limited to them; conformance/run.sh green; written_files_validate_without_problems green.
- Dirty-set test on the element-kind-framework-10 API: SetReferenceLevels and a SetSettings that changes only non-geometric settings (for example an ID prefix of task 02) dirty no element, while a tessellation change still re-evaluates every element.
- Satisfies the model and file parts of STR-007 and STR-011 (one datum, exported and re-read without asking twice); the readouts follow in task 04.
notes:
SRS: STR-007 STR-011
IFX-070 (terrain-and-site) owns the EPSG height attribute and the SurveyPoint child; this task keeps RefElevation as written today. Open question: a per-field override of the display reference is deferred (one project-wide reference meets 'relative to any of them'). Appendix D.1 storeys: 00 Ground floor ±0.000 m and 01 First floor +3.000 m (the sign convention used by format_elevation).

title: Mark references by dwell or key and generate inference guides
description:
WHY: The user shall be able to mark points and edges as snap references by hovering for a configurable dwell time (default 1.0 s, Appendix D.1) or instantly with a key; marked references generate temporary inference guides: horizontal, vertical, angle increments, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, the bisector of two marked edges and the line through two circle centres; guide intersections are snappable, and marks clear when the input ends or on Esc (INP-011). Guide intersections and guides take their places in the precedence of INP-009, the constraint modifier may hold the cursor on the nearest guide (INP-006), and absolute coordinates may be measured from a temporarily marked snap point (INP-004). None of this exists today: no dwell timer, no marks, no guide generation.

WHAT: Add input/marks.rs: Marks { points, edges, circles } capped at 8 (oldest dropped), identified by (TargetOwner, segment index) so they survive incremental index updates. PointInput::tick(now, &Resolved) marks the hovered snap when the cursor has stayed on the same snap for the dwell time; Q marks instantly (provisional). Add input/inference.rs: generate(&Marks, previous, increment) -> Vec<GuideShape> producing horizontal, vertical and angle-increment lines through every marked point and through the previous point, parallels and perpendiculars to each marked edge through the previous point and the marked points, tangents from the previous point to marked circles, both bisectors of two marked edges and the line through two marked circle centres. candidates() takes these guides and yields GuideIntersection and Guide candidates; Shift holds the cursor on the nearest guide (hook from task 08); Origin::Marked resolves to the latest marked point. Marks clear on finish, on tool switch and on the first Esc, and survive commits within one input. Preference snap_dwell_seconds (default 1.0, clamp 0.2–5.0) with a dialog row. Marks are drawn as small glyphs, inference guides dashed and clipped to the view. Out of scope: persistent guides (11), tangents to arc walls (curved-geometry).
design: Dwell time comes from the egui input time already read in plan.rs (ui.input(|i| i.time), plan.rs:396) passed into tick(); tests advance a plain f64 clock. Guides are regenerated only when the marks or the previous point change (at most 8 marks × about 6 guides) and intersected lazily inside candidates() with the edges and guides within the radius (GuideShape::intersect from task 08), so the 50 ms budget holds. Infinite lines are clipped to the view rect for drawing (Liang–Barsky). Angle-increment lines use prefs.angle_increment_deg. If a marked owner disappears (deleted or excluded), the mark is dropped. Tangent and centre-line guides are tested against synthetic circles until guide circles (task 11) and arc walls (curved-geometry) exist. Add the dwell row next to the snap rows of the Preferences dialog (the 'Input' group once task 14 has landed).
acceptance_criteria:
- Dwell tests with an injected clock: hovering 0.9 s does not mark, 1.0 s marks; moving off the snap resets the timer; Q marks instantly; the ninth mark drops the oldest.
- Guide tests: a marked point yields horizontal, vertical and increment lines (four lines at 45°); a marked edge yields a parallel and a perpendicular through the previous point; two marked edges at 90° yield bisectors at 45° and 135°; a previous point outside a marked circle yields two tangents; two marked circles yield the line through their centres.
- Precedence tests: guide ∩ edge and guide ∩ guide are GuideIntersection candidates below Division and above Edge; a Guide candidate ranks below Edge and above Grid.
- Clearing tests: the first Esc clears marks (with typed text and locks) before any point is dropped; finish() clears them; a commit keeps them; typed absolute coordinates from the marked point resolve correctly.
- Nearest-guide test (INP-006): with an inference guide within the radius, Shift holds the cursor on the nearest guide (its projection) instead of an angle-increment direction; with no guide in range Shift constrains directions as before.
- Owner test: a mark on an element that is deleted, or that stops providing snaps through task 12's Project::provides_snaps, is dropped on the next index update.
- Preference test: snap_dwell_seconds round-trips through Preferences, sanitized() clamps it to 0.2–5.0, and the Preferences dialog shows a 'Reference dwell (s)' row.
- kittest: after advancing the harness clock by 1.0 s over a wall corner a mark glyph is drawn, and the label reads 'guide' when the cursor sits on an inference guide.
- Satisfies INP-011, completes the guide levels of INP-009, the nearest-guide clause of INP-006 and the marked-point origin of INP-004.
notes:
SRS: INP-011 INP-009 INP-006 INP-004
Appendix D.1: reference dwell 1.0 s. Provisional binding: Q marks the hovered snap instantly; confirm with commands-and-l10n (D.8).

title: Rotate plan views with snapping and constraints on rotated axes
description:
WHY: VIEW-060 (S): a 2D view is rotatable, for example to align with a building wing, without rotating the model; the epic acceptance requires that snapping and constraints follow the rotated axes, and VIEW-004 stores rotation in saved views. Gap row: Camera2d has only center and scale (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/camera.rs:13-16).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/camera.rs: Camera2d.rotation (radians, view-only) used by to_screen, to_world, pan, zoom_at and fit; ZoomHistory records it. crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draw_grid draws in the rotated frame. crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs: snap() computes grid points in the view frame and constrain() takes a base angle so increments are measured from the view's x axis. Actions: SetViewRotation (numeric field in the plan status bar), RotateViewByTwoPoints (two clicks; the picked direction becomes screen X), ResetViewRotation (View menu). Rotation is captured into and applied from ViewCamera::Plan.rotation (09). Out of scope: 3D views, typed absolute coordinates (stay in model axes), the user origin (point-input-snapping).
design: screen = R(-theta)(p - center) x scale with +Y up flipped as today; to_world applies the inverse. Grid: transform the visible rect corners into the view frame, iterate lattice lines there, map back. Snap grid: rotate the cursor into the view frame, round to the step, rotate back. constrain(from, to, increment, base) adds base before rounding. The project origin marker stays on the model axes, which makes the rotation visible. If point-input-snapping has landed, expose the frame through its ViewSurface so locks, guides and inference use the rotated axes; the snap radius in screen points is unaffected. Pitfalls: pan deltas and keyboard nudges are in screen space and must be rotated; ZoomHistory equality now includes rotation; camera changes never create undo steps (existing behaviour). If point-input-snapping-08 has landed, the view rotation is one more frame source for constraint directions next to the construction-grid rotation (its preference decides which one applies).
acceptance_criteria:
- camera.rs unit tests: to_world(to_screen(p)) == p within 1e-9 for rotations 0, 30, -90 and 123.4 degrees; zoom_at keeps the anchor under the cursor; fit contains the rotated bounds.
- tools.rs tests: in a 30 degree view the grid snap returns points of the rotated lattice; constrain with a 45 degree increment returns directions of 30 + k x 45 degrees.
- Headless test: drawing a wall with the constraint modifier in a 30 degree view yields a wall along 30 degrees in model coordinates; rotating the view leaves the model revision unchanged.
- A saved plan view stores and re-applies its rotation (capture/apply of 09).
- kittest: 'Reset view rotation' is in the View menu and sets the active plan's rotation to 0.
- Satisfies VIEW-060.
notes: SRS: VIEW-060. Open question: whether typed polar angles should be relative to the rotated view (kept absolute here).

title: Persist display ranges, plan display and view-range limits in IFCX
description:
WHY: IFX-060 (M) requires everything needed to restore the editable model in archicraft:: attributes; PRJ-007 and SET-002 (M) require project-level settings, including cut-plane defaults and views, in the project file so every user who opens it sees the same values. The ELM-008, ELM-009, ELM-018, VIEW-011 and VIEW-012 data added in 01 would otherwise be dropped on save. Gap rows: SET-002 and PRJ-007 are partial; the writer stores only the per-storey cut plane (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:318) and the project cut-plane default (writer.rs:162). Exists and kept (PRJ-007/SET-002 partial): project_attribute (writer.rs:144-190) already writes units, the cut-plane default, tessellation, location, layers, materials, tool defaults and views; storeys are nodes with cutPlaneHeight (writer.rs:298-322); read_project_data (reader.rs:301-431) restores them and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:48-62 asserts Project equality. Missing: the keys below.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs, writer.rs and reader.rs: archicraft::element gains 'displayRange' {mode, up?, down?, outline?, coverFill?} and 'planDisplay' (enumeration from PlanDisplay); archicraft::storey gains optional 'viewRange' {bottom: {storeys, offset}, top: {storeys, offset}} next to cutPlaneHeight; archicraft::project settings gain 'remoteStoreyStyle' {above, below: {pattern, color?, cutFill}}; material records gain optional 'coverFill' with the cutFill shape (skipped if plan-attributes already writes cover-fill references). FORMAT_VERSION is bumped once for this epic (an older ArchiCraft would otherwise drop the new keys on save; IFX-062 makes it warn instead) with an entry in MIGRATIONS of crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs (created by element-kind-framework-12) that fills descriptor defaults for files of the previous version; before re-blessing, freeze crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/format-v<N>/walls-and-slab.ifcx (N = the version current when this task starts) as a copy of the current golden and never regenerate it. The round-trip project of the acceptance test is built inside crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs; the existing goldens are re-blessed (every element gains displayRange and planDisplay) and reviewed; golden coverage of Custom, a storey viewRange and a non-default remote style comes from samples::display_ranges() of task 04, which therefore waits for this task. Out of scope: views, folders and layer combinations (08).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md: declare with object()/optional() in schema.rs, enumerations derived from the model ALL arrays via .map(code), write in element_attributes/project_attribute and the storey block, read with report.or(...) defaults. The envelope fields belong to archicraft::element (common data), not to the per-kind codecs of the framework. Write displayRange and planDisplay for every element (explicit and byte-stable) but viewRange only when Some (mirrors cutPlaneHeight). Parameters are written at full precision (float_roundtrip, NFR-ACC-002); only mesh coordinates are rounded. Pitfall: reader downgrades must use the element's kind descriptor, so read the kind before the envelope; keep the migration entry idempotent.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: a project with every DisplayRange mode, a Custom{up 2, down 1, outline on, cover fill off}, each PlanDisplay, a storey viewRange override, a non-default RemoteStoreyStyle and a material cover fill is equal after write and read.
- A file of the previous FORMAT_VERSION (the frozen crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/format-v<N>/walls-and-slab.ifcx) opens without error, elements get their descriptor defaults and the migration report names the upgrade (IFX-062).
- Unknown mode codes, Custom on a wall or a planDisplay outside the kind's set read as the descriptor default with a warning Problem (PRJ-008: nothing is dropped silently).
- All new keys are declared in the schemas section and the offline validator (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs) accepts the files (IFX-061); conformance/run.sh is green on the re-blessed goldens; the golden diff touches only archicraft:: attributes (IFX-063).
- Persistence of ELM-008, ELM-009, ELM-018, VIEW-011 and VIEW-012 data and the cut-plane-defaults clause of PRJ-007/SET-002 are satisfied.
notes: SRS: ELM-008 ELM-009 ELM-018 VIEW-011 VIEW-012 PRJ-007 SET-002. One FORMAT_VERSION bump for the epic: 08 adds further optional keys under the same version if no release happens in between.

title: Draw and snap to the construction grid and the rotated snap grid
description:
WHY: A drafting grid shall be provided, configured per view type with one plan grid shared by all storeys: an invisible snap grid with X/Y steps and a visible construction grid with main and auxiliary spacing, rotation and local origin whose intersections are snappable; in 3D the working plane carries the same grid (INP-013). Constraint directions are measured from the X axis or from the construction-grid orientation (INP-006). Today the snap grid is a single step in user preferences (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:45-46, dialogs.rs:733-738) applied by snap() as plain rounding (views/tools.rs:254-262), the visible grid is a fixed power-of-ten display grid (views/plan.rs:150-190) and its intersections are not snap targets. Task 16 stores the PlanGrid in the project settings; this task makes input and drawing use it.

WHAT: Grid candidates come from ProjectSettings.plan_grid (task 16), the same for every storey: snap-grid rounding in the grid frame (origin and rotation, Frame2d of task 07) plus the construction-grid intersections (main and auxiliary) within the radius, both at Grid level; snap_enabled false switches the snap grid off. ViewSurface::frame() and InputContext expose the grid rotation so the constraint directions of task 08 follow it when its preference selects the grid orientation. Remove snap_step from Preferences and its dialog row (dialogs.rs:733-738); old preferences files still load. plan.rs draws the construction grid (main and auxiliary lines, rotated about the local origin) when visible and keeps the adaptive power-of-ten grid (plan.rs:150-190) as the background when hidden. UI: a 'Drafting grid' dialog in ui/dialogs.rs opened from the View menu (ui/shell.rs:78) with snap step X/Y, main and auxiliary spacing, rotation and origin, committing through Command::SetSettings as one undo step, plus the actions 'Show construction grid' and 'Snap to grid' in ui/actions.rs, which toggle PlanGrid.visible and PlanGrid.snap_enabled the same way. Out of scope: the PlanGrid model and its IFCX persistence (task 16), the working-plane grid in 3D (3d-input-navigation reuses PlanGrid through ViewSurface::frame()) and grids for section views (sections-elevations-dims).
design: Both grids share the construction grid's origin and rotation (decision: a snap grid that ignored the grid rotation would fight the constraint directions). Rounding: frame.to_local(cursor), round per axis by snap_step, frame.from_local. Construction intersections: find the lattice cell around the cursor in the grid frame and offer its corners within the radius; lines that are not on the main spacing are auxiliary lines. Drawing: compute the visible lattice range in the grid frame from the view rect; skip drawing when more than 4,000 lines would be visible (like plan.rs:158-161). Pitfall: Preferences is #[serde(default)] without deny_unknown_fields (prefs.rs:27-29), so an old snap_step key is ignored; keep it that way and test it. The dialog edits a copy of ProjectSettings and executes one SetSettings on OK, so dragging a value does not flood the history.
acceptance_criteria:
- Input tests: snap-grid rounding in a frame rotated by 30° with origin (1, 1) lands on the rotated lattice; construction intersections (main and auxiliary) are Grid-level candidates below Guide; snap_enabled false yields no snap-grid candidates; with the grid orientation selected Shift directions follow the rotation (30°, 75°, …).
- One plan grid for all storeys: the ground and upper floor of two_storey_shell yield identical Grid candidates for the same cursor; changing the grid in the dialog creates exactly one undo step and undo restores the previous candidates.
- Preferences test: an old preferences file containing snap_step still loads with every other value intact.
- Drawing: a kittest frame with the construction grid visible and rotated by 30° renders without panic and skips drawing when more than 4,000 lines would be visible; with it hidden the adaptive background grid is drawn as before.
- kittest: the View menu opens the 'Drafting grid' dialog with 'Snap step', 'Main spacing', 'Auxiliary spacing', 'Rotation' and 'Origin'; 'Show construction grid' and 'Snap to grid' exist.
- Satisfies INP-013 for plan views (storage in task 16) and the grid-orientation clause of INP-006 (the working-plane grid follows in 3d-input-navigation through the same PlanGrid frame).
notes:
SRS: INP-013 INP-006
No Appendix D drafting-grid default (the 6.00 m 'Grid' row of D.2 is the structural grid of GRD); defaults are set in task 16. The 3D working plane reuses PlanGrid through ViewSurface::frame() in 3d-input-navigation.

title: Complete WAL-007: 3D reference lines, preview arrows, one undo step
description:
WHY: WAL-007 (M): while drawing, a key shall cycle the reference-line location; the reference line and its direction shall be shown while drawing and when a wall is selected; a view option shows the reference lines of all walls and beams and never affects exported data. Gap (partial, S): reference lines appear only in plan views, not in 3D (render3d.rs build_scene draws meshes and feature edges only); the in-progress preview has no direction arrow; beams did not exist (now tasks 07 and 08); and the R key records a SetToolDefaults command in the undo history on every press (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:712-720).

Exists (keep and regress): the R key cycles the wall reference line (views/plan.rs:712-720, ReferenceLine::next element.rs:118-125); the plan draws the selected wall's reference line, or all with the view option, with a direction arrow (views/plan.rs:290-298, reference_line() at 225-235); the tool preview draws the pending line without an arrow (views/tools.rs:553-555, views/plan.rs:585-593); prefs.show_reference_lines (persistence/prefs.rs:48) is toggled from the View menu (ui/shell.rs:89-93, app.rs:447-449) and lives outside the project, so export is unaffected.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-app/src/views/overlay3d.rs: project(view_proj, scene_origin, rect, p: DVec3) -> Option<Pos2> (None behind the near plane) and a polyline-with-arrow painter. views/view3d.rs draws ElementGeometry.axis of selected walls and beams, and of all walls and beams when prefs.show_reference_lines is on, over the 3D image in the plan's reference and selection colours with a direction arrow at the midpoint. views/plan.rs draws the pending segment of the wall and beam tools with reference_line() (plan.rs:225-235) so the preview shows the direction. Model: History::execute_coalescing(project, command) merges a SetToolDefaults into the previous transaction when that transaction is also a coalesced SetToolDefaults and nothing was executed, undone or redone in between, keeping the first inverse and the newest forward edits; the wall R handler (views/plan.rs:712-720 today, in tools/wall.rs if point-input-snapping-01 moved key handling into the consumer) and the beam R handler of task 11 use it. Out of scope: reference lines in sections and elevations (sections-elevations-dims), storing the option per saved view (plan-views-browser).
design: An egui overlay instead of a GPU line pass: the axes must stay visible inside bodies (a centre-anchored beam axis lies inside the beam), the selection already redraws the frame, and no shader or FrameKey change is needed; points are transformed with the same view_proj and scene origin that view3d.rs passes to Renderer3d::render (view3d.rs:215-221). Coalescing lives in History, not in the app, so undo semantics stay testable headlessly; only SetToolDefaults is coalescable, and only through the explicit method, so ordinary property edits keep one undo step each. Pitfall: the coalesced transaction must keep the original inverse, otherwise undo returns to an intermediate state; the 3D overlay helper is reused by the handles of task 13.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: five coalesced SetToolDefaults followed by one undo restore the original defaults; an AddElements in between breaks coalescing (two undo steps); redo after undo reapplies the last state; the journal still records every execution.
- overlay3d.rs unit tests: a point in front of the camera projects inside the rect, a point behind it returns None.
- Headless app test: selecting a wall in a 3D view yields overlay segments for its axis with an arrow; with the view option on, the overlay contains every wall and beam axis of two_storey_shell plus an added beam; with the option off and nothing selected it is empty.
- The wall tool and beam tool previews contain a direction arrow (preview test through the arrow helper).
- Saving with the view option on and off produces byte-identical files apart from the header timestamp.
- Regression: the plan still draws the selected wall's reference line with its arrow and all reference lines with the view option on (existing behaviour unchanged).
- WAL-007 is fully satisfied (status partial to done in docs/implementation-status.md).
notes: SRS: WAL-007

title: Draw beams and columns in plan: projected, overhead and axis lines
description:
WHY: BEA-008 (M): in plan, beams below the cut plane shall be drawn projected and beams above it as overhead outlines (default dashed), with an optional axis line; angled end cuts appear correctly in both representations. WAL-007 (M): a view option shows the reference lines of all walls and beams and never affects exported data. INP-008 (M) snaps to the axis points of columns and beams; point-input-snapping left that SnapSource to this epic. Today crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:131-147 classifies whole parts by their z-bounds and draws up- and down-facing outlines (mesh.rs:195-237): a part crossing the cut contributes only its cut polygon, so an inclined beam crossing the cut plane shows nothing below or above it, the crease where a top face meets an angled end face is never drawn, and the axis line exists for walls only (PlanElement.reference_line, plan.rs:148-150).

WHAT: Geometry: TriMesh::facing_outline_clipped(up, limit) clips triangles to z <= cut (projected) or z >= cut (overhead) and drops boundary edges lying on the cut plane, used by plan_drawing for parts that cross the cut; TriMesh::up_facing_creases(min_angle_deg) adds the visible creases between two up-facing faces to projected lines; PlanElement.reference_line keeps its name and type (plan-views-browser and curved-geometry build on it) and is filled for beams with the anchor line; a new `axis_point: Option<DVec2>` carries the column axis point; both come from a per-kind plan hook of the geometry registry (GeometryKind::plan_axis), so plan.rs drops its as_wall match (plan.rs:148-150) and keeps no kind match. App: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draws beam axes with the wall reference-line style (selected, or all with prefs.show_reference_lines; the View menu entry in ui/shell.rs:89-93 is relabelled 'Reference lines and axes') and column axis points as a small cross; crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs gains MemberAxisSource implementing the point-input SnapSource: column axis points and beam axis end and mid points as node targets, beam axes as edge targets; MemberAxisSource also implements the point-input ContextProvider (input/context.rs, point-input-snapping-13) with column section outlines and beam footprint edges, so live context distances include columns and beams (the INP-021 provider hand-off). Out of scope: elements from other storeys (plan-views-browser), per-kind display options ELM-018, pens and hatches (plan-attributes, plan-renderer), priority cleanup of columns and beams against walls and slabs (cleanup-and-trims).
design: Clipping uses Sutherland-Hodgman per triangle against the horizontal plane (a triangle or quad, fan-split); crossing points are computed with the endpoints in lexicographic order, as slice.rs does, so triangles sharing an edge produce bit-identical points and the existing Key2 edge counting of facing_outline (mesh.rs:207-230) still finds the region boundary. Edges whose endpoints both lie on the cut plane within MODEL_TOLERANCE are dropped because the cut outline already draws them. Creases reuse the feature_edges logic (mesh.rs:239) restricted to edges whose two faces both face up, with a 1 degree threshold, so coplanar triangulation edges never appear. Walls and slabs are unaffected: their side faces have zero z-facing and their tops and bottoms lie wholly on one side. The overhead dashed style already exists (views/plan.rs:246-262). Axis lines are not added to PlanElement::segments(), so the snap index does not see them twice; MemberAxisSource is the only producer of axis targets. Pitfall: plan-views-browser will replace the home-storey loop (plan.rs:120) with a z-extent index; keep the change at the per-part classification level so both merge cleanly.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs plan cases: the D.2 beam on the ground floor (bottom 2.30 m, cut 1.10 m) yields only overhead segments forming its footprint rectangle; the same beam with its top at 0.80 m yields only projected segments; a projected beam with an Angle(30 degrees) end cut yields the footprint outline plus one crease segment, both matching analytic coordinates within 1e-9; an overhead beam with the same cut yields exactly the analytic footprint outline and no crease.
- An inclined beam from 0.30 m to 2.50 m crossing the cut yields its cut polygon, projected segments only where z < 1.10 and overhead segments only where z > 1.10, with no segment duplicated on the cut outline.
- The D.2 column is cut with a reinforced-concrete fill region that merges with touching reinforced-concrete cut regions (unary_union), and exposes axis_point at its position.
- Regression: the plan segments of storey_with_walls_and_slab and two_storey_shell are unchanged (sorted coordinates compared with the output before this task), because vertical extrusions gain no clipped or crease segments.
- App tests: a cursor within the snap radius of a column's axis point snaps as a node to it; on a beam axis it snaps to the midpoint (node) or the axis (edge); with the view option on, the plan shows the axes of all beams and walls; saving with the option on and off gives identical bytes apart from the header timestamp.
- Context distances: with the wall tool's reference edge 0.40 m from a column face the context distance to that face reads 0.40 m; the same holds for a beam footprint edge.
- Satisfies BEA-008 (projected, overhead dashed by default, cut, optional axis line, angled end cuts) and the beam part of WAL-007's view option; delivers INP-008's column/beam axis-point snap clause.
notes:
SRS: BEA-008 WAL-007
Also touches INP-008 (axis points of columns and beams) and INP-021 (column and beam context-distance providers, handed over by point-input-snapping-13). Appendix D.1: plan cut plane 1.10 m above the storey, view range from the storey elevation to the next storey.

title: Add the Profile resource with commands and validation
description:
WHY: PRF-004 (M): the system shall provide named profiles, usable by columns and beams; a profile is edited in a profile editor as one or more closed regions, holes allowed, each region with a material, plus an insertion origin and flags for the element kinds that may use it; editing a profile shall update every element that uses it. PRF-005 (M): parametric standard profiles shall be available: rectangle, circle, rectangular and circular hollow sections, I/H, T, L, U/C and Z shapes defined by their dimensions. SRS 3.4 makes the profile a project resource referenced by stable ID, and PRJ-007 stores profiles in the project file. Status: PRF-004 missing ('no Profile type anywhere', XL), PRF-005 missing (gap row: the parametric definition must be stored, not only the polygon). The command core has resource edits only for layers and materials (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:616-633 and :686-712), and plan_delete_material (command.rs:520-552) and Project::integrity_problems (project.rs:327) know nothing about materials referenced by profile regions. Every later task of this epic (sections, kinds, persistence, editor) builds on this resource.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/src/profile.rs and ProfileId (one id_type! line in ids.rs). `Profile { id, name, shape: ProfileShape, origin: DVec2, usage: ProfileUsage, catalogue: Option<String> }`; `ProfileShape::{Parametric { shape: ParametricShape, material: MaterialId }, Custom { regions: Vec<ProfileRegion> }}`; `ParametricShape::{Rectangle { width, height }, Circle { diameter }, RectangularHollow { width, height, thickness, outer_radius }, CircularHollow { diameter, thickness }, IShape { height, width, web, flange, root_radius }, TShape { height, width, web, flange, root_radius }, LShape { height, width, thickness, root_radius, toe_radius }, UShape { height, width, web, flange, root_radius }, ZShape { height, width, web, flange }}` with code()/label()/ALL; `ProfileRegion { outer: Vec<DVec2>, holes: Vec<Vec<DVec2>>, material }`; `ProfileUsage { columns, beams, walls, railings }` (walls and railings stored for PRF-010, not enforced yet); `Profile::bounds()` (analytic for parametric shapes, which are centred on their bounding box; ring bounds for custom), `materials()`. `Project.profiles: Vec<Profile>` (#[serde(default)]) with profile(id) and profile_users(id). Add `fn profiles(&self) -> Vec<ProfileId>` (empty default) and `fn replace_profile(&mut self, from: ProfileId, to: ProfileId) -> bool` (no-op default) to the framework's Kind trait (kinds/mod.rs), so users and DefaultsSlot prototypes are found and re-pointed without kind matches in command.rs. Edit::apply records InsertProfile, RemoveProfile and ReplaceProfile in both directions as changed profile ids in Project.changes (the ChangeLog of element-kind-framework-10), which task 06 turns into dirty elements. validate.rs: validate_profile(&Project, &Profile) -> Result<Profile, String> (dimension ranges and consistency, material references, custom rings normalised with validate_slab_polygon, regions of a custom profile must not overlap, touching is allowed). command.rs: Command::{AddProfile(Profile), UpdateProfile(Profile), DeleteProfile { profile, replacement: Option<ProfileId> }} with labels; Edit::{InsertProfile { index, profile }, RemoveProfile { id }, ReplaceProfile(Profile)} mirroring the material edits; plan_delete_profile re-points users and tool-default slots to the replacement through Kind::replace_profile (rejected when the replacement lacks a needed usage flag, Invalid when in use and no replacement); UpdateProfile re-validates every user through validate_element and rejects removing a usage flag that a user needs; plan_delete_material also reassigns parametric and region materials of profiles with ReplaceProfile edits; integrity_problems reports dangling profile materials. Out of scope: section polygons (task 03), persistence (02), the catalogue (04), the column and beam kinds (06, 07) and every UI (14, 15).
design: Follow the 'Add a command' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md (Extension points) and mirror Material: id_type!, Vec storage, Insert/Remove/Replace edits returning exact inverses via std::mem::replace, delete-with-replacement planning like plan_delete_material (command.rs:520-552). ProfileShape stores parameters only; polygons are generated in archicraft-geometry (task 03) so the model stays free of tessellation and of the geo dependency (archicraft-model depends only on glam, indexmap, serde, thiserror and uuid). The overlap check therefore uses the existing helpers segments_touch and point_in_ring in validate.rs (validate.rs:64-91): two regions overlap if an edge of one properly crosses an edge of the other or a vertex of one lies strictly inside the other; collinear shared edges are touching. Coordinate convention, documented on Profile: the profile plane is seen from the member's start looking along its axis (columns: looking down), x to the right, y up; parametric shapes are centred on their bounding box and origin defaults to DVec2::ZERO. Field names use the EN symbols in doc comments (h, b, tw, tf, r, r1, r2, t, D). Pitfalls: UpdateProfile must re-validate users, otherwise a deeper section could make a short beam's end cuts cross (BEA-002 validation in task 07); the user scan iterates project.elements through Kind::profiles(), so no kind-specific code enters command.rs (framework module-layout tests stay green); keep messages user-facing, for example 'Profile IPE 300 is used by 3 elements; choose a replacement'.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs: every ParametricShape variant accepts typical dimensions (IPE 200: h 200, b 100, tw 5.6, tf 8.5, r 12 mm; CHS 168.3 x 8; L 100 x 100 x 10, r1 12, r2 6) and rejects zero, negative, NaN and out-of-range values and inconsistent combinations (2 x flange >= height, RHS thickness >= half the smaller side, a root radius that does not fit between web and flange tip) with a message naming the field.
- Custom profiles: zero regions, a self-intersecting ring, a hole outside its region and two overlapping regions are rejected; two regions sharing an edge are accepted; outer rings are returned CCW and holes CW.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddProfile, UpdateProfile and DeleteProfile execute, undo to the exact starting project and redo; a duplicate id is rejected with CommandError::Invalid; an unchanged UpdateProfile returns CommandError::NoChange; deleting an unused profile succeeds (the re-pointing path through Kind::replace_profile is exercised by tasks 06 and 07 once users exist).
- Edit::InsertProfile, RemoveProfile and ReplaceProfile record the profile id in Project.changes on apply and on undo, so incremental evaluation sees profile edits.
- deleting_resources_requires_a_replacement is extended: deleting a material used by a parametric profile and by one region of a custom profile reassigns both to the replacement in one transaction, and undo restores both exactly.
- Project::integrity_problems lists a profile region whose material is missing; Profile::bounds returns (-width/2, -height/2)..(width/2, height/2) for every parametric shape (circle: diameter) and the ring bounds for custom profiles.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy and fmt are green; journal replay of a history without profiles still deserialises (serde default).
- Satisfies the model clauses of PRF-004 (named resource, regions with holes and materials, insertion origin, usage flags, update and delete semantics) and PRF-005 (parametric shapes stored by their dimensions).
notes:
SRS: PRF-004 PRF-005
Also touches PRJ-007 (profiles as project resources). Open question: the SRS gives no plain Z-shape fillet or lip parameters; ZShape is the hot-rolled form with sharp corners, cold-formed lipped Z sections are deferred. Usage flags for walls and railings are stored but only enforced for columns and beams until PRF-010 (members-profiles-adv).

title: Arithmetic expressions and field addressing in typed values
description:
WHY: Typed values shall accept arithmetic (+ − × ÷) and field addressing, for example X3 or A35 (INP-022), while unit suffixes and imperial fractions such as 3'-4 1/2" keep working in any unit setting (INP-005). INP-005 is done (parse_length and parse_angle with split_unit_suffix, parse_mixed_number and parse_feet_inches in units.rs:391-553, tests units.rs:557-643): keep it and regress it; the expression parser calls these functions for every operand instead of re-implementing unit and fraction parsing. Today parse_length reads one number plus a unit (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:391-424, '-' is only a sign), and the character whitelist in plan.rs:359-361 does not even admit *, × or ÷; the whitelist is listed as technical debt.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs (or a units/expr.rs submodule) add a tokenizer and recursive-descent parser with parse_length_expr and parse_angle_expr supporting + - − * × / ÷, parentheses and unit-suffixed operands, keeping mixed numbers and feet-inch fractions. TypedInput uses them for every field, and field addressing works when the active field is empty: x, y, z select the Cartesian fields, d and a the polar fields, l and c the stretch fields (switching the field set as needed). TypedInput::accepts(char) replaces is_numeric_input (plan.rs:359-361). Out of scope: references to other fields' values inside expressions.
design: Grammar: expr = term (('+' | '-') term)*; term = factor (('*' | '/') factor)*; factor = '-' factor | '(' expr ')' unit? | quantity; quantity = number unit? with the existing suffix and feet-inch rules of units.rs. Fraction rule (documented in the module doc and tested both ways): 'a b/c' (whole number, space, fraction) and anything containing a foot or inch mark is an imperial mixed number; a bare 'b/c' is a division. normalize_number_text (units.rs:471) runs first, so decimal commas and the typographic signs × ÷ − work. Operands are converted to metres before combining; multiplication and division need one dimensionless operand (length × length is rejected as 'not a length'). The model crate owns the grammar so it stays headless and fuzzable (regression-and-status fuzzes parsers). Pitfall: the suffixes m, mm, cm, ft, in share letters with no addressing letter, and addressing applies only to an empty field.
acceptance_criteria:
- units tests: '2.5+0.3' = 2.8 m; '3*1.2m' = 3.6 m; '(1+2)/2' = 1.5; '10/4' = 2.5 in the default unit; '2m-15cm' = 1.85 m; 3'-4 1/2" and 3′-4 1/2″ (typographic marks) still parse as feet-inches and '2 1/2' as a mixed number; '45+15' = 60° through parse_angle_expr; '2.5 +', '2//3' and '2m*3m' are errors with a message; every existing INP-005 test passes unchanged.
- Property test: 200 seeded random expressions of up to four decimal operands evaluate equal to the f64 computation within 1e-12.
- Addressing tests: 'a35' with the polar set sets the angle to 35°; 'x3' switches to the Cartesian set and sets ΔX to 3; a letter typed into a non-empty field is treated as a unit suffix, not an address.
- plan.rs no longer contains is_numeric_input; the accepted characters come from TypedInput::accepts (the done task drops the 'Typed-input character whitelist' technical-debt entry).
- Satisfies INP-022 and keeps INP-005 done.
notes:
SRS: INP-022 INP-005
Interpretation: 'field addressing' is read as a field letter typed first (X3 sets X to 3, A35 the angle to 35°); if the SRS authors meant spreadsheet-like references to other fields, the parser keeps a Token::FieldRef hook. The final letters are part of the D.8 keymap deliverable.

title: Make automatic element ID prefixes configurable per kind
description:
WHY: ELM-019 (S): new elements get an automatically incremented ID per kind with a configurable prefix (for example W-001, D-001). Counters per kind exist and are undoable (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:267-277 next_element_name, command.rs:331-334; after element-kind-framework they are a map keyed by kind and written as an array in archicraft::project), but the prefix is hard-coded in KindTag::name_prefix (element.rs:218-224, afterwards KindDescriptor.name_prefix), so an office cannot use its own convention (gap row ELM-019: 'not configurable in the project or template'). Tool defaults and templates live in the project (ELM-001), so the prefixes belong there too.

WHAT: archicraft-model: ProjectSettings gains `id_prefixes: BTreeMap<KindTag, String>` holding only overrides; `Project::id_prefix(kind)` returns the override or descriptor.name_prefix and next_element_name uses it (the format stays `{prefix}-{n:03}`); check_settings (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:595-611, run by Command::SetSettings) rejects an empty prefix, more than 8 characters, whitespace or characters other than letters, digits, '_' and '.', and a prefix that equals (case-insensitively) the effective prefix of another registered kind, each with an explanation; changing a prefix renames nothing and leaves the counters alone. template.rs keeps the descriptor defaults (no overrides). archicraft-ifcx: optional `settings.idPrefixes` array of {kind, prefix} in archicraft::project, written only when non-empty; unknown kinds are ignored with a warning. archicraft-app: Project settings dialog section 'Element IDs' (ui/dialogs.rs project_window) listing every registered kind with a prefix field and a weak preview of the next ID ('next: W-004'), applied with the dialog's OK through SetSettings. Out of scope: renaming existing elements to a new prefix, per-storey numbering, a configurable separator or digit count.
design: Approach: store overrides only, so templates and older files keep the descriptor defaults and no golden data node changes (only the embedded declaration); a BTreeMap keyed by KindTag (Ord derived through the kinds! macro of element-kind-framework) serialises deterministically. Validation sits in check_settings (command.rs:595-611), which takes &ProjectSettings only; the uniqueness rule needs nothing but KINDS, so its signature stays, and the dialog shows the model's message. A prefix edit is an Edit::SetSettings; task 03 makes the element-kind-framework-10 ChangeLog stamp a full invalidation only when the tessellation changed, so prefix edits dirty no geometry once both have landed. Uniqueness compares effective prefixes of all registered kinds case-insensitively; descriptor defaults are already unique (registry test of element-kind-framework-02), so only overrides can clash. Dialog: the project dialog already uses a draft and issues several commands on OK (dialogs.rs:608-616, a known debt); put the prefixes into draft.settings so they travel with SetSettings rather than adding a fifth command. Pitfalls: KindTag must serialise by code in IFCX, not by Rust variant name; the reader must keep unknown-kind entries out of the map so a later save does not write them back. Pointers: project.rs:45-62 and 267-277, element.rs:218-224, writer.rs project_attribute settings block (around 160-172), reader.rs settings read (around 330-360), alpha/schema.rs settings object (130-160), dialogs.rs:480-626.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs: without an override next_element_name(Wall, 0) is "W-001"; with the override "AW" and a wall counter of 3 it is "AW-004"; the counter value is not changed by setting the prefix.
- Command tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: SetSettings with a wall prefix of "", "A B", "ABCDEFGHI" or the slab prefix "sl" is rejected with CommandError::Invalid and a message naming the problem, and the project is unchanged; a valid change is one undo step, undo restores the old prefix, and the names of existing elements are unchanged.
- IFCX round trip: a project with a wall override saves and reloads with the same override; a file without idPrefixes loads without problems and with the descriptor defaults; no golden data node changes because no sample overrides a prefix, and the goldens are re-blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 only for the new optional settings.idPrefixes declaration in the embedded schemas section (reviewed diff: schemas only); written_files_validate_without_problems passes.
- kittest: in Project settings the 'Element IDs' section shows one row per registered kind; setting the wall prefix to 'AW' updates the preview label to 'next: AW-00n' before OK; after OK a wall added through the wall tool path is named 'AW-00n'.
- Satisfies ELM-019 (per-kind counter already present; the prefix is now configurable and stored in the project and therefore in templates).
notes:
SRS: ELM-019
Prefixes are written in archicraft::project.settings (IFX-060 authoring data). The SRS example D-001 is the doors descriptor default of doors-windows-core; W and SL stay the defaults for walls and slabs.

title: Live context distances with a selectable reference edge
description:
WHY: While an element is placed or moved, the system shall show live distances from it to the nearest context elements (grid axes, walls, columns, beams); the user can change which edge is the reference and type a distance to place the element (INP-021). Creation and transforms must behave identically (INP-001), and the tracker accepts typed values (INP-002). Nothing of this exists today.

WHAT: Add input/context.rs: a ContextProvider trait (fn nearby(&self, p: DVec2, radius: f64, out: &mut Vec<ContextEdge { owner, segment, label }>)) implemented by the SnapIndex for wall faces and reference lines; grid axes, columns and beams implement it in grids and profiles-columns-beams. Preview gains reference_edges (the wall tool offers the reference line and both faces of the wall being drawn; the TransformStub offers its outline edges). ContextDistances measures from the active reference edge to the nearest context edge on each side (perpendicular distance, foot on the segment), within 120 screen points; Alt+R (provisional) cycles the reference edge, Alt+N the side. A Context field in TypedInput places the point so that the active reference edge sits at the typed distance from the chosen context edge, the other coordinate coming from the cursor or another typed field. Leader lines and distance labels are drawn in the preview colour. Out of scope: grid-axis, column and beam providers (their epics).
design: Typing into the context field acts like a lock: the resolved point is the cursor projected onto the line parallel to the context edge at the typed distance (GuideShape::Line and candidates_on from task 08), so snapping still works along it. Providers are passed in InputContext (providers: &[&dyn ContextProvider]) so later kinds register without touching the service. Only edges within 15° of parallel to the reference edge count as context edges, which keeps the overlay readable. Pitfall: when the reference edge touches the context edge the distance is 0 and the normal undefined; keep the last normal.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests on two_storey_shell: drawing a wall 0.3 m beside the interior wall lists the distances to its nearer face on one side and to the exterior wall on the other; Alt+R cycles reference line, left face and right face and wraps; typing 0.5 into the context field places the wall so its active face is exactly 0.5 m from the context edge (1e-9); the TransformStub moving a rectangle reports distances from its outline edges, so creation and transforms share the code.
- Timing test: nearby() on two_storey_shell averages under 1 ms per call in debug.
- kittest: while drawing a wall near an existing wall the formatted distance label is drawn (asserted through the tracker/overlay text).
- Satisfies INP-021 for walls (other providers come with grids and profiles-columns-beams) and the context-distance clauses of INP-001 and INP-002.
notes:
SRS: INP-021 INP-001 INP-002
Provisional bindings Alt+R (reference edge) and Alt+N (side); confirm with commands-and-l10n. INP-021 is Should; walls are the only provider until grids and profiles-columns-beams land.

title: Add ViewDefinition, view folders and layer combinations to the model
description:
WHY: VIEW-004 (M): a saved view stores camera or zoom and rotation, drawing scale, layer states, element-kind filters, storey range, cut planes, hidden elements, display style and sun settings; opening it re-applies the state to the current model, not to a snapshot; it can be redefined from the current window keeping its ID and name, and is visually distinguishable from plain viewpoints. VIEW-003 (M) asks for folders for saved views. LAY-003 (S): layer combinations are storable and applicable with one command, and saved views reference a combination or store their own layer states. PRJ-007 (M) lists views among the project settings. Gap rows: View3d holds only id, name and projection (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:111-116), there are no view commands and no combinations.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/views.rs: ViewDefinition {id, name, kind: ViewKind {Plan {storey}, Model3d {projection}}, saved: bool (false = plain viewpoint), folder: Option<ViewFolderId>, camera: Option<ViewCamera {Plan {center, zoom, rotation}, Model3d {target, distance, yaw, pitch, fov_y}}>, scale: Option<DrawingScale>, layers: Option<LayerStates {Combination(LayerCombinationId), Own(Vec<LayerState>)}>, plan: Option<PlanViewSettings {range: PlanRange (01), show_overhead, underlay: Option<TraceUnderlay {source: Storey|View, opacity, offset, rotation, enabled}>}>, restrictions: Option<ViewRestrictions {kinds, storey_range, hidden, cut_planes, section_box}>, style: Option<ViewStyle {mode: RenderMode}>, sun: Option<SunSettings>}; ViewFolder {id, name, parent}; layer.rs LayerState {layer, visible, locked} and LayerCombination {id, name, states}; ViewFolderId and LayerCombinationId through id_type! in ids.rs; DrawingScale from crates/archicraft-model/src/drawing.rs (plan-renderer-01), or introduced in that file here with plan-renderer-01's spec (denominator, presets, parse and format '1:50', serde). Project: views: Vec<ViewDefinition> replacing Vec<View3d> (template's two 3D views become plain viewpoints), view_folders, layer_combinations. Commands: AddView, UpdateView (rename and redefine), DeleteView, AddViewFolder, UpdateViewFolder, DeleteViewFolder (children move to the parent), AddLayerCombination, UpdateLayerCombination, DeleteLayerCombination (referencing views receive a copy of its states), SetLayerStates(Vec<LayerState>) as one undo step; DeleteLayer also strips the layer from combinations and view states. ViewDefinition::resolve(&Project) -> (ResolvedView, Vec<ViewIssue>) for tolerant re-apply. The writer and reader keep compiling by mapping plain 3D viewpoints to today's record and skipping the rest until 08. Out of scope: IFCX (08), app (09 onward), behaviour of restrictions, style and sun (3d-view-restrictions, 3d-display-styles).
design: Superset of View3d: Model3d {projection} plus saved = false is exactly today's view, so call sites migrate mechanically (Project::view, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/browser.rs:86-96, app.rs:744-747, views/view3d.rs). ViewCamera mirrors the app's Camera2d and Camera3d (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/camera.rs) so capture and apply are 1:1; RenderMode {Shaded, ShadedWithEdges, HiddenLine, Wireframe} with code() lives in the model so render3d's DisplayMode maps to it without a UI dependency (NFR-MNT-002). Sections are Option so a view stores what the user chose; capture stores all available sections by default. Edits: Edit::SetViews {views, folders}, Edit::SetLayerCombinations and a layers snapshot for SetLayerStates, per the 'prefer Set* snapshots' rule of the command extension point. ViewRestrictions and SunSettings are defined now with plain data (kind codes, StoreyId range with a trim flag, ElementId list, cut planes as origin/normal with optional storey binding, section box min/max; sun with date, time and shadows) so the schema is fixed once; 3d-view-restrictions and 3d-display-styles may only add optional fields. Pitfalls: DeleteStorey keeps plan views of that storey (they report on open) instead of cascading; resolve must never panic on dangling ids; LayerState equality includes locked.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: every new command executes, undoes and redoes to the identical project (revision normalised); invalid commands (plan view on an unknown storey, folder cycle, empty name, unknown layer in states, unknown combination) fail with Invalid or NotFound and change nothing.
- Redefine: UpdateView with the same id, name and folder replaces all sections; a rename through UpdateView keeps every other section bit-identical.
- DeleteLayer with combinations and views referencing the layer removes those LayerState entries in the same undo step; undo restores them.
- DeleteLayerCombination referenced by a view converts the reference to LayerStates::Own with the combination's states; undo restores the reference.
- resolve: a view referencing a deleted layer, a deleted storey, a deleted combination and deleted hidden elements yields one ViewIssue each and keeps everything else; layers added after saving are left untouched (re-applies to the current model, not a snapshot).
- A view or combination edit leaves the evaluated geometry untouched: the framework's incremental evaluation reports an empty dirty set (Arc::ptr_eq on all element geometries).
- Template test: two plain 3D viewpoints (perspective, parallel), no saved views, folders or combinations; round-trip tests and goldens stay unchanged.
- Satisfies the VIEW-004 data model with redefine and open semantics, the LAY-003 model and one-command apply, and the VIEW-003 folder model.
notes: SRS: VIEW-004 LAY-003 VIEW-003 PRJ-007. UI-016 (drag-and-drop folders) belongs to templates-presets. Open question: whether users can choose to store only some sections (Archicad always stores all).

title: Generate plans across storeys from a z-extent index and PlanOptions
description:
WHY: VIEW-010 (M): a storey's plan view is generated by a horizontal cut plane at the cut-plane height within a view range; intersected elements are drawn cut, elements between the cut plane and the bottom limit projected, elements between the cut plane and the top limit overhead in a dashed, lighter style that can be switched off; both limits are adjustable per view. VIEW-011 (M): elements shown on storeys other than their home storey follow their display range (ELM-008) and are drawn in the remote-storey style. VIEW-012 (S): each plan view can override cut height and view range, for example for split levels. ELM-008 (M): the display range sets the plan views an element is drawn in. Known debt (docs/implementation-status.md, technical debt, first item): crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:120 iterates only project.elements_on(storey), so a wall on the storey below that reaches into this storey's range is never cut or shown; the overhead class cannot be switched off and crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:115 always uses ViewRange::for_storey. Exists and kept (VIEW-010 and VIEW-012 partial): ViewRange::for_storey (plan.rs:59-78; cut from Project::cut_plane_height per STR-008, bottom at the storey elevation, top at the storey height), the cut/projected/overhead classification with the same-material merge (plan.rs:111-170), PlanDrawing::pick (plan.rs:270) and the app's heavier cut and dashed, lighter overhead drawing (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:241-282); these are extended, not rewritten. Missing: cross-storey admission, per-view limits and the overhead switch.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: PlanOptions {range: PlanRangeKey (the per-view overrides of 01, quantised), show_overhead: bool} (extend the struct if plan-renderer-04/05 already created it with its skin-separator and layered-display switches); PlanIndex, a z-extent index of all evaluated elements in absolute elevations plus a 'forced' list of elements whose display range admits storeys regardless of intersection; plan_drawing(project, geometry, index, storey, &PlanOptions, shown) admits home elements as today and remote elements through DisplayRange::admits with strict intersection against the effective range from Project::view_range; PlanElement.remote: Option<RemoteSide>; remote cut polygons stay out of the home same-material merge (own remote regions per element); remote elements admitted by their display range but outside the range contribute their outline (up-facing when below the range, down-facing when above). crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs: Document::plan(storey, &PlanOptions) caching per (StoreyId, PlanOptions) (extend that signature if plan-renderer-10 already introduced it) with the index rebuilt per geometry revision, and cross-storey invalidation. Out of scope: per-kind plan display filtering, custom-range toggles and cover fills (04), drawing and picking in the app (05), per-view editors (06).
design: Index: Vec<(lo_abs, hi_abs, ElementId)> sorted by lo, built from ElementGeometry::bounds plus the home storey elevation; query = partition_point(lo < top) then filter hi > bottom, which is linear only in the candidates and well below a millisecond at 20,000 elements; rebuild per geometry revision (the framework's incremental ModelGeometry keeps per-element Arcs, so this stays cheap). Meshes are storey-local (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:1-7): never translate meshes, shift bounds and the slice height by dz = home elevation - plan storey elevation (slice_loops(&part.mesh, range.cut - dz)). PlanOptions is a cache key and must stay Copy + Eq + Hash: store override lengths as i64 micrometres via the framework's tolerance module, never f64. Order: elements in model order (IndexMap) so picking keeps 'later on top'; remote elements precede home elements. Invalidation: the framework invalidates plans by changed_storeys, which only names home storeys; additionally invalidate every cached plan whose element set contains a changed element and every storey whose index query now admits it (keep the element ids in PlanDrawing). Pitfalls: negative storey elevations, top-storey nominal height, slabs topped exactly at a storey elevation (touching), elements whose home storey index is missing. Pointers: plan.rs:59-78 (ViewRange), :111-170 (classification and merge), document.rs:105-121, tools.rs:164-187 (snap targets read the drawing).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs wall_from_storey_below_is_cut_remote_style: three storeys; a wall homed on storey n-1 with top linked to home+2 is cut on storey n (non-empty cut polygons, remote == Some(Below)), is absent from storey n's merged home cut regions, is found by PlanDrawing::pick on n, and its home plan is unchanged; with HomeOnly it is absent on n (regression for the plan.rs:120 debt).
- walls_ending_at_the_storey_above_stay_home: default walls (top = home+1, offset 0) do not appear on the storey above (ranges that only touch within MODEL_TOLERANCE are not intersections); plan_cuts_walls_and_projects_slab passes unchanged.
- overhead_class_switches_off: a slab at +2.0..+2.2 above its home storey is overhead with show_overhead = true and absent with false; cut and projected output is identical in both runs.
- cut_override_moves_the_cut_plane: a cut override of 2.10 m cuts that slab; a bottom override of -1.0 m projects an Intersecting element of the storey below; a PlanRange with bottom >= cut is rejected by Project::view_range.
- home_and_above_slab_outline_on_next_storey: a slab with HomeAndAbove draws its outline with remote == Some(Below) on home+1 although outside the range, and nothing on home+2.
- PlanIndex unit test: queries equal a brute-force filter for 500 random ranges on samples::stand_in(1_000).
- crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs test: moving an Intersecting wall that spans storeys 0 and 1 regenerates both storeys' plans (Arc::ptr_eq false) and keeps an unrelated third storey's plan (Arc::ptr_eq true); geometry_and_plans_follow_the_model still passes.
- Satisfies the geometry of VIEW-010 (adjustable limits, overhead switch), VIEW-011, VIEW-012 and ELM-008.
notes: SRS: VIEW-010 VIEW-011 VIEW-012 ELM-008. Appendix D.1 range defaults. Open question: whether remote cut regions of the same material should merge with each other (kept per element here, never with home regions).

title: Profiles, columns and beams
description:
Add the Profile resource (parametric standard shapes and a steel catalogue) and the column and beam kinds with anchors, end cuts, inclination by end elevations, chain input, plan representation and axis export, as the first new element kinds built through the registry and the first consumers of profiles.

Risks: Profile editor scope creep: user-drawn profiles use the polygon input of the point-input service; creation from geometry and stretch zones belong to members-profiles-adv.
design: archicraft-model kinds/column.rs, kinds/beam.rs and profile.rs (regions with holes and materials, insertion origin, kind flags, catalogue data file); archicraft-geometry sweep.rs sweeps a profile along a segment and cuts the ends with its own convex plane clipper (no Boolean kernel needed for planar end cuts), caps triangulated with triangulate.rs; archicraft-ifcx archicraft::column|beam|profile codecs and Axis basiscurves; archicraft-app tools per the tool-extension recipe. Cross-kind cleanup by priority (COL-006, BEA-004) follows in cleanup-and-trims.
acceptance_criteria: D.2 column and beam defaults in the template; a column is placed with one click plus an optional rotation click, a beam between two points and as a chain; end-cut angles editable numerically and by handle; the profile editor produces closed cross-sections for rectangle, circle, hollow sections, I/H, T, L, U/C and Z with area regression tests and a catalogue of IPE/HEA/HEB/HEM/UPE/L/W/C/HSS sections; IfcColumn and IfcBeam with Axis basiscurves pass conformance; beams below and above the cut plane are classified projected and overhead with correct angled end cuts.
notes: SRS: PRF-004 PRF-005 PRF-011 COL-001 COL-002 COL-003 BEA-001 BEA-002 BEA-008 BEA-010 WAL-007 IFX-035

title: Extract the headless PointInput service and the tools module
description:
WHY: Every point the user defines shall pass through one shared point-input service that provides snapping, inference guides, constraints and numeric entry with identical behaviour at every step, covering element creation, transforms, reshaping, guides, measuring and dimensioning; each step shows a live preview and a prompt naming the expected input (INP-001). The user types without focusing a field, the first keystroke goes to the active field, Tab moves between fields, Enter commits the point and Esc cancels only the current step of the command (INP-003). Today the pipeline (typed value → Shift constraint → snap) is inlined in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:466-491 with its key handling in plan.rs:638-726, it serves only the creation tools of crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs, and Esc without typed text calls ToolState::reset() (plan.rs:701-711), discarding every entered point instead of one step. selection-transforms (tools/transform.rs), edit-reshape-palette (tools/reshape.rs), doors-windows-core (insert tool) and 3d-input-navigation (Camera3d surface) all plug into this contract, so it must be right before they start.

WHAT: Create crates/archicraft-app/src/input/ without any egui dependency: mod.rs (the PointInput state machine and Resolved), typed.rs (TypedInput and Field moved from views/tools.rs:86-118), snap.rs (SnapKind, Snap, SnapTargets and snap() moved unchanged from tools.rs:120-267), constrain.rs (constrain() from tools.rs:269-280), surface.rs (the ViewSurface trait and SurfaceFrame), consumer.rs (the InputConsumer trait with StepSpec, Expect, Preview, CursorState and Outcome: the step/preview API) and keys.rs (KeyInput and Modifiers independent of egui). Move views/tools.rs into a crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/ module (mod.rs with ToolKind and ToolState, wall.rs, slab.rs) where later epics add transform.rs, reshape.rs and insert.rs; ToolState implements InputConsumer. Add a TransformStub consumer in the input tests (move by vector with copy and multiple-copy variants, emitting Command::MoveElements) as the second consumer. Reduce plan.rs to building a PlanSurface (Camera2d, rect, storey elevation), translating egui events into KeyInput and pointer calls, and drawing Resolved and Preview. The status-line prompt (ui/shell.rs:170) comes from StepSpec; the single-key shortcut suppression in app.rs:466-476 asks ws.input.captures_keys(). Implement the Esc ladder. Register input and tools in src/lib.rs, drop `pub mod tools` from src/views/mod.rs and update every importer of views::tools (workspace.rs:13 and 205, app.rs:22, ui/shell.rs:13, ui/properties.rs:21, views/plan.rs:17, tests/ui.rs:12). Out of scope: the rstar index (02), new snap kinds and cycling (03), Cartesian and absolute fields (05), locks (08), the 3D ViewSurface implementation (3d-input-navigation) and real transform commands (selection-transforms).
design: PointInput { typed: TypedInput, cycle: Option<(DVec2, usize)>, last: Option<Resolved> } with resolve(&mut self, cursor: DVec2, mods: Modifiers, ctx: &InputContext) -> Resolved { point, snap: Snap, candidates: Vec<Snap>, guides: Vec<GuideShape> (empty until task 08) }, key(&mut self, KeyInput, &mut dyn InputConsumer, &InputContext) -> Effect { None, Execute(Command), Error(String) }, click(), double_click(). InputContext<'a> { project, storey, targets, previous, radius (prefs.snap_radius × surface.model_per_pixel()), units, number format, angle increment, snap step, frame: SurfaceFrame }. ViewSurface: to_plane(screen: DVec2) -> Option<DVec2>, to_screen(plane: DVec2) -> DVec2, model_per_pixel() -> f64, frame() -> SurfaceFrame; SurfaceFrame { origin: DVec3, x: DVec3, y: DVec3 } with to_model(DVec2) -> DVec3 and to_plane(DVec3) -> DVec2; plan views use origin (0, 0, storey elevation) and identity axes, and the 3D working plane of INP-015 fills origin and axes from a horizontal, vertical, three-point or face plane. Screen positions are DVec2 pixels so input/ stays egui-free; plan.rs converts egui::Pos2. InputConsumer: step() -> Option<StepSpec { prompt, hints: Vec<KeyHint>, expects: Expect { Point, Direction { from }, Angle { centre }, Distance { from } }, tracker: TrackerMode::Relative, repeat: bool }>, reference_point(), preview(&Resolved) -> Preview { outlines: Vec<(Vec<DVec2>, bool)>, cursor: CursorState::Normal }, commit(&mut self, &Project, StoreyId, DVec2) -> Outcome { Continue, Execute(Command), Done }, cancel_step() -> bool, backspace() -> bool, finish(&Project) -> Outcome. Workspace gains input: PointInput next to tool (workspace.rs:49-66). Move the storey guard on the previous point (plan.rs:467-472) into InputContext construction; keep the focus-lock filter (plan.rs:382-394), the Select tool's Tab cycling (plan.rs:669-678) and the context menu's full 'Cancel input' (plan.rs:737-740). The prompt strings of tools.rs:373-405 become StepSpec prompts whose key hints are generated from the hint list (NFR-USE-003). Pitfall: keep the wall chain's per-segment AddElements for now so this task stays a refactor (task 14 changes it); keep egui_kittest at the pinned =0.36.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- The existing tests pass unchanged from their new modules: wall_chain_closes_into_joined_walls, rectangle_tools, slab_polygon_finishes_on_enter, snapping_precedence and typed_distance_and_constraint; crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs passes with ToolKind imported from archicraft_app::tools.
- Unit tests in input/mod.rs drive PointInput without egui through two consumers that use only the InputConsumer trait: the wall tool (chain of three points, Enter finishes, two walls created) and TransformStub (base point, then the typed distance 2.5 with the cursor along +X yields Command::MoveElements with delta (2.5, 0); the multiple-copy variant keeps committing copies until Esc or double-click, and the copies already placed stay; the preview returns the translated outline).
- Identical behaviour at every step (INP-001): for the same cursor, modifiers, typed text and InputContext, the wall tool's second step and TransformStub's second step receive an identical Resolved (point, snap, candidates); a table test walks every WallMode and SlabMode step and asserts a non-empty StepSpec prompt at each step and a non-empty Preview once the first point is set.
- A rotate-shaped stub consumer with the steps Expect::Point (centre), Expect::Direction (reference) and Expect::Angle (target or typed angle) completes with the typed value 30 as exactly 30°, proving the API covers the EDT-001 shapes (move, rotate, mirror) without changes.
- ViewSurface test: a stub surface with a SurfaceFrame elevated to z = 3.0 and rotated by 30° round-trips screen → plane → model and back within 1e-9 and reports model_per_pixel; the plan adapter agrees with Camera2d::to_world/to_screen (views/camera.rs:31-41).
- Esc ladder test: with typed text, Esc clears only the text and keeps all points; on a clean step of a rotated rectangle with two points, Esc returns to the second step with one point left and the Wall tool stays active; with no points Esc clears the selection, then switches to the Select tool. Backspace removes one typed character, then one point.
- Module-layout test: no file under src/input/ mentions egui (include_str! scan), and views/plan.rs no longer calls snap(), constrain() or apply_typed().
- kittest: after clicking 'Wall' the status line shows the StepSpec prompt 'Wall: click the start point of the reference line'.
- Satisfies INP-001's service boundary, live preview and step prompt for the plan creation tools (transform, reshape, measuring and dimensioning consumers arrive in their epics through this trait) and INP-003's Esc clause.
notes:
SRS: INP-001 INP-003
Decision: Esc removes one step per press (typed text, then the step in progress, then the selection, then back to the Select tool); the context menu keeps the full reset. The InputConsumer trait is the contract for selection-transforms, edit-reshape-palette, doors-windows-core and 3d-input-navigation: review it with the owners of those epics before merging.

title: Apply the STR-002 storey shift defaults with a per-edit alternative
description:
WHY: STR-002 (M): changing a storey's height shifts all storeys above it by the difference; changing a storey's elevation changes the height of the storey below; the user may choose, per edit, to keep the other storeys' elevations instead. The model supports both behaviours (crates/archicraft-model/src/storey.rs:252-305 set_elevation/set_height with shift_above; command.rs:186-207; tests storey.rs:335-352 and tests/commands.rs:148-168), but the Storeys dialog has one checkbox 'Changes move the storeys above' that defaults to false (Dialogs derives Default, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:34-37, used at 96-99 and 129-150), so by default a height change moves only the next storey (the SRS alternative) and one flag cannot give the SRS defaults for both kinds of edit (gap row STR-002). The epic acceptance: the storey-height default shifts the storeys above.

WHAT: ui/dialogs.rs Storeys dialog: replace storey_shift_above by a per-edit choice group 'For the next change' with 'Height: move all storeys above' (default on) and 'Elevation: move all storeys above' (default off); both reset to these defaults when the dialog opens and after every committed storey edit, so an alternative applies to one edit only; hover texts state the STR-002 behaviour. Every other place that edits a storey height or elevation (a storey settings view in the browser, if present) uses the same defaults. Elevation fields keep the datum display of task 04. Out of scope: model changes (none needed), storey insertion and deletion (STR-003, STR-004, present).
design: Approach: a UI-only change; shift_above stays explicit in the commands so journals replay deterministically. Resetting after each edit avoids a sticky mode that would silently change later edits and matches 'per edit'. Pitfalls: Dialogs derives Default, so implement Default manually (or store the choices as Option overrides of constants) to get 'height on' as the initial value; Edited::Changed arrives in the same frame for one field only, so reset after the execute call, not before; with the datum display of task 04 the typed elevation is converted back to project zero before SetStoreyElevation. Pointers: dialogs.rs:34-53 and 87-202, storey.rs:252-305, command.rs:186-207.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest height_change_shifts_storeys_above_by_default: storeys 0 (±0), 1 (+3.000) and 2 (+6.000, inserted above the Appendix D.1 template storeys); typing 3.5 into storey 0's height moves storeys 1 and 2 to +3.500 and +6.500 in one undo step.
- kittest elevation_change_adjusts_the_storey_below_by_default: typing +3.200 into storey 1's elevation makes storey 0 3.200 high and leaves storey 2 at +6.000.
- kittest alternatives_apply_to_one_edit: unchecking 'Height: move all storeys above' and changing storey 0's height moves only storey 1, and the option is checked again afterwards; checking 'Elevation: move all storeys above' moves storeys 1 and 2 together for one edit only.
- The existing model tests (storey.rs:335-352, tests/commands.rs:148-168) pass unchanged.
- Satisfies STR-002.
notes:
SRS: STR-002
Appendix D.1 default storeys: 00 Ground floor ±0.000 m and 01 First floor +3.000 m, both 3.00 m high.

title: Apply per-kind plan display options, custom ranges and cover fills
description:
WHY: ELM-018 (M): each element kind offers plan display options for its cut, projected and overhead parts, at least projected, projected with overhead and cut only where meaningful. ELM-009 (S): slabs (roofs and terrain later) have a custom display range of N storeys up and M down with outline and cover fill set independently. VIEW-010 (M): projected elements show uncut lines 'plus cover fill where defined' (gap: no cover fill exists). ELM-008 (M): the epic acceptance asks that each display-range mode produces the expected drawing on every storey, proven on a fixture. Today the generator always emits all three classes (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:131-147) and the settings dialog's plan display section is a placeholder.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: a classification filter per element from Element.plan_display (CutOnly drops projected and overhead, Projected drops overhead) combined with PlanOptions.show_overhead; PlanElement.cover: Vec<Polygon<f64>> (the field plan-attributes-06 defines: reuse it if that task has landed and add only the remote handling and the Custom toggles) plus cover_fill: Option<(MaterialId, FillMesh)> for projected parts whose material has a cover fill, on home and remote storeys; Custom {outline: false} suppresses the remote lines while keeping the cover, {cover_fill: false} the reverse.
