New fixture samples::display_ranges() in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs built with the framework's FixtureBuilder (storeys at -3.0, 0.0, 3.0 and 6.0 m, one element per display-range mode, a slab with Custom {2, 1} and a cover-filled material), registered in samples::catalogue() (element-kind-framework-03), which feeds crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs; the fixture also carries a cut and top override on the 6.0 m storey and a non-default RemoteStoreyStyle, so its golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/display-ranges.ifcx (blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS) covers every key of task 02. Out of scope: drawing (05), editors (06), the stair break-line display (STA-046, stair-body-plan).
design: Cover polygons: union of up-facing triangles (normal z > 1 - 1e-9) projected to XY with geo::unary_union, triangulated with the existing fill_mesh so the app draws them like cut fills; compute only when the material defines a cover fill (Material.cover_fill from 01 or the plan-attributes cover reference), so plans without cover fills cost nothing extra. Apply the option filter after classification so picking and snapping reflect exactly what is drawn. The matrix test is table-driven (element name x storey -> expected tuple) so roofs, stairs and terrain add rows when they register. Use FixtureBuilder for v5 ids so the golden is deterministic. Pitfall: the option set is per kind (descriptor), the value per element; validation already rejects out-of-set values (01), so the generator may treat unknown combinations as ProjectedWithOverhead defensively.
acceptance_criteria:
- storey.rs plan_display_options_per_kind: for every kind in KINDS (feature test-kinds) and every PlanDisplay in its descriptor, a fixture element yields exactly the expected non-empty classes from a table in the test; the Dummy kind only offers Projected.
- view_overhead_switch_combines_with_element_option: overhead lines appear only when both the element's option and the view's show_overhead allow them.
- display_range_matrix: on samples::display_ranges(), a data-driven table asserts for every storey and element presence, remote side and class set (cut, projected, overhead, outline, cover) for HomeOnly, Intersecting, HomeAndAbove, HomeAndBelow, HomeAboveAndBelow, All and Custom{2,1}.
- custom_range_outline_and_cover_independent: Custom with outline off and cover fill on emits only cover polygons on remote storeys, the reverse emits only lines; the home storey is unaffected.
- projected_slab_has_cover_where_defined: with a cover fill on its material a projected slab emits one cover polygon whose area equals the outline area (geo::Area, 1e-9); without a cover fill none is emitted; the four projected lines of plan_cuts_walls_and_projects_slab are unchanged.
- The display-ranges golden is reproduced byte-identically by catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files (element-kind-framework-03), reads back to an equal Project and passes conformance/run.sh.
- Satisfies ELM-018, the geometry of ELM-009, the cover-fill clause of VIEW-010 and the per-storey matrix of ELM-008.
notes: SRS: ELM-018 ELM-009 ELM-008 VIEW-010. Archicad also offers 'outlines only' and 'overhead all'; ELM-018 says 'at least', so they are not required.

title: Verify exit criterion: Plan view range and display ranges, saved views, project browser, layers and layout persistence
description:
WHY: The epic closes only when its exit criterion holds as a whole: cross-storey plans with display ranges and the remote style (VIEW-010, VIEW-011, VIEW-012, ELM-008, ELM-009, ELM-018), saved views with redefine and open semantics persisted in the project (VIEW-004, PRJ-007, SET-002), the full project browser (VIEW-003), layer warnings, sorting and combinations (LAY-001, LAY-002, LAY-003), view rotation (VIEW-060), the trace underlay (VIEW-015) and per-user layout persistence (UI-004). Later kinds (columns, beams, roofs, stairs) and 3d-view-restrictions and 3d-display-styles build on this.

WHAT: Run the full workspace quality gates, re-run every acceptance test named by tasks 01-14 together, walk the epic acceptance list item by item, update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID with evidence (file:line and test names), record the residual items owned by other epics (sections and elevations in the browser, PRJ-007 resources not yet in the model, personal shortcuts and navigation scheme, restriction/style/sun behaviour, Intersecting and Custom display ranges of columns, beams, roofs, stairs, curtain walls and terrain), and close the epic in beads. No new features.
design: Verification only. Run the gates locally and in CI on all three platforms; check the golden diffs once more for non-archicraft changes (IFX-063); confirm that ELM-009 for roofs and terrain and VIEW-003 for sections and elevations are recorded as completed by roofs, terrain-and-site and sections-elevations-dims; confirm that the optional ViewDefinition sections (restrictions, style, sun) are documented as filled by 3d-view-restrictions and 3d-display-styles; file beads for any defect found instead of widening this task.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs: a wall on storey n-1 reaching into storey n's range is cut on n and drawn remote-style (regression for the known plan.rs debt).
- Each display-range mode produces the expected drawing on every storey (samples::display_ranges fixture).
- The overhead class can be switched off per view; a per-view cut-plane override round-trips.

- Views and layer combinations persist in archicraft::project and round-trip.
- The browser lists storeys highest first, 3D views and saved views in folders, double-click opens a tab, the context menu offers rename, delete, settings and save-as-view (kittest).
- A rotated plan view keeps snapping and constraints aligned to the rotated axes.
- The trace underlay with opacity and offset toggles with one command.
- Placing on a hidden layer warns.
- The egui_tiles tree is serialised in preferences and restored.
- cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are green on the workspace.
- conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files, including the re-blessed ones and display_ranges.

- The epic plan-views-browser is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: VIEW-010 VIEW-011 VIEW-012 ELM-008 ELM-009 ELM-018 VIEW-003 VIEW-004 VIEW-060 VIEW-015 LAY-001 LAY-002 LAY-003 UI-004 PRJ-007 SET-002

title: Draw plans from pens, line types and fills
description:
WHY: DSP-001 (M): editing an attribute updates all referencing elements in all views. DSP-002 (M): the default set suffices to draw and read a plan without defining any attribute. DSP-005 (S): screen-only pens are used for on-screen feedback only. DSP-008 (S): lines follow their line type, paper- or model-size. DSP-010 (M): solid fills draw their foreground pen and fills have an optional background pen or transparency. DSP-011 (M) and MAT-002 (M): a material change is visible in every plan, 2D hatching included, and in 3D. What exists (MAT-002 partial): UpdateMaterial bumps the revision (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:244-251, 703-709), Document drops the plan caches (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-121) and the 3D scene is rebuilt on the revision key and reads the material colour and opacity (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:203-214, render3d.rs:130-146); no test asserts the propagation. Today plan colours and weights are the hard-coded Palette and CUT_WIDTH/PROJECTED_WIDTH (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:91-143), overhead lines use a fixed 6/4 pt dash (plan.rs:250-255) and fills are flat tones (plan.rs:264-282).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan_style.rs (new) and views/plan.rs: PlanPens resolved once per frame from the project (Color32 and a screen width per pen) replaces Palette for every model line and fill; screen width is a monotonic map of the paper weight that keeps today's look (0.50 mm -> 1.8 pt, 0.18 mm -> 0.9 pt, hairline -> 1 px) and therefore DSP-004's cut-over-projected hierarchy at every zoom until plan-renderer resolves true weights at scale; projected and overhead lines use each PlanElement's pens and line types (paper-mm dashes at the 1:100 default via Shape::dashed_line_with_offset, model-size dashes through the camera scale); cut outlines use the region's cut pen; cut and cover fills come from plan_fills: background pen fill (or none), then hatch segments in the fill's foreground pen, or the 25 percent tone when the hatch is truncated or its spacing is below 3 px on screen; selection, hover, preview and snap glyphs use the screen-only pens; paper and grid colours stay a small canvas setting following the UI theme until task 10. document.rs: cache plan_fills per (revision, storey) next to plans; with the per-storey invalidation of element-kind-framework-11, a fill attribute stamp (task 05) or a material edit invalidates the plan_fills of every storey, while pen and line-type edits invalidate no cache because PlanPens is resolved per frame. Out of scope: GPU rendering, drawing scale and paper-true weights (plan-renderer), per-view pen tables (10).
design: Resolution order: element style -> pen or line type -> (task 10: pen-table entry) -> Color32 and width; the only fallback is a visible magenta 'missing attribute' colour for dangling references, logged once through tracing. Keep the egui painter in this epic; plan-renderer replaces model drawing with lyon and wgpu and should build its PenSet (plan_gpu/pens.rs) from the same resolution function. Batch hatch segments per region (one Shape per region, skip regions outside the clip rect) to protect frame time; hatch lines are regenerated on revision change only, never on zoom. Pitfall: dashed_line_with_offset takes separate dash and gap arrays; convert the alternating list and give zero-length dots a 0.5 px minimum. Pitfall: the per-frame allocation debt listed in docs/implementation-status.md - build PlanPens once per frame and reuse cached hatches. Pointers: views/plan.rs:91-143, 240-320, 436-440 (palette selection), 583-597 (snap and preview glyphs); document.rs:97-121; render3d.rs:102-180 (build_scene).
acceptance_criteria:
- plan_style.rs unit tests: the template pens give a cut width strictly greater than the uncut width; the six standard weights map to strictly increasing screen widths of at least 1 px; a DASH line type converts to the expected point lengths at 50 pt/m; screen-only pens are never chosen for model lines.
- Fill drawing (DSP-010), asserted on the shapes built by plan_style.rs: a solid fill paints its foreground pen colour; a hatch fill with a background pen paints that colour under its hatch lines; the same hatch with background None paints no background shape (transparent).
- Line-type scaling (DSP-008): the same dash list converts to screen lengths 100 times longer as a paper-size line type (paper mm x 100 at the interim 1:100 scale) than as a model-size one (model mm), both through the camera scale.
- Headless app test: after UpdateAttribute changing the uncut pen colour, the resolved style of every projected line of two_storey_shell uses the new colour while no element changed (DSP-001); after UpdateMaterial of a cut fill the cached plan_fills of the storey are regenerated (revision key) and differ.
- Cache rule: after UpdateAttribute changing CONC's hatch spacing every storey's cached plan_fills is regenerated while the PlanDrawing Arcs are reused (Arc::ptr_eq); after a pen colour edit no plan cache is regenerated and the next frame draws the new colour (DSP-001 'without editing the elements').
- MAT-002 test: after UpdateMaterial changing a material's colour, render3d::build_scene SceneData colours change for every element using it (3D clause), and plan_fills follow the material's fill (2D clause).
- Palette, CUT_WIDTH and PROJECTED_WIDTH no longer exist in views/plan.rs; drawing a fresh-template plan resolves every model line and fill from project attributes (a debug counter of 'missing attribute' fallbacks stays 0).
- Existing kittests in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs pass; the PR records a screenshot of two_storey_shell showing masonry and concrete hatches.
- Satisfied: DSP-001 for all plan views, DSP-002 (a plan drawn and read without defining attributes), the DSP-005 screen-only clause, DSP-008 rendering with both scaling modes, DSP-010 solid and background or transparent fills drawn, DSP-011 and MAT-002 visible in plan and 3D.
notes: SRS: DSP-001 DSP-002 DSP-005 DSP-008 DSP-010 DSP-011 MAT-002. The weight-to-point map is interim; plan-renderer-02 and -05 replace it with paper mm x scale x dpi and a 1 px floor.

title: Draw same-material cuts seamless and emit skin separator lines
description:
WHY: DSP-012 (S): touching cut regions of the same material (for example the cores of two joined walls) shall be drawn as one region without a seam, and separator lines between the skins of a layered element shall be drawn with their own pen and can be switched off per view. Same-material polygons are already merged with geo::unary_union (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:153-163), but every merged region's rings are stroked with the cut pen (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:283-288), and after plan-attributes-06 regions merge by (material, element cut pen, hatch placement) but are still stroked ring by ring; with six-skin walls every skin boundary would be drawn twice as a heavy cut line and never as a separator. Missing (gap analysis DSP-012 partial): the separator line class, its pen and the per-view switch.

WHAT: in plan.rs classify each boundary piece of the merged regions by what lies on its two sides: the same region key on both sides gives no line; nothing, or a different element, on the outer side gives a CutOutline of the inside element; a neighbouring skin with a different region key in the same element gives a SkinSeparator. Introduce `PlanOptions {show_skin_separators: bool (default true), ..}` passed to plan_drawing; when false no SkinSeparator strokes are emitted. Keep the CutRegion merge key of plan-attributes-06 (material, element cut pen, quantised hatch placement): the cut fill comes from the material (DSP-011), so one region has one fill and hatches continue across merged regions. Document::plan passes PlanOptions::default() until plan-renderer-10. Out of scope: pens and rendering (-02, -08), junction resolution of skins (junction-engine; skin ends stay square), the UI switch (-10) and the layered display option (-05).
design:
Algorithm per storey: (1) per merge key, merged = unary_union of the polygons (existing code). (2) Split every merged ring edge at the ring vertices of all other regions that lie on it within MODEL_TOLERANCE (an rstar R-tree of vertices; rstar is already in Cargo.lock through geo 0.33, add it as a direct workspace dependency at the same version), so every piece has exactly one neighbour. (3) For each piece, sample the midpoint offset by +/-0.1 mm along the edge normal and find the SkinCut (plan-renderer-03) containing each sample through an R-tree of SkinCut bounding boxes plus the shared point-in-polygon helper. (4) Classify: outer side empty -> CutOutline(inside element); outer side another region key and another element -> CutOutline, emitted only from the side with the smaller (region key, element) pair; another region key, same element -> SkinSeparator, emitted once the same way; same region key -> nothing. (5) Chain the pieces per (class, element) with the chaining utility of -03. Cost O(E log E); measured in plan-renderer-11.

PlanOptions: if plan-views-browser has already introduced PlanOptions (view range, cut height, overhead on/off), add the field there; otherwise create the struct here in plan.rs with a `range: ViewRange` member so plan-views-browser extends the same struct instead of adding a second one. New signature: `plan_drawing(project, geometry, storey, &PlanOptions, shown)`. Do not change the merge key of plan-attributes-06 (MaterialId, cut pen, quantised HatchPlacement): differing hatches, pens or placements never merge, and equal ones merge across elements.

Pitfall: after junction-engine resolves skins, wall A's plaster may meet wall B's concrete at a junction; by this rule that is an element boundary (CutOutline). Revisit in junction-engine if the reference product draws separators there.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/plan_layers.rs with archicraft_model::samples::f2_layered_wall(): its free straight 5.0 m wall yields six skin polygons, one closed CutOutline ring equal to the 680 mm x length rectangle (area within 1e-6 m2) and exactly five SkinSeparator strokes, parallel to the reference line at 120, 180, 360, 370 and 670 mm from the exterior face (within MODEL_TOLERANCE).
- In the 10 x 8 m ring of f2_layered_wall() the concrete cores of two walls meeting at a mitred corner form one region and no stroke lies on the joint inside the core (the SRS example 'the cores of two joined walls'); the brick skins merge the same way.
- Two collinear walls with the template structure 'Cavity wall 680' (layer-structures-09) butted end to end: per-material regions merge across the joint, no stroke of any class crosses the joint line, and the separator strokes cover the combined length on each of the five offsets without a gap.
- Two joined single-material concrete walls (L junction mitred by wall.rs) and the four walls of house(): one region, one CutOutline per ring and no stroke along the joint (plan_cuts_walls_and_projects_slab extended to strokes).
- Two butted walls of different materials: their shared edge is one CutOutline (emitted once), not a SkinSeparator.
- With show_skin_separators = false the F2 drawing has zero SkinSeparator strokes and identical regions and outlines.
- Satisfies DSP-012 clause 1 (seamless same-material regions) and the geometry part of clause 2 (separators as their own line class, switchable per view through PlanOptions).
notes: SRS: DSP-012. F2 skin boundaries measured from the exterior face: 120, 180, 360, 370 and 670 mm (Appendix D.7). Junction treatment of skins is junction-engine's (WAL-020..027); this task only fixes the classification rule.

title: Add the layered display option: full, core only or without finishes
description:
WHY: DSP-017 (C): a view option may show layered elements in full, as core only, or without finish skins. The skin roles core, finish and other come from PRF-001 and reach the plan through the SkinRef added in plan-renderer-03.

WHAT: `LayeredDisplay {Full, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes}` in PlanOptions (default Full). plan.rs skips body parts whose BodyPart.role (layer-structures-04) is filtered out before slicing and projecting, so outlines and separators are classified from the remaining skins and the core-only outline lies on the core faces. It applies to every element with skin-tagged parts (walls and slabs now, roofs when they register skins); single-material elements are unaffected; picking and snapping use what is drawn. Out of scope: 3D views (no SRS clause), the UI switch (plan-renderer-10) and persistence in saved views (plan-views-browser).
design: Filter in the part loop of plan_drawing (`for part in &body.parts`) with `options.layered.shows(part.role)`: CoreOnly shows Core only, WithoutFinishes hides Finish, Full shows everything, parts without SkinRef are always shown. PRF-001 guarantees at least one core skin; if an element would end up empty anyway, fall back to Full for that element and log at debug level. A layered slab below the cut plane projects the outline of its topmost remaining skin. The Document plan cache is keyed by PlanOptions from plan-renderer-10 on; until then only the default is requested.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/plan_layers.rs with the free wall of samples::f2_layered_wall(); the test reads the roles from its 'Cavity wall 680' structure, which layer-structures-09 defines as Brick 120 finish, Air gap 60 other, Mineral wool 180 other, Plaster 10 other, Concrete 300 core, Plaster 10 finish: Full gives six skin polygons and five separators; WithoutFinishes gives four polygons (air gap, mineral wool, plaster, concrete), three separators at 180, 360 and 370 mm from the exterior face and one 550 mm wide outline from 120 to 670 mm; CoreOnly gives one 300 mm concrete polygon whose CutOutline ring lies on the core faces (370 and 670 mm from the exterior face) and no separators.
- archicraft_model::samples::storey_with_walls_and_slab() (single-material walls) produces an equal PlanDrawing under all three options (equality test).
- In CoreOnly, plan.pick inside a hidden plaster skin of F2 returns nothing and inside the core returns the wall.
- Satisfies DSP-017 at the geometry level; the per-view switch is plan-renderer-10.
notes: SRS: DSP-017. PRF-001 roles: core, finish, other. F2 role assignment is defined by layer-structures-09 (template structure 'Cavity wall 680'); tests read it from the structure instead of hard-coding it, the numbers above are the expected values for that assignment.

title: Add attribute identity, pens, line types, fills and pen tables
description:
WHY: DSP-001 (M) requires every 2D graphic property of an element (outline pen, line type, cut-fill pattern and pens, cover fill) to be a reference to a project-level attribute. DSP-003 (M) requires every attribute to have a stable internal ID, a display name, an optional short code (for example MW1) and a description. DSP-005 (S) organizes pens by role (structural cut, non-structural cut, uncut, overhead; cut-fill foreground, cover-fill foreground, fill background; drafting, annotation line, annotation text; screen-only selection, pre-selection, guides, snap markers), each with colour and weight. DSP-007 (C) allows several named pen tables that change only colours and weights. DSP-008 (S) defines line types by repeating dash and gap lengths in millimetres with a paper-size or model-size flag. DSP-009 (M) makes each fill declare the roles it may serve (cut, cover, drafting). DSP-010 (M) requires solid fills (foreground pen, optional background pen or transparency) and hatch fills with angle, spacing and pen. DSP-020 (S) adds paper/model scaling for hatches and a per-element override of hatch rotation and origin. What exists today and is reused: typed UUID ids generated by id_type! (crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs:12-75), the identity fields id, name, optional code and description of Material (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:142-157), and the role-named Palette colours with three screen-point weight tiers (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:91-143), whose light and dark sets (plan.rs:106-138, chosen by UI theme at plan.rs:436) seed the default pens and the DARK table in task 02. Missing: pens, line types, fills and pen tables as project resources: the only graphic resource is Material.cut_fill, a closed FillPattern enum plus RGB tones (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:94-138), and every plan colour and weight is a constant in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:91-143.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/attributes.rs, re-exported from lib.rs: AttributeMeta { name, code, description } shared by all attributes (Material gets a meta-style accessor so pickers treat it uniformly); PenId, LineTypeId, FillId and PenTableId via id_type! in ids.rs; PenRole with the 14 DSP-005 roles (ALL, code, label, group, is_screen_only); PenWeight in paper millimetres with HAIRLINE = 0.0 and STANDARD = [0.0, 0.13, 0.18, 0.25, 0.35, 0.50]; Pen { id, meta, role, color: Rgb, weight }; Scaling { Paper, Model }; LineType { id, meta, dashes: Vec<f64> (alternating dash and gap in mm, empty = continuous), scaling }; FillRole and FillRoles { cut, cover, drafting }; Fill { id, meta, roles, foreground: PenId, background: Option<PenId> (None = transparent), kind: FillKind::{Solid, Hatch(Hatch)} } with Hatch { scaling, families: Vec<HatchFamily { angle_deg, spacing_mm, offset_mm, stagger_mm, dashes }> } (1 to 4 families); HatchPlacement { rotation_deg, origin: DVec2 } (value type for the DSP-020 override used in task 04); PenTable { id, meta, background: Rgb, entries: BTreeMap<PenId, PenValues { color, weight }> } where a missing entry means the pen's own values. Attributes { pens, line_types, fills, pen_tables } becomes Project.attributes (#[serde(default)]) with lookups pen, line_type, fill, pen_table, pens_with_role, fills_for(role), per-type validate() and Attributes::integrity_problems() (duplicate ids, fill or table entries pointing to missing pens). Every Project construction site (template.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs, test builders) uses Attributes::default(), so template content and IFCX output stay unchanged in this task. Out of scope: template content and IFCX (02), material and element references (03, 04), commands (05), any UI.
design: Plain data with serde derives and no egui types (NFR-MNT-002). Store pen weights and dash lengths in paper millimetres (DSP-019 arrives with plan-renderer); model-size line types and hatches also store millimetres and convert at use. Hatch family geometry: angle counter-clockwise from the x axis, spacing perpendicular between lines, offset perpendicular shift of the first line, stagger along-line shift per successive line (brick bond), dashes like LineType. Limit families to four because plan-renderer-06 evaluates each family in a shader loop. Vec storage with linear lookups like layers and materials (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:185-191); attribute counts are in the tens. PenTable as overrides on the pens' own values keeps tasks 02-09 independent of DSP-007 while still making the data persistent early, so the golden files are re-blessed only in 02, 03 and 04. Pitfalls: the existing FillPattern enum in material.rs stays until task 03 so IFCX keeps compiling; call the new enum FillKind to avoid a clash. Project derives PartialEq and Serialize and is journalled by History and autosave: add the field with #[serde(default)] so old journals and autosaves still load. Keep Rgb in material.rs and re-export it. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs:12-75 (id_type!), material.rs:140-178 (validation style), project.rs:164-200 (Project and lookups).
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check green; golden files unchanged (attributes are empty and not written yet).
- attributes.rs unit tests: PenRole::ALL holds exactly the 14 DSP-005 roles and is_screen_only() is true only for selection, pre-selection, guide and snap marker; PenWeight::STANDARD equals the six DSP-005 weights; Pen::validate rejects negative or non-finite weights, empty names and colour components outside 0..1.
- LineType::validate rejects odd-length or negative dash lists and a zero period; period_mm() and the continuous case (empty list) are tested.
- Fill::validate rejects a fill without any role, a hatch with 0 or more than 4 families, spacing <= 0 and non-finite angles; Fill::serves(FillRole) is tested for every role combination.
- AttributeMeta (DSP-003): for every attribute type an empty short code is valid (the code is optional) while an empty or whitespace-only name is rejected; meta() of Pen, LineType, Fill and PenTable returns id, name, code and description, and ids survive the serde round trip unchanged.
- Fill::validate accepts a solid fill with a background pen and the same fill with background None (transparent), the two solid-fill options of DSP-010.
- Attributes::integrity_problems reports a fill whose foreground pen is missing and a pen-table entry for a missing pen; a serde_json round trip of a hand-built Attributes value is lossless.
- Satisfied as data model: the identity clause of DSP-003 for pens, line types and fills, and the structure of DSP-005, DSP-007, DSP-008, DSP-009, DSP-010 and DSP-020.
notes: SRS: DSP-001 DSP-003 DSP-005 DSP-007 DSP-008 DSP-009 DSP-010 DSP-020. Roles exactly as listed in DSP-005; the screen-only group is split into four pens (selection, pre-selection, guide, snap marker).

title: Add the wgpu plan paint callback with retained fill buffers
description:
WHY: the egui painter re-tessellates every line and fill every frame (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:246-289) and is too slow for large plans (docs/technology-choices.md, "Plan views: lyon"), which blocks the NFR-PERF-004 clause of DSP-013; DSP-014 requires anti-aliasing without hardware multisampling, which needs our own shader; and VIEW-013 makes zoom a pure camera transform, so the drawing can be retained on the GPU and navigation only updates a uniform.

WHAT: a new crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan_gpu.rs with `PlanGpuResources` registered in the egui_wgpu renderer's callback_resources on the first frame that has a render state (as views/view3d.rs creates its GPU scene), holding the pipelines and an LRU cache of `PlanBuffers` keyed by (storey, plan revision, PlanOptions); an `egui_wgpu::CallbackTrait` paint callback (prepare: rebuild and upload only on key change, write the camera uniform every frame; paint: draw) that views/plan.rs ui() adds before its overlay shapes. This task draws the paper background (the background of the view's pen table, plan-attributes-10) and the base layer of every cut and cover fill of PlanFills (plan-attributes-06): the background pen of a hatch fill (none = transparent) or the foreground pen of a solid fill, over CutRegion.fill triangles and over cover polygons triangulated with crates/archicraft-geometry/src/triangulate.rs; fill vertices carry a fill index into a small colour buffer, so pen and pen-table edits never rebuild geometry. Hatch lines stay on the plan-attributes-07 painter until plan-renderer-09 and model lines until plan-renderer-08. The painter path remains the fallback when no render state exists (the current label-based kittest tests, GPU initialisation failure). Out of scope: strokes (-08), hatches (-09), golden images (-07) and any change to the 3D renderer.
design:
Follow the conventions of views/render3d.rs (wgpu only through the `eframe::egui_wgpu::wgpu` re-export, bytemuck Pod vertices, positions relative to a local origin near the model) but render through a paint callback instead of an offscreen texture: no texture lifetime side channel like ArchiCraftApp.released (app.rs:69,145,793), natural ordering with the egui overlays, and it works inside egui_kittest's WgpuTestRenderer, which sets frame.wgpu_render_state and supports callback_resources. Pass a `plan_gpu: bool` availability flag down to views::plan::ui alongside the render state the Behavior already carries (app.rs:723), so the view decides between callback and painter.

Uniforms: px_per_model_m = camera.scale * pixels_per_point, the camera centre minus the local origin computed in f64 on the CPU and cast to f32, viewport size from info.viewport_in_pixels, the drawing-scale factor k for later passes. Pipeline target format = render_state.target_format, premultiplied-alpha blending (One, OneMinusSrcAlpha) with gamma-space colours as egui uses, so edge coverage composes like egui's own shapes. Viewport and scissor come from the callback info. Bound the cache to the last 8 PlanBuffers to cap memory with many plan tabs; prepare runs every frame, so compare keys cheaply (revision u64 plus a PlanOptions hash).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test: the camera uniform maps sample world points to the same screen positions as Camera2d::to_screen within 0.01 px for several rect offsets, pixels_per_point 1.0 and 2.0, and coordinates 10 km from the project origin (local origin keeps f32 precise).
- Unit test with a rebuild counter: 200 simulated pan and zoom steps on a cached storey cause zero PlanBuffers rebuilds and zero vertex or index buffer writes; a revision change or a PlanOptions change causes exactly one rebuild; a drawing-scale change causes none (scale is a uniform).
- The plan pipelines are created with MultisampleState.count == 1 (asserted constant), so anti-aliasing never relies on hardware multisampling (DSP-014).
- Switching the view's pen table or editing a fill's background pen writes only the colour buffer (counter), never the vertex or index buffers.
- The existing label-based tests in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs pass unchanged through the painter fallback; with the GPU path the app shows fills under the painter lines and hover/selection overlays on top (manual check recorded in the pull request).
- Provides the retained-rendering prerequisite of DSP-013/NFR-PERF-004 and the zoom-independent drawing of VIEW-013 at renderer level.
notes: SRS: DSP-014 DSP-013 VIEW-013. Deviation from the roadmap sketch: a paint callback rather than an offscreen texture; the design-note intent (vertex buffers cached per revision and storey, egui painter kept for overlays) is unchanged.

title: Render anti-aliased plan strokes with lyon at resolved pen weights
description:
WHY: DSP-014 (M): lines in 2D views shall be anti-aliased with correct caps and joins at every zoom level without relying on hardware multisampling. DSP-004 (M): every line gets its weight from its pen, cut outlines visibly heavier than projected outlines at every zoom, no line thinner than one device pixel. DSP-019 (S): paper-millimetre weights including a hairline resolved at the view's drawing scale, and a true-weights/uniform-thin option. VIEW-013: the drawing scale, not the zoom, defines the paper size of lines. What exists (gap analysis DSP-014 partial): epaint's software feathering already anti-aliases without multisampling (eframe multisampling stays 0, crates/archicraft-app/src/main.rs) and cut rings are closed polylines with joins (views/plan.rs:286). Missing: joins on projected and overhead lines, which are independent line_segments (views/plan.rs:246-262); caps (epaint strokes are butt-only and its sub-pixel path has none); and a renderer that does not re-tessellate every frame. After plan-attributes-07 and plan-renderer-02 the painter widths follow pens at scale, but the painter path keeps the other gaps.

WHAT: add lyon (1.0.19) to the workspace dependencies; tessellate PlanDrawing.strokes (plan-renderer-03/-04) once per cache key with lyon's StrokeTessellator into vertices carrying position on path, extrusion normal, side, advancement and pen index; a pen storage buffer (colour, paper mm, hairline flag, floor class) uploaded separately from the geometry (line-type dash patterns get their own buffer in plan-renderer-13); a WGSL vertex shader that extrudes by the resolved half-width of plan-renderer-02 plus an anti-aliasing fringe and a fragment shader that computes coverage analytically; miter joins with limit 4 falling back to bevel and butt caps on open polylines; draw order fills, projected, overhead, separators, cut outlines; the pen buffer is filled from PlanPens::resolve(project, view pen table) of plan-attributes-07/-10, so pen tables apply on the GPU path. Strokes with a continuous line type (cut outlines, separators and SOLID projected lines) leave draw_plan when the GPU path is active; strokes with a dashed line type (overhead lines by default) stay on the plan-attributes-07 painter until plan-renderer-13; the painter keeps the no-GPU fallback and the overlays (hover and selection outlines, reference lines, snap markers, rubber bands, tracker). Out of scope: line-type dashes and overlay width floors (plan-renderer-13), hatches (-09), the view-option UI (-10), drafting line types (drafting-trim-split) and restyling of the selection overlays.
design:
Tessellation: lyon StrokeTessellator with StrokeOptions line width 1.0 (unit width: real widths are applied in the shader, so zoom and scale changes never re-tessellate), LineJoin::MiterClip with miter_limit 4.0, LineCap::Butt for start and end, tolerance 0.0005 m (only polylines exist today; arcs arrive with drafting-trim-split). A custom StrokeVertexConstructor fills GpuStrokeVertex {pos: position_on_path relative to the local origin, normal: the miter-scaled normal(), side: +1/-1 from side(), advance: advancement(), pen: u32}, the same screen-space-width pattern as lyon's own wgpu example.

WGSL: half_w = 0.5 * select(max(mm * k, floor_px), 1.0, hairline || thin) in device px with k = 1e-3 * denominator * px_per_model_m; world offset = normal * (half_w + 1.0) / px_per_model_m; varying d = side * (half_w + 1.0); coverage = clamp(half_w + 0.5 - abs(d), 0.0, 1.0), which integrates to the requested width and gives a one-pixel feather. Keep `advance` in the vertex layout: plan-renderer-13 evaluates dash patterns on it. The CPU resolver of plan-renderer-02 is the reference; tests compare measured widths with it.

Pens: dense remap PenId -> u32 per upload from the (element, class) mapping of plan-renderer-02; storage buffers are available on Vulkan, Metal and DX12 including lavapipe and WARP. Cut outlines are centred on the region boundary and drawn after fills, as in the reference product. CUT_WIDTH and PROJECTED_WIDTH (views/plan.rs:140-143 today) are already gone after plan-attributes-07; the painter keeps model lines only as the no-GPU fallback with the stroke_width_px widths of plan-renderer-02.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pixel assertions in crates/archicraft-app/tests/plan_pixels.rs through the plan-renderer-07 harness: a horizontal cut outline and a projected line with the default pens, rendered at 5, 20, 80, 320 and 1280 pt/m, pixels_per_point 1.0 and 2.0 and scales 1:50 and 1:100: the measured cut width is at least the projected width + 0.75 device px and every measured width is >= 0.95 device px (DSP-004).
- The hairline measures 1.0 +/- 0.1 device px at every sampled zoom; above the floor a 0.50 mm cut pen at 1:100 measures within 10 % of 0.05 m x zoom x ppp, and the measured widths match stroke_width_px of plan-renderer-02 within 10 % (DSP-019, VIEW-013).
- UniformThin: every line class measures 1.0 +/- 0.1 device px.
- Joins and caps, checked at the floor widths (2 px cut, 1 px projected, at 5 pt/m) and at 20 px: a closed square cut ring has coverage > 0.95 at the outer corner pixel (miter, no notch); an acute 10-degree projected chain shows no spike beyond the miter limit (bevel); open chains end at their endpoints within 0.5 px (butt caps).
- Anti-aliasing without multisampling: a 7-degree slanted 1-px line has partial-coverage pixels (0.2 to 0.8) in every column and a per-column coverage sum of 1.0 +/- 0.15, with the pipeline sample count 1.
- Vertex data contains pen indices, not colours or widths (unit test on the vertex builder), so pen edits only re-upload the pen buffer.
- Goldens for the two_storey_shell ground floor at 1:100 and 1:50, at fit and at 4x zoom, pass on the three CI platforms.
- Satisfies DSP-004, DSP-014 and DSP-019 (true weights and the thin option at renderer level) and the line-weight clause of VIEW-013 for continuous lines; dashed lines and overlays follow in plan-renderer-13.
notes: SRS: DSP-004 DSP-014 DSP-019 VIEW-013. Technology choices: lyon 1.0.19 (MIT/Apache, accepted by deny.toml), wgpu only through eframe::egui_wgpu::wgpu. Miter limit 4 is a proposal; record it with the fixtures in docs/testing.md.

title: Add attribute commands with in-use protection and replacement
description:
WHY: DSP-003 (M): elements and views reference attributes by ID so renaming never breaks a reference, and deleting an attribute that is in use requires choosing a replacement. DSP-006 (S): the user edits a pen's colour, weight and description. DSP-007 (C): pen tables are edited like other attributes and never touch element pen references. DSP-001 (M): editing an attribute updates every referencing element without editing the elements. DSP-009 (M): fills serve only their declared roles, so a replacement or a role change must keep every use valid. NFR-MNT-001 makes every change an undoable Command. Only materials and layers have commands today (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:72-83 and 489-552).

WHAT: command.rs: Attribute::{Pen, LineType, Fill, PenTable} and AttributeRef::{Pen(PenId), LineType(LineTypeId), Fill(FillId), PenTable(PenTableId)}; Command::AddAttribute(Attribute), UpdateAttribute(Attribute), DeleteAttribute { attribute: AttributeRef, replacement: Option<AttributeRef> } with labels such as 'New pen', 'Change fill', 'Delete line type'; Edit::InsertAttribute { index, attribute }, RemoveAttribute(AttributeRef) and ReplaceAttribute(Attribute) with exact inverses. New module crates/archicraft-model/src/references.rs: Project::attribute_uses(AttributeRef) -> Vec<AttributeUse> over element plan styles (common envelope plus a new KindDescriptor::attribute_refs hook, default empty), default slots, material cut and cover fills and their pen overrides, fill pens and pen-table entries, and rewrite(from, to) producing ReplaceElement, SetToolDefaults, ReplaceMaterial and ReplaceAttribute edits. Rules: Update validates values and rejects a fill update that drops a role still used in that role (the message names a user); Delete without replacement succeeds only when unused; a replacement must be of the same type, different and existing, a fill replacement must serve every role the deleted fill is used in, and a pen replacement used by elements must not be screen-only; the last pen of a role and the last pen table cannot be deleted; deleting a pen drops its entries from every pen table; NoChange when nothing changes. DeleteMaterial keeps its behaviour but enumerates users through references.rs. Attribute edits are style-only: Edit::apply of the three attribute edits records an attribute stamp (with the attribute type) in Project.changes, the ChangeLog of element-kind-framework-10, so they dirty no geometry in the incremental evaluator and task 07 can invalidate only the plan fill caches. Out of scope: UI (08, 09), view selection of pen tables (10).
design: Follow the 'Add a command' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md: plan into primitive edits, prefer ReplaceElement and SetToolDefaults snapshots, add only the three attribute edits. Compute all rewrite edits from the pre-command project in one pass, because deleting a pen used as a fill foreground rewrites the fill, and that fill may be used by materials. references.rs is the one place that knows who references what; later epics (layer-structures for skin materials, drafting-trim-split for 2D element pens, components-dw-catalogue for door and window parts) add their referrers there or through the kind hook, which the module documents. Pitfall: ReplaceAttribute and RemoveAttribute must keep the index (std::mem::replace, remembered position) so attribute order and golden bytes are stable across undo. Pitfall: the 3D scene key and the geometry cache must ignore attribute edits (only material edits touch 3D appearance). Pointers: command.rs:36-140 (Command, label), 210-260 (plan), 489-552 (delete with reassignment), 616-720 (Edit, apply), tests/commands.rs:208-251; crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-121 (cache invalidation).
acceptance_criteria:
- commands.rs test rename_keeps_references: UpdateAttribute renaming a pen, a line type and a fill leaves every element, slot and material identical (serde comparison) and resolution returns the renamed attribute; roundtrip.rs: after the rename a save/load keeps every reference (DSP-003 ID test).
- commands.rs test deleting_an_attribute_in_use_requires_a_replacement: DeleteAttribute of the structural cut pen without replacement fails with CommandError::Invalid stating the number of users; with a replacement every element, slot and fill pen is rewritten; undo restores the exact project; deleting an unused line type without replacement succeeds.
- Role rules: a fill used as an element cover cannot be replaced by a cut-only fill; an UpdateAttribute removing the cut role from CONC (used by materials) is rejected; the last pen of a role cannot be deleted; deleting a pen removes its pen-table entries and undo restores them.
- execute + undo + redo of every new command restores the project (revision normalised), following the existing command tests.
- An UpdateAttribute produces an empty geometry dirty set in the incremental evaluator (element-kind-framework equivalence test extended).
- deleting_resources_requires_a_replacement (materials, layers) still passes on the shared walker.
- Satisfied: DSP-009 role preservation on replace and update, DSP-003 for pens, line types, fills, pen tables and materials (layer structures and profiles plug into references.rs in their epics); DSP-006 command side; DSP-007 table editing without touching element references; DSP-001 'without editing the elements'.
notes: SRS: DSP-003 DSP-006 DSP-007 DSP-001 DSP-009.

title: Set up golden plan images on CI software adapters
description:
WHY: DSP-018 (S): 2D rendering shall match golden reference images on every supported platform within a per-pixel tolerance defined in the test plan. Today there are no image tests (egui_kittest is a dev-dependency with only the eframe feature, crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs has four label tests), no tolerance is written down and the CI runners have no GPU adapter (.github/workflows/ci.yml).

WHAT: enable the wgpu and snapshot features of the egui_kittest dev-dependency (`egui_kittest = { workspace = true, features = ["eframe", "wgpu", "snapshot"] }` in crates/archicraft-app/Cargo.toml); a new test target crates/archicraft-app/tests/plan_golden.rs; a test support module crates/archicraft-app/tests/support/plan_gpu.rs that creates a render state with egui_kittest's CPU-preferring adapter selector, registers PlanGpuResources and builds a Harness that shows only a plan pane for a given fixture project, storey, size, camera, drawing scale and PlanOptions; pixel helpers (column coverage profile, measured stroke width, block means, autocorrelation) used by plan-renderer-08 and -09; kittest.toml at the workspace root; CI installs lavapipe on ubuntu, relies on WARP on Windows and Metal on macOS, uploads *.new.png and *.diff.png on failure and offers a workflow_dispatch bless job on ubuntu; a new docs/testing.md with the 2D golden-image test plan (reference adapter, tolerance values, bless and review procedure); first goldens of the ground floors of archicraft_model::samples::storey_with_walls_and_slab() and two_storey_shell() at 1:100 (fills). Out of scope: stroke and hatch pixel assertions (-08, -09), 3D snapshots (3d-display-styles) and performance (-11).
design:
Harness: `let rs = egui_kittest::wgpu::create_render_state(egui_kittest::wgpu::default_wgpu_setup(), egui_wgpu::RendererOptions::PREDICTABLE)`, insert PlanGpuResources into `rs.renderer.write().callback_resources`, then `Harness::builder().with_size(..).with_pixels_per_point(ppp).renderer(WgpuTestRenderer::from_render_state(rs.clone())).build_ui_state(|ui, ws| views::plan::ui(..), workspace)` (egui_kittest 0.36.2's HarnessBuilder offers build_ui, build_ui_state and build_eframe; build_ui_state has no eframe Frame, so the support module passes its RenderState clone into the plan view itself); `harness.snapshot(name)` for goldens and `harness.render()` for pixel assertions. views::plan::ui must be callable with a Workspace built from a fixture (Workspace::new plus the fixture Document) and the plan_gpu flag set. Snapshot mode hides the grid and origin marker and shows no text, so goldens depend on the model drawing only, not on font rasterisation.

CI (ci.yml test job): on ubuntu `sudo apt-get install -y mesa-vulkan-drivers` and `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan`; default_wgpu_setup sorts CPU adapters first, which picks lavapipe on Linux and WARP ("Microsoft Basic Render Driver", DeviceType::Cpu) on Windows; macOS hosted runners only offer Metal on the paravirtual GPU. Upload tests/snapshots/*.new.png and *.diff.png with actions/upload-artifact when the job fails. The bless job runs only on workflow_dispatch, on ubuntu, with UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1, and uploads the new PNGs for review; goldens are always blessed on lavapipe so the reference is reproducible (macOS developers cannot produce lavapipe images locally).

Tolerance proposal for kittest.toml: threshold 0.6 (the kittest default perceptual delta), max_failed_pixels 0 on Linux (the reference adapter) and up to 0.1 % of the image area on Windows and macOS, where rasterisers differ in anti-aliasing fringes; record the observed failure counts in docs/testing.md and tighten after two weeks of CI history.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo test -p archicraft-app --test plan_golden` passes in CI on ubuntu-24.04 (lavapipe), windows-latest (WARP) and macos-latest (Metal) against one shared set of PNGs in crates/archicraft-app/tests/snapshots/.
- A smoke test logs the adapter info and, when CI=true on Linux or Windows, asserts DeviceType::Cpu, proving the software adapter is used.
- docs/testing.md states the per-pixel tolerance DSP-018 refers to (kittest threshold and max failed pixels per OS), the reference platform, the bless command (UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1, run by the ubuntu bless job) and that golden diffs are reviewed in pull requests; kittest.toml contains exactly those values.
- A deliberately changed fill colour makes the snapshot fail on all three platforms and CI uploads the diff image (verified once, noted in the pull request).
- .gitattributes marks *.png as binary; each snapshot is at most 200 kB.
- Provides the DSP-018 infrastructure; goldens for strokes, hatches and view options are added by plan-renderer-08, -09 and -10.
notes: SRS: DSP-018. Platforms per NFR-PORT-001..003. The tolerance numbers are proposals until CI history exists. egui_kittest 0.36.2 API: SnapshotOptions::threshold / max_failed_pixels, OsThreshold per OS, kittest.toml searched upward from the crate directory.

title: Select a named pen table per plan view
description:
WHY: DSP-007 (C): several named pen tables (for example colour, monochrome, dark canvas) may be defined and selected per view; switching changes only colours and weights, and element pen references are untouched. DSP-003 (M): views reference attributes by ID, so a plan view holds a PenTableId, never a table name. Today the light and dark palettes are chosen globally by the UI theme (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:106-138 and 436; persistence/prefs.rs:9-15), not per view, and are not project data.

WHAT: views/plan.rs: PlanViewState.pen_table: Option<PenTableId> (None = automatic: the DARK table in a dark UI theme, COLOUR otherwise; a stale id falls back to automatic); PlanPens::resolve(project, table) applies the table's entries over the pens' own values and takes the canvas background from the table (grid colours derived from it), replacing the theme-based canvas of task 07. ui/shell.rs status bar: a 'Pen table' combo for plan panes listing the project's tables by name, writing to the active pane's state. ui/attributes.rs Pens window: a 'Pen table' selector; with a table other than the base selected, colour and weight edits write that table's entries (UpdateAttribute(PenTable)) and a 'Reset to base' button removes an entry; next to the selector 'New table…', 'Duplicate', 'Rename' and 'Delete' define tables through AddAttribute, UpdateAttribute and DeleteAttribute(PenTable) (the last table cannot be deleted, task 05). Out of scope: persisting the per-view choice in saved views (plan-views-browser stores the PenTableId in its ViewDefinition), per-scale pen sets (SRS Section 8), 3D views.
design: Overrides on the pens' own values keep tasks 01-09 unchanged and make MONO and DARK small (only changed pens have entries). The single entry point PlanPens::resolve(project, table) should also be what plan-renderer-02's PenSet takes, so the GPU path honours the table. Follow the DisplayMode combo of 3D panes in ui/shell.rs status_bar (egui::ComboBox::from_id_salt) for the selector. Pitfall: the dark canvas needs screen-only pens with enough contrast, so DARK carries entries for selection, pre-selection, guide and snap marker. Pitfall: PlanViewState is created lazily per storey with Default, so automatic must be the default. Pointers: views/plan.rs:22-40 (PlanViewState), 106-138, 436; ui/shell.rs:167-241 (status_bar); persistence/prefs.rs:9-15 (ThemeChoice).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: the status bar of a plan pane shows 'Pen table' with 'Colour', 'Monochrome' and 'Dark canvas'; choosing 'Monochrome' in one plan tab leaves a second plan tab of the same storey on its own table (asserted on both PlanViewStates).
- Headless test: resolving two_storey_shell with COLOUR and with MONO yields different line colours and paper colours while every element's PlanStyle stays identical (DSP-007 'references untouched').
- kittest: editing a pen's colour in the Pens window with 'Dark canvas' selected changes only that table's entry; the base pen value is unchanged; undo restores the entry.
- kittest: 'New table…' followed by renaming the table to 'Print' adds a fourth table that the status-bar 'Pen table' combo lists; deleting it removes it, a pane that showed it falls back to the automatic table, and undo restores it (DSP-007 'may be defined').
- Headless test: a table entry that changes only a pen's weight changes the resolved screen width of that pen's lines and nothing else, while every element's PlanStyle stays identical (switching changes colours and weights).
- A view holding a deleted table id draws with the automatic table and does not panic.
- Satisfied: DSP-007 (Could) for plan views, tables defined and selected by PenTableId (DSP-003 views clause); persistence per saved view follows with plan-views-browser.
notes: SRS: DSP-007 DSP-003.

title: Generate hatch lines and cover regions in the plan output
description:
WHY: DSP-010 (M): hatch fills with angle, spacing and pen. DSP-011 (M): the cut fill comes from the material, and changing a material's cut fill updates every element that uses it. MAT-002 (M): editing a material updates every element using it in all views, its 2D hatching included. DSP-020 (S): paper- or model-size scaling and a per-element override of hatch rotation and origin. DSP-001 (M) lists the cover fill among the element's graphic properties. What exists (DSP-011 and MAT-002 partial): every BodyPart carries its material (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:23-28), plan_drawing merges cut polygons per material (plan.rs:119-163), UpdateMaterial bumps the revision (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:244-251) and Document drops the plan caches (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-121). Missing: hatch geometry; the plan generator only emits merged cut polygons with a flat triangle mesh (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:43-48 and 153-163), so nothing visible depends on the fill (gap analysis for DSP-011 and MAT-002).

WHAT: archicraft-geometry: new module hatch.rs with hatch_lines(hatch: &Hatch, region: &MultiPolygon<f64>, placement: HatchPlacement, paper_mm_to_model: f64, limit: usize) -> HatchLines { segments: Vec<[DVec2; 2]>, truncated: bool }: each family's parallel lines over the region's rotated bounding box, anchored at the placement origin (default model origin), with offset, stagger and dashes applied, clipped with geo BooleanOps::clip; truncated when the count would exceed limit. plan.rs: the CutRegion merge key becomes (material, element cut pen, hatch placement) and CutRegion gains cut_pen and placement; PlanElement gains its resolved line pens and line types and cover: Vec<Polygon<f64>> (union of the up-facing faces of projected parts, computed only when the element's cover resolves to a fill); new plan_fills(project, &PlanDrawing, paper_mm_to_model) -> PlanFills { cut: Vec<RegionFill>, cover: Vec<RegionFill> } where RegionFill { fill: FillId, foreground: PenId, background: Option<PenId>, hatch: Option<HatchLines> } is resolved through Project::resolve_fill. Out of scope: drawing (07), GPU hatching and the moire rule DSP-013 (plan-renderer), skin separators (plan-renderer-03).
design: geo 0.33 BooleanOps::clip(&MultiLineString, false) clips line strings against polygons robustly via i_overlay. Generate lines in a frame rotated by the family angle plus the placement rotation about the placement origin, so the pattern is anchored to the model; the line index range is floor((min - offset) / s) ..= ceil((max - offset) / s). Paper-size spacing = spacing_mm x paper_mm_to_model (0.1 m per paper mm at the 1:100 default of Appendix D.1 until plan-renderer-01 provides DrawingScale); model-size spacing = spacing_mm / 1000. Cover regions: geo::unary_union of the projected parts' up-facing triangles in plan (a slab yields its outline minus holes). Keep plan_fills separate from plan_drawing so it can be cached per (revision, storey, scale); plan-renderer-06 draws hatches procedurally on the GPU from the same RegionFill data while the no-GPU fallback keeps these CPU lines. Pitfall: precision far from the origin - compute relative to the region's bounding-box minimum and translate back. Pitfall: the merge key needs Ord for the BTreeMap; quantise the placement (1e-6) for the key. Pointers: plan.rs:21-56 and 110-170, slice.rs, mesh.rs up_facing_outline, tests/storey.rs:11-29.
acceptance_criteria:
- hatch.rs unit tests: a 1 x 1 m square with one 0 deg family of 0.1 m spacing yields 10 or 11 horizontal segments inside the square; a 90 deg placement rotation yields vertical segments; a hole receives no segments; dashes split each line into the expected number of pieces; paper scaling doubles the spacing when paper_mm_to_model doubles while model scaling does not; exceeding limit sets truncated.
- Plan regression in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs: in the house fixture with all walls in Brick, UpdateMaterial switching Brick's cut fill from MASONRY to INSUL makes plan_fills report INSUL for every wall region, the hatch segment sets differ from before, and no element changed (element maps equal) - the DSP-011 and MAT-002 clause.
- Two walls with different cut pens or hatch placements produce separate CutRegions; equal pens and placements still merge (the existing seam behaviour of joined walls is unchanged).
- A slab below the cut plane with cover FromMaterial and a material cover fill yields a cover region equal to its outline minus holes (area within 1e-6 m2); with cover None no region is produced.
- A ModelGeometry built directly in the test with one element of two BodyParts in different materials yields one RegionFill per material, each with its own material's fill, so skins of layered elements (layer-structures) take their material's cut fill without change (DSP-011 'each skin' mechanism).
- Satisfied: DSP-010 hatch geometry, the DSP-011 update clause, the MAT-002 2D-hatching clause at plan-output level, DSP-020 scaling and override behaviour, DSP-001 cover-fill output.
notes: SRS: DSP-010 DSP-011 MAT-002 DSP-020 DSP-001. Proposed default segment limit: 20,000 per region.

title: GPU plan renderer with drawing scale, line weights, hatches, skin separators and golden images
description:
Goal: Replace the egui-painter plan drawing with a lyon + wgpu renderer: a drawing scale per 2D view, paper-millimetre weights resolved at scale with hairline and uniform-thin option, anti-aliased lines with caps and joins, hatches without moire with the 3-pixel flat fallback, the layered-element drawing rules (same-material regions merged without seams, skin separator lines with their own pen switchable per view, and the Could option to show layered elements full, core only or without finishes) and cross-platform golden-image tests.

Risks: Platform rendering differences in snapshot tests: tolerance plus a software adapter in CI; lyon/wgpu version coupling handled by the pinned egui family.
design: archicraft-app views/plan_gpu.rs tessellates PlanDrawing into vertex buffers with lyon (stroke widths = paper mm x scale x dpi), cached per revision and storey; hatches as instanced line batches clipped to regions; the egui painter in views/plan.rs stays for overlays (snap markers, rubber bands); PlanOptions per view carry the separator and layered-display switches consumed by archicraft-geometry plan.rs when it emits skin regions; wgpu through the egui_wgpu re-export.
acceptance_criteria: egui_kittest wgpu snapshot tests of fixture plans pass on all three CI platforms within the per-pixel tolerance documented in docs/testing.md, rendered on a software adapter (lavapipe on Linux, WARP on Windows) in CI; cut lines are heavier than projected lines at every zoom and no line is thinner than one device pixel (pixel assertions); hatch spacing below 3 px renders as a tone; the hard-coded 'Scale 1:100' label becomes a per-view drawing scale in ViewState that zooming never changes (VIEW-013; the ViewDefinition of plan-views-browser persists it); the cores of joined same-material walls draw without a seam while the F2 wall shows six skin regions with separator lines in the separator pen that a per-view switch hides; the core-only view option hides finish skins.
notes: SRS: DSP-004 DSP-012 DSP-013 DSP-014 DSP-017 DSP-018 DSP-019 VIEW-013

title: Reference pens, line types and cover fills from elements
description:
WHY: DSP-001 (M): every 2D graphic property of an element (outline pen, line type, cut-fill pattern and pens, cover fill) is a reference to a project-level attribute, so editing the attribute updates every referencing element in all views without editing the elements. DSP-005 (S): screen-only pens are used for on-screen feedback only, so no element property may reference one. DSP-009 (M): element settings offer only the fills valid for the role being edited, so a cover fill must serve the cover role. DSP-020 (S): a per-element override of hatch rotation and origin. MAT-001 (M) gives materials an optional cover fill that elements can show. Elements carry no graphic property besides their material today (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:275-288).

WHAT: archicraft-model: PlanStyle { cut_pen, uncut_pen, overhead_pen: PenId, uncut_line_type, overhead_line_type: LineTypeId, cover: CoverFill::{None, FromMaterial, Custom(MaterialFill)}, hatch_placement: Option<HatchPlacement> } as the common field plan on the element envelope (Element after element-kind-framework) and on the DefaultsSlot of ToolDefaults, copied by Project::prototype, new_wall and new_slab. Template slots: cut_pen = structural cut pen, uncut_pen = uncut pen, overhead_pen = overhead pen, uncut line type SOLID, overhead line type DASH, cover FromMaterial. validate.rs validate_element: referenced pens and line types exist, screen-only pens are rejected for element properties (DSP-005), a Custom cover serves the cover role (DSP-009), the hatch rotation is finite; check_tool_defaults does the same for slots; integrity_problems reports dangling element style references. ElementKind::translate (and the transform hook of the kind registry) moves hatch_placement.origin with the element. IFCX: archicraft::element gains plan { cutPen, uncutPen, overheadPen, uncutLineType, overheadLineType, cover { mode, fill?, foreground?, background? }, hatchPlacement? { rotation, origin } } in the common element codec of schema.rs, writer.rs and reader.rs; toolDefaults slots carry it; the reader repairs missing or dangling references to the first pen of the matching role with a warning; the epic's migration step adds plan with role defaults to every element and slot of older files. crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs: one slab of two_storey_shell gets a hatch_placement so the golden files cover it. Re-bless (reviewed diff: only archicraft::element and toolDefaults change). Out of scope: drawing (06, 07), pickers (09), DSP-016 view overrides, per-skin pens (layer-structures, plan-renderer).
design: References are explicit ids, not 'use the role default' placeholders, so DSP-001's propagation falls out of resolution at draw time and DeleteAttribute (05) can enumerate every user. Cut fill and cut-fill pens are deliberately not on PlanStyle: DSP-011 sources them from the material, and the element only carries the hatch placement override. CoverFill::FromMaterial lets a material's optional cover fill (MAT-001) show on every slab using it. PlanStyle lives in the common envelope, not in kinds/wall.rs or kinds/slab.rs, so columns, beams, roofs and the 2D elements of drafting-trim-split get it for free; kinds with extra graphic properties register them through the attribute_refs hook that task 05 adds to KindDescriptor. Pitfall: hatch_placement.origin is in storey-local plan coordinates, so every transform (move now, rotate and mirror in selection-transforms) must transform it; rotation adds to rotation_deg. Pointers: element.rs:258-307, project.rs:120-157 and 281-326 (factories), validate.rs:244-282, command.rs check_tool_defaults, writer.rs:192-217, reader.rs:604-713, samples.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: a wall created from the template defaults references the structural cut pen, the uncut pen and the DASH overhead line type; AddElements with a screen-only pen, a missing line type or a Custom cover fill without the cover role is rejected with CommandError::Invalid naming the property; add_undo_redo_keeps_identity still passes.
- integrity_problems reports an element whose cut pen no longer exists (state built directly in the test).
- Moving an element with a hatch placement moves the origin by the same delta (MoveElements test).
- roundtrip.rs: plan styles of every sample element and default slot survive save/load; a reader test with a dangling pen id loads with a warning and the role default.
- Migration test: the frozen format-v<N> fixture loads with role-default styles on every element and no warnings.
- Golden files re-blessed with a reviewed diff; conformance/run.sh green; the standard geometry (meshes, transforms) is unchanged in the diff (IFX-063).
- Satisfied: DSP-005 screen-only pens excluded from element properties, DSP-001 data clause (every element 2D property is an ID reference; cut fill and its pens come from the material), DSP-009 validation clause, DSP-020 per-element override stored and transformed.
notes: SRS: DSP-001 DSP-005 DSP-009 DSP-020 MAT-001.

title: Verify exit criterion: Graphic attribute resources: pens, line types, fills and material plan display
description:
WHY: The epic is complete only when its exit criterion holds on the integrated workspace: project-level pens, line types, fills and pen tables with stable IDs exist in every new project, materials and elements reference them, they are protected when in use, editable in dialogs, drawn in every plan and round-trip through archicraft::project (DSP-001, DSP-002, DSP-003, DSP-005, DSP-006, DSP-007, DSP-008, DSP-009, DSP-010, DSP-011, DSP-020, MAT-001, MAT-002, MAT-003).

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged branch: cargo test, clippy and fmt on the workspace, conformance/run.sh on the golden files, the template, ID, command, plan-regression, round-trip, migration and kittest suites named by tasks 01-10; review the three golden re-bless diffs once more; update docs/implementation-status.md (requirement rows of all 14 IDs with evidence paths, the 4.5 and 4.27 section counts, the extension points with an 'Add a graphic attribute or referrer' entry, and remove the 'All fill patterns render as solid tones' debt item); close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new features; open findings become new beads.
design: Checklist task, no new code. Verify against the SRS text, not the task titles: DSP-001 'without editing the elements' (rename and update tests), DSP-002 'without defining any attribute' (fresh template plan with zero fallbacks), DSP-003 replacement rule for pens, line types, fills, pen tables and materials, DSP-009 role filtering in element settings, MAT-002 '2D hatching included'. Record which clauses remain for later epics: true paper weights at scale and moire-free GPU hatches (plan-renderer), per-saved-view pen tables (plan-views-browser), layer structures and profiles as attributes (layer-structures, profiles-columns-beams through references.rs). Pointers: docs/implementation-status.md sections 4.5 (line 286) and 4.27 (line 734), Extension points and Technical debt.
acceptance_criteria:
- The template contains the DSP-005 role pen table with the six weights, at least six line types and eight hatch fills (template test).
- Each of the 25 materials references a cut fill and the D.4 priority.
- Renaming an attribute keeps references (ID test).
- Deleting an in-use attribute requires a replacement (command test).
- Editing a material's cut fill changes every element's plan output (plan regression).
- Pen/line-type/fill dialogs with kittest labels.
- Attributes stored in archicraft::project round-trip.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green on the re-blessed golden files.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID: DSP-001 DSP-002 DSP-003 DSP-005 DSP-006 DSP-007 DSP-008 DSP-009 DSP-010 DSP-011 DSP-020 MAT-001 MAT-002 MAT-003.
- Deferred clauses are recorded in docs/implementation-status.md with their owning epic: DSP-011 per-skin cut fills and DSP-003 identity of layer structures (layer-structures), DSP-003 profiles and MAT-001 profile regions (profiles-columns-beams), MAT-001 face references (MAT-004), per-saved-view pen tables (plan-views-browser), paper-true weights at scale and moire-free GPU hatches (plan-renderer).
- The epic plan-attributes is closed in beads (bd close), with follow-up beads filed for any open finding.
notes: SRS: DSP-001 DSP-002 DSP-003 DSP-005 DSP-006 DSP-007 DSP-008 DSP-009 DSP-010 DSP-011 DSP-020 MAT-001 MAT-002 MAT-003

title: Resolve pen weights at the drawing scale with the one-pixel floor and thin-line mode
description:
WHY: DSP-004 (M) says every line gets its weight from its pen (DSP-001), cut outlines are drawn visibly heavier than projected outlines at every zoom level, and no line is thinner than one device pixel. DSP-019 (S) says weights are specified in paper millimetres including a hairline, resolved against the view's drawing scale (VIEW-013), with a view option switching between true weights and uniform thin lines. DSP-012 (S) says separator lines between the skins of a layered element are drawn with their own pen. What exists (gap analysis: DSP-004 partial, DSP-019 missing): today widths are constants in logical points (CUT_WIDTH 1.8, PROJECTED_WIDTH 0.9 at crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:140-143) that are never multiplied by pixels_per_point, so projected lines fall below one device pixel at 100 % DPI and take epaint's faded thin-line path. The prerequisite epic plan-attributes replaces the constants but not the resolution: plan-attributes-01 stores PenWeight in paper millimetres (HAIRLINE = 0.0), plan-attributes-04 gives every element a PlanStyle with cut_pen, uncut_pen and overhead_pen references, and plan-attributes-07 creates crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan_style.rs whose PlanPens maps paper weights to screen points through an interim monotonic map (0.50 mm -> 1.8 pt, 0.18 mm -> 0.9 pt, hairline -> 1 px) that ignores the drawing scale and pixels_per_point. Missing: resolution against the drawing scale and the display density, the one-device-pixel floor, the WeightMode option and a pen for every LineClass of plan-renderer-03.

WHAT: extend views/plan_style.rs of plan-attributes-07 (no second module): `pen_for(style, LineClass) -> PenId` mapping CutOutline to PlanStyle.cut_pen (CutRegion.cut_pen of plan-attributes-06 for merged regions), SkinSeparator to the project's SkinSeparator role pen (plan-renderer-12), Projected to uncut_pen, Overhead to overhead_pen and Hatch to the RegionFill foreground pen; `WeightMode {TrueWeights, UniformThin}`; `stroke_width_px` computing device-pixel widths from paper mm x scale denominator x zoom x pixels_per_point with the hairline at exactly one device pixel, a one-pixel floor for every line and a two-pixel floor for cut outlines; PlanPens::resolve(project, table) keeps resolving colours and pen-table values (DSP-007) but carries paper millimetres instead of interim points; paper/model length helpers delegate to DrawingScale (plan-renderer-01). The painter path in views/plan.rs, which draws model lines until plan-renderer-08 and remains the no-GPU fallback afterwards, switches to stroke_width_px(..) / pixels_per_point with the view's DrawingScale and TrueWeights, so DSP-004 holds before the GPU path lands. Out of scope: the separator pen attribute and its IFCX persistence (plan-renderer-12), GPU drawing (plan-renderer-08), the per-view UI for the weight mode (plan-renderer-10), separator pens per layer structure or per skin, and named pen tables per view (plan-attributes-10).
design:
Resolver: `pub fn stroke_width_px(weight: PenWeight, class: LineClass, scale: DrawingScale, zoom_pt_per_m: f64, ppp: f32, mode: WeightMode) -> f32`. true_px = paper_mm * 1e-3 * denominator * zoom_pt_per_m * ppp; Hairline -> 1.0; floors: CutOutline max(true_px, 2.0), every other class max(true_px, 1.0); UniformThin -> 1.0. Why this keeps DSP-004 at every zoom with the DSP-005 defaults (cut 0.35/0.50 mm vs projected 0.18/0.25 mm, ratio >= 1.4): while the projected width p < 2 px the cut line is >= 2 px; once p >= 2 px the cut line is >= 1.4 p >= p + 0.8 px. If a user makes a cut pen lighter than the projected pen, the pens win ("weight from its pen"); the 2-px floor still keeps cut lines >= 2 px at overview zooms. Document this in the module docs.

LineClass is the enum emitted by archicraft-geometry plan.rs (plan-renderer-03); add a Hatch class for hatch lines here if needed. Pen lookup uses the attribute API of plan-attributes (Attributes::pen(id), pens_with_role(role), the element's PlanStyle); PenWeight 0.0 is the hairline (plan-attributes-01). plan-attributes-07 asks plan-renderer to build its GPU pen set from the same PlanPens::resolve entry point; keep that single entry point. The GPU shader (plan-renderer-08) re-implements only `max(mm * k, floor)` with k = 1e-3 * denominator * px_per_model_m passed as a uniform; this CPU function is the reference that the pixel tests of -08 compare against, so the formula exists once.

The separator pen itself (role, template pen, IFCX) is plan-renderer-12; this task only resolves it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table-driven unit tests in views/plan_style.rs sweep zoom 1..5000 pt/m in logarithmic steps, pixels_per_point 1.0/1.25/2.0 and scales 1:50/1:100/1:200 with the template pens: the resolved cut-outline width is at least the projected width + 0.75 device px and every resolved width is >= 1.0 device px (DSP-004).
- The hairline (PenWeight 0.0) resolves to exactly 1.0 device px at every zoom; a 0.50 mm cut pen at 1:100 resolves to max(2.0, 0.05 m x zoom x ppp), i.e. 2.0 px at 20 pt/m and 20 px at 400 pt/m with ppp 1.0; halving the scale denominator halves every true width above the floor (DSP-019, VIEW-013).
- UniformThin resolves every LineClass to 1.0 device px (DSP-019 view option).
- Pen-mapping test on two_storey_shell with the template attributes: a wall's cut outline maps to its PlanStyle.cut_pen (the structural cut pen), the slab's projected outline to its uncut_pen, overhead lines to its overhead_pen, SkinSeparator to the separator role pen of plan-renderer-12 and hatch lines to the fill's foreground pen; changing the separator pen's weight with UpdateAttribute (plan-attributes-05) changes the resolved separator width without editing any element (DSP-001 by PenId).
- With the MONO pen table selected, PlanPens::resolve returns the table's colours and weights and stroke_width_px uses the table weight (DSP-007 keeps working).
- Painter path: views/plan.rs no longer uses the interim weight-to-point map for model lines; a unit test of the painter stroke helper at ppp 1.0 and 2.0 shows every model-line stroke >= 1 device px and cut wider than projected (DSP-004 before the GPU path).
- Length helpers: a 3 mm paper dash at 1:100 is 0.30 m in the model; a model-size hatch spacing of 0.10 m is the same at every scale (unit tests).
- Satisfies the resolution half of DSP-004 and DSP-019 (pen weight, paper mm, hairline, drawing scale, one-pixel floor, thin-line mode) on the CPU; the GPU strokes of plan-renderer-08 and the per-view switch of plan-renderer-10 complete them.
notes: SRS: DSP-004 DSP-019 DSP-012. DSP-005 default weights at 1:100: hairline, 0.13, 0.18, 0.25, 0.35 and 0.50 mm. Interpretation to confirm with the product owner: the heavier-cut clause of DSP-004 applies to true weights; the uniform-thin option of DSP-019 is an explicit user override in which every line is 1 device px (as in the reference product). Record it in the module docs and in docs/testing.md.

title: Build the Pens, Line types and Fills dialogs
description:
WHY: DSP-006 (S): the user edits a pen's colour, weight and description, and the description is shown wherever pens are selectable. DSP-005 (S): the pen table is organized by roles. DSP-008 (S): line types are defined by dash and gap lengths in millimetres with a paper- or model-size flag. DSP-009 (M), DSP-010 (M) and DSP-020 (S): fills declare their roles; hatches have angle, spacing, pen and scaling. DSP-003 (M): deleting an attribute in use requires choosing a replacement. No editor exists for any of these (gap analysis: DSP-006 missing).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/attributes.rs (new), following the Materials dialog pattern (ui/dialogs.rs:376-478): windows 'Pens', 'Line types' and 'Fills', each with search, a list (pens grouped by role with colour swatch and weight; line types with a dash preview; fills with a swatch drawn from archicraft_geometry::hatch_lines on a small square), an editor (name, short code, description; pen colour and a weight combo of the six standard weights plus a custom millimetre value; line-type dash/gap list in mm and the scaling flag; fill role checkboxes 'Cut', 'Cover', 'Drafting', Solid or Hatch, a family table with 'Angle', 'Spacing', 'Offset', 'Stagger' and dashes, add or remove up to four families, scaling, foreground and background pens), Duplicate, and Delete with a replacement chooser shown when attribute_uses is non-empty (with the user count), all through AddAttribute, UpdateAttribute and DeleteAttribute. ui/widgets.rs: pen_choice(ui, id, project, current, filter) showing swatch, code and name with the description as secondary text and hover text (DSP-006), line_type_choice, and fill_choice(role) offering only fills that serve the role (DSP-009). Dialogs state for the three windows; Action::Pens, Action::LineTypes and Action::Fills in ui/actions.rs, menu items next to Materials in ui/shell.rs and buttons in ui/browser.rs. Out of scope: material and element pickers (09), per-view pen-table selection (10), pen-table entry editing (10).
design: Mirror material_editor (ui/dialogs.rs:765-845): clone, edit, commit one Update command per completed change (drag_stopped for sliders and DragValues, so a drag is one undo step). A generic list/editor helper over AttributeMeta avoids three copies of the search, duplicate and delete code. The weight combo shows 'Hairline' for 0 and the standard values; a custom weight uses a DragValue in mm (0..=5). The fill swatch reuses hatch_lines with paper_mm_to_model chosen so 1 paper mm = 2 px. Pitfall: labels must be unique and stable for harness.get_by_label (see the existing tests). Pitfall: text fields must not trigger single-key tool shortcuts (UI-008, existing behaviour through works_while_typing). Pointers: ui/dialogs.rs:35-56 (Dialogs), 376-478, 765-845; ui/widgets.rs:96-127 (text, choice); ui/actions.rs:33, 68, 103 (Materials action); ui/shell.rs:108; ui/browser.rs:108; tests/ui.rs:18-40.
acceptance_criteria:
