- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): opening Pens from the Project menu shows the window 'Pens' with the role group labels 'Structural cut line' and 'Snap marker' and, for a selected pen, the labels 'Colour', 'Weight' and 'Description'; choosing 0.35 in the weight combo executes UpdateAttribute (the project pen weight changes and the Edit menu offers 'Undo Change pen').
- kittest: editing a pen's 'Colour' and its 'Description' each execute one UpdateAttribute (the Edit menu offers 'Undo Change pen'); in 'Line types', changing a dash length and switching the scaling flag to 'Model size' each execute one UpdateAttribute; a drag of a DragValue is a single undo step.
- kittest: the 'Line types' window lists the six template line types; the 'Fills' window lists the eight hatches and shows the role checkboxes 'Cut', 'Cover', 'Drafting' and the family fields 'Angle' and 'Spacing'.
- kittest: 'Delete…' on the structural cut pen shows 'Replace it in every element and tool with:' and a replacement choice; confirming rewrites the elements (asserted on the project) and one undo restores them.
- Unit tests of the widgets' option builders: pen options for element properties exclude screen-only pens; fill_choice(Cover) lists only cover-role fills; every pen option carries its description.
- Satisfied: DSP-006 in full, DSP-005 organization visible and editable, DSP-008 editability, DSP-009, DSP-010 and DSP-020 definition editing, DSP-003 delete-with-replacement in the UI.
notes: SRS: DSP-003 DSP-005 DSP-006 DSP-008 DSP-009 DSP-010 DSP-020. String literals stay plain until commands-and-l10n externalises them.

title: Ship the default attribute set and persist it in archicraft::project
description:
WHY: DSP-002 (M): every new project contains a default attribute set (pens, line types, fills, materials with cut fills) sufficient to draw and read a plan without defining any attribute. DSP-005 (S): the default pen table is organized by roles with default weights at 1:100 of hairline, 0.13, 0.18, 0.25, 0.35 and 0.50 mm. DSP-007 (C): named pen tables such as colour, monochrome and dark canvas. DSP-008 (S): at least six built-in line types (solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot, centre, hidden). DSP-010 (M): solid fills and at least one hatch each for concrete, masonry, timber, insulation and soil. DSP-020 (S): at least eight hatches (parallel lines, cross-hatch, diagonal, brick/masonry, concrete, insulation, earth, wood grain), each with paper- or model-size scaling. IFX-060 and IFX-067 store project resources in archicraft::project; IFX-062 requires a format version with migration. What exists (DSP-002 partial): the template already ships the 25 materials with a CutFill each (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs:31-257 and 274-296), and a fresh plan is legible only because the renderer hard-codes the Palette and line widths (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:106-143). Missing: the template has no pens, line types, fills or pen tables, and archicraft::project (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:126-209) has no place for them.

WHAT: (1) template.rs: pub fn default_attributes() -> Attributes with one pen per DSP-005 role (weights covering all six standard weights; screen-only colours taken from the light Palette in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:121-136), six line types with short codes SOLID, DASH, DOT, DASHDOT, CENTRE, HIDDEN, the solid fill SOLID (cut, cover, drafting) and eight hatch fills PARA, CROSS, DIAG, MASONRY, CONC, INSUL, EARTH, WOOD (cut and drafting; PARA, CROSS and DIAG also cover) using the cut-fill foreground and fill background pens, and three pen tables COLOUR (no entries, white background), MONO (model pens black or grey) and DARK (dark background and light lines from Palette::new(true), plan.rs:108-119); default_metric_project() fills Project.attributes with fresh identities (IFX-011). (2) schema.rs: pens, lineTypes, fills and penTables arrays inside the project object, enumerations derived from the model ALL arrays, attribute ids declared as string(), weights and lengths as Real millimetres. (3) writer.rs project_attribute: the four arrays after materials in model order, through a reusable writer::attribute_records(&Attributes). (4) reader.rs: read_pen, read_line_type, read_fill, read_pen_table in the read_material style (report.or with defaults, invalid values repaired with a warning, records without a valid id skipped); a fill pen that does not resolve is repaired to the first pen of the matching role with a warning. (5) FORMAT_VERSION + 1 with a Migration in alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework) that inserts template::default_attributes() into older files, so they open complete and without warnings; tasks 03 and 04 extend this same migration step. (6) Freeze the current golden file as crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/format-v<N>/walls-and-slab.ifcx, where N is FORMAT_VERSION before this task (2 after element-kind-framework-12 unless another epic bumped it first), then re-bless the golden files (reviewed diff: only archicraft::project and the schemas section change) and run conformance/run.sh. Out of scope: materials referencing the fills (03), element references (04), editing UI (08), per-view table selection (10).
design: Single source of truth: reader fallbacks and the migration both call template::default_attributes(), so a missing collection becomes the template set rather than an empty one. Short codes double as stable keys for migrations and tests; names are display text that users may rename. Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md. The migration works on the parsed JSON (Migration::apply(&mut IfcxFile, &mut Vec<Problem>) from element-kind-framework) and reuses writer::attribute_records so there is one serialisation. Pitfall: attribute ids are not node paths; declaring them as dataType Reference would make validate.rs and the reference viewer try to resolve them. Pitfall: do not use quantityKind Length for weights or dash lengths (IFCX Length means metres). Pitfall: keep archicraft::project member order stable (new arrays after materials) so diffs stay readable. Re-bless budget of the epic: 02 (attributes), 03 (material records), 04 (element styles), each diff reviewed for scope. FORMAT_VERSION is bumped once in this task; 03 and 04 extend the same step because no release is cut in between (if one is, bump again). Pointers: template.rs:274-296, schema.rs:126-209, writer.rs:122-140 (material_record pattern), reader.rs:212-263 (read_material pattern), tests/roundtrip.rs:48-62 and 198-231.
acceptance_criteria:
- template.rs test template_attributes: every PenRole has at least one pen; the pen weights contain all six DSP-005 weights; line types SOLID, DASH, DOT, DASHDOT, CENTRE, HIDDEN exist with millimetre dash lists and SOLID is continuous; at least eight hatch fills with the codes PARA, CROSS, DIAG, MASONRY, CONC, INSUL, EARTH, WOOD serve the cut role; at least one solid fill exists; every fill validates and its pens resolve; the tables COLOUR, MONO and DARK exist; every template pen, line type, fill and pen table has a non-empty name, a short code unique within its type and a description (DSP-003); every hatch fill declares its scaling (Paper for all template hatches, DSP-020); every_project_gets_new_identities covers pens, line types, fills and pen tables.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: round_trip_restores_the_editable_model passes with the populated template; a new test edits a pen (name, colour, weight), a line type (dashes, scaling), a fill (roles, families) and a pen-table entry and reloads them unchanged.
- Reader tests: a fill pointing to a missing pen loads with a warning and a repaired reference; a pen with weight -1 is clamped with a warning; an unknown role code is a warning, not an error.
- Migration test: the frozen format-v<N> fixture loads with one Info migration row, the template attribute set present and no warnings.
- Golden files re-blessed with a reviewed diff; written_files_validate_without_problems, golden_files_are_reproduced, container_matches_the_ifcx_json_schema and conformance/run.sh on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx green.
- Satisfied: DSP-002 for pens, line types and fills; DSP-005 default table with the six weights; DSP-007 tables defined; DSP-008 six line types; DSP-010 hatch availability; DSP-020 catalogue of eight; attributes persist in archicraft::project (IFX-060, IFX-067).
notes: SRS: DSP-002 DSP-005 DSP-007 DSP-008 DSP-010 DSP-020. Proposed default pens (light): structural cut 0.50 black; non-structural cut 0.35 black; uncut 0.18 grey 70; overhead 0.13 grey 150; cut-fill foreground 0.13 black; cover-fill foreground 0.13 grey 110; fill background hairline white; drafting 0.25 black; annotation line 0.18 black; annotation text 0.25 black; selection, pre-selection, guide and snap marker hairline in the current Palette colours. Proposed line types (paper mm): solid []; dashed [3.0, 1.5]; dotted [0.1, 1.0]; dash-dot [6.0, 1.5, 0.1, 1.5]; centre [12.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0]; hidden [1.5, 1.0]. Proposed hatches (paper mm): PARA 0 deg / 1.5; CROSS 45+135 deg / 2.0; DIAG 45 deg / 2.0; MASONRY 45 deg / 1.0; CONC 45 deg dashed [1.0, 1.5] + 135 deg dashed / 3.0; INSUL 60+120 deg / 2.5; EARTH 45 deg + 0 deg dashed [2, 2] / 3.0; WOOD 0 deg dashed [8, 1] stagger 3 / 1.2. Tune visually once hatches render (06, 07). Coordinate the FORMAT_VERSION number with epics landing concurrently (layer-structures, plan-views-browser). Related requirements owned by ifcx-interop: IFX-060, IFX-062, IFX-067.

title: Add DrawingScale and a per-view drawing scale to plan views
description:
WHY: VIEW-013 (S) requires that every 2D view has a drawing scale (default 1:100, Appendix D.1), that line weights, hatch spacing and annotation sizes are given in paper units at that scale (DSP-019), and that zooming does not change the scale. Today the status bar prints a literal "Scale 1:100" (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:241) that is unrelated to anything, ProjectSettings has no scale (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:47-52) and the only zoom quantity is Camera2d.scale in points per metre (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/camera.rs:13-16). Every later task of this epic resolves paper millimetres against the scale introduced here.

WHAT: archicraft-model gets a headless `DrawingScale` value type in a new crates/archicraft-model/src/drawing.rs (denominator, presets, parse and format "1:50", validation, serde, paper-to-model conversion helpers), re-exported from lib.rs so ViewDefinition (plan-views-browser), sections and annotations can use it. archicraft-app gets `PlanViewState.scale` (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:21-46), kept outside Camera2d so fit, zoom_at, zoom_to and previous/next zoom can never change it, and a "Drawing scale" combo in the status bar replacing the literal label, with presets and a typed custom value. Out of scope: persisting the scale in saved views or IFCX (VIEW-004, plan-views-browser maps ViewState to ViewDefinition), annotation sizes beyond the shared paper-to-model conversion (no annotation kind exists before sections-elevations-dims, increment 3), and using the scale for widths and hatches (plan-renderer-02, -08, -09).
design:
DrawingScale is a newtype over NonZeroU32 (the denominator) with `PRESETS = [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100, 200, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000]`, `MAX = 10000`, `fn ratio(self) -> f64`, `fn paper_mm_to_model(self, mm: f64) -> f64 { mm * 1e-3 * denominator }` and `fn model_to_paper_mm`. FromStr splits on ':' and trims; Serialize as the integer denominator so plan-views-browser can store it in ViewDefinition without a string format. It lives in the model crate because it is a pure value with no UI dependency (NFR-MNT-002) and several later crates need it.

PlanViewState (views/plan.rs:21-46) gains `pub scale: DrawingScale`. Do NOT put the scale into Camera2d: ZoomHistory (camera.rs:77-95) stores Camera2d copies, and previous/next zoom would then restore old scales. ws.plan_views is keyed by StoreyId (workspace.rs:56), so "per view" means per plan pane until plan-views-browser introduces ViewDefinition; Workspace::replace_document clears plan_views (workspace.rs:95), so the scale returns to 1:100 after opening a file until ViewDefinition persists it.

Status bar (shell.rs:228-249): replace `ui.label("Scale 1:100")` by `egui::ComboBox::from_label("Drawing scale")` over PRESETS plus a "Custom..." entry that opens a small text field parsed with DrawingScale::from_str (invalid input keeps the old value and shows the parse message as hover text). Keep the existing pt/m zoom readout so zoom and scale are visibly different quantities. Changing the scale is view state, not a model Command (not undoable, like zoom).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/drawing.rs: "1:50", "1 : 200" and "50" parse to 1:50, 1:200 and 1:50; "1:0", "0:1", "1:-5", "abc" and "1:100000" are rejected with a message; Display formats "1:100"; serde round-trips.
- `DrawingScale::default()` is 1:100 (Appendix D.1) and `paper_mm_to_model(0.5)` is 0.05 m at 1:100 and 0.025 m at 1:50; `model_to_paper_mm` is its inverse (unit tests).
- App unit test: on a PlanViewState, pan moves camera.center and zoom_at, fit, zoom_to, previous_zoom and next_zoom change camera.scale, while `scale` stays unchanged in every case (VIEW-013: zooming does not change the scale).
- Paper-unit clause of VIEW-013 for annotation sizes: a unit test converts a 2.5 mm paper text height to 0.25 m at 1:100 and 0.125 m at 1:50 through `DrawingScale::paper_mm_to_model`, the single conversion that line weights (plan-renderer-02), hatch spacing (plan-renderer-09) and the later annotations of sections-elevations-dims (ANN-004 to ANN-008) use; the module docs say so.
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the status bar of the ground-floor plan shows a combo labelled "Drawing scale" reading "1:100"; choosing "1:50" sets `workspace().plan_views[ground].scale` to 1:50 while the upper storey's plan view (opened from the project browser) stays at 1:100; a following FitWindow action keeps 1:50; no widget labelled "Scale 1:100" remains.
- cargo test, clippy -D warnings and fmt are green. Satisfies the VIEW-013 clauses "every 2D view shall have a drawing scale (default 1:100)" and "zooming does not change the scale"; the paper-unit clause is completed for line weights and hatch spacing by plan-renderer-02, -08 and -09; annotation sizes have no consumer in increment 1 and are handed to sections-elevations-dims by a follow-up bead from plan-renderer-done.
notes: SRS: VIEW-013. Appendix D.1: drawing scale 1:100. Open question: whether new plan views should take a project-level default scale (D.1 lists 1:100 as a default value); left to plan-views-browser/templates-presets, this task uses the constant default.

title: Emit pen-classed plan strokes as joined polylines with skin metadata
description:
WHY: DSP-014 (M) requires lines with correct caps and joins at every zoom level; today projected and overhead lines are independent two-point segments (PlanElement.projected/overhead in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs) drawn with egui line_segment (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:246-262), so corners have no joins at all. DSP-004 needs every line to be attributable to a pen, i.e. to an element and a line class. DSP-012 and DSP-017 need to know which skin of a layer structure (index and role core/finish/other, PRF-001) every cut polygon comes from.

WHAT: in archicraft-geometry plan.rs add `LineClass {CutOutline, SkinSeparator, Projected, Overhead}`, `PlanStroke {element, class, points, closed}` and `PlanDrawing.strokes`; a segment-chaining utility that joins segments sharing endpoints within MODEL_TOLERANCE into maximal open chains and closed loops and merges collinear consecutive segments; per-element skin-tagged cut polygons `PlanElement.cut_skins: Vec<SkinCut {skin: Option<SkinRef>, material, polygon}>`; and `BodyPart.skin_index: Option<u16>` (0-based structure order) in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs next to the `BodyPart.role: Option<SkinRole>` that layer-structures-04 adds, set where layer-structures-04 builds the Skin_1..Skin_n parts so the plan never parses part names; SkinRef {index, role} is built from both. In this task CutOutline strokes are simply the rings of the merged CutRegions of plan-attributes-06 (unchanged look). The egui painter path in views/plan.rs draws `strokes` with Shape::line/closed_line, so joins improve there immediately. Out of scope: separator classification and the seam rule (plan-renderer-04), layered display filtering (-05), GPU drawing (-06, -08), and cross-storey view ranges (plan-views-browser).
design:
Chaining: quantise endpoints to a MODEL_TOLERANCE grid (look up the 3x3 neighbouring cells to avoid cell-boundary misses), build an adjacency map, walk degree-2 vertices into chains and close a chain when it returns to its start; vertices whose degree is not 2 terminate chains so T-junctions keep separate polylines (their butt caps then end on the other line's centreline and leave no gap). Linear in the number of segments. Join endpoints with MODEL_TOLERANCE (1e-5 m; crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs after element-kind-framework, today crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:10), not with plan.rs EPS = 1e-9, which stays for the cut-plane height tests.

Keep mesh.up_facing_outline/down_facing_outline (mesh.rs) as the sources; chaining happens in plan_drawing after collection. SkinRef {index: u16, role: SkinRole} uses SkinRole of crates/archicraft-model/src/layer_structure.rs (layer-structures-01, PRF-001); the per-skin BodyParts named Skin_n (IFX-017) of layer-structures-04 carry the role, this task adds the index. CutRegion keeps its spade fill triangulation (geometry/src/triangulate.rs) which the GPU renderer reuses. PlanDrawing grows but the Document::plan cache (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:105-121) is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs: the slab below the cut plane in house() yields exactly one closed Projected stroke with four points (previously four segments); overhead parts yield Overhead strokes; the T-junction plan of two_storey_shell yields projected chains without duplicated endpoints.
- Unit tests for the chaining utility: the shuffled and partly reversed segments of a square form one closed loop; an L plus a detached segment form two open chains; endpoints closer than MODEL_TOLERANCE join and endpoints farther apart do not; collinear consecutive segments merge into one; a vertex of degree 3 ends the chains meeting there.
- The free 5.0 m wall of archicraft_model::samples::f2_layered_wall() (layer-structures-09) cut in plan: PlanElement.cut_skins has six entries with skin indices 0..5, the F2 materials in structure order and the roles stored in the structure; single-material walls have `skin: None`.
- Existing tests stay green, including plan_cuts_walls_and_projects_slab, picking and snapping: PlanElement.segments() still returns every outline segment.
- Provides the data prerequisites of DSP-014 (joined polylines), DSP-004 (lines attributable to element and class) and DSP-012/DSP-017 (skin identity).
notes: SRS: DSP-014 DSP-004 DSP-012 DSP-017. PRF-001 skin roles: core, finish, other. Appendix D.7 F2: brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm.

title: Make material cut fills references to fills and pens
description:
WHY: MAT-001 (M): a material is a project resource with identity (DSP-003), a category, appearance, a plan representation (a cut fill with pens and an optional cover fill) and an intersection priority 1-999. DSP-011 (M): the cut fill of a construction element, or of each skin, comes from its material, and changing a material's cut fill updates every element that uses it. MAT-003 (M): the default template contains 25 named materials, each with a colour, a cut fill and the Appendix D.4 priority. DSP-002 (M) requires materials with cut fills in the default set. What exists and stays (MAT-001 and MAT-003 partial): identity (id, name, code, description), category, colour, opacity and the validated priority 1-999 (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:142-178), element references by MaterialId, the 25 template names with their colours and Appendix D.4 priorities (template.rs:31-257), the Materials editor (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:765-845) and DeleteMaterial with a replacement (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:520-552). Missing: the template test asserts only count and validity (template.rs:391-402), there is no cover fill, and Material.cut_fill is a FillPattern label plus an RGB tone derived from the colour (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:94-138, template.rs:286-290), which the verifier graded as not a real cut fill (no fill definition, no pens).

WHAT: material.rs: replace CutFill and FillPattern by MaterialFill { fill: FillId, foreground: Option<PenId> (override of the fill's pen), background: FillBackground::{FromFill, Transparent, Pen(PenId)} }; Material gets cut_fill: MaterialFill and cover_fill: Option<MaterialFill>; Material::validate keeps the value ranges and a new validate_in(&Attributes) checks that the cut fill exists and serves the cut role and the cover fill the cover role; Project::integrity_problems reports dangling material fill or pen references. attributes.rs: Project::resolve_fill(&MaterialFill) -> Option<ResolvedFill { fill, foreground: &Pen, background: Option<&Pen> }>, the one resolution rule used by geometry, app and tests. template.rs: the MaterialEntry pattern column becomes a fill code; all 25 materials map to the catalogue (mapping in notes) with D.4 priorities unchanged and no cover fill. command.rs: Add/UpdateMaterial call validate_in. IFCX: schema.rs material record cutFill { fill, foreground (optional), background (enum fromFill/transparent or pen id) } and optional coverFill; writer.rs material_record and reader.rs read_material accordingly (an unknown or role-mismatched fill is repaired to the template fill with the same code, else SOLID, with a warning); the epic's migration step converts legacy cutFill { pattern, foreground, background } by mapping pattern codes (solid -> SOLID, concrete -> CONC, masonry -> MASONRY, timber -> WOOD, insulation -> INSUL, soil -> EARTH, diagonal -> DIAG) and reports one Info row that per-material cut-fill colours were replaced by pens. App, to keep building: ui/dialogs.rs material_editor replaces the pattern combo with a 'Cut fill' combo of cut-role fills (pens and cover fill follow in 09); views/plan.rs draws the region tone from the resolved fill (solid: foreground pen colour; hatch: foreground blended over background at 25 percent until hatch lines arrive in 07). Re-bless the golden files (reviewed diff limited to material records). Out of scope: hatch drawing (06, 07), pen and cover-fill pickers (09), MAT-004 face overrides, skins and profile regions referencing materials (layer-structures, profiles-columns-beams).
design: The three-state FillBackground keeps DSP-010's 'optional background pen or transparency' at the use site while the fill carries the defaults; the pen overrides let a material use CONC in another pen without duplicating the fill (decision D-5 spirit: no resource duplication). Material.color stays the 3D appearance only; the cut tone no longer derives from color.scaled(0.85), which is the deliberate visual change behind the epic's golden-file risk. Plan regions stay keyed by part.material (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:119-141), so skins added by layer-structures pick up their material's fill without change. Pitfall: Material::validate() without attributes is still used by the reader and commands; call validate_in wherever the project is available. Pitfall: the migration maps by short code against the template set inserted by task 02, never by name. Pointers: material.rs:91-178, template.rs:20-296, command.rs:234-252 and 520-552, writer.rs:122-140, reader.rs:212-263, ui/dialogs.rs:817-833, views/plan.rs:264-282.
acceptance_criteria:
- template_contents extended: the 25 MAT-003 names are present; every material has a colour with components in 0..1 and passes Material::validate, whose opacity and priority range checks are unchanged; a table-driven assertion checks each material's priority against the Appendix D.4 group value; every cut_fill references an existing fill serving the cut role; masonry materials use MASONRY, timber materials WOOD, insulation materials INSUL, soil and gravel EARTH, concrete materials CONC (DSP-010 coverage).
- Model tests: validate_in rejects a cut fill whose fill lacks the cut role and a cover fill lacking the cover role; integrity_problems reports a material pointing to a removed fill; resolve_fill applies the foreground override and all three background choices.
- IFCX: the 25 materials round-trip equal; a reader test with an unknown fill id loads with a warning and the template fill; the migration test on the frozen format-v<N> fixture maps legacy patterns to the expected fill codes and emits exactly one Info row about replaced colours.
- deleting_resources_requires_a_replacement (crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs) still passes; golden files re-blessed with a reviewed diff; conformance/run.sh green.
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the Materials dialog shows a 'Cut fill' combo for a selected material.
- Satisfied: MAT-001 plan representation as fill references with pens and an optional cover fill; MAT-003 in full; the DSP-011 model clause (the cut fill comes from the material); DSP-002 materials-with-cut-fills clause.
notes: SRS: MAT-001 MAT-003 DSP-011 DSP-002 DSP-003. Proposed mapping: reinforced concrete, concrete, screed -> CONC; brick, sand-lime brick, aerated concrete, clay block -> MASONRY; softwood, glulam, cross-laminated timber -> WOOD; steel, aluminium, membrane -> SOLID; glass, plaster, render, gypsum board -> PARA; tiles -> CROSS; natural stone -> DIAG; mineral wool, EPS/XPS, wood fibre insulation -> INSUL; soil, gravel -> EARTH; air gap -> SOLID with the fill background pen as foreground. Appendix D.4 priorities: RC 900, concrete 880, steel 860, masonry 800, CLT and glulam 760, softwood 740, screed 600, natural stone 560, glass and aluminium 500, insulation 400, gypsum board 350, plaster and render 300, tiles 280, membrane 200, air gap 100, soil and gravel 50. Open question: keep a tinted poche from the material colour? Proposal: no; colour plans come from pen tables (DSP-007) or the poche override preset (DSP-016).

title: Graphic attribute resources: pens, line types, fills and material plan display
description:
Introduce project-level graphic attributes (pens by role, line types, solid and hatch fills with roles) with stable IDs, references from elements and materials, a complete default set, in-use protection, editors, and material cut fills as real fill references, so that the plan renderer and every later element kind draw from one attribute system.

Risks: A large template change: golden files are re-blessed once with reviewed diffs.
design: archicraft-model attributes.rs (Pen, LineType, Fill{Solid, Hatch{angle, spacing, pen}} with roles) and ids via id_type!, Material.cut_fill becomes a fill reference plus pens; archicraft-ifcx project attribute schema extension with a format-version bump through the framework migration; archicraft-app dialogs following the Materials dialog pattern.
acceptance_criteria: The template contains the DSP-005 role pen table with the six weights, at least six line types and eight hatch fills (template test); each of the 25 materials references a cut fill and the D.4 priority; renaming an attribute keeps references (ID test); deleting an in-use attribute requires a replacement (command test); editing a material's cut fill changes every element's plan output (plan regression); pen/line-type/fill dialogs with kittest labels; attributes stored in archicraft::project round-trip.
notes: SRS: DSP-001 DSP-002 DSP-003 DSP-005 DSP-006 DSP-007 DSP-008 DSP-009 DSP-010 DSP-011 DSP-020 MAT-001 MAT-002 MAT-003

title: Pick fills and pens by role in materials and element settings
description:
WHY: MAT-001 (M): a material's plan representation is a cut fill with pens and an optional cover fill. DSP-009 (M): element settings offer only the fills valid for the role being edited. DSP-001 (M): an element's 2D graphic properties are attribute references, edited in its settings. DSP-006 (S): pen descriptions are shown wherever pens are selectable. DSP-020 (S): per-element override of hatch rotation and origin. MAT-002 (M): editing a material updates every element in all views. The settings dialog's Plan display section is a placeholder label (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:715-718) and the material editor offers only a fill combo (after task 03).

WHAT: ui/dialogs.rs material_editor: 'Cut fill' (fill_choice(Cut)), 'Cut fill pen' (pen_choice with a 'From fill' option), 'Cut fill background' (From fill, Transparent or a pen) and 'Cover fill' (None or fill_choice(Cover) with its pens). ui/properties.rs: the Grid layout's 'Plan display' section with 'Cut line pen', 'Uncut line pen', 'Overhead line pen' (pen_choice without screen-only pens), 'Uncut line type', 'Overhead line type', 'Cover fill' (None, From material or a cover-role fill with pens), 'Hatch rotation' (angle widget) and 'Hatch origin' (two lengths with Reset); mixed selections show common values as the other fields do (widgets::common) and tool defaults are edited the same way; changes go through the existing apply() path as one command per field change. The Strip layout shows only the cut line pen. Out of scope: DSP-016 view overrides, picking the hatch origin in the plan with the point-input service.
design: Use Fields::choice (ui/properties.rs:195-218) with option lists from the widgets of task 08, so mixed selections and None handling follow the existing pattern and properties-and-dialogs can later move the section into its settings-dialog framework unchanged. Keep one undo step per field change across the whole selection (the existing apply() batching). Pitfall: the cover-fill choice has three kinds of values (None, From material, a fill); model it as one option list so mixed selections display correctly. Pointers: ui/properties.rs:134-218, 466-478, 684-737; ui/dialogs.rs:765-845; ui/widgets.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: selecting a wall and opening its settings dialog shows the 'Plan display' section with 'Cut line pen', 'Overhead line type', 'Cover fill' and 'Hatch rotation'; the 'Cover fill' combo lists only cover-role fills and the Materials dialog's 'Cut fill' combo lists only cut-role fills (DSP-009, asserted by presence and absence of a role-specific fill label).
- kittest or app test: changing 'Cut line pen' with two walls selected executes one undoable command that sets both elements' cut_pen; setting it in the wall tool defaults makes the next wall use it.
- App test through the editor path: changing a material's cut fill updates plan_fills of every element that uses it (MAT-002, re-using task 06's fixture).
- Materials dialog: choosing a 'Cut fill pen' executes one UpdateMaterial that sets the material's foreground override, and plan_fills of its elements then use that pen; the material's 'Cover fill' combo lists only cover-role fills (MAT-001 plan representation editable).
- Every pen option shown in these pickers has hover text with the pen description (DSP-006 'wherever pens are selectable').
- Satisfied: MAT-001 editing of the full plan representation, the DSP-009 element-settings clause, DSP-001 element references editable, DSP-020 override editable, DSP-006 descriptions in pickers.
notes: SRS: MAT-001 MAT-002 DSP-001 DSP-006 DSP-009 DSP-020.

title: Render moire-free hatches with the 3-pixel flat-tone fallback
description:
WHY: DSP-013 (S): hatches shall be drawn without moire; when the hatch spacing falls below 3 device pixels a flat tone shall be drawn instead; with hatches shown plan navigation shall meet NFR-PERF-004. VIEW-013 gives hatch spacing in paper units at the drawing scale. Today every fill is a flat foreground tone (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:264-282). What the prerequisite epic adds: plan-attributes-06 generates CPU hatch lines per cut and cover region (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/hatch.rs hatch_lines -> HatchLines; plan_fills -> PlanFills with RegionFill {fill, foreground, background, hatch}) and plan-attributes-07 draws them with the egui painter, with a 25 % tone when the on-screen spacing is below 3 px or the line count is truncated. Missing: moire-free rendering (point-sampled egui strokes beat at 3 to 6 px spacing), a tone that matches the hatch's real coverage, spacing that follows the view's drawing scale without regenerating lines, and the frame rate of NFR-PERF-004 on large storeys.

WHAT: a hatch pass in views/plan_gpu.rs that draws each cut and cover region's fill triangles with a fragment shader evaluating the families of the region's Fill (plan-attributes-01: Hatch {scaling, families: HatchFamily {angle_deg, spacing_mm, offset_mm, stagger_mm, dashes}}, pen = the RegionFill foreground pen, paper- or model-size scaling per DSP-020), anchored at the region's HatchPlacement (project origin by default) so merged regions continue seamlessly; box-filtered pulse-train coverage over the pixel footprint so nothing aliases; below 3 device px spacing a family renders as its average tone, cross-fading between 3 and 4 px; the fill's background pen or transparency underneath; hatch definitions in a storage buffer indexed by fill and uploaded separately from geometry. The CPU HatchLines of plan-attributes-06 and the painter tone of plan-attributes-07 remain only as the no-GPU fallback. Out of scope: drafting fills (drafting-trim-split), the UI for per-element hatch origin or rotation (plan-attributes; rendered here from HatchPlacement), and the frame-rate measurement (plan-renderer-11).
design:
Per family in the fragment shader: u = dot(p - origin, n) / spacing_model with n the unit normal of the family angle; fw = fwidth(u); duty w = clamp(line_px / spacing_px, 0, 1) with line_px from the hatch pen through the plan-renderer-02 rule (floor 1 px); filtered coverage = (F(u + fw/2) - F(u - fw/2)) / fw, where F is the closed-form integral of the periodic pulse train of duty w (the filtered-stripes technique), which removes moire instead of point-sampling a distance. spacing_px = spacing_model * px_per_model_m; tone blend t = smoothstep(3.0, 4.0, spacing_px); colour coverage = mix(w, filtered, t). Dashed families (brick perpendiculars) add a second filtered pulse train along the line with a row offset; support up to 4 families per fill (proposal; cross-hatch and brick need 2).

Clipping: drawing the region's own fill triangles is the clip, so no stencil pass and no per-zoom geometry are needed. This replaces the roadmap's instanced line batches with the same visual result and no regeneration on zoom. Region vertices carry a fill index into the hatch storage buffer. Origin and rotation: CutRegion.placement of plan-attributes-06, which is part of the merge key, so every region has exactly one placement (the project origin by default) and merged multi-element regions stay seamless (DSP-012).
acceptance_criteria:
- Pixel tests in crates/archicraft-app/tests/plan_pixels.rs on a 4 m x 4 m region with one 45-degree family: at 12 px spacing the autocorrelation along the hatch normal peaks at 12 +/- 0.5 px; at 2.9 px and 1 px spacing the region's pixel standard deviation is below 2/255 (flat tone) and its mean equals mix(background, pen colour, line_px / spacing_px) within 2 %; for spacings 3.0 to 6.0 px in 0.25 px steps the 16x16-block means vary by less than 3 % across the region (no moire beat).
- Zooming from 12 px to 2 px spacing in 0.25 px steps changes the region mean monotonically, with steps below 2 % (no pop at the 3 px threshold).
- A paper-size hatch at 1:50 has half the model-space spacing of the same hatch at 1:100, while a model-size hatch keeps its spacing (VIEW-013, DSP-020 scaling flag).
- Two butted concrete walls merged into one region show hatch lines continuing across the former joint (pixel rows on both sides match within tolerance).
- At 12 px spacing the hatch lines measure the hatch pen's width resolved by plan-renderer-02 within 10 % and never below 1 device px; a dashed and staggered brick family (MASONRY) shows its stagger between successive rows (DSP-004 for hatch lines).
- Hatch parameters are not baked into vertices (unit test on the vertex builder): changing a fill's angle re-uploads only the hatch buffer.
- Goldens of samples::storey_with_walls_and_slab() with two walls set to Brick (MASONRY hatch) and two to Concrete (CONC hatch) in the test, and of two_storey_shell() with a slab cover fill, at fit, 4x and 0.25x zoom (tone), pass on the three CI platforms.
- Satisfies DSP-013 (moire-free hatches, flat tone below 3 device px) and the hatch-spacing clause of VIEW-013; the NFR-PERF-004 clause of DSP-013 is measured in plan-renderer-11.
notes: SRS: DSP-013 VIEW-013. Hatch definitions come from plan-attributes-01/-02 (DSP-010, DSP-020: up to four HatchFamily entries per Hatch, eight catalogue hatches PARA, CROSS, DIAG, MASONRY, CONC, INSUL, EARTH, WOOD). Threshold 3 device px (DSP-013); the 3-4 px cross-fade band is a proposal.

title: Resolve skins at junction nodes by material priority (F7)
description:
WHY: WAL-023: at junctions skins are resolved by material intersection priority (MAT-001); a higher-priority skin cuts through the lower-priority skins of the other element, and touching skins with the same material and priority merge into one region without a boundary line. WAL-024 lets a single skin override its material's priority. Fixture F7 is a T-junction of concrete and insulation whose result flips when the two priorities are swapped. Today priority is stored and edited (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:153, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:808-815) but never used (wall.rs has no priority logic; gap analysis: WAL-023 partial, WAL-024 missing), and layer-structures-04 only interpolates skin ends on the envelope's end edges (skin_rings), so equal structures meet on the mitre, T-branch skins stop at the through wall's face and no skin ever cuts another.

WHAT: Extend crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs from outline level to skin level: at each node extend every arm's skin bands (the SkinBand list of layer-structures-04, carried by WallOutline since task 03) through E, place them in descending effective priority (SectionSkin.priority of task 01, so per-skin overrides need no extra code) with the provisional wall rank for ties, clip tied equal-priority skins of ending arms to their mitre side or sector, subtract everything already placed, keep only the components that share an edge with the arm's own skin band, assign any uncovered remainder deterministically, and collect one MultiPolygon per wall and skin. The wall generator (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs, wired in task 13) extrudes each skin MultiPolygon into the Skin_n BodyPart of layer-structures-04 (name, material and role unchanged; disjoint pieces appended into one closed mesh). Add `fixtures::f7_t_junction(swapped: bool)` to crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs with the D.4 default priorities 880 / 400 (the values the fixture uses, stated in its doc comment as regression-and-status-02 asks of the owner) and assert F2 again at L and T junctions. Out of scope: the final tie rule and junction order (06), the plan region merge (07), and the 'between walls, columns and beams' clause of WAL-023, which cleanup-and-trims-02/03 deliver through the same SectionSkin.priority path (task 12 keeps those rows pending).
design: Placement: list the (arm, skin) entries and sort them by (effective priority desc, provisional wall rank, skin index from the exterior). For each entry: ext = skin band extended along the arm direction to the far boundary of E, intersected with E; if another arm has a skin of the same effective priority, clip ext to this arm's mitre half-plane (two ending arms) or sector (three or more), both bounded to the node zone; piece = ext minus union(placed); keep only components sharing a boundary longer than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH with the arm's unextended band, so a lower skin stops at the first equal or higher skin it meets (point contacts do not count); placed = placed union piece. A remainder of E larger than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH squared goes to the adjacent piece with the longest shared boundary (rank breaks ties); otherwise the node falls back. For single-skin walls this reproduces the outline result of 04 exactly, which keeps the ported tests green. Body parts keep the naming and order of layer-structures (Skin_n) and the skin material; store the effective priority on BodyPart for task 07. Pitfalls: flipped walls (WAL-006) and End contacts reverse the skin order relative to the arm direction; core-face reference lines only shift the bands; extruding a MultiPolygon appends one prism per polygon (mesh.rs:91 append) and check_closed accepts disjoint shells but not shells sharing an edge, so union same-skin pieces first.
acceptance_criteria:
- F7 with D.4 defaults (concrete 880, mineral wool 400): through wall of concrete 0.20 m plus insulation 0.16 m on the branch side, single-skin concrete branch 0.20 m: the branch cuts through the insulation and ends at the through wall's concrete face; the insulation splits into two closed pieces; golden skin outlines match (WAL-023).
- F7 swapped by material priorities (insulation 880, concrete 400): the insulation is continuous and the branch ends at the insulation face; golden outlines match. Swapping by per-skin overrides only gives the same outlines, while an identical T elsewhere that uses the materials without overrides keeps the default result (WAL-024).
- F7 with the KB values (concrete 740, insulation 420, set as per-skin overrides) gives the same outlines as 880 / 400, and swapping them gives the swapped outlines (only the order of priorities matters).
- Two F2 walls at an L: all six skins meet along the corner diagonal, outer brick and inner plaster run around the corner, every Skin part is closed; a 0.115 m masonry (800) branch from the interior cuts the inner plaster (300) and stops at the concrete core (880).
- Priority inversion: a reinforced concrete (900) branch into the F2 wall cuts through core, insulation, air and brick to the exterior face (golden outlines).
- Equal material and priority: branch concrete and through concrete share an edge and do not overlap (input of the plan merge in task 07).
- For every case the skin pieces cover E and are interior-disjoint (area identity within 1e-9 m2), and every BodyPart passes check_closed.
- A 48-skin structure at an X node resolves, or falls back with a problem, without producing an invalid mesh.
notes: SRS: WAL-023 WAL-024. Appendix D.4: reinforced concrete 900, concrete 880, masonry 800, thermal insulation 400, plaster 300, air gap 100. Appendix D.7 F7: T-junction with concrete and insulation, then priorities swapped (KB 303922; with D.4 defaults 880 / 400); F2: brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm. The exact F7 geometry is not in the SRS; the definition above is recorded in docs/junctions.md (task 06).

title: Generate sloped and tapered slab bodies
description:
WHY: SLB-006 (S): slabs shall support an inclined top and optionally an inclined bottom, sloped slabs of constant thickness and tapered slabs such as flat roofs with falls, with no roof, terrain or boolean workaround. IFX-017 (M): a layered sloped or tapered slab is still written as one Skin_n part per skin. Gap row SLB-006: missing (slab bodies are prisms between two horizontal planes: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:177-187, extrude.rs:18-58); this task delivers the geometry half on top of the model parameters of task 07 and the skin stacking of task 05.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs: `extrude_between(outer, holes, bottom: Plane, top: Plane) -> Result<TriMesh, GeometryError>` generalising extrude (the plan triangulation computed once and lifted onto both planes, vertical side quads, own vertices per face for IFX-038, closed and outward oriented for IFX-032); extrude() becomes the special case of two horizontal planes so flat bodies stay byte-identical. The slab generator of task 05 (kinds/slab.rs after element-kind-framework-07) builds one part per skin between consecutive planes of SlabSlope::boundary_planes (task 07): a single `Body` for Thickness slabs, `Skin_{i}` with BodyPart.skin for Layered slabs. Bodies come from planar extrusion only, never from a Boolean or an auxiliary element. Out of scope: model parameters (07), IFCX (08), UI (12), roofs (roofs-02 reuses the shared-plane approach).
design: Because the 60-degree limit of task 07 keeps planes far from vertical, a CDT of the plan polygon lifted onto a plane stays valid and correctly oriented, and the vertical side quads between two planes stay planar per edge. Evaluate each boundary plane once and share it between both neighbouring skins so their vertices are bit-identical. Slicing (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs:35-60) and facing outlines (mesh.rs:196-238) are already general, and plan.rs classifies by bounds (plan.rs:133-146), so the plan needs no slope-specific code; the task 05 segment deduplication also applies. Hoist the triangulation out of the per-skin loop (a 48-skin tapered slab triangulates once). Pitfall: side quads of a tapered skin can degenerate to a triangle where a skin thickness reaches the 0.1 mm minimum; task 07 validation prevents zero, so keep the quad and let check_closed guard it.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/slopes.rs: a 6 x 4 m sloped slab, perpendicular thickness 0.20 m, pitch 10 degrees towards +X, is closed, its top and bottom faces are parallel (normals 10 degrees from +Z within 1e-9) and its volume equals 24 x 0.20 / cos(10 deg) within 1e-9.
- A 10 x 5 m tapered single-thickness slab with a horizontal bottom, 0.20 m thick at the origin edge and a 2 % top fall towards that edge is closed, 0.40 m thick at the far edge and has the analytic volume (15.0 m3) within 1e-9.
- Optional inclined bottom: a tapered slab with a horizontal top and a 5 degree soffit, and one with both faces inclined at different pitches and directions, are closed and have the analytic volume within 1e-9.
- A layered tapered roof deck (membrane 5 / EPS 200 taper / membrane 2 / reinforced concrete 200 core) with a horizontal soffit: four closed Skin parts, only the EPS skin varies in thickness, and adjacent skins share their boundary vertices exactly.
- A sloped slab with a hole: every part is closed and contains the hole.
- No workaround: each test project holds exactly one Slab element per slab, and its body is produced by extrude_between alone (no Boolean, no auxiliary roof or terrain element).
- plan_drawing cuts an inclined slab that crosses the cut plane into closed polygons, and a sloped slab entirely below the cut plane is drawn projected with its outline.
- Flat slabs are unchanged: existing extrude tests and golden files are byte-identical.
- Satisfies the geometry clauses of SLB-006 and IFX-017 (geometry side) for sloped and tapered layered slabs.
notes: SRS: SLB-006 IFX-017. Split from task 07 because SLB-006 is rated L in the gap analysis; the plane maths is shared through SlabSlope::boundary_planes.

title: Add move-reference-line and flip commands for walls
description:
WHY: WAL-005 (M): a command shall move the reference line of selected walls to another location without moving the wall body or its hosted elements. WAL-006 (M): a command shall flip a wall's sides: its layer structure and exterior side swap while the reference line stays in place. The epic also asks for structure swaps that keep the body. Gap rows: WAL-005 partial (the properties panel changes reference_line but the body moves because start/end stay fixed, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:160-161; the compensating shift is missing); WAL-006 missing (no flip in Command, crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:36-92, nor in Action, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs:7-39).

WHAT: Add `Command::MoveWallReferenceLine { ids: Vec<ElementId>, location: ReferenceLine }` and `Command::FlipWalls { ids: Vec<ElementId>, keep_body: bool }` with labels ('Move reference line', 'Flip wall', 'Swap wall sides'). MoveWallReferenceLine shifts each selected wall's start and end along its left-hand normal by distance_from_exterior(new) - distance_from_exterior(old) and then restores every junction contact the wall had before (end-to-end L and end-on-reference-line T, detected with the framework tolerance): a shared end becomes the intersection of the two shifted reference lines; an unselected wall whose end touched the moved reference line (a T branch) is extended or trimmed along its own axis onto the new line; near-parallel partners (collinear continuation) need no change. FlipWalls swaps start and end, which swaps the exterior side while the reference line segment stays; keep_body = false keeps the location and mirrors the body about the reference line (WAL-006); keep_body = true also maps the location to its mirror (Outside <-> Inside, CoreExterior <-> CoreInterior, Custom(d) <-> Custom(total - d), Center unchanged) so the envelope stays and the skin order reverses in place. Both plan only ReplaceElement edits, reject locked walls (and locked T partners) via edit_lock_reason, and return NoChange when nothing changes. Hosted elements (WAL-005 'or its hosted elements'): both plans call one helper `plan_hosted_followups(project, wall_before, wall_after) -> Vec<Edit>` that walks the wall's Host relations in the relation store of element-kind-framework-08 and returns no edits while no hosted kind exists; host-openings fills it (re-anchoring hosted inserts) and the done task files that bead. Geometry tests live in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/layered.rs. Out of scope: UI (12), hosted elements (host-openings must re-anchor hosted inserts in these two plans), junction priorities (junction-engine).
design: Shift maths: the exterior face lies at p_ref - n * d (n = left normal, d = distance_from_exterior), so keeping it fixed means p_ref' = p_ref + n * (d' - d). Junction restoration must use the contacts detected before the shift; compute them with the same rules as wall.rs resolve_end (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:203-230) and the JOIN_TOLERANCE of crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs, but in the model crate (a small helper in the wall kind module or the relation store of element-kind-framework if junction edges are recorded there by then), because archicraft-model must not depend on archicraft-geometry. For a T branch the body stays because its end is trimmed to the through wall's face, which does not move. Determinism: process walls in id order and compute each shared end once. Flip is an involution; test it as such. Keep the ELM-012 position flag (interior/exterior) unchanged: the flip changes geometry, not classification. Pitfall: the properties panel path that changes reference_line without compensation remains as a 'location' property for walls being set up; task 12 routes the user-facing 'Move reference line' through the new command.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a ring of four F2 walls joined at L corners with Outside reference lines; MoveWallReferenceLine to Center, Inside, CoreExterior, CoreInterior and Custom(0.2) leaves every skin mesh equal to the original (sorted vertex sets within 1e-9 m), the L junctions are still detected (mitred, not square, ends), the reference lines lie on the requested location, and undo restores the project exactly.
- T case: an interior wall ending on an exterior F2 wall; moving the exterior wall's reference line to CoreInterior moves the branch end onto the new reference line, the branch body is unchanged and still trimmed at the through wall's face; with the branch locked the command returns Locked and changes nothing.
- FlipWalls keep_body = false on an Outside F2 wall: start/end swapped, the Axis segment is the same point set, the body is the mirror image about the reference line with equal skin volumes, and flipping twice restores the original wall exactly.
- FlipWalls keep_body = true: the union envelope and the reference-line segment are unchanged, Skin_1 (brick) now lies on the former interior side, and the location changed Outside -> Inside (CoreExterior -> CoreInterior, Custom(0.2) -> Custom(0.48) for F2).
- plan_hosted_followups is called once per changed wall by both plans (unit test with a counting stub) and returns no edits today; the hosted-element clause of WAL-005 is recorded as open for host-openings.
- Both commands on an empty selection return NoChange; on a locked wall Locked; each is one undo step in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs.
- Satisfies WAL-005 (body stays; hosted elements arrive with host-openings) and WAL-006 (structure and exterior side swap, reference line in place), plus the in-place swap of the epic goal.
notes: SRS: WAL-005 WAL-006. Note for host-openings: hosted inserts measured along the reference line from the start must be re-anchored when FlipWalls swaps start/end and when MoveWallReferenceLine moves an end along the axis.

title: Add fixtures F2 and F3 and the template layer structures
description:
WHY: Appendix D.7 defines F2 (layered wall: brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm, nominal height 3000 mm, KB 303787) and F3 (floating floor: storey (finished floor) at +6.10 m, structural slab top +6.00 m, soffit +5.75 m, so wall base offset -0.10 m; resilient layer 20-30 mm, KB 303722). The increment-1 exit criterion is 'Fixtures F2, F6, F7 pass' (Appendix F), the roadmap assigns F2 and F3 to this epic and asks for them in the D.7 fixture registry of regression-and-status, and the epic design says the template gains the D.2 structures. They exercise PRF-001, PRF-003, SLB-002, SLB-009 and IFX-017 on real build-ups.

WHAT: template.rs: a LAYER_STRUCTURES table built in default_metric_project_with(ids) of element-kind-framework-03 (structure ids from the ids closure, so default_metric_project() gets v4 and the FixtureBuilder v5 ids) with 'Cavity wall 680' (F2: Brick 120 finish / Air gap 60 other / Mineral wool 180 other / Plaster 10 other / Concrete 300 core / Plaster 10 finish), 'Plastered masonry 135' (Plaster 10 finish / Sand-lime brick 115 core / Plaster 10 finish), 'Floating floor 350' (Screed 70 finish / Mineral wool 30 other as resilient layer / Reinforced concrete 250 core) and 'Warm flat roof 407' (Membrane 5 finish / EPS/XPS 200 other / Membrane 2 other / Reinforced concrete 200 core); the D.2 tool defaults stay single-material. samples.rs: `f2_layered_wall()` and `f3_floating_floor()` built with the FixtureBuilder of element-kind-framework (deterministic v5 ids): F2 = one free 5.0 m wall plus a counter-clockwise 10 x 8 m ring of four walls, all 'Cavity wall 680', fixed height 3.0 m, reference line Outside; F3 = a storey at +6.10 m with a 'Floating floor 350' slab referenced to CoreTop at -0.10 and two walls with base offset -0.10 and the top linked to home + 1. Register both in the fixture registry of regression-and-status-02: set `build: Some(..)` and `seeded: true` on the F2 and F3 entries of `D7` in crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (with `fixtures::f2_layered_wall`/`fixtures::f3_floating_floor` delegating to the samples constructors so the paths other epics cite resolve) and add the fixture-specific assertions to the registry test crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs; the generic checks of crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/fixtures.rs and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures.rs then cover F2 and F3 automatically. If that registry has not landed, create crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs and tests/fixtures.rs with its entry shape (`Fixture { id, title, source, owner, increment, seeded, build }`, F2/F3 only) for regression-and-status to absorb. Add the geometry assertions in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/fixtures_f2_f3.rs. Golden files are re-blessed because every project now carries the template structures. Out of scope: the layered golden file (10), F2 at junction-resolved corners (re-asserted by junction-engine), F3 in RM-S (reference-models).
design: Material names come from the template table (template.rs:30-272): 'Air gap' (priority 100), 'Mineral wool' (400), 'Plaster' (300), 'Concrete' (880), 'Brick' (800), 'Screed' (600), 'Reinforced concrete' (900), 'Membrane' (200), 'EPS/XPS' (400), 'Sand-lime brick' (800); resolve them with the existing find_material closure so a renamed material fails loudly in template_contents rather than silently falling back to materials[0]. The F3 storey needs the storey above +6.10 to exist for the walls' top link; build it with the FixtureBuilder storey(..) API. Keep the fixtures as plain constructors in samples.rs (not test-only) because plan-renderer and junction-engine reuse them. Pitfall: template structures are new resources and must get fresh ids per project (IFX-011).
acceptance_criteria:
- F2: the structure totals 0.680 m with six skins in the order and roles above; each wall of the fixture evaluates into six closed Skin parts; the plan cut at 1.10 m has one polygon per skin per wall; reference lines and Axis points are unchanged by evaluation.
- F3: absolute elevations 6.10 (finished floor), 6.00 (core top) and 5.75 (soffit) within 1e-9; the walls' bodies start at 6.00; the resilient layer is 30 mm (inside the 20-30 mm range); redefining the slab as Top at 0.0 yields identical geometry; the slab's projected outline appears once in the plan of its home storey.
- The D7 table of crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs has build constructors for F2 and F3 (seeded, two builds equal); crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs builds them without integrity problems, and the generic geometry and IFCX registry tests (or, without the registry, fixtures_f2_f3.rs and a round trip in roundtrip.rs) pass on both.
- template_contents asserts the four structures and unchanged D.2 defaults (0.25 m Brick wall, 0.20 m reinforced concrete slab); every_project_gets_new_identities covers structure ids; the Appendix D defaults test of regression-and-status, if present, stays green.
- Golden files re-blessed with a reviewed diff limited to archicraft::project.layerStructures; round-trip and conformance green.
- Satisfies the F2/F3 parts of the epic acceptance (build, plan regions, F3 floating floor, registry) for PRF-001, PRF-003, SLB-002 and SLB-009.
notes: SRS: PRF-001 PRF-003 SLB-002 SLB-009 IFX-017. Appendix D.7 F2/F3 values as quoted; D.4 priorities of the chosen materials as listed. The four template structures beyond F2/F3 are proposals for the default template (O-11).

title: Host relation and the opening element (2D cuts in the host plane)
description:
Implement the hosted-element framework (host relation with cascade delete and copy, host picking with live preview in plan and, through the ViewSurface trait, in 3D, Void child nodes) and the generic single-host opening with rectangular, circular and polygonal cross-sections, perpendicular or vertical orientation, through or limited depth, storey-spanning shafts through several slabs and plan symbols, cut as 2D polygons in the wall's own plane or as slab holes before extrusion (technology-choices), so no Boolean kernel is needed; openings that cut further elements (OPN-002) arrive with the kernel in solid-kernel-ops. The base that doors, windows, roof openings and beam notches reuse.

Risks: Niches and openings crossing skin boundaries need robust 2D subtraction: geo Booleans with MODEL_TOLERANCE and validation of every resulting ring. Roofs as hosts are verified again in the roofs epic.
design: archicraft-model Host relation in the relation store and kinds/opening.rs with placement relative to the host face; archicraft-geometry cuts the void polygon in the wall plane per skin band before extrusion (extrude.rs gains holes in vertical faces), slab openings as outline holes, the Void prism kept as a separate part; incremental evaluation marks host and hosted elements dirty; archicraft-ifcx hosted children (IFX-015) and Void v5 sub-nodes (IFX-036); archicraft-app tools/opening.rs with host hover candidates and preview.
acceptance_criteria: The niche acceptance (limited opening 0 to 0.40 m in a 0.50 m wall leaves 0.10 m) as a geometry test; a 1.0 x 1.0 m opening in the F2 wall removes the volume from every skin (signed-volume check); an opening moves and is deleted with its host and copied with it (command tests with undo); a shaft from storey -1 to +2 cuts all slabs in range and follows a storey elevation change; the tool creates nothing without a host under the pointer (kittest) and the preview follows the host in plan and in a 3D view through the Camera3d ViewSurface (OPN-007, hence the dependency on 3d-input-navigation); IFCX: the opening is a child of its host with an invisible closed Void mesh (conformance and viewer); a file with an orphaned hosted element is repaired deterministically and reported on load; an opening at a wall end adjacent to a junction is added to the NFR-MNT-005 suite.
notes: SRS: OPN-001 OPN-003 OPN-004 OPN-005 OPN-006 OPN-007 OPN-009 ELM-016 IFX-015 IFX-036 NFR-REL-004

title: Persist layer structures, structures and slab slopes in IFCX
description:
WHY: IFX-060 (M) names layer structures explicitly among the authoring data that must be stored in archicraft:: attributes; IFX-061 (M) every archicraft:: attribute is declared in-file; IFX-067 (M) unused resources live in archicraft::project; IFX-064 (M) round-trip fidelity; IFX-062 (M) format version and migration. This persists PRF-001 (the resource), WAL-003 and SLB-002 (thickness or layer structure), SLB-009 (core reference planes, codes added in task 03) and SLB-006 (slopes). Gap row PRF-001 lists the IFCX schema/writer/reader in archicraft::project as missing.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: a `layer_structure()` record schema (the archicraft::layerStructure record of the epic design: id string, name string, skins array of {material reference, thickness length, role enumeration from SkinRole::ALL}) used as an optional `layerStructures` array in project(); wall and slab attributes and the wall/slab toolDefaults gain an optional `layerStructure` reference, while `thickness` (section total) and `material` (Thickness material or core material) stay as informative keys; slab gains an optional `slope` object {form enum sloped/tapered, origin point2, direction angle, pitch angle, oppositeDirection and oppositePitch optional angles, taperSkin optional integer}. writer.rs project_attribute and the wall/slab codecs of element-kind-framework (alpha/kinds/wall.rs, slab.rs) write them, and the temporary 'layer structure not saved yet' warning of task 02 is removed. reader.rs reads structures before elements (ReadContext of the framework): a skin with a missing material is repaired with the first material and a warning; a structure without core or with a zero-thickness skin is skipped with an error; an element referencing an unknown structure falls back to Structure::Thickness from the informative keys with a warning (envelope preserved); a malformed slope becomes Flat with a warning. Bump FORMAT_VERSION by one (recipe step 5: older ArchiCraft versions would reject the core reference codes and silently drop layered data, so they must flag newer_format) and register an identity migration from the previous version in MIGRATIONS of crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework-12); at the start of the task freeze a copy of the current walls-and-slab golden as crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/format-v2/walls-and-slab.ifcx (format 2 is what element-kind-framework-12 leaves; use the actual previous number if it differs), following the format-v1 convention of that task. ReadContext of the codecs gains the layer structures read so far. Out of scope: Skin_n export checks, the layered golden and conformance extensions (10), template structures (09).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe (docs/implementation-status.md, Extension points): declare with optional(...) so files of the previous version still validate, read with report.or(..) so missing values warn instead of failing, write parameters at full precision (round_coordinate is for mesh coordinates only), keep resource and skin order for determinism (IFX-007). The informative thickness/material keys keep files meaningful for older readers' leniency and for the fallback path. IFX-067: structures are resources of the project node, not root nodes; do not attach a separate per-node archicraft::layerStructure attribute. Pointers (today; the element and toolDefaults parts move into crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/ with element-kind-framework-06): schema.rs:15-25 and 180-257, writer.rs:94-117 and 144-217, reader.rs:212-264 (read_material as the lenient pattern), 301-430, 592-713.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: a project with three structures (one unused), layered walls with all six reference-line locations, layered slabs with all four reference planes, a sloped and a tapered slab saves without warnings, validates without problems (IFX-005, IFX-061) and reloads equal to the original bit for bit (IFX-064).
- A 48-skin structure and the wall and slab using it round-trip equal (PRF-001 'at least 48' in the file).
- The unused structure is stored in archicraft::project.layerStructures and the composed tree still has a single root (IFX-067, spatial-tree test).
- Lenient-reading tests: unknown layerStructure reference -> Thickness fallback with a warning naming the node path; skin material missing -> repaired with a warning; structure without core -> skipped with an error and its users fall back; malformed slope -> Flat with a warning.
- The frozen file of the previous FORMAT_VERSION loads through the migration without problems and equals the project it was written from; a file with FORMAT_VERSION + 1 sets newer_format.
- Golden files re-blessed once with the diff reviewed (formatVersion and the empty optional list only); conformance/run.sh green on all golden files.
- Satisfies the persistence clauses of PRF-001, WAL-003, SLB-002, SLB-009 and SLB-006 (IFX-060 for layer structures).
notes: SRS: PRF-001 WAL-003 SLB-002 SLB-009 SLB-006. Also IFX-060, IFX-061, IFX-062, IFX-064, IFX-067 (owned elsewhere, exercised here).

title: Detect junction nodes from reference-line contact in the model
description:
WHY: WAL-020 joins walls where their reference lines touch - end to end (L), end to body (T) or crossing (X) - and keeps walls whose bodies overlap without touching reference lines unjoined; decision D-6 makes reference-line contact the only detection criterion and requires order-independent results (WAL-026). WAL-025 excludes pairs in different join groups or in "never join", and the unjoin of WAL-022 needs an explicit junction relation because joins are otherwise implicit from contact (gap analysis: WAL-020 and WAL-026 partial, WAL-025 and WAL-022 missing). Today detection lives inside geometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:203-229): an all-pairs loop per storey, only the exactly-one-contact cases, and walls on different home storeys never join even when they overlap vertically (wall.rs:95-97). Join and unjoin, auto-join, incremental invalidation and geometry must all see the same contact graph, so it moves into the headless model.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs add `JunctionGraph` (canonically sorted `Node { point, members }`, `Member { wall, contact: Start | End | Body { t } }`), `detect(project)` and the local query `detect_around(project, ids)`, built on an rstar 0.12 RTree of reference-line segments inflated by JOIN_TOLERANCE: add rstar 0.12 to archicraft-model (the version geo pins, so no second copy compiles) and move the segment RTree that element-kind-framework-10 built in archicraft-geometry for contact neighbours into this module, so dirty-set derivation and junction detection share one index and one contact rule instead of a second, hand-written index. Contact is within JOIN_TOLERANCE of crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs (element-kind-framework-01: 0.01 mm, replacing the 0.1 mm of wall.rs:23-24); vertical overlap comes from absolute extents (Project::vertical_extent) so walls of different home storeys join where they overlap; the join-group filter of task 01 and the exclusion of Separated pairs apply; collinear overlapping reference lines are reported as `Overlap` diagnostics, not junctions. Extend the framework's `Relation::Junction { a, b }` (crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs, element-kind-framework-08, which leaves Junction parameters to this epic) with `mode: JunctionMode` (only `Separated` today) and a canonical pair order so its v5 RelationId does not depend on argument order. Reuse, do not re-implement, the framework's Edit::InsertRelation/RemoveRelation, the delete cascade of plan_delete_elements and the dangling-end check of integrity_problems; add the mode member to the junction entry of the archicraft::relations codec (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha) so a file holding one round-trips; make Edit::apply stamp both walls of an inserted or removed Junction relation in the ChangeLog of element-kind-framework-10. Out of scope: geometry (04, 13), creating Separated relations from a command (09), auto-join (10).
design: Inputs: `WallLine { id, start, end, bottom, top (absolute), join_group }` gathered from the project (this replaces evaluate.rs wall_inputs, lines 99-120, as the source of contact data). Detection: for each wall end query the RTree for segments within JOIN_TOLERANCE; classify end-end, end-body (t inside (0, 1) by more than tolerance/length) and body-body crossings (proper segment intersection); union-find over contact points so that a node with three or more walls is one node. Canonical node point: the shared endpoint when bit-identical; for a T the branch end point as stored; for an X the reference-line intersection computed in ElementId order (the ordered_intersect idea of wall.rs:121-125); for mixed clusters the lexicographically smallest member point. Members are sorted by outgoing direction angle (atan2(..).rem_euclid(TAU)), then ElementId; nodes by point. A cluster wider than 2 x JOIN_TOLERANCE is flagged ambiguous (geometry leaves it square and reports it). Vertical overlap needs more than MIN_HEIGHT (validate.rs:23) of common extent; home storeys are otherwise ignored (D-3 keeps one home storey per element; joining across storeys does not change containment). The derived graph is never stored: storing it would need a resync on every storey elevation or height edit. The relation store holds only explicit decisions (Separated, per pair), which matches D-6's 'detected from reference-line contact only'. Move point_segment_distance and the segment helpers from wall.rs into this module and reuse them (technical-debt item on duplicated helpers). Pitfalls: non-transitive tolerance chains, duplicate members when an end touches both an end and the body of the same wall, exactly opposite arms whose angles tie in floating point (compare with a tolerance, fall back to ElementId).
acceptance_criteria:
- junction.rs unit tests build graphs for L, T, X, collinear continuation, 3-wall and 4-wall nodes, and a T whose branch ends just inside and just outside JOIN_TOLERANCE, asserting members and contact kinds (WAL-020).
- Two parallel walls 0.10 m apart whose 0.25 m bodies overlap produce no node (WAL-020 'bodies overlap without touching reference lines stay unjoined').
- Different join groups produce no node, a NEVER wall belongs to no node, two walls in group 7 join (WAL-025); two walls on different layers in the same join group join, and hiding or locking one of those layers leaves the graph unchanged (WAL-025 'independent of layers and visibility').
- A Separated relation removes exactly that pair; a third wall at the same node stays joined with both.
- A double-height wall on storey 0 and a storey-1 wall meeting at an L form a node; walls stacked 0-3 m and 3-6 m do not.
- All 24 insertion orders of a 4-wall scene containing an X and a T give identical graphs with bit-identical node points (WAL-026).
- Relation tests (extending the framework's): InsertRelation of Junction(a, b, Separated) and of Junction(b, a, Separated) yield the same RelationId and the second is rejected as a duplicate; integrity_problems reports a Separated relation whose wall is missing; DeleteElements removes it and undo restores it; the ChangeLog stamps both walls on insert, remove and their undo; archicraft_ifcx save and load of a project with one Separated relation gives an equal project.
- dirty_set_after_one_edit_is_local of element-kind-framework-10 still passes on stand_in(5_000) with the moved index, and a candidate-pair counter shows that detection examines O(n) pairs (no all-pairs loop).
notes: SRS: WAL-020 WAL-025 WAL-026 WAL-022. Decision D-6 (contact-only detection, order independence), D-3 (one home storey). Appendix D.1: model tolerance 0.01 mm; minimum height 1 mm. JOIN_TOLERANCE comes from tolerance.rs of element-kind-framework (0.1 mm today in wall.rs:23-24). Open question: whether a Separated relation should also be expressed with a standard IFCX relation; this task keeps it in the archicraft:: namespace.

title: Add sloped and tapered slab parameters to the model
description:
WHY: SLB-006 (S): slabs shall support an inclined top and optionally an inclined bottom: sloped slabs of constant thickness, and tapered slabs such as flat roofs with falls; no roof, terrain or boolean workaround shall be needed. Simple ramps are modelled as sloped slabs (SRS 4.20 introduction). Gap row: missing, slab bodies are prisms between two horizontal planes (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:177-187, extrude.rs:18-58), effort L, depends on SLB-002 (tasks 02/03). Because of the L effort the requirement is split: this task delivers the model half (parameters, validation, extents, commands), task 14 the bodies.

WHAT: In the slab kind module (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/slab.rs after element-kind-framework-02, element.rs:178-188 today) add `Slab.slope: SlabSlope` with `enum SlabSlope { Flat, Sloped { origin: DVec2, incline: Incline }, Tapered { origin: DVec2, reference: Incline, opposite: Incline, taper_skin: Option<usize> } }` (default Flat, #[serde(default)]) and `Incline { direction: f64, pitch: f64 }` (radians; direction of steepest ascent in plan; a zero pitch is a horizontal face). The reference plane of task 03 passes through the reference elevation at `origin`. Sloped: top and bottom inclined in parallel, all skin boundaries parallel, thickness measured perpendicular to the plane. Tapered: the reference face follows `reference`, the opposite face follows `opposite` (so either face, or both with different pitches and directions, can be inclined), and the vertical thickness at `origin` equals the nominal total; in a layered tapered slab the taper skin (default: the first non-core skin on the reference side of the core, else the core) absorbs the variation, skins between it and the reference face follow the reference plane and the others the opposite plane. Provide `SlabSlope::boundary_planes(&CrossSection, reference_elevation) -> Vec<Plane>` (one plane per skin boundary, z(p) = z0 + g . (p - origin)) as the single source both validation and the geometry of task 14 use. Validation in the kind's validate hook: pitches finite and within 0..=60 degrees, origin finite, and at every outline vertex every skin's vertical thickness >= Skin::MIN_THICKNESS (planar faces have their extremes at vertices), with messages (NFR-REL-005). vertical_extent returns the minimum and maximum over the outline vertices. UpdateElements carries slope changes (no new command). Out of scope: bodies and plan (14), IFCX (08), UI fields (12), a slope-by-two-points tool, per-edge angles (SLB-005, edit-reshape-palette), roofs.
design: Plane representation: z(p) = z0 + g . (p - origin) with gradient g = tan(pitch) * (cos dir, sin dir); a perpendicular thickness t becomes the vertical offset t / cos(pitch) for Sloped slabs. Evaluate each boundary plane with one function shared by both neighbouring skins (and by task 14) so their vertices are bit-identical. Keep the slope in storey-local coordinates like the outline. Pitfall: vertical_extent is also used by validate_element (top above base) and by the plan view range; use min/max over vertices consistently. Ramps: a sloped slab of constant thickness is the SRS ramp representation (STA-050 is C). The 60-degree limit keeps planes far from vertical, which task 14 relies on for lifting a plan triangulation onto the planes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in the slab kind module: boundary_planes for a Sloped 0.20 m slab at 10 degrees gives two parallel planes whose vertical distance is 0.20 / cos(10 deg) within 1e-12; for a Tapered single-thickness slab with a horizontal bottom, 0.20 m at the origin edge and a 2 % top fall, the vertical thickness at a vertex 10 m up-slope is 0.40 m.
- Taper-skin rule: for the warm flat roof build-up (membrane 5 / EPS 200 / membrane 2 / reinforced concrete 200 core) the default taper skin is the EPS skin (index 1), and an explicit taper_skin overrides it.
- vertical_extent of a sloped and a tapered slab equals the analytic minimum and maximum over the outline vertices within 1e-12; Flat slabs return exactly the task 03 values.
- Validation rejects a pitch of 61 degrees, a NaN direction, a non-finite origin and a taper that makes any skin thinner than 0.1 mm at an outline vertex, each with a user-facing message; it accepts a tapered slab with a horizontal top and an inclined bottom, and one with both faces inclined at different pitches and directions (SLB-006 'optionally an inclined bottom').
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: UpdateElements changing Flat -> Sloped -> Tapered executes, undoes to the exact project and redoes; an invalid slope returns CommandError::Invalid and leaves the project unchanged.
- Flat is the default: existing projects, samples and golden files are unchanged.
- Satisfies the model clauses of SLB-006 (inclined top, optional independent inclined bottom, sloped constant-thickness and tapered slabs, as plain slab parameters without workarounds).
notes: SRS: SLB-006. Decisions to confirm: thickness of Sloped slabs measured perpendicular to the plane (constant-thickness ramps and decks), pitch limit 60 degrees (steeper planes are roofs), and the default taper-skin rule. Slope display follows the project's SlopeFormat (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:127, degrees by default, Appendix D.1).

title: Expose structures, core positions, slopes and wall flips in the UI
description:
WHY: WAL-003 (M) thickness or layer structure and the six reference-line locations, WAL-005 (M) move reference line without moving the body, WAL-006 (M) flip a wall's sides, SLB-002 (M) slab thickness or layer structure with its reference plane, SLB-009 (S) core top/bottom reference planes and SLB-006 (S) sloped and tapered slabs must be usable from the application.
