Gaps: the properties panel offers thickness and material only, its reference-line choice lacks the core options (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:253-320), the slab reference plane has two options (properties.rs:437-450), and no flip or move-reference-line action exists (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs:7-39).

WHAT: properties.rs (or the FieldSpec framework if properties-and-dialogs has landed): a 'Structure' choice for walls and slabs (Basic, then each layer structure by name), thickness and material fields only for Basic, the total thickness read-only for layered elements, and an 'Edit structure...' button that opens the dialog of task 11 at that structure; 'Reference line' with all six locations; slab 'Reference plane' with Top face, Bottom face, Core top and Core bottom; slab 'Shape' Flat/Sloped/Tapered with pitch (shown per the project SlopeFormat, degrees or percent), direction, origin X/Y, and for Tapered the opposite pitch/direction and the taper skin; the same fields edit the tool defaults (Subject::Defaults(kind) editing the wall and slab DefaultsSlot prototypes of element-kind-framework-04, which carry the structure and the slope). Actions in actions.rs with Edit or Design menu items in shell.rs: `MoveReferenceLine` ('Move reference line...', a popup choosing the target location, executes MoveWallReferenceLine on the selected walls), `FlipWalls` ('Flip wall', mirror about the reference line) and `SwapWallSides` ('Swap exterior and interior side', FlipWalls with keep_body = true); actions are disabled when no wall is selected. Out of scope: core-face snapping (13), slope by picked points, default shortcuts (none required by D.8).
design: Fields auto-hide when their getter returns None (properties.rs Fields pattern), so Basic-only fields return None for layered elements. Mixed multi-selection: the structure choice shows a mixed marker when walls differ and a commit applies to every editable selected element. The 'Move reference line' path must call the command of task 06, not the location setter, so the body stays; keep the plain location property for walls whose body may move (rename its label to 'Reference line location' to make the difference visible). Follow the 'Add a command' step 6 for actions (Action enum, ALL, label, run() arm in app.rs, menu item); test shortcut uniqueness stays green. Angle and slope inputs use widgets.rs (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/widgets.rs) with SlopeFormat from crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs. The kittests use the template structures and the F2 ring of task 09.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: selecting an F2 wall shows 'Structure' = 'Cavity wall 680' and the total 680 mm read-only; choosing 'Plastered masonry 135' executes one UpdateElements and the wall's start and end are unchanged (WAL-004 through the UI).
- kittest: the reference-line combo has six entries including 'Core exterior face' and 'Core interior face'; the slab reference-plane combo has four entries.
- kittest: 'Move reference line...' with 'Core interior face' on the selected F2 ring keeps every wall's geometry (bounds and volumes equal) and changes the reference lines; 'Flip wall' swaps start and end; 'Swap exterior and interior side' keeps the bounds; each is one undo step.
- kittest: setting a slab to Sloped with 10 degrees enlarges its z range; entering 70 degrees shows the validation message and leaves the slab unchanged.
- tools.rs state-machine test: with the wall tool default structure set to 'Cavity wall 680', the next drawn wall is layered and evaluates into six Skin parts.
- Satisfies the user-facing clauses of WAL-003, WAL-005, WAL-006, SLB-002, SLB-009 and SLB-006.
notes: SRS: WAL-003 WAL-005 WAL-006 SLB-002 SLB-009 SLB-006. Appendix D.1 slope display: degrees by default, percent selectable.

title: Auto-join wall ends within snap tolerance on placement and edits
description:
WHY: WAL-021: an auto-join option, on by default, shall extend or trim the end of a wall being drawn or edited so that it meets another wall's reference line when it comes within snap tolerance of it. Today snapping to reference lines gives exact contact only for pointer-snapped points (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:180-184, 216-267); there is no extension or trimming when a point lands off the line, and nothing happens when existing walls are moved (gap analysis: WAL-021 partial; the move and stretch UI it depends on does not exist yet). Moving a joined wall away again must unjoin it.

WHAT: Add `junction::auto_join(project, overrides, wall, ends, tolerance)` in crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs: for each free end, find the nearest reference line of a joinable wall within tolerance and move the end along its own reference line onto it, snapping to the other wall's endpoint when that is within tolerance; reuse meeting() of task 09. Add `Command::WithAutoJoin { command: Box<Command>, tolerance: f64, fixed_ends: Vec<(ElementId, WallEnd)> }`: its planner plans the inner command, derives the post-edit walls from the inner InsertElement and ReplaceElement edits without cloning the project, adjusts and validates them, and keeps the inner label; because the inner command is any Command, selection-transforms' Command::Transform and the stretch commands of edit-reshape-palette are wrapped the same way. Add a junction upkeep step to the planners of commands that insert, replace or move walls, dropping Separated relations whose pair no longer touches. Out of scope: the preference, the toggle and the wall tool wiring (11); the move, stretch and reshape tools of selection-transforms and edit-reshape-palette wrap their commands the same way when they exist.
design: The tolerance travels in the command in model units (the UI converts the 8 px snap radius at the current zoom), so planning stays deterministic for undo, redo and replay (NFR-MNT-001). Candidates come from the grid index of junction.rs; only ends that moved (or all ends of inserted walls) are considered, so editing unrelated properties never moves geometry. The end moves along the wall's own direction (the wall keeps its angle): intersect the wall's infinite reference line with the target segment; reject results that shorten the wall below MIN_EDGE_LENGTH or flip it. Overlay: a small ElementId -> Element map of post-edit versions consulted before the project. The upkeep step runs junction::detect_around on the touched walls only. Pitfalls: walls of one chain created in a single AddElements already touch exactly - skip ends already in contact within JOIN_TOLERANCE so shared vertices stay bit-identical; ends placed by typed values stay exact (AS-04 precision), the tool passes them as fixed_ends.
acceptance_criteria:
- auto_join unit tests with tolerance 10 mm: an end 4 mm short of another reference line is extended exactly onto it (T); a 4 mm overshoot is trimmed; an end within 10 mm of the other wall's endpoint snaps to it (L); 12 mm away, parallel, a different join group or NEVER: unchanged; the nearest candidate wins, ties go to endpoints before bodies, then distance, then ElementId.
- WithAutoJoin(AddElements) creates the adjusted wall in one undo step labelled "Create wall"; fixed (typed) ends are never moved (WAL-021 'being drawn').
- WithAutoJoin(MoveElements) moving a wall so that its end comes within tolerance of another reference line: the junction graph contains the pair and the geometry shows the L or T; moving it beyond tolerance again: no node and square ends (WAL-021 'edited'; epic acceptance 'auto-joins and moving it away unjoins').
- A move that breaks the contact of a Separated pair drops the relation, and undo restores it.
- Replaying a journal that contains WithAutoJoin reproduces the identical project.
notes: SRS: WAL-021. Appendix D.1: snap radius 8 px. Open question: should typed ends also auto-join when they fall within tolerance? Default here: typed values are exact and win (AS-04 measures typed lengths); pointer-placed ends auto-join.

title: Add core-face reference positions for walls and slabs
description:
WHY: WAL-003 (M): a wall shall have a reference-line location: exterior face, centre, interior face, core exterior face, core interior face, or a custom offset. PRF-003 (M): core faces shall be available as reference positions for wall reference lines (WAL-003), door/window reveals (DW-008) and snapping, and (with SLB-009) for slab reference planes. SLB-009 (S): the slab reference plane shall also be selectable as the top or bottom of the core. Gap rows: WAL-003 lacks the core variants (ReferenceLine has Outside/Center/Inside/Custom only, crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:87-125); PRF-003 missing (face_offsets takes a plain thickness, element.rs:99-107); SLB-009 missing (SlabReference has Top and Bottom only, element.rs:153-157, schema enumeration crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:116 and 251).

WHAT: Add `ReferenceLine::CoreExterior` and `CoreInterior` (labels 'Core exterior face', 'Core interior face') and a public `ReferenceLine::distance_from_exterior(&CrossSection) -> f64` (Outside 0, Center total/2, Inside total, CoreExterior core.0, CoreInterior core.1, Custom(d) d) on which face_offsets is built; task 06 and DW-008 reuse it. `next()` cycles Outside, Center, Inside, CoreExterior, CoreInterior and returns from Custom to Outside (the WAL-007 cycling key keeps working). Add `SlabReference::CoreTop` and `CoreBottom` (codes coreTop/coreBottom, ALL array) and a `SlabReference::distance_from_top(&CrossSection)`; `Project::vertical_extent` computes top = home + offset + distance_from_top and bottom = top - total. Extend the IFCX enumerations in alpha/schema.rs (REFERENCE_LINES and the slab reference options, derived from the model ALL arrays), the writer codes and the reader parsing (the reference_line helper in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/common.rs and the slab codec after element-kind-framework-06; reader.rs:170 and 685-712 today) so files stay valid; the format-version bump for the whole epic happens in task 08. In archicraft-app, properties.rs lists the new locations and planes, the Custom default stops using thickness/3 (technical debt at properties.rs:295) and starts at the current distance_from_exterior, and the wall tool preview and cycling use the cross-section of the tool defaults. Out of scope: per-skin geometry (04, 05), snapping (13), the move-reference-line command (06), DW-008 reveals (doors-windows-core consumes distance_from_exterior).
design: All reference positions are expressed as distances from the first face (exterior for walls, top for slabs) so one CrossSection drives walls, slabs and later roofs and reveals. A Thickness structure has a single core skin spanning the whole thickness, which makes the core variants valid for every wall instead of an error; the UI may still mark them as coinciding. Custom offsets stay measured from the exterior face towards the interior (element.rs:94-96), validation unchanged (within +/-10 m). Keep SlabReference's Default = Top (D.2). The reader maps unknown codes leniently to Outside/Top with a warning, as today for invalid values. Pitfall: the slab vertical extent must be computed from the top face for all four planes so F3's three equivalent definitions are bit-identical, not merely close; compute distance_from_top from the same cumulative skin sums the geometry uses (task 05).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: for the F2 section (core = concrete 300 mm at 370..670 mm from the exterior face) face_offsets returns (-0.370, 0.310) for CoreExterior and (-0.670, 0.010) for CoreInterior; for a Thickness 0.25 section CoreExterior equals Outside and CoreInterior equals Inside bit for bit.
- next() visits all five fixed locations in order and maps Custom(_) to Outside.
- DW-008 interface (PRF-003 reveal clause, consumed by doors-windows-core): ReferenceLine::distance_from_exterior and CrossSection.core are public and documented; a doc test computes the core exterior and core interior face lines of an F2 wall from model data only (no geometry crate).
- F3 numbers in crates/archicraft-model/tests (project-level): on a storey at +6.10 m a slab with the build-up screed 70 finish / resilient layer 30 other / reinforced concrete 250 core referenced to CoreTop at offset -0.10 has vertical_extent (5.75, 6.10); Top at 0.0, Bottom at -0.35 and CoreBottom at -0.35 give the same extent within 1e-12.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: walls with every reference-line location and slabs with every reference plane save, validate without problems and reload equal (IFX-064); the existing golden files are byte-identical because the samples use Outside and Top.
- Satisfies the reference-line clause of WAL-003, the wall-reference and slab-reference clauses of PRF-003 (model side) and SLB-009 (model and persistence).
notes: SRS: WAL-003 PRF-003 SLB-009. Appendix D.7 F3: storey (finished floor) +6.10 m, structural slab top +6.00 m, soffit +5.75 m, resilient layer 20-30 mm (30 mm used). The DW-008 clause of PRF-003 is consumed by doors-windows-core. Cross-epic: doors-windows-core-01 plans to reject 'a core face on a host without a core'; with this design every wall has a core (a Thickness structure is one core skin), so that branch is unreachable; the done task tells the doors-windows-core owner.

title: Generate the opening void prism and the invisible Void part
description:
WHY: Every opening needs one well-defined void volume that the host cuts (05, 06), the IFCX Void child (08), the tool preview (10, 11) and later doors and windows all use. OPN-003 (M) sections rectangular, circular or polygonal; OPN-004 (M) perpendicular to the host face or vertical; OPN-005 (M) through or limited depth. IFX-036 (M): 'Every door, window and opening shall have a Void child: a closed mesh that encloses the removed volume (it may extend beyond the host's faces)', on the occurrence 'because it depends on the host's thickness'; IFX-017: opening volumes are Void children; IFX-034 (M): curved geometry is tessellated with at most 2 mm chordal deviation and 10 degrees per segment (at least 36 segments per circle). Today BodyPart has only name, material and mesh (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:21-28) and nothing generates voids. IFX-034 is partial: the Tessellation setting exists and round-trips (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:27-43, writer.rs:163-164, reader.rs:347-356; keep), but no geometry consumes it (technical debt), which this task changes.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/opening.rs: `VoidPrism { to_storey: DAffine3, section: Vec<DVec2>, depth: (f64, f64) }` (opening-local frame: x along the host and z up for wall-face voids with the depth axis along the face normal into the wall; for plan voids the depth axis points down from the host top face; the frame's determinant is positive) and `void_prism(project, opening, host) -> Result<VoidPrism, GeometryError>` computed from model data only: the wall frame from the reference line and face offsets (layer-structures thickness), slab top and bottom from Project::vertical_extent, shaft ranges from the linked storeys. Through spans the full host thickness plus VOID_MARGIN = 0.05 m beyond each pierced face (the margin of the SRS Appendix C example); a limited void starting at the face and any section reaching the host base or top are extended by the margin, so no void face is coplanar with a host face. `section_ring(section, &Tessellation)`: rectangle, inscribed circle with n = max(36, ceil(360 / max_angle), ceil(pi / acos(1 - chord / r))) segments from project.settings.tessellation (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:27-51), polygon through validate_ring. `void_mesh(&VoidPrism) -> TriMesh` built with extrude() in the local frame and transformed. BodyPart gets `role: PartRole::{Body, Skin(SkinRef), Void}`, which absorbs layer-structures-04's BodyPart.skin (kept readable through BodyPart::skin() for plan-renderer-03, as layer-structures states); the opening's GeometryKind generator returns one part named 'Void' with role Void. ElementGeometry::volume() and bounds() and a new visible_parts() (parts plus the children parts of element-kind-framework-07) skip Void parts; plan.rs classification, render3d.rs build_scene, view3d.rs pick and PickIndex::build (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/pick.rs, 3d-input-navigation-06) use visible_parts(), so the invisible void never shows, snaps or picks as a body. Out of scope: cutting hosts (05, 06), IFCX (08), previews (10).
design: The void is the single source of truth: preview, cut, IFCX and later the door and window insert void (doors-windows-core) are derived from VoidPrism and never rebuilt by hand. The computation reads host parameters only, never host geometry, so evaluation has no cycle: voids first, then hosts. Coordinates are storey-local as everywhere in evaluate.rs. Inscribed polygons make the void slightly smaller than the true circle; document the choice and reuse the circle tessellator of profiles-columns-beams if it already exists instead of adding a second one. Pitfalls: a rotated Plan placement must still produce a counter-clockwise ring; the margin must not leak into the volume oracles of 05 and 06 (they use host-clipped volumes); PartRole must not change the IFCX bytes of existing parts (the writer keys children by name).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in opening.rs: void meshes for rectangle, circle and polygon sections, each perpendicular and vertical, through, limited and storey range, pass TriMesh::check_closed with positive signed volume.
- A 1.0 x 1.0 m through void in a 0.30 m wall has a volume of 1.0 x 1.0 x 0.40 m3 and extends 0.05 m beyond both faces (IFX-036 'may extend beyond the host's faces').
- Circular sections with default settings have at least 36 segments and at most 2 mm chordal deviation for diameters 0.30 m and 3.00 m; changing project.settings.tessellation changes the segment count (IFX-034, first consumer of the setting).
- A limited void from 0.00 to 0.40 m in a 0.50 m wall spans depth -0.05 to 0.40 m from the exterior face.
- A shaft void spans exactly the linked storey elevations plus offsets and follows SetStoreyElevation (model-level test through Project, no app).
- An opening's ElementGeometry has volume 0, plan_drawing emits no cut or projected lines for it, build_scene uploads no triangles for it and PickIndex::build stores none of its triangles; existing Body and Skin_n parts keep their names and IFCX bytes (goldens unchanged).
- The void side of OPN-003 and OPN-004 and the closed, extended Void mesh of IFX-036 (written in 08) are in place.
notes: SRS: OPN-003 OPN-004 OPN-005 IFX-036. Also IFX-017, IFX-034. Decision: VOID_MARGIN = 0.05 m as in SRS Appendix C (Void points from -0.05 to 0.35 m around a 0.30 m wall).

title: Verify exit criterion: Host relation and the opening element (2D cuts in the host plane)
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its exit criterion holds as a whole: the hosted-element framework (host relation, cascade delete and copy, host picking with live preview in plan and 3D, Void children) and the single-host opening with rectangular, circular and polygonal sections, perpendicular or vertical orientation, through or limited depth, shafts and plan symbols, cut as 2D polygons without a Boolean kernel. It covers OPN-001, OPN-003, OPN-004, OPN-005, OPN-006, OPN-007, OPN-009, ELM-016, IFX-015, IFX-036 and NFR-REL-004, and doors-windows-core, roofs, solid-kernel-ops, sections-elevations-dims, 3d-display-styles and members-profiles-adv build on it.

WHAT: Run and record the epic acceptance end to end on a clean checkout with the geometry, command, round-trip, conformance and kittest suites listed below; update the docs/implementation-status.md rows of every covered requirement ID, plus the hosted clause of WAL-005 (status, evidence with file:line, remaining gaps: OPN-002 with solid-kernel-ops, roofs as hosts with roofs, the types clause of NFR-REL-004 with components-dw-catalogue) and the readiness and technical-debt sections (tessellation setting now used, 3D hover overlay); file beads for anything left over; close the epic in beads. No new features: a failing criterion reopens the owning task.
design: Verification only: run the suites, compare the results with the acceptance list and fix nothing silently. Use the status script and the per-merge srs_ids check of regression-and-status (scripts/status.py) if they exist; otherwise edit the requirement rows by hand with file:line evidence, following the format of the existing rows.
acceptance_criteria:
- Niche acceptance as a geometry test: a limited opening from 0 to 0.40 m in a 0.50 m wall leaves a 0.10 m back (OPN-005).
- A 1.0 x 1.0 m opening in the F2 wall removes the volume from every skin (signed-volume check per Skin_i).
- An opening moves and is deleted with its host and is copied with it, each with undo (command tests of 02 and 13; ELM-016, OPN-001); MoveWallReferenceLine and FlipWalls keep hosted openings in place (WAL-005 hosted clause left open by layer-structures).
- A shaft from storey -1 to +2 cuts all slabs in range and follows a storey elevation change (OPN-006).
- The tool creates nothing without a host under the pointer (kittest), and the preview follows the host in plan and in a 3D view through the Camera3d ViewSurface (OPN-007).
- IFCX: the opening is a child of its host with an invisible closed Void mesh (conformance and viewer; IFX-015, IFX-036).
- A file with an orphaned hosted element is repaired deterministically and reported on load (NFR-REL-004).
- An opening at a wall end adjacent to a junction is part of the NFR-MNT-005 suite.
- Vertical openings through slabs show their outline and an optional per-view cross in plan (OPN-009).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all -- --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on every golden file, including openings-showcase.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for OPN-001, OPN-003, OPN-004, OPN-005, OPN-006, OPN-007, OPN-009, ELM-016, IFX-015, IFX-036 and NFR-REL-004, and the epic is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: OPN-001 OPN-003 OPN-004 OPN-005 OPN-006 OPN-007 OPN-009 ELM-016 IFX-015 IFX-036 NFR-REL-004

title: Add the LayerStructure resource with skins and resource commands
description:
WHY: PRF-001 (M): the system shall provide named layer structures, usable by walls, slabs and roofs; each is an ordered list of skins, each skin has a material, a thickness and a role (core, finish or other); a structure has at least one core skin and supports at least 48 skins. PRF-002 (M): editing a layer structure shall update every element that uses it; this task delivers the command half (UpdateLayerStructure), task 02 the propagation to elements. SRS 3.4 lists the layer structure as a project resource referenced by stable ID, NFR-REL-005 requires zero-thickness skins to be rejected with a message, and the 0.1 mm minimum follows the EDT-019/D.1 short-edge threshold. Gap rows: PRF-001 missing (no LayerStructure or Skin type in any crate; Project resources are only layers and materials, crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:171-172; the Edit enum has only layer and material resource edits, crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:616-633); PRF-002 missing, but the associative mechanism exists (revision-based re-evaluation, UpdateMaterial at command.rs:244-251).

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/src/layer_structure.rs (exported from lib.rs) with `LayerStructureId` (id_type! in ids.rs, next to MaterialId), `SkinRole { Core, Finish, Other }` (code/from_code/label/ALL like SlabReference), `Skin { material: MaterialId, thickness: f64, role: SkinRole }` and `LayerStructure { id, name, skins: Vec<Skin> }` with `total_thickness()`, `skin_boundaries()` (cumulative distances from the first face), `core_span() -> (usize, usize)` and `core_offsets() -> (f64, f64)` (distances from the first face to the outer and inner face of the core span), `MAX_SKINS = 64`, `Skin::MIN_THICKNESS = 0.0001` and `validate()`. The module is kind-independent (no use of Wall or Slab types), so the roofs epic binds the same resource without model changes (PRF-001 'usable by walls, slabs and roofs'; ROF-007). `LayerStructureId` gets the same constructors as MaterialId (random v4 and from_uuid) so the FixtureBuilder and default_metric_project_with of element-kind-framework-03 can seed it. Add `Project.layer_structures: Vec<LayerStructure>` with `Project::layer_structure(id)`; extend `integrity_problems` (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:327; IntegrityProblem entries after element-kind-framework-08) to report skins whose material is missing. Add `Command::AddLayerStructure(LayerStructure)`, `UpdateLayerStructure(LayerStructure)` and `DeleteLayerStructure { structure, replacement: Option<LayerStructureId> }` with labels, plans and the primitive edits `InsertLayerStructure { index, structure }`, `RemoveLayerStructure { id }` and `ReplaceLayerStructure(..)` with exact inverses; `plan_delete_material` (command.rs:520-551) also rewrites skins that use the deleted material to the replacement, so no skin can dangle. template.rs starts with an empty list (the template structures arrive with the fixtures in task 09). Out of scope: binding elements to structures and user replacement on delete (02), geometry (04, 05, 07), IFCX persistence (08), the editor dialog (11), per-skin priority overrides (junction-engine), per-kind usage flags.
design: Follow the 'Add a command' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md (Extension points) and mirror the Material resource (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:142-175 for the validate pattern, command.rs:234-252 for the commands, command.rs:686-709 for the Insert/Remove/Replace edit semantics with indices). Skin order convention, documented in the module: skin 1 is at the exterior face of a wall (the right-hand side of the reference line, element.rs:81-85) and at the top face of a slab or roof. The core span runs from the first to the last core skin inclusive, so a non-core skin between two core skins counts as part of the span for reference positions; document that rule because PRF-003 consumers (walls, slabs, DW-008 reveals) depend on it. Keep the list in insertion order for deterministic output (IFX-007). `#[serde(default)]` on Project.layer_structures keeps in-memory serde of older projects working. The total-thickness bounds reuse validate::MIN_THICKNESS/MAX_THICKNESS (validate.rs:182-187). Pitfall: validate on Add and Update inside plan(), not only in the UI, so scripted commands cannot create invalid structures (NFR-REL-005). Change tracking: after element-kind-framework-10 every Edit::apply records into Project.changes (ChangeLog); the three structure edits record a resource change there (task 02 turns it into the user elements' dirty set).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/layer_structure.rs: the F2 build-up 120/60/180/10/300/10 mm gives total_thickness 0.680, core_span (4, 4) (0-based, the concrete skin), core_offsets (0.370, 0.670) and the boundaries 0, 0.12, 0.18, 0.36, 0.37, 0.67, 0.68 within 1e-12.
- validate() rejects an empty name, no skins, no core skin, a skin of thickness 0, -0.01 or NaN (zero-thickness skins rejected with a message, NFR-REL-005), 65 skins and a total above 10 m, each with a user-facing message; it accepts 48 and 64 skins (PRF-001 'at least 48').
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddLayerStructure, UpdateLayerStructure and DeleteLayerStructure each execute, undo to the exact starting project (revision normalised) and redo; an invalid structure returns CommandError::Invalid and leaves the project untouched; updating an unknown id returns NotFound; an identical update returns NoChange.
- DeleteMaterial of a material used by a skin replaces it in every structure with the replacement material, and undo restores the original skins.
- integrity_problems reports a structure whose skin material is missing.
- layer_structure.rs has no dependency on the wall or slab kind modules (checked by the module-layout test of element-kind-framework), so roofs can reuse the resource.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check stay green; existing golden files are unchanged.
- Satisfies the resource clauses of PRF-001 (named, ordered skins with material, thickness and role, at least one core, at least 48 skins) and the command half of PRF-002.
notes: SRS: PRF-001 PRF-002. Decisions to confirm: MAX_SKINS = 64 (the SRS demands at least 48); minimum skin thickness 0.1 mm follows the D.1 short-edge repair threshold (membranes thinner than that are modelled at 0.1 mm). Open: whether structures need per-kind usage flags (walls/slabs/roofs) as in the reference product; PRF-001 does not require them, so none are added.

title: Verify exit criterion: Priority-based wall junction engine on per-skin footprints (F1, F6, F7)
description:
WHY: This closes the junction-engine epic and the wall half of the increment-1 exit criterion of Appendix F ('Fixtures F2, F6, F7 pass'). It confirms that WAL-020 (L, T, X joins), WAL-021 (auto-join), WAL-022 (join and unjoin), WAL-023 and WAL-024 (priority resolution with per-skin overrides), WAL-025 (join groups), WAL-026 and WAL-036 (order independence, documented rule, junction order), WAL-027 (plan, 3D and IFCX agree), WAL-008 (trapezoidal walls, F1), IFX-033 (exported geometry is the evaluated cleanup) and NFR-MNT-005 (junction regression suite) are met together on a clean main build, not only task by task.

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged state of tasks 01-13: workspace tests, clippy and fmt, the conformance job on all golden files, the junction suite and the IFX-033 test; check each clause of the epic acceptance against a named test; update docs/implementation-status.md (requirement rows, readiness per increment, technical debt) and close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new functionality; any defect found is fixed in the owning task or filed as a bead before closing.
design: Checklist procedure: (1) cargo build/test/clippy/fmt exactly as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs them; (2) cargo run --locked -p archicraft-ifcx --example reference_models -- target/reference-models, then conformance/run.sh target/reference-models/*.ifcx crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx; (3) map every acceptance clause to its test (F1/F6/F7 and F2 rows in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs, permutation tests of task 06, X and collinear tests of task 04, incremental-versus-full and dirty-set tests of task 13, auto-join tests of task 10, join/unjoin tests of task 09, never-join row, plan merge tests of task 07, IFX-033 hash test of task 08, catalogue and pending-row tests of task 12) and record the mapping in the closing comment; (4) update the twelve requirement rows in docs/implementation-status.md with evidence paths and line numbers, and the increment-1 readiness line; (5) bd close junction-engine with the summary; file follow-ups (stepped bodies for partial vertical overlap in cleanup-and-trims, the junction-order direction check against KB 303922 if still open, typed-end auto-join decision, auto-join wiring of move and stretch tools not yet wired, the beam join hook) as beads.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixtures F1 (300 to 500 mm trapezoidal wall with the reference-side face straight), F6 (junction orders 8/8/8 versus 8/8/7) and F7 (concrete 880 and insulation 400 priorities, then swapped) pass as geometry tests with golden skin outlines and closed bodies.
- a property test shuffles creation order over three to four walls at a node and gets identical meshes (WAL-026).
- X-junction and collinear continuation tests.
- a wall end moved within snap tolerance of another reference line auto-joins and moving it away unjoins.
- join on two selected walls extends or trims to the reference-line meeting point and unjoin separates them through the junction relation.
- a wall in a never-join group stays square.
- same-material same-priority skins merge into one plan region.
- the written mesh equals the evaluated resolved body (hash test, IFX-033).
- the suite enumerates every junction case of Section 4 (L, T, X, 3-way, equal priority, priority inversion, core-face reference lines, openings at ends) as a table-driven test in CI.
- the increment-1 exit 'F2, F6, F7 pass' is green.
- cargo test --workspace --locked, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green on the workspace.
- conformance/run.sh is green on the golden files, including crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/junction-showcase.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (WAL-020, WAL-021, WAL-022, WAL-023, WAL-024, WAL-025, WAL-026, WAL-027, WAL-036, WAL-008, IFX-033, NFR-MNT-005) with status and evidence paths, and the technical-debt entry 'Wall junctions limited to L and T' is removed or rewritten.
- Beads exist for every open follow-up: auto-join wiring of the selection-transforms and edit-reshape-palette tools if task 11 could not wire them, the beam implementation of the join hook (profiles-columns-beams, cleanup-and-trims), stepped bodies for partial vertical overlap, and the junction-order direction check against KB 303922 if still open.
- The epic junction-engine is closed in beads; follow-up work found on the way is filed as beads issues.
notes: SRS: WAL-020 WAL-021 WAL-022 WAL-023 WAL-024 WAL-025 WAL-026 WAL-027 WAL-036 WAL-008 IFX-033 NFR-MNT-005. Appendix F increment 1 exit: 'Fixtures F2, F6, F7 pass; a ground floor with openings can be drawn precisely' (the openings part belongs to host-openings and doors-windows-core). The 'openings at ends' row of the suite is enumerated here and runs as soon as host-openings registers the opening kind.

title: Layer structures, skins, core faces and multi-skin bodies
description:
Introduce the LayerStructure resource (ordered skins with material, thickness and role, at least 48), use it in walls and slabs with core-face reference positions, structure flips and swaps, slab core reference planes and sloped or tapered slabs, and write multi-material bodies as Skin_n parts; the prerequisite of the junction engine, doors (reveals) and roofs.

Risks: Per-skin geometry multiplies mesh count; kept per element in the incremental cache and merged for display where materials match.
design: archicraft-model LayerStructure resource and Structure::{Thickness, Layered(id)} on Wall and Slab; archicraft-geometry wall footprint per skin as offset bands along the reference line, extrusion per skin, slab skins stacked; archicraft-ifcx Skin_i child parts with v5 ids and an archicraft::layerStructure schema; the template gains the D.2 structures. Skin ends stay square at junctions in this epic; junction-engine resolves them and asserts F2 again.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture F2 (brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm) builds, cuts in plan with one region per skin and exports six Skin parts each naming its material (conformance plus viewer check); fixture F3 floating floor; editing a structure updates all users (command test); core-face reference-line locations, move-reference-line and flip commands keep the body in place (geometry tests); sloped constant-thickness and tapered slab bodies are closed. F2 and F3 are registered under their ids in the fixture registry of regression-and-status.
notes: SRS: PRF-001 PRF-002 PRF-003 WAL-003 WAL-004 WAL-005 WAL-006 SLB-002 SLB-009 SLB-006 IFX-017

title: Copy hosts together with their hosted elements
description:
WHY: ELM-016 (M): '... copying a host shall copy its hosted elements. Both are undoable.' IFX-011 (M, partial): copy, duplicate and array operations create new identities (random v4 ids exist in crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs; no copy exists). Gap-analysis ELM-016: 'no cascade on copy (copy itself does not exist)'. User-facing copy arrives with selection-transforms (EDT-002, EDT-016: Command::Transform { copy: true } planned through Project::duplicate), which is not a prerequisite of this epic, so the cascade must live in one model helper that every copy path (selection-transforms' copy and paste, drafting-trim-split's arrays, doors-windows-core, solid-kernel-ops) calls.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/copy.rs `duplicate(project, ids, &PlanTransform) -> Result<Vec<Element>, CommandError>`: the ids expanded by hosted_closure (02), new random ElementIds, names from the per-kind counters with nth offsets, locked = false, hosts first and hosted elements after them; hosted elements of copied hosts are copied with Kind::carry and re-pointed to the host copy, hosted elements copied without their host stay on the original host with Kind::transform and are rejected with a message when the moved placement leaves it. `Command::CopyElements(Vec<Element>)` carries the result, so journal replay is deterministic, and is planned like AddElements (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:320-342), whose validation gains an overlay lookup that accepts a host inserted earlier in the same command and whose counter update counts copied openings. If selection-transforms-02 has merged first, add no CopyElements: Project::duplicate delegates its id set and host re-pointing to copy::duplicate instead. Out of scope: copy UI, clipboard and paste (selection-transforms), arrays (drafting-trim-split).
design: The helper is a pure function returning elements so that every copy path builds its element list with it and the cascade rule exists once; journal replay stores the resulting elements, never re-runs id generation. Taking &PlanTransform (the framework type) instead of a delta lets selection-transforms' rotate-copy and mirror-copy reuse it unchanged. Pitfalls: re-pointing must happen before validation so the overlay lookup sees the host copy; keep the counter update in plan_add_elements in one place; copies of a locked host are unlocked like the copies of selection-transforms.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/hosting.rs copy_host_copies_hosted: CopyElements(duplicate([wall], translate d)) adds the wall copy and two opening copies hosted by it, all with new UUIDs and names (W-00n, OP-00n); undo removes all copies and redo restores them with the same ids (ELM-016 copy clause, undoable; IFX-011).
- Copying an opening alone keeps its original host and slides it along the wall; a copy whose moved anchor leaves the host is rejected with a message and the project is unchanged.
- Copying a slab carries its Plan openings and a shaft hosted by it keeps its storey links.
- A command that lists a hosted copy before its host copy is still valid (hosts are planned first); the name counters after the command equal the number of created elements per kind.
- The seeded property test of 02 includes copy steps and still finds no integrity problem after any step.
notes: SRS: ELM-016. Also IFX-011, OPN-001 (hosted copies keep their host-relative placement) (partial, copy identities). Coordination: selection-transforms owns the user-facing copy commands and must call copy::duplicate; doors-windows-core and solid-kernel-ops cite copy::duplicate as the hosted copy path.

title: Priority-based wall junction engine on per-skin footprints (F1, F6, F7)
description:
Replace the L/T-only mitre in archicraft-geometry wall.rs with a node-based junction engine over 2D per-skin footprints: X crossings, three or more walls per node with the documented deterministic rule and per-wall junction order, skins trimmed by material priority with per-skin overrides, join groups with a reserved never-join value, auto-join on placement and move, explicit join and unjoin commands, trapezoidal walls (fixture F1), agreement of plan, 3D and IFCX by slicing the resolved bodies, and the guarantee that exported geometry is the evaluated result of the cleanup (IFX-033, re-asserted by openings, trims and solid operations as they arrive). Built on geo/i_overlay polygon Booleans only, so the increment-1 exit criterion does not wait for the C++ Boolean kernel; cross-kind 3D cleanup (columns, beams, slabs) is cleanup-and-trims. Owns the NFR-MNT-005 regression suite.

Risks: The hardest geometry in v1 and the increment-1 exit criterion; reduced by writing F1/F6/F7 first and by falling back to square ends plus a reported problem instead of corrupt geometry (NFR-REL-005). Combinatorial growth at nodes is bounded by local per-node resolution.
design: archicraft-geometry junction.rs: node graph from reference-line contact within MODEL_TOLERANCE (decision D-6), per-node resolution producing per-skin polygons with geo/i_overlay Booleans in priority order, then extrusion; footprints become general polygons (prerequisite for arc walls); plan regions are slices of the resolved bodies (WAL-027). archicraft-model: JoinGroup and junction_order on Wall, Wall.end_thickness for WAL-008, commands JoinWalls/UnjoinWalls; junction edges recorded in the relation store. Determinism rule documented in docs/ and asserted by tests; fixtures f1/f6/f7 registered in crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures F1 (300 to 500 mm trapezoidal wall with the reference-side face straight), F6 (junction orders 8/8/8 versus 8/8/7) and F7 (concrete 880 and insulation 400 priorities, then swapped) pass as geometry tests with golden skin outlines and closed bodies; a property test shuffles creation order over three to four walls at a node and gets identical meshes (WAL-026); X-junction and collinear continuation tests; a wall end moved within snap tolerance of another reference line auto-joins and moving it away unjoins; join on two selected walls extends or trims to the reference-line meeting point and unjoin separates them through the junction relation; a wall in a never-join group stays square; same-material same-priority skins merge into one plan region; the written mesh equals the evaluated resolved body (hash test, IFX-033); the suite enumerates every junction case of Section 4 (L, T, X, 3-way, equal priority, priority inversion, core-face reference lines, openings at ends) as a table-driven test in CI; the increment-1 exit 'F2, F6, F7 pass' is green.
notes: SRS: WAL-020 WAL-021 WAL-022 WAL-023 WAL-024 WAL-025 WAL-026 WAL-027 WAL-036 WAL-008 IFX-033 NFR-MNT-005

title: Cut slab openings as outline holes and shafts across storeys
description:
WHY: Stair holes, duct penetrations and shafts are openings in slabs. OPN-001 (M) names slabs as hosts; OPN-005 (M) through or limited depth; OPN-006 (S): 'A vertical opening shall be able to span a range of storeys (shaft), cutting every slab and roof in that range, and shall follow later changes of storey elevations.' IFX-025 (M, done: slab holes are mesh geometry in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18-57 and the archicraft::slab 'holes' parameter in writer.rs:205-215; keep and regress) keeps holes drawn into a slab outline as geometry, distinct from opening elements. The epic acceptance requires 'a shaft from storey -1 to +2 cuts all slabs in range and follows a storey elevation change'. Gap-analysis OPN-006: 'No storey-spanning opening, no multi-host cutting, roofs absent', with TopLink (element.rs:71-80) and Project::top_elevation as the datum pattern to reuse. Cutting every slab in a vertical range needs no 3D kernel because each cut is a plan hole; general multi-element cuts (OPN-002) stay with solid-kernel-ops.

WHAT: The slab GeometryKind generator receives as cutters the plan voids of its hosted openings plus every opening with Depth::Storeys whose absolute range overlaps the slab's vertical extent and whose section bounding box meets the slab outline (`shaft_targets` in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/opening.rs, restricted to kinds whose HostCapability allows shaft cuts: slabs now, roofs once the roofs epic sets the flag). Per slab skin (layer-structures z bands), extrude_layers along z with sections equal to the skin outline including its own holes minus the union of the void sections covering that z-interval: a through void becomes an outline hole in every skin, a void ending inside the slab a recess with a floor, a section crossing the outline a notch, a section splitting the slab several shells in one closed part. The incremental dirty set gains a hook so that a dirty shaft dirties every slab meeting its old and new range and footprint; storey elevation changes reach shafts through their storey links (framework) and from there the slabs. A shaft that cuts no slab is reported in the warning list of 05 (not as a failed element). Out of scope: walls inside a shaft range (not required by OPN-006; OPN-002), roof hosts (verified in the roofs epic), perpendicular openings in sloped slabs (rejected by the validator of 01 until the inclined-plane path of the roofs epic).
design: Absolute elevations are needed only to select targets (a slab's extent from Project::vertical_extent, the shaft range from its storey links); the cut itself runs in the slab's storey-local coordinates after converting the void's z-range. Bounding-box prefiltering keeps the target search linear; use the framework's RTree if it indexes slabs, otherwise a per-storey scan (slabs per storey are few). Layer boundaries per skin: skin top and bottom plus every void z-bound inside the skin. Pitfalls: a shaft's own host is also a target, so do not cut it twice; ranges that only touch a slab face within MODEL_TOLERANCE must not create zero-thickness layers; the DirtySet hook must use both the old and the new shaft data so that removed or moved shafts restore their former targets, the same rule the framework applies to contact neighbours.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/openings.rs shaft_cuts_all_slabs_in_range: storeys -1, 0, +1, +2 and +3 with 0.20 m slabs (top at the storey elevation); a 1.20 x 2.00 m shaft hosted by the storey -1 slab from storey -1 offset -0.20 to storey +2 offset 0.00 reduces the volume of each slab on storeys -1 to +2 by 1.20 x 2.00 x 0.20 m3, leaves the +3 slab untouched, and all parts are closed (epic acceptance).
- follows_storey_elevation_change: SetStoreyElevation raising storey +2 by 0.50 m (shifting the storeys above) keeps the +2 slab cut through and +3 uncut; undo restores identical meshes (OPN-006 'follow later changes of storey elevations').
- A range ending inside a slab's thickness leaves a recess whose floor lies at the range end; a limited opening 0.05 m deep from a slab top leaves a floor; an opening across the slab edge cuts a notch; an opening splitting the slab yields one closed part with two shells.
- A through opening in the F3 floating floor (fixtures::f3_floating_floor of layer-structures-09) pierces every skin.
- shaft_targets selects targets by HostCapability only: the test-kinds Dummy flagged as shaft-capable inside the range is returned as a target, so the roofs epic only sets the flag and adds its cut path (OPN-006 'and roof', verified in roofs).
- Moving a shaft dirties the slabs of its old and new footprint; changing the elevation of storey 0 dirties the shaft and the slabs in range; incremental equals full evaluation.
- A slab hole drawn as part of the outline still creates no opening element and is written as archicraft::slab holes, never as IfcOpeningElement (IFX-025 preserved; the two_storey_shell stair hole is not counted as opening coverage).
notes: SRS: OPN-001 OPN-005 OPN-006. Also IFX-025. Decision to confirm: walls crossed by a shaft are not cut automatically (OPN-006 names slabs and roofs only).

title: Persist junction data in IFCX and assert exported cleanup (IFX-033)
description:
WHY: IFX-033: exported geometry shall be the evaluated result of all modelling operations - wall and beam junction cleanup, layer-structure intersections, openings and hosted doors/windows, trims to roofs and slabs, and solid operations. What exists (gap analysis: IFX-033 partial) and is kept: the writer takes meshes only from ModelGeometry (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:370-381) and the app saves the geometry evaluated for the current revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103, 134-142). What is missing: only L/T cleanup is covered by a golden file (two-storey-shell.ifcx) and no test asserts that written meshes equal the evaluated ones. The authoring data of WAL-025 (join group), WAL-036 (junction order), WAL-008 (end thickness), WAL-024 (skin priority override) and WAL-022 (separated pairs) must survive save and open, because IFCX is the native format (D-1).

WHAT: Declare optional attributes and write and read them through the codecs of element-kind-framework-06: joinGroup in the archicraft::element envelope (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/common.rs) and in the wall toolDefaults slot, junctionOrder and endThickness in archicraft::wall (alpha/kinds/wall.rs), the skin priority in the layer_structure() record of layer-structures-08 (schema.rs, writer.rs project_attribute, reader.rs); read leniently with report.or(..) and defaults. The Separated relation's mode member comes from task 02. Build `samples::junction_showcase()` through the FixtureBuilder with seeded ids (L, T, X, F6 8/8/7, F7, F1 in an L, a never-join wall and a pair separated with UnjoinWalls) and add it as one line to samples::catalogue() (element-kind-framework-03), which feeds crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and samples() of tests/roundtrip.rs; bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/junction-showcase.ifcx and run the conformance job on it; add a generic IFX-033 test over all catalogue samples and a document-level test that a save right after an edit writes the re-evaluated geometry. Out of scope: openings, trims and solid operations (their epics add catalogue samples that the generic test then covers).
design: Follow the extension-point recipe 'Add an IFCX attribute' in docs/implementation-status.md, applied to the codecs of element-kind-framework-06 (the element and slot parts of today's writer.rs element_attributes, writer.rs:192, live in alpha/kinds/ after that task): field and validation exist from task 01; declare each attribute with optional(...); write with json!; read with report.or(..., default). Write only non-default values (join group other than 1, junction order other than 8, end thickness when set, skin override when set): existing golden files stay byte-identical and old readers ignore nothing they need. Join group 0 means never join; state it in the schema declaration's description. The Separated relation codec comes from task 02. The showcase uses the framework's seeded builder (v5 ids from fixture names) so the golden file is deterministic. Hash for the IFX-033 test: FNV-1a over the coordinates rounded with round_coordinate (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/json.rs:153) and faceVertexIndices, implemented in the test, because std's DefaultHasher is not stable across Rust versions. conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx picks up the new golden file automatically; the CI job needs no change.
acceptance_criteria:
- A project with join groups (including NEVER), junction orders, an end thickness, a skin priority override, a wall tool-defaults slot with join group 5 and a Separated relation saves and loads equal (roundtrip.rs).
- Files without the new attributes (the existing golden files and an increment-0 file) load with defaults and no new problems; FORMAT_VERSION is unchanged, following the rule in alpha/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-12) that optional additions need neither a bump nor a migration.
- validate() passes on the written file with every new attribute declared in-file (IFX-061); the registry.rs tests pass.
- junction-showcase.ifcx is reproduced byte for byte by golden_files_are_reproduced and catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files, and conformance/run.sh passes on it (Skin parts compose in the reference viewer with valid bodies and colours).
- IFX-033 test: for every catalogue sample, each written Body or Skin mesh equals the evaluated mesh (points rounded with round_coordinate, identical indices, compared through a stable hash), and the geometry regenerated after load equals the stored meshes (extends regenerated_geometry_matches_the_stored_geometry, roundtrip.rs:64).
- crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs test: after JoinWalls executes, the saved file's meshes equal a fresh ModelGeometry::evaluate of the current project (Document::geometry re-evaluates per revision, document.rs:97-103; kept and regressed now that evaluation is incremental).
- The IFX-033 test iterates the catalogue, so its clauses arrive with their owners without changing it: wall junction cleanup and layer-structure intersections now; beam junction cleanup and trims to roofs and slabs (cleanup-and-trims), openings and hosted doors/windows (host-openings, doors-windows-core) and solid operations (solid-kernel-ops) when their samples join the catalogue; its doc comment lists them.
notes: SRS: IFX-033 WAL-025 WAL-036 WAL-008 WAL-024 WAL-022. Related: IFX-060 (authoring data stored), IFX-032 (closed meshes), IFX-007 (determinism), NFR-MNT-003 (golden files). ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 regenerates golden files; the diff is reviewed in the pull request.

title: Select openings and edit their parameters in the properties panel
description:
WHY: After placement an opening's section, orientation, depth and position must stay editable, with range checks that explain rejected values (ELM-017, NFR-REL-005): OPN-003 (rectangular, circular or polygonal section), OPN-004 (perpendicular or vertical), OPN-005 (through, or limited by start and end offsets), OPN-006 (a storey range that follows storey elevations) and OPN-001's position relative to the host. Because the Void is invisible (IFX-036), an opening cannot be picked by its body: plan picking uses the outlines of 07, and 3D picking needs a rule that finds the opening when the user clicks into its reveal. Today the properties strip knows only walls and slabs (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:47-131) and 3D picking returns the first body hit (view3d.rs:75, rebuilt on PickIndex by 3d-input-navigation-06).

WHAT: view3d.rs pick() (PickIndex::ray, which holds visible parts only, 03): when the hit point on a host lies inside one of its hosted elements' Void meshes taken from ModelGeometry (ray-parity point-in-mesh test on the closed Void), the hosted element is returned first and Tab cycling reaches the host; Void parts are never drawn. Plan picking returns the opening for hits on its symbol segments (07) before the host. properties.rs: prototype and defaults extraction for the opening kind; Fields getters and setters for the section kind with width, height or diameter (polygon sections show their vertex count; their rings are edited with the polygon tools of edit-reshape-palette), orientation, placement (along, elevation and face, or origin and rotation), and depth mode with start and end, or bottom storey plus offset and top link (reusing the wall-top storey combo); derived rows for the host name and the volume removed from the host. Every edit goes through Command::UpdateElements, and validator messages appear in the status line. Out of scope: reassigning the host and adding cut elements (OPN-002, solid-kernel-ops), surface overrides (OPN-008), polygon vertex editing (edit-reshape-palette).
design: Follow the properties.rs pattern (Fields getters returning None hide their rows) and the 'Add a dialog' extension point only if the settings dialog needs an opening page. The removed volume is the host volume without the opening minus the host volume with it; compute it from the cached geometry per revision rather than re-evaluating per frame. Pitfalls: the Tab cycling state lives in PlanViewState for plan (the pick tuple in plan.rs) and needs an equivalent per 3D view; the point-in-mesh test must apply the storey offset as pick does; changing the orientation from perpendicular to vertical must convert a WallFace placement to a Plan placement that keeps the world anchor.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: clicking an opening's outline in plan selects the opening, not its host; the properties strip shows the opening fields; changing the width from 1.00 to 1.20 m issues UpdateElements and the host's volume decreases accordingly; undo restores both.
- Entering a limited depth with start >= end shows the validation message and changes nothing (ELM-017, NFR-REL-005).
- 3D pick test: a ray onto the reveal face of a through opening returns the opening and Tab returns the host next; a ray onto the plain wall face returns the wall.
- Switching the depth to a storey range offers the storeys; setting the top to storey +2 extends the shaft, cuts the +2 slab and makes the symbol appear on the +2 plan.
- The OPN-003 to OPN-006 parameters and OPN-001's host-relative position are editable with explained rejections.
notes: SRS: OPN-001 OPN-003 OPN-004 OPN-005 OPN-006. Also ELM-017, NFR-REL-005.

title: Build the table-driven NFR-MNT-005 junction regression suite
description:
WHY: NFR-MNT-005: geometry regression tests shall cover all junction and intersection cases in Section 4 (for example L, T and X wall junctions, layered walls of different priorities, openings at element boundaries). Today only L and T of single-skin straight walls are covered (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:279-345, tests/storey.rs:30-76). The increment-1 exit criterion of Appendix F is 'Fixtures F2, F6, F7 pass', and this epic owns the suite that later epics extend (WAL-020 cases, WAL-023 priorities, WAL-026 order independence).

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs as one table of cases, each with its SRS reference, fixture builder, golden skin outlines (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/golden/junctions/<case>.json, regenerated with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 like the IFCX golden files) and expected problems. Active rows: L, T, X, collinear continuation (the result of a WAL-030 split), Y and 4-way, equal priority, priority inversion, per-skin override, F1 alone and in an L, F2 at L and T, F6 both variants, F7 both variants, core-face reference lines, join groups, never-join, separated pairs, cross-storey coverage, an acute-angle fallback and a short-wall node cluster. Pending rows for cases owned by later epics (openings at ends, corner windows, columns/beams/slabs, curved walls F8, chimneys, roofs, solid operations) switch on automatically once their kinds are registered. Drive the F-rows from the D.7 constructors that tasks 03, 05 and 06 registered in crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (fixtures::f1_trapezoidal_wall, f6_three_wall_node, f7_t_junction) instead of duplicating them, and assert that their D.7 entries are built. Out of scope: implementing the pending cases.
design: `struct Case { name: &'static str, srs: &'static [&'static str], build: fn() -> Project, expect: Expect, status: Status }` with `Status::{Active, Pending { owner: &'static str, requires_kind: &'static str }}`; build through the seeded fixture builder of element-kind-framework so ids and golden files are stable. Golden JSON per case: per element name and skin index the outline rings rounded to 1e-9 m, normalised to counter-clockwise order with the lexicographically smallest vertex first, so diffs show geometry changes only and never i_overlay's choice of start vertex. Reuse the agreement helpers of task 07 and the permutation helper of task 06 through a tests/common module. Keep each case small (two to four walls) so the suite stays fast; F2 cases are the slowest - keep the whole file within a few seconds under the dev profile (opt-level 1, Cargo.toml). If regression-and-status-02 had not landed, tasks 03, 05 and 06 created crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs in the shape it specifies; reuse that module, do not add a second registry.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test -p archicraft-geometry --test junctions runs every active row in the existing CI test job on all three platforms, checking per row: closed bodies (check_closed), golden skin outlines within 1e-9 m, coverage of each node envelope by interior-disjoint pieces, the cut-region count per material in the plan, and the expected problem list (empty except for fallback rows).
- The rows L, T, X, 3-way, equal priority, priority inversion and core-face reference lines exist and pass; the F2, F6 and F7 rows pass (increment-1 exit criterion).
- An 'openings at ends' row exists as Pending("host-openings"); a completeness test fails when the kind registry contains the opening kind while the row is still pending, naming the owning epic; the same holds for every other pending row (and the row is active from the start if host-openings closed first).
- A catalogue test lists the Section 4 requirement IDs that involve junctions or intersections (WAL-020 to WAL-027, WAL-008, WAL-030, WAL-034, WAL-036, COL-006, BEA-004, SLB-007, ROF-010, SOL-027, DW-016, CW-011) and fails if one has no row.
- Every row with up to four walls also runs the creation-order permutation check of task 06.
- Golden outlines are human-readable JSON and the bless workflow is described in the file's module doc.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-005 WAL-020 WAL-023 WAL-026. Appendix D.7: F1, F2, F6, F7 are active rows; F4/F5 (members-profiles-adv) and F8 (curved-geometry) arrive as pending rows. Owners of pending rows per the roadmap: host-openings (openings at ends), library-dw-exchange (DW-016 corner windows), cleanup-and-trims (COL-006, BEA-004, SLB-007, ROF-010), curved-geometry (F8), members-profiles-adv (WAL-034), solid-kernel-ops (SOL-027), curtain-walls (CW-011). WAL-030 split itself belongs to drafting-trim-split; its geometric result (collinear continuation) is an active row here.

title: Draw opening outlines and the per-view cross symbol in plan
description:
WHY: OPN-009 (S): 'In plan, vertical openings through slabs shall be drawn with their outline and an optional cross symbol, configurable per view.' Openings also need a pickable plan representation because their Void is invisible (selection in 12). Gap-analysis OPN-009: PlanElement has only cut, projected, overhead and reference_line (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:23-33), there is no symbol layer and no per-view display setting; plan views are implicit per storey (Workspace.plan_views is keyed by StoreyId), and plan.rs:120 draws only elements homed on the storey, so a shaft from another storey would never appear.

WHAT: plan.rs: PlanElement gains `symbols: Vec<PlanSymbol { class: SymbolClass::{OpeningOutline, OpeningCross}, line: LineClass::{Cut, Projected, Overhead}, segments: Vec<[DVec2; 2]> }>`. plan_drawing adds, for each storey, every vertical opening whose void cuts a slab inside the storey's view range, including shafts homed on other storeys (looked up through the relation store's storey index), with the section ring as outline and the two diagonals of the section's oriented bounding rectangle clipped to the ring (geo) as cross, in the line class of the slab it cuts (cut when the cut plane meets the slab, projected below, overhead above). Perpendicular wall openings contribute the plan projection of their void clipped to the host footprint as an outline only, no cross, when the cut plane does not cross them, so they stay pickable. Symbol segments are part of PlanElement::segments() (plan.rs:211) and therefore pickable and snappable. App: PlanViewState (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:22) gains `opening_cross: bool` (default on), toggled by a View menu item 'Opening cross symbols' for the active plan view and in the plan context menu; draw_plan (plan.rs:237) draws outlines in the element's line style and crosses only when the flag is on. If plan-views-browser's ViewDefinition exists, the flag is captured into and applied from its plan display section and saved with the view in the ArchiCraft namespace. Symbols follow the opening's layer visibility through the existing shown filter of plan_drawing. Out of scope: pens and line weights (plan-renderer), section views (OPN-013).
design: Generate symbols in the geometry crate as renderer-agnostic segments (the extension point 'Add a plan-view overlay or line class' in docs/implementation-status.md), so plan-renderer can style them later without new geometry code. Oriented bounding rectangle: the section itself for rectangles, the square in opening-local coordinates for circles, geo's MinimumRotatedRect for polygons. The flag is view state, not element data, because the SRS says 'configurable per view', and it must not affect IFCX (IFX-068). Pitfalls: plan caches are kept per storey (framework incremental plans), so a shaft edit must invalidate every storey in its old and new range; draw crosses after cut fills so they stay visible.
acceptance_criteria:
- plan.rs tests: a rectangular vertical opening through a slab yields a four-segment outline and two diagonals; a circular one a cross clipped to the circle; an L-shaped polygon clipped diagonals.
- The shaft from storey -1 to +2 appears on the plans of storeys -1 to +2 (one PlanElement each) and not on +3; its line class follows the cut slab's classification.
- Perpendicular wall openings produce an outline but no cross; PlanDrawing::pick on an outline segment returns the opening's id.
- kittest: switching the menu item off hides the cross in the active plan view only; another storey's plan keeps it; the setting survives switching tabs; the standard IFCX content (elements, Void and body meshes) is identical either way, and only an archicraft:: view definition differs when plan-views-browser's ViewDefinition stores the flag (IFX-068).
- Hiding the opening's layer hides its outline and cross; the host stays cut.
- OPN-009 satisfied.
notes: SRS: OPN-009. Decision: the cross is on by default; Appendix D has no value for it.

title: Export Skin_n parts and add the layered golden reference model
description:
WHY: IFX-017 (M): a body with several materials has one child per material part, named Skin_1 ... Skin_n for layer structures; IFX-043 (M): every material node carries bsi::ifc::prop::Name and every part of a layered element references a named material, so consumers can identify each component's material; IFX-010 (M): regenerated sub-nodes get v5 UUIDs from the owner and role; IFX-006 (M): files validate in the reference implementation and display correctly in the viewers. The epic acceptance asks for six Skin parts each naming its material, with a conformance and a viewer check. Gap row IFX-017: partial, golden files show only Body and Axis children.

WHAT: writer.rs write_element (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:361-412) already writes one child per part with sub_node_id(owner, part.name) and inherits the material; element-kind-framework-07 moves this into one helper that writes 'Body/Body_n/Axis children', so make sure that helper keys children by BodyPart.name (Skin_i) and never renames material parts to Body_n, verify Skin_n naming and ordering, and add a debug assertion that every part's material exists in the project. Existing behaviour kept and regressed: single-material elements keep one Body child, walls keep their Axis child (IFX-017 clauses already done). Add `samples::layered_structures()` to the samples catalogue (FixtureBuilder): the F2 ring, the F3 floor, one sloped and one tapered slab; it is picked up by examples/reference_models.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs through the catalogue, and its output is blessed as crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/layered-structures.ifcx. conformance/check.ts: for every element, children named Skin_<n> are numbered 1..n without gaps, each has a mesh, a diffuseColor and a composed bsi::ifc::prop::Name inherited from its material node, and no element has both Body and Skin children. Viewer check: if the Playwright viewer job of regression-and-status exists it covers the new golden automatically; otherwise open the golden in the hosted IFC5 viewer (R4) and attach a screenshot of the six coloured skins to the pull request (IFX-006 b, manual part). Out of scope: Void children (host-openings), Frame/Panel/Glazing parts (doors-windows-core).
design: No writer restructuring is expected: the generic part loop (writer.rs:366-381) was built for this, and element-kind-framework's compound-part codec handles parts with their own IFC class, which skins are not (skins are material parts of one element and carry no bsi::ifc::class). Keep the golden small: the 48-skin case stays a unit test, not a golden. check.ts composes inherits, so the material's Name appears on the Skin node; checking `typeof attributes['bsi::ifc::prop::Name'] === 'string'` on Skin meshes is enough. Follow 'Add a sample/golden model' in docs/implementation-status.md; run ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx --test roundtrip and review the diff.
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs test layered_bodies_are_skin_parts: every F2 wall node has children Skin_1..Skin_6 and Axis and no Body; each Skin node inherits a material node whose bsi::ifc::prop::Name is, in order, Brick, Air gap, Mineral wool, Plaster, Concrete, Plaster; Thickness elements keep a single Body child.
- The F3 slab node has children Skin_1..Skin_3 inheriting Screed, Mineral wool and Reinforced concrete and no Axis; the single-thickness sloped and tapered slabs have exactly one Body child; the layered tapered deck has Skin_1..Skin_4.
- Skin node ids equal Uuid::new_v5(wall uuid, "Skin_i") and are unchanged after editing the wall height and saving again (IFX-010).
- layered-structures.ifcx validates without problems (IFX-006 a), round-trips equal (IFX-064), its meshes are closed (IFX-032) and the regenerate test finds stored and regenerated geometry equal within 0.1 mm.

- Satisfies IFX-017 for layer structures (Skin_1 ... Skin_n children for walls and slabs, Body and Axis kept) and IFX-043 for layered parts; the Void clause of IFX-017 is delivered by host-openings-03 and the Frame/Panel/Glazing example by doors-windows-core, recorded as open in the status update of the done task.

title: Stack slab skins and honour core reference planes in geometry
description:
WHY: SLB-002 (M): a slab shall have a thickness or a layer structure and a reference plane at an offset; SLB-009 (S): the reference plane can be the top or bottom of the core; PRF-001 (M): layer structures are usable by slabs; IFX-017 (M): a multi-material body is written as Skin_1 ... Skin_n parts. Appendix D.7 F3 (floating floor) is the acceptance case. Gap rows: SLB-002 partial (geometry extrudes one part, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:177-187), SLB-009 missing (needs vertical_extent computing the core offset within the structure).

WHAT: In the slab geometry generator (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/slab.rs after element-kind-framework-07, evaluate.rs:177-187 today), for a Layered slab compute the top elevation from the reference plane (task 03) and stack the skins downwards (skin 1 at the top), extruding the outline with its holes once per skin into BodyParts `Skin_{i}` with material and BodyPart.skin (SkinRef of task 04); Thickness slabs keep one `Body`. Skin boundary elevations are computed once by cumulative sums from the top so adjacent skins share identical z values. In plan.rs deduplicate coincident projected and overhead segments within one element, so a layered slab below the cut plane draws its outline once instead of once per skin. Out of scope: sloped and tapered slabs (07), IFCX (08, 10), slab-wall cleanup by priority (cleanup-and-trims).
design: Reuse extrude() (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18-58) per skin; the outline triangulation is computed per call today, so hoist it (triangulate once, lift per skin) if a 48-skin slab is measurably slow. Elevations are storey-local as for all bodies (evaluate.rs:1-7, IFX-031). Keep the vertical_extent of the model and the geometry stack on the same arithmetic (distance_from_top of task 03) so F3's equivalent definitions are bit-identical. Segment deduplication uses the MERGE_STEP-style quantised keys of mesh.rs facing_outline (mesh.rs:205-237) or the framework tolerance module. Pitfall: a cut plane exactly at a skin boundary - classification in plan.rs:133-146 uses EPS so the boundary skin is not reported as cut twice; add a test at z = core top. Known limitation, not fixed here: plan.rs classifies each part by its z-bounds against a view range whose bottom is the storey elevation (plan.rs:70-77 and 133-146), so skins (and whole slabs) entirely below the storey elevation are not drawn in their home storey's plan (implementation-status observation); the done task files a bead for it.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/layered.rs: a 6 x 4 m slab with the floating-floor build-up (screed 70 / resilient 30 / reinforced concrete 250) on a storey at +6.10 m, referenced to CoreTop at -0.10, evaluates into three closed parts with storey-local z ranges Skin_1 -0.07..0.00, Skin_2 -0.10..-0.07, Skin_3 -0.35..-0.10; the same meshes result for Top at 0.0, Bottom at -0.35 and CoreBottom at -0.35.
- A wall on that storey with base offset -0.10 has its body bottom exactly at the top of Skin_3 (equal z, no gap or overlap).
- A layered slab with a hole: every skin part is closed and contains the hole.
- A 48-skin slab evaluates into 48 closed parts.
- The plan of a layered slab below the cut plane has no duplicated projected segments; the F3 slab (top skin at the storey elevation) shows its projected outline exactly once in its home storey's plan.
- Thickness slabs produce one `Body`; golden files are unchanged.
- Satisfies the layered alternative of SLB-002, SLB-009 (geometry) and IFX-017 for slabs (geometry side).
notes: SRS: SLB-002 SLB-009 IFX-017 PRF-001. Appendix D.7 F3 values as in task 03. Slab skin order: skin 1 = top face.

title: Build the node junction engine for L, T, X and n-way wall nodes
description:
WHY: WAL-020 requires L, T and X junctions whose bodies are trimmed or extended. Today X crossings and three or more walls at one node are left square (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:14-16, 223-227), the through wall of a T is never cut, and every result is computed per wall end rather than per node. WAL-026 requires results independent of creation and edit order, and NFR-REL-005 asks for a safe fallback instead of corrupt geometry. This task builds the node engine at full wall thickness on the model's junction graph (02) and the polygon outlines (03) as a pure, unit-tested function; task 13 wires it into evaluation, skin-level priority resolution follows in 05 and the final ranking rule in 06.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs with `resolve(graph: &JunctionGraph, walls: &[WallOutline]) -> BTreeMap<ElementId, ResolvedWall>`: for each node of archicraft_model::junction::JunctionGraph build arms (an ending wall gives one arm, a through wall two arms forming a through pair, a collinear pair of ending walls a virtual through pair), sort them by angle, compute the corners between neighbouring arms, the node envelope E (through bands, ending arms extended to their corners, and the central polygon when three or more ending arms meet), and assign overlap regions with a provisional rank (through before ending; two ending arms split along the corner diagonal; three or more by sectors from the node point). Resolve each wall's outline from its start, end and body nodes inside bounded node zones; validate (validate_ring, coverage of E, closedness of the extruded prism) and fall back to square ends at that node with one problem per affected wall naming the node position (NFR-REL-005). The old wall.rs resolution stays in place and in use until task 13 switches the pipeline, so this task is reviewed and tested in isolation. Out of scope: wiring into ModelGeometry and incremental evaluation and deleting l_junction, t_junction, resolve_end and footprints (13), per-skin priorities (05), junction order and the documented rule (06), plan merging (07).
design: Per node: (1) arms with outward direction and exterior/interior face lines oriented for that arm (an End contact reverses the direction, so left and right faces swap); (2) corner c_i = intersection of arm i's left outer face with arm i+1's right outer face, computed in ElementId order for bit-identical points, or the face foot point for near-parallel neighbours; (3) E = union of through bands, ending-arm bands cut at their corner line and polygon(c_0..c_n-1) when three or more ending arms meet; (4) provisional assignment: through pairs first, two ending arms split by the line c_outer-c_inner (this reproduces today's mitre, wall.rs:138-163), three or more by sectors bounded by rays from the node point to the corners. Node zone: a square of half-size r = 10 x the largest arm thickness around the node; wall parts outside zones are plain bands; nodes of one wall closer than 2r are resolved together as one cluster. Booleans use geo's BooleanOps (union, difference, intersection; geo 0.33 brings i_overlay and plan.rs:156 already uses unary_union) in node-local coordinates (translated by the node point) so the integer grid inside i_overlay is fine and the same everywhere; afterwards snap result vertices within JOIN_TOLERANCE to the node's exact corner points and clean them with validate_ring (Appendix D.1 repair thresholds). Output per wall: `ResolvedWall { outline: MultiPolygon<f64>, problems }`, collected in a BTreeMap so iteration order is fixed. Pitfalls: i_overlay can return pinch vertices (two pieces touching at one point), which must be split into separate polygons before extrusion; pieces thinner than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH are slivers and are dropped; no HashMap iteration order may reach the output (sort by node point and ElementId).
acceptance_criteria:
- The wall.rs tests are re-expressed against junction::resolve and pass: free wall, L mitre with bit-identical shared corners, order independence, opposite directions, T stopping at the near face, walls without vertical overlap; a comparison test shows that footprints() and resolve() give identical outlines for every L and T case (removed with the old code in 13).
- X crossing of two 0.25 m walls: pieces are interior-disjoint and cover the union of both bands; the first-ranked wall is continuous and the other has two closed pieces; the total area equals the union area (WAL-020 X).
- Collinear continuation: equal walls end to end meet in one plane with no gap or overlap; a 0.25 m and a 0.365 m wall with exterior-face reference lines step at the node's perpendicular.
- A Y node (0, 120, 240 degrees) and a 4-way node of ending walls: E is fully covered, pieces are interior-disjoint (area of the union equals the sum of areas within 1e-9 m2) and every outline extrudes to a closed prism.
- A never-join wall at a node with two joined walls stays square while the other two still form their L; a Separated pair resolves as if the other wall were absent.
- Fallback: an L at 3 degrees (corner beyond 10 x thickness) and a node with an injected resolution failure keep square ends and add one problem per affected wall naming the node position; no panic, no invalid outline (NFR-REL-005).
- resolve() over the same graph with the walls slice shuffled gives identical results (WAL-026 at engine level).
- cargo test -p archicraft-geometry is green and the golden files are unchanged, because evaluation still uses footprints() until task 13.
notes: SRS: WAL-020 WAL-026. NFR-REL-005 and NFR-REL-006 govern the fallback; decision D-6. Appendix D.1: model tolerance 0.01 mm, repair thresholds 0.1 mm and 0.1 degrees. Technology choices: geo (i_overlay) for 2D Booleans; Manifold is not used in increment 1.

title: Add the opening kind with host-relative placement and Host edges
description:
WHY: The user needs an opening element that is independent of doors and windows: a stair hole, a shaft, a niche, a duct penetration.
