OPN-001 (M): 'an opening element that has exactly one host element, is positioned relative to that host, moves with it and is deleted with it. Hosts shall be walls, slabs and roofs.' OPN-003 (M): cross-sections 'rectangular, circular or an arbitrary polygon'. OPN-004 (M): 'oriented perpendicular to the host face or vertically'. OPN-005 (M): depth 'through (the full thickness of every cut element) or limited by start and end offsets from the host face'. OPN-006 (S): a vertical opening 'able to span a range of storeys (shaft)' that 'shall follow later changes of storey elevations'. None of this exists (gap-analysis OPN-001: ElementKind/KindTag are {Wall, Slab} only, crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:191-201; Element has no host field; Project has no host relation). element-kind-framework delivers the KindDescriptor registry and the relation store with a Host variant, layer-structures the skin thicknesses that 'through' and the face offsets refer to; this task adds the opening's data model on top of them and nothing else.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/opening.rs with `Opening { host: ElementId, section: Section, orientation: Orientation, placement: HostPlacement, depth: Depth }`: `Section::{Rectangle { width, height }, Circle { diameter }, Polygon { ring: Vec<DVec2> }}` stored relative to the anchor (bottom-centre for wall-face placements, centre for plan placements; polygon rings counter-clockwise); `Orientation::{Perpendicular, Vertical}`; `HostPlacement::{WallFace { along, elevation, face: Face::{Exterior, Interior} }, Plan { origin: DVec2, rotation: f64 }}` (WallFace = anchor distance from the host reference-line start and height above the host base, only for perpendicular openings in walls; Plan = storey plan coordinates, for vertical openings in any host and perpendicular openings in flat slabs); `Depth::{Through, Limited { start, end }, Storeys { bottom: StoreyOffset { storey, offset }, top: TopLink }}` (Limited offsets measured from the placement face: the chosen wall face, the slab top, or the wall top for vertical openings in walls; Storeys only with Vertical). HostPlacement is #[non_exhaustive] so that the roofs epic adds its roof-plane placement (named HostFace::RoofPlane in that plan) and members-profiles-adv its Member and Face placements without touching the cut paths. Registry row: label 'Opening', code 'opening', name prefix 'OP', default class IfcOpeningElement (added to IfcClass by element-kind-framework-05), a new `HostCapability` on KindDescriptor (walls: wall-face and plan placements; slabs: plan placements and shaft cuts; the roofs epic sets it for roofs (ROF-012), members-profiles-adv for OPN-012 hosts) and `hosted: true` on the opening descriptor so doors and windows reuse the flag. `Kind::host()` returns the host, and the relation store (crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs, element-kind-framework-08) derives `Relation::Host { hosted, host }` from it in the derived index next to StoreyLink: element-kind-framework-08 declares Host as an explicit, serialised variant, and this task moves it to the derived side, so the edge has one source of truth, undo stays exact with InsertElement/RemoveElement/ReplaceElement only, InsertRelation(Host) is rejected with 'Host relations follow the hosted element.' and the archicraft::relations codec never writes Host; dependents_of keeps Host in both directions. `Kind::storey_links()` (the framework hook, returning StoreyLinkRef) lists the bottom and top links of a Storeys depth so shafts are storey dependents and DeleteStorey reaches them through unlink_storey. Validator: the host exists and its descriptor accepts the placement, element.storey equals the host's storey, finite sizes not below MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, polygons through validate_ring, 0 <= start < end, a Storeys range ordered bottom to top that contains the host, a WallFace anchor inside the host length; messages as full sentences (ELM-017, NFR-REL-005). An 'opening' DefaultsSlot (KindDescriptor.template_defaults of element-kind-framework-04: the slot carries a prototype Opening payload, not a parallel OpeningDefaults struct) with the default section sizes, depth and sill, a placeholder host id that check_tool_defaults ignores, and the template layer 'Openings' (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs LAYERS); `Project::new_opening(host, placement, &DefaultsSlot)` takes the storey from the host and layer, class and payload defaults from the slot. The framework's `Kind::transform(&PlanTransform) -> Result<(), TransformError>` hook for openings (translate: WallFace slides along the reference line by the projected delta, Plan moves the origin; rotate and mirror: Plan placements are transformed, a WallFace opening transformed without its host returns TransformError::Unsupported) and a new `Kind::carry(&PlanTransform)` hook whose default calls transform (opening: WallFace unchanged, Plan transformed), both consumed by 02, an empty geometry generator and a placeholder IFCX codec entry so the workspace builds before 03 and 08. Out of scope: cascades (02), geometry (03-06), IFCX content (08, 09), UI (10-12), cutting further elements (OPN-002, solid-kernel-ops), roof hosts (roofs).
design: Follow the 'Add an element kind' extension point as rewritten by element-kind-framework: one module under crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/, one registry line, counters and defaults keyed by kind code. Store only host-relative or storey-plan data, never absolute elevations: WallFace (along, elevation) stays meaningful when the wall moves, rotates, is stretched or changes thickness, so 'positioned relative to that host' and 'moves with it' fall out of the representation; Plan placements are carried by the cascade of 02 because slab outlines have no intrinsic frame (reshaping a slab keeps its openings in place, transforming it carries them). Derive the Host edge from the kind data (the framework's derived index for storey links is the pattern) instead of serialising it in the archicraft::relations attribute of element-kind-framework-08, so the IFCX tree position (IFX-015) plus archicraft::opening.host are the only persisted forms. Face offsets come from ReferenceLine::face_offsets (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:99-107) and the layer-structures thickness; Storeys links reuse TopLink and Project::top_elevation (project.rs:236). Pitfalls: junction-engine-12's completeness test fails as soon as a kind with code 'opening' is registered while its 'openings at ends' row is Status::Pending { owner: "host-openings", requires_kind: "opening" }; if that suite has merged before this task, activate the row here with the L and T cases of 05 built through Project::new_opening and their (still uncut) skin outlines blessed, and 05 re-blesses them with the cut (reviewed diff); element.storey must always mirror the host's storey (02 enforces it in rehome and relink); keep the model crate free of geometry and UI dependencies (NFR-MNT-002/004); the placeholder codec must write nothing into goldens (no sample contains openings until 08); keep serde variant names stable.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/openings.rs: AddElements of a wall and then an opening, undo and redo keep the opening's id; relations().dependents_of(wall) contains the opening through a Host edge, and the edge disappears on undo (OPN-001 'exactly one host').
- Rejected with CommandError::Invalid and an unchanged project: missing host, host is another opening, host kind without HostCapability, storey different from the host's, WallFace placement on a slab, a perpendicular opening in a sloped slab (layer-structures-07), Storeys depth with Perpendicular, Limited with start >= end, a self-intersecting polygon, zero width or diameter.
- Hosts (OPN-001 'walls, slabs and roofs'): walls and slabs accept their placements; with the test-kinds Dummy given a HostCapability an opening is accepted on it, so roofs only set their capability in the roofs epic (ROF-012 re-asserts the roof clause there).
- InsertRelation(Host) is rejected; the framework's relation tests that used Host as their example run with Junction; a saved project writes no Host entry into archicraft::relations.
- Registry tests pass with the new kind (unique code and prefix, default class contained in the class set; module-layout test: 'opening' only in kinds/opening.rs plus one registry line in the model crate); next_element_name yields 'OP-001'.
- Transform hook tests: translating a WallFace opening on a wall along +X by (1.0, 1.0) increases along by 1.0 and keeps the elevation; a Plan opening's origin moves by the delta; carry() leaves WallFace unchanged and moves Plan.
- An opening with Depth::Storeys appears in storey_dependents of both linked storeys, and a SetStoreyElevation that would invert its range is rejected by the framework's storey validation (OPN-006 'follow later changes').
- A template test pins the documented opening DefaultsSlot (1.00 x 1.00 m rectangle, through, sill 0.90 m, layer 'Openings'); Project::new_opening on a wall uses the 'Openings' layer and the host's storey.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy and fmt are green and all golden files are unchanged; if junction-engine-12 has merged, its pending-row completeness test stays green (see design).
notes: SRS: OPN-001 OPN-003 OPN-004 OPN-005 OPN-006. Also ROF-012 (roof hosts through HostCapability, verified in roofs), ELM-017, NFR-REL-005. Appendix D.2 has no opening row: proposed defaults are a 1.00 x 1.00 m rectangle, circle diameter 0.30 m, through, perpendicular in walls and vertical in slabs, sill 0.90 m above the host base for wall-face placements; record them in template.rs and docs and raise an SRS question. Decision: Limited depth of a vertical opening in a wall is measured from the wall top. Perpendicular openings in sloped slabs are rejected with a message until the inclined-plane cut path of the roofs epic exists.

title: Rank walls at nodes by a documented rule and junction order (F6)
description:
WHY: WAL-026: junction results do not depend on the order in which walls were created or edited, and where three or more walls of equal priority meet a documented deterministic rule applies; WAL-036: a per-wall junction order overrides that rule. Fixture F6 has three walls meeting at one node with junction orders 8/8/8 versus 8/8/7. Today the only rule is the ElementId ordering of the two-wall mitre (wall.rs:121-125) and three or more walls are left square; the provisional rank of tasks 04 and 05 has no junction order, no height awareness and no written definition.

WHAT: Replace the provisional rank in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs by the final key: (1) effective skin priority, (2) junction order, (3) vertical coverage (arms whose extent contains all others come first, so an L between a 3.00 m and a 1.00 m wall shows no exposed mitre), (4) continuity (through pairs before ending arms), (5) remaining ties between ending arms split by mitre or sectors, (6) remaining ties between through pairs by thickness, canonical direction angle in [0, 180) degrees and ElementId. Write docs/junctions.md with this rule, the join-group and Separated semantics, the fallback, the F6 and F7 definitions, the JoinGroup-on-Element deviation and the known limitation for partial vertical overlap. Register `fixtures::f6_three_wall_node(orders: [u8; 3])` in crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (D.7 F6 entry) and add exhaustive creation-order and edit-order tests. Out of scope: the junction order field in the UI (11) and stepped bodies for partial vertical overlap (cleanup-and-trims, with the Boolean kernel).
design: Implement the key as a `RankKey` struct with derived Ord so the order is explicit and testable, computed once per (arm, skin). Junction order: lower numbers resolve first and run through, so 8/8/7 singles out the order-7 wall; verify this direction against KB 303922 before closing and state it in docs/junctions.md. Vertical coverage uses the absolute extents carried by the junction graph; partial overlaps (neither extent contains the other) fall through to the next key, documented as a limitation because a single prism per skin cannot show a mitre in one height band and a butt joint in another. Exhaustive tests build scenes through the seeded fixture builder, permute insertion into Project.elements (IndexMap) with a small in-test permutation helper (no new dependency), and compare ModelGeometry part meshes bit for bit after sorting parts by name; regenerated ids are only used where no symmetric tie reaches step 6, because ElementId is the last key. Keep the helpers in a tests/common module so task 12 reuses them.
acceptance_criteria:
- F6 8/8/8: three 0.25 m masonry walls with centre reference lines ending at one node at 0, 90 and 180 degrees: the collinear pair runs through and the 90-degree wall butts against it (golden outlines).
- F6 8/8/7 (order 7 on the 90-degree wall): that wall runs through to the far face of the collinear pair, which butts against it; the golden outlines differ from 8/8/8 as documented (WAL-036).
- A Y node 8/8/8 resolves by symmetric sectors; with 8/8/7 the order-7 wall takes the central region.
- Junction order also decides ties at an L (8/7 gives a butt joint, 8/8 the mitre) and at a T (an order-7 branch cuts the through wall).
- An L between a 3.00 m and a 1.00 m wall gives the taller wall the full corner; both bodies are closed.
- Exhaustive order independence (the epic's property test, run over every permutation): all 6 creation orders of F6 and all 24 of a 4-wall node (same ids, shuffled insertion), and all orders with regenerated ids for the asymmetric scenes, give bit-identical meshes per wall (WAL-026).
- Edit-order independence: two edit sequences that reach the same final walls in different orders (move A then B versus B then A; a thickness change before versus after a junction-order change) give bit-identical meshes per wall (WAL-026 'or edited').
- docs/junctions.md states each rule step exactly as implemented, and one named test per step pins it to a case.
notes: SRS: WAL-026 WAL-036. Appendix D.7 F6: three walls at one node with junction orders 8/8/8 versus 8/8/7 (KB 303922); D.2: wall default 0.25 m masonry. Open question to settle in docs/junctions.md before closing: whether lower or higher junction order wins in the reference product (default here: lower resolves first).

title: Add JoinWalls and UnjoinWalls commands
description:
WHY: WAL-022: a join command shall extend or trim two selected walls or beams until their reference lines meet, and an unjoin command shall separate them. Nothing exists today (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:36-92, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs:7-39), and because joins are implicit from reference-line contact (D-6), unjoin needs the explicit Separated junction relation added in task 02.

WHAT: Add `Command::JoinWalls { a, b }` and `Command::UnjoinWalls { a, b }` with the labels "Join walls" and "Unjoin walls" and their planners in crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs, plus the shared helper `junction::meeting(a, b)` in crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs that classifies the pair: L - move the nearer end of each wall to the intersection of the infinite reference lines; T - the intersection lies inside one segment, so only the other wall's end moves; collinear with a gap - both ends meet at the gap midpoint; already crossing or touching - nothing to move; parallel - invalid. Join emits ReplaceElement edits and a RemoveRelation of the pair's Separated relation; Unjoin emits an InsertRelation (the relation edits of element-kind-framework-08) when the pair currently forms a node. The planners read and write positions only through two new hooks on trait Kind (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs, element-kind-framework-02), `reference_axis(&self) -> Option<[DVec2; 2]>` and `set_reference_axis(&mut self, [DVec2; 2]) -> bool` (defaults None and false), implemented by Wall, so beams join through the same commands as soon as profiles-columns-beams implements the hook and cleanup-and-trims resolves their geometry (the beam half of WAL-022, tracked there as a follow-up bead). Out of scope: menu items and shortcuts (11), auto-join (10).
design: Follow the 'Add a command' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md: variant, label() arm (command.rs:112), plan() arm (command.rs:148) built from Edit::ReplaceElement and the relation edits of element-kind-framework, tests in tests/commands.rs. meeting(): intersect the infinite reference lines in ElementId order for bit-identical points; pick the end to move by its distance to the meeting point; send every moved wall through validate_element (validate.rs:243) so ELM-017 messages and minimum lengths apply. Unjoin confirms contact with junction::detect_around(project, [a, b]). Both commands check locks through Project::edit_lock_reason. Pitfalls: a trapezoidal wall keeps its straight face when an end moves (end thickness belongs to the end, not to a position); a join that moves an end away from other walls it touched breaks those contacts, which is acceptable and visible in the result.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: joining two walls with a 0.40 m gap at a corner moves both nearer ends to the reference-line intersection; the geometry shows the L mitre; undo restores both walls exactly and redo reapplies (WAL-022 'extend').
- Two walls overshooting each other at a corner are trimmed to the meeting point (WAL-022 'trim').
- T join: only the branch end moves onto the through wall's reference line; the geometry shows the T.
- Walls already crossing or already joined give CommandError::NoChange; parallel non-collinear walls give Invalid("Parallel walls cannot be joined."); collinear walls with a gap meet at the gap midpoint.
- Different join groups or NEVER give Invalid naming the join groups; a locked wall gives Locked; a trim that would leave less than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH or reverse a wall gives Invalid.
- Join removes the Separated relation of the pair, and undo restores it.
- Unjoin of an L adds the Separated relation: both ends become square, bodies stay closed, the plan shows two regions (task 07); undo restores the mitre. Unjoin of walls that do not touch gives NoChange; unjoining one pair at a 3-wall node leaves the other pairs joined.
- A test-kinds Dummy (no reference axis) paired with a wall gives Invalid("Only walls and beams can be joined."), and a source scan finds no ElementKind::Wall match in the join planners, so the 'or beams' clause of WAL-022 needs only the hook.
- History replay of the applied commands reproduces the same project.
notes: SRS: WAL-022. Decision D-6. Beams (BEA-004) use the same commands in cleanup-and-trims. Open question: whether unjoin should also pull the walls apart; this task keeps positions and suppresses the cleanup, which is reversible and separates the junction as WAL-022 asks.

title: Cascade delete, move, storey and reference-line edits to hosted elements
description:
WHY: ELM-016 (M): 'Deleting a host shall delete its hosted elements, and copying a host shall copy its hosted elements. Both are undoable.' This task covers the delete clause; the copy clause is 13. OPN-001 (M): the opening 'is positioned relative to that host, moves with it and is deleted with it'. WAL-005 (M, owned by layer-structures): MoveWallReferenceLine moves the reference line 'without moving the wall body or its hosted elements', and layer-structures-06 left the hook plan_hosted_followups(project, wall_before, wall_after) -> Vec<Edit> (empty while no hosted kind exists) for this epic to fill, also for FlipWalls (WAL-006). Doors and windows (DW-001) reuse the same cascade. Today DeleteElements (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:344-360) and MoveElements (command.rs:153-166) touch only the listed ids (gap-analysis ELM-016: 'no cascade on delete, no cascade on copy'), and element-kind-framework left the cascade as a documented hook in plan_delete_elements.

WHAT: command.rs: `hosted_closure(project, ids)` from the relation store's Host dependents in deterministic order (listed order, then hosted elements by ElementId). plan_delete_elements expands the ids by the closure (a locked hosted element blocks with CommandError::Locked naming it, consistent with ELM-013) and the framework's RemoveElement handling drops the derived edges, so undo restores host, hosted elements and edges at their original indices. MoveElements (planned through the framework's Kind::transform hook) carries the hosted elements of moved hosts with Kind::carry (WallFace unchanged, Plan translated) and moves hosted elements listed alone with Kind::transform (sliding along the wall), never twice when both are listed. plan_hosted_followups (layer-structures-06) re-anchors WallFace placements so the world anchor and the void stay where they are: MoveWallReferenceLine shifts `along` by the start's displacement along the axis (junction restoration can move ends along it); FlipWalls sets along' = length - along and mirrors polygon sections in x, with keep_body = true also swapping the Face label so the opening keeps its physical face and keep_body = false keeping the label so the opening mirrors with the body; Plan placements need no follow-up. rehome and relink_to_storey (command.rs:399-433) and DeleteStorey (435-480) take hosted elements along with their host (the storey mirrors the host), and a shaft linked to a deleted storey is unlinked to a fixed offset through the framework's unlink_storey hook, as walls are (command.rs:457-468). Deleting an opening alone restores the host because the cut is derived from live hosted elements; nothing is stored on the host. Out of scope: copy (13), rotate, mirror and vertical-move cascades of user transforms (selection-transforms calls Kind::carry through the transform hook; document the contract in kinds/mod.rs), geometry.
design: One closure function used by every planner keeps the rule in one place; deterministic ordering matters for journal replay and for the framework's incremental-versus-full property test. Use the existing Edit primitives (InsertElement, RemoveElement, ReplaceElement): Host edges are derived (01), so no relation edits are needed. The re-anchoring is a pure function of (wall_before, wall_after, opening) so that later wall reshapes can call it too. Pitfalls: MoveElements must re-check that a slid WallFace anchor stays inside the host length and reject with a message instead of clamping silently; keep the relink semantics of command.rs:419-433 for wall tops and apply the same to shaft Storeys links; FlipWalls keep_body = false also mirrors the skins, so a Limited depth measured from the exterior face keeps measuring from the (now mirrored) exterior face.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/hosting.rs delete_host_deletes_hosted_and_undo_restores: a wall with two openings; DeleteElements([wall]) removes three elements and both Host edges; undo restores a project equal to the start (revision normalised) including element order; redo removes them again (ELM-016 delete clause, undoable; OPN-001 'deleted with it').
- A locked opening makes DeleteElements([host]) fail with CommandError::Locked naming the opening; the project is unchanged.
- move_host_carries_openings: MoveElements([wall], d) leaves the WallFace placement unchanged and moves the opening's resolved world anchor by d; a slab's Plan opening moves by d; listing host and opening together moves the opening once; moving the opening alone slides it along the wall and is rejected with a message when the anchor would leave the host length (OPN-001 'moves with it').
- reference_line_moves_keep_openings: MoveWallReferenceLine to Center, Inside and Custom on an F2 wall with a WallFace opening, including an L corner whose junction restoration moves the start, keeps the opening's world anchor within 1e-9 m (WAL-005 'or its hosted elements').
- flip_keeps_openings: FlipWalls keep_body = true keeps the opening's world anchor and physical face (Face label swapped, polygon section mirrored); keep_body = false mirrors the opening with the body; flipping twice restores the opening exactly; undo restores both.
- Relinking a wall to another storey and DeleteStorey with MoveTo move its openings' storey; DeleteStorey with Delete removes them; deleting a storey a shaft is linked to keeps the shaft valid with a fixed offset.
- Seeded property test (200 random sequences of add, move, delete, MoveWallReferenceLine, FlipWalls, undo and redo over two_storey_shell with openings): after every step Project::integrity_problems() is empty, so no orphaned hosted element can arise in a session (13 adds copy to the generator).
notes: SRS: ELM-016 OPN-001. Also WAL-005 and WAL-006 (hosted clause of the layer-structures-06 hook), ELM-013. Open question: whether a locked hosted element should block deleting its host (chosen: yes, with a message) or be deleted anyway.

title: Expose auto-join, join/unjoin and junction properties in the UI
description:
WHY: Users need controls for the new behaviour: the auto-join option of WAL-021, on by default; the join and unjoin commands of WAL-022 on two selected walls; the join group of WAL-025 and the junction order of WAL-036; the start and end thickness of a trapezoidal wall (WAL-008); and the per-skin priority override of WAL-024 in the layer-structure editor. None of these has a control today (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs, ui/actions.rs, ui/properties.rs, ui/dialogs.rs).

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-app add `Preferences.auto_join` (default true, prefs.rs) with a row in the preferences dialog and a checkable "Auto-join walls" item in the Design menu (Action::ToggleAutoJoin); make the wall tool wrap the commands of ToolState::add_point/complete (tools.rs:451-517) in Command::WithAutoJoin with the snap radius converted to model units and typed ends listed as fixed (through the PointInput service if point-input-snapping has landed); add Action::JoinWalls and Action::UnjoinWalls with menu items and shortcuts, enabled for exactly two editable walls; add properties strip and settings dialog fields Join group (Never join, 1-99, for every construction element), Junction order (1-16) and End thickness (single-material walls only, with the thickness row relabelled Start thickness); add a per-skin Priority column with an override to the layer-structure editor (`layer_structures_window` in ui/dialogs.rs, layer-structures-11); if the move, rotate or mirror tools of selection-transforms or the stretch and reshape tools of edit-reshape-palette exist when this task lands, wrap their wall-changing commands in Command::WithAutoJoin too (WAL-021 'edited'), otherwise task done files beads for those epics, which do not depend on junction-engine. Out of scope: building the move, stretch and reshape tools (selection-transforms, edit-reshape-palette) and plan rendering (plan-renderer).
design: Follow the extension-point recipes 'Add a preference' and 'Add a command' (UI part) and the Fields pattern of properties.rs (a getter returning None hides a row). Proposed shortcuts: Cmd+J (join) and Cmd+Shift+J (unjoin); check that they are free in actions.rs. Tolerance = prefs.snap_radius divided by the plan camera's pixels per metre - the same value the snapping in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:466-490 uses - so auto-join and snapping agree on 'within snap tolerance'. The status line shows NoChange and Invalid messages through Workspace::execute (workspace.rs:123). The join group choice lists 'Never join' first, then 1..99; junction order is an integer field. Pitfalls: single-key shortcuts are skipped while typing (app.rs shortcut handling); extend the layer-structure editor where layer-structures placed it (ui/dialogs.rs) rather than adding a second editor.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs (egui_kittest): the Design menu shows "Auto-join walls" checked by default; clicking it clears prefs.auto_join, and the prefs round-trip test keeps the value (WAL-021 'on by default').
- tools.rs unit test: with auto-join on, a wall whose second point lies 3 px short of an existing reference line at the current scale is created joined; with auto-join off its end stays where it was placed; a typed length is kept.
- Selecting two walls enables "Join walls" and "Unjoin walls"; invoking them executes the commands and the Edit menu shows "Undo Join walls"; with one or three walls selected both items are disabled with a tooltip giving the reason (WAL-022).
- Properties: Join group, Junction order and End thickness rows appear for a selected single-material wall, End thickness is hidden for a layered wall, differing values show "Mixed", and edits issue UpdateElements visible in ws.doc.project (WAL-025, WAL-036, WAL-008).
- Layer-structure editor: the Priority column shows the material priority; entering an override issues the structure update and clearing it restores the material value (WAL-024).
- If selection-transforms has landed: moving a wall with its move tool so that its end comes within the snap radius of another reference line joins the two, and with auto-join off it does not; otherwise the bead for that wiring is filed (checked in task done).
- The actions.rs tests shortcuts_are_unique and appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts pass.
notes: SRS: WAL-021 WAL-022 WAL-025 WAL-036 WAL-008 WAL-024. Appendix D.1: snap radius 8 px; D.8 lists the required default shortcuts (join and unjoin are not among them, so their keys are free choices). UI-003 (settings dialog reuses the properties fields) applies.

title: Add layered extrusion with interface face cancellation
description:
WHY: technology-choices.md: 'Openings are cut as 2D polygons, in plan or in the wall's own plane, before extruding', and the Boolean kernel (Manifold) arrives 'at the latest in SRS increment 2' with solid-kernel-ops, so increment-1 openings need a construction that uses 2D Booleans only. OPN-005 (M) needs a niche with a back face ('a limited opening from 0 to 0.40 m in a 0.50 m wall leaves a 0.10 m thick back'), slabs need recesses with a floor and notches, and openings crossing skin boundaries need exact layer splits. IFX-032 (M) demands closed, 2-manifold, consistently oriented meshes without degenerate or duplicate triangles; IFX-038 per-face vertices; NFR-REL-005 rejects invalid results instead of producing corrupt ones. Today extrude() (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18) extrudes one outline with holes vertically and nothing else (gap-analysis OPN-005). Kept and regressed: IFX-032 is done (TriMesh::check_closed, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:122) and IFX-038's per-face vertices come from TriMesh::add_face (mesh.rs:83); the new path reuses both instead of a second mesh builder.

WHAT: extrude.rs gains `extrude_layers(frame: &DAffine3, layers: &[Layer]) -> Result<TriMesh, GeometryError>` with `Layer { section: geo::MultiPolygon<f64>, t0, t1 }`: a stack of prisms along the frame's local z axis whose consecutive layers share their interface plane. Each layer contributes the side faces of its rings swept over [t0, t1]; the first layer's bottom and the last layer's top are full faces; at an interface the exposed faces are upper.difference(lower) facing down and lower.difference(upper) facing up (geo BooleanOps on i_overlay, already a dependency); an empty section is a gap that separates shells. All coordinates of one call are snapped to a MODEL_TOLERANCE grid (the tolerance module of element-kind-framework-01; today crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:10) before the Booleans, every result ring passes validate_ring, side-face edges are split at every interface vertex lying on them so that no T-junction remains, faces are triangulated with triangulate.rs and get their own vertices. extrude() becomes the one-layer case with unchanged output. Out of scope: wall and slab integration (05, 06), different axes per layer, curved faces.
design: Algorithm: (1) snap and normalise all sections (outer rings counter-clockwise, holes clockwise, canonical start vertex); (2) per interface compute both differences once and keep their rings; (3) collect per interface plane the vertices of the lower section, the upper section and both differences; (4) emit each layer's side faces per ring edge as planar polygons whose top and bottom edges contain every collected vertex lying on them, sorted along the edge, and triangulate them; (5) emit cap and interface faces with triangulate.rs (spade CDT with holes); (6) transform by the frame and append with per-face vertices (IFX-038). Use geo 0.33's BooleanOps (plan.rs:156 already uses geo::unary_union) and keep i_overlay behind geo as technology-choices asks. Pitfalls: i_overlay returns rings with collinear points and arbitrary start vertices, so normalise before comparing; slivers from near-coincident edges must be removed by the snap, not by a later area filter; long walls with many openings approach MAX_MESH_POINTS (IFX-038 splitting is a later concern, report it).
acceptance_criteria:
- extrude() output is bit-identical before and after (existing extrude tests and crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs unchanged).
- Unit tests: a niche stack [E minus P over 0.00-0.40, E over 0.40-0.50] is closed with volume 0.50 area(E) - 0.40 area(P) and a back face equal to P; a stack where every layer is E minus P gives a through hole; a section touching the boundary of E gives a notch; [E, E minus P, E] gives an enclosed cavity (two shells, closed).
- Coincident edges within MODEL_TOLERANCE are snapped; a layer thinner than MODEL_TOLERANCE is rejected with GeometryError::InvalidExtent; invalid rings are rejected, never emitted.
- Seeded property test (xorshift, 500 cases): random rectangular, rectilinear and tessellated circular sections in stacks of 1-5 layers give check_closed Ok, no degenerate triangles, and a signed volume equal to sum(area(layer) x thickness) within 1e-9 relative.
- Repeated calls with the same input give bit-identical meshes, as the framework's incremental-versus-full property test requires.
notes: SRS: OPN-005. Also IFX-032, IFX-038, NFR-REL-005. Reused by 05 (walls, layers along the face normal), 06 (slabs, layers along z) and doors-windows-core (insert voids).

title: Write openings as hosted children with an invisible Void
description:
WHY: Other IFC5 tools must see openings as semantic objects inside their hosts. IFX-015 (M): 'Hosted elements (doors, windows, openings) shall be children of their host element'; IFX-012 (M): hosted elements are contained through their host, not the storey; Table 5-1: an opening is IfcOpeningElement with the host element as parent and a Void child; IFX-036 (M): a closed Void mesh marked usd::usdgeom::visibility 'invisible', a child of the occurrence, with the host body already cut (IFX-033); IFX-031 placements relative to the parent; IFX-010 v5 ids for regenerated sub-nodes; IFX-061 every archicraft:: attribute declared; IFX-006 conformance and viewer display. Gap-analysis IFX-015 and IFX-036: missing (no host nesting, no per-element transform, no Void, no visibility attribute).

Done and reused, not re-implemented: IFX-010 (sub_node_id, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:46), IFX-014 (child_key, writer.rs:56), IFX-031 for storeys (translation, writer.rs:237, generalised here into a full 4x4 transform helper), IFX-005 and IFX-061 (check_attributes, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:239, and the in-file declarations); IFX-012 and IFX-006 are partial and gain the hosted clause.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/opening.rs: an OpeningCodec implementing element-kind-framework-06's KindCodec (ATTRIBUTE archicraft::opening; schema() with host, section {kind, width, height, diameter, points}, orientation, placement {kind, along, elevation, face, origin, rotation}, depth {kind, start, end, bottom {storey, offset}, top as the existing top-link schema}; write, read and the slot functions for the opening DefaultsSlot) registered with one line in codecs!, replacing the placeholder of 01; the kind enumeration, toolDefaults and counters follow from CODECS as the framework builds them; a FORMAT_VERSION bump with a no-op entry in the framework's migration table ('adds opening elements'), per the framework's bump rule. writer.rs: the storey loop (writer.rs:300-308) lists only non-hosted elements; write_element (361-406) writes the element's hosted children through the framework's contained_children hook, keyed child_key('Opening', uuid) (IFX-014); an opening node carries bsi::ifc::class IfcOpeningElement with its bSDD uri, bsi::ifc::prop::Name, usd::xformop with the opening-local transform relative to the host node (row-major, translation in the fourth row, positive determinant), archicraft::element and archicraft::opening, and a child 'Void' with id sub_node_id(opening, 'Void'), a usd::usdgeom::mesh in opening-local coordinates rounded by round_coordinate and the invisible visibility attribute (declared in the bundled usd@v1.ifcx), without material. The host's Body and Skin parts are the cut bodies of 05 and 06. samples.rs: `openings_showcase()` built through commands (a 0.50 m wall with the niche, the F2 wall with a 1.0 x 1.0 m through opening, a circular perpendicular opening, a polygonal vertical slab opening at an edge, a shaft over storeys -1 to +2), registered in examples/reference_models.rs and in samples() of tests/roundtrip.rs, with the golden openings-showcase.ifcx blessed. conformance/check.ts checkViewerTree (the compose3 tree of the reference viewer, check.ts:67-103, which is the viewer check of the epic acceptance) recurses into hosted children and, per IfcOpeningElement, asserts a parent of class IfcWall, IfcSlab or IfcRoof, exactly one Void child with visibility invisible and a valid closed triangle list of at most 65,535 points, and no colour requirement on the Void. Out of scope: reading (09), doors and windows (doors-windows-core), type nodes (IFX-050).
design: Follow the extension points 'Add an IFCX attribute' and 'Add a sample/golden model' in docs/implementation-status.md and the per-kind codec registration of element-kind-framework, so the opening codec lives in one place. The opening transform maps opening-local to storey coordinates because the host node carries no transform (walls and slabs are written in storey coordinates; writer.rs translation(z) sits on the storey); the Void mesh is the VoidPrism of 03 in opening-local coordinates, so file and model share one definition (SRS Appendix C, item 5). Parameters are written at full precision, mesh coordinates through round_coordinate. Pitfalls: child keys must be unique per parent (child_key, writer.rs:56); the conformance element loop (check.ts:82-100) would demand a body and a colour if openings were treated as storey elements, so recurse explicitly; the writer does not check MAX_MESH_POINTS today (technical debt), so assert it for the showcase in the test; regenerate goldens with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx --test roundtrip and review the diff.
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs: each opening's Void is a direct child of the opening occurrence node and no type node carries a Void (IFX-036 'child of the occurrence, not of its type'); the_srs_appendix_c_example_validates still passes.
- roundtrip.rs: no opening is a storey child; each is a child of its host under 'Opening_<first 8 hex digits>'; the Void path equals Uuid::new_v5(opening, 'Void') and is stable across saves; saving twice is byte-identical apart from timestamp and dataVersion (IFX-007, IFX-010, IFX-014, IFX-015).
- Every Void point composed with the opening and storey transforms lies within 0.1 mm of the evaluated void in world coordinates, and every written transform has a positive determinant (IFX-031).
- written_meshes_are_closed_bodies covers Void children and cut host parts; every Void carries visibility invisible; the niche wall's written Body volume equals the evaluated cut volume (IFX-033, IFX-036).
- The offline validator (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs) accepts the file with archicraft::opening declared (IFX-005, IFX-061).
- The removed host volume (uncut minus cut body) equals the volume of the void prism clipped to the host for every showcase opening, and the Void mesh contains that region (IFX-036 'encloses the removed volume').
- golden_files_are_reproduced passes with openings-showcase.ifcx and the existing goldens differ only in the format version (reviewed diff); conformance/run.sh is green on all goldens with the extended check.ts, and a negative control (a Void without visibility) fails it; the viewer tree of checkViewerTree shows every opening under its host, and regression-and-status's headless viewer step, where it exists, shows the same (IFX-006).
- IFX-015 and IFX-036 satisfied for openings; the IFX-012 hosted clause is in place.
notes: SRS: IFX-015 IFX-036. Also IFX-012, IFX-031, IFX-033, IFX-010, IFX-061, IFX-006 (re-asserted). doors-windows-core-05 adds IfcDoor and IfcWindow on the same hosted-children path.

title: Build the layer structure editor dialog
description:
WHY: PRF-001 (M): users need named layer structures with ordered skins, materials, thicknesses and roles, at least 48 skins; PRF-002 (M): editing a structure updates every element that uses it, which the user should see immediately. SRS 3.4 resources are edited in project-level dialogs like the Materials dialog. Gap row PRF-001 lists the editor dialog as missing.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs: a `layer_structures_window` opened by a new `Action::LayerStructures` ('Layer structures...', Project menu in shell.rs), modelled on materials_window (dialogs.rs:376-477) and material_editor (dialogs.rs:765-846): a list with name, total thickness and number of users (Project::layer_structure_users); New (one core skin of 0.20 m reinforced concrete), Duplicate, Rename and Delete (an egui::Modal asking for a replacement when the structure is used, DeleteLayerStructure); a skin table with index, material combo, thickness (widgets::length, unit-aware), role combo, move up/down, insert above/below and remove (disabled when it would leave no skin or no core); the total thickness and the core span; a cross-section preview strip painted in the material colours with 'Exterior / Top' and 'Interior / Bottom' labels. Every edit commits one UpdateLayerStructure; a rejected edit shows the validation message inline and leaves the model unchanged. Out of scope: the per-skin priority column (junction-engine), assigning structures to elements (12), skin separator and layered plan display options (plan-renderer).
design: Follow the 'Add a dialog' recipe (docs/implementation-status.md, Extension points) and the existing widgets (ui/widgets.rs length/choice/text). Commit per field like material_editor does, so each change is one undo step and the 3D/plan views update live through the geometry cache. Material combos list project materials by name; show the D.4 priority next to the name as a hint for later junction work. If properties-and-dialogs has landed, use its resizable-dialog and size-persistence helpers; otherwise a plain egui::Window. Strings go through the commands-and-l10n mechanism if it exists. Pitfall: the user-count column must not scan all elements per frame for every row on large models (technical debt already noted for layers at dialogs.rs:327); compute counts once per project revision.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: Project menu -> 'Layer structures...' opens the window; 'New' adds a structure to the list; 'Add skin' adds a row; typing 0 as a skin thickness shows the error text and leaves the project unchanged; Delete on a used structure opens the replacement modal.
- kittest: with a structure used by two walls, changing a skin thickness in the dialog bumps the project revision and both walls' evaluated volumes change in the next frame; Edit > Undo restores the previous structure and volumes (PRF-002 visible to the user).
- Skins can be added up to 64 (48 verified in a test); at 64 the add buttons are disabled with a tooltip.
- Removing the last core skin is disabled with an explanatory tooltip.
- Satisfies the user-facing parts of PRF-001 and PRF-002.
notes: SRS: PRF-001 PRF-002. Appendix D.4 priorities shown as hints only.

title: Register wall core faces as snap targets
description:
WHY: PRF-003 (M): core faces shall be available as reference positions for snapping (as well as for wall reference lines, reveals and slab reference planes); SLB-001 lists wall core faces among the edges slab outlines snap to, and fixture F8 later traces a slab from a core face. Gap row PRF-003: SnapTargets collects wall reference lines and plan outlines only (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:157-188).

WHAT: SnapTargets::from_plan (views/tools.rs:164) adds PlanElement::core_faces (task 04) of walls on visible layers as edge targets and their end points as node targets, independent of whether the wall is cut, projected or overhead in the current view; if point-input-snapping has replaced SnapTargets by its target provider, register them there as edge targets labelled 'Core face' for the snap feedback. Out of scope: DW-008 reveals (doors-windows-core reads ReferenceLine::distance_from_exterior and the CrossSection), contour detection (edit-reshape-palette), arc walls (curved-geometry).
design: Cut skin polygons already expose skin edges as snap edges when a wall is cut, but projected walls, merged regions and later junction resolution make that incidental; the explicit core_faces list makes the target independent of plan classification and lets the snap feedback name it. Keep precedence unchanged (edges below nodes and intersections, INP-009) and deduplicate segments that coincide with cut-polygon edges using MODEL_TOLERANCE from crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs. The slab tool test reuses the F2 ring of task 09. This touches the same file the point-input-snapping epic refactors; keep the change to one function and one test so it rebases trivially.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools.rs unit test: an F2 wall from (0, 0) to (5, 0) with an Outside reference line; a cursor at (2.5, 0.372) within the snap radius snaps onto the core exterior face at (2.5, 0.370) as an edge snap, and a cursor near (5.0, 0.670) snaps to the core interior face end node.
- The same holds for a wall entirely below the cut plane (projected), and a layered wall on a hidden layer contributes no core-face targets.
- Slab tool test: a rectangle whose corners snap to the intersections of the core interior faces of the F2 ring produces a slab outline that coincides with those faces within the model tolerance.
- Satisfies the snapping clause of PRF-003.
notes: SRS: PRF-003. Merge-order note: if point-input-snapping lands first, implement against its target provider instead of SnapTargets::from_plan.

title: Bind walls and slabs to a thickness or a layer structure
description:
WHY: WAL-003 (M), first bullet: a wall shall have a thickness, a layer structure or a profile. SLB-002 (M): a slab shall have a thickness or a layer structure, and a reference plane (top or bottom of the slab) at an offset from the home storey, by default the top of the slab at the storey elevation. WAL-004 (M): changing a wall's thickness or structure shall keep its reference line in place and move the faces. PRF-002 (M): editing a layer structure shall update every element that uses it. Gap rows: WAL-003 partial (single material only, crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:130-139); SLB-002 partial (the layer-structure alternative is missing, Slab has one thickness and one MaterialId, element.rs:178-188); WAL-004 partial (structure clause cannot be exercised, no explicit test); PRF-002 missing (needs UpdateLayerStructure plus propagation). Exists and is kept (regress, do not re-implement): base_offset and TopLink Fixed/Storey/Relative (element.rs:71-79, project.rs:236-242), the exterior-on-the-right direction rule (element.rs:81-85), face_offsets-derived faces so thickness edits keep the reference line (element.rs:99-107, properties.rs:254-266), SlabReference Top/Bottom with offset and the D.2 default top at storey elevation (template.rs:335-343), their properties fields (properties.rs:254-463) and IFCX codecs, and validation (validate.rs:199-226).

WHAT: In the wall and slab kind modules (kinds/wall.rs and kinds/slab.rs after element-kind-framework, element.rs today) replace `thickness` and `material` by `structure: Structure` with `enum Structure { Thickness { thickness: f64, material: MaterialId }, Layered(LayerStructureId) }` and add the resolved `CrossSection { total: f64, core: (f64, f64), skins: Vec<SectionSkin { material, thickness, role }> }` returned by `Project::cross_section(&Structure)`; a Thickness structure resolves to one Core skin, so its core faces coincide with its faces. `ReferenceLine::face_offsets` takes `&CrossSection`. `Project::vertical_extent` uses the section total for slabs. Replace the material/set_material hooks of the Kind trait (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs after element-kind-framework-02; ElementKind::material()/set_material() at element.rs:243-257 today) by `referenced_materials()`/`replace_material(from, to)` plus `structure()/structure_mut()` (default None, so the dummy and later kinds without a structure are unaffected), add `Project::element_materials(&Element)` and `Project::layer_structure_users(id)`, and update every caller: integrity_problems, validate_element (a Layered reference must exist), plan_delete_material (Thickness users), DeleteLayerStructure (now rewrites user elements and the wall/slab DefaultsSlot prototypes of element-kind-framework-04 to the replacement; a replacement is required while users exist), check_tool_defaults (validates the slot prototypes through validate_element, so a dangling Layered reference in a slot is caught), rehome/relink_to_storey, the Kind::vertical_extent hook (it takes (home, &StoreyList) after element-kind-framework-02 and gains the resolved CrossSection as an argument, so the slab kind never reaches into Project), Project::new_wall/new_slab, template.rs (Thickness 0.25 m Brick and 0.20 m reinforced concrete, D.2 unchanged) and samples.rs. Compile-preserving adaptions in the other crates: archicraft-geometry WallInput carries the CrossSection and the wall and slab GeometryKind generators (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs and slab.rs after element-kind-framework-07, evaluate.rs:150-188 today) still extrude one Body from the envelope (per-skin bodies are task 04); the archicraft-ifcx wall and slab codecs (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/wall.rs and slab.rs after element-kind-framework-06) write thickness = section total and material = the Thickness material or the core skin's material, and a Layered element adds a writer warning 'layer structure not saved yet' until task 08; archicraft-app properties.rs edits the thickness and material of Thickness structures and shows the total read-only for Layered ones. Extend the dirty-set derivation of the framework's incremental evaluation so Insert/Replace/RemoveLayerStructure edits mark every user element, and add layer-structure edits to the incremental-versus-full property test; the plan caches of element-kind-framework-11 (Document::geometry) invalidate the home storeys of those users (or fully, like material edits). Out of scope: core reference positions (03), per-skin geometry (04, 05), IFCX persistence (08), UI (11, 12), the profile alternative of WAL-003 (PRF-010, members-profiles-adv).
design: Data model: `Structure` is a closed enum now; the epic owning PRF-010 adds `Profile(ProfileId)` later, so match it exhaustively in one place per crate (helper methods on Structure/CrossSection) to keep that change small. Provide `Structure::thickness(t, material)` for tests and samples. The CrossSection is resolved per evaluation from the project, never cached on the element, so a structure edit cannot leave stale thickness data (PRF-002). Propagation: today the whole model is re-evaluated per revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103), so it works automatically; after element-kind-framework the incremental evaluator only re-evaluates the dirty set, which is why resource edits must contribute their users (pitfall: forgetting this makes PRF-002 fail silently, the property test is the guard). Validation of a Layered element only checks the reference; the structure itself is validated by its own commands (task 01). Pointers (today; after element-kind-framework the same code lives in the kinds/ modules, the DefaultsSlot map and the alpha/kinds codecs): element.rs:130-188 and 243-257, project.rs:120-150 and 245-323, validate.rs:199-290, command.rs:399-470 and 520-600, evaluate.rs:98-120 and 150-189, writer.rs:94-117 and 192-217, reader.rs:592-713, properties.rs:83-112 and 253-266, document.rs:97-103.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: with one structure used by two walls and a slab, UpdateLayerStructure thickening one skin by 50 mm changes the cross_section total of all three users, leaves both walls' start/end bit-identical and moves the slab face opposite its reference plane; undo restores the exact project (PRF-002, WAL-004).
- WAL-004 unit tests: changing a wall from Thickness 0.25 to Thickness 0.40, and from Thickness to Layered, keeps start/end and moves the faces according to the location (Outside: exterior face fixed; Center: both faces move by half the change; Inside: interior face fixed), checked through face_offsets.
- Regression of the existing WAL-003 clauses (keep): a Layered wall with base offset +0.50 and one with -0.10, each with Fixed, Storey and Relative tops, has the same vertical_extent as the equivalent Thickness wall, and crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs and the validate.rs tests pass unchanged.
- Regression of the existing SLB-002 clauses (keep): template_contents still asserts the D.2 slab default (Top at offset 0.0, 0.20 m reinforced concrete); a Layered slab of total 0.35 m on a storey at 0.0 gives vertical_extent (-0.35, 0.0) for Top at 0.0 and (0.30, 0.65) for Bottom at +0.30; roundtrip.rs:47-62 stays green.
- DeleteLayerStructure of a used structure without a replacement returns Invalid; with a replacement it rewrites the users and the wall/slab defaults slot prototypes, and undo restores them; check_tool_defaults rejects a slot whose Layered structure does not exist.
- validate_element rejects an element whose Layered structure does not exist; integrity_problems reports a dangling structure reference.
- The incremental-versus-full property test of element-kind-framework includes UpdateLayerStructure; after such an edit the dirty set contains exactly the users of the structure.
- Existing golden files are byte-identical (Thickness elements write the same keys and values); all round-trip, geometry and kittest suites pass; clippy and fmt green.
- Satisfies WAL-003 (thickness or layer structure, base offset, top link and the direction rule kept; the profile alternative stays with PRF-010 in members-profiles-adv), SLB-002 (thickness or layer structure, top/bottom reference at an offset, default top at storey elevation), WAL-004 and the propagation clause of PRF-002.
notes: SRS: WAL-003 WAL-004 SLB-002 PRF-002. Appendix D.2 defaults stay single-material: wall 0.25 m masonry (Brick), slab 0.20 m reinforced concrete, top at storey elevation. The temporary writer warning for Layered elements is removed by task 08; no UI can create Layered elements before task 12.

title: Merge plan cut regions by material, priority and junction
description:
WHY: WAL-023 ends with: touching skins with the same material and priority merge into one region without a boundary line. WAL-027 requires junction cleanup, solid operations and cut fills to be derived from the same 3D geometry, so that plan cuts, sections, 3D views and exported IFCX agree and no element kind shows its cut fill only in some views. The plan already slices the evaluated meshes (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:111-170) but merges all cut polygons of one material regardless of priority and adjacency (plan.rs:153-164), so two overlapping unjoined walls show as one region although 3D has two bodies (gap analysis: WAL-023 and WAL-027 partial). What exists and is kept: one ModelGeometry per revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103) feeds the plan, the 3D view and the writer.

WHAT: Carry the effective priority on each BodyPart (task 05) and expose junction clusters in ModelGeometry (connected components of the junction graph; walls in no node, never-join walls and separated walls form their own clusters); group cut polygons in plan_drawing by (material, priority, cluster) before geo::unary_union and record priority and cluster on CutRegion so the plan renderer can draw boundaries where regions differ; add agreement tests between the resolved 2D skin polygons, the plan cut and horizontal slices of the 3D meshes in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/agreement.rs, and the IFCX leg (slices of the meshes read back from a saved file) in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/agreement.rs, because archicraft-geometry must not dev-depend on archicraft-ifcx (the dependency runs the other way). Out of scope: drawing changes in crates/archicraft-app (plan-renderer), section views (VIEW-030), solid operations (solid-kernel-ops re-asserts agreement).
design: `BodyPart.priority: u16` (effective priority; slabs use their material's priority) and `ModelGeometry.clusters: HashMap<ElementId, ClusterId>` built from the JunctionGraph that task 13 keeps in ModelGeometry, with ClusterId = the smallest ElementId of the component, so it is stable across evaluations and independent of order. In plan.rs replace `BTreeMap<MaterialId, Vec<Polygon<f64>>>` (plan.rs:119) by a BTreeMap keyed by (MaterialId, priority, ClusterId); CutRegion gains `priority` and `cluster`. Agreement helper for tests: symmetric difference with geo BooleanOps and unsigned_area. The 3D view needs no change because render3d.rs builds its scene from the same meshes (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-180), and the IFCX writer writes the same meshes (writer.rs:361-416). Pitfall: boundary and separator lines between different-priority regions are drawn by plan-renderer (DSP-012); this task only provides the data and leaves crates/archicraft-app drawing code alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two concrete walls at an L give one cut region with no seam; overriding the priority of one wall's skin (WAL-024) gives two regions with a boundary (WAL-023 merge clause).
- Two overlapping walls in different join groups, or separated by a Junction Separated relation, give two regions while 3D has two bodies (the gap-analysis case).
- F7 default: branch and through concrete form one region; the two insulation pieces belong to one region of the through wall.
- Agreement for L, T, X, F1 and F7: per element the plan cut polygons equal the resolved skin polygons (symmetric-difference area below 1e-10 m2), equal slices of the 3D meshes at 0.1 m, at the cut plane and at top minus 0.1 m, and equal slices of the meshes read back from the saved IFCX (WAL-027).
- Every part straddling the cut plane yields a CutRegion with a non-empty fill mesh, for every registered kind with a body (walls and slabs today).
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs and the plan picking tests stay green.
notes: SRS: WAL-023 WAL-027. DSP-012 (seamless same-material regions, separator lines) is owned by plan-renderer and consumes CutRegion.priority and cluster. Sections do not exist yet; the vertical-slice agreement is re-asserted when VIEW-030 lands.

title: Generate per-skin wall bodies as Skin_n parts
description:
WHY: PRF-001 (M) makes walls multi-skin; IFX-017 (M): element geometry is stored in child nodes, a single-material body is a `Body` child and a body with several materials has one child per material part, named by role, for example `Skin_1` ... `Skin_n` for layer structures; IFX-043 (M): every part of a layered element references a named material; WAL-004 (M): a structure change keeps the reference line and moves the faces. Gap rows: IFX-017 partial (only a single "Body" part is ever produced, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:169-171; BodyPart with role name and material is ready, evaluate.rs:21-28; the writer is generic, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:366-381); PRF-001 names multi-skin body generation as missing.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs give WallInput the wall's `CrossSection` instead of `thickness` (face offsets via ReferenceLine::face_offsets) and keep the existing L/T resolution on the envelope footprint. Add `pub struct SkinBand { index: usize, material: MaterialId, role: SkinRole, from: f64, to: f64 }` (offsets along the left-hand normal, exterior to interior) built from the section and the reference-line location, and `pub fn skin_rings(envelope: &Footprint, bands: &[SkinBand]) -> Vec<(SkinBand, Footprint)>` that splits the junction-resolved envelope into one quadrilateral per skin by interpolating both end edges at the band boundaries. In the wall geometry generator (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs after element-kind-framework-07, evaluate.rs:158-176 today) extrude each ring into a BodyPart named `Skin_{i}` (1-based, structure order) with the skin's material and a new `skin: Option<SkinRef { index: u16, role: SkinRole }>` field (0-based index into the structure; None for the single `Body` of Thickness walls, which stay unchanged). This is the field shape plan-renderer-03 reads and host-openings-03 wraps into its PartRole, so neither epic adds a second one. If any skin ring of a wall degenerates (very short wall folded by a junction), fall back to square ends for all of its skins, as today for the envelope (evaluate.rs:161-166). In crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs add `PlanElement::core_faces: Vec<[DVec2; 2]>` (core exterior and interior face lines of layered walls, clipped to the resolved envelope) for snapping (task 13). Out of scope: priority-based skin resolution at junctions (junction-engine; here skin ends inherit the envelope's end edges, so equal structures meet on the mitre and T-branch skins stop at the through wall's face), slabs (05), the IFCX golden and conformance checks (10).
design: Interpolation: for one wall end with exterior corner E and interior corner I (envelope corners at offsets ext and int along the left normal), the point of a band boundary at offset o is E + (I - E) * (o - ext) / (int - ext); this is exact for square, mitred and T-trimmed ends because the offset is affine along the end edge. Compute each boundary point once and reuse it for both neighbouring skins so the skins tile the envelope without slivers and their union equals the increment-0 body. Use the shared tolerance module of element-kind-framework (crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs) instead of new epsilons. Keep `Footprint` as the envelope type: junction-engine replaces it with per-skin SkinFootprint rings and expects the band offsets of this task unchanged. BodyPart.skin is what plan-renderer reads to classify skin separators (PlanElement.cut_skins of plan-renderer-03). Mesh count: a F2 wall yields six parts; the per-element Arc cache of the framework keeps them, render3d build_scene (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-175) already flattens all parts into one vertex buffer per opacity class and plan.rs merges same-material cut regions (plan.rs:153-160), so draw calls do not grow; per-part feature edges show the skin boundaries at wall ends in 3D, which is intended.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/layered.rs: a free F2 wall 5.0 m long and 3.0 m high evaluates into six parts Skin_1..Skin_6, every mesh passes check_closed, each volume equals 5.0 x 3.0 x skin thickness within 1e-9, the materials follow the structure order, BodyPart.skin carries indices 0..5 and the roles are finish, other, other, other, core, finish.
- WAL-003 direction rule for layered walls: an F2 wall from (0, 0) to (5, 0) with an Outside reference line has its exterior face on the reference line (the right-hand side of the direction), Skin_1 (brick) at 0 <= y <= 0.12 and Skin_6 at 0.67 <= y <= 0.68; the same wall entered from (5, 0) to (0, 0) has Skin_1 at -0.12 <= y <= 0 and Skin_6 at -0.68 <= y <= -0.67.
- plan_drawing at the 1.10 m cut plane gives that wall six polygons in PlanElement.cut (one region per skin); the plaster CutRegion holds two polygons and every other material one.
- Four F2 walls in a counter-clockwise 10 x 8 m ring joined at L corners: all 24 skin parts are closed, matching skins of adjacent walls share their mitre corner points bit for bit, the result is identical when the walls are evaluated in reverse order, and the summed volume equals the increment-0 single-envelope volume within 1e-9.
- WAL-004 geometry test: thickening the insulation skin by UpdateLayerStructure keeps the Axis points identical and moves the faces; with the reference line at CoreInterior the core interior face stays where it was.
- A 48-skin wall evaluates into 48 closed parts, each below the 65,535-point limit of IFX-038.
- Thickness walls still produce exactly one `Body` part: existing wall.rs tests and golden files are unchanged.
- Satisfies IFX-017 for layered walls (geometry side), the multi-skin body clause of PRF-001 and the geometry clause of WAL-004.
notes: SRS: IFX-017 PRF-001 WAL-004. Appendix D.7 F2: brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm, nominal height 3000 mm. Skin ends stay as the envelope's end edges until junction-engine.

title: Read hosted openings back and repair orphans on load
description:
WHY: Saved openings must come back editable, and damaged files must open predictably. IFX-064 (M) round-trip fidelity; IFX-080 (M) open every file the system wrote; IFX-015 (M) hosted elements are children of their host; NFR-REL-004 (M): 'On opening, the system shall check the model's referential integrity (hosts, storeys, materials, layers, types). It shall repair what can be repaired deterministically (for example orphaned hosted elements or missing materials replaced by a default) and report the repairs to the user'; PRJ-008 never omits objects silently. Gap-analysis NFR-REL-004: 'Hosts and types do not exist in the model yet, so those checks are absent. A wall whose top-linked storey is missing is skipped (validate.rs:267-271 via reader.rs:724-730) instead of being repaired deterministically to a fixed height as DeleteStorey does (command.rs:457-468).' The epic acceptance requires that 'a file with an orphaned hosted element is repaired deterministically and reported on load'. Exists and is kept (regress): layer and material repairs (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:620-653), tool-default references (449-466), site, building and storey repairs (539-590, 765-801), coincident storeys (563-574), duplicate ids (873-879), the load report modal (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:168-172, 589-600), the problems panel (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:847), Project::integrity_problems (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:327-341) and the tests invalid_elements_are_skipped_and_reported and missing_references_are_repaired_and_reported (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:276-314). Missing: the host checks, the storey-link repair and the types check (components-dw-catalogue).

WHAT: reader.rs: after an element is read and inserted (storey loop, reader.rs:854-882), descend into its children that carry archicraft::element and read them with the opening codec; the parent element is the host (tree position wins over archicraft::opening.host, and a mismatch is repaired and reported); Body, Axis, Void and compound-part sub-nodes are skipped silently as before. New crates/archicraft-model/src/integrity.rs: a deterministic, idempotent `repair(project, &LoadHints) -> Vec<Repair>` built from a list of checks and run by the reader after all elements are read (crash recovery uses the same reader); LoadHints carries what only the file knows, so the model crate stays free of IFCX types: the hosted elements the reader could not attach, each with its world anchor composed from the usd::xformop chain of its node, and the stored mesh extent per element. Checks: (1) a hosted element whose host is missing, unreadable or not host-capable is re-hosted to the host-capable element on the same storey whose model footprint contains the opening's world anchor, ties broken by ElementId, with the placement re-expressed in the new host's frame, and is otherwise removed; (2) a hosted element whose storey differs from its host's gets the host's storey; (3) a hosted element found as a storey child with a valid archicraft::opening.host moves under that host; (4) a wall top or shaft link to a missing storey becomes TopLink::Fixed with the height taken from the stored Body or Void mesh extent in LoadHints, else the home storey height, replacing today's skip. Each repair is a Problem::warning (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:50) in ReadOutcome.problems naming the element and the action, shown by the existing load report (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:589-600) and the problems panel. The check list is open, so components-dw-catalogue adds the types check and doors-windows-core reuses the host checks. Out of scope: openings in third-party files (ifcx-interop), type placeholders (components-dw-catalogue).
design: Read hosted children recursively through the same descent that doors and windows will use; keep the reader lenient (report, never panic) per PRJ-008 and the ifcx_alpha style (report.or(...)). Composing usd::xformop up the tree uses the node map the reader already builds; compute the world anchor only when rule 1 needs it. Deterministic means ordered by ElementId and independent of HashMap iteration. Pitfalls: children of a host node that is skipped as invalid must still be visited so rule 1 can re-host or remove them with a report (PRJ-008); validate_element rejects a wall linked to a missing storey (validate.rs:264-271), so the repair must run before that element is validated or validation must report the condition as repairable; re-hosting must re-run the opening validator against the new host; never re-host across storeys.
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs: openings_showcase saves and loads equal (Project ==, revision normalised) with zero problems, and regenerated geometry equals the stored meshes within 0.1 mm (IFX-064, IFX-080).
- Corrupted variants generated in the test from the showcase JSON: (a) an invalid host element record -> the opening is re-hosted by the footprint rule or removed, and the report names it; (b) an opening listed under the storey with a valid host attribute -> moved under the host with a warning; (c) a host attribute disagreeing with the parent node -> the parent wins with a warning; (d) a wall top linked to a missing storey -> fixed height equal to the stored mesh height with a warning, no longer skipped; (e) a shaft top linked to a missing storey -> fixed with a warning.
- Each corrupted file loads to the same project on every load (deterministic), and saving and reloading the result reports no further repairs (idempotent); Project::integrity_problems() is empty after every load.
- A unit test on the load report text (or a kittest of the report modal) shows the repair lines.
- invalid_elements_are_skipped_and_reported and missing_references_are_repaired_and_reported pass unchanged (existing repairs kept).
- NFR-REL-004 satisfied for hosts and storeys (materials and layers already done, types through components-dw-catalogue); PRJ-008 holds for hosted elements; IFX-015 holds on the reader side.
notes: SRS: NFR-REL-004 IFX-015. Also IFX-064, IFX-080, PRJ-008. Decision to record in docs: orphan repair order is tree parent, attribute host, footprint search, removal.

title: Verify exit criterion: Layer structures, skins, core faces and multi-skin bodies
description:
WHY: The epic owns PRF-001, PRF-002, PRF-003, WAL-003, WAL-004, WAL-005, WAL-006, SLB-002, SLB-009, SLB-006 and IFX-017 and is the prerequisite of junction-engine (which re-asserts F2 at resolved junctions), host-openings, doors-windows-core (reveals at core faces, DW-008), plan-renderer (skin separators), roofs and templates-presets. This task verifies the whole against the epic acceptance, not against the individual tasks.

WHAT: Run the workspace quality gates and the conformance job, walk the epic acceptance item by item and name the test that proves each, fix or file beads for anything missing (at least: hosted-element re-anchoring in MoveWallReferenceLine/FlipWalls for host-openings, WAL-005; the plan visibility of slabs and skins entirely below the storey elevation; the note to doors-windows-core that every wall host has a core), update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID and the increment-1 readiness line, then close the epic in beads. No new features.
design: Checklist run: F2 build, plan regions and Skin export -> tests/layered.rs, fixtures_f2_f3.rs, roundtrip.rs layered_bodies_are_skin_parts, conformance/check.ts Skin checks plus the viewer evidence; F3 -> fixtures_f2_f3.rs; structure edit propagation -> commands.rs and the dialog kittest; core-face locations, move-reference-line and flip -> tests/layered.rs; sloped/tapered parameters and validation -> the slab kind unit tests and commands.rs (07), closedness -> tests/slopes.rs (14); registry -> crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs. Status rows use the gap-analysis vocabulary (done/partial/missing, remaining_effort, depends_on) and name the deferring epic for every clause left open.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture F2 (brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm) builds, cuts in plan with one region per skin and exports six Skin parts each naming its material (conformance plus viewer check); fixture F3 floating floor; editing a structure updates all users (command test); core-face reference-line locations, move-reference-line and flip commands keep the body in place (geometry tests); sloped constant-thickness and tapered slab bodies are closed. F2 and F3 are registered under their ids in the fixture registry of regression-and-status.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx including layered-structures.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (PRF-001, PRF-002, PRF-003, WAL-003, WAL-004, WAL-005, WAL-006, SLB-002, SLB-009, SLB-006, IFX-017) with status, evidence (file:line) and remaining gap.
- Beads exist for the open cross-epic items: plan_hosted_followups re-anchoring of hosted elements (host-openings, WAL-005), plan visibility of slabs below the storey elevation (task 05 limitation), and the always-a-core note for doors-windows-core (DW-008).
- The epic is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: PRF-001 PRF-002 PRF-003 WAL-003 WAL-004 WAL-005 WAL-006 SLB-002 SLB-009 SLB-006 IFX-017. Clauses deliberately left open: the profile alternative of WAL-003 (PRF-010, members-profiles-adv), the DW-008 reveal use of PRF-003 (doors-windows-core; the interface is delivered by task 03), the roof use of PRF-001 (roofs; the resource is kind-independent), hosted elements in WAL-005 (host-openings, via plan_hosted_followups), Void children of IFX-017 (host-openings-03) and its Frame/Panel/Glazing example (doors-windows-core), skin resolution at junctions (junction-engine).

title: Add join group, junction order, end thickness and skin priority
description:
WHY: The junction engine needs four pieces of authoring data that the model does not have yet; the gap analysis rates all four requirements 'missing'. WAL-025: join groups are an element property, independent of layers and visibility; elements in different join groups, or in the reserved "never join" group, are not joined or cleaned up against each other. WAL-036: a per-wall junction order overrides the deterministic rule of WAL-026. WAL-008: trapezoidal walls have separate start and end thicknesses, and the face on the reference-line side stays straight along the reference line. WAL-024: the priority of an individual skin in a layer structure is overridable without changing the material's priority elsewhere. The gap analysis confirms that Element has no join-group field (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:275-287), walls have a single thickness (element.rs:128-137; a `Structure` after layer-structures-02) and only Material.priority 1..999 exists (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:153-154, D.4 values in template.rs).

WHAT: In archicraft-model add (a) the new module crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs (exported from lib.rs; task 02 extends it) with a `JoinGroup` type, the reserved `NEVER` and the `DEFAULT` value and a `joins()` predicate, stored as `join_group` on the Element envelope and on the `DefaultsSlot` of element-kind-framework-04 (the slot keeps envelope fields such as layer and ifc_class beside the prototype payload, so the envelope default needs its own field); (b) `junction_order` (1..=16, default 8) and `end_thickness: Option<f64>` on the Wall payload (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/wall.rs after element-kind-framework-02) plus `Wall::face_offsets_at(section, u)`; (c) an optional `priority` override on the `Skin` of layer-structures-01 (crates/archicraft-model/src/layer_structure.rs) and the resolved effective priority as a new field of `SectionSkin`, filled by `Project::cross_section` of layer-structures-02: the override, else the skin material's priority, and for `Structure::Thickness { thickness, material }` that material's priority; (d) join group 1 and junction order 8 in the D.2 wall slot of template.rs, stamped by Project::new_wall / Project::new_element; (e) validation in the wall kind's validate hook and in LayerStructure::validate; (f) defaults for the new fields wherever the IFCX reader, samples.rs, the FixtureBuilder of element-kind-framework-03 and tests construct these structs, so every existing file and golden still loads and is reproduced unchanged. Out of scope: any geometry use (tasks 03-06), writing the attributes to IFCX (08), properties fields and dialogs (11).
design: JoinGroup(u8) with #[serde(transparent)], `pub const NEVER: JoinGroup = JoinGroup(0)` (shown as "Never join"), `pub const DEFAULT: JoinGroup = JoinGroup(1)`, user groups 1..=99, `pub fn joins(self, other: JoinGroup) -> bool { self != Self::NEVER && self == other }`. It sits on Element, not on Wall: SRS WAL-025 defines it as an element property and cleanup-and-trims reuses it for columns, beams and slabs; record this deviation from the epic design note in docs/junctions.md (task 06). `junction_order: u8` with DEFAULT_JUNCTION_ORDER = 8 (fixture F6 assumes 8 as the default). `end_thickness: Option<f64>`: the start thickness stays in `Structure::Thickness { thickness, material }` of layer-structures-02; `Wall::face_offsets_at(section: &CrossSection, u: f64)` (u = 0 at the start, 1 at the end) is built on ReferenceLine::distance_from_exterior of layer-structures-03 (today's face_offsets at element.rs:99-107) so that only the face away from the reference line moves - the WAL-008 invariant lives in one function that geometry (03) and the UI (11) share.
