Skin override `priority: Option<u16>` with #[serde(default)], validated against Material::MIN_PRIORITY..=MAX_PRIORITY (material.rs:159-161); resolving it once in Project::cross_section into SectionSkin means geometry (05), the plan merge (07) and the UI (11) read priorities through one path, and a priority edit can never leave stale data because the CrossSection is resolved per evaluation, never cached on the element. Put #[serde(default)] on every new field so command journals and autosaves still deserialise. Pitfalls: Element struct literals exist in reader.rs, samples.rs, the framework's FixtureBuilder and many tests - update them all in this task to keep the build green; the DefaultsSlot equality behind SetToolDefaults' NoChange detection must include join_group; do not bump FORMAT_VERSION; do not write the fields yet (golden files stay identical until task 08).
acceptance_criteria:
- A unit test in crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs pins the JoinGroup truth table: equal user groups join, different groups do not, NEVER joins nothing (not even NEVER), DEFAULT is group 1 (WAL-025).
- Validation tests: junction order 0 and 17, join group 100 and skin priority 0 and 1000 are rejected with CommandError::Invalid and a readable message; an end thickness outside MIN_THICKNESS..MAX_THICKNESS (validate.rs:19-21), on a Structure::Layered wall ("Only single-material walls can be trapezoidal.") or with a Center or Custom reference line ("A trapezoidal wall needs its reference line on a face.") is rejected; Outside, Inside, CoreExterior and CoreInterior are accepted, because the core faces of a Thickness structure coincide with its faces (layer-structures-03).
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: UpdateElements changing join group, junction order and end thickness, SetToolDefaults changing the wall slot's join group, and UpdateLayerStructure setting a skin override each execute and undo back to the starting project (revision normalised); invalid commands leave the project unchanged.
- Effective-priority test: overriding one skin of structure S changes only that skin's SectionSkin priority; another structure and a single-material wall using the same material keep the material priority (WAL-024 'without changing the material's priority elsewhere'); UpdateMaterial changing the material's priority changes every skin without an override and leaves the override.
- Tool-defaults test: Project::new_wall stamps join group 1 and junction order 8 and leaves end_thickness None (WAL-036 default, WAL-008 off by default).
- Face-offset test: Wall::face_offsets_at(section, 0.0) equals today's face offsets for every reference line, and with an end thickness only the face away from the reference line differs between u = 0 and u = 1 (WAL-008 invariant).
- All golden files are reproduced byte for byte (the new fields are not written yet); cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt are green.
notes: SRS: WAL-025 WAL-036 WAL-008 WAL-024. Appendix D.4: intersection priorities are integers 1-999 (overrides use the same range); D.2: wall 0.25 m masonry, reference line on the exterior face. Open question: join groups are plain numbers 1-99 plus 'Never join' (the glossary maps the reference product's Layer Intersection Group to Join group); named groups could follow without a format break. Junction order 1-16 with default 8 follows F6; whether lower or higher numbers win is fixed in task 06.

title: Find host candidates under the pointer and preview them in 3D
description:
WHY: OPN-007 (M): 'Openings shall be placeable in plan and 3D views with a live preview over the host under the pointer.' Doors and windows need the same host-under-pointer service (DW-001, DW-002; doors-windows-core-06 and -07 consume it). NFR-PERF-005 (M): input feedback within 50 ms. Gap-analysis OPN-007: tools are plan-only (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:451), previews are polylines only (tools.rs:547), and the 3D view picks (view3d.rs:75) but takes no tool input; technical debt: 3D hover highlighting is dead code (view3d.rs:213 passes None, SceneKey omits hover). point-input-snapping provides the PointInput service with its Preview type and the ViewSurface trait; 3d-input-navigation provides the Camera3d ViewSurface with face picking and working planes.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/input/host.rs: `HostCandidate { element, hit: HostHit, distance }` with `HostHit::{WallFace { along, elevation, face }, Plan { point, top_z }}`; `candidates_in_plan(project, plan, geometry, point, radius, filter)` returns walls whose resolved footprint contains the point or lies within the snap radius (face from the side of the reference line) and slabs whose outline contains the point, ordered by distance then ElementId and filtered by the registry's HostCapability for the hosted kind; `candidate_in_3d(pick_index, ray, project, filter)` uses PickIndex::ray (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/pick.rs, 3d-input-navigation-06, cached as Arc<PickIndex> in Workspace) with the ray of Camera3dSurface (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/surface3d.rs, 3d-input-navigation-07) and classifies Hit { element, part, face, point, normal } (wall exterior or interior face -> WallFace, slab top or bottom -> Plan). The point-input Preview (input/consumer.rs) gains `meshes: Vec<PreviewMesh { mesh, storey, style: PreviewStyle::{Void, HostHighlight} }>`; views/plan.rs draws their plan outlines in the preview colour; views/view3d.rs hands them to a new `Renderer3d::draw_overlay` (views/render3d.rs) that uploads a small transient vertex buffer per frame and draws it after the scene with depth test on and depth writes off, without touching GpuScene or SceneKey; the host highlight re-draws the candidate's visible parts tinted in the overlay instead of rebuilding the scene; outline edges of the void keep using 3d-input-navigation-07's Overlay3d segment helper, so the mesh overlay only adds the shaded faces. Out of scope: the opening tool (11), a host-cycling key (doors-windows-core builds DW-002 on this candidate list), working-plane mechanics (3d-input-navigation).
design: Reuse PlanDrawing::pick (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:270) and the resolved footprints instead of new hit tests; the 3D classification compares the hit point and face normal with the host's frame (wall: dot product with the left normal; slab: sign of the normal's z). The overlay is the cheapest correct path for previews and hover highlights and also retires the dead-code hover debt without re-uploading the scene on every pointer move. Pitfalls: overlay geometry is storey-local and must be offset by the storey elevation as build_scene does (render3d.rs:110-115); translucent overlay faces need culling off and must be drawn after opaque geometry; keep host.rs free of egui so it is unit-testable; NFR-PERF-005 means no per-frame rebuild of candidate structures beyond the result vector (see the per-frame SnapTargets debt).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in host.rs on two_storey_shell: a point inside a wall footprint returns that wall with along, elevation and face correct (exterior on the right of the reference line); a point over a slab returns only the slab; a point at a T junction returns both walls in deterministic order; empty space returns nothing; openings are never candidates.
- With a fixed Camera3d looking at a wall face, the ray through the face centre yields WallFace on the facing side with along within 1 mm; a ray onto a slab top yields Plan.
- Drawing overlay meshes changes neither SceneKey nor the revision and triggers no scene upload (debug counter); an empty preview clears the overlay.
- Candidate search plus preview build stays under 50 ms on two_storey_shell (frame-time assertion, or an #[ignore] smoke test in the performance harness).
- The host-under-pointer and 3D preview infrastructure of OPN-007 exists and is used by 11 and by doors-windows-core.
notes: SRS: OPN-007. Also NFR-PERF-005; DW-001 and DW-002 are consumers in doors-windows-core.

title: Wire the node engine into evaluation and incremental invalidation
description:
WHY: Task 04 delivers junction::resolve as a pure function; WAL-020 and WAL-026 are only met when every view and the IFCX writer see its result. Today ModelGeometry::evaluate (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:64-91) calls wall::footprints with wall_inputs (evaluate.rs:99-120), and after element-kind-framework-10 evaluate_incremental re-resolves only a dirty set built from per-end contact neighbours. Node-based resolution widens what an edit affects: every wall at the previous and the new nodes of an edited wall, the other walls of a node cluster, and - once priorities, join groups and junction orders matter (01, 05, 06) - the node partners of any wall whose effective priority, join group or junction order changes, including all users of an edited material or layer structure. WAL-026 forbids results that depend on edit history, so incremental and full evaluation must stay bit-identical.

WHAT: ModelGeometry::evaluate and evaluate_incremental build the JunctionGraph once per evaluation (junction::detect for a full evaluation, detect_around for the dirty region), keep the previous graph in ModelGeometry, run junction::resolve and hand each wall's ResolvedWall to the wall generator through the EvalContext of element-kind-framework-07 (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs). Extend dirty_set with the node partners at old and new nodes, cluster members, users of an edited material or layer structure plus their node partners, and both walls of an inserted or removed Junction relation. Record fallback problems in ModelGeometry.problems so the problems panel lists them. Delete l_junction, t_junction, resolve_end, footprints, Footprint and wall_inputs from wall.rs and evaluate.rs, keeping only the helpers junction.rs still uses (point_segment_distance moved to the model in 02). Out of scope: skin-level resolution (05), the final rank (06), the plan merge (07).
design: One graph per evaluation, never stored in the project (task 02). For the dirty set, compare the previous and the new graph around the stamped walls: the union of their node members, closed over clusters (nodes of one wall closer than 2r, task 04), is the set to re-resolve; walls outside it keep their ResolvedWall and Arc. Material and layer-structure edits arrive as resource stamps from the ChangeLog (layer-structures-02 made structure users dirty); map them to user walls with Project::element_materials and Project::layer_structure_users, then add node partners. Keep catch_unwind per element (evaluate.rs) and treat a panic inside junction::resolve as a node fallback for the walls of that node, not as a failed project. Sort everything that reaches the output by node point and ElementId; ModelGeometry.elements may stay a HashMap because it is only read by id. Pitfalls: a wall whose join group changes to NEVER leaves its nodes, so the old graph must contribute its former partners; undo of a relation insert must produce the same dirty set as the insert (framework rule); the first evaluation after load is full.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs and the ported junction.rs tests pass with the old wall.rs resolution deleted; golden files are reproduced, or re-blessed with a reviewed diff that only reorders vertices of joined walls (the T junction of two-storey-shell.ifcx keeps its geometry).
- incremental_equals_full of element-kind-framework-10, extended with L/T/X/Y scenes, random endpoint moves that create and break contacts, join-group and junction-order edits, material priority edits and Separated relation inserts and removals, stays bit-identical over 200 seeded sequences (WAL-026 'created or edited').
- dirty_set unit tests: moving one wall out of a 3-wall node dirties the two remaining walls; an UpdateMaterial priority change dirties its users and their node partners; a wall in the same node cluster that does not touch the edited wall is dirtied; unchanged walls keep their Arc (Arc::ptr_eq).
- A node forced into fallback appears as one problem per affected wall, with the node position, in ModelGeometry.problems and in the problems panel (UI-012), and those walls keep closed square-ended bodies.
- dirty_set_after_one_edit_is_local still holds on stand_in(5_000): one interior wall move dirties only the walls at its old and new nodes and their clusters.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt are green.
notes: SRS: WAL-020 WAL-026. Context: NFR-PERF-006 (200 ms after a single edit; the budget is verified by regression-and-status), NFR-REL-005 (fallback), UI-012 (problems panel), decision D-6. Split out of task 04 so the engine and its pipeline integration can be reviewed separately.

title: Build the opening tool for placement in plan and 3D views
description:
WHY: Users place openings with a tool. OPN-007 (M): placeable in plan and 3D views with a live preview over the host under the pointer; the parameters of OPN-003 (section), OPN-004 (orientation), OPN-005 (depth) and OPN-006 (storey range) are chosen while placing; UI-008 with Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for the opening tool. The epic acceptance requires that 'the tool creates nothing without a host under the pointer (kittest) and the preview follows the host in plan and in a 3D view through the Camera3d ViewSurface'. Today ToolKind is {Select, Wall, Slab} (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13-17) and there is no opening action.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/opening.rs (the tools module point-input-snapping-01 created from views/tools.rs; ToolKind::Opening in tools/mod.rs): `OpeningTool` implementing the InputConsumer trait (crates/archicraft-app/src/input/consumer.rs) with shape (rectangle, circle, polygon) and depth (through, limited, storey range) from the opening DefaultsSlot, and the orientation mode (auto: perpendicular in walls and vertical in slabs; perpendicular; vertical) kept as tool state because the payload has no 'auto'. Step 1 takes host and anchor from the candidate of 10 and previews the void of a transient opening built from the defaults (geometry::opening::void_prism and void_mesh, never a hand-drawn rectangle) plus the host highlight. Step 2 sets the size: the rectangle's opposite corner in the section plane (plan for vertical openings, the host-face working plane in 3D for perpendicular ones; in plan a perpendicular wall opening takes the width along the wall and keeps the default height), the circle's radius, or polygon points until Enter (vertical in plan, perpendicular in 3D on the face plane); Enter in step 2 accepts the default size; typed lengths go through PointInput. The commit emits Command::AddElements(vec![project.new_opening(..)]). Without a candidate the commit calls Workspace::error('Point at a wall or slab to place the opening.') (workspace.rs:111) and returns Outcome::Nothing, and the cursor shows a no-host state. 3D placement uses the same consumer on 3d-input-navigation-08's 3D host through Camera3dSurface (views/surface3d.rs) with WorkingPlane::Face (crates/archicraft-app/src/input/working_plane.rs) of the picked host face. Action::ToolOpening with a free single-key shortcut, a run() arm (app.rs:377), a toolbox button and a Design menu item (ui/shell.rs), the ToolKind-to-KindTag mapping in properties.rs gather (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:55) and tool_modes so the strip shows the opening DefaultsSlot with mode buttons, the select_all mapping (workspace.rs:204) and step prompts. The tool lands after the writer and reader (08, 09) so that openings placed in the UI survive saving, autosave (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/autosave.rs:89 writes through archicraft_ifcx::save) and reopening. UI-008 is partial (shortcuts in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs:114-146, test shortcuts_are_unique at actions.rs:177): extend both. Out of scope: editing placed openings (12), host cycling, drawing profiles in section views (OPN-013).
design: Follow 'Add a drawing tool' in docs/implementation-status.md as adapted to the InputConsumer contract of point-input-snapping: the tool keeps its state, the service resolves points, the tool returns Preview and Outcome. The preview path equals the result path (transient Element -> void_prism -> void_mesh), so what the user sees is what the command creates. Section-plane coordinates come from the candidate's HostHit (wall: along and elevation; slab: plan point) and, in 3D, from the working plane of the picked face, so one code path serves both views. Pitfalls: single-key shortcuts must not fire while typing (UI-008); Esc follows the service's one-step ladder (leaving step 2 keeps the host); the commit must re-check the host under the pointer at click time instead of reusing a stale hover; keep the state machine free of egui for unit tests; Key O is taken by orbit mode (actions.rs:140), so choose another key and record it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests without egui (stub host provider): a commit without candidate returns Nothing and records the message; with a wall candidate the default rectangle yields AddElements with a WallFace placement at the projected along and the default sill; a circle's radius comes from the second click; a vertical polygon in a slab closes on Enter with at least three valid points; the storey-range depth comes from the defaults.
- An opening placed in the UI survives save and reopen with equal parameters (end-to-end through 08 and 09).
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the toolbox button and the shortcut activate the tool; a click in empty plan space adds no element and the status line shows the message (epic acceptance); a click over a wall adds exactly one opening hosted by that wall; undo removes it and the wall is whole again.
- kittest in a 3D pane with a fixed camera: hovering wall A and then wall B moves the overlay void onto B's face; clicking places an opening hosted by B equal to one placed in plan at the same along and elevation (ViewSurface equivalence, as 3d-input-navigation tests walls).
- Preview feedback stays within 50 ms (NFR-PERF-005 harness or smoke test); the D.8 shortcut test lists the opening tool and shortcuts stay unique.
- OPN-007 satisfied; OPN-003 to OPN-006 parameters are selectable at placement.
notes: SRS: OPN-007 OPN-003 OPN-004 OPN-005 OPN-006. Also UI-008 (Appendix D.8 lists the opening tool). Open question: the shortcut letter (proposal H for 'hole'), to be confirmed against commands-and-l10n's command registry.

title: Cut wall skins in the wall plane before extrusion
description:
WHY: An opening must remove its volume from every skin of its host wall. OPN-001 (M): the opening has exactly one host, and SRS 3.2 says hosted elements cut it; OPN-005 (M): through 'the full thickness of every cut element' or limited by start and end offsets, with the acceptance 'a limited opening from 0 to 0.40 m in a 0.50 m wall leaves a 0.10 m thick back (niche)'; IFX-033 (M): exported bodies are the evaluated result of openings; NFR-MNT-005 (M): regression tests cover 'openings at element boundaries'. The epic acceptance adds 'a 1.0 x 1.0 m opening in the F2 wall removes the volume from every skin (signed-volume check)' and 'an opening at a wall end adjacent to a junction is added to the NFR-MNT-005 suite'. Today walls are extruded whole (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:150-170); IFX-033 is partial (the evaluated geometry is what gets saved, crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103 and writer.rs:370-381; keep) and NFR-MNT-005 is partial (L and T tests in wall.rs:279-345 and tests/storey.rs:30-76; keep). Gap-analysis OPN-005 notes that a niche cannot be produced by a plain 2D cut before extrusion; the layered extrusion of 04 now provides the construction.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall_cut.rs, called by the wall GeometryKind generator with the hosted VoidPrisms passed in a new `EvalContext::cutters` slot (collected from the relation store's Host dependents before the host is evaluated). Per skin (SkinBand intervals along the left normal and skin_rings from layer-structures-04, ends resolved by wall.rs or junction-engine's junction.rs): the straight span between the junction end pieces is built with extrude_layers along the face normal, with layer boundaries at the skin faces and at every void's depth bounds, each layer's section in the elevation plane being the span rectangle minus the union of the sections whose depth range covers it; the end pieces stay vertical prisms of their plan polygons, built with extrude_layers along z when a rectilinear void reaches into them; span and end pieces are stitched at the split planes by cancelling the identical split faces and welding. A non-rectilinear section that reaches into an end piece is cut up to the split plane and reported ('OP-007 is cut only up to the junction'), never left corrupt (NFR-REL-005). Vertical openings in walls use extrude_layers along z over the skin footprint. Overlapping voids with equal orientation and depth are unioned; other overlaps put a warning on the later opening (by ElementId) and skip it; a void that misses its host is reported as a warning 'does not cut its host'. Depth bounds within MODEL_TOLERANCE of a skin boundary snap to it, so no sliver layer arises. Assert that the framework's incremental dirty set follows Host edges in both directions. Switch the 'openings at ends' row of crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs (junction-engine-12) from Status::Pending { owner: "host-openings", requires_kind: "opening" } to Active with the cases 'opening at a wall end next to an L junction' and 'opening next to a T junction' (or re-bless the uncut outlines 01 activated), and update the row's entry in docs/junctions.md (both owned by junction-engine); if junction-engine has not merged yet, keep the cases in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/openings.rs and file a bead to move them. Out of scope: slabs and shafts (06), further cut elements (OPN-002), arc and inclined walls (curved-geometry), reveal materials (OPN-008).
design: Wall-local frame: origin at the reference-line start, x along the line, y the left normal (exterior faces on the right per the ReferenceLine docs in element.rs), z up from the storey; skin bands are y-intervals from layer-structures and the junction-resolved footprint gives each skin's end polygons. The split planes are the largest x of any skin's start end and the smallest x of any skin's far end; between them every skin is a box and elevation-plane layering is exact for any section, circles and polygons included. Stitching works because both sides of a split plane receive the same trace (rectangle minus the same void section), computed once and reused bit for bit. Keep the pipeline order base footprints -> junction resolution -> opening cuts -> extrusion, which solid-kernel-ops extends (junctions, openings, solid operations, trims). Pitfalls: ModelGeometry.problems marks failed elements (the fallback boxes of element-kind-framework-13), so partial-cut and overlap notes go into a separate warning list or carry a severity, and a host with such a note keeps its cut body; cuts never depend on layer visibility (IFX-068): hiding the 'Openings' layer hides the opening's symbols, never restores the host body; clip the margin-extended void to the wall length before layering; many openings in one long wall approach MAX_MESH_POINTS (report, do not split here); keep coordinates storey-local (evaluate.rs header comment); share test helpers through tests/common/mod.rs as junction-engine does; reference evaluate.rs:150-189 and the test pattern in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/openings.rs niche_leaves_a_ten_centimetre_back: a 0.50 m single-skin wall with a 1.0 x 1.0 m opening limited 0.00-0.40 m from the exterior face has a closed body whose volume is reduced by exactly 0.40 m3; a point 0.45 m deep inside the section is solid, one 0.35 m deep is empty, and the back face lies 0.10 m from the interior face (OPN-005 acceptance).
- A hidden 'Openings' layer leaves every host body cut (IFX-068); a partial-cut note does not turn the host into a fallback box.
- f2_opening_cuts_every_skin: the F2 wall (680 mm, six skins) with a 1.0 x 1.0 m through opening: each Skin_i signed volume decreases by 1.0 x 1.0 x t_i (1e-9 relative) and all six parts pass check_closed (epic acceptance).
- A limited depth ending on the air/insulation boundary of F2 (0.18 m) pierces only brick and air and leaves the insulation untouched without a zero-thickness layer.
- A rectangle starting at the host base gives a notch through the bottom face; the plan cut at 1.10 m of a window-like opening with a 0.90 m sill shows two pieces per skin.
- Circular and polygonal perpendicular sections and a vertical slot in a wall give closed bodies with volumes within the tessellation tolerance.
- A rectangle reaching into the mitre of an L corner is cut exactly (analytic volume); a circle reaching into it is cut up to the split plane with exactly one warning entry; two overlapping voids of different depth give one warning on the later opening.
- Editing an opening dirties exactly the opening and its host; editing the host thickness dirties host, opening and contact neighbours; incremental equals full evaluation for an edit sequence with openings.
- The NFR-MNT-005 table contains the two opening-at-junction cases with blessed golden rings, and docs/junctions.md no longer lists the entry as pending (or the local cases and the follow-up bead exist).
notes: SRS: OPN-001 OPN-005. Also IFX-033 and NFR-MNT-005 (owned by other epics, re-asserted here). Fixture F2 comes from layer-structures-09 (fixtures::f2_layered_wall in crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs; D.7: brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm). doors-windows-core-03 feeds its rectangular insert voids into the same wall_cut path.

title: Generalise wall outlines to polygons and add trapezoidal walls (F1)
description:
WHY: WAL-008 asks for trapezoidal walls with separate start and end thicknesses whose face on the reference-line side stays straight along the reference line; Appendix D.7 fixture F1 is a trapezoidal wall of 300 mm at the start and 500 mm at the end. The current footprint is a fixed `[DVec2; 4]` built from one thickness and faces parallel to the reference line (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:102, evaluate.rs:137-146), and layer-structures-04 splits that envelope into Skin_n rings by interpolating its end edges (skin_rings), which only works for four-corner footprints (gap analysis: WAL-008 missing). That blocks trapezoids, the node engine (04) and later arc walls, so footprints become general polygons built from face lines.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs replace `Footprint` (wall.rs:102) and `skin_rings` of layer-structures-04 by a `WallOutline` built from face lines - one band per `SkinBand` of layer-structures-04 (offsets and Skin_n order unchanged) and, for a trapezoidal wall, a tapered face through the start and end offsets of `Wall::face_offsets_at` (task 01) - that converts to `geo::Polygon<f64>`; extend the wall input with the end thickness; adapt the existing L/T code to face lines (parallel tests on face directions instead of `wall.dir()`) so that today's behaviour holds until tasks 04 and 13 replace it; make the wall generator (evaluate.rs:150-176, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs after element-kind-framework-07) extrude polygons, keeping the validate_ring fallback to square ends (evaluate.rs:161-166); add `fixtures::f1_trapezoidal_wall()` to crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (the D.7 registry of regression-and-status-02; if it has not landed, create the module in the shape that task specifies, as layer-structures-09 does) with its specific assertions in crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs. Out of scope: the node engine (04, 13), the endThickness IFCX attribute (08), the UI fields (11) and layered trapezoids (rejected by validation in 01).
design: Keep the `Line { point, dir }` faces of wall.rs:41-50: a band is the region between two face lines, capped by lines perpendicular to the reference line at the start and the end (square caps). For a trapezoid the tapered face passes through start + n * off_s and end + n * off_e, with n = dir.perp() and the exterior on the right of start -> end (ReferenceLine docs in element.rs). Skin bands come from the cumulative skin offsets of layer-structures; with a taper (single material only) there is one band. Convert to geo::Polygon only at the end and keep DVec2 maths for corner points so the mitre corners stay bit-identical (ordered_intersect, wall.rs:121-125). Pitfalls: `intersect` (wall.rs:53-60) rejects near-parallel lines below 1e-12 and a tapered face is almost parallel to the reference line, so test face directions consistently; the spike limit of l_junction (10 x thickness) must use the larger end thickness; outlines stay counter-clockwise for extrude (extrude.rs:18 normalises, but tests must not rely on it).
acceptance_criteria:
- F1 geometry test: a 5.00 m wall from (0, 0) to (5, 0), start 0.30 m, end 0.50 m, reference line on the exterior face gives the outline (0, 0), (5, 0), (5, 0.50), (0, 0.30); the body is closed (check_closed), its volume is 5.00 x 0.40 x height, and the plan cut polygon equals the outline (WAL-008, F1).
- With the reference line on the interior face, the interior face lies straight on the reference line and the exterior face tapers.
- Changing the start or end thickness keeps the reference line and the straight face in place (WAL-004 invariant for tapers).
- An L junction between the 0.50 m end of F1 and a constant 0.30 m wall: both bodies closed, shared corner points bit-identical, interior-disjoint (sum of areas equals the area of the union).
- Every existing wall.rs test (free wall, L mitre identical, order independence, opposite directions, T near face, other storeys) passes unchanged on WallOutline.
- F1 is registered as fixtures::f1_trapezoidal_wall (D.7 entry built through commands with seeded ids) and passes the registry's generic checks; existing golden files and the Skin_n parts of layered walls (layer-structures-04 tests) are reproduced unchanged.
notes: SRS: WAL-008. Appendix D.7 F1: trapezoidal wall, 300 mm at the start and 500 mm at the end (KB 303968). WAL-004 (a thickness change keeps the reference line) is re-asserted for tapers. Decision carried from task 01: trapezoids are single-material and need a face reference line; open question whether layered trapezoids are wanted later.

title: Extensible element kinds, relations, compound parts and incremental evaluation
description:
Replace the closed ElementKind/KindTag/IfcClass/NameCounters/ToolDefaults enums matched in about fifteen places across all four crates with a per-kind registry (KindDescriptor: label, code, name prefix, IFC class set and predefined types, defaults slot, validator, geometry generator, transform hook, part list, IFCX attribute codec), add the relation store of SRS 3.3 (host, junction, trim, solid operation, annotation binding, storey link) to Project with dependency queries and integrity checks, and make geometry evaluation incremental (dirty set = edited elements plus relation and contact neighbours). The same epic closes the increment-0 residuals that live in this layer: the full D.5 class list with predefined types in the archicraft namespace (IFX-024), the generic compound-part codec that writes child nodes with their own IFC class (IFX-016, first consumed by roofs and stairs), one coincidence tolerance module replacing the five ad-hoc constants (NFR-ACC-003), storey commands that validate the elements linked to them (NFR-REL-005), the fallback representation for failed elements (NFR-REL-006), the clickable problems panel (UI-012) and format-version migration (IFX-062). It also ships the seeded fixture builder (v5 UUIDs from fixture names) and synthetic 1,000/5,000/20,000-element stand-ins that the regression epic benchmarks. Built first because columns, beams, openings, roofs, stairs, terrain, grids and 2D elements all register through it.

Risks: Largest refactor of the codebase; reduced by doing it before any new kind exists and by using the round-trip, golden, geometry and kittest suites as the net. Missed invalidations in incremental evaluation are caught by the incremental-versus-full property test. Fourteen requirements in 15 days only works because most are S-effort residuals; the beads split is registry+relations+codec first, evaluation+tolerance+residuals second.
design: archicraft-model: element.rs split into kinds/{wall,slab}.rs behind a KindDescriptor table (kinds/mod.rs); relations.rs with typed edges keyed by ElementId and integrity_problems(); tolerance.rs exporting MODEL_TOLERANCE with JOIN_TOLERANCE derived from it; NameCounters becomes a map keyed by kind code (schema.rs counters object opened); samples.rs grows a public builder with deterministic v5 ids and stand_in(n). archicraft-geometry: evaluate.rs gains evaluate_incremental(dirty) with per-element Arc<ElementGeometry> keyed by element revision; wall.rs/mesh.rs/slice.rs/plan.rs read the shared tolerance. archicraft-ifcx: per-kind attribute codec registered in alpha/schema.rs, alpha/writer.rs and alpha/reader.rs; parts() of a kind written as child nodes with class and v5 ids (generalises the Skin_n mechanism of IFX-017); migration table in alpha/mod.rs; predefined types declared in registry.rs. archicraft-app: document.rs caches per element and per storey instead of dropping all caches; ui/dialogs.rs problems panel becomes clickable. Headless crates stay free of UI dependencies (NFR-MNT-002/004); the registry is a plain table, not a plugin system (Section 8).
acceptance_criteria: A module-layout test adds a test-only dummy kind and asserts that only its own module plus one registry entry changed; a test-only compound kind writes Part_n children with their own IfcClass and v5 ids, round-trips and passes the conformance job (IFX-016 mechanism; roofs and stairs re-assert it with real elements); IfcClass covers the full D.5 list and slab/footing predefined types round-trip in archicraft:: (IFX-024); after one edit in the 5,000-element stand-in the dirty set contains only the edited element and its relation/contact neighbours and a property test compares incremental against full evaluation on random edit sequences (bit-identical); MODEL_TOLERANCE (0.01 mm) is the only tolerance constant in model, geometry and snapping (grep test); moving a storey below a linked wall's base is rejected with CommandError::Invalid; a deliberately panicking test kind renders as a fallback box, is pickable and appears in the problems panel whose click selects and zooms (kittest); a FORMAT_VERSION n-1 file migrates with a report; all existing golden files, round-trip tests and the conformance job stay green.
notes: SRS: ELM-011 ELM-006 STR-006 IFX-012 IFX-060 IFX-062 IFX-024 IFX-016 NFR-ACC-003 NFR-PERF-006 NFR-REL-005 NFR-REL-006 VIEW-001 UI-012

title: Build contour.rs: planar graph, edge chains and minimal regions
description:
WHY — INP-018 (S): with a creation tool active, a key switches to contour detection; clicking then previews and creates an element of the active kind from the clicked edge or chain of connected edges, or from the smallest closed region bounded by existing elements around the clicked point. SLB-003 (holes traced) and SLB-001 ('traced from them in one pick') rely on it, and roofs (ROF-004 pick a closed polygon), spaces and the 2D elements of drafting-trim-split reuse it. Gap row INP-018: missing, needs a planar graph and region detection from plan outlines.

WHAT — crates/archicraft-geometry/src/contour.rs (exported from lib.rs): a `trait PlanSegmentSource` whose first implementation reads a PlanDrawing (union of all cut polygons, projected and overhead lines, optionally wall reference lines); drafting-trim-split-04 implements it for 2D drafting curves; `ContourGraph::build(segments, options)` nodes all segments (proper intersections, collinear overlaps, endpoint merging within MODEL_TOLERANCE) into a half-edge structure; queries `region_at(p) -> Option<Region { outer, islands }>` (smallest bounded face containing p, antennas removed, enclosed components as islands) `edge_at(p, radius) -> Option<Chain>` (the nearest straight edge: the collinear run between corners or vertices of degree other than 2, for 'the clicked edge') and `chain_at(p, radius) -> Option<Chain { points, closed }>` (the nearest edge extended through degree-2 vertices, collinear runs merged, for 'a chain of connected edges'). The graph works in the 2D coordinates of any plane, so the 3D clause of INP-018 later only needs a segment source for a working plane. Add rstar (the 0.12 workspace entry of point-input-snapping-02, the version geo pins) to crates/archicraft-geometry/Cargo.toml. Add `samples::two_storey_shell_with_shaft()` to crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs: two_storey_shell plus four 0.115 m interior walls with centred reference lines on the upper storey enclosing a shaft at x 1.0-3.0, y 6.5-8.0, joined at the corners (not a golden model). Out of scope: tool integration (task 12), arc preservation (curved-geometry-08 fills the graph edges' source), 3D views (follow-up bead with the working plane of 3d-input-navigation).
design: Input: merge cut polygons with geo::unary_union across all materials so joined walls of different materials give one boundary (CutRegion merges only per material, geometry/plan.rs:150-160), then add the rings, the projected/overhead segments and, with ContourOptions.reference_lines, wall reference lines. Noding: bulk-load segment envelopes into rstar (the 0.12 version geo uses), split at proper intersections and at endpoints lying on other segments within MODEL_TOLERANCE, key vertices with tolerance.rs quantise() plus a neighbour-cell check against grid-boundary splits, drop zero-length and duplicate edges. Half-edges: sort outgoing edges by angle (ties within is_parallel() of tolerance.rs broken by length); next(e) = the edge preceding twin(e) in CCW order at e's head; positive-area cycles are bounded faces, negative ones are outer boundaries of components. region_at: bbox prefilter, point-in-ring, smallest area wins; islands are component boundaries inside that face and in no smaller face. Antennas: remove consecutive twin pairs (u->v, v->u) from face cycles. Chain: walk both directions from the nearest edge while the vertex degree is 2, then merge collinear edges; edge_at stops the walk at the first corner (non-collinear continuation) as well. Graph edges carry `source: Option<CurveRef>` (None now) so curved-geometry can rebuild arcs. The epic's named risk is near-coincident segments: every comparison uses MODEL_TOLERANCE and intersection points snap to existing vertices within it.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/contour.rs, ground storey of two_storey_shell: region_at((2, 3)) returns one ring on the interior faces of the exterior walls with the notch of the interior T wall, area 97.08875 m² ± 1e-6 (11.5 x 8.5 - 0.115 x 5.75), no islands.
- Upper storey of two_storey_shell_with_shaft: region_at((2, 7.25)) returns the rectangle of the shaft walls' inner faces (x 1.0575-2.9425, y 6.5575-7.9425) within MODEL_TOLERANCE; region_at((2, 3)) has exactly two islands, the projected stair-hole loop and the outer faces of the shaft walls (x 0.9425-3.0575, y 6.4425-8.0575); a point outside the building gives None.
- Ground storey: edge_at((2, 0.25)) returns the straight interior face of the south wall from (0.25, 0.25) to (4.9425, 0.25), ending at the face of the interior T wall; chain_at((2, 0.25)) returns the closed interior boundary of eight points (rectangle plus the T-wall notch). Upper storey: edge_at on the stair-hole loop returns one side, chain_at the closed chain of four points.
- Noding: two segments 5 µm apart merge (the region closes); a 20 µm gap leaves it open (None); collinear overlapping segments are deduplicated; two crossing walls give four regions; slab outlines coinciding with wall faces create no zero-area faces.
- Determinism: segments supplied in reversed order give identical regions; 10,000 random segments build without panic (no timing assertion).
- No SRS clause closes by itself; this is the geometry half of INP-018.
notes:
SRS: INP-018
(geometry half) Consumers: task 12, drafting-trim-split (2D lines as a source), roofs (ROF-004), could-scope-polish (spaces). Shaft fixture values: inner faces 1.885 x 1.385 m = 2.610725 m².

title: Add door fixtures at L and T junctions and the host-split check
design:
Fixtures come from the seeded builder (v5 UUIDs from fixture names), so their golden data are stable. Use the fixture ids dw-l, dw-t and dw-near next to F2 in the D.7-style registry.

Volume expectations come from the 2D footprint areas (geo) of the junction engine times the skin height, minus w x h x t_n per skin for the void. This independent arithmetic keeps the test from re-running the code under test.
acceptance_criteria:
- The three fixtures exist in the NFR-MNT-005 suite (or its interim file) and pass. Each skin body is closed, each skin's volume equals the junction-resolved footprint area x height minus the void share, and the L and T footprints outside the void are bit-identical to the same fixture without the door (epic risk, DW-009).
- dw_near_junction_window produces exactly one warning naming the window and the joined wall (03 clear-length check).
- At the T junction, the CycleHost test of task 07 runs on dw_t_junction: one key press moves the candidate from the through-wall to the abutting wall (DW-002).
- Split test (crates/archicraft-model/tests/inserts.rs or the drafting-trim-split test module): after the split, each door is hosted by the part that contains it, its absolute anchor point is unchanged, the written IFCX nests it under the new parent wall node, and undo restores the single wall with both doors (WAL-030 hook, DW-001, DW-018).
- If drafting-trim-split or junction-engine has not merged, a follow-up bead linked to it exists, to re-run the check through Command::Split or to move the cases into junctions.rs.
notes: SRS: DW-001 DW-002 DW-009 DW-018 (plus WAL-030, NFR-MNT-005, IFX-033). Junction regression suite owner: junction-engine (host-openings and this epic add cases).

title: Retarget relations and rehost hosted elements when elements are replaced
description:
WHY: WAL-030 (M): "Hosted elements stay with the part they lie in." WAL-031 (S) merges walls "keeping all hosted elements", a two-sided trim (EDT-011) replaces a wall by two parts, and EDT-013 splits of any element must keep the relations of the replaced element consistent. SRS 3.3 makes host, junction, trim, solid-operation and annotation-binding relations part of the model: element-kind-framework-08's RelationStore in crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs with Relation::{Host { hosted, host }, Junction { a, b }, Trim { target, by }, SolidOperation { target, operator }, AnnotationBinding { annotation, target }}. doors-windows-core-02 implements kinds::insert::rehost_inserts against the descriptor hook `rehost(&hosted, &parts)` prepared here and names relations::retarget_after_replace as the integration point; the epic risk says the hosted clause is verified with doors only later, through a test hook re-run by doors-windows-core.

WHAT: `relations::retarget_after_replace(project, old: ElementId, parts: &[Element]) -> Result<Vec<Edit>, CommandError>` in relations.rs: Host relations whose host is replaced dispatch to the hosted kind's new descriptor hook `rehost(&hosted, &parts) -> Option<Result<(usize, Element), String>>` (default: the part whose carrier or outline contains the hosted element's anchor, the hosted element unchanged; doors-windows-core plugs kinds::insert::rehost_inserts in here); a hosted element straddling the cut makes the hook return Err and the whole command is refused; other explicit relations (Trim, SolidOperation, AnnotationBinding, Junction) follow the part they touch (the part nearest to the relation's anchor, or the first part when the relation has no anchor); the edits are RemoveRelation/InsertRelation and ReplaceElement for rehosted elements, planned inside Command::plan. Command::Split (task 10) calls it for every split element after the parts are planned and before validation; tasks 11 (two-sided trim) and 12 (merge) reuse it. Out of scope: real hosted kinds (host-openings, doors-windows-core), the ELM-016 delete cascade.
design: Relations are retargeted, never dropped, and because the first part keeps the original id only relations whose anchor lies on a new part need edits, which keeps undo small. RelationId is v5 of variant and ends (element-kind-framework-08), so retargeted relations get deterministic new ids. The rehost hook lives on the hosted kind's descriptor, so this epic needs no knowledge of doors; the default covers the Dummy and anything hosted by a point anchor. Pitfalls: run validation after the hooks in the same plan so a rehosted element that becomes invalid rejects the whole command (doors-windows-core-02 relies on this order); a merge passes several old elements, so the function must work when called per old element against the same part list.
acceptance_criteria:
- Test split_keeps_hosted_elements_on_their_part (crates/archicraft-model/tests/linear_edit.rs, feature test-kinds): a Dummy hosted on the south wall through a Host relation at x = 8 is hosted on the second part after Command::Split with Cutter::Point((3, 0)), one at x = 1 stays on the first; undo restores both relations exactly; doors-windows-core-11 re-runs this test with a door.
- A Dummy whose footprint straddles x = 3 makes the split fail with the hook's message and leaves the project unchanged.
- retarget_after_replace unit tests with stub Trim, Junction and AnnotationBinding relations: each ends on the part that contains or is nearest to its anchor; relations not touching the replaced element are untouched; integrity_problems() is empty afterwards.
- Journal replay of a split with hosted elements yields identical relation ids (v5 of variant and ends).
- WAL-030's hosted-element clause satisfied through the hook (re-verified with doors by doors-windows-core); the relation half of EDT-013 satisfied.
notes:
SRS: WAL-030 EDT-013 (hosted elements and relations)
Integration contract with doors-windows-core: relations::retarget_after_replace and the rehost(&hosted, &parts) descriptor hook; doors-windows-core implements kinds::insert::rehost_inserts and re-runs split_keeps_hosted_elements_on_their_part with a door.

title: Edit polyline and spline nodes through the reshape palette
description:
WHY: The epic risk limits splines to "node editing only", so node editing has to exist for ANN-011's splines; ANN-001's polylines with straight and arc segments are edited like every other element (NFR-USE-002: the same node and edge commands in every tool; EDT-008's palette offers move, insert and delete node and curve or straighten edge). edit-reshape-palette implemented these operations for Outline-based kinds only (Command::Reshape with ReshapeOp and outline/edit.rs from edit-reshape-palette-03, the palette and part handles of edit-reshape-palette-07 in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/); DraftPolyline (PolyCurve) and DraftSpline (through points) are not Outlines.

WHAT: Model: the selection-part hooks of selection-transforms-01 for DraftPolyline (PartRef::Node { ring: 0, index } and PartRef::Edge { ring: 0, index }, part_label, part_anchor, part_outline, validate_part) and DraftSpline (Node only); the Kind::reshape hook of edit-reshape-palette-03 implemented for both: MoveNode, InsertNode (on an arc edge it splits the arc at the parameter into two arcs with the same centre and radius bits), DeleteNode (merging two co-circular arcs through Segment::join of task 01), MoveEdge, Straighten (arc to line) and CurveEdge { through } (an exact three-point arc, allowed for 2D polylines before curved-geometry enables it for slabs) on polylines; MoveNode, InsertNode and DeleteNode on splines (an inserted node lies on the curve at the picked parameter, so the shape changes only locally). Results go through validate_polycurve and the minimum node counts (two open, three closed). App: the palette and handles show these parts for the two kinds without new UI code, because they read part_refs and the op list per part. Out of scope: fillet and chamfer on polylines (EDT-014; curved-geometry-10 hooks the 2D polyline in), offset edge on open polylines.
design: Reusing ReshapeOp and the palette keeps one command set (NFR-USE-002); only the kind hooks are new. PartRef::Node/Edge with ring 0 matches the Outline addressing, so the handles code needs no special case. Pitfalls: indices refer to PolyCurve nodes and edges, never to tessellation vertices; a closed polyline's last edge wraps to node 0; after DeleteNode the follow-up part is recomputed (the edit-reshape-palette-03 rule).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/reshape.rs (edit-reshape-palette-03): move, insert and delete node on a polyline and a spline with undo restoring the project exactly; deleting below two nodes (open) or three (closed) is rejected with the outline message; CurveEdge on a polyline edge stores an exact arc through the picked point (centre within 1e-12) and Straighten restores the straight edge; InsertNode on an arc edge gives two arcs whose centre and radius bits equal the original, and DeleteNode of that node restores one arc.
- A spline after InsertNode keeps all previous through points bitwise.
- kittest: clicking a node of a selected polyline opens the palette with Move node, Insert node and Delete node; clicking an edge offers Curve edge and Straighten.
- ANN-011's node editing for splines and the NFR-USE-002 node and edge commands for 2D polylines satisfied.
notes: SRS: ANN-011 ANN-001 (node editing of splines and polylines)

title: Split element kinds into a KindDescriptor registry
description:
WHY: SRS 3.2 gives every element a kind (the tool that created it). ELM-011 (M): every element has an IFC class defaulted by its kind (Table 5-1) with a per-kind set of selectable classes. ELM-006 (M): the top of vertical elements (walls, columns, curtain walls, stairs, storey-spanning openings) is a fixed height or linked to a storey, absolute or relative to the home storey, plus an offset, and linked elements follow storey changes; STR-006 (M) requires the same for storey edits. Today ElementKind and KindTag are closed enums (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:186-277) matched in project.rs:245-260 (vertical_extent) and :270-279 (next_element_name), validate.rs:243-282 (validate_element), command.rs:399-433 (rehome, relink_to_storey) and :435-482 (plan_delete_storey, linked tops at :457-468), and again in the geometry, IFCX and app crates; NameCounters {wall, slab} (project.rs:153-157) is hard-wired in command.rs:331-334, writer.rs:188 and reader.rs:406-409. The technical-debt list calls this a cross-crate shotgun change for every new kind; columns, beams, openings, roofs, stairs, terrain, grids and 2D elements must each register through one module, selection-transforms plans transforms through a per-kind hook, and the compound kinds need a part list. Status: ELM-006 is partial: TopLink { Fixed, Storey, Relative } plus offset (element.rs:69-79), top_elevation (project.rs:236-242), the Top fields of the properties panel (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:325-436), the DeleteStorey fixed-height rule (command.rs:457-468) and the persistence (writer.rs:76-82, reader.rs:154-167) exist for walls only; missing is one link type and hook set that columns, curtain walls, stairs and storey-spanning openings reuse. STR-006 is done for walls and slabs (storey-relative data resolved at evaluation time, project.rs:236-260; test storey_changes_move_linked_walls, tests/commands.rs:148-168): this task keeps that behaviour, moves it behind the kind hooks and regresses it with the existing tests plus a generic dummy test. ELM-011 is partial: the per-kind class sets exist as KindTag::ifc_classes (element.rs:226-232), checked in validate.rs:256-262 and command.rs:567-571; they move into the descriptor here (D.5 list and predefined types in task 05).

WHAT: Create crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/{mod.rs,wall.rs,slab.rs,dummy.rs}; element.rs keeps the Element envelope, IfcClass (plus a new BuildingElementProxy variant as the dummy's default), Position and TopLink. kinds/mod.rs holds one kinds! macro invocation listing every kind once (wall => Wall, slab => Slab, #[cfg(feature = "test-kinds")] dummy => Dummy) that generates ElementKind (serde variant names unchanged), KindTag (Ord, ALL, from_code, descriptor()), KINDS: &[&KindDescriptor], the Element::as_<kind>() accessors and the delegating ElementKind methods; mark ElementKind and KindTag #[non_exhaustive]. Each payload implements trait Kind in its own module: const DESCRIPTOR: KindDescriptor { label, code, name_prefix, default_class, ifc_classes, has_tool }, and hooks material/set_material, validate (normalising), transform(&PlanTransform) -> Result<(), TransformError> (MoveElements goes through it), vertical_extent (home, &StoreyList), storey_links() -> Vec<StoreyLinkRef>, rehome, relink, unlink_storey, parts() -> Vec<PartSpec { role, class, label }> (default empty, consumed by tasks 15 and 07; the dummy's parts() stays empty until task 15 because IfcMember and IfcPlate arrive with task 05), container() -> Container { Storey, Site } (default Storey, consumed by task 07) and plan_bounds() (consumed by task 13). A shared VerticalLink { base_offset, top: TopLink } with resolution helpers serves Wall and Dummy and is the type columns, curtain walls, stairs and openings reuse (ELM-006). NameCounters becomes a map keyed by KindTag with next()/bump(); the writer still writes counters for every kind with has_tool plus any non-zero counter, so files stay byte-identical, and the reader maps keys by kind code. Replace the matches in project.rs, validate.rs, command.rs (counters, MoveElements, rehome, relink_to_storey, the DeleteStorey linked-top rule) by descriptor and hook calls. The test kind Dummy { origin, size, link: VerticalLink, material, parts, panic_on_evaluate, site_level } (prefix "X") sits behind a cargo feature test-kinds, enabled for the crate's own tests through a self dev-dependency. Because the enums are #[non_exhaustive], geometry, IFCX and app matches get wildcard arms (geometry: GeometryError::UnsupportedKind listed as a problem; writer: element saved without kind attribute and a warning; properties: common fields only) that the registries of tasks 06 and 15 replace. Create the module-layout test. Out of scope: tool defaults by kind (task 04), the D.5 class list and predefined types (task 05), the IFCX and geometry registries (tasks 06, 15), any real new kind.
design: Keep the enum for serde, PartialEq and typed access, move behaviour into a trait per payload, and generate enum, tag, table and delegation from one macro invocation, so adding a kind is one new module plus one macro line. The registry is a static table of 'static descriptors, not a plugin system (Section 8). Trait hooks take a &StoreyList rather than &Project where storeys matter, so task 09 can validate against a proposed storey list. Feature instead of #[cfg(test)] because cfg(test) is per crate and the dummy must be visible to downstream tests; cargo only unifies dev-dependency features into test builds, so release binaries never contain it (state this in kinds/mod.rs; if the self dev-dependency proves awkward, CI can run cargo test --workspace --features test-kinds instead). Pitfalls: with test-kinds unified into a workspace test build, every exhaustive match downstream stops compiling, hence #[non_exhaustive] and the temporary wildcard arms; the counters writer must not emit a dummy key unless a dummy exists, or golden bytes would differ between test and release builds; keep the archicraft_model::{Wall, Slab, ...} re-export paths; IFCX does not use serde for elements, so the file format is untouched; properties.rs, tools.rs and workspace.rs keep their ToolKind-to-KindTag mapping (a tool concern). Pointers: element.rs:186-307, project.rs:153-157/236-322, validate.rs:243-282, command.rs:150-160/320-342/399-482, writer.rs:188, reader.rs:406-409.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test --workspace, clippy --all-targets and fmt green; golden files bit-identical; the four kittests pass.
- Registry tests: KINDS has wall and slab in release builds and also dummy with test-kinds; codes, labels and name prefixes are unique; KindTag::from_code(descriptor.code) round-trips; every default_class is in its ifc_classes.
- Module-layout test crates/archicraft-model/tests/module_layout.rs: the identifiers Dummy and "dummy" occur in crates/archicraft-model/src only in kinds/dummy.rs and in exactly one line of kinds/mod.rs, and nowhere in crates/archicraft-app/src; the test takes a list of crate roots so tasks 06 and 07 add archicraft-ifcx and archicraft-geometry.
- Source scan: ElementKind::Wall( and ElementKind::Slab( occur in crates/archicraft-model/src only under kinds/ and in #[cfg(test)] code.
- Dummy flow test (crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs, test-kinds): AddElements names it X-001 and bumps only its counter; UpdateElements, MoveElements, DeleteElements, undo and redo restore the exact project; a Dummy with an IFC class outside its descriptor set is rejected with CommandError::Invalid.
- Generic storey following (ELM-006, STR-006 regression): for each top link (Fixed height, Storey(first floor), Relative(+1), each with a non-zero offset) a dummy's vertical_extent equals a wall's with the same base offset and link; after SetStoreyElevation and SetStoreyHeight (shift_above true and false) Storey- and Relative-linked tops follow by exactly the storey change while Fixed tops stay at base + height, and every base (wall, slab, dummy) follows its home storey's elevation; DeleteStorey of the storey a dummy is linked to keeps its current top as a fixed height; relink_to_storey keeps the dummy's absolute position.
- Transform hook: rotating a wall 90 degrees about a point and mirroring a slab produce the expected coordinates, the mirrored slab outline stays counter-clockwise with clockwise holes; the dummy returns TransformError::Unsupported for a mirror (the refusal path selection-transforms needs); MoveElements behaviour unchanged.
- Existing tests storey_changes_move_linked_walls, relinking_keeps_the_absolute_position, deleting_a_storey_can_keep_its_elements, add_undo_redo_keeps_identity and invalid_commands_leave_the_project_unchanged pass unchanged; ELM-011 'defaulted by its kind' is descriptor.default_class, used by validate.rs and the reader's downgrade path instead of literal matches.
notes: SRS: ELM-011 ELM-006 STR-006. Appendix D.2 defaults stay in template.rs. The dummy's parts, panic_on_evaluate and site_level flags are consumed by tasks 15, 07 and 13. Downstream epics extend KindDescriptor with field specs (properties-and-dialogs), reshape (edit-reshape-palette) and PartRef (selection-transforms).

title: Write and read 2D elements in IFCX with optional IfcAnnotation curves
description:
WHY: IFX-060 (M) requires everything needed to restore the editable model in archicraft:: attributes, which for ANN-001 and ANN-002 means the geometry, pen, line type, view and layer of every 2D element. ANN-010 (C): "2D construction geometry may be written to IFCX as IfcAnnotation curves (Table 5-1). Text and dimensions are stored in the ArchiCraft namespace only." Table 5-1 maps '2D construction geometry, annotation' to IfcAnnotation, container Storey, representation Curves. NFR-ACC-002: parameters are written with round-trip precision; only mesh and curve coordinates are rounded to 10⁻⁶ m (IFX-007). IFX-062: files written by a newer format open with a warning. Epic acceptance: "2D elements round-trip in the archicraft:: namespace and optionally as IfcAnnotation curves". Gap row ANN-010 (missing): the writer already has a curve helper (curve_attribute, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:229, used for wall axes at :387) but writes no IfcAnnotation.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/drafting.rs with KindCodec implementations (element-kind-framework-06's codec registry, one codecs! line each) for line, arc and polyline: attributes `archicraft::line` {a, b}, `archicraft::arc` {centre, radius, startAngle, sweep}, `archicraft::polyline` {points, edges: [{type: 'straight'} | {type: 'arc', centre, radius, startAngle, sweep}], closed} and the shared `archicraft::drafting` {view: {type: 'plan', storey}, pen, lineType}, declared through the codec schema (emitted only when such elements exist) and written at full precision (no round_coordinate). Nodes are children of their storey with bsi::ifc::class IfcAnnotation. New project setting `ProjectSettings.export.annotation_curves: bool` (default true, #[serde(default)], written in archicraft::project, checkbox 'Write 2D construction geometry as IfcAnnotation curves' in the Project settings dialog of crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs, applied through Command::SetSettings): when on, each 2D node gets a `Curve` child (sub_node_id(owner, 'Curve'), Curve_n for several rings) whose usd::usdgeom::basiscurves points come from curve_attribute applied to ModelGeometry::curve(key) at z = 0 in storey coordinates, closed curves repeating their first point. Curve children are written only for kinds whose codec opts in (the drafting codecs), so the text and dimension kinds of sections-elevations-dims stay archicraft-only as ANN-010 demands. The writer stops warning 'saved without a body' for has_body = false kinds. Reader: rebuilds 2D elements from archicraft:: attributes only (Curve children are derived and ignored); a missing or screen-only pen falls back to the first drafting-role pen and a missing line type to SOLID, each with a warning (plan-attributes-04's repair rule). Add samples::drafting_sample() (built with element-kind-framework-03's FixtureBuilder: a line, a chain line-arc-line, a closed polyline with an arc edge, the three-point arc (0,0)/(1,1)/(2,0) and a circle by centre and radius) to samples::catalogue(), which feeds samples() in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs and crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs, and bless tests/golden/drafting.ifcx. Bump FORMAT_VERSION with a no-op step in alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework-12), following step 5 of the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md: an older release would drop the new kinds silently, while the bump makes it open the file with the IFX-062 warning. Out of scope: splines and fills (07 and 09 extend the codec), text and dimensions (sections-elevations-dims), the section view variant (sections-elevations-dims-02).
design: One source of truth: archicraft:: attributes restore the element (IFX-060); the IfcAnnotation class plus Curve child is a derived, optional representation for third-party viewers (ANN-010), so the reader never parses basiscurves. The node stays an element node with bsi::ifc::class in both modes (IFX-020 holds); only the geometry child is optional. Curve points come from the ModelGeometry cache built in 04: the writer must not call tessellate() itself, otherwise the bit-identity contract would depend on two call sites. The bundled usd schema declares basiscurves with `points` only (one polyline per attribute), hence one Curve child per ring. Pitfalls: the IFX-038 limit of 65,535 points also bounds curves (assert it); keep the child-key scheme `<Kind>_<8 hex>` (IFX-014); run ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 and conformance/run.sh as the extension point says; never regenerate the frozen format-v1 fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs: drafting_sample saves and loads to an equal project (PartialEq) and every Arc field is bit-identical after the round trip (to_bits), including centre (1, 0), radius 1 and sweep −π of the three-point arc; catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files covers drafting.ifcx.
- Golden drafting.ifcx blessed with a reviewed diff; saving twice is byte-identical (IFX-007); conformance/run.sh passes on all golden files; the existing golden files change only by the FORMAT_VERSION bump and the new archicraft::project export setting.
- With annotation_curves on, every 2D node has class IfcAnnotation and Curve children whose points equal ModelGeometry::curve(key) rounded to 10⁻⁶ (one producer); with it off no Curve child is written and the file still round-trips; the setting round-trips and undo restores it; a body-less test-kinds element without an opting-in codec gets no Curve child (the archicraft-only rule that text and dimensions inherit).
- A file whose 2D element references an unknown pen loads with a warning and a drafting-role pen; the frozen format-v1 fixture still loads through the migration chain; a file whose format version exceeds FORMAT_VERSION sets newer_format.
- kittest: the Project settings dialog shows the annotation-curves checkbox and toggling it with OK is one undo step.
- ANN-010 satisfied; the persistence clauses of ANN-001/ANN-002 (pen, line type, view, layer stored in archicraft::) satisfied.
notes:
SRS: ANN-010 ANN-001 ANN-002 (persistence)
Open question: default of annotation_curves (true chosen because Table 5-1 lists IfcAnnotation for 2D construction geometry; viewers then show construction lines at storey level).

title: Persist repair thresholds in IFCX and list repairs in the problems panel
description:
WHY — EDT-019 (M): both repair thresholds are project settings (Appendix D.1), so they must be saved with the project and editable, and edges shorter than 0.1 mm or sliver angles below 0.1° that result from editing are repaired automatically or listed in the problems panel (UI-012). EDT-018 (M): any remaining invalid element is listed in the problems panel. What exists and stays: the Project settings dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:485-626) with widgets::length and widgets::angle (ui/widgets.rs:63, 80), the archicraft::project attribute (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:154-165, alpha/schema.rs), invalid loaded elements skipped with an error (alpha/reader.rs:724-729) and the problems panel with its Geometry, References and File sections driven by the ProblemSource enum of element-kind-framework-14 (dialogs.rs:848-883), which reserves EDT-019 repair entries for this epic. Missing (gap row EDT-019): nothing is written to IFCX, the dialog has no fields and repairs are not reported. Task 02 delivered RepairThresholds, repair_outline and History::last_notes().

WHAT — IFCX: an optional `repair { minEdgeLength, minCornerAngle }` member of archicraft::project (declaration in alpha/schema.rs, writer project attribute, reader defaulting silently to D.1 when absent and range-checking with a warning); the reader runs repair_outline on every slab outline it loads and reports each repair as a Warning problem whose path is the element UUID; unrepairable elements stay skipped with an error (reader.rs:724-729). App: a 'Geometry repair' section with 'Minimum edge length' and 'Minimum corner angle' in the Project settings dialog, committed through Command::SetSettings; Workspace::execute (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:123-130) shows History::last_notes() as an info status and appends Repair notes to a session repair log; the problems panel gains `ProblemSource::Repair` with a 'Repairs' section of clickable '<name>: <message>' entries (a click selects and zooms through the Request::ZoomTo of element-kind-framework-14) kept until the element changes again or the log is cleared; the status-bar problem count (ui/shell.rs:177-190) includes them. Out of scope: the repair pipeline itself (task 02); the zero-thickness-skin and profile clauses of EDT-018 (layer-structures, profiles-columns-beams).
design: Optional member, so no FORMAT_VERSION bump (rule documented in alpha/mod.rs by element-kind-framework-12: optional additions need neither a bump nor a migration); follow the pattern point-input-snapping-16 uses for its project-settings member. Load-time repair goes through the same repair_outline as commands, so a file and an edit never disagree about validity. The session repair log lives in the Workspace (not in the project, never undone); an entry is dropped when its element changes or disappears. Pointers: dialogs.rs:485-626 and 848-883; workspace.rs:123-130; shell.rs:177-190; alpha/schema.rs project declaration; writer.rs:154-165; reader.rs:724-729; tests/roundtrip.rs:48.
acceptance_criteria:
- IFCX: the thresholds round-trip exactly; a file without them reads the D.1 defaults without a problem; a file whose slab outline has a 0.05 mm edge loads repaired with one warning carrying the element UUID path; a file whose slab outline intersects itself loads without that slab and lists it as a clickable entry in the problems panel's File section (EDT-018 'remaining invalid element' regression); round_trip_restores_the_editable_model passes; the golden files crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx are re-blessed once with only the archicraft::project addition in the reviewed diff; conformance/run.sh is green.
- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): the Project settings dialog shows 'Minimum edge length' 0.1 mm and 'Minimum corner angle' 0.10°; changing the edge length is one undo step; after an UpdateElements that removes a 0.05 mm edge the status line reports the repair, the problems panel lists '<name>: removed 1 edge shorter than 0.1 mm' under 'Repairs' and clicking it selects the element; editing that element again removes the entry.
- Then satisfied: EDT-019; EDT-018 except the zero-thickness-skin clause (layer-structures) and profile polygons (profiles-columns-beams).
notes:
SRS: EDT-018 EDT-019
Appendix D.1 defaults: 0.1 mm and 0.1°. Task 10 depends on this task so that the two golden re-blesses do not collide.

title: Evaluate, plan and pick 2D curves and register them as a contour source
description:
WHY: ANN-001 requires 2D elements to appear in plan views; ANN-002 (M): "They act as tracing input for contour detection (INP-018)". The epic acceptance requires that 2D elements "register as a segment source of the contour detection built in edit-reshape-palette, so a slab is traced from a closed chain of 2D lines in one pick" and that "two producers tessellating the same curve id yield bit-identical vertex lists". Today ElementGeometry has only parts and axis (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:32-36) and PlanElement (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:23) knows only cut and projected bodies; edit-reshape-palette-06's contour.rs offers a registration point for further segment sources and reserves `source: Option<CurveRef>` on its graph edges.

WHAT: Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/drafting.rs implementing element-kind-framework-07's GeometryKind for the three drafting kinds (one table line each) and returning `ElementGeometry { parts: [], axis: [], curves }`, where the new field `curves: Vec<Vec<DVec2>>` is filled by tessellate() with project.settings.tessellation and shared through the per-element Arc<ElementGeometry> of the incremental evaluator; `CurveKey { element: ElementId, index: u32 }` and `ModelGeometry::curve(key) -> Option<&[DVec2]>` are the single curve-id lookup every later producer uses (plan, snapping, IFCX writer, curved-geometry's arc walls and slab rings); body-less kinds get no fallback box (element-kind-framework-13) and never reach the 3D scene. Plan: plan.rs adds `PlanElement.drafting: Option<DraftingPlan { curves: Vec<CurveKey>, pen, line_type }>` (points resolved through ModelGeometry, not re-tessellated), added only to the PlanDrawing of the element's view storey and outside the z-extent/view-range classification; segments(), hit(), in_rect(), bounds() and pick() include them, with arc hit-testing against the exact circle (Segment::param_of), not the chords; layer visibility applies as for other elements. Contour: register drafting curves at contour.rs's segment-source registration point: lines as straight segments, arcs as their tessellated pieces with the graph edges' `source` filled as CurveRef { key: CurveKey, segment: Segment, piece: u32 }, so curved-geometry-08 can restore the arcs. Out of scope: drawing, snapping and tool-level tracing (16), IFCX (05), splines (07), fills (09).
design: One tessellation producer: only kinds/drafting.rs (and later curved-geometry's kinds) calls tessellate() for element curves; plan.rs, the snap source (16) and the IFCX writer (05) read ModelGeometry::curve(key), which makes the bit-identity contract hold by construction. The curve cache lives inside the per-element Arc<ElementGeometry> of element-kind-framework-10, so unchanged elements keep their tessellation and the dirty set governs re-tessellation. curves is a Vec<Vec<DVec2>> rather than Arc<[DVec2]> to avoid a second Arc next to curve::Arc. Plan inclusion: 2D elements bypass the z-extent/display-range path (they have no vertical extent) and are added by view binding. Contour graph: feed arc pieces, not one chord per arc, because a full circle's chord degenerates; the CurveRef source lets curved-geometry merge pieces back into arcs (outline/recover.rs of curved-geometry-01). Pitfalls: fallback-box construction must skip has_body = false kinds instead of building a zero-height box; never classify 2D curves as projected or overhead lines.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: a full-circle DraftArc of r = 1 m yields 50 distinct points and r = 0.5 m yields 36 under the defaults; after Command::SetSettings with a 0.001 m chord deviation the next evaluate_incremental re-tessellates every drafting element (element-kind-framework-10's settings stamp) and r = 1 m yields 71.
- Curve-id test: for the same CurveKey, ModelGeometry::curve and the points the PlanDrawing exposes are bit-identical (f64::to_bits), and two independent evaluations give bit-identical lists.
- Plan tests: a 2D line homed on the ground storey is in the ground plan and absent from the upper plan for every cut-plane and view-range setting; a pick within the pick radius hits a line and the true arc of a circle (a point 10 px inside the circle is not a hit, a point on the circle between two tessellation vertices is); marquee containment selects them; a hidden layer hides them; no BodyPart, fallback box or 3D scene block exists for a drafting element.
- Contour tests (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/contour.rs): four DraftLines forming a 4 × 3 m rectangle on an empty storey give region_at(centre) = the 4-node ring with exact coordinates; a closed chain of two lines and one arc gives a region whose arc side carries CurveRef sources with the arc's key; a DraftLine from (2.5, −1) to (2.5, 10) on the ground storey of two_storey_shell shrinks region_at((2, 3)) to the part west of x = 2.5.
- cargo test, clippy --all-targets and fmt green; golden files byte-identical.
- Geometry half of ANN-001 (plan presence) and the contour-source half of ANN-002's tracing clause satisfied.
notes: SRS: ANN-001 ANN-002 (geometry, plan presence, picking and the contour-source half of the tracing clause)

title: Cache plans and 3D scene blocks per storey and element
description:
WHY: VIEW-001 (M): all views derive from the single model and an edit in one view appears in all open views (NFR-PERF-006). NFR-PERF-006 (M): the plan view and the 3D view update within 200 ms after a single-element edit. VIEW-001 is partial: propagation is correct (all panes draw from Workspace.doc, crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:728-734; test geometry_and_plans_follow_the_model, document.rs:180) but not within a verified budget. Today Document::geometry clears every plan on any revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103), and the 3D view rebuilds the whole scene, computing triangle normals and feature_edges for every part (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-176), whenever SceneKey { revision, selection } (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:44-47) changes, so even a selection click recomputes every element's edges.

WHAT: Document::geometry uses evaluate_incremental (task 10); plan caches are invalidated only for changed_storeys and the home storeys of changed or removed elements, and fully on layer, material or settings edits (visibility and cut fills depend on them); Document::last_change() exposes the changed ids. render3d.rs gains a SceneCache of per-element blocks (triangle positions with normals and feature edges in storey-local f64) keyed by the Arc pointer of the element's geometry; build_scene concatenates cached blocks, applying offset, origin and colour at assembly, so selection and hover only recolour; SceneKey is split into geometry revision and selection. The GPU upload of the assembled buffers stays whole. Out of scope: per-element GPU buffers and partial upload (perf-tuning-rm-m-l), frame-time instrumentation and the CI gate (regression-and-status), plan drawing of other storeys' elements (plan-views-browser).
design: Cache f64 storey-local data per element and convert to f32 relative to the scene origin during assembly, so a moving origin (it is the rounded centre of the bounds) never invalidates blocks. Key blocks by Arc::as_ptr plus the element id and drop blocks of removed elements. Colour is per assembly, never cached. Plan invalidation errs on the side of regenerating a whole storey because cut regions merge neighbours. Pitfalls: Document::geometry is called lazily from several panels in one frame, take the Arc once per frame; kittest has no wgpu, so scene tests run on build_scene and the cache directly; the hover path is currently dead code (technical debt), do not revive it here. Pointers: document.rs:95-121, view3d.rs:195-220, render3d.rs:102-176, workspace.rs:42-47.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document test: after one edit on two_storey_shell only the edited storey's PlanDrawing is regenerated (Arc::ptr_eq on the other storey's plan); geometry_and_plans_follow_the_model and dirty_tracking_follows_undo still pass.
- SceneCache test: after one edit the number of recomputed blocks equals the number of changed elements; a selection change recomputes no block; the assembled vertex arrays equal the pre-cache build_scene output for both samples.
- kittest with a plan pane and a 3D pane open: an edit made in the plan view (a wall drawn with the wall tool) and an edit made in the properties panel (wall thickness) each change the plan pane's drawing and the 3D pane's scene key in the same frame, both read from the one Document (VIEW-001 'an edit in one view appears in all open views').
- Timing smoke test (#[ignore], release): on stand_in(5_000), one wall move followed by geometry, the affected plan and scene assembly completes under 200 ms of CPU time; the numbers are printed for regression-and-status.
- cargo test, clippy and fmt green; VIEW-001 propagation verified with per-element and per-storey caches; NFR-PERF-006 CPU path in place.
notes: SRS: VIEW-001 NFR-PERF-006. The whole-buffer GPU upload may still dominate on RM-L; perf-tuning-rm-m-l owns that, regression-and-status measures it.

title: Migrate files written by older ArchiCraft format versions
description:
WHY: IFX-062 (M): the ArchiCraft schema carries a format version; on opening, files written by older versions are migrated; files written by a newer version open with a warning and are not overwritten without explicit confirmation.
