FORMAT_VERSION = 1 exists (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:15, written at writer.rs:147), the newer-version warning and the overwrite prompt exist (reader.rs:307-316, crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:190-192/601-615, test newer_format_versions_are_flagged at tests/roundtrip.rs:331-338), but there is no version-dispatched conversion and no test (gap: 'the hook and its test are missing'). The registry creates the first real need: the flat toolDefaults slot mixes common fields (layer, position, ifcClass, predefinedType) with kind parameters and collides as soon as a kind has a parameter of the same name, such as a column's plan position.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs: Migration { from, description, apply: fn(&mut IfcxFile, &mut Vec<Problem>) }, MIGRATIONS in order, and migrate(&mut IfcxFile, &mut Vec<Problem>) -> Option<MigrationReport { from, to, steps }>; the reader runs parse, migrate, validate, read (it validates first today, reader.rs:735-737), and after migrating replaces the file's archicraft:: schema entries with the current declarations so validation checks the migrated data. Each step adds an Info problem 'migrated ArchiCraft format n to n+1: <description>'; ReadOutcome.migrated carries the report; the app shows it in the existing load-report prompt and the status line. Migration 1 to 2: every toolDefaults slot becomes { layer, position, ifcClass, predefinedType, parameters: { kind parameters } } (the codec slot functions of task 06 read and write the new shape) and the counters declaration is opened to an object without fixed members whose keys are kind codes; FORMAT_VERSION = 2. Freeze crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/format-v1/walls-and-slab.ifcx as a copy of the golden at the start of this task and never regenerate it. alpha/mod.rs documents the rule: bump FORMAT_VERSION and add a migration whenever a reader-visible shape changes; optional additions need neither. Goldens re-blessed. Out of scope: successor IFCX versions (IFX-090/IFX-091), a migration UI beyond the report, third-party files.
design: Migrations work on the parsed container (serde_json values) before flattening, so they are schema-level transformations independent of model types (NFR-MNT-004) and each is a pure, separately tested function. Replacing the archicraft:: schema entries after migrating is required, otherwise the old in-file schema rejects the new shape. Keep the newer-version path untouched. Pitfalls: copy the v1 fixture before re-blessing anything in this task; keep formatVersion a String as today; dataVersion (O-16) is a save counter unrelated to formatVersion; a test-kinds build must migrate a v1 file to the same bytes as a release build (content-derived declarations of task 06). Pointers: schema.rs:15/97-125/195-210, writer.rs:97-120/147-190, reader.rs:301-316/433-497/735-760, app.rs:155-192/601-615, tests/roundtrip.rs:331-338.
acceptance_criteria:
- format_v1_files_migrate_with_a_report: loading the frozen v1 fixture yields a project equal to loading the current golden walls-and-slab.ifcx, migrated == Some(report) with from 1, to 2 and one step, exactly one Info problem and no warning or error; saving it writes formatVersion "2" and nested slots, byte-equal to the current golden apart from header fields.
- migrations_are_contiguous: MIGRATIONS[i].from == i + 1 and the last from == FORMAT_VERSION - 1; every migration has a unit test on a minimal synthetic file.
- newer_format_versions_are_flagged still passes (version 99 flagged, project loaded, newer_format true); a missing or non-numeric formatVersion still loads with the existing warning and no migration.
- Golden files re-blessed (formatVersion 2, nested slots) and reviewed; conformance/run.sh, container_matches_the_ifcx_json_schema and written_files_validate_without_problems green.
- Newer-file protection regressed (existing app.rs:190-192/601-615): an app test opens a version-99 file, Save raises Prompt::OverwriteNewer and writes nothing, Cancel leaves the file byte-identical, 'Save anyway' writes it.
- App test: opening a migrated file shows the load report with the migration line, the document is not flagged newer_format and saving needs no confirmation.
- IFX-062 fully satisfied: older files migrate with a report, newer files warn and require confirmation before being overwritten.
notes: SRS: IFX-062. Also prepares IFX-090 (every version earlier releases wrote stays readable); the successor-adapter work stays with its owning epic.

title: Add the single circle-anchored tessellate(curve, settings) function
description:
WHY: The epic provides the one tessellation function that arc walls, slab rings, plan cuts and the IFCX writer reuse, so curved-geometry and fixture F8 (Appendix D.7: "Curved wall with a slab traced from its reference line, then from its core face: zero gaps") are not a retrofit; the epic acceptance requires that a three-point arc "tessellates per the IFX-034 settings" and that "two producers tessellating the same curve id yield bit-identical vertex lists". ANN-001 arcs and circles must be drawn. Appendix D.1 and IFX-034 (owned by curved-geometry) set 2 mm chord deviation and at most 10° per segment (at least 36 segments per circle); the values are stored in ProjectSettings.tessellation (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:27-43, Tessellation { chord_deviation, max_angle_deg }) but unused (technical-debt entry 'Tessellation settings ... unused because no curved geometry exists'). curved-geometry-03 specifies the station rule this function must follow (a circle-anchored grid, so sub-arcs and reversed arcs of one circle share vertices bit for bit); implementing it here means curved-geometry-03 only verifies it and adds tessellate_outline and smooth strips.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs exported from lib.rs: `pub enum TessCurve<'a> { Segment(&'a Segment), Poly(&'a PolyCurve) }` (task 07 adds Spline; named TessCurve so it does not clash with the CurveRef that edit-reshape-palette-06 reserves on contour graph edges), `pub fn circle_segments(radius: f64, settings: &Tessellation) -> usize` and `pub fn tessellate(curve: TessCurve<'_>, settings: &Tessellation) -> Vec<DVec2>`. Rule: n = max(ceil(360 / max_angle_deg), ceil(π / acos(1 − chord_deviation / r))) with 1 − δ/r clamped to [−1, 1]; the stations of an arc are the grid angles θ_k = 2πk/n lying strictly inside the arc's angular interval (taken from Arc::canonical()), plus the arc's own end points; every point comes from Arc::point_on(centre, radius, θ); clockwise arcs are emitted in canonical order and reversed. Lines yield their two end points; a PolyCurve concatenates its edges with the joint vertices taken verbatim from PolyCurve.points (never derived arc ends); closed curves and full circles do not repeat the first point. The module doc states the contract: a pure, deterministic function of the curve parameters and the settings, no caching here (the per-curve-id cache is task 04). Out of scope: callers (04, 05, 16), splines (07), the maximum-segment-angle field in the project dialog and smooth mesh strips (curved-geometry-03 with IFX-034).
design: Anchoring stations to the circle rather than to the arc's start makes every arc of the same circle (a wall reference line, the slab edge traced from it, a sub-arc after a trim) share its interior vertices bit for bit, which F8's zero-gap clause and SLB-004's 'tessellated identically' need later; evaluating end points with the same point_on keeps joints exact. The function stores nothing; callers cache by curve id (task 04), so plan, snapping and export read one list. Keep Tessellation in archicraft-model (no new dependency direction) and convert max_angle_deg with to_radians() once. Do not use lyon here: lyon strokes plan lines in the renderer (technology choices 'Plan views: lyon'), while model curve tessellation must be renderer-independent. Pitfalls: r < δ/2 makes acos undefined (clamp, leaving the angle limit); a station within 1e-12 rad of an end point is dropped so no zero-length segment appears; NaN parameters are rejected upstream by validate_arc.
acceptance_criteria:
- circle_segments with the defaults: r = 0.5 m gives 36, r = 1 m gives 50, r = 5 m gives 112, r = 6 m gives 122 and r = 10 m gives 158 (the curved-geometry-03 values); with max_angle_deg = 5 r = 0.5 m gives 72; with chord_deviation 0.001 m r = 1 m gives 71.
- A 90° arc of r = 1 m from 0 to π/2 yields 14 points (12 interior grid stations every 7.2° plus both ends); its sub-arc from 30° to 60° has every interior station bit-identical (f64::to_bits) to a station of the full arc; the reversed arc yields the reversed list bitwise.
- Property test over seeded random arcs with radii 0.05-100 m: every chord's sagitta is <= δ + 1e-12 and every angular step is <= θmax + 1e-12, the short first and last steps included.
- Bit identity: tessellate() called twice is identical; a PolyCurve's joint vertices equal its nodes bitwise; the first and last points of an open arc equal Arc::point_on at its start and end angles.
- A line is never subdivided; a line-arc-line PolyCurve yields its node count plus the interior stations of the arc.
- cargo test, clippy --all-targets and fmt green; no other crate changes behaviour.
notes:
SRS: ANN-001 (drawing of arcs and circles)
IFX-034 itself, including the dialog field for the maximum segment angle, is owned by curved-geometry-03, which reuses this function; this task only consumes the settings. Appendix D.1: 2 mm, 10°, at least 36 segments per circle.

title: Doors and windows in walls
description:
Place doors and windows as hosted elements with host-candidate cycling, exterior side, opening configuration, anchors, reveal offsets from faces or core faces, pinned-edge vertical position, live width and height edits, empty openings, IfcDoor/IfcWindow export with Void and parts, and the view option to hide them or show schematic versus detailed. Units in arc walls (DW-019) follow in curved-geometry.

Risks: Interaction with the junction engine at wall ends; fixtures with doors at L and T corners are added to the NFR-MNT-005 suite.
design: archicraft-model kinds/door.rs and kinds/window.rs sharing a WallInsert placement (host relation, anchor, reveal, vertical pin) bound to a catalogue definition; archicraft-geometry void from the insert rectangle cut in the wall plane per skin (the host-openings path), parts placed by the host transform; plan symbols generated from parameters as renderer-agnostic primitives; archicraft-ifcx hosted children plus type occurrences; archicraft-app tools/insert.rs on the point-input service.
acceptance_criteria: The tool creates nothing without a host and says so (kittest); placement next to a junction cycles hosts with one key; the void cuts all skins of an F2 wall and the host is restored on delete (geometry tests with undo); resizing keeps the pinned edge and the anchor; sill and head references to any storey follow storey changes; splitting a host wall keeps the door on the right part (WAL-030 hook); IfcDoor/IfcWindow occurrences with Void children and material parts pass conformance; the AS-01 'walls show openings' check passes in the viewer; a ground floor with openings is drawn precisely end to end (increment-1 exit scenario scripted under docs/).

title: Reshape tool: stretch, offset, chamfer, union and difference
description:
WHY — EDT-009 (M): nodes and edges are stretchable by dragging, with numeric input; the stretch clause of INP-002 (owned by point-input-snapping, which delivered the tracker modes and names this epic as its consumer): while stretching, the tracker shows the resulting total length by default and the length change on demand and accepts either as typed input. EDT-010 (M): offset one edge or all edges by a typed distance. EDT-008 (M): insert node and chamfer corner. EDT-015 (S): add or subtract a drawn polygon. SLB-003 (M): holes can be drawn. SLB-008 (M): slab outlines and holes are editable with these commands.

WHAT — Extend the ReshapeTool consumer (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/reshape.rs) with steps and live previews for Insert node (position on the edge, then placement), Move edge (stretch; a modifier translates freely), Offset edge and Offset all edges (typed distance, side from the cursor), Chamfer corner (typed distance), Add polygon, Subtract polygon and Add hole (polygon, rectangle or rotated rectangle input exactly like the slab tool's geometry methods, with the resulting outline previewed), each executing one Command::Reshape; enable the matching palette entries; add an 'Offset' action with a provisional default shortcut (Appendix D.8 lists offset) that starts Offset edge on the selected edge or ring. Out of scope: walls (task 09), traced holes (task 12), fillet (curved-geometry).
design: One consumer with a ReshapeCommand enum and per-command step lists (StepSpec prompts such as 'Offset edge: distance or side', 'Chamfer: distance', 'Subtract: first corner'); commit builds the ReshapeOp and the target list (the clicked part plus coincident nodes of other selected elements for node moves). Previews call the same Outline methods as the planner on a clone and run the task-02 repair on it, so the preview is what will be stored. Tracker: StepSpec carries TrackerMode::TotalLength{base} or LengthChange{base} from point-input-snapping; for an edge stretch the base is the distance between the edge and the farthest parallel edge of its ring (the width the user thinks in), falling back to LengthChange when there is none; for a node dragged along an adjacent edge the base is that edge's length. Polygon input reuses the slab tool's geometry methods (SlabMode Polygon/Rectangle/RotatedRectangle and the rectangle helpers in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/slab.rs, views/tools.rs:315-336 before point-input-snapping-01) through a shared helper, so behaviour is identical (NFR-USE-002). Offset sign follows the cursor side of the edge line; typed values are magnitudes. Pitfall: node indices change after InsertNode or DeleteNode; retarget with the follow-up PartRef.
acceptance_criteria:
- ReshapeTool unit tests driven through InputConsumer without egui (like the tools.rs tests): stretching the north edge of a 12 x 9 m slab with typed total 10 gives 12 x 10; with the change field 0.5 gives 12 x 9.5; a node dragged with typed distance 1 along +x moves exactly 1.000 m; Offset all edges with typed -0.25 gives 11.5 x 8.5; Chamfer 0.6 at a corner; Insert node placed 0.5 m off the edge; Subtract a rectangle drawn across the east edge gives a notch; Add polygon overlapping gives the union; Add hole drawn inside adds ring 1. Each executes exactly one Command::Reshape and one undo step.
- For every command the preview ring equals the ring the executed command stores (vertex lists compared).
- kittest: select a slab, open the edge palette, 'Offset edge', type 0.5 Enter: the slab area grows by 0.5 x edge length; Esc during a step cancels only that step (Esc ladder of point-input-snapping).
- kittest: press-drag on the north-edge midpoint handle of a selected 12 x 9 m slab and typing 10 Enter gives 12 x 10 m (EDT-009: dragging with numeric input); the palette entries disabled in task 07 are now enabled.
- Offset all edges on the stair hole of the upper slab (PartRef::Ring { ring: 1 }) with the cursor inside the hole and typed 0.1 shrinks the hole to 2.8 x 1.0 m.
- The 'Offset' action and its shortcut pass shortcuts_are_unique (ui/actions.rs).
- Then satisfied: EDT-009 for polygon parts, EDT-010 offset edge and offset all, EDT-015, the drawing clause of SLB-003, the polygon-editing clauses of SLB-008 and the stretch clause of INP-002.
notes:
SRS: EDT-009 EDT-010 EDT-015 EDT-008 SLB-003 SLB-008
(plus the INP-002 stretch clause owned by point-input-snapping) Appendix D.1: angle increment 45° (15° selectable) for constrained drags. Appendix D.8 lists 'offset' among the default shortcuts; the binding stays provisional until commands-and-l10n confirms it.

title: Reject storey edits that would invert storey-linked elements
description:
WHY: NFR-REL-005 (M): operations that would produce invalid geometry are prevented or rejected with an explanatory message and never silently create corrupt elements. STR-006 (M) and ELM-006 (M): elements linked to storeys follow storey changes. Existing (keep): validate_element (validate.rs:105-282) already rejects self-intersecting, degenerate and sliver polygons and zero or out-of-range thickness for every element command, which plans through it and fails without touching the model (command.rs:320-342/371-395); STR-006 (done) and ELM-006 (partial, walls) make linked elements follow (project.rs:236-260, test storey_changes_move_linked_walls), and this task keeps that behaviour while validating its result. Gap: SetStoreyElevation and SetStoreyHeight (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:186-207, through storey_edit at :313-318) only validate storey spacing; a wall on the ground storey with base offset 0.5 m and top 'home + 1' ends with its top below its base when the first floor is moved to 0.3 m, the command succeeds and the element only fails later in the problems panel. InsertStorey re-targets relative links ('home + 1' becomes the inserted storey) and DeleteStorey with MoveTo rehomes elements; neither checks the resulting extents.

WHAT: Add Project::vertical_extent_in(element, &StoreyList) on top of the Kind::vertical_extent hook (task 02) and a validate_storey_change(project, &new_list) step in command.rs used by storey_edit for SetStoreyElevation and SetStoreyHeight (both shift_above modes), by InsertStorey, and by DeleteStorey for the rehomed elements and the links it rewrites. Candidates come from the relation store (task 08): storey_dependents of every storey whose elevation changed between the old and new list, plus every relatively linked element when the storey order changed; each candidate must keep a resolvable extent with top - bottom >= MIN_HEIGHT. Defaults slots with storey links are checked the same way through their prototypes. The first failure returns CommandError::Invalid naming the element and the storey and suggesting the remedy (change the element's top link first or choose a smaller change); the status line already shows CommandError messages (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:121-136). Out of scope: a storey-dialog preview listing every affected element, the failed-Boolean clause of NFR-REL-005 (solid-kernel-ops).
design: Validate against the proposed StoreyList before producing the Edit::SetStoreys, so nothing is applied on failure and undo stays untouched. Compare old and new lists storey by storey to find moved storeys; shift_above moves many storeys at once, so collect the dependents of all of them. Message wording follows command.rs (full sentences, element names, storey names in quotes). Pitfalls: relative links of the top storey resolve through extrapolation (storey.rs:108-118); a slab's extent does not depend on other storeys but its home storey can move; fixed-height walls never invert. Pointers: command.rs:150-213/313-318/399-482, project.rs:236-260, storey.rs:100-131/256-306, validate.rs:243-282.
acceptance_criteria:
- moving_a_storey_below_a_linked_wall_base_is_rejected (crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs): with a ground-storey wall at base offset 0.5 m and top Relative(+1), SetStoreyElevation of the first floor to 0.3 m returns Err(CommandError::Invalid(msg)) with msg naming the wall and the storey, and the project is unchanged; the same for SetStoreyHeight of the ground storey with shift_above true and false.
- Inserting a storey that would make a relative link resolve below the element's base is rejected; DeleteStorey with MoveTo that would invert a rehomed element is rejected.
- The same rules hold for a dummy element with a VerticalLink (test-kinds), proving the check is generic.
- Property test (seeded PRNG, 200 cases) on two_storey_shell plus random linked walls: every random SetStoreyElevation/SetStoreyHeight/InsertStorey/DeleteStorey is either rejected or leaves every element passing validate_element (no silent corruption).
- Only storey_dependents of changed storeys are validated (asserted through a debug counter or an injected validator), so the check stays cheap on stand_in(5_000).
- Existing NFR-REL-005 clauses regress green: rejects_degenerate_rings, holes_must_be_inside and ring_cleanup_and_orientation (validate.rs) and invalid_commands_leave_the_project_unchanged (tests/commands.rs); a dummy with zero size is rejected through Kind::validate with an explanatory CommandError::Invalid (test-kinds).
- storey_changes_move_linked_walls, relinking_keeps_the_absolute_position and deleting_a_storey_can_keep_its_elements still pass; NFR-REL-005 storey clause closed; STR-006 and ELM-006 preserved for every kind.
notes: SRS: NFR-REL-005 STR-006 ELM-006. The bug type reflects that the current behaviour silently admits invalid elements. Failed Booleans are covered when solid-kernel-ops lands.

title: Make every problems-panel entry clickable across storeys
description:
WHY: UI-012 (M): a problems panel lists elements with failed geometry, missing definitions or broken references, and clicking an entry selects the element and zooms to it (NFR-REL-006, OBJ-005). Existing (keep): geometry failures are listed with click-to-select and a zoom request (dialogs.rs:866-872 -> app.rs:713-714 -> zoom_active app.rs:354-375), and the View menu, the status-bar count button and Cmd+Shift+P open the panel (shell.rs:95-98/177-186, actions.rs:141). Gaps: the structured integrity problems (task 08) are never listed; load problems are plain labels (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:874-881); zoom only works when the element is on the active plan's storey (views/plan.rs:66-76 looks it up in the active plan; app.rs:354-375 zoom_active; Request::ZoomTo(Vec<ElementId>) in workspace.rs:34-40), otherwise it selects without zooming; no test covers the panel. NFR-REL-006 requires failed elements to be listed in this panel.

WHAT: problems_panel (dialogs.rs:848-883) shows three sections with counts: Geometry (failed elements, marked when a fallback is shown), References (Project::integrity_problems(), clickable when an element is known) and File (load problems whose path parses to the UUID of an element in the project are clickable, the rest stay labels), driven by an extensible ProblemSource enum with a Definition source reserved for OBJ-005 (components-dw-catalogue). A click sets the selection to the element and pushes Request::ZoomTo { ids, storey: Some(home storey) }; handle_requests (app.rs:709-718) opens or activates the plan pane of the home storey when the active pane is a plan of another storey (a 3D pane zooms in place), then zooms using the fallback bounds where needed. The status-bar count (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:177-190) sums all sections. Out of scope: OBJ-005 definitions, EDT-019 repair entries (edit-reshape-palette adds them through ProblemSource), filtering and search in the panel.
design: Keep the panel a pure view over three sources so later epics only add a source. Carry the storey in the request rather than relying on request order, because handle_requests processes OpenPane and ZoomTo in sequence but the new pane's last_rect is unknown until it has been laid out once: if the rect is empty, remember the pending zoom in the plan view state and apply it on its first frame. validate::Problem.path is the node path, which for elements is the UUID string. Pitfalls: problems_panel borrows ws.doc.geometry(), take the Arc first; integrity problems are computed per frame, cache them per project revision. Pointers: dialogs.rs:847-883, app.rs:290-375/700-718, views/plan.rs:58-76, workspace.rs:34-47, shell.rs:177-190, crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest problems_panel_lists_failed_elements_and_zooms (test-kinds): with the ground-floor plan active and a panicking dummy on the upper storey, the panel lists '<name>: Geometry evaluation failed unexpectedly.'; clicking it selects exactly that element, makes the upper storey's plan the active pane and moves its camera so the element's bounds are in view; no crash report is written.
- A project with a dangling material reference (built directly in the test) lists '<name>: material is missing' as a clickable References entry that selects the element.
- A load problem whose path is an element UUID is clickable and selects the element; one with a non-element path stays a label.
- Missing definitions mechanism: a ProblemSource::Definition entry injected in a unit test renders in its own section and is clickable (OBJ-005 fills it later).
- With a 3D pane active, clicking an entry selects the element and the 3D camera frames its bounds (fallback bounds for a failed element).
- The status-bar count equals the panel's total; main_window_has_the_parts_of_ui_001 still finds 'No problems' on a clean project.
- UI-012 satisfied for failed geometry and broken references, with the missing-definitions source in place for OBJ-005 to fill; NFR-REL-006's 'listed in a problems panel' clause verified by kittest.
notes: SRS: UI-012 NFR-REL-006. OBJ-005 adds the Definition source later; EDT-018/EDT-019 repairs use the same mechanism.

title: Add trim and extend commands with 2D lines and walls as boundaries
description:
WHY: EDT-011 (M): "Trim shall remove the clicked portion of a linear element (line, arc, polyline segment, wall, beam) back to the nearest intersections. If a selection exists, only the selected elements act as cutting boundaries." EDT-012 (M): "Extend shall lengthen or shorten linear elements to a picked boundary, or to the boundary's extension. Walls and beams are adjusted along their reference line, and a picked wall face can be the boundary." ANN-002: 2D elements act as cutters for trim. Epic acceptance: "trimming a wall back to the nearest intersecting wall or 2D line, extending to a picked wall face" as fixtures. Gap rows EDT-011/EDT-012 (missing): no trim, no extend, no intersection search for linear elements and no boundary-from-selection logic; both list beams (BEA, profiles-columns-beams, not a prerequisite of this epic) as a dependency.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/linear_edit.rs: kind hook `cutting_curves(&self, project, target_kind) -> Vec<Segment>` (walls: their reference line when the target is a wall or beam, so a trimmed end lands on it and forms a T by contact, otherwise both face lines from ReferenceLine::face_offsets (element.rs:99); 2D elements: their segments; a default returning the outline edges of every kind exposing an Outline); planners `plan_trim(project, target, pick, boundaries, id_seed)` and `plan_extend(project, target, pick, boundary: BoundaryRef { element, part: Option<PartRef>, point })`; `Command::Trim { target, pick, boundaries: Vec<ElementId>, id_seed }` and `Command::Extend { target, pick, boundary }`. Trim: the parameters of all intersections of the picked carrier piece with the boundary curves (bounded), plus a polyline's self-intersections; remove the open interval around the pick between the nearest parameters on either side; one-sided means shorten; two-sided produces two parts through the split machinery of task 10 (derived id for the second part, relations retargeted through task 18, hosted elements inside the removed interval deleted with the command and named in a CommandNote of edit-reshape-palette-02); a circle needs two intersections and keeps the complementary arc; a closed polyline opens at the removed interval; no intersection gives NoChange 'Nothing to trim: no intersection on either side'. Extend: the end nearest the pick moves to the nearest intersection of the target's carrier (infinite line or full circle beyond the end) with the boundary's carrier (its extension counts), which may lengthen or shorten; walls move along their reference line; a picked wall face (the WallFace(Exterior|Interior) part of edit-reshape-palette-05) uses that face line; polylines extend their first or last segment; no intersection gives Invalid 'The boundary does not meet the extension of <name>'. Beams: implement carrier and cutting_curves in kinds/beam.rs if profiles-columns-beams-07 has landed (one function each), otherwise file a follow-up bead against profiles-columns-beams. Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/reshape.rs `boundary_candidates(plan, target, visible) -> Vec<ElementId>` (rstar query over plan-element bounds, including the 2D curves of task 04) supplies the tool's default boundary list when nothing is selected (task 13). Out of scope: tools and previews (13), roofs and shells as 3D boundaries (cleanup-and-trims), spline targets and boundaries (task 07 implements the spline hooks).
design: The command carries the explicit boundary list, so plan() is deterministic, replayable and independent of view visibility; the app chooses the list (the selection if non-empty per EDT-011, otherwise visible candidates from reshape.rs). Walls are trimmed to other walls' reference lines because junctions are defined by reference-line contact (D-6, WAL-020): trimming to a face would leave a gap the junction engine cannot close; for 2D targets the visible faces are the natural boundaries. All maths comes from curve.rs; tolerances convert MODEL_TOLERANCE to parameter space by segment length or radius·angle. Pitfalls: a pick exactly at an intersection (take the portion on the cursor side using a small offset along the carrier); coincident boundaries (deduplicate parameters within tolerance); a remaining piece shorter than RepairThresholds.min_edge_length is removed and reported; wall top links and every parameter other than the reference line stay untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture trim_wall_by_wall (crates/archicraft-model/tests/linear_edit.rs): wall A (0,0)-(6,0) crossed by wall B (4,−2)-(4,2); trimming with pick (5, 0) and boundaries [B] makes A end at (4, 0) exactly on B's reference line (T by contact); undo restores A bitwise.
- Fixture trim_wall_by_2d_line: a DraftLine at x = 3 crossing A; pick (4.5, 0) shortens A to (0,0)-(3,0); with lines at x = 2 and x = 4 and pick (3, 0) A becomes (0,0)-(2,0) and (4,0)-(6,0), the second with a derived id; with only the x = 2 line in the boundaries the x = 4 line is ignored (selection clause); a test-kinds Dummy hosted inside the removed span is deleted and named in the command's notes, one outside it stays on its part.
- Fixture extend_to_wall_face: wall A (0,0)-(3,0) and wall B with a centred reference line along x = 5 and thickness 0.25 m; extending A's end to B's west face moves it to (4.875, 0), to B's reference line to (5, 0); a boundary crossing A at x = 2 shortens A to (0,0)-(2,0) ('shorten' clause).
- 2D tests: a DraftLine crossed by two others and trimmed between them becomes two lines; a DraftArc trimmed by a line loses the clicked portion with the new end on the line within 1e-12; extending an arc to a line follows its circle; a circle trimmed between two lines becomes an arc; a DraftLine extends to the extension of a short boundary line; a polyline segment is trimmed back to a crossing with another of its segments.
- Invalid cases leave the project unchanged with the documented messages; journal replay gives identical ids; reshape.rs boundary_candidates equals a brute-force scan on two_storey_shell plus 50 seeded 2D lines.
- Beams: a beam is trimmed and extended like a wall if kinds/beam.rs exists; otherwise the follow-up bead is filed and linked from the done task.
- If regression-and-status-02 has landed, the three fixtures are EXTRA entries in crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs.
- EDT-011 and EDT-012 model clauses satisfied for lines, arcs, polyline segments and walls (beams as above); ANN-002's trim-cutter clause satisfied.
notes:
SRS: EDT-011 EDT-012 ANN-002 (trim-cutter clause)
Fixture coordinates are proposals; the fixtures join the D.7 registry's EXTRA list when regression-and-status provides it.

title: Merge collinear end-to-end walls with identical settings
description:
WHY: WAL-031 (S): "Two or more walls that touch end to end, are collinear (or lie on the same circle) and have identical settings shall be mergeable into one wall, keeping all hosted elements." It is the inverse of WAL-030 and cleans up after splits, trims and imports. Gap row WAL-031 (missing): no merge command. Built on the carrier hook of task 10, Segment::join and same_carrier of task 01 and relations::retarget_after_replace with the rehost hook of task 18. curved-geometry-17's WAL-032 combine is a different command, and no other epic owns WAL-031's same-circle clause, so the planner handles arc carriers now.

WHAT: `Command::MergeWalls { walls: Vec<ElementId> }` in crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs with its planner in linear_edit.rs: order the walls into a chain along their common carrier (the carrier() hook of task 10 and curve.rs same_carrier: collinear lines now, the same circle once curved-geometry gives walls arc carriers), require consecutive end-to-end contact within MODEL_TOLERANCE and identical settings through `Wall::same_settings` in kinds/wall.rs (every wall payload field except the reference-line end points, plus layer, home storey, IFC class, predefined type, position, top link, plan style and any junction settings; names may differ), join the carriers with Segment::join into one wall that keeps the id, name and direction of the first wall in model order, and remove the others; relations and hosted elements of all merged walls are retargeted through relations::retarget_after_replace (hosted elements keep their world position through the rehost hook). An Edit menu item 'Merge walls' (Action in ui/actions.rs or a registry command) and a context-menu entry (views/plan.rs context_menu, plan.rs:728), enabled only for qualifying selections and otherwise disabled with the reason as tooltip; afterwards the merged wall is selected. Out of scope: merging 2D lines (not required), combining parallel walls into one cross-section (WAL-032, curved-geometry-17).
design: Settings equality is a comparison of the wall payload with the reference line masked, so wall fields added by other epics (layer structure, join group, junction order, end thickness) are included automatically; implement it next to the kind in kinds/wall.rs. The merged reference line takes the outermost chain end points bitwise (no recomputation), so split-then-merge is an exact round trip. Pitfalls: a third wall touching a shared node keeps its contact and becomes a T on the merged wall (resolved by the junction engine); the hosted elements' anchors are recomputed against the merged reference line by the rehost hook, not by the merge code.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests: (0,0)-(3,0) and (3,0)-(7,0) with identical settings merge into (0,0)-(7,0) keeping the first id and name; a reversed second wall (7,0)-(3,0) merges the same way; a three-wall chain merges in one command; different thicknesses give Invalid 'Walls differ in thickness'; a 1 mm gap gives Invalid 'Walls do not touch end to end'; non-collinear walls give Invalid; walls on different storeys never merge; undo restores all walls bitwise.
- A test-kinds Dummy hosted on the second wall stays hosted on the merged wall at the same world position; a split (task 10) followed by a merge returns an element equal to the original (id, name, all fields, reference line bitwise).
- Same-circle branch: the chain-and-join step of the planner, run on two co-circular arc carriers touching end to end, yields one arc carrier with the inputs' centre and radius bits and the summed sweep, so arc walls merge as soon as curved-geometry's wall carrier hook returns arcs; the done task files a bead for curved-geometry to add the arc-wall test.
- kittest: Edit > Merge walls is disabled for a single wall and enabled for two qualifying walls; executing it leaves the merged wall selected.
- WAL-031 satisfied for straight walls; its same-circle clause is implemented in the planner and verified at carrier level.
notes: SRS: WAL-031

title: Place unit parts and plan symbols by the host frame
design:
One transform source: InsertFrame::unit_to_storey (01), shared with the IFCX writer (05) through InstanceGeometry.transform. Do not mirror meshes here; the catalogue's kit.rs mirror_x already builds natively mirrored types.

Plan symbols use the catalogue's unit-local SymbolPrimitive output; do not tessellate arcs here. Keep arcs exact (centre, radius, sweep), so the renderer and later the drafting arc type of drafting-trim-split can tessellate per IFX-034 settings.

The host cut fill is already absent inside the opening, because the plan slices the cut 3D body (03). The extended Mask only hides residual projected host lines inside the opening; build no second cut polygon.

Cost: the TypeCache of components-dw-catalogue-07 generates both detail levels lazily per TypeKey, which is the same sharing the IFCX type nodes need (IFX-037/050). Add no second cache.

Pitfall: the hinge mapping drifts if the unit-local origin is not pinned by a test; keep the pin test next to the catalogue's own layout tests, and test both reference-line directions.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/inserts.rs: for every DW-011 door and window type of Catalogue::builtin() with default parameters in a 0.30 m wall, all placed parts are closed with positive signed volume and lie inside the Void prism's bounds (tolerance MODEL_TOLERANCE), and the exterior frame face lies at the reveal distance from the chosen wall face (DW-008 through 01).
- Each of the four hinge x swing configurations puts the leaf's hinge at the expected along end and the swing arc on the expected wall side, in the 3D parts and the plan symbols; both sliding directions put the arrow the expected way (DW-004 'visible').
- FlipInsertSide moves the frame orientation and the inside and outside sill boards to the other side, while the leaf hinge and the swing arc stay where they were (DW-003 'without changing ... opening configuration').
- An empty opening produces no body parts besides the Void, and only the mask and jamb lines in plan (DW-010).
- world_parts_at(Simplified) and world_parts_at(Detailed) both exist for doors and windows and differ for door.hinged.single (one box per leaf versus the full part set) (VIEW-055 groundwork).
- Two identical doors share one Arc<TypeGeometry>; a door with the other hinge end uses the mirrored TypeKey; every InstanceGeometry.transform has a positive determinant.
- Plan test at the 1.10 m cut plane: the door symbol (leaf line plus arc at the plan opening angle) lies inside the opening; a window with its sill at 2.20 m is drawn in the Overhead style, and a window spanning the cut plane in the Cut style; picking on the leaf line returns the door.
- A pin test fixes the catalogue generator's local origin and axes as InsertFrame uses them (origin at the opening's lower AlongStart corner on the exterior frame face when exterior = HostExterior).
notes: SRS: DW-003 DW-004 DW-010 DW-018 VIEW-055 (plus DW-013 placement, IFX-017, IFX-032, IFX-051). The plan opening angle and part set come from the DW-012 parameters of components-dw-catalogue. VIEW-055 'schematic' = DetailLevel::Simplified and 'detailed' = DetailLevel::Detailed (components-dw-catalogue-04 note).

title: Add the per-view option to hide or simplify doors and windows
description:
WHY: VIEW-055: 'A view shall be able to hide doors and windows while keeping their openings, and to show doors and windows in a schematic or a detailed 3D representation.' The gap analysis lists it as missing, since doors and windows did not exist. VIEW-047 requires that view filters never change the model geometry or the standard IFCX content. View3d (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:114) stores only id, name and projection; plan-views-browser-07 later replaces it with ViewDefinition. The 3D scene is cached per revision and selection (SceneKey, crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:44), FrameKey (views/render3d.rs:235) drives re-renders, and there is no per-view element filtering. Task 04 makes both DetailLevels of every unit available through world_parts_at.

WHAT: Add InsertDisplay {units_visible: bool, representation: DetailLevel}, with Simplified labelled 'Schematic' in the UI. It defaults to visible plus Detailed, with serde default so old projects load. It lives in View3d, or in ViewDefinition's style section if plan-views-browser has landed. Plan views get shown/hidden only, as a flag in PlanViewState, or in ViewDefinition.plan when that exists. Add Command::SetViewInsertDisplay {view, display}, or extend UpdateView if plan-views-browser added it. Write the field as an optional key of the archicraft::project views entries (writer.rs:183-186, the reader, schema.rs); as an optional addition it needs no format bump (element-kind-framework-12 rule).

Rendering:
- views/render3d.rs build_scene puts the insert parts from world_parts_at into separate index ranges per DetailLevel, next to the rest of the scene (on the SceneCache blocks of element-kind-framework-11 when present);
- the draw call picks the range per view (Detailed, Simplified or none), and FrameKey includes InsertDisplay, so a toggle re-renders without rebuilding buffers;
- in plan, hidden units drop their symbols and parts while the host stays cut, because the void belongs to the host geometry (03).
UI: a 'Doors and windows' combo (Detailed, Schematic, Hidden) next to the DisplayMode combo in ui/shell.rs (line 202), the same entries in the 3D view's context menu (views/view3d.rs:265), and a 'Show doors and windows' toggle in the plan context menu (views/plan.rs:728). Out of scope: the general kind filter of VIEW-041 (3d-view-restrictions), display styles (3d-display-styles), and plan detail levels (DSP-015, components-dw-catalogue-10).
design:
Keep the filter purely at draw time: geometry and IFCX always contain both representations and all units (VIEW-047). Use world_parts_at from task 04 with the catalogue's DetailLevel instead of a new representation enum.

GpuScene: split the opaque and transparent buffers into [rest | insert-detailed | insert-simplified] ranges in one buffer, so the per-view choice is a draw-range selection, not a rebuild. This matters for NFR-PERF view switching.

FrameKey (render3d.rs:235) gains the InsertDisplay value, so a toggle re-renders only that view. SceneKey stays per revision and selection.

Follow the 'Add a 3D display feature' extension point for the FrameKey and status-bar wiring.

If 3d-view-restrictions has landed, honour VIEW-043: hidden doors and windows show the persistent indicator, and the 'clear restrictions' command resets this option.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: SetViewInsertDisplay with execute and undo restores the view; the option round-trips through IFCX in archicraft::project, and files without it load as visible plus Detailed.
- render3d unit test (no GPU) on a FixtureBuilder project with an F2 wall, a door, a window and an empty opening: build_scene yields separate insert ranges per DetailLevel; Hidden draws no insert triangles, while the wall triangles are unchanged and still show the openings (VIEW-055 'while keeping their openings').
- Schematic draws only the Simplified parts and Detailed only the Detailed parts, for the same set of elements (VIEW-055 'schematic or a detailed 3D representation').
- VIEW-047 test: writing the same project with each InsertDisplay value gives identical standard (non-archicraft::) content; only the archicraft::project view entry differs.
- kittest: the 'Doors and windows' combo exists in the 3D view's status area, and choosing 'Hidden' sets the view's option; switching tabs and back keeps it (PRJ-007: views are project settings).
- Plan test: with units hidden, the storey's PlanDrawing has no symbols or parts for doors and windows, while the wall cut regions still have the gaps.
- If 3d-view-restrictions has landed, hidden doors and windows count as an active restriction for the VIEW-043 indicator, and 'clear restrictions' resets the option to visible.
notes: SRS: VIEW-055 (plus VIEW-047, VIEW-043 interplay, PRJ-007). Default per view: visible, Detailed. Decision: plan views offer shown/hidden only, because VIEW-055 names the 3D representation; the plan detail level is DSP-015's per-view setting from components-dw-catalogue-10.

title: Verify exit criterion: Node/edge edit palette, offsets, polygon editing, contour detection and validation
description:
WHY — The epic is finished only when its exit criterion holds end to end on the integrated workspace: EDT-008 palette, EDT-009 stretching, EDT-010 offsets and offset copy, EDT-023 joined chain copies, EDT-015 union and difference, EDT-018 and EDT-019 validation and repair, WAL-033 wall direct manipulation, SLB-003 holes, SLB-005 edge angles, SLB-008 polygon editing and elevation dragging, and INP-018 contour detection, with the status document telling the truth about every covered requirement.

WHAT — Run the full acceptance listed below on a clean checkout after tasks 01-13 have merged; fix or file anything that fails. Update docs/implementation-status.md rows (status, evidence paths, remaining gap) for the twelve IDs and add the notes for INP-002, WAL-004, SLB-001 and NFR-USE-002. Check that the downstream tasks own the deferred clauses and file follow-up beads only where none does: fillet (EDT-014, curved-geometry-10) and curve/straighten/arc radius (EDT-008, WAL-033, curved-geometry-02 and -11); offset copy of lines, polylines and arcs (EDT-010, drafting-trim-split-03 through Kind::offset_copy); contour detection with arcs preserved (INP-018, curved-geometry-08); slab elevation dragging in section and elevation views (SLB-008, sections-elevations-dims-08); zero-thickness skins (EDT-018, layer-structures); contour detection in 3D views (INP-018, no owner yet: file it against the working plane of 3d-input-navigation); profile polygons validated through repair_outline (EDT-018: file it against profiles-columns-beams unless its tasks call repair_outline). Close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new features.
design: Verification only. Use the existing harnesses: crates/archicraft-model/tests (commands.rs, reshape.rs), crates/archicraft-geometry/tests (contour.rs, storey.rs), crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs with the golden files, crates/archicraft-app/tests (ui.rs, reshape_ui.rs) and conformance/run.sh. Check the NFR-USE-002 rule by inspection: every polygon command is an Outline<E> method reached through the kind's reshape hook, and the palette lists commands by part class, not by kind. The status rows follow the format of the requirement table in docs/implementation-status.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: clicking a selected slab node opens the palette with move/insert/delete, an edge with offset/offset-all/curve/straighten (curve is a stub until curved-geometry) (crates/archicraft-app/tests/reshape_ui.rs).
- Command::Reshape tests for every palette command with undo (crates/archicraft-model/tests/reshape.rs).
- Dragging a wall face changes the thickness while the reference line stays (WAL-004 invariant).
- Union and difference with a drawn polygon.
- A hole traced by contour detection from four interior walls of two_storey_shell (samples::two_storey_shell_with_shaft) subtracts exactly their enclosed region, and a slab is created from the smallest closed region inside the exterior ring.
- Validation tests: duplicate vertices removed, self-intersections rejected with a message, edges under 0.1 mm repaired or listed in the problems panel.
- Contour detection creates an element of the active kind from a single clicked edge, a chain and the smallest closed region, each matching its preview.
- Repair thresholds round-trip through IFCX and repairs appear in the problems panel; an inclined slab edge round-trips and evaluates to a closed mesh (SLB-005); a slab elevation is dragged in 3D with a typed ΔZ (SLB-008).
- Offset copy of a joined wall chain stays joined.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green on the workspace.
- conformance/run.sh is green on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (EDT-008, EDT-009, EDT-010, EDT-023, EDT-015, EDT-018, EDT-019, WAL-033, SLB-003, SLB-005, SLB-008, INP-018) with evidence paths and the deferred clauses, plus notes on INP-002 (stretch clause), WAL-004 (invariant test), SLB-001 (tracing clause) and NFR-USE-002.
- Follow-up beads are filed for the deferred clauses and the epic is closed in beads.
notes:
SRS: EDT-008 EDT-009 EDT-010 EDT-023 EDT-015 EDT-018 EDT-019 WAL-033 SLB-003 SLB-005 SLB-008 INP-018
Deferred clauses: EDT-014 fillet and the curve/arc parts of EDT-008/WAL-033 (curved-geometry-02, -10, -11); EDT-010 offset copy of 2D lines, polylines and arcs (drafting-trim-split-03); INP-018 with arcs (curved-geometry-08) and in 3D (no owner: follow-up bead); SLB-008 dragging in section/elevation views (sections-elevations-dims-08); EDT-018 zero-thickness skins (layer-structures) and profile polygons (profiles-columns-beams, bead if missing).

title: Complete the IFC class list and add predefined types
description:
WHY: ELM-011 (M): every element has an IFC class defaulted by its kind (Table 5-1), user-selectable from the Appendix D.5 list for free-form solids, objects and imported elements, IfcWall or IfcFooting for walls, IfcSlab, IfcFooting or IfcCovering for slabs, IfcBeam, IfcMember or IfcFooting for beams and IfcColumn or IfcMember for columns. IfcClass knows only Wall, Slab, Footing, Covering (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:8-33, plus BuildingElementProxy from task 02) and the reader downgrades every other class with a warning (reader.rs:625-638); the wall and slab sets (element.rs:226-232), their checks (validate.rs:256-262, command.rs:567-571) and the class combo (properties.rs:481-492) exist and stay. IFX-024 (M, status missing): information IFC 4.x expresses as a predefined type (slab floor / roof / base slab / landing, footing pad / strip) shall be stored in the ArchiCraft namespace, and also written with a standard attribute as soon as the pinned registry provides one (O-6). AS-02 checks IfcColumn, IfcBeam, IfcSlab and IfcFooting; the compound parts of task 07 need IfcMember, IfcPlate and IfcStairFlight.

WHAT: IfcClass covers the twenty D.5 classes (IfcBuildingElementProxy, IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcRoof, IfcColumn, IfcBeam, IfcMember, IfcPlate, IfcCovering, IfcFooting, IfcPile, IfcRailing, IfcStair, IfcRamp, IfcChimney, IfcShadingDevice, IfcCurtainWall, IfcFurniture, IfcSpace, IfcGeographicElement) plus the remaining Table 5-1 classes (IfcStairFlight, IfcOpeningElement, IfcDoor, IfcWindow, IfcGrid, IfcAnnotation) with ALL, SELECTABLE_D5 (D.5 order, proxy first), code()/from_code(). Named class sets cover every ELM-011 sub-bullet: WALL_CLASSES [IfcWall, IfcFooting], SLAB_CLASSES [IfcSlab, IfcFooting, IfcCovering], BEAM_CLASSES [IfcBeam, IfcMember, IfcFooting], COLUMN_CLASSES [IfcColumn, IfcMember] and SELECTABLE_D5 for free-form solids, objects and imported elements; the wall and slab descriptors reference them, and profiles-columns-beams, free-form-solids, components-dw-catalogue and ifcx-interop register their kinds with them. COMPOUND_PART_CLASSES lists the Table 5-1 part rows (stair: flight IfcStairFlight, landing IfcSlab, stringer IfcMember; railing: post and rail IfcMember, infill panel IfcPlate; curtain wall: frame IfcMember, panel IfcPlate; multi-plane roof: plane IfcSlab) for the PartSpec of later compound kinds (checked in task 07). New PredefinedType with the IFC 4.3 literals as codes (IfcSlabTypeEnum FLOOR, ROOF, LANDING, BASESLAB; IfcFootingTypeEnum PAD_FOOTING, STRIP_FOOTING), UI labels and for_class(IfcClass); Element.predefined_type and DefaultsSlot.predefined_type: Option<PredefinedType>; a descriptor hook predefined_types(class) defaulting to for_class; validate_element and check_tool_defaults reject a type that does not belong to the class. The dummy kind offers SELECTABLE_D5 with IfcBuildingElementProxy as default (standing in for free-form solids and objects). IFCX: archicraft::element.predefinedType as an optional enumeration in alpha/schema.rs, written when Some by write_element and for slots, read back with a warning on an unknown literal. App: properties.rs classification fields add a 'Predefined type' choice when for_class(class) is non-empty (Mixed state for multi-selection) and clear an invalid type when the class changes. Samples: the ground slab of two_storey_shell gets BASESLAB and the upper slab FLOOR; goldens re-blessed from the samples (task 03). crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/registry.rs gets a test asserting that the bundled ifc@v5a and prop@v5a schemas declare no predefined-type attribute, so the suite fails loudly when the pinned registry gains one (IFX-024 second clause, O-6). Out of scope: a footing kind, the beam and column kinds themselves (profiles-columns-beams registers them with BEAM_CLASSES and COLUMN_CLASSES), free-form solids, objects and imported elements (free-form-solids, components-dw-catalogue and ifcx-interop register them with SELECTABLE_D5), the standard attribute itself.
design: IfcClass stays a closed enum (a fixed IFC vocabulary needs no registry); the per-kind selectable set lives in the descriptor. PredefinedType is a common Element field because footing types apply to walls, slabs, beams and columns alike; the allowed set is a function of (kind, class) via the descriptor hook. Codes are the IFC 4.3 enumeration literals so a future standard attribute can be written verbatim. Writer: insert predefinedType after position to keep member order stable; schema: optional(enumeration(PredefinedType::ALL codes)); the writer's CLASS_URI base (bSDD 4.3) already yields valid URIs for every class. Pitfalls: declaring the new optional member changes the schemas section, so every golden changes and must be re-blessed and reviewed; the reader's unknown-class path keeps using descriptor.default_class; properties.rs:481-492 builds its class combo from descriptor.ifc_classes and needs no other change. Pointers: element.rs:8-33, validate.rs:256-262, command.rs:554-593, schema.rs:224-232, writer.rs:396-414, reader.rs:625-638, properties.rs:481-492, registry.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test compares IfcClass::SELECTABLE_D5 codes against the literal Appendix D.5 list (20 names, proxy first) and IfcClass::ALL against Table 5-1's class column; code()/from_code() round-trip for every variant.
- elm_011_class_sets_match_the_srs: WALL_CLASSES == [IfcWall, IfcFooting], SLAB_CLASSES == [IfcSlab, IfcFooting, IfcCovering], BEAM_CLASSES == [IfcBeam, IfcMember, IfcFooting], COLUMN_CLASSES == [IfcColumn, IfcMember], SELECTABLE_D5 equals the D.5 list; the wall and slab descriptors' ifc_classes are WALL_CLASSES and SLAB_CLASSES, the dummy's is SELECTABLE_D5, and every descriptor's default_class is the Table 5-1 class of its kind (wall IfcWall, slab IfcSlab, dummy IfcBuildingElementProxy as the free-form stand-in).
- COMPOUND_PART_CLASSES equals the Table 5-1 part rows (unit test against the literal table).
- PredefinedType::for_class(IfcSlab) == [FLOOR, ROOF, LANDING, BASESLAB], for_class(IfcFooting) == [PAD_FOOTING, STRIP_FOOTING], empty for IfcWall; validate_element rejects FLOOR on an IfcWall element and PAD_FOOTING on an IfcSlab element with CommandError::Invalid naming the class.
- Round-trip test predefined_types_round_trip: a slab (IfcSlab, FLOOR), a slab (IfcFooting, STRIP_FOOTING) and a wall (IfcFooting, PAD_FOOTING) save and load equal, the nodes carry archicraft::element.predefinedType with the IFC literal and the file validates; a file with an unknown literal loads with one warning and predefined_type None.
- A defaults slot with a predefined type round-trips; check_tool_defaults rejects a mismatched type.
- kittest (user-selectable class): selecting a wall offers exactly IfcWall and IfcFooting, a slab exactly its three classes and a dummy (test-kinds) the twenty D.5 classes in D.5 order; choosing IfcFooting for the wall issues one UpdateElements and undo restores IfcWall.
- kittest: selecting a slab shows the 'Predefined type' choice with four options plus none; selecting an IfcWall wall shows none; choosing 'Base slab' issues one UpdateElements and sets Some(BASESLAB).
- Golden files re-blessed with the two sample slab types and reviewed; conformance/run.sh green; the registry test is green against the pinned schemas.
- ELM-011 satisfied for every sub-bullet at the class-vocabulary level (walls and slabs end to end; beams, columns, free-form solids, objects and imported elements through the named sets their epics register with); IFX-024 first clause satisfied, second clause guarded by the registry test.
notes: SRS: ELM-011 IFX-024. Appendix D.5 verbatim; Table 5-1 part classes are consumed by task 07. O-6 stays open; the registry test is the reminder.

title: Add insert edit commands, storey following and host-change hooks
design:
Prefer whole-element ReplaceElement snapshots, following the 'Add a command' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md. These commands touch only insert fields, so no new Edit primitive is needed.

Keep the commands multi-target: a properties edit on a mixed selection of doors and windows (09) is one undo step.

Storey-following needs no code for elevation changes, because elevations are derived in InsertFrame::resolve (01). Only deletion, reassignment and rehoming need rules, and they reuse the absolute-elevation arithmetic of rehome (command.rs:399).

Host-change hooks register with the relation store, so other host edits (EDT reshape, offset, MergeWalls) pick them up without knowing about doors:
- the re-projection uses the old and new reference lines: new_along = (old_start + old_dir*along - new_start) . new_dir, accepted only when the lines are collinear within MODEL_TOLERANCE (new_dir = -old_dir for a reversed line);
- otherwise 'along' is kept, and rigid host transforms (rotate and mirror in selection-transforms) move the unit through Kind::carry.

The SetInstanceMirrored/SetInstanceParameters routing is a descriptor hook on the hosted kinds, so components-dw-catalogue's commands stay generic.

Validation must run after the hooks, in the same plan, so a host edit that makes a unit invalid is rejected as a whole.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/inserts.rs: for every new command, execute then undo restores the starting project (revision normalised), and an invalid command leaves it untouched.
- FlipInsertSide changes only 'exterior' and the re-derived instance fields; along, anchor, width, height, vertical, reveal and configuration are bit-identical before and after (DW-003).
- SetInsertConfiguration with only one field set changes only that field; the four hinge x swing combinations and both sliding directions are reachable; on a fixed window it is rejected with a message (DW-004).
- ResizeInserts with each anchor keeps the anchor point; with a Sill pin it keeps the sill and with a Head pin the head; a width that pushes the unit past the wall end is rejected with a message naming it; one command on two doors is one undo step (DW-005, DW-006, DW-007).
- SetStoreyElevation on a storey referenced by a window sill moves the resolved sill by the same delta and leaves the stored offset unchanged; SetInsertVertical with keep_elevation = true reassigns the reference to another storey, HostBase or HostTop and keeps the resolved sill (DW-007 'reassigned', epic 'follow storey changes').
- DeleteStorey of a referenced storey converts the reference to HomeStorey, keeps the absolute sill elevation and lists the conversion in the command report (NFR-REL-005 style).
- Moving a host wall to another storey (DeleteStorey with StoreyElements::MoveTo, and the vertical-move path) carries its doors with element.storey mirrored and unchanged absolute sill and head (DW-001, STR-004).
- Dragging the wall start along its line keeps the door's absolute position, and dragging it past the door is rejected; FlipWalls with keep_body = true and MoveWallReferenceLine leave every door's world interval, side and hinge position unchanged (DW-001 'move with it').
- WAL-030 hook: rehost_inserts on a wall replaced by two parts puts each door on the part that contains it, with 'along' re-based and the absolute anchor unchanged; a split inside a door's interval is rejected. If Command::Split from drafting-trim-split exists, the same test also runs through it with Cutter::Point.
- SetInstanceMirrored on a door changes its hinge end exactly like SetInsertConfiguration, and SetInstanceParameters on the bound width changes 'width' exactly like ResizeInserts.
notes: SRS: DW-001 DW-003 DW-004 DW-005 DW-006 DW-007 (plus WAL-030 hook, STR-004, NFR-REL-005). Integration point: drafting-trim-split-10 owns Command::Split, relations::retarget_after_replace and the rehost descriptor hook. It is not a prerequisite of this epic, so the test drives rehost_inserts directly, and task 11 re-runs it through Command::Split when available. Decision to confirm: a split inside a unit is rejected rather than moving the unit, because silently moving a door is worse than a clear refusal (ELM-017).

title: Split walls, slabs and 2D elements by point, edge or line
description:
WHY: EDT-013 (M): "Split shall divide linear and polygon-based elements (including slabs, roofs and terrain) by a picked edge, a guide or a temporary two-point line. The user chooses which part stays selected." WAL-030 (M): "Splitting a wall at a point shall create two joined walls. Hosted elements stay with the part they lie in." ANN-002 (M): 2D elements act as cutters for split. IFX-011: identities stay stable across edits and new parts get new identities. Gap rows EDT-013 and WAL-030 (missing): no split command (command.rs:36-92) and no D.8 split shortcut. doors-windows-core-02/-11 call `Command::Split { targets, cutter: Cutter::Point(..), id_seed }` from this task; relation retargeting and the hosted-element hook follow in task 18, the tool and the part choice in task 19.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/linear_edit.rs: `Cutter { Point(DVec2), Line { a, b }, Edge { element, part: Option<PartRef>, point } }` (a temporary two-point line or a guide's two defining points as Line; a picked edge of any element or a 2D line as Edge; Line and Edge cut along their carrier). Kind hooks on the Kind trait with None defaults: `carrier(&self) -> Option<Vec<Segment>>` (walls: the reference line; DraftLine, DraftArc and the DraftPolyline segments; beams in kinds/beam.rs if profiles-columns-beams-07 has landed, otherwise a follow-up bead), `with_carrier(&self, piece) -> Result<Self, String>` (all other parameters copied) and `split_polygon(&self, line)` with a default implementation for every kind exposing an Outline (slabs now, the fills of task 09 automatically, roofs and terrain when their epics expose their outline). `ElementId::derived(seed: Uuid, n: u32)` (UUID v5) in crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs. Planner `plan_split(project, targets, cutter, id_seed) -> Result<SplitPlan { parts: Vec<(Element, Side)>, replaced: Vec<(ElementId, Vec<ElementId>)> }>` and `Command::Split { targets, cutter, id_seed: Uuid }` planning through it. The first part keeps the original id and name; further parts get ElementId::derived(id_seed, n) and Project::next_element_name (ELM-019). Polygon split: geo BooleanOps intersection of the outline with the two half-planes of the carrier line clipped to the element's bounding box; every resulting polygon becomes its own element, normalised (exterior counter-clockwise, holes clockwise) and repaired through validate::repair_outline; per-edge data (the SLB-005 edge angle of Outline<SlabEdge>, edit-reshape-palette-10) is copied from the original edge each new edge lies on through EdgeData::split, and cut edges get the default (90°). Linear split: pieces between consecutive carrier intersections (Point: the closest carrier point); a circle needs two cut points and becomes two arcs; a polyline splits into two polylines. Side: Left/Right of the directed cutter line, Before/After along the carrier for point cuts, returned for the tool's part choice. Out of scope: relation retargeting and hosted elements (18), tools and previews (19), splitting by a 3D plane (EDT-024, solid-kernel-ops-15), spline targets (Unsupported, task 07).
design: Commands carry an id_seed (a v4 UUID drawn when the command is created) so derived part ids are replay-stable even after crash recovery, where project.revision restarts; never derive ids from the revision. Keeping the original id on the first part keeps references (annotations, relations, selection) stable. Polygon splitting uses geo (a dependency of archicraft-model since edit-reshape-palette-01); snap i_overlay output vertices to input vertices within MODEL_TOLERANCE as edit-reshape-palette-04 does before mapping edge data. 'Joined' in WAL-030 means contact per D-6/WAL-020: the parts share an end point bitwise and whatever junction engine is present resolves the collinear continuation (junction-engine-12 has an active row for it). Every part passes validate_element in plan() before edits are emitted. Pitfalls: a multipolygon result produces more than two parts (all reported with their sides); circles have no ends (open them at the first cut parameter); a split exactly through a polyline node must not create a zero-length edge.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture split_slab_by_line (crates/archicraft-model/tests/linear_edit.rs, built from two_storey_shell): the ground slab (12 × 9 m) split by the line x = 5 gives slabs of 45 and 63 m² (sum 108 within 1e-9) and the left part keeps the original id; the upper slab with the stair hole (6,1)-(9,2.2) split at x = 7.5 gives two notched parts of 65.7 and 38.7 m² (sum 104.4 within 1e-9); a slab edge with a non-default angle keeps it on both halves and the cut edges get 90°; SplitPlan reports Left/Right correctly; Cutter::Edge on a face line of the interior wall splits the ground slab along that face.
- Fixture split_wall_by_line: the south exterior wall (0,0)-(12,0) split by the line x = 3 gives (0,0)-(3,0) with the original id and name and (3,0)-(12,0) with a derived id and the next W- name; the split point is bitwise identical in both parts; the ground-plan cut shows the two parts as one continuous region and their footprint areas sum to the original within 1e-9; undo restores the project exactly.
- WAL-030 geometry: Cutter::Point((3, 0)) gives the same two walls, joined by reference-line contact (D-6): they share the end point bitwise and the plan shows no gap.
- 2D cutters and targets (ANN-002): a DraftLine crossing a wall, used as Cutter::Edge, splits the wall; a DraftArc split by a line gives two arcs whose sweeps sum to the original within 1e-12 with centre and radius bits unchanged; a circle cut by a line gives two arcs; a polyline split mid-segment gives two polylines sharing the cut point bitwise.
- Replay and invalid cases: executing the same Command::Split from the same start twice (journal replay) yields identical part ids; a cutter missing the target gives NoChange with 'The cutting line does not cross <name>'; a part below RepairThresholds.min_edge_length or with zero area gives Invalid with a message; every case leaves the project unchanged.
- If regression-and-status-02 has landed, both fixtures are registered as EXTRA entries in crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs.
- EDT-013 model clauses for linear and polygon elements (walls, slabs, 2D elements; edge, guide and two-point line cutters) and the geometric clause of WAL-030 (two joined walls) satisfied; roofs and terrain are recorded for their epics.
notes:
SRS: EDT-013 WAL-030 ANN-002 (cutter clause)
Integration contract with doors-windows-core: Command::Split { targets, cutter: Cutter::Point(..), id_seed } as used by doors-windows-core-02/-11; the hosted-element half follows in task 18.

title: Wall direct manipulation: endpoint, face, offset and offset copy
description:
WHY — WAL-033 (M): move an endpoint, drag a face to change the thickness and offset the whole wall in parallel, all with numeric input. WAL-004 (M): the reference line stays when the thickness changes. EDT-010 (M): offset copy of walls at a typed distance. EDT-023 (S): offset copy of a chain of connected walls as a joined chain. The model operations exist after task 05; nothing in the app drives them (gap row WAL-033, partial: the model command and the numeric thickness field exist, but nothing in the app calls MoveElements and there are no handles or drags).

WHAT — ReshapeTool commands for walls: Move endpoint (from task 07, now with the TotalLength tracker = wall length and its change), Change thickness (drag a WallPart::Face handle of task 07; the tracker shows and accepts the resulting thickness; the preview moves the faces while the reference line stays drawn), Offset wall (drag the reference-line handle; typed distance; keep-joined on by default, toggled by a modifier named in the prompt) and Offset copy (pick a wall; typed distance; side from the cursor; the chain of the picked wall, or of the selected walls, is copied through Command::OffsetCopy). Wall palette entries for these commands, with 'Curve wall' as a stub and 'Straighten wall' disabled; the 'Offset' action of task 08 starts Offset copy when walls are selected. The numeric Thickness field of the properties strip (ui/properties.rs:254-266) stays the numeric path outside the tool. Out of scope: curve, straighten and arc radius (curved-geometry-02 and -11).
design: Face handles sit at the face midpoints given by ReferenceLine::face_offsets; the drag projects the cursor onto the wall's left normal through the reference line, so dragged and typed values are the signed face offset of ReshapeOp::MoveFace. For Outside and Inside walls only the free face gets a thickness handle; the face on the reference line offers Offset wall (refusal rule of task 05). Offset copy previews run wall_chains and offset_polyline of the model on clones and draw the copied footprints in the creation preview style. New ids are generated at commit (ElementId::new) and passed in Command::OffsetCopy.new_ids. Repeated copies until Esc follow the multiple-copy variant of EDT-002 if selection-transforms exposes it; otherwise one copy per command. Pointers: element.rs:98-107 (face_offsets), ui/properties.rs:254-266 (numeric thickness, WAL-004 behaviour already), views/plan.rs:225-235 (reference-line drawing).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: dragging the interior face handle of a 0.25 m wall with the reference line on the exterior face, or typing 0.30 in the thickness tracker, sets the thickness to 0.30 m while start and end stay bit-identical (WAL-004 invariant) and the reference line is drawn where it was.
- Consumer tests: an endpoint drag with typed total length 5 gives a 5.000 m wall; Offset wall 0.5 with keep-joined keeps the neighbouring walls' endpoints on the new line; Offset copy of the four-wall ring of storey_with_walls_and_slab with typed 0.3 towards the interior creates four joined walls in one undo step; a single wall copies to one parallel wall.
- The palettes of a wall endpoint, face and body list 'Move endpoint', 'Change thickness', 'Offset wall', 'Offset copy', 'Curve wall' (stub) and 'Straighten wall' (disabled).
- Then satisfied: WAL-033 except curve, straighten and arc radius; EDT-010 offset copy for walls; EDT-023.
notes:
SRS: WAL-033 EDT-010 EDT-023
(WAL-004 invariant) Appendix D.2: wall default 0.25 m, reference line on the exterior face. Curve, straighten and arc radius of WAL-033 arrive with curved-geometry through the same palette entries.

title: Add array and path distribution planners and commands
description:
WHY: EDT-004 (M): "An array command shall offer linear, radial, vertical-stack and rectangular (two-direction) arrays, with the methods: count and spacing; count distributed between a start and an end; spacing with the count set by the cursor; and count with the spacing set by the cursor. An optional vertical displacement per copy is available, and vertical arrays can assign home storeys by elevation (ELM-007)." EDT-005 (S): "Copies shall be distributable along a picked path (line, arc, polyline, spline, wall reference line) with an optional offset. Their orientation is unchanged or aligned to the path." IFX-011: array operations create new identities. Gap rows EDT-004/EDT-005 (missing): no array command of any type and no path distribution. Existing code this task builds on: selection-transforms-02's Transform and per-kind transform hook, selection-transforms-03's Project::duplicate (new ids, names from the counters, relations inside the set remapped) and selection-transforms-14's Command::ReassociateStoreys and Project::storey_mismatches.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/array.rs: `ArrayKind { Linear { direction }, Radial { centre, rotate_copies }, Vertical, Rectangular { u, v } }`, `ArrayMethod { CountSpacing { count, spacing }, CountBetween { count, end }, SpacingToExtent { spacing, extent }, CountToExtent { count, extent } }` (radial: spacing and extent are angles; rectangular: one method per direction; the 'cursor' of methods 3 and 4 becomes an extent measured by the tool), `dz_per_copy` and `assign_storeys`; `ArraySpec::placements() -> Result<Vec<Vec<Transform>>>` (copies only, the original stays; each copy is a short sequence of Transforms, for example Rotate about the centre followed by Move with the dz component). `PathSpec { path: ElementId, segment: Option<usize>, method: PathMethod { CountBetween { count, include_ends }, Spacing { spacing } }, offset, orientation: Unchanged | AlignedToPath, base: DVec2 }` with a kind hook `path_curve(&self) -> Option<Vec<Segment>>` (lines, arcs and polylines exactly; walls through the carrier hook of task 10; splines in task 07) and `path_placements()` by arc length. `Command::Array { ids, spec, id_seed }` and `Command::DistributeAlongPath { ids, spec, id_seed }` expand into copies through Project::duplicate, extended to take a transform sequence and an id source so copy ids come from ElementId::derived(id_seed, n) of task 10 instead of random v4 ids (IFX-011, replay-stable); dz_per_copy goes through Transform::Move's dz component (walls raise base_offset); with assign_storeys copies are re-homed by elevation through the ReassociateStoreys planning; kinds whose TransformSupport has no vertical move (2D elements) are placed on the storey at the copy's target elevation when assign_storeys is set (their view follows the new storey) and refused with Unsupported naming the kind otherwise. Out of scope: tools and previews (15), associative arrays (copies are independent elements), the copy binding of annotations (sections-elevations-dims-17 hooks into this copy path).
design: Placements are pure data (sequences of Transform), so the tool's preview (15) and the command share them; copies are produced by the same transform hook and Project::duplicate as EDT-001/EDT-002, so every registered kind supports arrays without array-specific code and kinds that cannot represent a transform report Unsupported (EDT-007 convention). Arc length is exact for lines and arcs (radius·angle). selection-transforms-15's TransformEach can carry per-copy transforms if one edit list per array is preferred. railings-stairs-adv-01 may reuse the station arithmetic of path_placements, so keep it a pure function of length and parameters. Pitfalls: 'count distributed between a start and an end' puts the original at the start and the last copy at the end (spacing = length / count); zero spacing would stack copies on the original (reject); radial arrays of walls rotate their reference lines exactly; cap counts at 1,000 copies with a confirmation in the tool.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table-driven test over the 16 combinations of the four kinds and four methods with expected placements, for example linear CountSpacing(4, 1.5 m) along +x gives copies at 1.5, 3.0, 4.5 and 6.0 m; CountBetween(4, end 8 m) gives spacing 2 m with the last copy at the end; SpacingToExtent(1.2 m, 5.0 m) gives 4 copies; CountToExtent(4, 6.0 m) gives spacing 1.5 m; radial CountSpacing(5, 60°) with rotate_copies rotates copy k by k·60°; vertical CountSpacing(2, 3.0 m) on two_storey_shell with assign_storeys homes the first copy on the upper storey; rectangular 3 × 2 gives 5 copies.
- Command tests: arraying a wall and a 2D line creates elements with new ids and names, undo removes all copies and a save/load round trip keeps all ids unique (IFX-011); dz_per_copy 0.5 raises copy k's base offset by 0.5·k; a vertical array of a 2D line without assign_storeys is refused with a message naming the kind, with assign_storeys its copy is bound to the upper storey's plan.
- Path tests: CountBetween(5, include ends) along a 10 m DraftLine with offset 0.5 and orientation Unchanged places copies at 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5 and 10 m shifted 0.5 m to the left, none rotated; along a quarter arc with AlignedToPath each copy's rotation equals the tangent-angle change within 1e-12; along an L-shaped polyline with an arc corner the copies are equally spaced by exact arc length within 1e-12; a wall reference line behaves like a line.
- Replay with the same id_seed gives identical ids; invalid specs (count 0, spacing <= 0, parallel u and v) are rejected with messages; Project::duplicate without an id source keeps its random ids (copy-move unchanged).
- EDT-004 model clauses satisfied (all kinds and methods, vertical displacement, storey assignment); EDT-005 model clauses satisfied for lines, arcs, polylines and wall reference lines with offset and both orientations (splines in task 07).
notes:
SRS: EDT-004 EDT-005 (model)
Method names follow the SRS wording; the extent of methods 3 and 4 is the cursor distance or angle measured by the tool.

title: Add the spline kind with adaptive tessellation and its editing hooks
description:
WHY: ANN-011 (S): "Further 2D shapes shall be provided: rectangles and rotated rectangles, splines, and arcs and circles tangent to one to three elements (choosing among several solutions)." This task covers splines; rectangles and tangent arcs are task 08 and node editing is task 17. EDT-005 (S) distributes copies along a picked path that may be a spline, and ANN-002 makes every 2D element a cutter for trim and split. Epic risk: "Splines are a rabbit hole: v1 tessellates Catmull-Rom/Bezier through points with node editing only." The task runs after trim/extend (11) and path distribution (14) so the spline implements their hooks directly instead of leaving gaps. Gap row ANN-011 (missing): no 2D shapes of any kind.

WHAT: New kind `DraftSpline { points: Vec<DVec2>, closed: bool, style, view }` in kinds/drafting.rs (code spline, prefix SPL because SP is taken by spaces in could-scope-polish-06): a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline (α = 0.5) through its points, evaluated as cubic Bézier spans in a spline submodule of crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs with `Spline::flatten(&Tessellation) -> Vec<DVec2>` (adaptive subdivision until the chordal deviation is <= δ and the turning per segment <= θmax); tessellate() gains `TessCurve::Spline` delegating to it; geometry (a GeometryKind line in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/drafting.rs, curves through ModelGeometry), plan, picking, snapping (through points as node targets, flattened pieces as edge targets) and the contour source as in tasks 04 and 16; IFCX codec `archicraft::spline` {points, closed} with a Curve child in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/drafting.rs; drafting_sample extended and the golden re-blessed.
