Editing hooks: as a trim, split or extend target the spline returns Unsupported ('Convert the spline to a polyline first'); as a trim or extend boundary its cutting_curves (task 11) are the flattened pieces; a picked piece serves as Cutter::Edge for split (task 10); path_curve (task 14) is the flattened polyline measured by arc length; transforms apply to the through points (uniform scale included); offset copy returns Unsupported with a message. Tool: a Spline mode on the Polyline tool of task 06 (clicks add through points, Enter or double-click finishes, clicking the first point closes). Out of scope: node editing (17), tension or handle editing, NURBS, conversion to polyline (a cheap follow-up if users ask).
design: Centripetal Catmull-Rom avoids cusps and self-intersections on uneven point spacing; convert each span to a cubic Bézier with the centripetal parameterisation and subdivide by de Casteljau until the flatness bound (largest distance of the inner control points from the chord) is <= δ and the tangent turn is <= θmax: conservative, deterministic and without a new dependency (kurbo was dropped in the technology choices). Open splines use reflected phantom end points; closed splines wrap indices. Flattening lives in the model crate so the command planners (trim boundaries, path distribution) can use it inside Command::plan(); tessellate() in archicraft-geometry delegates to it, keeping one producer. Splines are approximations, not exact curves, which is why they serve as boundaries and paths but not as trim targets. Pitfalls: the IFCX codec stores the through points only, never the Bézier controls; picking spline pieces uses the tessellation; duplicate consecutive through points are repaired like polyline nodes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spline tests: the tessellation contains every input point bitwise as a vertex; the maximum distance between the tessellation and a dense 10,000-sample evaluation is <= δ; a closed spline is C1 at the seam (tangent difference < 1e-9); collinear points give a straight tessellation; tessellate(spline) twice is bit-identical and equals ModelGeometry::curve and the plan points bitwise.
- Hooks: trimming a DraftLine back to a crossing spline (task 11 planner) ends the line on the flattened spline within δ; distributing 5 copies along a spline (task 14 planner, CountBetween with ends) spaces them equally by arc length within δ (EDT-005 spline clause); Command::Trim, Split or Extend with a spline target returns CommandError::Unsupported with the conversion message; mirroring a spline mirrors its through points.
- IFCX: the extended drafting_sample round-trips with spline points bit-identical; golden re-blessed with a reviewed diff; conformance green.
- kittest: the Spline mode is reachable from the 2D group; a spline drawn by four clicks and Enter adds one element (undo label 'Create spline').
- ANN-011 spline clause satisfied; EDT-005's spline-path clause satisfied; ANN-002's cutter clause holds for splines as trim boundaries and split edges.
notes:
SRS: ANN-011 EDT-005 ANN-002 (spline kind, spline path, spline as boundary)
Prefix proposal SPL (SP is taken by could-scope-polish-06).

title: Read doors and windows from IFCX and add the ground-floor golden
description:
WHY: An exported door or window must come back as the same editable, hosted unit. DW-018's occurrences, Void children and typed parts satisfy the round trip only if the reader restores them, and AS-03 requires that elements stay parametric and keep their UUIDs after close and reopen. DW-001's host rule must survive loading: a door is restored only inside its host wall, and an orphan is repaired by the deterministic host-openings rule (NFR-REL-004). The epic acceptance also asks that IfcDoor/IfcWindow occurrences with Void children and material parts pass conformance on the golden files. Today reader.rs reads only storey children with kind wall or slab (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:604-607, 854-858). host-openings-09 adds the descent into hosted children and the integrity.rs repair of orphaned hosted elements, and components-dw-catalogue-08 reads archicraft::component, with placeholders for missing definitions.

WHAT: The read half of the door and window codecs (alpha/kinds/door.rs and window.rs) maps archicraft::door/window back into WallInsert. host-openings-09's descent reads them as hosted children of wall nodes, with the parent node as the host (tree position wins), and the instance comes from archicraft::component. Missing or invalid values become report warnings with defaults (report.or, reader.rs:57), and the integrity.rs host checks re-host or remove orphans with a report entry.

Add samples::ground_floor_with_openings() to crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs, built with the FixtureBuilder through commands:
- two storeys; on the ground floor, an exterior ring of F2 'Cavity wall 680' walls joined at L corners, plus two interior 0.25 m walls forming a T;
- a door at an L corner, a door next to the T, three windows (one with a Head pin referencing the upper storey) and an empty opening;
- one door flipped and one door with the other hinge end.
Register it in samples::catalogue() (element-kind-framework-03), which feeds crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and samples() of tests/roundtrip.rs, and bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/ground-floor-openings.ifcx. Extend conformance/check.ts so that every IfcDoor/IfcWindow node composes as a child of an IfcWall, with exactly one invisible Void and inherited material parts. Out of scope: third-party IfcDoor import without archicraft:: data (ifcx-interop).
design:
Follow the 'Add a sample/golden model' extension point (docs/implementation-status.md); with element-kind-framework-03 the single registration point is samples::catalogue(). Bless with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx --test roundtrip and inspect the diff.

The sample is built through Commands only (FixtureBuilder edit()), so it exercises the 02 commands and stays valid when validation tightens; the builder gives v5 ids derived from the fixture name.

Reader order: walls first, then hosted children, so the Host relation is validated against an existing wall. Run the relation-store integrity check (integrity_problems) after loading.

check.ts: extend the composition walk of host-openings-08 and components-dw-catalogue-09 instead of adding a second traversal.

Pitfall: the reader must not trust the occurrence transform for placement. The authoritative placement is the archicraft:: data; a mismatch with the stored transform is reported, not silently overwritten.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/roundtrip.rs: written_files_validate_without_problems, round_trip_restores_the_editable_model, regenerated_geometry_matches_the_stored_geometry, written_meshes_are_closed_bodies, spatial_tree_and_identities and golden_files_are_reproduced all pass with ground_floor_with_openings among the samples (DW-018, AS-03 UUID stability).
- Round trip: every door and window keeps its id, host, along, anchor, width, height, vertical pin and reference storey, reveal, exterior side, configuration, definition and parameters; the comparison is bit-exact, because parameters are written at full precision (NFR-ACC-002).
- An occurrence whose parent is not a wall, or whose host is missing, is repaired or removed by the host-openings integrity rule and reported with its node path; an unknown definition opens as a labelled placeholder (DW-001 on load, NFR-REL-004).
- An occurrence whose stored usd::xformop differs by more than 0.1 mm from the transform recomputed from archicraft::door loads from the archicraft:: data, and the mismatch is reported (IFX-031).
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green, including the new check.ts assertion (DW-018).
- A file at the previous FORMAT_VERSION still loads through the migration table (IFX-062).
- The golden diff is reviewed: one new file, and the existing goldens unchanged since the re-blessing in 05.
notes: SRS: DW-018 DW-001 (plus AS-03, IFX-006 a, IFX-011, IFX-031, IFX-062, NFR-ACC-002, NFR-REL-004, NFR-MNT-003). The same sample is the input of the split check (11), the scripted scenario (12) and the AS-01 'walls show openings' viewer check (12).

title: Script the increment-1 ground-floor scenario and the AS-01 openings check
design:
The scenario script is a procedure for a human tester (SRS 7.1 Test: 'scripted manual tests for interaction-heavy requirements'). Keep it short, deterministic and value-checked.

Keep the typed coordinates of the headless test and of the script identical, so a failing manual step can be reproduced headlessly. Expected values come from the sample and from independent arithmetic (footprint areas times heights minus voids), never from running the code under test.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ground_floor_precision.rs passes: the typed-input reconstruction equals samples::ground_floor_with_openings() for every wall end and every door and window placement within MODEL_TOLERANCE, and the formatted values match at 0.1 mm / 0.01 degrees (Appendix F increment-1 exit, AS-04 precision).
- docs/test-plan/increment-1-ground-floor.md exists with numbered steps, each naming the requirement it exercises (DW-001 to DW-008, DW-010, DW-018, VIEW-055), expected values to 0.1 mm / 0.01 degrees and a results table.
- The procedure has been executed once on one platform, with date, platform, build and pass/fail per step recorded in the document; failures are filed as beads under the epic.
- AS-01 'walls show openings': the headless viewer run on tests/golden/ground-floor-openings.ifcx shows the IfcDoor/IfcWindow nodes under their walls and the cut walls, with a screenshot attached to the run; or, if the viewer job does not exist yet, a manual viewer check with a screenshot is recorded in the scenario document (DW-018, IFX-006 b).
notes: SRS: DW-001 DW-002 DW-003 DW-004 DW-005 DW-006 DW-007 DW-008 DW-010 DW-018 VIEW-055 (plus Appendix F increment 1, AS-01, AS-04 display precision, SRS 7.1 scripted manual tests, IFX-006 b). reference-models reuses the scenario for AS-01.

title: Edit insert placement and size in the properties strip and dialog
design:
Follow the existing Fields getter/setter pattern in properties.rs (fields auto-hide when the getter returns None) and the unit-aware widgets in ui/widgets.rs, so lengths respect the project's units and typed-input parsing (units.rs).

If properties-and-dialogs has landed, its FieldSpec/registry-driven panel replaces the hard-coded geometry_fields (properties.rs:253-264). Then implement these fields as FieldSpec entries of the door and window descriptors; the acceptance is the same.

Field edits must not go through UpdateElements with a whole element copy. They map to the field-specific commands of 02, so multi-selection, the anchor and pin invariants and the storey reassignment rules apply uniformly.

The immediate void update relies on Document's revision-based re-evaluation (document.rs:97-103), or on the incremental evaluation of element-kind-framework-10. No UI-side geometry code.

Pitfall: the debt note for properties.rs:295 (an arbitrary default when switching a wall to a custom reference line) must not be copied. When the reveal face changes with 'keep position', SetInsertReveal converts the offset so the unit stays in place, and the field shows the converted value.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): with the door tool active and nothing selected, setting Width to 1.000 in the strip changes the door slot's width, no element changes, and the next placed door is 1.000 m wide (DW-006 'new elements when nothing is selected').
- kittest: with a door selected, setting Width to 1.000 updates the door and, in the next frame, the host wall's evaluated volume, so the void follows; undo restores both (DW-006 'selection otherwise', 'immediately').
- kittest: with anchor Right (AlongEnd), a width change keeps the right edge; with a Head pin, a height change keeps the head (DW-005, DW-007).
- kittest: 'Flip exterior side' changes only the side; the hinge, swing and sliding fields each change only their own value (DW-003, DW-004 'changed independently').
- kittest: switching the reference to another storey with 'keep elevation' checked keeps the derived sill, and with it unchecked keeps the offset (DW-007 'reassigned').
- kittest: switching the reveal face from Exterior to Core interior on an F2 host with 'keep position' checked keeps the unit in place and shows the converted offset; on a 0.25 m Thickness host the core-face options are not offered (DW-008).
- kittest: selecting two doors with different widths shows the field as mixed, and typing a value sets both in one undo step.
- Unit test: the field set for each catalogue type matches its leaf kind (no hinge fields for sliding or fixed types, no configuration fields for empty openings).
notes: SRS: DW-003 DW-004 DW-005 DW-006 DW-007 DW-008 (plus DW-012 schema inspector from components-dw-catalogue). Out of scope here, delivered by library-dw-exchange: DW-015 derived values.

title: Evaluate geometry incrementally from a dirty set
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-006 (M): after a single-element edit in RM-M the plan view and the 3D view shall be updated within 200 ms, including recomputing junctions and openings of affected neighbouring elements. VIEW-001 (M): all views derive from the single model and an edit appears in all open views (NFR-PERF-006). Gap: ModelGeometry::evaluate re-extrudes and re-triangulates every element on every revision (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:64-91), wall footprints compare every pair per storey (wall.rs:203-248) and the app drops all caches (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103). NFR-ACC-003's tolerance (task 01) defines contact, the relation store (task 08) defines dependency, the stand-ins (task 03) make locality testable, and the geometry registry (task 15) gives every kind one generator. Both requirements are partial: propagation is correct (one Document, revision-keyed caches, neighbours' junctions recomputed because all footprints are), but unmeasured and not incremental.

WHAT: Model: Project.changes, a ChangeLog (serde skip, PartialEq always true) that Edit::apply fills in both directions: per-element stamps for InsertElement and ReplaceElement, tombstones for RemoveElement, the storeys whose elevation, height or order changed for SetStoreys, and a full-invalidation stamp for SetSettings (tessellation). Geometry: ModelGeometry { revision, elements: HashMap<ElementId, Arc<ElementGeometry>>, problems, changed, changed_storeys, contact index }; dirty_set(project, previous) -> DirtySet = stamped and removed elements, the closure of relations.dependents_of over them, contact neighbours (walls on the same storey whose reference lines lie within MODEL_TOLERANCE of a dirty wall's old or new reference line, found through an rstar 0.12 RTree of segments inflated by MODEL_TOLERANCE), and storey_dependents of changed storeys; ModelGeometry::evaluate_incremental(project, &previous) re-evaluates only the dirty set through the geometry registry, recomputes footprints only for dirty walls with the same per-end resolution, keeps the Arc and problem entry of every clean element, and records changed and changed_storeys; ModelGeometry::evaluate becomes the incremental path from an empty previous and also uses the RTree instead of the per-storey pair scan. Property test with a seeded xorshift PRNG inside the test (no new dependency). Out of scope: app caches and 3D scene reuse (task 11), GPU upload (perf-tuning-rm-m-l), the CI timing gate (regression-and-status calls this API), openings (host-openings adds Host relations that flow through dependents_of).
design: Stamps instead of a per-consumer dirty queue so geometry, plans and the 3D scene can each diff against their own last revision. The junction resolution is already order-independent per end (decision D-6), which is what makes incremental and full results bit-identical: keep resolving each end from the same candidate set, only found through the index instead of a scan. Use rstar at the version geo pins (0.12, technology-choices) so only one copy is compiled. Keep catch_unwind per element and carry problems of clean elements forward. Pitfalls: a moved or deleted wall must dirty its neighbours at the old position, so ModelGeometry keeps the previous wall inputs; the ChangeLog is not saved, so the first evaluation after load is full; a storey elevation change does not alter storey-local bodies of slabs or fixed-height walls, but re-evaluate them anyway (correctness first; optimise later if measurements ask for it); ChangeLog must never take part in Project equality. Pointers: evaluate.rs:51-120, wall.rs:203-248, command.rs:616-728, document.rs:95-121.
acceptance_criteria:
- dirty_set_after_one_edit_is_local: on stand_in(5_000), moving one interior wall yields exactly the wall plus the walls touching its old or new reference line (checked against a brute-force contact computation); a storey elevation change dirties exactly the elements homed on or linked to the moved storeys; deleting a wall dirties its former neighbours.
- incremental_equals_full: 200 seeded random edit sequences of length 1-20 on stand_in(1_000) (move, thickness, reference line, delete, add, storey elevation, relink, undo, redo) give ModelGeometry contents (elements, parts, children, axes, problems) bit-identical (TriMesh ==) to a fresh ModelGeometry::evaluate; the seed is printed on failure.
- relation and junction neighbours: with a test-kinds dummy hosted in a wall of stand_in(1_000) through Relation::Host, moving the wall dirties the dummy and editing the dummy dirties the wall (the path host-openings' openings take, NFR-PERF-006 'openings of affected neighbouring elements'); the walls joined to an edited wall get recomputed footprints equal to a full evaluation ('recomputing junctions').
- Unchanged elements keep the same Arc (Arc::ptr_eq) across an incremental step; changed and changed_storeys equal the recomputed sets; undo produces the same dirty set as the original edit.
- Full evaluation of stand_in(20_000) uses the RTree path (asserted) and an #[ignore]d smoke test prints its duration.
- Timing smoke test (#[ignore], release, documented for regression-and-status): evaluate_incremental after one wall move on stand_in(5_000) completes well under 200 ms and prints the number.
- Existing geometry, slice, mesh, plan and round-trip tests and the goldens are unchanged; NFR-PERF-006 mechanism in place (budget verified by regression-and-status); NFR-ACC-003 governs contact.
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-006 VIEW-001 NFR-ACC-003. Open question: whether storey elevation edits should skip elements whose storey-local body is unchanged; not needed for the 200 ms target on 5,000 elements.

title: Add outline union, difference and hole commands
description:
WHY — EDT-015 (S): polygon-based elements shall support adding and subtracting a drawn polygon to or from their outline (union and difference of outlines). SLB-003 (M): a slab can contain any number of holes, editable like the outline, drawn or traced. SLB-008 (M) names EDT-015 for slab outlines and holes. Gap rows: no UI path creates a hole (every tool completion passes Vec::new(), views/tools.rs:510, 513, 527), and union/difference do not exist although geo's BooleanOps (i_overlay) is already a workspace dependency (used for unary_union in geometry/plan.rs:156).

WHAT — `Outline::union(&Ring)` and `Outline::difference(&Ring)` in crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/boolean.rs on geo::BooleanOps; `ReshapeOp::{Union{polygon}, Difference{polygon}, AddHole{polygon}, DeleteHole}` (DeleteHole addresses PartRef::Ring with ring >= 1); per-edge data inherited by collinear matching; every result validated and repaired by task 02. Out of scope: drawing the polygon (task 08), tracing it (task 12), splitting an element (EDT-013 in drafting-trim-split).
design: Convert through the geo conversions of task 01; BooleanOps returns a MultiPolygon: zero parts means everything was removed, more than one part is rejected (union: disjoint; difference: split). Post-process i_overlay output: rotate the result ring so it starts at the vertex nearest the original vertex 0 (stable node numbering for the palette), snap output vertices within MODEL_TOLERANCE of an input vertex back to its exact coordinates, and drop collinear vertices that exist in neither input. Edge data: for each result edge find a collinear, overlapping input edge (outline rings first, then the drawn polygon) and inherit its data. AddHole is a Difference restricted to polygons strictly inside the outline, so the intent stays explicit in the journal. Pitfalls: geo rings are closed (first == last); keep one fill rule consistent with the orientation normalisation; a polygon sharing an edge with the outline must not leave sliver residue (the repair pipeline removes sub-threshold edges, never silently self-intersections). Pointers: geo-0.33.1 src/algorithm/bool_ops/mod.rs (union/difference), geometry/plan.rs:150-160.
acceptance_criteria:
- reshape tests on a 12 x 9 m slab (108 m²): union with the rectangle x 11..14, y 2..4 gives one ring of 112 m²; difference with x 10..13, y 7..10 gives a notch and 104 m²; a difference strictly inside adds a hole (same result as AddHole); a difference overlapping an existing hole enlarges that hole (still one hole); a union covering a hole removes it.
- Rejections with messages: union with a disjoint polygon ('The polygon must overlap or touch the outline.'); a difference that would split the slab (message points to Split); a difference covering the whole slab ('Delete the slab instead.'); AddHole touching the outline (hole message).
- DeleteHole removes ring 1 and undo restores it; every op passes execute/undo/redo and a serde round trip.
- Per-edge data: TestEdge tags of untouched outline edges survive union and difference; edges created from the drawn polygon get Default; unchanged corners keep bit-identical coordinates.
- Then satisfied at model level: EDT-015 and the hole-editing clause of SLB-003.
notes:
SRS: EDT-015 SLB-003 SLB-008
Open question: whether a difference that splits a slab should create two slabs (EDT-013 split semantics) instead of being rejected; rejected here with a pointer to Split.

title: Add the split tool with part choice, menu commands and the gesture checklist
description:
WHY: EDT-013 (M): split by "a picked edge, a guide or a temporary two-point line. The user chooses which part stays selected." WAL-030 (M): splitting a wall at a point. EDT-020 (M) and D-7: every gesture-capable operation (trim, split, extend, parameter pick-up and inject, contour detection) is also an explicit command with a preview. Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for split (gap row WAL-030: 'D.8 split shortcut absent from actions.rs'). Epic acceptance: splitting "a slab or wall by a two-point line keep[s] the chosen part selected (fixtures)" and "every gesture has a menu command with a preview (inspection checklist)". The ChooseSide cursor exists in point-input-snapping-03's CursorState and persistent guides in input/guide_set.rs (point-input-snapping-11).

WHAT: A Split InputConsumer in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/linear_edit.rs: targets are the selection or one picked element; the cutter step takes a clicked edge of any element or 2D line (Cutter::Edge), a persistent guide (its two defining points as Cutter::Line), a temporary two-point line (Cutter::Line) or a single click on a linear target for a point split (Cutter::Point, WAL-030); the preview shows the cut line and the parts from plan_split in alternating tints; then the ChooseSide cursor: clicking a side keeps those parts selected, Enter keeps all parts selected, Esc cancels; execution uses Command::Split with a fresh id_seed and puts the SplitPlan part ids into the Workspace selection. Explicit commands: Edit > Split, the context-menu entry and the D.8 Split shortcut; extend `appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts` with Split. Checklist: docs/commands-and-gestures.md lists every gesture-capable operation (trim, extend, split, merge walls, contour detection from edit-reshape-palette-12, parameter pick-up/inject as open under ELM-003 with templates-presets-11) with its gesture, menu path, shortcut, preview and the test proving it. Out of scope: splitting by a 3D plane (solid-kernel-ops-16), array and path tools (15).
design: The preview runs plan_split, so preview and result cannot diverge; the cutter is resolved to plain points before the command is built (guides are app-side state, the command carries Cutter::Line points). Shortcut proposal (to be confirmed by commands-and-l10n): Split K. Pitfalls: the part tints must stay distinguishable from the selection colour and in dark mode; after Split the Workspace selection holds exactly the ids SplitPlan reports for the chosen side; contour detection's key and explicit command come from edit-reshape-palette-12 and are only listed in the checklist.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool tests without egui: splitting the ground slab of two_storey_shell by a two-point line at x = 5 with the side click on the left leaves exactly the left part selected; Enter keeps both parts selected; a persistent guide at x = 7.5 used as cutter splits the upper slab; a single click on the south wall at (3, 0) performs the WAL-030 point split and selects the chosen part; a Dummy hosted at x = 8 ends on the second part (task 18's hook through the tool); Esc before the side choice leaves the project unchanged.
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs kittests: the Edit menu contains Split; the Split shortcut activates the tool; a two-point split in the plan pane adds one element and the undo label reads 'Split'; the preview shows two tinted parts before the side click; `shortcuts_are_unique` and the extended `appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts` pass.
- docs/commands-and-gestures.md exists and every row names an existing test function (inspection checklist, ticked in the done task).
- EDT-020 satisfied for trim, split, extend and contour detection (pick-up/inject stays open with ELM-003 in templates-presets); the UI clauses of EDT-013 (edge, guide and two-point line cutters; part choice) and WAL-030 (split at a point) satisfied.
notes:
SRS: EDT-020 EDT-013 WAL-030 ANN-002 (split tool, part choice, explicit commands, gesture checklist)
EDT-020's parameter pick-up/inject clause stays open until templates-presets (ELM-003).

title: Draw and snap 2D elements in plan views and trace from them
description:
WHY: ANN-001: each 2D element has a pen and a line type, so it is drawn with them (DSP-001; DSP-004: colour and weight come from the pen and no line is thinner than one device pixel; DSP-008: lines follow their line type). INP-008 requires snapping to nodes, edge points, midpoints, intersections, perpendicular and tangent points and arc and circle centres, so 2D lines and arcs must feed the snap index. ANN-002 (M): 2D elements "act as tracing input for contour detection (INP-018)"; the epic acceptance says "a slab is traced from a closed chain of 2D lines in one pick". Existing code this task extends: views/plan_style.rs PlanPens and the line-type dash drawing (plan-attributes-07), the SnapIndex and SnapSource of crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs with circle and arc targets (centre, radius, sweep) and the full glyph set (point-input-snapping-02/-03), and the contour-detection step of the wall and slab tools (edit-reshape-palette-12).

WHAT: Drawing in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draw_plan (plan.rs:237 today): drafting curves from PlanElement.drafting through PlanPens (pen colour and screen width, floored at one device pixel) and the line type's dashes via the dashed-path helper plan-attributes-07 uses for overhead lines (paper-millimetre dashes at the 1:100 default, model-size dashes through the camera scale), with hover and selection highlighting in the screen-only pens like other elements; views/plan_gpu.rs instead if plan-renderer has landed. Snapping: a SnapSource for drafting elements in input/targets.rs: line end points and polyline nodes as element nodes, midpoints, arc ends, arc and circle centres (Node level, centre detail), lines as edges and arcs and circles as circle targets with their sweep, so Edge, Tangent, Perpendicular and Intersection snaps on arcs are exact rather than on chords; fingerprints from the stored parameters. Tracing: no new code path; with the segment source of task 04 registered, the contour-detection step of the slab and wall tools traces regions and chains bounded by 2D lines, and its ContourGraph cache (per plan revision and storey, edit-reshape-palette-12) is invalidated by 2D edits through the revision like any element edit. The 3D view skips body-less kinds (render3d build_scene filters descriptor.has_body). Out of scope: creation tools (06), splines (07), fills (09).
design: The drawing code reads curve points from ModelGeometry via the PlanDrawing (task 04) and never tessellates, so the screen shows the same vertices the IFCX writer exports. Exact circle targets keep typed and snapped points on arcs from being up to 2 mm off (AS-04 precision); point-input-snapping-03 already supports sweep-limited circle targets, so this task only produces them. Pitfalls: DSP-004's one-pixel floor applies to drafting pens; model-size dashes of a very long line must be capped like other dashed lines to avoid thousands of strokes; never draw 2D elements in render3d.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Snap tests on the SnapIndex without egui: Centre on an arc centre; Tangent from a previous point to a circle lands within 1e-9 of the analytic tangent point; Intersection of a 2D line with a wall face; an Edge snap on an arc lands on the circle within 1e-9 (not on a chord); a tangent candidate outside an arc's sweep is not offered; a locked 2D element still snaps (INP-017).
- Tracing test without egui (edit-reshape-palette-12's tool hook): with the slab tool and contour detection on, one click inside the four-line rectangle of task 04 emits AddElements of a slab whose outline equals the rectangle within 1e-12; with the wall tool a click on the chain creates four joined walls in one undo step (ANN-002 tracing clause).
- Drawing tests on the shapes built for one frame: a 2D line with the DASH line type produces more than one stroke and its dash period matches the line type at the default scale; a hairline pen draws at least one device pixel wide; a selected 2D line uses the selection pen.
- Kittest smoke in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: a plan with drafting elements renders without panic; hovering a 2D line shows the pre-selection highlight; the 3D view of the same project renders without a drafting body.
- App half of ANN-001 (drawn with pen and line type) and the tracing clause of ANN-002 satisfied end to end.
notes: SRS: ANN-001 ANN-002 (drawing, snapping and the tracing clause end to end)

title: Register per-kind IFCX attribute codecs
description:
WHY: IFX-060 (M): everything needed to restore the editable model is stored in archicraft:: attributes: element parameters, reference lines, storey links, junction settings, layer structures, profiles, presets, layers, views and project settings (examples archicraft::element, archicraft::wall, archicraft::slab, archicraft::project); IFX-061 requires every such attribute to be declared in the file. Writer, reader and schema hard-code wall and slab: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:20-25 (attribute names, KINDS), :97-124 (slot schemas), :207 (counters), :212-257 (declarations); writer.rs:97-120 and :192-217 (element_attributes); reader.rs:433-497 (read_tool_defaults) and :592-734 (read_element). IFX-060 is partial because junction settings, layer structures, profiles and presets do not exist yet; their epics (junction-engine, layer-structures, profiles-columns-beams, templates-presets) and every new kind need one place to plug in an attribute instead of editing three files. Existing (keep): project settings, layers, materials, tool defaults, views, counters, storey, element, wall and slab data are written (writer.rs:142-190/192-217/314-321/403-414) and round_trip_restores_the_editable_model (tests/roundtrip.rs:48) proves that they restore the model.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/{mod.rs,common.rs,wall.rs,slab.rs,dummy.rs} (dummy behind the crate's own test-kinds feature, which forwards archicraft-model/test-kinds and is enabled through a self dev-dependency). A KindCodec trait per payload (ATTRIBUTE, schema(), write(&payload) -> Map, read(attr, &ReadContext, &mut Report) -> Result<payload, String>, and slot_schema/write_slot/read_slot for the defaults parameters) plus an object-safe erased form and a codecs! macro producing CODECS with one line per kind. common.rs keeps the shared helpers (point2, top_link, reference_line, material reference repair). schema.rs builds the per-kind declarations, the kind enumeration, the toolDefaults object and the counters object from CODECS, emitting them only for kinds present in the project (an element, a defaults slot or a non-zero counter), in registry order. writer.rs element_attributes and the toolDefaults part of project_attribute dispatch through the codec; reader.rs read_element and read_tool_defaults dispatch through it with a ReadContext (materials, layers, storeys, element name), and today's lenient behaviour (thickness 0.25 m with a warning, missing parameters skip the element with an error) moves verbatim into kinds/wall.rs and kinds/slab.rs. The temporary writer wildcard arm of task 02 disappears. Extend the module-layout test to crates/archicraft-ifcx/src. Existing files stay byte-identical. Out of scope: compound parts and containment (task 07), relations (task 08), the nested slot shape and migration (task 12), project-level resources (their epics).
design: The trait lives in the ifcx crate and is implemented for model payload types (the orphan rule allows it because the trait is local); the erased form returns Some only for its own variant, so writer.rs calls CODECS.iter().find_map(...). Content-derived declarations are the answer to a real pitfall: with test-kinds unified into workspace test builds, a static declaration list would add archicraft::dummy and a dummy enumeration option to every golden written by cargo test, making test and release output differ. JSON member order must stay the insertion order used today (writer.rs:192-217, serde_json preserve_order) to keep goldens byte-identical. Keep the schema combinators (object, optional, enumeration, length, ...) pub(crate) for the codecs. The slot keeps today's flat member order (codec parameters, then material, layer, position, ifcClass, predefinedType); note that toolDefaults writes material as a String while elements use the Reference data type (schema.rs:106 vs :240). Pointers: schema.rs:15-125/195-257, writer.rs:97-120/144-217/361-417, reader.rs:433-497/592-734.
acceptance_criteria:
- Golden files bit-identical; all round-trip tests pass unchanged (validation, exact round trip, regenerated geometry, determinism, closed meshes, spatial tree, golden, JSON schema, lenient reading, malformed input, third-party rejection, cycles).
- every_kind_has_a_codec: CODECS covers every KindTag and no codec lacks a kind; attribute ids are unique and start with archicraft::.
- A dummy element (test-kinds) with each top link (Fixed, Storey, Relative, non-zero offset) and walls with each reference line round-trip through save and load equal and with no problems (IFX-060 element parameters, reference lines and storey links).
- every_project_field_is_persisted: the top-level fields of Project's serde form (minus #[serde(skip)] fields) and of every kind payload are each mapped to the archicraft:: member that stores them by a table in alpha/kinds/mod.rs; the test fails when a field is added without a mapping, so the IFX-060 categories that do not exist yet (junction settings, layer structures, profiles, presets) cannot be added by their epics without being stored.
- Module-layout test: Dummy and "dummy" occur in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src only in alpha/kinds/dummy.rs and one line of alpha/kinds/mod.rs.
- A project with walls only declares archicraft::wall but not archicraft::slab, its kind enumeration is ["wall"], and it validates without problems; a test-kinds build and a release build write identical bytes for the two samples (the goldens).
- invalid_elements_are_skipped_and_reported, missing_references_are_repaired_and_reported and schema_violations_are_reported pass through the codec path; a wall node without thickness loads with 0.25 m and one warning.
- Source scan: writer.rs, reader.rs and schema.rs contain no per-kind arm (no ElementKind::Wall/Slab, no "archicraft::wall"/"archicraft::slab" literal outside alpha/kinds/); IFX-060 element parameters and storey links of every registered kind are written by that kind's codec.
notes: SRS: IFX-060. Also keeps IFX-061 and IFX-064 green. The codecs are the hook later epics use for archicraft::column, archicraft::opening, archicraft::roof, archicraft::stair and so on.

title: Ship the seeded fixture builder and synthetic stand-ins
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-006 (M): after a single-element edit in RM-M (about 5,000 elements, SRS 7.3) the plan view and the 3D view shall be updated within 200 ms, including junctions and openings of affected neighbours; VIEW-001 (M) binds view propagation to that budget. Both are partial: views already refresh from project.revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:95-121) and junctions are recomputed for all walls, but the gap rows for both say no benchmark, criterion target or RM-M fixture exists; task 10 needs a 5,000-element model for its dirty-set test, and regression-and-status benchmarks 1,000/5,000/20,000-element stand-ins until reference-models delivers RM-M and RM-L (RM-L is repeated RM-M blocks). Identity (IFX-010, IFX-011): the template and Project::new_wall/new_slab create random v4 ids, so crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs writes different files on every run and the golden test can only load and re-save the stored files (tests/roundtrip.rs:198-230); NFR-MNT-003 wants the reference models' output to be the golden file.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs gains default_metric_project_with(ids: &mut dyn FnMut(&str) -> Uuid); default_metric_project() passes random v4 ids (unchanged behaviour). crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs gains a public FixtureBuilder: new(name) builds the template with v5 UUIDs under a FIXTURE_NAMESPACE from "<name>/<role>/<n>", storey(), element(storey, ElementKind) (generic over the registry of task 02, so the test-kinds fixture of task 07 uses the same builder), the wall()/slab() shorthands and edit() create or change elements through commands with v5 element ids "<name>/<kind code>/<n>", finish() returns the project. storey_with_walls_and_slab() and two_storey_shell() are rebuilt on it with unchanged geometry. stand_in(n) returns exactly n elements; STAND_IN_SIZES = [1_000, 5_000, 20_000]; catalogue() lists (name, constructor) and is the single list used by reference_models.rs and by samples() in tests/roundtrip.rs. New round-trip test catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files saves each catalogue sample with the golden file's header options and compares bytes; ARCHICRAFT_BLESS regenerates goldens from the samples; the goldens are re-blessed once (ids-only diff). Out of scope: criterion benches and the CI timing gate (regression-and-status), the D.7 fixture registry (regression-and-status, filled by owning epics), RM-S/M/L themselves (reference-models, perf-tuning-rm-m-l).
design: Ids via Uuid::new_v5(&FIXTURE_NAMESPACE, path.as_bytes()); the builder overwrites element.id before AddElements (validate_element does not care, counters follow the commands, names stay W-001...). Stand-in layout mirrors the reference models: a grid of 4 m rooms per storey with an exterior wall ring (L corners), interior walls ending on the ring and on each other (T junctions) and one slab per storey; up to five 3.0 m storeys (RM-M shape, about 1,000 elements per storey at n = 5,000); beyond 5,000, further five-storey blocks side by side along +X with a 2 m gap (RM-L shape); pad to exactly n with free-standing 1 m interior stubs on the top storey of the last block. One AddElements per storey keeps construction fast (target under 2 s for 20,000 in the dev profile). Pitfalls: v5 ids for template materials, layers and storeys must be used consistently in the tool defaults, so pass the id source into the template instead of rewriting ids afterwards; FixtureBuilder must not be feature-gated (the example uses it); stand-ins contain no test kinds; the golden test stays load-then-save, the new test adds sample-then-save. Pointers: samples.rs:16-83, template.rs default_metric_project, examples/reference_models.rs:24-35, tests/roundtrip.rs:30-32/198-230.
acceptance_criteria:
- fixtures_are_deterministic: building every catalogue sample and stand_in(1_000) twice gives equal projects including every id; two runs of cargo run -p archicraft-ifcx --example reference_models write byte-identical files.
- stand_in(1_000) has exactly 1,000 elements, integrity_problems() is empty, ModelGeometry::evaluate reports no problems, and every storey has at least one L and one T junction whose footprint differs from square ends; stand_in(5_000) has exactly 5,000 elements in the normal suite; stand_in(20_000) is checked behind #[ignore] if it exceeds 10 s in the dev profile.
- stand_in(1_000) round-trips through IFCX equal to itself in the normal suite; the 5,000 case runs behind #[ignore] with its runtime documented.
- catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files passes after a reviewed ids-only re-bless; golden_files_are_reproduced and conformance/run.sh stay green.
- samples_are_valid updated; the builder is documented with an example; adding a sample is one catalogue line.
- NFR-PERF-006 and VIEW-001 become measurable: task 10 and regression-and-status consume stand_in() as public API.
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-006 VIEW-001. Also IFX-010/IFX-011 (stable identities) and NFR-MNT-003 (golden equals reference-model output). Stand-ins are provisional until reference-models and perf-tuning-rm-m-l deliver RM-S/M/L (SRS 7.3).

title: Verify exit criterion: 2D construction geometry with the shared arc type, trim, extend, split and array
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its acceptance holds as a whole on the integrated workspace: the shared Arc/PolyCurve type and single tessellate() function that curved-geometry and fixture F8 build on, the 2D kinds of ANN-001, ANN-002, ANN-003, ANN-010 and ANN-011, the linear editing of EDT-011, EDT-012, EDT-013 and EDT-020, the arrays of EDT-004 and EDT-005, and wall split and merge (WAL-030, WAL-031). Later epics (curved-geometry, terrain-and-site, sections-elevations-dims) depend on this one through this task, and doors-windows-core re-runs its split hook.

WHAT: A checklist run, not development: execute the full test suite and the conformance job, walk the epic acceptance clause by clause and name the test that proves each, tick the inspection checklist docs/commands-and-gestures.md, update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence with file:line, remaining gap, depends_on), the increment-1 readiness line and the technical-debt list, file beads for every clause left open and close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new features; a failing clause reopens the task that owns it.
design: Use the epic acceptance as the checklist; for each clause record the test function names (curve.rs, tessellate.rs, kinds/drafting.rs, contour.rs, linear_edit.rs, relations.rs, array.rs, crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs, linear_edit.rs and reshape.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs, crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs). Status rows follow the gap-analysis vocabulary (done/partial/missing, remaining_effort, depends_on) and name the deferring epic for every clause left open: ANN-002 stays partial until section views exist; EDT-013 stays partial until roofs and terrain register; EDT-011/EDT-012 partial without beams; EDT-020 partial until pick-up/inject; WAL-031 done for straight walls with the same-circle clause verified at carrier level. The epic's task estimates sum to 18.75 days against the roadmap's 13; record the actual effort in the status report so the roadmap can be recalibrated.
acceptance_criteria:
- 2D elements round-trip in the archicraft:: namespace and optionally as IfcAnnotation curves (roundtrip.rs, golden drafting.ifcx; task 05).
- A three-point arc stores centre, radius and sweep exactly and tessellates per the IFX-034 settings, and two producers tessellating the same curve id yield bit-identical vertex lists (curve.rs, tessellate.rs, the curve-id test of task 04, the writer test of task 05).
- 2D elements register as a segment source of the contour detection built in edit-reshape-palette, so a slab is traced from a closed chain of 2D lines in one pick (tasks 04 and 16; ANN-002 tracing clause).
- Trimming a wall back to the nearest intersecting wall or 2D line, extending to a picked wall face and splitting a slab or wall by a two-point line keep the chosen part selected (fixtures trim_wall_by_wall, trim_wall_by_2d_line, extend_to_wall_face, split_slab_by_line, split_wall_by_line and the tool tests of tasks 13 and 19).
- Array tests for linear, radial, vertical and rectangular arrays with all four methods pass (table test of task 14).
- Splitting a wall yields two joined walls that keep their hosted elements (split_keeps_hosted_elements_on_their_part of task 18; the hook is re-run by doors-windows-core-11).
- Every gesture has a menu command with a preview (docs/commands-and-gestures.md inspection checklist ticked).
- The 2D tool group appears in the toolbox with its shortcuts (kittests of tasks 06, 07, 08 and 09).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are green on the workspace; conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID: ANN-001 ANN-002 ANN-003 ANN-010 ANN-011 EDT-004 EDT-005 EDT-011 EDT-012 EDT-013 EDT-020 WAL-030 WAL-031; the technical-debt entry 'Tessellation settings ... unused' is removed.
- Follow-up beads are filed or linked for every clause left open: ANN-002's section/elevation views (sections-elevations-dims-01/-11), EDT-013 for roofs and terrain (beads against roofs and terrain-and-site to expose their outlines to split_polygon), EDT-011/EDT-012 for beams if kinds/beam.rs did not exist (profiles-columns-beams), EDT-020's pick-up/inject (templates-presets-11), WAL-030's hosted clause with a door (doors-windows-core-11), WAL-031's arc-wall test (curved-geometry) and arc preservation in contour detection (curved-geometry-08).
- The epic drafting-trim-split is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: ANN-001 ANN-002 ANN-003 ANN-010 ANN-011 EDT-004 EDT-005 EDT-011 EDT-012 EDT-013 EDT-020 WAL-030 WAL-031 (verification)

title: Add 2D drafting kinds Line, Arc and Polyline bound to a plan view
description:
WHY: ANN-001 (M): "Plan views shall offer 2D construction lines (single, or chained with straight and arc segments), polylines, and arcs and circles by centre and radius or by three points. Each 2D element has a pen and a line type." ANN-002 (M): "2D elements shall belong to a view (the plan view of a storey, or a section/elevation view) and to a layer." DSP-001 makes pen and line type references to project attributes (PenId and LineTypeId of plan-attributes-01). SRS 3.2 lists '2D line/arc/polyline/fill' among the reference elements, written as IfcAnnotation (ANN-010). Gap rows ANN-001/ANN-002 (missing): no 2D element kinds (element.rs:191-194, kinds/ after element-kind-framework-02), elements carry storey and layer but no view membership (element.rs:230-240), plan views are implicit per storey (project.rs:112). edit-reshape-palette-05 deferred EDT-010's offset copy of lines, polylines and arcs to these kinds.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/drafting.rs with a shared `DraftingView` (serde-tagged, #[non_exhaustive] enum with only `Plan { storey: StoreyId }`; sections-elevations-dims-01 adds the section variant), `DraftStyle { pen: PenId, line_type: LineTypeId }` and three kinds, each registered with one kinds! line in kinds/mod.rs: `DraftLine { a, b, style, view }`, `DraftArc { arc: Arc, style, view }` (a circle is a full-sweep arc, labelled 'Circle' in the UI) and `DraftPolyline { curve: PolyCurve, style, view }`. KindDescriptor entries (element-kind-framework-02): labels Line/Arc/Polyline, codes line/arc/polyline, name prefixes LN/AR/PL (ELM-019), default_class and ifc_classes IfcClass::Annotation only (in the class list since element-kind-framework-05, not in SELECTABLE_D5), has_tool true, transforms declaring plan move, rotate, mirror and uniform scale (TransformSupport of selection-transforms-02), and a new descriptor flag `has_body: false` that geometry evaluation, fallback boxes (element-kind-framework-13), 3D picking and the IFCX body writer test instead of matching kinds. Kind hooks: transform (exact on the stored parameters through Segment::transform; vertical moves, non-uniform scale and tilted rotations return TransformError::Unsupported { kind_label, reason }); validate (validate_arc/validate_polycurve with project.settings.repair, home storey equals the view's storey, pen and line type exist, screen-only pens rejected per DSP-005); vertical_extent None and storey_links() empty; rehome and relink rebind the view to the target storey's plan; Kind::material becomes optional if element-kind-framework-02 made it mandatory (2D kinds have none; plan_delete_material skips them); layer reassignment on DeleteLayer covers them; the `attribute_refs` hook of plan-attributes-05 reports DraftStyle, so references.rs attribute_uses and rewrite (DeleteAttribute with replacement) include 2D elements. The envelope PlanStyle of plan-attributes-04 stays on every element but is not used by drafting kinds (documented in kinds/drafting.rs). Tool defaults: a DefaultsSlot per kind through KindDescriptor.template_defaults (element-kind-framework-04) with the first drafting-role pen (Attributes::pens_with_role(PenRole::Drafting)), the SOLID line type and the '2D construction' layer (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs LAYERS). Factories `Project::new_draft_line/new_draft_arc/new_draft_polyline(storey, geometry, nth)` as thin wrappers over Project::new_element, mirroring new_wall (project.rs:281). Offset copy: extend edit-reshape-palette-05's `Command::OffsetCopy { sources, distance, new_ids }` to DraftLine and DraftPolyline (straight runs through offset_polyline of outline/edit.rs, arc edges concentrically through Segment::offset with the joints recomputed) and DraftArc (radius ± d, refused when the radius would reach zero). Out of scope: geometry and plan (04), drawing and snapping (16), IFCX (05), tools (06), splines (07), node editing (17), rectangles and tangent arcs (08), fills (09).
design: Three kinds in one module because ELM-019 counters and tool defaults are per kind and the properties panel shows 'Line', 'Arc'/'Circle' and 'Polyline'; the chain method of ANN-001 creates separate line and arc elements (task 06), a polyline is one element. The view binding stores the storey because ViewDefinition arrives with plan-views-browser (not a prerequisite) and ANN-002 speaks of 'the plan view of a storey', so Plan { storey } stays valid once saved views exist and needs no migration. elements_on(storey) keeps returning 2D elements (selection, select_all at workspace.rs:204, browser counts), but every 3D consumer filters by descriptor.has_body, so nothing body-less reaches evaluate parts, render3d or the IFCX body path. Pen and line type live in the kind (DraftStyle) rather than in the envelope PlanStyle because a 2D element has exactly one pen and one line type, and plan-attributes-04 designates the attribute_refs hook for kind-specific graphic properties. Exactness: transforms apply to the stored parameters (centre, angles, nodes), never to tessellated points. Pitfalls: adapt the framework's Kind::material signature once and generically, not with a drafting special case; ELM-008 display ranges do not apply to 2D elements (drawn only in their own view, task 04); Position interior/exterior is irrelevant for them and hidden in the properties (06); prefixes were checked against the other epics (SP is taken by spaces, hence SPL for the spline of task 07).
acceptance_criteria:
- Registry tests: KINDS gains three entries with unique codes and prefixes; the module-layout test still finds each new kind only in kinds/drafting.rs plus one kinds/mod.rs line; every descriptor's default class is in its class set and IfcAnnotation is absent from SELECTABLE_D5.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements, UpdateElements, MoveElements and DeleteElements with undo/redo for each 2D kind; selection-transforms-03's transform_every_registered_kind covers them (rotating 90° maps an arc's centre and start angle within 1e-12, mirroring flips the sweep sign, a vertical move is refused with a message naming the kind, a uniform scale by 2 doubles an arc's radius).
- Validation tests reject with CommandError::Invalid: a zero-length line, a radius below RepairThresholds.min_edge_length, |sweep| > 2π, a polyline arc whose end is 1 mm off its node, a view storey different from the home storey, an unknown or screen-only pen, an unknown line type; duplicate consecutive polyline nodes are repaired with a Repair note (EDT-018).
- Moving a 2D element to another storey rebinds its view; deleting a pen or line type used by a 2D element requires a replacement that is then referenced (attribute_uses lists the element); deleting the '2D construction' layer reassigns the 2D elements.
- Template test: the line, arc and polyline slots reference a drafting-role pen, the SOLID line type and the '2D construction' layer.
- Offset copy: Command::OffsetCopy of a line by 0.5 m gives a parallel line 0.5 m to the left with a new id; of an arc gives radius + 0.5 with the centre bits unchanged; of a line-arc-line polyline keeps the joints coincident bitwise; undo removes the copies.
- DraftingView serialises as { "type": "plan", "storey": ... } so sections-elevations-dims-01 can add the section variant without migration; ANN-002's section/elevation-view clause is recorded as delivered by sections-elevations-dims-01/-11 (ANN-012).
- Golden files byte-identical (no 2D element in the existing samples); model clauses of ANN-001 (kinds, pen, line type) and ANN-002 (plan-view and layer membership) satisfied; EDT-010's offset copy of lines, polylines and arcs satisfied.
notes:
SRS: ANN-001 ANN-002 (model)
Proposals to confirm: prefixes LN/AR/PL. Also closes the offset-copy clause of EDT-010 for lines, polylines and arcs (EDT-010 is owned by edit-reshape-palette, whose done task deferred this clause here).

title: Drag slab elevation in 3D views with numeric input
description:
WHY — SLB-008 (M): the slab elevation can be changed numerically or by dragging in section, elevation or 3D views. The numeric part exists (ui/properties.rs:437-463, 'Elevation offset' through UpdateElements with undo); dragging does not: there are no section or elevation views (VIEW-030, increment 3) and the 3D view only orbits and picks (views/view3d.rs:153-190), gap row SLB-008.

WHAT — views/view3d.rs: with slabs selected and the Select tool active, draw a vertical drag handle at the centroid of each selected slab's reference face (projected through Camera3d with the HandleStyle and 3D anchor projection of selection-transforms-09); dragging follows the closest point between the pick ray (views/camera.rs:262) and the vertical line through the handle; a live preview draws the reference-face outline at the new elevation; a ΔZ field (TypedInput of input/typed.rs, point-input-snapping-01) accepts a typed value; release or Enter executes Command::Transform { transform: Transform::vertical(dz), copy: false } of selection-transforms-03, so the storey re-association offer of selection-transforms-14 (ELM-007) follows; Esc cancels. Keep: the numeric 'Elevation offset' field (ui/properties.rs:437-463, UpdateElements with undo) stays the numeric path of SLB-008. Out of scope: section and elevation views (sections-elevations-dims), the 3D working plane (3d-input-navigation).
design: Closest point between the line L(s) = h + s·z and the ray R(t) = o + t·d: solve the 2 x 2 normal equations for s and t; when |d·z| approaches 1 (looking straight down) fall back to the vertical mouse delta times the model-per-pixel at the handle depth. Handle hit radius 8 px (Appendix D.1). The preview is painted with the egui painter over the 3D texture, projecting points with the view and projection matrices used by views/render3d.rs. Committing through the vertical move of selection-transforms keeps copy variants and re-association in one implementation. Pointers: view3d.rs:102-190, camera.rs:233-275, properties.rs:437-463.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test of the drag math for perspective and parallel projections: a ray through a point N pixels above the handle yields the expected ΔZ (relative error below 1e-9); near-vertical view rays use the screen-space fallback.
- Workspace-level or kittest test: select the ground slab of two_storey_shell, start the handle drag, type 0.15 Enter: the slab offset rises by 0.150 m in one undo step; Esc during the drag leaves the slab unchanged.
- No handle is shown for locked slabs; dragging with several slabs selected moves all of them by the same ΔZ.
- Regression: the 'Elevation offset' field of the properties strip still raises a slab by a typed 0.15 in one undo step.
- Then satisfied: the 3D dragging clause of SLB-008; the section and elevation clause waits for sections-elevations-dims.
notes:
SRS: SLB-008
Dragging in section and elevation views follows with sections-elevations-dims (increment 3); the done task files the follow-up.

title: Add wall endpoint, face and offset ops plus chain offset copy
description:
WHY — WAL-033 (M): walls shall support direct manipulation with numeric input: move an endpoint; drag a face to change the thickness; offset the whole wall in parallel; curve or straighten it; change its arc radius. WAL-004 (M): changing a wall's thickness keeps its reference line in place and moves the faces. EDT-010 (M): offset copy creates a parallel copy of lines, polylines, arcs and walls at a typed distance. EDT-023 (S): offset copy also copies a chain of connected walls as a joined chain. Gap rows: WAL-033 is partial — the model has the undoable, lock-aware MoveElements (command.rs:41-44, 153-166; Command::Transform after selection-transforms-03) and the thickness is editable numerically while the reference line stays (ui/properties.rs:254-266), but no endpoint, face or parallel-offset operation exists; EDT-010 and EDT-023 are missing and nothing detects wall chains outside geometry/wall.rs:212-218 (footprint junctions).

WHAT — Model: the wall kind's reshape hook (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/wall.rs) implements, on the PartRef addressing of selection-transforms-01: Move endpoint as the shared `ReshapeOp::MoveNode { to }` on PartRef::Node { ring: 0, index: 0 | 1 } (the same node command as slabs, NFR-USE-002); `ReshapeOp::MoveFace { offset }` on a new `WallPart::Face { side: WallSide::{Exterior, Interior} }` beside WallPart::Skin (PartRef::Kind); and `ReshapeOp::OffsetWall { distance, keep_joined }` on the reference line PartRef::Edge { ring: 0, index: 0 }. With keep_joined = false OffsetWall reduces to the wall Kind::transform Move of selection-transforms-02 (successor of MoveElements, command.rs:153-166), which it calls instead of duplicating the translation; the numeric Thickness field (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:254-266) stays and shares the WAL-004 regression with MoveFace. New crates/archicraft-model/src/wall_chain.rs: `wall_chains(project, ids) -> Vec<WallChain { walls (ordered, with reversed flags), closed }>` from reference-line endpoint contact within MODEL_TOLERANCE (coincident()/quantise() of tolerance.rs). `Command::OffsetCopy { sources: Vec<ElementId>, distance: f64, new_ids: Vec<ElementId> }` copies every wall chain with a mitred offset of its reference polyline so consecutive copies share endpoints exactly, and every other source through a new `Kind::offset_copy(&self, distance: f64) -> Result<Self, Unsupported>` hook in kinds/mod.rs (default Unsupported naming the kind), so drafting-trim-split-03 registers Line, Arc and Polyline without touching the command (the lines, polylines and arcs of EDT-010); a shared `offset_polyline(points, closed, distances)` lives next to offset_ring in outline/edit.rs. Out of scope: UI (task 09); curve, straighten and arc radius of WAL-033 (curved-geometry-02 and -11 add CurveWall, StraightenWall and SetArcRadius); the 2D kinds' offset_copy implementations (drafting-trim-split-03).
design: Face offsets come from ReferenceLine::face_offsets (element.rs:98-107); MoveFace takes the signed target offset of the dragged face along the left normal and recomputes thickness (and, for Custom, the custom offset) so start and end never move. OffsetWall translates along the left normal; with keep_joined, every other wall on the storey with an endpoint within MODEL_TOLERANCE of a moved endpoint gets that endpoint moved to the intersection of its own line with the offset line (a nearly parallel neighbour is left alone and a note says so), and T stems ending on the moved line are extended or trimmed onto the new line; all touched walls go through plan_update_elements in one transaction. Chains: endpoint graph keyed by tolerance.rs quantise(), walk degree-2 nodes; copies keep each source wall's own direction so exterior sides stay consistent while the offset side follows the chain's left normal; the mitre point of each chain node is computed once and shared by both copies, so endpoints are bit-identical and the contact test of geometry wall.rs:212-218 (JOIN_TOLERANCE of tolerance.rs after element-kind-framework-01) finds L junctions. new_ids come from the caller, as AddElements carries full elements, so redo and journal replay are deterministic; plan_add_elements' counter logic names the copies. If the junction relation of junction-engine exists when this lands, OffsetCopy also creates relations between consecutive copies.
acceptance_criteria:
- MoveNode on a wall end (PartRef::Node { ring: 0, index: 1 }) changes only that end; MoveFace keeps start and end bit-identical for Outside, Center, Inside and Custom reference lines (WAL-004 invariant asserted for each) and yields the expected thickness (Center: 2 x |offset|; Outside interior face: offset; Custom: the dragged face moves, the other stays); dragging the face that carries the reference line of an Outside/Inside wall fails with 'This face carries the reference line; use Offset wall.'
- OffsetWall 0.5 on the east wall of storey_with_walls_and_slab with keep_joined moves its line and puts the coincident ends of the north and south walls on the new line (L junctions stay closed) in one undo step; keep_joined = false moves only that wall; a locked neighbour with keep_joined gives CommandError::Locked.
- wall_chains: the four exterior walls of storey_with_walls_and_slab form one closed chain; the interior T wall of two_storey_shell is its own open chain; a node with three walls ends a chain.
- OffsetCopy of that ring by 0.3 m towards the interior creates four walls whose consecutive endpoints coincide exactly and form the 9.4 x 7.4 m ring, with the supplied ids and names from the counters; a single wall copies to one parallel wall; undo removes the copies.
- archicraft-geometry test: footprints() of the copied ring resolves an L junction at every corner (no square end), proving the copy stays joined (EDT-023).
- Command::OffsetCopy of a test-kinds Dummy copies it through Kind::offset_copy with the supplied id; a slab source fails atomically with CommandError::Unsupported naming the kind; offset_polyline on an open three-point polyline gives mitred parallel segments at the distance and on a closed ring equals offset_ring.
- WAL-004 regression: changing the thickness through UpdateElements (the properties-strip path) keeps start and end bit-identical for all four reference-line locations.
- Then satisfied at model level: WAL-033 endpoint, face and parallel offset clauses, EDT-010 offset copy of walls (lines, polylines and arcs through Kind::offset_copy in drafting-trim-split-03), EDT-023.
notes:
SRS: WAL-033 EDT-010 EDT-023
(WAL-004 invariant) Appendix D.2: wall 0.25 m masonry, reference line on the exterior face. Open question: dragging the face that carries the reference line could switch the wall to a Custom reference location instead of being refused; refused so that WAL-004 stays literal.

title: Add Command::Reshape with node and edge operations on outlines
description:
WHY — EDT-008 (M): clicking a node or edge of a selected element opens a contextual edit palette; node commands are move node, insert node, delete node and fillet/chamfer corner, edge commands are offset edge, offset all edges, curve edge (make an arc) and straighten edge. EDT-009 (M): nodes and edges are stretchable by dragging, with numeric input. EDT-010 (M): offset moves one edge or all edges of a polygon-based element by a typed distance. SLB-008 (M) and SLB-003 (M): slab outlines and holes are editable with these commands, and NFR-USE-002 asks for the same commands on every polygon-based kind. Only Command::MoveElements (command.rs:41-44, 153-166) and, after selection-transforms-03, Command::Transform change geometry, both for whole elements; no command addresses a node or an edge (gap rows EDT-008, EDT-009, EDT-010).

WHAT — Model: `Command::Reshape { targets: Vec<PartTarget>, op: ReshapeOp }` with `PartTarget { element: ElementId, part: PartRef }` built from Selection::parts_of (crates/archicraft-model/src/selection.rs of selection-transforms-01, whose PartRef::Node { ring: u16, index: u32 } and PartRef::Edge { ring, index } already address outline nodes and edges; add the shared variant `PartRef::Ring { ring: u16 }` for whole-ring operations such as offset all edges of a hole and delete hole, with part_label/part_anchor/part_outline support in the slab Kind) and label() texts ('Move node', 'Insert node', 'Offset edge', …); `ReshapeOp::{MoveNode{to}, InsertNode{at}, DeleteNode, MoveEdge{delta, keep_directions}, OffsetEdge{distance}, OffsetAll{distance}, Chamfer{distance}, CurveEdge{through}, Straighten}`; the operations as methods of Outline<E> in crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/edit.rs that return the follow-up part (for selection retargeting), including the per-edge mitre routine `offset_ring(ring, distances)`; a `reshape(&mut self, part: &PartRef, op: &ReshapeOp) -> Result<Option<PartRef>, ReshapeError>` hook on `trait Kind` in crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-02; default ReshapeError::Unsupported naming the kind label), implemented by the slab kind in kinds/slab.rs through Outline; Selection::retain_valid (selection-transforms-08) keeps running after every command and the follow-up part replaces a stale one. Planning clones each target, applies the op, then runs plan_update_elements (validation and repair of task 02) into Edit::ReplaceElement, so undo and redo come for free. CurveEdge returns 'Curved edges arrive with arc geometry.' (stub until curved-geometry); Straighten is NoChange on straight edges. Out of scope: union, difference and holes (task 04), wall operations (task 05), UI (tasks 07-08), fillet (EDT-014, curved-geometry).
design: Outward normal = right of the edge direction; with outer rings CCW and holes CW that points away from the material for both. OffsetEdge moves edge i's supporting line by d and intersects it with the lines of edges i-1 and i+1; when a neighbour is parallel (is_parallel() of tolerance.rs, element-kind-framework-01) a connecting edge of length |d| is inserted instead. OffsetAll uses offset_ring with equal distances; if any offset edge reverses direction, it falls back to geo::Buffer with BufferStyle::new(d).line_join(LineJoin::Miter(..)) on that ring and re-maps edge data by matching parallel edges; an empty or multi-part result is rejected. MoveEdge{keep_directions: true} is OffsetEdge by the normal component of delta; false translates both nodes. Chamfer requires d below both adjacent edge lengths. The epic design names `Command::Reshape{target: PartRef, op}`; a target list is a superset that lets shared nodes of several selected elements move in one undo step (a single target is a one-element list). Pitfalls: the UI may hold stale indices, so the planner checks bounds and reports 'The node no longer exists.'; validation may merge vertices after the op, so the follow-up part is recomputed after repair. Pointers: command.rs:153-166 (MoveElements pattern), 372-395 (plan_update_elements); kinds/mod.rs `trait Kind` of element-kind-framework; validate.rs repair pipeline (task 02).
acceptance_criteria:
- New crates/archicraft-model/tests/reshape.rs, on the outer ring and on the stair hole (ring 1) of the upper slab of two_storey_shell: OffsetEdge 0.5 on the north edge gives 12 x 9.5 m with 4 nodes; OffsetAll -0.25 gives 11.5 x 8.5 m; MoveNode moves exactly one vertex; InsertNode adds a vertex on the addressed edge and returns the new node as follow-up part; DeleteNode on a triangle fails with 'A polygon needs at least three distinct points.'; Chamfer 1.0 replaces a corner by two nodes 1.0 m along both edges; MoveEdge with keep_directions keeps the neighbouring edge directions. Each case: execute, undo restores the project exactly (revision normalised), redo reapplies.
- Offsetting a hole edge until it touches the outline is rejected with the hole message; an OffsetAll whose mitre construction collapses an edge falls back to the buffer path and yields a valid ring or a clear rejection.
- A locked element gives CommandError::Locked, a missing element or an out-of-range index NotFound; CurveEdge gives the curved-geometry message; Straighten on a straight edge gives NoChange; two targets in one command change in one undo step.
- The same op tests pass on Outline<TestEdge>; per-edge data survives InsertNode (both halves) and DeleteNode (merge).
- Every ReshapeOp survives a serde round trip (command journal).
- PartRef::Ring { ring: 1 } survives a serde round trip and part_label gives 'hole 1'; OffsetAll addressed at it changes only the stair hole; Command::Reshape rejects a self-intersecting result with the task-02 message (joins the 'every edit is validated' regression); Selection::retain_valid drops a node part made stale by DeleteNode.
- Then satisfied at model level: EDT-008 node/edge commands except fillet and curve, EDT-009, EDT-010 offset edge and offset all, and the polygon-editing clauses of SLB-008 and SLB-003.
notes:
SRS: EDT-008 EDT-009 EDT-010 SLB-003 SLB-008
Appendix D.1 repair thresholds apply after every op. Open question: whether MoveEdge without a modifier should stretch along the neighbouring edges (chosen, matches 'stretch') or translate the edge freely.

title: Preview unit and void live and pick the opening configuration
design:
One preview pipeline: build a throw-away Element with the WallInsert the click would create, then run InsertFrame::resolve, insert_void and the instance evaluation on it. This guarantees that the preview equals the result (no duplicate math) and exercises the same code as the evaluated model.

Plan drawing uses the Preview of input/consumer.rs (point-input-snapping retires ToolState::preview, views/tools.rs:547). 3D uses the transient overlay of host-openings-10 (Renderer3d::draw_overlay), so FrameKey re-renders without rebuilding the model scene.

Quadrant choice in the wall frame: the sign of the along offset gives the hinge end, and the sign of the through offset gives the swing side. A dead zone of a few pixels around the click keeps the default (the last-used configuration, persisted in the tool defaults slot) until the pointer moves.

Pitfall: when the host is mirrored relative to the screen (reference line pointing left), the quadrant mapping must use the wall frame, not screen axes. Test both directions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in tools/insert.rs: the preview for a host and pointer equals the evaluated geometry of the element a click would create (same VoidPrism, same placed symbol primitives) (DW-002 'live preview of the door or window and its void').
- Moving the pointer from one wall to another, or pressing CycleHost at a junction, moves the preview to the new host in the same update (DW-002 'on the host under the pointer').
- Moving the pointer across the wall's reference line swaps the exterior-side marker and the unit orientation in the preview (DW-003 'shown in the preview').
- Configuration phase: pointer offsets in the four quadrants give the four hinge x swing combinations, for reference lines pointing both right and left on screen; for a sliding door the two sides give the two directions; a fixed window is created directly after the position click (DW-004).
- Esc in the configuration phase returns to hover without creating anything; a click creates exactly one element in one undo step.
- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): after the position click on a wall with the door tool, the prompt shows the configuration instruction and a 'DIN left' or 'DIN right' label; clicking in a quadrant creates a door with that configuration.
- The preview is recomputed only when host, pointer parameter, side or configuration change, not every frame, which avoids the per-frame allocation debt noted for views/plan.rs:487.
notes: SRS: DW-002 DW-003 DW-004 (plus DW-017 labels from components-dw-catalogue, Appendix D.6, OPN-007 preview mechanism). Appendix D.6: a leaf is 'left' if its hinges are on the left when viewed from the side towards which it opens; the convention text is to be verified against DIN 107 before release.

title: Add the relation store with dependency queries and persistence
description:
WHY: SRS 3.3: the model is associative; the relations storey link, host, junction, trim, solid operation and annotation binding are stored with the model, kept across save and open, and re-evaluated automatically when any participating element changes. IFX-060 (M) names storey links and junction settings among the authoring data that must be stored; UI-012 (M) lists broken references among the problems the panel shows; STR-006 (M) needs the elements linked to a storey to be found when it changes; it is done for walls and slabs (storey-relative data resolved at evaluation time, project.rs:236-260) and this task keeps that behaviour, only making the linked elements findable. Storey links are already stored through TopLink (writer.rs:76-82) and stay with the kind codecs (task 06); explicit relations have no home yet. No relation store exists: Project::integrity_problems (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:327-342) returns strings about storey, layer and material references only, and every later epic that relates elements (host-openings, junction-engine, cleanup-and-trims, solid-kernel-ops, sections-elevations-dims) needs one place to record, query, undo and persist relations; incremental evaluation (task 10) uses its dependency queries.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs: enum Relation with StoreyLink { element, storey, role: Base | Top } (derived) and the explicit variants Host { hosted, host }, Junction { a, b }, Trim { target, by }, SolidOperation { target, operator }, AnnotationBinding { annotation, target }, each carrying its ends only (owning epics add their parameters); RelationId as a v5 UUID of the variant and its ends (ids.rs id_type!). RelationStore inside Project holds the explicit relations (serialised, part of PartialEq) and a derived storey-link index built from home storeys and Kind::storey_links() (serde skip, excluded from PartialEq, rebuilt by Project::rebuild_indexes() after load and updated per touched element in Edit::apply). Queries: relations_of(id), dependents_of(id) with a per-variant direction (Host and Junction both ways, Trim target on by, SolidOperation target on operator, AnnotationBinding annotation on target, StoreyLink element on storey), neighbours(id) and storey_dependents(storey) (homed, absolutely and relatively linked). Project::integrity_problems() returns Vec<IntegrityProblem { element: Option<ElementId>, relation: Option<RelationId>, message }> and adds dangling relation ends; callers (samples test, reader repair report) are updated. New Edit::InsertRelation/RemoveRelation with exact inverses and validation (ends exist, distinct, no duplicate, at most one Host per hosted element and no Host cycle, so task 07 can nest hosted elements under their host); a host_of(id) query serves the writer; plan_delete_elements emits RemoveRelation for every relation touching a deleted element so undo restores it (the ELM-016 hosted cascade is host-openings'). IFCX: an archicraft::relations attribute on the first end's node, an array of { kind, target }, declared only when used (task 06 rule), restored after all elements are read, with dangling targets dropped and reported. Samples carry no relations, so goldens stay unchanged. Out of scope: junction detection and rules (junction-engine), trim and solid-operation semantics, host behaviour, any UI for relations.
design: Derived versus stored relations: storey links are a pure function of element data (TopLink stays the source of truth per IFX-060 and is written by the kind codecs), so the store only indexes them; explicit relations have no other home and are serialised. Updating the index per touched element in Edit::apply keeps undo exact and cheap; the debug-only counter of full rebuilds should stay at one per load. RelationId as v5 of (variant, ends) makes re-creation idempotent and diff-friendly. Relation edits are always planned inside Command::plan, never applied directly, so history and journal stay complete. The relation codec writes each relation as an open object ({ kind, target } plus optional members), so junction-engine can add junction settings (IFX-060) as optional members without a format bump (task 12 rule). Pitfalls: Project derives PartialEq, so the derived index must be excluded (custom PartialEq on the store) or round-trip comparisons fail; Relative links reach above the top storey through relative_elevation's extrapolation (storey.rs:108) and still count as dependents of the home storey; junction-engine adds Junction parameters and an Unjoined variant, keep Relation and its codec easy to extend. Pointers: project.rs:164-182/327-342, command.rs:344-360/616-728, ids.rs, reader.rs:735-880, writer.rs:361-417.
acceptance_criteria:
- relation_index_matches_brute_force: after random AddElements/UpdateElements (top-link changes)/DeleteElements/DeleteStorey sequences with undo and redo, storey_dependents(storey) equals the set computed from the elements' home storeys and links.
- InsertRelation(Host) then RemoveRelation and undo restore the exact project; inserting a relation with a missing end, a self-relation, a duplicate, a second Host for the same hosted element or a Host cycle returns CommandError::Invalid; host_of returns the host.
- Deleting an element removes its explicit relations through RemoveRelation edits and undo restores them exactly.
