- integrity_problems reports a dangling relation end with the element id; a project with a missing material still reports it in the structured form.
- dependents_of direction unit tests for every variant; Project equality ignores the derived index.
- Round trip: a project with an explicit test relation writes archicraft::relations, loads equal and validates; a file whose relation targets a missing element loads with the relation dropped and one warning; golden files bit-identical.
- IFX-060 storage of explicit relations in place; SRS 3.3 store and queries available; UI-012 broken references available as structured problems for task 14.
notes: SRS: IFX-060 UI-012 STR-006. Also prepares NFR-REL-004 (integrity at open, owned elsewhere). Consumers: task 07 (host_of for hosted containment), task 09 (storey_dependents), task 10 (dependents_of), task 14 (structured problems), host-openings, junction-engine, cleanup-and-trims, solid-kernel-ops.

title: Add rectangles and arcs and circles tangent to one to three elements
description:
WHY: ANN-011 (S) requires "rectangles and rotated rectangles" and "arcs and circles tangent to one to three elements (choosing among several solutions)". Typical uses are construction frames, circles between walls and lines, circles inscribed between three references and tangent continuations; they also serve as construction aids for the arc walls of curved-geometry. The slab tool already builds rectangles (rectangle and rotated_rectangle in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:315-321 today, tools/slab.rs after point-input-snapping-01; test rectangle_tools). Gap row ANN-011 (missing).

WHAT: Rectangle and Rotated rectangle modes on the Polyline tool producing closed DraftPolylines, reusing those builders. A tangent solver submodule tangent of crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs returning all solutions as Vec<Arc> for references given as Segment carriers (2D lines, arcs and circles, wall reference lines and faces, polyline segments): `tangent_arc_from_end(segment, end, through)` (one element: an arc leaving the element's end tangentially through a picked point), `circles_tangent_2(a, b, radius)` (line-line up to 4, line-circle up to 8, circle-circle up to 8 solutions) and `circles_tangent_3(a, b, c)` (generalised Apollonius for any mix of lines and circles, up to 8 solutions). Tool modes on the Arc tool: Tangent to 1, Tangent to 2 (typed radius) and Tangent to 3: pick the references (highlighted), all solutions are previewed faintly, the solution nearest the cursor is highlighted, Tab cycles them (INP-009 style) and a click confirms; for two references an option 'Arc between tangent points' emits the shorter arc between the tangent points instead of the full circle. Out of scope: tangency to splines (message), associative tangency (the result is a plain DraftArc).
design: Rectangles reuse the slab tool's builders so wall, slab and 2D rectangles behave alike (NFR-USE-002). Tangent solver: represent a line as n·x = d with a side sign and a circle as (c, r) with a sign s in {−1, +1} (external or internal tangency); for each sign combination subtract the squared tangency equations pairwise to get linear equations in (x, y, R), express x and y linearly in R and substitute into one quadratic; discard R <= MODEL_TOLERANCE and merge duplicates within tolerance. Degenerate determinants (tolerance.rs near_zero) are skipped, never panicked on, and every candidate is verified by its residual before it is returned. Order solutions by centre x, then y, so Tab order is stable. Pitfalls: concentric or coincident references; three parallel lines (no solution); nearly parallel lines amplify errors (verify residuals).
acceptance_criteria:
- Rectangle tool tests: a rectangle by two corners emits a closed counter-clockwise 4-node polyline; a rotated rectangle by three points has its first edge along the first two points and right angles within 1e-12.
- Solver tests: the three lines of a 3-4-5 triangle give 4 circles (incircle r = 1, excircles r = 2, 3 and 6) within 1e-9; three mutually external circles give 8 solutions; two crossing lines with r = 0.5 give 4; parallel lines with r different from half their distance give 0 and the tool shows 'No circle with this radius touches both elements'.
- Every returned circle satisfies its tangency conditions with residual < 1e-9 (| |centre − c_i| − |r ± r_i| | for circles, |distance to line − r| for lines); solutions are ordered deterministically.
- Tool tests without egui: picking three lines and clicking near the incircle emits a DraftArc equal to the incircle within 1e-9; Tab selects the next solution; the two-reference arc option emits an arc whose ends are the tangent points.
- kittest: Rectangle and Rotated rectangle are listed in the Polyline tool's mode bar and the tangent modes in the Arc tool's mode bar.
- ANN-011 rectangle, rotated-rectangle and tangent clauses satisfied.
notes: SRS: ANN-011 (rectangles, rotated rectangles, tangent arcs and circles)

title: Add trim and extend tools with previews, menu commands and the trim accelerator
description:
WHY: EDT-020 (M): "Every operation that a modifier gesture can trigger (trim, split, extend, parameter pick-up and inject, contour detection) shall also be available as an explicit command with a preview." Decision D-7: explicit commands for every reshape and transfer operation; modifier gestures are accelerators only. EDT-011 and EDT-012 need user-facing tools, and EDT-011's "If a selection exists, only the selected elements act as cutting boundaries" is decided in the tool. Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for trim. Gap row EDT-020 (missing): none of these exist as commands or gestures; previews exist only for element creation (views/tools.rs:547-572). The TrimTarget cursor glyph exists in point-input-snapping-03's CursorState.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/linear_edit.rs with two InputConsumers on the point-input service. Trim: hovering a linear element previews the portion to remove (plan_trim with boundaries = the selection if non-empty, else reshape::boundary_candidates over visible elements) in the preview colour with the TrimTarget cursor; a click executes Command::Trim with a fresh id_seed; it repeats until Esc; the selection stays as it was because it defines the boundaries. Extend: step 1 picks the boundary (2D line, wall face or reference line, slab edge, guide; highlighted), step 2 clicks near a target end with the new end previewed; repeating. Explicit commands: Edit menu items Trim and Extend (shell.rs:59 or the command registry), context-menu entries (views/plan.rs:728) and actions with the D.8 shortcut for Trim and a proposal for Extend; extend `appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts` (ui/actions.rs:187) with Trim. Accelerator (D-7): with the Select tool, holding the trim modifier (proposal Cmd/Ctrl) over a linear element shows the same trim preview and a click executes the same Command::Trim; no other new gesture. Out of scope: the split tool and the gesture checklist (19), array and path tools (15), parameter transfer (templates-presets).
design: Each tool computes its preview with the same pure planner that Command::plan() uses (plan_trim, plan_extend), so preview and result cannot diverge; planners run on pointer move only, never per frame, and the boundary candidate list is cached per plan revision like the snap index. The trim modifier-click is the only gesture overload, matching D-7. Shortcut proposals (to be confirmed by commands-and-l10n): Trim T, Extend E, single keys suppressed while ws.input.captures_keys(). Pitfalls: the trim modifier must not collide with Shift (constraint) or Tab (snap cycling); after Trim and Extend the selection stays on the edited element; every execution gets a fresh id_seed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool tests without egui on the fixtures of task 11: hovering A's overhang at (5, 0) previews the removed span (4,0)-(6,0) and the click emits the same Command::Trim as the model fixture; with a selection only the selected boundaries are used, without one the visible candidates; extend picks B's west face, then A's end, and emits Command::Extend with that face; Esc ends each tool.
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs kittests: the Edit menu contains Trim and Extend; the Trim shortcut activates the tool; a modifier-click trim in the plan pane changes the element and the undo label reads 'Trim'; the preview outline list is non-empty while hovering before the click; `shortcuts_are_unique` and the extended `appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts` pass.
- The boundary candidate list is built once per plan revision while hovering (unit test on the cache).
- EDT-020 satisfied for trim and extend (explicit command, preview, gesture only as accelerator); the UI clauses of EDT-011 (selection as boundaries) and EDT-012 satisfied.
notes: SRS: EDT-020 EDT-011 EDT-012 ANN-002 (trim and extend tools, previews, explicit commands)

title: Add the 2D tool group for lines, chains, polylines, arcs and circles
description:
WHY: ANN-001 (M): plan views offer single and chained construction lines with straight and arc segments, polylines, and arcs and circles by centre and radius or by three points, each with a pen and a line type; ANN-002: each belongs to the active plan view and a layer. INP-001 requires every creation step to use the shared point-input service. Epic acceptance: "the 2D tool group appears in the toolbox with D.8 shortcuts (kittest)". Gap row ANN-001: the tool palette has Select/Wall/Slab only (ToolKind in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13-17, tools/mod.rs after point-input-snapping-01).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/drafting.rs implementing point-input-snapping-01's InputConsumer for three tool kinds. Line with modes Single (two points per element, repeating) and Chain (consecutive DraftLine and DraftArc elements sharing their end points; a mode key toggles straight/arc for the next segment; arc segments start tangent to the previous segment through Arc::tangent_continuation, or use three points with a second modifier; the chain is committed as one AddElements on Enter, double-click or a click on the first point, like the wall chain of point-input-snapping-14). Polyline (one DraftPolyline with straight and arc segments; Enter or double-click finishes; clicking the first node closes). Arc with modes Centre-radius (centre, start point giving radius and start angle, end point giving the end angle, direction from the cursor side), Three points, Circle by centre and radius and Circle by three points. Previews through Preview outlines using tessellate() with the project settings; tracker fields length/angle for lines and radius/angle for arcs (typed values through the service). New elements take the tool-default slots of task 03 and the active plan's storey as view. App wiring: ToolKind variants with labels and descriptions in tools/mod.rs; the 2D toolbox group (ToolGroup::Annotation2d of commands-and-l10n-15 if the command registry has landed, otherwise a '2D' group in the ui/shell.rs toolbox, shell.rs:120) and the Design menu (shell.rs:100); Action::ToolLine/ToolPolyline/ToolArc in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs (or registry commands) with free single-key shortcuts; properties.rs gather() and tool_modes() (properties.rs:55 and :745) for the modes; Fields for 2D elements (length, angle, radius, sweep, centre, pen, line type, layer; Position, material and the envelope Plan display section hidden) editable through UpdateElements, with plan-attributes-08's widgets::pen_choice (screen-only pens excluded, descriptions shown per DSP-006) and line_type_choice; the select_all mapping (workspace.rs:204). Out of scope: splines (07), rectangles and tangent arcs (08), fills (09), section and elevation views (sections-elevations-dims-11).
design: Each mode is a short step list on the InputConsumer API; previews use the arc constructors of curve.rs, so the preview equals the committed element. Chain semantics follow the reference product: separate elements joined at nodes, which keeps trim and split per segment simple; the polyline is the single-element alternative. Shortcut proposals (to be confirmed by commands-and-l10n; concrete bindings are a UI design deliverable per D.8, which lists no 2D tool): Line L, Polyline Shift+L, Arc/Circle Shift+A. The single-key suppression asks ws.input.captures_keys() (point-input-snapping-01), which must cover the new keys. Pitfalls: ToolState::select resets pending points; the Centre-radius direction is ambiguous at exactly 180° (use the cursor side and show it in the preview); the view binding follows the active pane, not the last edited storey; curved-geometry-07 reuses these arc step specs for arc walls, so keep them free of drafting-specific state.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool tests without egui: Single emits one DraftLine on the active storey's view per two clicks; Chain with four clicks and one arc toggle emits two lines and one arc in one AddElements whose consecutive ends coincide bitwise and whose arc start tangent is parallel to the previous line within 1e-12; Polyline with an arc segment and a closing click emits one closed PolyCurve; Centre-radius with a typed radius of 2.5 m stores radius 2.5 exactly; Three points stores the Arc::through values bitwise; both circle modes emit full-sweep arcs; Esc and Backspace follow the service's ladder (one step back, then cancel).
- Precision: a polyline entered purely by typed polar and relative values measures back exactly (0.1 mm, 0.01°), the 2D analogue of AS-04.
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs kittests: the toolbox shows the 2D group with Line, Polyline and Arc buttons; clicking each sets ws.tool.kind; their shortcuts select them while no text field has focus and are ignored while ws.input.captures_keys(); two clicks in the plan pane with the Line tool add one element (undo label 'Create line'); a selected 2D line shows Pen and Line type pickers and changing the pen issues one UpdateElements; `shortcuts_are_unique` passes.
- Every mode shows its step prompt in the status line (StepSpec::prompt).
- ANN-001 satisfied in plan views (lines, chains, polylines, arcs and circles by centre/radius and three points, with pen and line type); ANN-002's view and layer membership holds for every created element.
notes: SRS: ANN-001 ANN-002 (tools and properties)

title: Contour detection in the creation tools and for slab holes
description:
WHY — INP-018 (S): with a creation tool active, a key shall switch to contour detection; clicking then previews and creates an element of the active kind from the clicked edge or chain of connected edges, or from the smallest closed region bounded by existing elements around the clicked point. SLB-003 (M): holes can be traced; SLB-001's 'traced from them in one pick' uses the same mechanism; EDT-020 (drafting-trim-split) later lists contour detection among the operations that need an explicit command with a preview.

WHAT — Tool state: a detection flag on the wall and slab tools, held with a key and toggled by a 'Contour detection' action (Design menu, status-bar indicator); while active, hover runs ContourGraph queries (task 06, cached per storey and plan revision in crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs beside the per-storey plan cache of element-kind-framework-11) and previews the region, the chain or, with Alt held (provisional), the single clicked edge (edge_at) under the cursor; a click creates a slab from the region (islands become holes) or from a closed chain with the slab tool, and walls along the edge or chain or around the region boundary (joined, closed for regions) with the wall tool and its reference-line location. In the reshape tool, 'Add hole' and 'Subtract polygon' accept a traced region (Command::Reshape AddHole or Difference). Out of scope: 3D views (follow-up bead filed by the done task, on the working plane of 3d-input-navigation) and arc preservation (curved-geometry-08), 2D lines as sources (drafting-trim-split registers them).
design: The graph is built lazily from the active storey's PlanDrawing (document.rs caches plans per storey) and dropped when the plan revision changes; it is never rebuilt per frame (technical-debt item on per-frame SnapTargets). Exclude the element being edited from the sources when tracing its own holes, so its coincident outline cannot create zero-area faces. Created slabs go through project.new_slab with the region rings (validation and repair of task 02); walls use the wall tool's chain completion (consecutive walls joined), with the reference line on the traced chain oriented counter-clockwise around a region so the interior side faces it. Key binding: holding Space is provisional (Appendix D.8 names no binding; commands-and-l10n confirms); the toggle action works without holding. The detection step is a StepSpec of the creation tool's InputConsumer, so prompts, preview and Esc follow INP-001.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest on samples::two_storey_shell_with_shaft, upper storey: select the upper slab, palette 'Add hole', hold the detection key, click inside the shaft: the slab gains a hole equal to the shaft walls' inner-face rectangle (x 1.0575-2.9425, y 6.5575-7.9425 within MODEL_TOLERANCE), its area drops by exactly 1.885 x 1.385 = 2.610725 m², and undo removes it.
- Ground storey, slab tool with detection on, click at (2, 3): a new slab whose outline is the task-06 region (area 97.08875 m²); the preview shown before the click has the same ring.
- Upper storey, wall tool with detection on, click on the projected stair-hole outline: four joined walls around the hole in one undo step.
- Ground storey, wall tool with detection on: Alt-click at (2, 0.25) creates exactly one wall along the clicked edge (0.25, 0.25)-(4.9425, 0.25), with the preview showing that edge only.
- Esc or releasing the key returns to normal input without side effects; the 'Contour detection' action is in the Design menu (kittest by label).
- Then satisfied: INP-018 in plan views (3D and arc clauses deferred), the tracing clause of SLB-003; the explicit contour-detection command that EDT-020 needs exists.
notes:
SRS: INP-018 SLB-003
(tracing clause; also SLB-001's tracing clause and EDT-020's contour-detection command) KB 303966, 303902, 656349, 669891 (Magic Wand). Open question: whether islands inside a traced region become holes of the new slab (chosen) or are ignored.

title: Add drafting fills with drafting-role patterns and area display
description:
WHY: ANN-003 (C): "2D drafting fills may be drawn with drafting fill patterns (DSP-009) and show their area." DSP-009 (M): each fill declares its roles (cut, cover, drafting) and "Element settings shall offer only the fills valid for the role being edited." ANN-002: fills belong to a view and a layer like every 2D element. NFR-USE-002: the same polygon commands for every polygon-based kind. Gap row ANN-003 (missing). Existing code this task builds on: Fill with FillRoles and Attributes::fills_for(role) (plan-attributes-01), template fills that all serve the drafting role (SOLID and eight hatches, plan-attributes-02), hatch_lines and RegionFill in archicraft-geometry (plan-attributes-06), their drawing in views/plan.rs (plan-attributes-07) and widgets::fill_choice(role) (plan-attributes-08).

WHAT: New kind `DraftFill { outline: Outline, fill: FillId, pen: Option<PenId> (contour pen; None draws no contour), line_type: LineTypeId, show_area: bool, view }` in kinds/drafting.rs (code fill, prefix FI), built on edit-reshape-palette's Outline (straight edges; arc edges arrive with curved-geometry together with slabs); validation rejects fills without the drafting role ('<fill> cannot be used for 2D fills') and runs validate::repair_outline; the Outline part refs are registered so the palette's node and edge commands, offset and union/difference apply, and attribute_refs reports fill, pen and line type. Geometry and plan: no body; plan.rs emits a FillMesh (triangulate.rs), the contour as drafting curves and, with show_area, an area label anchored at the centroid and formatted with units::format_area; plan_fills (plan-attributes-06) gains `drafting: Vec<RegionFill>` so solid and hatch fills are drawn through the existing RegionFill path, emitted before lines. Tool: a Fill tool in the 2D group with the polygon, rectangle and rotated-rectangle methods of the slab tool and the contour-detection step of edit-reshape-palette-12 (one click inside a region bounded by walls or 2D lines creates a fill). IFCX codec `archicraft::fill` {outline, holes, fill, pen, lineType, showArea} with one Curve child per ring; drafting_sample extended and the golden re-blessed. Properties: the fill picker through widgets::fill_choice(FillRole::Drafting), an area row. Out of scope: gradient or image fills, fills in sections (sections-elevations-dims-11).
design: Reusing Outline gives NFR-USE-002 for free (palette, offset, union/difference, repair, contour tracing and the split default of task 10) and means arcs appear in fills automatically when curved-geometry enables the arc edge in Outline (curved-geometry-10 already lists the 2D fill). The area label is plan data on PlanDrawing, not a text element (ANN-007 is out of scope). DSP-009 role filtering belongs to plan-attributes-08's fill_choice widget: pass the role, do not filter in the tool. Pitfalls: holes clockwise as for slabs; draw order (fills under lines: emit fills first in PlanDrawing); hatch truncation and the 3 px spacing rule of plan-attributes-07 apply unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: a fill referencing a fill without the drafting role (created in the test) is rejected; a 4 × 3 m fill at the origin with the 1 × 1 m hole (2.5, 1)-(3.5, 2) has an area of 11 m² within 1e-12; node move and offset edge on a fill through Command::Reshape with undo; Command::Split of that fill by the line x = 2 gives fills of 6 m² and 5 m² through the Outline default of task 10 (the generic polygon path beyond slabs).
- Plan test: the plan contains the fill mesh, a hatch fill yields hatch segments in its foreground pen, and with show_area the label '11.00 m²' (default metric template) sits at the centroid; a hidden layer hides all of it.
- Tool tests: a polygon fill by four clicks; a contour-detection click inside the four-line rectangle of task 04 creates a fill with that ring.
- IFCX round trip preserves the fill id, the hole and show_area; conformance green.
- kittest: the Fill button exists in the 2D group; the properties fill picker lists the drafting-role template fills and not a cut-only fill added in the test.
- ANN-003 satisfied (patterns with the drafting role, area shown); DSP-009's role filter exercised for the drafting role.
notes:
SRS: ANN-003 ANN-002
Needs the drafting fill role (DSP-009) from plan-attributes.

title: Add array and path distribution tools with live previews
description:
WHY: EDT-004 (M) and EDT-005 (S) need interactive commands: methods 3 and 4 set the count or the spacing "by the cursor", and transforms preview live (EDT-001 convention). Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for array. Epic acceptance: array tests for all kinds and methods and every command with a preview. selection-transforms-10 provides the transformed-outline preview in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/transform.rs.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/array.rs: an Array tool on the point-input service, opened by Edit > Array… (Action::Array or a registry command with the D.8 shortcut, proposal Cmd+U) for the current selection; the mode bar chooses kind and method; steps per kind: linear (base point, then direction and end point or cursor extent), radial (centre, start direction, end angle or cursor angle), vertical (typed dz and count), rectangular (base, u direction and extent, v direction and extent); typed count, spacing and dz fields in the tracker; options 'Vertical displacement per copy' and 'Assign home storeys by elevation'; the preview draws the transformed plan outlines of the whole selection for every copy with the count at the cursor; Enter or the final click executes Command::Array with a fresh id_seed; more than 1,000 copies ask for confirmation. Edit > Distribute along path…: pick the path (elements whose kind implements path_curve are highlighted: lines, arcs, polylines, walls and, after task 07, splines), the base point, then method, offset and orientation in the mode bar; preview; commit Command::DistributeAlongPath. Add Array to `appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts` (ui/actions.rs:187). Out of scope: 3D previews of copies (plan only; the 3D view shows the result after commit).
design: The tool only collects inputs and renders previews; placements come from array.rs, so previews equal results. Reuse the transformed-outline preview of tools/transform.rs (copy variants) instead of a new renderer, and recompute outlines only when the spec changes, not per frame. Pitfalls: radial angles follow the project angle unit; vertical arrays have no meaningful plan preview (show 'n copies, +dz each' in the tracker); the selection stays on the originals after commit, as with copy-move.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool tests without egui: each kind's step sequence emits the expected ArraySpec; SpacingToExtent and CountToExtent take their extent from the cursor distance (or angle for radial); typed values override the cursor; Esc cancels without a command.
- Preview test: for a selection of two elements and three copies the preview holds 6 outlines placed by ArraySpec::placements.
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs kittests: the Edit menu shows 'Array…' and 'Distribute along path…'; the Array shortcut opens the tool with a selection and reports a status message without one; a linear array with typed count 3 and spacing 2 m of the sample's interior wall adds 3 walls (undo label 'Array'); distributing a 2D line along a DraftArc adds the expected number of copies; `shortcuts_are_unique` and `appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts` pass.
- EDT-004 and EDT-005 satisfied end to end (commands, cursor-driven methods, previews, D.8 shortcut for array).
notes: SRS: EDT-004 EDT-005 (tools, previews, shortcut)

title: Introduce the shared tolerance module and retire ad-hoc epsilons
description:
WHY: NFR-ACC-003 (M) fixes the geometric coincidence tolerance at 0.01 mm: points closer than the tolerance are treated as identical in snapping, joining and Boolean operations (Appendix D.1: model tolerance 0.01 mm). Today crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:10 defines MODEL_TOLERANCE = 1e-5 m but only the segment-touching tests use it; wall joining uses its own JOIN_TOLERANCE = 1e-4 m, ten times coarser (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:24, used at :212-218), the parallel checks at wall.rs:129/:166 use 1e-6, mesh point merging uses MERGE_STEP = 1e-6 (mesh.rs:53, used by check_closed, the facing outlines the plan uses and feature_edges), slice.rs:13 keys at 1e-9, plan.rs:80 EPS = 1e-9, extrude.rs:19 and evaluate.rs:156 have their own height epsilons, storey.rs:128 uses 1e-9, and the snapping code has CLOSE_TOLERANCE = 1e-6 (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:338), a 1e-12 denominator (tools.rs:205) and a 1e-9 perpendicular test while SnapTargets::from_plan (tools.rs:163-187) keeps coincident nodes as separate targets. The gap row rates NFR-ACC-003 partial (S); the technical-debt list names the coexisting tolerances. Contact detection for incremental evaluation (task 10) and every later junction and Boolean epic need one definition.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs, re-exported from lib.rs, with MODEL_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-5 as its only literal, the derived JOIN_TOLERANCE = MODEL_TOLERANCE (reference-line contact, decision D-6) and ANGLE_TOLERANCE (the sine whose deviation over one metre equals MODEL_TOLERANCE), plus helpers coincident(a, b), coincident3(a, b), quantise(p)/quantise3(p) for hash keys, is_parallel(dir_a, dir_b) and near_zero(value, scale) for dimensionless robustness guards expressed relative to f64::EPSILON times the operand scale. validate.rs imports it (keep a pub use so archicraft_model::validate::MODEL_TOLERANCE stays valid). Replace every coincidence epsilon: wall.rs (local JOIN_TOLERANCE deleted, parallel checks via is_parallel, intersect() denominator via near_zero), mesh.rs (MERGE_STEP and Key2 via quantise3/quantise, degenerate and ray guards via near_zero), slice.rs key (slice.rs:12-14) and its collinearity guard (slice.rs:116, via near_zero), plan.rs EPS, extrude.rs:19, evaluate.rs:156, triangulate.rs:90, storey.rs:128, and in the snapping code (views/tools.rs, or crates/archicraft-app/src/input/ if point-input-snapping has already moved it there) CLOSE_TOLERANCE (tools.rs:338, chain closing at :460-479), the segment-intersection guard (tools.rs:205), the perpendicular-foot test (tools.rs:245), the constrain() guard (tools.rs:273), SnapTargets deduplication of nodes within MODEL_TOLERANCE and snap() treating candidates within the tolerance as one point before precedence decides. Add the grep test. Out of scope: the tolerance and repair thresholds as project settings (EDT-019, edit-reshape-palette), Boolean operations (solid-kernel-ops), camera math in views/camera.rs (not model, geometry or snapping).
design: One constant, named derivations and helper functions instead of loose literals, so that a later ProjectSettings.tolerance (EDT-019) can be threaded through the helpers. Length comparisons use MODEL_TOLERANCE; dimensionless guards (determinants, cross products of unit vectors, ray parameters) are not tolerances and become near_zero(value, scale) relative to f64::EPSILON, which keeps the grep rule simple and honest. Pitfalls: replacing the triangulate.rs:90 area guard (1e-14) by MODEL_TOLERANCE squared (1e-10 m^2) would drop legitimate slivers at the EDT-019 limits and open the cap, hence the scale-relative guard and its test; quantise() hashing splits points that straddle a cell boundary, harmless today because generators emit bit-identical shared points, but document it and use a neighbour-cell lookup if a test shows otherwise; mesh.rs facing_outline feeds the projected plan lines, so the coarser merge changes plan output only for features below 0.01 mm; extrude.rs keeps rejecting zero height (MIN_HEIGHT 1 mm is enforced earlier by validate.rs). point-input-snapping runs in parallel and may move the snap code: apply the same change wherever SnapTargets lives when this task lands. Pointers: validate.rs:9-14/57-88, wall.rs:24/57/129/166/212-218, mesh.rs:53-62/153/207-211/267/282, slice.rs:12-14, plan.rs:80/135-144, extrude.rs:19, evaluate.rs:156, triangulate.rs:90, storey.rs:128, tools.rs:163-260/338.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs exists and is re-exported; a unit test asserts MODEL_TOLERANCE == 1e-5 and the doc comment cites NFR-ACC-003 and Appendix D.1; every other item in the module is an expression of MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- Grep test only_model_tolerance_is_a_tolerance_constant (crates/archicraft-model/tests/tolerance_scan.rs) scans the non-test source (skipping #[cfg(test)] modules) of crates/archicraft-model/src, crates/archicraft-geometry/src and the snapping module and fails on: any const whose name contains TOLERANCE, EPS, MERGE or CLOSE outside tolerance.rs; any exponent-form float literal (regex \d(\.\d+)?e-\d+) outside tolerance.rs; a second literal-initialised const in tolerance.rs. The only allowlist is the named validation ranges of validate.rs (MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, MIN_CORNER_ANGLE_DEG, MIN_THICKNESS, MIN_HEIGHT, MAX_*), which are EDT-019/ELM-017 thresholds, not coincidence tolerances.
- wall.rs tests: two walls whose reference-line ends are 5 micrometres apart form an L junction; 20 micrometres apart they keep square ends (was 0.1 mm); the existing L and T junction tests pass unchanged.
- tools.rs tests: two plan nodes 5 micrometres apart yield a single snap target and a single Node snap at the stored point; wall_chain_closes_into_joined_walls passes.
- triangulate/extrude test: a ring at the EDT-019 limits (0.1 mm edge, 0.1 degree corner, sliver triangle area of about 8.7e-12 m^2) still triangulates completely and the extruded body passes check_closed.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs, the mesh/slice/plan unit tests and all round-trip tests (including written_meshes_are_closed_bodies) pass; golden files stay bit-identical (IFCX coordinates are rounded to 1e-6 m and parameters are untouched); cargo clippy and fmt green.
- Chain closing and mesh welding: a wall chain whose last click lands 5 micrometres from its first point closes into a ring (CLOSE_TOLERANCE retired); TriMesh vertices 5 micrometres apart are welded by check_closed and feature_edges, 20 micrometres apart they stay separate.
- NFR-ACC-003 is then satisfied for snapping and joining (existing MODEL_TOLERANCE in validate.rs:10 kept as the single source); for the Boolean clause tolerance.rs documents that the Boolean wrapper of solid-kernel-ops must pass MODEL_TOLERANCE as its merge tolerance, and the grep test scans the whole of crates/archicraft-geometry/src so a future Boolean module is checked automatically.
notes: SRS: NFR-ACC-003. Appendix D.1: model tolerance 0.01 mm; repair thresholds 0.1 mm and 0.1 degrees stay in validate.rs. Open question: whether ANGLE_TOLERANCE should be derived from the longer element length instead of one metre; one metre keeps today's behaviour for every drawn angle.

title: Key tool defaults by kind through per-kind defaults slots
description:
WHY: ELM-011 (M) requires the default IFC class per kind and its allowed set to hold for tool defaults as for elements; ELM-006 (M) makes the default top link part of every vertical kind's defaults, so deleting a storey must rewrite every defaults slot linked to it, not only the wall slot (command.rs:470-476 rewrites only defaults.wall.top). ToolDefaults { wall: WallDefaults, slab: SlabDefaults } (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:121-150) is matched in command.rs:489-519 and :520-553 (default-slot loops of plan_delete_layer and plan_delete_material), :554-593 (check_tool_defaults), template.rs:321-345, writer.rs:97-120, reader.rs:433-497 and crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:47-131 (prototype, gather, wall_defaults, slab_defaults, apply). Every kind added later would touch all of these; ELM-001 (tool defaults stored in the project, owned elsewhere) must stay intact.

WHAT: ToolDefaults becomes a newtype over IndexMap<KindTag, DefaultsSlot>, DefaultsSlot { layer, position, ifc_class, kind: ElementKind } holding a prototype payload with placeholder geometry; KindDescriptor gains template_defaults: Option<fn(&TemplateContext) -> DefaultsSlot> (None for the dummy: no toolbox entry and no template slot). Project::prototype(kind, storey) and a generic Project::new_element replace properties.rs prototype(); Project::new_wall/new_slab stay as thin wrappers in kinds/wall.rs and kinds/slab.rs so tools.rs and samples.rs compile unchanged. command.rs: slot loops iterate the map; check_tool_defaults validates each slot by building its prototype element through validate_element (layer, material, class set, kind.validate, storey links); plan_delete_storey rewrites every slot whose storey_links() include the removed storey through unlink_storey. template.rs fills the slots from Appendix D.2 in registry order. Writer and reader keep toolDefaults {wall, slab} byte-identical (the flat slot shape stays until tasks 06 and 12); the reader uses the template slot plus a warning for a missing slot and ignores an unknown key with a warning. properties.rs: Subject::Defaults(kind) edits the prototype and apply() writes the slot back generically; wall_defaults/slab_defaults are deleted; an element of a kind without kind-specific fields (the dummy) shows the common fields only. Out of scope: predefined types in the slot (task 05), codec-based slot serialisation (task 06), the nested slot file shape (task 12), a field framework (properties-and-dialogs).
design: IndexMap so template order controls JSON member order and golden bytes; PartialEq on the newtype keeps the no-change detection of SetToolDefaults. DefaultsSlot carries the payload itself instead of a parallel *Defaults struct: the properties panel already edits a prototype Element, and a kind's defaults are its payload minus geometry (placeholder geometry: wall from ZERO to X, slab unit square). Pitfalls: a template slot for the dummy would make test builds write a dummy defaults slot into every file and break the goldens, hence template_defaults: None; the reader must stay lenient (missing slot is a warning, not an error); keep the writer's toolDefaults member order wall, slab. Pointers: project.rs:116-157/281-322, command.rs:435-593, template.rs:321-345, writer.rs:97-120/190-196, reader.rs:433-497, properties.rs:47-131/221-264, workspace.rs:204-215.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test --workspace, clippy and fmt green; golden files bit-identical; conformance green.
- deleting_resources_requires_a_replacement extended: deleting the layer or material used by a slot rewrites exactly the slots that use it and undo restores them.
- check_tool_defaults rejects a slot whose ifc_class is outside its descriptor set and a slot whose payload fails validation (zero thickness), each with CommandError::Invalid and an explanatory message; SetToolDefaults with an unchanged map returns CommandError::NoChange.
- DeleteStorey rewrites every slot with a TopLink::Storey to the deleted storey (test with the wall slot and a dummy slot added through SetToolDefaults, both linked to the same storey) and undo restores them.
- Reader test: a file whose toolDefaults has an unknown key column and lacks slab loads with two warnings and template-equivalent slab defaults.
- kittest: tool_buttons_and_properties_follow_each_other passes, a thickness change in the properties strip updates the wall slot, and selecting a dummy element (test-kinds) shows name, layer and IFC class without panicking.
- ELM-011 default classes are validated per kind through the descriptor; ELM-006 default top links stay consistent with storey deletion for every kind.
notes: SRS: ELM-011 ELM-006. Also ELM-001 and ELM-019 (owned elsewhere, kept green). Appendix D.2: wall 0.25 m, reference line on the exterior face, top home + 1; slab 0.20 m, top at the storey elevation.

title: Cut the insert void through every host skin and restore on delete
description:
WHY: DW-009 requires that 'a door or window shall cut all skins of its host, the void shall update live when either changes, and deleting the door or window shall restore the host'. DW-006 requires that 'the element and the void shall update immediately' when width or height change. The empty opening of DW-010 cuts like any other unit, and DW-001 makes the cut follow the host. IFX-033 requires that exported host bodies already have the volume removed, and IFX-036 that every door and window has a closed Void enclosing the removed volume. The epic acceptance checks, through geometry tests with undo, that the void cuts all skins of an F2 wall and that the host is restored on delete. Today there is no host cutting: ModelGeometry::evaluate (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:64) evaluates every element independently, and walls are single prisms. host-openings delivers the whole cut path:
- VoidPrism, void_mesh and VOID_MARGIN (host-openings-03);
- extrude_layers (host-openings-04);
- wall_cut.rs, which cuts every skin band of a wall with the VoidPrisms collected into EvalContext::cutters from its Host dependents (host-openings-05).
This task feeds door and window voids into that path.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/insert.rs with insert_void(frame: &InsertFrame, section: &CrossSection) -> VoidPrism. The section is the definition's void profile (UnitGeometry.void_profile of components-dw-catalogue-04: the rectangle [0, w] x [0, h] for doors, windows and opening.rectangular), placed by frame.unit_to_storey. The depth is a through cut over the full host thickness plus VOID_MARGIN beyond both faces, independent of the reveal. Where the profile reaches the host base or top, it is extended by VOID_MARGIN, so no void face is coplanar with a host face.

The door and window GeometryKind modules (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/door.rs and window.rs) provide this VoidPrism through the cutter hook the opening kind uses, so wall_cut.rs cuts every Skin_n band unchanged. They also keep void_mesh as a part named 'Void' with role Void on the insert's ElementGeometry, for IFCX (05) and the preview (08); visible_parts() skips it.

Warnings go to ModelGeometry.problems without failing the element:
- a unit whose interval reaches past the junction-resolved skin face end points (the clear-length check against the joined wall's zone);
- a unit partly above the wall top or below its base, clipped to the wall.
The incremental dirty set already follows Host edges both ways (asserted by host-openings-05); add insert edits to the incremental-versus-full property test. Out of scope: frame, leaf and symbol parts (04), arc walls (DW-019, curved-geometry), and cuts of non-host elements (OPN-002, solid-kernel-ops).
design:
Reuse the host-openings cut path unchanged. A door is one more producer of VoidPrisms, so niches, openings and doors share the robust 2D subtraction: geo Booleans with MODEL_TOLERANCE and validation of every resulting ring.

Order of operations per wall: junction-resolved skin footprints (junction-engine, layer-structures), then wall-plane cuts (wall_cut.rs), then extrusion. The cut is defined in wall-local coordinates (s along the reference line, z up), so mitred skin ends at L corners do not change the cut rectangle.

Taking the section from UnitGeometry.void_profile means the arched and round-headed empty openings of components-dw-catalogue (DW-022) are cut as polygon sections without extra code, within wall_cut.rs's limits for non-rectilinear sections at end pieces.

The clear-length check compares [s0, s1] with the projections of the skin face end points of the resolved footprint (wall.rs footprints), which flags doors that would cut into the joined wall's zone. Report it as a warning; it is the junction risk named by the epic.

Dirty propagation: the Host edge already marks host and hosted elements dirty (host-openings). Make sure an insert edit invalidates the host's cached Arc<ElementGeometry>.

Pitfalls:
- Coincident edges when the door edge meets a skin end: snap within MODEL_TOLERANCE before the Boolean (wall_cut.rs does this for depth bounds; extend it to the along bounds if needed).
- Do not emit separate holes per skin for a void that spans several skins in one band; the per-skin loop must use the same rectangle.
- The Void prism must not share vertices across hard edges (IFX-038).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/inserts.rs: an F2 wall (680 mm, six skins) 5.00 m long with a 0.90 x 2.10 m door away from both ends. Each Skin_n's signed volume drops by 0.90 x 2.10 x t_n, the total drop is 1.2852 m3 within 1e-9 relative, and every part passes TriMesh::check_closed (DW-009 'all skins').
- History-driven test: execute DeleteElements on the door, and the wall volume returns to the gross volume; undo, and the cut is back; redo removes it again (DW-009 'restore the host').
- ResizeInserts and FlipInsertSide (02) followed by evaluation give the expected void (resize) and a bit-identical host body (flip) (DW-006 'immediately', DW-003).
- Host changes re-cut the wall: switching the host from F2 to a 0.25 m Thickness structure gives a drop of 0.90 x 2.10 x 0.25 m3, and MoveElements on the host moves the void with it (DW-009 'update live when either changes').
- The incremental-versus-full equivalence property test of element-kind-framework, extended with insert edits (add, resize, flip, move host, change host structure, delete), stays bit-identical.
- The Void part is closed and outward-oriented, contains the removed volume, reaches VOID_MARGIN beyond both faces and below the base for a door at floor level, and is not returned by visible_parts() (IFX-036 shape).
- A door whose head is above the wall top is clipped to the top and listed in problems; a door reaching into the joined wall's zone at an L corner is listed with a message naming both walls; an empty opening of the same size cuts exactly like a door (DW-010).
- plan_drawing at the default 1.10 m cut plane splits the wall's cut region at the door, and no cut polygon intersects the door's interval.
notes: SRS: DW-009 DW-006 DW-010 DW-001 (plus IFX-033, IFX-036 shape, NFR-REL-006). F2 per Appendix D.7: brick 120 / air 60 / insulation 180 / plaster 10 / concrete 300 / plaster 10 = 680 mm, nominal height 3000 mm. Void margin: VOID_MARGIN = 0.05 m from host-openings-03 (the margin of the SRS Appendix C example); do not introduce a second constant.

title: Show failed elements as pickable fallback boxes
description:
WHY: NFR-REL-006 (M): a failing element (for example a geometry evaluation that throws) shall not crash the application; the element is flagged, shown with a fallback representation and listed in a problems panel. Existing (keep): each element is evaluated inside catch_unwind (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:64-91), failures are flagged in ModelGeometry.problems and listed in the problems panel (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:847-883). Gaps: a failed element is skipped in plan (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:121-123) and 3D (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:111-113), so it cannot be seen, picked, highlighted or zoomed to; the global panic hook (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/crash.rs:66-89) also fires for panics that catch_unwind in evaluate.rs:69 swallows, writing a crash report and showing 'ArchiCraft crashed last time' after a recovered geometry failure; the writer saves such an element without a body and warns (writer.rs:390-394).

WHAT: ModelGeometry.problems becomes BTreeMap<ElementId, GeometryProblem { message, fallback: Option<Arc<ElementGeometry>> }>; a dummy with panic_on_evaluate (its geometry generator from task 15 panics) is the test subject; the fallback is a closed box extruded from Kind::plan_bounds() (task 02) and the element's vertical extent, built outside the kind's generator and itself guarded, with ElementGeometry.fallback = true; ModelGeometry::body_or_fallback(id) serves plan, picking and zoom; evaluate_incremental carries problems and fallbacks of clean elements. Geometry plan.rs classifies fallback bodies like bodies and tags PlanElement.fallback; views/plan.rs draws them with a dashed outline and a warning fill (Palette.fallback, at least 3:1 contrast against both canvas backgrounds); render3d.rs draws them edge-only in the warning colour; both stay pickable, and model_bounds and zoom_to include them. The geometry crate exposes a thread-local in_guarded_evaluation() set around its catch_unwind, and crash.rs's hook returns early when it is set (the message still goes to tracing). The writer never writes fallback meshes (IFX-063) and keeps its warning. Out of scope: problems-panel changes (task 14), EDT-018/EDT-019 repair reports (edit-reshape-palette).
design: Build the fallback with extrude() of the bounds rectangle so slicing, plan classification and ray picking reuse the existing paths. Keep the fallback out of a real ElementGeometry's parts by storing it in GeometryProblem. The guard is a Cell<bool> on the evaluating thread only; the panic hook reads it first. Run the per-element classification in plan_drawing inside the same guard, so a panic while slicing one element marks it failed instead of taking the frame down. Pitfalls: kittest cannot render wgpu, so the 3D pick is a unit test on view3d::pick; a kind without plan_bounds gets no fallback and only a panel entry (document this); the warning colour must meet the UI-010 contrast rule in light and dark themes. Pointers: evaluate.rs:51-91, plan.rs:111-150, render3d.rs:102-176, view3d.rs:59-100, views/plan.rs palette, crash.rs:66-89, writer.rs:361-417.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test (test-kinds): a project with a dummy whose panic_on_evaluate is set yields problems[id] with the message and a closed fallback box whose bounds equal plan_bounds and the vertical extent; no other element is affected; evaluate_incremental keeps the fallback while the dummy is unchanged.
- plan_drawing test: the fallback element appears with fallback == true, is classified by its box and pick() at its centre returns its id; render3d test: build_scene includes its edges; view3d::pick hits it.
- crash.rs test with a temporary directory: a panic inside guarded evaluation writes no crash report, an unguarded panic still does.
- Round trip: saving a project with a failed element writes the element without a body and one warning, never the fallback mesh.
- NFR-REL-006 satisfied: no crash, flagged, fallback shown and pickable, listed (panel click behaviour in task 14).
notes: SRS: NFR-REL-006. Also IFX-063 (consumers never see invented geometry), NFR-SEC-002 (no spurious crash report) and UI-010 (contrast of the warning colour).

title: 2D construction geometry with the shared arc type, trim, extend, split and array
description:
Add the 2D reference-element kinds (lines, chains, polylines, arcs, circles, then rectangles, splines, tangent arcs and drafting fills) bound to a view and a layer, usable as tracing input and as cutters, together with the exact Arc/PolyCurve type and the single tessellate(curve, settings) function that arc walls, slab rings, plan cuts and the IFCX writer reuse later (so curved-geometry and fixture F8 are not a retrofit), and the linear editing commands: trim, extend, split, explicit-command variants of every gesture (D-7), arrays and path distribution, plus wall split and merge. Join/unjoin (WAL-022) lives with the junction engine.

Risks: Splines are a rabbit hole: v1 tessellates Catmull-Rom/Bezier through points with node editing only. WAL-030's hosted-element clause can only be verified once doors exist; a test hook is prepared and re-run by doors-windows-core through the relation store. Arc parameters are written with float_roundtrip so round trips stay exact (NFR-ACC-002).
design: archicraft-model: curve.rs (Arc, PolyCurve with straight and arc segments, exact storage) and kinds/drafting.rs (Line, Polyline, Arc, Circle, Fill) with view binding and pen/line-type references, registered as a PlanSegmentSource for contour.rs (hence the dependency on edit-reshape-palette, whose Outline operations the cutters also reuse); archicraft-geometry: tessellate(curve, settings) reading ProjectSettings.tessellation (so far unused), intersection utilities in primitives, reshape.rs with segment intersection search on geo; archicraft-app: tools/drafting.rs and tools/linear_edit.rs with the cutter pick step through the point-input service; decision D-7: explicit commands first, modifier gestures as accelerators.
acceptance_criteria: 2D elements round-trip in the archicraft:: namespace and optionally as IfcAnnotation curves; a three-point arc stores centre, radius and sweep exactly and tessellates per the IFX-034 settings, and two producers tessellating the same curve id yield bit-identical vertex lists; 2D elements register as a segment source of the contour detection built in edit-reshape-palette, so a slab is traced from a closed chain of 2D lines in one pick (ANN-002 tracing clause); trimming a wall back to the nearest intersecting wall or 2D line, extending to a picked wall face and splitting a slab or wall by a two-point line keep the chosen part selected (fixtures); array tests for linear, radial, vertical and rectangular arrays with all four methods; splitting a wall yields two joined walls that keep their hosted elements (hook re-run by doors-windows-core); every gesture has a menu command with a preview (inspection checklist); the 2D tool group appears in the toolbox with D.8 shortcuts (kittest).
notes: SRS: ANN-001 ANN-002 ANN-003 ANN-010 ANN-011 EDT-004 EDT-005 EDT-011 EDT-012 EDT-013 EDT-020 WAL-030 WAL-031

title: Add the WallInsert placement and the door and window kinds
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/inserts.rs: Command::AddElements with a wall and a door, then undo and redo, keeps both ids and the Host relation (RelationStore::relations_of), and the door's storey equals the host's storey; a door added with another storey is normalised to the host's (DW-001 'take their storey association from the host').
- A door whose host is missing or is not a wall (a slab) is rejected with CommandError::Invalid and the project is unchanged; an interval outside [0, host length] is rejected with 'The door does not fit in wall W-003' (DW-001 'exist only in a host wall', ELM-017).
- Anchor table test: AlongStart, Centre and AlongEnd at pointer parameter p and width w give [p, p+w], [p-w/2, p+w/2] and [p-w, p]; changing w keeps the anchor point bit-identical (DW-005).
- Pin tests: with a Sill pin a height change keeps the sill, with a Head pin it keeps the head; HomeStorey, Storey(other storey), HostBase (wall base offset) and HostTop (through Project::top_elevation) resolve to the expected elevations (DW-007).
- Reveal tests on a 0.25 m Structure::Thickness wall and on the F2 'Cavity wall 680' structure: Exterior, Interior, CoreExterior (0.370 m on F2) and CoreInterior (0.670 m on F2), each with an offset, and Centred{Wall, Core} resolve to the expected distance from the exterior face (Centred{Core} on F2: unit mid-depth at 0.520 m); on the Thickness wall the core faces coincide with the wall faces; an offset that puts the unit outside the wall thickness is rejected with a message (DW-008).
- Appendix D table test: the door slot is door.hinged.single, 0.90 x 2.10 m, Sill pin on HomeStorey at 0, Centred{Wall}; the window slot is window.tilt-turn, 1.20 x 1.40 m, Sill pin on HomeStorey at 0.90 m, Centred{Core}; check_tool_defaults accepts both slots without a host (DW-006 defaults).
- An insert bound to opening.rectangular has class IfcOpeningElement and a definition without parts, and the anchor, pin and reveal table tests pass unchanged with it (DW-010 'same placement, anchor and reveal rules').
- MoveElements on the host keeps 'along' and moves the resolved frame; MoveElements on the door alone slides it along the host and is rejected when it would leave the host; deleting the host deletes the door, and undo restores both with the Host relation (DW-001 'move with it', 'deleted with it').
- effective_instance: for exterior HostExterior and HostInterior, unit_to_storey has a positive determinant, and the physical hinge end and swing side stay the same because mirrored and the swing parameter are re-derived (IFX-051 groundwork for DW-003).
- The registry completeness and module-layout tests of element-kind-framework pass with the two new kinds in all three crates, and cargo test is green on the workspace.

title: Build the door and window tools with host picking and cycling
design:
Follow the 'Add a drawing tool' extension point as rewritten by point-input-snapping (tools/ module, InputConsumer): the tool consumes resolved points (snap, constraint, typed value) and never reads raw pointer events.

Host candidates: reuse input/host.rs of host-openings-10 rather than a second query. The cycle index lives in the tool's step state and resets when the candidate set changes.

Feedback goes through the StepSpec prompt, and through Workspace::error (workspace.rs:111) only when the user clicks without a host, so hovering over empty space does not flash errors.

Compute 'along' with along_for_pointer from kinds/insert.rs (01), so tool and model cannot disagree.

Pitfalls:
- Projecting onto the reference line can give a parameter outside [0, L] at wall ends; clamp to the nearest valid interval and show the clamped preview rather than refusing.
- Locked or hidden-layer walls are not candidates (Project::is_editable, project.rs:222).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in tools/insert.rs, without egui: with no wall under the pointer, the commit returns Outcome::Nothing and sets the 'need a wall' message; over a wall, the AlongStart, Centre and AlongEnd anchors put the unit's left end, centre and right end at the pointer; the nearer face decides 'exterior' (DW-001, DW-003, DW-005).
- At an L junction the candidate list has both walls, and one press of the CycleHost key switches the active host; the created door is hosted by the active candidate. The same holds for two overlapping parallel walls, such as a lining in front of a wall (DW-002 'junctions, overlaps', 'a single key').
- A typed distance of 0.500 m from a snapped wall end puts the anchor exactly 0.500 m from that end, checked at 0.1 mm display precision (INP typed input, increment-1 'drawn precisely').
- ui/actions.rs tests: shortcuts_are_unique stays green with ToolDoor, ToolWindow and CycleHost, and appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts includes the door and window tools (UI-008, Appendix D.8).
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs (egui_kittest): the Door and Window toolbox buttons exist and set ws.tool.kind; with the door tool, a click on empty plan space adds no element and the feedback text is visible; a click on a wall adds one door hosted by that wall (DW-001 'clear feedback and create nothing').
- kittest: choosing an empty opening in the definition picker and clicking a wall creates a unit with class IfcOpeningElement (DW-010).
notes: SRS: DW-001 DW-002 DW-003 DW-005 DW-010 (plus SEL-001 highlight pattern, INP-009 Tab semantics, UI-008 / Appendix D.8 tool shortcuts, INP typed input). Appendix D.8 leaves concrete keys to UI design; pick free keys and record them in the shortcut table test. Decision to record: host cycling has its own key, because Tab already cycles snap candidates and fields in drawing tools (point-input-snapping-03).

title: Add the exact Arc and PolyCurve curve type with intersections
description:
WHY: ANN-001 (M) requires 2D construction lines "single, or chained with straight and arc segments", polylines, and "arcs and circles by centre and radius or by three points". ANN-002 (M) makes 2D elements cutters for trim and split; EDT-011 (M) trims "back to the nearest intersections" and EDT-012 (M) extends "to a picked boundary, or to the boundary's extension", so exact intersections of lines and arcs and of their carriers (infinite line, full circle) are needed. WAL-031 (S) merges walls that "are collinear (or lie on the same circle)", which needs a same-carrier test and an exact join of touching pieces. The epic requires one exact Arc/PolyCurve type that arc walls, slab rings, plan cuts and the IFCX writer reuse later (curved-geometry-01 converts its ArcEdge to and from this Arc; railings-stairs-adv-13 and members-profiles-adv-17 use `Curve::{Straight, Arc(Arc)}`), and NFR-ACC-002 requires parameters at full double precision. Gap row ANN-001 (missing): "no arc/circle geometry anywhere". Existing code this task builds on and does not change: edit-reshape-palette-01's `Outline<E>` in crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/ with `EdgeShape::Line` only (#[non_exhaustive]; curved-geometry-01 adds the arc edge), selection-transforms-02's `Transform` in crates/archicraft-model/src/transform.rs, element-kind-framework-01's tolerance.rs (MODEL_TOLERANCE, ANGLE_TOLERANCE, is_parallel, near_zero) and edit-reshape-palette-02's `ProjectSettings.repair: RepairThresholds { min_edge_length, min_corner_angle_deg }`.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs (exported from lib.rs): `Arc { centre: DVec2, radius: f64, start_angle: f64, sweep: f64 }` (radians per SRS 3.5, sweep signed with counter-clockwise positive, 0 < |sweep| <= 2π, a full circle has |sweep| = 2π) with constructors `Arc::centre_radius(centre, radius, start_angle, end_angle, ccw)`, `Arc::through(a, b, c)` (three points, collinear points rejected), `Arc::circle(centre, radius)`, `Arc::circle_through(a, b, c)` and `Arc::tangent_continuation(start, tangent, end)`, plus `Arc::point_on(centre, radius, theta)` as the one point evaluation every consumer uses; `Curve { Straight, Arc(Arc) }` as the shape of an edge between two nodes; `Segment { Line { a, b }, Arc(Arc) }` for standalone computation; `PolyCurve { points: Vec<DVec2>, edges: Vec<Curve>, closed: bool }` with segments(), node/edge accessors and the invariant that every arc edge starts and ends on its nodes within MODEL_TOLERANCE. Operations on Segment: start/end, point_at(t), tangent_at(t), param_of(point) (closest point, bounded or on the carrier), length, exact bbox (arc extrema inside the sweep), reversed, split_at(t), sub(t0, t1), offset(d) (positive to the left), `join(&Segment) -> Option<Segment>` (two pieces on the same carrier touching end to end become one; centre and radius bits kept, sweeps added), `transform(&Transform)` for the plan variants of selection-transforms-02 (Move without dz, Rotate, Mirror, uniform Scale; anything else returns an error) and translate. Intersections: `intersect(&Segment, &Segment, Extent) -> Hits` (an inline array of at most two `Hit { point, ta, tb, tangent }`, no new dependency) for line/line, line/arc and arc/arc with `Extent::{Bounded, CarrierA, CarrierB, Carriers}`; collinear or co-circular overlaps are reported as Overlap instead of hits; `same_carrier(&Segment, &Segment)` (collinear lines or the same circle within tolerance). Validation `validate_arc(&Arc, &RepairThresholds)` and `validate_polycurve(&PolyCurve, &RepairThresholds) -> Result<(PolyCurve, Vec<Repair>), String>` (finite values; radius and every edge length at least min_edge_length; arc ends on nodes; consecutive nodes within MODEL_TOLERANCE merged, mirroring validate::repair_outline). Out of scope: tessellation (02), element kinds (03), arc edges in Outline, arc walls and arc-preserving contour detection (curved-geometry).
design: Exact storage: an Arc keeps centre, radius, start angle and sweep exactly as its constructor computed them; nothing is re-derived from end points or tessellation, which makes a three-point arc round-trip exactly (NFR-ACC-002). End points are derived (Arc::point_on), so PolyCurve keeps its nodes explicitly and joints use the node, never the derived point. Add `Arc::canonical()` (counter-clockwise, start in [0, 2π)) for direction-independent consumers (the circle-anchored tessellation of task 02). Maths: line/arc by the quadratic in the line parameter with the discriminant clamped (|disc| <= tolerance² counts as tangent); arc/arc through the radical line; arc parameter t = normalised angle from the start along the sweep using rem_euclid; parallel and degenerate guards through tolerance.rs is_parallel and near_zero (element-kind-framework-01 replaced the literal epsilons of wall.rs intersect()); never compare with f64::EPSILON. Layering: the module must not depend on geo or archicraft-geometry, because the command planners of tasks 10, 11, 12 and 14 run inside Command::plan() in the model crate; archicraft-geometry re-exports what it needs. Naming: `Arc` clashes with std::sync::Arc, so consumers import curve::Arc and qualify std's Arc. Pitfalls: the atan2 branch cut at ±π; full circles have no ends (trim and split open them first, tasks 10 and 11); mirroring negates the sweep and reflects the start angle (the selection-transforms mirror rule); a non-uniform Scale is not representable for arcs and returns an error the kind hook turns into TransformError::Unsupported. Technology choices dropped kurbo ('straight lines and arcs are all we need'), so the spline of task 07 is a small module of our own.
acceptance_criteria:
- curve.rs unit tests: Arc::through((0,0), (1,1), (2,0)) stores centre (1, 0), radius 1, start angle π and sweep −π bit-exactly (f64::to_bits); collinear points return Err; circle_through gives |sweep| = 2π; tangent_continuation from a line end has a start tangent parallel to the line within 1e-12.
- Intersection table test: line/line crossing, parallel (no hit) and collinear overlap (Overlap); line/arc with 0, 1 (tangent) and 2 hits; arc/arc with 2 hits, external and internal tangency and concentric (none); a hit outside the sweep is returned only with a carrier extent; for every bounded hit point_at(ta) and point_at(tb) reproduce the point within 1e-12.
- Seeded xorshift property tests (no new dependency): split_at(t) halves sum to the original length within 1e-12 and share the split point bitwise; the two halves join() back to a segment with the original centre and radius bits and a sweep within 1e-12; reversed().reversed() is bit-identical; a Mirror applied twice restores the segment within 1e-12 and flips the sweep sign once; four Rotates by 90° restore it bitwise (exact quarter turns of selection-transforms-02); the bbox contains 1,000 sampled points.
- same_carrier is true for two collinear lines and two arcs on one circle and false for parallel offset lines and concentric arcs of different radius; join() of two co-circular arcs touching end to end gives one arc (the WAL-031 same-circle case); join() of non-touching or different-carrier pieces gives None.
- validate_arc/validate_polycurve reject NaN, a radius below RepairThresholds.min_edge_length, |sweep| > 2π and an arc end 1 mm off its node; duplicate consecutive nodes are merged and reported as a Repair.
- Arc, Curve, Segment and PolyCurve derive Serialize/Deserialize/PartialEq and round-trip bit-identically through serde_json (float_roundtrip is enabled in the workspace Cargo.toml:51), so commands stay journal-serialisable.
- edit-reshape-palette's outline tests and crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs pass unchanged; golden files are byte-identical; cargo test, clippy --all-targets and fmt are green.
- Prepares ANN-001, ANN-002 (cutters), EDT-011, EDT-012 and WAL-031 (same-carrier join); no requirement row changes status from this task alone.
notes:
SRS: ANN-001 ANN-002 EDT-011 EDT-012 WAL-031 (foundation only)
Entry task of the epic: it waits for element-kind-framework (tolerance module, kind registry), point-input-snapping, plan-attributes, selection-transforms (Transform type and mirror rule) and edit-reshape-palette (Outline, RepairThresholds).

title: Write compound parts, site-level and hosted elements in the spatial tree
description:
WHY: IFX-016 (M, status missing): parts of compound elements (stair flights, landings and stringers; railing components; curtain-wall frames and panels; the planes of a multi-plane roof) are child nodes of the compound element, each with its own IFC class according to Table 5-1. IFX-012 (M, partial): the spatial structure is expressed by children (IfcProject -> IfcSite -> IfcBuilding -> IfcBuildingStorey -> elements), and each element that is neither hosted (IFX-015) nor a part (IFX-016) is a child of exactly one spatial node, its home storey or the site for site-level elements such as terrain; hosted elements and parts are contained through their host or compound element. Existing (keep): writer.rs:252-307 writes project -> site -> building -> storeys -> elements, tested by spatial_tree_and_identities (tests/roundtrip.rs:143-191) and conformance/check.ts:67-103. Missing: the writer always nests elements under their home storey and writes one node per element plus Body and Axis sub-nodes (writer.rs:284-307/361-417), so site-level elements, hosted elements and parts have no place; check.ts only visits storey children and requires a mesh directly under each element. IFX-010 gives regenerated sub-nodes v5 ids from the owner's UUID and role, IFX-020 requires bsi::ifc::class on every compound part, IFX-017 names body children. Part bodies come from the geometry registry (task 15), part classes from Kind::parts() (task 02) and COMPOUND_PART_CLASSES (task 05), Host relations from the relation store (task 08). Roofs and stairs re-assert the mechanism with real elements.

WHAT: Writer (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs): one helper writes the Body/Body_n/Axis children for an element or a part from ElementGeometry and its children (task 15); each part of Kind::parts() becomes a child node of its compound element with bsi::ifc::class from its PartSpec (bSDD URI through the existing class() helper), bsi::ifc::prop::Name "<element name> <label>", path sub_node_id(owner, role) and no archicraft:: attributes (it is regenerated from the owner's parameters). Containment follows IFX-012: an element whose Kind::container() is Site (task 02) is written under the site node with a usd::xformop translating by its home storey elevation; an element that is the hosted end of a Relation::Host (task 08, host_of) is written as a child of its host's node instead of its storey, so every element node has exactly one parent; both write an optional archicraft::element.homeStorey member (declared in alpha/schema.rs only when used) because the parent no longer implies the storey. Reader (reader.rs): part nodes (no archicraft::element) are never read as elements and raise no warning; element nodes under the site or under another element are read with their homeStorey, and a missing or dangling homeStorey falls back to the ground storey with a warning. conformance/check.ts collects meshes recursively through part children, requires bsi::ifc::class and a name on every part, accepts element nodes under the site and under host elements and counts each element once. New golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/compound-parts.ifcx from a test-kinds fixture built with the FixtureBuilder of task 03 (compound dummy, site-level dummy, a dummy hosted in a wall, one wall), so the CI conformance job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:69 globs golden/*.ifcx) covers the mechanism. Out of scope: the geometry registry and part bodies (task 15), real compound kinds (roofs, stairs, railings and curtain walls re-assert the mechanism), hosting semantics, voids and the ELM-016 cascade (host-openings), Skin_n multi-material bodies (layer-structures), part selection (selection-transforms).
design: The model declares which parts exist and their classes, the geometry crate generates their bodies (task 15), the writer joins both by role. Part roles are stable per kind (Part_n in a stable order, later Flight_n, Landing_n, Frame_n) so v5 ids survive edits. The site node has no translation, so a site-level element needs its own transform; the reader must restore the home storey from homeStorey because the parent no longer implies it. Hosted nesting uses the relation store instead of a new element field, so host-openings only adds the Host semantics (voids, cascade); cycles are impossible because InsertRelation rejects Host cycles and second hosts (task 08). Pitfalls: the compound-parts golden only loads in test builds (test-kinds); the release-built reference_models example never includes it, and catalogue() keeps the test fixture behind #[cfg(feature = "test-kinds")]; use the fixed author/timestamp of the other goldens; emit the homeStorey declaration only when a site-level or hosted element exists (content-derived declarations of task 06) so the other goldens stay bit-identical; writer.rs still does not verify closedness or MAX_MESH_POINTS (technical debt), keep the dummy's meshes small. Pointers: writer.rs:243-417, reader.rs:735-880, schema.rs:212-257, conformance/check.ts:67-103, tests/roundtrip.rs:143-230.
acceptance_criteria:
- compound_parts_are_child_nodes_with_their_own_class (test-kinds): the compound element node has children Part_1 and Part_2 whose paths equal Uuid::new_v5(owner, "Part_1") and Uuid::new_v5(owner, "Part_2"), with bsi::ifc::class code IfcMember and IfcPlate plus a uri (IFX-020), a bsi::ifc::prop::Name and mesh bodies inheriting a material node; loading gives back the identical project with zero problems.
- site_level_elements_are_children_of_the_site: the site-level dummy is a child of the IfcSite node, not of a storey, its world position matches the model within 0.1 mm (IFX-031) and it loads back onto its home storey.
- hosted_elements_are_children_of_their_host: a dummy with a Relation::Host to a wall is a child of the wall node and of no storey, and loads back with its home storey and the relation; after RemoveRelation and a new save it is a child of its storey again.
- every_element_has_exactly_one_parent: in every golden and in the test-kinds fixture each element node occurs in exactly one children map (storey, site or host element) and parts are never counted as elements (IFX-012 'exactly one spatial node'); spatial_tree_and_identities still passes.
- part_classes_follow_table_5_1: every PartSpec of a non-test kind uses a class from the COMPOUND_PART_CLASSES row of its default class (vacuous until roofs and stairs, enforced afterwards).
- Saving twice yields identical part ids and bytes (IFX-010, IFX-007); written_meshes_are_closed_bodies covers part bodies and site-level elements.
- compound-parts.ifcx is reproduced by golden_files_are_reproduced and passes conformance/run.sh with the extended check.ts (bodies under parts found, every part classed, site and hosted children accepted); the other goldens stay bit-identical; the module-layout test for crates/archicraft-ifcx/src stays green.
- IFX-016 mechanism satisfied (roofs and stairs re-assert it with real elements); IFX-012 storey, site, part and hosted clauses satisfied; IFX-020 and IFX-010 hold for parts.
notes: SRS: IFX-016 IFX-012. Also IFX-010, IFX-015 (hosted containment mechanism), IFX-017 (Body naming kept), IFX-020 for parts, IFX-031 for site-level placement. Table 5-1 rows consumed later: stair (IfcStairFlight, IfcSlab landings, IfcMember stringers), railing (IfcMember, IfcPlate), curtain wall (IfcMember frames, IfcPlate panels), multi-plane roof (IfcSlab per plane), terrain (IfcGeographicElement under the site). Split from the former single task: the geometry registry is now task 15.

title: Write IfcDoor and IfcWindow occurrences with Void and typed parts
design:
Mirror Appendix C item 5 (SRS lines 1933-1936): the window occurrence is a child of its host wall, placed relative to it, inherits its type and carries its own invisible Void; the type holds only host-independent parts.

Transform: the wall node itself is untransformed below the storey (storey transform = elevation), so the occurrence transform is InstanceGeometry.transform from task 04, written row-major with the translation in the fourth row (IFX-031). Void and part meshes live in occurrence-local coordinates. Express reflections only through the mirrored type, never through the matrix.

Type dedup: use the catalogue's TypeKey and type writer (components-dw-catalogue-07/09) instead of a second key or writer, so v5 ids stay stable across saves (IFX-011).

Use round_coordinate only for mesh coordinates, and write parameters at full precision (writer.rs conventions).

Pitfalls:
- IFX-038: every planar face region gets its own vertices.
- The Void must not inherit any material (it is not a body).
- Child keys must be unique per parent (child_key, writer.rs:56) when a wall hosts many doors.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/inserts.rs, on a project with an F2 wall plus two identical doors, one door with the other hinge end, a window and an empty opening:
  - the file passes archicraft_ifcx::validate::validate with no problems, and conformance/run.sh passes on the written file (IFX-006 a);
  - each IfcDoor/IfcWindow node is a child of its IfcWall node, and its Void child is invisible, closed and outward-oriented (IFX-015, IFX-036);
  - the two identical doors inherit one type node with one part mesh set, and the other-handed door inherits a separate mirrored type (DW-018, IFX-050, IFX-051).
- No written transform has a negative determinant (the test walks every usd::xformop.transform), and each occurrence's world placement matches InsertFrame within 0.1 mm (IFX-031).
- The wall's exported Skin_n volumes equal gross minus the void share per skin, so the host was cut before writing (IFX-033).
- The empty opening is written as IfcOpeningElement with a Void and without parts or inherits.type (DW-010, IFX-025).
- The type's parts are named by role as written by components-dw-catalogue-09 (Frame, Leaf, Sash, Glazing, Sill), and each inherits its material node (DW-018 'material parts', IFX-017).
- A door in an exterior wall carries bsi::ifc::prop::IsExternal true (IFX-022); archicraft::door has no definition or parameter keys, because they are in archicraft::component.
- Output stays byte-deterministic (the output_is_deterministic_and_plain pattern); the re-blessed existing golden files differ only in the format version.
notes: SRS: DW-018 DW-010 (plus IFX-015, IFX-017, IFX-022, IFX-025, IFX-031, IFX-033, IFX-036, IFX-037, IFX-050, IFX-051, IFX-062, Table 5-1). The archicraft:: attribute layout is an ArchiCraft design deliverable (SRS Appendix C note); keep it close to the model's WallInsert fields, so the reader is a straight mapping.

title: Verify exit criterion: Extensible element kinds, relations, compound parts and incremental evaluation
description:
WHY: The element-kind-framework epic is the foundation every later element epic registers through; its exit criterion has to be shown on the merged result as a whole before columns, beams, openings, roofs, stairs, terrain, grids and 2D elements build on it. The covered requirements are ELM-011, ELM-006, STR-006, IFX-012, IFX-060, IFX-062, IFX-024, IFX-016, NFR-ACC-003, NFR-PERF-006, NFR-REL-005, NFR-REL-006, VIEW-001 and UI-012, and docs/implementation-status.md must show their new status with evidence.

WHAT: On the merged state of tasks 01-15: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test --workspace (module-layout, tolerance grep, registry, codec, geometry-registry, compound-part, hosted-containment, relation, storey-rejection, incremental-versus-full, migration and kittest suites included); the #[ignore]d stand-in and timing smoke tests once in release with the numbers recorded; cargo run -p archicraft-ifcx --example reference_models twice (byte-identical) and conformance/run.sh on target/reference-models/*.ifcx and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx (including compound-parts.ifcx); a review of every golden diff made in the epic. Then update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered ID (status, file:line evidence, remaining gap for clauses owned elsewhere: the Boolean clause of NFR-ACC-003, OBJ-005 for UI-012, the standard attribute of IFX-024 (O-6), the measured budget of NFR-PERF-006, hosted containment of IFX-012), rewrite the 'Add an element kind' extension point (one module per crate plus one registry line each), update the architecture summary, remove the closed technical-debt entries, file beads for anything deferred and close the epic with bd close. Git and Dolt sync follow the active beads profile; report the commands instead of committing when the profile is conservative.
design: A checklist run on the merged branch, not new code. Record the release-profile timings of evaluate_incremental on stand_in(5_000), of the plan and scene refresh, and of the full evaluation of stand_in(20_000) in the closing note so regression-and-status starts from a baseline. Status rows cite file:line evidence as docs/implementation-status.md does today; the gap-analysis rows of the covered IDs are the template for wording.
acceptance_criteria:
