- A module-layout test adds a test-only dummy kind and asserts that only its own module plus one registry entry changed; a test-only compound kind writes Part_n children with their own IfcClass and v5 ids, round-trips and passes the conformance job (IFX-016 mechanism; roofs and stairs re-assert it with real elements); IfcClass covers the full D.5 list and slab/footing predefined types round-trip in archicraft:: (IFX-024); after one edit in the 5,000-element stand-in the dirty set contains only the edited element and its relation/contact neighbours and a property test compares incremental against full evaluation on random edit sequences (bit-identical); MODEL_TOLERANCE (0.01 mm) is the only tolerance constant in model, geometry and snapping (grep test); moving a storey below a linked wall's base is rejected with CommandError::Invalid; a deliberately panicking test kind renders as a fallback box, is pickable and appears in the problems panel whose click selects and zooms (kittest); a FORMAT_VERSION n-1 file migrates with a report; all existing golden files, round-trip tests and the conformance job stay green.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on the golden files and on freshly written reference models.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (ELM-011 ELM-006 STR-006 IFX-012 IFX-060 IFX-062 IFX-024 IFX-016 NFR-ACC-003 NFR-PERF-006 NFR-REL-005 NFR-REL-006 VIEW-001 UI-012) with status, evidence and remaining gap, and its architecture summary, extension points and technical-debt list reflect the registry, relation store, codecs, tolerance module and incremental evaluation.
- The epic is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for deferred clauses.
notes: SRS: ELM-011 ELM-006 STR-006 IFX-012 IFX-060 IFX-062 IFX-024 IFX-016 NFR-ACC-003 NFR-PERF-006 NFR-REL-005 NFR-REL-006 VIEW-001 UI-012. Downstream epics waiting on this key: selection-transforms, plan-attributes, drafting-trim-split, plan-views-browser, layer-structures, profiles-columns-beams, host-openings, components-dw-catalogue, properties-and-dialogs, solid-kernel-ops, grids, terrain-and-site, stair-solver-tool, ifcx-interop, curtain-walls.

title: Slab edge angles: per-edge model, inclined faces, IFCX and palette
description:
WHY — SLB-005 (S): slab edges shall have an edge angle, vertical by default and settable per edge. Gap row SLB-005: missing; extrusion side faces are vertical quads (extrude.rs:47-56), a slab has no per-edge data, and a per-edge attribute on outline and holes, non-vertical side faces, per-edge UI, the IFCX schema and the reader are all needed.

WHAT — Model: `SlabEdge { angle_deg: f64 }` (default 90) as the slab's EdgeData (Slab.outline: Outline<SlabEdge>) with a validated range and `ReshapeOp::SetEdgeAngle { angle_deg, whole_ring: bool }`. Geometry: the ring of the face opposite the reference face is the reference ring offset per edge by t / tan(angle) through offset_ring of task 03, and extrude.rs gains a two-ring extrusion (separate top and bottom caps, planar trapezoid side faces) that the slab GeometryKind (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/slab.rs) uses when any edge, of the outline or of a hole, is not vertical. IFCX: optional `edgeAngles` (per outline edge) and `holeEdgeAngles` in archicraft::slab, written by the slab KindCodec (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/slab.rs) only when an edge is not vertical and read with 90° defaults, through a reusable outline helper in alpha/kinds/common.rs (rings plus an optional parallel per-edge array) that roofs reuses for its edge data; FORMAT_VERSION raised with a no-op step in MIGRATIONS (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs of element-kind-framework-12), deliberately against that module's 'optional additions need no bump' rule because an older reader would silently draw vertical edges; the exception is documented in alpha/mod.rs. App: an 'Edge angle…' entry in the slab edge palette with an angle field and a 'whole ring' option; the hover label of an edge shows its angle. Out of scope: inclined slab tops (SLB-006), roof edge parameters (roofs uses the same mechanism with its own EdgeData).
design: The angle is measured through the material between the reference face and the side face: 90° vertical; below 90° the opposite face is smaller on that edge (offset inward by t / tan(angle)); above 90° it is larger. Offsets apply to the face opposite the reference face (SlabReference, element.rs:146-174), so the drawn outline stays where it was drawn. Both rings have the same vertex count by construction (offset_ring keeps one vertex per input vertex); if a mitre collapses an edge, validation rejects the slab. Caps are triangulated separately with triangulate.rs; side quads are planar because top and bottom edges are parallel lines in one inclined plane. Plan: projected outlines use up_facing_outline, so a top-referenced slab draws its drawn outline. The IFCX arrays align with the vertex order (edge i starts at vertex i); coordinate the FORMAT_VERSION bump with any other bump of the same release and reuse it if one already happened. Pointers: extrude.rs:18-58; geometry kinds/slab.rs (evaluate.rs:177-186 in the increment-0 code); ifcx alpha/kinds/slab.rs and alpha/kinds/common.rs (schema.rs:247-256, writer.rs:205-215, reader.rs:685-712 in the increment-0 code); alpha/migrate.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: default edges are 90°; SetEdgeAngle 60° on one edge executes and undoes; 5° and 175° are rejected; InsertNode on an inclined edge gives both halves the angle (EdgeData::split); a union keeps the angles of untouched edges.
- Geometry tests: a 4 x 4 x 0.2 m slab (top reference) with one edge at 45° has its bottom ring offset 0.2 m inward on that edge; the mesh is closed and outward-oriented (check_closed); its volume is 3.2 - 0.5 x 0.2 x 0.2 x 4 = 3.12 m³; angles too flat for the thickness, which collapse the opposite ring, are rejected with 'The edge angles are too flat for this thickness.'; all-vertical slabs give byte-identical meshes as before.
- Hole edges: a stair-hole edge at 60° offsets the opposite-face hole ring by 0.2 / tan(60°) on that edge, the mesh stays closed, and the angle round-trips through holeEdgeAngles.
- IFCX: angles round-trip exactly; golden files change only in formatVersion (the samples have vertical edges) after one reviewed re-bless; a file of the previous format version opens with every edge vertical (migration test); conformance/run.sh is green, including a file with an inclined edge.
- kittest: edge palette 'Edge angle…', type 60 Enter: that edge's angle is 60°; with 'whole ring' every edge of that ring is 60°; the hover label of the edge shows 60.00°.
- Then satisfied: SLB-005.
notes:
SRS: SLB-005
Open question: valid range (chosen 10° to 170°) and whether the UI should also offer 'angle from vertical'; one convention is stored.

title: Node/edge edit palette, offsets, polygon editing, contour detection and validation
description:
Direct manipulation of element geometry: a contextual palette on nodes and edges, stretching with numeric input, offset edge/all edges and offset copy, chamfer, polygon union and difference, wall face and endpoint dragging, slab holes, edge angles and elevation dragging, with polygon validation and tolerance repair on every edit; plus contour detection (INP-018): with a creation tool active a key switches to detection, and clicking previews and creates an element of the active kind from the clicked edge, a chain of connected edges or the smallest closed region of the plan segments (walls, slabs and, once they exist, 2D lines). Fillet (EDT-014) waits for the arc edge type in curved-geometry.

Risks: Handle hit-testing and palette ergonomics; the NFR-USE-002 rule (same commands for every polygon-based kind) is met by building everything on the one Outline type. Contour detection on near-coincident segments is numerically fragile: it uses MODEL_TOLERANCE and is covered by F-style fixtures.
design: archicraft-model: one Outline type shared by slabs, roofs and 2D geometry with operations in validate.rs on geo (union/difference via i_overlay, buffer for offsets); Command::Reshape{target: PartRef, op} addressing node and edge indices through the PartRef of selection-transforms. archicraft-geometry: contour.rs builds the planar graph of the storey's plan segments with geo and finds minimal cycles and edge chains (reused by spaces and roof pivot polygons). archicraft-app: tools/reshape.rs on the point-input service, the palette as an egui popup anchored at the part, the detection key in the tool state machine. Arc edges are prepared in Outline and implemented in curved-geometry.
acceptance_criteria: kittest: clicking a selected slab node opens the palette with move/insert/delete, an edge with offset/offset-all/curve/straighten (curve is a stub until curved-geometry); Command::Reshape tests for every palette command with undo; dragging a wall face changes the thickness while the reference line stays (WAL-004 invariant); union and difference with a drawn polygon; a hole traced by contour detection from four interior walls of two_storey_shell subtracts exactly their enclosed region and a slab is created from the smallest closed region inside the exterior ring; validation tests: duplicate vertices removed, self-intersections rejected with a message, edges under 0.1 mm repaired or listed in the problems panel; offset copy of a joined wall chain stays joined.
notes: SRS: EDT-008 EDT-009 EDT-010 EDT-023 EDT-015 EDT-018 EDT-019 WAL-033 SLB-003 SLB-005 SLB-008 INP-018

title: Make repair thresholds project settings and repair outlines on every edit
description:
WHY — EDT-018 (M): polygons and profiles shall be validated on creation and on every edit; duplicate consecutive vertices and zero-length edges are removed automatically; polygons with fewer than three distinct vertices or zero area, self-intersecting outlines and zero-thickness skins are rejected or repaired with a message; any remaining invalid element is listed in the problems panel (UI-012). EDT-019 (M): the model tolerance (NFR-ACC-003) governs merging nearly coincident vertices; edges shorter than 0.1 mm and sliver angles below 0.1° that result from editing are repaired automatically or listed in the problems panel, and both thresholds are project settings (Appendix D.1). Both gap rows are partial. What exists and is extended, not rewritten: clean_ring removes duplicate and zero-length edges (validate.rs:38-51), validate_ring rejects fewer than three points, zero area, slivers and self-intersections with messages (validate.rs:115-152), validate_slab_polygon checks holes (validate.rs:163-181), validate_element runs on creation and on every edit (command.rs:330 and 387-388; after element-kind-framework-02 through the Kind::validate hook) and merging uses MODEL_TOLERANCE (tolerance.rs of element-kind-framework-01). What is missing: MIN_EDGE_LENGTH and MIN_CORNER_ANGLE_DEG are compile-time constants (validate.rs:11-14), ProjectSettings (project.rs:45-52) has no field for them, slivers are rejected instead of repaired (validate.rs:130-139) and repairs are silent. Every reshape command of this epic (tasks 03-05) runs through this gate.

WHAT — Model: `ProjectSettings.repair: RepairThresholds { min_edge_length: 1e-4, min_corner_angle_deg: 0.1 }` (#[serde(default)]; the Appendix D.1 values live in RepairThresholds::default, so template.rs default_metric_project inherits them through ProjectSettings::default) with range checks in Command::SetSettings (command.rs:260; edge length from MODEL_TOLERANCE to 10 mm, angle 0.01° to 5°). Turn clean_ring and validate_ring into the repair pipeline `validate::repair_outline(&Outline<E>, &RepairThresholds) -> Result<(Outline<E>, Vec<Repair>), String>`, called by the slab Kind::validate (kinds/slab.rs) for every ring: merge vertices within MODEL_TOLERANCE, drop edges shorter than the threshold (EdgeData::merge keeps per-edge data), remove sliver spikes while the ring stays simple, normalise orientation, and reject fewer than three vertices, zero area, self-intersection (the message names the ring and the approximate location) and hole violations with the existing messages; validate_ring stays as a thin wrapper for its current callers. Notes: generalise the TransformNote channel of selection-transforms-02/03 into `CommandNote::{Transform(TransformNote), Repair(Repair)}`; `Command::plan` delegates to `plan_with_notes(&Project, &mut Vec<CommandNote>)`, Command::preview_notes keeps its signature (it filters the Transform notes), and `History::execute` (command.rs:798-815) keeps the notes in the Transaction and exposes `last_notes()`. Out of scope: IFCX persistence, the settings dialog and the problems-panel entries (task 13); the zero-thickness-skin clause (layer-structures rejects zero-thickness skins with a message in its structure validation); profile polygons (profiles-columns-beams calls repair_outline; the done task checks this and files a bead otherwise); MODEL_TOLERANCE itself (fixed at 0.01 mm by NFR-ACC-003); new reshape commands.
design: Repair order: (1) coordinate check, (2) merge within MODEL_TOLERANCE using coincident()/quantise() of tolerance.rs, (3) short-edge removal against the threshold, collapsing onto the earlier vertex so indices of the remaining nodes stay stable and recording the removed index (the app retargets part selections with it), (4) iterative sliver removal while a corner is below the threshold and the ring stays simple, (5) orientation, (6) rejection checks. A self-intersection is never auto-repaired: a make-valid pass would change topology silently, and EDT-018 allows reject-with-message. `Repair { element: Option<ElementId>, ring: RingIndex, kind: RepairKind::{MergedVertices(n), ShortEdges(n), Slivers(n)}, message }`. Notes are not Edits: they are neither undone nor replayed; mark the Transaction field serde-skip if the journal persists transactions. validate_element(project, element) reads project.settings.repair; callers outside commands (tool previews of tasks 07-09) pass the project's thresholds, so a preview equals what is stored. Pointers: validate.rs:9-14, 38-51, 115-188, 243-282; command.rs:260 (SetSettings), 371-395 (plan_update_elements), 750-815 (Transaction, History); project.rs:45-61; kinds/slab.rs Kind::validate (element-kind-framework-02); transform.rs TransformNote (selection-transforms-02).
acceptance_criteria:
- validate tests: duplicate consecutive vertices and a vertex 5 µm from its neighbour are merged (one Repair each); a 0.05 mm edge is removed and reported; with min_edge_length = 0.01 mm the same edge is kept; a 0.05° sliver spike is removed and reported when the ring stays valid; a bow-tie outline is rejected with 'The polygon outline intersects itself near …'; fewer than three distinct points, zero area and hole violations keep their existing messages (the existing tests at validate.rs:297-331 pass unchanged).
- commands tests: an UpdateElements whose slab outline contains a 0.05 mm edge succeeds, the stored outline lacks it, History::last_notes() names the element and the repair, undo restores the original element; SetSettings with min_edge_length below MODEL_TOLERANCE fails with CommandError::Invalid; SetSettings with min_edge_length = 0.01 mm executes and undoes.
- Regression of 'validated on creation and on every edit': AddElements, UpdateElements and Command::Transform each reject a self-intersecting slab outline with the message (one test per command path; Command::Reshape joins in task 03); crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs:82-99 passes unchanged.
- Command::preview_notes of selection-transforms-03 returns the same NotScaled notes as before; a ProjectSettings value without the repair member deserialises to the D.1 defaults (command journal and autosave compatibility).
- Then satisfied at model level: the merge, short-edge and sliver clauses of EDT-019 and the automatic-removal and reject-or-repair clauses of EDT-018 for slab outlines (persistence, dialog and problems panel in task 13).
notes:
SRS: EDT-018 EDT-019
Appendix D.1: model tolerance 0.01 mm (NFR-ACC-003, constant); edges shorter than 0.1 mm and sliver angles below 0.1° are repaired or reported. Open question: whether the model tolerance itself should become a project setting; D.1 lists it in the same row, but NFR-ACC-003 fixes it at 0.01 mm, so it stays a constant.

title: Add part handles and the contextual edit palette in plan views
description:
WHY — EDT-008 (M): clicking a node or edge of a selected element shall open a contextual edit palette with the commands for that part plus the whole-element transforms, and the palette remembers the last-used command. EDT-009 (M): nodes and edges are stretchable by dragging. WAL-033 (walls) and SLB-008 (slab outlines and holes) are the first clients; NFR-USE-002 requires the same palette for every polygon-based kind. Today the plan view selects whole elements only (views/plan.rs:498-563), PlanDrawing::pick returns elements (geometry/plan.rs:270-282) and there are no handles (gap rows EDT-008, EDT-009); selection-transforms-05, -08 and -09 add node picking, edit-mode part selection and visual node handles, but no palette, no edge or face handles and no dragging.

WHAT — crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/handles.rs (beside tools/transform.rs of selection-transforms-10) extends, rather than duplicates, the part hit test of selection-transforms-08's edit mode (Kind::part_outline and part_anchor in model coordinates, precedence node > edge > band) and the handle drawing of selection-transforms-09 (HandleStyle::{Active, Ghosted} and its handle size constant) to every selected element outside edit mode, adding the handles those tasks do not draw: edge midpoints of every ring of a slab (outline and holes) and, for walls, the two face midpoints (WallPart::Face of task 05) and the reference-line midpoint (PartRef::Edge { ring: 0, index: 0 }) beside the end nodes; hit radius = the Appendix D.1 snap radius (Preferences.snap_radius, 8 px, through the view's model-per-pixel); hover highlight in views/plan.rs. crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/palette.rs: an egui Area anchored at the clicked handle listing the full command table of that part class (node: Move node, Insert node, Delete node, Chamfer corner, Fillet corner; edge: Move edge, Insert node, Offset edge, Offset all edges, Curve edge, Straighten edge; wall end: Move endpoint) plus the whole-element transforms Move, Rotate, Mirror and Elevate, which start the TransformTool of selection-transforms-10 (tools/transform.rs) on the element; entries whose consumer arrives in a later task are listed but disabled with a tooltip naming it; Curve edge and Fillet corner are stubs that report that arc edges arrive with curved geometry; Straighten is disabled on straight edges; arrows, Enter and Esc work; the last-used command per (kind, part class) is persisted in Preferences (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs) and preselected; press-drag on a handle runs it directly. Immediate commands (Delete node) execute Command::Reshape; interactive ones start the ReshapeTool consumer (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/reshape.rs), which implements the InputConsumer trait of point-input-snapping-01 (input/consumer.rs) and is delivered here with Move node, used for slab nodes and wall endpoints alike (ReshapeOp::MoveNode). Out of scope: the other interactive commands (tasks 08 and 09 enable their entries), the edge angle entry (task 10).
design: Handles come from the model, not from PlanDrawing, so they are exact and cheap: `handles(project, selection) -> Vec<Handle { target: PartTarget, class: PartClass::{Node, Edge, WallEnd, WallFace, WallBody} (a UI classification over the PartRef addressing: WallEnd = PartRef::Node of a wall, WallFace = WallPart::Face, WallBody = the wall's PartRef::Edge { ring: 0, index: 0 }), pos: DVec2, dir: Option<DVec2> }>` built from Kind::parts and part_anchor (selection-transforms-01) plus the edge midpoints and wall faces added here. Hit precedence node > wall end > edge > face > body mirrors the node-before-edge rule of INP-009. The palette is egui::Area::new(id).order(Order::Foreground).fixed_pos(anchor + offset) with labelled buttons (kittest finds them through AccessKit); it closes on Esc, on a click elsewhere or when a command starts. State: `Workspace.reshape: ReshapeState { palette: Option<Palette>, active: Option<ReshapeTool> }`; the ReshapeTool implements the InputConsumer trait of point-input-snapping, so snapping, typed input, tracker and the Esc ladder match the creation tools (INP-001, NFR-USE-002). Preferences: `palette_last: BTreeMap<String, String>` with #[serde(default)] (persistence/prefs.rs, sanitized()). After a command, retarget the part selection with the follow-up PartRef from the model. Pitfalls: handle hit-testing must run before element picking so a click on a node of a selected slab does not reselect; the palette must not keep keyboard focus once a command runs (INP-003 typing goes to the active field). Pointers: views/plan.rs:446-563 (hover, click, area selection), 321-356 (marker glyphs); views/camera.rs:31-41; app.rs:463-490 (shortcut suppression while typing).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/reshape_ui.rs (pointer events injected at Camera2d::to_screen of the part): with a slab selected, clicking a node opens a palette listing 'Move node', 'Insert node', 'Delete node', 'Chamfer corner' and 'Fillet corner'; clicking an edge midpoint lists 'Move edge', 'Insert node', 'Offset edge', 'Offset all edges', 'Curve edge' and 'Straighten edge'; both list 'Move', 'Rotate', 'Mirror' and 'Elevate'; 'Insert node', 'Chamfer corner', 'Move edge', 'Offset edge' and 'Offset all edges' are present and disabled until task 08.
- A node of the stair hole of the upper slab of two_storey_shell opens the same node palette as an outline node (holes editable like the outline, SLB-003).
- 'Delete node' on a five-node slab leaves four nodes; Edit > Undo restores five; reopening the node palette preselects 'Delete node', also in a new harness built with the saved preferences.
- 'Curve edge' and 'Fillet corner' put the curved-geometry message in the status line and change nothing; 'Straighten edge' is disabled on a straight edge; 'Move' starts the Move transform of selection-transforms-10 with the element selected.
- Move node: dragging the node at (12, 9) towards +x and typing 0.5 Enter puts it at (12.5, 9); one undo step. Move endpoint: on a free-standing wall from (0, 0) to (4, 0), dragging its end towards +x and typing 0.5 Enter puts the end at (4.5, 0).
- Unselected elements show no handles; a handle of a locked element is drawn ghosted (HandleStyle::Ghosted) and shows the lock reason instead of a palette; clicking a wall endpoint offers 'Move endpoint'.
- Then satisfied: the palette clauses of EDT-008 (fillet and curve as stubs until curved-geometry-10 and -11) and the drag start of EDT-009.
notes:
SRS: EDT-008 EDT-009 WAL-033 SLB-008
Appendix D.1: snapping radius 8 px, reused as handle hit radius. The reference product calls this the Pet Palette (SRS terminology table). Open question: palette anchored beside the part (chosen) or at the cursor.

title: Add the generic Outline type and move slab rings onto it
description:
WHY — Every polygon-editing requirement of this epic works on element outlines: EDT-008 (node and edge commands on a selected element), EDT-015 (union and difference of the outlines of polygon-based elements), SLB-003 (holes editable like the outline), SLB-005 (an angle per slab edge) and SLB-008 (slab outlines and holes editable with the polygon editing commands). NFR-USE-002 demands the same edit commands for nodes, edges and polygons in every element tool, so the operations must be written once against one outline type instead of per kind. Today a slab stores `outline: Vec<DVec2>` and `holes: Vec<Vec<DVec2>>` (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:176-188 in the increment-0 code, kinds/slab.rs after element-kind-framework), straight edges only and no per-edge data, and ring helpers are duplicated across crates (signed_area in validate.rs:26, extrude.rs:9, slice.rs:123 and tools.rs:328; point_in_ring in validate.rs:91, slice.rs:128, triangulate.rs:24 and plan.rs:172; technical-debt list).

WHAT — Add the module crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/mod.rs (tasks 03 and 04 add outline/edit.rs and outline/boolean.rs) with `Outline<E>`, `Ring<E>`, `Vertex<E>`, `Edge<E>` (`EdgeShape::Line` only, `#[non_exhaustive]` so curved-geometry can add the arc edge) and the `EdgeData` trait (implemented for `()`); ring queries (signed_area, area with holes, contains, node(i), edge(i) with wrap-around, segment iteration, bounding box, orientation normalisation); conversions to and from geo::Polygon<f64>; `RingIndex` addressing (0 = outer ring, 1.. = holes). Add geo (workspace version, default features off) to crates/archicraft-model/Cargo.toml. Change `Slab` to `outline: Outline` (edge data `()`; task 10 switches it to `Outline<SlabEdge>`) and update every caller: validate.rs (validate_slab_polygon works on the rings, same messages), project.rs new_slab (keeps its ring-based signature and converts), the slab Kind hooks in crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/slab.rs — validate (element-kind-framework-02), transform (selection-transforms-02; Mirror keeps reversing every ring with its documented node-index mapping) and parts/part_anchor/part_outline (selection-transforms-01, whose PartRef::Node/Edge { ring: u16, index: u32 } already address ring 0 = exterior and 1.. = holes, so RingIndex is u16 and node indices u32 to match) — samples.rs, the slab GeometryKind in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/slab.rs (element-kind-framework-07; evaluate.rs:177-186 in the increment-0 code; extrude from the rings), the slab KindCodec in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/slab.rs (element-kind-framework-06; alpha/writer.rs:205-215 and reader.rs:685-712 in the increment-0 code; the file format stays outline/holes arrays), crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:558-561 (area via Outline::area instead of validate::signed_area) and the slab tool completion in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/slab.rs (views/tools.rs:478-535 before point-input-snapping-01 moved it). SLB-003 is partial: keep and regress the hole support that exists — holes in the model (element.rs:181-182), hole validation (validate.rs:164-182), extrusion with holes (extrude.rs:18-58), plan slicing of holes (slice.rs:149-170), the IFCX holes array and the area deduction; only their storage type changes. Retire the model's duplicated signed_area/point_in_ring in favour of the Ring methods. Out of scope: editing operations (tasks 03-05), validation and repair changes (task 02), per-edge attributes (task 10), arc edges (curved-geometry), the geometry and app copies of the ring helpers (their own epics).
design: `pub struct Outline<E = ()> { pub rings: Vec<Ring<E>> }` with rings[0] the outer ring (CCW) and rings[1..] holes (CW): one Vec addressed by RingIndex gives a single code path for the outline and its holes (SLB-003 'editable like the outline') and a natural PartRef address (ring, index). `pub struct Ring<E> { pub vertices: Vec<Vertex<E>> }` and `pub struct Vertex<E> { pub point: DVec2, pub next: Edge<E> }`: edge i runs from vertex i to vertex i+1 (mod n), so inserting or deleting a node keeps points and per-edge data in step (no parallel arrays). `pub struct Edge<E> { pub shape: EdgeShape, pub data: E }`. `pub trait EdgeData: Clone + Default + PartialEq + Debug + Serialize + DeserializeOwned { fn split(&self) -> (Self, Self) { (self.clone(), self.clone()) } fn merge(first: &Self, _second: &Self) -> Self { first.clone() } }`. Slab keeps its serde derives (the command journal serialises elements). geo conversions add the closing point and never round, so golden files stay identical; MultiPolygon handling belongs to task 04. Check that geo's BooleanOps and Buffer compile with default-features = false (workspace Cargo.toml:47); if i_overlay multithreading is wanted later, enable it at the workspace level. Pitfalls: plan_update_elements detects 'no change' by Element equality (command.rs:372-395), so Outline must derive PartialEq; the reader path must normalise orientation exactly as validate_slab_polygon does today; keep archicraft-model free of UI dependencies (NFR-MNT-002). After element-kind-framework, edit kinds/slab.rs and the registered slab codec rather than the increment-0 match arms.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo test --workspace`, clippy and fmt are green; the golden files crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx are byte-identical (no re-bless) and round_trip_restores_the_editable_model passes.
- Unit tests in outline/mod.rs: from_rings normalises the outer ring counter-clockwise and holes clockwise; the 12 x 9 m outline with the 3 x 1.2 m stair hole of two_storey_shell has area 104.4 m²; contains() is true inside the outline, false inside the hole; node/edge indexing wraps; to_geo/from_geo round-trips bit-exactly; the serde JSON round trip of Outline<()> is lossless.
- A second instantiation `Outline<TestEdge { tag: u32 }>` (tests only) passes the same query tests, proving the operations are generic over edge data (NFR-USE-002 groundwork).
- Existing validate.rs tests, crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs, the tools.rs slab tests and the kittest suite pass unchanged.
- Hole regression on Outline (SLB-003 'any number of holes'): a slab with two holes validates, extrudes to a closed, outward-oriented mesh (check_closed), slices into a plan cut showing both holes, shows the area minus both holes in the properties strip and round-trips through IFCX with assert_eq.
- Kind hooks: mirroring the upper slab of two_storey_shell through Command::Transform (selection-transforms-03) keeps a counter-clockwise outer ring and a clockwise hole; Kind::parts lists the nodes and edges of ring 0 and ring 1 in the documented order and part_anchor(PartRef::Node { ring: 1, index: 0 }) is a stair-hole corner.
- No SRS clause closes by itself; this prepares EDT-008, EDT-015, SLB-003, SLB-005 and SLB-008.
notes:
SRS: SLB-003 SLB-005 SLB-008 EDT-008 EDT-015
(preparation only; no ID completes here). Open question: one rings Vec with RingIndex 0 = outer (chosen) versus separate outer/holes fields.

title: Register geometry generators per kind and evaluate compound part bodies
description:
WHY: The geometry crate dispatches on a closed match: local_extent and evaluate_element (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:123-188) know walls and slabs only and carry task 02's temporary UnsupportedKind wildcard arm, and ElementGeometry { parts, axis } (evaluate.rs:32-50) has no place for the bodies of compound parts. IFX-016 (M, status missing) needs part bodies per role so the writer (task 07) can emit Part_n child nodes; every later kind (columns, beams, roofs, stairs, terrain) needs one place to register its generator; incremental evaluation (task 10) and the fallback representation (task 13) need one generic evaluation path. VIEW-001 (M, partial): all views derive from the single evaluated model, so part bodies must be drawn and picked like element bodies, while today plan.rs:111-150 and crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-176 only read ElementGeometry.parts.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/{mod.rs,wall.rs,slab.rs,dummy.rs} with a GeometryKind trait implemented for the model payloads (local_extent(&EvalContext) -> Result<(f64, f64), GeometryError>, evaluate(&EvalContext) -> Result<ElementGeometry, GeometryError>) and a one-line-per-kind table; evaluate_element and local_extent in evaluate.rs dispatch through it and the wildcard arm disappears. EvalContext carries the project, the element and the junction footprint (walls only today; a neighbour-data slot later). The crate gets its own test-kinds feature forwarding archicraft-model/test-kinds, enabled for its tests through a self dev-dependency. ElementGeometry gains children: Vec<PartGeometry { role, parts: Vec<BodyPart>, axis }> whose roles equal the model's Kind::parts() (PartSpec of task 02, so the class stays a model decision); bounds() and volume() include children. The model's kinds/dummy.rs parts() returns Part_1 (IfcMember) and Part_2 (IfcPlate) when parts = true (classes from task 05); the geometry dummy extrudes a box from origin, size and its VerticalLink extent, adds one box per part and panics when panic_on_evaluate is set (consumed by task 13). plan.rs classifies children's bodies like the element's own body under the element id; render3d.rs build_scene includes children's triangles and feature edges; crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs pick returns the element id when a part is hit. Extend the module-layout test to crates/archicraft-geometry/src. Out of scope: writing parts to IFCX (task 07), incremental evaluation (task 10), fallback boxes (task 13), Skin_n bodies (layer-structures), part selection (selection-transforms).
design: A separate registry in the geometry crate because the model must not depend on geometry (NFR-MNT-002/004): the model declares which parts exist and their classes, the geometry crate generates their bodies, the writer joins both by role. Part roles are stable per kind (Part_n in a stable order, later Flight_n, Landing_n, Frame_n) so their v5 ids survive edits. Keep catch_unwind per element in evaluate.rs around the registry call. Pitfalls: with test-kinds unified into workspace test builds the geometry table contains the dummy, so nothing outside kinds/ may iterate the table to produce output that reaches goldens; keep wall footprints (wall.rs) outside the trait, passed in through EvalContext, so task 10 can make them incremental. Pointers: evaluate.rs:22-60/123-188, plan.rs:111-150, render3d.rs:102-176, view3d.rs:59-100, wall.rs:203-248.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry registry tests: every KindTag has a generator and no generator lacks a kind; for every registered kind the roles of ElementGeometry.children equal the roles of Kind::parts(); evaluate.rs contains no ElementKind::Wall/Slab arm (source scan).
- Module-layout test green for crates/archicraft-geometry/src: Dummy and "dummy" occur only in kinds/dummy.rs and one line of kinds/mod.rs.
- A compound dummy (parts = true) evaluates to a closed body plus two closed part bodies (check_closed); ElementGeometry::bounds and volume include the parts; a dummy with parts = false has no children.
- plan_drawing classifies a compound dummy's part bodies like its own body and PlanDrawing::pick returns the element id when a part is hit; build_scene includes part vertices and edges; view3d::pick returns the element id for a ray through a part (unit tests in plan.rs, render3d.rs and view3d.rs).
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs, all geometry unit tests, the round-trip tests and the goldens are unchanged; cargo clippy and fmt green.
- IFX-016 part geometry is available to the writer (task 07); VIEW-001 plan and 3D views show part bodies from the one evaluated model.
notes: SRS: IFX-016 VIEW-001. Also NFR-MNT-002/004 (headless crates). Split out of task 07. Consumers: task 07 (part nodes), task 10 (evaluate_incremental through the registry), task 13 (fallback beside the generator) and every later kind's generator.

title: Generate window geometry including multi-sash grids
description:
WHY: DW-011 (M) requires fixed, side-hung, tilt-and-turn, top-hung and horizontal sliding windows, multi-sash windows with configurable columns and rows where each sash has its own opening type, and transoms or sidelights as parameters. DW-012 (M) requires the number and division of sashes, sash thickness, glazing build-up and sill boards inside and outside with depth to shape the parts. OBJ-002 (M) asks for parametric geometry and IFX-051 (S) for natively mirrored geometry. This is the widest part of the epic (risk: DW-011 breadth), so every window type is expressed as a configuration of one cell generator.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/windows.rs on the kit and layout of task 04: UnitLayout splits the frame's clear area into optional transom and sidelight cells and a main grid of columns x rows from the weights; each cell gets either a fixed glazing pane in the frame or a sash ring with its pane (side-hung, tilt-and-turn, top-hung); mullions and transom bars belong to the single Frame extrusion (one hole per cell); horizontal sliding windows place 2-4 panels on two y tracks; sills inside and outside; glazing centred in the sash depth. Per-cell handing comes from sash_types and global mirroring reflects x, reverses winding and swaps left/right handing. Simplified detail: frame ring with cells and one pane per cell, no sash rings. Per-cell clear edges as key points and clear sizes as derived values (OBJ-014). Out of scope: plan symbols (06), corner windows (DW-016), curved units (DW-020), roof windows (DW-021).
design: One generic cell generator: fixed, side-hung, tilt-and-turn and top-hung windows are one-cell grids, multi-sash is the general case, sliding is a two-track variant; this keeps the breadth risk to one code path with table-driven tests. Point budget: a 6 x 4 grid is 24 cells with three parts each, far below IFX-038's 65,535 points. Pitfalls: sash rings of neighbouring cells are separated by the mullion width so shells never touch; reject frame and sash widths that leave no glass in layout (GeometryError with the parameter name) rather than producing self-intersecting rings; keep pane thickness from glazing_thickness and never thicker than the sash.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/catalogue.rs extended: every window definition at default parameters, both detail levels, mirrored false and true, yields closed, positive-volume parts with at most 65,535 points; Frame and Glazing always exist, Sash for operable sashes, Sill when enabled (DW-011, IFX-032).
- A 3 x 2 multi-sash grid with sash_types [fixed, tilt-turn-left, tilt-turn-right, top-hung, fixed, side-hung-left] yields six panes, four sash rings in the expected cells (cell bounds checked) and a Frame with six holes; column weights [1, 2, 1] give widths in ratio 1:2:1 within 1e-9 (DW-011 'each sash with its own opening type', DW-012 division).
- Inconsistent input that bypassed validation (sash_types shorter than columns x rows) returns a GeometryError instead of panicking.
- Transom on adds one cell above the grid at transom_height; sidelight both adds a left and a right cell; a three-panel horizontal sliding window yields three sash rings on two tracks with no touching shells inside the Sash part.
- sash_thickness sets the Sash part's y-extent and glazing_thickness the panes' y-extent (never thicker than the sash); the sash and glazing material parameters set the materials of the Sash and Glazing parts (DW-012 sash thickness, glazing build-up, material per part).
- A mirrored tilt-turn-left window reports tilt-turn-right handing in its layout and its parts equal the reflection (IFX-051); the Appendix D.2 default window (tilt-and-turn, 1.20 x 1.40 m) generates and reports its clear size.
notes: SRS: DW-011 DW-012 OBJ-002 IFX-051.

title: Drive the inspector from the parameter schema and show handedness
description:
WHY: DW-012 (M): the inspector shall be driven by each type's parameter schema. DW-017 (S): handedness is reported in the inspector according to a selectable convention, DIN 107 by default (Appendix D.6). OBJ-014 (S) derived values and OBJ-002 (M) parameter grouping should be visible to the user. Gap DW-012: 'the inspector is hard-coded per ElementKind (properties.rs:253-264 geometry_fields), not schema-driven ... and an inspector generator reading the schema'.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/parameters.rs: parameter_fields(ui, fields, schema, values) -> changed InstanceParameters, one collapsible section per ParamGroup in schema order: Length via widgets::length with the range, Angle via widgets::angle, Count via a clamped DragValue, Bool as a checkbox, Choice as a combo with labels, Material as a combo over project.materials, LengthList and ChoiceList as rows sized by their governing count (the multi-sash sash_types as a columns x rows grid of combos); parameters with a binding are hidden when the carrier owns them (doors-windows-core) and shown for free carriers. ui/properties.rs edit_fields (properties.rs:684) shows them when all selected elements expose component() with the same resolved definition and executes SetInstanceParameters per edit; mixed definitions show 'Parameters differ: select instances of one definition'; placeholders show the cached parameters read-only with 'Definition missing - relink to edit'. Read-only rows in derived (properties.rs:542): definition name, version and category, the handedness label via handedness(project.settings.handedness, Handing::from_instance) with a Mirror toggle executing SetInstanceMirrored, and derived values from the type layout (nominal and clear width and height, OBJ-014). ui/dialogs.rs project_window (dialogs.rs:479): a 'Door and window handedness' choice over HandednessConvention::ALL applied with SetSettings on OK. If properties-and-dialogs' FieldSpec framework has landed, render the same fields through it. Out of scope: door and window placement fields and tool defaults (doors-windows-core-08), DW-015 key-point snapping and sill/head rows (library-dw-exchange, doors-windows-core).
design: Extend the Fields pattern of properties.rs (a getter returning None hides the field) with a dynamic list built from the schema; compare ParamValue per key so only changed keys are sent (one command per edit, UND-002); format through units.rs. Pitfalls: a count change that resizes a list must send the resized list in the same command (fill new entries with the default) or validation rejects it; egui ids must be unique per parameter key and element; do not copy the thickness/3.0 default debt of properties.rs:295. Pointers: properties.rs:140-220 (Fields), :542 (derived), :684 (edit_fields), widgets.rs:63-131, dialogs.rs:479-627.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest (test-kinds): selecting a TestInstance of window.multi-sash shows the sections Size, Frame, Sash, Glazing, Sill, Transom/Sidelight and Materials with the schema labels; changing Columns from 2 to 3 and the new cell's sash type executes SetInstanceParameters and the geometry re-evaluates in the same frame; an out-of-range frame width shows the validation message and changes nothing (DW-012).
- A headless loop renders the schema of every catalogue definition (all twelve) with default values without panic.
- Choosing Aluminium as the frame material changes the Frame part's material in the evaluated geometry (DW-012 material per part).
- The default hinged door with swing interior shows the DIN 107 label from the D.6 table; switching the convention to US in the Project dialog shows the US label; the Mirror toggle flips the label and undo restores it (DW-017 inspector).
- Selecting a placeholder shows its parameters read-only with the relink hint; the derived rows show the default door's clear width equal to the layout value (OBJ-014).
notes: SRS: DW-012 DW-017 OBJ-014 OBJ-002.

title: Component definitions and the door/window catalogue
description:
Build the component-definition resource (ID, version, category, parameter schema, parametric 3D geometry and plan symbol, detail levels, key points), its storage in the project file, placeholders for missing definitions and shared type geometry in IFCX, then the built-in door, window and empty-opening catalogue with the DW-012 parameter set, generated plan symbols and handedness conventions.

Risks: DW-011 breadth (multi-sash grids, sidelights, transoms); generators share one kit and keep part geometry to boxes in v1.
design: archicraft-model components.rs (Definition, ParameterSchema, instance parameters) with the built-in catalogue as Rust generators (no scripting, O-12); archicraft-geometry part generators per door and window family sharing one frame/leaf kit; archicraft-ifcx type nodes plus occurrence inherits and archicraft::component; archicraft-app catalogue basics (the full browser is in library-dw-exchange).
acceptance_criteria: Catalogue tests instantiate every DW-011 type with default parameters into closed part meshes (frame, leaf or sash, glazing, sill) and generated plan symbols at two detail levels; a project with a missing definition opens with labelled placeholders and a relink list; identical instances share one type node and mesh in IFCX and mirrored ones a separate type (conformance); DIN 107 handedness label test; definitions embedded in archicraft::project so the project opens on any machine.
notes: SRS: OBJ-002 OBJ-004 OBJ-005 OBJ-006 OBJ-011 OBJ-014 IFX-037 IFX-050 IFX-051 DW-011 DW-012 DW-013 DW-017 DW-022 DSP-015

title: Add tool groups, the view-control bar and the project-name title
description:
WHY: UI-001 (M) requires a main window with a menu bar; a tool palette grouped into selection, modelling, 2D/annotation and view tools; a properties panel; a project browser; a tab bar for open views; a view-control bar (zoom, fit, view rotation, drawing scale, active display settings and the restriction indicator of VIEW-043); and a status line with the prompt for the next input step. Existing and kept: the menu bar (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:32-118), the toolbox with Selection, Modelling and View tools headers (shell.rs:120-162), the properties strip (ui/properties.rs, top panel in app.rs), the project browser (ui/browser.rs, right panel), the egui_tiles tab bar and the status-line prompt (shell.rs:170); tests/ui.rs main_window_has_the_parts_of_ui_001 checks them. Missing: there is no 2D/annotation group, and the view controls sit inside the status bar (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:167-254) without view rotation, with a hard-coded 'Scale 1:100' label (shell.rs:241), a 'pt/m' readout and no plan display settings. PRJ-003 (M) requires the window title to show the project name and an unsaved-changes indicator; today it shows the file name once the project is saved (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:125-131), so renaming the project in Project settings does not change it; the title is built in ArchiCraftApp::update_title_and_theme (app.rs:517-526). The other PRJ-003 clauses (New, Open, Save, Save As, Close, Recent projects, Quit, the first-save dialog, the dirty indicator and the Save / Don't save / Cancel prompt, app.rs:189-244 and 548-581) exist and are kept.

WHAT: The toolbox is generated from registry tool commands grouped by ToolGroup {Selection, Modelling, Annotation2d, View}; a group renders once it has a tool (drafting-trim-split fills Annotation2d). New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/view_bar.rs: a view-control bar strip with ordered slots Zoom (view.zoom-in, view.zoom-out and a zoom readout in percent), Fit, Rotation, Scale, Display settings and Restrictions, filled by a ViewBarProvider per pane type: the plan provider fills zoom, fit and display settings (reference lines), the 3D provider zoom, fit, display mode, presets and projection (commands of task 13); Rotation, Scale and Restrictions stay empty until plan-views-browser-12, plan-renderer-01 and 3d-view-restrictions provide them; the hard-coded scale label and the pt/m readout go. The status line keeps the prompt, the last message and the problem count. A pure window_title(&Document) builds the title from project.info.name and the dirty marker through a catalogue key; the unsaved-changes prompt names both the project and the file. Out of scope: the content of the rotation, scale and restriction slots, panel docking (UI-004, plan-views-browser-14).
design: Zoom readout: in plans, 100 % means paper size on screen at the drawing scale (camera.scale in points per metre against the pixels-per-point; document the formula next to the code); in 3D, the camera distance relative to the fitted distance. Zoom keys Primary+= and Primary+- collide with egui's built-in keyboard zoom of the UI scale: set egui Options zoom_with_keyboard = false and leave UI scaling (NFR-PORT-005) to a preference. The ViewBarProvider trait returns Option<slot content> per slot, so later epics fill a slot without touching view_bar.rs. Pointers: shell.rs:120-162 (toolbox), shell.rs:167-254 (status bar), app.rs:517-526 (title), document.rs:123-131 (display_name).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit: window_title for clean and dirty, saved and unsaved documents; after Command::SetInfo renames a project saved as other.ifcx, the title shows the new project name with the dirty marker.
- kittest: the toolbox shows the Selection, Modelling and View tools headers with their tools; a test registry with a stub Annotation2d tool shows the 2D and annotation header in third position.
- kittest: the view-control bar of a plan pane and of a 3D pane shows Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit and the zoom readout; the 3D bar shows the display-mode and projection controls; a test provider filling Rotation, Scale and Restrictions renders them in slot order; 'Scale 1:100' is gone.
- The status line still shows the tool prompt (last item of UI-001).
- Regression (UI-001): main_window_has_the_parts_of_ui_001 is extended to find the menu bar, the toolbox, the properties strip, the project browser, the tab bar, the view-control bar and the status line.
- Regression (PRJ-003): the dirty-tracking tests in document.rs keep passing; kittest: closing a dirty project shows the prompt with Save, Don't save and Cancel naming the project, and Cancel keeps the project open and dirty.
- Satisfied: UI-001 except the slot contents owned by plan-views-browser (rotation), plan-renderer (drawing scale), 3d-view-restrictions (indicator) and drafting-trim-split (2D tools); the title clause of PRJ-003.
notes: SRS: UI-001 PRJ-003

title: Draw plan symbols, placeholders and per-view detail levels
description:
WHY: DW-013 (M) symbols must be visible in plan and mask the host's cut fill; DSP-015 (S) the detail level is chosen per view and overridable per element; OBJ-005 (M) placeholders must be clearly visible, labelled, selectable and deletable; DW-017 (S) handedness appears in plan labels; OBJ-011 (S) instances are drawn from shared type geometry. The plan painter knows only cut fills, projected and overhead lines and reference lines today (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:237-320), and render3d builds scenes from ElementGeometry.parts (render3d.rs:102).

WHAT: views/plan.rs draw_plan: after the cut fills draw Mask primitives in the canvas background colour, then Polygon, Line, Arc and Arrow primitives with Palette colours and the existing line weights per LineStyle (Overhead dashed like overhead lines; arcs tessellated at screen resolution), and HandednessLabel text from handedness(project.settings.handedness, handing) at a fixed screen size; placeholders are drawn with a dashed outline in the fallback colour of element-kind-framework's problems work and the label 'Missing: <name>' centred in the box; selection and hover include symbols and placeholders. PlanViewState (plan.rs:22) gains detail: DetailLevel (default Detailed), switchable from the plan context menu (plan.rs:728) and a View menu item for the active plan pane; Document::plan (document.rs:106) caches by storey and detail and passes PlanOptions. ui/properties.rs: a 'Plan detail' choice (View default / Simplified / Detailed) for selections whose elements expose component(), executing SetDetailOverride. views/render3d.rs build_scene and views/view3d.rs pick iterate world_parts so instances render and pick in 3D, with placeholders edge-only in the warning colour. Deleting placeholders uses the existing delete_selection. Out of scope: the parameter inspector (11), the missing-definitions window (12), pens and line types (plan-attributes), lyon (plan-renderer), saving the detail level in saved views (plan-views-browser stores PlanViewState fields), the 3D detail option VIEW-055 (doors-windows-core-09).
design: Extension point 'Add a plan-view overlay or line class'. Draw order: cut fills, masks, symbols, reference lines, so masks never hide later elements' lines. Labels are formatted at draw time from the Handing (task 06), so convention changes only repaint. The placeholder colour must meet the UI-010 contrast rule on both canvas backgrounds. Pitfalls: the plan cache must include the detail level or switching views shows stale symbols; kittest cannot render wgpu, so 3D checks are unit tests on build_scene and view3d::pick; reuse widgets::choice for the properties field. Pointers: plan.rs:22-32 (PlanViewState), :92-148 (Palette), :237-320 (draw_plan), :728 (context_menu), document.rs:97-121, render3d.rs:102-180, view3d.rs:75-100, properties.rs:542-684.
acceptance_criteria:
- Painter unit test: every SymbolPrimitive variant draws without panic, and in the emitted shape list every Mask shape comes after all cut-fill shapes and before every symbol line; a door TestInstance placed across a wall's cut fill emits its mask rectangle after the wall's fill, covering the overlap (DW-013 'masks the host's cut fill'; the host-thickness extent follows in doors-windows-core-04).
- kittest (test-kinds): a TestInstance of door.hinged.single adds symbol shapes to the plan; switching the plan detail in the context menu changes PlanViewState.detail and the plan cache key; the properties strip's 'Plan detail' choice executes SetDetailOverride, which undo and redo restore (DSP-015).
- kittest: a TestInstance with a missing definition shows 'Missing: <name>', is selected by a click inside its box and removed by Delete, and undo restores it (OBJ-005 visible, labelled, selectable, deletable).
- With convention Din107 the default door's label equals handedness(Din107, handing); switching the project convention to UsHand changes the label without re-evaluating geometry (DW-017 plan label).
- build_scene includes the triangles of every instance (types x instances) and view3d::pick hits an instance; existing render3d tests pass (OBJ-011 drawing side).
- The placeholder outline and label colour (Palette.fallback from element-kind-framework-13) has at least 3:1 contrast against both canvas backgrounds (OBJ-005 'clearly visible', UI-010).
notes: SRS: DW-013 DSP-015 OBJ-005 DW-017 OBJ-011. Open question: the default plan detail per view (Detailed assumed; the SRS gives none).

title: Turn ui/actions.rs into a CommandRegistry that builds the menus
description:
WHY: UI-017 (M) requires every command to be reachable from a menu or the command palette and bindable to a shortcut without first adding it to a toolbar; UI-008 (M) requires default shortcuts that use Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, avoid combinations reserved by the operating system and do not fire single-key shortcuts while a text field has focus; HW-003 (M) requires all shortcuts to work from the keyboard. Today commands are a closed Action enum of 31 variants (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs:7-73) with English labels, a constant shortcut match (114-146) and a works_while_typing list; menus are written by hand in ui/shell.rs:32-118; dispatch is a match in app.rs:377-460, and the shortcut loop (app.rs:462-495) special-cases Cmd+Y, Backspace and Ctrl+Tab. The existing tests in actions.rs:176-205 (shortcuts_are_unique and the D.8 subset check) are the regression net for the 23 current bindings and are kept. Every later epic (selection-transforms, drafting-trim-split, doors-windows-core, 3d-view-restrictions and others) adds commands and needs one registration point with label and description keys, menu placement, scope and default shortcut.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-app/src/commands/ (mod.rs with Registry and CommandSpec, binding.rs, ctx.rs, and per-area registration files file.rs, edit.rs, view.rs, tools.rs, project.rs, help.rs) replacing ui/actions.rs. CommandSpec { id: CommandId (stable dotted id such as file.save), label_key, description_key, category, menu: Option<MenuPlace { path, group, order }>, palette_only, context_only (no main-menu item, but still listed in the palette and reachable by shortcut against Target::active(), so NFR-USE-005 and NFR-A11Y-001 cover it), default_bindings: Vec<Binding>, scope: Scope (Global, TextSafe, Canvas, PointInput), enabled: fn(&CommandCtx) -> Enabled (Yes or No(reason key)), checked, dynamic_label (for 'Undo Create wall', rendered with i18n::render from the Message that History::undo_label returns since task 02), handler }. Binding { primary, ctrl, alt, shift, key } is platform-neutral: primary means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. One dispatch entry ArchiCraftApp::invoke(id, Target, Origin) with Origin {Menu, Shortcut, Palette, ContextMenu, Toolbar, Test} and an optional test recorder that captures invocations without running handlers. Migrate all 31 actions with their current default shortcuts; Cmd+Y becomes a second binding of edit.redo and Backspace a Canvas-scope second binding of edit.delete. ui/shell.rs menu_bar builds File, Edit, View, Design, Project and Help from MenuPlace (Open recent stays a custom submenu hook; reference lines and problems are checkable entries); the toolbox and status-bar buttons invoke commands by id. Labels and descriptions are catalogue keys in locales/en/commands.ftl (descriptions newly written). Update tests/ui.rs imports. Out of scope: the view-local keys R, Tab and Backspace and the D.8 table (04), the palette (05), rebinding (06), tooltips (13).
design: The registry is built once at startup from registration functions per area, so a later epic adds commands/<area>.rs instead of editing three matches. Handlers are fn(&mut ArchiCraftApp, &egui::Context, Target), where Target { storey, pane, element } defaults to the active storey and pane and lets context menus (14) pass the right-clicked item. CommandCtx is a cheap snapshot (selection empty, active pane, drawing, can_undo and can_redo, text focused, dialog selections) built once per frame. Shortcut matching converts Binding to egui::KeyboardShortcut with Modifiers::COMMAND for primary and consumes in descending modifier count, because egui's consume_shortcut matches logically and Primary+Z would otherwise swallow Primary+Shift+Z. Scope rules: Global conflicts with everything; Canvas and PointInput overlap; TextSafe bindings stay active while a text field has focus (today's works_while_typing list: file commands, settings, problems). Command ids are a public contract (keymaps and exported preferences store them). Pointers: app.rs:377-460 run(), app.rs:462-495 shortcuts(), shell.rs:16-118, actions.rs:112-170, tests/ui.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- commands/tests.rs every_command_is_complete: ids are unique, lower-case and dotted; every spec has label and description keys with non-empty English text; every spec has a menu place or is palette_only or context_only; menu paths resolve to the six top-level menus; default bindings are unique within overlapping scopes. Tasks 04, 05 and 13 extend this test.
- A pinned-id test lists every command id, so renames of these public ids are deliberate.
- With the recorder installed, each of the 23 previously bound shortcuts invokes its command when its key events are fed to the harness; Primary+Y invokes edit.redo; Backspace invokes edit.delete only while no tool is drawing.
- kittest: main_window_has_the_parts_of_ui_001 and edit_menu_undoes_and_redoes pass with the generated menus; typing W into a focused text field of the Project settings dialog leaves the Select tool active (UI-008 text-field clause).
- ui/shell.rs references no individual command except the Open recent hook (source-scan test).
- Platform test: Binding Primary+S converts to Cmd+S (Modifiers::MAC_CMD) for macOS and to Ctrl+S for Windows and Linux, and its display text follows the platform (Cmd/Ctrl clause of UI-008).
- Regression: the tests of actions.rs:176-205 (shortcuts_are_unique, the D.8 subset) move into commands/tests.rs and keep passing; single-key tool shortcuts still do not fire while a tool is drawing (app.rs:475-477).
- Satisfied: the structure of UI-017 (every command in a menu and bindable), UI-008 defaults and text-field rule for the existing commands, HW-003 for the existing shortcuts.
notes:
SRS: UI-017 UI-008 HW-003
Extension point for later epics: a new command is one CommandSpec in commands/<area>.rs plus two catalogue keys; the epic exit documents this in docs/implementation-status.md.

title: Share type geometry in memory and evaluate placeholders
description:
WHY: OBJ-011 (S): identical instances shall share one geometry definition in memory and in IFCX (IFX-050), so that thousands of instances stay interactive. OBJ-005 (M): instances whose definition cannot be resolved appear as clearly visible, labelled placeholders (bounding box and name) and remain selectable. DSP-015 (S): the plan detail level is chosen per view and overridable per element. Gap OBJ-011: 'ModelGeometry stores one ElementGeometry per element (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:51-57)'.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/types.rs: TypeKey { definition: DefinitionRef, params: canonical resolved values (lengths quantised to 1e-6 m, angles to 1e-9 rad, materials by id), mirrored, class: IfcClass } with TypeKey::uuid() = Uuid v5 of TYPE_NAMESPACE (a fixed UUID constant in types.rs, never changed once released) and the canonical string (reused as the IFCX type path in task 09); TypeGeometry { key, units per DetailLevel, symbols per DetailLevel, layout } generated lazily per detail; a TypeCache (TypeKey -> Arc<TypeGeometry>) owned by ModelGeometry, carried across element-kind-framework's incremental evaluation and pruned of unused entries. ElementGeometry gains instance: Option<InstanceGeometry { key, transform: DMat4 (unit-local to storey, asserted det > 0), shared: Arc<TypeGeometry> }> and placeholder: Option<String>; TriMesh gains transformed(&DMat4) next to translated (mesh.rs:97), asserting a positive determinant; ElementGeometry::world_parts() yields transformed parts for instances (computed on demand, no per-instance mesh stored) and borrowed parts otherwise; bounds() and volume() use it. Shared entry point components::evaluate_instance(ctx, instance, transform) for carrier kinds: resolve through Project::resolve_definition, generate through the TypeCache, or build a closed placeholder box from last_known.extent (0.5 m cube when absent) labelled 'Missing: <name>' (OBJ-005). The TestInstance generator (stub from task 01) now calls it with translation(origin) x rotZ(rotation). crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: PlanElement (plan.rs:23-34) gains symbols: Vec<SymbolPrimitive> placed in plan coordinates (the field doors-windows-core-04 later fills by the host frame instead of adding it again; a Mask { x0, x1 } becomes the rectangle x0..x1 by the layout's frame depth, which doors-windows-core-04 widens to the host thickness) and placeholder: Option<String>; plan_drawing takes PlanOptions { detail } and uses detail_override.unwrap_or(view detail) per instance (DSP-015); classification and pick() iterate world_parts, so placeholders are cut, projected and pickable like bodies. Out of scope: painting (10), IFCX (08, 09), GPU instancing (perf-tuning-rm-m-l), host placement (doors-windows-core-04).
design: Keying on resolved, quantised parameters makes identical-instance detection automatic, and the quantisation equals IFX-007's coordinate rounding so in-memory sharing and IFCX sharing agree (task 09 reuses TypeKey). The cache is the in-memory half of OBJ-011; render3d still merges buffers (task 10), and GPU instancing is noted for perf-tuning-rm-m-l. Pitfalls: framework incremental evaluation keeps Arc<ElementGeometry> per element, so the cache must survive steps and must not leak HashMap order into outputs; a panicking generator still goes through catch_unwind and the framework's fallback box (NFR-REL-006), which differs from a placeholder; 3D detail is Detailed unless doors-windows-core-09 selects schematic (VIEW-055); keep placeholder parts out of the IFCX writer (IFX-063). Pointers: evaluate.rs:20-62, plan.rs:21-60 and the classification loop at :117-160.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test (test-kinds): 1,000 identical TestInstances produce one TypeCache entry, all InstanceGeometry.shared are Arc::ptr_eq, ElementGeometry.parts is empty for every instance and a call counter shows the generator ran once per TypeKey and detail level; a mirrored instance and one with a different width add exactly two entries (OBJ-011 memory clause).
- TypeKey: widths 0.9 and 0.9000000004 m give the same key, 0.9 and 0.9001 m different keys; TypeKey::uuid() matches a golden value in the test (stable across runs and platforms).
- world_parts of a rotated instance equal the transformed type parts; bounds and volume agree; every instance transform has a positive determinant (IFX-051 guard).
- A TestInstance with an unknown definition yields placeholder Some('Missing: <name>') and a closed box of last_known.extent at its transform; plan_drawing classifies it with placeholder set and pick() at its centre returns its id (OBJ-005 visible and selectable).
- plan_drawing with Simplified and Detailed yields the matching symbol sets; an instance with detail_override Detailed shows the detailed symbol in a Simplified view (DSP-015 per view and per element).
- element-kind-framework's incremental_equals_full property test stays bit-identical with TestInstances added to the stand-in edit generator; existing geometry tests are unchanged.
- An #[ignore]d release smoke test evaluates 5,000 identical TestInstances (the RM-M element count) and prints the evaluation time and TypeCache size, so regression-and-status can track OBJ-011's 'thousands of instances stay interactive'.
notes: SRS: OBJ-011 OBJ-005 DSP-015 (also IFX-050 key, IFX-051 guard).

title: Version preferences and export and import them with the keymap
description:
WHY: SET-004 (S) requires user preferences and shortcuts to be exportable and importable as a file, for transfer to another computer, and Appendix D.9 names this import as an external-file parser that must respect the size and nesting limits and be fuzzed (NFR-SEC-003). Existing and kept: Preferences (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:27-55) is a #[serde(default)] struct that load() and save() (prefs.rs:78-97) read and write at one fixed path, sanitized() clamps invalid values (prefs.rs:99-113), and the tests round_trip_and_recent_list and invalid_values_are_clamped cover it. Missing: preferences.json has no schema version, there is no export or import command and no file dialog for it (rfd is used only for .ifcx, crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:197, 257), and there is no shortcut data until task 06 adds the keymap. The SET-001 fields (UI language, author e-mail, default units) follow in task 17 on top of this format.

WHAT: prefs.rs gains schema_version (2; files without it are version 1 and migrate on load), a PortablePreferences view and an export envelope { format: 'archicraft-preferences', schemaVersion, application, preferences, keymap }; machine-local fields (recent, last_crash_report and any window or layout state) are neither exported nor overwritten by an import. import_bytes(&[u8]) -> Result<ImportOutcome { preferences, skipped: Vec<Message> }, ImportError> checks the size (1 MiB) and the JSON nesting (fewer than 128 levels, D.9) before deserializing, rejects a newer schemaVersion or a foreign format with a message, skips and reports unknown command ids and invalid bindings, and applies sanitized(). Commands file.export-preferences and file.import-preferences (File menu, and buttons in the Preferences dialog, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:679-762) use rfd .json dialogs behind a FileChooser trait for tests; an import takes effect at once (theme, number format, keymap) and reports what was skipped. Out of scope: the SET-001 fields language, e-mail and default units (17); the cargo-fuzz target (regression-and-status-10 owns the prefs_import placeholder); dwell time (point-input-snapping-09), tracker behaviour (point-input-snapping-05) and navigation scheme (3d-input-navigation, SET-003), which add their own fields.
design: PortablePreferences is a separate serde struct converted from and into Preferences, so new machine-local fields are excluded by default; fields that task 17 and later epics add are portable unless marked machine-local. serde_json already stops at 128 nesting levels; pre-scan the bytes for depth anyway to return a clear ImportError. Keep import_bytes public and pure so regression-and-status-10 can register it as a cargo-fuzz target (D.9 requires the preference import to be fuzzed). Pitfalls: keep #[serde(default)] on every field so older files load; write the export with to_vec_pretty so users can read and diff it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round trip: export, then import into default preferences, yields equal portable fields and keymap; recent projects and last_crash_report are unchanged by the import.
- Migration: an increment-0 preferences.json fixture without schema_version loads with every value kept and is saved as version 2; round_trip_and_recent_list and invalid_values_are_clamped keep passing.
- Rejection: a newer schemaVersion, a wrong format tag, more than 1 MiB, nesting depth 200, invalid UTF-8 and truncated JSON each return a distinct ImportError; a seeded robustness test feeds 10,000 random mutations of a valid export and never panics.
- Partial import: unknown command ids and unparsable bindings in an imported keymap are skipped and listed in ImportOutcome.skipped; everything else is applied.
- kittest with a stub FileChooser: Export writes the file; changing the theme and importing the file restores it in the same session without a restart; a rebinding made before the export is active again after the import.
- Satisfied: SET-004 (preferences and shortcuts as a file); fuzzing of import_bytes follows in regression-and-status-10.
notes:
SRS: SET-004
Follow-up: regression-and-status-10 turns its prefs_import placeholder into a cargo-fuzz target over prefs::import_bytes (D.9).

title: Make view-local keys commands and fix the D.8 default keymap
description:
WHY: UI-008 (M) requires default shortcuts for at least the commands of Appendix D.8, using Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, avoiding combinations reserved by the operating system, and never firing single-key tool shortcuts while a text field has focus. D.8 lists save, undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, delete, select all and the command palette; move, copy-move, rotate, mirror, vertical move, array, trim, split and offset; measure and every element tool (wall, slab, column, beam, roof, opening, door, window, stair, free-form solid); plan/3D switching, next and previous tab, fit to window, zoom to selection, orbit, show all, hide selection and isolate selection; the concrete bindings are a UI design deliverable. HW-003 (M) and NFR-A11Y-001 (S) need every shortcut and command operable from the keyboard. Today the view-local keys R (cycle the wall reference line), Tab (cycle overlapping candidates or switch the typed field) and Backspace (remove the last point) are hard-coded in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:638-725 outside the action system, so they can be neither listed consistently nor rebound (UI-009 gap), and most D.8 commands do not exist yet.

WHAT: Register tool.wall.cycle-reference-line, canvas.cycle-candidates, input.next-field, input.remove-last, input.finish and input.cancel-step in the Canvas and PointInput scopes; plan.rs handle_keys asks a binding provider (commands/bindings.rs, effective_binding(id), returning defaults until task 06 adds the user keymap) instead of matching Key::R, Key::Tab and Key::Backspace; typed characters stay raw text input. New commands/d8.rs with one entry per D.8 item: its reserved default Binding and either the registered CommandId or Pending { owner_epic } (selection-transforms for cut, copy, paste, move, copy-move, rotate, mirror and vertical move; drafting-trim-split for trim, split and array; edit-reshape-palette for offset; 3d-input-navigation for measure; profiles-columns-beams, roofs, host-openings, doors-windows-core, stair-solver-tool and free-form-solids for their tools; 3d-view-restrictions for show all, hide and isolate; task 05 for the palette). A later epic registers its command and the test then requires the reserved binding. New commands/os_reserved.rs with the reserved combinations of macOS, Windows and Linux (GNOME and KDE). Write docs/keymap.md, the default keymap per platform, generated from the registry and the D.8 table. Out of scope: implementing the pending commands, the rebinding UI (06).
design: Scopes: PointInput is active while ToolState::is_drawing(), Canvas while a plan or 3D pane is the active pane. Today R cycles the reference line whenever the wall tool is active (plan.rs:712), even at step 0, so a single-key Global tool binding may not equal a Canvas or PointInput binding: the conflict checker treats these scopes as overlapping. Enter and Esc in point input are registered as fixed (listed and shown in prompts, not rebindable) so text fields and modals keep standard behaviour. Display uses egui's format_shortcut per platform; docs/keymap.md lists both the macOS and the Windows/Linux spelling. Keymap constraints enforced by the tests: Primary for file and edit commands, single letters only for tools and view toggles, nothing from the OS tables. F3 (plan/3D, today) is a media key on macOS by default, so give plan/3D switching a second binding. Pointers: plan.rs:638-725 (handle_keys), app.rs:475-477 (single keys suppressed while drawing), actions.rs:177-204 (current shortcut tests).
acceptance_criteria:
- d8 test: every D.8 item appears exactly once; a registered item's command has exactly the reserved default binding; a pending item names an owner epic key of the roadmap; reserved bindings are unique within overlapping scopes; none appears in the OS-reserved table of any of the three platforms (all tables are checked on every host).
- The OS-reserved tables contain at least: macOS Cmd+H, Cmd+M, Cmd+Tab, Cmd+Space, Ctrl+Space, Cmd+`, Cmd+Alt+Esc, Cmd+Shift+3, 4 and 5, Ctrl+arrow keys; Windows Alt+Tab, Alt+Space, Ctrl+Esc, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Win+any key; Linux Alt+F2, Alt+F7, Alt+F8, Ctrl+Alt+T, Ctrl+Alt+arrow keys, Super+any key.
- every_command_is_complete is extended: every registered command that is a D.8 item has a default binding.
- Headless test: a binding provider that maps tool.wall.cycle-reference-line to Shift+R makes Shift+R cycle the reference line and plain R do nothing.
- kittest: with the wall tool active, R cycles the reference line (status message), Tab during drawing switches the typed field, Backspace removes the last chain point; typing R into a focused text field changes nothing.
- docs/keymap.md matches the registry (a test regenerates the table and compares).
- Satisfied: UI-008 for every D.8 command that exists, the shortcut clause of HW-003, and the keyboard path of NFR-A11Y-001 for the view-local actions.
notes:
SRS: UI-008 HW-003 NFR-A11Y-001
Open keymap decisions for docs/keymap.md: R is both the wall reference-line cycle and the natural roof-tool key; W is the wall tool, so the window tool needs another key; proposal: palette on Primary+Shift+P with Problems moving from Primary+Shift+P to Primary+Shift+M, Preferences on Primary+Comma (macOS convention).

title: Replace English strings in archicraft-model with message keys
description:
WHY: NFR-L10N-001 (M) requires all user-visible strings to be externalized, and the epic acceptance extends the literal-string lint to Command::label and CommandError messages in archicraft-model: keys live in the headless crate, the catalogue in the app, so the model stays free of UI and i18n dependencies (NFR-MNT-002). Today Command::label returns English text (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:112-144), shown as 'Undo Create wall' in the Edit menu through History::undo_label and redo_label (command.rs:862-868); CommandError::Invalid, Locked and NotFound carry English Strings built at about 30 sites (command.rs:94-108 and plan()); validate.rs, storey.rs and material.rs return English error Strings; units.rs has an English ParseError (377-385) and unit labels (56-65, 115-122); KindTag::label (element.rs:109, 204) is English.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/message.rs: Message { key: &'static str, args: Vec<(&'static str, Arg)> } with Arg::{Count(u64), Text(String), Length(f64), Angle(f64), Kind(KindTag), Nested(Box<Message>)}, a builder (Message::new(key).count(..).length(..)), serde derives and a key-form Display for logs and the journal; message::ALL_KEYS lists every key the crate emits. Command::label() returns Message; CommandError variants carry Message (NoChange maps to model-error-no-change); validate.rs, storey.rs and material.rs errors return Message with numeric limits as Length or Angle arguments; ParseError maps to keys; LengthUnit, AngleUnit, SlopeFormat, AreaUnit, VolumeUnit, KindTag and IfcClass get label_key() instead of label(); History::undo_label and redo_label return Option<Message>; JournalEntry stores Message. In archicraft-app: i18n::render(&Message, &UnitSettings, &NumberFormat) resolves Length and Angle arguments through units.rs formatting in project units and Kind arguments through their keys; update the consumers (workspace.rs execute errors, ui/shell.rs Undo and Redo items, ui/widgets.rs Edited::Invalid, unit choices in ui/dialogs.rs and ui/properties.rs) and fill locales/en/model.ftl. Remove command.rs, validate.rs, storey.rs, material.rs, units.rs and element.rs from the lint PENDING list; template.rs and samples.rs stay allowlisted as project data. Out of scope: archicraft-ifcx load-problem texts (shown under a localized heading; follow-up bead) and the app-side strings (10, 11, 12).
design: Keys are &'static str, so building a Message costs one small Vec; Message derives Clone, PartialEq, Serialize and Deserialize. CommandError derives Eq today: either wrap f64 arguments in a total-order newtype or drop Eq where no caller needs it. thiserror Display of CommandError uses the key form for logs only; the UI always goes through i18n::render. Validation limits become arguments, so messages show the user's units instead of the metre-only text of today. The Kind argument is resolved to a localized noun via model-kind-<code> keys, so translators get whole sentences ('Create { $kind }'). Pitfalls: element.tag().label().to_lowercase() in validate.rs:260 and command.rs:121 disappears; storey.rs errors flow through map_err(CommandError::Invalid) at command.rs:178-212, so change their Result types together; the journal is written into crash reports (persistence/crash.rs) and must stay readable, hence the key form there. Coordinate with element-kind-framework: when its kind registry lands, the KindTag label keys move into the registry entries unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- archicraft-model gains no dependency on egui, fluent or archicraft-app (test reading its Cargo.toml through include_str!).
- Model unit tests: every Command variant built in the tests yields a label whose key is in message::ALL_KEYS; a source-scan test over the model sources finds no Message::new key missing from ALL_KEYS.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs asserts error keys and arguments instead of English text (for example an out-of-range wall thickness reports its key with the minimum and maximum as Length arguments).
- App test: every ALL_KEYS key exists in locales/en/model.ftl, and the Fluent variables of each message equal the argument names of a representative Message (table-driven).
