- A serde round trip of a History journal with Message arguments is lossless; the journal and replay tests still pass.
- kittest edit_menu_undoes_and_redoes still finds 'Undo Create wall'; a validation error from the properties strip shows its limits in the project length unit.
- string_lint passes with the model files removed from PENDING: Command::label and the CommandError construction sites contain no prose literal.
- Satisfied: NFR-L10N-001 for archicraft-model.
notes:
SRS: NFR-L10N-001
Follow-up bead: localize the archicraft-ifcx Problem texts of the PRJ-008 load report with the same Message type.

title: Turn single-place controls into commands and add command tooltips
description:
WHY: UI-017 (M) requires every command to be reachable from a menu or the palette and to be bindable; the gap analysis lists commands that exist in one place only: the wall and slab geometry modes in the properties strip (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:745-768), display mode, view presets and the projection toggle in the status bar (ui/shell.rs:199-229), insert and delete storey in the browser context menu and the storey dialog (ui/browser.rs:56-81, ui/dialogs.rs:169-192), and duplicate material (dialogs.rs:423-431). UI-011 (S) requires tools and commands to have tooltips with a short description and their shortcut; existing and moved to the registry: the toolbox buttons show description and shortcut (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:125-133, ToolKind::description in views/tools.rs:30-36), the view-tool buttons have tooltips (shell.rs:150-157) and menu items show shortcut text (shell.rs:20-27); missing: description tooltips on menu items, on status-bar controls (Fit, Next and Previous zoom, display mode, Views) and on browser and dialog buttons, and Action has no description at all (eight tooltips in the whole app).

WHAT: Register tool.wall.mode.<mode> and tool.slab.mode.<mode> from WallMode::ALL and SlabMode::ALL, view3d.display.<mode> from DisplayMode::ALL, view3d.preset.<preset> from ViewPreset::ALL, view3d.toggle-projection, storey.insert-above, storey.insert-below, storey.edit (opens the storey dialog on the target), storey.delete (opens the STR-004 prompt) and material.duplicate (enabled when the Materials dialog has a selection); the existing widgets call invoke() instead of mutating state. New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/command_widgets.rs with menu_item, tool_button, bar_button and command_button: label, enabled and checked state and the tooltip 'description (shortcut)' come from the registry and the effective keymap; menus, toolbox, status bar, browser buttons and dialog buttons that run commands use them. Out of scope: the context-menu structure (14), the view-control bar layout (15), tooltips on plain property fields, which are not commands.
design: Parameterised families are registered in loops over the ALL arrays with ids built from enum codes (DisplayMode and ViewPreset need stable code() strings; add them). Mode commands are checkable (checked = current mode), so the strip, menus and palette show the same state. Tooltips use on_hover_text for enabled commands and on_disabled_hover_text with the disabled reason otherwise. Storey commands take Target.storey: the active storey when invoked from the palette, the right-clicked item when invoked from a context menu (14). Pitfall: properties-and-dialogs will rewrite the strip around ui/fields.rs; keep the mode buttons as command_button calls so they survive that rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
- every_command_is_complete is extended: every description has non-empty English text of at most 120 characters; the mode, display-mode and preset families are registered from their ALL arrays (counts compared), so new variants cannot be missed.
- kittest: hovering the Wall toolbox button shows 'Draw walls by their reference line (W)'; hovering View > Fit to window and the status-bar Fit button shows the same description and shortcut.
- kittest: storey.insert-above invoked through the palette inserts a storey above the active storey and Undo removes it; tool.wall.mode.chain invoked through the palette switches the wall mode and the strip shows Chain selected.
- Source-scan test: shell.rs, browser.rs and properties.rs no longer assign wall_mode, slab_mode, the display mode or the projection directly.
- Tooltip unit test over the registry: for every command, command_widgets::tooltip_text contains its English description and, when it has an effective binding, that binding's display text; with a binding provider that maps the Wall tool command to Shift+W, the Wall toolbox tooltip shows Shift+W.
- Satisfied: UI-011 for tools and commands, and UI-017 for the controls listed.
notes: SRS: UI-011 UI-017

title: Add slope formats and make slope, area and volume units editable
description:
WHY: STR-009 (M) requires the project to define the length unit and its display precision, the angle unit and its display precision, the slope format, and the area and volume display units, and changing a unit shall never change stored geometry; NFR-L10N-003 (M) requires metric and imperial lengths, angle units (decimal degrees, degrees-minutes-seconds, gradians, radians) and slope formats (degrees, percent, ratio) for input and display. Appendix D.1 sets decimal degrees with 2 decimals and roof pitch in degrees with percent selectable. Existing and kept: the six length units and four angle units with formatting and parsing (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:14-123, 283-467, tests 557-642), their storage in IFCX (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:155-161, reader.rs:326-355) and the length and angle rows of the Project settings dialog. Missing: SlopeFormat is an unused enum without format or parse functions (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:125-148); slope, area and volume units are stored in IFCX but not editable in the Project settings dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:509-540 covers length and angle only); parse_angle accepts only a degree suffix, and DMS display ignores the angle decimals (units.rs:349-354).

WHAT: units.rs: format_slope and parse_slope for Degrees ('30.00°'), Percent ('57.74 %') and Ratio ('1 : 1.732', rise to run; input also accepts a:b and a/b, so '6:12' works), with slopes stored as pitch angles in radians; parse_angle accepts the suffixes of all four units (degree sign, gon or grad, rad, and degrees-minutes-seconds notation) whatever the display unit, as parse_length does for lengths; DMS shows seconds with angle_decimals decimals. widgets::slope() edit widget for later consumers (roofs, sloped slabs of layer-structures-07). Factor the unit rows of the Project settings dialog into a reusable widgets::unit_settings_editor(&mut UnitSettings, &NumberFormat), which task 17 reuses for the default units of new projects. Project settings dialog: Slope format, Area unit and Volume unit rows with a live sample of a 30° pitch in the chosen format; unit labels through catalogue keys. Extend crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs with non-default slope, area and volume settings. Out of scope: slope consumers, area or volume units beyond m², ft², m³ and ft³, and the multi-command OK of the Project settings dialog (technical debt, dialogs.rs:609-615).
design: Percent = 100 · tan(pitch); ratio = 1 : 1/tan(pitch) with the run formatted with length_decimals decimals; zero slope shows as '0 : 1'. Accept both the ASCII colon and the ratio sign U+2236 in input. Parsing never depends on the display format alone: an explicit suffix ('%', '°', ':') wins, a bare number is read in the display format. Keep everything in units.rs so the headless crate stays the single place for formatting and parsing (NFR-MNT-002); widgets only call it. Area and volume formatting already exists and is used in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:560-564; only the pickers are new.
acceptance_criteria:
- Slope round trips at 0°, 15°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 89.99° in all three formats within display precision; 45° shows as 45.00°, 100.00 % and 1 : 1.000; '6:12' parses to atan(0.5); negative slopes keep their sign; 90° cannot be entered as percent or ratio and is displayed in degrees in those formats.
- parse_angle: '100gon' gives π/2 and '1.5708rad' gives 1.5708 with degrees as display unit; DMS with angle_decimals 1 shows seconds with one decimal; '57,74 %' parses under the comma separator.
- kittest: Project settings shows Slope format, Area unit and Volume unit; choosing Percent and square feet and pressing OK stores SlopeFormat::Percent and AreaUnit::SquareFoot, leaves every element unchanged (STR-009 clause), and Undo restores the previous settings.
- The IFCX round trip keeps non-default slope, area and volume settings; golden files are unchanged.
- Regression: the length unit, length decimals, angle unit and angle decimals rows still change the displayed wall length and rotation; table tests format and parse a value in each of the six length units and four angle units, and the existing units.rs tests keep passing.
- Satisfied: STR-009 (all unit settings editable) and NFR-L10N-003 input and display for lengths, angles and slopes.
notes:
SRS: STR-009 NFR-L10N-003
Open question: imperial roof pitch is usually written x:12 or x/12; v1 displays ratios as 1 : n (SRS O-3 covers the imperial formats).

title: Generate tool prompts from the keys each tool state handles
description:
WHY: NFR-USE-003 (M) requires every multi-step tool to show the next expected input in a prompt line, together with the available modifier keys and options, and the epic acceptance asks for a test that checks every ToolState prompt string against the keys actually handled in that state. Today ToolState::prompt() (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:373-405) is hand-written: the wall and slab rectangle first-corner steps and the rotated-rectangle width steps list no keys although Esc, R (walls), typed values, Shift and Backspace work there (views/plan.rs:473-486, 650, 696-712); Backspace is live in every drawing state but advertised only for chains; R is live in every wall mode but advertised only at step 0 of Single and Chain. No test asserts prompt text.

WHAT: In views/tools.rs add LiveKey {TypeValue, NextField, Constrain, Finish, RemoveLast, CancelStep, CycleReferenceLine, CycleCandidates} and ToolState::live_keys(); extract the key branch of plan.rs:638-726 into a headless ToolState::handle_key(LiveKey, ..) -> KeyEffect that plan.rs calls; prompt() becomes a step message (tool, mode, step) followed by hints rendered from live_keys() with the effective binding text of the matching command (tasks 04 and 06), so a rebinding updates the prompt. Externalize all of views/tools.rs (ToolKind labels and descriptions, WallMode and SlabMode labels, prompts) into locales/en/tools.ftl and remove it from the lint PENDING list. Out of scope: prompts of tools added by later epics, which reuse live_keys and the hint renderer.
design: live_keys() and handle_key() derive from one predicate per state, which is what makes the test meaningful; plan.rs keeps only the translation from egui events to LiveKey and the raw typed characters. Hints are rendered as key-action pairs from catalogue keys (prompt-hint-<live-key>) joined by a localized separator after the step message. Coordination: point-input-snapping-01 moves prompts into StepSpec hints and key handling into input::PointInput::key(); if it has landed first, implement live_keys as the StepSpec hint list and run the effect check against PointInput::key() instead of tools.rs. The test stays the same; whichever task lands second adapts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exhaustive test over ToolKind × geometry modes × point counts (0 up to the needed count; 0 to 3 for chains and polygons) × typed text empty or not: for every LiveKey, handle_key returns an effect other than Ignored exactly when the key is in live_keys(), and the prompt contains the hint of exactly the live keys.
- Regression cases from the gap analysis: the wall-rectangle first corner lists Esc and R; the rotated-rectangle width step lists typing a value, Shift, Backspace and Esc; every state with at least one point lists Backspace.
- With a binding provider that maps tool.wall.cycle-reference-line to Shift+R, the wall prompt shows Shift+R.
- kittest: after clicking Wall, the status line shows the step-0 prompt with its hints.
- string_lint passes with views/tools.rs removed from PENDING.
- Every prompt starts with a step message that names the tool, its active geometry method (the option the user can switch) and the next expected input; a step-message key exists in tools.ftl for every (tool, mode, step) combination of the exhaustive test.
- Satisfied: NFR-USE-003 for the wall and slab tools; later tools inherit the mechanism.
notes:
SRS: NFR-USE-003
Review the LiveKey and hint API with the owner of point-input-snapping-01 before merging.

title: Persist component instances and embedded definitions in IFCX
description:
WHY: OBJ-006 (M): definitions used by a project shall be stored in the project file so that it opens on any machine without external libraries. OBJ-004 (M): instances reference definitions by ID and version, never by file name or path. OBJ-005 (M): if a definition cannot be resolved, the project shall still open. DW-017 (S): the selected handedness convention belongs to the project. Existing code to extend, not replace: IFX-061 (declared attributes, schema.rs:126-257), IFX-064 (parameter and regeneration round trips, roundtrip.rs:47-73, goldens at :195-230) and IFX-067 (project resources in archicraft::project, writer.rs:142-190; only used materials become nodes, writer.rs:320-329) are done, so this task adds declarations, records and used materials to those paths and keeps their tests green as regressions; IFX-060 is partial (writer.rs:142-190) and gains the component data. Gap OBJ-006: 'Embed used definitions in the project file and read them back' (writer.rs:320-329 stores only used materials).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/components.rs: the archicraft::component codec (definition { id, version }, parameters keyed by parameter code with typed values, material parameters as Reference data type, mirrored, detailOverride, lastKnown { name, extent }), written by the generic writer path for every element whose kind exposes component(), next to the per-kind codec of element-kind-framework; the definition record codec for archicraft::project.components (sorted by code, id, version: id, version, code, name, category, generator, defaultClass, traits, schema entries with key, label, kind, default, range, group, binding and options, keyPoints, derived); schema.rs declarations for both, with enumerations from the model's ALL arrays, and an optional handedness member in the project settings (HandednessConvention codes, default din107). writer.rs fills lastKnown from the resolved definition's name and the evaluated layout extent on every save (left unchanged for missing definitions); until task 09 instance elements write their world_parts as ordinary Body children. reader.rs reads the store before the elements and archicraft::component through the codec ReadContext; for resolved definitions it drops unknown parameter keys and resets out-of-range values with warnings; for missing definitions it keeps the instance and its parameters verbatim and adds a Warning "Definition '<name>' (<id> v<version>) is missing; the instance is shown as a placeholder" with the element path; malformed component data skips the element with an error. Sample samples::component_instances() (test-kinds, built with the framework's seeded builder): two identical door.hinged.single instances and one mirrored, a 3 x 2 window.multi-sash, an opening.arched and a probe instance. Fixture crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/missing-definition.ifcx derived from it with one embedded definition removed and one generator key changed. Out of scope: type nodes and occurrence transforms (09), placeholder UI (10, 12), preserving foreign type geometry of unknown definitions (ifcx-interop, IFX-066).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe; one generic component codec instead of duplicating instance data per kind, so doors-windows-core-05 only adds its insert fields. Determinism (IFX-007): parameters in key order, the store sorted, numbers written at full precision through json.rs. Materials referenced only by instance parameters must count as used materials in the writer and go through the reader's material repair. Optional members need no FORMAT_VERSION bump under element-kind-framework's migration rule; bump only if a reader-visible shape changes. Pitfalls: the reader must not depend on node order; keep the store's definition records self-contained (schema included) so a placeholder can still show its parameters read-only (task 11). Pointers: schema.rs:126-257, writer.rs:144-217/320-329, reader.rs:301-433/592-735.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/roundtrip.rs (test-kinds): component_instances round-trips to an equal Project (definition refs, every ParamValue variant, mirrored, detail_override, the embedded store and the handedness setting); regenerate-and-save is idempotent; written_files_validate_without_problems covers the new declarations (IFX-061, IFX-064).
- The saved archicraft::project.components holds exactly the definitions referenced by instances, each once and sorted; reading with the built-in catalogue replaced by an empty one (test hook) still restores every instance with full geometry from the embedded copies (OBJ-006 'opens on any machine').
- Schema scan: no member of archicraft::component or of the definition records holds a path, URL or file name (OBJ-004).
- missing-definition.ifcx opens: a Project is returned, one Warning per affected instance names the definition, missing_definitions() lists both cases (not embedded, unknown generator), parameters are preserved verbatim and saving again writes them unchanged (OBJ-005 'shall still open').
- Lenient reading: an out-of-range parameter is reset with a warning, an unknown key on a resolved definition is dropped with a warning, a missing lastKnown loads with defaults; existing lenient-reading tests stay green.
- Existing goldens stay bit-identical and conformance/run.sh stays green.
notes: SRS: OBJ-004 OBJ-005 OBJ-006 DW-017 (also IFX-060 IFX-061 IFX-064 IFX-067). Open question: a file from a newer version whose definition is unknown here loses its type geometry on save (written without a body plus a warning, because IFX-063 forbids invented geometry); revisit with ifcx-interop (IFX-066 preservation).

title: Add component definitions, parameter schemas and instance references
description:
WHY: OBJ-002 (M) requires every component definition to have a persistent unique ID, a display name, a version and a category (door, window, furniture, sanitary, equipment, generic), a parameter schema (name, type, unit, default, range and grouping) and a parametric 3D geometry and plan symbol. OBJ-004 (M): instances reference definitions by ID and version, never by file name or path. OBJ-014 (S): definitions shall be able to provide plan symbols per detail level, named key points and derived values. DSP-015 (S): doors, windows and objects support at least two plan detail levels (simplified, detailed), chosen per view and overridable per element. The gap analysis lists OBJ-002 and OBJ-004 as missing: UUID id types exist (crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs:12-75) but there is no definition or instance type, and Project holds only layers, materials and views as resources (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:166-183). Everything else in this epic, and doors-windows-core's WallInsert (which carries a definition reference and instance parameters), builds on these types.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/src/components/{mod.rs,definition.rs,schema.rs,instance.rs}. Types: DefinitionId (id_type! in ids.rs); DefinitionRef { id, version: u32 }; ComponentCategory with exactly the six OBJ-002 categories (ALL/code/label); DetailLevel { Simplified, Detailed } (ALL/code/label); PartRole { Frame, Leaf, Sash, Glazing, Sill, Body } (ALL/code/label; the one role list shared by Material parameters, the geometry parts of tasks 04-05 and the IFCX part children of task 09, Body for generic objects such as the probe); ParameterSpec { key (stable snake_case code), label, kind: ParamKind { Length, Angle, Count, Bool, Choice { options }, Material { role: PartRole }, LengthList, ChoiceList { options } }, default: ParamValue, range, group: ParamGroup { code, label }, binding: Option<Binding { OpeningWidth, OpeningHeight }> } with ParameterSpec::unit() -> ParamUnit { Length, Angle, None } derived from the kind (OBJ-002 'unit'; displayed through the existing units.rs format_length/format_angle at units.rs:283/334, not a second formatter); ParameterSchema { params } with validate(&InstanceParameters), resolve() (fills defaults) and compatible(values, target) (keeps values whose key and kind match; used by relink and later by OBJ-008 upgrades); ParamValue with one variant per kind; InstanceParameters(BTreeMap<String, ParamValue>); Definition { id, version, code, name, category, schema, generator: GeneratorKey, key_points: Vec<NamedSpec>, derived: Vec<DerivedSpec>, default_class: IfcClass, traits: DefinitionTraits { has_parts, handed, insertable_as } }; ComponentInstance { definition: DefinitionRef, parameters, mirrored: bool, detail_override: Option<DetailLevel>, last_known: LastKnown { name, extent: Option<[f64; 3]> } } (cached name and local extent for OBJ-005 placeholders); a Catalogue type (lookup by DefinitionRef, latest(id), by_category) with Catalogue::builtin() empty until task 03 except, with the test-kinds feature, a probe definition (category generic; a length, a bool, a choice and a material parameter; generator key 'test.probe@1'). Extend element-kind-framework's trait Kind with component()/component_mut() defaulting to None, delegated by the kinds! macro, and Element::component(). Add the test carrier kinds/test_instance.rs behind test-kinds: TestInstance { origin: DVec3, rotation: f64, instance: ComponentInstance }, prefix 'TI', default class IfcBuildingElementProxy, with a stub geometry generator in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/test_instance.rs (empty ElementGeometry until task 07) and a codec in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/test_instance.rs (origin and rotation; the component attribute comes with task 08), so the registry completeness tests stay green. validate.rs (extend validate_element at validate.rs:243, do not add a second entry point) validates instance parameters when the definition resolves in Catalogue::builtin(); task 02 switches the lookup to Project::resolve_definition so embedded definitions count too. Write docs/components.md with the definition format. Out of scope: the project store and commands (02), catalogue content (03), geometry (04-07), IFCX persistence (08, 09), UI.
design: Plain serde data without geometry or UI dependencies (NFR-MNT-002/004). Lengths in metres and angles in radians as in units.rs; ranges stored in the same units. OBJ-002's 'parametric 3D geometry and plan symbol' is represented by the GeneratorKey because the generators live in archicraft-geometry (tasks 04-06); the model keeps a KNOWN_GENERATORS list (task 03) so resolution stays a model concern. The test carrier follows element-kind-framework's test-kinds pattern (kinds/dummy.rs): cargo unifies dev-dependency features only in test builds, so release binaries never contain it. Pitfalls: reject NaN and infinite values in validate; Material parameters hold MaterialId references, so plan_delete_material in crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs must treat them like element materials (reject or remap with the existing behaviour); keep parameter keys stable forever because they are written to IFCX (task 08) and keyed in types (task 07). Pointers: ids.rs:12-75, project.rs:146-186, validate.rs:243, kinds/mod.rs of the framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in components/schema.rs: validate accepts the defaults and rejects out-of-range lengths and counts, wrong value kinds, unknown choice codes and list lengths that do not match their governing count, each with a message naming the parameter label; resolve fills missing keys with defaults; compatible keeps values whose key and kind match and drops the rest (OBJ-002 schema clause).
- serde round trip of Definition and ComponentInstance is lossless; InstanceParameters iterates in key order.
- Source-scan test: no type under crates/archicraft-model/src/components has a path, URL or file-name field, and DefinitionRef equality uses id and version (OBJ-004).
- DetailLevel::ALL == [Simplified, Detailed] and ComponentInstance::detail_override defaults to None (DSP-015 per-element hook); Definition exposes key_points and derived specs (OBJ-014 API).
- With test-kinds: KINDS contains test-instance; Element::component() is Some for a TestInstance and None for walls and slabs; AddElements, undo and redo keep the TestInstance's id and instance data; the framework's module-layout test finds the kind only in its own modules and one registry line per crate.
- ComponentCategory::ALL lists exactly door, window, furniture, sanitary, equipment and generic with stable codes, and a Definition written and read back keeps its id, name, version and category (OBJ-002 identity clause).
- ParameterSpec::unit() is Length for Length and LengthList, Angle for Angle and None for Count, Bool, Choice, ChoiceList and Material; every ParameterSpec carries a group and a default inside its range (OBJ-002 unit, default, range and grouping clauses).
- cargo test, clippy and fmt on the workspace are green and the golden files are bit-identical.
notes: SRS: OBJ-002 OBJ-004 OBJ-014 DSP-015. Decision to record in docs/components.md: empty openings use category generic with traits.insertable_as [door, window], because OBJ-002's category list has no opening category.

title: Give panels and controls accessible names and verify keyboard reach
description:
WHY: NFR-A11Y-002 (S) requires UI panels and dialogs to expose accessible names and roles to screen readers, with the graphical viewports exempt; NFR-A11Y-001 (S) requires every command to be operable from the keyboard; HW-003 (M) requires all numeric entry and all shortcuts to work from the keyboard. AccessKit is enabled through the eframe feature (Cargo.toml:30-37), but checkboxes have empty labels (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:308, 316, 728, 744), text fields, combo boxes and drag values sit next to a separate ui.label() that is not associated with them (ui/widgets.rs:27-32, 113-122; dialogs.rs:523, 539, 689-745), colour buttons have no name (dialogs.rs:794, 829), panels have no names or roles, and no test drives a command by keyboard or audits the accessibility tree.

WHAT: ui/widgets.rs: every edit widget (length, angle, slope, text, choice, integer, decimal) takes a label key, draws the label and associates it through Response::labelled_by; checkboxes get their visible text; colour buttons get names (for example the cut-fill foreground of a named material); the menu bar, toolbox, properties strip, project browser, tab bar, view-control bar, status line and problems panel get AccessKit roles and names through Context::accesskit_node_builder; dialogs keep their window role and title; the plan and 3D canvases get a name and are documented as exempt. New audit and keyboard tests in crates/archicraft-app/tests/a11y.rs. Out of scope: entering the first point of an element by keyboard (absolute coordinates, point-input-snapping-05) and keyboard selection (selection-transforms), which complete NFR-A11Y-001 for drawing.
design: Roles: MenuBar for the menu bar, Toolbar for the toolbox and the view-control bar, a named Pane (or Group) for the browser, properties strip and problems panel, TabList for the tab bar as far as egui_tiles exposes it, Status for the status line; verify the exact accesskit Role names against the version pinned by egui 0.36.2. Response::labelled_by sets the AccessKit relation, so screen readers announce the field label with the control. Keep the audit table-driven (role list and exempt Ids), so later dialogs are covered automatically once they register a command. Pitfall: AccessKit nodes need ids that are stable across frames; build label Ids from the field Id, not from the label text, so translations do not change them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Audit kittest: in the main window and in every dialog opened through its registry command, every node with role TextInput, ComboBox, CheckBox, SpinButton, Slider or Button has a non-empty name; each listed panel is found by role and name with query_all_by_role.
- Keyboard-reach test: for every registered command (context_only ones run against Target::active()), opening the palette with its shortcut, typing the full label and pressing Enter records exactly that invocation (recorder, handlers not run).
- Shortcut test: every command with a binding is invoked by its key events in its scope (HW-003).
- Numeric entry: a length field reached with Tab accepts typed '2,5' under the comma setting and Enter commits 2.5 (numeric clause of HW-003).
- Dialog audit: every dialog opened through its registry command exposes a window node whose name is its localized title (dialog clause of NFR-A11Y-002).
- Point input (numeric clause of HW-003 through INP-003): with the wall tool active and a first point placed, typing '3' and Enter places the second point 3 m away and Tab switches to the angle field (existing behaviour, views/plan.rs:382-394, kept).
- Satisfied: NFR-A11Y-002 for panels and dialogs, NFR-A11Y-001 for all commands, HW-003.
notes: SRS: NFR-A11Y-002 NFR-A11Y-001 HW-003

title: Externalize the strings of the shell, views, workspace and persistence
description:
WHY: NFR-L10N-001 (M) requires all user-visible strings to be externalized. After the model (02) and the commands (03), the main-window chrome still uses literals: the unsaved-changes, message and load-report prompts in crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:554-600, the tab titles (app.rs:735-748), the status bar and toolbox headers in ui/shell.rs, the project browser (ui/browser.rs), the plan and 3D context menus and hover labels (views/plan.rs:728-779, views/view3d.rs:265-293), the DisplayMode and ViewPreset labels (views/render3d.rs:40, views/camera.rs:134), status messages in workspace.rs, and the recovery and crash-report notices in persistence/.

WHAT: Move every user-visible literal of app.rs, ui/shell.rs, ui/browser.rs, views/plan.rs, views/view3d.rs, views/render3d.rs, views/camera.rs, workspace.rs and persistence/{mod,autosave,crash}.rs into locales/en/app.ftl as whole-sentence messages with named arguments (storey names, counts, paths); replace 'problem(s)' with a Fluent plural; DisplayMode and ViewPreset get label_key(). Remove these files from the lint PENDING list except views/plan.rs and views/view3d.rs: their canvas context menus (plan.rs:728-779, view3d.rs:265-293) are rebuilt from registry labels in task 14, which then removes both files from PENDING; their other strings (hover labels, status texts) are externalized here. Out of scope: the canvas context-menu bodies (14), views/tools.rs labels and prompts (12), ui/dialogs.rs, ui/properties.rs and ui/widgets.rs (11), and strings added by later tasks, which use keys from the start.
design: Mechanical, but keep messages translatable: no concatenation of fragments, an argument for every variable part, plurals through Fluent selectors. egui Id salts (Id::new for display-mode and similar) and test anchors stay literal and are exempt from the lint. The plan tab title becomes a message with the storey name as argument, so the tests that query the English text keep working. Crash-report file content and log lines stay English because they are diagnostics for developers (NFR-SEC-002); only the notice shown to the user is localized.
acceptance_criteria:
- string_lint passes with the listed files removed from PENDING except views/plan.rs and views/view3d.rs, whose only remaining literals are inside the canvas context menus left to task 14.
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs passes unchanged in English ('Plan: 00 Ground floor', 'No problems' and 'Undo Create wall' are still found).
- The status bar shows '1 problem' and '3 problems' (unit test on the rendered message for counts 1 and 3).
- Pseudo-locale kittest: with en-XA installed, every AccessKit label of the menu bar, toolbox, status line, tab bar and browser headings carries the pseudo markers, except the user data listed in the test (storey and view names, numbers, file paths).
- Satisfied: NFR-L10N-001 for the main-window chrome.
notes: SRS: NFR-L10N-001

title: Write shared type nodes, occurrence inherits and mirrored types
description:
WHY: IFX-050 (S): doors, windows and objects that share a definition and differ only in placement shall be written as one type node plus occurrence nodes; the type holds the class, type-level attributes such as bsi::ifc::prop::TypeName and the host-independent part geometry, and each occurrence references it via inherits { type } with its own transform, Void and occurrence attributes. IFX-051 (S): mirrored occurrences reference a separate type with mirrored geometry; transforms with a negative determinant shall not be written. IFX-037 (S): identical meshes are not written repeatedly. OBJ-011 (S): sharing in IFCX. The gap analysis lists all three IFX requirements as missing (no type nodes, no inherits.type, no transform besides the storey translation).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/types.rs plus writer.rs: for every element with InstanceGeometry collect its TypeKey in first-occurrence order of the spatial tree; the type node's path is TypeKey::uuid(); attributes bsi::ifc::class (the occurrences' class), bsi::ifc::prop::TypeName ('<definition name> <w>/<h>' in centimetres when width and height exist, plus ' (mirrored)') and archicraft::componentType { definition, mirrored } declared in-file; children are the parts by role (PartRole: Frame, Leaf, Sash, Glazing, Sill, Body) with ids sub_node_id(type, role) (writer.rs:46, reused as IFX-010 is done) and material inherits (materials added to used_materials); part meshes in unit-local coordinates through round_coordinate (json.rs:153) are keyed by a content hash of their rounded points and indices, each distinct mesh is written once as a geometry-only node (path Uuid v5 of TYPE_NAMESPACE and the hash, only usd::usdgeom::mesh) and every part node inherits it through inherits { "geometry": <path> } next to inherits { "material": ... }, so types that differ only in a material or another non-geometric parameter write no mesh twice (IFX-037). Occurrences carry inherits { "type": <path> } (the key name doors-windows-core-05 reuses), usd::xformop with InstanceGeometry.transform relative to the parent node (row-major, translation in the fourth row; IFX-031 is done for the storey translation, so generalise translation() at writer.rs:237-239 into one DMat4 helper that still writes the storey transform byte-identically and that regression-and-status-04 rounds for IFX-007), no own mesh children, and archicraft::element, the kind codec and archicraft::component as before. A writer-wide guard rejects any usd::xformop whose upper 3x3 determinant is not positive (Problem::error, unreachable by construction). Type and geometry nodes are emitted after the storey subtree and before the materials, referenced only through inherits, so the single root of IFX-013 (done, writer.rs:252) is kept. reader.rs validates inherits.type (missing target or class mismatch gives a warning) and never visits type nodes as elements. conformance/check.ts: every inherits.type target exists with the same class code and a TypeName; occurrences have no mesh children except an invisible Void; no two mesh-bearing nodes have identical meshes (IFX-037); every usd::xformop transform has a positive determinant (IFX-051); the viewer-tree check finds occurrence meshes through inheritance. Golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/component-types.ifcx from samples::component_instances() (fixed author and timestamp, ARCHICRAFT_BLESS). Out of scope: Void children and host containment (host-openings, doors-windows-core-05), IfcDoor/IfcWindow codecs (doors-windows-core-05), third-party type import (ifcx-interop).
design: Layout follows SRS Appendix C example 5 (docs/SRS.md lines 1835-1870): type nodes are top-level data entries referenced only through inherits, like material nodes, so the composed tree keeps a single root. The occurrence transform composes with the storey translation; unit-local meshes keep coordinates small. Geometry nodes follow the material-node pattern (writer.rs:376 writes inherits.material on Body nodes), so composition already resolves them. Pitfalls: confirm how compose3 merges inherited children and inherited geometry into the occurrence; if it does not, extend checkViewerTree to follow inherits; child keys stay unique per type node; deterministic type order is first-occurrence order, never HashMap order; a user IFC class override yields a separate type because TypeKey includes the class. Pointers: writer.rs:243-418 (write/write_element), conformance/check.ts:67-104, roundtrip.rs:195-230 (golden handling).
acceptance_criteria:
- Writer tests (test-kinds): three identical TestInstances produce exactly one type node whose part children carry all part meshes (through their geometry nodes) and three occurrences with inherits.type to it and no own meshes (IFX-050); a mirrored twin references a second type whose meshes are the reflection and both occurrence transforms have a positive determinant (IFX-051); a different width gives a third type; the number of mesh-bearing nodes equals the number of distinct part meshes, and two types that differ only in the frame material share one Frame geometry node (IFX-037).
- A door whose swing is flipped to the exterior references its own type (a parameter difference, generated natively) and no written usd::xformop has a negative determinant (IFX-051 'a door opening to the other side').
- Type paths and part ids equal TypeKey::uuid() and its v5 children and are byte-identical across two saves apart from the header (IFX-010, IFX-007).
- Loading the golden returns an equal project and regenerated type meshes equal the stored ones within 0.1 mm (IFX-064).
- conformance/run.sh passes on component-types.ifcx and on all existing goldens, and check.ts fails on crafted negatives: a type whose class differs from its occurrence, an occurrence with a duplicate own mesh, two geometry nodes with identical meshes, a transform with a negative determinant; the composed tree still has exactly one root (IFX-013).
- An occurrence whose type node is missing loads with a warning and its parametric data intact.
- OBJ-011's IFCX clause is satisfied and doors-windows-core-05 can add Void children and IfcDoor/IfcWindow codecs without changing the type mechanism.
notes: SRS: IFX-050 IFX-051 IFX-037 OBJ-011 (also IFX-007 IFX-010 IFX-013 IFX-031 IFX-064). Decision: the inherits key is 'type', as in SRS Appendix C (IFX-050 leaves the name to ArchiCraft).

title: Externalize dialog and property strings and make the lint strict
description:
WHY: NFR-L10N-001 (M) is complete only when no user-visible literal is left, and the epic acceptance asks for a CI lint that finds no user-visible literal outside the strings table. The largest remaining sources are crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs (about 90 literals: storeys, layers, materials, project settings, preferences, settings and the delete-storey prompt), ui/properties.rs (about 40: field labels, 'n selected, m editable', mixed markers) and ui/widgets.rs ('Mixed', the length hint), all changed in the meantime by tasks 06, 07, 09 and 17; views/tools.rs, views/plan.rs and views/view3d.rs leave PENDING in tasks 12 and 14 first.

WHAT: Externalize dialogs.rs, properties.rs, widgets.rs and any file still on the PENDING list into locales/en/dialogs.ftl; empty the PENDING list and keep a test that it stays empty; add the lint as a named step (cargo test -p archicraft-app --test string_lint) to the lint job of .github/workflows/ci.yml; write docs/i18n.md (key naming, arguments, plurals, number arguments through NumberFormat, how to add a language) for later epics and reference it from the conventions section of CLAUDE.md; add a pseudo-locale audit that opens every dialog through its registry command. Out of scope: the German catalogue (release-candidate, NFR-L10N-002).
design: Field labels in properties.rs become keys shared by the strip and the settings dialog, so properties-and-dialogs (ui/fields.rs FieldSpec) can carry them over unchanged. Widgets that take a label receive keys, not strings (task 16 makes labels mandatory for AccessKit). The audit drives dialogs through invoke(id, Target, Origin::Test) and walks the AccessKit tree of the harness; dialogs that need a selection get one from a seeded project. Pitfall: lists of user data (layer and material names) must not fail the audit; the test excludes those rows by Id.
acceptance_criteria:
- string_lint: PENDING is empty; the allowlist contains only project data (template.rs, samples.rs), IFCX codes, Id salts and log messages, each with a reason; the CI lint job runs the lint as its own step.
- Pseudo-locale audit (kittest): with en-XA installed, every window title, heading, label, button and menu item of the main window and of every dialog opened through its registry command carries the pseudo markers, except the user-data fields listed in the test.
- All existing UI tests pass in English.
- docs/i18n.md exists and is referenced from CLAUDE.md.
- Satisfied: NFR-L10N-001 in full (English UI, every user-visible string externalized), together with tasks 02, 10 and 12.
notes: SRS: NFR-L10N-001

title: Detect the OS number locale and format every number through it
description:
WHY: STR-010 (M) requires the decimal separator and digit grouping to default to the operating-system locale, with an in-app override that takes effect without a restart; NFR-L10N-004 (M) requires number input and display to respect the selected decimal separator and digit grouping. Today 'Automatic' reads only the POSIX variables LC_ALL, LC_NUMERIC and LANG against a hard-coded language list (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:137-172); GUI launches on macOS and Windows normally have none of them, so Automatic silently means a point. The grouping character is derived from the separator (prefs.rs:129) instead of the locale, egui DragValue fields bypass NumberFormat (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:523, 539, 693-699, 731-741), and the typed-input filter is a literal character list (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:359-361).

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/i18n/os_locale.rs: OsNumberLocale { tag, decimal, grouping }, detected once at start: on Windows from GetLocaleInfoEx (LOCALE_SDECIMAL and LOCALE_STHOUSAND of the user default locale, which honours changes made in the Region settings) through windows-sys; on macOS from NSLocale.currentLocale (decimalSeparator, groupingSeparator) through objc2-foundation; on Linux and as fallback from the sys-locale tag mapped through a CLDR-derived table in i18n/cldr_numbers.rs. Preferences keep Automatic, Point and Comma for the separator and the grouping switch, with the grouping character taken from the locale and replaced by a no-break space when it would equal the chosen separator. In crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs, NumberFormat accepts any grouping character, and the input normalisation (469-482) strips the active grouping character plus no-break, narrow no-break and apostrophe groupings between digits, never inside feet-inches syntax. ui/widgets.rs gets integer() and decimal() widgets that format and parse with NumberFormat and still support dragging; every DragValue in dialogs.rs uses them. plan.rs derives its typed-input filter from a new units::input_alphabet(units, nf). Out of scope: slope and unit settings (09), language selection (07).
design: unsafe_code is denied workspace-wide (Cargo.toml [workspace.lints]): confine the FFI to i18n/os_locale/windows.rs and macos.rs with #[allow(unsafe_code)] and a SAFETY comment per call (or use safe objc2-foundation methods where they exist), and add the crates as target-specific dependencies. Licences: windows-sys and sys-locale MIT/Apache, objc2 and objc2-foundation MIT (or Zlib/Apache/MIT), CLDR data Unicode-3.0; all are on the deny.toml allow list. Generate the CLDR table once for about 80 locales and record the CLDR version in the file header. Indian two-digit grouping is not supported; such locales fall back to three-digit groups (documented). Pitfall: egui's default fonts may lack U+202F; map it to U+00A0 for display while still accepting it in input. Cache the detection in a OnceLock; number_format() stays a cheap per-frame computation, so the override keeps applying without a restart.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table tests: de-DE and de-AT give a decimal comma and the CLDR grouping, de-CH a point and an apostrophe, fr-FR a comma and a narrow no-break space, en-US a point and a comma; an unknown tag gives a point and a comma.
- units tests: 1234567.891 with two decimals, a point and an apostrophe grouping formats as 1’234’567.89; '1 234,5' with a no-break space parses as 1234.5 under a decimal comma; '1,2,3' is rejected under a decimal comma; a feet-inches value with a fraction still parses with grouping on.
- Platform tests through OS APIs: on macOS the test binary re-runs itself with LANG, LC_ALL and LC_NUMERIC removed and asserts the detected tag equals the normalised output of 'defaults read -g AppleLocale'; on Windows it asserts the detected decimal equals PowerShell (Get-Culture).NumberFormat.NumberDecimalSeparator; both run in the existing CI matrix.
- kittest: switching the separator to Comma in Preferences and pressing OK shows the storey elevations in the project browser with a comma on the next frame; the autosave field shows and accepts values through the new integer widget; typing '2,5' into a length field under the comma setting stores 2.5.
- plan.rs contains no literal typed-input character list (source-scan test).
- docs/technology-choices.md lists sys-locale, windows-sys and objc2-foundation (target-specific dependencies) with version, licence and health check; cargo deny check licenses passes on all three runners.
- Satisfied: STR-010 and NFR-L10N-004 on Windows, macOS and Linux.
notes: SRS: STR-010 NFR-L10N-004

title: Store used definitions in the project and add relink commands
description:
WHY: OBJ-006 (M): definitions used by a project shall be stored in the project file, so that the project opens on any machine without external libraries. OBJ-005 (M): if a referenced definition cannot be resolved, the project shall still open; affected instances appear as labelled placeholders (bounding box and name) that remain selectable and deletable, and the system lists all missing definitions and allows relinking them. DW-012 (M) requires the inspector to be driven by each type's parameter schema, which needs a parameter edit command, and DSP-015 (S) needs a per-element detail override command. The gap analysis lists OBJ-006 as missing (the writer stores only used materials, writer.rs:320-329) and OBJ-005 as missing (no placeholders, no missing-definition list, no relink).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/components/store.rs: ComponentStore { definitions: IndexMap<DefinitionRef, Definition> } as Project.components (serde default empty). Project::resolve_definition(r) -> Resolution { Resolved(&Definition), Missing { reason: NotEmbedded | UnknownGenerator(key) } }: an embedded definition whose generator key is in KNOWN_GENERATORS resolves; otherwise the built-in catalogue entry with the same id and version resolves; otherwise it is missing. Embedding: plan() of AddElements and UpdateElements appends a new Edit (InsertDefinition/RemoveDefinition, invertible) that copies a referenced built-in definition into the store, so the add and the embedding are one undo step (OBJ-006). Project::missing_definitions() -> Vec<MissingDefinition { reference, name (from last_known), reason, instances }> sorted by name. New commands with labels and plan() arms: RelinkDefinition { from, to } (rebinds every instance of from, maps parameters with ParameterSchema::compatible, resets values outside the new ranges to defaults, embeds the target; Invalid when the target is unresolvable or its traits are incompatible); SetInstanceParameters { ids, values } (partial update validated against the resolved schema; Invalid for instances whose definition is missing, so placeholders keep their parameters verbatim); SetInstanceMirrored { ids, mirrored }; SetDetailOverride { ids, detail: Option<DetailLevel> }. Deleting placeholders uses DeleteElements unchanged. Project::integrity_problems (element-kind-framework) gains one 'missing definition' entry per affected instance. Out of scope: catalogue content (03), IFCX persistence (08), UI (10-12), upgrades to newer versions (OBJ-008) and linked library folders (OBJ-007) in library-dw-exchange.
design: Follow the 'Add a command' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md. The store is keyed by DefinitionRef so two versions of one definition can coexist (OBJ-004, OBJ-008 later); the writer sorts it (task 08). Resolution is a pure function of the project and the static catalogue; geometry caches per revision. Embedding inside plan() keeps one undo step per user action (UND-002). Pitfalls: never normalise or drop parameters of unresolved instances, because relinking must restore them; plan_delete_material must see Material parameters; RelinkDefinition must be a single command even for thousands of instances (one ReplaceElement per instance in one Edit list). Pointers: command.rs:36-94 (Command), :95-104 (CommandError), :616-633 (Edit), :320-342 (plan_add_elements), :520 (plan_delete_material), project.rs:164-186 (Project), :327-342 (integrity_problems before element-kind-framework-08 structures it), validate.rs:243 (validate_element, whose instance check from task 01 now uses resolve_definition).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/components.rs (test-kinds, probe definition): adding a TestInstance of a built-in definition embeds exactly one copy; a second instance embeds nothing new; undo removes the instance and the copy, redo restores both (OBJ-006 model side).
- An instance referencing a DefinitionRef that is neither embedded nor built-in passes validation, the rest of the project stays editable, missing_definitions() lists it with the cached name and instance ids, and DeleteElements on it works with undo restoring it (OBJ-005 model side).
- An embedded definition with an unknown generator key is reported Missing with reason UnknownGenerator.
- RelinkDefinition rebinds every affected instance, keeps compatible values, resets incompatible ones to defaults, embeds the target and empties missing_definitions(); undo restores the original references; relinking to a missing target or across incompatible traits fails with CommandError::Invalid and leaves the project unchanged.
- SetInstanceParameters rejects out-of-range values with the parameter label in the message and returns NoChange for identical values; SetInstanceMirrored and SetDetailOverride round-trip through undo and redo (DW-012 command, DSP-015 per-element override).
- integrity_problems lists one entry per instance with a missing definition; cargo test, clippy and fmt are green.
notes: SRS: OBJ-005 OBJ-006 DW-012 DSP-015 (also OBJ-004). Open question: whether unused embedded definitions are purged on save; default keep them (IFX-067 allows unused resources in archicraft::project) and add a purge command later.

title: Add the searchable command palette
description:
WHY: NFR-USE-005 (S) requires all commands to be reachable through a searchable command palette that shows their keyboard shortcut; UI-017 (M) accepts the palette as the route for commands without a menu item; Appendix D.8 lists the palette itself among the commands with a default shortcut; and NFR-A11Y-001 (S) gets a keyboard path to every command through it. Nothing exists today beyond the read-only shortcut list (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:641-667); the gap analysis rates the palette small once the registry exists.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/palette.rs (rendering) and commands/search.rs (matcher and PaletteState without egui). The command app.command-palette, with the D.8 binding chosen in task 04, opens a modal at the top centre with a focused search field. Results come from the registry: localized label, category, a second line with the description, and the effective shortcut right-aligned; disabled commands are shown dimmed with their reason as tooltip and cannot run; Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home and End move; Enter runs through invoke(id, Target::active(), Origin::Palette); Esc closes. With an empty query the ten most recently used commands come first (Preferences.palette_recent, persisted). Commands flagged context_only are listed too and run against Target::active(), because NFR-USE-005 asks for all commands. Mark the D.8 palette entry as registered. Out of scope: searching elements or views, context menus (14).
design: Score = subsequence match over the normalized label plus the words of description, category and id, with bonuses for word starts and contiguous runs; ties broken by recent use, then alphabetically. Normalize with unicode-normalization (NFD, strip combining marks; MIT/Apache) and lower-casing, so translated labels work as well. PaletteState { query, selected, results } is pure and unit-tested; rendering uses egui::Modal with ScrollArea::show_rows and keeps the selection in view. The palette field has focus, so the TextSafe rules of task 03 already suppress single-key shortcuts; the shortcut loop additionally skips while the palette is open, so Primary+S typed in the palette does not save. Persist only command ids in palette_recent and drop unknown ids on load.
acceptance_criteria:
- Matcher unit tests: 'fit' ranks view.fit first; 'zoom sel' finds view.zoom-selection; 'undo' finds edit.undo first; case and diacritics are ignored ('PRÖJ' finds 'Project settings…'); an empty query lists recent commands, then all enabled commands alphabetically.
- every_command_is_complete is extended with the palette hit: for each registered command (context_only ones included), searching its full English label returns it as the first result, and English labels are unique across the registry.
- kittest: the palette shortcut opens the palette with keyboard focus in the field; typing 'wall' and Enter activates the Wall tool and closes the palette; the Wall tool row shows the shortcut 'W'; Delete with an empty selection is listed dimmed and Enter on it does nothing; Esc closes without running anything; global single-key shortcuts do not fire while typing in the palette.
- Satisfied: NFR-USE-005, the palette clause of UI-017 and the D.8 palette shortcut.
notes: SRS: NFR-USE-005 UI-017 NFR-A11Y-001

title: Command registry, palette, shortcuts, string externalization and units UI
description:
Make every command an Action with description, menu and palette entry and bindable shortcut (conflict detection, keymap export/import), complete the D.8 shortcut table as commands land, add context menus, tooltips, prompt lines with live keys and the main-window shell slots (tool groups, view-control bar), externalize all user-visible strings with a locale and number-format layer, detect the OS locale on all platforms, expose unit and slope settings, and give panels accessible names. Done in increment 1 so every later epic adds string keys instead of literals.

Risks: Externalizing strings late is expensive, hence increment 1; shortcut conflicts with OS-reserved keys are checked per platform in the uniqueness test.
design: archicraft-app ui/actions.rs becomes a CommandRegistry (id, label key, description key, category, default shortcut, enabled predicate); view-local keys (R, Tab, Backspace) become Actions; an i18n module with Fluent-style key tables (English default) and number formatting through units.rs; a preferences schema version for SET-004 import. fluent (MIT/Apache) message catalogues in archicraft-app and sys-locale for STR-010; the model crate exposes message keys only.
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts every Action has label, description, menu path, palette hit and a shortcut where D.8 requires one; palette kittest; rebinding with conflict confirmation and export/import round-trip; a CI lint finds no user-visible literal outside the strings table; OS locale detection on Windows and macOS through OS APIs with tests; slope formats and area/volume units editable in the project dialog; AccessKit names on all panels (kittest query by role); the window title shows the project name and a dirty marker. The literal-string lint also covers Command::label and CommandError messages in archicraft-model (keys live in the headless crate, the catalogue in the app); a test checks every ToolState prompt string against the keys actually handled in that state (NFR-USE-003).

title: Generate door and empty-opening geometry with a shared unit kit
description:
WHY: OBJ-002 (M) requires a parametric 3D geometry per definition, DW-011 (M) the door types and empty openings with sidelights and transoms as parameters, DW-012 (M) that frame width and depth, leaf thickness, division of leaves, glazing, threshold and sill boards with depth actually shape the parts, and DW-022 (S) arched and round-headed openings. IFX-051 (S) forbids negative-determinant transforms, so mirrored units need natively mirrored geometry. OBJ-014 (S) asks for named key points and derived values. Every part must satisfy IFX-032 (closed, 2-manifold, outward oriented, no degenerate triangles), IFX-038 (own vertices per planar face, at most 65,535 points) and IFX-034 tessellation. Gap DW-011: 'Each needs 3D parts (frame, leaf/sash, glazing, sill) and plan symbols'.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/{mod.rs,registry.rs,kit.rs,layout.rs,doors.rs,openings.rs}. GeneratorInput { definition, params: ResolvedParameters, mirrored, detail: DetailLevel, tessellation }; UnitGeometry { parts: Vec<UnitPart { role: PartRole (archicraft_model::components, task 01), material, mesh: TriMesh }>, void_profile: Vec<DVec2>, layout: UnitLayout } in unit-local coordinates (x along the wall seen from the exterior, 0 at the left outer frame edge; y through the wall, 0 at the frame's exterior face, +y to the interior; z up from the bottom of the opening); trait ComponentGenerator with generate() (symbols() follows in task 06) and a registry table keyed by generator key. kit.rs: frame_ring (one extrusion along y of the outer frame rectangle with one hole per cell, U-shaped when the threshold is off), panel (leaf, sash and glazing boxes), sill_board, mirror_x (reflects x into width - x and reverses triangle winding). layout.rs: UnitLayout computes frame, cell, leaf, glazing and sill rectangles from the parameters once, shared by 3D parts, plan symbols (06) and key_points()/derived_values() (OBJ-014). doors.rs: hinged single and double (leaf_division, glazed leaf, sidelight none/left/right/both, transom, threshold, sills) and sliding single (pocket or surface leaf position, panel on a track). openings.rs: rectangular, arched (segmental arc from the rise) and round-headed (semicircle) void profiles tessellated with ProjectSettings.tessellation, no parts. With test-kinds, components/probe.rs implements 'test.probe@1': one closed Body box sized by the probe's length parameter and coloured by its material parameter (its symbols follow in task 06), so every key in KNOWN_GENERATORS has a generator. Detail: Detailed is the full part set; Simplified keeps the roles with one box per leaf and the frame ring only (the 'schematic' 3D representation doors-windows-core-09 selects for VIEW-055). Out of scope: windows (05), plan symbols (06), type caching (07), placement in walls and void cutting (doors-windows-core-03/04).
design: One unit-local frame, documented in layout.rs, so doors-windows-core places every unit with one positive-determinant transform. Parts are extruded rings and boxes only (epic risk: breadth), built with extrude.rs: add an extrude_profile_along_y wrapper that maps an (x, z) profile into (x, y, z) and fixes the orientation, so caps keep the spade CDT and faces keep their own vertices (IFX-038). Mirroring happens in the generator, never in a transform. Pitfalls: shells inside one part must not touch (double-door leaves keep a 3 mm gap, sliding panels sit on separate tracks) or the part stops being 2-manifold; use MODEL_TOLERANCE from element-kind-framework; validate geometry preconditions in layout (frame wider than half the opening is a GeometryError, not a panic). 'Clear width' here is the frame's clear opening; the passage-width refinement of DW-015 belongs to library-dw-exchange-12. Pointers: extrude.rs:18, mesh.rs:49 (MAX_MESH_POINTS) and :122 (check_closed), project.rs:29-43 (Tessellation).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/catalogue.rs: every door and opening definition at default parameters, both detail levels, mirrored false and true, yields parts that pass TriMesh::check_closed, have positive signed volume, no degenerate triangles and at most 65,535 points; hinged doors have Frame and Leaf, glazed leaves, sidelights and transoms add Glazing, sills add Sill; openings have no parts and a closed counter-clockwise void profile (DW-011, IFX-032).
- Mirrored parts equal the reflection of the unmirrored ones (vertex sets compared after x -> width - x) with equal positive volumes within 1e-9 (IFX-051 geometry side).
- Parameters drive geometry: frame_width and frame_depth change the Frame bounds; threshold off removes the bottom member; sidelight both adds two glazed cells; leaf_division 0.6 splits the leaves 0.6/0.4; sill depths extend the Sill bounds in -y and +y (DW-012).
- Arched and round-headed void profiles reach the opening height at the apex, have rise r and width/2 respectively, and respect a 2 mm chord deviation and at most 10 deg per segment at the default tessellation (DW-022, IFX-034).
- Key points and derived values: every key point a definition declares is returned, and the clear width of the default single hinged door equals width - 2 x frame_width as documented in layout.rs (OBJ-014).
- leaf_thickness changes the Leaf part's y-extent and glazing_thickness the Glazing part's y-extent; every part's material equals the material parameter of its role (frame, leaf, glazing, sill) and changing one material parameter changes only that part (DW-012 leaf thickness, glazing build-up, material per part).
- sill_inside on with sill_outside off yields one Sill board on the +y side only, the reverse one on the -y side only, and both off no Sill part (DW-012 sill boards inside and outside on/off).
- door.sliding.single with mounting pocket and with mounting surface both yield closed Frame and Leaf parts: the surface leaf runs on a track on the interior face outside the frame depth, the pocket leaf inside the frame depth, and neither touches another shell (DW-011 'pocket or surface-mounted').
- registry_matches_known_generators: the registry keys equal archicraft_model::components::KNOWN_GENERATORS, including 'test.probe@1' with test-kinds.
notes: SRS: OBJ-002 DW-011 DW-012 DW-022 IFX-051 OBJ-014. The Simplified 3D level is what doors-windows-core-04/09 call the schematic representation (VIEW-055).

title: Add the i18n module, English Fluent catalogue and literal-string lint
description:
WHY: NFR-L10N-001 (M) requires an English UI in which all user-visible strings are externalized so the UI can be translated; the German translation (NFR-L10N-002) is planned in release-candidate on top of this. Today there is no message catalogue at all (no fluent, i18n or gettext dependency): roughly 300 capitalised literals sit in archicraft-app (dialogs.rs about 90, properties.rs 42, actions.rs 31, tools.rs 30, app.rs 28, shell.rs 26) and about 110 in archicraft-model (command.rs, validate.rs, storey.rs, units.rs, element.rs). The epic runs in increment 1 precisely so that every later epic adds string keys instead of literals, which needs the mechanism and a guard in place first; the migration itself happens in tasks 02, 10, 11 and 12.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-app/src/i18n/ (mod.rs with Localizer, the tr! macro and a thread-local current localizer; catalogue.rs loading the embedded resources; pseudo.rs for an en-XA pseudo-locale) and catalogue files crates/archicraft-app/locales/en/{app,commands,dialogs,tools,model}.ftl embedded with include_str!. New dependencies fluent-bundle and unic-langid in archicraft-app only. ArchiCraftApp::ui (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs) installs the localizer at the start of every frame. New integration test crates/archicraft-app/tests/string_lint.rs (syn as a dev-dependency) that scans crates/archicraft-app/src and crates/archicraft-model/src for user-visible literals, with an allowlist file crates/archicraft-app/tests/string_lint_allow.txt (one entry per literal with a reason) and a PENDING list of files not yet migrated; it fails on literals in files that are not pending and on pending files that no longer contain any. Pilot migration: the About window (ui/dialogs.rs info_windows) and the Help menu title. Out of scope: migrating the other files (02, 10, 11, 12), the UI-language preference (07) and number formatting (08).
design: fluent-bundle (FluentBundle<FluentResource>; the non-concurrent variant is enough because the localizer is thread-local) with set_use_isolating(false), because egui renders the FSI/PDI isolation marks as missing glyphs. Plural selection uses Fluent's built-in CLDR plural rules; numbers shown to the user are never formatted by Fluent but pre-formatted with archicraft_model::units::NumberFormat (task 08) and passed as string arguments, while a separate numeric argument drives plural selection. A thread-local CURRENT: RefCell<Rc<Localizer>> is set per frame (i18n::install) and a scoped i18n::with(localizer, f) serves tests, so parallel egui_kittest harnesses on different threads can use different locales without interfering. Key convention (module docs now, docs/i18n.md in task 11): kebab-case with an area prefix (menu-, cmd-<command-id>-label and -desc, tool-, prompt-, dlg-<dialog>-, status-, browser-, model-). The pseudo-locale is built at runtime from the English bundle with set_transform (accented vowels) and wrapped in ⟦ ⟧, compiled under cfg(any(test, debug_assertions)); it powers the runtime audits of tasks 10, 11 and 16. Lint: syn::visit over each file, skipping items under #[cfg(test)], tests/ directories, attributes, tracing macros, debug_assert!, include_str! and concat!; sinks are literal arguments (including format! literals) of egui label, button, small_button, heading, selectable_label, selectable_value, checkbox, radio_value, toggle_value, menu_button, hint_text, on_hover_text, on_disabled_hover_text, selected_text, RichText::new, Button::new, Button::selectable, Label::new, Window::new, CollapsingHeader::new, and of Workspace::info/error and ArchiCraftApp::message; in archicraft-model every non-test string literal containing a space or an uppercase letter counts, except allowlisted project data (template.rs storey and material names, samples.rs). What the lint cannot see (dynamic strings, .into() on literals) is caught by the pseudo-locale audits. Pitfall: egui Id salts and test anchors stay literal; they are not user-visible.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green; cargo deny check licenses passes with the new dependencies.
- i18n unit tests: every .ftl file parses without Fluent errors; no key is defined twice across files; tr! with a count argument renders the singular and plural forms of a test message ('1 element', '3 elements'); a missing key returns a visible fallback and is logged once; rendered strings contain no Unicode isolation marks (U+2068, U+2069).
- Key-usage test: every literal key used in a tr! call under src/ exists in the English catalogue, and every catalogue key is used or matches a declared dynamic prefix (model-, cmd-).
- string_lint self-test: a synthetic snippet passing a 'Hello world' literal to ui.label is reported; ui.label(tr!(..)), Id::new('project-settings'), tracing macros, #[cfg(test)] code and serde attributes are not.
- string_lint passes on the repository with the initial PENDING list; the About window and the Help menu title are no longer pending.
- kittest: the About window heading comes from the catalogue; with the en-XA pseudo-locale installed it is wrapped in the pseudo markers.
- docs/technology-choices.md lists fluent-bundle, unic-langid and syn (dev-only) in its library table with version, release date, downloads, licence and maintainer like the existing rows (rule 5: only what the current increment needs).
- Satisfied: the externalization mechanism of NFR-L10N-001 with English as default; completion is verified in task 11.
notes:
SRS: NFR-L10N-001
Decision: Fluent rather than a hand-rolled key table, because plurals and argument reordering are needed for the German translation (NFR-L10N-002, release-candidate). Licences to confirm with cargo deny: fluent-bundle, fluent-syntax, intl_pluralrules, unic-langid, self_cell, syn (dev only); all MIT/Apache.

title: Define the built-in door, window and opening catalogue
description:
WHY: DW-011 (M): the built-in catalogue shall contain at least doors (single-leaf hinged, double-leaf hinged, single sliding pocket or surface-mounted, sidelight and/or transom as parameters), windows (fixed, side-hung, tilt-and-turn, top-hung, horizontal sliding, multi-sash windows with configurable columns and rows, each sash with its own opening type, transom or sidelight as parameters) and empty openings. DW-012 (M): doors and windows expose at least frame width and depth, leaf or sash thickness, number and division of leaves or sashes, opening angle shown in plan, glazing build-up (thickness), threshold on/off, sill boards inside and outside on/off with depth, and a material per part (frame, leaf, glazing, sill). DW-022 (S): arched and round-headed empty openings. DW-017 (S): handedness reported per a selectable convention whose default, Appendix D.6, follows DIN 107 ('a leaf is left if its hinges are on the left when viewed from the side towards which it opens'). OBJ-014 (S): named key points and derived values. Appendix D.2: door 0.90 x 2.10 m single-leaf hinged, window 1.20 x 1.40 m tilt-and-turn single sash. All are missing in the gap analysis (DW-011 effort XL).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/components/catalogue.rs fills Catalogue::builtin() with twelve version-1 definitions whose ids are Uuid::new_v5(&COMPONENT_NAMESPACE, code), COMPONENT_NAMESPACE being a new fixed UUID constant in components/catalogue.rs that never changes once released (the code base has no project-wide namespace constant today; writer.rs:46 sub_node_id derives sub-node ids from owner UUIDs), and whose generator key is '<code>@1': door.hinged.single, door.hinged.double, door.sliding.single (mounting pocket | surface) in category door with class IfcDoor; window.fixed, window.side-hung, window.tilt-turn, window.top-hung, window.sliding.horizontal (panels 2-4) and window.multi-sash (columns 1-6, rows 1-4, column_weights and row_weights as LengthList, sash_types as ChoiceList row-major over fixed, side-hung-left/right, tilt-turn-left/right, top-hung) in category window with class IfcWindow; opening.rectangular, opening.arched (rise) and opening.round-headed in category generic, class IfcOpeningElement, has_parts false, insertable as door and window openings (DW-022). A parameter kit declares the DW-012 groups once: Size (width, height, bound to OpeningWidth/OpeningHeight), Frame (frame_width, frame_depth, threshold for doors), Leaf or Sash (leaf_thickness or sash_width and sash_thickness, leaf_division for double doors, panels, grid parameters), Opening (opening_angle shown in plan, swing interior | exterior for hinged leaves, opening_side for sashes), Glazing (glazing_thickness, glazed_leaf for doors), Sill (sill_inside, sill_inside_depth, sill_outside, sill_outside_depth), Transom/Sidelight (transom, transom_height, sidelight none | left | right | both, sidelight_width) on door and window families, Materials (frame, leaf or sash, glazing, sill). Catalogue::default_parameters(definition, project) resolves material defaults by template code (SW frame and leaf, GLS glazing, NS sill) with a category fallback. Key points (exterior and interior jamb faces, clear-opening edges) and derived values (nominal and clear width and height) are declared per family (OBJ-014). components/handedness.rs: HingeSide (as seen from the exterior), SwingSide, Handing, HandednessConvention { Din107, UsHand } with ALL/code/label, handedness(convention, handing) -> label ('DIN left' / 'DIN right'; 'LH', 'RH', 'LHR', 'RHR'), Handing::from_instance(definition, parameters, mirrored); ProjectSettings.handedness with the Din107 default in Default and template.rs (D.6). KNOWN_GENERATORS lists the twelve keys (plus 'test.probe@1' with test-kinds). Out of scope: geometry (04-06), IFCX for the setting (08), UI (11), furniture and the generic box/cylinder (OBJ-001, OBJ-013 in library-dw-exchange), corner windows (DW-016), door and window tool defaults (doors-windows-core-01).
design: Definitions are Rust tables built with small builder functions (no scripting, O-12), so the catalogue is reviewable and deterministic. Generator keys are immutable: a geometry-changing revision registers a new key and bumps the definition version, so projects keep regenerating identical geometry after updates (IFX-064). Mirroring is the only handing switch for hinged leaves (hinge right = mirrored type, IFX-051); the swing side is a parameter, so a door swinging to the exterior is not a mirrored type and the sill boards stay on their sides. Pitfalls: keep parameter keys identical across families (frame_width everywhere) so relinking and the inspector map values; range checks in SI units; the DIN 107 text must be verified against the standard before release (D.6), keep it in one function. ProjectSettings.handedness needs #[serde(default)] so projects serialised before this task still deserialise. Pointers: template.rs material table (codes SW, GLS, NS, AL), project.rs:47-61 (ProjectSettings).
acceptance_criteria:
- catalogue_contains_the_dw011_set: Catalogue::builtin() holds exactly the twelve codes (three door types, six window types, three openings); ids are unique, equal Uuid::new_v5(&COMPONENT_NAMESPACE, code) and match a golden UUID list in the test; every definition's defaults validate against its schema (DW-011).
- dw012_parameters_exist: every door and window schema contains frame_width, frame_depth, a leaf or sash thickness, a leaf/sash count or division parameter, opening_angle, glazing_thickness, threshold (doors), sill_inside, sill_inside_depth, sill_outside, sill_outside_depth and the four material parameters, each with a group and a range (DW-012).
- Appendix D.2 test: door.hinged.single defaults to 0.90 x 2.10 m and window.tilt-turn to 1.20 x 1.40 m.
- window.multi-sash: the default sash_types length equals columns x rows and a mismatched list is rejected; transom and sidelight parameters exist on door and window families (DW-011 'as parameters').
- opening.arched and opening.round-headed exist with has_parts false, insertable as door and window openings, and the arched rise is limited to (0, width/2] (DW-022).
- din107_handedness_table (Appendix D.6): hinge left seen from the exterior and swing to the exterior is 'DIN left', hinge left and swing to the interior is 'DIN right', hinge right and swing to the interior is 'DIN left', hinge right and swing to the exterior is 'DIN right'; the US table, seen from the exterior, yields 'LH' for hinge left and swing to the interior, 'RH' for hinge right and swing to the interior, 'LHR' for hinge left and swing to the exterior and 'RHR' for hinge right and swing to the exterior; the template default is Din107 (DW-017).
- default_parameters picks Softwood, Glass and Natural stone from the default template and falls back by category when the codes are missing.
notes: SRS: DW-011 DW-012 DW-017 DW-022 OBJ-014 (also OBJ-002). Catalogue defaults not given by Appendix D, to record in docs/components.md as design decisions: doors frame 0.06 x 0.10 m, leaf 0.04 m, opening angle 90 deg, threshold off, glazing 0.024 m, sills off; windows frame 0.07 x 0.08 m, sash 0.06 m face x 0.07 m, glazing 0.024 m, opening angle 0 (no plan arc), inside sill on 0.20 m, outside sill on 0.15 m; transom height 0.40 m; sidelight width 0.40 m; arched rise 0.30 m.

title: Rebind shortcuts with conflict confirmation in an editable keymap
description:
WHY: UI-009 (S) requires shortcuts to be reassignable for any command, with conflict detection: reassigning detaches the shortcut from its previous command after confirmation, and a complete shortcut list is viewable. UI-017 (M) requires every command to be bindable without first adding it to a toolbar. Today there is no reassignment UI and no keymap in Preferences (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:29-55); Help > Keyboard shortcuts (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:641-667) is a read-only grid that lists only bound actions plus hand-written view-local entries.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/commands/keymap.rs: Keymap = registry defaults plus user overrides (BTreeMap<CommandId, Vec<Binding>>, an empty list meaning unbound) behind the effective_binding provider of task 04, so the shortcut loop, plan keys, menus, palette, tooltips and prompts all show the effective bindings; assign(id, binding) -> Result<(), Conflict { other }>, reassign(id, binding) detaching the other command, remove, reset(id) and reset_all; OS-reserved and fixed bindings are rejected with a reason. Bindings serialize as platform-neutral text ('Primary+Shift+Z'); Preferences gains the keymap overrides with #[serde(default)]. Replace the shortcut grid with crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/keymap_dialog.rs: a searchable table of every registered command (category, label, bindings, a marker for changed defaults, unbound commands included); Record captures the next key chord (Esc cancels, modifier-only presses are ignored); a conflict asks whether to reassign '{shortcut}' from '{command}' with Reassign and Cancel; Remove, Reset and Reset all; a read-only section lists mouse and trackpad navigation, which are not commands. Out of scope: export and import (07), mouse-button bindings.
design: Store egui::Key by its name (Key::name and Key::from_name) so files stay readable and portable; Primary maps to Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, which keeps an exported keymap valid on another operating system (SET-004). While recording, pause the global shortcut loop (flag on the app) and swallow the captured event. Effective bindings are cached in a HashMap rebuilt on every change. Use a Grid inside ScrollArea::show_rows, or egui_extras TableBuilder pinned with the egui family at =0.36.2 if a sortable table is wanted (the technology choices list egui_extras for tables). Pitfall: two commands may legitimately share a binding in non-overlapping scopes (Backspace in Canvas for delete and in PointInput for remove-last); the dialog shows the scope next to such bindings.
acceptance_criteria:
