- Keymap unit tests: assigning a binding that another command in an overlapping scope uses returns Conflict naming that command; reassign moves the binding and leaves the other command without it; the same binding in non-overlapping scopes is accepted; OS-reserved and fixed bindings are rejected; reset and reset_all restore the defaults; Binding text round-trips for every key used by a default and displays as '⇧⌘Z' on macOS and 'Ctrl+Shift+Z' elsewhere.
- Persistence: overrides survive a save and load of preferences.json; unknown command ids are dropped with a warning.
- kittest: in Help > Keyboard shortcuts, search 'Slab tool', Record, press W: the conflict prompt names the Wall tool; Reassign; afterwards W activates the Slab tool, the Wall tool row shows no shortcut and its Design menu item shows none.
- The dialog lists every registered command including unbound ones (row count equals the registry size).
- Bindability (UI-017): a loop over the registry assigns a free test chord to every registered command (palette_only and context_only ones included); feeding that chord to the shortcut loop invokes exactly that command (recorder, handlers not run).
- Satisfied: UI-009 and the bindability clause of UI-017.
notes: SRS: UI-009 UI-017

title: List missing definitions and relink them from a catalogue picker
description:
WHY: OBJ-005 (M): the system shall list all missing definitions and allow relinking them. UI-012 (M) names missing definitions as a problems-panel category, which element-kind-framework left to this epic. The epic also provides catalogue basics in the app, while the full browser with thumbnails, search and previews (DW-014) belongs to library-dw-exchange. Today the problems panel lists failed geometry and load problems only (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:848-883).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/catalogue.rs: definition_picker(ui, project, filter) listing built-in and embedded definitions grouped by category with name, version and source (built-in or embedded) and a plain text filter, reusable by doors-windows-core-08's definition choice. ui/dialogs.rs: a 'Missing definitions' window (Dialogs flag, Action::MissingDefinitions in actions.rs, a Project menu item in shell.rs) with one row per Project::missing_definitions() entry: name, id and version, reason (not embedded, unknown generator), instance count, 'Select instances' (selection plus Request::ZoomTo) and 'Relink...' opening the picker filtered to compatible definitions and executing Command::RelinkDefinition; the window opens automatically after a file with missing definitions is opened and the status bar counts them. UI-012 is partial (problems_panel, dialogs.rs:848-883, lists geometry failures and load problems; element-kind-framework-14 adds the References and File sections and reserves ProblemSource::Definition): extend it by filling ProblemSource::Definition with a 'Missing definitions' section, one clickable entry per definition (selects and zooms to its instances) and a link to the window; the IntegrityProblem entries for missing definitions from task 02 appear only there, not again under References. Out of scope: thumbnails, previews and library search (DW-014), linked library folders (OBJ-007), upgrades (OBJ-008).
design: 'Add a dialog' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md; the window acts immediately through commands (no draft). Compatibility rules stay in the RelinkDefinition command (task 02); the UI only filters. Pitfalls: compute the list per revision, not per frame, if profiling shows cost; zooming relies on placeholder bounds from task 07; keep the picker free of egui_extras thumbnails so library-dw-exchange can extend it. Pointers: dialogs.rs:35-56 (Dialogs), :76-85 (Dialogs::show), :848-883 (problems_panel), actions.rs:7 (Action), shell.rs:105-110 (Project menu) and :167-190 (status_bar and its problem count), workspace.rs:34-40 (Request), :90 (Workspace::replace_document), app.rs:709-718 (handle_requests).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: opening crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/missing-definition.ifcx through the app's open path (or Workspace::replace_document with the read project and its problems) shows the Missing definitions window with both definitions and their instance counts; 'Select instances' selects exactly those elements and requests a zoom (OBJ-005 list).
- kittest: 'Relink...' and choosing door.hinged.single executes RelinkDefinition, the window empties, ModelGeometry has no placeholder left and undo brings the placeholders back (OBJ-005 relink).
- Picker test: the door filter lists the three built-in doors plus compatible embedded definitions and no windows; the text filter narrows by name.
- The problems panel lists the missing definitions with counts under ProblemSource::Definition, the References section does not repeat them, and the status-bar problem count includes each affected instance once (UI-012 missing-definitions clause).
- cargo test, clippy and fmt are green.
notes: SRS: OBJ-005 (also UI-012).

title: Generate plan symbols per detail level for every catalogue type
description:
WHY: DW-013 (M): plan symbols shall be generated from the parameters, never one definition per size; doors show the leaf and swing arc or the sliding direction, windows show frame, sash and glass lines and sill boards, and the symbol masks the host's cut fill inside the opening. DSP-015 (S) requires two plan detail levels (simplified, detailed) and OBJ-014 (S) plan symbols per detail level; DW-017 (S) reports handedness in plan labels; DW-012 makes the opening angle a plan parameter; OBJ-002 needs a parametric plan symbol per definition. Gap DW-013: 'No plan symbol generation; PlanElement has no symbol/annotation geometry (geometry/plan.rs:23-33)'.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/symbols.rs: SymbolPrimitive { Line { a, b, role, style }, Arc { centre, radius, start, sweep, role, style }, Polygon { points, role, filled }, Arrow { from, to }, Mask { x0, x1 }, HandednessLabel { at, handing } } with SymbolRole { Frame, Leaf, Sash, Glass, Sill, Swing, Threshold, Head } and LineStyle { Cut, Projected, Overhead } (nominal classes assuming the cut plane passes through the unit; doors-windows-core-04 reclassifies by height), in the unit-local plan coordinates of task 04; ComponentGenerator::symbols(input) for every generator, derived from UnitLayout so the symbol always matches the 3D parts. Content: hinged doors, simplified: leaf line at opening_angle from the hinge jamb and the swing arc; detailed: jamb frame rectangles, leaf rectangle of leaf_thickness rotated by opening_angle, arc, threshold line, sidelight frame and glass lines, sill boards; double doors: two leaves per leaf_division; the swing parameter puts the arc on the +y or -y side. Sliding: leaf rectangle on its track, an Arrow in the sliding direction, the pocket part in Overhead style. Windows, simplified: frame lines and one glass line per cell column; detailed: frame and mullion rectangles, sash rectangles, glass double lines at glazing_thickness, sill boards (Projected) with their depths, sash arcs when opening_angle > 0. Probe (test-kinds): an outline rectangle in Simplified and the outline plus a diagonal cross in Detailed, standing in for objects (DSP-015 names doors, windows and objects). Empty openings: the Mask, plus dashed Head lines for arched and round-headed openings in detailed. Every unit emits Mask { 0, width } (DW-013 masking clause; doors-windows-core-04 extends it across the host thickness) and a HandednessLabel for every side-hinged leaf or sash. Mirroring reflects x and the arc sweep. Out of scope: painting (10), host placement and cut/overhead classification (doors-windows-core-04), pens and line types (plan-attributes), lyon tessellation (plan-renderer).
design: Renderer-agnostic primitives (DW-013) so the lyon pipeline of plan-renderer can take them over without touching the generators; arcs stay analytic (centre, radius, sweep) and are tessellated at draw time. Labels carry the Handing, not text, so changing the project convention never invalidates cached type geometry (task 07). Pitfalls: mirroring is only in x, so a door swinging to the exterior is a parameter change, not a mirrored symbol; keep the y origin at the frame's exterior face so doors-windows-core can add the reveal offset directly; avoid per-frame allocations by generating symbols once per type (cached in task 07).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/symbols.rs: for every catalogue definition at default parameters, both detail levels and mirrored false/true, the symbol is non-empty, all coordinates are finite and a Mask spans [0, width]; for every door and window the detailed symbol has strictly more primitives than the simplified one (DSP-015, OBJ-014).
- Single hinged door, swing interior, opening_angle 90 deg: one Arc centred at the hinge-side clear edge with radius equal to the leaf width and a 90 deg sweep on the +y side; mirrored: centre at the opposite jamb and reversed sweep; opening_angle 30 deg gives a 30 deg sweep and a leaf line ending at that angle (DW-012 'opening angle shown in plan', DW-013).
- Double door: two arcs whose radii follow leaf_division; sliding door: one Arrow pointing in the sliding direction and no Arc (DW-013).
- Detailed window: frame rectangles of frame_width x frame_depth at both jambs, glass lines glazing_thickness apart, sill polygons extending the sill depths in -y and +y when enabled and absent when disabled (DW-013).
- The same definition at widths 0.80 m and 1.00 m yields symbols that follow the layout, proving there is no per-size definition (DW-013 'generated from the parameters').
- HandednessLabel exists for hinged doors and side-hinged sashes and carries Handing::from_instance; formatting it with handedness(Din107, ...) matches the D.6 table of task 03 (DW-017 plan label data); empty openings emit only the Mask and, in detailed, Head lines for arched and round-headed types (DW-022).
- Detailed windows draw one sash rectangle per operable sash and none for fixed cells, so a 3 x 2 multi-sash grid with two fixed cells shows four sash rectangles (DW-013 'frame, sash and glass lines').
- With test-kinds the probe symbol differs between Simplified and Detailed (DSP-015 two detail levels for objects).
notes: SRS: DW-013 DSP-015 OBJ-014 DW-017 OBJ-002 (also DW-012, DW-022).

title: Build context menus for tabs, browser items and canvases
description:
WHY: UI-005 (M) requires context menus on the canvas, on project-browser items and on tabs that offer the commands relevant to what was right-clicked. Today tabs have no context menu (the egui_tiles Behavior in crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:727-788 adds none), 3D-view items and the Project section of the browser have none (ui/browser.rs:86-116), and the plan and 3D canvas menus are hand-built button lists (views/plan.rs:728-779, views/view3d.rs:265-293) that duplicate command logic.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/context_menus.rs: ContextTarget {PlanCanvas { storey, hovered }, View3dCanvas { view, hovered }, Tab(Pane), BrowserStorey(StoreyId), BrowserView(ViewId), BrowserProject} and entries(target, &CommandCtx) -> Vec<MenuEntry> (command with target, separator, submenu), rendered by one function with labels, shortcuts and enabled states from the registry. Tabs get Close tab, Close other tabs, Switch between plan and 3D, Fit to window and Zoom to selection through Behavior::on_tab_button (app.rs:751), with the new commands view.close-tab and view.close-other-tabs; storey items use the storey commands of task 13 with the item as target; 3D-view items offer Open; the Project section offers Project settings, Storeys, Layers and Materials; the plan and 3D canvas menus are rebuilt from entries() with their current content plus a display-mode submenu in 3D, after which views/plan.rs and views/view3d.rs leave the lint PENDING list (task 10 externalized their other strings). Out of scope: saved-view commands (rename, delete, settings, save as view, VIEW-003), which plan-views-browser-10 adds through entries(); the edit palette at handles (edit-reshape-palette-07).
design: Keep entries() data-only, so plan-views-browser-10 and later epics extend menus by adding entries for their targets. egui_tiles passes the tab button response to on_tab_button; attach response.context_menu there and push the chosen (CommandId, Target) to ws.requests so the command runs after the tile tree is laid out (closing tabs inside the tree callback would invalidate it). Close other tabs closes panes of the same tab group only.
acceptance_criteria:
- entries() unit test: for each target kind the expected command ids appear and each exists in the registry; a canvas target with a hovered unselected element selects it first (current behaviour, plan.rs:741-745).
- kittest: a secondary click on the 'Plan: 00 Ground floor' tab shows 'Close tab' and 'Close other tabs'; Close other tabs leaves one tab; a secondary click on '3D perspective' in the browser shows 'Open'; on a storey it shows 'Insert storey above'.
- Context-menu items show shortcut text and use the same enabled predicates as the menus (Delete is disabled without a selection).
- string_lint passes with views/plan.rs and views/view3d.rs removed from PENDING.
- Satisfied: UI-005 for canvases, tabs and the current browser items.
notes: SRS: UI-005

title: Add UI language, author e-mail and default units to Preferences
description:
WHY: SET-001 (M) lists the user preferences stored outside projects (PRJ-007): UI language and theme; navigation scheme; autosave interval and number of backups; snap radius, dwell time and angle increment; tracker behaviour; author name (written to the IFCX header, an e-mail address only if the user enters one); default units for new projects. Existing and kept: theme, autosave_minutes, backups, snap_radius, angle_increment_deg and author in Preferences (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:29-55), stored as preferences.json in the data directory (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/mod.rs:46-48), edited in the Preferences dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:679-762); the author reaches the header through Document::to_bytes (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:134-143). Missing: the UI language (impossible before the catalogue of task 01), an optional e-mail, and default units: New always uses default_metric_project (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:248-249). Dwell time (point-input-snapping-09), tracker behaviour (point-input-snapping-05) and the navigation scheme (3d-input-navigation, SET-003) are added by their owners.

WHAT: Preferences gains language: LanguageChoice { System, Tag(String) }, negotiated with fluent-langneg against the compiled catalogues (English in v1, en-XA in debug builds; System reads the OS tag through sys-locale) and applied by swapping the localizer of task 01 on the next frame; author_email: Option<String>, written as 'Name <e-mail>' into the IFCX header only when non-empty, autosave files included; default_units: UnitSettings, applied by Then::New and Then::Close in ArchiCraftApp (both create a fresh document, app.rs:248-249) on top of default_metric_project(). Preferences dialog: a Language row, an E-mail row under Author, and a 'Default units for new projects' group that reuses widgets::unit_settings_editor of task 09. The three fields are portable in the export envelope of task 07. Record fluent-langneg (and sys-locale, shared with task 08) in docs/technology-choices.md. Out of scope: per-template units (templates-presets, PRJ-012), dwell time, tracker behaviour and navigation scheme.
design: Language negotiation: sys-locale gives the OS tag (the dependency is shared with task 08), fluent-langneg (Apache/MIT) picks the best available catalogue with English as the fallback; changing the language swaps the thread-local localizer of task 01 on the next frame. Default units reuse UnitSettings and the editor that task 09 factors out of the Project settings dialog, so both pickers stay identical. Pitfalls: keep #[serde(default)] on every new field so version-2 files of task 07 without them still load; store an empty e-mail as None; the e-mail must disappear from autosave headers too once the user removes it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Regression: theme, autosave interval, backups, snap radius, angle increment and author still round-trip through preferences.json and the dialog; creating, saving and reopening a project changes nothing in preferences.json except the recent list, and the project file carries no preference other than the header author ('stored outside projects').
- Language: with System and OS tag de-AT the negotiation falls back to English in v1; choosing en-XA in a debug build and pressing OK shows the pseudo markers on the next frame without a restart; importing an export that carries a language applies it at once.
- E-mail: with an e-mail entered, the written header author is 'Name <e-mail>'; without it, or after removing it, only the name, also in the next autosave file; golden files are unchanged.
- Default units: a project created with New after setting the default length unit to Millimetre and the slope format to Percent has settings.units.length == Millimeter and slope == Percent; Close then New uses them too; opening an existing project keeps its own units.
- The export round trip of task 07 includes language, author_email and default_units; a version-2 file without them loads with defaults.
- Satisfied: the language, author/e-mail and default-units items of SET-001; with the existing items only dwell time, tracker behaviour and navigation scheme remain, owned by point-input-snapping-09, point-input-snapping-05 and 3d-input-navigation (recorded at the epic exit).
notes:
SRS: SET-001
Split from task 07 so that the SET-004 file format and import and the SET-001 fields are separate, reviewable units of about one day each.

title: Draw region filters in plan and show inside or outside in 3D
description:
WHY: VIEW-044 (S): a region filter drawn in plan (rectangle or polygon) shows what lies inside or outside it, either trimming elements at its boundary or keeping them whole, and elements cut by it stay selectable. VIEW-040 (M) also asks to show only 'the contents of a marquee' in 3D; 05 covers a marquee dragged in the 3D view, this task the marquee drawn in plan. Gap row VIEW-044: missing.

WHAT: A '3D region' input in plan panes: rectangle by two corners or polygon by clicks closed with Enter or double-click, drawn as a dashed overlay (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs). On completion a popup offers 'Show inside in 3D', 'Show outside in 3D', 'Trim at boundary' and 'Isolate contents' (isolates the elements inside or crossing, the VIEW-040 marquee clause); the target is the most recently active 3D pane, or the default perspective view opened for it. The region goes into that pane's restrictions.region. Keep-whole classification in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/clip.rs: each element is inside, outside or crossing from its bodies' xy projection against the polygon; inside + keep whole shows inside and crossing elements, outside + keep whole shows outside and crossing; trimming uses the shader region test (06) and the region edge caps (15); 'Trim at boundary' is disabled with a tooltip for polygons with more than 16 edges (validation of 01). Picking of cut elements comes from 06. Out of scope: the persistent selection marquee of SEL-005 (templates-presets) and vertical limits (the region is an infinite vertical prism in v1).
design: Input reuses the plan point-input path (ToolState and snap in views/tools.rs, rectangle() at tools.rs:315; or the point-input service if point-input-snapping has landed) as a view tool that creates no Command. Classification with geo (Intersects, Contains) after a convex-hull early-out; cache per (revision, region) in the pane. The polygon is uploaded to the per-view storage buffer of 04 and 06. Pitfalls: the plan's camera may be rotated (plan-views-browser-12), so convert points with the plan camera's to_world; region polygons are stored counter-clockwise; polygon input must not fight click selection (it starts only once the tool is chosen). Pointers: plan.rs:364-780 (input, overlays, draw_snap_marker), clip.rs (06).
acceptance_criteria:
- clip.rs unit tests classify walls fully inside, crossing and outside an L-shaped polygon correctly.
- kittest: drawing a rectangle in plan and choosing 'Show inside in 3D' sets restrictions.region on the last active 3D pane (side Inside, trim false); 'Isolate contents' sets the isolation to the inside and crossing walls.
- Headless goldens 'region_trimmed' and 'region_whole': with trimming, walls crossing the boundary are cut at it with caps; keeping them whole shows the same walls complete.
- Clicking the visible part or the cut face of a trimmed wall in 3D selects it (VIEW-044 selectable clause).
- A 17-edge polygon can be shown inside or outside kept whole, while 'Trim at boundary' is disabled with the reason.
- Esc cancels the region input step by step; a self-intersecting polygon is refused with a message; Project.revision is unchanged.
- Satisfies VIEW-044 and the plan-marquee source of VIEW-040's marquee clause (the 3D marquee is in 05).
notes: SRS: VIEW-044 VIEW-040

title: Add a headless 3D render harness with pixel readback and goldens
description:
WHY: The epic's acceptance relies on images: 'a storey range with trimming shows capped bodies (snapshot)' (VIEW-041) and 'two cut planes plus a section box render closed caps in uniform or material colour' (VIEW-042). Today there is no image test (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs has label tests only), the CI runners have no GPU adapter (.github/workflows/ci.yml), Renderer3d::new requires an egui_wgpu::RenderState (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:270) and the rendered texture can only be composited by egui, never read back. 3D snapshots are otherwise first planned for 3d-display-styles in increment 3.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/Cargo.toml: enable the egui_kittest dev-dependency features wgpu and snapshot (today only eframe) and add image as a dev-dependency at the version egui_kittest 0.36.2 uses. Headless device: egui_kittest::wgpu::create_render_state(egui_kittest::wgpu::default_wgpu_setup(), RendererOptions::default()) returns a real egui_wgpu::RenderState that prefers software adapters, so Renderer3d::new and ensure_viewport (render3d.rs:270, 438) work unchanged and no constructor split is needed. render3d.rs: add COPY_SRC to the resolve texture (create_targets, render3d.rs:395-436) and Renderer3d::read_rgba(&Viewport) -> image::RgbaImage behind a test-support cargo feature. New crates/archicraft-app/tests/support/render3d.rs: one shared RenderState per test binary, scene from a fixture project, camera preset, display mode and (later) restrictions, comparison through egui_kittest::image_snapshot_options against PNGs in crates/archicraft-app/tests/snapshots/3d/. New crates/archicraft-app/tests/render3d_golden.rs with the first golden: two_storey_shell, isometric parallel, shaded with edges, no restrictions. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, matrix ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest, macos-latest): if plan-renderer-07 has landed, reuse its software-adapter setup (lavapipe on Ubuntu, WARP on Windows, Metal on macOS, diff upload, kittest.toml, docs/testing.md); otherwise add exactly that minimal subset here (new kittest.toml, new .gitattributes, new docs/testing.md with a 3D section). Out of scope: egui overlays in goldens, display styles.
design: Rendering is already offscreen (render3d.rs:395-436 create_targets, 501-580 render) and the kittest render state is an ordinary egui_wgpu::RenderState, so only the readback is new. Readback: copy_texture_to_buffer from the resolve texture with bytes_per_row aligned to 256 (COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW_ALIGNMENT), map_async and device.poll(wait) in tests only. Keep goldens text-free (the overlay label of view3d.rs:248 is egui, not part of the texture) so they do not depend on font rasterisation. Tolerances: reuse kittest.toml from plan-renderer-07 (threshold 0.6, 0 failed pixels on lavapipe, up to 0.1 % elsewhere) and record 3D observations in docs/testing.md; MSAA fringes differ between rasterisers. Pitfall: wgpu device creation per test is slow on lavapipe, so share one RenderState per test binary through a OnceLock.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test -p archicraft-app --test render3d_golden passes on ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest and macos-latest against one shared PNG set; the adapter info is logged and, with CI=true on Linux and Windows, DeviceType::Cpu is asserted.
- Pixel helper tests: a corner pixel equals the clear colour; the pixel at the projected centre of the ground-floor slab is a face colour.
- A deliberately changed material colour makes the golden fail on all three platforms and CI uploads the diff image (verified once, noted in the pull request).
- Snapshots are at most 200 kB each and *.png is marked binary in .gitattributes.
- Without CI=true and without any adapter the tests skip with a logged reason; in CI a missing adapter fails.
- Existing UI tests and the application's rendering path are unchanged (no readback in the UI path).
notes:
SRS: VIEW-041 VIEW-042
If plan-renderer-07 lands later, it must keep this harness and only add its plan-specific support module; the bless job (UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 on ubuntu) covers both directories.

title: Measure tool for distance, angle and height in plan and 3D
description:
WHY: A measure tool shall measure distances (cumulative along several picked points), angles and height differences in 2D and 3D views, using snapping (INP-001), reporting in working units and creating no model element (MEA-001). Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for 'measure', and AS-04 ends with 'Then measure it': measured lengths and angles must equal the typed values exactly at 0.1 mm and 0.01 degrees. The area of a picked polygon (MEA-006) is a further mode of this tool and follows in task 14. The gap analysis lists MEA-001 missing: ToolKind has no Measure (views/tools.rs:13-17) and Action has no measure command (ui/actions.rs:7-38); the building blocks exist: format_length and format_angle (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:283, 334) and the PointInput service of point-input-snapping.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/measure.rs: MeasureTool implementing InputConsumer in plan and 3D with the modes Distance (polyline with cumulative total, last segment, ΔX/ΔY/ΔZ, horizontal distance and slope), Angle (three points; in 3D the spatial angle and its projection on the working plane) and Height (ΔZ between two points with both elevations relative to project zero and to the active storey), in a mode enum that task 14 extends by Area. The tool never returns Outcome::Execute. A measure readout (status-line section and a small floating panel with copy to clipboard) formats through units.rs with the preference number format; measure lines are drawn in plan (plan.rs overlay) and 3D (Overlay3d) and cleared on Esc or tool switch. Add ToolKind::Measure, Action::ToolMeasure with a default shortcut, a toolbox button and a Design menu entry (ui/shell.rs:100-104), the tool's script in the task 08 registry test, and the measure step of crates/archicraft-app/tests/as04_precision.rs (created by point-input-snapping-15). Out of scope: the Area mode (14), selection quantities and derived values (MEA-002, MEA-003, properties-and-dialogs), union area (MEA-004, Could).
design: Values stay f64 end to end; formatting happens only in the readout (NFR-ACC-005). The readout reuses the tracker strings of point-input-snapping-05. The tool uses the step API with Expect::Point and repeat = true (polyline), its own mode buttons in the properties strip through tool_modes (ui/properties.rs:745), and does not declare needs_horizontal, so in 3D it receives full 3D points (task 08). Spatial angles use atan2(|a x b|, a.b) for accuracy near 0 and 180 degrees. Provisional shortcut: M (free today, actions.rs:118-143; check against commands-and-l10n's registry if it has landed). Pitfall: the AS-04 closing segment's direction is printed by format_angle without normalisation (-126.87 degrees, see point-input-snapping-15); compare formatted strings with the same function.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests on the consumer without egui: (0,0) -> (3,4) -> (3,10) reports total 11.000 m and last segment 6.000 m; for the 3D segment (0,0,0) -> (3,4,1.2) ΔX/ΔY/ΔZ, the horizontal distance 5.000 m and the slope are exact within 1e-12; the angle at (0,0) between (1,0) and (0,1) is 90.00 degrees; the 3D angle between (1,0,0) and (0,0,1) is 90.00 degrees and its projection on a horizontal working plane is reported separately; the height between z = 0.000 and z = 3.000 is 3.000 m with both elevations shown relative to project zero and to the active storey.
- No Command is ever produced: after 50 measure operations in plan and 3D project.revision and the undo count are unchanged (MEA-001 'creates no model element').
- Snapping (INP-001): in plan the measure points snap to wall nodes through the shared PointInput; in 3D a slab corner snapped through task 10 gives its exact model point and a height measured from it is exact.
- AS-04 measure step in as04_precision.rs: each wall of the typed closed polygon is measured by snapping to its nodes in plan and on the horizontal working plane in 3D; the formatted lengths at 0.1 mm and angles at 0.01 degrees are identical to the typed values (epic acceptance 'AS-04 step').
- An imperial project reports feet-inches through units.rs; a comma-decimal preference formats with commas (NFR-ACC-005: rounding only for display).
- kittest: the toolbox shows 'Measure', its shortcut activates it, the readout shows 'Total', 'Angle' and 'Height' labels, and Esc clears the measure lines; shortcuts_are_unique and appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts (actions.rs) include ToolMeasure.
- Satisfies MEA-001 and the measuring part of AS-04.
notes:
SRS: MEA-001
Appendix D.1: metre with 3 decimals, decimal degrees with 2 decimals; Appendix D.8: measure needs a default shortcut (provisional M).

title: Colour caps by element material and cap region boundaries
description:
WHY: VIEW-042 (M): cut solids are displayed closed with a uniform colour or the elements' own materials; 07 delivers the uniform colour only. VIEW-044 (S): a region filter may trim elements at its boundary, and those cut solids must be closed as well, since VIEW-042's capped display applies to every cut solid. Gap rows VIEW-042 and VIEW-044: missing.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs and views/shader.wgsl: material colour through one auxiliary single-sample back-face pass (front faces culled) into an Rgba8 + depth target that keeps the nearest back face beyond the ray's entry into the kept region, sampled by fs_cap with textureLoad when CapStyle::Material (01) is set; the element slot (04) is written to the auxiliary target too, so an id pass from selection-transforms-06 (if present) picks cut elements on their caps. Region boundary caps for trimmed regions: one parity and cap pass per polygon edge (01 limits trimming regions to 16 edges), the parity geometry clipped by that edge's vertical half-space only, the cap quad spanning only the edge segment and clipped by every resolved plane and the element flags; the per-pass uniform of 07 gains the region-edge mode. Out of scope: region input and keep-whole classification (12), hatched caps.
design: Material colour: in the auxiliary pass the fragment computes t_in from the inverse view-projection and discards back faces before it, so the nearest remaining back face belongs to the body containing the cap point; the target is single-sample and read at the pixel centre (1-px colour fringes at MSAA edges acceptable). Region edges: clipping the parity geometry by the edge's own half-space (kept side = left of a counter-clockwise edge for Inside, right for Outside) gives the correct parity at every point of that edge also for non-convex polygons, because only surfaces on one side of the edge's line are counted; restricting the cap quad to the segment keeps caps off the parts of the line that are not boundary. Skip edges whose segment prism misses the scene bounds. Pointers: render3d.rs (07's cap pipelines and per-pass uniform), shader.wgsl fs_cap, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/clip.rs (06).
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless golden 'one_plane_material': two_storey_shell with one vertical cut plane and CapStyle::Material; a probe inside a brick wall's cap matches that wall material's shaded colour and a probe inside the slab's cap the slab material's, within the kittest tolerance.
- Golden 'two_planes_and_box_material': the configuration of 07's 'two_planes_and_box_uniform' in material colour, closed at every probe.
- Golden 'region_caps': an L-shaped trimming region over part of two_storey_shell shows closed caps at probes on a convex and on a reflex polygon edge, in uniform and in material colour.
- A camera whose eye lies inside a wall shows no material-cap artefacts outside it; hidden and filtered elements contribute no caps.
- Draw counter: 1 + 2 x intersecting planes scene draws with material caps, plus 1 (uniform) or 2 (material) per region edge whose segment prism meets the scene bounds.
- The frame time with material caps, 8 planes, the box and a 16-edge trimming region is recorded against NFR-PERF-003 in the pull request; the goldens of 03 and 07 are unchanged.
- Satisfies the material-colour clause of VIEW-042 and the closed display of region-trimmed solids (VIEW-044).
notes: SRS: VIEW-042 VIEW-044

title: 3D view filters, hidden elements, cut planes and section box as GPU clip planes
description:
Per-view hide, isolate and show-all, kind and storey-range filters with trimming, user cut planes (two points or numeric, bindable to a storey) and an interactive section box with capped cut solids, region filters drawn in plan, the persistent restriction indicator with a one-command reset, exploded storeys, and the guarantee that none of this changes the model or the standard IFCX content. Implemented as GPU clip planes with a stencil cap pass in shader.wgsl, display-only, so it needs no Boolean kernel and ships in increment 1 as soon as saved views exist (VIEW-040/042/043 are Must and are not named by any Appendix F increment).

Risks: Capping with several planes and a box in the shader: stencil caps per plane, only when restrictions are active. Exploded storeys (Could) as a per-storey transform offset, time-boxed.
design: archicraft-app views/view3d.rs Restrictions in ViewState; views/shader.wgsl gains up to eight clip planes plus a box in uniforms and a stencil-based cap pass per plane; filters evaluated on the cached GpuScene per element, caps coloured from the style; actions for the D.8 view shortcuts; the model is untouched (decisions D-7, IFX-068). Kernel clipping is not required; trimmed storey ranges use clip planes at storey elevations.
acceptance_criteria: kittest for hide, isolate and show-all honouring layer visibility; a storey range with trimming shows capped bodies (snapshot); two cut planes plus a section box with draggable handles render closed caps in uniform or material colour; a cut plane bound to storey plus offset follows a storey edit; a region filter drawn in plan keeps cut elements selectable; the indicator appears whenever any restriction is active and the reset clears all; writer test: the file is byte-identical with and without restrictions (VIEW-047); restrictions are stored in saved views and re-applied.
notes: SRS: VIEW-040 VIEW-041 VIEW-042 VIEW-043 VIEW-044 VIEW-046 VIEW-047 VIEW-061

title: Clip faces and edges by planes in shader.wgsl; make picking clip-aware
description:
WHY: VIEW-042 (M) cut planes and the section box, VIEW-041 (M) trimming at storey range limits and VIEW-044 (S) trimming at a region boundary all remove parts of bodies from the display. The epic implements this as display-only GPU clipping with no Boolean kernel, so the model is never touched (VIEW-047). VIEW-044 also requires that elements cut by the filter stay selectable, which needs picking that knows the kept region. Today shader.wgsl and Uniforms (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:67-73) have no clip planes and the depth buffer has no stencil (render3d.rs:21).

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/clip.rs (pure): HalfSpace, ClipRegion {planes, region: Option<RegionPrism {polygon, side}>} with contains(p), ray_interval(origin, dir) -> Option<(t_in, t_out)> for the convex part, plane-AABB section polygon (for the caps of 07 and 15) and plane culling against the scene bounds; TriMesh::ray_hits (all hits, sorted) in mesh.rs next to ray_hit (mesh.rs:181). render3d.rs and shader.wgsl: uniforms planes: array<vec4<f32>, 16> plus plane_count; the region polygon (up to 256 vertices) and its side in the per-view storage buffer of 04; VertexOut carries the local position; fs_fill and fs_line discard fragments outside the kept region; DEPTH_FORMAT becomes Depth24PlusStencil8 to prepare the cap pass. views/view3d.rs pick: the nearest admitted hit with t >= t_in inside the region; when the ray's entry point into the kept region lies inside a body (odd number of that body's hits beyond t_in) the body is hit at t_in, so clicking a cut face selects the cut element. Out of scope: caps (07, 15), all UI.
design: Fragment discard instead of hardware clip distances (Features::CLIP_DISTANCES is not available on every backend); discard disables early depth, so guard it with a uniform branch on plane_count and the region flag. Plane convention n.p + d >= 0 kept (01). Positions are uploaded relative to the scene origin (render3d.rs:121), so convert each plane on the CPU in f64: d_local = d + n.origin. Region test: even-odd crossing in xy against the polygon from the storage buffer, with its bounding box as early-out. Depth24PlusStencil8 has less depth precision than Depth32Float: retune face_bias (render3d.rs:341) and check that edges do not z-fight in the golden. The kept region of user planes, box and storey trims is the intersection of half-spaces (convex), which ray_interval relies on; the region prism is tested separately per hit. Pointers: shader.wgsl (whole file), render3d.rs:59-75, 270-380, 501-580; view3d.rs:75-91.
acceptance_criteria:
- clip.rs unit tests: ray interval through a box; culling of a plane that misses the bounds; the plane-AABB section polygon has 3 to 6 vertices, counter-clockwise seen along the normal; inside and outside tests for an L-shaped (non-convex) region; a point on a plane within 0.01 mm (NFR-ACC-003) counts as kept.
- mesh.rs: ray_hits returns both hits of the unit box in ascending order.
- Headless render (03 harness): a horizontal plane at +1.50 m through samples::storey_with_walls_and_slab() removes every wall face and edge pixel above the projected cut line; the same fixture translated by 10 km renders the cut at the same pixel rows (planes converted to the local origin).
- Picking: a click where a removed wall part was returns what lies behind; a click on the open cut face of a wall selects the wall.
- With plane_count = 0 and no region the golden of 03 is unchanged.
notes: SRS: VIEW-042 VIEW-041 VIEW-044 VIEW-047

title: Mirror-about-plane tool with preview in plan and 3D views
description:
WHY: EDT-022 requires mirroring about a plane in 3D to be usable, which needs an interactive command that defines the plane with the same definitions as the working plane (INP-015) and works in 3D views like every edit command (VIEW-025). Task 13 provides the model reflection and the command; nothing in the app reaches it, and neither the Edit menu (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:59) nor the 3D context menu (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:265-291) offers a mirror.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/mirror3d.rs: an InputConsumer acting on the current selection whose plane comes from the task 09 definitions (three points, picked face, vertical through two points, horizontal at a typed elevation, current working plane), chosen with mode buttons through tool_modes (ui/properties.rs:745); it does not declare needs_horizontal, so in 3D it receives full 3D points (task 08). A live preview draws the mirrored outlines (ElementKind::mirrored of task 13, evaluated through archicraft-geometry) in plan and through Overlay3d in 3D, plus the plane as a translucent patch; the copy variant toggles on a modifier and the cursor shows it (CursorState::Copy of point-input-snapping-03). Commit executes the task 13 command as one undo step; an Unsupported result shows the refusal naming the kind in the status line, and top_fixed is reported as an info message. Add Action::MirrorPlane with a 'Mirror about plane' entry in the Edit menu and the 3D context menu, and the consumer's script in the task 08 registry test. Out of scope: mirror about a two-point axis (EDT-001, selection-transforms), multiple copies (EDT-002).
design: Plane input reuses the working-plane consumers of task 09 (SetThreePointPlane, PlaneFromFace, SetVerticalPlane, SetHorizontalPlane) as sub-steps instead of re-implementing them, so typed values keep AS-04 precision and faces come from the PickIndex. Preview cost: mirror the selection's plan outlines and, in 3D, the feature edges of the evaluated meshes (TriMesh::feature_edges, mesh.rs:239), cached by (selection, plane). With an empty selection the action shows 'Select elements to mirror' and starts nothing. If selection-transforms has landed, follow its tool layout (tools/transform.rs) and its copy-variant cursor handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless app test: with a wall selected, the consumer with three typed points (5,0,0), (5,1,0), (5,0,1) produces the task 13 command for the plane x = 5; a picked wall face as the plane produces the same command as the equivalent typed plane; the 'current working plane' option uses the pane's WorkingPlane (task 07).
- The copy modifier switches between the move and copy variants during the operation, the preview and cursor state follow, and one Undo reverts a mirror.
- An inclined plane on a selected wall shows a status-line error naming 'Wall' and creates no undo step; a horizontal mirror of a storey-linked wall shows the info that its top link became fixed.
- kittest: the Edit menu and the 3D context menu show 'Mirror about plane'; with a wall selected, the preview is drawn in the plan and the 3D view without panic.
- The task 08 registry test includes the consumer (an edit command in 3D, VIEW-025).
- Satisfies the interactive part of EDT-022 (with task 13).
notes:
SRS: EDT-022
Also: VIEW-025 (an edit command in 3D), INP-015 (plane definitions reused).
No default shortcut: Appendix D.8 does not list mirror about a plane; commands-and-l10n may assign one.

title: Reflect walls and slabs about a 3D plane: Plane3 and the mirror command
description:
WHY: Mirroring shall also be possible about a plane in 3D (EDT-022), extending the mirror about an axis defined by two points of EDT-001 (selection-transforms). Transforms that a kind cannot represent are refused with a message naming the kind (EDT-007 applicability, the rule selection-transforms establishes). The gap analysis lists EDT-022 missing and notes that walls and slabs are vertical extrusions whose parameters cannot represent a mirror about an arbitrary plane; the positive any-plane case belongs to free-form solids (free-form-solids asserts it through the same hook). Today nothing exists: ElementKind only translates (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:257-270) and the only transform command is Command::MoveElements (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:41-44). This task is the headless model part; the interactive tool is task 15.

WHAT: archicraft-model: Plane3 { point, normal } with a classification Vertical, Horizontal or Inclined; ElementKind::mirrored(&Plane3, storey elevation) -> Result<Mirrored { kind, top_fixed }, Unsupported> for walls (vertical plane: reflect start and end and swap them so the exterior face stays on the right of the reference line, element.rs:82-86; horizontal plane z = h: new base = 2h - top, new top = 2h - base with the top converted to TopLink::Fixed and reported through top_fixed) and slabs (vertical: reflect outline and holes and reverse their order to keep CCW outlines and CW holes, element.rs:180-183; horizontal: new top = 2h - bottom respecting SlabReference), inclined planes -> Unsupported naming the kind; a mirror command with a copy variant planned into Edit::ReplaceElement (in place) or Edit::InsertElement (copies) edits (command.rs:616-633), with label, plan() arm and tests following the 'Add a command' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md. Out of scope: the interactive tool, preview and menus (15), multiple-copy variants (EDT-002), any-plane mirroring of free-form solids and imported elements (their epics), rotating about arbitrary axes (EDT-007).
design: Coordination with selection-transforms (not a declared prerequisite of this epic): if its Command::Transform family and the per-kind transform hook of the kind registry have landed when this task starts, add TransformOp::MirrorPlane(Plane3) to that family and implement the wall and slab arms through the hook; otherwise add Command::MirrorElements { ids, plane, copy } following the 'Add a command' extension point and let selection-transforms fold it into its family. The reflection maths and the tests are identical either way. Reflection of a point: p' = p - 2 ((p - q).n) n. Wall rule: after reflection the left-hand normal flips, so swapping start and end restores the exterior-right convention and keeps skin order once layer structures exist. Horizontal mirrors of walls with TopLink::Storey or Relative convert to TopLink::Fixed { height } because the mirrored top no longer follows a storey; top_fixed lets the tool (task 15) tell the user, mirroring EDT-006's 'the user is told'. Copies get new ElementIds and names through Project::next_element_name.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: mirroring a wall from (2,0) to (6,0) about the vertical plane x = 5 gives start (4, 0) and end (8, 0) (the reflected end points (8, 0) and (4, 0), swapped by the documented rule); a vertical plane at 30 degrees reflects a wall and a slab exactly within 1e-12; a slab outline stays CCW and holes CW with unchanged area; execute + undo restores the project; the copy variant adds elements with new ids and names and leaves the originals unchanged.
- Horizontal mirror about storey elevation + 3.0 of a 3.0 m wall based at offset 0 gives base_offset 3.0 and TopLink::Fixed { height: 3.0 }, with top_fixed reported when the original top was linked to a storey; a slab mirrored about a horizontal plane keeps its thickness and gets the reflected reference elevation for both SlabReference values.
- An inclined plane returns CommandError::Invalid whose message names 'Wall' (or 'Slab') and leaves the project untouched (EDT-007 applicability).
- Geometry test (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/mirror.rs): the evaluated mesh of a free-standing wall and of a slab with a hole mirrored about a vertical plane equals the reflection of the original mesh (vertex sets equal within 1e-9).
- IFCX round trip (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs) of a project with mirrored walls and slabs passes without schema change.
- Satisfies the model part of EDT-022 for every kind that can represent the mirror (walls and slabs about vertical and horizontal planes) with the applicability refusal for the rest; the tool follows in task 15.
notes:
SRS: EDT-022
EDT-022 stays partial in docs/implementation-status.md until free-form-solids delivers the any-plane case.
Open question: should a horizontal mirror re-home elements to the storey containing their new base (ELM-007 assignment by elevation)? Proposal: keep the home storey and adjust offsets; confirm with the selection-transforms owner.

title: Define cut planes numerically with side, storey binding and toggle
description:
WHY: VIEW-042 (M): several user-defined cut planes, positioned numerically with an explicit side to remove; cut planes have a global on/off toggle; caps in a uniform colour or the elements' materials. VIEW-061 (S): a cut plane is bindable to a storey elevation plus offset, so that views of several storeys stay aligned. Gap rows: both missing; nothing in the UI creates or edits a plane.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs: a non-modal 'Cut planes' window for the active 3D pane with the list of up to 8 planes (name, enabled checkbox, delete) and an editor: orientation Horizontal, Vertical (azimuth) or Inclined (azimuth and inclination), reference point x, y, z (widgets::length and widgets::angle), side to remove (Above or Below for horizontal planes, Positive or Negative side otherwise, with an arrow preview in the 3D overlay), 'Bind to storey' combo plus offset, and the cap style (Element materials or Uniform colour with a colour picker). A global 'Cut planes' toggle in the 3D view-control bar and Action::ToggleCutPlanes (View menu). Out of scope: two-point placement (10), the section box (11).
design: Follow the 'Add a dialog' extension point (Dialogs state, Action, View menu item, kittest by window title). Normal from azimuth (counter-clockwise from +X in project coordinates) and inclination; the side flag flips it on resolve (01). The binding fixes the z of the reference point for any orientation; for an unbound plane z is absolute. The arrow preview is an egui overlay projected with Camera3d::projection_matrix * view_matrix; skip points behind the camera. Each edit bumps the pane's restrictions generation so FrameKey re-renders. Pointers: dialogs.rs (Window patterns, preferences_window), widgets.rs, shell.rs:193-227, actions.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: adding a horizontal plane at 1.10 m removing above creates one enabled plane in the pane's restrictions; switching 'Cut planes' off keeps the list while resolve yields no user plane; delete removes it; 'Add plane' is disabled with a tooltip when 8 planes exist.
- VIEW-061: a plane bound to storey 01 with offset 1.10 m follows Command::SetStoreyElevation moving storey 01 to +3.20 m with shift_above (resolved z = 4.30) and the headless golden's cut line moves accordingly; two 3D views bound to different storeys with the same offset show aligned cuts relative to their storeys.
- Switching the cap style stores CapStyle::Material or CapStyle::Uniform with the picked colour in the pane's restrictions, and a headless snapshot shows the picked uniform colour on the caps (material rendering is asserted by 15).
- Input parses in project units (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs); invalid input leaves the plane unchanged and shows the reason.
- No undo step, Project.revision unchanged.
- Satisfies the numeric placement, explicit side, global toggle and cap-colour clauses of VIEW-042, and VIEW-061.
notes: SRS: VIEW-042 VIEW-061

title: Cap cut solids per plane with a stencil pass in uniform colour
description:
WHY: VIEW-042 (M): cut solids are displayed closed (capped), with a uniform colour or the elements' own materials. The same caps close bodies trimmed at storey range limits (VIEW-041). The epic decision is a stencil-based cap pass per plane that runs only while restrictions are active; the risk named for the epic is capping with several planes and a box at interactive frame rates (NFR-PERF-003: at least 30 frames/s for RM-M). Gap row VIEW-042: missing (no capping). This task builds the stencil cap machinery and the uniform colour; material colour and region boundary caps follow in 15.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs: three pipelines - stencil parity (no colour writes, depth compare Always without writes, no culling, stencil Invert on both faces, write mask 1), cap (stencil Equal 1, depth LessEqual with writes, colour) and stencil reset (full-screen triangle, stencil Zero); per-pass parameters through a dynamic-offset uniform (bind group 1: mode and plane index) so the parity pass clips by plane i only while cap fragments are clipped by every other plane, the region and the element flags. Cap polygons are the plane sections of the expanded scene AABB (clip.rs, 06), uploaded per view when the planes change, drawn after opaque faces and before edges and transparent faces. views/shader.wgsl: vs_cap and fs_cap entry points; uniform colour from the view's CapStyle::Uniform (01), shaded with the plane normal; until 15 lands, CapStyle::Material renders in the proposed default cap colour #A0A0A0. Every resolved plane is capped: user planes, the six box faces and the storey trim planes. Planes that miss the scene bounds are skipped; with no active plane no extra pass runs. Out of scope: material colour and region boundary caps (15), cut-plane UI (09 to 11), hatched caps (cut fills are plan-only, DSP).
design: Parity: with geometry clipped only by plane i, a point on plane i lies inside a closed body exactly when the number of that body's surfaces on the kept side along the view ray is odd, independent of the viewer's position; this needs closed, outward meshes, which archicraft-geometry produces (add a debug_assert on TriMesh::check_closed, mesh.rs:122, in build_scene under cfg(debug_assertions)). Overlapping, unjoined bodies cancel each other's parity and leave a hole in the cap: a known limitation until junction cleanup, documented in the overlay tooltip. Discarded fragments do not run stencil operations, so reset the stencil with the full-screen pass per plane instead of relying on the cap draw. MSAA: the stencil is per sample, so parity and cap pipelines use SAMPLE_COUNT (render3d.rs:19). Keep the per-pass uniform open for the region-edge mode and the material lookup of 15. Fallback if the per-plane passes miss the frame budget: back-face capping (shade back faces with the entry plane's normal and write frag_depth at the entry point), recorded as a decision. Pointers: render3d.rs:270-380 (pipelines), 501-580 (render pass), shader.wgsl.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless golden 'one_plane_uniform': two_storey_shell with one vertical cut plane shows closed caps (no background pixel at probes inside wall and slab cross-sections) in the uniform colour.
- Golden 'two_planes_and_box_uniform': two cut planes plus a section box set directly in the restrictions cap every plane, and corner probes outside the kept region show background (11 adds the handles, 15 the material variant).
- A camera whose eye lies inside a wall renders no cap artefacts outside that wall (probe).
- Hidden and filtered elements contribute no caps; a trimmed storey range (planes from 01) produces caps on both trim planes.
- A draw counter asserts 1 + intersecting planes scene draws per frame with uniform caps and exactly 1 without restrictions; the golden of 03 is unchanged.
- The frame time with 8 user planes plus the box on the largest available sample is measured on reference hardware and recorded in the pull request against NFR-PERF-003 (30 frames/s).
- Satisfies the capped-display clause of VIEW-042 for planes and the box in uniform colour, and the caps of VIEW-041 trimming.
notes: SRS: VIEW-042 VIEW-041

title: Handle DPI changes, a UI scale preference and multi-monitor windows
description:
WHY: The system shall support multiple monitors and high-DPI displays (HW-006), with UI scaling from 100% to 200% (NFR-PORT-005, done by inspection). The gap analysis left HW-006 partial: egui's zoom_factor is neither exposed in Preferences (persistence/prefs.rs:27-53) nor persisted, a DPI change when the window moves between monitors is unhandled and untested (only the 3D render target is sized with pixels_per_point, views/view3d.rs:217-222), and multi-monitor behaviour comes only from winit/eframe defaults (main.rs:21-29). The epic acceptance requires that a DPI change when moving between monitors re-renders correctly.

WHAT: Extract viewport_pixels(rect, pixels_per_point) from view3d.rs and add the pixel size and pixels_per_point to FrameKey (views/render3d.rs:235-240), so any DPI change re-renders the 3D view even when the rounded texture size is unchanged; check that plan line widths, glyphs and hit radii are in points (plan.rs:141-143) and that the snap radius is interpreted in logical points. Add Preferences.ui_scale (1.0-2.0) applied with ctx.set_zoom_factor at start and on change, kept in sync when the user uses egui's Ctrl/Cmd +/-/0 zoom, with an 'Interface scale' row in the Preferences dialog and the zoom shortcuts listed in the shortcuts window. Verify that eframe's window persistence (eframe feature 'persistence' is enabled in the workspace Cargo.toml) restores size and position clamped to the monitors present, and write docs/manual-tests/high-dpi.md. Out of scope: separate project windows that can be placed on another monitor (library-dw-exchange-17, PRJ-011).
design: egui-winit handles WindowEvent::ScaleFactorChanged (egui-winit lib.rs:312-330) and updates pixels_per_point; the only pixel-sized resource is the 3D render target, which ensure_viewport (render3d.rs:438-462) re-creates when the size changes. Adding size and pixels_per_point to FrameKey covers the case where egui's zoom and the DPI change cancel out in the rounded size but the texture filtering changes. ui_scale versus OS scale: egui multiplies both (pixels_per_point = native * zoom), so the preference is relative to the OS setting, as NFR-PORT-005 expects. Read ctx.zoom_factor() at the end of each frame and save the preference when it changed (app.rs save path at 181-185). eframe clamps restored window positions to the available monitors (egui-winit WindowSettings); verify on macOS and Windows instead of adding custom code.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: viewport_pixels for pixels_per_point 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0 and odd rect sizes; two FrameKeys that differ only in pixels_per_point are unequal.
- kittest: with the harness at pixels_per_point 1.0 and then 2.0 (two_storey_shell open), the plan view draws without panic and a primary click at the same logical position selects the same wall; the 3D pick ray through the same logical point is unchanged within 1e-9.
- Preferences: ui_scale round-trips, 0.5 is clamped to 1.0 and 3.0 to 2.0; the Preferences dialog shows 'Interface scale'; changing it with Ctrl/Cmd + is persisted on exit.
- docs/manual-tests/high-dpi.md records dragging the window with a plan and a 3D tab between a Retina display and a 1x monitor (macOS) and between 150% and 100% monitors (Windows): sharp re-render, correct picking of a wall corner in 3D, unchanged snap radius in points; restart on a single monitor restores the window onto it.
- Satisfies HW-006 (and re-confirms NFR-PORT-005 with a persisted UI scale).
notes:
SRS: HW-006
Appendix D.1 snap radius 8 px is interpreted as 8 logical points (it scales with the display), documented in the Preferences tooltip.

title: Show the restriction indicator, reset all, store restrictions in views
description:
WHY: VIEW-043 (M): whenever a view has an active restriction (kind filter, storey range, region, cut plane, hidden elements, isolation) it shows a persistent indicator, and one command clears all restrictions; UI-001 places this indicator in the view-control bar. VIEW-004 (M): saved views store kind filters, storey range, cut planes and hidden elements and re-apply them to the current model. VIEW-047 (M): filters, hidden elements and cut planes never change the model geometry or the standard IFCX content. Gap rows: VIEW-043 missing (the 3D overlay label at crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:248-263 shows only projection, mode and orbit); VIEW-047 partial (no test).

WHAT: shell.rs view-control bar: a 'Restricted' badge whenever ViewRestrictions::is_active() with a tooltip summary built from active_kinds() (for example '3 hidden, Kinds: Slab, Storeys 00-01 trimmed, 2 cut planes, Section box, Region inside') and a 'Clear restrictions' button; the same badge in the 3D overlay label; badge, tooltip and button read Workspace::restrictions(active pane) (04), not View3dState, so any pane kind that supports restrictions shows them; Action::ClearRestrictions in the View menu with a proposed shortcut. views/state.rs (plan-views-browser-09): capture copies the pane's ViewRestrictions into ViewDefinition.restrictions, apply restores them and reports resolve issues in the status line, redefine keeps id and name. A headless app test proves VIEW-047 on the application side. Out of scope: restrictions in plan views (none exist); section and elevation panes get the indicator and reset through the same Pane-keyed state once sections-elevations-dims adds them (follow-up bead filed by 3d-view-restrictions-done).
design: The indicator reads active_kinds() (01), so a restriction kind added later appears without UI changes; place the badge first in the right-to-left layout of status_bar (shell.rs:182) so narrow windows keep it visible. ClearRestrictions calls ViewRestrictions::clear() and bumps the generation. Because the live pane state is the model type, capture and apply are clones plus resolve(); apply never issues a Command. For the byte comparison call archicraft_ifcx::save with fixed WriteOptions (author, timestamp, data_version as in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:15-28). Pointers: shell.rs:166-256, view3d.rs:248-263, views/state.rs (plan-views-browser-09), app.rs:377.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: no badge without restrictions; each of the six restriction kinds alone (kind filter, storey range, region, cut plane or box, hidden elements, isolation) shows the badge with a tooltip naming it; 'Clear restrictions' (button, menu and shortcut) resets all and the badge disappears; exploded storeys alone show no badge; opening a saved view with restrictions shows the badge at once; a unit test builds the badge summary from a PaneRestrictions without any 3D view state.
- Saved views: save a 3D view with hidden elements, isolation, a kind filter, a trimmed storey range, two cut planes (one bound to a storey), a section box, a region and uniform caps; change all of them; open the view: the restrictions are equal to the saved ones; a hidden element deleted after saving is reported and ignored; redefine replaces the restrictions keeping id and name; save and reopen through IFCX (02) keeps them.
- VIEW-047 app test: applying every restriction kind to two open 3D panes leaves Project.revision, the undo stack and the geometry cache (Arc::ptr_eq) unchanged, and archicraft_ifcx::save produces byte-identical files before and after.
- Satisfies VIEW-043, the application side of VIEW-047 and the restriction clauses of VIEW-004.
notes: SRS: VIEW-043 VIEW-047 VIEW-040 VIEW-041 VIEW-042

title: Snap to vertices, edges and faces of 3D bodies in 3D views
description:
WHY: In 3D views snapping shall also find faces (point on face) and, from the last point, inference guides parallel to the X, Y and Z axes (INP-016; the guides follow in task 11); the cursor shall snap in 2D and 3D views to element nodes, points on edges, midpoints and intersections (the 3D clause of INP-008, left to this epic by point-input-snapping-03). Today the 3D view only picks whole elements (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:75-91) and offers no snap points; the measure tool (MEA-001) and element tools in 3D (VIEW-025) need them.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/input/snap3d.rs (egui-free): candidates from the PickIndex near the cursor ray: vertices (Node level), division points of the active INP-010 mode on the hovered edge (Division level, reusing the division function of point-input-snapping-04 on the edge's 3D segment; Half gives the midpoint), points where a hovered edge pierces a visible face of another element (Intersection level, a segment query against the BVH), the point on an edge closest to the ray (Edge level), the perpendicular foot from the previous 3D point onto an edge (Edge level), and the ray's hit on the front-most face (new Face kind, ranked after Guide and before Grid). Distances are measured in screen points after projection, within prefs.snap_radius; candidates occluded by a nearer face are dropped. Resolved gains model: DVec3 next to the plane point: a snapped 3D point reaches planar consumers projected onto the working plane along its normal (a slab corner above the plane gives its XY on a horizontal plane) and 3D consumers get it exactly. The 3D candidates merge with the plane candidates of task 08 into one list ordered by the INP-009 precedence, with Tab cycling. Glyphs (node, intersection, division, edge, perpendicular, face) and a face-outline highlight are drawn through Overlay3d. Out of scope: X/Y/Z guides (11), arcs and centres of curved bodies (curved-geometry).
design: Candidate query: PickIndex::near_ray with radius_at(t) = snap_radius x model_per_pixel(t), then exact screen-space distance per candidate. Closest point on a 3D segment to a ray: solve the 2x2 system of the skew-line closest points and clamp to the segment. Occlusion: compare the candidate's ray parameter with the front hit t_front from PickIndex::ray, keeping candidates with t <= t_front + 1e-6 x distance (edges of the hit face itself survive). Faces of hidden or excluded elements (INP-017 exclusion flags from point-input-snapping-12) are filtered the same way as in 2D. Face ranking decision: SRS INP-009 fixes seven levels for snap candidates in general; a point on a face is the weakest geometric target in 3D, so it ranks after Guide and before Grid and the precedence table in input/snap.rs documents this as the 3D-only position. Pitfall: the same geometric point may appear as a 2D plan target and as a 3D vertex; deduplicate within 1e-9 keeping the better level (point-input-snapping-03 rule).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests on two_storey_shell with fixed cameras: a cursor 3 points from a wall's top corner gives a Node candidate whose model point equals the geometry vertex plus storey elevation exactly; a cursor near the middle of a slab edge gives the Division midpoint; a cursor over a wall face away from edges gives a Face candidate lying on the face plane within 1e-9 m.
- Division and intersection: with the division mode 'N equal parts, N = 4' a hovered slab edge offers its quarter points; on a synthetic project in which a slab cuts through a wall, the point where the wall's vertical corner edge pierces the slab's top face is an Intersection candidate within 1e-9 m.
- Occlusion: a corner hidden behind a nearer wall is not offered; it is offered once the nearer wall's layer is hidden.
- Precedence test in 3D: node > intersection > division > guide intersection > edge > guide > face > grid in one assertion; Tab cycles through the 3D candidates in range.
- Projection: snapping a slab corner at z = 3.0 with a horizontal working plane at z = 0.0 yields plane point = corner XY and model = corner; a perpendicular foot from the previous point onto a wall top edge is exact within 1e-12.
- kittest: hovering a wall corner in the 3D view with the Wall tool active shows the tracker label 'node', over a face 'on face'.
- Timing (debug, loose, NFR-PERF-005 budget): 1,000 3D resolve() calls on two_storey_shell average under 2 ms; the PickIndex is not rebuilt during the sweep.
- Satisfies INP-016's face clause and INP-008's 3D node, edge, division, intersection and perpendicular targets.
notes:
SRS: INP-016
Also covers the 3D clause of INP-008 (owned by point-input-snapping) for nodes, edges, division points, intersections and perpendicular feet; tangent points and centres arrive with curved-geometry, axis points with profiles-columns-beams. Report it in the status update of the done task. Appendix D.1: snap radius 8 px.

title: Selectable navigation schemes for plan and 3D views
description:
WHY: Navigation presets shall include at least the ArchiCraft default (wheel zooms at the cursor, middle-drag pans, modifier with middle-drag orbits), a trackpad-first preset and presets resembling common CAD and 3D tools (SET-003), and SET-001 lists the navigation scheme among the user preferences. 3D navigation shall offer orbit as a persistent mode and temporarily with a modifier and the middle button without leaving the active tool, pan and zoom as in 2D, fit and zoom to selection and setting the orbit pivot by clicking an element, with configurable presets (VIEW-021). The mouse wheel and middle button drive navigation per VIEW-014 and VIEW-021 and the secondary button opens context menus (HW-001): done today (plan.rs:404-433 wheel and middle drag, plan.rs:634 and 728-780 context menu; view3d.rs:129-159 wheel and middle drag, view3d.rs:265-291 context menu), so this task keeps it and regresses it under every scheme. Navigation never creates undo steps and previous/next zoom covers the plan view history (UND-005, done: ZoomHistory camera.rs:68-99; kept). VIEW-021 is partial: persistent orbit mode (Action::OrbitMode, app.rs:426-446), temporary Shift+middle orbit, pan and zoom, Fit and Zoom to selection (view3d.rs:273-282, app.rs:366-372) and the double-click orbit pivot (view3d.rs:189-196) exist and stay; only configurable presets are missing. Today the bindings are hard-coded in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:398-433 and views/view3d.rs:124-163, Preferences (persistence/prefs.rs:28-55) has no scheme, and the shortcuts window lists fixed strings (ui/dialogs.rs:653-656).

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/navigation.rs with an egui-free core: NavInput (wheel with unit, delta and modifiers; pinch; rotate; drag with button and modifiers), NavIntent (Pan, ZoomAt, Orbit, Lens for the field of view, Fit) and NavigationScheme { ArchiCraft, TrackpadFirst, CadStyle, ModellerStyle } with a binding table per scheme and per view kind (plan views map orbit gestures to nothing). plan.rs and view3d.rs translate egui events into NavInput, apply the intents to Camera2d or Camera3d, and keep their picking, orbit mode and pivot code. Add the Lens intent (field of view by modifier plus wheel: the direct-manipulation clause of VIEW-020 for the field of view), a 'Set orbit pivot here' entry in the 3D context menu next to the existing double-click (view3d.rs:189-196), Preferences.navigation with a row in the Preferences dialog, and shortcuts-window rows generated from the active scheme. Switching applies on the next frame. Out of scope: trackpad classification and the macOS orbit modifier (04), walk mode (could-scope-polish).
design: Presets (product names are not used in labels): ArchiCraft (wheel zoom at cursor, middle pan, Shift+middle orbit, two-finger pan, pinch zoom, modifier+two-finger orbit); Trackpad-first (two-finger drag orbits in 3D and pans in plan, Shift+two-finger pans in 3D, pinch zooms, Cmd/Ctrl+two-finger zooms, rotate gesture yaws); CAD style (wheel zoom at cursor, middle pan, Shift+middle orbit, double-middle-click fits to window, wheel direction reversible); Modeller style (middle orbit, Shift+middle pan, Ctrl+middle dolly, wheel zoom, two-finger orbit, Shift+two-finger pan). The table is data (const arrays of (NavInput pattern, ViewKind, NavIntent)), so the shortcuts window and the tests read the same source. Keep NavInput independent of egui like input/keys.rs from point-input-snapping, so tests need no egui context. Lens: fov_y *= 1.1^-notches with Alt held in perspective (Option on macOS). The per-frame clone of i.raw.events (technical debt, plan.rs:400 and view3d.rs:127) is replaced by iterating the events in ui.input(|i| ...) and collecting NavInput only. Keep ZoomHistory recording (camera.rs:68-99) for plan zoom intents. The single-key shortcut suppression (app.rs:466-476) is unaffected because navigation uses no letter keys. In plan views every scheme maps middle drag and two-finger drag to pan and wheel and pinch to zoom at the cursor, because VIEW-014 is a Must that a preset may not configure away; the schemes differ in 3D bindings and in modifiers.
acceptance_criteria:
- navigation.rs table tests: for each of the four schemes, every NavInput of a fixed list maps to the expected NavIntent in plan and in 3D; the secondary button maps to no intent in every scheme (context menus keep working, HW-001).
- Regression table: the ArchiCraft scheme reproduces today's behaviour exactly (line wheel zooms by 1.2^-notches at the cursor, point-unit wheel pans, Shift plus point-unit wheel orbits, pinch zooms, middle drag pans, Shift plus middle drag orbits, Alt plus primary drag and orbit mode orbit).
- Preferences: navigation round-trips through preferences.json; an unknown value falls back to ArchiCraft; old files without the field load.
- kittest: the Preferences dialog shows 'Navigation' with four choices; selecting the modeller style and simulating a middle drag in the 3D view changes the camera yaw (orbit) without a restart; the shortcuts window lists the active scheme's bindings.
- The Lens intent changes fov_y within the task 01 range in perspective and does nothing in parallel projection.
- 'Set orbit pivot here' on a wall puts camera.target on the picked surface point.
- Kept VIEW-021 clauses under every scheme (kittest per scheme): persistent orbit mode orbits with the primary button, Fit to window and Zoom to selection (view3d.rs:273-282, app.rs:366-372) frame the model and the selection, a double-click on a wall still sets the orbit pivot (view3d.rs:189-196), and 3D pan and zoom use the same gestures as plan pan and zoom in that scheme ('as in 2D').
- HW-001 regression (kittest per scheme): a secondary click opens the plan context menu (plan.rs:728-780) and the 3D context menu (view3d.rs:265-291); in plan views a middle drag pans and a wheel notch zooms at the cursor in every scheme.
- UND-005 view history: plan zoom intents still record ZoomHistory under every scheme and Previous/Next zoom restore the cameras; the existing zoom_history test (camera.rs:307-315) is kept.
- The UND-005 regression test of task 01 is extended to drive every NavIntent: revision and undo count unchanged.
- Satisfies SET-003, VIEW-021's configurable presets and orbit pivot clauses (the existing orbit, pan, zoom and fit clauses regressed), the field-of-view direct manipulation of VIEW-020 (the 'without leaving the active tool' clause is tested with a 3D tool in task 08), keeps HW-001 done and adds the navigation scheme item of SET-001.
notes:
SRS: SET-003 VIEW-021 HW-001 UND-005 VIEW-020
The four presets exceed the epic's 'three presets' acceptance; labels and descriptions go through the string catalogue once commands-and-l10n has landed.

title: Verify exit criterion: 3D view filters, hidden elements, cut planes and section box as GPU clip planes
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its exit criterion is demonstrated as a whole on the integrated code: per-view hide, isolate and show all (VIEW-040), kind and storey-range filters with trimming (VIEW-041), cut planes and the section box with caps (VIEW-042) bound to storeys (VIEW-061), region filters (VIEW-044), the indicator and reset (VIEW-043), exploded storeys (VIEW-046), and the guarantee that none of it changes the model or the standard IFCX content (VIEW-047).

WHAT: Run the full workspace quality gates, walk through the acceptance list below on a clean checkout, fix or file beads for any gap, update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (VIEW-040, VIEW-041, VIEW-042, VIEW-043, VIEW-044, VIEW-046, VIEW-047, VIEW-061, plus the restriction clauses of VIEW-004 and the D.8 view shortcuts of UI-008) with evidence paths, file the follow-up bead for sections-elevations-dims (return true from ViewKind::supports_restrictions for section and elevation kinds, filter their slice input with ResolvedRestrictions::admits, and add the hide, isolate, show-all and indicator kittests there: the section and elevation clauses of VIEW-040 and VIEW-043), record VIEW-040 as done for 3D views and pending for section and elevation views, and close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new features.
design: Verification only. Use the goldens and tests added by tasks 01 to 15; measure the 3D frame time with 8 planes plus the box on reference hardware once more and record it next to NFR-PERF-003 in docs/implementation-status.md. Follow the session-completion protocol of the repository (conservative git profile: report, do not push without approval).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest for hide, isolate and show-all honouring layer visibility passes, including isolating the contents of a 3D marquee and of a plan region.
- A storey range with trimming shows capped bodies (snapshot) passes.
- Two cut planes plus a section box with draggable handles render closed caps in uniform or material colour (goldens).
- A cut plane bound to storey plus offset follows a storey edit (test).
- A region filter drawn in plan keeps cut elements selectable (test).
- The indicator appears whenever any restriction is active and the reset clears all (kittest).
- Writer test: the file is byte-identical with and without restrictions (VIEW-047), both for live restrictions and, after stripping archicraft:: attributes, for saved restricted views.
- Restrictions are stored in saved views and re-applied (test).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green on all three CI platforms, including the headless 3D goldens on the software adapters.
- conformance/run.sh is green on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx and the reference models.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID with evidence and remaining gaps (overlapping-body cap holes, axis-aligned box only, region without vertical limits).
- The follow-up bead for VIEW-040 and VIEW-043 in section and elevation views exists and is linked to sections-elevations-dims.
- The epic 3d-view-restrictions is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for anything deferred.
notes: SRS: VIEW-040 VIEW-041 VIEW-042 VIEW-043 VIEW-044 VIEW-046 VIEW-047 VIEW-061

title: Working-plane commands, look-perpendicular and align view to surface
description:
WHY: The working plane shall be definable as horizontal at a typed elevation (default the active storey elevation), vertical through two points, by three points or picked from a face, and a command shall make the view look perpendicular to it (INP-015). An align-view-to-surface command shall turn the camera to look perpendicular to a picked face, cut faces included, in both projections (VIEW-022). Camera moves shall not create undo steps (UND-005, done for navigation; this task keeps it for the new commands), and neither shall working-plane changes, which are view state like the camera. The gap analysis lists both commands as missing: pick returns no face normal (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:75-91) and there is no align command.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/working_plane.rs with InputConsumers SetHorizontalPlane (typed elevation field defaulting to the active storey elevation, or a picked point's Z), SetVerticalPlane (two points), SetThreePointPlane (three points), PlaneFromFace (a click picks a Face from the PickIndex of task 06, the hovered face outline is highlighted) and a ResetToStorey action; they run on the 3D host of task 08 with snapping. Actions LookPerpendicular (Camera3d::look_along the plane normal, keeping the point under the view centre) and AlignViewToSurface (pick a face, look along its normal with the target at the picked point; faces from PickPlane entries, i.e. the cut planes and caps that 3d-view-restrictions registers, work the same way), a View menu submenu 'Working plane' and 3D context-menu entries, and a status-bar indicator of the current plane.
