The plane is drawn in the 3D view through Overlay3d as a translucent patch with PlanGrid main and auxiliary lines around the cursor while a consumer is active or 'Show working plane' is on. Out of scope: cut planes themselves (3d-view-restrictions), storing planes in saved views (plan-views-browser).
design: Orientation conventions: a plane's visible side is the side the camera is on when it is defined, so LookPerpendicular never flips the view to the back; three-point normals follow the right-hand rule and are flipped towards the eye. look_along up vector: projection of +Z onto the view plane, or the plane's y axis when the normal is vertical (keeps north up when looking down, matching task 01). Keep the distance in perspective; in parallel projection keep the visible half-height. The plane patch is drawn as clipped lines only (no GPU change): a 20 x 20 lattice of auxiliary spacing around the cursor's plane point, main lines stronger, alpha fading with distance; skip when more than 2,000 lines would be drawn (the construction-grid limit of plan.rs:156-160). Face hover highlight uses the Face boundary loops from the PickIndex lifted to world coordinates. Working-plane changes are view state (not commands), consistent with camera state (UND-005).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: SetThreePointPlane with typed points (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,0,1) yields the XZ plane with normal (0, -1, 0) or (0, 1, 0) by documented orientation; SetVerticalPlane through (0,0) and (4,3) gives x axis (0.8, 0.6, 0); SetHorizontalPlane with the typed elevation 2.75 gives exactly 2.75; PlaneFromFace on the top of the highest slab of two_storey_shell gives a horizontal plane at that slab's top.
- Integration: after PlaneFromFace on a slab top, a wall drawn with the Wall tool gets base_offset = slab top - storey elevation (task 08 mapping).
- LookPerpendicular: camera back() equals the plane normal (facing the viewer) within 1e-12 in perspective and parallel projection, and the model point at the view centre stays at the centre within 1e-6 points.
- AlignViewToSurface on a wall side face: back() equals the face normal within 1e-12 in both projections; on a registered synthetic PickPlane (cut plane stand-in) it aligns to that plane (VIEW-022 cut faces; verified end to end when 3d-view-restrictions registers real cut planes).
- kittest: View > 'Working plane' lists 'Horizontal at elevation...', 'Vertical through two points', 'Three points', 'From face', 'Reset to storey', 'Look perpendicular'; the status bar shows 'Working plane: horizontal +2.750'; no plane or camera command creates an undo step (UND-005).
- Satisfies INP-015 (all four definitions and the look-perpendicular command) and VIEW-022.
notes:
SRS: INP-015 VIEW-022 UND-005
Provisional shortcuts: none by default (D.8 does not list working-plane commands); commands-and-l10n may assign them.

title: Trackpad pan, pinch and orbit gestures on macOS and Windows
description:
WHY: The system shall support trackpad two-finger pan and pinch zoom in all views (HW-002) and offer a trackpad orbit gesture (two-finger drag with a modifier) in 3D views (HW-007). The gap analysis found both only partial: two-finger pan and pinch exist in both view kinds (plan.rs:404-422, view3d.rs:129-147) and Shift plus two-finger drag orbits (view3d.rs:132-137), but pan versus zoom is decided solely by MouseWheelUnit::Point while winit reports Windows precision-touchpad scrolling as line deltas, so a two-finger drag zooms on the Windows reference laptops; horizontal deltas are ignored; on macOS AppKit turns Shift plus vertical scroll into horizontal deltas (egui 0.36.2 input_state/wheel_state.rs:127), so Shift plus two-finger drag can only yaw because Camera3d::orbit maps delta.y to pitch (camera.rs:185-188); there is no trackpad test on any platform.

WHAT: In views/navigation.rs add a WheelSource classifier { Mouse, Trackpad }: point-unit events (macOS PanGesture, egui-winit lib.rs:557) are trackpad; line-unit streams with fractional notches or non-zero horizontal deltas are a precision touchpad; the decision holds for a gesture (MouseWheel phase, 250 ms hysteresis) so it cannot flip mid-drag. Trackpad streams use both axes for pan and orbit. The orbit modifier for two-finger drag is Option/Alt on macOS (no axis swap) and Shift on Windows and Linux, per scheme; Event::Rotate (macOS RotationGesture, egui-winit lib.rs:544) yaws the 3D camera in the trackpad-first scheme; pinch (Event::Zoom) and Windows Ctrl+wheel keep zooming at the pointer. Plan and 3D views are all view kinds today; sections, elevations and layouts inherit HW-002 by routing their events through navigation.rs (documented as an extension point). Add the manual test record docs/manual-tests/trackpad.md and correct the shortcuts-window rows. Out of scope: 3D mouse and pen tablets (HW-004, HW-005 in could-scope-polish).
design: Fractional-notch detection: a classic wheel sends multiples of WHEEL_DELTA (120) per message, which winit divides by 120, so |delta - round(delta)| > 1e-3 on either axis marks a precision touchpad; also treat any non-zero x on a line-unit event as touchpad unless the stream started integral (tilt wheels). Scale line deltas to points with egui's line height (about 50 points per line, the factor plan.rs uses today for notches) so pan speed matches macOS. egui forwards MouseWheel.phase (TouchPhase); reset the classifier on Start and End, and fall back to the time gap when phase is unknown (Windows). Do not rely on egui's smooth_scroll_delta: the views read raw events (plan.rs/view3d.rs). Pitfall: Option plus two-finger on macOS must not reach the INP-007 lock keys (they are key events, not wheel events).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in navigation.rs on recorded synthetic streams: macOS point deltas pan in plan and 3D; Option plus point deltas (12, -8) change both yaw and pitch; a Windows stream of line deltas (0.25, 0.1), (0.5, 0.0) is classified as trackpad and pans instead of zooming; an integral 1.0-notch stream is a mouse and zooms; Ctrl plus fractional line deltas zoom; Event::Zoom(1.25) zooms at the pointer by the same factor in plan and 3D under every scheme; Rotate(0.1) yaws by 0.1 rad in the trackpad-first scheme.
- Hysteresis test: a gesture classified as trackpad stays trackpad for its whole phase even when one delta is integral; a new gesture after 250 ms is re-classified.
- kittest: injecting MouseWheel { unit: Point, delta: (0, -30), modifiers: alt } over the 3D view changes the camera pitch; the same without modifier pans; in a plan view it pans.
- docs/manual-tests/trackpad.md records, with date, device and scheme, pan, pinch and orbit in plan and 3D on a macOS built-in trackpad and on a Windows precision touchpad (the NFR-PERF-001 reference laptop), Linux libinput best effort; all Must rows pass (epic acceptance clause).
- The wheel classifier and the bindings live only in navigation.rs: plan.rs and view3d.rs no longer match on MouseWheelUnit (source scan test), so later 2D view kinds get HW-002 through NavInput.
- The shortcuts window names the orbit gesture per platform.
- Satisfies HW-002 and HW-007.
notes:
SRS: HW-002 HW-007
Windows verification needs the reference laptop chosen in regression-and-status (NFR-PERF-001); record the device model in the manual test file.

title: Explode storeys vertically in 3D views (time-boxed)
description:
WHY: VIEW-046 (C): an exploded display may offset storeys vertically by a configurable distance in 3D views. The epic plans it as a per-storey transform offset and time-boxes it because it is Could scope. Gap row: missing.

WHAT: restrictions.explode (01) drives the z_offset of the per-element flag buffer (04): offset = StoreyList::number(storey) x distance (crates/archicraft-model/src/storey.rs:93, ground = 0), so the ground floor stays in place. An 'Exploded storeys' toggle and a distance field (widgets::length; proposed default 3.00 m, see 01) in the Filters popover (08). Picking, fit to window and model_bounds apply the offsets; clipping is evaluated on unexploded positions so cuts stay attached to their storeys; caps (07, 15) are drawn per storey with that storey's offset (the parity and cap passes of a plane run once per storey whose admitted elements meet the plane, restricted by a storey filter in the per-pass uniform), so cut solids stay closed while exploded (VIEW-042). Time box: 1 day; if it is exceeded, exploded display is disabled while a cut plane, the box or a trimmed range or region is active (toggle disabled with a tooltip, recorded as a decision) and a follow-up bead is filed; the distance stays configurable in every case. Out of scope: individual storey offsets, animation.
design: vs_main adds z_offset after computing the unexploded local position, which is passed to the fragment stage for the clip test (06). The CPU pick subtracts the element's offset from the ray origin per element (view3d.rs:75-91). ElementView grows to {flags, z_offset, storey: i32} so the per-pass storey filter of the cap passes can select one storey; cap polygons are translated by that storey's offset. StoreyList::number (storey.rs:93) is already relative to the ground storey, so no index arithmetic is needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test: storeys -1, 0 and +1 with distance 3.0 m get offsets -3.0, 0.0 and +3.0 m.
- Headless golden 'exploded': two_storey_shell with distance 2.0 m shows a 2.0 m gap between the storeys; setting 4.0 m widens the gap accordingly (configurable distance).
- Golden 'exploded_cut': exploded with one vertical cut plane shows closed caps on both storeys at their offset positions; with the time-box fallback instead, the toggle is disabled while the plane is active.
- Picking an element of storey 01 in exploded mode selects it; fit to window includes the offsets.
- The toggle and distance are kept by saved views (13) and IFCX (02).
- No undo step, Project.revision unchanged.
- Satisfies VIEW-046.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-046
Default explode distance proposed in 01: 3.00 m (to be confirmed).

title: Filter elements per view with a GPU flag buffer, honoured by picking
description:
WHY: VIEW-040 (M) hides elements per view and isolates the selection; VIEW-041 (M) filters by kind and storey range. The epic design evaluates these filters on the cached GpuScene per element, so two 3D views with different restrictions share one uploaded scene and toggling a filter never rebuilds or re-uploads geometry (NFR-PERF-003). Elements hidden by a view filter must not be pickable there (SEL-007). Today one GpuScene is cached per (revision, selection) for all views (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:43-47, views/view3d.rs:200-214), build_scene and pick filter by layer only (render3d.rs:102-110, view3d.rs:59-91), and fit to window uses the same layer-only bounds.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs: Workspace gains restrictions: HashMap<Pane, PaneRestrictions {restrictions: ViewRestrictions (the live pane state, the model type so that capture and apply are a clone), generation: u64 bumped on every change, resolved: a cached ResolvedRestrictions keyed by (revision, generation)}> with restrictions(pane) and restrictions_mut(pane), which return Some only for panes whose ViewKind::supports_restrictions (01) is true. The state lives beside View3dState (view3d.rs:15-23), not inside it, so section and elevation panes can reuse it without the 3D renderer; replace_document (workspace.rs:90) keeps it only for panes that still resolve. render3d.rs: the Vertex gets an element slot (u32), reusing the 24/8-bit pick slot of selection-transforms-06 if it has landed, otherwise added with that layout; SceneData gets slots: Vec<ElementId>; each Viewport owns a storage buffer array<ElementView {flags: u32, z_offset: f32}> (binding 1) rebuilt only when the scene generation, the restrictions generation or the revision changes; shader.wgsl vs_main sends vertices of non-admitted elements outside the clip volume; FrameKey includes the restrictions generation. view3d.rs: pick, model_bounds and fit use the same admits() predicate. Selectability: if selection-transforms-04's ViewFilter trait exists, implement it for ResolvedRestrictions; otherwise add Workspace::is_selectable(&Element, Pane) with that signature and use it in pick and select_all. Out of scope: clip planes (06), commands and UI (05, 08).
design: Storage buffers in the vertex stage need DownlevelFlags::VERTEX_STORAGE, which Vulkan, Metal, DX12 and lavapipe provide; if it is missing (GL fallback), build a filtered SceneData per view instead, chosen once when the Renderer3d is created. Culling a vertex: out.clip = vec4(2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 1.0) puts all three vertices outside the clip volume so the triangle is dropped; edges (LineList) likewise; fs_fill and fs_line also discard when the flag is 0 as a safety net. 24 slot bits allow 16.7 million elements. The selection colour stays baked into vertex colours (SceneKey unchanged) until selection-transforms-06 moves it into uniforms. Bind group layout grows by one read-only storage binding visible to VERTEX_FRAGMENT (render3d.rs:276-288). Pointers: render3d.rs:59-75 (Vertex, Uniforms), 97-170 (build_scene), 270-380 (pipelines), 438-500 (viewport), 501-580 (render); view3d.rs:59-91, 195-235; workspace.rs:43-66.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure unit test of element_flags(&SceneData, &ResolvedRestrictions, &Project) -> Vec<ElementView>: a hidden element gets flags 0; an isolation set admits only its members; kinds = {Slab} hides every wall; storey range 01..01 without trim admits only home-storey-01 elements; layer-hidden elements never appear in the scene at all.
- Headless render test (harness of 03): hiding the slab of samples::storey_with_walls_and_slab() removes its pixels; two viewports with different hidden sets render from the same GpuScene (same generation, upload counter unchanged).
- Picking: a ray through a hidden wall returns the element behind it; Workspace::is_selectable (or the ViewFilter) is false for hidden, non-isolated and kind-filtered elements in that pane and true in another pane.
- Fit to window with a storey filter fits only the admitted elements.
- Moving the camera does not rebuild the flag buffer (rebuild counter), and FrameKey changes whenever the restrictions change.
- With default restrictions the golden of 03 is unchanged.
- Regression (existing layer filter kept): the render3d.rs tests scene_contains_every_visible_triangle and hidden_layers_and_selection (render3d.rs:589-616) pass unchanged, and layer-hidden elements stay out of the scene (render3d.rs:110).
- restrictions_mut returns None for a plan pane and Some for a 3D pane; entries for deleted views are dropped on replace_document.
notes: SRS: VIEW-040 VIEW-041

title: Camera3d: eye/target/FOV editing, custom preset, vertical correction
description:
WHY: 3D views shall support perspective and parallel projection switchable with one command; the perspective camera has an eye position, a target and a field of view, each editable numerically and by direct manipulation, and parallel projection offers top, front, side, isometric, dimetric and custom presets (custom: rotation angles and azimuth) (VIEW-020). Vertical correction ('two-point perspective') shall be a persistent camera property that keeps vertical edges vertical (VIEW-023). Navigation (pan, zoom, camera) shall not create undo steps (UND-005): done today because cameras live in per-view state (View3dState, views/view3d.rs:15-23; ZoomHistory, camera.rs:68-99, tested by zoom_history camera.rs:307-315), so this task keeps it and regresses it. Today Camera3d (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/camera.rs:102-113) stores target, distance, yaw, pitch and fov_y, but the field of view is fixed at 45 degrees (camera.rs:154), there is no setter for eye or target, the presets (camera.rs:117-146, apply_preset :218-229) have no custom entry, and there is no shear or lens-shift term for vertical correction.

WHAT: Make camera.rs the complete headless camera model that the UI (task 02), navigation schemes (03), the Camera3d ViewSurface (07) and the align commands (09) build on: set_eye_target(eye, target) deriving distance, yaw and pitch (rejecting coincident points); set_fov(radians) clamped to a documented range; look_along(direction, up_hint) that orients the camera to look along any direction including straight up or down; ViewPreset::Custom { altitude, azimuth } next to the five existing presets; toggle_projection() that keeps the apparent scale at the target; a persistent vertical_correction: bool (kept through every navigation operation, preset and projection switch until the user turns it off) applied as an off-axis lens shift in projection_matrix() with the view matrix levelled, so ray() (camera.rs:261-275) stays the exact inverse; serde derives on Camera3d and ViewPreset so saved views (VIEW-004, plan-views-browser) can store the camera unchanged. Keep UND-005 and add an explicit regression test over every camera operation (the existing zoom_history test stays). Out of scope: the camera panel, projection action and plan glyph (02), navigation bindings (03), the look-perpendicular and align-to-face commands (09).
design: Camera3d stays orbit-parametrised (target, distance, yaw, pitch) because orbit, pan and zoom_at (camera.rs:185-209) are written in those terms; eye/target setters convert: d = eye - target, distance = |d|, yaw = atan2(d.y, d.x), pitch = asin(d.z / |d|). look_along(dir) sets yaw/pitch from -dir and keeps the target; straight down maps to pitch = 90 degrees, so lift the MAX_PITCH clamp (camera.rs:148, 89.9 degrees) for look_along and presets only, and keep the up-vector switch of view_matrix() (camera.rs:233-240) consistent by storing yaw as the heading that keeps north up. Vertical correction: build the view matrix with the horizontal forward f_h = normalize((target - eye) with z = 0) and up = +Z; compute the target's NDC height s = (target.z - eye.z) / (|target - eye|_xy * tan(fov/2)) and post-multiply the projection by a clip-space shear M with M.col(3).y = -s (y_clip' = y_clip - s * w_clip), which is an off-axis frustum. Only perspective is affected (parallel projection already keeps verticals vertical with no roll). Suspend correction above |pitch| = 75 degrees (degenerate shift) and report it through an is_correction_active() flag that the label (view3d.rs:242-257) shows. Field-of-view range proposal 10-120 degrees, default 45 (no Appendix D value). Azimuth convention: compass bearing of the view direction, clockwise from north (+Y), the convention architects use for sun azimuth. Pitfall: glam's dcamera::rh::proj::directx matrices are column-major; test the shear against an explicit hand-computed projection of one point. ViewPreset derives Eq and its ALL: [ViewPreset; 5] feeds the status-bar 'Views' menu (shell.rs:205-212): Custom { altitude, azimuth } carries f64, so drop Eq (keep PartialEq) and leave Custom out of ALL; the UI offers it separately (task 02). 'Persistent' (VIEW-023) means the flag survives every camera operation and is part of the serialisable camera; storing cameras across sessions is the saved views' job (VIEW-004, plan-views-browser).
acceptance_criteria:
- camera.rs unit tests: set_eye_target round-trips eye() and target within 1e-12 for 20 seeded eye/target pairs, including eye straight above the target; coincident points return an error and leave the camera unchanged.
- set_fov(60 degrees) stores exactly 60 degrees in radians; values outside the range are clamped; fit() (camera.rs:212-216) uses the current field of view.
- Custom preset: altitude 30 degrees and azimuth 0 (view direction north, +Y) give back() = (0, -cos 30, sin 30) within 1e-12; azimuth 90 looks east; the five existing presets give unchanged yaw and pitch.
- look_along: for 26 directions (cube faces, edges and corners) the view direction equals the requested direction within 1e-12 and the screen up vector is the projection of +Z, or +Y when looking straight down or up (north stays up).
- Vertical correction: with pitch 30 degrees and correction on, both end points of five vertical segments (x, y, 0)-(x, y, 10) in front of the camera project to the same screen x within 1e-6 points; center_ray_hits_target and zoom_keeps_point_under_cursor (camera.rs:317-340) pass with correction on and off; a screen point projected and re-cast through ray() passes the model point within 1e-9 m.
- VIEW-023 persistence: with correction on, orbit, pan, zoom_at, fit, every preset (Custom included) and toggle_projection leave vertical_correction set; a serde_json round trip of Camera3d keeps it and every other field bit-identical; above 75 degrees pitch is_correction_active() is false while the property stays on, and it is active again once the pitch returns below.
- toggle_projection keeps the target's apparent size: a 1 m segment at the target has the same screen length within 1e-6 before and after.
- UND-005 regression test (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs tests): on a Workspace with two_storey_shell, orbit, pan, zoom_at, fit, every preset, set_eye_target, set_fov, look_along, toggle_projection and vertical correction leave project.revision and the undo count unchanged; the existing zoom_history test (camera.rs:307-315) is kept.
- Satisfies the camera-model clauses of VIEW-020 (numeric eye, target and field of view; custom preset) and VIEW-023; UND-005 stays done with an explicit test.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-020 VIEW-023 UND-005
No Appendix D values for the camera; proposals: field of view 45 degrees default, 10-120 degrees range; vertical correction off by default and suspended above 75 degrees pitch.

title: Measure the area of drawn and picked polygons in plan and 3D
description:
WHY: The measure tool shall also measure the area of a picked polygon (MEA-006). The gap analysis lists it missing (remaining effort S, depends on MEA-001); only the 2D signed_area helper exists (crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:26). 'Picked polygon' covers a polygon whose corners the user picks with snapping and an existing closed outline the user picks with one click, so both are offered in plan and 3D.

WHAT: Extend MeasureTool (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/measure.rs, task 12) with an Area mode with two input styles chosen in its mode strip (tool_modes, ui/properties.rs:745). Points: the corners are picked through PointInput (snapping, typed coordinates) and the polygon closes on Enter, double-click or a click on the first point; in 3D the corners are full 3D points (no needs_horizontal). Pick outline: a click takes an existing outline: in 3D the planar Face under the cursor from the PickIndex (task 06, inner boundary loops as holes); in plan the cut polygon of the PlanElement under the cursor (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs, PlanElement.cut) or, where no cut polygon is hit, the outline of the slab under the cursor minus its holes. The area is computed by Newell's method on the polygon's best-fit plane with holes subtracted, together with the perimeter; a non-planar point polygon gets a warning plus its area projected on the working plane. The readout gains 'Area' and 'Perimeter' rows formatted with format_area and format_length (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:359, 283); the polygon is drawn translucent in plan and as an outline through Overlay3d in 3D. Still no Command. Out of scope: the plan-projected union area of a selection (MEA-004, Could), selection quantities (MEA-002).
design: Newell normal n = sum over edges of ((y_i - y_j)(z_i + z_j), (z_i - z_j)(x_i + x_j), (x_i - x_j)(y_i + y_j)); area = |n| / 2; holes are measured with the outer ring's normal and subtracted. Planarity: the maximum distance of the vertices from the plane through the vertex centroid with normal n above the model tolerance (0.01 mm, NFR-ACC-003) triggers the warning and the projected area. Picked outlines use the exact source rings (geo polygons through polygon_rings, plan.rs:298, in plan; Face boundary loops in 3D) rather than re-sampled points, so the result equals the geometric area. Values stay f64 until the readout (NFR-ACC-005). The pick style is a mode button rather than a modifier so it cannot collide with the INP-007 lock keys or the Alt-drag orbit of the 3D view.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests on the consumer without egui: a 6 x 4 rectangle gives 24.00 m2 and perimeter 20.000 m; an L shape and a polygon on a vertical wall face (Newell) are exact within 1e-9; closing by Enter, by double-click and by a click on the first point gives the same area; a polygon with one corner lifted 0.1 m reports the non-planar warning and its area projected on the working plane.
- Pick in plan: on two_storey_shell a pick inside the upper slab gives its outline area minus the stair opening within 1e-9 m2; a pick on a wall gives the area of its cut polygon.
- Pick in 3D: a pick on the top face of the upper slab gives the same area as the PickIndex Face (task 06) and highlights the face boundary; a pick on a wall side face gives length x height of that face within 1e-9 m2.
- No Command is produced by any area variant: project.revision and the undo count are unchanged.
- An imperial project reports square feet through format_area; a comma-decimal preference formats with commas.
- kittest: the Measure tool's mode strip offers 'Area' with 'Points' and 'Pick outline', and the readout shows 'Area' and 'Perimeter' labels.
- Satisfies MEA-006.
notes:
SRS: MEA-006
No Appendix D value for areas; format_area (units.rs:359) shows 2 decimals in m2 or ft2.

title: Place cut planes by two points in an orthogonal view
description:
WHY: VIEW-042 (M): cut planes are positioned by two points in an orthogonal view (or numerically, 09). Placing a cut through a specific wall is the everyday use, and typing coordinates for it is slow.

WHAT: A 'Cut plane' view tool usable in plan panes (a top view: the two points define a vertical plane applied to the most recently active 3D pane) and in 3D panes whose camera looks along a principal axis (the parallel Top, Front and Side presets of crates/archicraft-app/src/views/camera.rs:218-226): click 1 and click 2 define a line in the view plane, the plane contains that line and the view direction, and click 3 picks the side to remove with a shaded preview of the removed half. Esc cancels one step, Backspace removes the last point, typed length and angle work for the second point through the existing typed-input path, and points snap to model vertices and edges within 8 px (D.1). The new plane opens in the dialog of 09 for adjustment. In a perspective or non-orthogonal view the prompt asks to switch to Top, Front or Side and offers buttons. Out of scope: working-plane input in arbitrary 3D views (3d-input-navigation).
design: Orthogonality test: the view direction lies within 0.5 deg of a principal axis (the Top preset uses pitch 89.9 deg, camera.rs:221, so a 0.01 deg tolerance would reject it); the constructor then uses that exact axis instead of the camera direction, so the plane is exactly vertical or horizontal. In 3D, points come from the pick ray intersected with the plane through the camera target perpendicular to the view direction (Camera3d::ray); in plan from Camera2d::to_world. Snapping: in plan reuse SnapTargets and snap() (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:158-270); in 3D use projected model vertices from the scene's CPU data. If the point-input service of point-input-snapping exists, implement the tool as a consumer of its step and preview API instead of duplicating input handling. Normal = normalise((p2 - p1) x view direction), oriented so the side click lies on the removed side. Pitfall: the tool must not change the element selection or create Commands.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test of the pure constructor: in a Top view, points (0, 0) and (4, 0) with the side click at (2, 1) give the vertical plane y = 0 removing y > 0; in a Front view the plane contains the viewing axis; collinear or coincident points are refused; the Top, Front and Side presets (camera.rs:218-226) count as orthogonal and give exactly vertical or horizontal planes.
- kittest: in a plan pane two clicks and a side click add a vertical plane to the last active 3D pane; the headless golden of that pane shows the cut with caps.
- Snapping to a wall corner within 8 px gives its exact coordinates (0.1 mm).
- The status line prompts each step; Esc and Backspace behave as in the element tools; a perspective view shows the 'switch to an orthogonal view' prompt.
- Satisfies the two-point placement clause of VIEW-042.
notes: SRS: VIEW-042

title: Add kind and storey-range filters with trimming to 3D views
description:
WHY: VIEW-041 (M): 3D views offer filters by element kind and by storey range (all storeys, or from-to, optionally trimming elements at the range limits). Epic acceptance: a storey range with trimming shows capped bodies (snapshot). Gap row VIEW-041: build_scene has no kind or storey filter (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-110).

WHAT: A 'Filters' popover in the 3D view-control bar (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:193-227) and a View menu item '3D filters...': a checkbox per registered element kind (from the kind registry of element-kind-framework; Wall and Slab today) with All and None; storey range 'All storeys' or From and To combos listed highest first, plus 'Trim at range limits'. Changes apply live to the active pane's restrictions (generation bump); trimmed limits become clip planes (06) with caps (07). A range whose storey was deleted is reported in the status line and treated as All. Out of scope: the indicator and reset (13), exploded storeys (14, which adds its toggle to this popover).
design: Popover built with egui::Popup or menu_button in the right-to-left status bar section, using widgets::choice (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/widgets.rs) for the storey combos; storeys from StoreyList::highest_first (storey.rs:134). Kind list iterates the kind registry so later kinds (columns, beams, roofs) appear without UI changes; kinds stored as codes in the model (01). Trim limits: bottom = elevation(from), top = elevation(to) + height(to); admission rules from 01. Pitfall: From above To must be swapped or refused with a message; keep the popover open while toggling checkboxes.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: opening Filters and unticking Wall removes the wall code from the pane's restrictions.kinds and makes walls non-selectable in that pane; From = To = '01 First floor' without trim admits only storey-01 elements; ticking 'Trim at range limits' adds the two trim planes to the resolved restrictions.
- Headless golden 'storey_range_trimmed': two_storey_shell with range 00..00 trimmed shows bodies cut at +3.000 m (D.1) with closed caps; a probe inside a wall's top cap has the cap colour.
- With range 00..00 trimmed, Command::SetStoreyHeight setting storey 00 to 3.20 m moves the top trim plane to +3.200 m without any edit of the restriction (resolved z = elevation + height).
- Deleting the 'To' storey shows a status issue and the view falls back to All storeys.
- No undo step, Project.revision unchanged.
- Satisfies VIEW-041.
notes: SRS: VIEW-041

title: Run point input, element tools and edit consumers in 3D views
description:
WHY: All element tools and edit commands shall work in 3D views on the working plane (VIEW-025, INP-015). The gap analysis found the 3D half missing: tools accept plan points only (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:451 add_point(project, storey, DVec2), moved to crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/ by point-input-snapping-01) and are driven solely from plan.rs:456-470; view3d.rs never feeds the tool; there is no 3D typed input or preview, and Command::MoveElements is not reachable from the UI. What exists stays: click and Shift-click selection (view3d.rs:165-188), Delete in the 3D context menu (view3d.rs:284-290) and properties edits on the global selection (workspace.rs:54, ui/properties.rs) already act on elements picked in 3D, and temporary orbit with Shift+middle drag (view3d.rs:153-158), Alt+primary drag and persistent orbit mode (view3d.rs:160-163) exist, but no tool runs in 3D yet. 3D orbit shall work temporarily with a modifier and the middle button without leaving the active tool (VIEW-021). The epic acceptance requires that drawing a wall in the 3D view on a storey working plane yields the same element as in plan, tested through the ViewSurface trait.

WHAT: view3d.rs hosts ws.input (PointInput) on a Camera3dSurface over the pane's working plane whenever a drawing tool or an InputConsumer is active: pointer moves resolve with grid and plane-projected plan targets of the storey snap index on horizontal planes, clicks and double-clicks commit, keys go through a views/input_bridge.rs shared with plan.rs (KeyInput translation and the focus-lock filter), the tracker and step prompt show as in plan, and previews, rubber bands and snap glyphs are drawn through Overlay3d. Add PlacementContext to InputContext: the vertical offset of a horizontal working plane above the active storey becomes the base offset of plan-based kinds (Wall base_offset, Slab offset), so a plane at the storey elevation gives exactly the plan element. Consumers flag needs_horizontal in StepSpec; on a vertical, three-point or face plane they continue on the horizontal plane through their first point, while consumers without the flag (move, measure, mirror) receive full 3D points via InputContext.frame. With the Select tool the existing selection picking stays. Navigation (task 03 intents) never touches the tool state. Out of scope: 3D mesh snap targets (10), axis guides (11), plane definition commands (09).
design: Event flow in view3d.rs: navigation intents first (task 03), then, if a consumer is active, PointInput; a primary click only commits when no orbit drag happened (respect egui's drag threshold). Previews: consumers return plane-coordinate outlines (Preview.outlines); lift them with frame.to_model and draw with Overlay3d; walls additionally draw the top outline at base + height from the tool defaults so the user sees the body. Plan snap targets on horizontal planes: the storey SnapIndex of point-input-snapping-02 is in plan coordinates, which equal plane coordinates (task 07), so it is reused directly for a plane at any elevation; for non-horizontal planes only grid and (task 10) 3D targets apply. Edge-on planes (to_plane None) show 'Working plane seen edge-on' in the tracker. Keep the per-element AddElements semantics the wall chain has after point-input-snapping-14 (one undo step per chain). The registry test is the guard rail for later epics: a new ToolKind without a script fails it.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/view3d_input.rs (headless, no egui context): the same wall-chain script (clicks at model points projected to screen through each surface, then a typed polar/Cartesian sequence) run on the plan surface and on Camera3dSurface (perspective yaw -60 pitch 30, parallel isometric, vertical correction on) with a horizontal working plane at the active storey elevation produces equal Commands: element fields equal within 1e-9 for snapped clicks and bit-identical for typed input (epic acceptance clause).
- A working plane at storey elevation + 1.20 m produces a wall with base_offset = default + 1.20 m on the active storey; on a vertical working plane the wall tool continues on the horizontal plane through its first point and the prompt says so.
- Registry test: every ToolKind in ToolKind::ALL and every InputConsumer exported for tests (including point-input-snapping's TransformStub, which emits Command::MoveElements) completes its scripted steps on Camera3dSurface, so kinds and edit commands added later are covered automatically (VIEW-025 'all element tools and edit commands').
- Orbiting with Shift+middle drag and with orbit mode during a wall chain keeps the pending points and the active tool (VIEW-021).
- kittest (runs without wgpu; input and overlays do not need the render state): with the Wall tool active in a 3D tab the status line shows the wall prompt, two clicks plus Enter create a wall, the Esc ladder works, Delete in the 3D context menu still deletes the selection, and one Undo removes the chain.
- Satisfies VIEW-025 (with 3D snapping completed by tasks 10 and 11) and VIEW-021's 'without leaving the active tool' clause; INP-015's default horizontal plane is usable end to end.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-025 INP-015 VIEW-021
Decision: plan-based kinds on a non-horizontal working plane use the horizontal plane through the first point (refusing would block drawing on top of a picked slab face); revisit when inclined kinds (roofs, free-form solids) arrive.

title: Build a BVH pick index with planar faces over evaluated geometry
description:
WHY: Point-on-face snapping in 3D (INP-016), a working plane picked from a face (INP-015), aligning the view to a picked face, cut faces included (VIEW-022), 3D measuring (MEA-001) and the area of a picked face (MEA-006, task 14) all need face-level picking that returns the exact f64 hit point, the face plane and normal, and the face boundary. Today pick() (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:75-91) loops over every element, part and triangle (TriMesh::ray_hit, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:181) on each click and returns only the element and the hit point; snapping on pointer move cannot afford that.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/pick.rs: PickIndex::build(&Project, &ModelGeometry) storing world-space triangles (storey elevation added, f64) tagged with element, part and planar face; planar faces formed by grouping edge-adjacent coplanar triangles, each Face carrying its plane (point, unit normal), boundary loops in 3D, area and edges; a median-split BVH over triangle bounds with ray(origin, dir, filter) -> Option<Hit { element, part, face, point, normal, t }>, ray_all(), and near_ray(origin, dir, radius_at_t) returning vertices and edges whose bounds come within a depth-dependent radius of the ray (for task 10). A PickPlane hook (extra analytic planes with an id and optional clip polygon) lets 3d-view-restrictions register cut planes and caps without changing the API. In the app, cache an Arc<PickIndex> in Workspace keyed by project revision next to `scene` (workspace.rs:44-66), built lazily, and make view3d.rs pick() use it with the visibility filter (Project::is_visible) passed as a closure. Out of scope: GPU id-buffer hover picking (selection-transforms), snap candidate logic (10).
design: Coplanarity: group triangles whose unit normals differ by less than 1e-6 rad and whose vertices lie within the model tolerance (0.01 mm, NFR-ACC-003; use the tolerance module of element-kind-framework if it has landed, otherwise a local constant with a TODO-free comment pointing to it) of the seed plane, flood-filling over shared edges keyed by quantised vertex positions (mesh.rs:53 uses 1e-6). Boundary loops: edges used once within a face. BVH: flat Vec<Node> with AABB and child indices, leaves of at most 8 triangles, split at the median of the longest axis; slab test for ray-AABB; Moller-Trumbore in f64 reusing ray_triangle (mesh.rs:262, made pub(crate)). No new dependency (rstar 0.12 has no ray traversal; a 150-line BVH is simpler than a custom SelectionFunction). The index lives in the headless geometry crate so tests need no GPU and the IFCX and model crates stay untouched. Incremental rebuilds can follow the per-element evaluation cache of element-kind-framework later; a full rebuild per revision is acceptable now (built lazily, only when a 3D view picks or snaps).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/pick.rs: on two_storey_shell, 10,000 seeded rays return the same nearest element and t within 1e-9 as brute force over ModelGeometry.
- A vertical ray from above at (6.0, 4.5) hits the top face of the highest slab with normal (0, 0, 1), the face plane at that slab's top elevation, and a face area equal to the slab outline area minus holes within 1e-9 m2.
- A ray hitting a wall's long side returns a face normal perpendicular to the reference line and horizontal; a face on storey 1 carries the storey elevation; the two triangles of a rectangular face form one Face with four boundary vertices.
- near_ray returns a wall's top corner vertex for a ray passing 0.02 m from it with radius 0.05 m and not with radius 0.01 m.
- A registered PickPlane nearer than any mesh is returned with its id; a filter that hides an element makes rays pass through it without a rebuild.
- Timing tests (debug profile, loose): building the index for the 5,000-wall stand-in (or a generated equivalent) under 2 s; 10,000 rays on two_storey_shell under 0.5 s in total.
- App regression: view3d pick() returns the same element as the old linear version for 100 seeded screen points; the index is built once per revision (debug counter).
- Provides the picking basis for INP-015, INP-016, VIEW-022 and MEA-001 (no SRS clause is closed by this task alone).
notes:
SRS: INP-015 INP-016 VIEW-022 MEA-001
(enabling task; the requirements are closed by tasks 08-15: working planes and align from faces in 09, face snapping in 10, measuring in 12 and 14, mirror planes from faces in 15)

title: WorkingPlane type and the Camera3d ViewSurface implementation
description:
WHY: In 3D, input shall happen on a working plane that can be horizontal at a typed elevation (default: the active storey elevation), vertical through two points, defined by three points, or picked from a face (INP-015), and all element tools and edit commands shall work in 3D views on it (VIEW-025). point-input-snapping defines the ViewSurface trait and SurfaceFrame (crates/archicraft-app/src/input/surface.rs) and implements them for plan views only; INP-013's 3D clause (the working plane carries the same grid) was explicitly left to this epic. Today view3d.rs has no working plane at all, only a pick ray (views/view3d.rs:166-169). The risk named for this epic is input precision in perspective views.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/input/working_plane.rs (egui-free): WorkingPlane { Horizontal { elevation }, Vertical { a, b, base_z }, ThreePoint { p0, p1, p2 }, Face { origin, normal, x_hint } } with frame() -> SurfaceFrame and validation (collinear points, zero-length bases). New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/surface3d.rs: Camera3dSurface { camera, rect, frame } implementing input::ViewSurface: to_plane by intersecting Camera3d::ray (camera.rs:261-275) with the plane, None for grazing rays or hits behind the eye; to_screen through projection and view matrices; model_per_pixel at the hit depth; plus an Overlay3d helper that projects 3D segments with near-plane clipping for drawing previews, guides, glyphs and the plane grid in later tasks. View3dState gains working_plane, defaulting to Horizontal at the active storey elevation and following storey changes until the user defines another plane. Horizontal frames take the PlanGrid rotation and origin from point-input-snapping-10 so grid snapping and constraint directions match plan views. Out of scope: hosting PointInput in the 3D view (08), the plane definition commands and plane drawing (09).
design: Horizontal planes use identity axes (x = +X, y = +Y, rotated only by the PlanGrid rotation), so plane coordinates equal model XY and consumers written for plan views work unchanged; this is what makes the 'same element as in plan' acceptance hold bit-for-bit for typed input. Vertical: x = normalize(b - a), y = +Z, origin (a.x, a.y, base_z). Three-point: x = normalize(p1 - p0), n = normalize((p1 - p0) x (p2 - p0)), y = n x x, reject when |(p1 - p0) x (p2 - p0)| < 1e-9 |p1 - p0| |p2 - p0|. Face: x along the longest boundary edge of the picked Face (PickIndex, task 06) for a stable grid orientation, or the PlanGrid x axis when the face is horizontal. Ray-plane: t = (origin_plane - o).n / (d.n), reject |d.n| < sin(1 degree); in parallel projection all rays are parallel, so a plane seen edge-on yields None and the host shows a hint (task 08). Screen coordinates cross into input/ as DVec2 points (egui-free contract of point-input-snapping-01); conversion from egui::Pos2 stays in views/surface3d.rs. Pitfall: Camera3d::ray uses the projection with scene radius = distance (camera.rs:264); keep to_screen on the same matrices.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: frame() is orthonormal (|x| = |y| = 1, x.y = 0 within 1e-12) for all four kinds; three collinear points and coincident vertical base points return errors; the horizontal frame at z = 3.0 maps plane (2, 5) to model (2, 5, 3.0) bit-identically to the plan surface at a storey of elevation 3.0.
- Camera3dSurface: screen -> plane -> screen round-trips within 1e-4 points and plane -> screen -> plane within 1e-9 x distance for perspective, parallel and vertical-correction cameras (task 01); a ray within 1 degree of the plane returns None; model_per_pixel agrees with a finite difference within 1%.
- Overlay3d: a segment crossing the near plane is clipped to its visible part; a segment fully behind the eye yields None.
- The default working plane equals the active storey elevation and follows a storey switch; after the user sets another plane it no longer follows.
- A PlanGrid rotated by 30 degrees with origin (1, 1) gives a horizontal working-plane frame with the same rotation and origin (INP-013 3D clause through ViewSurface::frame()).
- Precision: typed plane coordinates never pass through the ray; a test asserts that typed values resolve through frame.to_model only.
- Satisfies the data model and surface mapping of INP-015 (definitions UI in 09) and prepares VIEW-025.
notes:
SRS: INP-015 VIEW-025
The working plane is per-pane view state: not saved in the file and not undoable (decision; saved views may store it later through plan-views-browser).

title: Infer X, Y and Z axis guides from the last point in 3D views
description:
WHY: In 3D views snapping shall find, from the last point, inference guides parallel to the X, Y and Z axes (INP-016). The guide model of point-input-snapping (GuideShape in crates/archicraft-app/src/input/guide.rs, task 08 of that epic) is two-dimensional in plane coordinates, the Cartesian ΔZ field is display-only until a 3D working plane exists (point-input-snapping-05), and nothing lets the user leave the working plane along Z with a typed distance, which tools that accept 3D points (move with ΔZ, measure, mirror) and the AS-04 precision promise need.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/input/guide3d.rs: Guide3 lines through the previous 3D point along +X, +Y and +Z (and along the user-origin axes when a rotated user origin is set, INP-014), the closest point between each guide and the cursor ray as a Guide candidate, GuideIntersection candidates where a guide meets a picked face, the working plane or another axis guide from a marked 3D reference (INP-011 marks lifted to 3D), and the constraint modifier holding the cursor on the nearest axis. A typed distance while the cursor is on an axis guide resolves along that axis; the Cartesian ΔX/ΔY/ΔZ fields become fully active in 3D for consumers that accept 3D points. Guides are drawn dashed and colour-coded (X red, Y green, Z blue) through Overlay3d with a tracker label naming the axis. Out of scope: persistent guide lines in 3D (INP-012, owned by point-input-snapping).
design: Closest points between the guide line g(s) = p + s a and the ray r(t) = o + t d: with w = p - o, b = a.d, denominator 1 - b^2 (unit vectors); skip near-parallel guides (1 - b^2 < 1e-9). The candidate is accepted when the screen distance between g(s) and the cursor is within the snap radius. Typed distances along a guide use the guide direction directly (p + s a with s parsed), never the ray, keeping AS-04 precision. Lock interplay: an active INP-007 lock in 3D is the guide's 3D analogue; reuse Locks with a third axis for Z when the consumer accepts 3D points. The marks of point-input-snapping-09 store owners and segment indices; in 3D a mark stores the model point so it can generate axis guides through it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: previous point (1, 2, 3) and a cursor ray passing 4 points from the vertical through it give a Guide candidate with x = 1 and y = 2 exactly; typing 2.5 on that guide gives (1, 2, 5.5) exactly.
- The Z guide through a wall's base corner intersects the top face of the slab above at its top elevation as a GuideIntersection candidate; the X guide meets a vertical working plane at the exact intersection.
- Shift holds the cursor on the nearest axis guide; releasing it frees the cursor; with a user origin rotated by 30 degrees the X and Y guides follow the rotation.
- Cartesian ΔZ typed as 1.200 in 3D gives a point 1.200 m above the previous point for a test consumer that accepts 3D points; planar consumers ignore ΔZ as before.
- Precedence: guide intersections rank between division and edge, guides between edge and face (the task 10 table).
- kittest: drawing in the 3D view with the cursor above the previous point shows the label 'Z axis'; every guide colour is drawn without panic.
- Satisfies INP-016's axis-guide clause (completing INP-016 with task 10).
notes: SRS: INP-016

title: Add an interactive section box with draggable face handles
description:
WHY: VIEW-042 (M): besides cut planes, 3D views support a section box with interactive handles, covered by the global cut-plane toggle and capped like any cut. Epic acceptance: two cut planes plus a section box with draggable handles render closed caps in uniform or material colour.

WHAT: Action::SectionBox toggles the box of the active 3D pane; the first activation fits it to the selection or, without one, to the visible elements plus 0.10 m margin; 'Fit box to selection' refits. views/view3d.rs draws the 12 box edges and 6 face handles as an overlay and lets the user drag a handle to move its face along its axis (minimum box size 0.10 m), with hover highlight and cursor change; handles hide while orbiting. The 'Cut planes' dialog of 09 gets a 'Section box' section with min and max x, y, z. The box resolves to six planes with caps (01, 07, 15). Out of scope: rotated boxes (axis-aligned in project coordinates in v1).
design: Overlay with painter_at(rect) on top of the texture; project with the same view-projection as the render; clip box edges in homogeneous space before the perspective divide (Liang-Barsky against the near plane) so edges behind the eye do not wrap. Hit radius 8 px scaled by pixels_per_point; drag state stored in View3dState; drag_started over a handle takes precedence over orbit and pan (view3d.rs:120-165). Each drag step bumps the restrictions generation; to keep dragging fluid only the uniforms and cap polygons change, never the scene. Pointers: view3d.rs:102-160, camera.rs ray() and projection_matrix, render3d.rs FrameKey.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: the handle drag maps pointer motion to the face coordinate through the closest point between pick ray and axis line, for perspective and parallel cameras; the minimum size clamps; fit uses the selection bounds plus margin.
- kittest/headless: enabling the box with one wall selected clips everything outside it; a simulated drag of the +X handle changes only max.x, by the amount the math predicts; clicking a handle does not change the selection and navigation still works away from the handles.
- Golden 'two_planes_and_box' (pipelines of 07 and 15): two cut planes plus a box positioned by simulated handle drags render closed caps in uniform and in material colour.
- The global 'Cut planes' toggle hides box and planes together and restores both.
- No undo step, Project.revision unchanged.
- Satisfies the section-box clause of VIEW-042.
notes: SRS: VIEW-042

title: Persist the new restriction fields in IFCX and prove IFX-068
description:
WHY: Restrictions are stored in saved views (VIEW-004, epic acceptance), so the fields added in 01 must survive save and reopen in the archicraft:: views record that plan-views-browser-08 writes. VIEW-047 (M): view filters, hidden elements and cut planes shall never change the model geometry or the standard (non-archicraft::) IFCX content (IFX-068: elements are written regardless of layer visibility, view filters, hidden elements and cut planes). Gap row VIEW-047 (partial; exists and kept): the writer already writes every element independent of view state (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:301-327), but no test asserts that the saved file's standard content is identical with any view state.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: optional keys inside the restrictions object of a view: isolated (array of UUIDs), region {polygon [[x, y], ...], side inside|outside, trim}, per cut plane side, enabled and binding {storey, offset}, cutPlanesEnabled, sectionBox.enabled, caps {mode material|uniform, color}, explode. writer.rs writes them only when set or non-default; reader.rs reads them leniently (report.or with defaults), and dangling storey or element ids become warning Problems with the value dropped and the view kept (PRJ-008 style). samples.rs: the saved 3D view of plan-views-browser-08 gains a full restriction set (isolation, region, two cut planes of which one is bound to a storey, section box, uniform caps, explode); goldens are re-blessed and reviewed. Out of scope: app behaviour.
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md: declare with optional(...) in schema.rs, write with json! in writer.rs project_attribute, read with report.or(...) in reader.rs read_project_data. Enumerations derive from the model ALL arrays via .map(code); parameters at full precision; hidden and isolated lists as flat arrays to respect the D.9 nesting limit. Reuse the archicraft::-stripping helper of plan-views-browser-08's visibility_state_never_changes_standard_content test (move it into a shared test module if it is local). FORMAT_VERSION: unchanged if no release happened since plan-views-browser-08 bumped it, otherwise bump with a migration entry. Pitfalls: keep deterministic key order (json.rs) so golden diffs stay reviewable; write region polygons as plain [x, y] pairs in metres.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs restrictions_round_trip: every new field with non-trivial values survives write and read (Project equality).
- restrictions_never_change_standard_content (VIEW-047, IFX-068): the sample with and without the restricted saved view, with every element hidden or isolated away, and with every layer hidden, produces byte-identical JSON once all archicraft:: attributes are stripped; every element and mesh node is still written.
- old_files_without_restriction_keys: the previous golden reads with default restrictions and no Problem; a hand-edited file whose restriction references a deleted element and a deleted storey loads with one warning each and keeps the view.
- The offline validator accepts the declarations (IFX-061), conformance/run.sh is green on the re-blessed goldens, and the golden diff touches only the archicraft::project views record.
- Satisfies the IFCX side of VIEW-047 and the persistence of the restriction sections of VIEW-004.
notes: SRS: VIEW-047 VIEW-042 VIEW-044 VIEW-046 VIEW-061

title: Working plane, 3D input, measure tool, camera and navigation
description:
Make every tool and edit command work in 3D views on a working plane (horizontal, vertical, three-point or picked face), add face snapping and axis guides, align-view-to-surface, the measure tool in 2D and 3D, mirroring about a 3D plane, full camera editing with presets, orbit pivot, two-point perspective, navigation presets, trackpad gestures, high-DPI and multi-monitor behaviour. Walk mode, 3D mouse and pen tablets (Could) are in could-scope-polish.

Risks: Input precision in perspective views; numeric entry and typed working-plane elevations keep AS-04 precision.
design: archicraft-app input::ViewSurface for Camera3d (ray-plane intersection, face pick from a GpuScene BVH), WorkingPlane state per 3D pane, camera.rs presets and two-point correction, preferences for SET-003, winit gesture events for pinch and rotate.
acceptance_criteria: Drawing a wall in the 3D view on a storey working plane yields the same element as in plan (test through the ViewSurface trait); face snapping and X/Y/Z guides in 3D; look-perpendicular-to-working-plane and align-to-face commands; the measure tool reports distance, angle, height and area in working units in plan and 3D without creating elements (AS-04 step); camera eye, target and field of view editable numerically; three navigation presets switchable without restart; the trackpad orbit gesture works on macOS and Windows precision touchpads; a DPI change when moving between monitors re-renders correctly; camera moves never create undo steps (existing test kept).
notes: SRS: INP-015 INP-016 VIEW-020 VIEW-021 VIEW-022 VIEW-023 VIEW-025 MEA-001 MEA-006 EDT-022 SET-003 HW-001 HW-002 HW-006 HW-007 UND-005

title: Add hide, isolate (selection or 3D marquee) and show all with D.8 shortcuts
description:
WHY: VIEW-040 (M): in 3D, section and elevation views the user hides the selected elements in this view only, without changing layers, shows only the selection or the contents of a marquee, and restores everything with one show-all command; show all still honours layer visibility. UI-008 with Appendix D.8 requires default shortcuts for show all, hide selection and isolate selection; the UI-008 gap row (partial) lists exactly these as missing because the commands do not exist (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs:7-39). Exists and extended, not replaced: the shortcut table (actions.rs:114-146), the typing rules (is_single_key, app.rs:464-495) and the tests shortcuts_are_unique and appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts (actions.rs:177-204). UI-017: every command is reachable from a menu. Section and elevation views do not exist before sections-elevations-dims (increment 3), so this task keeps the actions independent of the 3D renderer and hands their section/elevation clause over explicitly.

WHAT: actions.rs: Action::HideSelection, Action::IsolateSelection, Action::IsolateMarquee and Action::ShowAll (ALL, labels, proposed shortcuts H, I, Shift+I and Shift+H; single keys are already blocked while typing by is_single_key), the three D.8 ones added to appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts. app.rs run() (app.rs:377): the actions edit the restrictions of the active pane through Workspace::restrictions_mut (04) and ViewRestrictions::hide/isolate/show_all (01), bumping its generation; in a plan pane they act on the most recently active 3D pane and say so in the status line, and are disabled when there is none. Isolate marquee contents: a one-shot screen rectangle dragged in the 3D pane (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs); on release the admitted elements inside it are isolated with the plan marquee's direction rule (left to right: fully inside, right to left: touching, as PlanElement::in_rect in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:246), evaluated on each element's bounds projected with the pane's camera (model_bounds, view3d.rs:59), or through selection-transforms-07's projected 3D area test if it has landed; the selection stays unchanged and Esc cancels. Menu items in the View menu (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:78) and in the 3D context menu (view3d.rs:265). Hiding clears the selection; isolating while isolated narrows the isolation. Status messages name the count and the view. No undo step and no revision change. Section and elevation panes: the dispatch only needs restrictions_mut(pane) to return Some, so they get the four actions once sections-elevations-dims adds their ViewKind (the exhaustive supports_restrictions match of 01 forces that decision) and filters its slice input with ResolvedRestrictions::admits; 3d-view-restrictions-done files that follow-up bead. Out of scope: the plan-drawn region and its 'Isolate contents' (12), the indicator and reset (13).
design: Follow the 'Add a command' extension point for the Action part only: these are view actions, not model Commands, so they never reach History. Keep the dispatch in ArchiCraftApp::run (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:377) and the text-focus rules of app.rs:462-495. Track the most recently active 3D pane in Workspace (set where active_pane is set, view3d.rs:116). The concrete key bindings are a UI design deliverable (D.8); H and I are proposals checked against the element-tool keys (W, S today; C, B, R, D, N, M planned). Marquee projection: project the 8 corners of each admitted element's bounds with Camera3d::projection_matrix * view_matrix (camera.rs:233-262) and skip elements behind the near plane; this conservative box test is replaced by selection-transforms-07's mesh test where available. Pitfalls: Shift+H and Shift+I must not collide with any planned Shift shortcut; prune_selection must not drop elements hidden only in one pane (they may be visible in another).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs (no GPU): with a 3D pane active and one wall selected, pressing H puts the wall into the pane's restrictions.hidden, makes it non-selectable there and empties the selection; I with two walls selected isolates exactly them; Shift+H restores the hidden wall while a wall on a hidden layer stays invisible and non-selectable (show all honours layer visibility).
- Marquee: in a 3D pane of samples::storey_with_walls_and_slab() with the parallel Top preset, Isolate marquee contents and a left-to-right drag around one wall isolates only that wall, a right-to-left drag across two walls isolates both, the selection is unchanged and Esc during the drag changes nothing (pure unit test of the projected test plus one kittest).
- Throughout these tests Project.revision and the undo stack are unchanged, and a second 3D view still shows the hidden wall (per-view state).
- A unit test runs hide, isolate and show all through Workspace::restrictions_mut for a pane that has no View3dState and no renderer, proving the dispatch does not depend on the 3D view (the hook section and elevation panes will use).
- Labels 'Hide selection', 'Isolate selection', 'Isolate marquee contents' and 'Show all' exist in the View menu and in the 3D context menu; the two selection-based ones are disabled with an explanatory tooltip when the selection is empty.
- shortcuts_are_unique and appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts pass with the new actions, and the existing D.8 subset in actions.rs:187-204 is unchanged.
- Satisfies VIEW-040 for 3D views including the marquee clause (12 adds the plan-drawn region as a second marquee source), provides the hook for its section and elevation clause, and adds the D.8 view shortcuts of UI-008.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-040
Concrete shortcut keys need the UI designer's sign-off (Appendix D.8 says the bindings are a UI design deliverable).

title: Complete ViewRestrictions and resolve it to filters and clip planes
description:
WHY: Every restriction of this epic needs one plain-data definition that the renderer, picking, the indicator, saved views and IFCX share. VIEW-040 (M): hide the selected elements in this view only without changing layers, show only the selection or the contents of a marquee, and restore everything with one show-all command that still honours layer visibility; it names 3D, section and elevation views, and section and elevation views only arrive with sections-elevations-dims (increment 3), so the definition and its evaluation must not depend on the 3D renderer. VIEW-041 (M): filters by element kind and by storey range (all storeys, or from-to, optionally trimming elements at the range limits). VIEW-042 (M): several user-defined cut planes with an explicit side to remove, a section box, a global on/off toggle, caps in a uniform colour or the elements' own materials. VIEW-061 (S): a cut plane bindable to a storey elevation plus offset. VIEW-044 (S): a region filter (inside or outside, trimming or keeping elements whole). VIEW-046 (C): exploded storeys by a configurable distance. VIEW-043 (M) needs a single 'is any restriction active' predicate and a single reset. plan-views-browser-07 already defines ViewRestrictions {kinds, storey_range, hidden, cut_planes, section_box} as plain data in crates/archicraft-model/src/views.rs and allows this epic to add optional fields only. The gap rows of all eight requirements say 'missing': the only visibility filter today is the layer (Project::is_visible, used by build_scene in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-110 and by pick in views/view3d.rs:75-91).

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/views.rs add the optional fields isolated: Option<Vec<ElementId>>; region: Option<RegionFilter {polygon: Vec<DVec2>, side: RegionSide {Inside, Outside}, trim: bool}>; per cut plane side: RemoveSide {Positive, Negative}, enabled: bool and binding: Option<StoreyBinding {storey, offset}> (reuse whatever plan-views-browser-07 already put there); cut_planes_enabled: bool (the global toggle, serde default true); SectionBox.enabled; caps: Option<CapStyle {Material, Uniform(Rgb)}>; explode: Option<f64>; StoreyRange keeps {from, to, trim}. ViewKind::supports_restrictions(&self) -> bool as an exhaustive match without a wildcard arm (Model3d true, Plan false), so the Section and Elevation kinds that sections-elevations-dims-01 adds force an explicit decision at compile time. Pure methods: is_active(), active_kinds() -> Vec<RestrictionKind> (for the indicator), hide(ids), isolate(ids), show_all() (clears hidden and isolation only), clear() (back to default) and resolve(&Project) -> ResolvedRestrictions {admit data (hidden and isolated sets, kind set, storey membership), planes: Vec<ClipPlane {normal, d, source: User(i) | BoxFace(f) | StoreyBottom | StoreyTop}> (at most 16), region, explode offsets per storey, cap style, issues: Vec<ViewIssue>} with admits(&Element, &Project). Validation in validate.rs: at most 8 user planes, non-zero normals, box min < max on every axis, region polygon simple with 3 to 256 vertices and, when trim is set, at most 16 edges (the cap budget of 15), explode distance in [0, 100] m. Out of scope: IFCX (02), GPU and picking (04, 06), region classification against meshes (06, 12), any UI.
design: Approach: plain data plus pure functions so the app, IFCX and tests consume one definition; only Option or #[serde(default)] fields, so plan-views-browser-08's schema and goldens stay valid. Plane convention: a point p is kept when n.p + d >= 0 (the kept half-space), so 'remove positive side' is stored as a side flag and resolved by flipping n; all resolved planes are in absolute model coordinates (storey elevation applied). Storey membership: without trim, home storey index within [from, to] (StoreyList::index_of, crates/archicraft-model/src/storey.rs:88); with trim, the element's absolute vertical extent (Project::vertical_extent, project.rs:245, or its kind-registry successor from element-kind-framework) overlaps [elevation(from), elevation(to) + height(to)], plus the two trim planes. A storey binding fixes the z of the plane's reference point for any orientation. Box planes from AABB min/max. ResolvedRestrictions stores hidden/isolated as sorted Vec<ElementId> for binary search; the app caches it per (project.revision, restrictions generation). archicraft-model has no geo dependency: use the segment helpers of validate.rs:64-91 for polygon simplicity. Pitfalls: normalise normals in f64 and reject near-zero ones; never index storeys without index_of; keep RestrictionKind ordered for a stable indicator text.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/views.rs: ViewRestrictions::default() is inactive; setting each field alone makes is_active() true and active_kinds() name exactly that kind; clear() returns the default; show_all() clears hidden and isolated and leaves kinds, storey range, cut planes, box and region untouched.
- resolve on samples::two_storey_shell(): storey range 00..00 without trim admits only elements whose home storey is 00 and yields no plane; with trim it yields two horizontal planes at +0.000 and +3.000 m (D.1 storeys) and admits by vertical extent.
- VIEW-061: a plane bound to storey 01 with offset 1.10 m resolves to z = 4.10; after Command::SetStoreyElevation moves storey 01 to +3.20 m with shift_above (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:58-62) it resolves to z = 4.30 without the restriction being edited.
- A section box resolves to six inward planes; box.enabled = false or cut_planes_enabled = false removes user and box planes but keeps the storey trim planes.
- Dangling ids (deleted hidden or isolated element, deleted storey in the range or in a binding) produce one ViewIssue each, are ignored, and never panic.
- Validation rejects a ninth user plane, a zero normal, an inverted box, a polygon with fewer than 3 or more than 256 vertices or a self-intersection, a trimming region with 17 edges (accepted with trim = false), and a negative explode distance; existing round-trip tests and goldens stay unchanged (all new fields are optional).
- ViewKind::supports_restrictions is true for Model3d and false for Plan, and its match has no wildcard arm (review item).
- No Command, Edit or Project field is involved: the functions are pure, so restrictions cannot change the model (VIEW-047 by construction).
- Provides the data model of VIEW-040, VIEW-041, VIEW-042, VIEW-043, VIEW-044, VIEW-046 and VIEW-061.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-040 VIEW-041 VIEW-042 VIEW-043 VIEW-044 VIEW-046 VIEW-061
Appendix D has no values for these features. Proposed defaults for product-owner confirmation: cap style = element materials, uniform cap colour #A0A0A0, explode distance 3.00 m (the D.1 storey height). Decision taken here: show all (VIEW-040) clears hidden elements and isolation only; the VIEW-043 reset clears everything. Without trimming, storey membership is by home storey; with trimming, by vertical extent. Trimming regions are limited to 16 edges so that every trimmed boundary can be capped (VIEW-042 'displayed closed').

title: Verify exit criterion: Working plane, 3D input, measure tool, camera and navigation
description:
WHY: Closes the epic 3d-input-navigation once its exit criterion holds: tools and edit commands work in 3D views on a working plane (INP-015, VIEW-025) with face snapping and X/Y/Z guides (INP-016), look-perpendicular and align-view-to-surface (VIEW-022), a numerically editable camera with presets and two-point perspective (VIEW-020, VIEW-023), configurable navigation with orbit pivot (VIEW-021, SET-003, HW-001), trackpad gestures (HW-002, HW-007), high-DPI and multi-monitor behaviour (HW-006), the measure tool with distance, angle, height and drawn or picked areas (MEA-001, MEA-006), mirroring about a 3D plane (EDT-022) and navigation without undo steps (UND-005).

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged branch, check the manual test records (docs/manual-tests/trackpad.md, docs/manual-tests/high-dpi.md), update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence with file:line, remaining gaps such as cut faces becoming end-to-end testable with 3d-view-restrictions and any-plane mirroring in free-form-solids), report the 3D clauses of INP-008 (nodes, edges, division points, intersections, perpendicular feet) and INP-013 closed here, EDT-022 as partial until free-form-solids, add extension points (ViewSurface for new view kinds, PickPlane registration, NavigationScheme table, InputConsumer needs_horizontal), and close the epic in beads. No new features.
design: Checklist run, not development: verify that view3d_input.rs compares plan and 3D commands through the ViewSurface trait only; that the registry test covers every ToolKind; that the UND-005 regression test drives every camera operation and NavIntent; that the manual records name devices, dates and schemes for macOS and Windows; that FrameKey includes pixels_per_point; that no file under crates/archicraft-app/src/input/ depends on egui; that the IFCX golden files are unchanged by this epic (no schema change). Also verify that the registry test includes ToolKind::Measure and the mirror consumer, and that no navigation scheme maps plan middle drag to anything but pan.
acceptance_criteria:
- Drawing a wall in the 3D view on a storey working plane yields the same element as in plan (test through the ViewSurface trait); face snapping and X/Y/Z guides in 3D; look-perpendicular-to-working-plane and align-to-face commands; the measure tool reports distance, angle, height and area in working units in plan and 3D without creating elements (AS-04 step); camera eye, target and field of view editable numerically; three navigation presets switchable without restart; the trackpad orbit gesture works on macOS and Windows precision touchpads; a DPI change when moving between monitors re-renders correctly; camera moves never create undo steps (existing test kept).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green on the golden files.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID: INP-015 INP-016 VIEW-020 VIEW-021 VIEW-022 VIEW-023 VIEW-025 MEA-001 MEA-006 EDT-022 SET-003 HW-001 HW-002 HW-006 HW-007 UND-005, plus AS-04 (3D measure step) and the extension-point section.
- The epic 3d-input-navigation is closed in beads with a comment naming the tests that prove the 'same element as in plan' claim (tests/view3d_input.rs) and the AS-04 measure step.
notes: SRS: INP-015 INP-016 VIEW-020 VIEW-021 VIEW-022 VIEW-023 VIEW-025 MEA-001 MEA-006 EDT-022 SET-003 HW-001 HW-002 HW-006 HW-007 UND-005

title: Camera panel, projection command and draggable camera glyph in plan
description:
WHY: The perspective camera's eye position, target and field of view shall each be editable numerically and by direct manipulation, projection shall be switchable with one command, and the parallel presets including the custom one (rotation angles and azimuth) shall be reachable (VIEW-020); the persistent vertical correction of VIEW-023 (camera model in task 01) needs a switch in the UI; none of this may create undo steps (UND-005, done: camera state is per-view state outside the model, and this task keeps it that way). Today the projection switch is only a status-bar toggle (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:214-226) with no Action or shortcut, presets sit in a status-bar 'Views' menu (shell.rs:205-212), and there is no camera properties UI at all.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/camera_panel.rs: a non-modal 'Camera' window for the active 3D pane with Eye X/Y/Z, Target X/Y/Z (unit-aware widgets::length), Field of view (widgets::angle), Projection, Vertical correction, the preset buttons and the custom preset's Altitude and Azimuth fields, applied live through the task 01 setters (no Command, no draft). Actions in ui/actions.rs: ToggleProjection (provisional F4), CameraSettings, and one entry per preset in a View menu submenu '3D view presets' (shell.rs), with the status-bar controls calling the same actions. Direct manipulation in plan: when 'Show 3D camera in plan' is on, plan.rs draws the active 3D view's camera (eye disc, target cross, field-of-view wedge at the eye height) and lets the user drag the eye or the target glyph, which moves it in XY and keeps Z. Out of scope: navigation gestures and the lens (field of view) gesture (03), saving cameras in saved views (plan-views-browser).
design: The panel holds no copy of the camera: each frame it reads ws.views_3d[active] and writes through setters, so navigation and the panel never disagree. Use the 'Add a dialog' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md (Dialogs flag + Action + View menu item). When no 3D pane is active the panel shows the first 3D view's camera (like Action::OrbitMode, app.rs:426-446). Plan glyph: draw in views/plan.rs after the drawing, through Camera2d::to_screen (camera.rs:31-35); hit-test with the snap radius; drag with response.dragged_by(Primary) only while the Select tool is active and the pointer started on a glyph, so it never competes with drawing tools. The field-of-view wedge uses the horizontal field of view atan(tan(fov_y/2) * aspect) from the 3D pane's last_rect (view3d.rs:46-48). Pitfall: F4 may be a media key on macOS keyboards; the final binding belongs to commands-and-l10n (D.8 lists 'switch between plan and 3D' and 'orbit', not projection).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): View > 'Camera...' opens a window with the labels 'Eye X', 'Target X', 'Field of view', 'Vertical correction', 'Altitude' and 'Azimuth'.
- kittest: typing eye (10, -5, 1.6) and target (5, 4, 1.5) in metres moves the camera so eye() and target equal the typed values within 1e-9; typing 60 in Field of view stores 60 degrees exactly; typing in a feet-and-inches project parses through units.rs (INP-005 path).
- The ToggleProjection action switches projection from the menu, the shortcut and the status bar alike; shortcuts_are_unique (actions.rs:166-174) passes with the new bindings.
- kittest: View > '3D view presets' > 'Custom' with altitude 45 and azimuth 225 gives the expected back() vector.
- Plan glyph test: dragging the eye glyph by 40 points in a plan view with Camera2d.scale 40 moves the eye by 1.0 m in XY and keeps Z; dragging the target glyph moves only the target; the glyph is hidden when the toggle is off.
- kittest: ticking 'Vertical correction' sets camera.vertical_correction, the pane label (view3d.rs:248-262) shows it, and it is still on after an orbit drag, a preset and a projection switch (VIEW-023 persistent property).
- UND-005: after all of the above project.revision is unchanged and Edit > Undo stays disabled.
- Satisfies VIEW-020 (numeric editing, direct manipulation of eye and target, one-command projection switch, custom preset in the UI) together with task 01, and the user-facing switch of VIEW-023; the field-of-view gesture follows in task 03.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-020 VIEW-023 UND-005
Provisional binding F4 for ToggleProjection; confirm with commands-and-l10n.

title: Thin terrain points within a vertical tolerance
description:
WHY: TER-010 (C): terrain points may be thinned or simplified with a vertical tolerance (KB 337306: dense point sets; without point-cloud import, dense typed or generated sets). Status: TER-010 missing.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/terrain.rs thin(terrain, tolerance) -> ThinResult { keep: Vec<u32>, removed, max_deviation } by greedy insertion: start from the CDT of the boundary (derived heights), breaklines and their nodes (never removed), then repeatedly insert the remaining point with the largest vertical error against the current TIN until every candidate is within the tolerance, updating errors only for candidates in re-triangulated faces (bucketed by containing triangle). Model: Command::ThinTerrain { terrain, keep: Vec<u32> } removes all other points in one ReplaceElement after validating the ids. App: a 'Thin points' dialog from the terrain context menu with the tolerance (default 0.05 m) and a preview 'Removes N of M points; max deviation X', computed on a background thread and cancellable; OK executes. Out of scope: XY decimation, smoothing, breakline simplification.
design: Greedy insertion only inserts into spade's CDT, which avoids vertex removal in a constrained triangulation and guarantees the maximum error by construction. A binary heap keyed by (error, id) keeps the order deterministic. Pitfalls: points outside the boundary are kept, because they only feed boundary heights; the preview must not block the UI (NFR-PERF-007).
