Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/terrain.rs (task 04), triangulate.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: a planar terrain with 2,000 points thins to no interior points at tolerance 0.001 m; a noisy 10,000-point surface at 0.05 m passes a brute-force check that every original point lies within 0.05 m vertically of the thinned TIN; breakline nodes and points on the boundary are never removed; the result is deterministic.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: ThinTerrain removes exactly the points not kept and undo restores them; unknown ids are Invalid.
- Thinning the 50,000-point synthetic terrain runs under 2 s in release (criterion bench).
- Kittest: the dialog shows the preview text and OK reduces the point count shown in the properties.
- TER-010 satisfied.
notes:
SRS: TER-010
Default tolerance 0.05 m is a proposal.

title: Write and read terrain as IfcGeographicElement under the site
description:
WHY: TER-012 (M): terrain is written to IFCX as IfcGeographicElement, a child of the site, with a closed body mesh (Table 5-1, IFX-038). TER-014 (S): the top surface is additionally written as a separate, non-volumetric TopSurface part so consumers can recover the TIN. IFX-012 places site-level elements under the site; IFX-060 and IFX-061 keep the parametric data in archicraft:: attributes declared in-file; IFX-064 demands round-trip fidelity. Status: TER-012 and TER-014 missing; at increment 0 the writer nests elements only under storeys (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:297-317) and the reader reads elements only under storeys (reader.rs:504). element-kind-framework-07 adds site containment and the Body/Body_n helper, element-kind-framework-06 the per-kind codecs and element-kind-framework-05 IfcClass::GeographicElement.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/terrain.rs, registered with one codecs! line: archicraft::terrain { boundary: [[x, y]], points: [{ id, x, y, z }], breaklines: [{ id, nodes: [[x, y, z]], closed, contour }], bottom: { mode: depth | elevation, value }, material reference through the common helper, display: { smooth, planMode, contours: { base, interval, majorEvery, labelMajor, labelHeight }, tinSnaps }, nextId } plus the tool-defaults slot schema; numbers at full precision (NFR-ACC-002). Writer: bodies through the framework helper (Body or Body_1..n) and TopSurface or TopSurface_n children marked invisible through usd::usdgeom::visibility { visibility: 'invisible' } (declared in the bundled usd@v1 schema) and inheriting the terrain material, with v5 ids from their role names (IFX-010). Reader: through the codec, lenient defaults with warnings; Body and TopSurface children of a terrain are never read as elements. Rust test written_meshes_are_closed_bodies checks volumetric parts as closed and TopSurface parts as open upward surfaces. conformance/check.ts extends the site-level element handling of element-kind-framework-07: an IfcGeographicElement child of the site needs at least one Body or Body_n mesh, TopSurface parts are counted, and the edge-pairing closedness check of solid-kernel-ops-03 skips meshes named TopSurface or TopSurface_n (non-volumetric, IFX-032). New catalogue sample terrain_site (FixtureBuilder: two_storey_shell plus a terrain with 40 typed spot elevations and two contour breaklines on the ground storey) with golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/terrain-site.ifcx. Out of scope: SolidOperation relations on terrain (written by the solid-kernel-ops codec, exercised in task 11), georeferencing (task 02).
design: Follow the codec pattern of alpha/kinds/slab.rs (element-kind-framework-06) and the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point. Breakline nodes as [x, y, z] arrays and points as objects with ids keep diffs readable; ids are authoring data so selections and relations survive a round trip. Writing TopSurface invisible avoids z-fighting with the Body top in the reference viewer while consumers can still read the TIN (open question in notes). Terrain meshes are storey-local (task 04) and the site-level transform of element-kind-framework-07 translates by the home storey elevation, so world Z equals the input elevation. Pitfalls: declare the schema only when used, or goldens of other samples change; keep point and breakline order deterministic (IFX-007); the conformance job globs golden/*.ifcx, so the new golden is covered automatically. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/{mod,common,slab}.rs, alpha/schema.rs, writer.rs:355-417, reader.rs element dispatch, tests/roundtrip.rs, conformance/check.ts:67-103, crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs catalogue.
acceptance_criteria:
- terrain_roundtrip (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs): the terrain_site sample saves and loads to an equal project (ids, points, breaklines, bottom, display) with zero problems, and regenerated geometry equals the stored meshes within 0.1 mm (IFX-064).
- The terrain node is a child of IfcSite with bsi::ifc::class IfcGeographicElement and its bSDD uri, bsi::ifc::prop::Name, archicraft::element with homeStorey, and Body and TopSurface children with v5 paths; Body passes check_closed; TopSurface is invisible and open-manifold.
- Forced-budget test: a 10,000-point terrain written with a 2,000-point budget has Body_1..Body_n and TopSurface_1..m children, each within the budget and each Body_n closed (IFX-038).
- terrain-site.ifcx is reproduced byte for byte from the catalogue, passes conformance/run.sh with the extended check.ts (site-level element counted, Body parts closed, the open TopSurface exempt from the closedness check) and the offline validator; archicraft::terrain is declared only when a terrain or terrain slot exists, so every other golden stays bit-identical.
- A file whose terrain lacks the display object loads with defaults and one warning; a terrain with an invalid breakline loads as a failed element listed in problems, never dropped silently.
- TER-012 and TER-014 satisfied.
notes:
SRS: TER-012 TER-014
Open question: TopSurface is written invisible to avoid z-fighting in viewers; revisit if consumers expect a visible surface. TopSurface is the uncut TIN; cuts of task 11 change only the Body parts.

title: Save, pick and manage presets in tool settings and properties
description:
WHY: ELM-002 (S): users shall save a tool's settings as a named preset, apply a preset to new or selected elements and manage presets per tool (rename, delete, reorder, search); every settings dialog (UI-003) offers preset selection, and applying a preset also sets the element's layer. UI-014 (owned by properties-and-dialogs) requires incremental search on the presets list. The model is task 03; the settings dialog with four sections is properties-and-dialogs-09, the SearchField properties-and-dialogs-12.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/presets.rs: a preset selector (combo with search, accessible label 'Preset') at the top of the properties strip and of every settings dialog (ui/properties.rs settings_dialog): for tool defaults it runs ApplyPresetToDefaults, so the next element carries element.preset; for a selection it runs ApplyPreset on the editable subset (Workspace::editable_subset of selection-transforms-04, lock reasons in the status line). 'Save as preset…' asks for a name and runs AddPreset from the current defaults or from the first selected element. A 'Presets' manager window (Design menu): kind filter, list in stored order with search, inline rename, delete with confirmation naming the number of referencing elements, reorder by drag (egui drag and drop) or up/down buttons (MovePreset), 'Overwrite with current tool settings'. The properties strip shows 'Preset: X' or 'Preset: X (modified)'. Out of scope: preset folders (task 19), cross-kind injection (task 11).
design: One widget for strip and dialog, fed by Project::presets_of(kind) in stored order. The '(modified)' marker compares the element's transferable FieldSpec values with the preset slot (task 02 vocabulary) and is computed, not stored. Pitfalls: commit or discard a pending field edit before applying a preset; egui ids keyed by preset id so renames keep focus; locked elements are skipped with reasons, never silently; strings in the Fluent catalogue (string_lint).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/presets.rs: with the Wall tool, change the thickness, 'Save as preset…' 'Partition 100' → the selector lists it; draw a wall → the wall has element.preset 'Partition 100' and the preset's layer.
- Select two walls and choose another preset in the strip → both get its settings and its layer in one undo step, and one undo reverts both (epic: a preset is saved from a tool and applied to a selection).
- Manager: rename, delete (element references cleared), reorder (order kept after save and reopen) and search filtering all work.
- A test iterating the kind registry finds the Preset selector in every kind's settings dialog.
- Satisfies the UI clauses of ELM-002 (save from tool, apply to new and selected elements, manage, selection in every settings dialog).
notes: SRS: ELM-002

title: Add the start screen as the no-project state with template choice
description:
WHY: PRJ-009 (S): a start screen shall offer New (with template choice), Open, and a searchable list of recent projects with thumbnails (thumbnails in task 08). PRJ-013 (C): a sample project may be offered on the start screen. PRJ-001, PRJ-002 and PRJ-012 need the template choice when a project is created. Gap rows: PRJ-009 missing (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:92-128 starts directly in a default project; the app always holds a project, app.rs:248-255); PRJ-013 partial (samples::two_storey_shell exists, crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs:46-83, but only tests use it); PRJ-012 lacks the choice at New (app.rs:249 calls default_metric_project unconditionally, ui/actions.rs:8 has a single New). Epic risk: the 'no project open' state touches the app.rs flow and must be covered by kittest flows for New, Open and Recover.

WHAT: app.rs: `Screen { Start, Project }` in ArchiCraftApp; new() starts on Start unless a path is given on the command line; Close returns to Start instead of creating a default project (proceed, app.rs:247-255); on Start the autosave timer is idle (app.rs:497-515), the title is 'ArchiCraft', only New, Open, Open recent, Preferences and Quit are enabled, and the browser, tabs and properties strip are hidden. New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/start.rs: buttons 'New project…', 'Open…' and 'Sample project', a 'Recent projects' list (Preferences.recent, prefs.rs:50, maintained by add_recent at prefs.rs:116-120) with the SearchField of properties-and-dialogs-12 matching file name and folder, each entry with name, folder, modified date and a thumbnail slot (placeholder until task 08), missing files greyed with 'Remove from list'. New dialog (also behind File > New after the unsaved-changes guard): built-in templates from archicraft_ifcx::templates::built_in() with name, description and unit system, preselecting Preferences.last_template; OK instantiates through load_template into Document::new. Sample project: samples::two_storey_shell() as an unsaved document named 'Sample project' (path None). The Recover window (app.rs:633-678) shows over the start screen. Test seam: the two blocking rfd calls (save dialog app.rs:197, open dialog app.rs:257) move behind a `FileDialogs` trait (pick_open, pick_save) whose default implementation is rfd; `ArchiCraftApp::with_file_dialogs(Box<dyn FileDialogs>)` lets kittests script the answers and record the requests, so 'Open…', Open recent and Save As are testable without blocking (task 09 reuses it). crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs gets a harness helper that passes New → OK so the existing tests keep their assertions. Out of scope: thumbnails (08), user templates and Save as template (07), in-use detection (09).
design: Keep Workspace holding a Document even on the start screen (an empty placeholder) instead of Option<Document>, so the many ws.doc accesses stay unchanged; the Screen flag gates rendering, autosave and action availability. New is then 'instantiate template bytes', identical for built-in and user templates. Build the egui_tiles tree only when entering Project (default_tree, app.rs:81-87, needs storeys); if plan-views-browser-14 restores a persisted layout, apply it there. Read file metadata for the recent list once when the screen opens, not per frame. Strings go through the Fluent catalogue of commands-and-l10n (string_lint) and the actions through its CommandRegistry. Pitfalls: Quit from Start needs no unsaved prompt; Open from Start uses the same open_path as the menu so task 09's lock check covers it; the placeholder document must never be autosaved or offered for recovery.
acceptance_criteria:
- New kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/start_screen.rs: the app starts on the start screen with 'New project…', 'Open…', 'Sample project', 'Recent projects' and 'Search'; with three recent files in the preferences, typing part of one name leaves one entry, and clicking it opens that project; 'Open…' with a scripted FileDialogs returning a fixture path opens that file through open_path, and Cancel stays on the start screen.
- New → 'Imperial' → OK gives a project with LengthUnit::FeetInches whose ids differ from the template file; New → 'Metric' gives the D.1 storeys; the last choice is preselected next time.
- 'Sample project' opens walls and slabs with the title 'Sample project — ArchiCraft' and no path, so Save asks for a location.
- Close returns to the start screen; File > New from a dirty project asks to save first; an abandoned autosave shows the recovery window over the start screen and Recover opens the project (New/Open/Recover flows of the epic risk).
- A command-line path opens directly without the start screen; while on the start screen no autosave is written (test on Session folder contents).
- Every existing test in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs passes through the updated harness.
- Satisfies PRJ-009 except the thumbnail clause (task 08), PRJ-013, and the choice-at-New clauses of PRJ-001, PRJ-002 and PRJ-012.
notes:
SRS: PRJ-009 PRJ-013 PRJ-001 PRJ-002 PRJ-012
Decision: the sample is samples::two_storey_shell(); switch to the RM-S model of reference-models if a sample constructor for it exists by then.

title: Verify exit criterion: Stair element, rule-based solver and placement tool
description:
WHY: The stair-solver-tool epic delivers the Stair kind, the rule-based solver and the placement tool that stair-body-plan, templates-presets, railings-stairs-adv and reference-models build on; its exit criterion has to be shown on the merged result as a whole. The covered requirements are STA-001, STA-002, STA-003, STA-004, STA-005, STA-006, STA-007, STA-008, STA-009, STA-010, STA-011 and STA-024, and docs/implementation-status.md must show their new status with evidence.

WHAT: On the merged state of tasks 01-12: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test --workspace (stair_solver, commands, geometry stair, roundtrip, golden and kittest suites included); conformance/run.sh on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx (including stairs.ifcx) and on the reference-model output; a review of the golden diff. Then update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered ID (status, file:line evidence, and the remaining gap for clauses owned elsewhere: landings and supports of STA-001 and the plan symbol in stair-body-plan, the 'unlock the baseline' alternative of STA-011 with STA-029 in stair-body-plan-14, national presets with STA-052), rewrite the 4.20 readiness note and the extension points if the Kind trait gained resolve(), file beads for anything deferred and close the epic with bd close. Git and Dolt sync follow the active beads profile; report the commands instead of committing when the profile is conservative.
design: Checklist that maps each acceptance clause to the test that proves it: STA-003..008 numbers in crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs (task 02, stair-level cases from task 03); storey re-solve in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs (task 05); band, side and walking-line geometry in stair/walking.rs (task 12); conflict naming and alternatives, including change N, change offset and the drawn-geometry case, in stair_solver.rs (task 03) and the dialog kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs (task 11); read-out in tools/stair.rs and the status-bar kittest (task 08), properties read-out kittest (task 10); walking-line check in stair_solver.rs (task 03) and the properties warning row (task 10); IFCX round trip and golden in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs (task 07). Re-run with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS unset; any golden difference is a failure unless it is the intended stairs.ifcx. Status rows should cite the new modules (stair/rules.rs, solver.rs, walking.rs, solve.rs, conflict.rs, status.rs, kinds/stair.rs, geometry stair.rs, alpha/kinds/stair.rs, tools/stair.rs, ui/stair.rs).
acceptance_criteria:
- Every numeric test of STA-003 to STA-008 exists as a solver unit test and passes (3.000 m / 19 gives 157.89 mm; N in {15..20}; 300 <= G <= 350 at R = 150; 2R+G = 550 reported against 600).
- Changing the storey height from 3.000 to 3.300 re-solves to 22 risers through the storey link (sta_003_storey_link).
- A rule conflict (min G 350, max 2R+G 600 at R 170) is reported with both rule names and alternatives and the last valid stair is kept (conflict dialog kittest).
- STA-011's change-N, relax-a-bound and change-offset alternatives are offered and applied (stair_solver.rs and the conflict dialog kittests); 'unlock the baseline' is recorded as open with STA-029 (stair-body-plan-14).
- The live '19 R x 157.9 mm, 2R+G = 616 mm' read-out appears during input (tool test and status-bar kittest).
- The walking line distance is checked against the rule (sta_010_walking_line and the properties warning row).
- The rule set and all parameters round-trip in archicraft::stair and archicraft::stairRules (roundtrip test and stairs.ifcx golden).
- cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green on the workspace.
- conformance/run.sh is green on the golden files.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID.
- The epic is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: STA-001 STA-002 STA-003 STA-004 STA-005 STA-006 STA-007 STA-008 STA-009 STA-010 STA-011 STA-024

title: Benchmark 50,000-point terrains and guard 3D navigation
description:
WHY: TER-013 (M): a terrain with 50,000 points is created in under 5 s on reference hardware (NFR-PERF-001) and does not reduce 3D navigation below the targets of NFR-PERF-003 (RM-M at least 30 frames/s shaded, RM-S at least 30 frames/s on minimum hardware). The epic acceptance asks for 50,000 points with 200 breaklines building in under 5 s in a benchmark and tiling into closed Body_n parts of at most 65,535 points. Status: TER-013 missing; the performance harness (criterion benches, the perf feature with ARCHICRAFT_PERF_SCRIPT=orbit, the CI smoke gate, docs/performance results) comes from regression-and-status-16, -17 and -18, an increment-1 epic that is not a declared dependency of this epic: if it has not landed, add criterion and the bench target here, time frames with a release kittest frame timer and file a bead to move the measurement onto the harness.

WHAT: Using samples::synthetic_terrain (task 05) with 50,000 points and 200 breaklines: criterion bench terrain_50k_create in crates/archicraft-geometry/benches/terrain.rs covering AddElements apply and full evaluation (TIN, tiles, TopSurface, contours at 0.50 m) in smooth and faceted modes; a release-only integration test terrain_50k_builds_under_5s that also includes render3d::build_scene and asserts every part closed and within 65,535 points; frame-time measurement of orbiting the 5,000-element stand-in plus the terrain through the harness instrumentation, recorded for reference and minimum hardware in docs/performance/<date>-<machine>.md; hot spots fixed where found (bulk loading, parallel tile building, no per-triangle allocations). A single point edit on the 50,000-point terrain is timed and logged. Out of scope: RM-M and RM-L tuning (perf-tuning-rm-m-l), incremental re-triangulation.
design: The generator lives in archicraft-model samples without a rand dependency so benches, tests and later performance epics share it. Measure in release with the harness's profile. Pitfalls: CI runners are slower than the reference machines, so the CI assertion acts as a regression ceiling and the requirement itself is verified on reference hardware; GPU upload of faceted terrains (about 300,000 vertices) is part of the frame-time check, not of the creation time. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/benches/ (regression-and-status), crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs build_scene, docs/performance/.
acceptance_criteria:
- terrain_50k_builds_under_5s passes in release in the CI smoke job, and the reference-hardware result (target under 5 s) is recorded under docs/performance/.
- Every Body_n of the 50,000-point terrain in faceted mode is closed with at most 65,535 points; TopSurface parts pass check_open_surface within the same limit.
- The criterion benches are registered in the CI smoke gate (20 % regression rule of regression-and-status).
- Frame-time record with and without the terrain: orbiting the 5,000-element stand-in plus the terrain stays at 30 frames/s or more on reference hardware, an RM-S-sized scene plus the terrain at 30 frames/s or more on minimum hardware, and the 20,000-element stand-in plus the terrain at 20 frames/s or more on reference hardware where the stand-in alone reaches it (otherwise the terrain adds at most 10 % frame time and the shortfall is filed against perf-tuning-rm-m-l) (NFR-PERF-003).
- A single point edit on the 50,000-point terrain re-evaluates in under 500 ms; if it exceeds the 200 ms NFR-PERF-006 budget, a follow-up bead for incremental TIN updates is filed.
- TER-013 satisfied.
notes: SRS: TER-013

title: Show terrain contours in plan and convert them to 2D lines
description:
WHY: TER-007 (S): contours are drawn from a base elevation and interval with every n-th major contour labelled; they can replace or accompany the triangulation edges and can be converted to static 2D lines on request. The static form is the ANN-001 2D polyline (drafting-trim-split-03). Status: TER-007 missing; there is no text drawing in plan (gap row).

WHAT: App: a 'Plan display' section for terrains in the properties panel and settings dialog with display (Contours, Triangulation, Both), base elevation, interval, major every n, label major contours and label height in mm, edited through UpdateElements on the display settings. crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draws the contour line classes (minor thin, major medium, with the pens of plan-attributes) and the labels of task 12 through the text-drawing path that drafting-trim-split-09 added to views/plan.rs for area labels, extended with rotation (epaint TextShape angle; the text primitive of the plan renderer where plan-renderer has replaced the painter), sized from paper height and drawing scale and kept out of the snap targets. Model: Command::ConvertContours { terrain, storey, polylines, id_seed } creates one DraftPolyline { curve: PolyCurve of straight edges, style: DraftStyle { pen, line_type }, view: DraftingView::Plan { storey } } (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/drafting.rs, drafting-trim-split-03) per contour polyline (major ones with the major pen, minor with the minor pen, solid line type, on the terrain's home storey plan and the '2D construction' layer); the command carries the polylines from the current evaluation so replay is deterministic; one undo step; the terrain display stays unchanged. 'Convert contours to 2D lines' appears in the terrain context menu and edit palette. Out of scope: converting labels (no 2D text kind yet), section views.
design: The conversion command carries the geometry rather than a reference to derived contours, so journal replay yields identical elements even after geometry code changes (id_seed pattern of drafting-trim-split-10). Rotated text uses epaint's TextShape angle. Pitfalls: label collisions are not resolved in v1 (one label per 100 mm on paper); if plan-attributes offers no contour pen role, use the drafting pens and file a follow-up bead. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draw_plan, ui/properties.rs, ui/dialogs.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/drafting.rs, command.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Kittest: changing the interval in the properties panel from 0.50 to 1.00 halves the number of contour lines in the next PlanDrawing, and switching to Triangulation removes them.
- Plan view test: labels of major contours are painted with the formatted elevation text (inspect the painted text shapes or the PlanDrawing labels consumed by the painter).
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: ConvertContours with 12 polylines adds 12 DraftPolyline elements on the home storey, the major ones with the major pen; undo removes them; derived ids are replay-stable through id_seed.
- After conversion, editing a terrain point regenerates the live contours while the converted 2D lines stay unchanged.
- TER-007 display settings, label drawing and convert-to-2D-lines clauses satisfied.
notes:
SRS: TER-007
Follow-up: convert labels as well once an annotation text kind exists (ANN).

title: Preview the stair being placed in 3D views
description:
WHY: STA-002 (M): during input, the preview in plan and 3D shows the live riser count. Gap: the 3D view has no tool preview at all (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs), and the GpuScene is cached by revision and selection (SceneKey, workspace.rs:44), so a transient body needs its own path. The provisional body of task 06 makes a meaningful 3D ghost possible before stair-body-plan.

WHAT: InputConsumer gains an optional preview_body(&Project, &Resolved) -> Option<PreviewBody { storey_elevation, parts: Vec<TriMesh>, label: (DVec3, String) }> with a default None; the stair tool returns the provisional body of its candidate and the 'k/N risers' label anchored at the cursor. Workspace keeps the latest PreviewBody with a generation counter, set by the plan view's input handling and cleared when the tool resets or commits. views/render3d.rs builds preview vertices (ghost tint, alpha, edges) into a separate transient buffer uploaded only when the generation changes and drawn after the opaque scene without depth writes; views/view3d.rs draws the label in an egui Area at the camera-projected anchor (camera.rs, or the Overlay3d projection helper when 3d-input-navigation-07 has landed) so AccessKit sees it. Out of scope: 3D input on a working plane (3d-input-navigation; when present the same consumer works there), previews for other tools.
design: Keep the preview outside the cached scene so a pointer move never invalidates GpuScene, and upload only on a generation change. Reuse the provisional generator of archicraft-geometry (already an app dependency) so plan and 3D show the same stair. Pitfalls: free the transient buffer with the viewport (see the released-viewport side channel in app.rs); kittest has no wgpu, so assertions target vertex building and the egui label; drawing the ghost without depth writes keeps it from hiding the model.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test in render3d.rs: build_preview_vertices for the read-out example's candidate yields the provisional body's triangles offset by the storey elevation with the ghost alpha; no preview yields no buffer.
- Unit test: the preview generation changes on pointer moves and resets on Esc and commit; preview changes never rebuild the cached GpuScene (SceneKey unchanged).
- kittest with a plan and a 3D pane: during stair input the 3D pane shows the label '10/19 risers' (queried by label; wgpu output is not asserted under kittest) and the label disappears after commit.
- Input feedback stays inside point-input-snapping-15's 50 ms frame-time assertion (crates/archicraft-app/tests/input_latency.rs) on two_storey_shell with the stair tool and its 3D preview active.
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green.
notes: SRS: STA-002.

title: Render and cache recent-project thumbnails for the start screen
description:
WHY: PRJ-009 (S): the start screen shall offer a searchable list of recent projects with thumbnails. The gap row names a snapshot rendered at save and cached outside the project as the missing piece. IFCX is the only file format (D-11), so thumbnails are a private cache, never part of the project file.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs: Renderer3d::render_to_rgba(render_state, scene, camera, size) -> Option<Vec<u8>> rendering into an offscreen target (ensure_viewport/render, render3d.rs:438-520) and reading it back through a mapped buffer (copy_texture_to_buffer with 256-byte row alignment, map_async, non-blocking device poll over the next frames). New persistence/thumbnails.rs: ThumbnailCache in DataDirs::thumbnails() keyed by a stable hash of the canonical project path, file '<hash>.rgba' = width and height header plus RGBA8, written atomically on a worker thread, read into egui::ColorImage, pruned to the recent list. app.rs: after a successful save_to (app.rs:214-235) queue a capture for the next frame, from the first 3D view fitted to the model (Camera3d fit, views/camera.rs), 320 × 200 px. ui/start.rs loads thumbnails lazily as textures, frees them when leaving the start screen and shows 'No preview' otherwise. Out of scope: thumbnails in the IFCX file, plan-view thumbnails, thumbnails of templates.
design: A raw RGBA cache avoids an image-encoding dependency (about 256 KB per entry, at most 10 entries) and the health check a new crate would need. Reuse the existing pipeline rather than a second renderer; the preview path of properties-and-dialogs-09 already renders into a small Viewport the same way. Readback must not stall the frame: poll the mapping without blocking and finish on a later frame; drop the capture if the document changes meanwhile. Pitfalls: canonicalise paths (macOS /private/tmp symlinks, Windows case) before hashing; no adapter or a software adapter means no thumbnail, silently; release the offscreen Viewport through the released-textures path (app.rs:69, 793-849).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in persistence/thumbnails.rs: an RGBA buffer round-trips; the key is stable for one path and differs between paths; prune keeps only recent entries; a truncated file reads as None.
- Unit test of the row-unpadding helper for widths that are not multiples of 64 px.
- kittest without GPU: a recent entry with a pre-written cache file shows an image with the accessible label 'Preview of <name>'; an entry without one shows 'No preview'.
- With a wgpu adapter available (skipped otherwise, like other GPU tests), saving a project creates its thumbnail file and the start screen shows it.
- Satisfies the thumbnail clause of PRJ-009.
notes: SRS: PRJ-009

title: Select groups as one, ungroup and suspend groups in the UI
description:
WHY: ELM-015 (S): clicking one member selects the group; groups can be nested, ungrouped and temporarily suspended. The epic acceptance requires that a group moves as one and ungroups. Model and persistence come from task 15.

WHAT: Workspace gains `groups_suspended: bool` (session only) with a 'Suspend groups' toggle in the Edit menu and a status-bar indicator. Selection::expand_groups(&Project) is called by every selection entry point (plan and 3D picking, Shift-toggle, area selection, select all, select similar of task 12, criteria results of task 14 and selection-set recall of task 22, which is why this task waits for them): a member selects all members of its outermost group unless groups are suspended. Transforms (selection-transforms Transform tool) therefore move the whole group; handles show one bounding box per group. Actions Group and Ungroup in the Edit menu and the canvas context menu (shortcuts proposed in notes); the properties strip shows 'Group: Group 3 (5 elements)' with rename; 'Edit element in group' selects a single member (also the way into SEL-008 edit mode). Out of scope: group-specific properties beyond the name.
design: Expansion lives in one function so every selection path behaves the same; suspend is session state, matching 'temporarily'. Locked members inside a moved group are skipped through editable_subset with reasons. Pitfalls: area selection with 'fully inside' still expands to the whole group once any member qualifies (document); group expansion must not re-add elements hidden in the active pane.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/groups.rs: select two walls, Group → clicking one wall selects both; a move by a typed vector moves both; Ungroup → clicking selects one wall (epic: a group moves as one and ungroups).
- Nested: group (A, B), then group it with C → clicking A selects A, B and C; Ungroup once → clicking A selects A and B.
- Suspend groups: a click selects a single member and a move affects only it; turning suspension off restores group selection; the setting is not saved in the project.
- Groups survive save and reopen (through task 15) and Shift-click toggles a whole group; select similar, a criteria result and a recalled selection set that contain one member select the whole group unless groups are suspended.
- Satisfies ELM-015.
notes:
SRS: ELM-015
Proposed shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl+G Group, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+G Ungroup (check against D.8 and OS reservations in the commands-and-l10n keymap).

title: Load and write IFCX templates with fresh identities
description:
WHY: PRJ-001 (M): a new project shall be created from a template that supplies project settings, storeys, layers, materials, layer structures and views, and a default template ships with the product. PRJ-002 (S): users shall be able to save a project as their own template and choose it when creating a project. IFX-011 (M, owned by selection-transforms): a project created from a template gets new UUIDs for the project and for every node taken from the template. Gap rows: PRJ-001 partial, because the 'template' is the hard-coded function default_metric_project() (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs:295-383) and there is no template artefact that PRJ-002 or PRJ-012 could build on; PRJ-002 missing (no template store, no save-as-template). Fresh identities exist today only because that function constructs every node anew (ProjectId::new(), SiteId::new() and friends, template.rs:346-383; test every_project_gets_new_identities at template.rs:404-411, which is kept and stays green); a file-based template needs real remapping, which selection-transforms-13 provides as Project::reidentify_all and this task reuses.

WHAT: archicraft-model (template.rs): `TemplateInfo { name, description, unit_system: UnitSystem { Metric, Imperial }, built_in: bool }`; `Project::to_template(&self, include_elements: bool) -> Project` (the template is a clone, so every resource is kept by construction: settings, storeys, layers, materials, layer structures, profiles, views, view folders, layer combinations, tool defaults and any resource added later such as presets, stair rule presets, criteria sets and resource folders; without elements it clears the elements and their relations and resets the name counters; the element-scoped collections added later in this epic, groups (task 15) and selection sets (task 22), are cleared by those tasks, which depend on this one and extend its unit test); `Project::instantiate_template(self) -> Project` (reidentify_all, info.name 'Untitled project', data_version 0). archicraft-ifcx: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs `TEMPLATE = "archicraft::template"` ({name, description, unitSystem, builtIn}) on the root node, declared only when written; WriteOptions (alpha/writer.rs:23-31) gains `template: Option<TemplateInfo>`; ReadOutcome (alpha/reader.rs:31-38) gains `template: Option<TemplateInfo>`; next to save/load in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/lib.rs:30-51 new `archicraft_ifcx::save_template(project, info, geometry, options)` and `load_template(bytes) -> Result<TemplateOutcome { project, info, problems }, Problem>` (lenient read, then instantiate; a project file without the marker is accepted as a template with info derived from its name). `load()` of a template file keeps identities, so a template can be opened and edited. Out of scope: the shipped template files (task 05), New dialog and start screen (06), Save as template UI and the user template folder (07), the Save As new-project/copy choice (selection-transforms-13).
design: A template is an ordinary IFCX project file plus the archicraft::template marker, so one reader handles both (IFX-090) and a template stays inspectable in any IFCX viewer. Identity remapping goes through Project::reidentify_all (selection-transforms-13) instead of the ad-hoc code in template.rs:347-374; rule for this epic: every task that adds a resource (presets, stair rule presets, criteria sets, selection sets, groups, folders) extends reidentify_all and its test. header.id is derived from the ProjectId (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:39-42), so a new ProjectId yields a new header id without extra code. Remap in one pass over a HashMap<Uuid, Uuid> with a typed visitor so references inside resources (skins, preset slots, view layer states, default slots) cannot be missed. Pitfalls: the new Document starts with an empty undo history and dirty = false only after New; data_version 0 so the first save writes 1; declare the marker only when present so golden files do not change; templates with the newer FORMAT_VERSION go through the migration table of element-kind-framework-12.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/templates.rs identity test: a template written from a sample project and loaded twice with load_template gives, for each load, a project whose ProjectId, SiteId, BuildingId, StoreyIds, LayerIds, MaterialIds, LayerStructureIds, ViewIds, view folder and layer combination ids (and ElementIds when elements are included) all differ from the file and from the other load; header.id (writer.rs dataset_id) differs as well.
- After instantiation integrity_problems() is empty and every reference resolves: element storey, layer, material and layer structure, skin materials, tool-default slots, views to storeys and layer combinations.
- The marker round-trips: save_template then load() returns template: Some(info) with identical fields and unchanged identities; a plain project file has template: None and load_template still accepts it.
- Unit tests in template.rs: to_template(false) has no elements or relations and zeroed counters while every resource collection equals the source; to_template(true) keeps the elements; the existing every_project_gets_new_identities test stays green.
- A minimal template written by the test validates without problems (validate::validate) and passes conformance/run.sh (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/template-minimal.ifcx).
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check stay green; existing golden files are unchanged.
- Satisfies the template mechanism of PRJ-001 and PRJ-002 and exercises the template clause of IFX-011.
notes:
SRS: PRJ-001 PRJ-002
Decision: a template may carry model elements (include_elements, off by default in the UI), as in the reference product. IFX-011 stays owned by selection-transforms; only its template clause is exercised here.

title: Draw, move and remove the persistent selection region and limit commands to it
description:
WHY: SEL-005 (S): a persistent selection region shall be drawable that stays after it is drawn; it can be moved and removed, covers the current storey or all storeys, limits select all and edit commands, and moving it stretches the nodes inside it. SEL-004 (M, selection-transforms) leaves the hook: ws.selection_region: Option<SelectionRegion { shape, storeys }> read by select_all (selection-transforms-07). Gap row SEL-005 missing: the area rectangle is discarded when the drag stops (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:545-560). The stretch targets and the Stretch command are task 20; this task is the tool, its display, the command limits and the wiring of Move to Stretch.

WHAT: App: a 'Selection region' tool (ToolKind in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13, toolbox next to Select) drawing the SelectionShape variants of selection-transforms-07 (Rect, RotatedRect, Polygon in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs) with the tool mode 'Storeys: Current / All' and writing ws.selection_region; the region is drawn as a thick dashed outline with a light tint in plan views (its storey or all storeys) and as a vertical prism outline in 3D; it can be relocated without touching the model (Alt-drag of its outline or 'Move region' with a typed vector) and removed ('Remove selection region' action, or Esc with nothing pending while the region tool is active). Workspace::command_subject(): with a region, the elements partially inside it on its storeys (intersected with the selection when one exists), filtered by Workspace::editable_subset (selection-transforms-04); used by Delete, the transform tool (move, rotate, mirror, vertical move of selection-transforms-10), copy and property edits; select all already honours the region, and tasks 12 and 14 read the same field. Moving the content: the Move transform with a region and no selection resolves the region through archicraft_geometry::plan::stretch_targets and executes Command::Stretch (task 20) in one undo step, and the region follows the content. Out of scope: regions in section views, saving regions in the file.
design: The region is per-project workspace state in model coordinates with a storey binding, not saved, like the reference product's marquee. 'Partially inside' uses the same predicate as SelectionShape (selection-transforms-07), so select all, command_subject and stretch_targets agree on membership. Pitfalls: region drawing must not fight click selection (the region tool owns the clicks); the region outline is excluded from snapping targets except its own nodes; edit commands on an empty subject report 'Nothing inside the selection region'.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/region.rs: a drawn rectangle region stays after the tool finishes and after switching tools; select all selects only elements in it; Delete deletes only elements in it; Rotate with the region active and no selection rotates only elements in it (edit commands limited); with 'Storeys: All' both storeys are affected, with 'Current' only the region's storey.
- Move region relocates it without changing the model revision; Remove selection region clears it and select all acts on the whole view again.
- Moving with the region active stretches the nodes inside: a slab with two of four outline nodes inside changes only those nodes and a wall with one end inside is stretched (kittest asserting the resulting geometry); one undo restores the model and the region outline follows the content.
- An edit command with nothing inside reports 'Nothing inside the selection region' and changes nothing.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check stay green.
- Satisfies SEL-005 (with task 20) and completes the region clause of SEL-004.
notes:
SRS: SEL-005
The model half (stretch targets and Command::Stretch) is task 20, which carries the implicit prerequisite on edit-reshape-palette.

title: Add the terrain kind with points, breaklines, boundary and commands
description:
WHY: TER-001 (M): the system provides a terrain element that is a closed solid; its top surface is a TIN through 3D points and optional breaklines inside an editable boundary polygon; its bottom is flat at a user-defined elevation or thickness. TER-002 (M): terrain is creatable by drawing a boundary and adding points with elevations, and from 2D contour polylines. TER-005 (M): points, breaklines and the boundary are editable in plan and 3D (add, move, delete, numeric elevation input). Section 3 and Table 5-1 make terrain a site-level element (IfcGeographicElement child of IfcSite); Appendix D.2 sets the bottom 5.00 m below the lowest terrain point. Status: TER-001, TER-002 and TER-005 missing; only the layer 'Terrain' and the material 'Soil' exist (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs:222 and 268). The framework supplies the kind registry (kinds/mod.rs, element-kind-framework-02), site containment through the Kind::container() hook (element-kind-framework-02, written under the site by element-kind-framework-07), IfcClass::GeographicElement (element-kind-framework-05), the Outline type (crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/mod.rs, edit-reshape-palette-01), PartRef and the kind's `type Part` (selection-transforms-01) and the KindDescriptor flag solid (solid-kernel-ops-04).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/terrain.rs registered with one kinds! line: label 'Terrain', code terrain, name prefix 'TR', only class IfcGeographicElement, container Site, has_tool true, solid true (so AddSolidOperations of solid-kernel-ops-04 accepts terrain as target and operator), no storey top link. Payload Terrain { boundary: Outline (one ring, no holes), points: Vec<TerrainPoint { id: u32, position: DVec3 }>, breaklines: Vec<Breakline { id: u32, nodes: Vec<DVec3>, closed: bool, contour: Option<f64> }>, bottom: TerrainBottom::{Depth(f64) below the lowest input elevation, Elevation(f64)}, material: MaterialId, display: TerrainDisplay { smooth, plan: TerrainPlanMode::{Contours, Triangulation, Both}, contours: ContourSettings { base, interval, major_every, label_major, label_height_mm }, tin_snaps }, next_id: u32 }. Elevations are absolute (relative to project zero). validate_terrain: boundary through the Outline validation (simple, at least three nodes, holes rejected), coordinates within MAX_COORDINATE, at least three non-collinear inputs, no two inputs at the same XY within MODEL_TOLERANCE with different Z, breaklines with at least two nodes and without crossings except at shared nodes, contour breaklines with every node Z equal to the contour value, bottom below the lowest input by at least MIN_THICKNESS, ids unique and below next_id. A terrain defaults slot in template.rs (Soil, layer Terrain, Depth(5.00) per D.2, smooth, Contours, base 0.00 m, interval 0.50 m, every 5th major, labels on, 2.0 mm) and kinds::terrain::new_terrain(project, storey, boundary, points) -> Element built from that slot (project.rs stays untouched). Command::EditTerrain { element, op: TerrainOp } with AddPoints, MovePoints { ids, delta: DVec3 }, SetPoints(Vec<(u32, DVec3)>), DeletePoints, AddBreakline { nodes, closed, contour }, SetBreakline { id, nodes }, SetContourElevation { ids, elevation }, DeleteBreaklines and SetBottom, each planned into one ReplaceElement with a label() text and refused on locked elements. Kind hooks: transform (move, rotate and mirror boundary, points and breaklines exactly; vertical move shifts all Z and an Elevation bottom), the outline accessor and reshape hook for the boundary (Command::Reshape of edit-reshape-palette-03), empty storey_links, vertical_extent from bottom to highest Z. Part addressing: the kind's `type Part = TerrainPart::{Point { id }, Breakline { id }, BreaklineNode { id, index }}` (KindPart is generated by the kinds! macro, selection-transforms-01, so selection.rs needs no change) with the part_refs, part_label, part_anchor and part_outline hooks; the boundary uses the shared PartRef::Node/Edge { ring: 0, index } addressing and the Kind::reshape hook of edit-reshape-palette-03. Out of scope: geometry (task 04), IFCX (task 06), tools and UI (tasks 07-09), contours from polylines (task 10), cutting (task 11), thinning (task 15).
design: Stable u32 ids instead of indices, because deleting a point must not retarget selections, relations or undo (the stable-addressing rule of selection-transforms-01); next_id lives in the payload so ids are never reused within an element. A Depth bottom is measured from the lowest input elevation (points and breakline nodes); the derived boundary elevations of task 04 never fall below it because they are convex combinations of inputs. Breakline crossing validation uses geo segment intersection on XY with the shared MODEL_TOLERANCE (element-kind-framework-01) through an rstar index on segments, so 200 breaklines with thousands of nodes validate quickly. Absolute elevations: a site-level element has a home storey only for placement (element-kind-framework-07 writes a transform translating by its elevation), so the geometry generator subtracts it (task 04); never let storey-following logic (STR-006, Kind::storey_links) touch terrain Z. Points outside the boundary are valid and stay editable (they help derive boundary heights in task 04). Pitfalls: an Outline with holes is rejected until openings in terrain arrive (OPN-012, members-profiles-adv); Command derives Serialize and Deserialize, so TerrainOp does too; route messages through the command string externalisation of commands-and-l10n where it exists. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs and kinds/slab.rs (pattern), outline/mod.rs, selection.rs, template.rs:222-268 and 331-361, validate.rs, command.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- The registry and module-layout tests stay green with the new kind: beyond kinds/terrain.rs, one kinds! line in kinds/mod.rs, the defaults slot in template.rs and the EditTerrain variant in command.rs (planning delegated to kinds/terrain.rs), nothing in archicraft-model changes.
- The descriptor declares solid: true: AddSolidOperations with a terrain as target and with a terrain as operator passes the solid-kernel-ops-04 validation.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements with new_terrain names it TR-001 and places it at site level (container Site); every TerrainOp executes, undoes and redoes to the exact project; invalid inputs (duplicate XY with different Z, crossing breaklines, a contour node off its elevation, an Elevation bottom above the lowest point, a two-node or self-intersecting boundary) return CommandError::Invalid naming the point or breakline id; a locked terrain refuses edits with CommandError::Locked.
- Storey independence: changing the home storey's elevation or height does not change any terrain Z; DeleteStorey of the home storey rehomes the terrain to the nearest storey without moving it.
- Transform hook tests: rotating by 90 degrees about a point and mirroring keep ids and exact coordinates and keep the boundary counter-clockwise; a vertical move by +0.50 m shifts every point, breakline node and an Elevation bottom by 0.50 m.
- PartRef tests: part labels 'point 7', 'breakline 2', 'node 3 of breakline 2'; Selection::retain_valid drops parts of deleted points.
- Defaults test pins the D.2 bottom (Depth 5.00 m) and the template slot (Soil, layer Terrain).
- TER-001 data model and TER-005 edit operations available headless; TER-002 creation from a boundary and points available as a command.
notes:
SRS: TER-001 TER-002 TER-005
Appendix D.2: terrain bottom 5.00 m below the lowest terrain point. Contour defaults (base 0.00 m, interval 0.50 m, every 5th major, 2.0 mm labels), smooth display and the name prefix 'TR' are proposals not covered by Appendix D.

title: Transfer compatible settings between elements and tool defaults
description:
WHY: ELM-003 (S): the user shall be able to pick up an element's settings into the active tool's defaults and inject them into other elements; between different element kinds only the compatible settings are transferred. ELM-002 (S): applying a preset to new or selected elements is the same operation with a preset as the source (task 03). Gap row ELM-003 missing: no pick-up or inject commands and no compatibility filter; the building blocks are the per-kind defaults slots of element-kind-framework-04 (replacing wall_defaults()/slab_defaults() at crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:83-112) and the FieldSpec getters and setters of properties-and-dialogs-05, which already describe every parameter of every registered kind.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/transfer.rs: FieldSpec gains `transfer: Transfer { Always, Never }` (Never for name/ID, home storey and geometry anchors); `transfer_settings(source: &Element, target: &mut Element, project: &Project) -> TransferReport { applied: Vec<&'static str>, skipped: Vec<(&'static str, String)> }` copies, in the target's FieldSpec order, every transferable field whose key and quantity also exist on the source kind and whose value the target accepts (options such as the IFC class set, ranges, layer structure usage), then normalises through validate_element. `SettingsSource { Element(ElementId), Defaults(KindTag) }` (task 03 adds Preset). Commands in command.rs: `InjectSettings { source, targets }` (label 'Inject settings into n elements', planned through plan_update_elements so lock checks, validation and NoChange are reused; Unsupported when no target accepts any field) and `PickUpSettings { element, into: KindTag }` planned as SetToolDefaults on the slot of `into` (same kind: every transferable field; other kind: the compatible subset; the slot's layer follows the element). Out of scope: gestures, latch mode and previews (task 11), presets (task 03).
design: FieldSpec is the transfer channel: compatibility = same key + same quantity + value accepted by the target, so a kind registered later gets correct transfer without an N-by-N kind matrix. This needs one key vocabulary across kinds (thickness, layer_structure, material, layer, position, ifc_class, base_offset, top_mode, top_offset, rules, ...); document it in fields.rs and keep keys stable (they are also the criteria fields of task 13). Composite parameters such as the stair rule set are one FieldSpec ('rules'). Apply in FieldSpec order and run the kind's normalisation once at the end, because setters such as the wall top mode (moved into kinds/wall.rs by properties-and-dialogs-05) need the target's storey context. A value the target rejects is reported as skipped instead of failing the whole command, so a mixed target set still gets everything that fits. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs plan_update_elements (lock and validation), kinds/mod.rs FieldSpec lists, project.rs tool defaults.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in transfer.rs: wall to wall copies thickness or layer structure, reference line location, base offset, top link and offset, material, layer, position and IFC class while the reference line points, name and home storey of the target stay unchanged.
- Wall to slab copies only the compatible fields (thickness or structure, material, layer, position); IfcWall is reported as skipped because it is not in the slab class set, and wall-only fields such as the top link are skipped as absent.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: InjectSettings and PickUpSettings execute, undo to the exact starting project (revision normalised) and redo; injecting into a locked element returns CommandError::Locked with the lock reason; a target already equal to the source gives NoChange.
- PickUpSettings from a wall into the wall slot makes the slot's prototype carry the wall's settings and layer; into the slab slot only compatible fields change.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check stay green.
- Satisfies the model half of ELM-003 (pick up into defaults, inject into elements, only compatible settings between kinds).
notes:
SRS: ELM-003 ELM-002
EDT-020 (explicit commands with preview for pick-up and inject) is served by these commands plus the previews of task 11.

title: Add EPSG code, latitude and longitude to the project location
description:
WHY: STR-012 (M): the project location includes the survey point (the coordinates of the project origin in the surveyor's projected coordinate system) and the angle between project north and true north. STR-015 (S): the location also includes latitude and longitude and the EPSG code of the projected CRS. NFR-ACC-004 (M): large survey coordinates (6-7 digit eastings and northings) are never used as modelling coordinates; they are handled through the survey point offset so precision is not lost. O-2 fixes the depth: offset, rotation and the EPSG code of one projected CRS, no reprojection. Status: STR-012 partial (Location at crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:64-73 holds altitude, survey_point [E, N] and true_north; dialog crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:553-592; validation command.rs:288-302; stored in archicraft::project.location, writer.rs:166-170, reader.rs:370-378, schema.rs:153-160); STR-015 missing (no latitude, longitude or EPSG anywhere); NFR-ACC-004 partial (MAX_COORDINATE = 100 km, validate.rs:17 and check_coordinates validate.rs:105-113, rejects 6-7 digit values as model coordinates, but the survey point is never applied). The SurveyPoint export (task 02), typed survey-coordinate entry of terrain points (task 18) and the sun position of 3d-display-styles consume these values.

WHAT (extend; keep altitude, survey_point, true_north, their dialog rows, SetLocation and the archicraft::project.location keys, regressed by the existing round-trip and command tests): Location gains epsg_code: Option<u32>, latitude: Option<f64> and longitude: Option<f64> (radians, the internal angle unit), is_georeferenced() (EPSG code set), and exact conversions survey_to_model(DVec2) -> DVec2, model_to_survey(DVec2) -> DVec2, altitude_of(z) and elevation_at_altitude(h) built from survey_point, true_north and altitude (STR-011 single datum). Command::SetLocation validation grows: finite values, latitude in [-90, 90] degrees, longitude in (-180, 180] degrees, both or neither, EPSG code in 1024..=32767. check_coordinates' error message gains a hint that survey coordinates belong in Project settings > Location. IFCX: archicraft::project.location gains optional epsgCode (integer), latitude and longitude (angle), declared with optional(...) in alpha/schema.rs, written only when set (existing goldens stay byte-identical), read with None defaults; FORMAT_VERSION unchanged. App: the Project settings dialog gets an EPSG code field (hint 'projected CRS, e.g. 2056 or 25832') and latitude/longitude through widgets::angle, all feeding the existing SetLocation. Out of scope: the standard-namespace SurveyPoint nodes (task 02), survey coordinates in the terrain point table (task 18), reprojection or CRS name lookup (O-2), sun position (3d-display-styles), the multi-command OK of the project dialog (existing debt, not worsened).
design: Keep the survey point at full f64 precision (a 7-digit easting still resolves about 1e-9 m); conversions subtract the survey point first and rotate afterwards, so model coordinates never carry the large offset (NFR-ACC-001). Document on Location that true_north is the counter-clockwise angle from project north (+Y) to true north seen from above (matching the dialog label 'Project north to true north') and that the projected CRS grid north is treated as true north because there is no reprojection (O-2; meridian convergence ignored). Store latitude and longitude in radians like every other angle (STR-009 display units apply); the writer of task 02 converts to degrees for epsg4326. Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point (optional schema member, write only when set, read with report.or). Pitfalls: Location derives Copy and Default, which Option fields keep; Command derives Serialize and Deserialize (crash reports, scripting), so the new fields get serde(default) and older serialised commands stay readable; widgets::length must not round 7-digit values to display precision when storing (NFR-ACC-002). Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:64-73, command.rs:288-302, validate.rs:17 and 105-113, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:153-160, writer.rs:166-170, reader.rs:370-378, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:553-592.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs: survey_to_model(model_to_survey(p)) equals p within 1e-9 m for p within +-10 km and a survey point with 7-digit eastings (E 2,600,000.123, N 1,200,000.456, EPSG 2056); with true_north = 0 the conversion is a pure offset; with true_north = 90 degrees the project +Y axis maps to the direction pinned in the Location doc comment (the convention task 02 and VIEW-052 reuse).
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: SetLocation with latitude 91 degrees, a latitude without longitude, EPSG code 0 or 99999, or a non-finite value returns CommandError::Invalid and leaves the project unchanged; a valid location undoes and redoes exactly.
- NFR-ACC-004 test: AddElements with a wall at x = 2,600,000 m is rejected with the hint naming the project location, while the same wall entered through survey_to_model lies within +-100 m of the origin.
- Round trip in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: a project with EPSG 2056, a 7-digit survey point, latitude, longitude and true north 3.2 degrees loads equal; a project without them writes no new keys and every existing golden file stays bit-identical.
- Kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the Project settings dialog shows 'EPSG code', 'Latitude' and 'Longitude', and OK stores the typed values (including an easting of 2600000.123 at full precision) in site.location.
- STR-015 satisfied in model, file and UI; STR-012 location content complete (export clause in task 02); NFR-ACC-004 conversion path available.
notes:
SRS: STR-015 STR-012 NFR-ACC-004
Open question: a vertical CRS EPSG code for the height attribute of IFX-070 is not modelled; until R2 shows an EPSG-named height attribute the height is written with the projected code (task 02, epic risk).

title: Add nested resource folders as metadata on project resources
description:
WHY: UI-016 (S): project resources (materials, layer structures, profiles, presets, saved views) shall be organizable in nested folders by drag and drop, without affecting references (DSP-003). DSP-003 (M): every attribute has a stable internal ID and elements and views reference attributes by ID, so renaming never breaks a reference. Gap row UI-016 missing: resources are flat Vec<Layer>/Vec<Material> (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:171-172), the writer writes flat arrays (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:144-186), no folder concept. Saved views already have ViewFolder { id, name, parent } (plan-views-browser-07); drag and drop between view folders was left to this epic (plan-views-browser-10).

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/folders.rs: ResourceFolderId, `ResourceKind { Material, LayerStructure, Profile, Preset }`, `ResourceFolder { id, name, parent: Option<ResourceFolderId>, kind }`, Project.resource_folders; an optional `folder` field on Material, LayerStructure, Profile (the resource of profiles-columns-beams) and Preset. Commands: AddFolder, RenameFolder, MoveFolder { id, parent } (cycle and kind checks), DeleteFolder (contents move to the parent; undoable) and `MoveToFolder { items: Vec<FolderItem { Material, LayerStructure, Profile, Preset, View }>, target }`, where View items reuse the ViewFolder tree through UpdateView. reidentify_all remaps folders; templates keep them. IFCX: `resourceFolders` in archicraft::project ([{id, name, parent, kind}]) and an optional `folder` on material, layer structure, profile and preset records; dangling folders and cycles are repaired with warnings. Out of scope: the tree UI (task 19), folders for layers (not in UI-016's list).
design: 'Path metadata on resources' (epic design) is realised as a folder id on each resource plus a parent-linked folder tree per resource kind, mirroring ViewFolder so one tree widget can serve both (task 19). Ids never change, so DSP-003 holds by construction and the test proves it across every referencing place. Order inside a folder is the resource order already stored. Pitfalls: validate that an item's kind matches its folder's kind; the Materials dialog's delete-with-replacement flow (dialogs.rs:436-473) must also clear folder references of deleted resources.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: folder commands undo and redo; moving a folder into its own descendant or a folder of another kind is CommandError::Invalid; DeleteFolder moves its contents to the parent and undo restores them.
- DSP-003 test: moving a material that is used by walls, a layer-structure skin, a preset slot and the wall defaults into a nested folder leaves every reference resolving, integrity_problems() empty and the evaluated geometry unchanged; only the folder field differs (epic: moving a material into a folder keeps all references).
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: folders and memberships round-trip; a sample with one nested folder is added to the goldens (re-blessed, reviewed) and passes conformance/run.sh.
- Satisfies the model and persistence clauses of UI-016.
notes:
SRS: UI-016
Assumes the Profile resource of profiles-columns-beams (increment 1) exists; if not, the Profile variant is added when it lands.

title: Terrain, site-level elements and georeferencing
description:
Terrain as a closed solid with a TIN top through typed points and breaklines inside a boundary, created from points or from 2D contour polylines, edited in plan and 3D, cut associatively by building elements, drawn with labelled contours, smooth or faceted in 3D, thinned on demand, written as IfcGeographicElement under the site with a TopSurface part and meeting the 50,000-point budget; plus the site's georeferencing: survey point with EPSG code, latitude and longitude, true north written as the SurveyPoint node per IFX-070, with large survey coordinates never used as model coordinates.

Risks: TIN and Boolean cost on large terrains: tiles are cut only where touched; terrain edges excluded from snap targets by default (INP-017). Georeferencing is offset, rotation and EPSG code only, no reprojection (O-2, O-8); the EPSG height attribute follows R2 when it appears.
design: archicraft-model site-level containment (Element.storey becomes Container::{Storey, Site} through the framework) and kinds/terrain.rs; Location gains latitude, longitude and EPSG code; archicraft-geometry terrain.rs with spade CDT and constraint edges (via geo), skirt and flat bottom, contour extraction by slicing the TIN, tiling in mesh.rs; archicraft-ifcx site children, SurveyPoint with usd::xformop and in-file epsg schema declarations through registry.rs; archicraft-app terrain tool with point elevation entry in 3D and the contour-pick step.
acceptance_criteria: AS-01 terrain from typed spot elevations is a closed manifold body; picking 2D contour polylines into a selected terrain assigns one elevation per contour and picking without a selection creates nothing; a basement slab subtracted with upward extrusion removes the soil above it and follows when the slab moves (SOL-021 relation); contour lines regenerate on edit with every n-th labelled and can be frozen to 2D lines; 50,000 points with 200 breaklines build in under 5 s in a benchmark and tile into closed Body_n parts of at most 65,535 points; IfcGeographicElement as a child of IfcSite with Body and TopSurface passes conformance; a project with 7-digit eastings keeps model coordinates near the origin and writes a SurveyPoint child with epsg<code> eastings/northings, the height attribute, epsg4326 latitude/longitude and the second +Y reference point, schemas declared in file; F9's sloping site with storeys -3..+1 is built as the RM-S base.
notes: SRS: TER-001 TER-002 TER-004 TER-005 TER-006 TER-007 TER-008 TER-010 TER-012 TER-013 TER-014 STR-012 STR-015 IFX-070 NFR-ACC-004

title: Add region stretch targets and the Stretch command
description:
WHY: SEL-005 (S): moving the persistent selection region stretches the nodes inside it. Gap row SEL-005 missing, depending on 'EDT stretch/reshape' and the SEL-004 region limit. Building blocks from earlier epics: Command::Reshape with ReshapeOp::MoveNode on PartRef::Node, which also addresses wall ends as Node { ring 0, index 0|1 } (edit-reshape-palette-03/05), Transform::Move (selection-transforms-03), and SelectionShape with its partially-inside predicate in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs (selection-transforms-07). The region tool and the UI wiring are task 17.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: `stretch_targets(project, shape: &SelectionShape, storeys: &[StoreyId]) -> StretchTargets { translate: Vec<ElementId>, nodes: Vec<PartTarget>, skipped: Vec<(ElementId, String)> }`: on the given storeys, elements whose every addressable node is inside (geo contains-or-touches with MODEL_TOLERANCE from crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:10) go to translate; elements with some nodes inside contribute a PartTarget { element, part: PartRef::Node { ring, index } } per inside node (slab outline and hole nodes, wall ends); kinds without node addressing translate when their anchor is inside and are otherwise skipped with a reason. It lives in the geometry crate because SelectionShape and geo are there and archicraft-model must not depend on archicraft-geometry (crates/archicraft-model/Cargo.toml). crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs: `Command::Stretch { translate: Vec<ElementId>, nodes: Vec<PartTarget>, vector: DVec3 }` (label 'Stretch n elements'), planned as Transform::Move edits for translate plus ReshapeOp::MoveNode { to: node + vector } for the nodes, validated atomically through validate_element and the outline repair of edit-reshape-palette-02, with the existing lock checks (CommandError::Locked) and one undo step. Out of scope: the region tool, its display and the command limits (task 17), regions in section views.
design: Resolve the targets in the geometry crate and mutate in the model: the inside test needs geo and SelectionShape, the command must stay headless and undoable. Reusing ReshapeOp::MoveNode keeps validation and repair identical to manual node edits (EDT-019). Pitfalls: a wall with both ends inside translates (it is not stretched twice); hosted elements follow their host through ELM-016; the whole command is atomic, so one invalid element rejects the stretch.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of stretch_targets: a slab with two of four outline nodes inside yields exactly those two node targets; a wall with one end inside yields that end; an element entirely inside goes to translate; nodes on the boundary count as inside (tolerance); storeys [first, second] collect both storeys and elements on other storeys are ignored; a kind without node addressing is skipped with a reason when its anchor is outside.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: Stretch moves only the targeted slab nodes, stretches the wall end and translates the whole element; undo restores the exact starting project (revision normalised) and redo reapplies; a stretch that would make a slab self-intersect is rejected atomically with CommandError::Invalid naming the element; a locked target returns CommandError::Locked with the lock reason.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check stay green.
- Satisfies the 'moving it stretches the nodes inside it' clause of SEL-005 at model level.
notes:
SRS: SEL-005
Implicit prerequisite: Command::Reshape and ReshapeOp::MoveNode on wall ends (edit-reshape-palette-03/05, increment 1, closed before increment 3 starts but not a declared dependency of this epic). If they are missing, move nodes directly through the PartRef::Node addressing of selection-transforms-01.

title: Extract contour lines and labels from the terrain surface
description:
WHY: TER-007 (S): in plan, terrain is drawable with contour lines from a base elevation and interval, every n-th line a major contour labelled with its elevation; contours update automatically when the terrain changes and can replace or accompany the triangulation edges. Status: TER-007 missing; plan drawings contain only cut, projected and overhead lines derived from bodies (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:23-55), with no isoline code and no text in plan.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/contours.rs: contours(faces, settings) -> Vec<Contour { level, major, polylines: Vec<Vec<DVec2>> }> slicing the up-facing triangles of the evaluated terrain tiles at levels base + k * interval between the lowest and highest Z (per triangle only the levels inside its Z range), with symbolic perturbation for vertices exactly at a level (z == L treated as above), segments stitched across triangles and tiles through quantised endpoint keys into open or closed polylines, collinear points removed within 0.01 mm. Labels: each major polyline longer than 15 label heights on paper gets a label at its arc-length midpoint (and every further 100 mm on paper), oriented along the line and flipped to read upright, text = elevation in the project length unit; Labels reuse the plan label record that drafting-trim-split-09 added to PlanDrawing for fill area labels (adding an angle field if it has none); only if no such record exists, add PlanDrawing.labels: Vec<PlanText { position, angle, text, height_mm, element }>. The terrain plan symbol of task 04 follows display.plan: Contours, Triangulation or Both, with minor and major contours as separate line classes. Automatic update follows from evaluation (no cache outside ModelGeometry). Bench in the new crates/archicraft-geometry/benches/terrain.rs using samples::synthetic_terrain (task 05), next to the benches/geometry.rs of regression-and-status-16 (an increment-1 epic that is not a declared dependency: if criterion and the bench target are still missing, add the dev-dependency and the [[bench]] entry here). Out of scope: settings UI, drawing the labels and converting to 2D lines (task 13), section and elevation views.
design: Slicing the evaluated up-facing faces instead of the raw TIN makes contours follow solid-operation cuts (task 11) and tiles for free. Stitching by quantised keys (1e-9 m grid) instead of vertex indices works for shared (smooth) and per-triangle (faceted) vertices alike and relies on the bitwise-equal cell-line points of task 05. Per-triangle level ranges give O(triangles + segments) instead of O(triangles x levels). Label height is in paper millimetres and scales with the view's drawing scale. Pitfalls: flat areas exactly at a level (pit floors, flat terrain) must not produce filled regions, which the perturbation rule prevents; labels on very short closed contours are skipped. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs PlanDrawing and PlanElement, terrain.rs, slice.rs (quantisation pattern), mesh.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in contours.rs: a sampled cone gives concentric closed contours every 0.50 m with radii matching the analytic values within 1e-6 m; the plane z = 0.1x gives straight contours at x = 10 L; a vertex exactly at a level produces no duplicate or zero-length segment; from base 0.00 every 5th contour is major.
- Contours of a four-tile terrain (forced budget) are continuous across tile boundaries: the polyline count equals the untiled result.
- Labels: a 40 m major contour at 1:100 gets a label at its midpoint with an angle in (-90, 90] degrees and text in the project unit (for example '2.500').
- Editing a point with EditTerrain SetPoints changes the contours of the next PlanDrawing without an explicit refresh (auto-update through ModelGeometry::evaluate).
- Plan mode tests: Contours draws no TIN edges, Triangulation no contours, Both draws both.
- Contour extraction for the 50,000-point synthetic terrain at 0.50 m runs under 300 ms in release (criterion bench).
- TER-007 contour, label, auto-update and replace-or-accompany clauses satisfied in the drawing data.
notes:
SRS: TER-007
Contour defaults (task 03) are proposals outside Appendix D: base 0.00 m, interval 0.50 m, every 5th major, 2.0 mm labels.

title: Write and read archicraft::stair and archicraft::stairRules
description:
WHY: IFX-060 (M): everything needed to restore the editable model is stored in archicraft:: attributes, and IFX-061 declares each of them in the file; STA-051 (stair-body-plan) adds the compound parts but already states that solver inputs and results live in the ArchiCraft namespace. The epic acceptance requires the rule set and all parameters to round-trip in archicraft::stair and archicraft::stairRules: STA-001's parameters (baseline, width, storey link, bottom and top offsets, rule set), STA-002's side and offset, STA-005's flags and bounds and STA-024's start and end conditions must survive save and open, and PRJ-007 stores the stair rule defaults with the project. The codec registry of element-kind-framework-06 (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/) makes this one module.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs implementing KindCodec: archicraft::stair { baseline: [point2], width, side, offset, baseOffset, top (top_link of crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/common.rs, element-kind-framework-06), riser { mode count|height, value }, going { mode free|fixed, value? }, walkingLine { mode halfWidth|fromInner, value? }, start, end (riser|tread), material reference, solution { riserCount, riserHeight, going, goings, totalRise, runLength } } and archicraft::stairRules { riserHeight, going, stepFormula, ratio, sum, pitch, walkingLineDistance, landingLength: { enabled, min?, max? } } as a second attribute on the element node (KindCodec gains an optional list of extra attributes, default empty) and nested in the stair defaults slot of toolDefaults; declarations are emitted only when a stair or a stair slot is present. The element is written as IfcStair with its provisional Body and Axis children. Reader leniency: missing rules fall back to D.3 with a warning; a missing or internally inconsistent solution is re-solved with a warning; a solution that no longer fits the levels is kept as the last valid one (task 05 reports it as stale); an invalid baseline skips the element with an error. New sample samples::stairs() in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs, built with element-kind-framework-03's FixtureBuilder and listed in samples::catalogue() so tests/roundtrip.rs samples() and examples/reference_models.rs pick it up, and the golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/stairs.ifcx. Both attributes are optional additions, so under element-kind-framework-12's rule (alpha/mod.rs) FORMAT_VERSION (alpha/schema.rs) stays and no migration is added. Out of scope: IfcStairFlight/IfcSlab children and IfcStair predefined types (stair-body-plan, STA-051), rule presets as resources (templates-presets).
design: Two attributes because the rule set is a reusable value (templates-presets stores the DIN and ÖNORM presets with the same schema, STA-052) and because consumers can read the rules without parsing stair geometry. Write parameters at full precision with insertion-ordered members (serde_json preserve_order) for deterministic goldens. Storing the solution lets keep-last-valid survive reopening and lets the reader reproduce the same body; the reader checks it with solve() and replaces it only when missing or internally inconsistent (N × R ≠ total rise, run ≠ goings × G). Pitfalls: use the schema's angle type for the pitch bounds (radians in the model); align the defaults slot with element-kind-framework-12's nested slot shape; follow the FORMAT_VERSION policy that framework set for new kinds instead of bumping ad hoc; bless with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 and review the diff.
