Pointers: alpha/kinds/wall.rs as the codec template, alpha/schema.rs combinators, tests/roundtrip.rs samples() and the FixtureBuilder in samples.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/roundtrip.rs: round_trip_restores_the_editable_model covers samples::stairs() — stair A Count(19), Fixed(0.300), Centre, 3.000 m; stair B TargetHeight(0.150), free going, Left with offset 0.050, FromInner(0.400), end with tread, ratio and pitch enabled with non-default bounds; stair C an L-shaped baseline — with every parameter, rule flag, bound and the solution equal after reading.
- golden_files_are_reproduced and catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files pass with stairs.ifcx; the two existing goldens stay byte-identical (no stair declarations without stairs).
- written_files_validate_without_problems and written_meshes_are_closed_bodies pass for the stair sample; conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx passes with an IfcStair node under its storey and a Body mesh (conformance/check.ts extended only if it rejects the class).
- Leniency: removing archicraft::stairRules restores D.3 with one warning; removing the solution re-solves with one warning; a corrupted baseline skips that stair with one error and keeps the rest.
- A stair defaults slot with a modified rule set round-trips (PRJ-007).
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green.
notes: SRS: STA-001 STA-002 STA-005 STA-024.

title: Pick up and inject parameters in section and elevation views
description:
WHY: ELM-003 (S) requires parameter pick-up and inject 'in plan, section and 3D views', with the latch mode and the compatible-only transfer in every one of them. Task 11 delivers plan and 3D through a pane-agnostic pick handler in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/transfer.rs; section and elevation panes get element picking from sections-elevations-dims-07 (SectionSurface in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/section_surface.rs and SectionDrawing::pick), which is in the same increment but not a dependency of this epic.

WHAT: register the transfer handler of task 11 for section and elevation panes: Alt and Alt+Cmd/Ctrl cursors, clicks resolved through SectionDrawing::pick (cut parts first, then projected parts nearest first, Tab cycling as in sections-elevations-dims-07), hover highlight and the TransferReport tooltip, latch mode from the Edit menu and the command palette, and the same status-line messages. No new commands: PickUpSettings and InjectSettings of task 02. Out of scope: drawings placed on layouts.
design: The handler of task 11 takes a pane-provided pick function, so this task adds one adapter instead of a third code path. Pitfalls: in sections the projected element behind a cut one must be reachable (Tab cycling); a click on a level line or grid axis is not an element and must do nothing.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/transfer.rs: in an open section, Alt-click on a cut 0.365 m wall sets the wall defaults to 0.365 m and that wall's layer; Alt+Cmd-click on another wall in an elevation view injects them; one undo reverts the inject.
- Injecting wall defaults into a slab cut in the section transfers only the compatible settings and the status line names the skipped IFC class.
- Latch mode started from the Edit menu works in a section pane without modifiers and ends with Esc; the hover tooltip lists transferred and skipped settings before the click.
- Satisfies the section-view clause of ELM-003; with task 11, ELM-003 is complete.
notes:
SRS: ELM-003
External prerequisite: sections-elevations-dims-07 (section and elevation element picking). It is in the same increment but outside this fragment, so there is no edge: claim this task only after it is closed. templates-presets-done waits for this task, so the epic closes when both are in.

title: Cut terrain associatively with solid operations, tile by tile
description:
WHY: TER-006 (M): building elements cut the terrain associatively; a basement slab subtracted with upward extrusion (SOL-021) removes the soil above it, and a path slab intersected with the terrain follows the grade. SOL-020 applies solid operations to every element with a closed body including terrain, SOL-022 makes them associative (moving an operator by 0.10 m moves the cut), SOL-028 demands identical results in 3D, plan and IFCX. Epic risk: TIN and Boolean cost on large terrains, so tiles are cut only where touched. Status: TER-006 missing (no relation or Boolean concept at increment 0); solid-kernel-ops delivers the SolidKernel trait (boolean(op, a, b)), Relation::SolidOperation { targets, operators, kind, extrusion, material_source }, the pipeline stage and the operation dialog.

WHAT: Reused unchanged: SolidKernel and kernel::boolean (solid-kernel-ops-02), sweep_z (solid-kernel-ops-06), apply_operations (solid-kernel-ops-18), the SolidOperations stage with its failure path (solid-kernel-ops-05) and normalize_parts (solid-kernel-ops-03); this task adds only the per-tile application and the terrain operator. Terrain becomes a valid SolidOperation target and operator through solid: true on its descriptor (task 03) and its geometry hooks. As target, the Boolean stage applies an operation per Body_n tile only where the operator's extruded XY bounds intersect the tile bounds; untouched tiles pass through unchanged (Arc reuse keyed by tile index and terrain revision); results are re-checked for closedness and the 65,535-point limit and re-split by the kernel's splitter if needed; the +Z sweep limit follows sweep_z's target-bounds rule (top + 1.0 m) applied to the bounds of the whole terrain, so every tile sees the same operator prism. As operator, terrain::solid_within(rect) builds a closed sub-terrain clipped to the target's XY bounds (the tile builder of task 05 with one cell), so a path slab intersected with the terrain uses a small operator instead of the whole terrain. Plan: the terrain plan symbol (task 04 TIN edges, task 12 contours) is derived from the up-facing faces of the evaluated, cut bodies, so a pit appears in plan with its outline and without contours or TIN edges inside it; TopSurface stays the uncut TIN. A failed Boolean keeps the uncut tile and lists the terrain (NFR-REL-005, NFR-REL-006). Out of scope: openings in terrain (OPN-012, members-profiles-adv), excavation volumes (OPN-011), new relation UI (the solid-kernel-ops dialog lists terrain automatically).
design: Per-tile Booleans keep kernel inputs small and most edits cheap; the tile grid of task 05 is anchored at the boundary box, so tiles stay stable while operators move. Up-facing faces are those with normal.z above cos(89 degrees); a horizontal pit floor exactly at a contour level is handled by the perturbation rule of task 12. Pitfalls: solid-kernel-ops-05 transforms operator bodies into the target frame with a 'site-level frame elevation 0', while element-kind-framework-07 writes site-level elements translated by their home storey elevation and task 04 builds terrain bodies storey-local to it; use one frame_elevation(project, element) helper (home storey elevation for every element, site-level included) in the stage, the writer and build_scene, and change the stage if it still uses 0; coplanar faces (a slab top exactly at the terrain surface) are a known Boolean robustness case, so add a regression fixture; the pipeline order of solid-kernel-ops (base bodies, junctions, openings, solid operations, trims) applies unchanged; dirty propagation along relation edges (element-kind-framework-10) re-evaluates the terrain when an operator moves. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kernel/ (solid-kernel-ops), terrain.rs (tasks 04 and 05), crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs, plan.rs terrain symbol.
acceptance_criteria:
- Basement cut (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/terrain.rs): a flat terrain at +0.00 with bottom -5.00 and a 10 x 8 m slab with its bottom at -3.00 subtracted with +Z extrusion lowers the terrain volume by exactly 10 x 8 x 3.00 m3 (within 1e-6 relative) and every tile stays closed; MoveElements of the slab by 0.10 m in X moves the pit by 0.10 m with no further action (SOL-022), and undo restores the previous body.
- Path slab: a 0.30 m slab spanning above and below a sloping terrain, intersected with the terrain as operator, keeps only the part below the terrain surface, and its top follows the TIN within 1e-6 m at 20 sampled points.
- Tile locality: on a 20,000-point terrain with at least four tiles (forced budget), a small subtract re-evaluates only the intersecting tiles through the kernel (call counter).
- Round trip: the relation (solid-kernel-ops codec) and the cut bodies survive save and open, the cut-terrain file passes conformance and every Body_n is closed.
- Plan: after the basement cut the terrain drawing shows the pit outline, no contour above -3.00 inside the pit and no triangulation edges there (SOL-028).
- An injected kernel failure keeps the last valid tile and lists the terrain in problems.
- Frame regression: with the terrain's home storey at +3.00 m the basement pit lies at the same absolute elevations as with the home storey at +-0.00.
- TER-006 satisfied.
notes:
SRS: TER-006
Open question: TopSurface stays the uncut TIN after cuts (the 'recover the TIN' clause of TER-014); revisit if consumers need the excavated surface.

title: Organise resources in folder trees by drag and drop
description:
WHY: UI-016 (S): project resources (materials, layer structures, profiles, presets, saved views) shall be organizable in nested folders by drag and drop, without affecting references (DSP-003). The incremental search of UI-014 must keep working inside folder trees, and plan-views-browser-10 left drag and drop between saved-view folders to this epic.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/folder_tree.rs: a generic FolderTree widget over a FolderSource trait (folders with parent links; items with folder, label and id), implemented for resource folders (task 18) and view folders (plan-views-browser-07): a collapsible tree (CollapsingState ids from folder ids), egui drag and drop (dnd_set_drag_payload / dnd_release_payload) to move items and folders onto folders or the root, multi-item drag of the list selection, context menu New folder / Rename / Delete folder / 'Move to folder…' (keyboard alternative), and a search field that filters items and keeps their folder path expanded. Used in the Materials dialog (materials_window, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:376-478), the layer structure list of layer-structures-11, the profile list when present, the Presets manager of task 10 and the Saved views group of the project browser (ui/browser.rs after plan-views-browser-10). Each drop issues one MoveToFolder command (undoable). Out of scope: dragging between projects or windows (library-dw-exchange).
design: One widget with adapters per source instead of five copies; the drop target resolves to a FolderTarget and the adapter builds the command. kittest drag: press on the source, move over the target across several frames beyond the drag threshold, release. Pitfalls: keep delete-with-replacement reachable from the tree's context menu; stable egui ids per item id so renames keep the drag state; strings in the Fluent catalogue.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/folder_tree.rs: in the Materials dialog create 'Masonry' and its subfolder 'Brick', drag the material 'Brick' into it with injected pointer events → the tree shows Masonry/Brick/Brick; walls using it render unchanged and the properties panel still names 'Brick' (DSP-003); undo moves it back.
- Drag a saved view into a view folder of the project browser and a preset into a preset folder; dropping a folder onto its own descendant issues no command.
- Searching 'bri' shows the material under its expanded folder path; 'Move to folder…' moves an item without the mouse.
- Satisfies UI-016.
notes: SRS: UI-016

title: Warn when a project is open elsewhere and open it read-only
description:
WHY: PRJ-006 (S): if a project file is already open in another ArchiCraft instance, the system shall warn the user and offer to open it read-only. Gap row PRJ-006 missing: no per-project lock, no in-use detection, no read-only mode; the only lock is the per-instance autosave session lock (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/autosave.rs:43-56), which is not tied to a project file. The epic design keeps the per-project lock separate from that session lock; PRJ-011 in library-dw-exchange relies on this for two instances on one file.

WHAT: New persistence/lock.rs: ProjectLock::acquire(path) -> Result<ProjectLock, LockError { InUse(LockInfo), Io }> creating the sibling file '.<file name>.lock' (hidden and outside the .ifcx filter of the open dialog, like backups in PRJ-005) holding LockInfo { user, host, pid, since } as JSON and an OS lock through File::try_lock (as autosave.rs:53); a lock file whose OS lock can be taken is stale and is taken over; the lock is released on close, on drop and when Save As moves the document (the new path is locked first). Document gains read_only and lock. app.rs open_path (app.rs:152-180, shared by File > Open, recent entries, the start screen and the command line): on InUse a modal 'Project in use' names user, host and time with 'Open read-only' and 'Cancel'; a read-only document shows '(read-only)' in the title and a status-bar badge, Save acts as Save As, saving onto a locked path is refused with a message, autosave still writes to the recovery folder. Out of scope: guarantees on network shares (documented), force unlock.
design: The OS advisory lock decides and the JSON only informs the message, so a crash (which releases the OS lock but leaves the file) is detected exactly on local disks. std File::try_lock (flock on Unix, LockFileEx on Windows) is the same primitive the autosave session uses: no new dependency. save_atomically (persistence/mod.rs) replaces the project file by rename; the lock is a sibling file and is unaffected. Pitfalls: SMB and NFS lock semantics vary, so when the info file exists but its holder cannot be confirmed the warning is still shown; never put the project lock in the recovery folder; the read-only flag must survive replace_document and be cleared by Save As.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in persistence/lock.rs: a second acquire on the same path through another file handle returns InUse with the first holder's info; dropping the first lets the second succeed; a stale lock file without an OS lock is taken over; a clean release removes the file.
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/project_lock.rs re-executes the test binary (std::env::current_exe) as a second process that holds the lock; the parent's acquire reports InUse with the child's pid (the lock-file test of the epic acceptance).
- kittest: opening a file whose lock is held shows 'Project in use' with 'Open read-only'; choosing it opens the project with '(read-only)' in the title, and Save requests the Save As dialog (recorded by the scripted FileDialogs of task 06) instead of writing to the locked path.
- Closing the project or quitting releases the lock and removes the lock file; Save As to a new path moves the lock.
- Satisfies PRJ-006.
notes: SRS: PRJ-006

title: Add tool presets as a project resource with apply and reorder
description:
WHY: ELM-002 (S): users shall save a tool's settings as a named preset, apply a preset to new or selected elements and manage presets per tool (rename, delete, reorder, search); presets are stored in the project and template, templates supply presets (PRJ-001), every settings dialog offers preset selection, and applying a preset also sets the element's layer. PRJ-007 lists presets among the project-level settings, and SEL-010 (task 12) needs to know which preset an element came from. Gap row ELM-002 missing: no Preset resource, no storage in project, template or IFCX, no management, no apply-to-selection.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/preset.rs: PresetId (id_type! in ids.rs), `Preset { id, name, kind: KindTag, slot: DefaultsSlot }` reusing the defaults slot of element-kind-framework-04 (layer, position, IFC class, prototype payload); Project.presets: Vec<Preset> in display order and Project::presets_of(kind). The Element envelope gains `preset: Option<PresetId>`, set by AddElements when the tool's defaults came from a preset and by ApplyPreset. Commands: AddPreset { preset, index }, UpdatePreset (rename, or overwrite the slot), DeletePreset (clears element references, undoable), MovePreset { id, to_index } (within its kind), ApplyPreset { preset, targets } (same kind only, through transfer_settings with SettingsSource::Preset, plus the layer) and ApplyPresetToDefaults { preset } (SetToolDefaults). The replacement loops of DeleteLayer, DeleteMaterial and DeleteLayerStructure also rewrite preset slots, check_tool_defaults validates them, reidentify_all remaps presets and Element.preset. IFCX: `presets` array in archicraft::project ([{id, name, kind, slot}] with the slot written by the kind codec exactly like toolDefaults) and an optional `preset` reference on archicraft::element; dangling references are dropped with a warning. template.rs: one preset per tool kind named after its D.2 default plus typical wall and slab variants (see notes). Out of scope: UI (task 10), folders (task 18), stair rule presets (task 04).
design: A preset is a full DefaultsSlot, so 'save from tool' copies the slot and 'apply to tool' is SetToolDefaults: no parallel settings type, and every kind that registers a defaults slot gets presets for free. Applying to elements reuses transfer_settings (task 02) with all transferable fields of the same kind and sets the layer explicitly, as ELM-002 demands. Presets are per kind (ELM-002 'per tool'); tool modes such as slab polygon/rectangle share the kind's presets. Reorder and bulk changes use an Edit::SetPresets snapshot (the 'prefer Set* snapshots' rule of the command extension point). Element.preset is advisory: later edits keep it, and the UI computes 'modified' by comparing transferable values. Bump FORMAT_VERSION through the migration table of element-kind-framework-12 (tasks 03, 04, 12, 13, 15 and 18 of this epic may share one bump per release). Pitfalls: Project derives PartialEq, so order is semantic; keep the toolDefaults key order of the writer unchanged; the reader must resolve preset references after reading all presets.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: every preset command executes, undoes exactly and redoes; a preset with an unknown layer or a class outside the kind's set is CommandError::Invalid; MovePreset reorders only within its kind; DeletePreset clears Element.preset and undo restores it.
- ApplyPreset on two walls sets their transferable settings and their layer from the preset, keeps their geometry and records element.preset; applying a wall preset to a slab returns CommandError::Unsupported (cross-kind transfer is task 11's injection).
- DeleteMaterial and DeleteLayer with a replacement rewrite preset slots; undo restores them.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: presets (order included) and element preset references round-trip; a file without presets loads with an empty list and no warning; a dangling preset reference is dropped with a warning; the written file validates.
- The reidentify_all test covers presets and element preset references.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check and conformance/run.sh on the golden files stay green (goldens re-blessed and reviewed if a sample gains a preset).
- Satisfies the storage, apply (including the layer) and management-command clauses of ELM-002 at model level.
notes:
SRS: ELM-002 PRJ-001
Template presets (proposal): 'Wall 250 masonry' (D.2 default), 'Interior wall 115 masonry' on layer 'Interior walls', 'Exterior wall layered' using the template's layered structure from layer-structures-09; 'Slab 200 reinforced concrete'; one '<Kind> default' per other registered kind. Open: show 'Preset: X (modified)' when an element's values differ from its preset (computed, not stored).

title: Build the terrain TIN and its closed body in archicraft-geometry
description:
WHY: TER-001 (M): terrain is a closed solid whose top surface is a TIN through 3D points and optional breaklines inside an editable boundary polygon, with a flat bottom at a user-defined elevation or thickness. TER-012 needs that closed body for IFCX, and IFX-032 requires closed, 2-manifold, outward-oriented meshes. Status: TER-001 missing; the gap row points to the spade constrained Delaunay triangulation already wired in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/triangulate.rs (constraint edges, can_add_constraint, duplicate detection) and to TriMesh::add_face and check_closed (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:81-175). The plan view also needs a terrain representation so the element is visible once the tool exists.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/terrain.rs. (1) Boundary elevations: a provisional CDT of all points and breaklines, including points outside the boundary, gives every boundary node its Z by barycentric interpolation inside the convex hull or the linear Z at the closest point of the hull boundary outside it; boundary edges are densified at about twice the mean point spacing with derived Z so long edges do not flatten the surface. (2) Final CDT: points inside the boundary, breakline segments clipped to the boundary with geo (LineString intersected with the Polygon) as constraint edges, boundary edges as constraints split where a breakline meets the boundary (the breakline Z wins), triangles outside the boundary removed; result Tin { vertices: Vec<DVec3>, triangles: Vec<[u32; 3]>, boundary_loop: Vec<u32> } with elevation_at(xy) by locate and barycentric interpolation. (3) Body: the TIN top, one vertical skirt face per original boundary edge (top polyline from the TIN boundary loop, triangulated in its plane), and a flat bottom at the resolved bottom Z triangulated with triangulate(); planar faces get their own vertices, TIN triangles share vertices (smooth default; faceted in task 14); Z is offset by the home storey elevation because bodies are storey-local (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:1-7). Registration through the geometry kind registry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/terrain.rs, GeometryKind of element-kind-framework-15). Plan: plan.rs gets a terrain plan symbol instead of slicing by the cut plane: the boundary outline as a projected line and the TIN edges as thin projected lines in their own line class (so the plan SnapSource can skip them, task 07) on the home storey, picking inside the boundary. GeometryError variants naming point or breakline ids for degenerate inputs, listed as problems (NFR-REL-006). Out of scope: tiling and TopSurface (task 05), contours (task 12), the smooth/faceted switch (task 14), Booleans (task 11).
design: spade through geo, as technology-choices names for 'the terrain surface with its breaklines (SRS TER-001)'; bulk-load points, then insert constraints, which keeps a 50,000-point CDT in the tens of milliseconds. Two passes (provisional CDT for boundary heights, final CDT for the surface) keep the surface inside the hull equal to the point TIN except next to the boundary constraint, where Delaunay flips are expected; tests therefore compare at input points, not at arbitrary XY near the boundary. One skirt face per original boundary edge keeps the bottom ring equal to the boundary nodes, so skirts and bottom close exactly. Pitfalls: spade returns the existing handle for a duplicate position (detect it as triangulate.rs does); add_constraint must be guarded by can_add_constraint and turned into an error naming the breakline; remove outside triangles by constraint-bounded faces or the shared Ring/Outline contains, not by another copy of point_in_ring (technical debt); keep vertex order deterministic (inputs in id order, then breaklines) for byte-stable files (IFX-007). Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/triangulate.rs, extrude.rs (face pattern), mesh.rs:81-175, evaluate.rs:1-70, plan.rs:111-150, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/ registry of element-kind-framework-15.
acceptance_criteria:
- terrain_body_is_closed (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/terrain.rs): seeded random terrains (10 to 5,000 points, 0 to 20 breaklines, convex and concave boundaries) produce a body that passes TriMesh::check_closed with positive volume.
- Planar input: points on z = 0.1x + 0.05y + 3 inside a 20 x 30 m rectangle with bottom Elevation(-2) give the analytic prism volume within 1e-9 relative, and elevation_at matches the plane within 1e-9 m.
- Every input point inside the boundary is a TIN vertex with its exact Z; every clipped breakline segment is a union of TIN edges; contour breaklines yield flat TIN edges at their elevation.
- Boundary heights: a boundary node inside the hull gets the barycentric Z, one outside gets the hull-edge Z; a point outside the boundary influences boundary heights but is not a TIN vertex.
- Default bottom: Depth(5.00) puts the bottom exactly 5.00 m below the lowest input elevation (D.2).
- Errors: collinear points, two points at the same XY or crossing breaklines produce a GeometryError naming ids; the terrain appears in problems and other elements still evaluate.
- Site-level placement: with the home storey at +3.00 m the body lies 3.00 m lower in storey-local coordinates, so world Z after the site-level transform equals the input elevations within 0.1 mm (IFX-031).
- plan.rs unit test: the terrain plan element holds the boundary outline and the triangulation edges and no cut regions; pick() inside the boundary returns the terrain.
- TER-001 geometry satisfied (single body; tiling follows in task 05).
notes: SRS: TER-001

title: Ship metric and imperial default templates as .ifcx data
description:
WHY: PRJ-001 (M): a default template shall ship with the product and supply project settings, storeys, layers, materials, layer structures and views. PRJ-012 (S): an imperial default template (feet-inches) shall ship in addition to the metric template (O-11: one metric template per Appendix D, imperial is S). Appendix D.1 and D.2 define the metric defaults. Gap rows: PRJ-001 partial (code-only template without layer structures); PRJ-012 partial, where the verifier confirms that feet-inches support is complete (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:14-82, 294-337, 377-425; Project settings dialog dialogs.rs:509-521; IFCX round trip writer.rs:155-161, reader.rs:328-352) and only the template artefact and the choice at New are missing. The roadmap assigns the shipped-template template_contents test to this epic; the epic risk 'template files as data can drift from code defaults' is pinned by it.

WHAT: template.rs stays the single source: default_metric_project() gains the presets of task 03, the stair rule presets of task 04 and (already from layer-structures-09) the D.2 layer structures; new default_imperial_project() with feet-inches units, imperial storeys, cut plane, drawing scale and tool defaults (values in notes) and the same layers, materials, structures (imperial thicknesses), presets and views; both are built with the seeded FixtureBuilder (element-kind-framework-03) so the files are byte-stable. Shipped artefacts crates/archicraft-ifcx/templates/default-metric.ifcx and default-imperial.ifcx, written by save_template with a fixed author and timestamp; `archicraft_ifcx::templates::built_in() -> &'static [BuiltInTemplate { info, bytes }]` via include_bytes!. New tests in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/templates.rs: `shipped_templates_are_current` (regenerates in memory and compares bytes; ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 rewrites, like the golden files) and `template_contents`, which moves here from template.rs:391-402 and reads only the shipped bytes through load_template. CI runs conformance/run.sh on the two template files too. Out of scope: New dialog and start screen (06), user templates (07).
design: Code is the source, the file is the reviewed artefact: the bless test keeps the .ifcx a derivative of template.rs and template_contents reads only the file, so drift in either direction fails CI. Seeded v5 ids make the shipped bytes deterministic; instantiation re-randomises them (task 01). Imperial values are exact inch values (0.0254 m per inch) so they display without rounding noise; tests compare formatted strings. D.1 rows owned by other epics are asserted through their fields (drawing scale of plan-renderer, view range of plan-views-browser, repair thresholds of edit-reshape-palette). Kinds of parallel increment-3 epics (railings, curtain walls) get their D.2 rows when they register; the registry check forces it. Pitfalls: the template ships no elements; keep file size small (no geometry beyond what the writer requires for an empty model); never read the shipped bytes in template.rs itself (archicraft-model has no IFCX dependency).
acceptance_criteria:
- template_contents loads default-metric.ifcx and asserts every project-level D.1 value: metre with 3 decimals; decimal degrees with 2 decimals and roof pitch in degrees; storeys '00 Ground floor' at ±0.000 m and '01 First floor' at +3.000 m, both 3.00 m high; plan cut plane 1.10 m; view range bottom at the storey elevation and top at the next storey; drawing scale 1:100; model tolerance 0.01 mm; repair thresholds 0.1 mm and 0.1°; tessellation 2 mm chord deviation and at most 10° per segment.
- The same test asserts every D.2 default table-driven, one row per kind: wall 0.25 m masonry, reference line on the exterior face, base offset 0, top linked to home + 1 with offset 0; slab 0.20 m reinforced concrete, top at the storey elevation; column 0.30 × 0.30 m reinforced concrete, centre anchor, top home + 1; beam 0.25 × 0.50 m reinforced concrete, top-centre anchor, top at the home elevation + 2.80 m; door 0.90 × 2.10 m wall opening, single-leaf hinged, sill at the storey elevation, centred in the wall; window 1.20 × 1.40 m wall opening, tilt-and-turn single sash, sill 0.90 m, centred in the core; roof pitch 35°, 0.30 m thick, eaves overhang 0.50 m, pivot at the top of the walls; stair width 1.00 m, D.3 rule set, monolithic structure with smooth underside, tread and riser finish 0.025 m; railing height 1.00 m, inner posts at most 1.20 m apart, top rail 50 × 50 mm, vertical bars with at most 0.12 m clear spacing; curtain wall grid 1.50 × 3.00 m, aluminium frames 0.05 × 0.15 m, glass panels 0.03 m; terrain bottom 5.00 m below the lowest terrain point; grid spacing 6.00 m with axes A, B, C… and 1, 2, 3…. Rows whose kind is not registered when this task lands (railing and curtain wall come with their increment-3 epics) stay in the table as pending; a registry check fails when a registered kind with a tool has no active row, so the epic that registers it must add the template default and re-bless.
- It also asserts the D.2 layer structures, at least one preset per tool kind, the stair rule presets of task 04 and the saved views (both 3D viewpoints and every other ViewDefinition the template carries after plan-views-browser-07); the personal D.1 rows (autosave 5 min, 1 backup, 100 undo steps, snap radius 8 px, dwell 1.0 s, 45° angle increment) are asserted against Preferences::default() in the same file, with a note that they are user preferences (PRJ-007).
- The imperial template loads with LengthUnit::FeetInches, formats the first-floor elevation as 10'-0", passes integrity_problems() and validates every tool-default slot.
- shipped_templates_are_current fails when template.rs changes without re-blessing; both files validate (validate::validate) and pass conformance/run.sh.
- New from either template has fresh UUIDs (identity test of task 01 applied to the shipped bytes).
- Satisfies PRJ-001 (a default template ships and supplies settings, storeys, layers, materials, layer structures, views and presets) and PRJ-012 (the imperial template ships).
notes:
SRS: PRJ-001 PRJ-012
Proposed imperial content (O-11, to confirm): ft-in to 1/16", ft² and ft³; storeys at 0 and 10'-0" with heights 10'-0"; cut plane 4'-0"; scale 1/8" = 1'-0" (1:96); wall 8" masonry; slab 8"; column 12" × 12"; beam 10" × 20" with top at home + 9'-2"; door 3'-0" × 7'-0"; window 4'-0" × 4'-6", sill 3'-0"; roof 35° (or 8:12 if commands-and-l10n slope formats offer rise per 12), 12" thick, eaves 1'-6"; stair width 3'-8" with the D.3 rules (no reviewed US preset); railing 3'-6"; grid 20'-0".

title: Edit terrain points, breaklines and boundary in 3D views
description:
WHY: TER-005 (M): terrain points, breaklines and the boundary shall be editable in plan and 3D: add, move and delete points and breaklines, with numeric elevation input. Task 08 covers plan views; this task covers 3D views. Status: TER-005 missing (gap row: no vertex or handle editing, the 3D view has picking at crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:75-99 but no point input). Provided upstream: GPU id-buffer part picking (selection-transforms-06) and edit mode (selection-transforms-08), WorkingPlane, Camera3dSurface and Overlay3d (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/surface3d.rs, 3d-input-navigation-07), point input and InputConsumers in 3D views (3d-input-navigation-08), the face PickIndex (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/pick.rs, 3d-input-navigation-06); from this epic the TerrainOp commands and TerrainPart addressing (task 03), the TIN elevation_at (task 04) and the palette entries of task 08.

WHAT: 3D edit mode for terrains in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs: point, breakline-node and boundary-node markers drawn through Overlay3d as screen-space glyphs at their world positions (home storey elevation added once, through the helper shared with task 04) and registered as part slots in the GPU id buffer, culled by frustum and screen density and hidden while orbiting. The palette of task 08 opens on a picked marker and its consumers run unchanged on the Camera3dSurface: Move on the working plane (Z kept, MovePoints), Move vertically with a typed delta (SetPoints), Set elevation (numeric), Delete. 'Add point' picks the terrain surface through the PickIndex (XY from the hit on a Body top face, default Z = hit Z, editable in the tracker's Z field) and commits AddPoints; 'Add breakline' draws a polyline on the surface whose node Z come from the hits and stay editable per node, committing one AddBreakline; 'Delete breakline' acts on a picked breakline; boundary nodes move in XY on the working plane through Command::Reshape MoveNode, and Insert node / Delete node act on picked boundary edges and nodes (edit-reshape-palette-03). Out of scope: the point table (task 18), contour picking (task 10), plan editing (task 08).
design: Reuse, do not duplicate: the palette entries and consumers of task 08 implement the InputConsumer contract and therefore run on the 3D surface unchanged (3d-input-navigation-08), so 3D adds only markers, surface-pick defaults and the vertical move. Pitfalls: markers live at absolute Z while bodies are storey-local, so add the home storey elevation in exactly one helper; a surface pick must hit the Body top faces and never the TopSurface part (Surface role, excluded from the PickIndex by task 05); thousands of markers need frustum and density culling or the 50 ms feedback budget breaks; consumers flagged needs_horizontal continue on the horizontal plane through their first point (3d-input-navigation-08). Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs, views/surface3d.rs, views/render3d.rs (id buffer), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/pick.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/{palette,reshape,terrain}.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/terrain.rs (task 03).
acceptance_criteria:
- Through a mocked Camera3dSurface: clicking the terrain surface at (5, 5) in 'Add point' mode adds a point with Z = elevation_at(5, 5); a typed vertical move of +0.30 on a selected point emits SetPoints with Z + 0.30; dragging a marker on the working plane emits MovePoints with delta.z = 0.
- 'Add breakline' with three surface picks emits one AddBreakline whose node Z equal the surface Z at the picks within 1e-9 m; typing 2.50 for the second node stores 2.50; Delete on a picked breakline emits DeleteBreaklines.
- A boundary node dragged in 3D emits Command::Reshape MoveNode with the same resulting terrain as the equivalent plan edit of task 08; Insert node on a picked boundary edge in 3D adds a boundary node.
- Markers are pickable through the id-buffer test harness of selection-transforms-06 with the part labels of task 03; with the home storey at +3.00 m the markers sit at the absolute input elevations.
- Undo restores the exact terrain after each 3D operation; invalid edits (duplicate XY with a different Z, crossing breaklines) show the validation message and change nothing.
- Kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): entering edit mode on a terrain in a 3D pane shows markers, and the palette for a point lists 'Move', 'Move vertically', 'Set elevation' and 'Delete'.
- TER-005 3D clauses satisfied: add, move and delete points and breaklines and edit the boundary in 3D, with numeric elevation input.
notes: SRS: TER-005

title: Write the SurveyPoint and +Y reference point nodes under the site
description:
WHY: IFX-070 (S): if a project location is defined (STR-012), the site node has a SurveyPoint child whose usd::xformop places it at the survey point; it carries the projected coordinates as epsg<code> (eastings, northings), the height as an EPSG-named height attribute and, with STR-015, epsg4326 (latitude, longitude), as in R2's PCERT and Georeferencing examples; a second reference point on the project +Y axis is written the same way so consumers can derive the orientation to true north (resolves O-8); the altitude of project zero (STR-011) is bsi::ifc::prop::RefElevation on the site node; the epsg schemas are declared in-file, latitude and longitude with quantityKind 'Plane angle', heights, eastings and northings with 'Length'. STR-012 (M) requires 'IFCX export writes it (IFX-070)', and NFR-ACC-004 (M) keeps survey coordinates in the survey point offset only. Status: IFX-070 partial: only RefElevation is written (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:276-279); survey point and true north live only in archicraft::project.location (writer.rs:166-170), so standard consumers cannot georeference the model.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/georef.rs producing, when Location::is_georeferenced() (task 01), two site children: SurveyPoint (path Uuid::new_v5(site, 'SurveyPoint')) at the project origin with usd::xformop::transform translating by (0, 0, 0), the epsg<code> attribute with eastings/northings = survey_point, the EPSG-named height = altitude, and epsg4326 latitude/longitude in degrees when both are set; and SurveyPoint_Y (path v5(site, 'SurveyPoint_Y')) at model (0, 100 m, 0) with eastings/northings = Location::model_to_survey((0, 100)) and the same height; both named with bsi::ifc::prop::Name ('Survey point', 'Survey point +Y'). writer.rs (extended; the RefElevation write at writer.rs:276-279 is kept and regressed) inserts them after the Building child (spatial-tree order, IFX-007). georef::declarations(code) adds the epsg<code> and epsg4326 schemas to the file's schemas section only when written, through the per-project declarations builder of element-kind-framework-06; crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs accepts object-valued in-file attributes with quantityKind 'Plane angle' if it does not yet; registry.rs gets a test that no bundled schema declares an epsg attribute. reader.rs skips SurveyPoint and SurveyPoint_Y silently (archicraft::project.location stays authoritative) and warns when they disagree with it by more than 1 mm (IFX-065 spirit). New catalogue sample georeferenced_shell (FixtureBuilder: two_storey_shell plus EPSG 2056, E 2,600,123.456, N 1,199,876.543, altitude 512.30 m, true north 3.20 degrees, latitude 46.948, longitude 7.447) with golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/georeferenced-shell.ifcx; conformance/check.ts asserts that SurveyPoint nodes are site children with a transform and that every epsg attribute has an in-file schema. Out of scope: reprojection and latitude/longitude of the +Y point (would need a CRS transform, O-2), third-party SurveyPoint import (ifcx-interop), sun position (3d-display-styles).
design: Copy the exact attribute spelling (an epsg<code> object with members versus flattened epsg<code>::eastings keys, and the name of the height attribute) from R2's Georeferencing and PCERT examples at the IFC5-development commit pinned in conformance/run.sh (1a63082...), keep it in constants in georef.rs with a comment naming the example path, and do not invent members. The survey point is the project origin, so its transform is the identity translation; a 100 m reference offset gives an orientation resolution of about 1e-8 rad after 1e-6 m rounding. Eastings and northings are parameters written with full round-trip precision (NFR-ACC-002), not rounded like mesh coordinates. Whether the nodes carry a bsi::ifc::class follows R2's example; if they carry none, check.ts must not require classes on site children that are neither spatial nor element nodes (coordinate with the site-level element counting added by element-kind-framework-07). Pitfalls: child keys SurveyPoint and SurveyPoint_Y must stay stable and never collide with <Kind>_<hex> keys (IFX-014); the reader must not treat these nodes as unknown elements or foreign content; the degree conversion happens only in the writer. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:243-280, schema.rs declarations, validate.rs, registry.rs:1-55, reader.rs site handling, conformance/check.ts:67-103, crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs catalogue.
acceptance_criteria:
- georeferenced_site_writes_survey_points (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs): the site node has children SurveyPoint and SurveyPoint_Y with v5 paths and usd::xformop::transform matrices (row-major, translation in the fourth row, IFX-031) translating by (0, 0, 0) and (0, 100, 0); SurveyPoint carries eastings 2600123.456, northings 1199876.543, height 512.30 and latitude/longitude in degrees; SurveyPoint_Y carries the E/N of Location::model_to_survey within 1e-6 m; atan2 of the E/N difference of the two points recovers true north within 1e-9 rad.
- The schemas section declares epsg2056 (eastings, northings, height with quantityKind Length) and epsg4326 (latitude, longitude with quantityKind 'Plane angle'); the offline validator reports no undeclared attribute; the registry test confirms the bundled schema files do not declare them.
- RefElevation on the site node still equals the altitude (STR-011 regression).
- A project without EPSG code writes no SurveyPoint and all existing golden files stay bit-identical; a project with a survey point but no EPSG code saves with one warning 'Set the EPSG code to write the survey point' instead of dropping it silently.
- Loading the georeferenced golden yields the identical project with zero problems; a hand-edited SurveyPoint 5 cm off yields one warning naming the node path.
- georeferenced-shell.ifcx is reproduced byte for byte from the catalogue sample and passes conformance/run.sh with the extended check.ts; saving twice gives identical bytes apart from header timestamp and dataVersion (IFX-007).
- Every mesh coordinate in that golden lies within +-100 m of the origin while the survey point has 7-digit eastings (NFR-ACC-004).
- IFX-070 satisfied; STR-012 export clause satisfied.
notes:
SRS: IFX-070 STR-012 NFR-ACC-004
Open questions: R2 shows no EPSG-named vertical datum attribute yet (epic risk); until it does, the height is written with the projected code. Latitude and longitude are written for the SurveyPoint only, because the +Y point would need reprojection (O-2).

title: Generate a provisional stepped stair body
description:
WHY: STA-001 (M): changing any input regenerates all steps without manual repair; NFR-REL-006 needs every element to have a body or a fallback; the epic design note asks for a provisional stepped extrusion along the baseline so the stair is visible in plan and 3D and can be exported before stair-body-plan builds flights, landings and finishes. STA-002's side and offset and STA-024's start and end conditions must show in the body. Gap: the only generator is a vertical extrusion of a 2D ring (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18), TriMesh offers only translated() (mesh.rs:97), and the geometry registry of element-kind-framework-15 has no stair entry.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair.rs: provisional_body(params: &StairParams, solution: &StairSolution, z0) -> Result<Vec<BodyPart>, GeometryError> with one closed prism per baseline segment whose vertical profile (walking-line arc length, z) is the step sawtooth of the risers on that segment over a smooth underside parallel to the pitch line at a provisional waist of 0.15 m (D.2: monolithic, smooth underside), falling back to a solid block down to z0 when the profile would self-intersect (N ≤ 2), extruded across the band from its right to its left edge; corners stay unresolved until stair-body-plan. mesh.rs: TriMesh::transformed(&DAffine3), flipping winding for negative determinants; extrude.rs: extrude_profile(profile, frame, w0, w1) on top of extrude() and transformed(). crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/stair.rs implements element-kind-framework-15's GeometryKind trait (local_extent and evaluate over EvalContext) and registers it in the one-line table of kinds/mod.rs, with the local extent base_offset .. base_offset + solution.total_rise and the walking line at z0 as the axis. Out of scope: treads, risers, finishes, structure, landings, winders and the plan symbol (stair-body-plan, railings-stairs-adv); IFCX (task 07).
design: Extruding a vertical profile horizontally reuses extrude()'s CDT capping (spade handles the concave sawtooth) and keeps every part one closed manifold that slicing, picking, the writer and check_closed already understand. Work per segment in the walking-line frame: u = segment tangent, w = left normal, up = Z, profile x = arc length within the segment, so risers stay perpendicular to the walking line (STA-010). Underside: z = (s − s_first) × R/G − waist / cos(pitch), clipped at z0; check the profile with validate_ring and fall back to the block. Riser positions come from the model's riser_lines (task 12), never recomputed here. Pitfalls: transformed() must flip winding for left-handed frames or the outward test fails; keep vertices per planar face (IFX-038) as extrude does; the writer does not check MAX_MESH_POINTS (technical debt), so build one prism per segment, not one per step; this body is replaced wholesale by stair-body-plan, so add no options to it.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair.rs: the 5.400 m, 19-riser, G 0.300, width 1.00 straight stair yields one closed (check_closed), outward-oriented part with bounds 5.400 × 1.000 × 3.000 m in storey coordinates, a volume equal to profile area × width within 1e-9, and up-facing tread faces at heights k × R.
- Left, Centre and Right with offset 0.100 shift the bounds as expected (STA-002); start with tread adds a floor-level going and end with tread a top tread (STA-024).
- An L-shaped two-segment stair yields two closed parts whose riser counts add up to N; 1- and 2-riser stairs use the block fallback and stay closed.
- STA-001 regeneration: after an UpdateElements changing any one input (a baseline node, width, side, offset, bottom or top offset, top link, riser spec, rules or start/end condition) or a storey edit (task 05), evaluate_incremental re-evaluates the stair and the body matches the new solution (step count and bounds); a stale stair (task 05) keeps the body of its stored solution. Landings and supports are not generated here (stair-body-plan-04/05 regenerate them; the done task records that part of STA-001 as open).
- plan_drawing of the home storey cuts the body at 1.10 m (generic slicing) and lists the stair as a cut element; picking in plan and view3d::pick return the stair id.
- The module-layout test (extended to archicraft-geometry by element-kind-framework-15) shows the stair only in stair.rs, kinds/stair.rs and one kinds/mod.rs line.
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green; existing geometry tests unchanged.
notes: SRS: STA-001 STA-002 STA-024. The 0.15 m waist is provisional, not a D.2 value; stair-body-plan takes structure thicknesses from STA-041.

title: Save projects as user templates and offer them at New
description:
WHY: PRJ-002 (S): users shall be able to save a project as their own template and choose it when creating a project. Gap row PRJ-002 missing: no 'Save as template', no template store under DataDirs, no user templates at New. Tasks 01 and 06 provide the file mechanism and the New dialog.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/mod.rs: DataDirs::templates() (root/templates). New persistence/templates.rs: list_user_templates(dir) -> Vec<UserTemplate { path, info, modified }> (reads the archicraft::template marker; broken files are listed as broken), save_user_template(dir, project, info, include_elements) with a sanitised file name through save_atomically (0 backups), rename and delete. Action::SaveAsTemplate in the File menu: dialog with name, description and 'Include model elements' (off); the unit system is derived from the project's length unit. The New dialog of task 06 lists 'My templates' below the built-in ones, with a context menu Rename, Delete and 'Edit template', which opens the file with load() (identities kept); Document gains `template: Option<TemplateInfo>` so saving an edited template writes the marker again. Out of scope: template sharing, template thumbnails.
design: The template store is a plain folder of .ifcx files, so users can copy templates between machines and back them up. Listing parses each file once and caches by modification time; the dialog never blocks on a large folder. Pitfalls: Save as template must not touch Document.path, the recent list or the autosave session; the template is written through to_template(include_elements) so selection sets and groups do not leak into templates without elements.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in persistence/templates.rs: save then list returns the info; a corrupt file is listed as broken without panicking; names containing path separators or reserved characters are sanitised; rename and delete work.
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/start_screen.rs: in a project with a custom layer and a preset, File > 'Save as template…' named 'Office' adds 'Office' to the New dialog; New from it gives the layer and the preset with new UUIDs and no elements; the current document's path and dirty state are unchanged by the save.
- Edit template → change a layer → Save keeps the archicraft::template marker (round trip).
- Satisfies PRJ-002.
notes: SRS: PRJ-002

title: Verify exit criterion: Templates, start screen, presets, parameter transfer, groups, selection criteria and resource folders
description:
WHY: The epic owns PRJ-001, PRJ-002, PRJ-006, PRJ-009, PRJ-012, PRJ-013, ELM-002, ELM-003, ELM-015, SEL-005, SEL-006, SEL-009, SEL-010, UI-016 and STA-052 and is a prerequisite of release-candidate. This task verifies the merged state against the epic acceptance as a whole, not against the individual tasks.

WHAT: Run the workspace quality gates and the conformance job, walk the epic acceptance item by item and name the test that proves each, then map every owned requirement ID to its tasks and tests, including the clauses the epic acceptance does not name (PRJ-013 sample, SEL-005 region and stretch, SEL-009 sets, SEL-010 select similar, ELM-015 suspend, ELM-003 in section views, UI-016 profiles), fix or file beads for anything missing (for example an outstanding O-4 reviewer record), update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID and the increment-3 readiness line, then close the epic in beads. No new features. Do not commit or push beyond what the active profile allows; report the commands.
design: Checklist: fresh UUIDs and template_contents (every D.1/D.2 value) -> crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/templates.rs; imperial feet-inches -> templates.rs imperial test and the New → Imperial kittest; start screen with searchable recent list and sample -> crates/archicraft-app/tests/start_screen.rs; second instance warns and opens read-only -> persistence/lock.rs unit tests, tests/project_lock.rs (child process) and its kittest; preset saved from a tool and applied to a selection -> tests/presets.rs; DIN and OENORM presets -> stair/presets.rs tests, the doc-sync test and the verification record in docs/stair-rule-presets.md; pick-up and inject between walls -> transfer.rs unit tests and tests/transfer.rs; criteria set survives save/load -> roundtrip.rs and tests/criteria.rs; group moves as one and ungroups -> tests/groups.rs; material moved into a folder keeps references -> the DSP-003 command test and tests/folder_tree.rs; beyond the epic acceptance: select similar -> tests/select_similar.rs; selection sets -> tests/selection_sets.rs; region and stretch -> tests/region.rs and the Stretch tests in tests/commands.rs; transfer in sections -> the section cases in tests/transfer.rs. Status rows use the gap-analysis vocabulary (done/partial/missing, remaining_effort, depends_on) and name the owning epic for every clause left open.
acceptance_criteria:
- New from the default template gives layer structures, presets and views with fresh UUIDs (identity test) and a template_contents test loads the shipped .ifcx template and asserts every D.1/D.2 value; the imperial template opens in feet-inches; start-screen kittest with a searchable recent list and the sample project; a second instance on the same file warns and opens read-only (lock-file test); a preset is saved from a tool and applied to a selection; the DIN and OENORM stair presets load with values documented against the standards (O-4); pick-up and inject between walls transfer only compatible settings; a criteria set survives save/load; a group moves as one and ungroups; moving a material into a folder keeps all references (DSP-003).
- Every owned requirement ID has at least one named passing test per clause, including select similar (tests/select_similar.rs), selection sets (tests/selection_sets.rs), the region and stretch (tests/region.rs and the Stretch command tests), group suspend (tests/groups.rs), parameter transfer in a section view (tests/transfer.rs) and the sample project (tests/start_screen.rs).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx and on crates/archicraft-ifcx/templates/*.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (PRJ-001, PRJ-002, PRJ-006, PRJ-009, PRJ-012, PRJ-013, ELM-002, ELM-003, ELM-015, SEL-005, SEL-006, SEL-009, SEL-010, UI-016, STA-052) with status, file:line evidence and remaining gaps, and the architecture summary and extension points mention templates, presets, resource folders and the add-a-resource rule for reidentify_all.
- The epic is closed in beads.
notes:
SRS: PRJ-001 PRJ-002 PRJ-006 PRJ-009 PRJ-012 PRJ-013 ELM-002 ELM-003 ELM-015 SEL-005 SEL-006 SEL-009 SEL-010 UI-016 STA-052
Clauses that may stay open with a follow-up bead: STA-052 until the O-4 reviewer record exists; Profile folders if profiles-columns-beams has no Profile resource. ELM-003 in section views is task 21, which waits for sections-elevations-dims-07.

title: Build the F9 sloping-site fixture with storeys -3..+1, georeferenced
description:
WHY: Appendix D.7 F9 is a two-storey family house on a sloping site with storeys -3, -2, -1, 0 and +1, stepped footings, a single-slope roof and a flat terrace with falls, the source of RM-S's site, footing and terrace details. The epic acceptance requires F9's sloping site built as the RM-S base; reference-models registers it and adds the roof. It is also the integrated check of TER-001, TER-002 and TER-004 (terrain from typed spot elevations and from picked 2D contour polylines, the AS-01 path), TER-006 (basement slabs cutting the terrain), STR-012 and IFX-070 (SurveyPoint export) and NFR-ACC-004 (7-digit eastings with model coordinates near the origin).

WHAT: samples::f9_site(&mut FixtureBuilder) (storeys, location and terrain; the public step function reference-models-01 and -03 reuse) and samples::f9_sloping_site() (f9_site plus footings, base slabs and terrace) through the FixtureBuilder of element-kind-framework-03 (seeded v5 ids) and in the catalogue: storeys -3 (-8.40), -2 (-5.60), -1 (-2.80), 0 (+-0.00) and +1 (+2.80), each 2.80 m high; a 40 x 30 m terrain falling from +1.00 m in the north to -9.00 m in the south, built from 36 typed spot elevations (AddElements with new_terrain) and 4 contours drawn as DraftPolylines and picked with Command::AddContours (task 10), all through commands; a house footprint stepping down the slope with exterior walls per storey, base slabs (predefined type BASESLAB) on storeys -3 to -1 each subtracting the terrain with +Z extrusion, strip footings as slabs with class IfcFooting and STRIP_FOOTING under the stepped walls, and a flat terrace slab with falls (sloped slab of layer-structures-07) on storey 0; project location EPSG 2056, E 2,600,512.345, N 1,199,321.678, altitude 548.20 m, true north 4.00 degrees, latitude 46.95, longitude 7.44. Golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/f9-sloping-site.ifcx reproduced by the catalogue test, plus a fixture test of the F9 properties. Out of scope: the single-slope roof and the RM-S house content (reference-models, roofs), the D.7 registry entry (reference-models).
design: Build everything through commands in the FixtureBuilder so the fixture doubles as an integration test of the command layer, as RM-S will. Storey elevations are chosen so each basement storey cuts the terrain on its uphill side only (stepped section). Pitfalls: golden churn when terrain code changes later, so re-bless only with a reviewed diff (ARCHICRAFT_BLESS); keep the element count around 40 so the golden stays reviewable; the footing class needs IfcFooting and the predefined types of element-kind-framework-05. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs FixtureBuilder and catalogue, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs, conformance/check.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- f9_sloping_site test: five storeys -3..+1 at the given elevations; every terrain tile is closed; each basement slab removes the soil above it (terrain volume equals the analytic expectation within 0.1 %); moving the base slab of storey -1 by 0.10 m moves its pit (SOL-022 regression).
- NFR-ACC-004: every element coordinate and every written mesh point lies within +-100 m of the origin while the SurveyPoint carries 7-digit eastings; the file has SurveyPoint and SurveyPoint_Y children with epsg2056 and epsg4326 declared in-file (IFX-070).
- f9-sloping-site.ifcx is reproduced byte for byte, passes conformance/run.sh (IfcGeographicElement under IfcSite with Body or Body_n and TopSurface, IfcFooting and IfcSlab elements on the storeys) and round-trips with unchanged UUIDs.
- The F9 terrain is created only from typed spot elevations and from 2D polylines picked with AddContours, through commands, never by constructing the struct directly (AS-01 terrain path); f9_site is public and reusable by reference-models.
- TER-001, TER-002, TER-004, TER-006, STR-012, IFX-070 and NFR-ACC-004 re-asserted on an integrated model.
notes:
SRS: TER-001 TER-002 TER-004 TER-006 STR-012 IFX-070 NFR-ACC-004
Storey elevations and site geometry are proposals derived from KB 364093; Appendix D.7 gives only the storey list and the element types.

title: Verify exit criterion: Terrain, site-level elements and georeferencing
description:
WHY: The epic delivers terrain as a closed solid with a TIN top from typed points and contours, edited in plan and 3D, cut associatively, drawn with labelled contours, smooth or faceted, thinned on demand, written as IfcGeographicElement under the site with TopSurface parts and within the 50,000-point budget, plus georeferencing written as SurveyPoint nodes without large survey coordinates in the model: TER-001, TER-002, TER-004, TER-005, TER-006, TER-007, TER-008, TER-010, TER-012, TER-013, TER-014, STR-012, STR-015, IFX-070 and NFR-ACC-004. reference-models, 3d-display-styles, members-profiles-adv and could-scope-polish build on it, so the exit has to be verified as a whole before the epic closes.

WHAT: Run the epic acceptance end to end on the merged state: the unit, integration, golden, conformance and kittest suites added by tasks 01-18, the 50,000-point benchmark and the F9 fixture; update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence with file paths, remaining gaps); close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new functionality; any defect found becomes a bead blocking this task.
design: Verification only. Walk the epic acceptance clause by clause and point each clause at the test or record that proves it (test names of tasks 01-18, docs/performance/ record of task 16). Golden diffs since the last blessed state are reviewed before closing. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/terrain.rs, crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs, conformance/run.sh, docs/implementation-status.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- AS-01 terrain from typed spot elevations is a closed manifold body.
- Picking 2D contour polylines into a selected terrain assigns one elevation per contour, and picking without a selection creates nothing.
- A basement slab subtracted with upward extrusion removes the soil above it and follows when the slab moves (SOL-021 relation).
- Contour lines regenerate on edit with every n-th labelled and can be frozen to 2D lines.
- 50,000 points with 200 breaklines build in under 5 s in a benchmark and tile into closed Body_n parts of at most 65,535 points.
- IfcGeographicElement as a child of IfcSite with Body and TopSurface passes conformance.
- A project with 7-digit eastings keeps model coordinates near the origin and writes a SurveyPoint child with epsg<code> eastings/northings, the height attribute, epsg4326 latitude/longitude and the second +Y reference point, schemas declared in file.
- F9's sloping site with storeys -3..+1 is built as the RM-S base.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on every golden file, including georeferenced-shell.ifcx, terrain-site.ifcx and f9-sloping-site.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for TER-001, TER-002, TER-004, TER-005, TER-006, TER-007, TER-008, TER-010, TER-012, TER-013, TER-014, STR-012, STR-015, IFX-070 and NFR-ACC-004.
- The epic terrain-and-site is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: TER-001 TER-002 TER-004 TER-005 TER-006 TER-007 TER-008 TER-010 TER-012 TER-013 TER-014 STR-012 STR-015 IFX-070 NFR-ACC-004

title: Ship DIN 18065 and OENORM B 5371 stair rule presets as data
description:
WHY: STA-052 (S): stair rule presets for DIN 18065 and ÖNORM B 5371 / OIB-RL 4 shall ship, with values verified against the standards (O-4). O-4: the international default of Appendix D.3 ships; national presets replace that table; rules drive the solver and a fixed going yields warnings (STA-008). PRJ-007 stores stair rule defaults in the project. Gap row STA-052 missing (no preset resource, no DIN or OENORM values). stair-solver-tool delivers RuleSet/RuleKind/Rule with RuleSet::international() (crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/rules.rs), rules on every stair and in the stair defaults slot, the archicraft::stairRules codec and the rules grid in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs, and explicitly leaves rule presets as resources to this epic.

WHAT: Data files crates/archicraft-model/data/stair-rules/{international,din-18065,oenorm-b-5371}.json embedded with include_str! and parsed by serde in crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/presets.rs (serde_json moves from [dev-dependencies] to [dependencies] in crates/archicraft-model/Cargo.toml; it is already a workspace crate, so no new dependency) into `StairRulePreset { id, code, name, standard, edition, scope, rules: RuleSet, sources: Vec<RuleSource { rule: RuleKind, clause, note }> }`, one preset per regulated building scope (for example DIN 18065 'buildings with at most two dwellings' and 'other buildings'; OIB-RL 4 'main stairs' and 'stairs within dwellings'); `built_in_rule_presets()`. Project.stair_rule_presets holds the presets (copied in by the template so the file is self-contained, PRJ-007); `Command::ApplyStairRules { preset, target: StairRuleTarget { Elements(Vec<ElementId>), Defaults } }` replaces the rule set through UpdateElements or SetToolDefaults so the stair solver re-runs and a conflict surfaces through the STA-011 path (RuleConflict, keep last valid). IFCX: `stairRulePresets` array in archicraft::project reusing the archicraft::stairRules shape of stair-solver-tool-07 plus code, name, standard, edition and scope. UI: a 'Rule preset' combo at the top of the Rules section in ui/stair.rs that loads a preset into the draft and shows 'Custom' when the rules match none. Documentation: docs/stair-rule-presets.md with one table per preset (rule, enabled, min, max, clause, edition) and a verification record (editions consulted, reviewer, date). Out of scope: further national presets, headroom and railing rules (not part of RuleSet), inferring the building scope.
design: Presets are data, not code (epic goal), so a corrected value is a reviewed data change next to its documentation; the doc-sync test makes the documentation the contract. Resource ids are re-randomised on template instantiation like every other resource (IFX-011 treatment in task 01); `code` identifies the built-in source across projects and releases. Values are stored in SI (metres, radians) like RuleSet; the JSON holds millimetres and degrees for reviewability and converts on load (documented in the file header). Rows a standard does not regulate are disabled and documented as 'not regulated' rather than guessed. Pitfalls: never compare floats with ==; keep the international preset identical to RuleSet::international() (test) so D.3 has one source; a preset loaded into the dialog must not commit until OK/Apply (stair-solver-tool-10 commit semantics).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in stair/presets.rs: every built-in preset parses, passes RuleSet::validate and has a RuleSource with clause and edition for each enabled rule.
- A doc-sync test parses the tables in docs/stair-rule-presets.md and compares them with the data files, so documented and shipped values cannot drift.
- Solver tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs: for a total rise of 3.000 m each national preset yields the admissible riser-count set recorded in the doc during verification.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: ApplyStairRules on a stair and on the stair defaults slot executes, undoes and redoes; a preset that makes an existing stair infeasible returns the rule conflict naming the rules and keeps the last valid stair.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: stairRulePresets round-trip; reidentify_all covers them.
- kittest: choosing a DIN 18065 preset in the stair settings Rules section updates the grid and the live R/G/2R+G read-out; editing one bound shows 'Custom'.
- O-4 gate: docs/stair-rule-presets.md names the standard editions consulted and the reviewer who checked every value against the standard text; the task is not closed before that record exists.
- Satisfies STA-052.
notes:
SRS: STA-052
Candidate values from secondary sources, all to be verified against the standard text before release (O-4): DIN 18065:2020-08 Table 1, buildings with at most two dwellings and stairs within dwellings: riser 140-200 mm, going 230-370 mm; other buildings: riser 140-190 mm, going 260-370 mm; step formula 2R+G 590-650 mm. OIB-RL 4 (2023) Table 1 with ÖNORM B 5371: maximum riser and minimum going, for example 180/270 mm for main stairs and 200/240 mm within dwellings, plus the ÖNORM step-formula range. Walking-line distance and landing length per standard: verify or disable.

title: Evaluate selection criteria and store named criteria sets
description:
WHY: SEL-006 (S): criteria-based selection shall combine element kind with parameters (at least storey, layer, material, layer structure, dimensions, name/ID and IFC class) using the operators equals, not equals, contains and does not contain; results can be added to or removed from the selection, criteria values can be filled from a picked element, and named criteria sets are saved in the project. Gap row SEL-006 missing, depending on the IFC class list (element-kind-framework-05), layer structures and IFCX persistence. This task builds the headless half; the dialog is task 14.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/criteria.rs: the data types `CriterionField { Storey, Layer, Material, LayerStructure, Preset, Name (Element.name, the name/ID of ELM-004, crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:277), IfcClass, Dimension(DimensionKey { Thickness, Height, Length, Width, Area, Volume, Elevation }), Field(key) }` (Field reaches any FieldSpec key of the task-02 vocabulary), `Operator { Equals, NotEquals, Contains, DoesNotContain }`, `Criterion { field, op, value: CriterionValue { Text, Number, Ref(Uuid), Code } }`, `CriteriaSet { id, name, kinds: Vec<KindTag> (empty = all kinds), criteria: Vec<Criterion> }` combined with AND; evaluation lives in new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/criteria.rs: `evaluate(project, geometry: &ModelGeometry, set) -> Vec<ElementId>` and `criterion_from_element(field, element, project, geometry)` for fill-from-picked, because Length, Area and Volume come from ElementGeometry.quantities (archicraft-geometry quantities.rs of properties-and-dialogs-08) and archicraft-model must not depend on archicraft-geometry (crates/archicraft-model/Cargo.toml); Thickness, Height and Elevation are read through the model FieldSpec getters (fields.rs of properties-and-dialogs-05). Semantics: references compare by id for equals/not equals and by display name, case-insensitively, for contains; text by case-insensitive substring; numbers equal within MODEL_TOLERANCE, contains on the value formatted in project units. Project.criteria_sets with AddCriteriaSet, UpdateCriteriaSet and DeleteCriteriaSet; DeleteLayer/DeleteMaterial/DeleteLayerStructure replacements rewrite criterion references; reidentify_all remaps; templates keep criteria sets. IFCX: `criteriaSets` in archicraft::project with enumerations from the ALL arrays; unknown field or operator codes drop that criterion with a warning. Out of scope: the dialog (task 14), OR groups.
design: A headless evaluator (data in the model, evaluation in the geometry crate that owns the quantities) keeps the semantics testable without UI and lets other features (select all limits, future schedules) reuse it. One quantities function shared with the properties derived values avoids a second definition of length, area or volume. References by id survive renames (DSP-003). AND-only criteria keep the model simple; OR is achieved by running a second set in 'add to selection' mode (document). Pitfalls: 'contains' on numbers is ambiguous, so define and document it as a substring of the formatted value; evaluation must ignore elements on hidden layers only in the UI (task 14), not in the evaluator.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table-driven unit tests in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/criteria.rs on a fixture with walls and slabs on two storeys: kind Wall AND layer equals 'Exterior walls' AND thickness equals 0.25; material contains 'concrete' matches 'Reinforced concrete'; IFC class not equals IfcWall; name does not contain 'W-00'; storey equals the first floor; layer structure equals a named structure; every operator is exercised for a reference, a text and a numeric field.
- Numeric equals honours the tolerance (0.2500004 equals 0.25) and contains on numbers uses the formatted value.
- criterion_from_element fills storey, layer, material, layer structure, name, IFC class and dimensions from a wall.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: criteria-set commands undo and redo; DeleteMaterial with a replacement rewrites criterion references.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: a criteria set survives save and load (epic acceptance); an unknown operator code drops the criterion with a warning.
- Satisfies the model clauses of SEL-006 (fields, operators, kind combination, named sets saved in the project).
notes: SRS: SEL-006

title: Add element groups with nesting, ungroup and IFCX persistence
description:
WHY: ELM-015 (S): elements shall be groupable; clicking one member selects the group; groups can be nested, ungrouped and temporarily suspended. Gap row ELM-015 missing: no group relation, no group selection semantics, no nesting, ungroup or suspend, no persistence. The epic design models groups as resources and relations. This task is the model and file half; selection semantics and suspend are task 16.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/group.rs: GroupId (id_type!), `Group { id, name, parent: Option<GroupId> }`, Project.groups; the Element envelope gains `group: Option<GroupId>` (innermost group). Queries Project::outermost_group(element), group_members(group) (recursive) and group_path(element). Commands: `Group { elements }` creates a group; selected elements that already belong to groups are grouped through their outermost groups, which become children (nesting); `Ungroup { group }` removes one level (direct child groups become children of the old parent, direct members get the old parent); deleting elements removes groups left empty (undoable); Project::duplicate (selection-transforms-03) and the clipboard paste remap groups so a copy of a whole group forms a new group and a partial copy is ungrouped; reidentify_all remaps groups; to_template(false) of task 01 clears groups and its unit test covers them. IFCX: `groups` in archicraft::project ([{id, name, parent}]) and an optional `group` reference on archicraft::element; the reader repairs parent cycles and dangling parents with warnings (PRJ-008). Out of scope: selection semantics, suspend and UI (task 16).
design: Membership on the element plus parent links on groups keeps nesting a tree by construction and answers 'which group?' in O(depth); a relation-store variant (element-kind-framework-08) would need ends that are not elements. Group names 'Group n' from a per-project counter. Grouping is not an edit of geometry or parameters, so locked elements may be grouped (ELM-013 lists move, delete, resize and parameter changes). Hosted elements (doors, windows) follow their host through ELM-016 regardless of grouping. Pitfalls: Project PartialEq includes group order; keep the archicraft::element attribute optional so existing goldens stay unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: Group and Ungroup undo and redo exactly; grouping (A, B) then (that group, C) and ungrouping the outer group restores the inner group (A, B) unchanged.
- Duplicating all members of a group yields a new group with a new id containing only the copies; duplicating one member yields an ungrouped copy.
- Deleting all members removes the group and undo restores both the elements and the group.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: nested groups and memberships round-trip; a parent cycle in the file is broken with a warning.
- The reidentify_all test covers groups.
- Satisfies the grouping, nesting and ungroup clauses of ELM-015 at model level.
notes:
SRS: ELM-015
IFCX alpha has no standard group assignment in the bundled schemas; groups stay in the archicraft:: namespace until IFCX defines one (IFX-090 adapter).

title: Register the Stair kind with solve-on-commit and rule conflicts
description:
WHY: STA-001 (M): the system provides a parametric stair defined by a plan baseline (at least two nodes), a width, a home storey, a top storey link, a bottom offset, a top offset and a rule set, and changing any input regenerates it without manual repair. STA-002 (M) adds the side and offset of the body. STA-011 (M): a rule-violating stair is never output silently and the last valid stair is kept meanwhile. ELM-006 (M) makes the top a storey link as for walls; PRJ-007 stores stair rule defaults in the project; Appendix D.2 gives width 1.00 m and rule set D.3 as tool defaults; the template layer 'Stairs and railings' exists (template.rs:260-268, LAY-004). Gap: no stair exists, ElementKind and ToolKind are wall/slab only (element.rs:191-204, tools.rs:13-20). After element-kind-framework, a kind is one module behind the KindDescriptor registry (kinds/mod.rs) with the shared VerticalLink and a defaults slot; the existing storey-link resolution (Project::top_elevation, crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:236; StoreyList::relative_elevation, storey.rs:108) is reused through VerticalLink, not re-implemented.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/stair.rs: Stair { params: StairParams, link: VerticalLink (base_offset = bottom offset, top link carrying the top offset), material: MaterialId, solution: StairSolution } implementing the Kind trait: DESCRIPTOR { label 'Stair', code 'stair', name_prefix 'ST', default_class IfcClass::Stair and ifc_classes &[IfcClass::Stair] (the variant comes with element-kind-framework-05's D.5 class list), has_tool: true }; material/set_material; validate (structural only: at least two distinct nodes, finite coordinates inside the model limits, no zero-length segment, width > 0, RuleSet::validate, Count ≥ 1, positive target and fixed going, FromInner inside the width); a new Kind hook resolve(&mut self, home, &StoreyList) -> Result<bool, Box<RuleConflict>> with a default Ok(false) for other kinds, where the stair computes total_rise (task 02) from the elevations its VerticalLink resolves and runs solve() (task 03), storing the adjusted baseline and the solution only on success; transform (translate and rotate the baseline; mirror swaps Left and Right and negates a Centre offset); vertical_extent from the stored solution; storey_links, rehome, relink and unlink_storey through VerticalLink; plan_bounds from the band polygon; parts() empty. One registry line in kinds/mod.rs. command.rs calls resolve right after validate_element (validate.rs:243, whose plain String error cannot carry the conflict) in plan_add_elements (command.rs:320), plan_update_elements (:371), rehome (:399) and relink_to_storey (:419), and gains CommandError::RuleConflict(Box<RuleConflict>) whose message names the rules, and ChangeOffset alternatives are mapped to base_offset or the top offset. The descriptor's template_defaults fn (element-kind-framework-04) builds the stair DefaultsSlot that template.rs fills in registry order (D.2/D.3: width 1.00, Centre, offset 0, RuleSet::international(), TargetHeight(0.175), Free going, HalfWidth, riser/riser, top 'home + 1' with offset 0, Reinforced concrete, layer 'Stairs and railings'); Project::new_stair(storey, baseline, nth) wraps the generic factory. Out of scope: re-solving on storey edits and the stale status (task 05), geometry (task 06), IFCX (task 07), UI (tasks 08-11).
design: Embed the solver's StairParams unchanged so the tool, properties and codec share one parameter type; the element adds only the storey link, the material and the stored solution. The stored solution is the last valid one: resolve writes only on success, so a stair in the model is always consistent with the rise it was last solved for (task 05 builds keep-last-valid on this).
