Direct edits that conflict are rejected atomically through the new structured CommandError variant (the dialog of task 11 needs rules and alternatives, not a string); box it to keep CommandError small. Defaults: Centre puts the drawn baseline on the default half-width walking line, so the drawn length is the run; TargetHeight(0.175) is the middle of the D.3 riser range (template choice under O-4). The defaults-slot prototype keeps the placeholder geometry of element-kind-framework-04 and is never solved. Until tasks 06 and 07 land, the geometry and IFCX registries treat the stair as an unsupported kind (problem entry, writer warning), which is the framework's documented behaviour. Pitfalls: CommandError derives PartialEq and Eq (command.rs:93) while RuleConflict carries f64 values, so derive PartialEq on RuleConflict and implement Eq by hand (solve rejects non-finite input, so no NaN reaches a conflict) or drop Eq from CommandError if nothing needs it; resolve must be idempotent (task 03 property test) or every UpdateElements would report a change; vertical_extent uses the stored solution, never a fresh solve, so a stale stair keeps its body; keep ElementKind serde names stable. Pointers: kinds/wall.rs for the VerticalLink hooks, validate.rs validate_element, command.rs CommandError (command.rs:95-108) and plan_add_elements.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements of new_stair on the template's ground floor with Count(19), Fixed(0.300) and a 5 m baseline names it ST-001, stores N 19, R 0.157894…, total rise 3.000 and moves the last node to 5.400 m; undo and redo restore the exact project.
- STA-001 'changing any input': an UpdateElements changing, one at a time, a baseline node, the width, the side or offset, the bottom offset, the top offset, the top storey link, the riser spec, the going spec, the walking-line spec, the start or end condition and the rule set re-solves within the same command and stores the new solution (no manual repair); moving the stair to another home storey (rehome) re-solves too; an UpdateElements that changes only the material leaves baseline and solution bit-identical.
- A conflicting AddElements or UpdateElements (the task 03 case) returns CommandError::RuleConflict naming 'Going G' and 'Step formula 2R+G' and leaves the project bit-identical (keep-last-valid for direct edits, STA-011).
- Structural validation: a one-node baseline, a zero-length segment, width 0 and min > max rules are CommandError::Invalid with the stair's name.
- The framework's registry tests cover the stair (unique code and prefix, default class in its set) and the test iterating every kind through transform and undo includes it; mirroring swaps Left and Right; the module-layout test shows the stair only in kinds/stair.rs, stair/ and one kinds/mod.rs line of archicraft-model.
- template_contents asserts the stair slot values above; check_tool_defaults validates the slot structurally without solving its placeholder baseline.
- If crates/archicraft-model/tests/defaults.rs (regression-and-status-03) is present, its D.2 stair row is a check for width 1.00 m and rule set D.3 against the stair slot; the structure and finish parts of that row stay Pending with owner stair-body-plan.
- ELM-006/STR-006: relink_to_storey keeps the absolute bottom; DeleteStorey of the top storey turns the top into a fixed height equal to the current rise.
- The landings and supports named in STA-001 do not exist yet; stair-body-plan regenerates them (STA-020..023, STA-041/042) and the done task records that part of STA-001 as open.
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green; all existing golden files byte-identical.
notes: SRS: STA-001 STA-002 STA-011. Template choices to confirm: side Centre, riser target 0.175 m, start and end with riser.

title: Tile large terrains into closed Body_n parts plus a TopSurface part
description:
WHY: IFX-038 (M): no single mesh has more than 65,535 points; larger bodies such as terrain are split into closed sub-solids, for terrain tiles of the TIN each extruded down to the terrain bottom, each written as its own Body_<n> child with IFX-032 applying to each. TER-012 (M): terrain is written with a closed body mesh (Table 5-1, IFX-038). TER-014 (S): the top surface is additionally a separate, non-volumetric TopSurface part so consumers can recover the TIN. TER-013 (M): a 50,000-point terrain must stay within that budget. Status: IFX-038 partial: MAX_MESH_POINTS is only checked (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:47-49 and 126-128), never split; TER-014 missing: every BodyPart is a closed material body (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs BodyPart, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:365-379) and check_closed rejects open meshes. solid-kernel-ops-03 already splits any oversized part by kernel.split at the median of its longest axis (normalize_parts, kept for Boolean results); the TIN tiling is terrain-specific and belongs here, because IFX-038 asks for TIN tiles extruded to the bottom and tiles must stay stable under local edits. host-openings-03 gives BodyPart a role: PartRole::{Body, Skin, Void} and ElementGeometry::visible_parts().

WHAT: Tiling in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/terrain.rs: estimate the emitted points (top vertices, skirt face points, bottom ring); above the budget (60,000, headroom below 65,535 for later cuts) split the boundary bounding box as a quadtree of axis-aligned cells anchored at the box origin until every cell fits; clip TIN triangles to each cell (a convex polygon in the triangle's plane, fan-triangulated) and the boundary polygon to the cell with geo; build per tile a closed sub-solid from the clipped top, vertical faces along cell lines and boundary edges inside the cell, and the flat bottom of the tile footprint (each multi-polygon component closed). Parts are named Body for one tile and Body_1..Body_n otherwise, in row-major cell order. PartRole gains Surface for non-volumetric parts (no second flag on BodyPart); TopSurface (TopSurface_1..m on the same cells when the TIN exceeds the budget) is the uncut TIN with shared vertices, oriented upward, role Surface. mesh.rs adds check_open_surface() (2-manifold with boundary, consistent upward orientation, no degenerate or duplicate triangles, point limit). ElementGeometry::visible_parts() skips Surface like Void, so volume(), bounds(), plan classification and picking, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs build_scene, view3d.rs pick and PickIndex::build ignore TopSurface (no z-fighting in 3D, no double lines in plan); normalize_parts and the strict pre-write check in writer.rs write_element (both solid-kernel-ops-03) check Surface parts with check_open_surface and never split them, because IFX-032 applies to volumetric parts only. samples::synthetic_terrain(points, breaklines, seed) (deterministic splitmix64 and an analytic surface; 400 x 400 m boundary; non-crossing breaklines on the surface) serves these tests and the later benches; a test-only TileBudget parameter forces small tiles. Out of scope: writing the parts (task 06), the vertex-sharing switch (task 14), Booleans on tiles (task 11).
design: Clipping to straight cell lines instead of assigning whole triangles to tiles avoids pinch vertices (a tile touching itself at one vertex would make its side faces non-manifold) and keeps the visible surface identical, because clipped pieces stay in their triangle's plane. Cells are anchored at the boundary box and subdivided deterministically, so a local edit changes only the tiles it touches, which the per-tile Boolean cache of task 11 relies on. Clip points on a cell edge are computed once per cell edge so neighbouring tiles share bitwise-equal coordinates (contour stitching in task 12 depends on it). If a tile still fails check_closed (a sliver where the boundary grazes a cell corner), shift the grid origin by a deterministic fraction of a cell and retry once, otherwise report a GeometryError (NFR-REL-005). Pitfalls: TriMesh.indices are u32 while the viewer limit is 16-bit (technical debt), so assert per part before returning; the estimate must count the points of the active vertex-sharing mode (faceted triples the top points, task 14). Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:47-175, evaluate.rs BodyPart, PartRole, visible_parts and normalize_parts, slice.rs, plan.rs pick, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-176, crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- terrain_tiles_are_closed (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/terrain.rs): with a forced budget of 2,000 points, a 10,000-point synthetic terrain yields Body_1..Body_n (n >= 4), each passing check_closed with at most the budget; with the real budget a 50,000-point terrain with 200 breaklines yields parts of at most 65,535 points.
- The sum of tile volumes equals the untiled body volume within 1e-9 relative; the tile top areas sum to the TIN plan area within 1e-9 relative; tile top triangles lie in the planes of their source TIN triangles within 1e-9 m.
- TopSurface passes check_open_surface, has exactly the TIN vertices and triangles with shared vertices, and its plan area equals the boundary area.
- A terrain under the budget yields exactly one Body and one TopSurface without suffix.
- Tiling is deterministic: two evaluations produce bit-identical parts.
- ElementGeometry::volume ignores TopSurface; build_scene emits no triangles for Surface parts; plan slicing never classifies TopSurface; normalize_parts and the writer's strict check accept a valid TopSurface and still reject an open Body; existing wall, slab and opening (Void) tests unchanged.
- IFX-038 terrain clause and the geometry side of TER-014 satisfied; the closed-body precondition of TER-012 holds for any terrain size.
notes:
SRS: TER-012 TER-014 TER-013
The 60,000-point tile budget is a proposal that leaves headroom under the 65,535 limit for Boolean cuts (task 11).

title: Edit terrain points, breaklines and boundary in plan edit mode
description:
WHY: TER-005 (M): terrain points, breaklines and the boundary are editable in plan and 3D: add, move and delete points and breaklines, with numeric elevation input. EDT-008 opens a contextual palette on nodes and edges, SEL-008 gives an edit mode for parts. Status: TER-005 missing (no vertex or handle editing existed at increment 0). edit-reshape-palette provides handles (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/handles.rs), the palette (tools/palette.rs) and Command::Reshape on Outline; selection-transforms provides EditMode and PartRef; task 03 provides the TerrainOp commands and TerrainPart addressing.

WHAT: Plan edit mode for a selected terrain: handles for points (with elevation labels), breakline nodes and boundary nodes and edges, drawn and hit-tested by the handle infrastructure through the kind's part hooks. Clicking a point or breakline node opens the palette with Move (drag or typed delta through PointInput, keeping Z), Set elevation (numeric field applied to all selected points, or to the whole breakline for contours) and Delete; 'Add point' places a point inside the boundary with a typed Z; 'Add breakline' draws a polyline whose node Z default to the TIN elevation_at of task 04 and stay editable per node. Boundary node and edge operations go to Command::Reshape through the terrain outline hook (move, insert, delete node, offset edge). Shift adds parts to the selection and area selection selects points inside a rectangle. Every action is one EditTerrain or Reshape command, with a throttled live TIN preview while dragging. Out of scope: 3D editing (task 09), the point table (task 18), contour picking (task 10).
design: No terrain-specific handle system: TerrainPart registers part_anchor and part_outline so tools/handles.rs and the palette render and hit-test it, and the palette gains entries per PartRef variant. Elevation edits are separate from XY moves so a drag never changes Z by accident; a vertical move of selected points uses the vertical-move transform of selection-transforms with numeric input. Pitfalls: thousands of handles: draw point handles only above a zoom density threshold and hit-test through the rstar index of the point-input service; default Z for a new breakline node comes from the TIN evaluated without that breakline. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/{handles,palette,reshape}.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/selection.rs, kinds/terrain.rs (task 03), views/plan.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless tool tests: dragging point 4 by (1, 2) emits EditTerrain MovePoints { ids: [4], delta: (1, 2, 0) }; Set elevation 3.25 on three selected points emits SetPoints with Z 3.25 for each; Delete on a selected breakline emits DeleteBreaklines; 'Insert node' on a boundary edge emits Command::Reshape with PartTarget { part: PartRef::Edge { ring: 0, index } } and ReshapeOp::InsertNode and changes the boundary.
- Undo restores the exact terrain after each operation; invalid edits (moving a point onto another point's XY with a different Z, a breakline crossing another) are refused with the validation message in the status line and no change.
- Area selection in edit mode selects exactly the points inside the rectangle; part labels match task 03.
- Kittest: entering edit mode on a terrain shows point handles, and the palette for a point lists 'Move', 'Set elevation' and 'Delete'.
- The live TIN preview while dragging a point of a 5,000-point terrain stays within the 200 ms single-edit budget (timing test in the style of NFR-PERF-006).
- TER-005 plan clauses satisfied (add, move and delete points and breaklines, boundary editing, numeric elevation); the 3D clauses follow in task 09 and table entry in task 18.
notes: SRS: TER-005

title: Add the terrain tool: boundary, spot elevations and terrain settings
description:
WHY: TER-002 (M): terrain is creatable by drawing a boundary and adding points with elevations. TER-005 (M): numeric elevation input. AS-01 builds its terrain from typed spot elevations. INP-015 and the shared PointInput service make one tool usable in plan and 3D, and the epic risk asks that terrain edges are excluded from snap targets by default (INP-017). Status: TER-002 missing: at increment 0 ToolKind has no terrain (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13-17, moved to crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/ by point-input-snapping-01) and the toolbox lists only select, wall and slab (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:138-142).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/terrain.rs, a headless state machine on PointInput with steps Boundary (polygon or rectangle through the slab tool's polygon input) -> Points (each click or typed X/Y places a spot whose elevation comes from the tracker's Z field, typed relative to project zero or, with the elevation-reference toggle, relative to sea level and converted through Location's altitude of task 01, STR-011 single datum; default Z is the last typed elevation) -> Finish (Enter or double click) committing one AddElements(new_terrain(...)) undo step; Esc cancels a step, Backspace removes the last point. In 3D views the same steps run through the Camera3d ViewSurface of 3d-input-navigation: the boundary on the working plane, spot points on any picked face or on the working plane at the typed elevation. Preview: boundary rubber band and point markers with elevation labels. Toolbox button, Design menu entry and an action with a free shortcut (actions.rs uniqueness test). Terrain sections in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs and the settings dialog (bottom mode Depth or Elevation and its value, material, layer), through the FieldSpecs of properties-and-dialogs-05 and the settings dialog of properties-and-dialogs-09 where they have landed (that epic is not a dependency of this one; otherwise through the existing Fields getters). TerrainSnapSource in crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs: boundary nodes and edges and terrain points (with Z) as targets; triangulation edges only when display.tin_snaps is set (default off): the SnapSource for PlanElement skips the TIN-edge line class of task 04, and in 3D the mesh snap of 3d-input-navigation-10 skips edges of terrain top faces (vertices stay); element and layer snap_excluded honoured (point-input-snapping-12). Out of scope: contour picking (task 10), point editing (tasks 08 and 09), contour display settings (task 13), the smooth toggle (task 14).
design: Reuse the slab polygon input for the boundary (same snapping and contour detection of edit-reshape-palette-12), so a boundary can be traced from 2D lines. The elevation-reference toggle lives in the tool session and defaults to project zero; sea-level display uses the reference levels of properties-and-dialogs where present (STR-007), otherwise the altitude offset directly. The tool emits one command at Finish rather than one per point, so undo removes the whole new terrain. Pitfalls: the Z field of PointInput is secondary in plan views, so make it primary in the Points step; typed X/Y follow the relative/absolute conventions of point-input-snapping-05; preview labels use the project length format. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/ (slab tool), input/ (PointInput, targets.rs), ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs, ui/properties.rs, views/view3d.rs and views/surface3d.rs (3d-input-navigation-07).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool state-machine tests without egui: a 30 x 20 m rectangle boundary followed by five typed points with elevations 1.20, 1.45, 0.90, 2.10 and 1.75 creates one terrain with exactly those points in one undo step; Esc during Points keeps the boundary; Backspace removes the last point; an elevation typed as 513.50 m above sea level with an altitude of 512.30 m stores 1.20 m.
- 3D: the same sequence through a mocked Camera3d ViewSurface (working plane at 0.00) yields an identical terrain; a point picked on an existing slab face takes the face Z as default elevation.
- Snap tests: terrain points and boundary nodes are node targets; the TIN edges drawn in plan and the top-face edges in 3D give no target unless tin_snaps is set; a snap_excluded terrain provides none.
- Bottom: switching the bottom to Elevation -6.00 in the properties panel emits one EditTerrain SetBottom and the evaluated body's lowest Z is -6.00; switching back to Depth 5.00 restores it (TER-001 user-defined elevation or thickness).
- Kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): the Terrain toolbox button activates the tool, the prompt reads 'Draw the terrain boundary', and after a typed sequence the properties panel shows the terrain with the bottom depth 5.000.
- Input feedback stays under 50 ms with a 5,000-point terrain in the scene (frame-time assertion of point-input-snapping-15).
- TER-001 bottom choice, TER-002 boundary-and-points clause satisfied; TER-005 numeric elevation input at creation satisfied; the AS-01 terrain path is usable interactively.
notes: SRS: TER-002 TER-005

title: Switch terrain 3D display between smooth and faceted
description:
WHY: TER-008 (S): terrain display in 3D is selectable as smooth or faceted. IFX-038 shares vertices only across smooth edges and notes that the reference viewer averages normals over shared vertices, so the written mesh must match the displayed shading. Status: TER-008 missing; the renderer computes one flat normal per triangle (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:152-158) and draws feature edges above 1 degree (mesh.rs feature_edges at line 239), which would outline every TIN edge.

WHAT: Geometry: the terrain generator honours display.smooth: smooth shares vertices between the TIN triangles of a tile, faceted gives every TIN triangle its own vertices, and the tile point estimate of task 05 counts the tripled top points. mesh.rs gains TriMesh::vertex_normals() (area-weighted averages). render3d.rs build_scene uses per-vertex normals averaged over the triangles that share a vertex index inside a part (the reference viewer's rule, IFX-038; walls and slabs, whose faces never share vertices, render unchanged), and TriMesh::feature_edges skips edges whose two triangles share both vertex indices (smooth edges by the IFX-038 convention), so smooth terrains lose the TIN creases while skirt and bottom edges stay, and faceted terrains show every TIN edge above 1 degree. free-form-solids plans the same per-vertex rule; whichever epic lands second keeps and regresses the first one's code instead of adding a parallel path, and no smooth flag is added to BodyPart. App: a 'Smooth surface' checkbox in the terrain 3D section of the properties panel (UpdateElements). Writer: unchanged code path; the meshes carry the sharing as generated, and terrain-site.ifcx is re-blessed. Out of scope: global display styles (3d-display-styles), subdivision smoothing.
design: The setting is element data (archicraft::terrain.display since task 06), not view state, so writing smooth or faceted meshes respects IFX-068. Normals are averaged per mesh as in the reference viewer, so terrains above the tile budget keep a faint shading seam on cell lines in both viewers; this is accepted and documented, not worked around. Pitfalls: the scene must rebuild when the setting changes (it does through the project revision in SceneKey); faceted meshes triple top points and therefore tiles, so the estimate must use the mode. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-176, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:239, terrain.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: the same terrain evaluates to a top with V shared vertices when smooth and 3T own vertices when faceted, both closed; in faceted mode the 50,000-point synthetic terrain still tiles into parts of at most 65,535 points.
- render3d unit test: a smooth terrain part gets per-vertex normals (adjacent triangles share the normal at a common vertex index), a faceted one per-triangle normals, and a wall's normals are unchanged; a smooth terrain emits no feature edges on interior TIN edges, a faceted one emits every TIN edge with a dihedral above 1 degree.
- Writer test: a smooth terrain's Body top shares vertices across TIN edges and a faceted one does not (IFX-038 sharing rule); conformance stays green after re-blessing terrain-site.ifcx with a reviewed diff limited to terrain meshes.
- Kittest: toggling 'Smooth surface' changes display.smooth and creates one undo step.
- TER-008 satisfied.
notes:
SRS: TER-008
Default smooth is a proposal; Appendix D has no value.

title: Templates, start screen, presets, parameter transfer, groups, selection criteria and resource folders
description:
Templates as data (default metric and imperial, save-as-template, choice at New with fresh UUIDs), a start screen with recent projects, thumbnails and the sample project, in-use detection with read-only open, presets per tool with management, stair rule presets DIN 18065 and OENORM B 5371 as data, parameter pick-up and inject, select-similar, criteria selection, persistent selection regions, named selection sets, groups and nested resource folders by drag and drop. PRJ-001 stays in increment 3 because its remaining gap (template as a selectable artefact) only matters once layer structures and presets exist to be carried; multi-window and cross-project paste are library-dw-exchange.

Risks: The 'no project open' state touches app.rs flow: covered by kittest flows for New/Open/Recover. Template files as data can drift from code defaults: the template_contents test pins them.
design: Templates as .ifcx files under DataDirs with an archicraft::template marker and load_as_template id remapping (IFX-011); a Preset resource per kind in archicraft::project; per-project lock file separate from the autosave session lock; start screen as the 'no project open' app state; resource folders as path metadata on resources; selection sets and groups as resources and relations.
acceptance_criteria: New from the default template gives layer structures, presets and views with fresh UUIDs (identity test) and a template_contents test loads the shipped .ifcx template and asserts every D.1/D.2 value; the imperial template opens in feet-inches; start-screen kittest with a searchable recent list and the sample project; a second instance on the same file warns and opens read-only (lock-file test); a preset is saved from a tool and applied to a selection; the DIN and OENORM stair presets load with values documented against the standards (O-4); pick-up and inject between walls transfer only compatible settings; a criteria set survives save/load; a group moves as one and ungroups; moving a material into a folder keeps all references (DSP-003).
notes: SRS: PRJ-001 PRJ-002 PRJ-006 PRJ-009 PRJ-012 PRJ-013 ELM-002 ELM-003 ELM-015 SEL-005 SEL-006 SEL-009 SEL-010 UI-016 STA-052

title: Solve stairs along the walking line with conflicts and alternatives
description:
WHY: STA-011 (M): if no stair satisfies the enabled rules and the drawn geometry, the system shall not output a rule-violating stair silently; it names the conflicting rules, offers alternatives (change N, relax a bound, unlock the baseline, change an offset) and keeps the last valid stair meanwhile. STA-010 (M): the walking-line distance from the inner edge is checked against the rule minimum (D.3: 300 mm). STA-004 and STA-008 apply to the whole stair (N from the spec, a fixed going used exactly with its violations listed) and STA-024's start and end conditions decide the run length. The gap analysis lists STA-011 as missing with L effort (no detection, naming, alternatives or keep-last-valid; ElementGeometry has no warnings, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:31-35) and STA-010 as missing. Doing the whole-stair solve as pure functions over the solver of task 02 and the walking line of task 12, before the element exists, keeps STA-001's extra-large scope split.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/: mod.rs gains StairParams { baseline: Vec<DVec2>, width, side: BaselineSide, offset, riser: RiserSpec, going: GoingSpec { Free, Fixed(f64) }, walking_line: WalkingLineSpec, start: StairEnd, end: StairEnd, rules: RuleSet } (BaselineSide and WalkingLineSpec from task 12, RiserSpec and StairEnd from task 02) and StairSolution { riser_count, riser_height, going, goings, total_rise, run_length }. solve.rs: solve(params, total_rise) -> Result<Solved { solution, baseline (adjusted), warnings: Vec<Violation> }, RuleConflict>: task 12's walking line gives the drawn length and the inner-edge distance, which is checked against the WalkingLineDistance rule; N from choose_riser_count (task 02); the going is Fixed(g) exactly or, when free, the drawn walking-line length divided by the goings and clamped into going_range; the run length goings × G is reached by moving the last baseline node along its segment (the unlocked-baseline behaviour); warnings are the violations caused by values the user fixed (a fixed going, a FromInner distance). conflict.rs: RuleConflict { rules: Vec<(Limit, actual)>, cause: Rules | WalkingLine | DrawnGeometry, alternatives: Vec<Alternative> } with Alternative { ChangeRiserCount(u32), RelaxRule { rule, bound, value }, ChangeOffset { which: Bottom | Top, delta }, AdjustRun { length }, SetWalkingLine(f64), Widen(f64) }, each offered only when re-solving the modified parameters succeeds. 'Unlock the baseline' has no variant yet: the baseline is always unlocked here, AdjustRun covers drawn-geometry conflicts meanwhile, and Alternative::UnlockBaseline arrives with the lock option in stair-body-plan-14 (STA-029). Out of scope: band and walking-line geometry (task 12), storey links and the stored last-valid solution (tasks 04 and 05), the lock-baseline option, landings and turning types (STA-029, STA-020..023 in stair-body-plan), geometry (task 06).
design: One pure solve over (StairParams, total_rise) serves the element hook, the tool preview and the properties panel (ELM-017 live values), so what is shown is what is stored. Candidate order: TargetHeight walks choose_riser_count's list and takes the first N with a non-empty going range whose run fits the drawn geometry; Count(n) tries only n, and a non-admissible n is a Rules conflict naming the riser rule or the binding going rules. Naming: report going_range's binding lower and upper limits of the requested candidate (for TargetHeight the candidate nearest the target), so the message matches what the user asked for. Alternatives: ChangeRiserCount scans admissible N (nearest three); RelaxRule moves the binding bound to the opposing limit rounded outward (1 mm, 0.1°, 0.01); ChangeOffset searches the smallest rise change δ through riser_range_for_going and the riser bounds (the element layer maps it to the bottom or top offset); AdjustRun only for DrawnGeometry conflicts (the last segment would shrink below one going) and is what stair-body-plan reuses for 'unlock the baseline' once the lock option exists. Task 12's PlanError (one node, zero-length or reversing segments, turns of 170° or more) becomes a DrawnGeometry conflict without alternatives. Pitfalls: idempotence — skip moving the last node when |L − run| < MODEL_TOLERANCE and compute the new node from the segment start, never by incremental shifts; no ids, storeys or elements in this module.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs gains:
  - The read-out example: a straight centred baseline, 3.000 m, Count(19), Fixed(0.300) solves to N 19, R 157.89 mm, G 0.300, 18 goings, run 5.400 m and no warnings.
  - TargetHeight(0.150) with a free going and a 5.700 m baseline gives N 20 and G 0.300; the same parameters at 3.300 m give N 22, R 0.150, G 0.300, run 6.300 m and the last node moved by +0.600 m.
  - sta_011_conflict_names_rules: R 0.170 (3.400 m, Count(20)) with Going min 0.350 and StepFormula max 0.600 returns a RuleConflict with cause Rules naming exactly Going Min 0.350 and StepFormula Max 0.600; the alternatives contain RelaxRule { Going, Min, 0.260 } and RelaxRule { StepFormula, Max, 0.690 } and no ChangeRiserCount or ChangeOffset (none can solve).
  - sta_011_change_count_and_offset: Count(21) at 3.000 m (R 142.86 mm, below the 150 mm minimum) returns a Rules conflict naming RiserHeight Min 0.150 with actual 0.142857…; its alternatives contain ChangeRiserCount(20) first, ChangeOffset { Bottom, −0.150 } and ChangeOffset { Top, +0.150 } (rise 3.150 m, R 0.150) and RelaxRule { RiserHeight, Min, 0.142 }, and each of them re-solves.
  - sta_011_drawn_geometry: Count(20) with a free going on a centred L-shaped baseline whose first segment (8.000 m) is longer than the longest admissible run at 3.000 m (19 × 0.350 = 6.650 m) returns a DrawnGeometry conflict naming Going Max 0.350 and offering an AdjustRun that re-solves.
  - sta_010_walking_line_rule: width 1.00 with HalfWidth (0.500 m from the inner edge) solves without warning; FromInner(0.250) solves with one warning { WalkingLineDistance, Min, 0.300, actual 0.250 }; width 0.50 with HalfWidth returns a WalkingLine conflict offering SetWalkingLine(0.300), RelaxRule { WalkingLineDistance, Min, 0.250 } and Widen(0.600); an L-shaped baseline (5 m, then 3 m turning left, Centre, FromInner(0.300)) uses task 12's mitred inner walking line of 7.600 m as the drawn length.
  - STA-008 at stair level: Fixed(0.250) at R 0.150 is used exactly with the warning StepFormula Min 0.600 / actual 0.550.
  - STA-024: the four start/end combinations give run lengths 5.400, 5.700, 5.700 and 6.000 m for N 19 and G 0.300, and task 12's riser_lines for the solution place the first riser at s = 0 (start riser) or s = G (start tread).
- Seeded property tests: every Ok result satisfies all enabled rules except the listed warnings; solving the adjusted baseline again is bit-identical (idempotence); every alternative of every conflict re-solves; degenerate baselines (task 12 PlanError: one node, zero-length or reversing segments) return DrawnGeometry conflicts and never panic.
- STA-011 coverage: change N, relax a bound and change an offset are offered and verified; 'unlock the baseline' is deferred with STA-029 to stair-body-plan-14 and recorded as open by the done task.
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green.
notes: SRS: STA-004 STA-008 STA-010 STA-011 STA-024. Policy (O-4 resolution 'rules drive the solver; a fixed going yields warnings'): the solver's free choices must satisfy every enabled rule or produce a conflict; values the user fixes (a fixed going, an explicit walking-line distance) are used exactly and their violations are listed as warnings. The baseline behaves as unlocked here; STA-029's lock option and Alternative::UnlockBaseline arrive with stair-body-plan-14. The band and walking-line geometry was split out into task 12 during review.

title: Add the stair tool with baseline input and live riser count
description:
WHY: STA-002 (M): input is possible upward (first click at the bottom) or downward, the body lies left of, centred on or right of the baseline with an offset, and during input the preview shows the live riser count. STA-009 (M): while placing, the system displays R, G, 2R + G, N and the pitch, for example '19 R × 157.9 mm, 2R+G = 616 mm'. STA-010: the walking line is part of the preview. UND-003: Backspace removes the last stair-baseline point without cancelling the input. Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for the stair tool. Gap: no stair tool, the tracker shows distance and angle only (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:429-448 today, input/tracker.rs after point-input-snapping-05) and previews are 2D outlines (views/tools.rs:547-580). point-input-snapping provides the PointInput service, the InputConsumer step/preview API and the tools/ module this tool plugs into.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/stair.rs: StairTool implementing InputConsumer with a polyline baseline (two or more points; Enter, double-click or the context menu's Finish commits; Backspace and Esc remove the last point), modes Upward/Downward and the side Left/Centre/Right (cycled by a key like the wall's reference-line key, shown in the properties tool_modes); downward input reverses the points before building the element, swaps Left and Right and negates a Centre offset (task 12's reversed()), and homes the stair on the storey below with top 'home + 1' (refused with a message on the lowest storey). preview() builds a candidate from the tool defaults (Project::new_stair) and runs solve() on every move: the band outline, the riser lines up to the cursor with a 'k/N risers' label at the cursor, the dashed walking line and a read-out. The consumer API's Preview gains readout: Vec<ReadoutLine { text, severity }> and labels: Vec<(DVec2, String)> with defaults, so wall and slab stay untouched; views/plan.rs draws them under the tracker and mirrors the read-out headline into the status-bar prompt (ui/shell.rs). crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs: readout(solution, warnings, going range, units, nf) producing the headline '19 R × 157.9 mm, 2R+G = 616 mm', a second line with G, the permitted going range and the pitch, and one line per warning or conflicting rule. Commit executes Command::AddElements; a RuleConflict keeps the points and shows its message in the status line until task 11. ToolKind::Stair in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/mod.rs, Action::ToolStair in ui/actions.rs with a free single-key shortcut, toolbox button and Design menu entry (ui/shell.rs), properties gather mapping to KindTag::Stair and select_all mapping (workspace.rs). Out of scope: 3D preview (task 09), properties fields (task 10), the conflict dialog (task 11), the plan symbol (stair-body-plan).
design: The tool owns no solver logic: it builds the candidate element and calls the model's solve(), so the preview shows exactly what the command will store (STA-009). The cursor sets the drawn length; with a free going the solver clamps L/T into the going range, so outside the range the preview run stops short of or passes the cursor and the 'k/N' label counts risers up to the cursor, which is the live riser count of STA-002. Format R with one decimal and 2R+G with none in millimetres for metric projects and in inches for imperial ones (units.rs format_length), the pitch in the project angle unit with two decimals (D.1). Pitfalls: solve() runs per pointer move and must stay well inside point-input-snapping's 50 ms feedback budget (it is O(N)); swap the side when reversing for downward input; a downward stair is homed one storey down, so the status message names that storey; keep strings in the string table if commands-and-l10n has landed. Ordering: the tool lands after the IFCX codec (task 07), so no interim build lets a user place a stair that saving would drop.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless tests in tools/stair.rs with the template, Count(19) and Fixed(0.300): clicking (0, 0) and moving to (5.4, 0) gives a read-out headline exactly '19 R × 157.9 mm, 2R+G = 616 mm' and a second line containing 'G 300 mm' and '27.76°'; at (2.7, 0) the label reads '10/19 risers'; committing emits one AddElements with that stair.
- Upward and downward input of the same two points on the first floor store the same bottom-to-top baseline; downward input on the ground floor is refused with a message; a Left side drawn downward is stored as Right.
- Backspace removes the last point without leaving the tool (UND-003); a typed distance of 5.400 m from the point-input service places the end exactly.
- A conflicting candidate shows the read-out with error severity naming the rules, and its commit leaves the project unchanged.
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the Stair toolbox button and its shortcut select ToolKind::Stair and the properties strip shows the stair defaults; two clicks in the plan view show the read-out headline in the status bar.
- appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs lists Action::ToolStair and shortcuts_are_unique passes; cargo test/clippy/fmt green.
notes: SRS: STA-002 STA-009 STA-010. The concrete shortcut key is a UI design deliverable (D.8); pick a free one and record it in the shortcut test.

title: Add parameter pick-up and inject with a latch mode
description:
WHY: ELM-003 (S): pick up an element's settings into the active tool's defaults and inject them into other elements, in plan, section and 3D views; a latch mode keeps pick-up or inject active without holding keys; between different kinds only compatible settings transfer. EDT-020 requires every modifier-gesture operation, parameter pick-up and inject included, to exist as an explicit command with a preview. Gap row ELM-003 missing; picking exists in plan (selection-transforms-05) and 3D (id-buffer picking of selection-transforms-06, replacing views/view3d.rs:75-100), and the commands are task 02.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/transfer.rs, an egui-free state machine unit-tested like views/tools.rs: TransferMode { PickUp, Inject } with latched. Gestures (through the commands-and-l10n keymap): holding Alt shows the pick-up cursor and a click runs PickUpSettings into the active tool's kind (with the selection tool: into the clicked element's kind, which also activates that tool); holding Alt+Cmd/Ctrl shows the inject cursor and a click runs InjectSettings from the active tool's defaults into the clicked element, or into the whole selection when the clicked element is selected. Explicit actions 'Pick up parameters' and 'Inject parameters' (Edit menu and command palette) latch the mode until Esc or a second invocation. Hover preview: the candidate is highlighted and a tooltip lists what would transfer and what would be skipped with reasons (TransferReport on a clone). Wired into views/plan.rs and views/view3d.rs through one pane-agnostic pick handler; section and elevation panes are wired to the same handler in task 21 once sections-elevations-dims-07 provides element picking there. Status line: 'Picked up 7 settings from W-003', 'Injected 4 of 9 settings into SL-002 (IFC class not allowed, …)'. Out of scope: presets UI (task 10).
design: Modifiers follow the reference product (Alt pick-up, Alt+Cmd inject) but live in the keymap so they are remappable and checked against D.8 and OS reservations; on Linux window managers may grab Alt-click, so the latch actions are the dependable path (document). The transfer state sits beside ToolState so a creation tool keeps its pending input. Check the modifier table of point-input-snapping for collisions before binding Alt. Cursor feedback uses egui CursorIcon plus a small glyph near the pointer (no custom cursors). Pitfalls: injecting into a locked element reports the lock reason; inject onto the selection uses editable_subset.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of the state machine: Alt → PickUp, Alt+Cmd → Inject, releasing modifiers returns to the tool; a latched mode survives clicks and modifier changes until Esc.
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/transfer.rs: with the Wall tool, Alt-click on a 0.365 m wall sets the wall defaults to 0.365 m and that wall's layer; Alt+Cmd-click on another wall injects them; injecting wall defaults into a slab transfers thickness, material and layer only and the status line names the skipped IFC class (epic: pick-up and inject between walls transfer only compatible settings).
- The same pick-up works from a 3D view through the pane-agnostic handler (kittest on the CPU pick path or a unit test of the handler).
- Latch mode started from the Edit menu works without modifiers and ends with Esc; the hover tooltip lists transferred and skipped settings before the click.
- Satisfies ELM-003 in plan and 3D views (pick-up into the active tool's defaults, inject, latch mode, compatible-only transfer between kinds) and the pick-up/inject part of EDT-020; the section and elevation clause is task 21.
notes: SRS: ELM-003

title: Add the criteria selection dialog with fill from element
description:
WHY: SEL-006 (S), UI clauses: results can be added to or removed from the selection, criteria values can be filled from a picked element, and named criteria sets are saved in the project (model in task 13). The epic acceptance requires that a criteria set survives save and load in the application.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/criteria.rs: a 'Find and select' window (Edit menu and command palette): kind multi-select, criteria rows (field combo; operator combo filtered by field type; value editor as a searchable combo for storeys, layers, materials, layer structures, presets and IFC classes, a unit-aware length widget for dimensions, text otherwise), add and remove rows, a live match count ('12 elements match') from archicraft_geometry::criteria::evaluate on the document's ModelGeometry, buttons 'Select', 'Add to selection' and 'Remove from selection'. 'Fill from element' arms a pipette; the next click in a plan or 3D pane (pane-agnostic pick handler of task 11) fills the row values through criterion_from_element. A saved-sets list with search: 'Save as…', overwrite, rename, delete. Results are filtered by Workspace::is_selectable (SEL-007), span all storeys and honour ws.selection_region when one exists (SEL-005). Out of scope: OR groups, criteria in schedules.
design: The dialog edits a draft CriteriaSet; saving issues AddCriteriaSet or UpdateCriteriaSet, so undo covers set changes. Re-evaluate when the draft or the project revision changes, not every frame. Pitfalls: the window is non-modal, so the pipette must cancel with Esc and must not conflict with the active tool; group expansion (task 16) applies to the results.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/criteria.rs: kind Wall plus Material equals Brick → 'Add to selection' adds exactly the brick walls; 'Remove from selection' removes them; 'Select' replaces the selection.
- Fill from element: arm the pipette, click a wall in the plan → the Layer row takes that wall's layer.
- Save as 'Brick walls', save the project, reopen it → the set is listed and reproduces the same result (epic: a criteria set survives save/load).
- Elements on hidden layers are never selected; typing in a value field does not trigger single-key tool shortcuts (UI-008).
- Satisfies SEL-006.
notes: SRS: SEL-006

title: Re-solve storey-linked stairs and report stale stairs
description:
WHY: STA-003 (M): the total rise is re-evaluated whenever a linked storey changes. STA-011 (M): when no stair satisfies the rules after such a change, the last valid stair is kept and the conflicting rules are named, never silently. STR-006 and ELM-006 (M): linked elements follow storey changes. The epic acceptance requires that changing the storey height from 3.000 to 3.300 re-solves to 22 risers through the storey link. Gap: re-evaluation of a stored link would come for free (document.rs:98-99), but the riser count, going and run of a stair are solved values, so a storey edit has to re-solve them inside the same undoable command; element-kind-framework-09 already collects the storey dependents in validate_storey_change.

WHAT: command.rs: after validate_storey_change accepts a new StoreyList (SetStoreyElevation, SetStoreyHeight in both shift modes, InsertStorey, DeleteStorey with relinks and rehoming), call Kind::resolve with the proposed list for every storey dependent from the relation store; Ok(true) adds a ReplaceElement edit to the same command, a conflict adds nothing. New crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/status.rs: stair_status(project, element) -> StairStatus { Valid, Warnings(Vec<Violation>), Stale { conflict: RuleConflict, solved_rise, current_rise } }, computed purely from the element, its link and the current storeys, and Project::stair_problems() listing every stale stair and every stair with warnings (fixed values of STA-008 and STA-010) for the problems panel. Out of scope: showing problems and the dialog (task 11); geometry (task 06 renders the stored solution, which is the kept stair).
design: Re-solving inside the storey command keeps the model consistent and undoable as one step, and storey_dependents (element-kind-framework-08) already yields the candidates, so no stair-specific query is needed. Keep-last-valid falls out of the stored solution: a failed re-solve produces no edit, and stair_status compares the stored rise with the current one. Unlike framework-09's inverted-extent rule, a stair conflict never rejects the storey edit: the user changes the building and the stair reports. Pitfalls: run validate_storey_change first so inverted extents still reject; resolve against the proposed list, not the current project; stair_status will be called by the panel, so the app caches it per project revision (task 11); a top link that becomes fixed after a storey deletion keeps the rise exactly.
acceptance_criteria:
- sta_003_storey_link in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: a stair with TargetHeight(0.150), a free going and a 5.700 m baseline on the template storeys has N 20; SetStoreyHeight of the ground floor to 3.300 with shift-above yields N 22, R 0.150, G 0.300 and run 6.300 m in one undo step; undo restores N 20 and the original baseline exactly.
- STA-003 values through real storeys: storeys at 0 and 3.000 m with both offsets 0.100 m store a total rise of 3.000 m; storeys at 0 and 3.400 m with bottom offset 0.100 m and top offset 0 store 3.300 m.
- A storey change that makes a Count(20) stair unsolvable (rules of the conflict case) succeeds, leaves the stair bit-identical, and stair_status returns Stale naming the rules with solved_rise ≠ current_rise; stair_problems() lists it; changing the storey back makes it Valid without any stair edit.
- InsertStorey re-targets a 'home + 1' stair and re-solves it; DeleteStorey of its top storey keeps the current rise as a fixed height.
- element-kind-framework-10's incremental-versus-full property test still passes with stairs in the random edit sequences.
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green.
notes: SRS: STA-003 STA-011.

title: Show rule conflicts with alternatives and keep the last valid stair
description:
WHY: STA-011 (M): if no stair satisfies the enabled rules and the drawn geometry, the system shall not output a rule-violating stair silently; it names the conflicting rules, offers alternatives (change N, relax a bound, unlock the baseline, change an offset) and keeps the last valid stair meanwhile. Violations of user-fixed values under STA-008 and STA-010 must be visible, not silent. UI-012 lists such problems in the problems panel, and the epic acceptance asks for a conflict-dialog kittest with min G 350 and max 2R+G 600 at R 170. Gap: no conflict UI exists, and ModelGeometry records only a failure string (evaluate.rs:57, 78-85).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs: a 'Stair rule conflict' modal driven by Dialogs.stair_conflict: Option<PendingConflict { origin: Add | Update | Stale, element (the last valid stair, if any), candidate, conflict }>; it lists each conflicting rule with bound, limit and actual value, then the alternatives with their effect ('Relax Going G minimum to 260 mm', 'Use 18 risers', 'Change the bottom offset to −0.050 m', 'Adjust the run to 6.000 m', 'Set the walking line to 0.300 m'), the families that cannot help as disabled entries with a reason ('No riser count satisfies the rules'), and 'Keep last valid stair'. An alternative re-executes the originating command with the modified candidate (AddElements or UpdateElements, one undo step). Workspace::execute routes CommandError::RuleConflict from the tool, the properties and the rules grid into this dialog. The problems panel's ProblemSource enum (element-kind-framework-14) gains a Stair source fed by Project::stair_problems(), cached per revision: stale stairs as warnings ('ST-001: no longer fits its storeys — …; last valid stair kept') whose click selects, zooms (element-kind-framework-14) and opens the dialog with origin Stale, and fixed-value violations as warnings. 'Unlock the baseline' has no entry yet: the baseline is always unlocked until stair-body-plan-14 adds Alternative::UnlockBaseline and its label. Out of scope: the lock-baseline option (stair-body-plan), presets (templates-presets).
design: The dialog is a pure view over the model's RuleConflict: the model has already computed and verified every alternative (task 03), the app only labels them and wraps the modified candidate in the originating command, so the behaviour is testable headless and the dialog never invents a fix. Keep-last-valid is the default because nothing was applied: Add and Update conflicts were rejected atomically (task 04) and stale stairs keep their stored solution (task 05). ChangeOffset maps onto the base offset or the top offset named by the alternative, AdjustRun onto the last baseline node. Pitfalls: the modal can open mid-input, so 'Keep' must not reset the tool state; compute problems per revision, not per frame; handle egui::Modal::should_close as the existing confirmations in dialogs.rs do; use the string table if commands-and-l10n has landed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Conflict kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: a stair with R 170 mm (3.400 m, 20 risers); in the rules grid set Going minimum 350 mm and step-formula maximum 600 mm and press OK; the dialog shows 'Going G' and 'Step formula 2R+G' with 350 mm and 600 mm, offers 'Relax Going G minimum to 260 mm' and 'Relax Step formula 2R+G maximum to 690 mm', and shows the change-N and change-offset entries disabled; 'Keep last valid stair' closes it and the project equals the state before OK.
- Choosing 'Relax Going G minimum to 260 mm' applies the rules plus the relaxation in one undo step and the read-out shows G 260 mm.
- Tool path: committing a conflicting candidate opens the dialog with origin Add; 'Keep last valid stair' creates nothing and leaves the tool's points intact.
- Stale path: raising the first floor so the stair cannot be solved lists it as a warning in the problems panel; clicking selects and zooms to it and opens the dialog; plan and 3D still show the stored (last valid) stair.
- Change-N and change-offset path: on the template with the first floor raised to 3.300 m, a Count(21) stair is placed (R 157.1 mm); setting the first floor back to 3.000 m leaves it stale (R 142.9 mm); its dialog names 'Riser height R' with 150 mm and 142.9 mm and offers 'Use 20 risers' and 'Change the bottom offset to −0.150 m' enabled; choosing 'Use 20 risers' re-solves in one undo step, the read-out shows '20 R × 150.0 mm' and the problems entry disappears.
- Drawn-geometry path: committing the task 03 L-shaped case (first segment 8.000 m) from the tool offers 'Adjust the run to … m' and no unlock entry; choosing it creates the stair in one undo step.
- A fixed going of 250 mm at R 150 mm appears as a warning entry naming the step formula (STA-008 not silent).
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green.
notes: SRS: STA-011 STA-008 STA-010.

title: Add select similar by preset, material or layer structure
description:
WHY: SEL-010 (S): select similar shall select the elements of the same kind and the same preset, material or layer structure as the selection. Gap row SEL-010 missing (effort S): kind and material exist in the model today (Element.kind and the wall/slab material, crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:130-196), presets and layer structures did not; Element.preset now comes from task 03 and Structure::{Thickness, Layered} from layer-structures-02. Select all (Workspace::select_all, crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:204) already limits itself to the active pane through Workspace::is_selectable and to ws.selection_region (selection-transforms-04/07); select similar reuses both. Named selection sets (SEL-009) are task 22.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/selection.rs (selection-transforms-01): `SimilarBy { Preset, Material, LayerStructure }` and `similar(project, selected: &[ElementId], by) -> Vec<ElementId>`: every element of the same kind as a selected element whose value equals that element's value (preset id; material = the Thickness structure's material, or the kind's material for kinds without a structure; layer structure = the Layered structure id); elements without a value (no preset, or no layer structure) are never similar to each other; a mixed-kind selection unions the per-kind results. App: Edit > Select similar > By preset / By material / By layer structure and the same entries in the canvas context menu of plan and 3D panes, disabled with a tooltip reason when no selected element has the value; the result replaces the selection (Shift adds), filtered by Workspace::is_selectable for the active pane and by ws.selection_region when one exists. Out of scope: selection sets (task 22), criteria selection (tasks 13, 14), group expansion (task 16).
design: A pure model function keeps the semantics testable without UI; the app only adds the pane and region filters, exactly as select all does, so view filters and hidden layers apply the same way. Comparing by resource id (not by name) survives renames (DSP-003). Pitfalls: a slab and a wall sharing a material are not similar (same kind is part of the rule); group expansion (task 16) applies to the result like any other selection entry point.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of similar() on a FixtureBuilder project with walls of two presets, walls and slabs of the same material and walls and slabs with layer structures: By preset selects only walls of the selected wall's preset; By material selects walls of that material but no slabs of the same material (same kind required); By layer structure groups walls and slabs separately; elements without a preset are not similar to each other by preset; a wall-plus-slab selection unions both kinds.
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/select_similar.rs: select a brick wall, Edit > Select similar > By material selects every brick wall shown in the active plan and nothing on another storey; elements on hidden layers are never selected (SEL-007); with a selection region active only walls inside it are selected; By preset is disabled with a reason when the selected wall has no preset.
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check stay green.
- Satisfies SEL-010.
notes: SRS: SEL-010

title: Store and recall named selection sets
description:
WHY: SEL-009 (C): named selection sets may be stored and recalled. Gap row SEL-009 missing: it needs a project resource, IFCX persistence in the archicraft namespace and a panel. Select similar (SEL-010) is task 12.

WHAT: Model: new crates/archicraft-model/src/selection_sets.rs with SelectionSetId (id_type! in crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs), `SelectionSet { id, name, members: Vec<ElementId> }` and Project.selection_sets; commands AddSelectionSet, UpdateSelectionSet (rename or redefine members) and DeleteSelectionSet; plan_delete_elements removes deleted members from every set (undoable); reidentify_all (selection-transforms-13) remaps set ids and members; to_template(false) of task 01 clears the sets and its unit test covers them. IFCX: `selectionSets` array in archicraft::project ([{id, name, members}]) written by crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs project_attribute and read in reader.rs; dangling members are dropped with a warning. App: new crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/selection_sets.rs, a 'Selection sets' window (Edit menu and command palette) with the SearchField of properties-and-dialogs-12: 'Save selection as set…', recall (replaces the selection, Shift adds), 'Redefine from selection', rename and delete; recall filters through Workspace::is_selectable for the active pane. Out of scope: select similar (task 12), criteria sets (tasks 13, 14), group expansion (task 16).
design: Members are stored by element id, stable per IFX-011; ids missing at recall are ignored. Sets are an element-scoped collection, so templates drop them while resources are kept. Pitfalls: recall must not select elements hidden in the active pane; group expansion (task 16) applies to the recalled selection like any other selection entry point.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: the three selection-set commands execute, undo to the exact starting project and redo; deleting a member removes it from its sets and undo restores the membership.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: selection sets round-trip with member order; a dangling member is dropped with a warning; a file without sets loads with an empty list and no warning; the reidentify_all test covers sets.
- kittest crates/archicraft-app/tests/selection_sets.rs: select three walls, save as 'Facade', clear, recall restores the three; Shift-recall adds to an existing selection; redefine and rename persist after save and reopen; elements on hidden layers are not selected on recall (SEL-007).
- cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check stay green.
- Satisfies SEL-009.
notes: SRS: SEL-009

title: Edit terrain points in a table with survey coordinates and altitudes
description:
WHY: TER-005 (M): terrain points shall be editable with numeric elevation input. NFR-ACC-004 (M): large survey coordinates (6-7 digit eastings and northings of a projected CRS) shall never be used as modelling coordinates; they are handled through the project location's survey point offset (STR-012) so precision is not lost. A surveyor's spot heights arrive as E/N and altitudes, and with survey file import withdrawn (TER-003, D-11) typed entry is the only path. Status: NFR-ACC-004 partial: MAX_COORDINATE (crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:17) and check_coordinates (validate.rs:105-113) already reject 6-7 digit values as model coordinates (keep and regress), and the survey point is stored (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:64-73) but never applied: there is no input or readout of coordinates in the survey system (gap row). Task 01 adds Location::survey_to_model, model_to_survey, altitude_of and elevation_at_altitude; task 03 the EditTerrain commands; task 08 the edit-mode selection of points.

WHAT: New 'Terrain points' dialog in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs, opened from the terrain properties section (task 07) and the edit palette (task 08): a virtualised table (egui ScrollArea::show_rows, so only visible rows build widgets) with columns id, X/Y or E/N and elevation. Coordinate mode Model (X, Y) or Survey (E, N) through Location::model_to_survey and survey_to_model, enabled only when Location::is_georeferenced(); elevation relative to project zero or above sea level through the altitude (STR-011 single datum). Editing a cell, adding a row and deleting selected rows each commit one EditTerrain command (SetPoints, AddPoints, DeletePoints); the table selection follows the edit-mode Selection and vice versa. Values are parsed at full precision through crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/widgets.rs length (a 7-digit easting is not rounded to display precision, NFR-ACC-002) and shown rounded only for display (NFR-ACC-005). The model only ever stores model coordinates: conversion happens at this UI boundary (subtract the survey point, then rotate, task 01). Out of scope: pasting or importing point lists (TER-003 withdrawn by D-11), a breakline node table, reprojection between CRSs (O-2), survey readouts in other tools.
design: The table is the precision path (values stored at full precision, rounded only for display), the 3D markers of task 09 the quick path. Grid north of the projected CRS is treated as true north (task 01 note, O-2). Pitfalls: survey values need 10 significant digits in the default metre format, so check the formatting width of widgets::length; parse thousands separators only as NumberFormat allows; the elevation-reference choice uses the same conversion helpers and labels as the terrain tool's toggle (task 07); keep the dialog egui-light with a headless row model so the conversions are unit-testable without egui. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs (Project settings dialog at 553-592 as the pattern), ui/widgets.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs Location, validate.rs:17 and 105-113, crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/terrain.rs (task 03).
acceptance_criteria:
- Survey entry: with EPSG 2056, survey point E 2600123.456 / N 1199876.543, altitude 512.30 m and true north 3.20 degrees (the georeferenced_shell values of task 02), typing E 2600130.000 and N 1199880.000 stores model coordinates equal to survey_to_model within 1e-9 m with |x| and |y| below 100 m, and switching the row to survey mode shows the typed values again.
- Altitude entry: typing 514.00 m in sea-level mode with altitude 512.30 m stores 1.70 m; switching back to project-zero mode shows 1.700.
- NFR-ACC-004 regression: every stored coordinate stays within MAX_COORDINATE, and typing 2600130.000 into X in Model mode is refused with the check_coordinates hint naming Project settings > Location.
- Survey mode is disabled with an explanatory tooltip when no EPSG code is set.
- Deleting three selected rows is one undo step; editing a cell to a duplicate XY with a different Z is refused with the validation message; selecting a row selects that point part in edit mode.
- A 50,000-point terrain opens the dialog and scrolls with only the visible rows laid out (row-count assertion in a kittest frame).
- Kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): the Terrain points dialog opens from the properties panel, shows 'E' and 'N' headers in survey mode, and an edited elevation appears in the properties.
- TER-005 numeric point editing in a table satisfied; the NFR-ACC-004 typed survey-coordinate input and readout path satisfied.
notes:
SRS: TER-005 NFR-ACC-004
Survey readouts in the point-input tracker of other tools are not part of this epic; file a follow-up bead if users ask for them.

title: Edit stair parameters and rules with live solver values
description:
WHY: STA-009 (M): while editing, R, G, 2R + G, N and the pitch are displayed (MEA-003 names STA-009 as the stair's derived values). STA-006 (M): the selectable values of N are limited to the admissible set. STA-007 (M): the permitted going range is shown to the user when the going is free. STA-008 (M): a fixed going lists every violated rule with actual and limit value. STA-005 (M): every rule has an independent enable flag and min/max values. STA-010 (M): the walking-line distance from the inner edge is configurable and checked against the rule minimum. STA-024 (M): start and end with riser or tread are selectable. ELM-017 (M): numeric parameters are range-checked and dependent values such as a stair's riser count update live while editing. Gap: the properties panel is wall/slab only (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:253-460) and derived rows refresh only after a command (properties.rs:541-575).

WHAT: Stair fields in the properties strip and settings dialog — through the field specs of ui/fields.rs from properties-and-dialogs when present, otherwise kind-specific Fields rows in properties.rs as for walls: width, side, offset, bottom offset, top link and top offset (reusing the TopMode rows), riser mode with N as a combo box listing exactly admissible_riser_counts for the current rise or a target R, going Free/Fixed with value and the permitted range label ('300 mm ≤ G ≤ 350 mm'), walking line half width or distance from the inner edge, start and end riser/tread, material; derived rows from ui/stair.rs readout plus a violation list ('2R+G 550 mm < min 600 mm'). A Rules section (rules_grid in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs) with one row per RuleKind — enable checkbox, min and max in mm, plain ratio or degrees — committed as one UpdateElements on OK/Apply, also for Subject::Defaults(stair). While a field holds an uncommitted value, the derived rows re-solve a candidate copy every frame (ELM-017; through properties-and-dialogs-07's live dependent values when that task has landed). Conflicts from commits show in the status line until task 11. Out of scope: the conflict dialog (task 11), rule presets (templates-presets), segment and landing fields (stair-body-plan).
design: Every number shown comes from the model's solve() on a candidate element, so properties, tool and stored solution agree; the combo's choices are admissible_riser_counts at the stair's current rise, which implements STA-006's 'selectable values' literally. The whole rule set commits as one command so combined edits such as the acceptance conflict (min G 350 with max 2R+G 600) are judged together. Units: lengths in mm with one decimal for R, ratios as plain numbers, pitch in the project angle unit; inputs go through widgets::length and widgets::angle (datum-aware if properties-and-dialogs added that). Pitfalls: build the candidate once per frame, not per row; mixed selections (stair plus wall) show only common fields; reuse the tool's readout formatter so both strings are identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest on samples::stairs() stair A: selecting it shows '19 R × 157.9 mm, 2R+G = 616 mm' and the pitch among the derived values; the N combo lists exactly 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20 (3.000 m, D.3, STA-006); choosing 18 executes one UpdateElements and updates the read-out.
- kittest: a stair with R 150 mm and a free going shows '300 mm ≤ G ≤ 350 mm' (STA-007); switching to a fixed going of 250 mm lists the step-formula violation with 550 mm and 600 mm (STA-008).
- kittest: typing a new width without committing updates the derived rows while the model stays unchanged until Enter (ELM-017).
- Rules grid: disabling the riser rule and enabling pitch 20°/30° commits as one undo step and shows again after reopening (STA-005); an inverted range is rejected with the rule's label and leaves the model unchanged (NFR-REL-005).
- A walking-line distance of 0.250 m under the D.3 minimum shows a warning row naming 'Walking line distance from inner edge' (STA-010); the start/end selectors change the displayed run length (STA-024).
- Editing the stair defaults' rule set changes the rules of the next placed stair (PRJ-007).
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green.
notes: SRS: STA-005 STA-006 STA-007 STA-008 STA-009 STA-010 STA-024.

title: Compute the stair band, inner side and walking line
description:
WHY: STA-010 (M): goings shall be measured along a walking line, by default at half the stair width, and its distance from the inner edge is configurable (the check against the D.3 minimum of 300 mm belongs to the whole-stair solve of task 03). STA-002 (M): the stair body lies left of, centred on or right of the baseline, with an offset, which fixes the band edges and therefore where the walking line runs. The gap analysis lists STA-010 as missing (M: no walking line, no configurable inner-edge distance, no check) and STA-002 as missing (L: no body side or offset). The solve of task 03, the riser positions of the provisional body (task 06), the tool preview's walking line and riser lines (task 08) and later stair-body-plan's flight layout all need the same plan geometry, so it is one pure module; separating it from the solve keeps STA-001's extra-large scope in reviewable pieces. Nothing reusable exists in archicraft-model beyond ReferenceLine::face_offsets (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:99), whose wall convention (signed offsets along the left-hand normal) the stair side follows; the wall mitring in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs lives in a crate the model cannot depend on.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/walking.rs (declared in stair/mod.rs): BaselineSide { Left, Centre, Right } with edge_offsets(width, offset) -> (right, left) signed distances along the baseline's left-hand normal (Left: offset .. offset + width; Centre: offset − width/2 .. offset + width/2; Right: −offset − width .. −offset) and mirrored() (swaps Left and Right); WalkingLineSpec { HalfWidth, FromInner(f64) }; InnerSide { Left, Right } from the sign of the sum of signed turning angles (Left, looking up the stair, for a straight or net-zero baseline); band(baseline, width, side, offset) -> Result<Band { left: Vec<DVec2>, right: Vec<DVec2>, inner: InnerSide }, PlanError> with mitred offset polylines; walking_line(&Band, spec, width) -> Result<WalkingLine { points, distance_from_inner, length }, PlanError> with point_at(s), tangent_at(s) and segment_at(s) by arc length; riser_lines(&WalkingLine, &Band, first: f64, going: f64, count: u32) -> Vec<[DVec2; 2]> placing riser k at s = first + k × going as a segment across the band perpendicular to the walking-line tangent (at a corner the incoming segment's tangent); reversed(baseline, side, offset) for downward input (task 08). PlanError names the cause: fewer than two distinct nodes, a zero-length segment, a turn of 170° or more, non-finite coordinates, a FromInner distance outside (0, width). Pure glam arithmetic, no new dependency. Out of scope: the WalkingLineDistance rule check, run fitting and moving the last node (task 03), landings, corner riser offsets and winders (stair-body-plan), curved baselines (STA-027).
design: Pure functions on glam values (archicraft-model depends only on glam, indexmap, serde, thiserror and uuid) keep the plan geometry testable without fixtures and shared by the solve, the geometry, the tool and stair-body-plan. The side convention follows ReferenceLine::face_offsets (element.rs:99): signed offsets along the left-hand normal, so mirroring and reversing are sign flips. Mitre each join by intersecting the offset lines of adjacent segments (collinear neighbours share the offset point); reject turns of 170° or more instead of producing spikes, because winders arrive later (STA-025). Inner side by the sum of signed turning angles; a straight or net-zero baseline uses Left so the default is deterministic. Pitfalls: compare through MODEL_TOLERANCE from tolerance.rs (element-kind-framework-01), never ==; keep point_at stable at segment boundaries (the corner belongs to the incoming segment) so the riser counts per segment add up in task 06; no ids, storeys or elements in this module.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/walking.rs:
  - STA-002: width 1.00 and offset 0.100 put the band edges of a straight baseline along +X at y ∈ [0.100, 1.100] for Left, [−0.400, 0.600] for Centre and [−1.100, −0.100] for Right; mirrored() swaps Left and Right.
  - STA-010 default: HalfWidth puts the walking line 0.500 m from the inner edge, on the baseline for Centre with offset 0 and at y = 0.600 for Left with offset 0.100; FromInner(0.250) puts it 0.250 m from the inner (left) edge of a straight stair.
  - An L-shaped Centre baseline (5.000 m along +X, then 3.000 m along +Y, width 1.00) has the inner side Left; HalfWidth gives a walking line of 8.000 m on the baseline, FromInner(0.300) one offset by +0.200 m with a mitred length of 7.600 m, and the band edges meet at mitred corners; the mirror image (turning right) has the inner side Right and the same lengths.
  - riser_lines on a straight 5.400 m Centre stair with first 0, going 0.300 and 19 risers gives segments at x = 0.3 k spanning y ∈ [−0.500, 0.500]; with first 0.300 the first riser moves to x = 0.300.
  - reversed() of a Left stair yields a Right stair over the same band (equal edge polylines within MODEL_TOLERANCE).
- Seeded property tests (xorshift PRNG inside the test, 10,000 random polylines, no new dependency): each band edge keeps its signed distance from its baseline segment within MODEL_TOLERANCE away from the joins; point_at(0) and point_at(length) are the walking line's end points and arc length is monotone; every riser segment ends on both band edges within MODEL_TOLERANCE; degenerate inputs (one node, zero-length or reversing segments, turns of 170° or more, NaN) return PlanError and never panic.
- cargo test -p archicraft-model, clippy --all-targets and fmt green; the plan-geometry part of STA-010 (walking line at half width by default, configurable inner-edge distance) and of STA-002 (side and offset of the band) is in place.
notes: SRS: STA-002 STA-010. Split from task 03 during review so the plan geometry and the whole-stair solve are separate reviewable pieces. Decision to confirm: the inner side of a straight stair is its left side looking up the stair.

title: Pick 2D contour polylines into a selected terrain with one elevation
description:
WHY: TER-004 (M): the user picks existing 2D polylines into a selected terrain as breaklines (contours) and assigns one elevation to all vertices of a picked contour in one action; picking linework without a selected terrain shall not create new terrain silently. TER-002 (M): terrain is creatable from 2D contour polylines. D-11: terrain is built from typed points and drawn contour lines, no DXF. Status: TER-004 missing; drafting-trim-split-03 provides DraftPolyline, DraftLine and DraftArc, drafting-trim-split-02 the single tessellate(curve, settings).

WHAT: Model: Command::AddContours { terrain: ElementId, picks: Vec<ContourPick { source: ElementId, nodes: Vec<DVec2>, closed: bool, elevation: f64 }>, remove_sources: bool } planning into one ReplaceElement of the terrain (breaklines with contour = Some(elevation) and every node at that elevation) plus optional RemoveElement edits for the sources. The caller tessellates the source curve with archicraft_geometry::tessellate (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs, drafting-trim-split-02) under project.settings.tessellation and passes the nodes, because archicraft-model cannot depend on archicraft-geometry; carrying them also keeps journal replay deterministic (the ConvertContours pattern of task 13). Sources must be DraftLine, DraftArc or DraftPolyline (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/drafting.rs, drafting-trim-split-03); Invalid when terrain is not a terrain, a source is not a 2D linear kind, or the result fails validate_terrain (crossing contours named by their source element names). App: the 'Add contours' command (Design menu, terrain edit palette and the terrain tool's 'From contours' mode) is enabled only with exactly one terrain selected; otherwise it shows 'Select a terrain first' and creates nothing. Pick step in tools/terrain.rs: hover highlights a 2D polyline, a click picks it and opens the elevation field prefilled with the previous elevation plus the terrain's contour interval, Enter commits one AddContours per contour (one action, one undo step), Esc ends the step. 'From contours' mode: the boundary is drawn first (explicit creation), then the pick step starts with the new terrain selected. Source linework is kept by default, with an option to remove it. Out of scope: associativity between a contour and its source polyline (copied geometry), 3D polylines (TER-009 withdrawn), automatic elevation guessing.
design: The command takes the terrain id explicitly, so silent creation is impossible by construction; the UI rule is the second guard. Contours are copies (non-associative): editing the source afterwards does not change the terrain, which the tooltip states. Tessellation goes through the single tessellate() of drafting-trim-split-02, so a curve yields the same vertices as in plan (bit-identical rule). Pitfalls: a polyline partly outside the boundary is stored whole and clipped only at evaluation (task 04), so it stays valid when the boundary grows; duplicate nodes after tessellation are merged within MODEL_TOLERANCE; contour elevations typed relative to sea level use the toggle of task 07. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/drafting.rs, curve.rs, command.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/terrain.rs (task 07), ui/actions.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddContours with two polylines at 2.00 and 2.50 adds two contour breaklines whose every node Z equals the elevation; remove_sources removes the polylines and undo restores terrain and polylines exactly.
- AddContours with a wall as source or a slab as terrain returns CommandError::Invalid; crossing contours are refused naming both polylines.
- Tool tests: with no terrain selected, invoking Add contours leaves the element count unchanged and sets the status message; with a terrain selected, pick + typed 3.00 + Enter emits exactly one AddContours; the next pick defaults to 3.50 (interval 0.50); picking a DraftArc passes nodes bit-identical to tessellate() of that arc, within the 2 mm chord deviation.
- 'From contours' mode: boundary drawn, three contours picked, giving one terrain with three contour breaklines that the TIN of task 04 honours as constraint edges.
- Kittest: the Add contours menu item is disabled without a terrain selection and enabled with one.
- TER-004 satisfied; the TER-002 'from 2D contour polylines' clause satisfied.
notes: SRS: TER-004 TER-002

title: Implement the pure rise, riser and going solver functions
description:
WHY: The core contract of SRS 4.20 is the rise/going solver: an integer number of equal risers that fits the levels exactly and a going that satisfies every enabled rule. STA-003 (M): total rise = (top-storey elevation − home-storey elevation) + top offset − bottom offset; storeys at 0 and 3.000 m with both offsets 0.100 m give 3.000 m, storeys at 0 and 3.400 m with bottom offset 0.100 m and top offset 0 give 3.300 m. STA-004 (M): N equal risers with R = total rise / N; the user sets N or a target R, in which case the system chooses the integer N that keeps R within the enabled bounds and reports the actual R (3.000 m / 19 ≈ 157.89 mm, 3.300 m / 22 = 150.00 mm). STA-006 (M): the selectable N are those with R inside the riser bounds for which a going satisfying the other enabled rules exists (default rules, 3.000 m: N ∈ {15..20}). STA-007 (M): with a free going, the permitted going range is the intersection of all enabled constraints for the current R (default rules, R = 150 mm: 300 ≤ G ≤ 350 mm).
