STA-008 (M): a fixed going is used exactly and every violated enabled rule is listed with its actual and limit value (R 150/G 300: 2R+G = 600, no violation; R 150/G 250: 2R+G = 550 reported against the 600 minimum). STA-024 (M): bottom and top each start or end with a riser or a tread, which fixes the number of goings. All are missing with S effort in the gap analysis, and the epic's risk note asks for the solver to ship first, testable in isolation.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/solver.rs with pure functions over plain numbers and RuleSet (no Project, no Element): total_rise(home_elevation, top_elevation, bottom_offset, top_offset); riser_height(rise, n); StairEnd { Riser, Tread } and goings(n, start, end) = n − 1 + [start = Tread] + [end = Tread]; going_range(r, rules) -> GoingRange { lower: Limit, upper: Option<Limit> }, empty when lower > upper, intersecting the G bounds, 2R+G → [min − 2R, max − 2R], R/G → [R/max, R/min], R+G → [min − R, max − R] and pitch → [R/tan(max), R/tan(min)], each limit tagged with the RuleKind and Bound that produced it; riser_range_for_going(g, rules), the inverse used by the offset alternatives of task 03; admissible_riser_counts(rise, rules) -> Vec<u32>; RiserSpec { Count(u32), TargetHeight(f64) } and choose_riser_count(rise, spec, rules, filter) returning N, the actual R and the ordered candidate list (nearest R to the target first, ties to the lower R); Violation { rule, bound, limit, actual } and check(r, g, walking_line_distance, rules) -> Vec<Violation>. total_rise takes resolved elevations only: task 04 obtains them through VerticalLink, which wraps the existing Project::top_elevation (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:236) and StoreyList::relative_elevation (crates/archicraft-model/src/storey.rs:108), so no storey-link arithmetic is duplicated here. The SRS numeric tests go into a new crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs, one test per requirement named after its ID. Out of scope: walking line, baselines and the whole-stair solve with conflicts and alternatives (task 03), the Stair element (task 04).
design: Pure functions on SI numbers keep the solver independent of storage and testable without fixtures (epic design note: stair/solver.rs, pure and property-tested). Provenance on each limit is what lets task 03 name the conflicting rules (STA-011): the binding lower limit is the maximum over the enabled lower bounds, the binding upper limit the minimum over the upper bounds, and a conflict is exactly the pair (lower.rule, upper.rule) when lower > upper + tolerance. Inverses: R/G ≤ max ⇒ G ≥ R/max, a ratio or pitch minimum of 0 gives no upper bound, pitch bounds go through tan() in radians. admissible_riser_counts scans N from ceil(rise/R_max) to floor(rise/R_min) (with a small epsilon before ceil/floor); if the riser rule is disabled, cap the scan at N ≤ 100 and document it. choose_riser_count takes an optional filter closure so task 03 can drop N whose drawn geometry fails without duplicating the ordering. Pitfalls: inclusive comparisons through MODEL_TOLERANCE (element-kind-framework-01 tolerance.rs), never ==; deterministic tie-breaking everywhere (RuleKind order for limits, lower R for targets) so read-outs and goldens are stable.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs passes:
  - sta_003_total_rise: both SRS cases (3.000 m and 3.300 m).
  - sta_004_riser_height: 3.000/19 within 1e-9 of 0.157894736842 m (reported as 157.89 mm); 3.300/22 = 0.150 within MODEL_TOLERANCE; TargetHeight(0.150) picks N = 20 at 3.000 m and N = 22 at 3.300 m; TargetHeight(0.250), above the 200 mm maximum, picks N = 15 (R = 0.200) and TargetHeight(0.120), below the minimum, picks N = 20 (R = 0.150), so the chosen R always lies inside the enabled bounds and the actual R is returned; Count(0) is rejected (N is a positive integer).
  - sta_006_admissible_counts: default rules at 3.000 m give exactly [15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20].
  - sta_007_going_range: R = 0.150 gives lower 0.300 (StepFormula Min) and upper 0.350 (Going Max; ties resolved in RuleKind order).
  - sta_008_fixed_going: R 0.150 / G 0.300 gives no violation and 2R+G = 0.600; R 0.150 / G 0.250 gives exactly one Violation { StepFormula, Min, limit 0.600, actual 0.550 }.
  - sta_024_goings: N = 19 gives 18 (riser/riser), 19 (tread/riser), 19 (riser/tread) and 20 (tread/tread).
- Disabled rules have no effect; enabling ratio, sum and pitch one at a time narrows going_range as the formulas say (hand-computed cases, e.g. pitch max 30° at R 0.150 gives G ≥ 0.2598).
- Inclusive boundary: 3.000 m / 15 (R = 0.200) yields the one-point range [0.250, 0.250] and N = 15 stays admissible.
- Seeded property tests (xorshift PRNG inside the test, 10,000 cases, no new dependency): every G in going_range(r) passes check() for the going-related rules; g ∈ going_range(r) iff r ∈ riser_range_for_going(g) within MODEL_TOLERANCE; every admissible N has R inside the riser bounds and a non-empty going range; non-finite or non-positive rises return empty results without panicking.
- cargo test/clippy/fmt green; STA-003 (formula), STA-004, STA-006, STA-007, STA-008 and the counting rule of STA-024 are satisfied at function level.
notes: SRS: STA-003 STA-004 STA-006 STA-007 STA-008 STA-024. Decision to confirm: goings T = N − 1 + [start is tread] + [end is tread]; 'end with tread' puts the last tread at the top level, 'start with tread' puts a floor-level going before the first riser. TargetHeight tie-break: the lower R (more risers).

title: Manifold Boolean kernel and associative solid operations
description:
Bring in the 3D Boolean engine (Manifold) as the first epic of increment 2 (technology-choices: 'when the first case cannot be built from 2D cuts, at the latest in increment 2') and build on it the associative solid operations: subtract, intersect and add with plus/minus Z extrusion variants, several targets and operators, mutual relations acting on unmodified bodies (order independence), persistence in the relation store, related-element queries and relation removal restoring the target, operators keeping their effect while hidden or ghosted, face material choice, identical results in all views and IFCX, explicit operations prevailing over the automatic junction cleanup because the pipeline places the Boolean stage after the junction stage (SOL-027), splitting by a 3D plane, openings that cut further elements with host reassignment (OPN-002), the auxiliary flag with its IFCX exclusion and export-visible-only variant, and the IFX-038 mesh validity rules enforced before every Boolean and before writing.

Risks: A C++ toolchain on three platforms and a one-owner binding crate: own bindings, CI from day one, kernel trait, vendored cmake build with caching. Boolean robustness on coplanar faces (walls on slabs) is covered by dedicated regression fixtures. Native crashes from the C++ kernel are the trigger for the minidump handler in release-candidate (NFR-SEC-002).
design: Manifold through thin own bindings to its C API (or the manifold3d crate after a health check), isolated in archicraft-geometry kernel/ behind the SolidKernel trait so a pure-Rust fallback can be swapped; Relation::SolidOperation{targets, operators, kind, extrusion, material_source} in the relation store; evaluation pipeline order fixed as base bodies -> junction cleanup -> openings -> solid operations -> trims with check_closed before every Boolean and dirty propagation along relation edges; archicraft::solidOperation schema with a format-version bump through the framework migration; archicraft-model auxiliary flag on Element with pick exclusion; archicraft-app operation dialog, operator display states and relation inspection (decision D-7). cmake and a C++ toolchain added to .github/workflows/ci.yml and documented.
acceptance_criteria: CI builds the kernel on ubuntu, windows and macos runners with cached cmake builds and a feature flag disables it; archicraft-geometry exposes boolean(op, a, b) behind a SolidKernel trait and property tests show every result is closed, 2-manifold, outward-oriented and split at hard edges with at most 65,535 points per Body_n (IFX-038); a failed Boolean returns Err, the element keeps its last valid body and is listed (NFR-REL-005 clause); SOL-022: moving an operator by 0.10 m moves the cut by 0.10 m with no further action; random operator orderings give identical meshes; deleting an operator restores the target; an explicit subtract between two joined walls overrides their automatic junction where the two conflict (SOL-027 conflict test); a multi-element opening cuts two walls and both show the void in plan and IFCX, and moving the non-host cut element leaves the opening in place; a golden file with subtract/intersect/add round-trips its relations and passes IFX-006; auxiliary elements are absent from the standard IFCX building elements and the export-visible-only variant omits hidden elements while the default export does not; split by plane yields two closed solids; the plan slice, the 3D body and the exported mesh hash identically.
notes: SRS: IFX-038 OPN-002 SOL-020 SOL-021 SOL-022 SOL-023 SOL-024 SOL-025 SOL-026 SOL-027 SOL-028 ELM-014 IFX-068 EDT-024

title: Stair element, rule-based solver and placement tool
description:
Goal: Add the Stair kind with baseline, width, side and offset, storey-linked total rise and the Appendix D.3 rule set with independent enable flags and bounds, the placement tool with upward/downward input and live riser-count preview, and the solver as pure functions: riser count or target riser within the rules, admissible riser-count set, going range from the enabled constraints, fixed-going mode with a violation list, live R/G/2R+G/N/pitch read-out, walking line with the inner-edge rule, conflict detection naming the rules with alternatives and keep-last-valid, start and end with riser or tread. Runs in parallel with roofs; the flight and landing geometry follows in stair-body-plan.

Risks: STA-001 is extra large: the solver is testable in isolation and ships first. National rule semantics (O-4) are open: the international default ships here, DIN and OENORM presets are templates-presets. No admissible N must never produce invalid geometry: keep-last-valid plus a reported problem.
design: archicraft-model stair/solver.rs (pure, property-tested functions over baseline and rules) and kinds/stair.rs with RuleSet and the D.3 values in template.rs; archicraft-geometry a provisional stepped extrusion along the baseline so the element is visible before stair-body-plan; archicraft-ifcx archicraft::stair codec; archicraft-app tools/stair.rs with the baseline polyline through the point-input service and the read-out in the tracker and in the properties fields (ELM-017 live values).
acceptance_criteria: Every numeric test of STA-003 to STA-008 as a solver unit test (3.000 m / 19 gives 157.89 mm; N in {15..20}; 300 <= G <= 350 at R = 150; 2R+G = 550 reported against 600); changing the storey height from 3.000 to 3.300 re-solves to 22 risers through the storey link; a rule conflict (min G 350, max 2R+G 600 at R 170) is reported with both rule names and alternatives and the last valid stair is kept (conflict dialog kittest); the live '19 R x 157.9 mm, 2R+G = 616 mm' read-out during input; the walking line distance is checked against the rule; the rule set and all parameters round-trip in archicraft::stair and archicraft::stairRules.
notes: SRS: STA-001 STA-002 STA-003 STA-004 STA-005 STA-006 STA-007 STA-008 STA-009 STA-010 STA-011 STA-024

title: Build none, smooth and stepped stair structures with materials
description:
WHY: STA-041 (S): flight and landing structures shall be selectable independently: none, or monolithic with a smooth or stepped underside (stepped: separate vertical and horizontal thickness), each with a material (KB 303716 terrazzo, 303670). Appendix D.2 makes a monolithic structure with smooth underside the default, so without this task the default stair has floating treads. STA-001 requires that supports regenerate with every input change. Gap row STA-041: per-part materials are supported by BodyPart (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:22-28) but nothing generates a structure.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/structure.rs: flight structure as one prism per flight in the flight frame; its top follows the underside of the finish (tread bottoms and riser backs), its underside is either a line parallel to the pitch at the perpendicular waist thickness (Smooth) or the step zigzag offset by the vertical and horizontal thicknesses (Stepped), clipped by the storey-local floor plane at the bottom and by the landing or the top floor at the top; landing structure as the landing polygon extruded below the landing finish by the landing thickness. Joints: the flight profile ends in a vertical cut at the landing edge, and its underside meets the landing underside when the geometry allows it (the corner case that cannot be built is task 07). Part named Structure with the structure material inside each Flight_n and Landing_n child; None generates no body; flight and landing settings are independent. Re-bless stairs.ifcx. Out of scope: stringers and beams (STA-042), cantilever, plate and pan structures (SRS 8), seams (06).
design: Build the structure profile in the flight's (u, z) plane as one simple polygon (finish underside polyline on top, underside line or zigzag below, vertical cuts at both ends) and extrude it with extrude_profile (stair-solver-tool-06, reused by task 04), so one triangulation path serves smooth and stepped bodies. The smooth underside starts at the bottom where the pitch line offset hits the floor plane, which avoids slivers at the first step; if the offset line would cut through the first riser profile, start with a vertical face instead. Landing structure thickness is measured downwards from the landing finish underside. Coplanar faces (structure top against tread bottom) must be exactly coplanar from the same layout values, not recomputed, so the seam pass of task 06 can recognise them. Pitfalls: a stepped profile with horizontal thickness larger than the going self-intersects (validate with validate_ring before extrusion and return a part error for task 07); landing slabs at a polyline corner can be non-convex (triangulate handles it). Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/finish.rs (04), extrude.rs extrude_profile, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/triangulate.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs validate_ring.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair.rs smooth_underside_matches_analytic_area: a straight flight with waist t and pitch theta has a structure profile area equal to the analytic value within 1e-9 and an underside parallel to the pitch line.
- stepped_underside_thicknesses: at every step the measured vertical and horizontal thicknesses equal the Stepped settings.
- independent_settings: None on flights with Monolithic on landings and the reverse each give exactly the expected part sets per child.
- Every structure body is closed (the property test of task 04 extended to random structure settings), and finish and structure profiles do not overlap (2D intersection area of the profiles in the flight frame below 1e-12).
- Materials per part follow the settings; DeleteMaterial of the structure material regenerates bodies with the replacement material.
- samples::u_stair() (D.2 defaults) has a Structure part in every flight and landing child; stairs.ifcx re-blessed, conformance/run.sh green.
- Satisfies STA-041.
notes:
SRS: STA-041
Appendix D.2: monolithic structure, smooth underside. Structure thickness defaults are a proposal from task 01 (0.15 m waist, 0.20 m landing).

title: Split elements by a 3D plane with associative half-space clips
description:
WHY: EDT-024 (S): 'Elements shall also be splittable by a plane in 3D.' Gap-analysis EDT-024: missing; it needs 3D Booleans, and EDT-013's 2D split (drafting-trim-split) covers only splits by an edge or line in plan. The epic acceptance: 'split by plane yields two closed solids'. A wall split by an inclined plane cannot be expressed by wall parameters, and converting the halves to free-form solids would lose the parametric definition (free-form solids arrive later in free-form-solids).

WHAT: archicraft-model: Element.clips: Vec<HalfSpace { origin: DVec3, normal: DVec3 }> (storey-local coordinates; the half on the normal side is removed; #[serde(default)]), carried by MoveElements and by the transform-hook contract documented in kinds/mod.rs for the rotate and mirror commands of selection-transforms. Command::SplitByPlane { ids, plane, keep: Side }: for each solid element the plane crosses, the original gets clip(+plane) and a duplicate with a new identity (IFX-011; name from the counters; copy::duplicate without hosted elements) gets clip(-plane); hosted elements stay with the half containing their void centroid (re-hosted to the copy with the ReassignHost rule of 13); solid-operation relations of the original are duplicated for the copy in both roles; elements the plane misses are skipped with a message, locked ones are rejected. Geometry: a Clip stage directly after the generator, applied to both the junction-cleaned body and the operator's own body (so a half acts only with its half), using kernel.split and keeping the inner side. IFCX: archicraft::element gains optional clips (origin, normal). FORMAT_VERSION rule for this epic: its reader-visible additions (08 solid-operation parameters, 09 auxiliary records, 14 opening cuts, 15 clips) share one bump with one no-op migration entry in alpha/migrate.rs; whichever of these tasks lands first bumps, the others extend the entry's description, unless a release was cut in between (then bump again, per the rule in alpha/mod.rs). Out of scope: the UI (16), parametric horizontal splits into two walls with adjusted base and top (follow-up), conversion to free-form solids.
design: Half-space clips keep both halves parametric and work for every kind with a body without per-kind split code; the kernel's exact plane split (02) gives closed halves. Applying clips to the own body as well keeps SOL-024 consistent (a split operator cuts only with its half). Pitfalls: clips must be storey-local so storey moves carry them; a split through a hosted element must not duplicate it (the ELM-016 copy cascade is wrong here, hence duplicate without hosted elements); repeated splits add further clips. Pointers: element.rs:275-287, command.rs MoveElements, copy.rs (host-openings-02), evaluate.rs stage order (05), kernel split (02), writer.rs and reader.rs archicraft::element.
acceptance_criteria:
- solid_ops.rs: splitting a 5.00 x 0.30 x 2.80 m wall by a plane inclined 30 degrees gives two elements whose bodies pass check_closed, whose volumes sum to the original within 1e-9 relative, and whose union equals the original body (empty symmetric difference through the kernel).
- Both halves stay parametric: changing the thickness of one half changes only that half; moving one half moves its clip with it.
- A horizontal split of a slab and a vertical split of a wall give closed solids; a plane that misses the element returns a message and no change; undo restores the original element and removes the copy.
- An opening on the copy's side is re-hosted to the copy; solid operations of the original apply to both halves.
- tests/roundtrip.rs: clips round-trip and the copy keeps its new UUID across save and reopen (IFX-011).
- Satisfies EDT-024 in model, geometry and IFCX.
notes: SRS: EDT-024. Open question: parametric horizontal splits of walls and columns (two elements with adjusted base and top) as a refinement; vertical planes may delegate to EDT-013 once drafting-trim-split is available.

title: Evaluate solid operations in a fixed stage order after junctions
description:
WHY: SOL-020 (M): operations on every element with a closed body. SOL-022 (M): solid operations are associative - 'Any change to an operator or target (move, reshape, thickness, slope, profile) shall update the result in all views without a manual rebuild'; acceptance 'moving an operator by 0.10 m moves the cut by 0.10 m without further action'. SOL-024 (M): 'Every operator shall act with its own unmodified body, so that results do not depend on evaluation order and cannot loop.' SOL-027 (S): 'Explicit solid operations shall take effect regardless of automatic junction priorities. Where an automatic junction conflicts with an explicit operation, the explicit operation prevails.' SOL-023: deleting an operator restores the target. NFR-REL-005 (M): failed Boolean operations never create corrupt elements; the epic asks that the element keeps its last valid body and is listed. Gap-analysis SOL-024/SOL-027: evaluation computes each body once from parameters (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:64-91, no raw versus modified body) and the junction stage is a 2D footprint resolution before extrusion (wall.rs, called at evaluate.rs:65) that no later stage can override.

WHAT: evaluate.rs gets an explicit, documented stage order Stage::{Base, Junction, Openings, FurtherCuts, SolidOperations, Trims, Normalize} (module docs and docs/geometry-pipeline.md): Base, Junction and Openings are the existing generator path with the junction-resolved footprint and the hosted cutters of host-openings (EvalContext::cutters); FurtherCuts is filled by 14; Trims is an empty hook that cleanup-and-trims fills, and its priority cleanup goes between Openings and SolidOperations; Normalize is 03. New: an operator's own body is the same generator run without junction resolution (unjoined ends, own hosted cutters kept), cached per element revision in ModelGeometry.own_bodies for elements that are operators. The SolidOperations stage gathers, for every element with incoming SolidOperation relations, each operator's own body transformed into the target's storey frame (elevation difference; site-level frame elevation 0) together with its SolidOp, and calls apply_operations of 18, whose parts replace the target's parts; Void parts and the Normalize stage follow unchanged. Dirty propagation: the framework's dirty set adds the targets of every element whose own body may have changed (stamped elements and hosts of stamped hosted elements), one hop only, never from a target on to its own targets. Failures: a KernelError keeps the target's body from the previous ModelGeometry (on a full evaluation its pre-operation body) and records a GeometryProblem naming target, operator and reason; a completely removed target is valid, has no visible parts and gets an informational problem. The kernel is injected (ModelGeometry::evaluate_incremental_with(project, previous, &dyn SolidKernel)) so tests can use a failing kernel. Out of scope: the Boolean semantics of the three operations and their canonical order (18), Up/Down extrusion (06), face material runs (07), IFCX (08), further cuts (14), clips (15).
design: The single rule 'targets are modified after their own junction cleanup, operators act with their own unjoined body' gives both SOL-024 (no operator ever sees another operation's result, so there is no order and no loop) and SOL-027 (the junction cannot shield a target region from an operator, because the operator's body ignores the junction and the Boolean stage runs later). The order-free combination itself is 18's pure function, so this task only gathers operators, transforms them and handles failures. Pitfalls: bodies are storey-local (evaluate.rs header), so always transform operators by the frame difference; the previous-body fallback breaks incremental-versus-full equality for failed elements only, so exclude elements with kernel problems from that property test and document it; own bodies cost a second generator run, so compute them only for operators; keep catch_unwind around the whole element (evaluate.rs:69 today, element-kind-framework-13 guard). Pointers: evaluate.rs:51-120 and 140-189, wall.rs footprints, the framework's dirty_set and GeometryProblem, host-openings' EvalContext::cutters and wall_cut.rs, kernel/ops.rs apply_operations (18).
acceptance_criteria:
- SOL-022 acceptance in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/solid_ops.rs: a 5.00 x 0.30 x 2.80 m wall and a 1.00 x 1.00 x 0.30 m slab operator crossing it at mid-height; after MoveElements of the operator by 0.10 m in x the cut faces of the wall (triangles sourced from the operator) are shifted by 0.100 m within 1e-9 m and the wall volume is unchanged, with no command other than the move.
- SOL-022 parameter changes: increasing the operator's thickness by 0.05 m through UpdateElements widens the cut by 0.05 m, and moving one reference-line end of the target (reshape) re-cuts the reshaped target, each after one evaluate_incremental with no other action; slope and profile parameters reach the same path through the element stamp and are re-asserted by roofs and profiles-columns-beams for their kinds.
- Order independence: a target with Subtract, Intersect and Add operators created in all 24 permutations of command order, and 200 seeded random add/remove/re-add sequences, yields bit-identical meshes (TriMesh ==).
- Mutual relations: a slab subtracts a wall and the wall subtracts the slab; both volumes equal their own volume minus the overlap and evaluation terminates (SOL-024).
- Deleting the operator, or RemoveSolidOperations, gives a target mesh bit-identical to a project in which the relation never existed; undo restores the cut (SOL-023 geometry clause).
- SOL-027 conflict test: two walls joined automatically at an L corner (the L junction of wall.rs, or junction.rs once junction-engine has landed) with their reference lines on the outer faces, so the mitre gives each wall half of the corner square; an explicit subtract of B from A removes A's half (the intersection volume of A's result with B's own body is 0) while A elsewhere equals its junction-cleaned body; without the operation the junction result is unchanged; once junction-engine's priorities exist, the explicit result is the same with either wall given the higher junction priority ('regardless of automatic junction priorities').
- Failure test with a kernel double that fails: the target keeps the mesh of the previous revision, ModelGeometry.problems names target, operator and reason, nothing panics; on a fresh full evaluation the target keeps its pre-operation body (NFR-REL-005 clause).
- Cross-storey test: an operator homed on the upper storey cuts a target on the ground storey at the correct world height.
- The framework's incremental-versus-full property test, extended with random solid-operation edits, stays bit-identical for all elements without kernel problems; editing B in a chain B -> A -> C (A target of B, C target of A) leaves C clean.
- Satisfies SOL-020 (evaluation), SOL-022 (associativity of the model geometry; persistence is 08, all views 17), the geometry-restore clause of SOL-023, SOL-024 and SOL-027.
notes: SRS: SOL-020 SOL-022 SOL-023 SOL-024 SOL-027. SOL-023 here is its geometry-restore clause. Also NFR-REL-005. Slope and profile changes are re-asserted by roofs and profiles-columns-beams. The Boolean semantics decisions (Intersect operators as a union, material of Added parts) are recorded in 18.

title: Edit stair turns, finishes and break line; insert nodes in plan
description:
WHY: The options of this epic are useless until users can set them: STA-020 segment types and corner turning types, STA-021 riser offsets (fixed or minimum, length or goings, linked, sum to one going), STA-022 automatic landings by inserting a node with minimum length and surplus placement, STA-023 equal flights, STA-029 the lock-baseline option, STA-040 finish settings for flights and landings, STA-041 structure settings, and STA-045 the break-line height (cut plane, custom height, n-th riser). STA-011's 'unlock the baseline' alternative needs a label in stair-solver-tool-11's conflict dialog once task 14 offers it. ELM-017 requires range checks with explanations and live dependent values (riser counts) while editing. What exists: stair-solver-tool-10's stair fields, read-out (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs) and rules_grid with the Automatic landing length row, the stair tool in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/stair.rs, the edit mode of selection-transforms-08 and the plan context menu (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:728).

WHAT: Stair settings, placed into the four sections of the settings-dialog framework (properties-and-dialogs-09) as FieldSpecs (properties-and-dialogs-05) if that epic has landed, otherwise as stair-specific groups beside stair-solver-tool-10's fields in ui/stair.rs and ui/properties.rs: Geometry and positioning gets Segments and turns (per segment: flight or landing; per corner: turning type, before and after offsets with unit length or goings, fixed or minimum, linked, sum to one going), Landings (minimum from the rule or n goings, surplus placement; the minimum length and its flag stay in the rules_grid row) and Distribution (equal flights, lock baseline); Model and appearance gets Finish (flight and landing tabs: tread and riser thickness, nosing, gaps, open risers, materials) and Structure (flight and landing: none, smooth, stepped, thicknesses, material); Plan display gets the break line (cut plane, height, n-th riser). Live read-outs of risers per flight, going and landing lengths re-run solve() and layout() on the draft candidate as stair-solver-tool-10 does for its read-out (ELM-017). Per-segment and per-corner lists are a list field kind (added to the FieldSpec framework if missing, documented for curtain-wall grids). Edit mode (12): context-menu 'Insert node' on a selected flight inserts at the clicked point through Stair::insert_node (03) and 'Remove node' on an automatic landing calls remove_node, each one UpdateElements. Lock baseline is a plain field: the stored baseline already holds the effective nodes because resolve stores the adjusted baseline (02), so switching the lock on changes nothing else. The stair rule conflict dialog of stair-solver-tool-11 (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs) labels task 14's Alternative::UnlockBaseline as 'Unlock the baseline' and applies it as one UpdateElements. The stair tool defaults (Subject::Defaults(stair), stair-solver-tool-10) expose the same groups, so new stairs placed with tools/stair.rs take the D.2 finish and structure. Out of scope: rule presets (STA-052, templates-presets), winders and stringers (railings-stairs-adv).
design: Reuse the settings-dialog framework (four sections and live preview, properties-and-dialogs-09) and declare every field as a FieldSpec in the stair module, so ui/fields.rs renders them without stair-specific code; per-segment and per-corner lists are a FieldSpec list kind (add it to the framework if missing, documented for curtain-wall grids later). The insert gesture uses the clicked plan point projected onto the walking line of the selected flight, through the point-input service so typed distances work. Lock switching is a single UpdateElements of lock_baseline, never two commands. Pitfalls: offsets in goings must be shown with their unit and never converted to lengths in the field; the dialog draft must re-run the layout for live values without executing commands; keyboard focus must not move while typed input is active (INP-003). Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs (settings dialog and stair conflict modal), ui/fields.rs (properties-and-dialogs, if landed), ui/stair.rs (stair-solver-tool-10), crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs context_menu (:728) and edit mode (selection-transforms-08), crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/stair.rs (stair-solver-tool-08), crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/edit.rs (03), stair/conflict.rs Alternative::UnlockBaseline (14).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: open the stair settings dialog on samples::u_stair(), set the flight tread thickness to 0.040 m: one UpdateElements, the model value is 0.040 and the plan and 3D caches regenerate; entering -0.010 is rejected inline with an explanation and the model is unchanged (ELM-017).
- kittest: in edit mode, right-click inside flight 1 and choose 'Insert node': the stair gains an automatic landing (one more Landing part) and one undo restores the original; 'Remove node' on that landing removes it again.
- kittest: switching Lock baseline on keeps the displayed node positions (stored nodes equal the layout nodes); a later storey-height change keeps them (STA-029 through the UI).
- kittest: a locked stair made stale by a storey-height change opens the conflict dialog (origin Stale, stair-solver-tool-11) with 'Unlock the baseline'; choosing it unlocks and re-solves with moved nodes as one undo step (STA-011 alternative).
- kittest: break line 'n-th riser' with 5 moves the plan symbol's break station to riser 5 (asserted on the regenerated PlanDrawing).
- Changing the corner offsets to Goings(0.5) linked updates the live riser read-out without committing until OK (live dependent values); the offset field shows its unit as goings.
- A new stair placed with the stair tool carries the D.2 finish and structure from the defaults.
- Satisfies the user-facing part of STA-020, STA-021, STA-022, STA-023, STA-029, STA-040, STA-041 and the break-line option of STA-045.
notes:
SRS: STA-020 STA-021 STA-022 STA-023 STA-029 STA-040 STA-041 STA-045
Related: ELM-017 (range checks, live dependent values), STA-011 (unlock-the-baseline alternative in the conflict dialog).

title: Add the SolidKernel trait with IFX-038 result normalisation
description:
WHY: SOL-020 (M) needs one Boolean entry point for every later stage (openings cutting several elements, solid operations, trims, splits), and NFR-REL-005 (M) requires that failed Boolean operations are rejected with an explanatory message and never silently create corrupt elements. IFX-038 (M): the IFCX mesh has no normals, so 'vertices shall therefore not be shared across hard edges: each planar face region gets its own vertices', vertices are shared only across smooth edges, and no single mesh may exceed 65,535 points; IFX-032 (M): closed, 2-manifold, outward-oriented meshes without degenerate, duplicate or unreferenced elements. Today TriMesh (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:7-13) gives each planar face its own vertices by construction (add_face, mesh.rs:81-89) and check_closed exists but runs only in tests (technical debt); a Boolean engine returns merged vertices and re-triangulated faces, so its output must be normalised back to the IFX-038 convention (gap-analysis IFX-038: partial).

WHAT: Kept as is: TriMesh, add_face and check_closed (mesh.rs:7-13, 81-89, 116-160) and the generator-level IFX-032 validity that is done today, regressed by the existing mesh.rs tests (box_is_closed_with_unit_volume: 24 points for a box). New: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kernel/{mod.rs, manifold.rs, null.rs, convert.rs}: `trait SolidKernel: Send + Sync { fn boolean(&self, op: BoolOp, a: &TriMesh, b: &TriMesh) -> Result<KernelMesh, KernelError>; fn union_all(&self, meshes: &[TriMesh]) -> Result<KernelMesh, KernelError>; fn split(&self, mesh: &TriMesh, plane: Plane) -> Result<(KernelMesh, KernelMesh), KernelError>; }` with BoolOp::{Union, Intersect, Subtract}, KernelMesh { mesh: TriMesh, sources: Vec<Source> } (per triangle: input index and input face region), KernelError::{Unavailable, InvalidInput(usize, MeshIssue), Failed(String), InvalidResult(MeshIssue)} with user-facing Display, default_kernel() -> &'static dyn SolidKernel (ManifoldKernel with the `manifold` feature, NullKernel returning Unavailable without it) and the convenience kernel::boolean(op, a, b) named by the epic acceptance. convert.rs: every input is checked with check_closed and refused with InvalidInput before any FFI call; face regions are the vertex-connected components of the TriMesh (the IFX-038 convention of add_face) and become Manifold face ids; coincident points are merged on the MODEL_TOLERANCE grid; output triangles are grouped by (input, face id) and every group gets its own vertices, so hard edges never share vertices while smooth regions of one input face keep theirs; groups and triangles are emitted in a canonical order; the result passes check_closed except TooManyPoints (partitioned in 03) or the call fails with InvalidResult; an empty result is Ok with an empty mesh. Out of scope: Body_n partitioning and writer checks (03), evaluation stages (05), extrusion sweeps (06), use of the material provenance (07).
design: Keep the trait mesh-in/mesh-out on TriMesh so the stages never see FFI types and a pure-Rust kernel can be swapped (technology-choices). Vertex-connected components are a reliable face-region key because every generator writes planar faces with their own vertices; when curved-geometry adds smooth regions, a smooth surface is one component and stays one group, which is exactly IFX-038's 'shared only across smooth edges'. Canonical output order: groups sorted by (input index, face id), triangles within a group by their smallest quantised vertex key, so property tests can compare with ==. Manifold's runOriginalID identifies the input mesh of each triangle and faceID its region; request both through the binding of 01. Pitfalls: check_closed merges on MERGE_STEP = 1e-6 (mesh.rs:53) while MODEL_TOLERANCE is 1e-5 m; use the framework's tolerance module for the kernel merge and document which step wins; cache input validation per Arc so stages do not re-check the same body; never feed a mesh with several components to boolean unless intended (union_all handles several). Pointers: mesh.rs:7-13, 47-53, 81-89, 116-160; extrude.rs; the framework's tolerance module (element-kind-framework-01).
acceptance_criteria:
- Property tests in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/kernel.rs with a seeded xorshift PRNG (no new dependency; the seed is printed on failure), 300 cases per operation over random boxes, rotated boxes and extruded concave prisms built with extrude(): every non-empty result passes check_closed (closed, 2-manifold, outward-oriented, no degenerate, duplicate or unreferenced elements), has positive signed volume, satisfies |A u B| = |A| + |B| - |A n B| within 1e-9 relative, and every point is referenced only by triangles of one plane (hard-edge test, IFX-038).
- Determinism: identical inputs give bit-identical TriMesh values; union_all of a shuffled input list equals union_all of the sorted list.
- Coplanar regression fixtures: a wall standing on a slab (touching faces) unions into one closed solid; a body minus itself is empty; face-touching boxes intersect to empty; a box flush with a face subtracts to a closed notch; each case is listed in the NFR-MNT-005 regression table.
- An open or inside-out input returns Err(InvalidInput) without calling the FFI layer; NullKernel returns Err(Unavailable), and the --no-default-features job runs the tests in their 'unavailable' form.
- split of a unit cube by an inclined plane returns two closed solids whose volumes sum to 1.0 within 1e-12.
- Smooth-edge clause: a synthetic input whose curved side is one vertex-connected region (a 32-sided prism whose side quads share their vertices) minus a box keeps shared vertices inside the remaining side region and shares none across its hard edges to the caps or the cut faces (IFX-038 'shared only across smooth edges'; curved-geometry and free-form-solids re-assert it with real kinds).
- Satisfies the kernel clauses of SOL-020 and IFX-038 (hard-edge and smooth-edge vertices, closedness, outward orientation) for every Boolean result, and the NFR-REL-005 clause that a failed Boolean returns Err.
notes: SRS: IFX-038 SOL-020. Also IFX-032 (done at generator level; kept and regressed) and NFR-REL-005 (re-asserted). Decision: an empty Boolean result is valid (the element has no body); the evaluation stage of 05 reports it.

title: Add the split-by-plane command to 3D and plan views
description:
WHY: EDT-024 (S) needs a user-facing command, and decision D-7 requires an explicit command rather than a gesture. The 3D view offers only picking and orbiting (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:160-195) and there is no plane input anywhere.

WHAT: Action::SplitByPlane ('Split by plane', Edit menu, enabled with a selection) starts a state machine in the active view: in 3D, three picked points on bodies (view3d::pick hit points, snapped through the 3D input service of 3d-input-navigation if present) or a picked face (the plane of the hit triangle) define the plane; in plan, two points define a vertical plane; a numeric option 'horizontal plane at elevation' is offered in both; a translucent preview quad and an arrow show the plane and the side that stays selected (Tab flips it); the third point or Enter executes Command::SplitByPlane, Esc cancels, and the status line prompts each step. Out of scope: input in section views (sections-elevations-dims).
design: Mirror the tool pattern of views/tools.rs (ToolState, prompt, add_point) for a 3D-capable tool and draw the preview quad with the overlay path of render3d.rs. Pitfalls: picked points are world coordinates, so convert to the target's storey-local frame when building HalfSpace; Alt-drag remains orbit; register the action through the command registry if commands-and-l10n has landed. Pointers: views/tools.rs:13-17 (ToolKind) and 285-451 (ToolState, prompt, add_point), view3d.rs:59-200, render3d.rs overlays, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs Edit menu.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of the state machine without egui: three points give the expected plane; collinear points are refused with a prompt; Tab flips the kept side; Esc resets.
- kittest: the Edit menu item is disabled without a selection and enabled with one; choosing it shows the first prompt in the status line.
- Integration test: the command emitted for a selected wall produces two elements through Command::SplitByPlane.
- Satisfies the user-facing part of EDT-024 under D-7.
notes: SRS: EDT-024. Decision D-7.

title: Add the export-visible-elements-only IFCX export
description:
WHY: IFX-068 (M): 'A separate "export visible elements only" IFCX export may exist, and it shall state its effect; it never replaces saving the project.' The epic acceptance requires that this variant omits hidden elements while the default export does not. Gap-analysis IFX-068: the variant does not exist (allowed) and the writer has no element filter (writer.rs:296-330).

WHAT: writer.rs: WriteOptions gains scope: WriteScope::{Full, Visible(BTreeSet<ElementId>)}; Visible writes only the listed elements (hosted elements only with their host), drops relation entries and opening cut references whose other end is not written, still writes evaluated meshes (targets of omitted operators stay cut), omits auxiliary elements entirely, and marks the project node with export information in archicraft::project (scope 'visible-only', view name) so ArchiCraft warns when such a file is opened as a project. archicraft-app: Action::ExportVisible ('Export visible elements only...') in the File menu; a modal states the effect ('Writes only the elements visible in the active view. Hidden layers, hidden elements and filtered elements are left out. This is an export, not a save of the project.'), then a file dialog; the visible set comes from the active view (layer visibility, plus the view's hidden set and filters once 3d-view-restrictions provides them); the document path, dirty flag, dataVersion and autosave are untouched. Out of scope: other formats, selection-only export.
design: One writer with a scope instead of a second writer keeps determinism and conformance shared. Pitfalls: header.id stays the project's (same dataset) and dataVersion is not incremented by an export; the blocking file dialog is existing debt (app.rs:197-208), follow the current pattern; if commands-and-l10n has introduced the command registry and string externalisation, register the action and strings there. Pointers: writer.rs WriteOptions and write(), app.rs save path, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs File menu, ui/dialogs.rs modal pattern.
acceptance_criteria:
- Writer test: with one wall on a hidden layer, Full writes it and Visible omits it; the Visible file passes conformance (IFX-006) and validate.rs reports no dangling references.
- App test: after the export the document is still dirty with an unchanged path and dataVersion, and Save still writes every element (IFX-068 'never replaces saving the project').
- Reader test: opening a visible-only file shows a warning naming the scope.
- kittest: the File menu item opens the dialog with the effect text.
- Satisfies the export-visible-elements-only clause of IFX-068.
notes: SRS: IFX-068.

title: Suppress seam edges between same-material stair parts
description:
WHY: STA-043 (S): treads and risers of the same material shall render as one continuous surface without seam edges (KB 303716, monolithic terrazzo finish). The epic acceptance requires that feature edges between same-material treads are suppressed. Gap row: feature_edges (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:239) works per mesh by coplanarity and would draw every tread and riser boundary; render3d draws them for every part (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:164).

WHAT: (1) Continuous finish: when a flight's tread and riser materials are equal, both gaps are zero and risers are closed, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/finish.rs emits one Finish shell per flight, the zigzag tread-and-riser profile extruded across the width, instead of separate Treads and Risers shells, so no seam exists inside the finish and IFCX writes one body. (2) Per-part edge flags: BodyPart gains seams: Vec<[DVec3; 2]> listing edges that lie inside a continuous same-material surface across parts (finish side faces flush with structure side faces, flight finish meeting the landing finish, tread ends against a same-material structure); the stair generator records them because it knows which faces it built coplanar. TriMesh::feature_edges gets a variant that skips a given seam set (keys through the tolerance module), used where crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs builds an element's feature edges (build_scene, or the per-element SceneCache block of element-kind-framework-11). The plan is unaffected (task 08 replaces the stair's generic plan slicing by its symbol), and IFCX only sees the merged Finish body of (1) (edges are not written). Out of scope: display styles (3d-display-styles), seams of other kinds (the flag is generic and documented for them).
design: Two complementary mechanisms, both cheap: geometry that is truly continuous (the zigzag Finish shell) needs no flags at all, and touching shells of different parts carry generator-known seam edges, as the roadmap asks ('seam suppression via per-part edge flags'). A generic post-pass that detects coplanar contacts between arbitrary meshes would be slower and fragile with the 1e-6 merge step, so it is not used. Seam keys are quantised point pairs (order-independent) computed with the shared tolerance module, so a seam listed by the generator matches the edges produced by feature_edges exactly. Pitfalls: a seam flag must never hide a real crease (only edges whose two adjacent visible faces are coplanar with equal normals qualify; assert it in debug builds); the continuous Finish profile must keep IFX-038 face-own vertices; changing the part grouping changes golden bytes, so re-bless after this task. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:239 (feature_edges), mesh.rs:53 (MERGE_STEP), evaluate.rs:22-28 (BodyPart), crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:150-172 (feature edges per part at :164).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair.rs monolithic_same_material_has_no_seams: a three-step flight whose finish and structure share one material yields feature edges (after seam filtering) only on the silhouette and the step corners: no edge lies in the side plane between finish and structure and none between tread and riser; the expected edge count is asserted.
- different_materials_keep_edges: with distinct finish and structure materials the boundary edges are present.
- One Finish body per flight when tread and riser share the material with zero gaps and closed risers; separate Treads and Risers otherwise; every body still passes check_closed.
- mesh.rs unit test: feature edges with a seam set omit exactly the listed edges of a box pair.
- render3d.rs unit test: build_scene edge count for the monolithic fixture equals the filtered count.
- IFCX: a flight with a continuous finish is written with one Finish body child that passes written_meshes_are_closed_bodies; stairs.ifcx is re-blessed and its diff reviewed.
- Satisfies STA-043.
notes: SRS: STA-043

title: Partition oversized bodies into closed Body_n parts before writing
description:
WHY: IFX-038 (M): 'No single mesh shall have more than 65,535 points, because the reference viewer uses 16-bit indices. Larger bodies ... are split into several parts. A split body shall be partitioned into closed sub-solids ..., each written as its own Body_<n> child; IFX-032 applies to each sub-solid.' Gap-analysis IFX-038 (partial): no splitting of large bodies; the writer writes a part of any size (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:372-381) and, per the technical debt, never verifies closedness or the point limit before writing. Boolean results with many cuts (and later terrain) reach the limit, and the epic acceptance asks for at most 65,535 points per Body_n with validity enforced before writing.

WHAT: Kept: MAX_MESH_POINTS and its check inside check_closed (mesh.rs:47-49, 126-128) and the 65,535-point check of conformance/check.ts:92. Added here: a normalisation stage normalize_parts(parts, kernel) -> Result<Vec<BodyPart>, GeometryError> at the end of element evaluation in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs (it becomes the Normalize stage of 05): each visible part is checked with check_closed; a part over MAX_MESH_POINTS is split recursively with kernel.split at the median of its longest bounding-box axis until every piece is within the limit; pieces are named Body_1..Body_n for a single-material body and <part name>_<n> for named parts (Skin_2_1, ...), keep their PartRole and material, and get v5 sub-node ids from their names (IFX-010); Void parts are only checked. A part that fails check_closed becomes a geometry problem of the element, which keeps its last valid body (the failure path of 05). writer.rs write_element checks every part again (check_closed including the point limit) and refuses to write an invalid mesh, with a warning naming the element (strict writing; never truncating). conformance/check.ts gains an edge-pairing closedness check per mesh so the viewer job also enforces IFX-032. Bodies within the limits are untouched, so existing goldens stay byte-identical. Out of scope: terrain TIN tiling (terrain-and-site may reuse this splitter), vertex sharing across smooth edges (curved-geometry).
design: Partitioning at evaluation time rather than in the writer keeps the plan slice, the 3D scene and the file on the same parts (hash test of 17). Median splits along the longest axis converge quickly and keep pieces compact; each split is an exact kernel plane split, so the union of the pieces equals the original. Pitfalls: a split plane through existing vertices produces slivers, so offset it by half a MODEL_TOLERANCE step when it hits a vertex; the reader and the v5 ids key children by name, so an unsplit part must keep its name (Body); check.ts sees composed meshes, so pair edges on quantised coordinates. Pointers: evaluate.rs:21-36 (BodyPart, ElementGeometry), mesh.rs:47-49 and check_closed, writer.rs:361-406 (write_element, sub_node_id), conformance/check.ts:82-100.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a slab whose outline is a 40,000-gon (over 65,535 points after extrusion) evaluates into Body_1..Body_n, each passing check_closed with at most 65,535 points, with a total volume equal to the unsplit volume within 1e-9 relative and the same names and v5 ids on re-evaluation.
- Writer test: a hand-made ModelGeometry with an open part or a 70,000-point part is written without that mesh and with one warning naming the element; no mesh in any golden exceeds 65,535 points.
- conformance/check.ts fails a test file containing an open mesh and passes all goldens; conformance/run.sh is green.
- Round-trip test: the split slab saves and reopens with equal parameters and regenerates the same Body_n parts (IFX-064).
- Without the kernel feature, an oversized part is listed as a problem ('needs the solid kernel to be split for export') and is not written.
- Satisfies the partition and point-limit clauses of IFX-038 and the 'enforced before writing' part of the epic acceptance.
notes: SRS: IFX-038. Also IFX-032 and IFX-010 (re-asserted). The terrain clause of IFX-038 (TIN tiles extruded down to the terrain bottom) is re-asserted by terrain-and-site, which reuses this splitter's naming and checks. The naming of split skins (Skin_2_1) is a proposal; the SRS fixes only Body_<n>.

title: Add the stair rule set with the Appendix D.3 defaults
description:
WHY: The rise/going solver of SRS 4.20 is driven by a rule set. STA-005 (M) requires independent enable flags and min/max values for riser height R, going G, step formula 2R + G, ratio R/G, sum R + G, pitch atan(R/G) and the minimum walking-line distance from the inner edge, with inclusive bounds and the defaults of Appendix D.3 (R 150–200 mm, G 250–350 mm and 2R+G 600–650 mm enabled; R/G 0.10–1.00, R+G 450–600 mm and pitch 20°–30° disabled; walking line at least 300 mm enabled; automatic landing length at least 1.00 m enabled). PRJ-007 stores stair rule defaults in the project. The gap analysis finds no rule-set type and only wall and slab tool defaults in crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs:300-412. The solver, the element, the codec, the properties grid and later the DIN/ÖNORM presets of templates-presets all use this type, so it lands first and alone.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/ (mod.rs, registered in src/lib.rs, and rules.rs). RuleKind { RiserHeight, Going, StepFormula, Ratio, Sum, Pitch, WalkingLineDistance, LandingLength } with ALL, a stable code() (riserHeight, going, stepFormula, ratio, sum, pitch, walkingLineDistance, landingLength), from_code(), a message key plus the English label used to name rules in messages ('Riser height R', 'Going G', 'Step formula 2R+G', 'Ratio R/G', 'Sum R+G', 'Pitch', 'Walking line distance from inner edge', 'Automatic landing length') and its quantity (length in metres, ratio, angle in radians). Rule { enabled: bool, min: Option<f64>, max: Option<f64> }; RuleSet with one Rule per kind and get/get_mut by RuleKind; RuleSet::international() with the D.3 values; RuleSet::validate() (finite, min ≤ max, lengths > 0, ratio > 0, pitch inside (0°, 90°), min-only rows for walking line and landing) returning a message that names the rule. Bound { Min, Max } and Limit { rule, bound, value } are defined here for the solver's provenance. When regression-and-status-03's crates/archicraft-model/tests/defaults.rs exists, its Pending rows for the D.3 rule set (owner stair-solver-tool) become checks against RuleSet::international(). Out of scope: solver functions (task 02), storing the rules on a stair, in the defaults slot or in IFCX (tasks 04 and 07), the rules UI (task 10), national presets (STA-052, templates-presets).
design: Plain serde data (the model's convention, project.rs) with no behaviour beyond validation, so the codec and the presets reuse it unchanged. One Rule shape for every kind with Option bounds instead of per-kind structs: the solver iterates rules generically, the properties grid renders rows generically, and a disabled or absent bound is simply ignored. SI storage (metres, radians) as everywhere in the model (units.rs header comment); the UI formats millimetres and degrees. Bounds are inclusive and every comparison later uses MODEL_TOLERANCE from tolerance.rs (element-kind-framework-01) so that 3.000 m / 15 = 200 mm passes a 200 mm maximum. The landing-length row belongs to D.3 and is stored now so archicraft::stairRules keeps its shape when stair-body-plan consumes it (STA-022). Messages: expose RuleKind::key() for the string table of commands-and-l10n and keep label() as the English text. Pitfall: never compare D.3 values against computed numbers with == in tests; compare against the same literals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/rules.rs: RuleSet::international() matches Appendix D.3 row by row (enabled flags, min, max; pitch 20° and 30° stored as radians, compared with to_radians() of the literals).
- Independence (STA-005): toggling the enabled flag or a bound of any one rule leaves every other rule bit-identical (test iterates RuleKind::ALL).
- validate() rejects min > max, a negative length, a pitch of 90° or more, NaN and a max on the walking-line row, each with a message containing the rule's label; it accepts the D.3 set.
- RuleKind::ALL has 8 entries with unique codes; from_code(code()) round-trips; a serde round trip of RuleSet is lossless.
- If crates/archicraft-model/tests/defaults.rs (regression-and-status-03) is present, every D.3 row there is a check against RuleSet::international() instead of a Pending entry.
- cargo test -p archicraft-model, clippy --all-targets and fmt green; no other crate changes; the data part of STA-005 (flags, inclusive bounds, D.3 defaults) is in place.
notes: SRS: STA-005. Appendix D.3: R 0.150–0.200 m (on), G 0.250–0.350 m (on), 2R+G 0.600–0.650 m (on), R/G 0.10–1.00 (off), R+G 0.450–0.600 m (off), pitch 20°–30° (off), walking line ≥ 0.300 m (on), automatic landing ≥ 1.00 m (on, consumed by stair-body-plan). O-4: national presets replace this table later (templates-presets).

title: Combine operator bodies into subtract, intersect and add results
description:
WHY: SOL-020 (M): 'solid operations - subtract, intersect, add - between a set of target elements and a set of operator elements'. SOL-024 (M): 'One operation may involve several targets and several operators' and results 'do not depend on evaluation order'. SOL-026 (S) needs to know which faces of a result an operator created, and the SOL-021 variants (06) must plug into the subtract step. Gap-analysis SOL-020 and SOL-024: missing; nothing combines the bodies of different elements today (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:64-91 evaluates each element alone, 'no notion of raw vs modified body'), and the kernel of 02 offers only pairwise and batch Booleans on TriMesh. Keeping the semantics in one pure function, separate from the pipeline wiring of 05, makes them testable on meshes without a Project.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kernel/ops.rs: apply_operations(target: &[BodyPart], operators: &[OperatorBody], kernel: &dyn SolidKernel) -> Result<Vec<BodyPart>, OperationFailure>, with OperatorBody { id: ElementId, parts: Vec<(TriMesh, MaterialId)>, op: SolidOp } (SolidOp of 04; the operator already transformed into the target's frame by 05) and OperationFailure { operator: Option<ElementId>, error: KernelError }. Semantics, independent of the input order: operators are sorted by ElementId; the groups run in the fixed order Add, Intersect, Subtract; Add: the union of the Add operators' visible parts minus the target's visible parts becomes extra parts Added_1..Added_n (one per Add operator part, material per material_source: the operator part's material, or the target's first visible part's), and Added parts belong to the target from then on; Intersect: every visible part is intersected with the union of the Intersect operators (keep what lies inside any of them); Subtract: every visible part has the union of the Subtract operators removed, each Subtract operator mesh first passing through prepare_subtract(mesh, extrusion, target bounds), the identity until 06 adds the sweeps. Void parts (PartRole of host-openings) pass unchanged; a part that becomes empty is dropped; a target removed completely returns Ok with no visible parts. Every result triangle carries the kernel source of 02 (target part, or operator id and part) for 07. Out of scope: gathering operators, storey frames, dirty propagation and the failure fallback (05), sweeps (06), face material runs (07).
design: A fixed group order (add, intersect, subtract) and sorting operators by id before union_all make mixed operations order-free by construction and remove floating-point order effects; Booleaning parts one by one keeps layered skins separate closed parts (IFX-017). Pitfalls: union each operator group once, not once per target part; keep the function free of Project and storey data so 05 alone owns frames and failure fallback; give every operator part its own original id before the union so 07 can map provenance to materials. Pointers: kernel/mod.rs and convert.rs (02), evaluate.rs:21-36 (BodyPart), relations.rs SolidOp (04), PartRole (host-openings).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/kernel_ops.rs with boxes: subtract, intersect and add of a 2 x 1 x 1 m target and a 1 x 1 x 1 m operator overlapping it by half give 1.5 m3, 0.5 m3, and the unchanged 2.0 m3 target plus an Added_1 part of 0.5 m3, within 1e-12; two overlapping Subtract operators remove their union (overlap counted once).
- Order independence: all 24 permutations of a list with one Add, one Intersect and two Subtract operators give bit-identical parts (TriMesh ==), and 200 seeded random operator lists equal their sorted form (SOL-024).
- A layered target (two skins and a Void) keeps its skins as separate closed parts with their names and materials and an untouched Void (IFX-017, IFX-036); an emptied part is dropped; an operator enclosing the whole target leaves no visible parts and returns Ok.
- Added parts take the operator part's material with MaterialSource::Operator and the target's first visible part's material with Target, and are named Added_1..Added_n in operator order; an Added part overlapped by a Subtract operator of the same target is cut.
- A kernel double that fails on the second operator returns Err naming that operator; nothing panics.
- Every triangle of a result has a source naming a target part or an operator part.
- Satisfies the Boolean semantics of SOL-020 (subtract, intersect and add with several operators) and the order-independence clause of SOL-024 at mesh level; 05 wires it into the model.
notes: SRS: SOL-020 SOL-024. Also IFX-017 and IFX-036 (re-asserted). Decisions: several Intersect operators combine as a union (keep what lies inside any of them); Added parts with material_source Target take the target's first visible part material; Added parts go through Intersect and Subtract like any other target part.

title: Edit cut elements and the host of an opening in properties
description:
WHY: OPN-002 (M): 'The user can add and remove cut elements and reassign the host.' Decision D-7: explicit commands for every transfer operation, gestures are accelerators only. host-openings-12 built the opening section of the properties panel and left the cut-element list and the host change to this epic; the commands exist after 13 and the geometry and persistence after 14, but no UI reaches them (gap-analysis OPN-002: no cut-element list, no host reassignment command).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs, opening section: a 'Cut elements' list by name with click-to-select and a remove button per row (Command::RemoveOpeningCuts); 'Add selected elements', enabled when the selection is the opening plus at least one other element (Command::AddOpeningCuts); 'Use selected element as host', enabled when the selection is the opening plus exactly one other element (Command::ReassignHost). Command errors (non-solid element, host capability refused) appear in the status line through Workspace::error, and the commands' labels appear as Edit menu undo entries. Out of scope: picking cut elements graphically in 3D (a later accelerator under D-7), reveal materials on further cuts (OPN-008).
design: Follow the 'Add a command' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md: the buttons call Workspace::execute with the commands of 13, so undo, journal and status reporting stay shared. Pitfalls: the selection order is not reliable, so 'Use selected element as host' takes the element of the selection that is not the opening; cache the names of the cut list per revision instead of resolving them per frame; register actions and strings through commands-and-l10n's externalisation if it has landed. Pointers: ui/properties.rs opening section (host-openings-12), workspace.rs execute and error, tests/ui.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: with an opening and a second wall selected, 'Add selected elements' adds the wall to 'Cut elements' and the Edit menu shows the undo label; the row's remove button removes it and undo restores it.
- kittest: 'Use selected element as host' re-hosts the opening to the selected wall, the old host appears under 'Cut elements', and the old host's evaluated volume is unchanged.
- kittest: adding an element without a closed body (a second opening) leaves the project unchanged and shows the validator message in the status line.
- Satisfies the UI clauses of OPN-002 (add and remove cut elements, reassign the host) under D-7.
notes: SRS: OPN-002. Decision D-7.

title: Model stair segments, corner offsets, landings, finish and structure
description:
WHY: The stair delivered by stair-solver-tool is a single run: StairParams (crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/mod.rs: baseline, width, side, offset, riser and going specs, walking line, start/end, and the RuleSet of stair/rules.rs with the D.3 rows, including RuleKind::LandingLength, enabled, 1.00 m) embedded in the Stair payload of crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/stair.rs together with its VerticalLink, its single material and the stored StairSolution. There are no flights, landings, turns, finish or structure, so none of the shapes and parts of this epic can be expressed yet. STA-020 (M): straight, L-shaped, U-shaped and arbitrary polyline stairs; baseline segments have the type flight or landing, and every interior corner has a turning type, at least landing. STA-021 (M): a landing corner has two riser offsets (before and after the corner), each fixed or a minimum, in length units or in multiples of the going, optionally linked to be equal and optionally constrained to sum to one going; an offset of 0 places the riser flush with the landing edge. STA-022 (M): automatic landings have a minimum length (length or number of goings) and a surplus placement (landing start, end or split equally). STA-023 (M): both flights of a half-landing stair can get the same riser count. STA-029 (S): a lock-baseline option. STA-040 (M): the finish provides tread and riser thickness, tread overhang (nosing projection), tread and riser gaps, an open-riser (tread-only) mode and separate settings for flights and landings. STA-041 (S): flight and landing structures are selectable independently: none, or monolithic with a smooth or stepped underside (stepped: separate vertical and horizontal thickness), each with a material. STA-045 (M): the break line height is configurable (default the plan cut-plane height, alternatively a custom height or the n-th riser). Appendix D.2: monolithic structure, smooth underside, tread and riser finish 0.025 m; D.3: automatic landing length enabled, 1.00 m (already stored as the LandingLength rule). All twelve gap rows of this epic are 'missing'.

WHAT: archicraft-model only, as data plus validation, extending stair-solver-tool's types instead of adding a parallel definition, so that the solver (02, 14), the node edit (03), the bodies (04, 05), IFCX (11) and the UI (13) consume one definition. New module crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/config.rs (next to rules.rs, solver.rs, walking.rs, solve.rs and conflict.rs of stair-solver-tool) with SegmentKind {Flight, Landing}; StairSegment {kind, automatic}; TurningType {Landing} (#[non_exhaustive]; railings-stairs-adv adds the winder turns of STA-025/026); RiserOffset {amount: OffsetAmount {Length(f64), Goings(f64)}, mode: OffsetMode {Fixed, Minimum}}; StairCorner {turning, before, after, link_equal, sum_to_one_going}; LandingSettings {minimum: LandingMinimum {Rule, Goings(u16)}, surplus: SurplusPlacement {Start, End, Split}}, where Rule takes the enabled flag and the length of the existing RuleKind::LandingLength row of the stair's RuleSet (stair-solver-tool-01) and Goings(n) replaces that length by n goings, so the minimum keeps one source of truth; FinishSettings {tread_thickness, riser_thickness, nosing, tread_gap, riser_gap, open_risers, tread_material, riser_material} and StairFinish {flight, landing}; StructureSettings {None, Monolithic {underside: Underside {Smooth {thickness}, Stepped {vertical, horizontal}}, material}} and StairStructure {flight, landing}; BreakLine {CutPlane, Height(f64), Riser(u16)}. StairParams (stair/mod.rs, stair-solver-tool-03), which the Stair payload embeds unchanged, gains segments (one per baseline segment), corners (one per interior node), landing, equal_flights, lock_baseline, finish, structure and break_line, so solve(), the tool preview, the properties and the archicraft::stair codec keep sharing one parameter type. StairParams::sync_topology() keeps segments and corners in step with the baseline and is called by the stair's normalising Kind::validate (stair-solver-tool-04), which also copies `before` to `after` when link_equal is set; StairParams::validate_config(), called from the same hook, rejects negative or non-finite thicknesses, gaps, nosings and offsets, Riser(0), LandingMinimum::Goings(0), zero stepped thicknesses, fixed offsets that violate sum_to_one_going, and unknown materials (a negative landing length is already rejected by RuleSet::validate). Materials: Stair.material (stair-solver-tool-04) stays what Kind::material() returns and is the initial value of every finish and structure material slot; the kind's material-reference hooks list and replace every slot so DeleteMaterial reassigns them. The stair's transform hook (stair-solver-tool-04, signature of selection-transforms-02) keeps segments, corners, finish and structure unchanged under mirror and rotation. The stair defaults slot that stair-solver-tool-04 filled in crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs gets the D.2/D.3 values. Until task 11 lands, the archicraft::stair reader of stair-solver-tool-07 (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs) fills these defaults, so round-trip equality and stairs.ifcx stay unchanged. Out of scope: riser distribution, landing geometry and the lock behaviour (02, 14, 03), bodies, plan output, IFCX members (11), UI (13), winder turns and stringers (railings-stairs-adv).
design: Plain data with pure normalisation, the pattern of plan-views-browser-01. Putting the new fields into StairParams rather than the Stair envelope keeps stair-solver-tool's rule that the solver modules see no ids, storeys or elements, and the solver, the tool preview and the codec already take StairParams. Offsets in goings stay symbolic (Goings(0.5)) and are never converted at input time, because the going changes with the storey height and the lock state; the solver resolves them. The landing minimum reuses the D.3 LandingLength rule (stair-solver-tool-01 stored it 'so archicraft::stairRules keeps its shape when stair-body-plan consumes it'); LandingMinimum only adds the goings alternative of STA-022. Segments and corners are parallel vectors indexed by baseline segment and interior node, so node insertion (03) is one insert in each; a collinear interior corner with turning Landing is how an in-run automatic landing is represented (StairSegment.automatic marks the flights it created), which gives L/U corner landings and in-run landings one mechanism. No Winder variant now; #[non_exhaustive] keeps matches in other crates future-proof. Material references: if layer-structures already added a multi-material hook to the Kind trait, implement it; otherwise add materials()/replace_material(old, new) with defaults delegating to material/set_material (element-kind-framework-02) and use it in plan_delete_material (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:520) and the defaults-slot loop. Pitfalls: every StairParams literal in tests and samples must set the new fields (add StairParams::with_defaults); checking the finish thickness against the riser height needs the solved R and belongs to the part report of task 07, not to validation; keep the field order stable for the archicraft::stair JSON of task 11; serde(default) on the new fields keeps journals of older sessions replayable. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/mod.rs and rules.rs, kinds/stair.rs (stair-solver-tool-01/03/04), crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs (defaults slot), crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs (envelope).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/stair.rs: a new stair from the template slot has 0.025 m tread and riser thickness on flights and landings, Monolithic Smooth structure on flights and landings, LandingMinimum::Rule backed by the enabled 1.00 m RuleKind::LandingLength row, BreakLine::CutPlane and lock_baseline false (Appendix D.2, D.3).
- sync_topology: adding a node through UpdateElements yields params.segments.len() == nodes - 1 and params.corners.len() == nodes - 2; the new corner is a landing turn with Fixed Length(0) offsets; removing a node drops the matching corner; the other segment kinds and corner settings keep their positions.
- link_equal copies the before offset to after on normalisation; two Fixed offsets in goings that do not sum to one going with sum_to_one_going set are rejected with an explanation; Minimum offsets with sum_to_one_going are accepted (the solver resolves them).
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: UpdateElements with each invalid value (negative tread thickness, negative gap, NaN nosing, Riser(0), LandingMinimum::Goings(0), Stepped {vertical: 0}, unknown material) returns CommandError::Invalid with a message naming the stair and the field and leaves the project unchanged; valid changes execute, undo and redo to the identical project.
- DeleteMaterial of the finish material reassigns tread, riser and structure references to the replacement material; undo restores them.
- The transform hook's mirror swaps the stair side (stair-solver-tool-04 behaviour) and leaves segments, corners, finish and structure untouched; rotation leaves them untouched.
- All new types derive Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize and Deserialize (journal and autosave), and the new StairParams fields carry serde(default); the stair-solver-tool tests (crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs, commands.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair.rs), crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs and every golden file including stairs.ifcx pass unchanged.
- The data side of STA-020, STA-021, STA-022, STA-023, STA-029, STA-040, STA-041 and the break-line option of STA-045 is in place.
notes:
SRS: STA-020 STA-021 STA-022 STA-023 STA-029 STA-040 STA-041 STA-045
Appendix D.2: stair width 1.00 m, monolithic structure, smooth underside, tread and riser finish 0.025 m. D.3: automatic landing length enabled, minimum 1.00 m (RuleKind::LandingLength of stair-solver-tool-01).
Open: D.2 gives no structure thickness; proposed defaults 0.15 m smooth waist (perpendicular to the pitch), 0.15 m / 0.15 m stepped vertical/horizontal and 0.20 m landing structure, to be confirmed and added to Appendix D. The default surplus placement (Split proposed) and the default of equal_flights (true proposed) are not specified by the SRS.

title: Round-trip stair segments, finishes and solver results in IFCX
description:
WHY: STA-051 (M): stairs shall be written to IFCX as IfcStair with IfcStairFlight, IfcSlab (landing) and, where present, IfcMember (stringer) children (Table 5-1); solver inputs and results are stored in the ArchiCraft namespace. IFX-016 (M) is re-asserted with a real compound kind (element-kind-framework-07 proved it with a test kind), IFX-024 (M) stores the landing predefined type in the archicraft namespace, IFX-010 gives parts v5 ids and IFX-062 requires migrating older files. The epic acceptance: the AS-01 U-stair exports IfcStair with IfcStairFlight and IfcSlab landing children and passes conformance. Gap row STA-051 lists the missing classes, reader support, schema and golden file. What exists: stair-solver-tool-07's codec crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs writes archicraft::stair (base parameters and a solution object) and archicraft::stairRules (including landingLength), the sample samples::stairs() (stairs A, B and an L-shaped stair C) and the golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/stairs.ifcx; tasks 04-07 already produce the classed children.

WHAT: Extend that codec (KindCodec of element-kind-framework-06) instead of adding a second one: archicraft::stair gains segments, corners (turning, before/after {amount, unit: length|goings, mode: fixed|minimum}, linkEqual, sumToOneGoing), landing {minimum: rule|goings, goings?, surplus: start|end|split} (the minimum length and its flag stay in archicraft::stairRules.landingLength), equalFlights, lockBaseline, finish {flight, landing}, structure {flight, landing} and breakLine {mode, value}; the existing solution object gains flights [{risers, goings, going}] (tasks 02, 14) and the layout results (landing lengths and surpluses, effective nodes). The stored solution keeps stair-solver-tool-07's keep-last-valid semantics; the layout results are informational and regenerated on read. Declarations in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs with enumerations from the model's ALL arrays. Format version: follow element-kind-framework-12's rule in alpha/mod.rs; the new members are optional with defaults (a stair written before this epic reads as one flight per baseline segment with landing turns and D.2 finish and structure), so FORMAT_VERSION is bumped, with a step in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs, only if a reader-visible shape has to change. Landing parts carry IfcSlab and PredefinedType::Landing (IFC literal LANDING, element-kind-framework-05) in the archicraft namespace (IFX-024): PartSpec gains predefined_type: Option<PredefinedType>, written on the part node like element predefined types. Fixtures: register samples::u_stair() (task 02, the AS-01 U-stair: storeys 0 and 3.30 m, 22 risers, width 1.00 m, landing segment, D.2 finish and structure) in samples::catalogue(), which feeds crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs, with the new golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/u-stair.ifcx; extend the existing samples::stairs() with a straight stair with an automatic landing, an L with offsets and an open-riser stair with stepped structure, and re-bless stairs.ifcx; conformance/check.ts asserts the Table 5-1 child classes of IfcStair. Out of scope: IfcMember stringers (STA-042, railings-stairs-adv), mesh-versus-parameter comparison on open (IFX-065).
design: Write inputs at full precision and results rounded like parameters, never meshes; results exist so other tools and later versions can read the solved stair without re-solving (STA-051), but the reader always regenerates them from the inputs to avoid two sources of truth. Keep the per-kind codec self-contained in the stair module so the module-layout test of element-kind-framework stays green.
