The predefined type on a part node is the one exception to 'parts carry no archicraft attributes'; check that conformance/check.ts and the viewer composition accept it. Fixture u_stair() uses storeys 0 and 3.30 m so that 22 risers are admissible (STA-004 test: 3.300 m / 22 = 150 mm); reference-models later places the same generator in the AS-01 house. Pitfalls: golden bytes depend on shell order and seam grouping (04-06) and on FORMAT_VERSION, so bless once here and review the diff for non-archicraft changes (IFX-063); FixtureBuilder v5 ids keep the goldens deterministic; the test-kinds golden of the framework must stay untouched. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs (stair-solver-tool-07), alpha/mod.rs and alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework-12), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:15 (FORMAT_VERSION) and declarations(), writer.rs:46 (sub_node_id), :192 (element_attributes), :361-417 (write_element), reader.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:30/131/198, conformance/check.ts:67-103, crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: round_trip_restores_the_editable_model is equal for samples::u_stair() and the extended samples::stairs() (every new parameter); regenerated_geometry_matches_the_stored_geometry is byte-identical.
- stair_children_are_classed_parts: in u-stair.ifcx the IfcStair node is a child of its storey and has children Flight_1 (IfcStairFlight), Landing_1 (IfcSlab with the archicraft predefined type LANDING) and Flight_2 (IfcStairFlight) with paths Uuid::new_v5(stair, role), each with Body children (Finish or Treads/Risers, Structure) inheriting material nodes; written_meshes_are_closed_bodies covers them.
- The solution object of u_stair() reports flights with risers [11, 11], riser height 0.150 m and the going of the layout.
- golden_files_are_reproduced and catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files cover the new u-stair.ifcx and the re-blessed stairs.ifcx; the other goldens (including compound-parts.ifcx of element-kind-framework-07) stay byte-identical; conformance/run.sh is green on all goldens with the extended check.ts (IfcStair children classes, every part classed and named).
- compatibility test: a copy of stairs.ifcx as written before this task (frozen at the start of the task under crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/ and never regenerated) loads with one flight per baseline segment, landing turns and defaults, one warning per missing member (reader.or pattern) and no error; if FORMAT_VERSION was bumped, it goes through the migration and reports it.
- The archicraft::stair declaration validates the written values (container_matches_the_ifcx_json_schema and the in-file schema check).
- Satisfies STA-051 (stringer clause deferred with STA-042) and re-asserts IFX-016, IFX-024 for landings and IFX-010 for parts.
notes:
SRS: STA-051
Related: IFX-016, IFX-024, IFX-010, IFX-062. Table 5-1: Stair -> IfcStair under the storey with IfcStairFlight, IfcSlab (landings), IfcMember (stringers).

title: Add the upward and downward extrusion variants of subtraction
description:
WHY: SOL-021 (M): 'Subtraction shall offer variants in which the operator body is first extruded upward (+Z) or downward (-Z) to infinity. For example, a roof then removes everything of a wall above the roof's underside, and a slab removes all terrain above it.' TER-006 (terrain-and-site) and the AS-01 gable walls rely on it. Gap-analysis SOL-021: missing; the up- and down-facing outlines of a body exist (mesh.rs:196-203), but a footprint prism built from them would be wrong for inclined undersides such as roof planes.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kernel/sweep.rs: sweep_z(kernel, body: &TriMesh, dir: ZDir, limit: f64) -> Result<TriMesh, KernelError>: for Up every face region of the body whose normal has z < 0 (for Down z > 0) is extruded vertically to the limit plane as a closed prism, and the prisms are unioned with the body through union_all; vertical faces contribute nothing. The limit is finite: the target's bounding-box top + 1.0 m for Up and bottom - 1.0 m for Down, in the target's frame, so coordinates stay small (NFR-ACC-004) and the result equals 'to infinity' for that target. prepare_subtract in apply_operations (18) sweeps every Subtract operator with Extrusion::Up or Down before the subtract union, with the limit taken from the bounds of the target parts it receives. Out of scope: the UI choice (12), persistence (08).
design: The union of prisms over the down-facing faces equals the upward sweep of the body: every vertical line through the body enters it through a down-facing face, and everything above that entry point lies in the sweep. Merging coplanar triangles is unnecessary because face regions are already planar groups (IFX-038 convention). Pitfalls: neighbouring prisms touch along coplanar side faces, so add the case to the coplanar fixtures of 02; take the limit from the target, not the whole model; transform the operator into the target frame before sweeping. Pointers: mesh.rs:196-203 (facing outlines), extrude.rs, kernel/mod.rs (02), apply_operations and prepare_subtract (18).
acceptance_criteria:
- kernel test: a wedge whose underside rises 1.0 m over 4.0 m, swept Up, gives a closed solid equal to the region above the underside up to the limit (analytic volume within 1e-9 relative); a box swept Down reaches the lower limit; vertical faces are ignored.
- solid_ops.rs: a slab operator subtracted with Up from a 2.80 m wall leaves exactly the wall part below the slab underside; with Down it leaves the part above the slab top.
- apply_operations test with the wedge as operator: the remaining wall top follows the incline (gable stand-in for the roofs epic).
- Moving the operator up by 0.10 m raises the remaining wall top by 0.10 m (SOL-022 with the variant).
- Satisfies SOL-021.
notes: SRS: SOL-021. The 1.0 m margin beyond the target bounds is a proposal.

title: Insert baseline nodes that create automatic landings with surplus
description:
WHY: STA-022 (M): inserting a node on a flight shall create an automatic landing; its length is at least the configured minimum (length or number of goings), and any surplus from whole-step quantization is placed at the landing start, at its end, or split equally, as configured. Appendix D.3: automatic landing length enabled, minimum 1.00 m. The epic acceptance requires that inserting a node creates an automatic landing and that the surplus is placed per option. The gap row lists 'EDT insert node / reshape' as a dependency, but edit-reshape-palette works on outlines and is not a prerequisite of this epic, so the stair gets its own baseline edit in the model.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/edit.rs: Stair::insert_node(segment, at: DVec2) -> Result<Stair, StairEditError> projects `at` onto the flight segment and splits it into two flights (automatic = true) joined by a collinear corner with turning Landing; Stair::remove_node(corner) merges two automatic flights again. stair/layout.rs (02) gains in-run landings for collinear landing corners: the landing span is the gap between the last riser of the lower flight and the first riser of the upper flight; its length is the minimum (LandingMinimum::Rule: the length of the stair's LandingLength rule when enabled, 0 when disabled; LandingMinimum::Goings(n): n x going) plus the surplus; the nominal landing (the minimum) sits at the end, start or centre of that span according to SurplusPlacement (Start: surplus before the nominal landing; End: after it; Split: half on each side), and the node is the reference of the nominal landing. Unlocked (STA-029 off): the landing gets exactly the minimum, the node is moved onto the nominal landing and the following nodes move (the per-flight node adjustment of solve.rs, task 02); locked (task 14): the stored nodes stay, the solver's going is kept, the lower flight gets the whole goings that place the node inside the nominal landing, and the remaining length of the fixed run is the surplus; only if the landing would fall below its minimum does the going adapt within the enabled rules, otherwise solve returns a RuleConflict with task 14's UnlockBaseline alternative. LandingRun.surplus and surplus_at carry the result. Rejections with explanation: insertion on a landing segment, within MODEL_TOLERANCE of an existing node, or where a flight would get no riser. The edit is one UpdateElements (one undo step). Out of scope: the UI gesture and node removal command in edit mode (13), winder turns.
design: The collinear landing corner from task 01 is the only new topology: no new segment type and no new part role scheme (the landing becomes Landing_n in walking-line order, the flights renumber, and Selection::retain_valid drops stale part references). Choose the lower flight's riser count by scanning the admissible counts and taking the one whose nominal landing contains the node, ties to the lower count; this is deterministic and keeps the node visually inside the landing. Keep the surplus semantics in one function (landing_span(run_length, risers, going, minimum, placement)) with a doc comment and a worked example, because the exact Archicad behaviour (KB 303685, 304145) is described only loosely; the test table is the contract. Pitfalls: insertion near a corner landing must not create two landings closer than the minimum (reject); STA-024 end conditions shift the station of the first riser; floating-point quantisation of goings uses the tolerance module (floor((x + tol) / going)). Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/layout.rs and solve.rs (02, 14), crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/config.rs (01), crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs UpdateElements planning.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_layout.rs automatic_landing_has_minimum_length: unlocked straight 22-riser stair, going 0.300 m, LandingMinimum::Rule with the D.3 1.00 m rule: a node inserted 2.00 m along the walking line gives two flights, one LandingRun with source Corner and length 1.00 m, and the sum of risers stays 22.
- surplus_placement (locked): a straight run of fixed length between first and last riser (22 risers, going 0.300, minimum 1.00 m, surplus computed in the test from the run length): landing length = minimum + surplus for Start, End and Split, the node lies at the end, start or centre of the nominal landing as specified, and the flight riser counts and landing stations match the table in the test within 1e-9.
- LandingMinimum::Goings(3) with going 0.300 gives a landing of at least 0.90 m; with the LandingLength rule disabled the landing is exactly the quantisation remainder.
- A locked insertion whose landing would fall below the minimum and whose going cannot adapt within the rules returns RuleConflict offering UnlockBaseline (task 14); the project is unchanged.
- remove_node on an untouched automatic landing restores the original stair (equality).
- Inserting on a landing segment, on an existing node, or so close to an end that a flight would have no riser returns StairEditError with an explanation; crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: UpdateElements with the inserted node executes, undoes and redoes to the identical project.
- Satisfies STA-022 in the model; together with 02 the locked case keeps STA-029 (nodes authoritative).
notes:
SRS: STA-022 STA-029
Appendix D.3: automatic landing length enabled, 1.00 m.
Open: confirm the surplus semantics (nominal landing at the start/end/centre of the span, node as its reference) against KB 303685 and 304145 before the UI exposes it.

title: Draw the upper stair part on the storey above via display range
description:
WHY: STA-046 (S): by default a stair shall appear on its home storey and on the storey above, where only the part above the break line is drawn; the display range can be extended to all storeys the stair intersects (ELM-008). ELM-008 (M) lists 'all storeys it intersects' for stairs and draws outlines on other storeys in the project-wide remote style; VIEW-011 (M) applies that style. The epic acceptance: the storey above shows only the part above the break line (ELM-008 range). Gap row: elements appear only on their home storey (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:109-120); plan-views-browser has since added display ranges, cross-storey admission and the remote style, and explicitly left the stair break-line display to this epic.

WHAT: The stair KindDescriptor offers every ELM-008 display range of plan-views-browser-01 except Custom (which ELM-009 reserves for slabs, roofs and terrain): HomeOnly, Intersecting, HomeAndAbove (default), HomeAndBelow, HomeAboveAndBelow and All (descriptor fields display_ranges and default_display_range; template defaults updated). stair/symbol.rs (08) handles relation Above(1): only the lines beyond the break station computed with the home storey's break height (the home storey's effective cut plane for CutPlane), drawn as Below class (solid, the stair lies below the upper storey's cut plane), plus the break line, the walking-line end with its arrow and the label Down at the top. Every other admitted storey (Intersecting, HomeAndBelow, HomeAboveAndBelow or All) gets the stair outline from the layout as remote lines (PlanElement.remote of plan-views-browser-03, drawn by plan-views-browser-05 in the project-wide RemoteStoreyStyle of its side), because a symbol kind emits no generic outline. Plan admission itself stays plan-views-browser's DisplayRange::admits. Cache invalidation: the storey-above plan depends on the home storey's view range, so crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs invalidates the plans of every storey that displays a changed stair and of the storey above when the home storey's cut plane changes. Out of scope: drawing (10), railings on the storey above (RAI-009).
design: Decision recorded in the code: on the storey directly above, the stair's own representation (part above the break line, solid) takes precedence over the generic remote outline style, because that part is genuinely seen from above on that floor; further storeys of an extended range use the generic remote style for the outline. The break station must come from the home storey, otherwise the two plans would disagree; pass the home storey's effective view range in PlanSymbolContext even when drawing another storey. Pitfalls: the plan cache key of the storey above does not contain the home storey's cut plane, so invalidation must be explicit (document.rs keeps the element ids per drawing, plan-views-browser-03); a stair whose top storey is not the next storey (linked to home + 2) must still mark 'above' relative to the home storey. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/symbol.rs (08), crates/archicraft-model/src/display.rs (DisplayRange, plan-views-browser-01), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs (PlanIndex and admission, plan-views-browser-03), crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs (plan cache).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/storey.rs stair_upper_part_on_storey_above: samples::u_stair() (storey 0 at 0.00 m to storey 1 at 3.30 m, defaults) with a storey -1 at -3.00 m and a storey 2 at 6.60 m added in the test: the storey-1 plan contains only symbol lines beyond the home break station, the break line and the label Down; no line before the break; the storey-2 plan contains nothing of the stair.
- HomeOnly: nothing on storey 1. HomeAndBelow: the outline on storey -1 in the RemoteSide::Above style and nothing on storey 1. HomeAboveAndBelow: the upper part on storey 1 and the outline on storey -1. All: the upper part on storey 1 and the outline on every other storey in remote style. Intersecting with the top linked to home + 2: the expected per-storey content of a table in the test.
- display_range_matrix of plan-views-browser-04 gains stair rows (table-driven).
- Changing the home storey's cut plane from 1.10 to 1.50 m moves the break line consistently on storeys 0 and 1; the document.rs test asserts that both plans regenerate (Arc::ptr_eq false) and an unrelated storey keeps its cached plan.
- PlanDrawing::pick on storey 1 returns the stair (editable wherever displayed, ELM-008).
- Satisfies STA-046 and the stair rows of ELM-008 in the geometry.
notes:
SRS: STA-046
Related: ELM-008, VIEW-011.
Open: confirm with the product owner that the stair's own representation on the storey above (solid, KB 303689) takes precedence over the VIEW-011 remote style; if not, tag those lines PlanElement.remote = Some(RemoteSide::Below) so plan-views-browser-05 draws them in the remote style.

title: Cut further elements with the opening void and save cut lists
description:
WHY: OPN-002 (M), as in 13, plus IFX-033 (M): exported bodies are the evaluated result of openings. The epic acceptance: 'a multi-element opening cuts two walls and both show the void in plan and IFCX, and moving the non-host cut element leaves the opening in place'. docs/technology-choices.md (line 156) names OPN-002 a Manifold case: the host is cut in its own plane before extrusion (host-openings-05), but a further element can have any orientation relative to the void. IFX-060 (M): the cut list of 13 is authoring data and must be saved.

WHAT: Geometry: the FurtherCuts stage of 05 subtracts, from every visible part of an element with incoming OpeningCut edges, the union of the corresponding void prisms (VoidPrism and void_mesh of host-openings-03, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/opening.rs) transformed from the opening's storey frame into the element's frame, before the SolidOperations stage. For Through depth, void_prism extends the depth range to cover every cut element's extent along the depth axis (from Kind::plan_bounds and the vertical extent) plus VOID_MARGIN, so 'the full thickness of every cut element' (OPN-005) holds and the host's Void child encloses the whole removed volume (IFX-036); Limited depth keeps its offsets from the host face. IFCX: archicraft::opening gains an optional cuts array of element references in ElementId order, declared when used (content-derived declarations of element-kind-framework-06); the reader drops dangling references with a warning. FORMAT_VERSION rule for this epic: its reader-visible additions (08 solid-operation parameters, 09 auxiliary records, 14 opening cuts, 15 clips) share one bump with one no-op migration entry in alpha/migrate.rs; whichever of these tasks lands first bumps, the others extend the entry's description, unless a release was cut in between (then bump again, per the rule in alpha/mod.rs). Out of scope: the properties UI (19), reveal materials on further cuts (OPN-008), shafts through slabs (already host-openings-06).
design: Reusing the void prism keeps one definition for the host cut, the further cuts, the Void child and the preview. Cutting further elements with the kernel instead of the in-plane path is what allows any orientation; the host keeps its exact in-plane cut. Pitfalls: when host and cut element are joined walls, the further cut runs after the junction stage, so it follows the cleaned shape (consistent with the stage order of 05 and SOL-027); an extended through void cuts a third element only if it is in the list; transform by the storey elevation difference as in 05. Pointers: geometry/src/opening.rs (host-openings-03), evaluate.rs stage order (05), kernel/mod.rs (02), alpha/schema.rs archicraft::opening and the reader's opening codec (host-openings-08/09), alpha/migrate.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/openings.rs: a 1.00 x 1.00 m through opening hosted by wall A with a parallel wall B (0.50 m gap) in its cut list removes exactly 1.00 x 1.00 x thickness from each wall (volume within 1e-9); the plan drawing at cut height shows the gap in the cut regions of both walls.
- Moving B by 0.20 m away from A keeps the opening's placement and still cuts B through (void depth recomputed); moving A moves the opening and the cut in B.
- Removing B from the cut list restores B's body bit-identically; the host's Void child encloses the removed volume of both walls.
- tests/roundtrip.rs: an opening with two cut elements saves cuts under archicraft::opening, stays a child of its host (IFX-015) and reopens equal; both written wall meshes are cut (IFX-033) and conformance passes; a dangling cut reference loads with one warning; the case 'opening cutting a further element' joins the NFR-MNT-005 regression table.
- Satisfies OPN-002 in geometry, plan and IFCX (the multi-element opening of the epic acceptance); the UI is 19.
notes: SRS: OPN-002. Also IFX-033, IFX-036, IFX-015, IFX-060, OPN-005 and NFR-MNT-005 (re-asserted).

title: Let openings cut further elements and reassign their host
description:
WHY: OPN-002 (M): 'An opening shall be able to cut further elements besides its host. The user can add and remove cut elements and reassign the host. Moving a cut element that is not the host shall not move the opening.' host-openings delivered the opening kind with exactly one host (Opening.host, the derived Host relation, host-relative placements) and explicitly left OPN-002 to this epic; gap-analysis OPN-002: no cut-element list, no host reassignment command, no multi-element void subtraction.

WHAT: kinds/opening.rs: Opening.cuts: Vec<ElementId> (sorted, unique); the relation store derives Relation::OpeningCut { opening, element } from it as it derives Host (one source of truth), with dirty propagation in both directions because a through void spans every cut element. Validator: cut elements exist, are solid kinds (descriptor flag of 04), are neither the host nor hosted elements, and may sit on any storey. Commands: AddOpeningCuts { opening, elements }, RemoveOpeningCuts { opening, elements } and ReassignHost { opening, host }: the placement is converted to the new host keeping the world anchor and orientation (WallFace <-> Plan through the host frames of host-openings-03), rejected with a message when the new host's HostCapability does not accept it, the opening's storey follows the new host (the host-openings-02 rehome rule), the new host leaves the cut list and the old host joins it, so a reassignment alone never changes geometry. plan_delete_elements removes a deleted element from every cut list (ReplaceElement of the opening, undoable); MoveElements of a cut element that is not the host never carries the opening (only Host dependents are carried). Until 14 the cut list is model data only. Out of scope: the geometry of further cuts and their IFCX persistence (14), the properties UI (19).
design: Deriving OpeningCut edges from kind data follows host-openings' design for Host and keeps undo exact with ReplaceElement only. Keeping the old host in the cut list on reassignment is the least surprising rule (geometry unchanged; the user removes it explicitly). Pitfalls: storey moves of the host keep the cut list unchanged; cross-storey cuts need frame transforms in 14, so store element ids only; the v5 RelationId of a derived edge depends on its ends, so a re-added cut keeps its id; copies of an opening (copy::duplicate of host-openings-02) keep its cut list, copies of a cut element do not join it. Pointers: kinds/opening.rs, relations.rs, command.rs plan_delete_elements and MoveElements, copy.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/commands.rs: AddOpeningCuts and RemoveOpeningCuts execute, undo and redo; adding the host, a hosted element or a non-solid element is rejected with a message.
- ReassignHost from wall A to a parallel wall B keeps the opening's world anchor within 1e-9 m, makes B the host, puts A into the cut list, follows B's storey and undoes exactly; reassigning to a host that cannot take the orientation is rejected.
- Moving a cut element that is not the host leaves the opening's placement unchanged; moving the host carries the opening (host-openings behaviour re-asserted).
- Deleting a cut element removes it from the list and undo restores both.
- Satisfies the model clauses of OPN-002 (add and remove cut elements, reassign the host, a moved non-host cut element does not move the opening); geometry and persistence follow in 14, the UI in 19.
notes: SRS: OPN-002. Open question: copying an opening keeps its cut list (chosen) or clears it.

title: Render stair symbols, arrows and up/down labels in the plan view
description:
WHY: STA-045 (M) and STA-046 (S) are only satisfied when the user sees the symbol: solid lines below the break line, dashed lines above it, the break line, the walking line with its arrow, and the up/down label, on the home storey and the storey above. Gap row STA-045: the app draws no element text except hover names (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:624-628); dashed overhead rendering exists (plan.rs:248-255).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs: a pure function symbol_shapes(&PlanSymbol, &Camera2d, rect, &Palette, scale) -> Vec<Shape> called from draw_plan: Below and WalkingBelow lines solid in the projected stroke, Above and WalkingAbove dashed (Shape::dashed_line as for overhead), the break line solid with its zigzag, the start dot as a filled circle, arrows as filled triangles and labels with Painter text rotated along the walking line; sizes from paper millimetres through the view's drawing scale (plan-renderer-01 DrawingScale where present, otherwise the current 1:100 assumption). Label strings Up and Down come from the string table of commands-and-l10n keyed by SymbolText if that epic has landed, otherwise from one English match on SymbolText in views/plan.rs marked for externalisation. Hover and selection highlighting cover symbol lines; snap targets take step-line ends from segments(). If the plan-renderer stroke path has landed (increment 1), the symbol line classes register there (lyon tessellation) instead of the painter path. Out of scope: per-pen symbol styling (plan-attributes overrides), numbering (STA-047).
design: Keep the mapping from PlanSymbol to shapes pure and unit-tested, because AccessKit (kittest) cannot see painter text; the kittest then only proves selection through the symbol. Draw order: remote, overhead/Above, projected/Below, symbols, cut regions, reference lines, highlights, so stair symbols are not hidden by cut fills of slabs. Text uses egui's default font at a size converted from paper millimetres and is skipped below 4 px to avoid clutter when zoomed out. Pitfalls: rotated labels must stay readable (flip by 180 degrees when the walking-line direction points left); dashed patterns are in screen pixels today, keep them consistent with the overhead dash (6/4 px) unless plan-attributes line types exist. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:237-320 (draw_plan, overhead dashes at 248-255), :145 (rgb), Palette in plan.rs, SnapTargets in crates/archicraft-app/src/input/snap.rs (moved there from views/tools.rs by point-input-snapping), plan-renderer-01/03 (DrawingScale, stroke classes).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests for symbol_shapes (no GPU): Above lines produce dashed shapes, Below lines plain segments, the arrow a filled triangle whose size doubles from 1:100 to 1:50, labels a text shape with the localised 'Up' or 'Down'.
- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): open samples::u_stair(), click a step line on the home storey: the stair is selected and the properties strip shows the stair; switch to the storey above, click the upper part: the same stair is selected.
- If the plan golden-image infrastructure of plan-renderer exists, the U-stair plan on both storeys is added to the golden set within its tolerance.
- The existing kittests pass.
- Satisfies the visible part of STA-045 and STA-046.
notes: SRS: STA-045 STA-046

title: Build the solid operations palette and relation inspector
description:
WHY: SOL-020 (M) and SOL-021 (M) need a way to create subtract, subtract with upward or downward extrusion, intersect and add between chosen targets and operators; SOL-026 (S) a per-operation choice of the face material; SOL-023 (M): 'For a selection, the user shall be able to select its related targets or operators, see which elements modify an element, and remove relations: against all targets, all operators, or only the other selected elements.' Decision D-7: explicit commands for every operation, gestures are accelerators only. Nothing exists in the UI (gap-analysis SOL-023: select related, show modifiers in the properties panel, remove relations).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/solid_ops.rs: a non-modal 'Solid operations' window (Design menu, Action::SolidOperations): 'Get targets' and 'Get operators' capture the current selection and list names and counts; a radio group offers Subtract, Subtract with upward extrusion, Subtract with downward extrusion, Intersect and Add; a choice 'New faces take the material of: target / operator'; Execute runs Command::AddSolidOperations and is disabled, with an explanation, when a set is empty, the sets overlap or an element has no closed body. ui/properties.rs gains a 'Solid operations' section for a single selected element listing 'Modified by' (operator, operation) and 'Modifies' (target, operation) with click-to-select. An Edit menu submenu 'Solid operations' offers Select targets and Select operators (the selection is replaced by the related elements, hidden and auxiliary ones included and kept per 11) and Remove relations with all targets, with all operators, or among the selected elements (Command::RemoveSolidOperations). The status line reports the number of relations created or removed. Out of scope: ghosting and pick rules (11), the opening cut UI (19).
design: Follow the 'Add a dialog' and 'Add a command' extension points in docs/implementation-status.md; the window keeps its own draft (targets, operators, op) like ProjectDraft, so nothing changes until Execute. If commands-and-l10n has introduced the command registry and string externalisation, register the actions and strings there instead of extending ui/actions.rs directly. Pitfalls: captured sets may contain elements deleted meanwhile, so re-validate on Execute (the command does too); keep labels stable for kittest; cache the inspector's relation lists per revision instead of querying per frame. Pointers: ui/dialogs.rs (Dialogs and window pattern), ui/properties.rs:47-131, ui/shell.rs:59-104 (Edit and Design menus), ui/actions.rs, workspace.rs selection, tests/ui.rs harness.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: select two walls and Get targets, select a slab and Get operators, choose Subtract with upward extrusion and Execute; the project has two SolidOperation relations with Extrusion::Up and the Edit menu shows the undo label.
- kittest: with the target selected the inspector lists the operator under 'Modified by'; clicking it selects the operator; Select operators and Select targets replace the selection accordingly.
- kittest: Remove relations among the selected elements removes only pairs inside the selection; with all operators removes every pair of the target; each is undoable.

title: Persist solid operations in IFCX with a format bump and golden file
description:
WHY: SOL-022 (M): 'relations shall persist through save and open'. IFX-060 (M): everything needed to restore the editable model is stored under archicraft::; IFX-061 (M): every archicraft:: attribute is declared; IFX-062 (M): the format carries a version and older files are migrated; IFX-033 (M): exported geometry is the evaluated result including solid operations; IFX-006 (M): every written file passes the reference implementation. The epic acceptance asks for 'a golden file with subtract/intersect/add [that] round-trips its relations and passes IFX-006'. element-kind-framework writes explicit relations as an archicraft::relations array of { kind, target } on the first end's node and owns the migration table (alpha/migrate.rs); gap-analysis SOL-022: today there is no relation attribute and the reader resolves no relations (schema.rs:52-54 has only a Reference helper).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: the solidOperation relation entry declares, besides the framework's kind and other-end reference (the operator; the entry sits on the target node), operation (subtract | intersect | add), extrusion (none | up | down) and materialSource (target | operator), all optional with defaults so reading stays tolerant; the codes come from the model enums' ALL arrays. writer.rs and reader.rs extend the framework's relation codec: unknown codes produce a warning and drop the relation, dangling operators are dropped and reported (NFR-REL-004 spirit). FORMAT_VERSION rule for this epic: its reader-visible additions (08 solid-operation parameters, 09 auxiliary records, 14 opening cuts, 15 clips) share one bump with one no-op migration entry in alpha/migrate.rs; whichever of these tasks lands first bumps, the others extend the entry's description, unless a release was cut in between (then bump again, per the rule in alpha/mod.rs). An older ArchiCraft would read the pair as a plain placeholder relation and lose its parameters, hence the bump. crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs: solid_operations() built through commands - a ground slab, four walls, a slab operator subtracting with Up from one wall, a wall intersected with a slab volume, a wall with an added block, a mutual pair - registered in crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and in samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs; the golden solid-operations.ifcx is blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 and reviewed. Out of scope: auxiliary operators (09), opening cuts (14), clips (15), consistency hashes (17).
design: Follow the extension points 'Add an IFCX attribute' and 'Add a sample/golden model' in docs/implementation-status.md and the framework's per-kind and relation codecs, so schema, writer and reader each get one entry. The relation sits on the target node because the target's mesh depends on it and the framework writes on the first end. Pitfalls: bless the golden only after 05-07 so its meshes are final; keep the relation array sorted by RelationId for determinism; declarations are content-derived (element-kind-framework-06), so files without solid operations keep their bytes. Pointers: alpha/schema.rs:15, 25, 97-125; writer.rs:361-417; reader.rs:735-880; alpha/migrate.rs; samples.rs; tests/roundtrip.rs; examples/reference_models.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/roundtrip.rs: solid_operations() saves and reopens equal (assert_eq on Project including relations and their SolidOp); regenerated geometry equals stored geometry within 0.1 mm (IFX-064); a second save is byte-identical apart from the header fields (IFX-007).
- The written target meshes are the cut results (volume compared with the evaluated geometry, IFX-033).
- A file whose relation names a missing operator loads with the relation dropped and one warning; an unknown operation code likewise; a FORMAT_VERSION n-1 file migrates with an Info entry; a file claiming n+1 is flagged newer_format.
- conformance/run.sh passes on solid-operations.ifcx (IFX-006 a and the viewer tree) in the CI conformance job.
- Satisfies the persistence clause of SOL-022 and IFX-060/IFX-061 for solid operations.
notes: SRS: SOL-022 SOL-020 SOL-021 SOL-026. Also IFX-033, IFX-060, IFX-061, IFX-062, IFX-006, IFX-064 (re-asserted).

title: Give faces created by an operation the chosen material
description:
WHY: SOL-026 (S): 'For each operation, faces newly created on the target shall take either the operator's or the target's materials, as chosen by the user.' Gap-analysis SOL-026: missing; it needs face provenance from the Boolean result mapped onto BodyParts. Decision D-5 keeps one material concept with per-face overrides.

WHAT: The kernel's per-triangle sources (02) identify triangles that came from an operator's surface. BodyPart gets face_materials: Vec<FaceMaterialRun { first: u32, count: u32, material: MaterialId }> (sorted, merged, empty by default; the triangles of a run are contiguous in the canonical output order); apply_operations (18) records, for each operation with MaterialSource::Operator, a run for the triangles sourced from that operator part with the operator part's material, while Target leaves them in the part material. crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs build_scene colours triangles by run; geometry plan.rs keeps cut fills per part (a cut region is volume, not face) and is unchanged; the IFCX writer keeps writing each closed part with its part material, because the registry mesh schema has no per-face material and IFX-032 forbids splitting a volumetric part into open face groups; runs are derived data and are regenerated after reading. Normalize (03) splits runs with their triangles. Out of scope: user per-face overrides (3d-display-styles, OPN-008), free-form solid face materials (free-form-solids).
design: Provenance comes from Manifold's run original ids: give every operator part its own original id before the union, so a run knows which operator part, and so which material, it came from. Runs on the part are cheaper than a per-triangle Vec. Pitfalls: SceneData colours per part today (render3d.rs:120-160), so add per-triangle colour without breaking the selection and hover tint; keep TriMesh equality free of runs (runs live beside the mesh); Body_n splitting in 03 must carry runs. Pointers: evaluate.rs BodyPart, render3d.rs:102-176, kernel sources (02), apply_operations (18).
acceptance_criteria:
- solid_ops.rs: a subtract with MaterialSource::Operator yields runs covering exactly the cut faces (as many triangles as are sourced from the operator) with the operator's material; with Target there are no runs; mixed operations on one target give non-overlapping runs in canonical order.
- render3d unit test: build_scene colours run triangles with the operator material and the rest with the part material; selection and hover tints still apply.
- Writer test: the file is byte-identical for both material sources (runs are not exported) and goldens are unchanged.
- Satisfies SOL-026 in the model and the 3D view; the IFCX limitation is recorded in docs/implementation-status.md.
notes: SRS: SOL-026. Open question for 3d-display-styles: exporting per-face materials of closed parts (same issue as OPN-008 reveal materials and SOL-003); until then only the 3D view shows them.

title: Verify exit criterion: Stair flights, landings, finishes, plan symbol and compound parts
description:
WHY: The epic closes only when its exit criterion holds as a whole: straight, L, U and polyline stairs with landing turns and riser offsets (STA-020, STA-021), automatic landings with minimum length and surplus placement (STA-022), symmetric riser distribution (STA-023), the baseline lock (STA-029), finish and structure (STA-040, STA-041), seam suppression (STA-043), part failure reporting with fallback (STA-044), the plan symbol and the storey-above display (STA-045, STA-046) and IfcStair with classed children (STA-051). reference-models (AS-01 without railings, the increment-2 exit) and railings-stairs-adv build on it.

WHAT: Run the workspace quality gates, re-run every acceptance test named by tasks 01-14 together, walk the epic acceptance item by item, update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID with evidence (file:line and test names), plus the rows STA-001 (landings and supports clause) and STA-011 (unlock-the-baseline alternative) that stair-solver-tool-done left to this epic, record residual clauses owned by other epics (stringers STA-042 and the IfcMember clause of STA-051, winders, railings using the break line RAI-009), and close the epic in beads. No new features; defects found become new beads.
design: Verification only. Run the gates locally and in CI on all three platforms; review the golden diffs once more for non-archicraft changes (IFX-063); confirm that the default stair (D.2) and the D.3 landing minimum appear in the Appendix D defaults test of regression-and-status; confirm the open questions recorded in tasks 01 and 03 (structure thickness defaults, surplus semantics) are either answered in docs/SRS.md or filed as beads; file beads for any defect instead of widening this task.
acceptance_criteria:
- A U-stair with 22 risers has 11 + 11 with a landing of at least 1.00 m and the surplus placed per option (stair_layout.rs tests).
- Inserting a node creates an automatic landing (model test and edit-mode kittest).
- Locking the baseline keeps node positions and adapts the step distribution only.
- All parts are closed bodies (closedness property test) and feature edges between same-material treads are suppressed (seam tests).
- An unbuildable part is reported and the stair falls back to the last valid body (fallback tests, problems panel).
- The plan symbol shows step lines, walking line, arrow and the break line at the configured height, and the storey above shows only the part above the break line (ELM-008 range).
- The AS-01 U-stair exports IfcStair with IfcStairFlight and IfcSlab landing children and passes conformance (IFX-016 re-asserted).
- Entering edit mode selects a single flight and its properties (kittest on PartRef::Flight).
- cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are green on the workspace.

- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for STA-020, STA-021, STA-022, STA-023, STA-029, STA-040, STA-041, STA-043, STA-044, STA-045, STA-046 and STA-051 (remaining clauses named and attributed to their owning epics), and the STA-001 and STA-011 rows record the landings, supports and unlock-the-baseline clauses delivered here.
- The epic stair-body-plan is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: STA-020 STA-021 STA-022 STA-023 STA-029 STA-040 STA-041 STA-043 STA-044 STA-045 STA-046 STA-051

title: Vendor Manifold behind own bindings and build it on all CI runners
description:
WHY: SOL-020 (M) requires subtract, intersect and add between target and operator elements for every element with a closed body, and OPN-002, SOL-021, SOL-024 and EDT-024 all need general 3D Booleans that 2D cuts cannot express. docs/technology-choices.md (section '3D geometry' and 'Planned for v1', lines 150-160, 216, 256-259) names Manifold for this case 'at the latest in SRS increment 2', through own bindings to its C API or the manifold3d crate, and lists the risks: a C++ compiler and CMake on three platforms (selection criterion 4) and Rust bindings with one owner (risk 7). Today Cargo.lock holds only 2D Booleans (i_overlay under geo), the workspace denies unsafe code (Cargo.toml [workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny") and .github/workflows/ci.yml builds pure Rust only. NFR-PORT-001..003 (Windows, macOS, Linux) and NFR-LEG-001 (permissive licences, inventory) apply to the new dependency.

WHAT: Run and record the health check (manifold3d 0.4.1 versus own bindings; boolmesh as the pure-Rust fallback candidate) in docs/technology-choices.md and, unless it overturns the roadmap's choice, create crates/archicraft-manifold: the Manifold sources of one pinned 3.x release vendored under vendor/manifold with VERSION and sha256 recorded and scripts/update-manifold.sh to re-download and verify them; a build.rs using the cmake crate (MANIFOLD_CBIND=ON, MANIFOLD_PAR=OFF, cross-section/Clipper2, tests, samples and Python bindings off, always built in Release, MSVC runtime matching Rust's /MD, libc++ or libstdc++ linked per platform); raw extern "C" declarations for the subset needed (MeshGL64 in and out with face ids and run original ids, boolean, batch boolean, split by plane, status, tolerance) plus, if the C API lacks a double-precision or provenance accessor, a small C++ shim compiled into the same library; and a safe layer exposing plain data only (Solid::from_mesh(&[f64], &[u32], &[u32]) -> Result<Solid, Error>, boolean, batch_union, split, to_mesh() -> MeshOut { points, triangles, face_ids, original_ids }). The crate allows unsafe_code locally with a documented exception and is the only place FFI exists. archicraft-geometry gets a default cargo feature `manifold` depending on it (no use yet). CI: the test matrix builds the crate on ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest and macos-latest with the cmake output cached by Swatinem/rust-cache keyed by the vendored VERSION, plus a job `cargo test -p archicraft-geometry --no-default-features` proving the build without the kernel; deny.toml covers the cmake/cc crates; Manifold's LICENSE and NOTICE (Apache-2.0) ship with the vendored source; README or docs/building.md lists the prerequisites (CMake >= 3.18, a C++17 compiler). Out of scope: the SolidKernel trait and mesh conversion (02), any evaluation use, the minidump handler for native crashes (release-candidate).
design: Own bindings are the roadmap's mitigation for the one-owner crate: keep them thin and data-only so the safe API is the whole surface and a pure-Rust kernel can replace it behind the trait of 02. Use MeshGL64 (double precision, Manifold 3.x computes in double) so NFR-ACC-001 holds; set the kernel tolerance to the framework's MODEL_TOLERANCE (0.01 mm, NFR-ACC-003) at the call site, not in the build. MANIFOLD_PAR=OFF keeps results deterministic and avoids TBB. Pitfalls: Windows needs CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreadedDLL or link errors follow; macOS needs cargo:rustc-link-lib=c++, Linux stdc++; debug builds of Manifold make tests slow, so force Release in cmake::Config; exclude Manifold's tests and assets from the vendored tree; rust-cache only helps when build.rs does not rerun, so emit precise rerun-if-changed lines (VERSION and the shim) instead of the whole vendor tree; build with exceptions disabled or catch them in the shim and return a status, because a C++ exception unwinding into Rust is undefined behaviour. The workspace lint unsafe_code = "deny" can be lowered per crate with #![allow(unsafe_code)]; document the exception in the crate docs. Pointers: Cargo.toml (members, workspace lints), .github/workflows/ci.yml (test and lint jobs), deny.toml, docs/technology-choices.md:150-160, 216, 256-259, 281, 303.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-manifold smoke tests pass on all three CI runners: a unit cube minus a cube offset by 0.5 m in x, y and z has volume 0.875 m3 within 1e-12; their intersection 0.125; the union of two disjoint cubes has volume 2.0; splitting a unit cube at z = 0.3 gives closed halves of 0.3 and 0.7.
- A second CI run on an unchanged tree shows the crate as Fresh (no cmake rebuild) on every runner; the cache key changes when vendor/manifold/VERSION changes.
- The job `cargo test -p archicraft-geometry --no-default-features` passes and its `cargo tree` contains no archicraft-manifold (the feature flag disables the kernel).
- No `unsafe` outside crates/archicraft-manifold (grep check in CI); a non-manifold input mesh returns Err instead of aborting, so no C++ exception crosses the FFI boundary.
- cargo deny check licenses sources bans passes; docs/technology-choices.md moves Manifold from 'Planned for v1' into the stack with the health-check row and the binding decision; build prerequisites are documented.
- Prepares SOL-020 (engine available); the NFR-PORT and NFR-LEG-001 clauses hold for the new dependency.
notes: SRS: SOL-020. Decision to record: own bindings (preferred) or manifold3d after the health check; boolmesh (MPL-2.0, 0.1.x) stays the documented pure-Rust fallback and would need a deny.toml review. Native crashes inside Manifold are not caught; release-candidate adds the minidump handler (NFR-SEC-002).

title: Add the lock-baseline option with per-flight goings
description:
WHY: STA-029 (S): a lock-baseline option shall be provided; turned off, flights between turns lengthen or shorten automatically so that all enabled rules are met exactly (task 02); turned on, the node positions are authoritative and only the step distribution adapts. The epic acceptance requires that locking the baseline keeps node positions and adapts the step distribution only. STA-011 (M, stair-solver-tool) lists 'unlock the baseline' among the alternatives of a rule conflict; stair-solver-tool-03 prepared AdjustRun for it and stair-solver-tool-done leaves the lock-baseline alternative of STA-011 to this epic. Gap row STA-029: no lock option, no automatic flight lengthening or shortening. StairParams.lock_baseline exists as data since task 01 and is ignored by solve() until this task.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/solve.rs: with params.lock_baseline set, solve keeps the stored baseline bit for bit; N still comes from the RiserSpec and is distributed over the flights by task 02's apportionment; per flight the going = available walking-line length after the riser offsets / goings, with Minimum offsets absorbing what whole goings cannot fill; StairSolution.flights carries the per-flight goings and layout() uses them. Every per-flight (R, G) is checked with solver.rs check() against every enabled rule (and the walking-line rule); violations return RuleConflict {cause: DrawnGeometry, rules with limit and actual per flight}, whose alternatives in conflict.rs gain Alternative::UnlockBaseline, offered only when solving the same parameters with the lock off succeeds, next to the existing ChangeRiserCount and RelaxRule. With the lock off solve behaves as in task 02. Switching the lock on needs no node conversion because resolve already stores the adjusted baseline; switching it off re-solves with node movement. Kind::resolve and the storey re-solve of stair-solver-tool-05 need no change beyond passing the flag through. Out of scope: in-run landing surplus (03), the UI toggle and the dialog label for the new alternative (13), winders.
design: Keep one solve() with a single branch on lock_baseline, so the tool preview, the properties read-out and resolve keep sharing it (stair-solver-tool-03 design). Per-flight goings are the only new freedom of the locked mode; the riser count stays a whole-stair decision because R must be equal across the stair (STA-004). Prefer adapting Minimum offsets before goings when a flight cannot be filled exactly, so goings stay as uniform as possible, and record that order in the doc comment. The UnlockBaseline alternative is verified like the others by re-running solve with lock_baseline = false; applying it is an UpdateElements of the flag (task 13), never a direct node edit. Pitfalls: compare against the rule bounds through MODEL_TOLERANCE (inclusive bounds); a locked stair whose stored solution no longer fits after a storey change becomes stale through stair-solver-tool-05, it is not rejected; keep the alternative order deterministic for the dialog. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/solve.rs, solver.rs (check), conflict.rs (Alternative, RuleConflict) and status.rs (stair-solver-tool-02/03/05), stair/layout.rs (02).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_layout.rs lock_baseline_keeps_nodes: samples::u_stair() locked, storey height 3.300 -> 3.000 m through the storey command: the stored nodes are unchanged bit for bit, N becomes 20 (10 + 10), each flight's going equals its available walking-line length / goings within 1e-9 and every enabled rule holds.
- The same edit unlocked moves the nodes and keeps the solver going (cross-check with task 02's unlocked_flights_follow_the_rules); the two results differ only in nodes and goings.
- locked_too_short: a locked stair whose flights cannot satisfy the rules returns RuleConflict naming each violated rule with actual and limit value and offering UnlockBaseline; re-solving the parameters with the alternative applied succeeds; nothing panics.
- UnlockBaseline is not offered when the unlocked solve fails as well (only alternatives that verify are offered, stair-solver-tool-03 rule).
- Toggling the lock on and off without other changes leaves the baseline and the solution unchanged (resolve stays idempotent).
- The STA-011 cases of crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs gain the unlock alternative; crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: a locked UpdateElements that conflicts is rejected with CommandError::RuleConflict and leaves the project unchanged.
- Satisfies STA-029 in the model and the 'unlock the baseline' alternative of STA-011.
notes:
SRS: STA-029
Related: STA-011 (the 'unlock the baseline' alternative left open by stair-solver-tool-done), STA-008 (violations listed with actual and limit values), STA-010.
Test values: STA-004 3.300 m / 22 = 150.00 mm and 3.000 m / 20 = 150.00 mm (TargetHeight 0.150).

title: Add the auxiliary flag and exclude auxiliary elements from IFCX
description:
WHY: ELM-014 (S): elements 'markable as auxiliary ... are excluded from the building elements written to IFCX. They still act as operators of solid operations and trims.' IFX-068 (M): 'The standard IFCX content shall not depend on view state. Elements are written regardless of layer visibility, view filters, hidden elements and cut planes. Auxiliary elements (ELM-014) are not written as building elements; they are kept in the ArchiCraft namespace only.' SRS 3.2 lists auxiliary among the element flags. Gap-analysis ELM-014: missing (no flag); IFX-068: partial - every element of every storey is written (writer.rs:301, 324-326) and no test asserts independence from view state (VIEW-047 partial).

WHAT: Kept and regressed: the writer already writes every element of every storey regardless of layer visibility (writer.rs:296-330; visibility only filters the plan drawing, document.rs:116-118 and project.rs:206-209). New: archicraft-model: Element.auxiliary: bool (#[serde(default)]) next to locked, edited through UpdateElements and Command::SetAuxiliary { ids, auxiliary } for multi-selections (labels 'Mark as auxiliary' and 'Mark as building element'); hosted elements follow their host (an opening cannot be auxiliary on its own, validator message); auxiliary elements may be targets and operators. archicraft-ifcx: the storey loop and the hosted-children path skip auxiliary elements; each storey node gets an optional archicraft::auxiliaryElements attribute holding, per auxiliary element, its id, the archicraft::element common data and its kind attribute through the per-kind codec (no class, no Name, no mesh, no transform), declared only when used; hosted elements of an auxiliary host are nested in its record; relations referencing auxiliary elements stay on the target nodes; the reader restores auxiliary elements before resolving relations. FORMAT_VERSION rule for this epic: its reader-visible additions (08 solid-operation parameters, 09 auxiliary records, 14 opening cuts, 15 clips) share one bump with one no-op migration entry in alpha/migrate.rs; whichever of these tasks lands first bumps, the others extend the entry's description, unless a release was cut in between (then bump again, per the rule in alpha/mod.rs). A writer test asserts that layer visibility, any per-view hidden set or filter present in the project and cut planes do not change the standard (non-archicraft) content. Out of scope: ghost drawing and picking (11), the visible-only export (10).
design: Records on the storey node keep a single root (IFX-013) and mirror IFX-067's rule for unused resources; reusing the per-kind codec avoids a second serialisation path. Generic consumers never see auxiliary elements but see their effect, because targets are written evaluated. Pitfalls: child keys and counters of building elements must not change when another element becomes auxiliary; integrity checks must treat auxiliary elements as normal elements; the reader must not report the records as unknown attributes. Pointers: element.rs:275-287, writer.rs:296-330 and write_element, reader.rs element loop, the framework codec registry, project.rs:207 (is_visible).
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/commands.rs: SetAuxiliary on two elements executes, undoes and redoes; marking an opening alone is rejected with a message.
- tests/roundtrip.rs: a project with an auxiliary slab operator cutting a wall saves with no node for the slab in any storey's children or anywhere in the composed tree, the slab inside archicraft::auxiliaryElements, the wall mesh already cut (IFX-033), and reopens equal including the relation.
- conformance/run.sh: the viewer tree of that file lists only building elements and passes IFX-006.
- View-state independence test: saving with layers hidden, elements in a view's hidden set (when 3d-view-restrictions provides one) and cut planes set gives standard attributes identical to the default save (IFX-068, VIEW-047).
- Evaluation never reads the auxiliary flag: toggling it on every element of a sample leaves ModelGeometry bit-identical, so auxiliary elements keep acting as operators of solid operations, and of trims once cleanup-and-trims adds them.
- Satisfies ELM-014 (flag, exclusion from IFCX building elements, still acts as operator) and the auxiliary and view-state clauses of IFX-068.
notes: SRS: ELM-014 IFX-068. Also IFX-033, IFX-013 and VIEW-047 (re-asserted). The trim clause of ELM-014 is re-asserted by cleanup-and-trims. Decision: auxiliary records live on the home storey node; site-level auxiliary elements (later) on the site node.

title: Verify exit criterion: Manifold Boolean kernel and associative solid operations
description:
WHY: The epic opens SRS increment 2 (Appendix F: roofs, trim and solid operations, free-form solids, terrain) by bringing in the 3D Boolean kernel, and it owns IFX-038, OPN-002, SOL-020, SOL-021, SOL-022, SOL-023, SOL-024, SOL-025, SOL-026, SOL-027, SOL-028, ELM-014, IFX-068, EDT-024; cleanup-and-trims, free-form-solids, terrain-and-site and release-candidate build on it. This task verifies the whole against the epic's acceptance, not against the individual tasks.

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged work: CI on ubuntu, windows and macos with the kernel plus the --no-default-features job; cargo test, clippy (-D warnings) and fmt on the workspace; conformance/run.sh on every golden including solid-operations; the kernel property tests and the kernel_ops, solid_ops, openings and consistency suites; the kittest suite. Then update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence and gap rows in sections 4.8, 4.9, 4.17, 4.22, 5.2.4 and 5.2.7, the readiness line of increment 2, and the technical-debt entries this epic removes: the writer not verifying closedness and the point limit, check_closed used only in tests), update docs/technology-choices.md (Manifold in use, health-check row), file beads for leftovers (per-face material export, parametric horizontal splits, the minidump handler trigger for release-candidate, any Boolean robustness case found) and close the epic in beads.
design: Verification only; no new code except status and documentation edits. Use `bd show solid-kernel-ops` to walk the task list, run the commands of .github/workflows/ci.yml locally and on the three runners, and compare the srs_ids of the epic with the changed rows of docs/implementation-status.md (regression-and-status adds a CI check for this; do it by hand if that check is not there yet).
acceptance_criteria:
- CI builds the kernel on ubuntu, windows and macos runners with cached cmake builds, and a feature flag disables it.
- archicraft-geometry exposes boolean(op, a, b) behind a SolidKernel trait and property tests show every result is closed, 2-manifold, outward-oriented and split at hard edges with at most 65,535 points per Body_n (IFX-038).
- A failed Boolean returns Err, the element keeps its last valid body and is listed (NFR-REL-005 clause).
- SOL-022: moving an operator by 0.10 m moves the cut by 0.10 m with no further action; random operator orderings give identical meshes; deleting an operator restores the target.
- An explicit subtract between two joined walls overrides their automatic junction where the two conflict (SOL-027 conflict test).
- A multi-element opening cuts two walls and both show the void in plan and IFCX, and moving the non-host cut element leaves the opening in place.
- A golden file with subtract/intersect/add round-trips its relations and passes IFX-006.
- Auxiliary elements are absent from the standard IFCX building elements, and the export-visible-only variant omits hidden elements while the default export does not.
- Split by plane yields two closed solids.
- The plan slice, the 3D body and the exported mesh hash identically.
- cargo test, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green on the workspace; conformance/run.sh is green on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for IFX-038, OPN-002, SOL-020, SOL-021, SOL-022, SOL-023, SOL-024, SOL-025, SOL-026, SOL-027, SOL-028, ELM-014, IFX-068, EDT-024 with evidence pointing at the new modules and tests, and docs/technology-choices.md lists Manifold as in use.
- The epic is closed in beads with follow-up beads filed for remaining work.
