title: Ghost auxiliary elements and keep hidden operators selectable
description:
WHY: ELM-014 (S): 'Auxiliary elements are drawn ghosted, are not picked by default (they can be with a modifier or filter)'. SOL-025 (M): 'Operators shall keep their effect when hidden, ghosted or shown as wireframe, and shall remain selectable and editable in these states.' Gap-analysis SOL-025: hidden-layer elements are excluded from the 3D scene and from picking (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:99-111, view3d.rs:77), DisplayMode is per view (render3d.rs:25-37), and evaluation ignores visibility (evaluate.rs:68), so effects persist; in addition Workspace::prune_selection drops every element on a hidden layer after each command (workspace.rs:156-159), so a hidden operator cannot stay selected for editing.

WHAT: render3d.rs build_scene draws auxiliary elements ghosted (neutral colour at reduced opacity through the transparent path, light edges) and draws selected elements that are hidden as edge-only overlays in the selection colour, so the user sees what is being edited; views/plan.rs draws auxiliary elements with a ghost pen and no cut fill (Palette.ghost meeting the UI-010 contrast rule on both canvases). Picking: view3d.rs pick, archicraft-geometry PlanDrawing::pick (plan.rs:270), the marquee and select-all (workspace.rs:203-224) skip auxiliary elements unless the 'Pick auxiliary elements' toggle (View menu, status-bar indicator) is on or the pick modifier is held (proposed Alt-click; Alt-drag stays orbit). prune_selection keeps elements selected through relation queries or the inspector of 12 even when hidden, and drops hidden elements only when the user hides them. properties.rs shows an Auxiliary checkbox for the selection (SetAuxiliary). Tests prove that hiding, ghosting and wireframe never change evaluated targets. Out of scope: display styles (3d-display-styles), per-view hidden sets themselves (3d-view-restrictions).
design: Visibility stays a pure display concern - evaluation never reads it - which is what makes SOL-025's effect clause hold; the work is the selection and drawing rules. One pick predicate pickable(project, element, PickFilter) shared by plan and 3D (or the selection model's predicate, if selection-transforms has introduced one) keeps the auxiliary rule in one place. Pitfalls: transparent faces are drawn unsorted (render3d.rs:311, technical debt), so ghosted bodies in front of glass may blend oddly, acceptable for v1; Alt is the orbit modifier (view3d.rs:160-163), so distinguish click from drag; the scene cache key (SceneKey, workspace.rs:44) must include the toggle and the auxiliary flags. Pointers: render3d.rs:90-176, view3d.rs:59-100, views/plan.rs drawing and Palette, geometry plan.rs:270, workspace.rs:156-159 and 203-224, ui/properties.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: the target mesh is bit-identical when its operator is on a hidden layer, marked auxiliary, in a view's hidden set (when available) or shown with DisplayMode::Wireframe (SOL-025 effect clause).
- Pick tests: view3d::pick and PlanDrawing::pick ignore an auxiliary element by default and return it with the modifier or with the toggle on; select-all skips auxiliary elements unless the toggle is on.
- Workspace test: a hidden operator selected through Select operators stays selected after an UpdateElements that moves it by 0.10 m, and the target's cut follows (SOL-025 selectable and editable; SOL-022).
- Wireframe and ghosted states: with DisplayMode::Wireframe, view3d::pick returns the operator and a MoveElements of it moves the target's cut; an auxiliary (ghosted) operator picked with the modifier is moved the same way (SOL-025 'selectable and editable in these states').
- render3d unit tests: auxiliary parts are emitted with the ghost colour and opacity; a selected hidden element yields edge-only selection lines and no faces.
- kittest: the Auxiliary checkbox toggles the flag through a command (undo label 'Mark as auxiliary').
- Satisfies ELM-014 (ghosted drawing, no picking by default, modifier and filter) and SOL-025.
notes: SRS: ELM-014 SOL-025. Also UI-010 (contrast). Proposed pick modifier Alt-click; the concrete binding is a UI design deliverable (Appendix D.8).

title: Add solid-operation parameters, commands and relation queries
description:
WHY: SOL-020 (M): solid operations - subtract, intersect, add - 'between a set of target elements and a set of operator elements', for every element with a closed body. SOL-024 (M): 'One operation may involve several targets and several operators. An element may be the target of some operations and the operator of others, including mutual relations.' SOL-023 (M): for a selection the user can select its related targets or operators, see which elements modify an element, and remove relations 'against all targets, all operators, or only the other selected elements'; 'Deleting an operator or removing a relation shall restore the target's unmodified geometry.' element-kind-framework added Relation::SolidOperation { target, operator } carrying its ends only, Edit::InsertRelation/RemoveRelation and the delete cascade; gap-analysis SOL-022/SOL-023: no relation storage or removal exists today (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:275-287, project.rs:164-182, DeleteElements at command.rs:38 knows no relations).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs: SolidOperation gains op: SolidOp { kind: SolidOpKind::{Subtract, Intersect, Add}, extrusion: Extrusion::{None, Up, Down}, material_source: MaterialSource::{Target, Operator} }; the RelationId stays the v5 of the ends, so a pair has at most one operation and re-applying replaces its parameters; dependents_of keeps 'target depends on operator'. crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs: Command::AddSolidOperations { targets, operators, op } planned as InsertRelation (or RemoveRelation + InsertRelation for an existing pair with other parameters) for every target x operator pair, validated: both sets non-empty and disjoint, every element exists and its KindDescriptor declares a closed body (new descriptor flag solid: bool, default false; true for walls, slabs and every construction kind already registered when this epic starts, such as the columns and beams of profiles-columns-beams; false for openings, other hosted elements and 2D kinds), extrusion only with Subtract, locked targets rejected with CommandError::Locked (ELM-013), NoChange when nothing differs; Command::RemoveSolidOperations { elements, scope: RemoveScope::{AllTargets, AllOperators, AmongSelection} }; labels for the Edit menu. Queries on Project: operators_of(id), targets_of(id) and solid_operations_of(id) -> Vec<(ElementId, ElementId, SolidOp)> in ElementId order. Until 08 the framework's relation codec writes the pair without parameters (no sample contains one). Out of scope: geometry (05-07), IFCX parameters (08), UI (12), opening cut relations (13).
design: Pairwise storage instead of the roadmap's operation record { targets, operators, kind, extrusion, material_source }: SOL-023's removal scopes and the per-target evaluation of SOL-024 work on pairs, the framework's RelationId is already pair-based, and an 'operation' is just the set of pairs one command creates; the palette of 12 groups pairs with equal parameters for display. Plan everything inside Command::plan with the existing Edit primitives so history and journal stay complete. Pitfalls: SolidOp is part of the journal and of Project PartialEq, so keep its serde names stable; Up and Down are SOL-021 variants of Subtract only; the descriptor flag must default to false so future 2D kinds are excluded without code. Pointers: relations.rs and kinds/mod.rs (KindDescriptor) from element-kind-framework, command.rs:36-125 (Command, label) and plan_delete_elements, tests/commands.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/commands.rs: AddSolidOperations with 2 targets and 3 operators inserts 6 relations; undo restores the exact project and redo re-applies; re-applying with Intersect replaces the 6 parameter sets in one undo step; applying identical parameters returns NoChange.
- Validation tests: overlapping target and operator sets, a missing element, an opening as target, Up extrusion with Intersect and a locked target are rejected with explanatory messages and leave the project unchanged.
- Mutual relations: A subtracts B and B subtracts A coexist as two relations (SOL-024).
- RemoveSolidOperations: AllTargets on an operator removes its relations to every target, AllOperators on a target removes every operator, AmongSelection removes only pairs inside the given set (SOL-023); each is undoable.
- DeleteElements of an operator removes its relations and undo restores them with their parameters (framework cascade re-asserted).
- operators_of and targets_of return the same order for any insertion order (property test with shuffled commands).
- Registry test over KINDS: every kind whose generator yields closed visible parts declares solid: true and is accepted as target and operator by AddSolidOperations; kinds without a closed body are refused (SOL-020 'every element with a closed body').
- Satisfies the model clauses of SOL-020, SOL-023 (queries, three removal scopes) and SOL-024 (several targets and operators, mutual relations).
notes: SRS: SOL-020 SOL-023 SOL-024. Terrain and free-form solids set solid: true in terrain-and-site and free-form-solids, which re-assert SOL-020 for them. Open question: whether a locked operator may be used (chosen: yes, it is not modified).

title: Generate the stair plan symbol with walking line and break line
description:
WHY: STA-045 (M): in plan, a stair shall be drawn with step lines; a walking line with a direction arrow and an up/down label; and a break line at a configurable height (default: the plan cut-plane height; alternatively a custom height or the n-th riser); the part below the break line is drawn solid, the part above it dashed (KB 303689). The epic acceptance asks for step lines, walking line, arrow and the break line at the configured height. Gap row: no stair symbol; the generic plan classification works per body part against one cut height (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:133-143) and PlanElement has no symbol or text fields (plan.rs:23-34). RAI-009 later reuses the break line for railings.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: PlanElement gains symbol: Option<PlanSymbol>; PlanSymbol {lines: Vec<SymbolLine {a, b, class: SymbolClass {Below, Above, Break, WalkingBelow, WalkingAbove}}>, arrows: Vec<SymbolArrow {tip, direction, size_mm}>, markers: Vec<SymbolMarker {at, kind: StartDot}>, labels: Vec<SymbolLabel {anchor, direction, text: SymbolText {Up, Down}, height_mm}>}, renderer-agnostic, with text as a semantic enum so localisation stays in the app; PlanElement::segments() includes symbol lines, so picking and snapping see them. The GeometryKind trait gains plan_symbol(&PlanSymbolContext) -> Option<PlanSymbol> (default None keeps the generic slicing); PlanSymbolContext carries the element, its geometry, the storey relation (Home, Above(n), Below(n)), the effective view range (cut, bottom, top from Project::view_range, plan-views-browser-01/03) and the home storey elevation. New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/symbol.rs for relation Home: stair outline and landing outlines, one step line per tread nosing edge, the walking line from the first to the last riser with a start dot and an arrow pointing uphill, the label Up at the start, and the break line across the full width at the walking-line station where the stair surface reaches the break height (BreakLine::CutPlane = the view's cut height, Height(h) storey-local, Riser(n) = top of riser n), drawn perpendicular to the walking line with a zigzag mark; everything before the break station is Below, everything after Above. For kinds with a symbol the generic cut, projected and overhead lines of their bodies are not emitted. The stair descriptor's plan displays (ELM-018, plan-views-browser-01): ProjectedWithOverhead (default: below solid, above dashed) and Projected (below the break line only); plan-views-browser-04's per-element plan_display filter and PlanOptions.show_overhead act on the symbol classes (Above and WalkingAbove dropped by Projected or when overhead is hidden). PlanElement.footprint (selection-transforms-05) of a stair is its layout outline. Out of scope: other storeys (09), drawing (10), riser numbering (STA-047), ramps (STA-050).
design: Compute the symbol from StairLayout (02; the automatic landings of 03 are ordinary LandingRuns, so no extra dependency) in plan coordinates, not by slicing bodies: step lines and the walking line are layout data, which keeps the symbol exact and cheap and independent of finish and structure. The break station is found by a search along the walking line over the riser z values (the stair surface is piecewise constant per tread, so the break falls on a tread or landing; for Riser(n) it is the riser line). Drawing the break line perpendicular to the walking line avoids splitting step lines (a diagonal break would cut through several step lines); record this as a convention in the doc comment. Label and arrow sizes are in paper millimetres (2.5 mm text, 3 mm arrow proposed) so the app scales them with the drawing scale. The plan cache key (PlanOptions) already contains the cut override, so a CutPlane break follows per-view overrides for free; a Height or Riser break does not depend on the view. Pitfalls: walking-line arrows on U-stairs must follow the landing turn (polyline through the landing on the walking-line offset); downward input (STA-002) does not change the uphill arrow; keep PlanSymbol Clone + Debug and free of f32 so plan caching stays deterministic. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:23-34 (PlanElement), :111-150 (plan_drawing classification), :211 (segments), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/ (GeometryKind, element-kind-framework-07), plan-views-browser-03 (PlanOptions, Project::view_range).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair.rs u_stair_symbol_at_default_cut: samples::u_stair() (the AS-01 U-stair, R = 0.150 m) with the D.1 cut plane 1.10 m: one step line per tread, step lines with tread top at or below 1.10 m are Below and the rest Above, the break line lies between the 7th and 8th riser (1.05 m and 1.20 m), the walking line starts with a StartDot at the first riser and ends with an arrow at the last riser pointing uphill, and the label Up sits at the start.
- break_line_modes: Height(1.50) puts the break between risers 10 and 11; Riser(5) at riser 5; a per-view cut override of 2.00 m (PlanOptions, plan-views-browser-03) moves the CutPlane break and produces a different cache entry.
- projected_display_drops_above: plan display Projected, and PlanOptions.show_overhead = false, emit no Above or WalkingAbove lines.
- generic_lines_replaced: the stair contributes no cut polygons and no generic projected or overhead lines; wall and slab plan output of plan_cuts_walls_and_projects_slab is unchanged.
- pick() on a step line returns the stair; snapping sees step-line end points through segments(); the stair's PlanElement.footprint equals the layout outline.
- Straight, L, U and polyline stairs produce symbols whose lines lie inside the stair outline within MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- Satisfies STA-045 in the geometry (drawing in task 10).
notes:
SRS: STA-045
Appendix D.1: plan cut plane 1.10 m above the storey elevation; drawing scale 1:100.
Proposed paper sizes: label 2.5 mm, arrow 3 mm, start dot 1.5 mm (to be aligned with plan-attributes pens).

title: Prove identical solid-operation results in plan, 3D, slices and IFCX
description:
WHY: SOL-028 (M): 'Results of solid operations shall be identical in 3D, plan, section and elevation views and in the geometry exported to IFCX.' Gap-analysis SOL-028: holds by construction once Booleans are applied inside ModelGeometry (plan.rs:111-145, render3d.rs:104-111 and writer.rs:361-382 all consume the same ModelGeometry), but slicing is horizontal only (slice.rs:35), section and elevation views do not exist yet, and no consistency test exists. The epic acceptance: 'the plan slice, the 3D body and the exported mesh hash identically'.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs: slice_plane(mesh, plane) -> Vec<Vec<DVec2>> generalising slice_loops to any plane (rotate into the plane frame, reuse the horizontal routine), the primitive sections-elevations-dims builds on. mesh.rs: mesh_hash(&TriMesh) with coordinates quantised to 1e-6 m and triangles rotated to their smallest key and sorted. samples::solid_operations() is extended with an auxiliary operator, a multi-element opening and a split wall; the golden is re-blessed. New crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/consistency.rs: for every element of the sample, the hash of each evaluated part equals the hash of the mesh read back from the written file (Body_n parts by name, storey transform applied); the plan drawing at the cut height built from the evaluated geometry equals the one built from a ModelGeometry reconstructed from the file's meshes; a vertical slice_plane through every target gives identical loops from both; an archicraft-app test shows that build_scene emits exactly the evaluated part triangles. The solid-operation and further-cut cases join the NFR-MNT-005 table. Out of scope: section and elevation views themselves.
design: Hash identity is meaningful because plan, scene and writer read the same Arc<ElementGeometry>; the test guards against any view-specific geometry path appearing later. Quantise to the IFCX write precision (IFX-007) so file and memory compare exactly. Pitfalls: reading back needs the composed tree (container parse and flatten in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs) and the storey transforms; f32 scene positions cannot be compared bit-exactly, so compare within 1e-4 m relative to the scene origin; keep the reconstruction helper in test code, not in the reader. Pointers: slice.rs:35, plan.rs:111-145, render3d.rs:102-176, writer.rs mesh_attribute, validate.rs, tests/roundtrip.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- consistency.rs passes for every element of solid_operations() and openings_showcase(): equal part hashes, equal plan cut regions, equal vertical slices.
- The app scene test passes: same triangle count and positions equal within f32 precision after removing the scene origin.
- App test for SOL-022 'update the result in all views without a manual rebuild': after Workspace::execute moves an operator by 0.10 m, the next Document::plan drawing and the next build_scene (new SceneKey revision) both show the cut shifted by 0.10 m, with no rebuild action.
- slice_plane unit tests: a unit cube cut by a vertical, a horizontal and an inclined plane gives the expected square, square and rectangle loops.
- The golden solid-operations.ifcx is re-blessed and reviewed; conformance/run.sh passes on all goldens.
- Satisfies the 'in all views' clause of SOL-022 and SOL-028 for plan, 3D and IFCX now, and prepares it for section and elevation views through the shared ModelGeometry and slice_plane (re-asserted by sections-elevations-dims).
notes: SRS: SOL-028 SOL-022. SOL-022 here is its 'update in all views without a manual rebuild' clause. Also NFR-MNT-005 and IFX-007 (re-asserted).

title: Stair flights, landings, finishes, plan symbol and compound parts
description:
Build the stair geometry: straight, L, U and polyline stairs with flight and landing segments and corner turning types, landing-corner riser offsets, node insertion with automatic landings of at least 1.00 m and surplus placement, symmetric riser distribution, the locked-baseline option, finishes and structure (none, monolithic smooth or stepped), seam suppression between same-material parts, part-level failure reporting with fallback, the plan symbol with step lines, walking line, break line and up/down label, display on the home storey and the storey above through the display range, and IfcStair with IfcStairFlight and IfcSlab children through the compound codec, with parts addressable in the edit mode.

Risks: Stepped bodies with finishes have many coplanar faces; closedness and tolerance merging are asserted on every generated stair. Winders, spirals, stringers and conversions are railings-stairs-adv.
design: archicraft-geometry stair.rs with flight and landing generators producing parts (treads, risers, structure) from a general polyhedron builder beyond extrude.rs, seam suppression via per-part edge flags, the plan symbol as renderer-agnostic primitives with the break line computed from the cut plane; archicraft-model segment list on Stair and PartRef::{Flight, Landing, Step} with ids derived from segment index and role; archicraft-ifcx compound children Flight_n and Landing_n through the framework's parts codec.
acceptance_criteria: A U-stair with 22 risers has 11 + 11 with a landing of at least 1.00 m and the surplus placed per option; inserting a node creates an automatic landing; locking the baseline keeps node positions and adapts the step distribution only; all parts are closed bodies and feature edges between same-material treads are suppressed; an unbuildable part is reported and the stair falls back to the last valid body; the plan symbol shows step lines, walking line, arrow and the break line at the configured height, and the storey above shows only the part above the break line (ELM-008 range); the AS-01 U-stair exports IfcStair with IfcStairFlight and IfcSlab landing children and passes conformance (IFX-016 re-asserted); entering edit mode selects a single flight and its properties (kittest on PartRef::Flight).
notes: SRS: STA-020 STA-021 STA-022 STA-023 STA-029 STA-040 STA-041 STA-043 STA-044 STA-045 STA-046 STA-051

title: Report unbuildable stair parts and fall back to simple joints
description:
WHY: STA-044 (S): if a requested part (for example a stringer corner piece) cannot be built from the available geometry, the system shall report the element and the cause and fall back to a simple joint, never silently omitting geometry (KB 304002). The epic acceptance adds that an unbuildable part is reported and the stair falls back to the last valid body. NFR-REL-005/006 and STA-011 (keep the last valid stair) set the same rule at element level. Gap row STA-044: ElementGeometry has no per-part warnings (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:31-35); element-kind-framework-13 only offers a fallback box for a whole failed element.

WHAT: ElementGeometry gains warnings: Vec<PartWarning {role, cause, fallback}> (role = Flight_n or Landing_n); ModelGeometry exposes them to the problems panel (UI-012, element-kind-framework-14) as warnings with element and part label, for example 'ST-001 Stair, landing 1: the smooth underside of flight 1 cannot meet the landing; simple joint used'. Fallback rules in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/: the flight-to-landing underside corner that cannot be built becomes a vertical butt joint; a stepped underside whose profile self-intersects becomes a smooth underside; a landing polygon that degenerates at a sharp polyline corner becomes a square joint at the flight end; a finish whose tread thickness reaches R or whose nosing reaches the going is clamped to the largest buildable value. Whole-stair failure: rule conflicts never reach the geometry, because stair-solver-tool rejects conflicting edits atomically and keeps a stale stair's stored solution (stair-solver-tool-04/05, STA-011); a geometry-level failure (layout() failing on the stored parameters, a part still unbuildable after its fallback, or a generator panic caught by the framework guard) sets GeometryProblem.fallback (element-kind-framework-13) to the element's last valid ElementGeometry instead of the framework box when one exists (kept per element id in ModelGeometry next to problems, carried by evaluate_incremental for clean elements, dropped on delete), so plan, 3D and picking keep showing the previous stair; the framework box remains for stairs that were never valid. Part warnings appear in the Geometry section of the problems panel through element-kind-framework-14's ProblemSource, next to stair-solver-tool-11's stair_problems entries. The writer keeps the framework rule (no fallback mesh written, one warning, IFX-063). Out of scope: stringer corner pieces themselves (STA-042, railings-stairs-adv; the warning type is ready for them).
design: Distinguish part fallbacks (deterministic geometry from the current parameters, written to IFCX, listed as warnings) from element fallbacks (previous geometry or the framework box, never written, listed as problems). Implement each fallback as an explicit branch with a test fixture rather than catching generator errors generically, because the cause text must name the part and the reason. The last-valid cache lives in ModelGeometry next to problems (BTreeMap<ElementId, Arc<ElementGeometry>>) and is updated only when an element evaluates without problems; incremental evaluation (element-kind-framework-10) must carry it for clean elements. Pitfalls: the in_guarded_evaluation flag of element-kind-framework-13 must also cover stair evaluation so a generator panic does not write a crash report; warnings must be deterministic (sorted by role) so the problems panel does not flicker; the clamped finish must still respect the closedness invariant. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:31-60 (ElementGeometry, ModelGeometry.problems), element-kind-framework-13 (GeometryProblem, body_or_fallback), stair/structure.rs and finish.rs (04, 05), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:361-417.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair.rs impossible_underside_corner: a stair whose flight waist cannot meet the landing underside yields one PartWarning naming the stair, Landing_1 and the cause, the butt-joint bodies are present and closed, and every flight and landing role still has a non-empty child.
- stepped_underside_fallback: horizontal thickness larger than the going gives a warning and a smooth underside.
- sharp_corner_fallback: a 30 degree polyline corner whose landing polygon degenerates gives a warning and a closed square joint.
- never_silently_omitted: property test over random settings: every layout flight and landing has a non-empty child, or the stair has a warning or problem that names it.
- last_valid_body: a stair whose geometry fails after all part fallbacks (the test writes such parameters into the project directly, as the framework's fallback-box tests do, because commands reject rule conflicts) is listed as a problem, plan and 3D show the previous ElementGeometry (equal to the geometry before the change) and pick() returns the stair; restoring the parameters clears the problem; a stair that was never valid shows the framework box.
- A stair made stale by a storey-height change (stair-solver-tool-05) keeps the body of its stored solution and has no geometry problem (regression).
- Headless workspace test: the problems panel lists the warning and selecting it selects the stair (UI-012 path of element-kind-framework-14).
- Round trip: saving a stair in fallback state writes it without a body plus one warning; a stair with only part warnings writes its fallback-joint bodies (they are real geometry from the parameters).
- Satisfies STA-044 and the keep-last-valid clause of the epic acceptance.
notes:
SRS: STA-044
Related: STA-011 (keep last valid stair), NFR-REL-005, NFR-REL-006, UI-012, IFX-063.

title: Lay out flights, landings and risers with corner offsets
description:
WHY: The user-visible core of the epic is a stair that turns: STA-020 (M) asks for straight, L-shaped, U-shaped and arbitrary polyline stairs built from flight and landing segments with landing turns at every interior corner; STA-021 (M) defines the two riser offsets of a landing corner (fixed or minimum, length or multiples of the going, optionally linked, optionally summing to one going, 0 = flush with the landing edge); STA-023 (M) asks that both flights of a half-landing stair can get the same riser count and that equal offsets at both corners produce a symmetric U-stair, with the test 22 risers with one landing give 11 + 11; STA-029 (S) with the lock off (the default): flights between turns lengthen or shorten automatically so that all enabled rules are met exactly (the locked mode is task 14). The epic acceptance repeats the 11 + 11 U-stair. What stair-solver-tool already provides and this task extends: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/walking.rs (band edges with mitred joins, inner side, walking line at the inner-edge distance, arc-length parametrisation point_at/tangent_at, riser_lines across the band), stair/solve.rs solve(params, total_rise) -> Solved {solution, baseline, warnings} that reaches the run length by moving only the last baseline node, StairSolution with one going, stair/conflict.rs RuleConflict with verified alternatives, and Kind::resolve storing the adjusted baseline and the solution on success (stair-solver-tool-03/04). Missing (gap rows STA-020, STA-021, STA-023, STA-029): landing polygons, corner offsets, the distribution of risers over several flights and per-flight node adjustment.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/layout.rs with the pure function layout(&StairParams, &StairSolution) -> Result<StairLayout, LayoutError>, built on walking.rs's band edges and walking-line parametrisation (no second offset implementation). StairLayout {nodes (effective baseline), outline, walking_line, flights: Vec<FlightRun {segment, first_riser, risers, going, origin, direction, outline}>, landings: Vec<LandingRun {source: LandingSource {Segment(u16), Corner(u16)}, polygon, z, length, surplus, surplus_at}>, risers: Vec<RiserLine {a, b, z, station}>}, everything in walking-line order, plus roles() returning [Flight_1, Landing_1, Flight_2, ...] for the parts of task 04. Algorithm: build each landing polygon from the two adjacent flight bands (90 degree L, U through a landing segment between two corners, arbitrary polyline angles); resolve the riser offsets at each landing corner along the walking line (Fixed exactly, Minimum at least its value and absorbing what whole goings cannot fill, Length in metres or Goings(k) x going, link_equal, sum_to_one_going); distribute N over the flights by largest remainder proportional to the available walking-line length, at least one riser per flight, with equal_flights giving ceil/floor halves to the two flights of a half-landing stair. walking.rs riser_lines delegates to the layout, so risers skip landings. solve.rs is extended, not replaced: the run length counts flights only, and each flight's end node moves along its stored segment direction so that its goings x going plus offsets fit exactly (generalising stair-solver-tool-03's last-node move; resolve keeps storing the adjusted baseline, so the stored nodes are always the effective ones); StairSolution gains flights: Vec<FlightSolution {risers, goings, going}> (equal goings while unlocked; task 14 adds per-flight goings), and the archicraft::stair reader of stair-solver-tool-07 recomputes flights when an older file lacks them. Layout failures inside solve (LayoutError::SegmentTooShort with the segment index, a turn of 170 degrees or more through a single corner) become RuleConflict {cause: DrawnGeometry} with the existing AdjustRun alternative, so a stored stair always lays out. New samples::u_stair() in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs through the FixtureBuilder (element-kind-framework-03): storeys 0 and 3.30 m, TargetHeight(0.150) giving 22 risers, width 1.00 m, flight / landing / flight baseline, D.2 finish and structure from the template slot; it is not yet listed in samples::catalogue(), which would require its golden (task 11), and tasks 04-13 use it. Out of scope: the lock-baseline option (14), in-run node insertion and surplus placement (03), Kind::parts() and bodies (04), plan symbol (08), winders.
design: Keep the layout headless next to the solver: the bodies (04), the plan symbol (08) and the part outlines of edit mode (12) all consume StairLayout, and the model must not depend on geometry (NFR-MNT-002); glam suffices (archicraft-model has no geo dependency; reuse validate::validate_ring for checks). Work in walking-line stations (arc length along the walking line, walking.rs) and convert to plan points per flight frame; riser lines are perpendicular to the flight direction across the full width. Landing polygon: intersect the left and right edge lines of the adjacent flights (parallel-line guard through the tolerance module's is_parallel), close with the flight end lines. Distribution: largest-remainder apportionment is deterministic, ties go to the earlier flight, equal_flights applies only to exactly two flights (document). Lock off adjusts the stored baseline through resolve exactly as stair-solver-tool already does for the last node, so node positions have one source of truth and switching the lock on later (14) needs no conversion. A landing counts as the tread of the riser before it; STA-024 ends change goings = risers +/- 1 per flight end. Tolerances through the framework's tolerance module (MODEL_TOLERANCE 1e-5 m). Pitfalls: offsets longer than the segment (SegmentTooShort with the segment index); the walking line on a turn is measured on its own offset line, not on the baseline; downward input (STA-002) stores the baseline bottom-up so the layout never sees reversed stairs; resolve must stay idempotent (stair-solver-tool-03 property test) with several moved nodes; the L-shaped stair C of samples::stairs() now gets a corner landing and a new solution, which changes stairs.ifcx only when task 04 re-blesses it (review that diff). Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/walking.rs, solve.rs, solver.rs (check, going_range), conflict.rs and kinds/stair.rs (stair-solver-tool-02/03/04); crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs (validate_ring, segment helpers); crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs (FixtureBuilder).
acceptance_criteria:
- New crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_layout.rs: straight stair, storeys at 0 and 3.300 m, 22 risers (R = 150 mm, STA-004 test), going 0.300 m: one flight, 22 riser lines, riser k at z = k x 0.150 within 1e-9, and the walking-line distance between first and last riser equals the number of goings x 0.300 for the STA-024 default ends; the straight-stair cases of crates/archicraft-model/tests/stair_solver.rs (stair-solver-tool) pass unchanged.
- u_stair_has_symmetric_flights: samples::u_stair() (flight, landing segment, flight; width 1.00 m; 22 risers; equal riser offsets 0 at both corners): flights 11 + 11, landing depth along the walking line at least 1.00 m, riser lines of the two flights mirror each other about the stair axis within MODEL_TOLERANCE (STA-023 test).
- 21 risers with equal_flights give 11 + 10 (lower flight takes the extra riser, documented); without equal_flights the split is proportional to the flight lengths.
- l_stair_offsets: 90 degree L with before Fixed Length(0) and after Fixed Goings(0.5): the first riser after the corner lies half a going from the landing edge; Fixed Length(0.10) puts it exactly 0.10 m from the edge; link_equal makes both 0.5 going; Minimum offsets with sum_to_one_going resolve to before + after = one going; a Minimum Goings(0.5) offset is never shorter than half a going and grows by the remainder its flight cannot fill with whole goings; offset 0 puts the riser line on the landing edge within MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- polyline_120_degrees: a three-segment polyline with a 120 degree corner yields a landing polygon accepted by archicraft_model::validate::validate_ring and flight outlines that do not overlap.
- unlocked_flights_follow_the_rules: samples::u_stair() with its storey height changed from 3.300 to 3.000 m through the storey command (stair-solver-tool-05 re-solve): the first node stays, the other nodes move along their segment directions, every flight uses the solver going, every enabled rule holds exactly, and one undo restores the original baseline (STA-029 off).
- A drawn segment too short for its risers returns RuleConflict {cause: DrawnGeometry} naming the segment and offering AdjustRun; nothing panics.
- Property test (seeded random loop): 2-5 nodes, corner angles 30-180 degrees, random widths, sides and offsets give either Ok with the sum of risers = N, strictly increasing riser z and every riser line inside the outline, or a RuleConflict; never a panic or a NaN.
- roles_follow_topology: StairLayout::roles() of samples::u_stair() is [Flight_1, Landing_1, Flight_2] before and after a storey-height change.
- Satisfies the layout of STA-020, STA-021, STA-023 and the lock-off behaviour of STA-029.
notes:
SRS: STA-020 STA-021 STA-023 STA-029
Test values: STA-004 3.300 m / 22 = 150.00 mm; STA-007 default rules with R = 150 mm give 300 <= G <= 350 mm.
Related: STA-011 (layout failures surface as RuleConflict with alternatives), STA-024.
Open: rounding rule for odd counts with equal_flights (lower flight takes the extra riser, proposed).

title: Select flights, landings and steps in stair edit mode
description:
WHY: The epic acceptance requires that entering edit mode selects a single flight and shows its properties (kittest on PartRef::Flight). SEL-008 (M, delivered as infrastructure by selection-transforms) gives compound elements an edit mode in which parts are selectable, explicitly naming segments and steps; the flights and landings of STA-020 are the stair's parts, and STA-022 node edits renumber them. selection-transforms-01 lets each kind register its own part enum through the kinds! macro and the Kind selection-part hooks (part_refs, part_ref_for_role, part_label, part_anchor, part_outline, validate_part); selection-transforms-08 enables 'Edit parts' for kinds with non-empty part_refs; no stair parts are registered yet.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/stair.rs registers type Part = StairPart {Flight {index: u16}, Landing {index: u16}, Step {flight: u16, index: u16}} and implements the hooks: part_refs (flights and landings in walking-line order, then the steps), part_ref_for_role (Flight_n -> Flight {n - 1}, Landing_n -> Landing {n - 1}; used by the 3D id buffer of selection-transforms-06), part_label ('flight 2', 'landing 1', 'step 5 of flight 1'), part_anchor (walking-line midpoint of the part), part_outline (flight, landing or tread polygon from StairLayout, tasks 02-03) and validate_part (indices within the current layout); KindDescriptor.part_roles lists the role stems Flight and Landing (1-based suffix, documented), indices in walking-line order matching the IFCX roles (role index = index + 1). Steps are selected in plan only. Properties: the part section of the properties strip (selection-transforms-08 keeps element fields read-only in edit mode) shows for a flight its riser count, riser height, going and length (computed) and its segment type (flight or landing, editable); for a landing its length and surplus (computed), for a corner landing its turning type and before/after riser offsets (editable), and the stair-wide landing minimum and surplus placement (editable, labelled as stair-wide); for a step its index, z, R and going; edits issue one UpdateElements on the stair. The fields go through the stair's FieldSpec declarations with a part-aware getter if properties-and-dialogs-05 has landed, otherwise as part rows beside stair-solver-tool-10's stair fields in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs; the app code stays kind-agnostic in the first case. Out of scope: settings dialogs and node insertion (13), part transforms.
design: Indices refer to the parametric definition in walking-line order, never to mesh triangles (selection-transforms risk note); they are the same order that produces the IFCX roles, so 'flight 2' in the UI is Flight_2 in the file. Step selection in 3D would need per-tread ids in the id buffer; resolving to the flight is enough for this epic and is documented. The part section fields go through the kind's FieldSpec declarations (properties-and-dialogs-05) with a part-aware getter so the app stays kind-agnostic; computed fields use the ELM-017 live mechanism. Pitfalls: the layout must be available to part hooks without the geometry crate: call the model's layout with the solver result, cached per element revision if profiling shows it matters; segment-type edits change the part list, so run retain_valid after the command. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/selection.rs (selection-transforms-01), kinds/stair.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs edit-mode overlays and crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs (selection-transforms-08), crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs id buffer (selection-transforms-06).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in kinds/stair.rs: part_refs of samples::u_stair() are [Flight 0, Landing 0, Flight 1] followed by its steps; part_ref_for_role('Landing_1') is Landing {0}; part_outline equals the layout polygons; validate_part rejects Flight {5} and steps beyond the flight's riser count; after remove_node (03) Selection::retain_valid drops a stale Flight {1}.
- kittest stair_edit_mode_selects_single_flight: samples::u_stair(), select the stair, press Enter, click inside the second flight: the selection is exactly [(stair, Some(PartRef::Kind(KindPart::Stair(StairPart::Flight {index: 1}))))], the strip shows the stair name with 'flight 2', 11 risers and the going; Esc leaves edit mode and the selection is [(stair, None)].
- kittest: with landing 1 selected in edit mode, changing the surplus placement and the after offset each execute one UpdateElements and undo restores them.
- render3d/view3d unit test: a pick on the landing body returns PartRef Landing {0}.
- The module-layout test of selection-transforms stays green (no StairPart in crates/archicraft-app/src).
- Satisfies the stair side of SEL-008 and makes the STA-020 flights and landings addressable.
notes:
SRS: STA-020 STA-022
Related: SEL-008 (edit-mode infrastructure owned by selection-transforms).

title: Generate closed tread, riser and landing bodies as stair parts
description:
WHY: Users must see and export real stairs: STA-020 (M) shapes become bodies, STA-040 (M) the finish (tread and riser thickness, nosing projection, tread and riser gaps, open-riser mode, separate settings for flights and landings) shapes them, and STA-001 requires that changing any input regenerates all steps and landings without manual repair. The epic acceptance requires that all parts are closed bodies, and the epic risk names coplanar faces of stepped bodies. What exists: stair-solver-tool-06 added crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair.rs with provisional_body (one stepped prism per baseline segment), TriMesh::transformed(&DAffine3) in mesh.rs and extrude_profile(profile, frame, w0, w1) in extrude.rs on top of extrude() (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18), and registered the stair GeometryKind in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/stair.rs; element-kind-framework-07 already writes compound children with their own class from ElementGeometry.children (PartGeometry {role, parts, axis}) keyed by Kind::parts(), which is still empty for the stair.

WHAT: Reuse stair-solver-tool-06's profile extrusion: extrude_profile and TriMesh::transformed (winding flipped for negative determinants) already extrude a planar profile in an arbitrary frame, so no second prism builder is added; mesh.rs gains only TriMesh::append_disjoint(&TriMesh), which appends a closed shell and asserts in debug builds that no edge is shared. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair.rs becomes crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/mod.rs plus finish.rs: from StairLayout (02, 03, 14), per flight in its frame: treads (with nosing and tread gap, thickness from the flight FinishSettings), risers (between the tread planes, shortened by the riser gap, absent with open_risers), per landing a finish slab from LandingRun.polygon with the landing FinishSettings (extrude() as is); output ElementGeometry.children in walking-line order with the roles of StairLayout::roles(), each with body parts named by role and material (Treads, Risers; IFX-017). provisional_body and its block fallback are deleted, and the stair tool's 3D preview (InputConsumer::preview_body, stair-solver-tool-09) switches to the new generator. The stair's Kind::parts() in crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/stair.rs now returns PartSpec Flight_n -> IfcClass::StairFlight and Landing_n -> IfcClass::Slab from StairLayout::roles(), in the same task as the children so the framework's role-equality test never fails in between. The stair GeometryKind calls layout() with the stored StairSolution and never re-solves (a stale stair keeps its body, stair-solver-tool-04/05). Structure bodies come in task 05 (until then StairStructure is ignored and documented so). Re-bless stairs.ifcx (stair-solver-tool-07) and review the diff (the framework codec now writes IfcStairFlight and IfcSlab children). Out of scope: structure (05), seam suppression (06), part failure fallbacks (07), plan symbol (08), stringers (STA-042).
design: Approach: every tread, riser and landing finish is a prism of a 2D profile, so stair-solver-tool-06's extrude_profile covers them all: a tread is a rectangle in the flight's (u, z) plane extruded across the width, a landing finish is the plan polygon extruded vertically (extrude.rs as is). Group same-role shells of one flight into one mesh only if they are disjoint (treads of consecutive steps are separated by R minus the tread thickness; risers never touch each other), which keeps check_closed valid for multi-shell meshes; touching shells of different roles stay in different BodyParts. Use the frame transform from FlightRun.origin/direction with the storey-local z of the layout (bodies are storey-local, evaluate.rs header). Pitfalls: tread thickness >= R or nosing >= going makes shells touch or overlap (return a part error that task 07 turns into a report; never emit overlapping shells); coincident points from different shells must not be merged by MERGE_STEP (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:53) inside one mesh; keep shells in deterministic order so golden bytes are stable (IFX-007); MAX_MESH_POINTS is not checked by the writer (technical debt), so keep one mesh per role and flight instead of one per stair. Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs (extrude, extrude_profile), mesh.rs (transformed, add_face at mesh.rs:83, check_closed at mesh.rs:122), evaluate.rs:22-48 (BodyPart, ElementGeometry, children from element-kind-framework-07), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/stair.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:361 (write_element), crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:131 and :198.
acceptance_criteria:
- mesh.rs unit test: append_disjoint of two separated boxes passes TriMesh::check_closed, and appending a touching box panics in debug builds; the extrude_profile/transformed tests of stair-solver-tool-06 are extended with a non-convex L profile in a rotated and in a mirrored frame: closed, outward oriented (signed volume = area x depth within 1e-9) and with its own vertices per planar face (IFX-038).
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair.rs (stair-solver-tool-06, provisional-body cases replaced): samples::u_stair() has children Flight_1, Landing_1, Flight_2; tread and riser counts per flight follow the layout (11/11 risers); the tread top of step k lies at k x R within 1e-9; the nosing projects by FinishSettings.nosing beyond the riser face; open_risers removes the Risers part; tread and riser gaps shrink the bodies by the gap; the landing finish top lies at the landing z; a landing finish of 0.040 m with a flight finish of 0.025 m gives a 0.040 m landing slab while the treads stay 0.025 m (separate flight and landing settings).
- Closedness property test over random layouts (seeded, reusing the generator of task 02): every BodyPart mesh passes check_closed, has positive volume, at most MAX_MESH_POINTS points and no edge shared between two shells of the same mesh.
- The framework registry test 'roles of ElementGeometry.children equal Kind::parts()' passes for stairs; changing the storey height regenerates all treads without stale children (STA-001).
- The stair tool's 3D preview builds its ghost from the new generator (stair-solver-tool-09 vertex-building test updated) and the module-layout test shows the stair only in stair/, kinds/stair.rs and one kinds/mod.rs line of archicraft-geometry.
- plan_drawing slices the new bodies through the generic classification (until 08) and render3d build_scene includes them; crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs written_meshes_are_closed_bodies and golden_files_are_reproduced pass after re-blessing stairs.ifcx, and conformance/run.sh is green.
- Satisfies the body part of STA-020 and STA-040 (flight and landing finish, open risers, gaps, nosing).
notes:
SRS: STA-020 STA-040
Appendix D.2: tread and riser finish 0.025 m. MAX_MESH_POINTS 65,535 (IFX-038).

title: Verify exit criterion: Single- and multi-plane roofs with a pitch-weighted straight skeleton
description:
WHY: The epic delivers ROF-001, ROF-002, ROF-003, ROF-004, ROF-005, ROF-006, ROF-007, ROF-008, ROF-009, ROF-011, ROF-012 and DW-021 for increment 2 (Envelope and site), whose exit criterion 'AS-01 without railings and AS-02 pass' needs the gable roof that cleanup-and-trims then trims the gable walls to. This task verifies the whole against the epic's acceptance, not against the individual tasks.

WHAT: On the merged work run cargo test, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check; conformance/run.sh on every golden file including roofs.ifcx; the roof corpus, randomised and body suites; the kittest suite; the release-mode performance test of roofs-10, now with a roof opening and a roof window on the dragged roof; and a split of a roof carrying a roof window. Update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence and gap rows in section 4.16, DW-021 in 4.18, the roof-host clauses of OPN-001 and OPN-006 in 4.17, the roofs row of MEA-003, the notice clause of NFR-USE-004, IFX-016 re-asserted, the increment-2 readiness line), file follow-up beads (limited-depth openings in roofs, perpendicular openings in sloped slabs through the roof-plane hole path (deferred by host-openings-01 and -06), per-edge level pitches if users ask for them (O-9), the IFCX parent of hosted elements in multi-plane roofs if the viewer check suggests the plane node) and close the epic in beads.
design: Verification only; no new code except status and documentation edits. Walk the task list with `bd show roofs`, run the commands of .github/workflows/ci.yml locally (build, test, fmt, clippy, the reference_models example and conformance/run.sh), run the performance test with --release, and compare the epic's SRS IDs with the changed rows of docs/implementation-status.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fixture corpus (rectangle, L, T, U, notched footprints; equal and mixed pitches; gable edges) produces planes whose ridge heights and hip/valley lines match hand-computed values and every roof body is closed and manifold.
- A randomised footprint test asserts closed output or a reported problem.
- The four eaves-cut variants pass.
- A mansard with one break level passes.
- The AS-01 gable roof is generated from the selected exterior walls with the pivot at the wall top.
- Dragging the pivot line regenerates within 200 ms on the stand-in.
- IfcRoof with one part per plane passes conformance (IFX-016 re-asserted).
- A roof window is hosted in a plane and cuts it with a Void.
- Split into single-plane roofs shows the one-time notice.
- cargo test, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green on the workspace.
- conformance/run.sh is green on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx (including roofs.ifcx) and on the reference models written by examples/reference_models.rs.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for ROF-001, ROF-002, ROF-003, ROF-004, ROF-005, ROF-006, ROF-007, ROF-008, ROF-009, ROF-011, ROF-012 and DW-021 with evidence pointing at the new modules and tests, plus the roof-host clauses of OPN-001 and OPN-006 and the notice clause of NFR-USE-004.
- The epic is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for remaining work.
notes: SRS: ROF-001 ROF-002 ROF-003 ROF-004 ROF-005 ROF-006 ROF-007 ROF-008 ROF-009 ROF-011 ROF-012 DW-021. Appendix F increment 2 exit criterion: AS-01 without railings and AS-02 pass (the gable-wall trim belongs to cleanup-and-trims).

title: Add the as08_check checker for the NFR-USE-001 modelling task
description:
WHY: NFR-USE-001 (M) counts a participant as successful when, within 30 minutes and without assistance, they model a single-storey building with exterior and interior walls, a floor slab, two doors, three windows and a gable roof and save it as IFCX; AS-08 needs at least 4 of 5. Whether a saved model meets that must be judged the same way for every participant and recorded, otherwise the verdict depends on the moderator. No such check exists (gap row NFR-USE-001: nothing planned or run).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/as08_check.rs, declared in crates/archicraft-ifcx/Cargo.toml as an [[example]] with test = true so its unit tests run under cargo test --workspace (usability-specific logic stays out of the IFCX adapter, NFR-MNT-004). It loads the file with archicraft_ifcx::load and checks the loaded Project: (1) exactly one storey holds elements; (2) at least four walls whose position is exterior (written as bsi::ifc::prop::IsExternal, IFX-022) form one closed loop, consecutive reference lines meeting within MODEL_TOLERANCE; (3) at least one interior wall; (4) at least one floor slab; (5) at least two doors and (6) at least three windows, each hosted in a wall; (7) a gable roof: at least two roof planes with pitch > 0 whose eave lines are parallel and on opposite sides of a common ridge, as separate roofs or one multi-plane roof; (8) the file passes the in-process IFCX validation with no errors. It prints one PASS or FAIL line per criterion and a summary, exits 0 only when all pass, and with --json writes the results for the session sheet. Out of scope: the protocol and pilot (13), the sessions (14).
design: The checker judges the model the participant built, not strings in the file: after archicraft_ifcx::load it uses the kind registry of element-kind-framework (doors and windows through their host relation, roofs through their planes and pitches, exterior walls through the element position). Gable rule: at least two roof planes with pitch > 0 whose eave lines are parallel and on opposite sides of a common ridge, either as separate roofs or as one multi-plane roof; a hip roof fails, a gable roof with trimmed gable walls passes. Counts are minimums (an extra window does not fail a participant). Build the seeded variants with the FixtureBuilder of element-kind-framework so they stay valid as kinds evolve.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests on seeded projects built through commands: a house that meets the task passes every criterion; variants without a roof, with a mono-pitch roof, with one door, with two windows, with an open exterior loop, without an interior wall, with a door not hosted in a wall, and with elements on two storeys each fail exactly the expected criterion.
- The seeded house saved through Document::to_bytes and reloaded passes, so the check works on files written by the application.
- `cargo run -p archicraft-ifcx --example as08_check -- house.ifcx` prints one line per criterion and exits 0 only when all pass; --json output is documented in docs/testing.md.
- cargo test --workspace runs the example's tests; clippy -D warnings and fmt are green.
- Prepares the objective success check of NFR-USE-001 and AS-08.
notes:
SRS: NFR-USE-001
Split out of release-candidate-13 during review.

title: Write the AS-08 usability protocol and materials and run a pilot
description:
WHY: NFR-USE-001 (M, demonstration): users who know another CAD/BIM tool watch a 15-minute introduction; within 30 minutes they shall model a single-storey building with exterior and interior walls, a floor slab, two doors, three windows and a gable roof, and save it as IFCX; at least 4 of 5 test users must succeed without assistance. AS-08 (SRS 7.2) runs it with five participants. Nothing exists yet: no protocol, introduction or task card (gap row NFR-USE-001; AS-08 not yet possible). Without a fixed protocol the result is neither repeatable nor defensible.

WHAT: docs/usability/protocol.md (goal and pass rule; participant profile and screener: trained in Archicad, Revit, Vectorworks or AutoCAD, not involved in ArchiCraft, a mix of operating systems; setup: release build from the release workflow on reference-class hardware, an empty ARCHICRAFT_DATA_DIR so the first start is real, mouse with wheel, 1920x1080 display, UI language of the participant's choice; moderator and observer roles; timing: 15-minute introduction, then 30 minutes from reading the task card; assistance: any hint about the product counts and fails the participant, a crash counts as a product failure; success: the saved file passes as08_check (19) within the 30 minutes; recorded data; privacy: pseudonymous ids P1..P5, recordings only with written consent and deleted after analysis, no personal data in the repository; finding severity 1 to 4 and the rule that every finding becomes a bead labelled usability and as-08), docs/usability/introduction.md (timed script and demo project), docs/usability/task-card.md (the NFR-USE-001 task with a 10 x 8 m footprint, in English and German), docs/usability/session-sheet.md and docs/usability/consent-form.md (template). One pilot session with a person outside the core team on a release build (a release-workflow artefact if 02 has landed, otherwise `cargo build --release`), results in docs/usability/pilot-<date>.md, and the protocol adjusted. Out of scope: the checker (19), the five real sessions (14).
design: Rehearse the introduction in the pilot to keep it within 15 minutes; a recorded screen video of the introduction gives every participant the same content (decide in the protocol). The task card names the outcome, not the commands, so it does not double as assistance. The likely test location is Austria or Germany, so the consent-form template names purpose, storage period and deletion (GDPR); signed forms and recordings never enter the repository.
acceptance_criteria:
- The five documents exist (the task card in English and German) and the AS-08 row of docs/test-plan/README.md (or docs/testing.md) links them.
- The protocol states the pass rule exactly as NFR-USE-001 does: participants who know another CAD/BIM tool, a 15-minute introduction, 30 minutes for the task (single storey, exterior and interior walls, a floor slab, two doors, three windows, a gable roof, saved as IFCX), success without assistance, at least 4 of 5; and it prescribes as08_check (19) on every saved file.
- A timed rehearsal shows that the introduction fits in 15 minutes.
- The pilot ran on a release build, and its results file records time, completion, assists, as08_check output and the protocol changes it caused.
- Prepares NFR-USE-001 and AS-08.
notes:
SRS: NFR-USE-001
Epic risk: participant recruitment for AS-08; start recruiting when this task starts.
Review: the as08_check checker moved to release-candidate-19.

title: Fix remaining findings and confirm the fixes (buffer, part 2)
description:
WHY: The second part of the five-day buffer closes the remaining severity-2 and selected severity-3 findings and confirms that the fixes help users and broke nothing before the release candidate is cut, so that the NFR-USE-001 result of AS-08 holds for the released build.

WHAT: Fix the remaining findings within a two-day time box under the rules of 15; then, if AS-08 passed in 14, run a confirmation session with two new participants on the fixed build using the unchanged protocol and checker; if AS-08 failed, make sure the second full round (its own bead) is scheduled. Record outcomes in the results file and close or defer the remaining beads. Out of scope: the second full round itself.

title: Implement the pitch-weighted straight skeleton for roof planes
description:
WHY: ROF-003 (M): all planes, hips, valleys and ridges of a multi-plane roof shall be computed automatically, including for non-convex footprints and for different pitches per edge. Acceptance: an L-shaped footprint with all six edges sloped at 35° yields six planes with five hips, one valley and a ridge along the centre line of each wing, with adjacent planes meeting without gaps or overlaps (within 0.1 mm). docs/technology-choices.md (3D geometry) assigns this to our own code: a straight skeleton weighted by each edge's pitch, which no library in the stack provides. Gap row ROF-003: missing, effort XL, no skeleton code anywhere (crates/archicraft-geometry/Cargo.toml has glam, geo and spade only).

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/skeleton.rs, independent of model types: `weighted_skeleton(ring: &[DVec2], weights: &[f64]) -> Result<Skeleton, SkeletonError>` for a simple counter-clockwise ring with weights w_e = cot(pitch_e) > 0, returning `Skeleton { nodes: Vec<SkNode { pos, height }>, arcs: Vec<SkArc { a, b, left, right, class: Hip | Valley | Ridge }>, faces: Vec<SkFace { edge, ring }> }`. Implement event-driven wavefront propagation with edge events, split events and batched simultaneous events at one point (the equal-wing L and the square apex need them), ridge formation when parallel wavefront edges meet, deterministic tie-breaking and the result checks below. Create the fixture corpus in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/roof_corpus/mod.rs (rectangle, square, L with equal and with unequal wings, T, U, notched rectangle; 35° and mixed pitches) with the hand-computed expectations written next to each fixture, and the tests in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/roof_skeleton.rs. Out of scope: zero weights (gables), vertex events between several reflex vertices, collinear edges and the randomised test (all 04), break levels (09), bodies and overhangs (05).
design: Wavefront model after Felkel and Obdržálek (1998), generalised to weights (Eppstein and Erickson 1999; Kelly and Wonka 2011 for roof-style weighted events): time t is the height above the pivot elevation and edge e moves inward at w_e = cot(pitch_e) metres per metre, so the face of e is exactly the part of the roof lying in e's plane. Active vertex between edges a and b: stored creation point p0 and time t0, velocity v solving n_a · v = w_a and n_b · v = w_b (inward unit normals), position p(t) = p0 + v (t − t0) evaluated from the creation data, never accumulated. Edge event of the edge between i and j: the time its length reaches zero; split event of a reflex vertex r and a non-adjacent edge e: t = (c_e − n_e · p_r) / (n_e · v_r − w_e), accepted when the hit point lies between e's endpoints at time t. Queue: BinaryHeap keyed by (time via f64::total_cmp, event kind, smallest edge index) with lazy invalidation by vertex version counters. Batching: pop every event with time <= t0 + MODEL_TOLERANCE, cluster by position within MODEL_TOLERANCE, place the node at the least-squares point of the incident offset lines at that time (keeps the plane equations consistent), and splice the circular vertex lists around the node by angle. Arc class: horizontal arcs are ridges, arcs traced by a convex wavefront vertex are hips, by a reflex vertex valleys. Faces: walk the arcs from each edge's start to its end vertex. O(n² log n) is fine for roof outlines (< 100 edges, budget < 5 ms in release). Pitfalls: use MODEL_TOLERANCE and the near_zero/quantise helpers of crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs (element-kind-framework-01) only; keep the output deterministic (same input, same bits) by ordering clusters by edge indices; the 4-way node of the equal-wing L is one batched edge-plus-split event and must not be resolved as two nodes a few micrometres apart.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equal-wing L (0,0)-(12,0)-(12,6)-(6,6)-(6,12)-(0,12), all 35°: 6 faces, 5 hips, 1 valley (6,6)-(3,3), 2 ridges y = 3 (x 3..9) and x = 3 (y 3..9) at height 3 · tan 35° = 2.1006 m within 0.01 mm; this is the ROF-003 acceptance footprint.
- Unequal-wing L (0,0)-(14,0)-(14,6)-(8,6)-(8,14)-(0,14), all 35°: nodes (11,3) and (5,3) at 2.1006 m, (4,4) and (4,10) at 2.8008 m; 6 hips, 1 valley, 2 ridges.
- Rectangle 12 × 9 at 35°: ridge y = 4.5 from x = 4.5 to 7.5 at 3.1509 m; square 10 × 10: one apex node (5,5) at 3.5010 m with four hips.
- Mixed pitches, rectangle 10 × 8 with south 30° and north, east and west 45°: ridge at y = 5.0718 from x = 2.9282 to 7.0718 at 2.9282 m; T, U and notched footprints match the face counts, arc classes and node heights documented in the corpus.
- Invariants checked by every test (and inside the function in debug builds): face areas sum to the ring area within 1e-9 relative; every face ring is simple; every interior arc is shared by exactly two faces; at every node, height = tan(pitch_e) · dist(node, line_e) for every edge e whose face contains it, within 0.01 mm, so adjacent planes meet without gaps or overlaps within 0.1 mm.
- Invalid input (self-intersecting ring, non-positive weight, fewer than 3 vertices) returns SkeletonError and never panics.
- ROF-003 plan-level clauses satisfied for sloped edges; gables follow in roofs-04 and bodies in roofs-05.
notes: SRS: ROF-003. References: Felkel & Obdržálek 1998 (straight skeleton implementation), Eppstein & Erickson 1999 (raising roofs, crashing cycles), Kelly & Wonka 2011 (procedural extrusions), Biedl et al. 2015 (weighted straight skeletons: faces need not be monotone for arbitrary weights). Appendix D.1: model tolerance 0.01 mm. tan 35° = 0.70021, tan 30° = 0.57735.

title: Smoke-test release builds per OS and gate notes on hardware
description:
WHY: NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 (M) are only demonstrated when the packaged builds actually start, render and save on each OS, including both supported macOS majors and the current Ubuntu LTS; CI pins ubuntu-24.04 although 26.04 is the current LTS and tests a single macOS version (gap rows NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003). NFR-PORT-006 (M) requires a hardware-accelerated, non-deprecated API per OS and the minimum and reference hardware of NFR-PERF-001 to be published with every release; no release notes exist and README.md has no hardware section today. NFR-SEC-002 (M) forbids sending usage data, telemetry or crash reports, and NFR-SEC-004 allows network access only for consented import fetches; the no-telemetry clause holds today (no HTTP crate in Cargo.lock, gap row NFR-SEC-002), and a release should prove it on the shipped binary rather than by reading Cargo.lock.

WHAT: release.yml gains a smoke job matrix on the downloaded artefacts: windows-latest; the runner labels of the current and the previous macOS major, held in MACOS_CURRENT and MACOS_PREVIOUS next to MACOS_MIN of 02 (expected macos-27 and macos-26 in late 2026; re-check Apple's current major and GitHub's runner images for every release; a major without a hosted image records an explicit skip with the reason and makes the real-hardware run in 17 mandatory for it); and ubuntu-26.04 (or an ubuntu:26.04 container on ubuntu-24.04 while that runner image is not available) with Xvfb and Mesa lavapipe. Each runs `archicraft --smoke-test report.json` (18) from the unpacked archive, uploads the report and fails unless the exit code is 0, frames >= 60, reopened_ok is true, the os_version major matches the matrix entry and the backend is Dx12 or Vulkan on Windows, Metal on macOS and Vulkan on Linux. On Linux the smoke run also runs (a) under `unshare -rn` (no network namespace) to show fully offline operation and (b) under `strace -f -e trace=connect,sendto,sendmsg`, with scripts/check-no-network.py failing on any AF_INET or AF_INET6 connect to a non-loopback address. The ci.yml test matrix moves from ubuntu-24.04 to ubuntu-26.04. Release notes: docs/release-notes/TEMPLATE.md (Highlights; System requirements with operating systems, graphics API per OS, Minimum hardware and Reference hardware; Known limitations including unsigned builds and first-start registration; Licences) and scripts/check-release-notes.sh <version>, which fails when docs/release-notes/v<version>.md is missing or its hardware lists differ from the 'System requirements' section of README.md. That section is written by regression-and-status-18 from the NFR-PERF-001 decision; regression-and-status is not an ancestor of this epic, so if the section is missing this task adds it with the NFR-PERF-001 classes (marked as proposals while O-15 is open) and the graphics API per OS. On v* tags a publish job (permissions contents: write) runs check-release-notes.sh and creates a draft GitHub Release with the notes as body and the archives plus SHA256SUMS; a maintainer publishes it. Out of scope: runs on real hardware (17), choosing the concrete machines (regression-and-status-18, O-15).
design: CI smoke runs use software adapters (WARP on Windows, lavapipe on Linux; macOS runner VMs expose a paravirtualized Metal device), so device_type Cpu is accepted in CI while the real-hardware runs in 17 must report IntegratedGpu or DiscreteGpu. If a macOS runner exposes no Metal device, the job records an explicit skip with the reason and the manual check in 17 becomes mandatory for that version; never pass silently. Container packages: mesa-vulkan-drivers, xvfb, libxkbcommon-x11-0, libwayland-client0, strace; run under xvfb-run -a. unshare -rn needs unprivileged user namespaces, which Ubuntu 24.04 and later restrict through AppArmor (kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns): lift the restriction with sudo sysctl on the throwaway runner or use `sudo unshare -n` and drop back to the runner user; inside a container run privileged or skip with a message. Windows runners are Windows Server 2025 (Windows 11 24H2 code base), close to but not identical with Windows 11, so 17 keeps a manual run on Windows 11. Create the draft release with the gh CLI (gh release create --draft --notes-file), not a third-party action. Scripts use the Python 3 standard library and POSIX sh only.
acceptance_criteria:
- A workflow_dispatch run shows the smoke jobs green with uploaded reports: Windows, both macOS majors (os_version majors equal to MACOS_PREVIOUS and MACOS_CURRENT, or a recorded skip with its reason) and Linux 26.04.
- Each smoke job asserts the backend from the report: Dx12 or Vulkan on Windows, Metal on macOS, Vulkan on Linux; a scratch run with ARCHICRAFT_GRAPHICS=gl on Linux fails the job.
- A scratch run with a forced smoke failure fails the job and names the failing step in the log.
- check-no-network.py unit tests: a canned strace log with connect() to 127.0.0.1, ::1 or an AF_UNIX path passes; one with connect() to a public IPv4 or IPv6 address fails and names it.
- The Linux smoke run passes under unshare -rn and under strace with no non-loopback connect.
- check-release-notes.sh shell tests in scripts/tests/: a notes file created from the template with README's hardware lists passes; a differing hardware bullet or a missing section fails.
- README.md has a 'System requirements' section with the minimum and reference hardware and the graphics API per OS.
- A dry-run input (or a test tag in a fork) creates a draft release with the notes and four files (three archives, SHA256SUMS); the publish job refuses to run without a notes file.
- The ci.yml test job runs on ubuntu-26.04, windows-latest and macos-latest and is green.
- Satisfied: NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 for the CI-reachable OS versions; the API clause of NFR-PORT-006 checked on every release build and its publication clause; the automated no-traffic evidence for NFR-SEC-002 (Linux) and NFR-SEC-004.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003 NFR-PORT-006 NFR-SEC-002
Related: NFR-SEC-001 and NFR-SEC-004 (owned by regression-and-status, re-verified here); NFR-PERF-001 hardware classes (source: README 'System requirements', regression-and-status-18, not an ancestor in the epic graph: check with bd show and fall back as described). Re-check at release time which macOS major is current and which runner images exist.

description:

No new features. Defects found become new beads under the epic before it closes. The open follow-ups are recorded as beads or dependencies: the railing variant of RM-S (railings-stairs-adv) and the RM-M/RM-L goldens (perf-tuning-rm-m-l).

title: Add break levels for mansard roofs: skeleton, bodies and settings
description:
WHY: ROF-005 (S): a multi-plane roof shall support additional break levels (height above the pivot elevation and pitch above it), for mansard and similar roofs. Gap row: missing, effort L, depends on ROF-003. The epic time-boxes break levels because they are Should; keeping them in one leaf task lets the epic close without them if the box runs out.

WHAT: skeleton.rs: `weighted_skeleton_levels(ring, weights, levels: &[(height, weight)])` runs the propagation to each level height, flushes the events at that height, snapshots each wavefront component as a ring whose edges keep their original edge index, and restarts with the level weight for sloped edges (gables stay 0); faces are labelled (edge, level) and the horizontal break lines become a Break arc class. roof/regions.rs and roof/body.rs: one plane per (edge, level) with the bisector side plane on the break line and roles Plane_<k>_L<level> above level 0; metrics per plane. UI: a levels list in the roof settings (add and remove rows, height and pitch with unit-aware widgets, validation messages). IFCX: add a mansard to roof_showcase and re-bless roofs.ifcx. Out of scope: per-edge pitches per level.
design: At level height H: process every event with time <= H + MODEL_TOLERANCE first, then evaluate all active vertices at H, drop wavefront edges shorter than MODEL_TOLERANCE (merging their labels into the neighbours) and start a fresh propagation on the snapshot rings with the new weights; the faces of level k lie between the snapshots. The break line is horizontal, so the side plane between (e, k) and (e, k + 1) is the bisector of the two reference planes, as for hips, and the roofs-05 builder needs no new case. Part roles: roofs-01's parts() lists Plane_<k>_L<j> for every sloped edge and level, because the model cannot know which planes collapse; a plane that collapses below its level yields a PartGeometry without BodyPart, so element-kind-framework-15's role-equality test holds, and the part writer of element-kind-framework-07 skips part nodes without bodies (rule and test added here), so conformance never sees an empty part. Pitfalls: a level within tolerance of an event height (for example exactly at the ridge) must not create zero-length edges; a restart may split one wavefront into several components; extend the roofs-04 randomised test with one random level, and if vertex events at level heights fail there, limit levels to three and file a follow-up bead instead of extending the time box.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mansard fixture: rectangle 10 × 8, all edges 70°, one level at 2.40 m with 30°: the lower planes end at the break line 0.8735 m inside the pivot polygon and the ridge runs along y = 4.0 from x = 4.0 to 6.0 at 4.2051 m above the pivot elevation; 8 closed plane bodies; the lower and upper body of each edge share the break-line side face within 0.1 mm; node plane equations hold within 0.01 mm.
- An edge that collapses below the level gets no upper plane (its Plane_<k>_L1 child is empty and is not written to IFCX); a level above the ridge has no effect and raises no error; gable edges stay vertical through the level.
- roofs.ifcx with the mansard is reproduced, conformance/run.sh is green, Plane_<k>_L1 parts are present and the round trip restores the levels.
- kittest: adding a level in the roof settings regenerates the roof; a level height of 0 or below the previous level is rejected with a message.
- Satisfies ROF-005.
notes: SRS: ROF-005. Time-boxed (Should). Open question (O-9): one pitch per level for all sloped edges; per-edge level pitches are not offered. Hand values: 2.40 · cot 70° = 0.8735 m; 2.40 + 3.1265 · tan 30° = 4.2051 m.

title: Write minidump crash reports through an out-of-process handler
description:
WHY: NFR-SEC-002 (M) says the application shall not send usage data, telemetry or crash reports (D-12), and after a crash it shall store a crash report on the local disk and show its location at the next start, so the user can decide whether to pass it on. The no-telemetry clause holds. The local report exists only for Rust panics: crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/crash.rs:66-89 installs std::panic::set_hook and the start-up notice (app.rs:679-706) lists crash-*.txt files, while native crashes in a GPU driver or in Manifold's C++ code (solid-kernel-ops), aborts and stack overflows leave nothing (docs/technology-choices.md:194, deferred at :271; gap row NFR-SEC-002). Since increment 2 ships a C++ kernel, native crashes are a realistic class.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-platform (created in 04) gains native_crash: an out-of-process minidump handler using crash-handler and minidumper (EmbarkStudios, MIT/Apache-2.0). At start, main.rs spawns the same executable as `archicraft --crash-monitor <socket>` (a flag added to the Args parser of 01; no window, no Dock icon, CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows), connects a minidumper::Client and attaches a crash_handler::CrashHandler whose crash event requests a dump; the monitor writes crash-<stamp>-<pid>.dmp into DataDirs::crash_reports() and then a companion crash-<stamp>-<pid>.txt built by a new crash::native_report_text (version, OS, graphics info from 01, crash kind, dump file name, the last log lines the app streamed to the monitor), and exits when the client disconnects. The Rust panic hook stays the baseline; if the monitor cannot start, the app logs a warning and continues with panic reports only. crash::reports_since groups .txt and .dmp files by stamp and pid, and the start-up notice (the crash entry of the StartupPrompt queue of 06) shows one entry per crash with both paths, 'Copy path' and 'Show in folder', and says that nothing was sent and that the .dmp file may contain parts of the open project, so the user can decide whether to pass it on. A hidden ARCHICRAFT_SIMULATE_CRASH=segfault|abort|stack-overflow (plus kernel: a null dereference in a crash-test-only C function compiled into crates/archicraft-manifold under a crash-test cargo feature, inside the shim of solid-kernel-ops-01 if one exists) triggers a crash right after the handlers are installed and before the GUI starts. release.yml keeps the release symbols (PDB, dSYM, split debuginfo) as workflow artefacts for developers. docs/technology-choices.md moves the minidump handler from deferred into the stack. Out of scope: any upload or server, symbolication tooling for users.
design: Out-of-process dumping is the reliable variant: the crashed process only signals the monitor over a local socket (a named pipe on Windows) and the monitor reads its memory with minidump-writer, so a corrupted heap or an overflowed stack does not prevent the dump. The crash-event closure must be async-signal-safe: no allocation, locks or logging; it only calls client.request_dump(cc). Socket names are per process (archicraft-crash-<pid>); on macOS minidumper uses a Unix socket path, which must stay under 104 bytes, so use a short temporary directory.
