Log context: a background thread sends the RecentLog snapshot (persistence/crash.rs:19-43, filled by the RecentLayer of logging.rs:12-33) to the monitor with client.send_message at most every 2 s, so the report has recent lines without work in the signal handler. Install the panic hook first so panics keep their readable text; group panic and abort artefacts rather than deduplicating them. On macOS the monitor child runs before eframe and never initialises NSApplication, so no Dock icon appears; on Windows the release binary is a GUI-subsystem executable (main.rs:4), so spawning itself opens no console. Pointers: persistence/crash.rs (report_text, install, reports_since), main.rs:14-16, app.rs:679-706, prefs.rs:51-52.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-app/tests/native_crash.rs on the ubuntu, windows and macos runners: spawning the built binary with a temporary ARCHICRAFT_DATA_DIR and ARCHICRAFT_SIMULATE_CRASH=segfault ends with a non-zero status and, within 10 s, a .dmp and a .txt with the same stamp and pid exist; the minidump crate (dev-dependency) parses the dump and finds an exception stream (access violation, SIGSEGV or EXC_BAD_ACCESS) and the crashing thread; the abort and stack-overflow variants also produce a pair.
- With the crash-test feature, the kernel variant produces a dump whose faulting module is the binary containing the archicraft-manifold shim.
- kittest on that DataDirs: 'ArchiCraft crashed last time' lists the .dmp and .txt paths, 'Nothing was sent' and the note that the dump may contain project data; OK records the newest crash in last_crash_report and the next start shows nothing.
- A Rust panic still produces one entry (the panic text, plus the dump grouped under the same pid if the process aborts afterwards).
- The monitor exits within 5 s after a normal application exit (no leftover processes on any runner); a failing spawner (unit test) leaves the app running with a logged warning.
- The companion text contains nothing beyond what the panic report already holds (version, OS, graphics, crash-folder paths, log lines) and states that nothing was sent.
- cargo deny passes with crash-handler, minidumper and minidump-writer; unsafe only in crates/archicraft-platform with SAFETY comments; workspace tests, clippy and fmt are green.
- Satisfied: the local crash-report clause of NFR-SEC-002 for native crashes (best effort per OS) in addition to Rust panics; the no-telemetry clause is re-verified by 03 and 17.
notes:
SRS: NFR-SEC-002
Licences to confirm: crash-handler, minidumper, minidump-writer (MIT or MIT/Apache-2.0), minidump (dev only). Epic risk: native handlers vary per OS; Rust panic reports stay the baseline and minidumps are best effort.
Depends on 06 because the crash notice becomes an entry of its StartupPrompt queue.

title: Complete fixture F9 with its roof, register it and re-run F3
design:
Approach: F9 stays a catalogue sample with its golden from terrain-and-site-17, plus the D.7 registry entry; adding the roof is the only model change, which keeps the re-bless diff small (epic risk). Keep the roof constants (pitch, pivot line) next to the existing constants of the constructor. Sample the terrain surface for the footing check with the TIN query of terrain-and-site (point elevation by barycentric interpolation), not with a mesh ray. The terrace fall is the inclined-slab representation of layer-structures-07 (SlabSlope::Sloped or Tapered), not a roof or terrain workaround: SLB-006 forbids workarounds.

Pitfall: five storeys on a slope with a 'home + 1' top link on the highest storey extrapolate. Give the top walls a fixed height, or trim them to the roof.

Pointers: terrain-and-site-17 (f9_sloping_site, golden), regression-and-status-02 (Fixture, D7, REQUIRED_INCREMENT, all(), check()), layer-structures-09 (F2/F3 entries), junction-engine-12 (registry use from tests), terrain-and-site terrain.rs TIN query, roofs-01/02 single-plane roof.
acceptance_criteria:
- F9 keeps five storeys named and ordered -3, -2, -1, 0, +1 at the elevations of terrain-and-site-17. integrity_problems() is empty, evaluation reports no problems and every body is closed.
- Stepped footings form a contiguous chain (each step's upper bottom equals the lower top within MODEL_TOLERANCE), and every footing bottom lies below the terrain surface at its centre (TIN point query).
- The single-slope roof has one plane whose pitch equals the typed value within 1e-9 rad; every trimmed top-wall vertex lies on the roof underside within MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- The terrace top falls by the typed gradient towards its drain edge: the top-surface z at two sample points differs by gradient x distance within 1e-6 m. Its body (the sloped or tapered slab of layer-structures-07, as terrain-and-site-17 built it) is closed (SLB-006).
- f9_sloping_site() contains no inline terrain or footing construction; it calls the step functions of samples/site.rs that RM-S also uses.
- f9-sloping-site.ifcx is re-blessed with a diff limited to the roof and trims; catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files reproduces it byte for byte and conformance/run.sh passes on it.
- F3 from the registry passes again on the full workspace: +6.10 / +6.00 / +5.75 within 1e-9, base offset -0.10, resilient skin 30 mm, wall bodies starting at the core top.
- Registry: the D7 entries F3 and F9 have constructors and seeded: true; two builds of each are equal; the model, geometry and IFCX registry tests pass on both. REQUIRED_INCREMENT is 2, or a bead names the missing increment-2 constructor and its owner.
- Satisfies the F3/F9 part of the epic acceptance and widens the NFR-MNT-003 conformance inputs (written in 04).
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003. Also Appendix D.7 F3/F9 (KB 303722, KB 364093), ROF-001, SLB-006. Review: the F9 storey elevations, terrain and terrace are those of terrain-and-site-17; this task adds only the roof (proposed pitch 8 degrees, to be confirmed in review) and the registry entry.

title: Run the AS-08 usability test with five participants
description:
WHY: AS-08 (SRS 7.2) runs NFR-USE-001 (M) with five participants and passes when at least four succeed without assistance within 30 minutes; it is a v1 acceptance scenario, and Appendix F places usability testing in increment 4. The run must use the build that will be released, after the interaction review (10), with the first-start consent (06) and the German UI (12) available and with builds that passed the OS smoke runs (03), so that participants see what users will see.

WHAT: Run five sessions following docs/usability/protocol.md on release builds from release.yml, on more than one operating system where participants allow, in each participant's preferred language; collect session sheets, timings, assists and as08_check output; analyse; write docs/usability/results-<date>.md (per participant: pseudonymous id, OS, language, time to completion, success, assists, checker result; SUS scores if collected; findings with severity, frequency and bead id; the AS-08 verdict); and file every finding as a bead (labels usability, as-08, severity-N; bug for defects, feature for missing affordances) with reproduction steps. Out of scope: fixing findings (15, 16).
design: Spread the sessions over several days with a moderator and an observer each. Change the build between sessions only for crashes, and record any change in the results. Severity scale: 1 blocks completion, 2 causes a major delay or an assist, 3 minor delay, 4 cosmetic. File beads with bd create and the labels above; merge duplicates and count frequency.
acceptance_criteria:
- Five sessions are recorded in the results file with pseudonymous ids and no personal data; the checker output is attached for each saved file.
- The AS-08 outcome is stated: pass when at least 4 of 5 succeeded without assistance within 30 minutes; otherwise fail, naming the blocking findings.
- Every finding has a bead with severity, steps and the session ids that hit it; severity-1 and -2 beads are linked to task 15.
- If AS-08 failed, a bead for a second full round with five new participants after the fixes is filed and blocks the release candidate.
- Demonstrates NFR-USE-001, or documents precisely why it is not yet met.
notes:
SRS: NFR-USE-001
Epic risk: participant recruitment; the five-day findings buffer follows in 15 and 16.

title: Build single-plane roof bodies with skins and eaves cuts
description:
WHY: ROF-001 (M) needs a closed body for the single-plane roof. ROF-007 (M) requires the layer structure to be measured perpendicular to the roof plane and the pivot elevation to refer to a selectable reference surface (bottom, top or top of the core skin). ROF-006 (M) makes the cut of each roof edge selectable: plumb (vertical), square (perpendicular to the roof plane), horizontal or a custom angle. ROF-002's clause that the outline may extend beyond the pivot line on either side must hold for the body. Gap rows: ROF-001 lists the missing evaluation of a sloped body (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18 builds vertical prisms only); ROF-007 notes that the writer already emits one child per BodyPart (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:372-382, IFX-017), so a per-skin body is all that is missing.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/{mod.rs, plane.rs, body.rs}. plane.rs: `RoofPlane` from pivot line, slope side, pitch and pivot elevation (height function, unit normal, plane frame u/v/n, perpendicular offset surfaces) and `SidePlane` construction for an edge from its EdgeCut. body.rs: a general `plane_body(plane, region, sides, layers) -> Result<Vec<BodyPart>, GeometryError>` that builds a closed prism between two offset surfaces of a tilted plane, bounded by one side plane per region edge, used once per skin (Skin_n names and PartRole::Skin(SkinRef) as in layer-structures-04 and host-openings-03) or once for a Thickness structure (Body), reusing the Plane type and the triangulate-once-and-lift approach of layer-structures-14's extrude_between (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs) but with general side planes instead of vertical side quads. Replace the stub of roofs-01 in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/roof.rs, the roof's GeometryKind (element-kind-framework-15): the single-plane case calls plane_body; the multi-plane case still reports 'not available' until roofs-05. Geometry tests go to crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/roofs.rs. Out of scope: multi-plane roofs (05), hole rings for openings (11), plan symbols beyond the generic slicing, UI.
design: Plane: P0 = (pivot_line[0], z_pivot), d = unit(pivot_line[1] − pivot_line[0]), s = ±perp(d) by slope side (uphill), z(p) = z_pivot + tan(pitch) · s · (p − pivot_line[0]); upward unit normal n = (−sin(pitch) s, cos(pitch)). An offset surface at perpendicular distance o is the plane shifted by o · n (vertical shift o / cos pitch). The reference surface is the offset matching RoofReference (Bottom: 0 at the bottom face; Top: the total; CoreTop: CrossSection.core.0 of layer-structures-02/03, measured from the first face, which is the top face for roofs as for slabs, skin 1 at the top face). Side plane for a plan edge (a, b): the line L on the reference surface above the edge; Plumb = vertical plane through L, Square = plane through L containing n, Horizontal = plane through L and the horizontal direction perpendicular to L (valid only for horizontal L, validated in roofs-01), Custom(a) = the Square plane rotated about L by (a − 90°). The vertex of surface o at the corner between edges i and i+1 is the intersection of three planes (surface o, side_i, side_i+1) by a 3 × 3 solve; |det| < 1e-12 is a GeometryError. Faces: top and bottom rings projected to plan, validate_ring (crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:117; simple, CCW), triangulated with triangulate.rs:41 in plan and lifted onto their plane (bottom reversed); side quads are planar by construction because both edges lie in side_i; own vertices per face as extrude.rs does (IFX-038). Compute each offset surface once and share it between neighbouring skins (as layer-structures-14 does for the boundary planes of sloped slab skins) so boundaries are bit-identical. Build the builder generically: roofs-05 passes bisector side planes per plane and roofs-11 adds hole rings. Pitfalls: with Horizontal or Custom cuts the top and bottom eaves vertices have different plan positions, so skins have different footprints; vertical extent and plan classification come from mesh bounds (plan.rs:111); bodies stay in storey-local coordinates (evaluate.rs:1-7).
acceptance_criteria:
- A 6 × 4 m single-plane roof, pitch 30°, 0.30 m Thickness, plumb cuts on all edges is closed and outward (mesh.rs check_closed, signed volume > 0) with volume = plan area × 0.30 / cos 30° within 1e-9 relative.
- Reference surfaces: with Bottom, Top and CoreTop (three-skin test structure) the corresponding surface evaluates to the pivot elevation along the pivot line within 1e-9 in storey-local coordinates, i.e. relative to the home storey (ROF-001 clause; a roof on the upper storey of two_storey_shell has its absolute reference height at storey elevation + pivot elevation), and the other surfaces are offset by the perpendicular skin distances.
- The four eaves-cut variants on the low edge: the plumb end face is vertical, the square end face is perpendicular to the roof plane (normal · roof normal = 0 within 1e-9), the horizontal end face has normal (0, 0, ±1), the custom 60° face makes 60° with the roof plane; each body is closed with its analytic volume.
- A Thickness roof has one part named Body (PartRole::Body) and no children (Kind::parts() is empty for single-plane roofs).
- A layered structure produces one Skin_n part per skin, each closed; adjacent skins share bit-identical boundary vertices; the skin volumes sum to the Thickness-equivalent volume within 1e-9.
- An outline extending 1 m beyond the pivot line on the low side gives a body that continues below the pivot elevation (ROF-002 clause).
- A structure too thick for its outline (a 0.2 m wide strip with a 0.5 m structure and square cuts) returns a GeometryError with a message instead of a corrupt mesh (NFR-REL-005).
- plan_drawing of a storey whose cut plane crosses the roof yields one cut region per skin and the projected remainder (plan.rs test).
- Satisfies ROF-001 (body), ROF-006 and ROF-007 for single-plane roofs.
notes: SRS: ROF-001 ROF-002 ROF-006 ROF-007. Related: IFX-017, IFX-038, NFR-REL-005. Appendix D.2: 0.30 m roof thickness. Pointers: extrude.rs:18, triangulate.rs:41, mesh.rs:105 signed_volume, mesh.rs:122 check_closed, evaluate.rs:23-36 BodyPart and ElementGeometry, validate.rs:117 validate_ring; after the prerequisites: kinds/roof.rs (element-kind-framework-15), extrude_between and Plane (layer-structures-14), PartRole (host-openings-03).

title: Add the release workflow with per-OS archives and app bundle
description:
WHY: NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 (M) require ArchiCraft to run on Windows 11 x64, macOS (current and previous major, Apple silicon) and the current Ubuntu LTS x64, and decision D-12 rules out installers, updaters and online services, so a release is a set of self-contained archives that users unpack and start. There is no release process today: .github/workflows holds only ci.yml, README.md tells users to cargo run, and there is no application icon, macOS bundle, Linux desktop entry or Windows version resource (the gap rows of NFR-PORT-001..003 and NFR-PORT-006 all name the missing release process). The bundle metadata created here is also what the SW-001 .ifcx registration (04, 05) reuses.

WHAT: .github/workflows/release.yml, triggered by v* tags and workflow_dispatch, with a build matrix windows-latest (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, static CRT), macos-latest (aarch64-apple-darwin, MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET set to MACOS_MIN, the previous supported macOS major, defined once in release.yml and rendered into Info.plist; 26.0 while macOS 27 is current, re-checked for every release) and ubuntu-24.04 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, a glibc baseline that also runs on the current LTS), installing CMake and the C++ toolchain as ci.yml does for crates/archicraft-manifold, running `cargo build --release --locked -p archicraft-app` and packaging with scripts/package.sh into dist/ArchiCraft-<version>-windows-x64.zip (archicraft.exe), ArchiCraft-<version>-macos-arm64.zip (ArchiCraft.app, ad-hoc signed) and ArchiCraft-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz (binary, desktop entry, icons, MIME XML), so archicraft --version (01) runs from each unpacked archive, each with LICENSE and README-FIRST.txt, plus SHA256SUMS, uploaded as workflow artefacts. New packaging/ tree: icons (packaging/icons/archicraft.svg as source; PNGs 16 to 1024 px, archicraft.ico and archicraft.icns generated by scripts/make-icons.sh and committed), packaging/macos/Info.plist.in (bundle id, version from Cargo.toml, LSMinimumSystemVersion MACOS_MIN, NSHighResolutionCapable, icon), packaging/linux/archicraft.desktop.in and packaging/linux/archicraft-ifcx.xml (shared-mime-info type application/x-ifcx, glob *.ifcx). crates/archicraft-app gets a Windows-only build.rs with winresource (icon and VERSIONINFO) and a runtime window icon (ViewportBuilder::with_icon in main.rs). A packaging check in ci.yml (desktop-file-validate, xmllint, plutil -lint, a dry run of package.sh on a debug build). Out of scope: smoke runs on the OS matrix and release notes (03), CFBundleDocumentTypes (05), THIRD-PARTY.md in the archives (07), any installer, paid code signing or notarisation (depends on the open distribution model O-5), automatic updates (D-12).
design: Static CRT on Windows through RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+crt-static' in the release job only, so a clean Windows 11 needs no VC++ redistributable; the cmake crate follows crt-static, but crates/archicraft-manifold/build.rs was set to /MD by solid-kernel-ops-01, so CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY must follow CARGO_CFG_TARGET_FEATURE (MultiThreaded with crt-static) or the link fails. macOS: MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET must also reach CMake (CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET), otherwise the linker warns about objects built for a newer macOS; arm64 executables must be signed, so sign ad hoc (codesign --force --sign -) after assembling the bundle; downloaded unsigned apps are quarantined, so README-FIRST.txt explains System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway (macOS 15 removed the Control-click bypass) and the Windows SmartScreen 'More info > Run anyway' path. One bundle identifier constant (proposal com.graphicraft.archicraft, after the repository owner) for Info.plist and later UTI declarations; the Wayland app id 'archicraft' (main.rs with_app_id) must equal the desktop file basename archicraft.desktop so compositors find the icon. scripts/package.sh is POSIX sh (Git Bash on Windows runners), reads the version with cargo metadata and runs locally. Icons are own artwork (NFR-LEG-002). Reuse the pinned actions of ci.yml (actions/checkout@v4, Swatinem/rust-cache@v2) and keep permissions: contents: read here; 03 adds contents: write for the draft release.
acceptance_criteria:
- A workflow_dispatch run on a branch produces the three archives and SHA256SUMS as artefacts; the job unpacks each archive on its runner and `archicraft --version` exits 0.
- The Windows binary is an x64 (PE32+, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc) image, imports no vcruntime140.dll (dumpbin /dependents step) and its VERSIONINFO (product name, version) reads back in a PowerShell step; Explorer shows the icon.
- The macOS archive contains ArchiCraft.app with a valid Info.plist (plutil -lint), CFBundleShortVersionString equal to the Cargo version, LSMinimumSystemVersion equal to MACOS_MIN and an icns, and passes `codesign --verify --deep --strict`; `otool -l` reports minos MACOS_MIN for the executable, including the linked Manifold objects; `lipo -archs` reports arm64 only (Apple silicon).
- The Linux tarball's desktop entry passes desktop-file-validate, its MIME XML is well-formed against the shared-mime-info format (xmllint), and the binary requires no GLIBC symbol newer than Ubuntu 24.04 provides.
- The ci.yml packaging check runs on pull requests touching packaging/, scripts/package.sh or crates/archicraft-app/Cargo.toml and fails on a broken plist or desktop file (scratch check).
- README.md gains a 'Downloading a release' paragraph (unpack, start, Gatekeeper and SmartScreen notes, no installer).
- cargo test, clippy -D warnings, fmt and cargo deny stay green with winresource added as a Windows-only build dependency.
- Satisfied: the build-and-package part of NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 without an installer (D-12).
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003
Open decisions: the bundle identifier; MACOS_MIN for each release (the previous supported macOS major, see 03); whether a paid code-signing certificate and notarisation are wanted (depends on O-5). D-12: no installer; a .zip or .tar.gz archive is not an installer.

title: Verify exit criterion: Three-OS acceptance, usability test, German translation, legal and security checks
description:
WHY: The epic turns the release properties of SRS increment 4 into verified facts: it owns NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002, NFR-PORT-003, NFR-PORT-006, SW-001, NFR-LEG-001, NFR-SEC-002, NFR-USE-001, NFR-USE-002 and NFR-L10N-002, and with AS-08 it supplies one of the two Appendix F increment-4 exit scenarios (AS-07 is perf-tuning-rm-m-l). This task verifies the whole against the epic's acceptance, not against the individual tasks.

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged work: ci.yml on ubuntu-26.04, windows-latest and macos-latest; release.yml with the smoke matrix (Windows, the current and previous macOS majors, ubuntu-26.04); cargo test, clippy (-D warnings) and fmt on the workspace; conformance/run.sh on every golden file; the smoke-mode tests, native_crash.rs, interaction_model.rs, l10n_de.rs, the as08_check tests and the association integration tests; cargo deny and the THIRD-PARTY.md freshness check. Then update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence and gap rows in sections 5.5, 6.4, 6.5, 6.7, 6.8 and 6.10, the AS-08 row, the readiness line of increment 4, and the technical-debt entries this epic removes: unknown schema-file licence, native crashes not caught), update docs/technology-choices.md (minidump handler and platform crate in the stack, release process), confirm against docs/test-plan/results/rc-<version>.md (17, 20) and docs/usability/results-<date>.md that the manual and demonstration parts are recorded, file beads for leftovers and close the epic in beads.
design: Verification only; no new code except status and documentation edits. Use `bd show release-candidate` to walk the task list, run the commands of .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml locally and on the runners, compare the srs_ids of the epic with the changed rows of docs/implementation-status.md (the per-merge check of regression-and-status, or by hand), and confirm against docs/test-plan/results/rc-<version>.md and docs/usability/results-<date>.md that the manual and demonstration parts are recorded.
acceptance_criteria:
- CI produces release builds for the three operating systems and the release notes name minimum and reference hardware (NFR-PORT-006).
- Scripted manual tests for AS-01..AS-05 exist under docs/test-plan/ and their automated parts run on all three OSes.
- The first start asks for consent and registers .ifcx (per-OS integration test); native dialogs and the recent list are unchanged (SW-001).
- The smoke run passes on real hardware of every platform with a non-Cpu adapter on DX12, Metal or Vulkan (NFR-PORT-006).
- AS-01..AS-05 have pass entries for Windows 11, macOS current, macOS previous and Ubuntu LTS in docs/test-plan/results/rc-<version>.md (SRS 7.2; NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002, NFR-PORT-003).
- cargo deny check advisories licenses sources bans passes, THIRD-PARTY.md is generated and the schema-file licence is resolved.
- A simulated native crash leaves a minidump-based report whose path is shown at the next start, and a network monitor shows no traffic except the consent-gated import fetch.
- AS-08: at least 4 of 5 participants complete the NFR-USE-001 task following docs/usability/protocol.md.
- The interaction-model checklist passes for every tool.
- The German catalogue has every key and switches the whole UI (kittest).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green on the workspace; conformance/run.sh is green on crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002, NFR-PORT-003, NFR-PORT-006, SW-001, NFR-LEG-001, NFR-SEC-002, NFR-USE-001, NFR-USE-002 and NFR-L10N-002 with evidence pointing at the new modules, tests and documents.
- The epic is closed in beads with follow-up beads filed for remaining work.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003 NFR-PORT-006 SW-001 NFR-LEG-001 NFR-SEC-002 NFR-USE-001 NFR-USE-002 NFR-L10N-002
Sizing: after the review the task estimates sum to about 31 engineer-days (14,880 minutes; 5 days of them the usability buffer, about 3 the German translation) against the roadmap's 12-day epic size; the roadmap figure did not include executing AS-01..AS-05 on four platforms (20) or the release tooling in full. If the epic must shrink, cut 12 and then 11 first (NFR-L10N-002 is Should).

title: Edit roof parameters numerically and show computed roof values
description:
WHY: ROF-008 (M): pitch, pivot elevation, overhangs, edge types and the outline shall be editable numerically (direct manipulation is roofs-10), and the roof shall regenerate immediately (NFR-PERF-006). ROF-011 (S): for each roof the system shall show computed values: ridge elevation, eaves elevation, and the plan area and sloped area of each plane; MEA-003 lists ridge and eaves elevation and the area of each plane for roofs. ROF-006 (M) makes the eaves cut of each edge selectable and ROF-007 (M) the reference surface the pivot elevation refers to; both are chosen here after creation. ELM-017 requires range checks that reject invalid values with an explanation. Gap rows: ROF-008 (the numeric editing pattern exists in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs) and ROF-011 (the derived section exists, properties.rs:542 derived()); MEA-003 is partial: the wall and slab rows (properties.rs:556-565) exist and stay unchanged, the roofs row is missing.

WHAT: properties.rs: roof fields for selected roofs (pitch with widgets::slope, pivot elevation, structure, reference surface; a 'Flip slope side' button for single-plane roofs) through the Fields getter and setter pattern; per-edge fields when edges of a roof are selected in edit mode (selection-transforms-08, PartRef::Edge): edge type, pitch, overhang, eaves cut and custom angle with common values over the selected edges; a 'Roof edges' table in the settings dialog (properties.rs:770 settings_dialog) listing every edge, editable in place; outline and pivot-polygon vertices stay editable through the node coordinates of edit-reshape-palette. derived(): ridge elevation and eaves elevation (storey-local and absolute) and one row per plane with plan area and sloped area from roof::metrics (roofs-05). Every committed field is one UpdateElements command. Out of scope: the break-level list (09), handles and dragging (10).
design: Fields getters return None for non-roofs so rows auto-hide (properties.rs:134-218); add roof()/roof_mut() accessors like wall_mut/slab_mut (properties.rs:224-235); tool defaults need no roof_defaults() extraction, because element-kind-framework-04 edits the DefaultsSlot prototype generically (Subject::Defaults(kind)) and deletes wall_defaults (properties.rs:83 today). Per-edge fields read Selection::parts_of(id) and write through a `Roof::edge_mut(ring, index)` helper of the kind module. Metrics are computed on demand for a single selected roof (skeleton < 5 ms) and memoised per (element id, revision) in the panel state; with several roofs selected the per-plane rows are hidden. Elevations relative to project zero add the storey elevation. Pitfalls: a whole-roof selection must not show per-edge fields; keep derived rows read-only; the table commits on Enter or focus loss like the existing widgets (committed_text, widgets.rs:17) so typing does not create one undo step per keystroke.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: selecting the AS-01 roof shows Ridge elevation, Eaves elevation and two plane rows whose values equal roof::metrics; setting Pitch to '40' regenerates in the same revision (the ridge moves) and Undo restores 35°.
- Invalid input ('95', '-5 %', an overhang of −1 m) shows the validation message in the status line and leaves the project unchanged (ELM-017, NFR-REL-005).
- In edit mode two selected edges set to Gable change in one command; the Roof edges table changes one edge's overhang; the custom-angle field appears only for Custom cuts.
- Typing '3.20' as pivot elevation regenerates the roof with its reference surface at 3.20 m along the pivot line; switching the reference surface of a layered roof from Bottom to Top keeps the pivot elevation value and lowers the body by the structure thickness / cos(pitch) (ROF-007).
- Typing new coordinates for a pivot-polygon node in the node fields of edit-reshape-palette regenerates the roof in one command (outline edited numerically, ROF-008); the eaves cut of a selected edge switches between Plumb, Square, Horizontal and Custom (ROF-006).
- A single-plane roof shows one plane row with its plan and sloped area.
- Flip slope side mirrors a single-plane roof about its pivot line (command test with undo).
- Values follow the project units and slope format (Percent shows percent, imperial lengths in feet-inches).
- Satisfies the numeric clauses of ROF-008, ROF-011, the selection clauses of ROF-006 and ROF-007 after creation, and the roofs row of MEA-003.
notes: SRS: ROF-006 ROF-007 ROF-008 ROF-011. Related: MEA-003, ELM-017, NFR-PERF-006. Appendix D.1: roof pitch in degrees, percent selectable.

title: Automate AS-03 on RM-S: reopen, change structure and storey height
description:
WHY: AS-03 'Round trip. Close and reopen the AS-01 project. Change the exterior wall structure thickness and the upper storey height.' It passes when 'all elements are still parametric. Junctions, openings, slabs and the roof follow the change. The re-saved file passes IFX-006, and element UUIDs are unchanged.' The status document rates AS-03 partial: round trip, regeneration and identities are tested on the small samples (roundtrip.rs:47-73, 142-191, commands.rs:147-168), but 'no test reopens, edits wall thickness and storey height, and re-validates IFX-006'. NFR-MNT-003 puts the re-saved file into the conformance run on every change, and the epic acceptance names this test explicitly. PRF-002 (editing a layer structure updates every user) and IFX-011 (identities stable across edits and save/open cycles) are exercised on a real model.

WHAT: Add `samples::as03_edits(&Project) -> Vec<Command>` to samples/rm_s.rs, so the test, the example and the app test of task 07 share one definition. It produces:
- Command::UpdateLayerStructure (layer-structures-01) on 'Cavity wall 680', with the core skin (Concrete) changed from 300 to 250 mm (total 680 to 630 mm), so the interior faces move 0.05 m towards the fixed exterior face;
- Command::SetStoreyHeight { shift_above: true } on '01 First floor' from 3.10 to 3.40 m, shifting the storeys above.
Add crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/as03.rs, which loads tests/golden/rm-s.ifcx with archicraft_ifcx::load (reopen with a fresh History), executes the edits, evaluates, saves, reloads and asserts the AS-03 criteria. reference_models.rs writes rm-s-as03.ifcx by the same load, edit, save path, so the CI conformance job runs the buildingSMART reference implementation on the re-saved file. Out of scope: the UI path of closing and reopening (07), and a golden file for the AS-03 variant (it is regenerated, not blessed).
design:
Approach: reopen by loading the golden bytes, never by reusing the in-memory builder project, so the reader's lenient paths are part of the test. Compare ids with a helper that walks validate::flatten of both files and classifies paths by role (the spatial_tree_and_identities test pattern, roundtrip.rs:142-191).

Why the core skin is changed: with the reference line on the exterior face, a 50 mm thinner core keeps the exterior face and the core's exterior face fixed. The slab outlines of task 01 (on the core's exterior face) therefore stay valid without associativity, while every interior face, inner corner, T end and void depth moves measurably. Changing an outer skin instead would move the bearing line and would need associative slab outlines, which v1 does not have.

Expected values come from the layout constants and the structure table by independent arithmetic: 0.05 m and 0.30 m. The test must not re-run the code under test to obtain them. The storey change uses StoreyList::set_height with shift_above, so the attic and everything homed there moves, while elements linked to storeys re-resolve their tops (relink semantics in command.rs).

Pitfall: if the stair solver changes the 01-02 riser count, step parts may legitimately change. Write stair parts per flight and landing (stair-body-plan) and treat step-level sub-nodes, if any, as regenerated roles listed explicitly in the test.

Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:47-73, :142-191; crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs:147-168; layer-structures UpdateLayerStructure propagation (PRF-002).
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003. Also AS-03, IFX-006, IFX-010, IFX-011, PRF-002, NFR-USE-004 (both edits undoable). 'Upper storey' is read as the upper floor (01) of AS-01's 'ground floor and upper floor plus attic'. Changing it moves the attic and the roof, which is what the scenario wants to exercise.

title: Prove the RM-S builder needs no attribute beyond the template
design:
Approach: two independent guards. The journal guard checks what the builder did. The collection-equality guard checks the result, and also catches attribute changes smuggled in through a non-attribute command. Comparing against FixtureBuilder::new("rm_s").finish() works because the seeded template gives the same resource ids in both projects (element-kind-framework-03: the id source is passed into default_metric_project_with).

Classify Project fields once, in an `attributes_of(&Project)` function that returns a comparable struct. Model data that are not attributes: elements, relations, storeys, counters, info, site/building names and location, data_version, revision. Changing tool defaults (element settings) is allowed by NFR-USE-006. Treat SetToolDefaults as None, but list it in the usage table so reviewers see which defaults RM-S changed.

The demonstration document follows SRS 7.1 'Demonstration: observed task execution by users'. Keep it short, and separate observer instructions from participant steps.

Pitfall: do not compare by names alone. A builder that deletes and recreates a material under the same name must fail, which the id-based equality and the journal guard both ensure.

Pitfall: History drops transactions beyond its limit (DEFAULT_UNDO_LIMIT = 200) and its journal keeps labels only, so every guard reads FixtureBuilder::commands().

Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs (Command enum, label(), History, replay()), template.rs:391-410 (template tests), the per-kind defaults slots of element-kind-framework-04.
acceptance_criteria:
- rm_s_uses_only_template_attributes passes.
- A test-only variant of the builder that adds one Command::AddMaterial makes the check fail with a message naming the command and its index in commands() (negative test).
- A unit test lists every Command variant with its AttributeEffect. A new variant does not compile until it is classified (exhaustive match, no wildcard arm).
- Every Project field is classified as attribute or model data by an exhaustive destructuring (`let Project { id, info, ..., } = p;` without `..`). Adding a field to Project without classifying it breaks the build, so future attribute kinds (pens, profiles, surfaces) are covered automatically.
- Replaying commands() on FixtureBuilder::new("rm_s").finish() gives a project equal to rm_s() (NFR-MNT-001 replay on a real model), and the number of replayed commands equals the builder's execute calls, above the 200-step undo limit.
- Element settings: for every element kind present in rm_s() (wall, slab, footing override, door, window, stair, roof, column, beam, terrain), the template's tool defaults exist and every resource they name is a template resource; the usage table lists per kind which default parameters RM-S overrode.
- docs/test-plan/nfr-use-006-defaults-demonstration.md exists with participant profile, observer sheet, steps referencing docs/test-plan/as-01-two-storey-house.md and the usage table. One run is recorded with date, platform, build and 'attributes created: none'. Duration is noted for information only.
- If template.rs changed: template_contents and the Appendix D defaults test are updated, and the golden re-bless diff is limited to the template sections.
- Satisfies NFR-USE-006 by test and demonstration for AS-01 without the railing. The railing clause is recorded as open for railings-stairs-adv.
notes: SRS: NFR-USE-006. Also AS-01, NFR-MNT-001 (journal replay), PRJ-001 (template supplies layer structures). The railing part of AS-01 (Should) and its D.2 railing defaults are demonstrated when railings-stairs-adv adds the railing variant of RM-S.

title: Ask for .ifcx registration consent at first start and in Preferences
description:
WHY: SW-001 (M) and D-12 require the .ifcx registration to happen only with the user's consent at first start, since no installer asks, and the user must be able to change the decision later. Because the application is unpacked from an archive, users move it, which leaves a Windows or Linux registration pointing at an old path. Existing and kept (the other two SW-001 clauses): File > Open and Save as use rfd's native dialogs (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:197-207, 257) and every opened file enters the recent list (persistence/prefs.rs add_recent, File > Open recent in ui/shell.rs:39-49, and the start screen of templates-presets); a file delivered by the association must go through that same open flow. The prompt must coexist with the other start-up dialogs: the crash notice (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:679-706), the recovery offer (app.rs:634-676) and the start screen of templates-presets.

WHAT: persistence/prefs.rs gains file_association: AssociationConsent { NotAsked, Declined, Accepted } (serde default NotAsked, machine-local and never exported by the preference export of commands-and-l10n-07). ArchiCraftApp holds an Arc<dyn FileAssociation> injected through its constructor (main.rs passes archicraft_platform::association::system(), tests pass FakeAssociation). At start, when consent is NotAsked and the status is NotRegistered, a modal 'Open .ifcx files with ArchiCraft?' explains that this registers ArchiCraft for the current user only and can be undone in Preferences, with 'Register' and 'Not now'; both answers are stored and 'Not now' does not ask again. Accepted with status Stale shows a non-modal notice offering 'Update registration'; Registered with is_default false (Windows UserChoice) offers 'Open Windows default apps'. Preferences gains a 'File association' row with the status and Register and Unregister buttons. Start-up prompts are queued (crash notice, then recovery, then consent) so only one modal shows at a time; smoke and test modes never show the prompt. All strings are catalogue keys (with German text once release-candidate-11 has landed). Out of scope: the platform backends (04, 05).
design: Keep consent and status separate: consent is the user's decision (preferences), status is what the OS reports now (backend), so a user who later removes the association in OS settings is not asked again. Inject the backend through the constructor (or an AppEnv struct) rather than a global, because kittest harnesses run on parallel threads. Replace the independent if-blocks for recovery and crash notice in app.rs with a small VecDeque<StartupPrompt>, so new prompts cannot overlap. Pitfalls: kittest builds ArchiCraftApp with Preferences::default() (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs), so without injection every existing test would see the modal; current_exe may be a symlink on Linux, register the canonical path; registration failures (read-only home, missing update-mime-database) must not crash the start-up.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest with FakeAssociation reporting NotRegistered and default preferences: the consent modal appears once; 'Register' calls register with the current executable and stores Accepted; a second harness with the saved preferences shows no prompt.
- kittest: 'Not now' stores Declined and the next start shows no prompt; the Preferences row then offers Register, which works.
- kittest: with an abandoned recovery session and a new crash report present, the crash notice shows first, then recovery, then the consent modal, never two modals at once, and the templates-presets start screen stays underneath.
- kittest: status Stale shows the update notice and 'Update registration' re-registers the current path; Registered { is_default: false } shows the default-apps button (the fake records the request instead of launching Settings).
- Existing UI tests pass unchanged because their harness injects a fake that reports Unsupported.
- Preferences round trip: file_association survives save and load, is absent from the exported preferences file, and an import leaves it unchanged.
- A registration error (fake returns Err) shows its text and leaves consent NotAsked.
- Regression of the kept SW-001 clauses: a path passed on the command line opens through the unsaved-changes guard and is added to prefs.recent and File > Open recent; persistence/prefs.rs round_trip_and_recent_list stays green; File > Open and Save as still call rfd (no egui file dialog is introduced).
- Satisfied: SW-001 on Windows and Linux (native dialogs and recent list kept and regression-tested; registration with consent at first start); on macOS together with 05.
notes: SRS: SW-001

title: Add the --smoke-test mode that renders, saves and reopens RM-S
description:
WHY: NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 (M) require ArchiCraft to run on Windows 11 x64, macOS (current and previous major) on Apple silicon and the current Ubuntu LTS x64. CI only builds and runs headless tests (.github/workflows/ci.yml:21-36), so nothing proves that the GUI starts, obtains an adapter, renders a plan and a 3D view and saves a file on each OS (gap rows NFR-PORT-001..003: no GUI smoke run on record). NFR-PORT-006 (M) also needs evidence of which graphics API actually ran. This task provides one self-checking run that the release workflow (03), the macOS file-opening test (05) and the real-hardware checklist (17) execute.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-app/src/smoke.rs behind the --smoke-test flag parsed in 01: `archicraft --smoke-test <report.json> [file.ifcx]` opens the given file through ArchiCraftApp::open_path or otherwise builds samples::rm_s() (reference-models-01; storeys, layered walls, openings, stairs, the gable roof and trims, so the Manifold kernel of solid-kernel-ops runs too), shows a plan pane and a 3D pane, renders at least 60 frames, saves through Document::to_bytes and persistence::save_atomically into a temporary folder, reopens the saved file, writes a JSON SmokeReport {version, os, os_version, arch, backend, adapter, driver, device_type, frames, frame_ms_p50, frame_ms_p95, pixels_per_point, opened_paths, saved_bytes, reopened_ok, elapsed_ms, failed_step} and closes the viewport; exit code 0 on success, 1 with failed_step set otherwise. The steps run as a SmokeRun state machine driven by a FrameDriver trait, so tests can drive it without a GPU. Smoke mode uses a temporary DataDirs unless ARCHICRAFT_DATA_DIR is set, never opens rfd dialogs and never shows or consumes start-up prompts (crash notice, recovery offer, the consent prompt of 06), so running it on a user's machine leaves their data folder untouched. docs/testing.md documents the flag, the report shape and the exit codes. Out of scope: the CI jobs that run it (03), packaging (02), waiting for files sent while running (05 adds that option).
design: The smoke run reuses Workspace commands, Document and ArchiCraftApp::open_path so it exercises the real open and save path (atomic save, backups 0). Frame times come from Instant between frames; p50/p95 in a small unit-tested helper. Close with ctx.send_viewport_cmd(ViewportCommand::Close) and return the exit code through an Arc<AtomicI32> read after eframe::run_native. The FrameDriver abstraction (next frame, elapsed time) lets the kittest harness step frames without a GPU; the backend fields come from GraphicsInfo (01) and are 'none' under kittest. os_version comes from the OS (sw_vers ProductVersion on macOS, the Windows build number, VERSION_ID of /etc/os-release on Linux) so 03 can assert the OS majors. Pitfalls: Windows release builds have no console (main.rs:4), so the run reports through the JSON file and the exit code only; RM-S evaluation is slow in debug builds, so CI runs the release binary; never block on rfd in smoke mode or CI hangs.
acceptance_criteria:
- SmokeRun state-machine tests with a fake FrameDriver: steps run in order (open, panes, frames, save, reopen, report, close); a failing save produces exit code 1 and a report whose failed_step is 'save'.
- kittest (no GPU): ArchiCraftApp in smoke mode on a temporary DataDirs writes a report with frames >= 60, saved_bytes > 0, reopened_ok true, backend 'none' and empty opened_paths, and requests ViewportCommand::Close.
- kittest: with an abandoned recovery session and a crash report in ARCHICRAFT_DATA_DIR, smoke mode shows no start-up window, and the session and the report are still there afterwards.
- With a file argument, the report lists the file in opened_paths and the reopened project has the same element ids as the opened one.
- Unit test of the percentile helper on known series (p50, p95).
- The flag, the report shape and the exit codes are documented in docs/testing.md.
- Manual: `cargo run --release -p archicraft-app -- --smoke-test /tmp/r.json` on a developer machine exits 0 and reports Metal, DX12 or Vulkan with a non-Cpu device type.
- Existing tests pass; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- Satisfied: the evidence hook for NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002, NFR-PORT-003 and NFR-PORT-006 that 03, 05 and 17 run.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003 NFR-PORT-006
Split out of release-candidate-01 during review.

title: Add the gable roof, trims, members and terrace to RM-S
design:
Approach: continue the step functions of tasks 01 and 02 and keep the roof, member and terrace constants in the same constant block. Generate the roof from the knee walls with the pivot at their top. Add the trims after the roof in the same stage, as the AS-01 gable case of cleanup-and-trims does (gable walls of fixed height above the ridge, Downward volume). Build the terrace and garden steps through the same step functions F9 uses.

Indicative budget for 250-350 elements, doors and windows included in the storey counts: site and terrace 20, footings, plinth and ground slab 30, ground floor 65, first floor 70, attic 45, stairs 2, roof and its timber members 25, terrace canopy 20 (about 277). Cut the members first if the kernel time grows.

Determinism pitfall: trims and cleanup run through Manifold. Its output must be identical on the three CI operating systems for the byte-for-byte golden of task 04. Keep inputs exactly representable where possible (typed millimetre values), and let rm_s_fingerprint catch a divergence on the runner where it happens.

Pointers: roofs kinds/roof.rs and roof/body.rs, roofs-07 wall-outline mode, cleanup-and-trims-05 (Relation::Trim, KeepSide, TrimmingVolume, Command::TrimElements) and cleanup-and-trims-07, profiles-columns-beams for the column and beam kinds, layer-structures-07 and -14 for tapered slabs.
acceptance_criteria:
- rm_s() has between 250 and 350 elements, and the per-storey budget is documented in the module doc. integrity_problems() is empty and ModelGeometry reports no problems. Every body passes check_closed and stays below 65,535 points.
- Roof: one IfcRoof with two planes. The ridge height equals the value computed by hand from pitch, pivot elevation and plan width within 1e-6 m.
- Trims: every top vertex of the gable and knee walls lies within MODEL_TOLERANCE of a roof underside plane, and no wall body intersects the roof (zero intersection volume through the SolidKernel). The Trim relations survive an IFCX round trip.
- Members: column bases and tops and beam ends lie on their storey levels or supports within MODEL_TOLERANCE; purlins and the ridge beam have zero intersection volume with the roof.
- Terrace: the top falls by the typed gradient towards its drain edge (the top-surface z at two sample points differs by gradient x distance within 1e-6 m), and its body is closed (SLB-006).
- Every body part's material is a template material (by seeded id). commands() still contains no attribute-creating command.
- rm_s_fingerprint is updated for the final model and passes on all three CI runners.
- cargo test --workspace is green and the existing golden files are byte-identical.
- Satisfies the complete AS-01 content (without railing) of the NFR-MNT-003 reference model RM-S and the template-only rule of NFR-USE-006 for the roof, trims and members.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003 NFR-USE-006. Also AS-01 (gable roof, trimmed gable walls), AS-03 (roof follows), SRS 7.3 RM-S size, D.2 roof/column/beam defaults, SOL-030, DW-021, SLB-006, Appendix D.7 F9 (terrace details).

title: Index the AS-01..AS-05 procedures and run their tests on three OSes
description:
WHY: SRS 7.1 makes scripted manual tests the method for interaction-heavy requirements, and 7.2 accepts v1 only when AS-01..AS-05, AS-07 and AS-08 pass on Windows, macOS and Linux, which is how NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 are accepted in practice. Procedures and automation were written by the owning epics: AS-01 as docs/test-plan/as-01-two-storey-house.md with the as01 block of conformance/check.ts and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/rm-s.expect.json (reference-models-05, -07); AS-03 as docs/test-plan/as-03-round-trip.md with crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/as03.rs and the kittest as03_reopen_edit_save in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs (reference-models-06, -07); the increment-1 ground floor as docs/test-plan/increment-1-ground-floor.md (doors-windows-core-12); AS-02 as samples::structural_frame with crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/as02.rs and its golden file (grids-11); AS-04 as crates/archicraft-app/tests/as04_precision.rs (point-input-snapping-15); AS-05 as docs/test-plan/as-05.md with crates/archicraft-app/tests/crash_recovery.rs (regression-and-status-15). There is no single index, AS-02 and AS-04 have no scripted procedure, and nothing proves that every automated part runs, and is not ignored, on all three OS runners.

WHAT: docs/test-plan/README.md with one row per scenario AS-01..AS-08: procedure file, automated tests (crate and test path), CI jobs (test matrix, conformance matrix), the Should-only parts (railing in AS-01, AS-06), and result columns for Windows 11, macOS current, macOS previous and Ubuntu LTS. Write the missing procedures in the format of docs/test-plan/increment-1-ground-floor.md: docs/test-plan/as-02.md (grid of 4x3 bays of 6.00 m, columns at the intersections on three storeys, beams on grid lines, slabs, pad footings; IFC classes and NFR-ACC-003 alignment checked with the measure tool) and docs/test-plan/as-04.md (a closed wall polygon by typed relative and polar coordinates, measured back with the measure tool of 3d-input-navigation-12 at 0.1 mm / 0.01 degree); fill any gaps in the AS-01, AS-03 and AS-05 documents (expected-value tables, pass/fail boxes per OS). scripts/check-test-plan.py parses the README's test column and the output of `cargo test --workspace -- --list` and fails when a listed test is missing or ignored; it runs as a step of the ci.yml test matrix on all three OSes; the conformance matrix includes the RM-S and AS-02 golden files. Precondition: regression-and-status (crash_recovery.rs, as-05.md, conformance-matrix.yml of regression-and-status-13) is not an ancestor of this epic in the graph; check with bd show before starting and, if it has not landed, file a blocker bead instead of duplicating its work. Out of scope: executing the manual procedures (20), AS-06 (ifcx-interop), AS-07 (perf-tuning-rm-m-l), AS-08 (13, 14).
design: Link and complete the procedures other epics own; do not rewrite them. The test column uses full test paths so the script can match `cargo test -- --list --format terse` output exactly (lines end in ': test'); diff it against `--list --ignored` to find ignored ones. If a scenario test is OS-gated (cfg(target_os)), the README says so and the script accepts a per-OS exception list with a reason. The AS-05 row points at regression-and-status-15's crash_recovery.rs; no second test is added. Python 3 standard library only.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/test-plan/README.md exists, is linked from docs/testing.md and README.md, and maps AS-01..AS-05 to procedure files that all exist (as-01-two-storey-house.md, as-02.md, as-03-round-trip.md, as-04.md, as-05.md) and AS-06..AS-08 to their owners.
- as-02.md and as-04.md have numbered steps, expected-value tables (0.1 mm / 0.01 degree; IFC classes IfcColumn, IfcBeam, IfcSlab, IfcFooting) and a results table per platform.
- check-test-plan.py unit tests: a canned list output containing all tests passes; a missing or ignored test fails and names it.
- The ci.yml test job runs check-test-plan.py on ubuntu, windows and macos and is green, so the AS-01/AS-03 RM-S tests, the AS-02 structural-frame test, the AS-04 precision test and the AS-05 crash-recovery test run on all three OSes.
- The conformance matrix (conformance-matrix.yml of regression-and-status-13) lists the RM-S and AS-02 golden files and is green on three OSes.
- Satisfied: the epic acceptance item 'scripted manual tests for AS-01..AS-05 exist under docs/test-plan/ and their automated parts run on all three OSes'; evidence for NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003
Related: SRS 7.1 (scripted manual tests) and 7.2 (AS-01..AS-05 on three OSes).

title: Add the roof kind with single- and multi-plane definitions
description:
WHY: ROF-001 (M) requires a single-plane roof defined by an outline polygon in plan, a pivot line (the line in plan along which the roof's reference surface lies at the pivot elevation), the slope side, the pitch entered as angle, percent or rise/run, the pivot elevation relative to the home storey, and a thickness or a layer structure (PRF). ROF-003 (M) requires a multi-plane roof generated from a closed pivot polygon in which every edge has a pitch, an eaves overhang and an edge type (sloped or gable). ROF-005 (S) adds break levels (height above the pivot elevation and pitch above it), ROF-006 (M) a selectable eaves cut per edge (plumb, square, horizontal or a custom angle) and ROF-007 (M) layer structures measured perpendicular to the roof plane, with the pivot elevation referring to a selectable reference surface (bottom of the structure, top of the structure or top of the core skin). NFR-L10N-003 and STR-009 require slopes in degrees, percent and ratio for input and display. Gap rows: all missing. There is no roof kind (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:190-201, ElementKind and KindTag are Wall | Slab); SlopeFormat exists and is persisted (crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:125-145, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:145) but nothing parses or formats a slope (units.rs has parse_length:391 and parse_angle:428 only); only a 'Roof' layer exists (template.rs:265).

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/roof.rs, registered in the kind registry of element-kind-framework (label 'Roof', code 'roof', name prefix 'RF', IfcClass::Roof, defaults slot, validator, transform hook, part list): `Roof { shape: RoofShape, pivot_elevation: f64, structure: Structure, reference: RoofReference }`, `RoofShape::SinglePlane { outline: Outline<EdgeCut>, pivot_line: [DVec2; 2], slope_side: Side, pitch: f64 }` and `RoofShape::MultiPlane { pivot_polygon: Outline<RoofEdge>, levels: Vec<RoofLevel> }`, `RoofEdge { kind: RoofEdgeKind::{Sloped, Gable}, pitch, overhang, cut: EdgeCut }`, `EdgeCut::{Plumb, Square, Horizontal, Custom(f64)}`, `RoofLevel { height, pitch }` and `RoofReference::{Bottom, Top, CoreTop}` with code/from_code/label/ALL, plus EdgeData impls so per-edge data follows node insertion and deletion. Add a 'roof' DefaultsSlot through KindDescriptor.template_defaults with the Appendix D.2 values (element-kind-framework-04: the slot carries a prototype Roof payload, so there is no parallel RoofDefaults struct), `Project::new_single_plane_roof` and `Project::new_multi_plane_roof` as thin wrappers over the generic Project::new_element in kinds/roof.rs, validation, and these Kind hooks: the structure hooks of layer-structures-02 (structure()/structure_mut(), referenced_materials()/replace_material(), CrossSection through Project::cross_section) so DeleteLayerStructure, material replacement and the PRF-002 dirty propagation reach roofs; the transform hook in the form selection-transforms-02 left it (`transform(&Transform, &TransformContext) -> Result<Transformed<Roof>, TransformError>` plus KindDescriptor.transforms: Move including a vertical dz on the pivot elevation, Rotate, Mirror, Scale with NotScaled notes for pitch, thickness and overhangs, RotateAxis about a non-vertical axis Unsupported); `parts()` with one PartSpec { role 'Plane_<k>' (k = pivot edge index + 1, '_L<j>' appended for break levels), class IfcClass::Slab from COMPOUND_PART_CLASSES, label } per sloped pivot edge and level and none for single-plane roofs; the selection hooks of selection-transforms-01 with `RoofPart` as the kind's `type Part` (PivotLine, PivotLineEnd(0 | 1), Eaves { edge }, Plane { edge, level }; outline and pivot-polygon nodes and edges use the shared PartRef::Node/Edge; part_ref_for_role maps 'Plane_<k>' to RoofPart::Plane for the 3D pick); and a conservative vertical extent. In units.rs add `parse_slope(text, format, nf)` and `format_slope(radians, units, nf, with_unit)`. Stubs keep the registry-completeness and module-layout tests green, as doors-windows-core-01 does: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/roof.rs returns a 'roof geometry not available yet' GeometryError (shown as the framework's fallback box) until roofs-02 and roofs-05, and crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/roof.rs is a placeholder codec that writes the envelope and warns 'roof parameters not saved yet' until roofs-06 (the precedent of layer-structures-02). Out of scope: bodies (02, 05), the skeleton (03, 04, 09), IFCX persistence (06), tools and panels (07, 08, 10), hosted elements and the roof's HostCapability (11, 12, 14).
design: Roofs use the `Outline<E>` of edit-reshape-palette-01, so Command::Reshape (node and edge operations, offsets, union and difference) works on roof outlines and pivot polygons without roof-specific code (NFR-USE-002), and per-edge data rides on `Vertex.next.data` so splitting an edge copies its parameters. Angles are stored in radians; a gable is `RoofEdgeKind::Gable` (skeleton weight 0), never a 90° pitch. `Side::{Left, Right}` is relative to pivot_line[0] -> pivot_line[1] and names the side on which the roof rises. The reference surface passes through the pivot line (single plane) or every pivot edge (multi-plane) at pivot_elevation; skins are offset perpendicular from it in geometry. `EdgeCut::Custom(a)` stores the angle between the cut plane and the roof plane about the edge line on the reference surface (90° = Square) so that the ROF-009 split can express hip bisector planes exactly; the UI labels it 'angle to roof plane'. Vertical extent without geometry: from pivot − max(overhang · tan pitch) − total thickness / cos(max pitch) to pivot + tan(max pitch) · bbox diagonal + total thickness / cos(max pitch); conservative because a point of edge e's face lies tan(pitch_e) · dist(p, line_e) above the pivot and that distance is bounded by the diagonal; exact extents come from the evaluated bodies (plan.rs classifies by mesh bounds). Follow the 'Add an element kind' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md as reshaped by element-kind-framework (kinds/mod.rs registry; codec slot filled in roofs-06); `#[serde(default)]` on new fields keeps journal replay working. parts() derives the plane roles from the pivot polygon alone (one per sloped edge and level), because the model never sees the skeleton; a plane that collapses below a break level is an empty PartGeometry in roofs-09, so element-kind-framework-15's role-equality test holds. Pitfalls: mirror must reverse rings and edge data together (use the Outline helper, not a manual reverse); the model never calls the skeleton, so skeleton failures are geometry problems handled in roofs-05; keep archicraft-model free of geometry and UI dependencies (NFR-MNT-002).
acceptance_criteria:
- units.rs tests: parse_slope reads '35' and '35°' as degrees, '70' and '70 %' as percent (atan 0.70 = 34.99°) and '7:10', '7/10' and '1:2' as rise:run, honours the decimal comma of NumberFormat and rejects negative, vertical (>= 90°) and non-finite values with a ParseError; format_slope gives '35.00°', '70.02 %' and '0.700:1' in the three SlopeFormats.
- validate.rs tests reject, each with a user-facing message: a pitch outside 0.5°..85°, a negative overhang or one above 5 m, a custom cut within 1° of the roof plane, a Horizontal cut on a single-plane edge that is not parallel to the pivot line, a pivot line shorter than 0.1 mm, an invalid outline or pivot polygon (the Outline validation of edit-reshape-palette-02), an outline or pivot polygon with hole rings (ROF-001 and ROF-003 define one polygon; holes in roofs come only from openings), a multi-plane roof without any sloped edge, and break levels that are not strictly increasing, not above 0 or have a pitch out of range.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements, UpdateElements and DeleteElements of both shapes execute, undo to the exact project and redo; mirroring a multi-plane roof reverses the ring together with its edge data so every physical edge keeps its pitch, overhang, type and cut (asserted via edge midpoints); mirroring a single-plane roof flips the slope side.
- Kind hooks: parts() of a six-edge multi-plane roof with two gable edges lists Plane_k (IfcSlab) for the four sloped edges only and a single-plane roof lists none; part_refs, part_anchor and part_outline return the pivot line, its two ends, the eaves lines and every outline or pivot-polygon node and edge; rotating a single-plane roof by 90° rotates outline and pivot line, Scale keeps pitch, thickness and overhangs and returns NotScaled notes, and a RotateAxis about a tilted axis returns TransformError::Unsupported whose message names roofs.
- DeleteLayerStructure with a replacement rewrites a layered roof and the roof DefaultsSlot prototype to the replacement, and replacing a material reaches a Thickness roof (layer-structures-02 users path).
- `Project::new_*_roof` applies the D.2 defaults (35°, 0.30 m Thickness structure, 0.50 m overhang, Sloped edges, Plumb cuts, reference Bottom) on the 'Roof' layer; template, samples and the framework's registry-completeness and module-layout tests pass (roof kind code in kinds/roof.rs of each crate plus one registry line each); cargo test, clippy and fmt stay green.
- Satisfies the model clauses of ROF-001, ROF-003, ROF-005, ROF-006 and ROF-007.
notes: SRS: ROF-001 ROF-003 ROF-005 ROF-006 ROF-007. Related: NFR-L10N-003, STR-009, ELM-017, PRF-001, PRF-002 (structure hooks), EDT-001 and EDT-007 (transform hook), SEL-008 (part hooks). Appendix D.2: roof pitch 35°, 0.30 m thick, eaves overhang 0.50 m, pivot elevation at the top of the walls; D.1: roof pitch in degrees, percent selectable. Assumptions to confirm with users (open issue O-9): pitch range 0.5°..85°, overhang 0..5 m, name prefix 'RF', default reference surface Bottom, one pitch per break level for all sloped edges, ratio displayed as rise:1.

title: Register .ifcx on macOS and open documents sent by Finder
description:
WHY: SW-001 (M) applies to macOS too: there a document type is declared in the bundle's Info.plist (CFBundleDocumentTypes plus a UTI declaration) and the default handler is chosen through Launch Services, again only with the user's consent at first start (D-12). There is a second, macOS-specific gap: Finder does not pass a double-clicked file on the command line but sends an open-documents Apple Event, and winit (under eframe 0.36) does not surface that event, so a double-clicked .ifcx would start ArchiCraft with an empty project although main.rs:18 handles command-line paths on Windows and Linux.

WHAT: packaging/macos/Info.plist.in (from 02) gains CFBundleDocumentTypes (IFCX project, role Editor, the lowest LSHandlerRank that still lets ArchiCraft become the default after consent (see design), LSItemContentTypes the IFCX UTI) and UTImportedTypeDeclarations (IFCX UTI conforming to public.json and public.data, extension ifcx, MIME application/x-ifcx). crates/archicraft-platform gains association/macos.rs, implementing the FileAssociation trait of 04: status through NSWorkspace URLForApplicationToOpenContentType, register through setDefaultApplicationAtURL:toOpenContentType:completionHandler: for the running bundle (recording the previous default handler so unregister can restore it), Unsupported when not running from an .app bundle; and open_documents.rs, an Apple Event handler for kAEOpenDocuments that forwards file URLs into a channel, with ArchiCraftApp polling archicraft_platform::take_opened_files() each frame and routing each path through the existing open flow (unsaved-changes prompt, recent list). The smoke mode of 18 gains --smoke-wait-open <seconds>, which keeps the run alive that long and records every delivered file in opened_paths. The consent dialog of 06 then works unchanged on macOS. Out of scope: Windows and Linux (04), the consent UI (06), notarisation.
design: Use objc2, objc2-foundation and objc2-app-kit (MIT), the family winit already depends on, so no second Objective-C binding enters the tree. Apple Event timing is the main pitfall: NSApplication delivers the launch-time open-documents event during finishLaunching, so a handler installed after the first frame misses it. Spike first: (a) install the handler with NSAppleEventManager setEventHandler:andSelector:forEventClass:andEventID: immediately before eframe::run_native; if NSApplication replaces it, (b) add application:openURLs: to winit's application delegate class at runtime with objc2 (class looked up by name at start; if absent, fall back to (a) with a logged warning). Keep whichever passes both the launch and the running test, document the choice in the module docs and re-test on every winit upgrade. SW-001 asks for consent before ArchiCraft becomes the handler, but a declared CFBundleDocumentTypes entry lets Launch Services consider the bundle as soon as it sees it. Spike the rank: use LSHandlerRank None if setDefaultApplicationAtURL still succeeds with it (nothing is claimed before consent); otherwise Alternate, which never wins over another handler; if ArchiCraft is then the only app declaring the type, Finder may use it before consent, which is Launch Services behaviour and is stated in the consent dialog text and in docs/release.md. setDefaultApplicationAtURL may ask the user for confirmation; treat a completion error as 'not changed' and report it. The UTI is imported because we do not own the buildingsmart.org domain; proposal org.buildingsmart.ifcx until buildingSMART publishes one.
acceptance_criteria:
- plutil -lint passes on the rendered Info.plist, and a unit test (plist as dev-dependency) asserts the document type, the rank chosen in the spike and the UTI tags.
- On both macOS runners of the release smoke job of 03 (MACOS_CURRENT and MACOS_PREVIOUS), after unpacking: before consent, `lsregister -f` alone does not make the bundle the default for .ifcx (or the observed Launch Services behaviour is documented and named in the consent text); `archicraft --register-association-for-test` sets the default, after which NSWorkspace URLForApplicationToOpenURL for a sample .ifcx returns the bundle; unregister restores the previous handler.
- `open -a ArchiCraft.app sample.ifcx --args --smoke-test r.json` at launch and `open sample.ifcx` during a run with --smoke-wait-open both open the file: the smoke report lists the opened path in both cases.
- kittest: a path fed through take_opened_files (fake source) opens the file and enters the recent list, and when the document is dirty the unsaved-changes prompt appears first.
- Running the bare binary (cargo run) reports Unsupported with a reason, and the first-start prompt of 06 is not shown.
- No unsafe outside crates/archicraft-platform and crates/archicraft-manifold; cargo deny passes with the objc2 crates.
- Satisfied: SW-001 registration and file opening on macOS, together with 06.
notes:
SRS: SW-001
Open: the exact UTI identifier (no official one exists) and the LSHandlerRank chosen in the spike. Tested on both macOS runners of task 03.

title: Add the platform crate with Windows and Linux .ifcx registration
description:
WHY: SW-001 (M) requires the system to use native file dialogs, register as handler for .ifcx files (with the user's consent at first start, because there is no installer, D-12) and keep a list of recent projects. Native dialogs (rfd, crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:197-207 and 257) and the recent list (persistence/prefs.rs:49, 116-120; menu ui/shell.rs:39-49) exist, and a path given on the command line is opened (main.rs:18, app.rs:124-126). The registration is missing on every platform (gap row SW-001: no HKCU ProgId, no CFBundleDocumentTypes, no .desktop file with xdg-mime). It needs OS APIs and, on Windows and macOS, unsafe FFI, which the workspace forbids outside crates/archicraft-manifold (CI grep check from solid-kernel-ops-01).

WHAT: New crate crates/archicraft-platform (no egui dependency; the documented second place where unsafe code is allowed, added to the CI no-unsafe allowlist) with module association: trait FileAssociation { status, register(exe), unregister, open_default_apps_settings }, AssociationStatus { NotRegistered, Registered { exe, is_default }, Stale { registered }, Unsupported(reason) }, a FakeAssociation for tests (feature test-support) and system() choosing the backend; macOS returns Unsupported until 05. Windows backend (winreg; windows-sys for SHChangeNotify and AssocQueryStringW): per-user keys only under HKCU\Software\Classes (.ifcx with OpenWithProgids, ProgId ArchiCraft.Project.1 with friendly name, DefaultIcon and shell\open\command "<exe>" "%1", Applications\archicraft.exe\SupportedTypes) plus a Capabilities key registered under HKCU\Software\RegisteredApplications so ArchiCraft appears in Settings > Default apps; status detects a foreign UserChoice and reports is_default false. Linux backend: writes $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/packages/archicraft-ifcx.xml and $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/archicraft.desktop from the packaging templates of 02 (include_str!, Exec with the absolute current_exe path), installs the hicolor icons, runs update-mime-database and update-desktop-database when present, and sets the default by merging the [Default Applications] entry into $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mimeapps.list (no xdg-utils needed). archicraft-app depends on the crate; nothing calls register yet. Out of scope: the consent UI (06), macOS (05), forwarding a second double-click to a running instance (each double-click starts a process; templates-presets' lock file handles opening the same file twice).
design: Write only per-user locations (nothing outside HKCU or $HOME, no admin rights), so registration and unregistration are reversible without an installer. Windows: Explorer honours a hash-protected UserChoice set by the user; an application cannot and must not overwrite it, so register adds ArchiCraft to Open with and Default apps, and when UserChoice points elsewhere the UI (06) offers ms-settings:defaultapps?registeredAppUser=ArchiCraft, which works because of the RegisteredApplications entry. Call SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, SHCNF_IDLIST, null, null) after every change or Explorer keeps stale icons. Record the created keys under the Capabilities key so unregister never removes foreign values (reset the .ifcx default value only when it is ours). Linux: MIME type application/x-ifcx (no IANA type exists; sub-class-of application/json); the desktop file basename must match the Wayland app id 'archicraft' (main.rs); the shared-mime-info cache must be rebuilt or the glob is not seen; the mimeapps.list merge is a small INI edit that preserves comments and order. Moving the unpacked folder breaks Exec paths, hence Stale and the re-registration offer in 06; register the canonicalised current_exe. The trait is object-safe and Send + Sync so ArchiCraftApp can hold Arc<dyn FileAssociation> and kittest can inject the fake.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests on all OSes through injected roots, never the real profile: the Linux backend with temporary XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME writes the three files; mimeapps.list keeps unrelated entries and gains `application/x-ifcx=archicraft.desktop;`; unregister removes exactly what register created; a registered path that differs from current_exe yields Stale; Exec quotes paths with spaces.
- Windows unit test against a scratch root (HKCU\Software\ArchiCraftTest\<uuid>\Classes) checks every value and that unregister deletes the scratch tree.
- Integration tests marked #[ignore] and run in a dedicated CI step: on windows-latest, registering under the real HKCU makes AssocQueryStringW(ASSOCSTR_EXECUTABLE, ".ifcx") return the test executable and unregister restores the previous state; on ubuntu, with xdg-utils, shared-mime-info and desktop-file-utils installed and XDG_* pointed at temporary folders, `xdg-mime query filetype sample.ifcx` prints application/x-ifcx, `xdg-mime query default application/x-ifcx` prints archicraft.desktop, and desktop-file-validate passes.
- The CI no-unsafe grep allows crates/archicraft-platform and still fails for unsafe anywhere else (scratch check); every unsafe block has a SAFETY comment.
- cargo deny check passes with winreg and windows-sys; workspace tests, clippy -D warnings and fmt are green.
- Prepares SW-001 registration on Windows and Linux (consent and UI follow in 06).
notes:
SRS: SW-001
No IANA media type exists for IFCX; revisit application/x-ifcx if buildingSMART registers one. Licences to confirm with cargo deny: winreg (MIT), windows-sys (MIT/Apache-2.0).

title: Split multi-plane roofs into single-plane roofs with a notice
description:
WHY: ROF-009 (S): a multi-plane roof shall be splittable into independent single-plane roofs, after a warning that the shared definition is lost. NFR-USE-004: every change is undoable and no operation asks 'are you sure?' when undo is available, but conversions that drop a parametric definition (ROF-009 is named) may show one notice with a 'do not show again' option. The epic acceptance: split into single-plane roofs shows the one-time notice. Gap row ROF-009: missing; needs a split command and a warning dialog (the dialog pattern exists in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs).

WHAT: Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/split.rs `split_into_single_planes(project, geometry, roof) -> Result<SplitPlan>` producing one single-plane Roof per plane (outline = the plane's reference-surface region including overhang; pivot line = the pivot edge, or the break line with pivot elevation plus level height for upper levels; slope side towards the face; the plane's pitch; edge cuts: the eaves cut kept, hip, valley, ridge and break edges as Custom with the bisector angle, verges plumb; same structure and reference surface) and the re-hosting of hosted openings and roof windows to the roof whose plane contains them (HostPlacement::RoofPlane and RoofInsert keep u and v on the replacement's PlaneRef::Single; Plan placements go to the replacement whose region contains their origin). Model: `Command::SplitRoof { roof, replacements, rehosted }` validated in plan() (the roof exists and is multi-plane, every replacement validates, every hosted element of the roof is re-hosted) and applied as one undo step with Remove, Insert and Replace edits. App: 'Split into single-plane roofs' in the roof context menu and the roof palette; a notice modal ('Splitting turns every plane into an independent roof. The shared definition (pivot polygon, edge pitches, levels) is lost. You can undo this.') with Continue, Cancel and 'Do not show again' stored in Preferences, plus a row in the Preferences dialog to show dismissed notices again ('Add a preference' recipe). NFR-USE-004 is done (only storey deletion and discarding unsaved changes confirm: dialogs.rs:227-269, app.rs:557-581); keep that, this notice is the permitted exception. If free-form-solids-17 has already delivered its reusable conversion notice and skip preference, reuse and generalise them instead of adding a second mechanism. Out of scope: merging roofs back, roof joins (ROF-010, cleanup-and-trims).
design: Exactness follows from the shared body builder: single-plane side planes come from EdgeCut, and roofs-01 defines Custom(a) as the angle between the cut plane and the roof plane about the edge line, so the bisector at a hip (half the dihedral angle) is representable and the split bodies match the originals. The single-plane outline is the plane's reference-surface region, which is also what the cuts are defined against. Ids: replacements get fresh ids from the project id generator (IFX-011: conversions create new identities; the old Plane_<k> part ids disappear with the roof). Re-hosting: a hosted element's (PlaneRef, u, v) maps to PlaneRef::Single of the replacement whose plane it was on, with u and v unchanged because the plane frame is the same. Preferences: `dismissed_notices: BTreeSet<String>` with #[serde(default)] and sanitized() (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:100), notice id 'roof-split', reusable for SOL-004 and STA-048; the modal uses egui::Modal as delete_storey_window does (dialogs.rs:204-276). Pitfalls: build the SplitPlan from the current evaluated geometry; refuse the split with a message when the roof's geometry is a fallback (skeleton failed), because there are no planes to split.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry: splitting the 12 × 9 hip roof yields four single-plane roofs whose bodies equal the original plane bodies (vertex sets within MODEL_TOLERANCE, volumes within 1e-9 relative); the unequal-wing L yields six; a mansard (when roofs-09 is in) yields eight with the upper pivot elevations 2.40 m higher.
