- Command test: after SplitRoof the multi-plane roof is gone, the new roofs have new UUIDs and the original's storey, layer and structure, hosted openings and roof windows are re-hosted at unchanged world positions (within MODEL_TOLERANCE); one undo restores the original roof and its hosted elements exactly.
- kittest: the first split shows the notice; Cancel leaves the project unchanged; Continue splits; after ticking 'Do not show again' the next split shows no notice and the preference survives a restart (prefs round trip); the Preferences dialog re-enables the notice.
- Satisfies ROF-009 and the ROF-009 notice clause of NFR-USE-004.
notes: SRS: ROF-009. Related: NFR-USE-004 (done; notice clause added here), IFX-011, ROF-010 (out of scope, cleanup-and-trims).

title: Add the German catalogue with a key and placeable parity test
description:
WHY: NFR-L10N-002 (S): a German UI translation shall be provided. commands-and-l10n externalized every user-visible string into Fluent catalogues (crates/archicraft-app/locales/en/{app,commands,dialogs,tools,model}.ftl, the tr! macro, the en-XA pseudo-locale, the string lint and docs/i18n.md), including the message keys of the headless model crate (Command labels, CommandError messages, unit labels), and its language negotiation (LanguageChoice with fluent-langneg and sys-locale, commands-and-l10n-17) offers only English (and en-XA in debug builds). Every later epic added keys; a German catalogue must cover all of them and stay complete as keys are added (gap row NFR-L10N-002 depended only on the externalization, now done).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/locales/de/{app,commands,dialogs,tools,model}.ftl with a translation for every English key, embedded like the English files and registered in the language negotiation of commands-and-l10n-17 (the Preferences language list shows 'Deutsch'; that task's test expectation that de-AT falls back to English is updated); docs/i18n-glossary-de.md fixing terminology (for example Wand, Decke, Geschoss, Ebene for graphic layers, Schichtaufbau, Schicht, Öffnung, Tür, Fenster, Dach, Stütze, Träger, Treppe, Geländer, Fang, Hilfslinie, Referenzlinie, Rückgängig) and style (neutral imperatives, typographic quotes „…“, numbers left to the number formatter); parity tests in crates/archicraft-app/src/i18n: every English key exists in German and vice versa, attributes match, each message uses the same set of variables, plural selectors cover the German CLDR categories (one, other), every file parses, and no German message equals its English source except an allowlist (IFCX, OK, unit symbols, product names); docs/i18n.md gains the rule that a new key needs its German text in the same change. Out of scope: switching and layout fixes (12), project data such as the default template's storey and material names (template content, not UI), a German template.
design: Same Fluent conventions as English (kebab-case keys with area prefixes, set_use_isolating(false), numbers passed pre-formatted plus a numeric selector argument for plurals). Compare variable references structurally by parsing the .ftl files with fluent-syntax in the tests rather than with regular expressions. Shortcut text comes from the keymap through ctx.format_shortcut (ui/shell.rs:23, 125, 152 today), not from catalogue strings; 12 replaces it with a localised formatter for modifier and key names. Terminology must not copy any third-party product's German UI strings (NFR-LEG-002); use general German building terms. Machine translation may draft the files, but a German-speaking architect reviews the glossary and, in 12, every string in context.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parity tests pass: no missing or extra keys between en and de, identical variable sets per message and attribute, no Fluent parse errors, plural variants valid for de.
- The untranslated-copy check passes with an allowlist of technical entries, each with a reason.
- A scratch English key without German text fails the parity test and names the key, so later work cannot add keys without German.
- Language negotiation tests: OS locales de-AT, de-CH and de-DE select German when the preference is System (replacing the English-fallback expectation of commands-and-l10n-17); en-US selects English; an explicit preference overrides the OS locale.
- docs/i18n-glossary-de.md exists, docs/i18n.md documents the rule, and the catalogue has been checked against the glossary (reviewer and date recorded).
- cargo test, clippy and fmt green; the string lint and the key-usage test pass.
- Satisfied: the catalogue part of NFR-L10N-002.
notes:
SRS: NFR-L10N-002
Related: NFR-L10N-001 (externalization, commands-and-l10n), NFR-LEG-002. Austrian and Swiss users get de; no de-AT or de-CH variants in v1. NFR-L10N-002 is Should: with 12, the first candidate to cut if the epic overruns.

title: Assert the AS-01 pass criteria on RM-S in conformance/check.ts
design:
Approach: keep check.ts generic and drive the checks from data. The as01 block only switches on assertions whose expectations it lists, so RM-M can reuse them in increment 4.

Geometry in TypeScript:
- Compose world coordinates by multiplying usd::xformop::transform matrices down the composed tree (row-major 4x4 as written by writer.rs).
- The host's thickness direction is the horizontal normal of the wall axis (the usd::usdgeom::basiscurves Axis child).
- Point-in-mesh uses ray parity with a jittered direction and a 1e-6 m boundary band, so that shared faces at junctions do not count as overlaps.
- Limits: vertex-in-mesh does not catch every overlap of non-convex pieces. This is acceptable because the Rust side (task 01, junction-engine coverage helper) is the thorough check. check.ts proves that the file as the viewer composes it still holds that result.

Colour lookup: the composed mesh node inherits its material node by id (writer.rs:376 sets inherits.material; layer-structures-10 Skin parts do the same per skin). Compare against the archicraft::project.materials entry with that id (color, opacity) with the Rgb to 0..1 conversion of writer.rs, name the material in messages, and skip invisible Void meshes.

Mutations are built in memory from the parsed golden by a small conformance/test/mutate.ts, so no broken files are committed. Keep conformance build artefacts git-ignored (regression-and-status).

Pointers: conformance/check.ts:68-105 (checkViewerTree), grids-11 sidecar, doors-windows-core-05 (doors as children of walls with an invisible Void), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs (transforms, colours).
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003. Also AS-01 pass criteria, IFX-006 (a, b tree), IFX-036 (invisible Void), IFX-022 (IsExternal). The hosted IFC5 viewer check (R4) remains a manual release step recorded in docs/test-plan/as-01-two-storey-house.md (task 07).

title: Switch the whole UI to German and fix layout for longer labels
description:
WHY: NFR-L10N-002 (S) is only met when choosing German switches the whole UI: menus, toolbox, prompts, properties, every dialog, the start-up prompts, status line, problems panel, messages from the model crate and shortcut labels. Shortcut labels are formatted with egui's Context::format_shortcut (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:23, 125, 152), which uses English modifier and key names. German labels are about 30 % longer than English ones on average, so fixed-width controls in the properties strip (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs), the toolbox (ui/shell.rs) and dialogs (ui/dialogs.rs) may clip or overflow at the minimum window size of 800x500 (main.rs).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/tests/l10n_de.rs: with the language preference set to German, open the main window and every dialog through its registry command (reusing the walker of the pseudo-locale audit of commands-and-l10n-11), plus the start-up prompts seeded through a temporary DataDirs (the crash notice with a native .dmp/.txt pair of 08, the recovery offer, the consent modal of 06 with FakeAssociation), and assert that every label, button, menu item, window title and tooltip renders German text (no node's text equals its English rendering outside the allowlist), that a command run from the palette shows its German undo label in the Edit menu, and that switching back to English at runtime works without a restart. A localised shortcut formatter replaces format_shortcut: a German egui::ModifierNames (Strg, Umschalt, Alt on Windows and Linux; the symbols on macOS) and catalogue keys for named keys (Entf, Eingabe, Rücktaste, Leertaste, Einfg, Pos1, Ende, Bild auf, Bild ab, Tab, Esc). A layout check in German at 800x500 and 1400x900 asserts that no widget rect exceeds its parent's clip rect in the main window and the largest dialogs, with wgpu snapshot images of those screens for review; fixes use wrapping, ellipsis with tooltip or wider minimums. A German-speaking architect reviews screenshots and strings in context; corrections go into the de catalogue and the glossary. Out of scope: other languages.
design: Run audits under i18n::with(german_localizer, ..) per harness thread (thread-local localizer of commands-and-l10n-01), so parallel English tests are unaffected. The English rendering for comparison comes from rendering the same frame under the English localizer and diffing the AccessKit trees by node id (ids are built from field ids, not label text, per commands-and-l10n-16). The overflow check walks AccessKit node bounds and compares them with the containing panel's rect. Fix widths centrally (for example the properties label column sized from the longest label in the current font) rather than per label.
acceptance_criteria:
- l10n_de.rs passes: every node in the main window, in every registry-opened dialog and in the three seeded start-up prompts shows German text except allowlisted technical tokens and user data; Edit > Undo shows the German command label; after switching back at runtime the same audit passes in English.
- Unit test of the shortcut formatter: menus and the palette show Strg+Z and Entf on Windows and Linux and the symbol form on macOS; in English they keep Ctrl+Z and Delete.
- Layout check: no overflow in German at 800x500 and 1400x900 for the main window, Preferences, Project settings, Materials, Layer structures and the element settings dialog; snapshot images follow the golden-image tolerance of docs/testing.md.
- The in-context review is recorded (reviewer, date, number of corrections) in docs/i18n-glossary-de.md.
- All English UI tests still pass; workspace tests, clippy and fmt green.
- Satisfied: NFR-L10N-002 (the German catalogue switches the whole UI, verified by kittest).
notes:
SRS: NFR-L10N-002
Depends on 06 and 08 so that the start-up prompts are audited in their final form. NFR-L10N-002 is Should: with 11, the first candidate to cut if the epic overruns.

title: Place roof windows with the window tool and write them to IFCX
description:
WHY: DW-021 (S): roof windows follow the host rules of DW-001, including the tool rule: without a valid host under the pointer the tool gives clear feedback and creates nothing. ROF-012 (M) delegates roof windows to DW-021. Table 5-1 gives IfcWindow the parent 'host wall or roof' with a Void and parts via its type where IFX-050 applies; IFX-015 makes hosted elements children of their host and IFX-036 requires the invisible Void child. The epic acceptance requires a roof window hosted in a plane that cuts it with a Void. Gap row DW-021: missing. Existing by then (extend, do not re-implement): the InsertTool with host candidates, CycleHost and previews (doors-windows-core-07/08, host-openings-10), the window codec with Void and type parts (doors-windows-core-05/06, components-dw-catalogue-09), HostHit::RoofPlane (roofs-11) and the RoofWindow kind (roofs-12).

WHAT: App: the InsertTool of crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/insert.rs creates RoofWindow elements when the chosen definition is flagged for roof hosts: hover uses candidates_in_plan and candidate_in_3d (crates/archicraft-app/src/input/host.rs) filtered by the roof-window HostCapability, previews unit and void on the plane through the PreviewMesh overlay, and a click creates exactly one RoofWindow through Project::new_element with the roof-window DefaultsSlot; without a roof under the pointer the StepSpec prompt and Workspace::error say 'Roof windows can only be placed in a roof' and nothing is created; Action::CycleHost steps through overlapping planes. crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs shows u, v, width and height of selected roof windows through the Fields pattern, as doors-windows-core-09 does for wall inserts. IFCX: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/roof_window.rs replaces the stub of roofs-12 with a codec (archicraft::roofWindow: host, plane, u, v, anchor, width, height and the instance reference as the window codec writes it); the IfcWindow node is written as a child of the IfcRoof node (contained_children hook) with its Void child and its parts through the shared type node (IFX-050 as components-dw-catalogue-09 writes window types); the reader restores host and placement and repairs orphans as host-openings-09 does; conformance/check.ts accepts an IfcWindow under an IfcRoof parent; add one roof window to roof_showcase and re-bless roofs.ifcx. Out of scope: dormers, flashings, DW-003 side reversal.
design: No new tool: the window tool's phases (hover, position, configuration) are reused and the definition decides the kind, so the D.8 window shortcut covers roof windows and NFR-USE-002 holds. The host filter comes from HostCapability, so roof windows never offer wall hosts and wall windows never offer roofs. The codec mirrors the window codec member order so goldens stay deterministic; parameters at full precision, mesh coordinates through round_coordinate. Pitfalls: the IfcRoof node of a multi-plane roof is the parent, not the Plane_<k> part node (decided in roofs-11; revisit only if the viewer check suggests otherwise); keep the existing window files unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool kittest: with the roof-window type active, hovering a wall shows the no-host feedback and a click creates nothing; hovering the roof previews unit and void on the plane; a click creates exactly one window with the roof's home storey; Undo removes it.
- Properties: editing v of a selected roof window moves it up the slope in one command; an out-of-plane value is rejected with a message (ELM-017).
- IFCX: the IfcWindow node is a child of the IfcRoof node with an invisible closed Void child and parts through its type (IFX-050 where it applies); the round trip restores host, plane and placement; roofs.ifcx is reproduced byte for byte and conformance/run.sh is green on it.
- Satisfies the tool and persistence clauses of DW-021 and the roof-window clause of ROF-012.
notes: SRS: DW-021 ROF-012. Related: DW-001, DW-002, IFX-015, IFX-036, IFX-050, OPN-007, ELM-017. Dependency note: as roofs-12 (doors-windows-core and components-dw-catalogue are not declared prerequisites of roofs).

title: Review every tool against the interaction-model checklist
description:
WHY: NFR-USE-002 (M, inspection) requires all element tools to follow one consistent interaction model: the same geometry-method choices, the same numeric input and snapping, and the same edit commands for nodes, edges and polygons. At increment 0 only the wall and slab tools existed (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13-17, 41-84) and the edit-command clause had nothing behind it (gap row NFR-USE-002). Since then the shared PointInput service (point-input-snapping), the transform commands (selection-transforms), the node/edge palette on the one Outline type (edit-reshape-palette) and many element tools landed in separate epics, each of which may have drifted. The usability test of NFR-USE-001 (13, 14) should not spend participants' time on inconsistencies an inspection can find.

WHAT: No shared geometry-method type exists in the codebase or in the earlier epics: every tool has its own mode enum (WallMode and SlabMode today, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:41-84, plus the roof, beam, stair and other modes added later), so 'the same geometry-method choices' needs one vocabulary first. views/tools.rs gains GeometryMethod descriptors (id, label key, icon, shortcut, point steps: single, chain, rectangle, rotated rectangle, polygon, arc variants and so on) and every tool mode enum a method() mapping onto them. docs/usability/interaction-checklist.md: a matrix of every element tool (wall, slab, column, beam, roof, opening, door, window, stair, terrain, grid and 2D lines, and, if they are merged when the review runs, free-form solid, railing and curtain wall: free-form-solids, railings-stairs-adv and curtain-walls are not ancestors of this epic) against the criteria: geometry methods taken from the shared GeometryMethod set with the same labels, icons, shortcuts and point steps; every point through the PointInput service (typed distance and angle, relative and absolute coordinates, locks, snap precedence, Tab cycling, Esc one step back, Backspace one point); a prompt line listing the available keys (NFR-USE-003); the shared transform commands for selected elements and, for every outline-based kind, the same node, edge and polygon palette commands. crates/archicraft-app/tests/interaction_model.rs makes the automatable part table-driven over the tool and kind registries: every tool mode maps to a GeometryMethod and the same method has the same label key, icon, shortcut and step count in every tool; the same scripted typed input (2.5 m at 30 degrees, then an X lock) through a ViewSurface stub yields the same first segment for every point-based tool; the same snap scenario (cursor within the snap radius of an existing wall endpoint, then of an edge midpoint) yields the same snapped point and snap kind for every point-based tool; Esc and Backspace behave alike; for every kind whose PartRef has outline nodes and edges the palette offers the canonical command set, with deviations only through an explicit, reasoned allowlist. A reviewer then walks the checklist in a release build, fixes small deviations (each with a test) and files beads for larger ones. Out of scope: new tools, a palette redesign.
design: Build on the existing registries instead of a new layer: the tool list in views/tools.rs (or the tool registry that replaced ToolKind::ALL), KindDescriptor and PartRef from element-kind-framework and selection-transforms, Command::Reshape and the palette command list from edit-reshape-palette, input::PointInput and the ViewSurface trait from point-input-snapping, and the prompt-key test of commands-and-l10n-12. The scripted-input test drives each tool's state machine headlessly (as the tools.rs tests do) and compares resulting points within MODEL_TOLERANCE. A deviation usually means a tool bypassed a shared service, so fix it in the service. GeometryMethod is a descriptor table introduced here, not a behaviour layer; tools keep their state machines and only map their modes. Time-box fixes to half a day in total; everything else becomes a bead labelled usability and interaction-model.
acceptance_criteria:
- interaction_model.rs passes and iterates the registries, so a tool or kind added later is checked without editing the test; a scratch tool with its own method enum or its own point parsing makes it fail.
- Every tool mode maps to GeometryMethod; a scratch mode that labels its rectangle method differently, or takes a different number of points for it, fails the test.
- The typed-input and snap scenarios give the same first segment and the same snapped point and snap kind for every point-based tool (the numeric-input and snapping clause).
- The allowlist holds only reasoned exceptions (for example doors and windows have no outline palette because they are positioned along their host) and each entry names the SRS clause.
- docs/usability/interaction-checklist.md exists with every tool row filled (pass, fixed here with the test name, or bead id) and the reviewer and date.
- No row is left failing without a bead; fixes made here come with kittest or unit tests; workspace tests, clippy and fmt are green.
- Satisfied: NFR-USE-002 by inspection backed by automated checks; supports NFR-USE-003 and NFR-USE-001.
notes:
SRS: NFR-USE-002
Related: NFR-USE-003 (prompt lines), D-7 (explicit commands; modifier gestures only as accelerators).

title: Execute the AS-01..AS-05 procedures on the four target platforms
description:
WHY: SRS 7.2 accepts v1 only when AS-01..AS-05 (with AS-07 and AS-08) pass on Windows, macOS and Linux, which is how NFR-PORT-001 (Windows 11 x64), NFR-PORT-002 (macOS current and previous major on Apple silicon) and NFR-PORT-003 (current Ubuntu LTS x64) are accepted in practice. The automated parts run in CI on all three OSes (09), but AS-01's viewer check (the hosted IFC5 viewer, manual once per release, docs/technology-choices.md:202), AS-02's measured alignment, AS-03's close and reopen in the application, AS-04's measure tool and AS-05's force-kill of the windowed binary are interactive and need a person on each platform.

WHAT: Execute docs/test-plan/as-01-two-storey-house.md, as-02.md, as-03-round-trip.md, as-04.md and as-05.md (index docs/test-plan/README.md of 09) with the release-candidate archives from release.yml on real Windows 11 x64, macOS current and macOS previous on Apple silicon, and the current Ubuntu LTS x64; the railing step of AS-01 only if railings are in the release (Should part, SRS 7.2). Save the AS-01 project on one platform and reopen it on the others for AS-03 (platform-independent files, NFR-PORT-004). Fill the per-OS result columns of docs/test-plan/README.md and the AS section of docs/test-plan/results/rc-<version>.md (OS build, machine, archive SHA-256, commit, tester, date, expected and measured values, conformance/run.sh and compare_ids output for the saved files); file a bead per failure naming the procedure step. Out of scope: AS-06 (ifcx-interop, Should), AS-07 (perf-tuning-rm-m-l), AS-08 (14, 16), fixing failures.
design: Run on the build produced after 16, so usability fixes are included. One tester per platform needs about half a day for the five procedures. Keep screenshots out of the repository unless they are listed in scripts/asset-allowlist.txt (the NFR-LEG-002 guard of regression-and-status-01); link them from the results instead. If a platform's machine is missing (for example the previous macOS major), record it as a blocker rather than skipping silently. Keep the results factual: OS build numbers, commit hash, archive checksums.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every procedure AS-01..AS-05 has a pass or fail entry for Windows 11 x64, macOS current, macOS previous and Ubuntu LTS, with OS build, machine, archive SHA-256 and commit.
- AS-01: on each platform the saved file passes conformance/run.sh, and the hosted IFC5 viewer shows project/site/building/3 storeys, walls with openings and clean L/T junctions, and the modelled materials and colours.
- AS-02: members sit on grid lines and storey levels within 0.01 mm when measured, and the IFC classes are IfcColumn, IfcBeam, IfcSlab and IfcFooting.
- AS-03: after close and reopen and the two changes, junctions, openings, slabs and the roof follow, compare_ids reports no changed element UUIDs and the re-saved file passes conformance/run.sh; the file saved on another platform reopens identically.
- AS-04: measured lengths and angles equal the typed values at 0.1 mm / 0.01 degree.
- AS-05: force-terminating the windowed binary (End task, kill -9, Force Quit) six minutes after the last save offers recovery, the recovered model contains everything up to the last autosave, and the original file is byte-identical.
- Every failure has a bead linked from the results file.
- Satisfied: the per-platform execution of AS-01..AS-05 (SRS 7.2) as evidence for NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003
Related: SRS 7.2, NFR-PORT-004, IFX-006 (b). Split out of release-candidate-17 during review (executing five procedures on four platforms is about two days).

title: Script the AS-01 and AS-03 procedures and test reopening in the app
description:
WHY: SRS 7.1 uses 'scripted manual tests for interaction-heavy requirements', and 7.2 accepts v1 only when AS-01 to AS-05 pass on Windows, macOS and Linux. The visual part of IFX-006 (b) is manual, once per release. The roadmap assigns the scripted AS-01 and AS-03 procedures under docs/test-plan/ to this epic. AS-03's 'close and reopen' is an application action that the headless test of task 06 only approximates: the real path includes File > Open, the atomic save with backups and the dirty-state handling of the app. NFR-USE-006 is verified by demonstration: a new user models the AS-01 house from the defaults. Task 08 runs that demonstration on the AS-01 procedure written here. NFR-MNT-003's 'run on every change' covers the automated app-level check added here.

WHAT:
- docs/test-plan/as-01-two-storey-house.md. Starting from docs/test-plan/increment-1-ground-floor.md (doors-windows-core), it adds: a new project from the default template; the attic storey; terrain from typed spot elevations; footings; the upper floor and attic; stairs through the openings; the gable roof from the walls; trimming the gable walls; save as IFCX; opening the file in the pinned reference viewer and in the hosted IFC5 viewer (R4). The expected-values table is derived from the rm_s.rs constants. The railing step is marked as increment 3 (railings-stairs-adv).
- docs/test-plan/as-03-round-trip.md: close and reopen; change the core thickness in the layer structure editor and the upper storey height in the storey settings; a checklist of what must follow; save; run conformance/run.sh on the file; compare the UUIDs.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/compare_ids.rs: prints the differences of element and sub-node UUIDs between two IFCX files, for the manual AS-03 and for later debugging.
- A kittest as03_reopen_edit_save in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: open a temporary copy of tests/golden/rm-s.ifcx with ArchiCraftApp::open_path, check the browser and problems panel, apply samples::as03_edits through the workspace, save with ArchiCraftApp::save_to, reopen and compare.
Both procedures are linked from docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md (regression-and-status-13) if it exists, next to the manual R4 viewer check. Out of scope: executing the procedures on all three operating systems (release-candidate), the railing, and usability testing (NFR-USE-001).
design:
Approach: the procedures are short, deterministic and value-checked, like the increment-1 ground-floor script. Each step has an action, the typed values and an expected observation. The expected values are those of RM-S's layout constants. A tester's model has random ids, so compare_ids has two modes:
- by id, for the same project before and after the AS-03 edits (ids must match);
- by element name, for comparing a tester's model with the golden (the parameters must match).
The check.ts summary gives a further comparison. compare_ids reuses validate::flatten and the role classification helper of task 06; move that helper into archicraft_ifcx as a small public module if the example needs it.

The kittest uses the label-based harness of crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs:17-37 with DataDirs::at(temp). It drives the edits through `harness.state_mut().workspace().execute(...)`: the dialog widgets are covered by the layer-structures and properties-and-dialogs kittests. It reads geometry through Document::geometry() to assert that the problems list is empty, and must not depend on wgpu.

Pitfall: opening a ~300-element file in kittest runs evaluation on the UI thread. Allow enough run_steps, and keep the test under the CI time budget by not rendering 3D panes.

Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:152 (open_path), :214 (save_to); persistence/mod.rs:55-110 (backup_path, save_atomically); doors-windows-core-11 for the scenario-document format.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both documents exist, with numbered steps, expected values at 0.1 mm / 0.01 degree display precision and a pass/fail results table. Each was executed once on one platform, with results, date, platform and build recorded in it.
- `cargo run -p archicraft-ifcx --example compare_ids -- rm-s.ifcx rm-s-as03.ifcx` reports identical element ids with their count and exits zero. On two unrelated files it lists the differences and exits non-zero. The by-name mode compares a tester's model with the golden. as-03-round-trip.md uses it.
- kittest as03_reopen_edit_save runs on all three CI runners without a GPU. After opening, the labels '00 Ground floor', '01 First floor', '02 Attic' and 'No problems' are present.
- After the two edits, Edit > Undo shows the commands' labels, and undo then redo leaves the project equal.
- After save_to and a reopen of the saved file: element ids equal those of the golden; the file validates without problems; a backup exists at persistence::backup_path(path, 1); the document is not dirty.
- The procedures cite the automated counterparts (check.ts as01 block, as03.rs, the kittest), so a reader knows which steps are covered on every change.
- Supports AS-01/AS-03 acceptance (SRS 7.2), gives NFR-USE-006 its demonstration procedure, and adds the app-level AS-03 check to the NFR-MNT-003 suite.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003 NFR-USE-006. Also AS-01, AS-03, SRS 7.1 (scripted manual tests), IFX-006 (b) manual visual check, IFX-011. The three-OS execution of these procedures belongs to release-candidate.

title: Pin native GPU backends, report the adapter and parse start-up arguments
description:
WHY: NFR-PORT-006 (M) requires 2D and 3D rendering to use a current, non-deprecated, hardware-accelerated graphics API on each supported operating system. Existing and kept: crates/archicraft-app/src/main.rs:21-29 selects eframe's wgpu renderer, the 3D view renders through the egui_wgpu::wgpu re-export (views/render3d.rs, views/shader.wgsl) and the plan view is painted by egui on the same wgpu device, so 2D and 3D already share one GPU path (docs/technology-choices.md:108-118). Missing: egui-wgpu's default backends are PRIMARY|GL (egui-wgpu 0.36.2 src/setup.rs:245-246), so a machine without a working Metal, DX12 or Vulkan driver silently falls back to OpenGL (deprecated by Apple) or to a software adapter; nothing records which API and device actually ran; a missing adapter ends in an eframe error instead of a message; wgpu device loss leaves no report (gap observation of nfr-quality); and main.rs:18 treats any first argument as a file to open. NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 (M) build on this: the smoke run (18) and the release builds (02, 03) need the backend policy, the adapter report and a real argument parser. README.md:41-43 still tells Linux users that OpenGL is enough.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-app/src/gpu.rs: backends_for(target_os) -> wgpu::Backends (Windows DX12 with Vulkan as second choice, macOS METAL, Linux VULKAN; OpenGL only when ARCHICRAFT_GRAPHICS=gl is set on Linux, logged as an unsupported fallback) and the egui_wgpu::WgpuConfiguration passed in NativeOptions. The adapter info (backend, name, driver, device type) is read from CreationContext::wgpu_render_state, logged, kept in a process-wide GraphicsInfo, shown in the About window (ui/dialogs.rs info_windows, with a copy button) and added as a 'Graphics:' line to crash reports (persistence/crash.rs report_text). Device type Cpu (a software adapter such as WARP or lavapipe) shows a non-modal notice that rendering is not hardware-accelerated and the performance targets do not apply. The wgpu device-lost and uncaptured-error handlers log the event and write a report through a new crash::write_report(kind, text) helper (kinds gpu-device-lost and gpu-error), so GPU failures leave a local report in DataDirs::crash_reports() like panics do. When no adapter is found, main.rs maps eframe's error to an rfd::MessageDialog naming the required API per OS and exits with code 2 instead of panicking. main.rs gains a small argument parser (Args { open, smoke_test, version }) that ignores macOS -psn_* arguments and unknown flags instead of opening them as files; --version prints 'ArchiCraft <version>' and exits 0; --smoke-test <report.json> is parsed here and implemented in 18. README.md:41-43 states the Vulkan requirement on Linux, and docs/technology-choices.md (GPU rendering) records the backend policy and the Linux OpenGL decision. New strings are catalogue keys (with German text once release-candidate-11 has landed, enforced by its parity test). Out of scope: the smoke mode (18), the CI jobs (03), packaging (02), the hardware-class decision (regression-and-status-18, O-15).
design: egui_wgpu::WgpuConfiguration { wgpu_setup: WgpuSetup::CreateNew(WgpuSetupCreateNew { instance_descriptor: wgpu::InstanceDescriptor { backends, .. }, .. }), .. }: verify the exact struct names against egui-wgpu 0.36.2 (the gap row cites src/setup.rs:245-246) and always go through the egui_wgpu::wgpu re-export (docs/technology-choices.md:118) so versions cannot drift. GraphicsInfo lives in a std::sync::OnceLock<String> that the panic hook reads without locking. The device-lost callback and Device::on_uncaptured_error are registered on the device egui-wgpu creates (RenderState::device); check how wgpu 30 exposes the device-lost callback before coding, and keep both handlers free of egui calls because they may run on another thread. crash::write_report reuses the stamp and file-name scheme of crash::install (crash-<stamp>-<pid>.txt), so the start-up notice and reports_since need no change. Pitfalls: run_native returns Err(eframe::Error::Wgpu(..)) when no adapter exists, map it to the message dialog; Windows release builds have no console (main.rs:4), so --version output is visible only when the caller redirects stdout (the release workflow does); current macOS no longer passes -psn, but some launchers still do; WARP on Windows and lavapipe on Linux report device type Cpu, which CI accepts (03) and real hardware must not show (17).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: backends_for maps windows to DX12|VULKAN, macos to METAL, linux to VULKAN, and linux with the GL override to VULKAN|GL; no OS gets GL by default.
- Unit tests for Args: a file path opens it; `--smoke-test out.json` sets the report path; `--version` is recognised; `-psn_0_12345` and unknown `--flags` are ignored and logged; a path and the smoke flag combine.
- Unit test with an injected GraphicsInfo: a crash report written after adapter creation contains the Graphics line; kittest: the About window shows backend, adapter, driver and device type, and the copy button copies them.
- kittest with an injected GraphicsInfo of device type Cpu: the software-adapter notice appears once and can be dismissed; with IntegratedGpu or DiscreteGpu on Metal, DX12 or Vulkan no notice appears.
- Unit test: calling the device-lost handler with a temporary DataDirs writes crash-<stamp>-<pid>.txt with the kind gpu-device-lost and the Graphics line, and crash::reports_since lists it, so the existing start-up notice shows its path.
- Unit test of the error mapping: eframe::Error::Wgpu(..) from run_native becomes the no-adapter message and exit code 2.
- Manual: `cargo run --release -p archicraft-app` on a developer machine logs and shows Metal, DX12 or Vulkan with a non-Cpu device type, and the plan and the 3D pane both render (2D and 3D on the same backend).
- README.md and docs/technology-choices.md state the backend per OS and that OpenGL is an unsupported opt-in on Linux.
- Existing UI and persistence tests pass; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green; the string lint passes.
- Satisfied: the API clause of NFR-PORT-006 in code, for 2D and 3D; the prerequisites of the NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 evidence (18, 03).
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-006 NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003
Open: whether Linux may keep an OpenGL fallback at all; the default here is opt-in only, recorded in docs/technology-choices.md.
Review: the smoke-test mode moved to release-candidate-18 (01 held two tasks' worth of work).

title: Single- and multi-plane roofs with a pitch-weighted straight skeleton
description:
Single-plane roofs (outline, pivot line, slope side, pitch formats, pivot elevation, thickness or structure measured perpendicular, eaves cuts, direct manipulation) and multi-plane roofs from a pivot polygon with per-edge pitch, overhang and gable type, break levels, straight-skeleton plane generation for non-convex footprints with mixed pitches, the three pivot-polygon modes (draw, pick a closed polygon through contour detection, outline of selected walls from the junction engine's outer boundary with the pivot at the wall top), splitting into single planes, computed values, hosted openings and roof windows, and IfcRoof with one child per plane through the compound codec. Plane bodies are prisms in the tilted plane clipped by their neighbours with own code; no Boolean kernel is needed. Trims of walls to roofs and roof joins are cleanup-and-trims.

Risks: Skeleton robustness on degenerate events: exact event ordering with MODEL_TOLERANCE, the fixture corpus and the randomised test; on failure keep the last valid roof and report (NFR-REL-005). Break levels (Should) are time-boxed.
design: archicraft-geometry roof/skeleton.rs with a pitch-weighted straight skeleton (own code per technology-choices) and roof/body.rs building each plane as a prism in its plane clipped by the neighbouring planes with layer thickness perpendicular to the plane; archicraft-model kinds/roof.rs with per-edge parameters and the structure reference surface, slope parsing in units.rs; archicraft-ifcx compound children per plane through the framework's parts codec; archicraft-app tools/roof.rs (pivot line, slope side, outline, wall-outline mode) on the point-input service with per-edge handles in the reshape palette.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture corpus (rectangle, L, T, U, notched footprints; equal and mixed pitches; gable edges) produces planes whose ridge heights and hip/valley lines match hand-computed values and every roof body is closed and manifold; a randomised footprint test asserts closed output or a reported problem; the four eaves-cut variants; a mansard with one break level; the AS-01 gable roof is generated from the selected exterior walls with the pivot at the wall top; dragging the pivot line regenerates within 200 ms on the stand-in; IfcRoof with one part per plane passes conformance (IFX-016 re-asserted); a roof window is hosted in a plane and cuts it with a Void; split into single-plane roofs shows the one-time notice.
notes: SRS: ROF-001 ROF-002 ROF-003 ROF-004 ROF-005 ROF-006 ROF-007 ROF-008 ROF-009 ROF-011 ROF-012 DW-021

title: Generate THIRD-PARTY.md and gate releases on the licence inventory
description:
WHY: NFR-LEG-001 (M, inspection) requires every third-party component to be inventoried with its licence, and only the permissive licences allowed by the technology choices to be used while the distribution model is open (O-5). cargo-deny enforces the allow-list in CI (deny.toml:1-43, ci.yml:71-79), but no inventory artefact is generated, committed or shipped; the bundled IFCx.dev schema files have no identified licence (crates/archicraft-ifcx/schemas/README.md:13-16) and are invisible to cargo-deny; the vendored Manifold C++ sources in crates/archicraft-manifold/vendor (Apache-2.0, with their own bundled dependencies) sit in a private crate that cargo-deny skips (deny.toml: private = { ignore = true }); and the egui font licence exception (deny.toml:23-29) is marked 'recheck before any public release' (gap row NFR-LEG-001).

WHAT: about.toml and packaging/about.hbs for cargo-about, producing THIRD-PARTY.md at the repository root for the shipped dependency graph of the three release targets (development and build dependencies excluded) with the full licence texts; third-party/inventory.toml listing every non-Cargo component (each vendored directory under crates/archicraft-manifold/vendor, the four schema files and ifcx-container.schema.json, egui's bundled fonts with the OFL-1.1 and Ubuntu Font Licence texts, the application icons as own work) with name, version, source URL, SPDX licence and licence-text path, rendered into the same THIRD-PARTY.md; scripts/check-inventory.sh, failing when a vendored directory or schema file lacks an entry or an entry's SPDX id is not on deny.toml's allow-list or exceptions; a CI step that regenerates THIRD-PARTY.md and fails on a diff; THIRD-PARTY.md opens with a statement that the distribution model is still open (O-5) and that until it is decided only the permissive licences of deny.toml's allow-list are used (R8); deny.toml [advisories] release policy (yanked deny, unmaintained workspace, every ignore with a reason and review date) and `cargo deny check advisories licenses sources bans` also run in release.yml before packaging and in ci.yml's licences job (regression-and-status-01 normally adds advisories there; regression-and-status is not an ancestor of this epic, so add it here if it is missing); later dependency additions (04, 05, 08) regenerate THIRD-PARTY.md, which the diff check enforces; scripts/package.sh adds THIRD-PARTY.md to all three archives; the About window gains a 'Third-party licences' view of the embedded file. Resolve the schema-file licence: check the IFCx.dev repository for a licence, otherwise ask buildingSMART in writing, and record the outcome (licence, permission or a product-owner decision) in crates/archicraft-ifcx/schemas/README.md and docs/technology-choices.md. Out of scope: deciding the distribution model (O-5), the trademark check (O-17), the test-only Node tooling of conformance/ (listed as not distributed).
design: cargo-about (MIT/Apache-2.0) is a CI tool installed at a pinned version (taiki-e/install-action), not a dependency. Configure targets = [x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu], ignore-dev-dependencies and ignore-build-dependencies = true, and accepted = the deny.toml allow-list so both tools agree; attach the font licence files through a clarification for epaint_default_fonts. The output must be deterministic (sorted, no timestamps) for the diff check. Embed THIRD-PARTY.md with include_str! from the workspace root (about 1-2 MB, acceptable) so the About view always matches the build. Use the current cargo-deny configuration schema (the vulnerability and notice keys were removed in 0.16). Pitfall: the private-crate ignore hides archicraft-manifold's C++ licences from both tools, so the inventory file is the only record and the directory check is what keeps it complete. If buildingSMART grants no licence before the release, public distribution is blocked until the product owner records a decision; internal release candidates may proceed with the open item listed in the release notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo about generate` with the committed configuration reproduces THIRD-PARTY.md byte for byte in CI; adding a dependency without regenerating fails the job with a hint.
- THIRD-PARTY.md lists target-specific crates of all three targets (for example windows-sys for Windows and objc2-metal for macOS, both already in Cargo.lock through wgpu and winit), Manifold and its vendored dependencies, the schema files and the font licences.
- THIRD-PARTY.md starts with the O-5 statement and the permissive allow-list.
- scripts/check-inventory.sh passes; scratch checks: a new directory under vendor/ without an entry fails, and an entry with GPL-3.0-only fails.
- `cargo deny check advisories licenses sources bans` passes in ci.yml and release.yml; a scratch yanked dependency fails it.
- The three release archives contain LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY.md (checked by the package.sh dry run).
- kittest: About > Third-party licences opens a window that contains the heading of THIRD-PARTY.md.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/schemas/README.md states the resolved licence or the recorded decision with date and source; the font-licence recheck is recorded in deny.toml; the schema-licence item leaves the technical-debt list of docs/implementation-status.md.
- Satisfied: NFR-LEG-001 (inventory with licences, permissive licences only).
notes:
SRS: NFR-LEG-001
Related: O-5 (distribution model, open), NFR-LEG-003 (R2 examples are fetched at test time, never shipped), regression-and-status-01 (advisories in the CI command; not an ancestor in the epic graph, so this task adds advisories itself if missing, plus the release policy and the release-workflow run).

title: Host openings in roof planes with perpendicular or vertical voids
description:
WHY: ROF-012 (M): roofs shall host openings (OPN-001: exactly one host, positioned relative to it, moving and deleted with it; hosts are walls, slabs and roofs). OPN-003 (rectangular, circular or polygonal cross-section), OPN-004 (perpendicular to the host face or vertical) and OPN-007 (live preview over the host under the pointer in plan and 3D views) apply; IFX-015 and IFX-036 make hosted openings children of their host with a Void. OPN-006 (S): a storey-spanning shaft cuts every slab and roof in its range; host-openings-06 delivers shafts and leaves the roof cut path to this epic. Gap rows: ROF-012 missing; OPN-001 names roofs as hosts; host-openings states that roofs as hosts are verified again in this epic. Existing by then (keep and extend, do not re-implement): the opening kind, Void part, host cascade, orphan repair, host candidates and the opening tool of host-openings-01 to -11.

WHAT: Model: the roof descriptor's HostCapability (host-openings-01) accepts roof-plane placements, plan placements and shaft cuts; the #[non_exhaustive] HostPlacement of crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/opening.rs (host-openings-01) gains `HostPlacement::RoofPlane { plane: PlaneRef, u, v, rotation }` (named HostFace::RoofPlane in that plan; PlaneRef = Single or Multi { edge, level }; u along the pivot edge, v up the slope) for perpendicular openings, while vertical openings in roofs use the existing HostPlacement::Plan; the opening validator accepts both on roofs and rejects WallFace placements there. Geometry: the roofs-02 builder takes hole rings per plane: a perpendicular opening is a hole in plane coordinates with side faces perpendicular to the plane; the plan polygon of a vertical opening, and of a shaft (Depth::Storeys) whose range contains the roof (shaft_targets of host-openings-06 selects the roof once its HostCapability allows shaft cuts), is clipped against every plane region it crosses and cut with vertical side faces; each opening keeps its Void part; the dirty set marks the host roof and its openings, and a dirty shaft dirties the roofs it meets. App: crates/archicraft-app/src/input/host.rs (host-openings-10) gains `HostHit::RoofPlane { plane, u, v }`: candidates_in_plan returns the topmost plane region of a roof under the pointer and candidate_in_3d maps the PickIndex hit's part to its plane through Kind::part_ref_for_role; the opening tool (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/opening.rs, host-openings-11) offers roofs as host candidates with the void previewed on the plane. IFCX: the opening codec (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/opening.rs, host-openings-08) writes placement kind 'roofPlane' with plane, u, v and rotation; openings are children of the IfcRoof node (the contained_children hook); add a perpendicular and a vertical opening to roof_showcase and re-bless roofs.ifcx. Out of scope: limited-depth openings in roofs (the 'limited' variant of OPN-005 needs a pocket cut; it is refused with 'Limited-depth openings in roofs are not supported yet' and a follow-up bead), openings cutting several elements (OPN-002, solid-kernel-ops), roof windows (12, 14), perpendicular openings in sloped slabs (host-openings rejects them until an inclined-plane path exists; follow-up bead from the done task).
design: Each plane exposes `PlaneFrame { origin, u, v, n }` from roof/plane.rs (origin on the reference surface at the pivot edge start). A perpendicular opening polygon in (u, v) maps to lines on the reference surface; its hole side planes contain each hole edge line and n, so the same three-plane vertex construction as for the outer sides keeps skins consistent. Vertical openings use vertical planes through the plan polygon's edges. After clipping (geo intersection in plan) hole rings must lie inside the plane region by MODEL_TOLERANCE; a perpendicular hole crossing the plane boundary is clipped to the host plane and reported ('Opening OP-002 extends beyond its roof plane'). Openings keep (PlaneRef, u, v), so pitch and pivot-elevation edits keep them on their plane; when a PlaneRef disappears (edge deleted) the opening is reported and handled by host-openings' orphan repair. Host relation, Void sub-node ids from the opening UUID and incremental dirty marking of host and hosted follow host-openings; holes in the roof outline itself stay geometry, not openings (IFX-025).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry: a 1.0 × 1.2 m perpendicular opening in a 35° plane of the 12 × 9 hip roof removes 1.0 × 1.2 × 0.30 m³ from that plane (signed-volume difference within 1e-9), cuts every skin of a layered roof and leaves all bodies closed; a 0.6 × 0.6 m vertical opening across a hip cuts both planes with vertical faces and removes in total 0.36 m² × 0.30 / cos 35° (each plane loses its share of the plan area times its own vertical thickness).
- Shaft: a Depth::Storeys opening spanning the upper storey and the roof's storey cuts every roof plane it crosses with vertical faces, and follows a storey elevation change (OPN-006 roof clause delegated by host-openings-06).
- Model: the roof's HostCapability accepts RoofPlane and Plan placements and rejects a WallFace placement on a roof with a message.
- Commands: the opening moves and is deleted with its roof (host-openings cascade) and keeps its (plane, u, v) through a pitch change (tests with undo); an opening that falls outside its plane after an edit is reported instead of producing corrupt geometry.
- Tool kittest: hovering a roof in plan with the opening tool previews the void on the plane; clicking where there is no host creates nothing and shows the host feedback.
- IFCX: the opening is a child of the IfcRoof node with an invisible closed Void mesh; the round trip restores host and placement; roofs.ifcx is reproduced and conformance/run.sh is green.
- Satisfies ROF-012 for through openings, perpendicular and vertical.
notes: SRS: ROF-012. Related: OPN-001, OPN-003, OPN-004, OPN-005, OPN-006 (roof clause), OPN-007, IFX-015, IFX-025, IFX-036. Follow-up bead to file: limited-depth openings in roofs (OPN-005) once a pocket cut or the solid kernel is available.

title: Write docs/release.md and run the release-property checks on real machines
description:
WHY: Several requirements of this epic are release properties that only a run on real machines proves. NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002 and NFR-PORT-003 name Windows 11 x64 (CI uses Windows Server), macOS current and previous on Apple silicon, and Ubuntu LTS; NFR-PORT-006 asks for a hardware-accelerated API (CI uses software adapters) and published hardware; NFR-SEC-002 forbids any outgoing data; SW-001's native dialogs, recent list, consent and registration and the minidump report of 08 must be seen working on each OS. docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md (regression-and-status-13) holds the earlier items (manual hosted-viewer check of IFX-006 (b), fuzz hour per release, AS-05 on three OSes, hardware publication, status table), and docs/technology-choices.md:202 keeps the visual check in the hosted IFC5 viewer manual, once per release.

WHAT: docs/release.md: the release procedure (version scheme; choosing MACOS_MIN, MACOS_CURRENT and MACOS_PREVIOUS for the release; the release-notes file from the template of 03; cargo deny and THIRD-PARTY.md freshness; tagging; the release workflow; verifying archives and SHA256SUMS; publishing the draft release; keeping symbols), linking the checklist. Extend docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md (regression-and-status is not an ancestor of this epic: if the file is missing, create it with the IFX-006 (b) hosted-viewer, fuzz-hour, NFR-LEG-002 and status-table items) with this epic's items: the --smoke-test run (18) on real Windows 11 x64, macOS current and previous on Apple silicon and Ubuntu LTS, on a minimum-class and a reference-class machine where available, reporting a non-Cpu device type and DX12, Metal or Vulkan; File > Open and Save as show the operating system's native dialog and the recent list survives a restart (the kept SW-001 clauses); the first start asks for consent, registration works and a double-clicked .ifcx opens; ARCHICRAFT_SIMULATE_CRASH=segfault leaves a minidump report shown at the next start; a network monitor (Little Snitch or LuLu on macOS, Resource Monitor or Wireshark on Windows, nethogs or ss -tp on Linux) shows no traffic during a modelling session, a save and a crash, and traffic only to the import host after consenting to a remote import (the consent-gated fetch of ifcx-interop, also not an ancestor: if it has not landed there is no network code and the expectation is no traffic at all); the German UI switch; THIRD-PARTY.md in each archive; the AS-01..AS-05 results of 20; O-5 and O-17 listed as blockers for a public release. Execute the checklist for the release candidate and record the results in docs/test-plan/results/rc-<version>.md with a per-platform matrix (20 adds the AS-01..AS-05 section); file beads for failures. Out of scope: executing AS-01..AS-05 (20), publishing a public release (O-5, O-17 open).
design: If a minimum-class machine is not available for a platform (O-15), record which one is missing and why rather than skipping silently. The import-fetch check needs a file with a remote import (an RX example) and the consent dialog of ifcx-interop. Keep the results file factual (OS build numbers, commit hash, archive checksums). Run the checklist on the build produced after 16, so usability fixes are included.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/release.md exists, is linked from README.md, and following it step by step produced the release candidate's draft release.
- release-checklist.md contains every item listed above as a checkbox with the expected observation.
- docs/test-plan/results/rc-<version>.md records every item for Windows 11, macOS current, macOS previous and Ubuntu LTS with pass or fail, the smoke reports (backend, adapter, device type) and the machines used; the AS-01..AS-05 section of 20 is complete; every failure has a bead.
- The network-monitor check shows no connection except the consented import fetch on every platform.
- The native-dialog and recent-list items and the consent, registration and double-click items pass on every platform (SW-001).
- The candidate's release notes name minimum and reference hardware (check-release-notes.sh passes).
- Satisfied: the manual verification of NFR-PORT-001, NFR-PORT-002, NFR-PORT-003, NFR-PORT-006, SW-001 and NFR-SEC-002.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003 NFR-PORT-006 SW-001 NFR-SEC-002
Related: NFR-SEC-004, IFX-006 (b) manual check, D.9 fuzz hour, O-5 and O-17 (open, block a public release only).

title: Harden the skeleton for degenerate events, gables and random input
description:
WHY: ROF-003 (M) also requires that setting two opposite end edges to gable yields vertical gable ends, and that every footprint works, convex or not, with any mix of pitches; real footprints produce simultaneous events (symmetric reflex corners, crosses, notches), collinear edges and very short edges. NFR-REL-005 (M): operations that would produce invalid geometry shall be rejected with an explanatory message and never silently create corrupt elements. The epic names skeleton robustness on degenerate events as its main risk, mitigated by exact event ordering with MODEL_TOLERANCE, the fixture corpus and a randomised test.

WHAT: Extend crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/skeleton.rs: zero weights for gable edges (the wavefront line stays put, neighbouring vertices slide along it, the gable face is returned as a vertical SkFace with zero plan area and `gable: true`); general vertex events (two or more reflex vertices meeting) and several split events at one point resolved in one batch; collinear consecutive edges (equal weights merged, different weights give a vertical step face through an inserted zero-weight wavefront edge); nearly parallel neighbours and edges down to the EDT-019 thresholds; `SkeletonError { kind, at, message }` with user-facing messages for anything left unresolved. Extend the corpus with gable and degenerate fixtures and add the randomised test crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/roof_skeleton_random.rs, with the footprint generators in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/roof_corpus/random.rs so the body-level random test of roofs-05 reuses them. Out of scope: element evaluation and the 'keep the last valid roof' fallback (05), break levels (09).
design: Batch resolution generalises the roofs-03 batching: cluster events within MODEL_TOLERANCE in time and position, collect all wavefront vertices reaching the cluster, sort the incident wavefront edges by angle around the node and reconnect consecutive pairs into new vertices (the multi-split handling described by Huber and Held), dropping pairs whose new edge has zero length. Zero weights: a vertex between a zero-weight edge g and an edge e of weight w moves along g's line with speed w / sin(angle(e, g)); between two zero-weight edges it is stationary; a split event against a zero-weight edge happens on the gable line itself. Collinear neighbours with different weights: insert a zero-weight wavefront edge perpendicular to them at the shared vertex (the treatment of Kelly and Wonka), which yields a vertical step face. Randomised input: star-shaped polygons from sorted random angles and radii, orthogonal polygons from random grid walks; the generator is a seeded SplitMix64 in the test support module (no new dependency, like the seeded xorshift of element-kind-framework-10's property test); a failing case prints its seed and ring so it can be added to the corpus. Determinism: ties ordered by edge indices so repeated runs give bit-identical output. Pitfalls: events slightly more than MODEL_TOLERANCE apart create tiny arcs; reject them only when they would form sliver faces below the EDT-019 thresholds; guard the event loop by 10 n² events so a bug can never hang the UI.
acceptance_criteria:
- Gable fixture: rectangle 12 × 9 with both 9 m edges gable and both 12 m edges at 35°: two sloped faces meeting in a ridge along y = 4.5 over the full length x = 0..12 at 3.1509 m and two vertical gable faces with zero plan area; one gable plus three sloped edges gives a ridge from the gable edge to a hip apex.
- The equal-wing L with its two opposite end edges (x = 12 and y = 12) set to gable: the ridges run to the gable edges and the gable faces lie in the vertical planes of those edges (ROF-003 acceptance, second clause).
- The degenerate corpus passes the roofs-03 invariants: plus-shaped cross (reflex vertices meeting in pairs), H shape, a rectangle with two symmetric notches (several splits at one point), collinear edges with equal pitch (one merged face) and with 30°/45° pitches (vertical step face), neighbours within 0.1° of parallel and edges of 1 mm.
- Randomised test with a fixed seed: 2,000 star-shaped and orthogonal polygons of 3-40 vertices satisfying the EDT-019 thresholds, pitches 10°-70°, 10 % gable edges; every case returns Ok with all invariants or Err with a message; zero panics (catch_unwind), zero invalid outputs, error rate <= 1 %, runtime < 10 s in the dev profile.
- A 100-edge orthogonal footprint is resolved in < 5 ms in release (timed test skipped in debug builds).
- ROF-003 plan-level clauses complete (non-convex footprints, mixed pitches, gables).
notes: SRS: ROF-003. Related: NFR-REL-005. Appendix D.1: edges shorter than 0.1 mm and sliver angles below 0.1° are repaired or reported (EDT-019). Open question (O-9): collinear edges with different pitches yield a vertical step face; confirm with users.

title: Three-OS acceptance, usability test, German translation, legal and security checks
description:
Verify the Must NFRs that are release properties: release builds for Windows 11, macOS (current and previous) and Ubuntu LTS with published minimum and reference hardware, .ifcx registration with consent at first start, the licence inventory gate, native-crash reports through a minidump handler (needed since the C++ kernel arrived), the usability test protocol and execution (NFR-USE-001, AS-08) with a five-day buffer for findings filed as beads, the interaction-consistency review, and the German translation.

Risks: Usability findings may require late UI changes: five days reserved and findings filed as beads. Participant recruitment for AS-08. Native crash handlers vary per OS: Rust panic reports stay the baseline, minidump is best effort.
design: A CI release workflow (no installer, decision D-12), per-OS file-association code (HKCU ProgId, CFBundleDocumentTypes, xdg-mime) behind a consent dialog, a minidump handler (minidumper/crash-handler, permissive) next to persistence/crash.rs, docs/usability/protocol.md, deny.toml advisories, docs/release.md checklist including the manual hosted-viewer check.
acceptance_criteria: CI produces release builds for the three operating systems and the release notes name minimum and reference hardware (NFR-PORT-006); scripted manual tests for AS-01..AS-05 exist under docs/test-plan/ and their automated parts run on all three OSes; the first start asks for consent and registers .ifcx (per-OS integration test); cargo deny check advisories licenses sources bans passes, THIRD-PARTY.md is generated and the schema-file licence is resolved; a simulated native crash leaves a minidump-based report whose path is shown at the next start and a network monitor shows no traffic except the consent-gated import fetch; AS-08: at least 4 of 5 participants complete the NFR-USE-001 task following docs/usability/protocol.md; the interaction-model checklist passes for every tool; the German catalogue has every key and switches the whole UI (kittest).
notes:
SRS: NFR-PORT-001 NFR-PORT-002 NFR-PORT-003 NFR-PORT-006 SW-001 NFR-LEG-001 NFR-SEC-002 NFR-USE-001 NFR-USE-002 NFR-L10N-002
Dependencies not guaranteed by the epic graph: regression-and-status (docs/test-plan/release-checklist.md, crash_recovery.rs and docs/test-plan/as-05.md, conformance-matrix.yml, README 'System requirements', the HTTP-crate ban) and ifcx-interop (the consent-gated import fetch) are not ancestors of release-candidate; tasks 03, 07, 09 and 17 check them with bd show before starting and fall back as their descriptions say. Recommendation for the epic graph: add regression-and-status and ifcx-interop to the epic's depends_on. free-form-solids, railings-stairs-adv and curtain-walls are not ancestors either; task 10 reviews their tools only if they are merged.
macOS majors: NFR-PORT-002 means the current and the previous major at release time (expected macOS 27 and 26 in late 2026); release.yml holds them as MACOS_CURRENT, MACOS_PREVIOUS and MACOS_MIN (02, 03, 17).
Size: the reviewed task estimates sum to about 31 engineer-days against the roadmap's 12 (see release-candidate-done).

title: Drag roof pivot lines, edges and nodes with live regeneration
description:
WHY: ROF-008 (M): pitch, pivot elevation, overhangs, edge types and the outline shall be editable by direct manipulation (dragging the pivot line, edges and nodes), and the roof shall regenerate immediately (NFR-PERF-006: after a single-element edit in RM-M, plan and 3D views are updated within 200 ms, including the openings of affected neighbours). EDT-008 and EDT-009 provide the palette and handle stretching for every polygon-based kind (NFR-USE-002), and NFR-REL-005 forbids committing invalid geometry. The epic acceptance requires that dragging the pivot line regenerates within 200 ms on the stand-in. Gap row ROF-008: no drag-handle editing existed for any element (now provided by edit-reshape-palette) and full re-evaluation had to stay within 200 ms.

WHAT: Register roof parts in tools/handles.rs (edit-reshape-palette-07) through the kind's part list: for single-plane roofs the pivot line (body handle: move parallel; end handles: rotate and stretch) plus the outline nodes and edges, for multi-plane roofs the pivot-polygon nodes and edges (move node, offset edge keeping the edge's parameters) and the eaves lines (RoofPart::Eaves of roofs-01: dragging perpendicular to the edge sets that edge's overhang with UpdateElements, so overhangs are directly manipulable). Palette entries for roofs in tools/palette.rs: Move pivot line, Rotate pivot line, Flip slope side, Make gable or Make sloped, Set pitch (focuses the field of roofs-08), next to the generic outline commands. During a drag the candidate roof (the Reshape operation applied to a clone) is evaluated with evaluate_element on every pointer move and drawn as an overlay in plan and as a transient mesh in 3D; release commits one command; an invalid candidate (validation or SkeletonError) keeps the last valid preview, shows the reason in the status line and commits nothing on release. Add the performance test. Out of scope: hosted elements in the timed scenario (re-run with an opening and a roof window in the done task).
design: Roofs address their rings through the shared PartRef::Node/Edge, so the generic handles, Command::Reshape operations and palette entries apply unchanged (NFR-USE-002); RoofPart::PivotLine and PivotLineEnd (roofs-01) add the roof-specific handles via part_anchor and part_outline. The drag runs on the ReshapeTool consumer of edit-reshape-palette-07, so snapping, typed distances and the Esc ladder behave as everywhere (INP-001). Preview: `archicraft_geometry::evaluate_element` on a cloned element, never on the document; the 3D overlay is a transient mesh keyed by a preview counter, not by the document revision, so autosave and undo are untouched; at most one evaluation per frame. Commit: Command::Reshape for ring operations and UpdateElements for pivot-line operations. Timing uses std::time::Instant around execute, incremental evaluation, plan regeneration of the storey and build_scene (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs) and relies on element-kind-framework's evaluate_incremental and per-storey plan caches. Pitfalls: hit precedence node > pivot line end > pivot line > eaves line > edge, so a pivot line lying on an outline edge stays reachable, with Tab cycling overlapping handles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reshape command tests: moving the single-plane pivot line 0.50 m perpendicular changes the plane height over the outline by 0.50 · tan(pitch) and undoes exactly; moving a pivot-polygon node of the unequal-wing L keeps every edge's data on the right edge; Offset edge keeps the edge's pitch and type.
- kittest: clicking a selected roof's pivot line opens the palette with the roof entries; dragging a pivot-polygon node updates the preview before release and creates exactly one undo step on release; Make gable turns the edge vertical.
- Dragging the eaves handle of an edge with a 0.50 m overhang outwards by 0.30 m (or typing 0.30) sets the overhang to 0.80 m in one undo step; dragging it inside the pivot edge is refused with the negative-overhang validation message.
- Failure path: dragging a node so that the polygon self-intersects shows the validation message, keeps the last valid preview and leaves the project unchanged on release.
- Performance test (release only, skipped in debug builds): in the 5,000-element stand-in of element-kind-framework with an added multi-plane roof, a pivot-line move re-evaluates incrementally (dirty set = the roof and its hosted elements) and regenerates the storey plan and the 3D scene within 200 ms; one preview evaluation takes < 50 ms.
- Satisfies the direct-manipulation clauses of ROF-008 and NFR-PERF-006 for roof edits.
notes: SRS: ROF-008. Related: NFR-PERF-006, NFR-REL-005, EDT-008, EDT-009, NFR-USE-002. Stand-in: the 5,000-element synthetic model of element-kind-framework (RM-M size).

title: Add the roof-window kind with a roof-plane insert and its void
description:
WHY: DW-021 (S): roof windows shall be placeable in roofs, with the same host rules as DW-001: they exist only in a host, take their storey association from it, move with it and are deleted with it, and without a valid host under the pointer the tool gives clear feedback and creates nothing (the tool clause is roofs-14). ROF-012 (M) delegates roof windows to DW-021, and Table 5-1 gives IfcWindow the parent 'host wall or roof' with Void and parts. The epic acceptance requires a roof window hosted in a plane that cuts it with a Void. Gap row DW-021: missing; needs roofs plus a sloped-host placement variant of DW-001. Existing by then (keep and reuse, do not re-implement): WallInsert, the InsertFrame resolver and the Door(WallInsert)/Window(WallInsert) kinds of doors-windows-core-01 (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/insert.rs, kinds/window.rs), the DW-001 host-rule checks and cascades (doors-windows-core-02, host-openings-02), the built-in catalogue and the shared unit kit (components-dw-catalogue-03 to -05).

WHAT: Model: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/insert.rs gains `RoofInsert { host, instance: ComponentInstance, plane: PlaneRef, u, v, anchor: Anchor, width, height }` (u along the pivot edge, v up the slope, anchor semantics as WallInsert) and InsertFrame::resolve a roof branch that derives unit_to_storey from the plane frame with the exterior on the roof top; a new kind module crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/roof_window.rs registers `RoofWindow(RoofInsert)` with one kinds! line (label 'Roof window', code 'roofWindow', name prefix 'RW', default class IfcWindow, class set [IfcWindow, IfcOpeningElement], hosted: true, Kind::host(), HostCapability: roof-plane placements on roofs only, a normalising validator with element.storey := host storey, translate sliding within the plane and carry unchanged, a template_defaults slot with the roof-window definition at 0.78 × 1.18 m on the window slot's layer). Catalogue: crates/archicraft-model/src/components/catalogue.rs gains the definition window.roof (category window, class IfcWindow, frame, sash and glazing parameters from the window kit, flagged for roof hosts; the flag defaults to Wall so every existing definition is unchanged) and 'window.roof@1' in KNOWN_GENERATORS, with its generator in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/ next to the window generators of components-dw-catalogue-05 (frame ring, sash and glazing from kit.rs). Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/roof_window.rs places the unit parts by the plane frame and hands the roof generator a rectangle void in plane coordinates through all skins, cut through the roofs-11 hole path (no new cutting code); the Void part as for wall inserts. A stub codec crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/roof_window.rs keeps the registry complete until roofs-14. Out of scope: the tool, properties and IFCX (14), flashings and accessories (Section 8 excludes roof accessory generators), dormers.
design: A separate kind instead of a second variant inside Window(WallInsert): the window payload, its codec, the doors-windows-core goldens and journal replay stay untouched, the roof window gets its own DefaultsSlot size and name prefix, and HostCapability states the host kind per kind; the DW-001 host-rule checks live once in insert.rs, parameterised by host kind, so both kinds share them. RoofInsert reuses WallInsert's anchor and size semantics: the DW-005 horizontal anchor runs along u and the vertical position is the distance up the slope along v instead of a sill height. The void goes through the roofs-11 hole path, so there is no new cutting code; parts are placed by the plane frame as doors-windows-core-04 places them by the host wall frame. The exterior side is always the roof top (DW-003 reversal is not offered for roof windows). Pitfalls: a window crossing the plane boundary is reported rather than clipped; the roof-window kind must not appear in wall host candidates (HostCapability filter); keep the definition's host flag out of the existing window files so their goldens stay byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry: a 0.78 × 1.18 m roof window in a 35° plane of the AS-01 roof cuts a void of that size perpendicular to the plane through every skin; its frame parts lie in the plane; all bodies are closed; window.roof@1 generates closed parts at Detailed and Simplified detail.
- Commands: the window moves with its roof (a pivot-elevation change and a pitch change keep it on the plane at the same (u, v)), is deleted with it and restored by undo, and takes the roof's home storey; a RoofWindow whose host is a wall, a slab or missing is rejected with a message (DW-001 host rules).
- Registry: KINDS lists roofWindow; every KindTag has a geometry generator and a codec entry; the module-layout and registry-completeness tests pass; the existing window definitions and goldens are unchanged.
- Satisfies the model and geometry clauses of DW-021 and the roof-window clause of ROF-012.
notes: SRS: DW-021 ROF-012. Related: DW-001, DW-003, DW-005, IFX-036. Dependency note: needs the insert kinds and WallInsert of doors-windows-core and the catalogue of components-dw-catalogue (increment 1, scheduled before this increment-2 epic but not declared prerequisites of roofs, and this fragment may only reference the five prerequisite epics): if doors-windows-core is not closed when this task starts, add a blocks edge roofs-12 -> doors-windows-core-done. Assumption: default roof-window size 0.78 × 1.18 m (Appendix D.2 has no roof-window default).

title: Commit the RM-S golden file and feed every fixture to conformance
description:
WHY: NFR-MNT-003 (M): 'The test suite shall contain golden-file tests for IFCX export of the reference models, plus automated conformance tests against the buildingSMART reference implementation (IFX-006). These tests run on every change.' IFX-006 says item (a) and the spatial tree of (b) 'are verified by automated tests on the reference models of Section 7.3'. The epic acceptance asks that 'cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx reproduces RM-S byte for byte from the builder (seeded ids) and the conformance job runs on RM-S, the AS-02 frame and every registered fixture'. The epic risk is golden churn when writers change: 'bless only with a reviewed diff'. A multi-megabyte compact golden is unreadable in a plain diff. SRS 7.3 also uses RM-S for minimum-hardware performance, and NFR-MNT-003's 'run on every change' means the RM-S tests run in the per-push jobs, not behind #[ignore].

WHAT:
- Register ("rm-s", samples::rm_s) in samples::catalogue(). reference_models.rs then writes rm-s.ifcx, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/rm-s.ifcx is blessed once, and catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files, golden_files_are_reproduced, round_trip_restores_the_editable_model, regenerated_geometry_matches_the_stored_geometry and container_matches_the_ifcx_json_schema cover it through the catalogue.
- Extend crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs to also write every built entry of fixtures::all() (crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs) that is not already a catalogue sample as fixture-<id>.ifcx into the same directory, plus a manifest.txt listing every file it wrote (with the --indented variant of regression-and-status-05, the indented files too). conformance/run.sh fails when a manifest entry has no PASS line, so a missing file is caught as well as a failing one. The existing CI glob target/reference-models/*.ifcx picks the files up, so .github/workflows/ci.yml changes only if the manifest is passed explicitly.
- Reviewable golden diffs: add rm-s to the review-view snapshots of regression-and-status-04 (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/snapshots/: indented JSON with mesh and curve arrays replaced by their count and an FNV-1a hash), so a writer change shows as a readable hunk next to the blessed compact golden. If that task has not landed, add the same review-view snapshot for rm-s here; do not build a second diff tool. docs/testing.md's bless workflow says to review that hunk in the pull request.
- Append rm_s to samples::bench_models(), the bench-model list of the regression-and-status-16 harness (open, save, evaluate, slice). If the harness has not landed, file a bead for it under regression-and-status.
Out of scope: the AS-01 assertions in check.ts (05), the AS-03 file (06) and fixture goldens (fixtures without a catalogue entry are checked for conformance, not blessed).
design:
Approach: the catalogue of element-kind-framework-03 is the single list for the example and roundtrip.rs, so adding RM-S is one line plus the blessed file. Bless with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 and review the review-view snapshot hunk, not the raw compact JSON. Keep goldens compact. The indented option (IFX-008, regression-and-status-05) is for human inspection only.

Cross-platform byte identity is the main pitfall. Parameters are written at full precision and mesh coordinates are rounded to 1e-6 m (IFX-007, json.rs round_coordinate). Rounding can still flip at a boundary when a transcendental function (sin, cos, atan2 for roof pitches or stair angles) differs by one ulp between platform libms. Mitigation, in order:
1. find the element through rm_s_fingerprint (tasks 01, 02, 10);
2. route the geometry crate's transcendental calls through the pure-Rust libm crate (MIT/Apache, allowed by deny.toml);
3. as a last resort, exact rational construction of the offending input.
Do not relax the byte comparison.

Manifest: the example writes a plain list. run.sh reads it when present and compares it with the PASS lines of check.mjs. Without a manifest, run.sh keeps today's behaviour.

Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:30-32 (samples), :198-232 (golden test), examples/reference_models.rs:24-35, conformance/run.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-69, fixtures::all() (regression-and-status-02), the review view of regression-and-status-04, bench_models() of regression-and-status-16, the 'Add a sample/golden model' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx: catalogue_samples_reproduce_the_golden_files reproduces tests/golden/rm-s.ifcx byte for byte from samples::rm_s() on the ubuntu, windows and macos CI runners. golden_files_are_reproduced (load then save) passes on it.
- The rm-s golden loads without problems, round-trips equal to rm_s() (with revision and data_version normalised), regenerated geometry equals the stored geometry, and the container JSON-schema check passes.
- 'Run on every change': no rm-s test is #[ignore]d; they run in the per-push test job on all three runners, and their dev-profile duration is recorded in the test module doc.
- Two runs of `cargo run -p archicraft-ifcx --example reference_models -- <dir>` produce identical bytes for every file, manifest included.
- conformance/run.sh is green on rm-s.ifcx, structural-frame.ifcx and every fixture-*.ifcx. The CI conformance log shows one PASS line per manifest entry. Removing a fixture file from the directory makes run.sh fail with a message naming it.
- The rm-s review-view snapshot is committed. On an unchanged workspace insta reports no change; a deliberate change (for example renaming a material in a scratch copy) shows a hunk naming the node path and the attribute key.
