- The golden size is recorded in the test module doc. The file is written compact (IFX-008 default) and stays below 10 MB.
- samples::bench_models() lists rm_s and the harness benches it, or a bead for the missing harness exists.
- Satisfies NFR-MNT-003 for RM-S (golden file of the reference model plus conformance on every change) and the automated IFX-006 (a) and tree check on the Section 7.3 model RM-S.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003. Also IFX-006, IFX-007, IFX-008, SRS 7.3. If the libm switch is needed, record it in docs/technology-choices.md (testing and geometry rows) and in the licence inventory (NFR-LEG-001).

title: Persist roofs in IFCX and write IfcRoof with one IfcSlab per plane
description:
WHY: Table 5-1 maps a single-plane roof to IfcRoof with Body or skin parts and a multi-plane roof to IfcRoof with one IfcSlab child per roof plane. IFX-016 (M): parts of compound elements, including the planes of a multi-plane roof, shall be child nodes of the compound element with their own IFC class; element-kind-framework built the mechanism on a test-only kind and roofs re-assert it with a real element. IFX-017 (skin parts), IFX-024 (the ROOF predefined type stored in the archicraft namespace), IFX-022 (IsExternal; done for every element with a known position at crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:399-402, kept and regressed for roofs) and IFX-033 (exported geometry is the evaluated result) apply. The parameters of ROF-001, ROF-003, ROF-005, ROF-006 and ROF-007 must survive save and open so the roof stays parametric (AS-03). Gap row ROF-001 lists the missing archicraft::roof attribute, schema and reader.

WHAT: Replace the placeholder codec of roofs-01 with a RoofCodec implementing element-kind-framework-06's KindCodec in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/roof.rs (one line in codecs!; schema.rs, writer.rs and reader.rs dispatch through the registry): an `archicraft::roof` object with shape code, pivotElevation, structure (the layer-structures structure schema), reference code, a single object (outline rings with a parallel `edges` array of cut objects, pivotLine, slopeSide, pitch) and a multi object (pivotPolygon rings with per-edge type, pitch, overhang, cut and cutAngle; levels with height and pitch). Writer: single-plane roofs as IfcRoof with Body or Skin_n; multi-plane roofs as IfcRoof whose Plane_<k> parts are written by the part writer of element-kind-framework-07 as IfcSlab nodes with their own Body or Skin_n children; the ROOF predefined type reaches them through a new `predefined: Option<PredefinedType>` on the model's PartSpec (PredefinedType of element-kind-framework-05, set to ROOF by roofs-01's parts()), written as an `archicraft::part` attribute declared only when used (IFX-024); IsExternal from the element position as today. Reader: restore the roof, defaults with warnings for missing values; parts are not re-read. Add `samples::roof_showcase()` to crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs through the seeded fixture builder (a layered single-plane shed roof with a square eaves cut, the unequal-wing L hip roof with mixed pitches, the 12 × 9 gable roof), add it as one line to samples::catalogue() (element-kind-framework-03), which feeds samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs and crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs, and bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/roofs.ifcx. Bump FORMAT_VERSION (schema.rs:15) with a no-op entry in the migration table of crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs ('adds roof elements'), per the framework's bump rule as host-openings-08 does for openings. Remove the 'roof parameters not saved yet' warning of roofs-01. Out of scope: hosted openings and roof windows (11 and 12 extend the golden), the mansard (09).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md (Extension points) through the framework's codec registry; enums derive their schema options from the model's ALL arrays (.map(T::code)); parameters are written at full precision and only mesh coordinates are rounded (round_coordinate). Reuse the Outline codec of edit-reshape-palette (ring arrays with a parallel per-edge array as introduced for slab edge angles in edit-reshape-palette-10). Part names '<roof name> Plane <k>' follow the framework's part-naming decision. The predefined type of a part is a model decision like its class, so it lives on PartSpec (default None, so the compound-parts golden of element-kind-framework-07 stays bit-identical), never on PartGeometry; the archicraft::part declaration is content-derived (element-kind-framework-06) and a standard attribute follows once the registry has one (O-6). Pitfalls: goldens use the fixed author and timestamp of the existing goldens and seeded ids; per-plane ids must be identical across save cycles (deterministic roles); keep bodies inside MAX_MESH_POINTS.
acceptance_criteria:
- round_trip_restores_the_editable_model covers roof_showcase (identical Project including per-edge data, levels, structure and reference surface) with zero problems; regenerated_geometry_matches_the_stored_geometry stays byte-identical over save, load and save.
- spatial_tree_and_identities: the multi-plane roof is a storey child classed IfcRoof with children Plane_1..Plane_n whose ids equal Uuid::new_v5(roof, b"Plane_k"), each classed IfcSlab with a Name, the ROOF predefined type in archicraft:: and mesh children inheriting their materials; the single-plane roof has Body or Skin_n children directly; plane parts are not read back as elements and cause no warning.
- The generic IFX-033 test of junction-engine-08 (it iterates samples::catalogue()) and written_meshes_are_closed_bodies cover roof parts.
- Exterior roofs carry bsi::ifc::prop::IsExternal true (IFX-022 regression); the layered roof references its layer structure in the layer-structures-08 schema and round-trips it; FORMAT_VERSION is bumped with a no-op migration entry and the migration tests of element-kind-framework-12 stay green.
- Golden roofs.ifcx is reproduced byte for byte and conformance/run.sh is green on it (check.ts finds the bodies under parts and a class on every part): IFX-016 re-asserted with a real compound element.
- Reader leniency: a roof without pitch reads the D.2 default with a warning; an unknown shape code skips the element with a problem and no panic.
- Persistence clauses of ROF-001, ROF-003, ROF-005, ROF-006 and ROF-007 satisfied.
notes: SRS: ROF-001 ROF-003 ROF-005 ROF-006 ROF-007. Related: IFX-016, IFX-017, IFX-022 (done, writer.rs:399-402), IFX-024, IFX-033, AS-03. Table 5-1 rows 'Roof, single plane' and 'Roof, multi-plane'. Open question: hosted elements of a multi-plane roof are written as children of the IfcRoof node with the plane recorded in archicraft:: (decided in roofs-11).

title: Regenerate the implementation status for the increment-2 exit
design:
Approach: regenerate, do not hand-edit tables. The table comes from docs/status/requirements.json, maintained with the status script; the narrative sections are rewritten by hand from verified facts. Use the status vocabulary (done/partial/missing, remaining_effort, depends_on), and name the deferring epic for every clause left open.

The test-name check is a few lines in status.py: for every evidence token of the form 'fn_name (path)', grep 'fn fn_name' in that file. Run it as part of `check`, which the per-merge status job already runs.

Pointers: docs/implementation-status.md sections 'Readiness per Appendix F increment', 'Acceptance scenarios', 'Technical debt'; regression-and-status-19 (docs/status/requirements.json, scripts/status.py generate/check/merge-check, scripts/tests/test_status.py).
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/implementation-status.md is regenerated, and its counts are consistent: the requirement table holds the 567 live IDs, and the per-status and per-priority counts equal the table.
- With regression-and-status-19: `python3 scripts/status.py check` passes: the document is in sync with docs/status/requirements.json, every live ID has one row, and no cited evidence path or test name is dangling. A unit test in scripts/tests/test_status.py covers the test-name check if this task added it.
- With regression-and-status-19: `python3 scripts/status.py merge-check` passes for this epic's srs_ids (NFR-MNT-003, NFR-USE-006) in the epic's final pull request.
- The increment-2 readiness row states whether 'AS-01 without railings and AS-02 pass' is met, citing the tests and documents that prove it. AS-01, AS-02 and AS-03 rows carry the new evidence.
- NFR-MNT-003 row: golden plus conformance for RM-S and the AS-02 frame on every change, as status and evidence. RM-M and RM-L goldens are named as the remaining gap with owner perf-tuning-rm-m-l.
- NFR-USE-006 row: the test and the recorded demonstration as evidence, with the railing clause named as remaining for railings-stairs-adv.
- The reference-models and D.7 lines list RM-S and every registered fixture (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7, F9, and F8 if curved-geometry has closed) as present, and the remaining fixtures with their owners.
- Without regression-and-status-19: the rows and counts are edited by hand consistently and a bead for the per-merge check exists.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003 NFR-USE-006. Also Appendix F increment 2. Decide in review whether NFR-MNT-003 can be 'done' before RM-M/RM-L exist. SRS 7.3 lists all three reference models as golden sources, so 'partial' with an owner is the honest default.

title: Add the roof tool: pivot line, slope side, outline and wall outline
description:
WHY: ROF-002 (M): a single-plane roof shall be input by drawing the pivot line, indicating the slope side, and drawing the outline as a rectangle, rotated rectangle or polygon; the outline may extend beyond the pivot line on either side. ROF-004 (M): the pivot polygon of a multi-plane roof shall be creatable by drawing it, by picking an existing closed polygon, or from the outline of selected walls; when created from walls, the pivot elevation defaults to the top of those walls. ROF-001 (M) requires the pitch to be entered as angle, percent or rise/run; INP-001 routes every point through the point-input service and Appendix D.8 gives each element tool, roof included, a default shortcut. The epic acceptance generates the AS-01 gable roof from the selected exterior walls with the pivot at the wall top. Gap rows: ROF-002 missing (the tool framework and outline modes exist as a pattern, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13-16 and :69-71; actions.rs:18-20 has no roof action); ROF-004 missing (reusable: unary_union of footprints at crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:156, wall selection at workspace.rs:54).

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/roof.rs, a RoofTool implementing the InputConsumer of point-input-snapping with `RoofMethod::{SinglePlane, MultiPlane}` and `RoofMode::{Polygon, Rectangle, RotatedRectangle}`. Single plane: pivot line start, pivot line end, slope-side click, then the outline per mode. Multi-plane: the pivot polygon per mode, or a contour-detection pick with the detection key of edit-reshape-palette-12 (a click on an edge takes the closed chain from ContourGraph::chain_at, a click inside takes the outer ring of region_at). Both commit Command::AddElements with the factories of roofs-01 and the tool defaults. Add crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/from_walls.rs: `pivot_polygon_from_walls(project, geometry, walls) -> Result<WallRing { storey, ring, top }, RoofInputError>` (WallRing, not WallOutline, which junction-engine-04 already uses) built from the junction engine's resolved outlines (ResolvedWall.outline of junction::resolve in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs, junction-engine-04, on the JunctionGraph that junction-engine-13 keeps in ModelGeometry) and the 'Roof from selected walls' action (Design menu and a tool mode button) that creates the roof on the walls' storey in one command. Add ToolKind::Roof with its ToolKind-to-KindTag mapping in gather() (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:55), Action::ToolRoof with a provisional free single-key shortcut and its run() arm in app.rs, appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts (actions.rs:187) extended by the roof tool, the toolbox button and Design-menu item (ui/shell.rs), the roof tool defaults in the properties strip (method, mode, pitch through a new widgets::slope, structure, pivot elevation, reference surface, overhang, eaves cut) through the Fields pattern, and the select_all mapping. Out of scope: per-edge editing after creation (08), handles (10), hosted elements (11, 12).
design: One InputConsumer with a method switch, like the slab tool's modes (tools/slab.rs after point-input-snapping-01); the slope-side step uses Expect::Point and takes the side from the sign of cross(pivot direction, p − pivot start), refusing points within the snap radius of the line. The single-plane outline's first point defaults to the pivot start. Pivot elevation default: the home storey height for drawn roofs (where D.2 walls end), the walls' top for wall-derived roofs (ROF-004), converted through storey elevations when the walls' top is linked to another storey. from_walls: union the junction engine's resolved per-wall footprints (all skins) of the selected walls with geo::unary_union, take the polygon with an interior ring (an enclosed area) and the largest area, use its exterior ring (the exterior faces) normalised counter-clockwise, and remove collinear vertices within MODEL_TOLERANCE so each wall side becomes one pivot edge. The contour pick reuses the cached ContourGraph of edit-reshape-palette-12. widgets::slope wraps parse_slope/format_slope like widgets::angle (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/widgets.rs:80). Follow the 'Add a drawing tool' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md. Pitfalls: the home storey of a wall-derived roof is the walls' storey, not the active one; a selection mixing storeys is refused with a message; the multi-plane preview uses the roofs-05 regions (outline plus hips) without building bodies every frame.
acceptance_criteria:
- State-machine tests in tools/roof.rs without egui: pivot line (0,0)-(10,0), slope-side click at (5,3) and a rectangle outline (−0.5,−0.5)-(10.5,6) create a roof rising towards +y; rotated-rectangle and polygon outlines and typed values work; an outline extending beyond the pivot line is accepted; a slope-side click on the pivot line is refused with a prompt; Esc cancels one step and Backspace removes one point (INP-003).
- Multi-plane polygon and rectangle modes create roofs with the D.2 edge defaults; on two_storey_shell a contour pick on the exterior face line of the ground-floor walls yields the 12 × 9 ring, a pick inside a room yields the room's ring, and an open chain is refused with 'Pick a closed polygon'.
- from_walls tests: the four upper-storey exterior walls of two_storey_shell give the ring (0,0),(12,0),(12,9),(0,9) within MODEL_TOLERANCE and top = 3.00 m above the upper storey; walls that enclose no area return RoofInputError with a message; walls with different tops use the highest and say so in the status line.
- AS-01 roof test in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: select the upper exterior walls, run 'Roof from selected walls', set the two 9 m edges to Gable with UpdateElements; the evaluated roof has two plane children, the reference ridge along y = 4.5 at storey-local 6.1509 m and the eaves at 2.6499 m, with the pivot at the wall top (3.00 m).
- kittest: the toolbox button and the Design-menu item select the roof tool; the strip shows Pitch '35.00°' and, with the project slope format Percent, '70.02 %'; typing '70%' or '7:10' stores 34.99° (angle, percent and rise/run input of ROF-001); shortcuts_are_unique and appendix_d8_commands_have_shortcuts pass.
- Satisfies ROF-002, ROF-004 and the pitch-input clause of ROF-001.
notes: SRS: ROF-001 ROF-002 ROF-004. Related: INP-001, INP-003, INP-018, NFR-L10N-003. Appendix D.2: pivot elevation at the top of the walls; D.8: the roof tool has a default shortcut (binding provisional until commands-and-l10n). AS-01 uses two_storey_shell dimensions: 12 × 9 m exterior faces, reference line on the exterior face (D.2).

title: Build multi-plane roof bodies with overhangs, gables and skins
description:
WHY: ROF-003 (M) requires the planes of a multi-plane roof to meet without gaps or overlaps (within 0.1 mm) and gable edges to give vertical gable ends; ROF-006 (M) applies the selected eaves cut to every eaves edge, ROF-007 (M) measures the layer structure perpendicular to each plane, and ROF-011 (S) needs the ridge elevation, the eaves elevation and the plan and sloped area of each plane (MEA-003 lists the same values for roofs). Table 5-1 maps a multi-plane roof to IfcRoof with one IfcSlab child per plane (IFX-016), so geometry has to deliver one part per plane. NFR-REL-005 and the epic risk require that a roof whose skeleton fails keeps its last valid geometry and is reported.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/regions.rs (per-plane plan regions: the skeleton face of each sloped edge extended outward to its eaves line, which is the pivot edge offset by its overhang, and bounded by the outward extensions of the corner arcs; gable edges add a verge strip of their overhang to the neighbouring planes) and complete roof/body.rs for multi-plane roofs with the roofs-02 builder: side planes are the bisector planes of the two reference planes at hips, valleys and ridges, the eaves cut plane at eaves edges and vertical planes at gable verges, skins perpendicular as in 02. The roof's GeometryKind (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/roof.rs) returns `ElementGeometry.children` with one `PartGeometry { role: 'Plane_<k>', parts: Body or Skin_n, axis: empty }` per plane (element-kind-framework-15), whose roles equal the roof's Kind::parts() of roofs-01; the IfcSlab class comes from the model's PartSpec, not from geometry. Add roof/metrics.rs for single- and multi-plane roofs (a single-plane roof has one plane): `metrics(project, element) -> Result<RoofMetrics { ridge_elevation, eaves_elevation, planes: Vec<PlaneMetrics { role, pitch, plan_area, sloped_area }> }>`. Fallback: a SkeletonError or body error records a GeometryProblem { message, fallback } (element-kind-framework-13) whose fallback is the element's previous Arc<ElementGeometry> from evaluate_incremental's cache, so the last valid roof stays visible and pickable; a roof that never evaluated gets the framework's fallback box from Kind::plan_bounds(). Add the body-level randomised test crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/roof_bodies_random.rs on the generators of roofs-04. Out of scope: break levels (09), hole rings for openings (11), IFCX (06), UI (07, 08).
design: Regions: for each pivot corner c between edges a and b, the separation line is the skeleton's corner arc extended backwards from c (the line where the planes of a and b intersect); plane a's overhang strip is the band between pivot edge a and its eaves line a', restricted to a's side of the separation lines at both ends. At convex corners this extends the strips to the separation line, at reflex corners it clips them, with one formula. When a and b have different eaves heights, the separation line meets a' and b' at different points and the outline jogs along it; document that convention in the module. Gable edge g with overhang o_g: the neighbouring planes gain the strip between g and its offset line and get a vertical verge side plane there. Assemble each region by walking face-ring and strip vertices with shared DVec2 values instead of a polygon Boolean, so neighbouring regions share exact vertices. Side planes: one bisector plane per arc, computed once and used by both bodies (with equal perpendicular offsets the top and bottom intersection lines both lie in it), which gives identical vertices on both sides. Plane roles: 'Plane_<pivot edge index + 1>' (break levels add '_L<k>' in roofs-09); stable while the pivot polygon topology is unchanged (IFX-010 regenerated part ids), renumbered by node insertion, which is acceptable for regenerated parts. Metrics: plan area of the reference-surface region, sloped area = plan area / cos(pitch), elevations from the body vertices plus the storey elevation (StoreyList). Fallback: the framework's evaluate_incremental keeps a per-element Arc<ElementGeometry>; on error keep the old Arc as the fallback of the GeometryProblem in ModelGeometry.problems (evaluate.rs:57-58 today, GeometryProblem after element-kind-framework-13). Pitfalls: zero-length arcs at 4-way nodes make consecutive side planes coincide, so drop them before body construction; steep pitches with thick structures fold the offset surfaces near acute apexes, so validate the face rings and report per roof; plan classification is generic (plan.rs:111, mesh.rs:196 up_facing_outline) because each plane is its own part.
acceptance_criteria:
- On every corpus footprint of roofs-03/04 with a 0.30 m Thickness and with a three-skin structure: every plane body and skin is closed and outward; for every hip, valley and ridge the two neighbouring bodies' side faces have the same vertices within 0.1 mm (ROF-003: no gaps or overlaps); the reference-surface plan regions sum to the eaves polygon area within 1e-9 relative.
- Body-level randomised test (fixed seed, 300 footprints from the roofs-04 generators, pitches 10°-70°, 10 % gable edges, 0.30 m Thickness): every case yields closed, outward bodies for every plane or exactly one GeometryProblem with a message; zero panics and zero open meshes (epic acceptance: closed output or a reported problem).
- The registry test of element-kind-framework-15 holds for roofs: the roles of ElementGeometry.children equal Kind::parts() for every corpus roof.
- AS-01-type gable roof: pivot polygon 12 × 9, the 9 m edges gable with 0.50 m verges, the 12 m edges at 35° with 0.50 m overhang, 0.30 m Thickness, reference Bottom, pivot elevation 3.00 m: two plane children; reference-surface eaves lines at y = −0.5 and 9.5 at z = 2.6499, reference ridge along y = 4.5 at z = 6.1509, top-surface ridge 0.3662 higher, vertical verges at x = −0.5 and 12.5.
- 12 × 9 hip roof at 35° with 0.50 m overhang: metrics give four planes whose plan areas sum to 130.00 m² and sloped areas to 158.70 m²; ridge elevation = highest body point, eaves elevation = lowest body point on the eaves edges, both storey-local and absolute; the 6 × 4 m single-plane roof of roofs-02 at 30° gives one plane with plan area 24.00 m² and sloped area 27.71 m².
- Overhangs of 0.50 m and 0.80 m meeting at a corner with equal pitch produce the documented outline jog along the extended hip and closed bodies; the four eaves-cut variants on a hip-roof eaves edge give the end faces specified in roofs-02.
- Fallback: an evaluation whose skeleton is forced to fail (test-only fault injection behind cfg(test)) keeps the previous geometry and lists exactly one problem ('the roof planes could not be computed at (x, y) ...; the last valid roof is shown'); without previous geometry the fallback box appears and the roof is listed in the problems panel.
- plan_drawing of the equal-wing L roof above the cut plane shows the 5 hips, 1 valley and 2 ridges among the projected segments; build_scene includes the plane children.
- Satisfies ROF-003 (bodies, gable ends), ROF-006 and ROF-007 for multi-plane roofs and the computation of ROF-011.
notes: SRS: ROF-003 ROF-006 ROF-007 ROF-011. Related: MEA-003, IFX-016, NFR-REL-005, NFR-REL-006. Appendix D.2: 35°, 0.30 m, 0.50 m overhang. tan 35° = 0.70021, cos 35° = 0.81915. Conventions to document: ridge elevation = highest point of the roof body, eaves elevation = lowest point of the body on the eaves edges.

title: Reference model RM-S, AS-01/AS-03 automation and the defaults demonstration
description:
Turn the increment-2 exit into repository assets: RM-S (the AS-01 house on the F9 sloping site: storeys with attic, layered exterior walls, interior walls, slabs with stair opening, U-stair, doors and windows, gable roof with trimmed gable walls, stepped footings, terrain, about 300 elements) built through commands in the seeded fixture builder and kept as the golden IFCX file of NFR-MNT-003, automated AS-01 pass criteria and AS-03 (reopen, change the exterior structure thickness and a storey height, re-validate with unchanged UUIDs), the F3 and F9 fixtures registered, the NFR-USE-006 demonstration that the RM-S builder creates no material, layer structure or other attribute beyond the template, and the status document regenerated for the increment-2 exit. The railing variant of RM-S and RM-M follow in increment 3 and 4.

Risks: RM-S needs most increment-2 kinds, so this epic runs last in increment 2 while the builder grows with every epic. Golden-file churn when writers change: bless only with a reviewed diff.
design: crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs rm_s() built through commands with v5 ids; crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs writes RM-S; fixtures f3/f9 in the registry; conformance/check.ts extended with the AS-01 assertions; golden regeneration via ARCHICRAFT_BLESS; scripted manual procedures for AS-01 and AS-03 under docs/test-plan/.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx reproduces RM-S byte for byte from the builder (seeded ids) and the conformance job runs on RM-S, the AS-02 frame and every registered fixture; conformance/check.ts asserts the AS-01 criteria (tree project/site/building/3 storeys, openings in walls, clean junctions, modelled colours against the material table); the AS-03 test reopens RM-S, changes the exterior structure thickness and the upper storey height, re-saves and passes IFX-006 with unchanged UUIDs while junctions, openings, slabs and roof follow; F3 (floating floor +6.10 / +6.00 / +5.75, base offset -0.10, resilient layer) and F9 pass; a test asserts the RM-S builder uses only template attributes (NFR-USE-006 demonstration script under docs/); docs/implementation-status.md reflects the increment-2 state.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003 NFR-USE-006

title: Build the RM-S site, storeys and layered shell through commands
design:
Approach: keep the layout constants (exterior-face rectangle, storey table, spot-elevation table, footing runs, opening, stair and roof positions for tasks 02 and 10) at the top of samples/rm_s.rs. Tests then derive their expectations from the same constants by independent arithmetic. Never hard-code a structure thickness: read it from the template structure by name, so AS-03 (task 06) and template changes propagate. Resolve every template resource through one `template_resource(kind, name)` helper that panics with the missing name. Do not copy the silent fallback to materials[0] of template.rs:298-304, so a renamed template entry fails loudly.

Layout rules that later tasks depend on:
- Floor slab outlines follow the core's exterior face, i.e. the exterior-face rectangle offset inward by brick + air + insulation + plaster = 0.370 m. They are the realistic bearing line and stay fixed when AS-03 changes the core thickness with the reference line on the exterior face. Where slab and wall overlap, the cleanup-and-trims priority stage (SLB-007: reinforced concrete 900 against concrete 880, plaster 300) resolves the band, which is why 'slabs follow' in AS-03 needs no associative outline.
- Interior walls end on the exterior walls' interior faces (T) and on each other (L/T), so AS-03 exercises T re-resolution.
- Footings are slab class overrides with STRIP_FOOTING, exactly as F9 builds them (Table 5-1 allows wall, slab, beam or column), so RM-S and F9 share one footing code path; the predefined type is written per IFX-024.
- Plinth walls close the height between the stepped footing tops and the ground-slab soffit on the downhill side, so no wall floats above a footing.
- Terrain boundary: about 10 m beyond the house on every side. Bottom: the D.2 default (5.00 m below the lowest point).

Structure: one step function per storey taking &mut FixtureBuilder, so that tasks 02 and 10 and perf-tuning-rm-m-l (RM-M from repeated blocks) can reuse them, with one AddElements per stage for speed. Record build plus evaluation time in the test output, so a regression of the dev-profile test time is visible.

Pitfalls:
- Inserting a storey above the template's top storey keeps the template storey ids (seeded 'rm_s/storey/<n>').
- Walls on the top storey with the D.2 'home + 1' link would extrapolate (StoreyList::relative_elevation), so give attic walls fixed heights above the ridge for the trim of task 10.
- If the relation store assigns ids to junction overrides, seed them as well.

Pointers: samples.rs:16-83 (add_wall_ring, execute), template.rs default_metric_project, StoreyList::insert/set_height (storey.rs), History and replay in command.rs, layer-structures-09 for the F3 build pattern, terrain-and-site-17 for the F9 site and footings, grids-11 for a FixtureBuilder sample built through commands, junction-engine-12 for the coverage helpers.
acceptance_criteria:
- rm_s_is_deterministic (crates/archicraft-model/tests/rm_s.rs): two builds give equal projects including every id, and every id is a v5 UUID under the fixture namespace (no v4 id remains from template or factories).
- FixtureBuilder::commands() returns every executed command in order. A unit test executes more than 200 commands and finds all of them, which History::applied_commands() would not.
- Exactly three storeys: '00 Ground floor' +0.000 / 3.00 m, '01 First floor' +3.000 / 3.10 m, '02 Attic' +6.100. integrity_problems() is empty.
- F3 inside RM-S: the attic floor slab's absolute vertical extent is (5.75, 6.10) with core top 6.00 within 1e-9; its resilient skin is 30 mm (inside 20-30 mm); the attic walls' bodies start at 6.00 with no gap or overlap against the core top. The 00 and 01 slabs show the same relation 0.10 m below their storey elevation.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/rm_s.rs: ModelGeometry::evaluate reports no problems; every body passes check_closed and stays below 65,535 points; every L and T node of the shell is covered by interior-disjoint skin pieces (the node-envelope coverage check of the junction-engine-12 suite, reused through its tests/common helpers); the exterior-face corners of each storey ring equal the layout constants within MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- Terrain: one closed manifold body contained by the site, created only through the terrain commands from the typed spot-elevation table, never as a struct literal (AS-01 'terrain from typed spot elevations').
- Footings: every footing is an IfcFooting class override with STRIP_FOOTING; every footing bottom lies below the terrain surface at the footing's centre; consecutive steps touch (upper bottom = lower top within MODEL_TOLERANCE); every exterior wall and plinth wall rests on a footing or plinth top within MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- f9_sloping_site() reproduces f9-sloping-site.ifcx byte for byte after the step functions are promoted.
- rm_s_fingerprint (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/rm_s.rs) compares a hash of the evaluated meshes, rounded to 1e-6 m, with a committed value. A platform-dependent kernel result (the slab-wall cleanup runs through Manifold) then fails on the runner that differs before task 04 commits the golden. Tasks 02 and 10 update the value with their stages.
- No command in commands() adds, changes or deletes a material, layer, layer structure or other attribute (inline check; task 08 adds the classified test).
- cargo test --workspace is green and the existing golden files are byte-identical.
- Satisfies the shell part of the NFR-MNT-003 reference model and the template-only rule of NFR-USE-006 for walls, slabs, footings and terrain.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003 NFR-USE-006. Also AS-01 (SRS 7.2), SRS 7.3 RM-S, Appendix D.7 F3/F9. Review decision: RM-S shares F9's site and footing code path and project location, not F9's terrain data. F9 falls 10 m over 30 m (terrain-and-site-17), which under the 8.5 m deep house would be about 2.8 m of fall, i.e. a basement storey AS-01 does not have; D.7 calls AS-01 a simplified variant. Proposed layout, to be confirmed in review: exterior-face rectangle 10.00 x 8.50 m; RM-S site falling about 10 % from north to south; ground floor +-0.00 about 0.20 m above the terrain on the uphill side; footing steps of 0.40 m. The attic storey at +6.10 makes the attic floor reproduce F3 exactly.

title: Add doors, windows and the two stairs to RM-S
description:
WHY: AS-01 also needs 'floor slabs with stair opening, U-shaped stair with railing, doors and windows'. Its pass criteria include that 'walls show openings and clean L/T junctions'. The increment-2 exit is 'AS-01 without railings' (Appendix F), so the railing is left to railings-stairs-adv. NFR-MNT-003 needs RM-S complete before task 04 takes its golden file. NFR-USE-006 requires that doors, windows and stairs come from the D.2 defaults (door 0.90 x 2.10 m, window 1.20 x 1.40 m with sill 0.90 m, stair width 1.00 m with rule set D.3) and the built-in catalogue, never from new attributes. AS-03 later raises the upper storey, so the 01-02 stair must re-solve instead of conflicting (STA-003, STA-004, STA-011).

WHAT: In samples/rm_s.rs, add the stage `rm_s_openings_and_stairs` after the shell of task 01:
- doors and windows hosted in the exterior and interior walls (doors-windows-core): mostly the D.2 defaults and built-in catalogue definitions, a few with non-default widths and anchors at typed distances from corners, at least one window near an L corner and one door next to a T junction, plus gable-wall windows on 02 placed below the future roof line;
- a U-stair from 00 to 01 through the 01 stair opening and a straight stair from 01 to 02 through the 02 opening (stair-body-plan; D.3 rule set, D.2 width 1.00 m).
Geometry assertions extend crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/rm_s.rs. Out of scope: the roof, trims, roof windows, members and terrace (task 10), the railing (railings-stairs-adv), the curtain-wall entrance (RM-M, perf-tuning-rm-m-l), objects and furniture (library-dw-exchange), and the golden file (04).
design:
Approach: continue the step functions of task 01 and keep the layout constants for openings and stairs in the same constant block. Place inserts through the WallInsert placement (InsertFrame::resolve of doors-windows-core: along, anchor, vertical pin, reveal), never through absolute coordinates, so AS-03's thickness change moves voids correctly. Build stairs from typed baseline nodes in the stair openings. The U-stair needs a riser count that the D.3 solver accepts for 3.00 m (for example 17 x 176.5 mm). Build the 01-02 stair with a target riser height and a free going on an unlocked baseline long enough for N up to 20, so that AS-03's taller storey re-solves it (STA-003, STA-004) instead of raising an STA-011 conflict, and size the 02 opening for that N.

Indicative opening budget (part of the 250-350 elements asserted in task 10): ground floor 14 doors and windows, first floor 14, attic 4 gable windows, 2 stairs.

Pointers: doors-windows-core-01 (WallInsert, InsertFrame), doors-windows-core-11 corner cases, stair-body-plan PartRef::{Flight, Landing, Step} and StairLayout::roles(), samples::u_stair() of stair-solver-tool.
acceptance_criteria:
- integrity_problems() is empty and ModelGeometry reports no problems. Every body passes check_closed and stays below 65,535 points.
- Openings: every door and window is hosted by a wall of its storey (Host relation). Each host's per-skin volume equals the gross volume minus the void volumes, so every skin is cut. The near-L window and the near-T door leave the junction footprints outside the void bit-identical to the same walls without them.
- Doors and windows without an explicit size carry the D.2 sizes and sill (0.90 x 2.10 m; 1.20 x 1.40 m at 0.90 m), and every definition is a built-in catalogue definition (by seeded id).
- U-stair: an automatic landing of at least 1.00 m and every riser and going within D.3 (R 150-200 mm, 2R + G 600-650 mm). It starts at +-0.00 and arrives at +3.00. No stair part intersects the 01 slab: the bounds of every stair part above the slab soffit lie inside the stair-opening polygon. The riser, going and clearance checks also apply to the straight 01-02 stair arriving at +6.10.
- Every body part's material is a template material (by seeded id). commands() still contains no attribute-creating command.
- rm_s_fingerprint is updated for the new stage and passes on all three CI runners.
- cargo test --workspace is green and the existing golden files are byte-identical.
- Satisfies the openings and stairs of the NFR-MNT-003 reference model RM-S (AS-01 without railing) and the template-only rule of NFR-USE-006 for doors, windows and stairs.
notes: SRS: NFR-MNT-003 NFR-USE-006. Also AS-01 (without railing), D.2 door/window/stair defaults, D.3, STA-003, STA-004, STA-011. Open question: if the solver of stair-body-plan places the landing surplus differently from the U-stair acceptance of that epic, assert the solver's documented rule rather than a fixed split.

title: Generate corner window units with frame, corner post and frameless mitre connections
description:
WHY: DW-016 (S): 'Corner windows shall span the junction of two walls, with a corner connection of frame or corner post and a connection angle per side.' DW-023 (C): 'Corner windows may use a frameless mitred-glass connection.' The epic acceptance: a corner window spans an L-junction with a post or a frameless connection. Task 13 delivered the kind, the corner frame with the joint plane, the host cuts and the void; the units themselves are missing. DW-015 (S) covers every door and window, so the corner unit also exposes key points and derived values (task 12 API).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/corner_window.rs (task 13) gains the leg units: each leg is evaluated from the window generators (components/windows.rs, components-dw-catalogue-05) in its own unit-local frame with a corner end condition: Frame mitres the frame members on the joint plane through the planar end cut of sweep.rs (CutPlane, profiles-columns-beams-05); CornerPost adds a post part (PartRole::Frame, the post width parameter) sized to both frame depths and butts both frames against its faces; FramelessMitre omits the corner stile and mitres the glass panes on the joint plane with a 2 mm joint, and the head and sill members on the same plane (DW-023). Plan symbols for Simplified and Detailed with both legs and the post outline or the mitre line, through components/symbols.rs (components-dw-catalogue-06). Type geometry: the TypeKey of components-dw-catalogue-07 extended with legs, angles and connection (mirroring and class as before), cached in the TypeCache so identical corner windows share one Arc<TypeGeometry>, placed by a proper rotation at the outer corner. Key points per leg ('leg0.jamb.exterior.end', 'leg1.clear.start', 'corner.outer', 'corner.inner') through component_key_points of task 12, and per-leg derived values (sill and head, nominal size, clear width and height) through insert_derived of task 12 extended for corner windows. Out of scope: IFCX, tool and inspector (14), arc hosts.
design: Reuse the window generators per leg and cut them on the joint plane instead of writing corner-specific generators; CutPlane keeps volumes exact. The post is a separate closed part, never merged with the frames (IFX-032). Pitfalls: the joint plane passes through the outer corner from the junction-resolved faces (task 13), not through the reference-line intersection; mirroring swaps the leg order, so key point codes are defined per host leg; keep vertex counts small because corner types are rarely shared. Pointers: corner_window.rs (task 13), components/windows.rs and layout.rs (components-dw-catalogue-04/05), sweep.rs (profiles-columns-beams-05), components/types.rs TypeKey and TypeCache (components-dw-catalogue-07), component_key_points and insert_derived (task 12).
acceptance_criteria:
- Frame: the mitred end vertices of the frame members lie on the joint plane within 1e-9 and all meshes are closed and outward; CornerPost: a post part of the given width exists and the frames end at its faces; FramelessMitre: no frame part crosses the corner's vertical line, the glass corner edges lie on the joint plane and the joint is 2 mm.
- Angles 60/60 at a 120-degree junction put the joint plane on the bisector; angles 40/50 at a 90-degree junction turn it accordingly (Frame).
- Two identical corner windows share one Arc<TypeGeometry>; a mirrored one has its own type whose meshes keep positive signed volume.
- Plan symbols are non-empty at both detail levels and show the post outline or the mitre line.
- The corner key points lie on the frame and glass geometry within 1e-9 and are SnapKind::KeyPoint targets; insert_derived returns per-leg clear widths consistent with the frame layout.
- Covers the connection geometry of DW-016 (frame or corner post, angle per side) and DW-023 (frameless mitred glass), and DW-015 key points and derived values for corner windows.
notes:
SRS: DW-016 DW-023 DW-015
Also: IFX-032, IFX-050, IFX-051, OBJ-014.
DW-023 is Could: cut the frameless variant first if the epic runs late.

title: Meet plan navigation and update targets on every RM-M storey
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-004 (M): plan-view panning and zooming shall run at >= 30 frames/s for any storey of RM-M; DSP-013 adds that this holds with hatches shown; after a single-element edit the plan shall update within 200 ms (NFR-PERF-006, owned by element-kind-framework). plan-renderer-11 met the frame-rate target provisionally on the stand_in(5_000) storey with tile culling and left both incremental per-element re-tessellation and the final RM-M acceptance to this epic. RM-M storeys hold about 1,000 elements with layered walls, hatches and skin separators, door and window symbols, stair symbols with the display range of the storey above (plan-views-browser-05) and the curtain wall's symbolic plan. The plan view also still picks by scanning all elements on every hover frame (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs:453) unless selection-transforms-05 replaced it.

Exists (extend): the per-storey PlanDrawing cache keyed by revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:105-121), the wgpu plan renderer with retained buffers and tile culling (plan-renderer-06 and -11) and plan candidates from cached PlanDrawing data (selection-transforms-05). Missing: RM-M measurement, incremental re-tessellation, an index for picking, cache sizing and background builds.

WHAT: Run the plan-render benchmark and the plan-storeys script on all RM-M storeys and on RM-L's storeys, then fix what the profile shows, in this order: (1) plan update after an edit: per-element slice and classification results cached by element geometry, with cut-region unions and tessellation recomputed only for the tiles touched by dirty elements; (2) plan picking and hover through an rstar index over plan element bounds; (3) the PlanBuffers cache sized to the storeys of the open project (at least 8, least recently used) so switching storeys does not re-tessellate; (4) a storey plan that takes more than 100 ms to build is built by a job on the JobRunner of task 07 while the view shows a placeholder. Out of scope: 3D views, new plan features.
design:
Tile-level union: per material, union of the cut polygons of the elements whose bounds touch a tile, clipped to the tile; outlines are the union boundaries minus segments lying on internal tile borders with fill on both sides, which keeps same-material cuts seamless (the plan-renderer-04 rule). Clip with geo boolean operations and the shared tolerance module, and snap tile borders to exact coordinates to avoid slivers. rstar 0.12 (the version geo pins); remote-storey elements of plan-views-browser-05 take part in the caches with their own keys.

Pitfalls: the snapping index of point-input-snapping-02 is separate and already incremental, do not merge them; plan caches are invalidated through the change log (element-kind-framework-11), so cached slices are keyed by the geometry Arc, not by the revision. Pointers: archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:111-200, views/plan.rs:440-460, views/plan_gpu.rs (plan-renderer-06 and -11), document.rs plans cache.
acceptance_criteria:
- All five RM-M storeys with hatches shown: median >= 60 and 99th percentile >= 30 frames/s during pan and zoom on the developer machine (twice the target), recorded in docs/performance; the CI counters of plan-renderer-11 (no buffer writes while navigating) pass on RM-M storey 02.
- After a single wall move on RM-M, plan update and re-tessellation of the affected tiles take at most 60 ms (release, #[ignore]), and fills, strokes and pick segments equal a full regeneration for 20 random edits (comparison test).
- Plan picking on an RM-M storey returns the same candidates in the same order as the linear scan for 1,000 seeded points and costs under 0.2 ms per hover (bench).
- Switching through the five RM-M storeys twice tessellates each storey once (counter).
- A cold storey build over 100 ms never produces a frame over 100 ms (longest-frame metric).
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-004
Related: DSP-013 (hatches), NFR-PERF-006.
Estimate raised from 1.25 to 2 days: tile-level incremental unions with seamless outlines, the rstar pick index, cache sizing, background builds and the RM-M measurements are four separate changes.

title: Turn the perf scripts into the AS-07 protocol runner
description:
WHY: AS-07 performs the NFR-PERF measurements on RM-M and RM-L and passes when all Must targets are met on reference hardware. The epic acceptance lists every measurement: open and save times (NFR-PERF-002), 3D frame rates for orbit, pan, zoom and walk on RM-M and RM-L and for RM-S on minimum hardware (NFR-PERF-003, VIEW-054), plan pan and zoom on every RM-M storey (NFR-PERF-004), a single edit visible within 200 ms (NFR-PERF-006), no freeze over 1 s during long operations (NFR-PERF-007), RM-L memory (NFR-PERF-008) and autosave blocking (NFR-PERF-009). regression-and-status-17 delivered the perf feature (PerfRecorder, frame time, edit latency to cache refresh, UI time of the autosave request, frames over 1 s) with the scripts orbit, pan, zoom and plan-pan, and regression-and-status-18 the results convention docs/performance/<date>-<machine>.md and the machine ids. Walk, open, save, edit-to-pixels, autosave, per-storey plan and memory scripts, GPU-inclusive frame times without the vsync cap and an AS-07 results generator are missing, and every tuning task needs them to report before and after.

WHAT: The archicraft-app perf feature gains the scripts walk (eye-height camera along samples::walk_path for RM-M/RM-L and a generic path from the model bounds for RM-S), plan-storeys (plan-pan and zoom on every storey in turn), open (open a file; time to first interactive frame and longest frame), save (Save As to a temporary path; time to completion and longest frame), edit (20 scripted single-element edits; latency from Workspace::execute to the first presented frame in which both the plan and the 3D view show the new revision), autosave (five requests with the interval forced to zero; UI-thread time and longest frame while writing) and memory (peak and current physical footprint after the sequence). Perf runs use PresentMode::AutoNoVsync and close each frame sample after GPU completion. Every 3D row runs in the default display style of a new 3D view (today DisplayMode::ShadedWithEdges, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:29; the template's default named style once 3d-display-styles has landed, with shadows as that style sets them) and with default view settings: all layers visible, no view filter, cut plane or section box, level of detail and culling automatic. No row may depend on the user simplifying the model (NFR-PERF-003 'default shaded style', VIEW-054); the style is recorded in the results header. Every script records its longest frame, and the generator adds one row for the longest frame over the whole sequence (<= 1 s, NFR-PERF-007). The scripts call the app's public entry points (open_path, save_to, Workspace::execute) and wait until the app reports no running job, so they keep working when tasks 07 and 08 move these operations to worker threads. scripts/as07.py builds the release binary with --features perf, writes RM-S/RM-M/RM-L with the example, runs every model/script pair three times and writes docs/performance/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<machine-id>.md with the header table and one row per AS-07 measurement (target, median, worst run, PASS/FAIL), exiting non-zero on a failed Must row. A first run on the untuned code is committed as the before-picture. Out of scope: tuning; the runs on the reference and minimum machines (task 15).
design:
Walk mode (VIEW-024) is a Could item of could-scope-polish and may not exist: the walk script moves Camera3d directly along the polyline at 1.4 m/s with a look-ahead target and a 0.1 m near plane; if VIEW-024 has landed, drive its camera instead. GPU completion: wgpu timestamp queries when Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY is available, otherwise device.poll(Maintain::Wait) after submit, only inside perf scripts. Edit latency closes when the plan pane's PlanBuffers key and the 3D GpuScene generation both match the new revision in a submitted frame.

Memory probe in crates/archicraft-app/src/perf/memory.rs (a submodule of regression-and-status-17's src/perf.rs), compiled only with the perf feature: macOS task_info(TASK_VM_INFO).phys_footprint (what Activity Monitor shows; includes GPU allocations on unified memory), Linux /proc/self/status VmHWM and VmRSS, Windows GetProcessMemoryInfo PeakWorkingSetSize and PrivateUsage through windows-sys (already in Cargo.lock through winit; as a direct, perf-only dependency it is recorded in docs/technology-choices.md and passes cargo deny check).

Pitfalls: egui repaints only on input, so scripts request a repaint every frame; fanless MacBook Airs throttle, so each script runs at least 30 s after a 10 s warm-up and the median of three runs counts; the first frame after opening includes GPU uploads and is reported separately, not inside navigation frame rates. Pointers: src/perf.rs (regression-and-status-17), app.rs open_path/save_to/autosave, views/view3d.rs and views/camera.rs (Camera3d), main.rs NativeOptions.
acceptance_criteria:
- `python3 scripts/as07.py --machine dev-<name> --quick` produces a results file with rows for: open RM-M, save RM-M, open RM-L; orbit, pan, zoom and walk frame rates on RM-M, RM-L and RM-S; plan pan/zoom frame rate per RM-M storey; edit latency p95; longest frame during open, save and autosave and over the whole sequence (<= 1 s); RM-L peak memory; autosave UI blocking on RM-M; each with target and PASS/FAIL, Must and Should rows distinguished, the RM-M 3D rows showing both the >= 30 frames/s Must threshold and the 60 frames/s target; the header records the display style; the exit code is non-zero when a Must row fails.
- scripts/tests/test_as07.py renders the table from canned perf JSON (pass, fail, missing metric) and checks the file-name convention.
- A perf-feature test asserts that every 3D script runs in the default display style of a new 3D view with no hidden layer, view filter, cut plane or section box.
- Rust unit tests: walk paths stay inside the model bounds at eye height; the memory probe returns a plausible non-zero value on the CI operating system; perf builds select AutoNoVsync.
- kittest (--features perf) on two_storey_shell: the edit script records three edit-latency samples, each closed only after the plan and the 3D scene of the new revision were drawn (without a GPU the 3D part is reported as skipped, never as zero).
- docs/performance/README.md describes the AS-07 protocol: machines and operating systems per NFR-PERF-001, preparation (mains power, native resolution and OS scaling recorded, other applications closed, warm-up), repetitions, Must versus Should rows.
- The baseline results file of the untuned code is committed.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-003 NFR-PERF-004 NFR-PERF-007 NFR-PERF-008 NFR-PERF-009 VIEW-054
Measurement only. Hardware classes and machine ids per NFR-PERF-001 (regression-and-status-18). Related: NFR-PERF-006 (edit latency, owned by element-kind-framework).

title: Detect newer definition versions and upgrade instances keeping compatible values
description:
WHY: OBJ-008 (S): 'When a newer version of a used definition is available, the system shall offer to upgrade instances, keeping compatible parameter values.' Gap: missing (M), 'Version upgrade offer keeping compatible parameter values.' OBJ-004 references definitions by id and version and OBJ-006 embeds the used version, so an upgrade is an explicit, journaled command that embeds the new version. Task 07 provides the CatalogueSet with its sources in precedence order; components-dw-catalogue-02 provides ParameterSchema::compatible and RelinkDefinition. This task delivers the headless detection and command; the offer (notice, review, buttons) is task 09.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/components/upgrade.rs: Project::available_upgrades(&CatalogueSet) -> Vec<Upgrade { from: DefinitionRef, to: DefinitionRef, source, instances: Vec<ElementId> }> (the highest version above the used one, from the highest-precedence source on equal versions, in deterministic order); map_parameters(from_schema, to_schema, values) -> (values, UpgradeReport { kept, reset, dropped }) built on ParameterSchema::compatible and shared with RelinkDefinition, which is refactored onto it without behaviour change; `Command::UpgradeDefinition { from, to: Definition, ids: Option<Vec<ElementId>> }` carrying the full target definition so the journal replays without the library, mapping parameters, resetting out-of-range values to defaults, embedding the new version in the ComponentStore and removing the old embedded record when no instance uses it, in one undo step; UpgradeDefinition::preview(project) -> UpgradeReport. Locked instances (ELM-013) are skipped and reported, never upgraded silently. Geometry needs no new code: the version is part of the TypeKey, so upgraded instances regenerate. Out of scope: the notice and the Libraries window (09).
design: One mapping helper for relink and upgrade keeps the compatibility rules from diverging. The command carries the full definition so replay and undo never depend on the file system (NFR-MNT-001/002). Pitfalls: the embedded copy wins resolution (OBJ-006), so the upgrade replaces the embedded record instead of only changing the reference; keep older records while any instance uses them; deterministic ordering by precedence, then category, then code. Pointers: components/store.rs and RelinkDefinition (components-dw-catalogue-02), components/schema.rs ParameterSchema::compatible (components-dw-catalogue-01), components/library.rs CatalogueSet (task 07), command.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/upgrades.rs: UpgradeDefinition from v1 to a v2 that renames one parameter and narrows one range: the preview lists the kept, reset and dropped keys; execute plus undo restores the project bit for bit; with ids given only those instances move to v2; the v1 record is removed only when unused; a locked instance is skipped and reported.
- available_upgrades ignores versions lower than or equal to the used one, prefers the higher-precedence source on equal versions and returns the same order across runs.
- The RelinkDefinition tests of components-dw-catalogue-02 stay green after the refactor onto map_parameters (regression).
- A journal containing UpgradeDefinition replays on a project without any linked library.
- Geometry test: upgraded instances reference a new TypeKey, and two identical upgraded instances still share one Arc<TypeGeometry>.
- Satisfies the model part of OBJ-008 (detection of newer versions, upgrade keeping compatible values); the offer is task 09.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-008
Also: OBJ-004, OBJ-006, ELM-013, NFR-MNT-001.

title: Let curved doors and windows follow the curvature of arc walls
description:
WHY: DW-020 (C): 'Curved doors and windows may follow the curvature of arc walls.' DW-019 (curved-geometry-12) places straight units on the chord with a radial void; gap DW-020: missing (L), 'would need curved frame/leaf generators following the arc'. The epic acceptance: a curved unit follows an arc wall.

WHAT: Model: WallInsert gains `curvature: UnitCurvature { Chord, FollowHost }` (serde default Chord) and traits.curvable on definitions whose units can bend (window.fixed, window.multi-sash with fixed sashes only, window.sliding.horizontal, door.sliding.single surface-mounted, empty openings); a check function shared with the inspector refuses FollowHost on straight hosts and unsupported types with a reason ('Hinged leaves cannot follow a curved wall'); a SetInsertCurvature command. Geometry, new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/insert_curved.rs: bend(parts, ArcFrame { centre, radius at the reveal face, start angle, sense, exterior side }) refines each unit-local mesh with planes x = const at the stations of the host's circle-anchored tessellator (TriMesh::split_by_planes, new in mesh.rs, convex triangle clipping that keeps closedness), then maps (x, y, z) to centre + (R -/+ y)(cos t, sin t) with t = t0 +/- x / R, sharing vertices along curved faces and keeping hard edges; the void is the exact radial annular-sector prism over [s0, s1] without chord widening; plan symbols turn x-parallel lines into exact arcs concentric with the wall and radial lines stay lines. IFCX: an optional curvature member in archicraft::door and archicraft::window, bent parts in type nodes keyed with the radius (TypeKey includes curvature and radius); curved_walls() gains a curved window and curved-walls.ifcx is re-blessed. Inspector: 'Follow wall curvature' checkbox disabled with the reason where not allowed. Key points and derived values of task 12 follow the bend: the declared key points are mapped through the same (x, y, z) map, and the clear opening width of a FollowHost unit is the chord between its clear-opening edges (documented in docs/components.md). Out of scope: curved hinged leaves, units in polygonal walls.
design: Bend instead of writing curved variants of every generator: the catalogue generators already emit unit-local meshes (x along the wall, y through it, z up, origin pinned by doors-windows-core-04), so a refine-and-map step turns any box-like frame into its curved counterpart. Refining at the host's own tessellation stations guarantees that unit faces coincide with the wall's curved faces and jambs (the F8 lesson of curved-geometry). Planar glass becomes a cylindrical panel tessellated with the same stations (IFX-034 tolerances). Pitfalls: the refinement must split triangles exactly on the station planes without creating T-junctions (split neighbours consistently, then check_closed); the exterior side decides whether y adds to or subtracts from the radius; units wider than about a quarter circle may self-intersect at small radii, so refuse when the inner radius of any part falls below the frame depth. Pointers: the door and window GeometryKind modules that call components::evaluate_instance with InsertFrame's unit_to_storey (doors-windows-core-04), component_key_points and insert_derived (task 12), radial void and the arc InsertFrame (curved-geometry-12), tessellate() (curved-geometry-03), mesh.rs, alpha/writer.rs door and window codecs (doors-windows-core-05).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a 2.0 m fixed window following an arc wall of r = 5 m has every frame vertex at its intended radius within 1e-6 and the glass at a constant reveal from the exterior wall face within 1e-6; all meshes are closed and outward.
- Unit faces and wall jamb faces share their angles (no gap above 1e-9 at the jambs), because both use the host's tessellation stations.
- Plan symbol arcs have centre bits equal to the wall centre; FollowHost on a side-hung window or in a straight wall is refused with the reason.
- curved-walls.ifcx with the curved window round-trips equal and passes conformance/run.sh; a curved and a straight window of the same definition reference different type nodes.
- The jamb-face and clear-opening key points of a FollowHost window lie on the bent frame within 1e-6 and are snap targets; its inspector shows the documented clear width.
- Satisfies DW-020.
notes:
SRS: DW-020
Also: DW-019, IFX-034, DW-015 (key points and derived values of bent units).
Could requirement: cut first if the epic runs late.

title: Move per-project state into project windows with owned GPU resources
description:
WHY: PRJ-011 (S): 'At least two projects shall be open at the same time in separate windows, so that elements can be copied between them (SW-003).' Gap: missing (L), a single eframe window with one Workspace and Document (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:53-71, main.rs:30-34). Epic risk: multi-viewport wgpu lifetimes; the texture side channel ArchiCraftApp.released: Vec<View3dState> (app.rs:69, 145, 793), a technical-debt item in docs/implementation-status.md, exists because Workspace::replace_document cannot reach the render state, and it is replaced by per-viewport render state first.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/window.rs: ProjectWindow { id: WindowId (the root window uses ViewportId::ROOT), ws: Workspace, tree: Tree<Pane>, dialogs: Dialogs, load_problems, prompt, title, autosave slot, close state }, built from the per-project fields of ArchiCraftApp; ArchiCraftApp keeps dirs, the authoritative preferences (copied into each window on change), the process Session, the Autosaver, crash reports and recovery, and `windows: Vec<ProjectWindow>` with exactly one window in this task. GPU resources become owned: the offscreen Viewport of View3dState holds a clone of egui_wgpu::RenderState and frees its egui texture in Drop (the body of render3d.rs free_viewport, render3d.rs:496), Workspace.renderer and scene are owned per window, and the `released` field plus the Behavior.closed release loop (app.rs:842-849) are removed; replacing a document or closing a tab simply drops the old state. Autosave gets per-window slots (session-<pid>-<ts>/window-<n>/ with the model and info files); find_abandoned returns one Abandoned per slot and recovery restores the first into the root window, queueing others for task 17. Out of scope: a second window (17), the shared clipboard (19).
design: RAII instead of a release queue: egui_wgpu::RenderState is Clone (shared device, queue and renderer behind Arc), so a viewport can free its own texture when dropped. eframe shares one device and one egui renderer across viewports; 'own wgpu state' per window therefore means each window owns its Renderer3d, scene buffers, offscreen targets and textures, which is what lets a window close without touching the other. Pitfalls: never drop a GPU-owning value while the renderer RwLock is held (inside a paint callback) or it deadlocks, so drops happen in UI code; preferences are personal settings shared by all windows (PRJ-007), so edits in one window propagate; keep ArchiCraftApp::workspace() for tests returning the focused window's workspace. Pointers: app.rs:53-150 and :791-875, views/view3d.rs:51 release, views/render3d.rs:270-500, workspace.rs:50-100, persistence/autosave.rs:37-160.
acceptance_criteria:
- All existing tests stay green (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs, persistence tests).
- With a counting texture registry (or the kittest wgpu render state), replacing the document 100 times leaves the registered texture count at the number of live 3D views; closing a 3D tab decrements it.
- The `released` field and its drain loop no longer exist; View3dState frees its texture on drop.
- Autosave writes into the window slot; an abandoned session directory with two window slots yields two Abandoned entries, and discarding one leaves the other.
- Prepares PRJ-011 (per-window state and render resources).
notes:
SRS: PRJ-011
Also: PRJ-003, PRJ-004, PRJ-007; resolves the technical-debt item 'GPU texture lifetime is handled by a side channel'.

title: Build the catalogue browser with category tree, sources and search
description:
WHY: DW-014 (S): 'The catalogue shall offer a category tree, thumbnails, search, and a preview in plan, elevation and 3D that can show either side.' This task delivers the tree, the search and the placement entry point; thumbnails and previews follow in task 10. OBJ-001 (M) makes the built-in library accessible from every project, and OBJ-007 (S) requires duplicates across sources to be reported with their precedence. Gap DW-014: missing (L), 'No catalogue UI. Needs category tree, thumbnails, incremental search (UI-014), and plan/elevation/3D preview'. components-dw-catalogue-12 left a plain definition_picker in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/catalogue.rs to be extended here.

WHAT: ui/catalogue.rs: a CatalogueBrowser pane (Pane::Catalogue in egui_tiles, toggled by Action::Catalogue in the View menu) with an incremental search field (case- and accent-insensitive over name, code, group and category label, matches highlighted, Esc clears), a source filter (All, Built-in, This project, each linked library), a category tree (the six OBJ-002 categories, then groups) with counts, and a result list (name, version, source, a duplicate badge 'Also in: <library>' with shadowed entries greyed). Double-click or Place activates ToolKind::Object (task 05) for object categories or the door and window tools (doors-windows-core-07) for door, window and opening definitions, with the definition set in the tool defaults; 'Show in catalogue' on a selected instance reveals its definition. The listing comes from CatalogueSet::listing (task 07), cached per (project revision, library generation). Out of scope: thumbnails and previews (10), library management (09).
design: Extend definition_picker instead of writing a second list, so the missing-definitions relink picker gains search for free. egui_extras (pinned with the egui family by commands-and-l10n) provides TableBuilder for the result list; the tree uses egui::collapsing_header::CollapsingState with ids derived from category and group codes (stable across frames), as plan-views-browser does for its tree. Accent folding with a small static table (no new dependency). Pitfalls: compute the listing per (revision, generation), not per frame; keyboard focus in the search field must not trigger tool shortcuts (works_while_typing false for single-key shortcuts); keep labels unique for AccessKit lookups. Pointers: ui/catalogue.rs (components-dw-catalogue-12), app.rs Pane and Behavior, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs View menu.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of the filter: 'slid' finds the sliding door and the horizontal sliding window but not the box; 'cyl' finds the cylinder; matching ignores case and accents; tree counts equal the filtered listing.
- kittest: the catalogue opens from the View menu; typing 'cyl' shows 'Cylinder' and hides 'Box'; expanding 'Generic' lists Box, Cylinder and the empty openings.
- kittest: double-clicking 'Box' activates the Object tool with object.box in the tool defaults; double-clicking a window definition activates the Window tool.
- A definition present in two linked libraries shows the duplicate badge naming the shadowed source.
- In a new project (Project::new) and in a project from each template the browser lists the built-in doors, windows, empty openings, Box and Cylinder (OBJ-001: every project has access).
- Covers the category tree and search of DW-014 and the visible-duplicate clause of OBJ-007.
notes:
SRS: DW-014 OBJ-001 OBJ-007
Also: UI-014 (incremental search).

title: Chunk the 3D scene for frustum culling and partial uploads
description:
WHY: VIEW-054 (M): 3D views shall meet the performance targets of NFR-PERF-003 automatically, through level-of-detail and culling, without the user having to simplify the model; NFR-PERF-003 includes walking, where an eye-height view sees a small part of the model. NFR-PERF-007: no frame may freeze the UI for 1 s, yet uploading all RM-L buffers in one frame after opening risks exactly that. A single edit must be visible within 200 ms (NFR-PERF-006, owned by element-kind-framework, which left per-element GPU buffers and partial upload to this epic). The gap rows: one draw call per buffer over the whole scene, no culling of any kind (render3d.rs:560-575), back-face culling off (cull_mode: None, render3d.rs:311), no spatial structure.

WHAT: The scene is split into chunks per storey on a spatial grid (proposal: 16 m cells, split until at most 64k triangles per chunk, merged below 4k), each with its own vertex and index buffers, f64 bounds and local origin. Every frame the CPU tests chunk bounds against the view frustum and against active cut planes and the section box (3d-view-restrictions), sorts opaque chunks front to back and draws only the visible ones. Back-face culling is enabled in the opaque colour pass for closed bodies (IFX-032 guarantees closed, outward-oriented meshes) while the stencil cap pass keeps both faces. After an edit only chunks containing dirty elements are rebuilt and re-uploaded. After opening or a large change, uploads are paced with a per-frame byte budget (proposal 64 MB): pending chunks appear a few frames later instead of freezing a frame. The id pass and fit-to-window use the same chunks. The Open job of task 08 builds the chunk CPU data on its worker instead of the whole SceneData, so only GPU uploads remain on the UI thread. Out of scope: level of detail (task 11), occlusion culling (a follow-up bead only if task 15 measurements require it).
design:
Chunk key (storey, cell x, cell y); an element spanning cells goes to the cell of its bounding-box centre and chunk bounds are the union of member bounds; the SceneCache keeps the element-to-chunk map for dirty propagation. Frustum planes are extracted from the f64 view-projection relative to the scene origin (Gribb and Hartmann) and tested against chunk AABBs. One buffer pair per chunk is simple and fast enough (RM-L yields a few hundred chunks); multi_draw_indirect is not available on every backend and is not needed. Pending uploads form a queue drained each frame within the budget, with request_repaint until it is empty.

Pitfalls: the per-viewport state buffer is indexed by the global element slot and is unaffected by chunking; hidden-line mode draws faces depth-only and keeps culling; a shadow pass (3d-display-styles) must cull against the light's frustum, not the camera's; transparent chunks keep back-to-front order. Pointers: render3d.rs:182-200 (upload_scene), 302-380 (render), view3d.rs:195-235, workspace.rs scene cache.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: chunking of RM-M is deterministic, every element is in exactly one chunk, no chunk exceeds 64k triangles; the frustum test is right for chunks inside, outside, straddling and behind the camera; a chunk outside a section box is skipped.
- Counters: during the walk script on RM-M fewer than 25 % of the chunks are drawn per frame on average; orbiting RM-L at fit distance draws every chunk (no false culling).
- After a single wall move on RM-M only the chunks of the wall and its junction neighbours are re-uploaded, and the edit script of task 03 reports a 3D-side p95 latency of at most 100 ms on the developer machine.
- Opening RM-L produces no frame over 250 ms from uploads, and all chunks are resident within 2 s after the document appears.
- Pixel goldens are unchanged for all display modes, cut-plane caps (3d-view-restrictions-07) and transparency.
- RM-M and RM-L orbit and walk frame rates improve on the task-09 numbers (recorded in docs/performance).
notes:
SRS: VIEW-054 NFR-PERF-003 NFR-PERF-007
Related: NFR-PERF-006 (owned by element-kind-framework).

title: Verify exit criterion: Object library, advanced doors and windows, multi-window and cross-project exchange
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its acceptance holds end to end on the integrated workspace, not task by task: the furniture and fixture library as IfcFurniture types, object placement with snapped rotation, mirroring and the EDT-007 refusal, relinking a moved library folder, save-selection-as-component appearing in the catalogue, catalogue search and two-sided previews, snappable clear-opening key points, corner windows with post and frameless connections, curved units in arc walls, and two project windows exchanging a layered wall with its resources. It covers OBJ-001, OBJ-003, OBJ-007, OBJ-008, OBJ-009, OBJ-012, OBJ-013, EDT-025, DW-014, DW-015, DW-016, DW-020, DW-023, PRJ-011, SW-003 and PRF-009.

WHAT: Run the full verification: cargo test, clippy and fmt on the workspace, conformance/run.sh on every golden file (including objects.ifcx, furniture-library.ifcx, corner-windows.ifcx and the re-blessed curved-walls.ifcx), the headless viewer run, and a manual pass on macOS, Windows and Linux with two project windows, the catalogue browser, the library manager with a moved folder, the object, corner window and curved unit tools and cross-window paste. Update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence with file paths and test names, remaining gaps; EDT-025 through ObjectOrientation and the per-instance 'Free orientation' override, with the product owner's confirmation of that resolution recorded), mark the GPU side-channel debt item resolved, file follow-up beads for deferred clauses, and close the epic in beads.
design: Verification only; no new features. Use the CI jobs of .github/workflows/ci.yml on the three platforms as the source of truth for test, clippy, fmt and conformance; the kittest wgpu snapshot of task 10 needs the software adapter configured by plan-renderer. Run the moved-library integration test and the two-window paste kittest once more on the integrated build. For the status document follow the existing requirement-table format (status, evidence, gap) and update the technical-debt section (texture side channel removed).
acceptance_criteria:
- The built-in library lists at least 30 furniture and fixture definitions placed as IfcFurniture with shared type geometry.
- An object is placed by insertion point and snapped rotation, rotates about the vertical axis and mirrors on request while a request to rotate it about a horizontal axis is refused with the EDT-007 message.
- Relinking a moved library folder restores instances.
- A selection saved as a component appears in the catalogue immediately.
- Catalogue search and preview from both sides (kittest).
- Clear-opening values and jamb key points are snappable.
- A corner window spans an L-junction with a post or a frameless connection.
- A curved unit follows an arc wall.
- Two windows each hold a project with their own wgpu state and pasting a layered wall from one to the other brings its structure, materials and profiles with the use-existing / keep-both / overwrite choice (tests on the headless payload).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx).
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for OBJ-001, OBJ-003, OBJ-007, OBJ-008, OBJ-009, OBJ-012, OBJ-013, EDT-025, DW-014, DW-015, DW-016, DW-020, DW-023, PRJ-011, SW-003 and PRF-009 with evidence.
- The epic library-dw-exchange is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for every deferred clause.
notes: SRS: OBJ-001 OBJ-003 OBJ-007 OBJ-008 OBJ-009 OBJ-012 OBJ-013 EDT-025 DW-014 DW-015 DW-016 DW-020 DW-023 PRJ-011 SW-003 PRF-009

title: Add the corner window kind spanning an L-junction with its host cuts
description:
WHY: DW-016 (S): 'Corner windows shall span the junction of two walls, with a corner connection of frame or corner post and a connection angle per side. Options a type does not support shall be shown disabled with the reason.' DW-023 (C): 'Corner windows may use a frameless mitred-glass connection.' Gap DW-016: missing (L), 'a unit spanning two hosts contradicts the single-host model and must cut both walls at the L junction ... Needs two-host placement, corner connection types, per-side angles, and disabled-with-reason options'; DW-023: missing (M). The epic acceptance: a corner window spans an L-junction with a post or a frameless connection.

WHAT: Model, new crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/corner_window.rs: CornerWindow { legs: [CornerLeg { width }; 2] measured along each host's exterior face from the outer corner, height, vertical: VerticalPin and reveal: Reveal (shared with WallInsert), connection: CornerConnection { Frame, CornerPost { width }, FramelessMitre }, angles: [f64; 2] (connection angle per side between the leg's wall face and the joint plane, default half the junction angle), instance: ComponentInstance }, hosted by two Host edges (leg order = edge order); validation: both hosts straight walls on the same storey joined at an L junction (the junction relation of junction-engine) at a common end, legs fit their walls, and for Frame and FramelessMitre the two angles sum to the junction angle within 0.1 degrees. Catalogue: window.corner (sash type per leg: fixed, side-hung, tilt-and-turn; post width) and window.corner.fixed, with traits.corner: CornerSupport and CornerSupport::check(connection, parameters) -> Result<(), reason> (FramelessMitre requires fixed glazing next to the corner) shared by validation and the inspector of task 14. Host behaviour: deleting either host deletes the corner window, moving the hosts carries it, unjoining them reports the problem 'The corner window needs walls joined at an L corner' and shows the placeholder. Geometry, new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/corner_window.rs: CornerFrame::resolve (outer corner from the junction-resolved exterior faces, leg directions, reveal planes, the joint plane from the per-side angles); per host a wall-plane cut rectangle from the leg's far jamb to beyond the reference-line end at the corner, fed into the host-openings cut path (wall_cut.rs, host-openings-05) so the mitred skin ends inside the window band are removed; one closed Void part from the 2D union of both leg footprints extruded from sill to head; a labelled placeholder (bounding box of both legs, OBJ-005 style) while validation fails. Out of scope: the leg units and their corner connections (21), IFCX, tool and inspector (14), arc hosts (refused).
design: A separate kind instead of a WallInsert variant, because every WallInsert invariant (one host, one along-wall interval) would need exceptions. Cutting reuses the developed (s, z) cut path of host-openings: extending each host's rectangle past the reference-line end removes exactly the junction zone of the mitred skins inside the window band, so no 3D Boolean is needed. The Void is one closed mesh because both legs share the same z range: a 2D union with geo extruded once (IFX-036 wants one invisible closed Void). Pitfalls: the outer corner must come from the junction engine's resolved faces, not from reference-line intersections, or layered walls with offset reference lines misplace the unit; keep host order stable (relation order) for deterministic output; a T or X junction is not an L corner and is refused. Pointers: kinds/insert.rs, InsertFrame and the Host relation edges (doors-windows-core-01), insert.rs insert_void (doors-windows-core-03), wall_cut.rs (host-openings-05), the junction relation and footprints of junction-engine, components/catalogue.rs (components-dw-catalogue-03).
acceptance_criteria:
