- Geometry tests on two 300 mm walls joined at 90 degrees with legs 1.20 m and 0.80 m: inside the window band no wall material remains in the void footprint (plan slice at sill + 0.5 m), the removed volume equals the void volume within 1e-6, and the Void is one closed mesh.
- A 120-degree junction with angles 60/60 works; angles 50/60 with Frame are rejected with a message; FramelessMitre with a side-hung sash next to the corner is rejected with the CornerSupport reason; a T junction, an arc host or hosts on different storeys are refused with a message.
- Deleting either host deletes the corner window and undo restores both; moving the joined hosts carries the corner window; unjoining the walls reports 'The corner window needs walls joined at an L corner' and shows the labelled placeholder.
- Adding a corner window and undoing it restores the project bit for bit.
- Covers the model, host cuts and void of DW-016 (two-host span, connection choice, angle per side) and the model side of DW-023 (FramelessMitre with its CornerSupport rule).
notes:
SRS: DW-016 DW-023
Also: DW-001 (host rules carried over), IFX-036, OBJ-005 (placeholder).
Decision to record: a connection angle is measured between the leg's exterior wall face and the joint plane; for frame and frameless connections the two angles must close the joint. DW-023 is Could: cut the frameless variant first if the epic runs late.

title: Run AS-07 on minimum and reference hardware and close gaps
description:
WHY: AS-07 (perform the NFR-PERF measurements on RM-M and RM-L; all Must targets met on reference hardware) is part of v1 acceptance on Windows, macOS and Linux (SRS 7.2) and of the increment-4 exit (Appendix F). NFR-PERF-001 defines the minimum and reference classes and measures Linux on each class's Windows laptop; regression-and-status-18 recorded the concrete machines and the ids min-mac-m1, min-win-i5, ref-mac-m2 and ref-win-u7. This task collects the evidence for NFR-PERF-002, NFR-PERF-003 (including RM-S >= 30 frames/s on minimum hardware), NFR-PERF-004, NFR-PERF-007, NFR-PERF-008, NFR-PERF-009 and VIEW-054.

WHAT: Run scripts/as07.py (task 03) in full mode from one tagged commit on ref-mac-m2 and ref-win-u7 (Windows 11 and Ubuntu LTS) and on min-mac-m1 and min-win-i5 (Windows 11 and Ubuntu LTS; the RM-S row is Must there, the other rows are recorded for information); commit one results file per machine and operating system. For each failing Must row, profile with the platform tools (Instruments, Windows Performance Analyzer or PIX, perf), fix it here if the fix is small (one day in total), otherwise file a bead with the measurement and the profile, linked to this task, and keep the epic open; re-run after fixes. Check progress and cancellation of open, save and explicit regeneration manually on one machine per operating system (checklist rows in the results files). Update the summary table in docs/performance/README.md and, if needed, the system requirements in README.
design:
Protocol per docs/performance/README.md: mains power, display at native resolution with the OS scaling recorded, other applications closed, release build with --features perf, 10 s warm-up, three repetitions, median reported and worst run listed. Windows: current GPU driver, Balanced power plan; Ubuntu: current Mesa with the Vulkan backend. Raw perf JSON goes to the CI artefact store, or to docs/performance/raw/ if small; numbers are never edited by hand.

If a minimum-class machine is unavailable (epic risk, O-15), record that in the results and file a bead; the RM-S clause of NFR-PERF-003 cannot be closed without it. If the save or open budgets are still missed after tasks 04 to 06, the deferred SQLite store is evaluated in a bead with these measurements (epic risk), not inside this task.
acceptance_criteria:
- Results files exist for ref-mac-m2, ref-win-u7 and ref-win-u7-ubuntu, and with the RM-S row for min-mac-m1, min-win-i5 and min-win-i5-ubuntu, all produced by scripts/as07.py from the same tagged commit, with machine headers (class, CPU, GPU, RAM, display and scaling, OS, driver, commit, toolchain).
- On every reference machine every Must row passes: RM-M open <= 10 s and save <= 5 s, RM-L open <= 30 s, RM-M orbit, pan, zoom and walk >= 30 frames/s in the default shaded style of a new 3D view with default view settings (no hidden layer, filter, cut plane or section box; level of detail and culling automatic, VIEW-054) and reported against the 60 frames/s target, RM-L >= 20 frames/s, plan pan and zoom >= 30 frames/s on every RM-M storey, single edit visible within 200 ms (p95), no frame over 1 s during open, save and regeneration (task 13 rows) or anywhere else in the sequence; on every minimum machine RM-S >= 30 frames/s.
- Should rows recorded: RM-L peak memory below 4 GB and autosave blocking at most 200 ms on RM-M; a failure is filed as a bead with a release decision.
- The manual checklist (progress shown; save, export and explicit regeneration cancellable; viewport navigable during save) is ticked per operating system in the results files.
- Every remaining Must failure has a bead with profile evidence, and the epic stays open until it is fixed.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-003 NFR-PERF-004 NFR-PERF-007 NFR-PERF-008 NFR-PERF-009 VIEW-054
NFR-PERF-001 classes (proposal): minimum MacBook Air M1 8 GB and a Windows laptop with Core i5-1135G7 (Iris Xe), 8 GB, 1920x1080; reference MacBook Air M2 16 GB and a Windows laptop with Core Ultra 7 155H (Arc), 16 GB; Linux on each Windows laptop with the current Ubuntu LTS.

title: Add digest goldens, conformance and benches for RM-M and RM-L
description:
WHY: The epic acceptance requires that the RM-M and RM-L golden files pass IFX-006 (a: load with schema validation in buildingSMART's ifcx-core without errors or cycles; b: correct tree, geometry and colours in the R2 viewer), and NFR-MNT-003 makes the reference models' IFCX output the golden file. Written RM-M and RM-L files are expected in the range of a hundred to several hundred megabytes (about 2 and 8 million triangles), beyond GitHub's 100 MB file limit and too large to diff, so byte goldens like tests/golden/*.ifcx do not scale. The criterion benches of regression-and-status-16 measure the NFR-PERF-002 quantities (open, save, evaluate) only on provisional stand-ins; every tuning task of this epic needs RM-M/RM-L numbers and a recorded baseline.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs gains --large, writing rm-m.ifcx and rm-l.ifcx with the fixed author, timestamp and dataVersion of the other goldens. crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/large/rm-m.json and rm-l.json are committed manifests (SHA-256 of the compact bytes, byte size, node count, element count per bsi::ifc::class and per storey, triangle count), checked by crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/large_models.rs (#[ignore], run with --release --ignored in a new large-models CI job), which also asserts the RM-M round trip; ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 rewrites the manifests. The job runs conformance/run.sh (ifcx-core, compose3 and the Playwright viewer step of regression-and-status-12) on rm-m.ifcx, the nightly job does the same for rm-l.ifcx, and check.ts gains expectations for five storeys, IfcCurtainWall with IfcMember and IfcPlate children, IfcStair with flights and door and window occurrences of shared types. bench_models() registers rm_m and rm_l (not flagged ci), so the regression-and-status-16 benches (crates/archicraft-ifcx/benches/ifcx.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/benches/geometry.rs) run on them; a new crates/archicraft-app/benches/scene.rs (criterion as a dev-dependency of archicraft-app) measures views::render3d::build_scene on the evaluated model, the CPU-side baseline for tasks 09 to 11; bench inputs are cached under target/bench-fixtures keyed by the manifest hash. A first full-mode bench run is committed as the baseline results file, and docs/testing.md documents the digest-golden convention. Out of scope: any performance change.
design:
sha2 as a dev-dependency of archicraft-ifcx (MIT/Apache-2.0; cargo deny check), recorded with its health check among the test tools of docs/technology-choices.md (principle 5: nothing added unrecorded). Manifests are pretty JSON with stable key order so pull requests show reviewable count diffs; the file itself is regenerable from the builder, which is the asset kept in the repository (SRS 7.3). The manifest triangle count is taken from the written meshes, not from ModelGeometry, so it also catches writer regressions.

Conformance: run Node with --max-old-space-size=8192. If rm-l.ifcx exceeds V8's maximum string length (about 512 MiB), JSON.parse fails: then parse it with a streaming JSON parser (stream-json, MIT) into the same object before handing it to ifcx-core and the viewer harness, and document the deviation in conformance/README.md. CI: the large-models job runs on ubuntu with a cached release build and a target under 15 minutes; RM-L conformance runs nightly only.

Pitfalls: the builder is the single source of manifest and bench inputs, so cache keys must include the manifest hash, otherwise stale bench inputs survive a builder change. Pointers: examples/reference_models.rs:24-35, tests/roundtrip.rs:193-232, conformance/run.sh:12-16, conformance/check.ts:67-103, .github/workflows/ci.yml:51-69, samples::bench_models (regression-and-status-16).
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo test --release -p archicraft-ifcx --test large_models -- --ignored` passes: the written RM-M and RM-L bytes match their manifests, and two consecutive writes are byte-identical (IFX-007).
- RM-M round trip: the loaded project equals the built one (assert_eq as in round_trip_restores_the_editable_model) and re-saving yields identical bytes.
- A deliberate builder change (one wall thickness) fails the manifest test with a readable diff of the counts and writes the new file and manifest under target/large-golden/ for review.
- conformance/run.sh passes on rm-m.ifcx in the large-models job (schema validation without errors or cycles; tree project/site/building/five storeys; bodies and material colours found by the viewer step) and on rm-l.ifcx in the nightly job.
- bench_models() lists rm_m and rm_l; `cargo bench -p archicraft-ifcx -p archicraft-geometry -p archicraft-app -- rm_m` runs ifcx/load, ifcx/save, ifcx/save_indented and ifcx/validate, the geometry benches evaluate, plan (per storey) and edit_then_evaluate, and the new scene/build bench; the CI smoke gate of regression-and-status-18 excludes them and stays under 10 minutes.
- docs/performance/<date>-dev-<name>-baseline.md records these numbers plus the file sizes of RM-M and RM-L; docs/testing.md explains manifests, blessing and the large-models job.
- Satisfies the epic clause "RM-M and RM-L golden files pass IFX-006" (re-checked by the exit task) and provides the NFR-PERF-002 baseline.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-002
Related (owned elsewhere): IFX-006, IFX-007, NFR-MNT-003. Open question for the product owner: Git LFS for the full files instead of digest manifests, if the files themselves must live in the repository.

title: Add the library manager, moved-folder relink and the upgrade offer
description:
WHY: OBJ-007 (S) requires linking library folders, re-pointing a moved library, unlinking without losing instance references and a user-controllable precedence with duplicates reported; OBJ-008 (S) requires the system to offer upgrades when newer versions of used definitions are available. The epic acceptance: relinking a moved library folder restores instances. Task 07 delivered the model, resolution and file format and task 22 the upgrade detection and UpgradeDefinition; nothing reads folders or shows libraries yet.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/library.rs: LibraryLoader scans a linked folder recursively for *.ifcx in sorted path order through archicraft_ifcx::read_library, resolves locations relative to the project file, records problems per file and produces LoadedLibrary values; it runs at project open, after LinkLibrary or RepointLibrary and on Rescan, and hands Document a new Arc<CatalogueSet> with a bumped generation. ui/dialogs.rs: a 'Libraries' window (Project > Libraries...) with rows in precedence order showing status ('42 definitions', 'Missing: folder not found at <path>', 'Invalid: <reason>'), Move up and Move down (ReorderLibraries), Link folder... (rfd folder picker), Re-point..., Unlink (with the note 'Instances keep their definitions'), Rescan, a Duplicates section and an Updates section listing available_upgrades with instance counts, 'Review...' showing the UpgradeReport and 'Upgrade all' / 'Upgrade selected instances' executing UpgradeDefinition. The offer: after open and after a rescan, a non-modal status-bar notice 'Newer versions of N definitions are available' opens the window; a library missing at open shows a notice with Re-point.... The missing-definitions window of components-dw-catalogue-12 shows the reason 'Library <name> not found' with a Re-point button. Out of scope: saving components into libraries (11).
design: Keep file-system access in the app crate (persistence/), the model and geometry only see the CatalogueSet. Scanning is synchronous on explicit actions and at open; if profiling shows long scans, move it to a background thread that posts the result (the Autosaver thread pattern in persistence/autosave.rs). The notice is non-modal to avoid nagging (NFR-USE). Native folder pickers block the UI thread like the existing file dialogs (known debt, app.rs:197-208); do not make it worse with repeated pickers. Pitfalls: compare library identity by LibraryId, never by path; a folder containing two files with the same LibraryId is a duplicate library, reported, first path wins; relative locations must be recomputed after Save As to another folder. Pointers: ui/dialogs.rs 'Add a dialog' recipe, :848-883 problems panel, document.rs, app.rs open_path, missing-definitions window (components-dw-catalogue-12).
acceptance_criteria:
- Integration test crates/archicraft-app/tests/library.rs (headless, temporary directory): write a library with definition D, link it, place an instance, save the project with the embedded copy stripped (fixture helper), move the folder and reopen: the library is Missing and the instance is a listed placeholder; RepointLibrary to the new folder resolves the instance and the placeholder disappears.
- Same test with the embedded copy kept: the instance stays resolved while the folder is missing, and the library association and upgrade detection return after re-pointing.
- A library containing D v2 produces the notice text; upgrading from the window moves the instances to v2 and undo restores v1.
- kittest: the Libraries window opens from the Project menu, shows 'Missing' and a 'Re-point...' button for the moved library, and Move up reorders the rows (and the chosen source of a duplicate).
- Satisfies the user-facing parts of OBJ-007 and the offer of OBJ-008.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-007 OBJ-008
Also: OBJ-004, OBJ-006.

title: Keep RM-L below 4 GB: measure owners and trim memory
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-008 (S): memory use with RM-L open shall stay below 4 GB; minimum-class machines have 8 GB shared with the GPU. The gap row lists the pressure points: non-indexed f32 vertex arrays (addressed by task 09), the serde Value tree of the whole file on open and save (tasks 04 and 05), a full Project clone per autosave (task 07), per-face vertices in every TriMesh (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:40-56) and undo history holding full element clones (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:750-756); since then plan caches, the 3D pick index (3d-input-navigation-06), scene caches and level-of-detail proxies (task 11) were added. Nothing measures them. Exists (keep): one Arc<ModelGeometry> is shared by document, autosave and views (document.rs:29, autosave.rs:148), and the CPU scene data is dropped after upload (view3d.rs:211-214).

WHAT: A memory report under the perf feature (in the Performance window and the memory script of task 03) estimates bytes per owner: Project, History, ModelGeometry per kind, SceneCache and proxies, GPU buffers (tracked creation sizes, 3D and plan), plan caches, PickIndex, and IFCX buffers during load and save. Measure the peak physical footprint across the AS-07 RM-L sequence (open, all navigation scripts, edits, save, autosave) and reduce the largest owners until the peak is at most 3 GB on the developer machine, for example: drop CPU chunk data after upload when it can be rebuilt from geometry, build the pick index per storey on demand, bound plan caches by bytes, release IFCX input and raw buffers right after reading, store undo edits per changed element only. Out of scope: changing the global allocator; instanced rendering of shared door and window types (a follow-up bead if measurements require it).
design:
Estimates through a small HeapBytes trait implemented by hand for the big owners (no deepsize or get-size dependency); GPU bytes are the sum of buffer and texture sizes created by Renderer3d and the plan renderer. Measure the footprint after a 2 s settle because the allocator returns pages lazily. On Apple Silicon the physical footprint includes GPU allocations; on Windows integrated GPUs shared memory is only partly counted, so the protocol records the OS readings next to the in-app value. Geometry stays f64 (technology choices); sharing identical type meshes in memory is OBJ-011's concern and is revisited only through a bead.

Pointers: render3d.rs and plan_gpu.rs buffer creation, document.rs caches, command.rs:740-760 (History), archicraft-geometry mesh.rs and extrude.rs, perf/memory.rs (task 03).
acceptance_criteria:
- Owner estimates sum to within 25 % of the measured footprint growth after opening RM-M (perf-feature test).
- The memory script on RM-L reports a peak physical footprint of at most 3 GB on the developer machine for the whole sequence, recorded with the breakdown in docs/performance.
- Closing RM-L and opening two_storey_shell returns the footprint to within 300 MB of the level before RM-L was opened (release, #[ignore] leak check).
- 100 single-element edits on RM-L grow memory by less than 50 MB (history test).
- A normal-suite test on stand_in(20_000) asserts that the owner estimates per element stay within 20 % of recorded bounds, so later bloat fails visibly.
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-008

title: Reference models RM-M and RM-L, AS-07 and performance tuning
description:
Goal: Generate RM-M (five storeys, stairs, layered walls, curtain-wall entrance, about 5,000 elements) and RM-L (repeated RM-M blocks, about 20,000) in-process from the seeded builder, run the AS-07 protocol with the harness of regression-and-status on the two documented hardware classes (open and save timing, frame rates for orbit, pan, zoom and walk, plan navigation, edit latency, memory, autosave blocking) and tune level of detail, culling, indexed GPU buffers, plan caches, background open/save with progress and cancellation until every NFR-PERF target is met.

Risks: Targets may need rayon or the SQLite store (deferred candidates), added only after measuring; availability of minimum-class hardware (O-15 recorded in increment 1).
design: samples::rm_m() and rm_l(blocks) through the seeded builder (no out-of-process interface needed); criterion benches in benches/ extended to the reference models; views/render3d.rs indexed buffers, frustum culling and screen-size LOD; plan-renderer caches; open and save on worker threads with a progress channel (NFR-PERF-007); autosave snapshot as Arc<Project> clone-on-write.
acceptance_criteria: The AS-07 results file docs/performance/<date>-<machine>.md records every measurement on both reference machines with all Must targets met: RM-M opens in <= 10 s and saves in <= 5 s, RM-L opens in <= 30 s, >= 30 fps on RM-M, >= 20 fps on RM-L and >= 30 fps on RM-S on minimum hardware, plan navigation >= 30 fps, a single edit visible in <= 200 ms, no UI freeze over 1 s with progress and cancellation for long operations, RM-L under 4 GB, autosave blocking <= 200 ms; RM-M and RM-L golden files pass IFX-006; a kittest shows the progress dialog while opening RM-L and the viewport stays navigable during save.
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-003 NFR-PERF-004 NFR-PERF-007 NFR-PERF-008 NFR-PERF-009 VIEW-054

title: Paste across windows with the resource conflict dialog
description:
WHY: SW-003 (S) requires elements copied in one open project to be pasteable into another; PRF-009 (S) lets the user choose use existing, keep both or overwrite on name conflicts; PRJ-011 (S) opens projects in separate windows 'so that elements can be copied between them'. The epic acceptance: pasting a layered wall from one window into the other brings its structure, materials and profiles with the use-existing / keep-both / overwrite choice. Task 17 opened several windows and task 18 built the payload and conflict rules; the in-process clipboard fallback of selection-transforms-13 still lives in one Workspace.

WHAT: App-level clipboard ArchiCraftApp.clipboard: Option<ClipboardPayload> shared by all windows, plus the OS clipboard text with the marker 'archicraft-clipboard/2' through ctx.copy_text, so paste works across windows and across processes (the fallback of task 17); Event::Paste text is parsed when it carries the marker, otherwise the app-level payload is used. Paste and Paste at point in the target window compute the PastePlan; with conflicts an egui::Modal 'Paste: resolve conflicts' lists one row per conflict (kind, name, 'Clipboard: 680 mm, 6 skins' against 'This project: 365 mm, 3 skins', a choice of Use existing / Keep both / Overwrite, Overwrite rows warning how many target elements change), 'Apply to all of this kind', OK and Cancel; OK executes the paste command as one undo step, Cancel pastes nothing. The status line summarises the result ('Pasted 1 element; added 1 layer structure and 5 materials; kept both: Concrete (2)').
design: egui turns Cmd+C, Cmd+X and Cmd+V into Event::Copy, Event::Cut and Event::Paste(text) per viewport, so handle them inside each window's viewport closure and only when no text field has focus (selection-transforms-13 rule). The OS clipboard carries the full serialised payload so a second process (or a second instance on Wayland) can paste; very large payloads are still fine as text but log their size. Summaries come from the resources (total thickness and skin count for structures, shape and size for profiles, category and cut fill for materials) and are formatted through units.rs. Pitfalls: the modal belongs to the target window, not the root; never execute a paste while a modal of the same window is open; keep the payload free of file paths (selection-transforms-13). Pointers: clipboard.rs (tasks 18, selection-transforms-13), app.rs shortcuts and run(), window.rs (task 16), ui/dialogs.rs Modal pattern, workspace.rs status.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest with two embedded project windows: select the F2 wall in window A, Copy, focus window B (whose 'Concrete' was changed), Paste: the modal lists 'Concrete'; Keep both plus OK adds 'Concrete (2)' to B and B's history gains exactly one step 'Paste 1 element'.
- Cancel leaves B unchanged; Overwrite shows the affected-element count before OK.
- The OS clipboard text starts with the marker and pastes into a fresh harness (second-process simulation); pasting text without the marker does nothing and reports nothing.
- Headless test: the app-level clipboard is shared by all windows and survives closing the source window.
- Completes SW-003 and the user choice of PRF-009 across the windows of PRJ-011.
notes:
SRS: SW-003 PRF-009 PRJ-011
Also: EDT-016.

title: Render catalogue thumbnails and two-sided plan, elevation, 3D previews
description:
WHY: DW-014 (S) requires thumbnails and 'a preview in plan, elevation and 3D that can show either side'. The epic acceptance checks catalogue search and preview from both sides with kittest. Epic risk: GPU lifetimes across viewports, so thumbnails are textures owned by the per-window render state introduced in task 16 rather than by a global side channel.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/thumbnails.rs: a ThumbnailCache keyed by (DefinitionRef, TypeKey uuid of the default parameters, theme) rendering offscreen with Renderer3d into 128 x 128 textures (isometric camera fitted to the TypeGeometry bounds, flat shading with edges), at most four renders per frame with a placeholder while pending, an LRU limit of 256 entries, textures freed with the window's GPU state (task 16). The catalogue browser shows thumbnails in the result list and a preview pane with tabs Plan (the TypeGeometry symbol at the chosen detail level drawn with the plan painter helpers into a fitted rect, with the nominal size), Elevation (parallel projection from 3d-input-navigation's camera looking along the local -y or +y axis) and 3D (offscreen orbit by dragging). 'Show other side' flips the view direction of Elevation and 3D and the viewing side of the plan symbol, labelled Exterior/Interior for doors and windows and Front/Back for objects; the preview uses the definition defaults or, with instances selected, their parameters. Headless helpers in new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/preview.rs compute camera framing from bounds and the 2D symbol fit transform. Out of scope: library management (09), editable previews.
design: Reuse Renderer3d and GpuScene for one-definition scenes instead of a second renderer; build the scene from TypeGeometry parts in unit-local coordinates. Elevation is a parallel projection render, which is honest for a preview and avoids a hidden-line generator (sections-elevations-dims owns real elevations). The render budget keeps the frame time within NFR-PERF while the list scrolls. Pitfalls: never free a texture inside a paint callback while the renderer lock is held; textures belong to the window that displays them, so a second window has its own cache; kittest cannot render wgpu without the software adapter, so label and state tests carry the acceptance and the snapshot test needs the adapter configured in CI (plan-renderer is an increment-1 epic, complete before this increment). Pointers: views/render3d.rs:270-500 (offscreen targets, register_native_texture, free_viewport), views/camera.rs, views/plan.rs drawing helpers, ui/catalogue.rs (task 08), window GPU state (task 16).
acceptance_criteria:
- Framing tests: the fitted camera keeps the whole bounds in view; front and back directions are exactly opposite; the plan fit preserves the aspect ratio.
- ThumbnailCache tests with a fake renderer: pending entries become ready, no more than four renders run per frame, LRU eviction frees textures through the window's release path, and a definition change invalidates its entry.
- kittest: selecting 'Box' shows the preview with 'Plan', 'Elevation' and '3D' tabs; 'Show other side' switches the label from 'Front' to 'Back'; for 'Tilt-and-turn window' it switches from 'Exterior' to 'Interior'.
- A wgpu snapshot test on the software adapter configured by plan-renderer (with its documented per-pixel tolerance) shows that the elevation preview of an asymmetric definition differs between the two sides.
- kittest: every row of the result list shows its thumbnail image or the pending placeholder (checked for 'Box' and 'Tilt-and-turn window').
- Completes DW-014 together with task 08 (thumbnails, previews in plan, elevation and 3D, either side).
notes:
SRS: DW-014
Also: NFR-PERF frame budget; plan-renderer's software-adapter tolerance in docs/testing.md.

title: Expose on-canvas parameter handles for components
description:
WHY: OBJ-012 (C): 'Components may expose on-canvas handles for their main parameters (width, depth, height, arc rise).' Gap: missing (M), no on-canvas handles for any component; profiles-columns-beams-13 introduced crates/archicraft-app/src/views/handles.rs (MemberHandle with HandleRole::{ColumnTop, ColumnBottom, BeamStart, BeamEnd} and the HandleDrag consumer) and edit-reshape-palette-07 crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/handles.rs (plan part handles), which this task extends to component parameters.

WHAT: Model: ParameterSpec (components-dw-catalogue-01) gains `handle: Option<ParamHandleRole { Width, Depth, Height, ArcRise }>` (serde default None; named so it does not collide with the member HandleRole), set on the box, cylinder (diameter as Width with Depth tied) and the shared Size kit of the furniture and fixture definitions (tasks 03 and 04), on the door and window width and height bindings, and on the rise of opening.arched. Geometry: new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/handles.rs: component_handles(project, geometry, element) -> Vec<ParamHandle { role, key, position: DVec3, direction: DVec3, value }> from the instance transform and the type layout (Width at the local +x face centre, Depth at +y, Height at the top centre, ArcRise at the arch apex), and the pure mapping drag_to_value(handle, cursor or ray) -> (value, placement adjustment) that keeps the opposite face fixed for objects (the insertion point moves when the origin is centred). Model command `ResizeComponent { id, key, value, insertion }` so value and compensating move are one undo step; doors and windows map width changes to ResizeInserts of doors-windows-core-02, so the DW-005 anchor rule decides which jamb stays. App: handles drawn and hit-tested for exactly one selected, unlocked instance: plan shows Width and Depth (and door or window jambs), 3D shows all roles through overlay3d; dragging uses the HandleDrag consumer (press-drag-release or click-click per preference, typed value plus Enter, Esc cancels), shows the live value and clamps to the parameter range with a status message. Out of scope: handles for non-component kinds, multi-element handle edits.
design: All interaction geometry lives in pure functions over model values (tested without egui); egui code only draws and routes pointer events, as in profiles-columns-beams-13. Handle positions come from the type layout, not from the mesh, so they are exact and cheap. Hit radius 8 px (D.1). Pick handles before element picking so a handle press does not change the selection. Coordination: if edit-reshape-palette's plan handles and the member handles already share a hit-testing module, add ParamHandle to it instead of a third list. Pitfalls: a mirrored instance flips the local +x direction; tied parameters (cylinder diameter) update both keys in one command; locked elements show no handles (ELM-013). Pointers: views/handles.rs and overlay3d (profiles-columns-beams-12/13), components/types.rs layout (components-dw-catalogue-07), ResizeInserts (doors-windows-core-02).
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure tests: dragging the Width handle of a box rotated by 30 degrees by +0.2 m along its local x increases width by 0.2 and keeps the opposite face fixed in world coordinates within 1e-9; the Height handle maps a 3D ray to the new height on the vertical drag plane.
- Dragging the ArcRise handle of an arched opening changes rise and the void follows (geometry test on the host volume).
- A door with anchor AlongStart keeps its start jamb when the width handle is dragged; with anchor Centre both jambs move.
- A value outside the parameter range clamps to the limit and the status line names the range.
- Each completed drag is exactly one undo step; Esc during a drag leaves the project unchanged.
- Satisfies OBJ-012.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-012
Could requirement: cut first if the epic runs late.

title: Verify exit criterion: Reference models RM-M and RM-L, AS-07 and performance tuning
description:
WHY: Closes the epic. AS-07 must pass for the increment-4 exit (Appendix F: AS-07 and AS-08 pass; release candidate) and for v1 acceptance (SRS 7.2). The epic covers NFR-PERF-002, NFR-PERF-003, NFR-PERF-004, NFR-PERF-007, NFR-PERF-008, NFR-PERF-009 and VIEW-054, all partial or missing in docs/implementation-status.md before this epic.

WHAT: A checklist run on the merged branch, not new code: run the workspace quality gates with and without the perf feature, the large-models job (RM-M and RM-L manifests, round trip, conformance) and the named kittests; review the AS-07 results files of task 15 against every acceptance clause; update docs/implementation-status.md; close the epic in beads and link the follow-up beads filed by the tasks.
design: Use the gap-analysis rows of the covered IDs as the wording template and cite the results files by path. A failed Should row (NFR-PERF-008, NFR-PERF-009) is documented with the release decision instead of blocking; a failed Must row blocks closing.
acceptance_criteria:
- The AS-07 results file docs/performance/<date>-<machine>.md records every measurement on both reference machines with all Must targets met: RM-M opens in <= 10 s and saves in <= 5 s, RM-L opens in <= 30 s, >= 30 fps on RM-M (in the default shaded style with default view settings, no user simplification), >= 20 fps on RM-L and >= 30 fps on RM-S on minimum hardware, plan navigation >= 30 fps, a single edit visible in <= 200 ms, no UI freeze over 1 s with progress and cancellation for long operations, RM-L under 4 GB, autosave blocking <= 200 ms.
- RM-M and RM-L golden files pass IFX-006 (large-models job and nightly conformance green).
- A kittest shows the progress dialog while opening RM-L (opening_rm_l_shows_progress) and the viewport stays navigable during save (the gated save kittest of task 07).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green, with and without --features perf.
- conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (NFR-PERF-002, NFR-PERF-003, NFR-PERF-004, NFR-PERF-007, NFR-PERF-008, NFR-PERF-009, VIEW-054) with file:line and results-file evidence, plus the AS-07 row and the RM-M/RM-L reference-model rows.
- The epic perf-tuning-rm-m-l is closed in beads; follow-up beads filed by tasks 06, 10, 14 and 15 are linked.
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-003 NFR-PERF-004 NFR-PERF-007 NFR-PERF-008 NFR-PERF-009 VIEW-054

title: Open files on a worker with a progress dialog and cancel
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-007: opening may block viewport navigation, but the UI shall not freeze for more than 1 s and shall show progress; opening does not change the current model, so it is cancellable and the current document must survive a cancel. NFR-PERF-002: RM-M opens in at most 10 s and RM-L in at most 30 s, measured to the first interactive frame. The epic acceptance asks for a kittest showing the progress dialog while opening RM-L. Today open_path reads, parses, validates, reads and evaluates on the UI thread (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:152-179), Document::new evaluates the whole model (document.rs:35), and the first plan and 3D scene are then built synchronously inside the first frame.

WHAT: open_path (menu, recent list, command-line path at startup, drag-and-drop and recovery) starts an Open job on the JobRunner of task 07: read the file, load_with (task 05), build the Document with evaluate_with (and the parallel stage of task 06), and prebuild the active storey's plan and the 3D SceneData (views/render3d.rs build_scene) on the worker; task 10 replaces the SceneData with per-chunk CPU data built in the same place. A modal window "Opening <file>" shows the phase (Reading, Checking, Building model, Generating geometry, Preparing views), a progress bar and Cancel; the current document stays visible and unchanged until the job finishes; success replaces the document and shows the load report (PRJ-008) as today; cancel or error keep the previous document. The unsaved-changes guard and the newer-format confirmation keep their order (guard first, then the job). Out of scope: GPU upload pacing (task 10), saving (task 07).
design:
The Document is built entirely on the worker and moved to the UI thread (Document and its caches are Send; assert it statically). The modal uses egui::Modal; while it is open, shortcuts are suspended except Esc (Cancel). load_with and evaluate_with poll the cancel flag; the worker drops partial results. replace_document still runs on the UI thread because releasing GPU textures needs the render state (app.rs:142-149, ArchiCraftApp.released). An Open requested during a running save waits for it (task 07); prefs.add_recent runs only after success. The kittest harness gets a helper that steps until the app reports no running job.

Pitfalls: drop the read buffer right after parsing to lower RM-L peak memory (task 14); errors from the worker carry the path for the message; the load-report prompt must not appear for a cancelled job. Pointers: app.rs:140-180 (replace_document, open_path), 266-287 (Then::Recover), main.rs command-line argument, document.rs:33-66.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest with a gated Open job: the modal "Opening ..." with progress bar and Cancel is shown while the job runs, the panes behind it ignore input and the window keeps repainting (frame counter advances); Cancel keeps the previous document (same project id, not dirty) and no load report appears.
- kittest opening_rm_l_shows_progress (release, #[ignore], run in the large-models CI job with rm-l.ifcx of task 02): the dialog appears in the first frame after the request, its phase text advances, it closes when done, and the browser lists five storeys and the RM-L element count.
- A truncated file still yields today's message and keeps the previous document; a newer-format file still asks for confirmation; opening a recovered autosave uses the same job (tests adjusted).
- Startup with a path argument and opening from the recent list run through the job (harness tests).
- Release measurement with the open script: RM-M reaches the first interactive frame within 5 s and RM-L within 15 s on the developer machine (half of NFR-PERF-002), longest UI frame during opening under 250 ms; recorded in docs/performance.
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-007 NFR-PERF-002

title: Parallelise full geometry evaluation once measurements require it
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-002 (RM-L opens in at most 30 s) and NFR-PERF-007 (regenerating all geometry shows progress and must not freeze the UI) both include a full evaluation of the model. docs/technology-choices.md lists rayon as a deferred candidate to add "when mesh generation is measurably slow", and the epic risk repeats that deferred candidates are added only after measuring. After task 05 the evaluation phase is expected to dominate opening RM-L (about 8 million triangles from extrusions, triangulations, solid operations, curtain-wall sweeps and stair bodies).

WHAT: Measure the share of evaluation in opening RM-M and RM-L with the open script of task 03 and the evaluate bench. If evaluation exceeds 40 % of the NFR-PERF-002 budget on the developer machine (4 s for RM-M or 12 s for RM-L), add rayon to archicraft-geometry: a sequential stage computes everything that couples elements (junction footprints and relation-ordered inputs per storey), a parallel stage generates element bodies with catch_unwind per element, and results are inserted in ElementId order; evaluate_incremental uses the parallel stage when the dirty set exceeds 256 elements. The app runs evaluation on a dedicated pool of the available cores minus one, never on the UI thread, and docs/technology-choices.md moves rayon from the deferred table to the stack with the measurement. If evaluation stays below the threshold, the measurement is recorded and rayon stays deferred. Out of scope: parallel plan generation and scene assembly (only if task 15 measurements ask for them).
design:
Never depend on completion order: collect Vec<(ElementId, Result<ElementGeometry, String>)> and insert in sorted order, so the HashMap content and the BTreeMap of problems equal the sequential path. Junction resolution is order-independent per end (decision D-6), which is what makes the split possible. Build the pool with rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder (thread names evaluate-n) and call it from the job workers of tasks 07, 08 and 13, so rayon never borrows the UI thread. catch_unwind inside each closure (rayon would otherwise propagate the panic); keep panic=unwind.

Pitfalls: the per-element Arc<ElementGeometry> cache keyed by element revision (element-kind-framework-10) is updated after the parallel stage, not inside it; use one tracing span per stage, not per element. Pointers: archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:51-120 (catch_unwind at :69), wall.rs footprints, docs/technology-choices.md deferred table.
acceptance_criteria:
- The decision is recorded with sequential evaluate times and budget shares for RM-M and RM-L in docs/performance and, if rayon is added, in docs/technology-choices.md (licence MIT/Apache-2.0; cargo deny check passes).
- If parallel: ModelGeometry from the parallel path equals the sequential one bitwise (meshes and problems) for RM-M, every catalogue sample and 50 random incremental edit sequences on stand_in(5_000) (the property test of element-kind-framework-10 extended); ARCHICRAFT_THREADS=1 gives identical results.
- A deliberately panicking test kind inside the parallel stage still becomes a fallback box with a problem entry (the element-kind-framework-13 test passes).
- Solid operations run in the parallel stage only if the Manifold bindings are thread-safe (documented and checked by a stress test evaluating RM-M four times concurrently); otherwise those elements run in a sequential tail stage.
- The evaluate bench on RM-L is at least 2.5x faster on an 8-core machine (recorded).
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-007
Deferred-candidate rule in docs/technology-choices.md: 'Parallel mesh generation | rayon | Mesh generation is measurably slow'.
Estimate covers the expected parallel path (task 05 predicts evaluation dominates opening RM-L); if the measurement keeps rayon deferred, the task closes early.

title: Freeze a selection into a reusable frozen-geometry component definition
description:
WHY: OBJ-009 (S): 'A selection of model elements shall be saveable as a reusable component, choosing category, name, destination (project or library folder) and frozen geometry. All categories shall be choosable in the UI, and the component appears in the catalogue immediately.' Gap: missing (L), no copy or grouping of elements exists (command.rs:36-93). O-12 rules out user-authored parametric content in v1, so the saved component stores a frozen copy of the evaluated geometry; D-11 makes the library destination an .ifcx file. This task delivers the headless part (frozen definitions, the save command, freezing and persistence in project and library files); the dialog, the destinations and the immediate catalogue entry are task 20.

WHAT: Model, new crates/archicraft-model/src/components/frozen.rs: FrozenGeometry { parts: Vec<FrozenPart { role, material (Material parameter key), positions: Vec<[f64; 3]>, triangles: Vec<[u32; 3]> }>, symbol (plain polylines and arcs per detail level), extent } with validation (finite, indices in range, at most MAX_MESH_POINTS per part, every edge used twice); Definition.frozen: Option<FrozenGeometry> and the generator key 'frozen@1' in KNOWN_GENERATORS; ObjectOrientation Free (task 01); the default class follows the category (door IfcDoor, window IfcWindow, furniture and sanitary IfcFurniture, equipment and generic IfcBuildingElementProxy). Command::AddDefinition { definition } and Command::SaveSelectionAsComponent { definition, replace: Option<{ ids, object }> } inserting the definition, deleting the selection and adding one Object instance in one undo step; every ComponentCategory is accepted. Door and window categories get traits.insertable_as with fixed opening bindings equal to the frozen extent, so the door and window kinds of doors-windows-core place them with a rectangular void. Geometry, new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/frozen.rs: freeze(project, geometry, ids, origin) -> Result<FrozenGeometry, FreezeError> from world_parts (voids excluded, instances included) relative to the chosen origin, one Material parameter per distinct material defaulting to the source material, plan symbols from the projected outline (union of triangle projections with geo) for Simplified and the horizontal cut at the project cut-plane height (slice.rs) for Detailed; the 'frozen@1' generator emits the parts with their material slots. IFCX: the definition record codec (alpha/components.rs, components-dw-catalogue-08) gains an optional frozen member (mesh points through round_coordinate, triangles, roles, material keys), used by project files and by library files through write_library (task 07). Add a frozen instance to samples::objects() and re-bless objects.ifcx. Out of scope: the dialog and destinations (20), editing frozen geometry, parametric authoring (Section 8).
design: Freezing happens in archicraft-geometry because only it has evaluated meshes; the model command receives a finished Definition so it stays geometry-free and journal-replayable (NFR-MNT-001/002). One Material parameter per distinct source material keeps the frozen component recolourable without making it parametric. Frozen definitions are Free (task 01), so they can be tilted. Pitfalls: convert storey coordinates to the origin before writing, otherwise components saved on upper storeys float; the frozen mesh can exceed the IFX-038 point limit for large selections, so split parts at MAX_MESH_POINTS or refuse with a message; keep the frozen data out of the in-memory TypeKey canonicalisation (hash the definition id and version instead). Pointers: components/store.rs (components-dw-catalogue-02), alpha/components.rs (components-dw-catalogue-08), evaluate.rs world_parts (components-dw-catalogue-07), slice.rs, mesh.rs MAX_MESH_POINTS, alpha/library.rs (task 07), kinds/object.rs (task 01), the insert void path of doors-windows-core-03.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: SaveSelectionAsComponent with replace is one undo step and undo restores the original elements bit for bit and removes the definition; it accepts each of the six ComponentCategory::ALL values with the matching default class; frozen-geometry validation rejects NaN, out-of-range indices and open meshes.
- Geometry tests: freezing two joined walls and a slab gives closed parts whose total volume equals the evaluated volumes within 1e-9; an instance placed at the chosen origin reproduces the world vertex positions within 1e-9; overriding one material parameter changes only the parts of that material; a selection on an upper storey freezes relative to the origin (no floating component).
- A frozen definition with category Window placed as a window in a 300 mm wall cuts a rectangular void of its frozen extent through every skin (geometry test).
- A selection exceeding MAX_MESH_POINTS in one part is split into several parts or refused with a message, never written invalid (IFX-038).
- IFCX: a frozen definition round-trips equal in a project and in a library file (write_library/read_library of task 07); objects.ifcx with the frozen instance passes conformance/run.sh.
- Satisfies the headless part of OBJ-009 (frozen geometry, category, name, storage in project and library files); task 20 completes it.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-009
Also: O-12, D-11, IFX-038, OBJ-006.
Interpretation recorded in docs/components.md: 'frozen geometry' is the only v1 geometry mode for saved components (O-12); the dialog of task 20 states it instead of offering a choice.

title: Carry layer structures, profiles and materials in the clipboard
description:
WHY: PRF-009 (S): 'When elements are copied between projects, the layer structures, profiles and materials they reference shall be brought along. Name conflicts are resolved by the user's choice: use existing, keep both (rename), or overwrite.' SW-003 (S): elements copied in one open project shall be pasteable into another, together with their materials, layer structures and profiles (EDT-016, PRF-009). Gap rows: both missing (L). selection-transforms-13 delivered ClipboardPayload format 1 (elements, relations, layers, materials, source storey and bounds) whose paste maps resources by id and adds unknown ones; layer structures and profiles are not carried and there is no conflict handling. The epic acceptance requires tests on the headless payload. The object kind of task 01 carries an embedded definition, which the bundle must bring along too.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/clipboard.rs: payload format 2 with source: PayloadSource { project: ProjectId, name } and resources: ResourceBundle { materials, layer_structures, profiles, layers, definitions } collected transitively through the kind hooks (element materials, the layer structure of walls, slabs and roofs, profiles(), component() with its embedded definition; materials referenced by skins and profile regions included); format-1 payloads still paste. Project::paste_plan(payload, placement) -> PastePlan { conflicts: Vec<ResourceConflict { kind: Material | LayerStructure | Profile, source_id, name, target_id, source_summary, target_summary }> } with the matching rules: same id and equal content reuses silently; same id or same name (trimmed, case-insensitive) with different content is a conflict; otherwise the resource is added (with a new id if the id is taken). Project::paste(payload, placement, &Resolutions) -> Result<Command, CommandError> where every conflict maps to UseExisting, KeepBoth or Overwrite (a missing entry is CommandError::Invalid). Order: materials, then layer structures and profiles with their material references remapped, then definitions (an equal DefinitionRef is identical by construction, otherwise embedded), then layers (by name, added when missing, never a conflict), then the elements. KeepBoth inserts 'Name (2)' (next free number); Overwrite replaces the content and keeps the target id so every user in the target updates (PRF-002), and validates all affected target elements, refusing with a message when one becomes invalid. The whole paste is one undo step. Pasting into the source project keeps the format-1 behaviour. Out of scope: the dialog and cross-window transport (19).
design: Matching on id first and name second covers both cases that occur: projects created from the same template share resource ids, and projects created separately share names. Conflict detection is a pure function returning data, so the UI (task 19) and scripts use the same rules (NFR-MNT-001). Resolve materials first because structures and profiles reference them; resolutions therefore cascade (KeepBoth on a material makes the pasted structure reference the renamed copy). Pitfalls: content equality must ignore ids inside the compared resource but not referenced material identities after remapping; Overwrite must go through the existing Update* commands' validation so junctions and voids of target users re-evaluate; keep resource order deterministic (source order) for stable names. Pointers: clipboard.rs and Project::paste (selection-transforms-13), layer_structure.rs and UpdateLayerStructure (layer-structures-01), profile.rs and UpdateProfile (profiles-columns-beams-01), command.rs plan_delete_material for reference rewriting, components/store.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/paste_between_projects.rs with two projects from the seeded builder: copying the F2 wall (680 mm, six skins, Appendix D.7) from A into B, which lacks the structure, adds the structure and its materials to B and the pasted wall references them.
- With B's 'Concrete' changed, the conflict is listed; UseExisting maps the skins to B's Concrete; KeepBoth adds 'Concrete (2)' used by the pasted skins; Overwrite replaces B's Concrete, B's existing walls using it change (PRF-002), and undo restores B exactly.
- A column with a custom profile carries the profile and its region materials; an object carries its embedded definition; an Overwrite that would make a target element invalid is refused with a message and leaves B unchanged.
- A format-1 payload still pastes; a missing resolution returns CommandError::Invalid with B unchanged; a format-2 payload round-trips through serde_json.
- Satisfies the headless part of PRF-009 and SW-003 (resources carried, three-way conflict resolution).
notes:
SRS: PRF-009 SW-003
Also: EDT-016, PRF-002.
The epic acceptance names profiles for a layered wall; profiled walls arrive with PRF-010 (members-profiles-adv), so the test pastes the wall together with a profiled column.

title: Regenerate all geometry in the background with progress
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-007 (M) names regenerating all geometry among the operations that shall show progress and shall not block viewport navigation, and those that do not change the model shall be cancellable. Project-wide edits (a layer structure used by every wall, a material priority, a storey height under linked elements, the tessellation settings of IFX-034, the regenerate choice of IFX-065) dirty thousands of elements; on RM-L, evaluate_incremental for all of them runs synchronously in Document::geometry() on the UI thread (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103) and can exceed 1 s.

WHAT: Document::geometry() estimates the cost of the dirty set from per-kind evaluation timings kept by ModelGeometry; above a threshold (proposal: an estimate over 150 ms) it starts a Regenerate job on the snapshot (task 07) and returns the previous geometry marked stale. Views keep drawing the previous geometry with the plan and scene of its own revision and stay navigable; the status bar shows "Regenerating geometry n/m" with progress; a finished job is swapped in if the revision still matches, otherwise its result becomes the base for an incremental pass over the newer dirty set. Editing stays possible. A new View action "Regenerate all geometry" re-evaluates every element as a cancellable job; cancelling keeps the current geometry because the model is unchanged. Implicit regeneration after an edit belongs to a model-changing command and shows progress without a Cancel button. Save and autosave of a stale snapshot evaluate on their own worker (task 07). The perf feature gains a regenerate script (the explicit action on RM-L while the orbit script keeps the 3D view moving), and scripts/as07.py gains the rows 'longest frame during regeneration' (<= 1 s, Must) and '3D frame rate during regeneration' (recorded), so the regeneration clause of NFR-PERF-007 is measured in AS-07 (task 15). Out of scope: what counts as dirty (element-kind-framework-10).
design:
Keep stale geometry together with the project snapshot it was evaluated from, because plan_drawing and build_scene need a matching project and geometry; panes draw from that pair until the swap, while the properties panel and commands use the current project. Cost model: the per-kind mean evaluation time from the last full evaluation times the dirty counts; before the first measurement fall back to an element count over 1,000.

Pitfalls: the selection may name elements deleted in the newer revision, so prune it against the current project; an undo during a job is just another edit; at most one Regenerate job runs, newer requests replace queued ones. Pointers: document.rs:95-121, archicraft-geometry evaluate.rs (evaluate_incremental), jobs.rs (task 07), ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs View menu, app.rs run().
acceptance_criteria:
- On RM-L, changing the exterior wall structure returns within 50 ms of UI time with stale geometry and a running Regenerate job; afterwards the geometry equals a synchronous full evaluation bitwise and its revision matches the project.
- Property test on stand_in(5_000) with forced background mode: two or three random edits during a running job end with geometry equal to a full evaluation of the final project.
- kittest with a gated Regenerate job: progress shows in the status bar and camera navigation works; the explicit action shows Cancel, and Cancel keeps the previous geometry and leaves the History state id unchanged.
- Picking and selection on stale geometry never return or keep deleted elements.
- A single wall move on RM-M stays synchronous (no job; the edit script of task 03 is unchanged).
- `python3 scripts/as07.py --quick` includes the regeneration rows; on RM-L no frame exceeds 250 ms during the explicit regeneration on the developer machine (recorded in docs/performance).
- The action has a label, a View menu entry and no default shortcut (the Appendix D.8 uniqueness test passes).
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-007

title: Write corner windows to IFCX and add the corner window tool
description:
WHY: DW-016 (S) requires options a type does not support to be shown disabled with the reason and the corner window to be placeable at the junction of two walls; DW-023 (C) adds the frameless option. DW-018 writes windows as IfcWindow occurrences with a Void child and shared types; IFX-033 requires exported host bodies to have the volume removed. Task 13 delivered the kind, the host cuts and the void, and task 21 the units, key points and per-leg derived values; nothing persists or places it yet. DW-015 applies to corner windows too, so the inspector shows their derived values.

WHAT: IFCX: the archicraft::cornerWindow codec (legs, height, vertical pin, reveal, connection, angles, both host ids) through the per-kind codec registry; one IfcWindow occurrence written as a child of the leg-0 host with a proper-rotation usd::xformop at the outer corner, inherits.type to its type node, an invisible Void child (the union mesh) and IsExternal; FORMAT_VERSION bump with a migration step; the reader restores both Host edges and skips a corner window whose second host is missing with a warning naming it. Sample samples::corner_windows() with frame, post and frameless variants on template walls, golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/corner-windows.ifcx. App: new crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/corner_window.rs: ToolKind::CornerWindow on the PointInput service; hover finds L junctions of the active storey within the pick tolerance and highlights both walls and the corner; a click places the default unit, then typed or dragged leg widths; without a corner the prompt says 'Corner windows need two walls joined at an L corner' and nothing is created. Inspector: legs, height, vertical pin, reveal, the connection choice (Frame, Corner post, Frameless mitred glass) with unsupported options disabled and the CornerSupport reason as hover text and an inline note, per-side angles with 'Match junction', the schema parameters per leg, and the read-only DW-015 rows per leg (sill and head elevation, nominal size, clear opening width and height) from insert_derived (task 21). Action::ToolCornerWindow, toolbox and Design menu.
design: Writing one occurrence under the first host keeps the IFCX tree a tree (Table 5-1 hosts children under one wall); the second host is named in the archicraft attribute and its body is cut in geometry, which is all IFX-033 needs. Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe and the type writer of components-dw-catalogue-09. The tool reuses the host-candidate highlighting of doors-windows-core-07 but searches junctions instead of walls. Disabled-with-reason uses CornerSupport::check so model and UI agree; egui shows the reason with on_disabled_hover_text. Pitfalls: child keys stay unique when a wall hosts several units (child_key, writer.rs:56); the reader must not depend on node order when the second host appears later in the file. Pointers: alpha/writer.rs:243-418, alpha/reader.rs, alpha/types.rs, alpha/migrate.rs, tools/insert.rs (doors-windows-core-07), ui/properties.rs, conformance/check.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- corner-windows.ifcx round-trips equal and passes conformance/run.sh: the occurrence is a child of its first host, the Void child is invisible and closed, no transform has a negative determinant, and both host bodies already have the volume removed (IFX-033).
- Reader test: removing the second host from the file skips the corner window with a warning naming it; the rest loads.
- Tool state-machine tests: hovering near an L corner selects it, a click creates one corner window, clicking a straight wall away from corners creates nothing and sets the prompt text.
- kittest: for window.corner with a side-hung sash next to the corner, 'Frameless mitred glass' is disabled and its hover text contains the reason; choosing 'Corner post' adds exactly one undo step.
- kittest: a selected corner window shows a read-only 'Clear opening width' row for each leg.
- Completes DW-016 and DW-023 (persistence, placement, disabled-with-reason options).
notes:
SRS: DW-016 DW-023
Also: DW-015 (corner window rows), DW-018, IFX-033, IFX-036, IFX-050, Table 5-1.
Defaults (design decision, D.2-aligned): legs 1.20 m each, height 1.40 m, sill 0.90 m above the storey, frame connection.
Open question: whether consumers expect two Void children (one per host); one closed union Void is written (IFX-036).

title: Add the Save as component dialog with project and library destinations
description:
WHY: OBJ-009 (S): 'A selection of model elements shall be saveable as a reusable component, choosing category, name, destination (project or library folder) and frozen geometry. All categories shall be choosable in the UI, and the component appears in the catalogue immediately.' The epic acceptance: a selection saved as a component appears in the catalogue immediately. Task 11 delivers the frozen definition, freeze() and SaveSelectionAsComponent; task 08 the catalogue browser whose listing is keyed on (project revision, library generation); task 09 the LibraryLoader, linking and rescans. Nothing lets the user save a component yet.

WHAT: App: 'Save selection as component...' (Edit menu and the plan and 3D context menus, Action::SaveAsComponent, enabled for a non-empty selection) opens a dialog in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs with Name (required, unique within the destination), Category (all six ComponentCategory::ALL values), Group (free text with suggestions from existing groups), Insertion point (nine anchors of the selection's base bounds, or Pick point through the PointInput service), Destination (This project, each linked library, or 'Choose folder...' which links the folder through LinkLibrary), 'Replace selection with an instance', and the note 'Geometry is frozen: later edits to the elements do not change the component' (the frozen-geometry choice of OBJ-009 under O-12). OK runs freeze() of task 11 and then either executes SaveSelectionAsComponent (destination This project) or, for a library destination, writes <folder>/<sanitised name>.ifcx through write_library (task 07) atomically via crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/mod.rs, rescans that library synchronously through LibraryLoader (task 09) so the CatalogueSet generation bumps before the next frame, and executes SaveSelectionAsComponent with the definition embedded only when 'Replace selection' needs an instance (OBJ-006). Freeze errors (empty selection, point limit) and name clashes show inline; an existing file is never overwritten without confirmation. After OK the catalogue browser reveals and highlights the new entry. Out of scope: editing frozen geometry, parametric authoring (Section 8).
design: 'Appears immediately' is guaranteed by keying the catalogue listing on (revision, library generation) and bumping the generation synchronously after the write and rescan. Library writes reuse the atomic save with backups of persistence/mod.rs. The dialog never computes geometry itself: freeze() of task 11 is the only path, so the dialog and scripted saves produce identical definitions. Pitfalls: sanitise file names (path separators, reserved Windows names, trailing dots); after 'Choose folder...' store the location relative to the project file when possible (task 07 rule); native folder pickers block the UI thread like the existing file dialogs (app.rs:197-208), so open at most one; never rescan libraries other than the destination. Pointers: ui/dialogs.rs 'Add a dialog' recipe, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs Edit menu, persistence/mod.rs, persistence/library.rs (task 09), ui/catalogue.rs (task 08), components/frozen.rs (task 11), tools/object.rs (task 05).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: the dialog's Category choice lists Door, Window, Furniture, Sanitary, Equipment and Generic; after OK with destination 'This project' the catalogue browser lists the new name under its category in the next frame without reopening anything.
- Integration test in crates/archicraft-app/tests/library.rs (temporary directory): with a linked library as destination the file <folder>/<name>.ifcx exists, read_library reads it back, and the browser lists the component with that library as its source in the same frame sequence; saving again under the same name asks before overwriting.
- kittest: a component saved with category Window is offered by the Window tool and placing it cuts a rectangular void of its frozen extent; one saved as Furniture is placed by the Object tool.
- 'Replace selection with an instance' removes the selected elements and adds one object at the chosen insertion point in one undo step; undo restores the elements.
- Satisfies OBJ-009 together with task 11 (category, name, destination, frozen geometry, all categories choosable in the UI, immediate catalogue entry).
notes:
SRS: OBJ-009
Also: O-12, D-11, OBJ-006, UI-012 (inline errors).

title: Speed up opening with one flatten pass and typed mesh validation
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-002 requires opening RM-M in at most 10 s and RM-L in at most 30 s; NFR-PERF-007 requires progress for opening (navigation may be blocked while a file is being opened) and, since opening does not change the current model, cancellation. The gap row names the hotspots: the file is parsed into a serde Value per attribute (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:324-333), the schema check walks every mesh point through the generic check_value (validate.rs:239-254), the file is flattened twice with full attribute clones (validate.rs:342 and alpha/reader.rs:737), and geometry is re-evaluated for the whole model when the Document is created (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:35). The stored meshes are needed only for validation and for the stored-versus-regenerated comparison of IFX-065 (ifcx-interop).

WHAT: archicraft-ifcx gains load_with(bytes, progress) -> Result<ReadOutcome, LoadError> (load() wraps it). Parsing keeps the known bulk attributes (usd::usdgeom::mesh, usd::usdgeom::basiscurves) as raw JSON (serde_json's raw_value feature is already enabled) and decodes them once into typed arrays; flatten borrows attributes instead of cloning and runs once, shared by validate and the reader; a typed validator for these attributes, equivalent to check_value against the bundled usd schema, runs when the attribute's schema is the bundled one (generic check_value otherwise, for example in third-party files); the IFX-065 comparison first compares digests of the stored and the regenerated rounded meshes and falls back to the 0.1 mm point comparison only on mismatch. Progress phases parse, validate, read and evaluate, with cancellation checks between phases and every 256 nodes. archicraft-geometry gains ModelGeometry::evaluate_with(project, progress) (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs; evaluate() wraps it with NoProgress, cancellation checked every 256 elements), and Document construction (document.rs:33-66) uses it. Out of scope: worker threads and the dialog (task 08), parallel evaluation (task 06).
design:
Container change: Node.attributes keeps Value for ordinary attributes and gains a raw variant for bulk ids (an Attr enum, or a parallel raw map), serialised back verbatim so that writing an opened third-party file stays lossless (preservation in ifcx-interop). Decode raw meshes once into a typed struct { points: Vec<[f64; 3]>, faceVertexIndices: Vec<u32> }; the validator and the IFX-065 comparison share it. Digests hash the f64 bits of points rounded to 1e-6 m (json::round_coordinate) and the indices, so an unchanged ArchiCraft file matches without per-point tolerance checks. Typed error messages must equal the generic ones because problem lists are compared in tests. Flatten with lifetimes (FlatNode<'a>) over the parsed file; the reader takes the flattened map from the validator instead of calling flatten again.

Pitfalls: Box<RawValue> copies the slice while &RawValue borrows the input buffer; prefer borrowing and drop the bytes after reading to lower RM-L peak memory; keep serde_json's recursion limit (D.9 nesting) on; the node progress total is the length of the data array. If RM-L open still misses 30 s on reference hardware after this task and task 06, the deferred SQLite store is evaluated in a separate bead with the measurements (epic risk). Pointers: validate.rs:239-360, container.rs (Node), alpha/reader.rs:728-745 and 840-880, lib.rs:42-52, document.rs:20-60.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equivalence: for every golden file, the RM-M file, the corrupted fixtures of regression-and-status (PRJ-008) and the fetched third-party examples (ifcx-interop), load_with returns the same project and the same problems (severity, path, message, order) as before.
- Property test: mutated mesh and curve attributes (wrong arity, strings, negative or fractional indices, missing keys) get the same verdict and message from the typed and the generic validator.
- The fuzz targets build and the seed corpus replays without a crash; the Appendix D.9 limits still apply before the full parse.
- IFX-065: an RM-M file with one point moved by 0.5 mm reports exactly that element as deviating; the unmodified file reports none.
- Cancelling during the read phase returns Cancelled without a partial project; phases arrive in order with totals.
- Bench ifcx/load/rm_m and the open script of task 03: RM-M parse, validate, read and evaluate at least 2x faster than the task-02 baseline; RM-L open time and peak memory recorded in docs/performance.
- Round-trip, lenient-reading and golden tests and the conformance job unchanged.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-007
Related: IFX-065 (ifcx-interop); NFR-SEC-003 and Appendix D.9 limits (2 GB, JSON nesting below 128, composition depth 64, 32 imports).

title: Upload the 3D scene as compact indexed buffers
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-003 requires >= 30 frames/s on RM-M (target 60), >= 20 on RM-L and >= 30 for RM-S on minimum hardware (Iris Xe, Apple M1 with 8 GB); VIEW-054 requires that 3D views meet these targets automatically; NFR-PERF-008 caps RM-L at 4 GB. The gap row: vertices are non-indexed, 40 B each (position, normal and colour as f32), three per triangle plus two per feature edge (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:58-64, 151-172), about 240 MB for RM-M and 1 GB for RM-L on the GPU and as much again on the CPU while building; the selection colour is baked into vertices, so a selection change rebuilds and re-uploads the scene (views/view3d.rs:203-214). element-kind-framework-11 moved recolouring to assembly time and keeps per-element blocks in f64, but the upload is still whole.

Exists (keep and regress): the scene stays GPU-resident and is uploaded only when the SceneKey changes (workspace.rs:44, view3d.rs:203-214), a frame is re-rendered only when the FrameKey changes (render3d.rs:235, 500-520), and positions are relative to a local origin (render3d.rs:7, 121).

WHAT: render3d.rs gets a compact 24 B vertex (position as f32 relative to a local origin, normal octahedron-encoded as snorm16x2, material colour as unorm8x4, the u32 pick slot of selection-transforms-06) with u32 index buffers; vertices are shared within each planar face (identical position and normal per part); feature edges become indexed line lists. Selection and hover move to the per-element state buffer (the ElementView flags of 3d-view-restrictions-04 gain selected and hovered bits; the hover uniform of selection-transforms-06 is folded in), so selection or hover changes never write vertex or index buffers. The SceneCache blocks of element-kind-framework-11 store this compact form relative to each block's f64 origin. All pipelines (fill, transparent, lines, id pass, stencil caps and shadows where present) use the new layout. Out of scope: chunking and culling (task 10), level of detail (task 11).
design:
Positions stay precise because each block keeps its f64 origin and assembly converts to f32 relative to the chunk or scene origin (the local-origin rule of render3d.rs:121). Octahedron normal encoding after Cigolle et al. (2014), decoded in vs_main. VertexFormat::Snorm16x2, Unorm8x4 and Uint32 are core formats on Metal, DX12 and Vulkan. Flag bits SELECTED = 1 << 4 and HOVERED = 1 << 5 in ElementView.flags; the shader mixes SELECTION_COLOR and the hover tint.

Pitfalls: never merge vertices across a sharp edge (different normals stay separate, so flat shading is unchanged); transparent parts stay in their own buffer; keep the eframe::egui_wgpu::wgpu re-export; the id pass needs the pick-slot attribute at the same location. Pointers: render3d.rs:58-200 (Vertex, build_scene, upload), 270-380 (pipelines), views/shader.wgsl, view3d.rs:195-220, workspace.rs SceneKey.
acceptance_criteria:
- The headless 3D goldens (3d-view-restrictions-03, and the 3d-display-styles snapshots on RM-S) are unchanged within the documented tolerance for every display mode and for selected and hovered elements.
- Unit tests: octahedron encoding keeps 10,000 random normals within 0.001 rad; a box part yields 24 vertices, 36 indices and 12 indexed edges; the pick-slot decoding tests of selection-transforms-06 pass.
- On RM-M a selection change writes zero vertex or index bytes (upload counter), only the state buffer.
- GPU vertex plus index bytes per RM-M triangle at most 30 (previously about 120), CPU scene-cache bytes per triangle at most 30; RM-M and RM-L totals from the scene statistics recorded in docs/performance.
- RM-M orbit frame time (task 03 script) is not slower than the baseline.
notes: SRS: NFR-PERF-003 NFR-PERF-008 VIEW-054

title: Save and autosave from document snapshots on worker threads
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-007 (M): the user interface shall not freeze for longer than 1 s; saving and exporting shall show progress, shall not block viewport navigation and, because they do not change the model, shall be cancellable. NFR-PERF-009 (S): autosave (PRJ-004) shall not block interaction for more than 200 ms on RM-M. NFR-PERF-002: RM-M saves in at most 5 s. Today Save serialises, writes and copies the backup on the UI thread with no progress (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:214-235), and an autosave request clones the whole Project on the UI thread (persistence/autosave.rs:205) and may trigger a full geometry evaluation when the geometry is stale (app.rs:503). Exists (keep and regress): the Autosaver already writes on its own thread and coalesces pending snapshots (persistence/autosave.rs:153-224), and the backup rotation and atomic rename of save_atomically (persistence/mod.rs:70-110) satisfy NFR-REL-001/-003; only the UI-thread side changes. The epic design asks for an Arc<Project> clone-on-write snapshot; the epic acceptance asks for a kittest showing that the viewport stays navigable during save.

WHAT: document.rs: Document.project becomes Arc<Project>; execute, undo and redo mutate through Arc::make_mut, which copies only while a worker still holds a snapshot; Document::snapshot() returns { project, geometry if current, state id, revision } in O(1). New crates/archicraft-app/src/jobs.rs: a JobRunner with named worker threads and jobs { kind (Save, SaveAs, Autosave; later Open and Regenerate), label, JobProgress (atomic phase, done, total and cancel flag; implements archicraft_model's Progress), completion channel }, polled once per frame. Save, Save As and any IFCX export variant (Action::ExportVisible, 'Export visible elements only', of solid-kernel-ops-10) run as jobs: the worker evaluates geometry for the snapshot if needed and calls save_atomically_with with save_to_writer (task 04); on success the document records the snapshot's state id, so edits made during the save keep it dirty; the status bar shows label, progress and Cancel; a Save while one runs is coalesced; Close, Quit or Open during a save show a modal "Finishing save" with progress and wait. Autosave hands the snapshot to the Autosaver (no clone, no evaluation on the UI thread) and writes with the streaming writer; the recovery format is unchanged. Out of scope: opening (task 08), regeneration (task 13), the native file dialogs (they stay synchronous before the job starts).
design:
Arc::make_mut keeps all read sites unchanged (ws.doc.project.x works through Deref); History::execute receives Arc::make_mut(&mut self.project). Progress crosses threads through atomics read by the UI each frame plus one completion message; request_repaint_after(50 ms) while jobs run. The JobRunner allows at most one write job per target path; autosave keeps its own worker thread with the new input. Session::clear() runs when the save completes, not when it starts; on_exit waits for running saves behind a progress modal with a timeout log.

Pitfalls: never call Document::geometry() on the UI thread in the save path; a stale snapshot is evaluated on the worker (with the parallel stage of task 06 if present); a save that fails after the user edited must not mark anything saved; the overwrite-newer prompt and the Save As dialog run before the job is queued. Pointers: app.rs:186-235 (save), 497-515 (autosave), persistence/autosave.rs:145-224, document.rs:20-125, persistence/mod.rs:70-110, workspace.rs execute.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document tests: a snapshot shares the project (Arc::ptr_eq) until the next edit, which copies once and leaves the snapshot unchanged; saved_to with an older state id keeps is_dirty() true; dirty_tracking_follows_undo still passes.
- Job tests: progress is visible through JobProgress; cancelling before the final rename leaves the original and its backups byte-identical and removes the temp file; a failing write shows the same message as today (failed_save_leaves_the_original still passes); two queued saves write once, from the newest snapshot.
- kittest with a save job gated by a test barrier: the status bar shows "Saving <name>" with a progress bar and a Cancel button; dragging in the plan pane and in the 3D pane changes their camera state; an edit made during the save is accepted and the title shows unsaved changes after completion; Cancel leaves the file on disk unchanged.
- Export: Action::ExportVisible (solid-kernel-ops-10) runs through the same job path; a job test shows its progress and Cancel, a cancelled export leaves the target path untouched, and the document path, dirty flag and dataVersion stay unchanged.
- Release tests (#[ignore], perf feature) on RM-M: the autosave request costs at most 20 ms of UI-thread time and no frame during the autosave write exceeds 200 ms (NFR-PERF-009 with margin); Save completes within 2.5 s on the developer machine with no frame over 100 ms (half of the 5 s of NFR-PERF-002).
- The AS-05 automation and the autosave tests of regression-and-status still pass; recovery files stay compatible.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-007 NFR-PERF-009 NFR-PERF-002
Appendix D.1: autosave every 5 minutes, 1 backup version. IFCX is the only file format (D-11), so 'exporting' means any IFCX export variant (IFX-068's optional visible-only export).

title: Open projects in separate native windows
description:
WHY: PRJ-011 (S) requires at least two projects open at the same time in separate windows; PRJ-003 requires each window title to show its project name and unsaved indicator and closing with unsaved changes to ask save, discard or cancel.
