The epic acceptance: two windows each hold a project with their own wgpu state. Task 16 moved per-project state into ProjectWindow; this task opens more than one.

WHAT: File menu items 'New Window' (default template in a new window) and 'Open in New Window...', 'Open in new window' on recent projects, and a Window menu listing open project windows (focus through ViewportCommand::Focus). Secondary windows are shown each frame from the root ui() with Context::show_viewport_immediate (ViewportId derived from the window id, ViewportBuilder with title, size and app id), capturing a RenderState clone because eframe::Frame is not available inside the viewport closure; when the viewport class is Embedded (kittest, or a backend without multi-viewport support) the window appears as an egui::Window. Each window has its own Workspace with its own Renderer3d and scene, tree, dialogs, prompts, title 'name - ArchiCraft' with the unsaved indicator, autosave slot (task 16) and close handling (close requests read per viewport, save/discard/cancel prompt); closing the root window or quitting walks every dirty project with the prompt in turn and then exits. Opening a file that is already open focuses its window instead of loading it twice (canonical path comparison). Recovery restores several abandoned slots into separate windows. Actions and shortcuts apply to the focused window only. Document the fallback in the module docs of crates/archicraft-app/src/window.rs (task 16) and in docs/testing.md (created by regression-and-status, increment 1): where native multi-viewport fails, 'Open in New Window' spawns std::env::current_exe() with the path as a second process, and copy and paste then travel through the OS clipboard (task 19).
design: Immediate viewports keep all state on the UI thread (deferred viewports would need Send + Sync state behind locks); two or three windows render comfortably within the frame budget. The root viewport cannot outlive the app, so closing it closes all windows; a hidden root window is avoided because platform behaviour differs. Input must be read per viewport (ctx.input inside the viewport closure), otherwise shortcuts typed in one window act in the other. Pitfalls: native file dialogs block all windows (existing debt, app.rs:197-208); window titles go through ViewportCommand::Title per viewport (update_title_and_theme, app.rs:517); the process holds one Session with per-window slots, so a crash recovers every open project. Pointers: app.rs, window.rs (task 16), ui/shell.rs File menu, persistence/autosave.rs, main.rs viewport builder.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless WindowSet tests: opening A then B gives two windows with independent histories (a command in B leaves A's revision unchanged); opening A again focuses the existing window; closing the root with a dirty secondary window queues the prompts in order and cancelling one aborts the close.
- kittest (embedded viewports): 'New Window' from the File menu shows a second window with its own title; drawing a wall in it changes only its project and its title shows the unsaved indicator; quitting with two dirty projects prompts twice.
- Each window owns a separate Renderer3d; closing a secondary window drops its GPU resources (texture count returns to the root window's views).
- Manual check recorded in docs/testing.md on macOS, Windows and Linux (X11 and Wayland): two native windows, 3D views render in both, closing one produces no wgpu validation errors in the log.
- Satisfies PRJ-011 (two projects in separate windows).
notes:
SRS: PRJ-011
Also: PRJ-003, PRJ-006 (in-process complement), HW-006.

title: Add screen-size level of detail and small-feature culling in 3D
description:
WHY: VIEW-054 (M) names level of detail explicitly: 3D views shall meet NFR-PERF-003 automatically, through level-of-detail and culling, without the user having to simplify the model. NFR-PERF-003 asks for >= 20 frames/s on RM-L (about 8 million triangles) and >= 30 frames/s for RM-S on minimum hardware. At fit-to-window distance, door and window frames, curtain-wall mullions, stair treads and similar details cover a few pixels but dominate the triangle count, and frustum culling (task 10) does not help when the whole model is in view. The gap row: no level of detail exists.

WHAT: archicraft-geometry gains lod.rs: for every body part above a triangle threshold (proposal 48) a coarse proxy by vertex clustering on a grid of one eighth of the part's bounding-box diagonal with degenerate triangles removed, or the part's oriented bounding box when clustering keeps more than 25 % of the triangles; proxies are computed and cached with the element geometry and are render-only (never in IFCX, plans or picking). In render3d each chunk holds a full and a proxy index range, each split into size buckets by element bounding radius (large, medium, small), so whole buckets switch between full, proxy and skipped (projected size below 1.5 px) without per-element draw calls; 20 % hysteresis prevents popping; selected, hovered and edit-mode elements always draw in full; a developer toggle (perf feature and test harness only, never a user preference; also used by goldens) disables level of detail. Out of scope: occlusion culling, impostors, topology-preserving simplification (meshoptimizer).
design:
Projected size: radius x viewport_height / (2 x distance x tan(fov_y / 2)) in perspective, radius x pixels per metre in parallel projection; distance from the camera to the chunk centre and the bucket's maximum element radius, so the choice is conservative. Vertex clustering after Rossignac and Borrel (linear, no dependency); the oriented box from the element's local frame where the kind has one (walls, stairs, members), PCA otherwise. Thresholds are constants tuned with the AS-07 runner and documented next to them.

Pitfalls: transparent glass proxies keep their opacity and stay in the transparent pass; proxies have no feature edges, so hidden-line and wireframe skip edges of proxy buckets; the shadow pass may always use proxies; IFX-068 holds because proxies never leave the renderer. Pointers: archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs (ElementGeometry), mesh.rs, render3d.rs after tasks 09 and 10.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: proxies lie inside the part's bounds plus 1 %, have at most 25 % of the triangles of parts above the threshold and are deterministic; parts below the threshold have none.
- Render unit tests: bucket selection for canned distances (full near, proxy mid, skipped far; perspective and parallel projection); a distance oscillating by 10 % does not toggle; selected elements always draw in full.
- RM-L at fit distance draws less than 30 % of its full triangle count; along the RM-M walk path the drawn count of visible chunks stays within 5 % of full (no visible coarsening up close).
- Goldens of RM-S and of the 3D harness are unchanged (thresholds not reached at golden distances); a new RM-M golden at fit distance differs from the level-of-detail-off render in at most 0.5 % of pixels.
- VIEW-054 'automatically, without the user having to simplify the model': level of detail and chunk culling are on in every new 3D view and in the default Preferences, no user-facing setting is needed or offered, and the AS-07 rows of task 03 run with these defaults (test on a new View3dState and default Preferences).
- Proxy memory is at most 15 % of the full geometry for RM-L (scene statistics); RM-L orbit median >= 40 frames/s on the developer machine (twice the target), recorded in docs/performance.
notes: SRS: VIEW-054 NFR-PERF-003

title: Show derived door and window values and snap to named key points
description:
WHY: DW-015 (S): 'For each door and window, the inspector shall show read-only derived values: sill and head elevation, nominal size, and clear opening width and height (accounting for frame and leaf). Components shall expose named key points (jamb faces, clear-opening edges) that snapping and dimensioning can target.' Gap: missing (M): no derived values, snap targets only collect plan nodes and edges; the derived() section of properties.rs (properties.rs:542) is the place for read-only rows. components-dw-catalogue-03 declared key points and derived values per family (OBJ-014) and -11 shows type-level values; this task resolves them per placed instance. The epic acceptance: clear-opening values and jamb key points are snappable.

WHAT: Geometry crates/archicraft-geometry/src/insert.rs (doors-windows-core): insert_derived(project, element) -> InsertDerived { sill, head (relative to the home storey), sill and head as project elevations, nominal (w, h), clear (w, h) } with the clear opening from the generator layout: inner frame width minus the leaf thickness for hinged leaves opening by 90 degrees or more, and opening height minus the head frame and the threshold. component_key_points(project, geometry, element) -> Vec<KeyPoint { code: KeyPointCode (the stable NamedSpec codes declared by the definitions, such as 'jamb.exterior.start', 'jamb.interior.end', 'clear.start', 'clear.end', 'clear.head', 'sill.inside'), label, position: DVec3 }> transforms the declared key points by the instance transform, for doors, windows and objects (objects through the instance transform of task 02), with a resolve_key_point(element, code) lookup so dimension bindings (element id plus semantic feature key) can target them. Coordination with sections-elevations-dims (parallel in increment 3): its FeatureKey has the Kind(KindFeature) extension point, so component key points are published as KindFeature::KeyPoint(KeyPointCode) in ElementGeometry.features; whichever epic lands second adds that mapping. Snapping: a key-point SnapSource in crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs feeding SnapKind::KeyPoint in the Node level (ranked after element nodes) in plan and through the 3D targets of 3d-input-navigation, with the key point label in the snap tooltip and the exclusions of point-input-snapping-12 honoured. Inspector: read-only rows Sill elevation, Head elevation (absolute value in the tooltip), Nominal size 'w x h', Clear opening width and Clear opening height, formatted through units.rs. Out of scope: dimension tools themselves (sections-elevations-dims), corner and curved units (21 and 15 add their own key points).
design: Derived values are computed, never stored (doors-windows-core rule: store only parameters). The clear-opening formula lives next to the generator layout so frame and leaf changes cannot drift from it; record it in docs/components.md. Key point codes are stable strings because dimension bindings persist them (the sections-elevations-dims rule: element id plus semantic feature key, never mesh indices). Key points are cheap to compute from the type layout, so the SnapIndex fingerprints stay content-based. Pitfalls: mirroring swaps start and end jambs, so key point codes must be defined in host-axis terms like the WallInsert anchors; key points of locked elements stay snappable (INP rule), excluded ones do not. Pointers: insert.rs and InsertFrame::resolve (doors-windows-core-01/03), components/types.rs layout, input/targets.rs and input/snap.rs (point-input-snapping-02/03), properties.rs:542.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: the D.2 door (0.90 x 2.10 m, catalogue frame 0.06 m, leaf 0.04 m, threshold off) has clear width 0.74 m and clear height 2.04 m; the D.2 window (sill 0.90 m, height 1.40 m) has head 2.30 m; sill and head follow DW-007 pin and reference changes.
- Jamb-face key points of a window in a 300 mm wall lie on the wall face planes within 1e-9 and move with the wall.
- Snapping test: a cursor 3 px from a clear-opening edge snaps to SnapKind::KeyPoint labelled 'Clear opening edge' ahead of the plain edge snap; an excluded element yields no key points.
- resolve_key_point returns the same position as the snap target for every declared code; after changing the frame width and after mirroring the unit, 'clear.start' still resolves to the clear-opening edge on the host start side (bindings keep their feature: the dimensioning clause of DW-015).
- The declared key points of object.box (base corners, top centre) are SnapKind::KeyPoint targets at their transformed positions for a rotated, elevated box.
- kittest: selecting the D.2 door shows the read-only rows Sill elevation, Head elevation, Nominal size, Clear opening width (740 mm) and Clear opening height (2040 mm), none of them editable.
- Satisfies DW-015.
notes:
SRS: DW-015
Also: OBJ-014, Appendix D.2.
Design decision to verify with users: the clear width of a hinged door deducts the leaf thickness only when the opening angle is at least 90 degrees.

title: Add linked library sources, precedence and library files
description:
WHY: OBJ-007 (S): 'Linked external library folders shall be supported. Moving a library is a re-point operation, and unlinking keeps instance references so that relinking restores them. A definition found in more than one source shall be reported, with a deterministic, user-controllable precedence.' OBJ-004 keeps instance references by id and version, never by path, and D-11 makes library files .ifcx. Gap row: OBJ-007 missing (L). components-dw-catalogue left linked libraries to this epic and provided ComponentStore, Project::resolve_definition, ParameterSchema::compatible and RelinkDefinition. The CatalogueSet built here is also the source of the OBJ-008 upgrade detection of task 22.

WHAT: Model, new crates/archicraft-model/src/components/library.rs: LibraryId (id_type!), `LibraryLink { id, name, location }` with the location stored relative to the project file when possible, `Project.libraries: Vec<LibraryLink>` whose order is the precedence (first wins), commands LinkLibrary { link, index }, RepointLibrary { id, location }, UnlinkLibrary { id } (never touches instances or the embedded store) and ReorderLibraries { order }. Runtime (not serialised): LoadedLibrary { id, name, status: Loaded | Missing | Invalid(reason), definitions } and CatalogueSet { libraries, generation }. Resolution Project::resolve_definition_with(r, &CatalogueSet): embedded copy with a known generator, then linked libraries in precedence order, then the built-in catalogue, else Missing { NotEmbedded | LibraryMissing(name) | UnknownGenerator }. CatalogueSet::listing(project) lists every definition once with its source and the sources it shadows; Duplicate { id, sources, chosen } is reported when one definition id occurs in more than one source, and a library record that differs from the embedded copy of the same id and version is reported as a mismatch (the embedded copy wins, OBJ-006). The evaluation context of ModelGeometry::evaluate and the incremental evaluator receives the CatalogueSet; Document holds an Arc<CatalogueSet> and the geometry caches key on its generation. IFCX: new crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/library.rs: a library file is an IFCX file with archicraft::library { id, name, description } on its root node and definition records in the codec of components-dw-catalogue-08; read_library(bytes) and write_library(&LibraryFile) (deterministic, IFX-007); an optional `libraries` member (id, name, location) in archicraft::project. Out of scope: upgrades (22), folder scanning and the dialog (09), frozen-geometry definitions (11).
design: Library files reuse the definition record codec of the project store, so a library is just a project-shaped IFCX file without spatial elements: one format (D-11), validated by the same offline validator, and definitions copy between project and library without conversion. Precedence is the stored link order because it is deterministic, visible and reorderable; the built-in catalogue comes last so a linked library can supersede it deliberately, while embedded copies always win for resolution of used definitions so projects regenerate identical geometry (OBJ-006, IFX-064). Paths are hints only: links are identified by the LibraryId stored in the library file, which is what makes re-pointing a moved folder safe. Pitfalls: the evaluator must not read the file system (NFR-MNT-002); a CatalogueSet change bumps its generation so plan and 3D caches invalidate without a model revision; keep listing order deterministic (precedence, then category, then code). Pointers: components/store.rs and RelinkDefinition (components-dw-catalogue-02), alpha/components.rs (components-dw-catalogue-08), evaluate.rs, document.rs:97-121, schema.rs optional members.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/libraries.rs with two in-memory libraries that both contain definition X: listing reports one Duplicate with the sources in link order, ReorderLibraries changes the chosen source, and the result is identical across runs (no HashMap order).
- UnlinkLibrary leaves every instance's DefinitionRef unchanged; an instance without an embedded copy resolves Missing(LibraryMissing) while its library is missing and Resolved after RepointLibrary to the new location; an embedded instance stays Resolved throughout.
- UnlinkLibrary followed by LinkLibrary of the same library (same LibraryId, any location) resolves the instances of the previous case again without touching them (relinking restores references).
- A library record that differs from the embedded copy of the same id and version is reported as a mismatch and the embedded copy is used; a linked library shadows the built-in catalogue only for definitions that are not embedded.
- A CatalogueSet change bumps its generation, and the plan and 3D caches re-evaluate placeholder instances without a model revision.
- write_library/read_library round-trip equal; a written library file passes archicraft_ifcx::validate (IFX-006 offline); the project's libraries member round-trips; files without it still load.
- Satisfies the model and file parts of OBJ-007 (re-point, unlink keeps references, relink restores them, duplicates with deterministic, reorderable precedence).
notes:
SRS: OBJ-007
Also: OBJ-004, OBJ-006, IFX-007, IFX-064, D-11; the OBJ-008 detection and upgrade command build on the CatalogueSet in task 22.
Decision to record in docs/components.md: library links are project data (so everyone sees the same precedence) with machine-specific locations as relative hints; the alternative, personal settings, would make precedence differ between users.

title: Build RM-M and RM-L through the seeded fixture builder
description:
WHY: SRS 7.3 defines RM-M (five-storey residential building with stairs, layered walls and a curtain-wall entrance, about 5,000 elements; SRS 6.1: about 2 million triangles) and RM-L (generated from repeated RM-M blocks, about 20,000 elements, about 8 million triangles) as the loads of AS-07 and of every target this epic must meet: NFR-PERF-002 (open RM-M <= 10 s, save <= 5 s, open RM-L <= 30 s), NFR-PERF-003 (3D navigation >= 30 frames/s on RM-M, >= 20 on RM-L), NFR-PERF-004 (plan pan and zoom >= 30 frames/s on any RM-M storey), NFR-PERF-008 (RM-L below 4 GB) and NFR-PERF-009 (autosave blocking <= 200 ms on RM-M). The gap rows of all of them start with "no RM-M/RM-L models": samples.rs holds models of at most 15 elements, and the stand_in(n) models of element-kind-framework-03 are walls and slabs only, explicitly provisional until this epic. reference-models built rm_s() and builder methods for every increment-2 kind; curtain-walls built the RM-M entrance curtain wall as a fixture.

WHAT: a new crates/archicraft-model/src/samples/rm_m.rs (next to samples/rm_s.rs and samples/site.rs, which reference-models-01 split out of today's samples.rs; re-exported from samples/mod.rs) gains rm_m() -> Project and rm_l(blocks: usize) -> Project with RM_L_BLOCKS = 4, both built only through FixtureBuilder commands with v5 ids, plus walk_path(model) giving an eye-height corridor polyline for the AS-07 walk script (task 03). A private rm_m_block(builder, origin, id_prefix) lays out one five-storey block: an apartment floor plate along a central corridor with two stair cores (a U-stair per storey transition, stair holes in the slabs), layered exterior walls, layered party walls and partitions with L, T and X junctions, doors and windows of a few shared types hosted in the walls, floor slabs and a flat roof slab, columns and beams in the entrance hall, and on the ground floor the two-storey entrance curtain wall placed by samples::rm_m_entrance_into(builder, storey, origin) of curtain-walls-14 (no re-modelling). rm_l places blocks in a 2 x 2 arrangement sharing storeys, materials, structures and door/window types. Both are listed in a new large_catalogue(), kept out of the byte-golden catalogue() (task 02 adds digest goldens). Out of scope: railings and terrain (not part of RM-M in SRS 7.3; RM-S covers them), golden files and conformance (task 02), any tuning.
design:
Layout as a parameterised module grid, so counts are tuned by constants and never by special cases: an apartment module (rooms, bath, kitchen; about 30 to 40 elements including its doors and windows) repeated along both sides of the corridor, the module count chosen so a storey lands near 1,000 elements, and the detail of the door and window types and the stair riser count chosen so the triangle total lands near 2 million (SRS 6.1). Use the template's structures and materials (as RM-S does for NFR-USE-006); share door and window types across the block so the IFX-050 type nodes keep the file small. Reuse the RM-S helpers of reference-models in samples/rm_s.rs (wall rings, room partitioning, door and window placement) and rm_m_entrance_into of curtain-walls-14 for the entrance instead of re-modelling them.

Id paths "rm-m/<kind>/<storey>/<module>/<n>" and "rm-l/b<k>/..." through the FixtureBuilder id source; never iterate a HashMap while building. Batch commands as element-kind-framework-03 recommends: one AddElements per storey and kind, hosted doors and windows after their walls, stairs after slabs, slab holes traced from the stair outlines; this keeps validation linear. RM-L blocks sit 2 x 2 with a 12 m gap, so no junction or cleanup crosses blocks and every storey plan holds four blocks.

Pitfalls: the model crate cannot evaluate geometry, so triangle and junction assertions live in archicraft-geometry tests; FixtureBuilder must stay ungated because the example uses it; large models must never enter catalogue(), whose members are written as byte goldens. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/samples/mod.rs (today samples.rs; FixtureBuilder, catalogue and stand_in of element-kind-framework-03), samples/rm_s.rs (rm_s, reference-models-01), samples::rm_m_entrance_into (curtain-walls-14), crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:327 (integrity_problems), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:122 (TriMesh::check_closed), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests (crates/archicraft-model): rm_m() has 4,750..5,250 elements on five storeys with 900..1,100 per storey; it contains walls with a layer structure of at least three skins, doors, windows, slabs with stair holes, at least two stairs per storey transition, columns, beams and exactly one curtain wall; integrity_problems() is empty; building it twice yields equal projects including every id.
- rm_l(4) has 19,000..21,000 elements with unique ids; block k's elements equal block 0's translated by the block offset (parameters compared for a seeded sample of 200 elements).
- Geometry tests (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/reference_models.rs): ModelGeometry::evaluate(&rm_m()) reports no problems; the triangle count lies in 1.6..2.4 million; every storey has at least one L, one T and one X junction whose footprint differs from square ends; check_closed passes for a seeded sample of 500 parts in the normal suite and for all parts behind #[ignore].
- rm_l(4) evaluates without problems to 6.4..9.6 million triangles (#[ignore], release).
- An #[ignore] release test prints build times: rm_m() under 3 s and rm_l(4) under 12 s on the developer machine.
- walk_path stays inside the building outline at 1.60 m above storey 02 and runs through the corridor of block 0.
- cargo test, clippy and fmt green; existing golden files untouched. Provides the RM-M/RM-L loads on which NFR-PERF-002, -003, -004, -008 and -009 are measured.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-003 NFR-PERF-004 NFR-PERF-008 NFR-PERF-009
The apartment layout is a proposal within SRS 7.3; the product owner may adjust it. Counts follow the SRS 'about' values (elements +-5 %, triangles +-20 %). Appendix D.1 curve tessellation (2 mm chord, at most 10 degrees) applies to curved parts.

title: Add kitchen, sanitary, vegetation and vehicle definitions
description:
WHY: OBJ-013 (S) names kitchen units, sanitary fixtures (WC, washbasin, bathtub, shower tray), simple vegetation and vehicles in addition to furniture, at least 30 definitions in total. The epic acceptance requires at least 30 furniture and fixture definitions placed as IfcFurniture with shared type geometry, checked in a file. Appendix D.5 offers IfcFurniture, IfcGeographicElement and IfcBuildingElementProxy for objects but no sanitary terminal class.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/components/builtin/{kitchen,sanitary,site}.rs (registered like task 03) and the matching generators in new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/{kitchen,sanitary,site}.rs: kitchen (kitchen.base with doors or drawers, kitchen.wall, kitchen.tall, kitchen.sink with bowl count, kitchen.cooktop, kitchen.fridge; category furniture, class IfcFurniture), sanitary (sanitary.wc wall-hung or floor-standing, sanitary.washbasin, sanitary.bathtub, sanitary.shower-tray rectangular or quadrant, sanitary.bidet, sanitary.urinal; category sanitary, class IfcFurniture), vegetation (vegetation.tree.deciduous, vegetation.tree.conifer, vegetation.shrub; category generic, group 'vegetation', class IfcGeographicElement) and vehicles (vehicle.car, vehicle.bicycle; category equipment, group 'vehicles', class IfcBuildingElementProxy): 17 definitions, so the built-in library holds 36 furniture and fixture definitions (plus the generic box and cylinder of task 01), of which 31 default to IfcFurniture. Kitchen units declare a worktop key point and the 0.90 m worktop default; sanitary items declare their wall-side origin. A completeness test builtin_library_meets_obj_013. Sample samples::furniture_library() placing every built-in object definition once on a grid plus a second instance of the dining table, registered like task 02, golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/furniture-library.ifcx. docs/components.md lists the full library. Out of scope: thumbnails (10), linked libraries (07).
design: Same builders and Assembly kit as task 03. Vegetation is deliberately simple (trunk cylinder plus low-poly canopy ellipsoid; plan symbol a canopy circle with a few radial lines at Detailed), vehicles are an extruded side profile plus wheel cylinders. Sanitary fixtures default to IfcFurniture because D.5 has no IfcSanitaryTerminal; the user can override the class per element (ELM-011). Pitfalls: the bathtub inner basin must stay a separate closed shell (or a single closed shell with the cavity, not an open surface); quadrant shower trays use exact arcs in the symbol and the shared tessellator in 3D; keep the golden deterministic (seeded builder, first-occurrence type order). Pointers: components/primitives.rs (task 03), samples.rs, tests/roundtrip.rs samples(), examples/reference_models.rs, conformance/check.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- builtin_library_meets_obj_013: at least 30 object definitions in the furniture, sanitary, generic (vegetation) and equipment (vehicles) groups, with at least one table, chair, sofa, bed, wardrobe, kitchen unit, WC, washbasin, bathtub, shower tray, vegetation item and vehicle, and at least 30 definitions whose default class is IfcFurniture.
- The parameter-sweep, symbol and snapshot tests of task 03 cover the seventeen new definitions.
- furniture-library.ifcx round-trips equal and passes conformance/run.sh; it contains at least 30 IfcFurniture type nodes, and the two dining tables reference one type node (shared type geometry, IFX-050).
- Vegetation is written as IfcGeographicElement and vehicles as IfcBuildingElementProxy as children of the storey.
- Completes OBJ-013 together with task 03.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-013
Also: OBJ-002, OBJ-011, IFX-050, Appendix D.5.
Open question: D.5 lacks IfcSanitaryTerminal; if the class list is extended later, sanitary definitions switch their default class with a definition version bump.

title: Stream the IFCX writer with progress and cancellation
description:
WHY: NFR-PERF-002 requires saving RM-M in at most 5 s; NFR-PERF-007 requires that saving (and any export) shows progress, does not block viewport navigation and, because it does not change the model, is cancellable; NFR-PERF-008 caps RM-L at 4 GB, which includes the peak of a save or autosave. Today the writer builds an IfcxFile whose attributes are serde Values, converts the whole file into a second Value tree with serde_json::to_value and then into one String (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:420-424); every float goes through format!("{:e}") plus a rewrite (json.rs:107-118); the previous file is copied for the backup (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/mod.rs:95); and the headless crates cannot report progress or stop.

WHAT: archicraft-model gains progress.rs: a UI-free Progress trait (phase name and total, advance, cancelled), a NoProgress implementation and a Cancelled error, used by all crates. archicraft-ifcx gains save_to_writer(project, geometry, options, pretty, out: &mut dyn Write, progress) -> Result<Vec<Problem>, SaveError>, which emits nodes as they are generated through a streaming emitter in json.rs that follows exactly the existing compact and indented rules; meshes are written straight from TriMesh (rounded per point) without intermediate Values, small attributes may still be built as one Value per node and emitted at once, and floats are formatted into a reused buffer without per-number allocation. save() stays a Vec<u8> wrapper and write() keeps returning IfcxFile for tests, both fed by the same node generator. archicraft-app persistence gains save_atomically_with(path, write_fn, backups), which streams into the temp file through a BufWriter, rotates the backup by hard link with a copy fallback and removes the temp file on error or cancellation. Out of scope: worker threads and UI (task 07), reading (task 05).
design:
A NodeSink visitor separates generation from output: writer.rs walks the spatial tree once and hands each node (path, children, inherits, attributes, with mesh attributes as a typed MeshRef { points: &[DVec3], indices: &[u32] }) to a FileSink (builds IfcxFile; used by write(), validation and tests) or a StreamSink (writes JSON). serde_json is built with preserve_order, so Map keeps insertion order: the stream must emit object keys in the order the json! macros and IndexMaps insert them, exactly as today.

Float output keeps the shortest round-trip digits and the existing exponent-free rule; write!(buf, "{:e}") into a reused String is enough unless profiling says otherwise (ryu is not in Cargo.lock today and would need a cargo deny check). Backups: std::fs::hard_link(path, backup) and then rename(temp, path); fall back to fs::copy on any hard-link error (unsupported file systems, cross-device, files held open on Windows).

Pitfalls: the header's dataVersion and timestamp still come from WriteOptions; warnings collected while streaming are returned at the end; use a 1 MiB BufWriter and keep sync_all plus the directory sync. Pointers: alpha/writer.rs:243-424, json.rs:12-150, lib.rs:30-38, persistence/mod.rs:70-110.
acceptance_criteria:
- Byte identity: for every catalogue sample and golden file the streamed output, compact and indented, equals the previous output byte for byte; no golden is re-blessed; the RM-M and RM-L manifests of task 02 pass unchanged.
- Property test: one million random f64 (subnormal, 1e-7..1e15, negative, integral, rounded coordinates) format to the same text as the previous format_f64 and parse back to the same value.
- Cancellation: a Progress that cancels after N nodes makes save_to_writer return Cancelled; through save_atomically_with the original file and its backups stay byte-identical and no temporary file remains (tests in persistence/mod.rs); atomic_save_keeps_backups and failed_save_leaves_the_original still pass; an injected hard-link failure falls back to copying.
- Progress phases arrive in order and the node phase advances to the node count.
- Release test (#[ignore]) with a counting allocator: writing RM-M to a file allocates at most 64 MB beyond project and geometry.
- Bench ifcx/save/rm_m is at least 2x faster than the task-02 baseline; the result is appended to docs/performance. NFR-PERF-002's save clause is confirmed on reference hardware in task 15.
notes:
SRS: NFR-PERF-002 NFR-PERF-007 NFR-PERF-008
Keeps IFX-007 determinism and NFR-REL-001 atomic saving.

title: Add the object placement tool, inspector fields and axis rotation
description:
WHY: OBJ-003 (M) requires placement by insertion point and rotation with rotation snapping, at an elevation relative to the home storey, mirroring on request and parameter editing in the inspector. Appendix D.1 sets the angle snapping increment to 45 degrees with 15 degrees selectable. The epic acceptance demands that an object rotates about the vertical axis and mirrors on request while a request to rotate it about a horizontal axis is refused with the EDT-007 message; EDT-025 (S) asks any-axis rotation, which applies to Free definitions and to every object whose 'Free orientation' override is set (task 01). Gap OBJ-003: no tool, and properties are hard-wired to wall and slab fields (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:91-120).

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/object.rs (the tools/ module of point-input-snapping) on the PointInput service: ToolKind::Object with modes One click (insertion; rotation from the tool defaults) and Two clicks (insertion, then a direction whose angle snaps to the angle increment and to the direction of an edge or wall face within the snap radius; a typed angle overrides), a live preview of the instance outline in plan and a ghost in 3D, the elevation relative to the active storey and a Mirror toggle in the properties strip, and the definition from ToolDefaults (picked through definition_picker of components-dw-catalogue-12 until the catalogue browser of task 08 sets it). Each placement is one Command::AddElements. Action::ToolObject (free D.8 shortcut only), toolbox button and Design menu item. ui/properties.rs: object fields X and Y of the insertion point, Elevation (relative to the home storey, absolute value in the tooltip), Rotation, Mirror (SetInstanceMirrored), a 'Free orientation' checkbox (SetObjectOrientation of task 01; ticking it on an Upright object allows tilting, unticking clears the tilt), a read-only 'Tilted' row with 'Reset tilt' for tilted objects, then the schema-driven parameter sections of ui/parameters.rs (components-dw-catalogue-11), each edit one SetInstanceParameters; Subject::Defaults(Object) edits ObjectDefaults. The Rotate-about-axis dialog of selection-transforms-12 consults KindDescriptor.transforms and the effective orientation per object: for Upright selections the X and Y axis options and typed axes are disabled with the EDT-007 explanation and the hint 'Tick Free orientation to tilt this object' as hover text, a forced typed axis shows the CommandError::Unsupported message, and Free objects (by definition or override) rotate. Out of scope: the catalogue browser (08), handles (06).
design: Follow the 'Add a drawing tool' extension point adapted to the PointInput service (tools consume resolved points, never raw events), like tools/insert.rs of doors-windows-core. Rotation snapping reuses the angle-increment constraint of point-input-snapping (the same increment preference as Shift constraints) plus an edge-direction candidate from the SnapIndex within the snap radius (D.1: 8 px). The preview reuses the type outline (TypeGeometry bounds and symbol) transformed by the candidate placement, so no element is created until the click. Fields follow the Fields getter/setter pattern (fields hide when the getter returns None) or properties-and-dialogs' FieldSpec if it has landed; each field edit is one SetObjectPlacement. Pitfalls: entering a rotation in the strip must not snap; the Mirror toggle mirrors about the definition's local y-z plane through the insertion point, so the insertion point stays fixed; keep egui ids unique per element. Pointers: tools/ and input/ (point-input-snapping), ui/properties.rs:140-220 and :542-684, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs toolbox, the Rotate-about-axis dialog in ui/dialogs.rs (selection-transforms-12).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool state-machine tests without egui: one click places at the snapped point with the default rotation; in Two clicks a direction at 55 degrees yields 45 degrees with the 45-degree increment and 60 degrees with the 15-degree increment; a direction within the snap radius of a wall face aligns to the face; a typed 30 gives 30 degrees; Esc cancels without a command.
- An elevation of 0.75 entered in the strip places the insertion point 0.75 m above the active storey; Mirror on places a mirrored instance.
- kittest: the toolbox button 'Object' activates the tool; selecting an object shows 'Elevation', 'Rotation' and 'Mirror' plus the schema groups; toggling Mirror adds exactly one undo step.
- kittest: for a selected chair (Upright, task 03) the Rotate-about-axis dialog shows the X axis option disabled with hover text containing 'vertical axis'; after ticking 'Free orientation' rotating the chair 90 degrees about X executes; for a selected box (Free) rotating 90 degrees about X executes and the 'Tilted' row appears.
- kittest: changing the Width of a selected box in the inspector's parameter section executes one SetInstanceParameters (one undo step) and the plan outline updates in the same frame; an out-of-range value is rejected with the parameter label (OBJ-003 inspector clause).
- Satisfies OBJ-003 (placement, rotation snapping, storey-relative elevation, mirroring, inspector) and the user-facing parts of EDT-025 and the EDT-007 refusal for objects.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-003 EDT-025
Also: EDT-007, Appendix D.1 (angle increment 45 degrees, 15 selectable; snap radius 8 px), Appendix D.8 shortcut uniqueness.

title: Group the material browser by category; import materials from files
description:
WHY: MAT-006 (S): a material browser offers search, categories and swatch previews, and imports materials from another project or a material library (an IFCX file, D-11) by copying them into the project. Gap: search and swatches exist (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:376-410, reachable via Project > Materials…), but there is no category grouping or filter and no import from another project or library. Imported materials must still be written per MAT-007 (category code and uri from the table of task 06).

WHAT: materials_window in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs: a category filter and collapsible groups per category (label and code from the CategoryTable) with counts. 'Import from file…' opens a native .ifcx dialog and calls archicraft-ifcx `read_materials(bytes, &LoadContext) -> MaterialLibrary { materials, fills, pens, problems }`: ArchiCraft files (projects, or libraries = ArchiCraft files whose archicraft::project holds the materials, IFX-067) give complete materials with the fills and pens they reference; third-party files give materials from their material nodes through the mapping of task 07, keeping their Classification (Preserved or Unclassified, task 06). An import dialog lists the file's materials with swatch, category and checkbox, marks name collisions (skip, or add as copy with a ' (2)' suffix) and executes Command::ImportMaterials { materials, attributes }: new MaterialIds (copies get new identities, IFX-011), referenced fills and pens matched by code or copied with new ids. Out of scope: exporting material libraries (templates-presets), textures (MAT-005 withdrawn by D-11).
design: Reuse the reader rather than duplicating it: read_project_data's material path for ArchiCraft files and the third-party material mapping for other files; the source file is never modified. Fill and pen references are the MaterialFill { fill: FillId, ... } of plan-attributes-03 (attributes.rs); same code means same fill. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:376-410 and 782-791, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:301 (read_project_data), third_party.rs (07), material.rs CategoryTable (06), crates/archicraft-model/src/attributes.rs (plan-attributes), crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Command test: importing three materials, one colliding by name, from an ArchiCraft library fixture adds two plus one renamed copy with new ids and matched or copied fills and pens; undo removes them all.
- ifcx test: read_materials on the third-party fixture of task 07 returns materials with colour, opacity and category from the mapping table.
- kittest: the browser shows category groups; filtering by Concrete shows only concrete materials; importing from the library fixture copies the chosen materials, which appear under their categories (MAT-006).
- Problems in the source file are shown in the import dialog, never silently dropped; imported materials are written with bsi::ifc::material per MAT-007 (writer test).
- Regress: search by name or code and the swatch previews (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:383-410) keep working with grouping on (kittest).
notes:
SRS: MAT-006 MAT-007
MAT-006 partial: search and swatches exist (keep); category grouping and import are new. MAT-007: imported materials are written per IFX-040/IFX-043/IFX-041.

title: Show grid spacings as a dimension chain that follows the axes
description:
WHY: GRD-008 (S) requires the spacings of grid axes to be shown as a dimension chain. The gap analysis rates it missing: no dimension drawing of any kind exists, and the associative dimensions of ANN-004 arrive later in sections-elevations-dims, which depends on this epic. The chain is therefore derived from the grid itself, not stored as a dimension element, which also guarantees the epic acceptance that the chain updates when an axis moves.

WHAT: archicraft-geometry: add `GridPlan.chains: Vec<DimensionChain { set, baseline: [DVec2; 2], ticks: Vec<DVec2>, values: Vec<(DVec2, f64)> }>` computed from the axis offsets for each set whose ChainSide is not None: a baseline parallel to the crossing direction beyond the bubbles on the chosen side, a tick at every axis, the consecutive spacings as values and an optional overall dimension; the offset beyond the bubbles is resolved in paper millimetres at draw time. archicraft-app: draw extension lines from the axis ends to the baseline, 45-degree ticks and upright value texts formatted in project units (units::format_length with the project number format); add the chain-side combo per set (none, start, end) to the grid settings dialog of grids-06, each change one UpdateElements undo step (the ChainSide field is persisted since grids-01 and grids-04). Out of scope: chains in sections and elevations (GRD-009), user-overridden chain text, associative dimensions to other elements (ANN-004).
design: Approach: chain geometry is a pure function of the grid payload, computed with the GridPlan in grids-03's module, so no cache or relation is needed and undo works for free. Baseline distance beyond the axis end = bubble diameter + 4 paper mm gap (resolved with the paper-size helper of grids-05). Upright rule: flip text direction when the baseline points into the left half-plane. Pitfalls: spacings smaller than the text width; open ends of the chain at the outermost axes must align with the extension lines; keep values exact (format from the stored offsets, never from rounded screen positions). Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs:283 (format_length), :246 (format_decimal), views/plan.rs draw_plan, plan-renderer stroke roles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: the default 5 x 4 grid at 6.00 m gives a set-0 chain with 5 ticks and four values of 6.00 m and a set-1 chain with 4 ticks and three values; after EditGridAxes::Move of axis 3 by +1.20 m the set-0 values become 6.00, 7.20, 4.80, 6.00 (the 'chain updates when an axis moves' acceptance); ticks lie on the axis lines within 1e-9; at rotation 30 degrees the baseline stays parallel to the crossing axes.
- Formatting tests: 6.0 m shows as '6.00' in metres with two decimals, '6000' in millimetres and per the feet-inch format in imperial projects (project unit settings, not hard-coded).
- Plan data or kittest: hiding the chain of set 1 removes it; value texts stay upright at rotation 170 degrees; texts that do not fit their spacing alternate sides instead of overlapping.
- kittest: setting the chain side of set 0 to End in the grid settings dialog creates one undo step and puts the set-0 chain on the end side in the plan data; None removes it.
- GRD-008 satisfied.
notes: SRS: GRD-008. A future option is to switch the chain onto the ANN dimension renderer once sections-elevations-dims exists; not required.

title: Evaluate grid geometry and add it to plans across the storey range
description:
WHY: GRD-001 requires visible axes with labels, bubbles at one or both ends and extension lengths, and GRD-004 (M) requires a grid to be visible on all storeys of a chosen range (default all). The gap analysis rates GRD-004 missing because every element has exactly one home storey (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:280) and plan_drawing only iterates elements_on(storey) (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:120); the cross-storey plan generation of plan-views-browser works from z-extents of 3D bodies, which grids do not have. GRD-006 and IFX-035 need the axis curves as evaluated geometry for the writer (grids-04).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/grid.rs (the framework's GeometryKind table): evaluate a grid into an ElementGeometry without body parts or children (element-kind-framework-07) plus `curves: Vec<NamedCurve { role: String ('Axis_<label>'), seed: Uuid (axis id), points: Vec<DVec3> }>` in home-storey coordinates at z = 0 (ElementGeometry gains the curves field; walls, columns and beams keep `axis`; bounds() includes curve points). Add `PlanDrawing.grids: Vec<GridPlan { id, axes: Vec<AxisPlan { axis: AxisId, label, segment: [DVec2; 2], bubbles: Vec<BubbleAnchor { at: DVec2, outward: DVec2 }> }>, intersections: Vec<(AxisId, AxisId, DVec2)> }>` filled for every visible grid whose StoreyRange contains the plan storey, regardless of its home storey; PlanDrawing::hit/pick/bounds consider axis segments so clicking an axis selects the grid. crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs: a grid edit invalidates the cached plans of every storey in its range, and storey list changes invalidate grid-bearing plans. Out of scope: painting (grids-05), snap targets (grids-08), dimension chains (grids-09), sections and elevations (GRD-009 in sections-elevations-dims).
design: Approach: reuse the model-side axis_line/intersections of grids-01 and only convert to storey-local 3D and plan structs, so there is one implementation of the grid math. Visibility path: a kind hook `visible_on(&self, storeys: &StoreyList, home, storey) -> bool` with the default `home == storey`, overridden by grids with the range; plan_drawing asks it for bodiless reference kinds, which later reference kinds can reuse. Invalidation: element-kind-framework-11 invalidates plan caches only for changed storeys and the home storeys of changed elements; add `affected_storeys(&StoreyList)` returning the range so per-storey caches drop every storey in it (if the cache is still cleared wholesale, the test still passes and documents the contract). Emit grids first in PlanDrawing so they paint beneath elements. Bubble size is paper-based, so geometry stores only anchor and outward direction; the radius is resolved at draw time (grids-05). Pitfalls: open-ended ranges and storeys inserted later; negative storey indices; never translate curves by storey elevation (IFCX nodes carry the storey transform, IFX-031). Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:22-57 (PlanElement, PlanDrawing), :111-170 (plan_drawing), :211-296 (segments, hit, pick, bounds), evaluate.rs:30-36 (ElementGeometry), crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-121 (geometry and plan caches), plan-views-browser-03 design (z-extent index that grids bypass).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry unit tests: a 5 x 4-axis 6.00 m grid with extension 1.50 m evaluates to 9 curves named Axis_1..Axis_5 and Axis_A..Axis_D; Axis_1 runs from (0, -1.5, 0) to (0, 19.5, 0) at rotation 0; at rotation 30 degrees every endpoint equals the rotated value within 1e-9; the geometry has no body parts and ModelGeometry::evaluate reports no problem for the grid.
- Plan test (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/grid.rs) with storeys -1, 0, 1, 2: range 0..1 puts the grid in the plans of storeys 0 and 1 only; the default range puts it in all four; a storey inserted between 0 and 1 shows it; the home storey alone does not decide visibility; a grid on a hidden layer is absent.
- BubbleEnds None, Start, End and Both give 0, 1, 1 and 2 BubbleAnchors per axis, each exactly at the extended axis end it belongs to (start = the end at the lowest offset of the crossing set) with a unit outward direction along the axis; changing bubbles or extension moves only anchors and segment ends.
- PlanDrawing::pick at a point on Axis_C returns the grid id; bounds() include the axes and bubble anchors.
- document.rs test: editing a grid whose home storey is 0 refreshes the cached plan of storey 2 inside its range (new Arc, contains the change).
- Existing geometry tests, plan tests and golden files unchanged (no sample contains a grid).
- GRD-004 satisfied for plan data; GRD-001 axis, extension and bubble geometry available to rendering and export.
notes: SRS: GRD-001 GRD-004. Related, owned elsewhere: GRD-009 and VIEW-031 (grids in sections and elevations, sections-elevations-dims) will read the same curves.

title: Build the furniture primitive kit and nineteen furniture definitions
description:
WHY: OBJ-013 (S): 'The built-in library shall add at least 30 furniture and fixture definitions: furniture (tables, chairs, sofas, beds, wardrobes), kitchen units, sanitary fixtures (WC, washbasin, bathtub, shower tray), simple vegetation and vehicles.' Gap row: missing (L). Every definition needs a parameter schema, parametric 3D geometry and a parametric plan symbol (OBJ-002) and may declare key points and derived values (OBJ-014). NFR-LEG-002 forbids reference-product content, so the definitions are original, primitive-based designs. The epic acceptance requires at least 30 definitions placed as IfcFurniture with shared type geometry; this task delivers the reusable kit and the furniture half, task 04 the rest.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/primitives.rs (kit.rs of components-dw-catalogue-04 stays the door and window unit kit; its panel and mirror_x are reused): a primitive kit (box, chamfered box, cylinder, frustum, extruded outline through extrude.rs, low-poly ellipsoid) and an Assembly builder that collects named parts with material slots into the UnitGeometry parts, plus symbol helpers added to components/symbols.rs (components-dw-catalogue-06: outline, inner lines, cushion and pillow lines, door swing arcs as exact SymbolPrimitive arcs) for Simplified and Detailed plan symbols; PartRole (components-dw-catalogue-01: Frame, Leaf, Sash, Glazing, Sill, Body) gains Top, Leg, Seat, Upholstery, Carcass and Front with codes and labels (IFX-017 part names). Model: new crates/archicraft-model/src/components/builtin/furniture.rs, registered from components/catalogue.rs (components-dw-catalogue-03), adds nineteen version-1 definitions in category furniture, class IfcFurniture, orientation Upright, with groups: tables (table.dining.rect, table.dining.round, table.desk, table.coffee, table.bedside), chairs (chair.dining, chair.armchair, chair.office, chair.stool), sofas (sofa.two-seat, sofa.three-seat, sofa.corner, left or right through mirroring), beds (bed.single, bed.double, bed.bunk) and storage (wardrobe.hinged with a door count, wardrobe.sliding, shelf.open, chest.drawers). A shared parameter kit declares Size (width, depth, height, with the same keys everywhere; task 06 sets its handle roles) and Materials (body, top or upholstery as Material parameters with template-code defaults) plus family parameters (leg style, seat height, seat count, drawer and door counts). Each definition documents its origin (centre of the base for free-standing items such as tables, back centre for wall-standing items such as beds, sofas and wardrobes) and declares key points (front centre, corners). Generators in new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/furniture.rs, registered in components/registry.rs, keys '<code>@1' in KNOWN_GENERATORS. docs/components.md gains the library table (code, parameters, defaults, origin). Out of scope: kitchen, sanitary, vegetation and vehicles (04), handles (06), thumbnails (10).
design: Definitions are Rust tables built with small builder functions like the door and window catalogue (components-dw-catalogue-03): no scripting (O-12), deterministic and reviewable. Generators stay simple and parametric: a table is a top plus legs or a pedestal, a sofa is a base, back and arm boxes with chamfers, a wardrobe is a carcass plus door fronts and plinth. Every part goes through the Assembly builder so material slots, part names (IFX-017) and closedness checks are uniform. Keep vertex counts small (a chair below about 400 vertices) because thousands of instances share types but still render (OBJ-011, NFR-PERF). Pitfalls: touching parts must be separate closed meshes, never merged into one non-manifold mesh; quantise nothing in the generators (TypeKey does that); generator keys are immutable once released. Pointers: components/catalogue.rs and the parameter kit of components-dw-catalogue-03, components/kit.rs, registry.rs and layout.rs (components-dw-catalogue-04), components/symbols.rs SymbolPrimitive (components-dw-catalogue-06), extrude.rs, mesh.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Catalogue::builtin() contains the nineteen furniture definitions with category furniture, class IfcFurniture, orientation Upright and a group under 'furniture/'.
- A parameter-sweep test generates every definition at its defaults and at the minimum and maximum of each length and count parameter: all meshes closed and outward (check_closed, positive signed volume) and the bounding box equals width x depth x height within 1 mm.
- Simplified and Detailed plan symbols are non-empty for every definition and lie inside the width x depth rectangle.
- A generator snapshot table (vertex count and volume per definition at defaults) is asserted, so unintended geometry changes fail the test; changing it requires a new generator key and version (IFX-064).
- Every declared key point lies on or inside the bounding box; parameter keys width, depth and height are identical across the families (relink and inspector mapping).
- Contributes nineteen of the at least 30 OBJ-013 definitions.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-013
Also: OBJ-002, OBJ-014, NFR-LEG-002, IFX-017, IFX-064.
Default sizes (design decision, recorded in docs/components.md): dining table 1.60 x 0.90 x 0.75 m, round table d 1.10 m, desk 1.40 x 0.70 m, chair seat height 0.45 m, double bed 1.80 x 2.00 m, single bed 0.90 x 2.00 m, wardrobe 1.00 x 0.60 x 2.20 m.

title: Crop elements permanently by a plane into free-form solids
description:
WHY: SOL-033 (S): a non-associative crop shall permanently cut the selected elements above or below a plane — the plane of a single-plane roof, a picked face or a plane through three points — and the result does not change when the reference later moves or is deleted. The gap row notes that only horizontal slicing exists (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs:35) and that cropping rewrites the element, so the roadmap places it here. SOL-008 (M): every cropped result is a closed manifold.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/crop.rs: crop_element(project, geometry, id, plane, keep: KeepSide { Above, Below }) -> Result<CropOutcome, CropError>. Free-form solids are cut by PolyMesh::split_by_plane in crates/archicraft-model/src/solid/ops.rs (exact planar clipping of every face loop, cap faces from the chained intersection segments including holes, cap material from the face contributing the longest boundary to each cap loop, uncut faces keep ids, materials and flags, cap edges hard and visible). Every other kind is cut part by part through the SolidKernel's plane split (solid-kernel-ops, EDT-024), which caps each part in its own material, and then solid_from_parts (task 08) builds one solid, so a layered wall's cap shows every skin band. CropOutcome reports 'nothing left' (element kept, reported) and 'not touched by the plane' (element kept unconverted). Planes are the Plane3 { point, normal } of 3d-input-navigation-13 (archicraft-model), converted to the kernel's Plane for SolidKernel::split. Plane sources: a Kind::crop_plane(&self, ctx) -> Option<Plane3> hook with default None in crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs (the roofs epic registers the single-plane roof plane; the test-kinds Dummy registers one for tests), Plane3::from_points rejecting collinear points, and Plane3::from_face for a picked solid face (FaceId) or a PickIndex face hit (3d-input-navigation-06). KeepSide is relative to the plane normal oriented upward (for vertical planes, the side the user picks). The command is ReplaceWithSolids (task 08) with one replacement per cropped element and the HostedPolicy of conversion; no relation is stored. Out of scope: associative trims (cleanup-and-trims), the tool UI (15).
design: Split by plane: classify vertices by signed distance with MODEL_TOLERANCE snapping (vertices within tolerance count as on the plane, which avoids slivers), clip each loop, collect intersection segments oriented so the cap is outward-facing on the kept side, chain them into loops and classify outer and hole loops in the plane frame. Going through solid_from_parts for parametric kinds keeps one code path with conversion and its face-material guarantees. The roof plane hook keeps this epic independent of the roofs epic while letting single-plane roofs plug in with one method. Pointers: solid/ops.rs (task 06), solid_convert.rs (task 08), SolidKernel split (solid-kernel-ops), kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-02), relations.rs (element-kind-framework-08).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/crop.rs: a 5 m long, 3 m high wall cropped below the plane z = 2 + 0.2·x becomes a closed solid whose top vertices satisfy the plane equation within MODEL_TOLERANCE and whose volume equals the analytic value.
- The F2 layered wall cropped below an inclined plane gives one solid whose cap consists of six faces in the skin materials with areas proportional to the skin thicknesses.
- The unit cube solid cropped to keep below z = 0.5 has volume 0.5, a cap face, and its uncut faces keep their ids and materials; kept above z = 0.5 it also has volume 0.5.
- Two selected walls cropped by one plane become two solids in one ReplaceWithSolids (one undo step).
- Non-associativity (SOL-033 acceptance): a wall cropped below the top face of a slab is unchanged, bit for bit in PolyMesh and evaluated geometry, after the slab is moved by 0.10 m and after it is deleted, and the relation store holds no relation for it.
- Plane::from_points rejects collinear points; an element entirely on the removed side is reported and left unchanged; undo restores the original wall with its parameters.
- The golden sample gains a cropped wall; conformance/run.sh stays green.
- Satisfies SOL-033 (engine and permanence) and SOL-008 for crop results.
notes:
SRS: SOL-008 SOL-033
The single-plane roof case is asserted with a real roof in the roofs epic or in reference-models once both exist; here the Dummy kind proves the hook.

title: Edit grid settings: axis table, spacings, labels and storey range
description:
WHY: GRD-001 (M) makes label series, bubble ends, extension lengths, rotation and origin user-configurable, GRD-002 (M) requires axes to be addable, deletable and renamable with spacings editable numerically, and GRD-004 (M) requires a chosen storey range (default all storeys). The settings dialog is where these values are typed exactly (NFR-ACC-002 input resolution), complementing the graphical palette of grids-07; the gap analysis lists 'an edit dialog' as missing.

WHAT: archicraft-app ui/dialogs.rs (or the settings-dialog framework of properties-and-dialogs where it exists): a 'Grid settings' window for the selected grid, or for the grid tool defaults when no grid is selected, with origin X/Y and rotation (unit-aware widgets::length and widgets::angle), bubbles (none, start, end, both) and diameter, extension at start and end, storey range (bottom and top combos where 'lowest' / 'highest' mean an open end), and per axis set a table of axes: label (editable), spacing (editable, with a ShiftFollowing / KeepOthers toggle), offset (editable, EditGridAxes::Move), add-after and delete buttons, and relabel with series and start. Every change executes immediately as Command::EditGridAxes (grids-02) or UpdateElements for scalar fields, so each edit is one undo step. Properties-panel rows for grids (origin, rotation, axis counts, range) with fields auto-hiding for other kinds. Out of scope: graphical axis editing (grids-07), the chain-side control (grids-09), radial families (grids-12).
design: Approach: immediate application per field like the properties panel (no draft and OK), because GRD-002 edits are individually undoable; the dialog re-reads the grid each frame. Table built with egui::Grid (a layout widget, unrelated to structural grids). Pitfalls: typing in a table cell must not trigger tool shortcuts (works_while_typing); after Delete move focus to the next row; the project settings dialog's multi-command OK (technical debt, dialogs.rs:609-615) is the anti-pattern to avoid. Pointers: the 'Add a dialog' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs, ui/widgets.rs (length, angle, text, choice), ui/properties.rs Fields getters and setters, workspace.rs execute.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: select a grid, open 'Grid settings' from the properties panel; typing '7.5' as spacing of axis 3 shifts axes 3..5 by +1.50 m (ShiftFollowing default); renaming B to 'B1', adding an axis after D (gets E) and deleting axis 2 each create exactly one undo step whose Edit-menu label names the axis.
- Scalar fields: switching bubbles to Start, setting the end extension to 2.00 m, the rotation to 15 degrees and the origin to (3, 4) each create exactly one undo step and the plan data of the active storey reflects each change; typing 13.20 as offset of axis 3 moves it through EditGridAxes::Move.
- Relabel: applying Numbers with prefix 'X' to the numbered set renames 1..5 to X1..X5 in one undo step and leaves the lettered set unchanged.
- Invalid input (duplicate label 'A', spacing 0) shows the CommandError text next to the field and leaves the project unchanged (NFR-REL-005).
- Storey range: bottom '00' and top '01' on a four-storey project makes the grid visible on 00 and 01 only (plan data asserted); choosing 'lowest' and 'highest' restores all storeys.
- With no grid selected the dialog edits the grid defaults slot in one undo step and the next grid drawn with the tool uses the new values.
- Table rows are keyed by AxisId: editing a spacing that re-sorts nothing keeps keyboard focus in the edited row.
- GRD-002 numeric spacing, numeric move, rename, add and delete satisfied in the UI; GRD-001 configurability and GRD-004 range selection satisfied.
notes: SRS: GRD-001 GRD-002 GRD-004.

title: Grid systems
description:
Orthogonal (optionally radial) grid systems as reference elements with axes, labels, bubbles, extensions, rotation and origin; axis editing; snapping in all views; storey-range visibility; the spacing dimension chain; columns at intersections and beams along axes in one command; IfcGrid export. Kept in increment 2 per Appendix F but buildable as soon as the framework exists.

Risks: Radial grids (Could) are time-boxed.
design: archicraft-model kinds/grid.rs (reference element with storey range) and a label-series generator; archicraft-geometry axis segments into the plan drawing and snap targets; archicraft-ifcx IfcGrid node with Axis children; archicraft-app tools/grid.rs and an axis edit palette reusing PartRef. samples::structural_frame built through commands with seeded ids; its golden file joins the conformance run.
acceptance_criteria: AS-02 as a committed asset samples::structural_frame: 4 x 3 bays of 6.00 m, columns at all 20 intersections on three storeys via GRD-005, beams along the axes, slabs and pad footings as slabs with the IfcFooting class; a test asserts every member sits on its grid line and storey level within MODEL_TOLERANCE (NFR-ACC-003 alignment) and the conformance job verifies IfcColumn, IfcBeam, IfcSlab, IfcFooting and IfcGrid with one basiscurve per axis; axes snap in plan and 3D; the grid is visible on the chosen storeys; the spacing dimension chain updates when an axis moves; radial grids (Could) last.
notes: SRS: GRD-001 GRD-002 GRD-003 GRD-004 GRD-005 GRD-006 GRD-007 GRD-008

title: Add open auxiliary sheets as construction aids
description:
WHY: SOL-011 (C): open sheets may be used as construction aids; they are always auxiliary (ELM-014: drawn ghosted, not picked by default but with a modifier or filter, excluded from the building elements written to IFCX). The gap row notes that Element had no auxiliary flag; solid-kernel-ops adds it together with the IFX-068 exclusion.

WHAT: Solid { open: true } validated with ValidateOptions { allow_open: true } (boundary edges allowed, still 2-manifold, oriented and planar). The solid kind sets Element.auxiliary (solid-kernel-ops-09) on creation for open sheets and rejects clearing it through UpdateElements or SetAuxiliary (CommandError::Invalid 'Open sheets are always auxiliary.'). Geometry: open sheets produce a display-only surface and no volumetric part, so they are left out of plan cut fills and the SolidKernel; a new Kind hook has_closed_body(&self) -> bool (default: the descriptor's solid flag) is false for sheets, so AddSolidOperations (solid-kernel-ops-04) rejects a sheet as target or operator (SOL-020 applies to closed bodies only, so ELM-014's 'still act as operators' cannot hold for an open sheet), and Merge solids (18) and Crop (14) reject sheets with a message naming open sheets. Display: ghosted (solid-kernel-ops-11); faces and edges are 3D snap targets (3d-input-navigation-10) and pickable with the 'Pick auxiliary elements' toggle or the pick modifier of solid-kernel-ops-11; a sheet face is a valid picked face for working planes (3d-input-navigation) and for the crop plane (tasks 14, 15). IFCX: written only in the archicraft namespace inside archicraft::auxiliaryElements (solid-kernel-ops-09, IFX-068) through the solid codec (task 04) with open: true. Tool mode Sheet: a planar polygon on the working plane, or an open polyline extruded by a height. Out of scope: thickening sheets into solids.
design: Open sheets reuse PolyMesh and the solid kind rather than adding a kind, so editing (tasks 06, 07, 09) works on them too; validate's allow_open path only skips the closedness and volume checks. The geometry generator returns ElementGeometry without volumetric parts plus its surface for display, so plan.rs slicing never sees an open mesh. Pointers: solid/validate.rs (task 01), kinds/solid.rs (task 02), auxiliary flag and IFX-068 records (solid-kernel-ops-09), ghosting and picking (solid-kernel-ops-11), tools/solid.rs (task 05), snap target provider (point-input-snapping, 3d-input-navigation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: a planar sheet validates with allow_open and the same mesh as a closed solid is rejected; clearing the auxiliary flag of a sheet is rejected; create, undo and redo work.
- Writer test: a project with a sheet writes no building element node and no body for it in the spatial tree, keeps it in archicraft::, and round-trips its faces and open flag.
- A subtract operation with a sheet as operator, Merge solids with a sheet and Crop of a sheet are rejected with messages naming open sheets.
- kittest: in the crop tool (task 15) 'Pick face' accepts a sheet face as the crop plane.
- kittest: Sheet mode creates a ghosted element; a plain click does not pick it, the auxiliary modifier does; 3D point input snaps to a sheet vertex.
- Satisfies SOL-011.
notes: SRS: SOL-011

title: Resolve imports from bundled copies, local files and a local cache
description:
WHY: IFX-004 (M): the system ships local copies of all schema files it writes against, resolves imports from these copies and from the cache of IFX-066, and never requires network access to open, validate or save. IFX-066 (S) clause: imports outside Table 5-2 are kept, with a local copy cached when the file is opened. IFX-081 (S): imports are resolved from the bundled schema copies or from local files; remote URIs are fetched only after consent. IFX-083: unresolved imports are reported. Existing (keep): the bundled copies of the four Table 5-2 files (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/registry.rs:12-17, lookup registry::bundled at 29-35, test at registry.rs:47-54), the unresolved-import warning of IFX-083 (validate.rs:138-145) and the absence of any network code, so the bundled-copies and no-network clauses of IFX-004 already hold. Gap: SchemaSet::for_file (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:116-146) knows only registry::bundled; every other import is a warning and its attributes stay unchecked; there is no cache and no local-file resolution (gap rows IFX-004 and IFX-066); and check_attributes (validate.rs:239-256) reports every attribute that comes from an unresolved import as an undeclared Error, so a third-party file with one unavailable import cannot open cleanly.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/resolve.rs: `ImportResolver` with an ordered chain Bundled (registry.rs) -> ImportCache -> LocalFiles (relative paths and file:// URIs against the opened file's directory) and `Resolution::{Bundled, Cached(PathBuf), Local(PathBuf), NeedsFetch(String), Unresolved(String)}`; resolved imports return the whole IfcxFile so data layers reach compose (task 01) and schemas reach validation. `ImportCache::open(dir)`, `get(uri)`, `put(uri, bytes, source)` (parses as IFCX, enforces the D.9 size limit), with a deterministic index.json; a local import is copied into the cache when the file is opened. `SchemaSet::for_file_with(file, &resolver, problems)` (for_file delegates with a bundled-only resolver); lib.rs gains `load_with(bytes, &LoadContext { resolver, base_dir })` and `pending_fetches(&IfcxFile, &resolver) -> Vec<String>` for the consent step of task 09. The headless fetch seam: `pub trait RemoteFetch: Send + Sync { fn fetch(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FetchError>; }` and `ImportCache::fetch_into(&self, fetcher: &dyn RemoteFetch, uris: &[String]) -> Vec<Result<PathBuf, FetchError>>`, which validates and stores each download through put; the crate ships no implementation (the HTTP fetcher is the app's, task 09). Lenient checking: attributes that are undeclared while at least one import is unresolved are reported as one Warning per unresolved import ('attributes from … cannot be checked') instead of one Error per attribute; with every import resolved the Error stays (IFX-083). App: DataDirs::import_cache() (root/import-cache) in crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/mod.rs; open_path and recovery call load_with with the cache and the file's directory; NeedsFetch is treated as unresolved (today's warning) until task 09. Out of scope: HTTP and consent (09), keeping imports on save (16).
design: Cache file names from Uuid::new_v5(&Uuid::NAMESPACE_URL, uri) (uuid v5 is already a dependency), index.json written with crate::json for byte-stable output and replaced atomically (temp file plus rename; the app's save_atomically lives in the app crate, so add a small helper here). Record the optional Import.integrity (container.rs) in the index but do not verify it until R2 defines its format. Windows paths and file:// URIs need explicit tests; never follow http(s) here. Create the cache directory lazily. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:116-146, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/registry.rs:29-35, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/lib.rs:43-51 (load), crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/mod.rs:16-50 (DataDirs), crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:152-180 (open_path) and 262-285 (recovery).
acceptance_criteria:
- Test: an import given as a relative path next to the file is resolved and its attributes are validated; after that open the file is in the cache, and a second open with the local file removed still resolves it from the cache.
- Test: an https import that is neither bundled nor cached appears in pending_fetches as NeedsFetch, produces the 'not available offline' Warning and the load continues (IFX-083, lenient reading).
- Test: imports of imports resolve recursively with the D.9 cap of 32 imports and a cycle guard; a corrupt cache entry is reported and ignored; put rejects non-IFCX bytes.
- The headless crates have no network-capable dependency (a test asserting archicraft-ifcx's Cargo.toml lists no HTTP client), so opening, validating and saving never need the network (IFX-004).
- Bundled resolution of the four Table 5-2 URIs is unchanged; the registry test and all roundtrip.rs tests stay green.
- The app opens files through load_with; crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs keeps using DataDirs::at(tempdir), so tests never touch the user's cache.
- Test: a file with one unresolvable import and attributes from it gives one Warning naming the import and no Error; once that import is cached, an attribute violating the cached schema gives an Error with the node path (IFX-083).
- Test: ImportCache::fetch_into with a stub RemoteFetch stores and then resolves the download; a stub returning non-IFCX bytes is rejected (no network in tests).
- Registry test (extended): every attribute namespace the writer emits for the samples and goldens is declared by a bundled Table 5-2 file or by alpha/schema.rs (IFX-004: local copies of everything written).
notes:
SRS: IFX-004 IFX-066 IFX-081 IFX-083
IFX-004 partial: bundled copies and offline operation exist (keep); the cache is new. IFX-083 done: unresolved imports stay reported (extend). Appendix D.9: at most 32 imports per file, files up to 2 GB.

title: Add the convert action with the one-time notice and segmentation field
description:
WHY: SOL-004 (M): conversion keeps the evaluated geometry and face materials after confirmation that the parametric definition is lost; NFR-USE-004 (M) allows exactly one notice with a 'do not show again' option for such conversions. SOL-006 (S): when a solid is converted from a curved element, the segmentation is user-controllable and by default no coarser than IFX-034. Epic acceptance: converting a layered wall keeps the evaluated geometry and face materials after one confirmation. Task 08 delivers the headless engine and command.

WHAT: Action ConvertToSolid ('Convert to free-form solid') in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs, the Design menu and the plan and 3D context menus (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs), enabled when the selection contains elements whose KindDescriptor.solid is true. An egui::Modal notice in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs (the Modal pattern of dialogs.rs:227, 'Add a dialog') lists the elements and their hosted elements, states that the parametric definition is lost, offers the HostedPolicy for hosted elements with a body of their own (convert into own solids, default, or delete), shows a segmentation field when a selected element is curved (GeometryKind::is_curved, task 08; 'Auto (n)' from the project tessellation, or a number) and offers 'Do not show again', stored as Preferences.skip_convert_notice in crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs (per user, not in the project, PRJ-007; 'Add a preference' pattern with a row in the Preferences dialog to show it again). OK runs convert_element for each element and executes one Command::ReplaceWithSolids; ConvertError cases are listed and nothing changes; locked elements are reported and skipped (ELM-013). The notice is a reusable component that the crop tool (15) shows as well. Out of scope: the engine and command (08), imported elements (ifcx-interop).
design: One notice for any number of elements (NFR-USE-004 allows exactly one); the component takes the element list and returns the user's choices, so crop shows the same notice and honours the same preference. Conversion runs on the current ModelGeometry; elements with geometry problems are listed as not convertible. Pointers: ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs, ui/dialogs.rs:227 (Modal), persistence/prefs.rs (Preferences, 'Add a preference'), solid_convert.rs and Command::ReplaceWithSolids (task 08).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest convert_layered_wall_after_one_confirmation: run the action on the F2 wall, the notice appears once, OK yields a solid with class IfcWall whose evaluated volume and per-material exposed areas match the wall (task 08 tolerances); with 'Do not show again' ticked a second conversion shows no notice, and the Preferences dialog can turn the notice back on.
- kittest: converting a round test-kinds Dummy with 72 typed into the segmentation field gives 72 side faces; for a straight wall the field is hidden.
- One undo step restores the wall with its hosted opening; Cancel leaves the project unchanged; a ConvertError is listed in the notice and nothing changes.
- Satisfies the confirmation clause of SOL-004 (NFR-USE-004), the user-control clause of SOL-006 for conversions and the epic acceptance for converting a layered wall.
notes:
SRS: SOL-004 SOL-006
Split from task 08 so the engine and the UI are separately sized.

title: Place columns at grid intersections and beams along axes at once
description:
WHY: GRD-005 (S) requires columns to be placeable at all intersections of selected grid axes in one command, and beams along selected grid axes between intersections (COL-002, BEA-010). The gap analysis rates it missing because columns and beams did not exist; the prerequisite epic profiles-columns-beams supplies the column and beam kinds, their Project factories and the Appendix D.2 defaults (column 0.30 x 0.30 m reinforced concrete, centre anchor, top linked to home storey + 1; beam 0.25 x 0.50 m, top-centre anchor). AS-02 requires columns at all 20 intersections on three storeys via this command.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs: `Command::PlaceOnGrid { grid, axes: Vec<AxisId> (empty = all), storeys: Vec<StoreyId>, columns: Option<MemberPlacement>, beams: Option<MemberPlacement> }` where MemberPlacement carries an optional element prototype (default: the column or beam tool-defaults slot) and, for beams, an optional elevation (Beam start_elevation = end_elevation relative to the home storey; with the D.2 top-centre anchor this is the beam top).
