It plans one AddElements: one column per storey and intersection of two selected axes from different sets through Project::new_column(storey, intersection, grid rotation); one beam per storey, selected axis and pair of consecutive intersections with selected crossing axes through Project::new_beam(storey, start, end). Positions already holding a column (same storey, axis point within MODEL_TOLERANCE) or an identical beam are skipped and reported in the outcome message. archicraft-app: a 'Place on grid...' dialog from the grid context menu and the edit-mode palette, using the selected axes (GridPart::Axis, grids-07) or all axes, a storey multi-select (default the active storey) and column/beam checkboxes showing the current defaults; one undo step. Out of scope: junction cleanup between members (COL-006, BEA-004 in cleanup-and-trims), curved beams on radial grids (grids-12), a relation binding members to axes.
design: Approach: use the model-side intersections() of grids-01 (the model crate must not depend on geometry, NFR-MNT-002/004). Beams along an axis: sort the selected crossing axes by offset and emit segments between neighbours. The anchor point of the column prototype (centre by default) is what lands on the intersection, and the beam's top-centre anchor puts its axis on the grid line; document this in the dialog tooltip. Performance: 150+ elements in one AddElements rely on the framework's incremental evaluation; assert the command plans in well under 50 ms on the AS-02 layout. Pitfalls: storeys without a storey above (top storey) for linked column tops - the column kind's validation decides and the command reports the rejected storey instead of failing silently; duplicate detection uses MODEL_TOLERANCE from tolerance.rs. Pointers: profiles-columns-beams kinds/column.rs, kinds/beam.rs and kinds/member.rs (Anchor, CrossSection) with Project::new_column and Project::new_beam (tasks 06 and 07 of that epic), command.rs plan_add_elements (name counters), views/plan.rs:728 (context_menu), ui/dialogs.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- commands.rs: on a 5 x 4 grid with all axes and storeys [00, 01, 02], columns only create exactly 60 columns, each axis point equal to an intersection within MODEL_TOLERANCE and rotation equal to the grid rotation; beams only create 3 x (5 x 3 + 4 x 4) = 93 beams with endpoints at consecutive intersections; one undo removes everything; a second identical run returns NoChange with a message naming the occupied count.
- Selecting axes 1, 3, A and C creates 4 columns per storey and beams only on axes 1 and 3 between A and C and on A and C between 1 and 3.
- Rotation 30 degrees and origin (5, 7): every position equals the rotated intersection within 1e-9.
- Members use the column and beam tool-defaults slots (layer, class, profile, material) and names from the per-kind counters; the beam elevation override sets start_elevation and end_elevation exactly to the given value.
- kittest: select two axes of each set in edit mode, open 'Place on grid...', tick columns and two storeys, OK -> element count grows by 8 and Edit > Undo names the command ('Place 8 columns on grid GR-001').
- GRD-005 satisfied; the grid clauses of COL-002 and BEA-010 are served.
notes: SRS: GRD-005. Related, owned elsewhere: COL-002, BEA-010 (profiles-columns-beams).

title: Capture foreign attributes, nodes and schemas in the model on open
description:
WHY: IFX-066 (S, missing): attributes and nodes from other namespaces or authors that the system does not interpret are preserved unchanged on save as long as the node they belong to still exists; preserved attributes keep their schemas: in-file schemas are copied and imports outside Table 5-2 are kept, with a local copy cached when the file is opened. Today the reader builds a Project and drops everything else (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:735-889) and the writer regenerates the whole document (gap row IFX-066, effort L); crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:317 schema_violations_are_reported shows foreign attributes are reported, never kept. This task gives foreign data a home in the model and captures it on open; writing it back and deriving the written imports from it (IFX-003) is task 16. The same mechanism serves ArchiCraft files annotated by another tool (for example cost codes on walls) and the third-party files of tasks 07-08.

WHAT: Model, format-agnostic: crates/archicraft-model/src/foreign.rs `ForeignData { nodes: IndexMap<String, ForeignNode { attributes: Arc<str> (JSON object text in file order), children: Vec<(String, String)> }> }` on Element (the element node and its sub-nodes by path), Material, Storey, Site, Building and the project node, and `Project.foreign: ForeignStore { nodes: IndexMap<String, Arc<str>> (unowned composed nodes), schemas: IndexMap<String, Arc<str>>, imports: Vec<PreservedImport { uri, integrity }> }`; foreign data travels with element edits, so DeleteElements drops it, undo restores it and Project::duplicate (selection-transforms-03) gives the copy an equal ForeignData (the writer of task 16 remaps its sub-node paths). IFCX reader (ArchiCraft files, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs): per node, attributes the codec does not interpret and children not mapped to model objects go to the owner's ForeignData in file order, unowned nodes to ForeignStore, together with the in-file schemas they need (plus the schema-inherits closure) and the non-Table-5-2 imports (cached on open by task 02, recorded with their integrity). The interpreted key set per node role is declared by the codecs of element-kind-framework-06 (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/), so standard attributes ArchiCraft does not write survive. Schema-violating foreign attributes are captured too and reported with node path on open (IFX-083); dropping them is the writer's decision (task 16). Out of scope: writing (16), third-party element mapping (07, 08), remote fetch (09), material classifications (06).
design: Arc<str> JSON keeps serde_json out of archicraft-model (it is only a dev-dependency there) and the model independent of the file format (NFR-MNT-004). The 'interpreted' key set per node role is declared by the codecs (element codec: bsi::ifc::class, bsi::ifc::prop::Name, IsExternal, Description, usd::xformop, mesh, basiscurves; material node: Name, diffuseColor, opacity, bsi::ifc::material), so standard attributes ArchiCraft does not write (for example a fire rating) survive. Keep a completeness check in debug builds: every attribute of the flattened file is either interpreted or captured. IndexMap everywhere; no HashMap iteration (epic risk: deterministic ordering, IFX-007). Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:735-889 (read), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs (flatten, SchemaSet), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/container.rs:31-36 (Import with integrity), crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:164-185 (Project), crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:317-330.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests (crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs): ForeignData on a wall survives UpdateElements and Transform unchanged; DeleteElements drops it and undo restores it; Transform with copy gives the copy an equal ForeignData; Project PartialEq and the serde round trip include it.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/preservation.rs (capture half) on a golden with injected data (an acme:: attribute with an in-file schema on a wall node, on its Body sub-node and on a material node; a foreign child node under a storey; a non-Table-5-2 import served from a test cache): the attributes land in the owners' ForeignData in file order, the foreign child and its subtree in the storey's ForeignData, the acme schema with its schema-inherits closure and the import in ForeignStore.
- Completeness: every attribute of the flattened input is either interpreted by a codec or captured; a standard attribute ArchiCraft does not interpret (bsi::ifc::prop::FireRating on a wall) is captured.
- Schema-violating foreign attributes are captured and reported with node path (IFX-083).
- Existing goldens load with empty ForeignData and an empty ForeignStore; all roundtrip.rs tests and golden_files_are_reproduced stay green.
notes:
SRS: IFX-066
Writing, schema copying on save and import derivation are task 16. Epic risk: preservation ordering must stay deterministic (IFX-007).

title: Object library, advanced doors and windows, multi-window and cross-project exchange
description:
Generic objects (box, cylinder) and a furniture and fixture set of at least 30 definitions, placement by insertion point with rotation snapping, storey-relative elevation and mirroring (objects rotate about the vertical axis per EDT-007), linked library folders, definition upgrades, save-selection-as-component, on-canvas handles; the catalogue browser with categories, thumbnails, search and two-sided previews, derived values and key points, corner windows, curved units in arc walls and arched openings; and two projects open in separate native windows with copy and paste between them carrying materials, layer structures and profiles with conflict resolution.

Risks: Multi-viewport wgpu lifetimes: the texture side channel is replaced by per-viewport render state first. Content authoring effort; definitions are primitive-based and contain no Graphisoft content (NFR-LEG-002).
design: archicraft-model components extended with library sources and versions; clipboard payload of selection-transforms extended with resource bundles (PRF-009); archicraft-geometry object placement transforms (objects do not cut); archicraft-app catalogue browser with egui_extras thumbnails rendered offscreen, a second eframe viewport with per-viewport render state (fallback: a second process exchanging the serialised payload through the OS clipboard); library files are .ifcx (D-11).
acceptance_criteria: The built-in library lists at least 30 furniture and fixture definitions placed as IfcFurniture with shared type geometry; an object is placed by insertion point and snapped rotation, rotates about the vertical axis and mirrors on request while a request to rotate it about a horizontal axis is refused with the EDT-007 message; relinking a moved library folder restores instances; a selection saved as a component appears in the catalogue immediately; catalogue search and preview from both sides (kittest); clear-opening values and jamb key points are snappable; a corner window spans an L-junction with a post or a frameless connection; a curved unit follows an arc wall; two windows each hold a project with their own wgpu state and pasting a layered wall from one to the other brings its structure, materials and profiles with the use-existing / keep-both / overwrite choice (tests on the headless payload).
notes: SRS: OBJ-001 OBJ-003 OBJ-007 OBJ-008 OBJ-009 OBJ-012 OBJ-013 EDT-025 DW-014 DW-015 DW-016 DW-020 DW-023 PRJ-011 SW-003 PRF-009

title: Open dropped IFCX files; show load problems with node paths
description:
WHY: SW-002 (S, missing): IFCX files dropped onto the application window are opened. Gap: no use of egui raw.dropped_files or hovered_files anywhere in crates/archicraft-app; the drop must go through guard(Then::Open(path)) (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:238-244, the done PRJ-003 unsaved-changes guard) so the unsaved-changes prompt applies. D-11 makes IFCX the only file format, so other files are refused. IFX-083 (S, done): problems are reported with the affected node path and the file opens as far as possible. Existing (keep, extend): the load-report prompt (app.rs:589-600) lists Problem::to_string() lines, and the problems panel (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:848-883) shows load problems, made clickable by element-kind-framework-14 when a path parses to an element UUID. Third-party files (task 07) bring many more problems, often on non-UUID paths, so the report must group and link them.

WHAT: Drag and drop in ArchiCraftApp::ui (the eframe::App method, app.rs:791-866), next to the recent-file guard at app.rs:860-862: the first dropped file with an .ifcx extension and a path goes to self.guard(ctx, Then::Open(Some(path))); other files give the status message 'Only .ifcx files can be opened' (Workspace::error); entries without a path are ignored; drops while a prompt is open are ignored; while ctx.input(|i| i.raw.hovered_files) is non-empty a 'Drop to open' overlay is painted. Load report (Prompt::LoadReport): problems grouped by severity with counts, each row showing the node path and, when the path belongs to an element (its UUID, or Imported.source.node_path of task 04 for third-party paths), the element name and a 'Show' button that selects the element through the problems-panel mechanism of element-kind-framework-14; the File section of the problems panel uses the same path-to-element lookup. Out of scope: consent (09), the 'Changed geometry' section (10).
design: egui gives DroppedFile.path as Option on native; ignore entries without a path. Tests push egui::DroppedFile values into the harness input (RawInput.dropped_files) with the DataDirs::at(tempdir) harness of crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:238-290 (guard, proceed), 548-632 (prompts, LoadReport at 589-600), 791-866 (ui); crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:848-883 (problems_panel); crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs (Workspace::error).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: an .ifcx DroppedFile in RawInput.dropped_files opens it, with the unsaved-changes prompt first when the document is dirty; a dropped .dxf shows the message and changes nothing (SW-002).
- kittest: hovered files show the 'Drop to open' overlay, which disappears when the hover ends.
- kittest: dropping the third-party fixture of task 07 opens it, and the load report groups its problems by severity with node paths (IFX-083); 'Show' on a row of an imported element selects it.
- Regress: the problems of invalid_elements_are_skipped_and_reported and missing_references_are_repaired_and_reported still appear in the load report and in the problems panel.
notes:
SRS: SW-002 IFX-083
IFX-083 done: the load report and the problems panel are extended, not replaced. D-11: IFCX is the only file format.

title: Add the grid kind with axis sets, label series and storey range
description:
WHY: GRD-001 (M) requires orthogonal grid systems, each defining two sets of axes with individual spacings, axis labels from configurable series (A, B, C... and 1, 2, 3...), label bubbles at one or both ends, extension lengths, a rotation angle and an origin. GRD-004 (M) requires a grid system to be visible on all storeys of a chosen range, by default all storeys. SRS 3.2 classes grids as reference elements that are written as IfcGrid (GRD-006; Table 5-1 names the storey as parent node), and decision D-3 keeps exactly one home storey per element, so the range is a visibility property, not a second containment. The gap analysis rates GRD-001 missing with effort L: ElementKind has only Wall and Slab (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:190-194), and the only 'grid' in the code is the drafting snap grid of INP-013 (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:128,254-262, views/plan.rs:150-201 draw_grid), which must stay separate. Every later task of this epic (geometry, IFCX, tools, snapping, GRD-005 placement, AS-02) builds on this payload.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/grid.rs, registered with one line in the kinds! macro of kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework): `Grid { origin: DVec2, rotation: f64, layout: GridLayout, bubbles: BubbleEnds, bubble_diameter: f64 (paper mm), extension: [f64; 2] (start, end), storeys: StoreyRange, chain: [ChainSide; 2] }` with `GridLayout::Orthogonal { sets: [AxisSet; 2] }`, `AxisSet { series: LabelSeries, axes: Vec<GridAxis> }`, `GridAxis { id: AxisId, label: String, offset: f64 }`, `LabelSeries { style: Letters | Numbers, start: u32, prefix: String }` with `label(n)` (A..Z, AA, AB...; 1, 2, 3...), `BubbleEnds { None, Start, End, Both }`, `ChainSide { None, Start, End }` (persisted now, drawn by grids-09) and `StoreyRange { bottom: Option<StoreyId>, top: Option<StoreyId> }` (None = open end; default all storeys) with contains(&StoreyList, StoreyId) and storeys(&StoreyList). Pure headless math in the same module: axis_line(axis) -> [DVec2; 2] including extensions, intersection(a, b) and intersections() -> Vec<(AxisId, AxisId, DVec2)>, so model commands (grids-02, grids-10) never need the geometry crate. Kind descriptor: label 'Grid', code 'grid', name prefix 'GR', default and only class IfcGrid, no top link, vertical_extent None, linked_storeys = range ends, unlink_storey narrows or opens the range, translate moves the origin. Defaults slot in template.rs (Appendix D.2) and a Project::new_grid factory through the defaults slot; validation through the kind's validate hook. Out of scope: geometry and plans (grids-03), IFCX (grids-04), axis edit commands (grids-02), any UI, radial layout (grids-12).
design: Approach: offsets instead of spacings are the stored truth (spacing = difference of consecutive offsets), so moving one axis changes exactly two spacings and the GRD-002 'spacing editable numerically' becomes an offset operation in grids-02. Set 0 holds axes running along local +Y, spaced along local +X and labelled 1, 2, 3...; set 1 holds axes along local +X, spaced along +Y and labelled A, B, C...; the local frame is rotated by `rotation` about `origin`. Each axis spans from the lowest to the highest offset of the other set, extended by extension[0] at its start and extension[1] at its end. GridLayout is an enum from day one so grids-12 adds Radial without touching call sites. AxisId is a Uuid newtype from the ids.rs macro (v4 on creation; fixtures overwrite with v5), because the PartRef addressing of selection-transforms demands stable ids, never indices, and IFCX child ids must survive renames (grids-04). Pitfalls: the framework's Kind::material() returns a MaterialId but grids have no material and no body - change the hook to Option<MaterialId> (or reuse a materials() list if the framework already generalised it) and make plan_delete_material, the material in-use scan and the properties panel skip None; vertical_extent None must not make the framework's storey-command validation (NFR-REL-005) reject grids; storey deletion must go through unlink_storey, never leave a dangling StoreyId in the range. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:190-201 (enums before the framework), kinds/mod.rs kinds! macro and trait Kind (element-kind-framework task 'Split element kinds into a KindDescriptor registry'), ids.rs, storey.rs:88 index_of and :183/:216 insert/remove, template.rs tool defaults, tolerance.rs MODEL_TOLERANCE (moved from validate.rs:9-10 by the framework), command.rs DeleteStorey handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in kinds/grid.rs: LabelSeries Letters maps 1 -> A, 26 -> Z, 27 -> AA, 52 -> AZ, 53 -> BA; Numbers start 1 maps 1 -> 1; prefix 'G' with Numbers gives G1, G2.
- axis_line and intersections for a 5 x 4-axis grid at 6.00 m (4 x 3 bays) with extension 1.50 m: 20 intersections, axis 5 x axis D at (24, 18) for rotation 0, and the rotated values for rotation 30 degrees about origin (5, 7), all within 1e-12; extension [1.00, 2.50] lengthens each axis by exactly 1.00 m at its start and 2.50 m at its end.
- StoreyRange tests on storeys -1, 0, 1, 2: the default contains all four; bottom 0 / top 1 contains exactly 0 and 1 (StoreyList order, negative indices included); a storey inserted later between 0 and 1 is contained.
- Validation rejects with an explanatory CommandError::Invalid and leaves the project unchanged (NFR-REL-005): an empty axis set, duplicate labels across both sets, empty labels or labels containing '/', offsets not strictly increasing by more than MODEL_TOLERANCE, negative extensions, non-finite origin or rotation, bubble diameter <= 0, range bottom above top, range ends missing from the StoreyList.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements, UpdateElements, MoveElements (origin moves), DeleteElements with undo and redo restore the project exactly; DeleteStorey of the range's top storey narrows the range to the storey below through unlink_storey and undo restores it.
- The framework's registry and module-layout tests pass with the new kind: code and prefix unique, IfcGrid is the default class and the only member of ifc_classes, and the code 'grid' occurs only in kinds/grid.rs, one kinds! line and the template defaults.
- cargo test, clippy and fmt green; existing golden files unchanged (no sample contains a grid yet).
- Model part of GRD-001 (axis sets, spacings, label series, bubbles, extensions, rotation, origin) and GRD-004 (storey range, default all) satisfied.
notes: SRS: GRD-001 GRD-004. Appendix D.2: Grid spacing 6.00 m; axes labelled A, B, C... and 1, 2, 3.... Proposed template values not fixed by the SRS: 5 numbered and 4 lettered axes (the AS-02 layout), extension 1.50 m, bubbles at both ends, bubble diameter 8 paper mm, chains off. Open question: roadmap-final.md mentions site-level containment for grids under D-3, but SRS Table 5-1 names the storey as the IfcGrid parent node; this task follows the SRS (home storey = active storey at creation, range for visibility only, Kind::container() of element-kind-framework-07 stays Storey).

title: Merge selected free-form solids into one solid
description:
WHY: SOL-010 (S): free-form solids shall be creatable by merging several selected free-form solids; the gap row notes that merging needs a 3D Boolean union (Manifold, delivered by solid-kernel-ops). SOL-008 (M): the merge result must be a closed manifold or the operation is rejected (NFR-REL-005). SOL-003 (M): face materials and edge flags of the inputs survive where their faces survive.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/solid_convert.rs (task 08): merge_solids(project, geometry, ids) -> Result<MergeOutcome { mesh: PolyMesh, shells: usize }, ConvertError>: every input body is moved into the first solid's storey frame (z by the elevation difference), the bodies are united through solid_from_parts (SolidKernel::union_all with face provenance, face materials kept), coplanar faces of equal material are merged by the planar grouping of task 08, a result face whose plane and material match an input face inherits that face's edge flags on edges that still exist, new intersection edges are hard and visible, and the result is validated; disjoint inputs give a multi-shell PolyMesh (task 01) plus an informational message. App: action 'Merge solids' in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs, the Design menu and the plan and 3D context menus (ui/shell.rs), enabled for two or more selected solids; it executes Command::ReplaceWithSolids { replacements: [(first, merged)], remove: the others } (task 08) as one undo step; name, class and layer come from the first solid; locked solids are refused (ELM-013). Out of scope: subtract and intersect between solids (associative solid operations of solid-kernel-ops), merging non-solid elements (convert them first, task 17).
design: Merging is conversion of several bodies: going through solid_from_parts keeps one code path for provenance, welding and planar grouping. Edge-flag carry-over is a lookup from (plane, material) of each result face to the input faces; an ambiguous match (two input faces in one plane with the same material) takes the first by input order. Multi-shell results are allowed by validate (each shell closed and manifold). Pointers: solid_convert.rs and Command::ReplaceWithSolids (task 08), kernel/ (solid-kernel-ops-02), ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs, docs/implementation-status.md 'Add a command'.
acceptance_criteria:
- Merge tests (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/convert.rs): two unit cubes offset by 0.5 in X merge into a 1.5 × 1 × 1 solid (volume 1.5, 6 faces after coplanar merging); a red and a blue cube keep their colours on their exposed faces; a smooth, hidden edge of an untouched face stays smooth and hidden; two disjoint cubes merge into one element with two shells plus the message; a merge whose result fails validation leaves the project untouched and reports why.
- Solids homed on storeys at 0.00 m and 3.00 m merge onto the first storey with all absolute vertex positions kept.
- kittest: select two solids, run 'Merge solids' → one solid remains; one undo step restores both; with one solid selected the action is disabled.
- The golden sample gains a merged solid; conformance/run.sh stays green.
- Satisfies the merge creation path of SOL-010 and SOL-008 for merge results.
notes:
SRS: SOL-003 SOL-008 SOL-010
Split from task 12 (revolve and sweep tools) because merge depends on the conversion engine, not on the generators.

title: Link IFCX files as read-only reference models shown in 3D
description:
WHY: IFX-084 (C): the user may link an IFCX file as a read-only reference model (for example a structural model or a neighbouring building); it is displayed and snappable, is not merged into the project, and can be reloaded or unlinked. O-14 keeps it C for v1. Gap: no reference-model concept exists in model, document or views (gap row IFX-084, effort L, depending on third-party reading, rendering of external geometry and snapping to it). This task delivers linking, persistence, reload and unlink, the read-only 3D display and the browser entry; plan display and snapping are task 18.

WHAT: Model: `ReferenceModel { id, name, path (relative to the project file where possible), visible }` in Project.references with Command::LinkReference, UnlinkReference and SetReferenceVisible (undoable), persisted as an optional archicraft::project.references member (alpha/schema.rs, declared only when used); no standard content is written for references, so they are never merged (IFX-063 and IFX-068 unaffected). App: the Document (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs) caches one ReferenceScene per reference, composed with tasks 01/02 (remote imports through the consent flow of task 09) and converted to world-coordinate meshes with the mesh extraction of task 07 without creating elements; File > Link reference model… (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs); a 'Reference models' section in the project browser (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/browser.rs) with visibility, Reload and Unlink; crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs build_scene draws reference meshes with a distinct tint, and they are excluded from picking, selection, commands and the writer. A missing file gives a problem and keeps the link. Out of scope: plan display and snapping (18), positioning offsets, clash detection, selecting elements inside references.
design: Reference geometry lives in the app Document cache, never in Project.elements, so selection, commands and the IFCX writer ignore it. Reference coordinates are taken as project coordinates (no alignment offset in v1; noted in the dialog). Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs (project declaration), crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs (build_scene at 102), crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs (pick at 75), crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/browser.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Command tests: link, unlink and visibility with undo; persistence round trip; the standard content of a saved file is identical with and without a linked reference (not merged).
- kittest: linking the task 07 fixture shows it in the browser and in 3D; hiding it removes it from the 3D view; Reload picks up a changed file; Unlink removes it.
- Read-only: clicking a reference mesh in 3D selects nothing, Select all, Delete and transforms never touch reference geometry, and Project.elements is unchanged by linking.
- A missing reference file opens the project with a problem naming it and keeps the link (IFX-084).
notes:
SRS: IFX-084
O-14: reference models are C in v1. Plan display and snapping: task 18.

title: Ship the material category mapping table; write bsi::ifc::material
description:
WHY: IFX-040 (M): every material used by an element or part is written as a node with diffuseColor and opacity, and if the material has a category it also carries bsi::ifc::material with code and uri. IFX-041 (S): categories (code and uri) come from a configurable mapping table delivered with the default template (initially CONCRETE, MASONRY, WOOD, STEEL, ALUMINIUM, GLASS, INSULATION, GYPSUM, STONE, SOIL, PLASTIC, OTHER), with URIs from a bSDD dictionary (open issue O-7). MAT-007 (M): materials are written according to IFX-040, IFX-043 and IFX-041 where implemented. Existing (keep and regress): material nodes with bsi::ifc::prop::Name (IFX-043, done), diffuseColor [r, g, b] and opacity for every used material (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:329-338) and bodies referencing them through inherits.material (writer.rs:376, test spatial_tree_and_identities, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:189). Gap: MaterialCategory is an enum with codes (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:33-89) but there are no URIs, no table, and nothing is written to the standard namespace (writer.rs:329-338); every template material has a category, so IFX-040 is violated today.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs: `CategoryTable { entries: Vec<CategoryEntry { category: MaterialCategory, code: String, uri: String }> }` with lookup, reverse lookup by code or uri (used by tasks 07 and 13) and validation (each of the 12 categories once, non-empty code, absolute https uri); Project.material_categories, filled from a const data table in crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs (default_category_table(), the one place to change when O-7 is decided); Command::SetCategoryTable, undoable. `Material.classification: Classification { FromTable (default), Preserved { code, uri }, Unclassified }` (optional member of the archicraft::project material record, absent = FromTable): FromTable writes the category's table entry; Preserved writes a classification read from another file verbatim (for example the MIDAS dictionary of R2's Hello Wall, task 07); Unclassified writes none (third-party materials without one, shown as 'Other (unclassified)'); changing a material's category in the materials editor sets FromTable. IFCX: optional archicraft::project member materialCategories [{ category, code, uri }] (absent: template table plus an Info problem; optional addition, so no FORMAT_VERSION bump under the alpha/mod.rs rule); the writer adds bsi::ifc::material { code, uri } to every written material node according to its classification (FromTable only when the entry is complete); the reader takes categories from archicraft::project for ArchiCraft files. App: 'Material categories…' dialog (Project menu) with a 12-row table for code and uri and 'Reset to template'; the materials editor shows the category's code. conformance/check.ts checks that bodies whose material has a category carry bsi::ifc::material::code and ::uri after composition. Goldens re-blessed with a reviewed diff. Out of scope: reverse mapping for third-party materials (07), browser grouping (13), an extensible category set.
design: The bundled ifc@v5a.ifcx declares bsi::ifc::material as an Object with String members code and uri, so write it only when both are non-empty. title: Generate revolved and swept solids with rotation-minimising frames
description:
WHY: SOL-010 (S): free-form solids are also creatable by revolving a profile around an axis and by sweeping a profile along a 2D or 3D path. SOL-007 (S): a profile swept along a 3D path keeps a continuous orientation, without flips or twists at direction changes, including between non-coplanar segments; the gap row asks for rotation-minimising frames and tests on non-coplanar segments. SOL-006 (S): revolved (curved) input is segmented by default no coarser than IFX-034 and user-controllable.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/solid/build.rs and a new solid/sweep.rs. revolve(profile in a plane frame, axis point and direction, angle, segments) -> PolyMesh: profile edges on the axis collapse to vertices (no degenerate faces), 360° closes the ring, partial angles add two planar profile caps, edges between consecutive segment faces are smooth and hidden while profile-corner edges stay hard, recorded as CurvedFeature::Revolve. sweep(profile, path: &[DVec3]) -> PolyMesh: the frame is transported along the polyline by the minimal rotation from each incoming to each outgoing tangent (parallel transport, the exact double-reflection result for polylines), the cross-section at a joint lies in the mitre plane so every segment shows the true profile perpendicular to it, open paths get end caps, closed paths distribute the residual twist evenly; tight corners and 180° reversals are rejected through validation and explicit checks. Profiles are simple polygons; 2D paths are lifted at an elevation. Segments for revolves come from segments_for(profile radius extent, angle, tessellation) unless overridden. Out of scope: the tools (12), arc path segments (callers pass polylines until curved-geometry's arcs exist), profile scaling or twist options.
design: Rotation-minimising frames after Wang, Jüttler, Zheng and Liu (2008, double reflection); for a polyline the minimal rotation from t_in to t_out about t_in × t_out is exact, so no numerical drift accumulates beyond floating-point error; keep frames orthonormal by re-orthogonalising once per joint. Mitre plane normal = normalize(t_in + t_out); the joint section is the segment's perpendicular section projected along the tangent onto the mitre plane. Path joints of a polyline are faceted, so side edges at joints are hard and visible. Pitfalls: antiparallel tangents leave the rotation axis undefined (reject); nearly collinear joints should be dropped before sweeping to avoid slivers; the profile's winding must be normalised so outward orientation holds after sweeping. Pointers: solid/build.rs, segments.rs and validate.rs (task 01).
acceptance_criteria:
- Revolve test: a profile from r = 1 to 2 m and 2 m high revolved 360° with n = 36 segments has volume h·(n/2)·sin(2π/n)·(r2² − r1²) within 1e-9 and validates; a profile touching the axis (r1 = 0) gives a closed solid without zero-area faces; a 90° revolve has two planar caps and validates.
- SOL-007 frame-continuity test (crates/archicraft-model/tests/sweep.rs): a 0.2 × 0.1 m rectangle swept along (0,0,0) → (2,0,0) → (2,2,1) → (2,2,3) → (0,3,3): the twist angle about the tangent between consecutive frames is 0 within 1e-9, consecutive profile normals have a positive dot product (no flip), every cross-section perpendicular to its segment is congruent to the profile (side lengths within 1e-9) and the solid validates.
- A path with a 180° reversal and a corner too tight for the profile are rejected with messages.
- A planar L-shaped path gives the same solid as a hand-built mitred prism (vertex sets within MODEL_TOLERANCE).
- Satisfies the generator side of SOL-010, SOL-007 and the revolve segmentation of SOL-006.
notes:
SRS: SOL-006 SOL-007 SOL-010
Closed non-planar paths: residual twist distributed evenly along the length (documented behaviour).

title: Write grids as IfcGrid with Axis_<label> curves and read them back
description:
WHY: GRD-006 (S) requires grids to be written to IFCX as IfcGrid with one curve per axis; Table 5-1 fixes class IfcGrid, parent node Storey and 'one Axis_<label> curve per grid line', and IFX-035 (S) writes grid lines as usd::usdgeom::basiscurves like wall axes. The parametric definition must survive a round trip in the archicraft:: namespace (IFX-060, IFX-061) and identities must stay stable (IFX-010, IFX-011). The gap analysis rates GRD-006 missing: the writer handles only walls and slabs (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:192-217, 361-416) while the basiscurves helper already exists (writer.rs:229-235, 382-389). The conformance check fails every storey child without a mesh body (conformance/check.ts:85-88), which an IfcGrid legitimately lacks.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: declare `archicraft::grid` (layout 'orthogonal', origin, rotation, sets with series and axes {id, label, offset}, bubbles, bubbleDiameter, extension, storeys {bottom, top} as optional ids, chain sides) through the per-kind codec registration of element-kind-framework-06, plus the 'grid' tool-defaults slot and counter; bump FORMAT_VERSION through the migration table of element-kind-framework-12 so older releases flag newer_format. writer.rs: an IfcGrid node under the home storey with bsi::ifc::class IfcGrid (code and uri) and Name, no Body, and one child `Axis_<label>` per NamedCurve, extending the existing wall Axis path of write_element (writer.rs:382-389) instead of adding a second curve writer: points through the existing curve_attribute (writer.rs:229-235, rounded per IFX-007) and node id sub_node_id(grid id, 'Axis/<axis uuid>') (writer.rs:46-48); the child key is the Table 5-1 name Axis_<label>, not the '<Kind>_<hex>' scheme of child_key() (writer.rs:56-66), which stays for the IfcGrid node itself. A grid always evaluates to an ElementGeometry with zero parts, so the 'saved without a body' warning (writer.rs:391-394, raised only when geometry is missing) stays reserved for failed elements. Keep: the wall Axis child and its id stay byte-identical in the existing goldens. reader.rs: read archicraft::grid leniently (report.or defaults with warnings; an unknown range storey becomes an open end with a warning) and ignore the curves, which are regenerated. conformance/check.ts: an IfcGrid needs no mesh but at least one basiscurves child and exactly one per axis declared in its composed archicraft::grid attribute; the summary counts grids and axes. New sample samples::grid_on_storeys (two storeys, rotation 15 degrees, bounded range) registered in samples::catalogue(), so the reference_models example, tests/roundtrip.rs and the CI conformance job pick up its golden file. Out of scope: the radial layout (grids-12), the AS-02 golden (grids-11), IfcGridAxis-style semantics (not in the pinned ifc@v5a schema).
design: Approach: the writer iterates ElementGeometry.curves generically (role -> child key, seed -> v5 node id), so later curve-bearing kinds (IfcAnnotation, ANN-010) reuse it unchanged. Child key from the label as Table 5-1 asks, node id from the axis id so a rename keeps identity; uniqueness and the '/'-free rule for labels are enforced by grids-01 validation, so child keys never collide. Schema enumerations come from model ALL arrays (BubbleEnds::ALL.map(code)); parameters are written at full precision (NFR-ACC-002), only curve points are rounded. In check.ts the composed tree flattens object attributes into 'name::field' keys (as 'usd::usdgeom::mesh::points' shows), so axis counts are read from the flattened archicraft::grid sets; keep the body check for every other class. Pitfalls: writer.rs:391-394 warns when geometry is missing - grids have geometry with zero parts and must be distinguished from failed elements; the IfcGrid uri comes from the framework's IfcClass::uri(); keep D.9 limits untouched. Pointers: writer.rs:192-217 (element_attributes), :229-235 (curve_attribute), :361-416 (write_element); reader.rs:604-713 (read_element); schema.rs:15 (FORMAT_VERSION), :25 (KINDS); conformance/check.ts:67-103; crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs; extension point 'Add an IFCX attribute' in docs/implementation-status.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/roundtrip.rs: grid_on_storeys loads back equal to itself (axis ids, labels, offsets, range, bubbles, extension, chain sides), save-load-save is byte-identical and the written file validates without problems.
- Spatial tree test: the IfcGrid node is a child of its home storey and has exactly one child per axis named Axis_<label>, each with usd::usdgeom::basiscurves of two points at z = 0 matching the evaluated endpoints within 1e-6 m (IFX-031 0.1 mm); renaming an axis changes the child name but not the child node id (IFX-011).
- Golden file grid-on-storeys.ifcx blessed (ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1) and reviewed; existing goldens bit-identical apart from the format version; conformance/run.sh green on all golden files.
- check.ts negative cases: a copy of the golden with one Axis child removed, and one with all curves removed, both fail with a message naming the grid (exercised by a script self-test or a documented manual run in the PR).
- Reader leniency tests: missing bubbleDiameter falls back to the default with a warning; a range naming an unknown storey opens that end with a warning; a FORMAT_VERSION n-1 file without grids still loads through the migration.
- Writing a project with a grid produces no warnings.
- GRD-006 satisfied; the grid clause of IFX-035 satisfied.
notes: SRS: GRD-006. Related, owned elsewhere: IFX-035 (profiles-columns-beams owns the column and beam axis part), IFX-016 compound-part codec (framework) is not needed because axes are curves, not parts.

title: Add the crop tool with roof plane, picked face and three points
description:
WHY: SOL-033 (S) needs a user flow for the non-associative crop with the three plane sources (single-plane roof plane, picked face, three points); decision D-7 asks for explicit commands with previews. Epic acceptance: cropping a wall below a picked face converts it into a closed free-form solid cut at that plane, and moving or deleting the reference afterwards changes nothing.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/crop.rs: CropTool on the current selection, an InputConsumer with steps (1) plane source — 'Pick roof' (only elements whose kind provides crop_plane), 'Pick face' (a PickIndex face hit of 3d-input-navigation-06, as in the PlaneFromFace consumer of 3d-input-navigation-09; sheet faces included once task 13 exists) or 'Three points' (three 3D points through the point-input service on Camera3dSurface, as in SetThreePointPlane of 3d-input-navigation-09); (2) the side to keep by clicking on it, a modifier picks the side to remove (as in SOL-030); preview: the plane as a translucent quad clipped to the selection bounds and the kept part highlighted, computed once per step change with crop_element and cached; commit after the conversion notice of task 17 (same component and 'Do not show again' preference) as Command::ReplaceWithSolids. Action 'Crop…' in the Design and context menus; status messages for elements not touched or fully removed. Out of scope: the associative trim UI (cleanup-and-trims).
design: The preview runs crop_element on clones of the selected elements' evaluated parts; for large selections it is computed on the step change, never per frame (NFR-PERF-005). The plane quad is drawn in the 3D overlay pass and, in plan, as the plane's trace line at the cut height. Use the keep/remove modifier convention SOL-030 prescribes for trims so cleanup-and-trims can adopt the same gesture; the plane quad follows the split-by-plane preview of solid-kernel-ops-16. Pointers: tools/ (point-input-snapping-01), input/surface.rs and face pick (3d-input-navigation), crop.rs (task 14), conversion notice (task 17), ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest crop_wall_below_picked_face (CPU fallback picking): select a wall, run Crop, pick the slab's top face in the 3D pane and click below it → the wall becomes a free-form solid whose top lies in that face's plane, in one undo step; moving and then deleting the slab afterwards leaves the solid's evaluated geometry unchanged.
- Tool unit tests: three collinear points are refused with a prompt; the modifier flips the kept side; Esc cancels one step.
- kittest: 'Pick roof' accepts only plane-providing elements (test-kinds Dummy now, single-plane roofs once roofs lands).
- The preview evaluates crop_element at most once per step change (counter).
- Satisfies SOL-033's user flow and the epic acceptance for cropping.
notes: SRS: SOL-033

title: Draw reference models in plan and snap to them
description:
WHY: IFX-084 (C): a linked reference model is displayed and snappable. Task 14 links it and shows it in 3D; plans and point input need it too. Existing (reuse): mesh slicing slice::slice_loops and loops_to_polygons (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs:35, 151), ViewRange::for_storey (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:70), the per-storey plan cache of Document::plan (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:106-123) and the snap-target index of point-input-snapping-02 (rstar tree in crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs with SnapSource).

WHAT: The Document caches one plan section per (reference, storey), sliced from the reference meshes at the storey's absolute cut height (elevation plus cut-plane height, STR-008) with slice_loops, plus projected outlines below it, and invalidates it on Reload; crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draw_plan draws them under the model with a reference pen from the plan-attributes pen table (a 'Reference' pen added to the default set if missing); point-input snapping gets their nodes and segments through a SnapSource with a new SnapOwner::Reference(id) owner, honouring the reference's visibility (hidden references give no targets). Reference geometry never enters ModelGeometry or PlanDrawing elements. Out of scope: positioning offsets, clash detection, snapping to references in 3D beyond what point-input-snapping offers.

Pointers: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs (draw_plan at 237), crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs (plan at 106), crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs (point-input-snapping-02), plan-attributes default pen set (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs).

- kittest: the plan of a storey shows the section of the linked task 07 fixture with the reference pen; hiding the reference removes it from the plan.

title: Write preserved foreign data back and derive the written imports
description:
WHY: IFX-066 (S): preserved attributes and nodes are written unchanged as long as their node exists, with their in-file schemas copied and their non-Table-5-2 imports kept; task 05 captures them in the model. IFX-003 (M, partial): `imports` references the standard schema files the written attributes come from, at the Table 5-2 versions, plus the imports needed by preserved foreign data. Existing (keep, extend): crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:348-354 writes [ifc core, prop, usd] from the registry.rs:7-10 constants, which is right for today's output (ifc-mat is bundled but correctly not written), but the list is hard-coded and cannot follow preserved data (gap row IFX-003, effort S, depends on IFX-066). IFX-004 (M): saving never requires the network. IFX-083 (S, done): 'lenient reading, strict writing'; schema violations are reported on open (keep, validate.rs:239-256) and must not be written.

WHAT: Writer (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs write and write_element): foreign attributes of task 05 follow ArchiCraft's own attributes per node in original order; foreign child keys and subtrees are written after the owner's own children in tree order; for copies, foreign sub-node paths are remapped to v5 UUIDs from the new owner and the original key (IFX-011); unowned nodes of ForeignStore are written only when reachable from written nodes, in original file order (keeps one root, IFX-013), and type and material nodes that nothing references any more are dropped by the same reachability rule; needed in-file schemas are written after the alpha/schema.rs declarations (a foreign schema whose id ArchiCraft declares loses with an Info problem); imports are computed: the Table 5-2 URIs from registry.rs whose namespaces are actually written (core, prop, ifc-mat only if a bsi::ifc-mat::prop:: attribute is written, usd) in table order, then preserved imports that declare a written attribute or whose content is unknown (unresolved, kept so that saving never needs the network), in original order. When ArchiCraft writes a key that was foreign (task 12 quantities), its own value wins and the foreign copy is dropped, documented in foreign.rs. Strict writing: attributes that violate their schema, or are undeclared although every import resolved, are dropped with a save warning naming path and attribute; schema_violations_are_reported (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:317-330) is updated to these rules. conformance/check.ts accepts `--cache <dir>` to serve cached imports next to the bundled ones (check.ts:40-56). Out of scope: capture (05), third-party element mapping (07, 08), remote fetch (09).
design: Write foreign values through serde_json::value::RawValue (the raw_value feature is already enabled in the workspace Cargo.toml) so they are reproduced byte for byte; round_coordinate (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/json.rs:153) is not applied to them. No HashMap iteration in the write path (epic risk: deterministic ordering, IFX-007). Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:243-424 (write, write_element, material nodes 329-338, imports 348-354), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/registry.rs:7-17, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs (declarations), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs (SchemaSet, check_attributes), crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:317-330, conformance/check.ts:40-56.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/preservation.rs (write half) on task 05's injected golden: all injected data survives save with equal values and order, and saving twice is byte-identical apart from timestamp and dataVersion (IFX-007).
- Deleting the wall drops its foreign attributes, including those of its Body node, from the next save; undo brings them back; a change that removes the Body node (another part layout) drops only the Body's attributes; a copied wall writes its foreign sub-nodes under new v5 paths.
- Foreign nodes that are no longer referenced after deletions are not written, and validate() reports a single root.
- Imports: the existing goldens still write exactly [ifc core, prop, usd] with the registry.rs Table 5-2 URIs and stay byte-identical; a foreign bsi::ifc-mat::prop:: attribute adds the ifc-mat import at its Table 5-2 version; a preserved non-Table-5-2 import is written only while one of its attributes is (IFX-003).
- A file whose non-Table-5-2 import is neither bundled nor cached saves offline with that import and its attributes kept (IFX-004).
- Schema-violating attributes are reported on open with node path (IFX-083) and dropped on save with a warning naming path and attribute; schema_violations_are_reported is updated to these rules.
- conformance/run.sh with --cache passes on the preservation test output (IFX-006 a and b).
notes:
SRS: IFX-066 IFX-003 IFX-004 IFX-083
IFX-003 partial: the registry.rs Table 5-2 constants stay the source of standard URIs (extend). IFX-083 done: extended with strict writing. Epic risk: deterministic ordering (IFX-007).

title: Add the object kind with storey-relative placement and transforms
description:
WHY: OBJ-003 (M): 'Objects shall be placed by insertion point and rotation (with rotation snapping), at an elevation relative to the home storey, and mirrored on request. Their parameters shall be edited in the inspector.' OBJ-001 (M): every project has access to a built-in library with the DW-011 doors, windows and empty openings (delivered by components-dw-catalogue) and generic parametric objects (box, cylinder), which do not exist yet. EDT-007 (M) requires objects to be rotatable about the vertical axis and the system to say when a requested transform cannot be applied; selection-transforms-02 built the per-kind transform hook with the Unsupported refusal and left the object case to this epic. EDT-025 (S): 'Objects shall be rotatable about any axis in 3D.' This task reconciles the two: Upright definitions refuse a plain horizontal-axis request with the EDT-007 message, and a per-instance 'Free orientation' override makes every object rotatable about any axis. Gap rows: OBJ-003 missing (L: no object kind, element.rs:258-270 translates only), OBJ-001 missing for the generic objects, EDT-025 missing. Free-standing component instances exist only as the test-kinds TestInstance carrier of components-dw-catalogue-01.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/object.rs with `Object { insertion: DVec2, elevation: f64, yaw: f64, tilt: Option<DQuat>, orientation: Option<ObjectOrientation>, instance: ComponentInstance }` (insertion point in storey plan coordinates, elevation of the insertion point above the home storey, yaw about the vertical axis, an optional extra orientation used only while the effective orientation is Free, and a per-instance override of the definition's orientation trait, None following the definition), registered with one line in the kinds! macro: label 'Object', code 'object', a name prefix checked by the registry uniqueness test (proposed 'OB', ELM-019), default class taken from the resolved definition, ifc_classes = the Appendix D.5 object list, component()/component_mut(), vertical_extent from the definition extent (last_known.extent for placeholders), rehome keeping the absolute elevation (ELM-007), validator and the transform hook. DefinitionTraits (components-dw-catalogue-01) gains `orientation: ObjectOrientation { Upright, Free }` (serde default Upright; named so it does not collide with host-openings' Orientation) and Definition gains `group: Option<String>` (catalogue group code under the category, e.g. 'furniture/tables'; the built-in door, window and opening definitions get their groups here). The catalogue gains object.box (width, depth, height, material) and object.cylinder (diameter, height, material), category generic, orientation Free, class IfcBuildingElementProxy, ids Uuid v5 of the code, generator keys 'object.box@1' and 'object.cylinder@1' in KNOWN_GENERATORS. Commands: placement through AddElements (definition embedding of components-dw-catalogue-02 applies), `SetObjectPlacement { ids, insertion, elevation, yaw }` with optional members and one undo step; mirroring on request reuses SetInstanceMirrored; `SetObjectOrientation { ids, orientation: Option<ObjectOrientation> }` sets the override in one undo step and clears the tilt when the effective orientation becomes Upright. Project::new_object factory and an ObjectDefaults slot (definition, elevation 0, yaw 0, mirrored false) filled in template.rs. Registry completeness: a geometry stub in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/object.rs (empty ElementGeometry until task 02) and the archicraft::object codec in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/object.rs (insertion, elevation, yaw, optional tilt as [x, y, z, w], optional orientation override; the component attribute comes from the generic codec of components-dw-catalogue-08). Out of scope: geometry and type nodes (02), the furniture set (03, 04), the tool and inspector (05), handles (06).
design: Follow the 'Add an element kind' recipe adapted to the registry (one module plus one kinds! line, as in kinds/insert.rs of doors-windows-core) and the 'Add a command' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md. Transform rules (all through glam, exact quarter turns as in selection-transforms-02): the world transform is T(insertion, elevation) x Rz(yaw) x tilt x S, with S = diag(-1, 1, 1) when mirrored. A reflection about a line with direction angle phi maps it to T' x Rz(2 phi - yaw + pi) x tilt' x S', i.e. mirrored flips and yaw' = 2 phi - yaw + pi, with tilt' = P tilt P for P = diag(-1, 1, 1). A tilted rotation R about an axis point composes Q = R x Rz(yaw) x tilt and splits it again by swing-twist about Z: twist = normalise(0, 0, q.z, q.w), yaw' = twist angle, tilt' = Rz(-yaw') x Q, stored as None when it is the identity within 1e-12. The refusal is a value carrying the definition name, so the message names what the user selected; KindDescriptor.transforms declares RotateAxis support and the effective orientation decides per instance, so the Rotate-about-axis dialog greys out tilted axes for Upright selections (task 05). Pitfalls: parameters of unresolved definitions must stay verbatim (placeholders keep their data); tilt is only meaningful with a resolved Free definition, so a definition swap through RelinkDefinition to an Upright definition drops the tilt with a note unless the instance override is Free; keep Object free of geometry types (NFR-MNT-002). Pointers: kinds/mod.rs (framework), components/{definition,instance}.rs (components-dw-catalogue-01), transform.rs (selection-transforms-02), command.rs SetInstanceMirrored, template.rs tool defaults, alpha/kinds/test_instance.rs as the codec pattern.
acceptance_criteria:
- The registry test lists the 'object' kind with a unique name prefix; the validator rejects non-finite values, a tilt on an Upright definition, and a door or window definition ('Doors and windows are placed in walls'), and normalises yaw to (-pi, pi].
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/objects.rs: Rotate by 90 degrees about a centre moves the insertion exactly (quarter-turn sine and cosine) and adds pi/2 to yaw; Mirror about the y axis flips instance.mirrored and negates yaw, and mirroring twice restores the object bit for bit; Move with dz = 0.4 raises the elevation by 0.4; Scale moves the insertion only and returns a NotScaled note.
- RotateAxis about a vertical axis equals Rotate; RotateAxis about the x axis on an Upright definition (a test definition registered in crates/archicraft-model/tests/objects.rs, because the built-in Upright furniture arrives in task 03) returns CommandError::Unsupported with a message that names the definition, says it can only be rotated about a vertical axis (the EDT-007 message) and names the 'Free orientation' option, and the project is unchanged.
- RotateAxis about the x axis on object.box (Free) and on the Upright test object after SetObjectOrientation(Some(Free)) is accepted: the insertion and elevation rotate about the axis point and the stored yaw and tilt recompose the requested rotation within 1e-12 (swing-twist test), so every object can be rotated about any axis (EDT-025).
- SetObjectOrientation back to None on that tilted Upright object clears the tilt in the same undo step, and undo restores tilt and override.

title: Compose IFCX layers per R2 with inherits expansion into a tree
description:
WHY: IFX-081 (S) requires third-party IFCX files to be composed according to R2: later entries win attribute by attribute, `null` removes children or inheritances, `inherits` is expanded, and children are composed recursively. Today crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:84-107 (flatten) merges same-path entries in file order (later attributes win), keeps null children as None and removes null inheritances, but inherits are never expanded into the inheriting node's attributes and children and there is no recursive composition into a tree (gap row IFX-081, effort L). IFX-083 (S, done) requires composition problems (cycles, unknown references, unresolved imports, schema violations) to be reported with the affected node path while the file still opens as far as possible; the new engine must keep that true. Existing (keep and regress, do not re-implement): Problem and Severity with node paths (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:26-74), schema violations in check_attributes (validate.rs:239-256), cycle and depth checks in roots (validate.rs:258-302), unknown references in dangling_references (validate.rs:305-319), unresolved-import warnings in SchemaSet::for_file (validate.rs:116-150), the lenient reader Report (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:41-66) and the load-report prompt (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:589-600). This is the risk slice of the epic: the R2 semantics are cheapest to prove right after element-kind-framework generalised the reader.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/compose.rs: `compose(layers: &[&IfcxFile]) -> Composition { roots: Vec<ComposedNode>, problems: Vec<Problem> }` where `ComposedNode { path, key, attributes: IndexMap<String, ComposedAttribute { value, origin: Own | Inherited(type path), layer: usize }>, children: Vec<ComposedNode> }`. Layers are stacked weakest first (imported data layers before the importing file, as resolved by task 02); same-path entries are flattened with validate::flatten semantics across layers; inherits are expanded in the order the reference applies them (inherited attributes and children merged beneath the node's own, own entries winning), including overrides of inherited children addressed by sub-path (`<path>/<child>`); children are composed recursively with the D.9 depth limit (MAX_COMPOSITION_DEPTH = 64) and cycle detection through children and inherits; dangling references and cycles are problems with paths, and the acyclic rest still composes. A `flattened_view()` helper produces the compose3 key form (`bsi::ifc::class::code`, `usd::usdgeom::mesh::points`) used for comparisons in task 03. validate::flatten, roots and dangling_references stay as they are for the existing reader; compose.rs reports through validate::Problem with the same messages ('composition cycle', 'composition is nested too deeply', 'refers to the unknown node …'). Out of scope: import resolution (02), R2 example fetching (03), mapping the tree to a Project (07).
design: Port the semantics from the reference code at R2 commit 1a63082 (the checkout conformance/run.sh already makes under conformance/.ifc5): src/ifcx-core layers (layer-stack) for layer order and null handling and src/viewer/compose-flattened.ts (compose3) for inherits order and how inherited children are named; write the findings into the module docs, each backed by a fixture test. Memoise expanded nodes in a HashMap<String, Arc<Expanded>> so a type shared by thousands of occurrences (likely in Tekla House) is expanded once; add a total-node guard with a problem instead of unbounded memory. Paths in third-party files need not be UUIDs; never parse them as such here. Keep IndexMap insertion order everywhere so output stays deterministic (IFX-007). Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/validate.rs:84-107 (flatten), 258-302 (roots, depth and cycle checks), 305-319 (dangling_references); crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/container.rs:37-48 (Option children and inherits for null).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/compose.rs) on synthetic fixtures: two entries for one path merge attribute by attribute with the later value winning; a null child removes the child; a null inheritance removes it; inherits expansion gives the node the type's attributes and children with its own attributes winning; several inherits apply in the documented order; a type inheriting a type composes transitively; an inherited child is overridden through a `<path>/<child>` entry; grandchildren compose recursively.
- Every composed attribute reports Own or Inherited(type path) and its layer (provenance test).
- A cycle through inherits and one through children are reported as Error problems naming the node path, depth > 64 is reported, dangling targets are Warnings with paths, and composition of the remaining nodes continues (IFX-083 re-asserted).
- A data layer below the file composes underneath it: the file's entries win (two-layer test).
- Composing every golden in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden yields one root and the node and mesh counts the writer produced; validate() output on the goldens is unchanged; cycles_are_detected and all other roundtrip.rs tests stay green.
- IFX-083 regress: invalid_elements_are_skipped_and_reported, missing_references_are_repaired_and_reported, schema_violations_are_reported and cycles_are_detected (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:270-381) pass unchanged, and compose problems carry validate::Problem node paths with the existing messages.
notes:
SRS: IFX-081 IFX-083
IFX-081 partial: flatten, roots and dangling_references exist (keep); inherits expansion and recursive composition are new. IFX-083 is done today (keep/regress): this task extends it to the composition engine. Appendix D.9: composition depth at most 64.

title: Ask consent before fetching remote imports; cache the downloads
description:
WHY: IFX-081 (S): remote import URIs are fetched only after user consent; D-12 makes this the only network access of the product. IFX-004 (M): opening, validating and saving never require the network, so declining must still open the file. IFX-066 (S): a local copy of non-Table-5-2 imports is cached when the file is opened (local files: task 02; downloads: here). docs/technology-choices.md:257 plans 'a small HTTP client, for example ureq' for exactly this, to be added with third-party opening (planned for increment 3, pulled into increment 2 with this epic). Gap: open_path (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:152-180) and the recovery arm of proceed (app.rs:262-285) call archicraft_ifcx::load directly, and nothing in the workspace can reach the network (gap row IFX-081).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/fetch.rs implements the RemoteFetch trait of task 02 with ureq (https only, timeouts, the D.9 size cap, no cookies, a plain 'ArchiCraft/<version>' User-Agent) and stores results through ImportCache::fetch_into. Open flow in crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs: read, parse, pending_fetches; if any, a modal Prompt::FetchImports lists the URIs with 'Download and open' and 'Open without them'; the download runs on a background thread with progress in the status line, then load_with; declining opens with unresolved-import warnings. The fetcher is injectable through a new ArchiCraftApp::with_fetcher(Box<dyn RemoteFetch>) for tests (ArchiCraftApp::new keeps the ureq fetcher). ureq is added to [workspace.dependencies] and the app crate only; deny.toml and docs/technology-choices.md (the row moves from 'Planned for v1' to the stack, with the health check and the TLS choice) are updated. Out of scope: remembering consent per host, proxy settings, drag and drop and the load-report upgrade (17), reference models (14).
design: ureq stays out of the headless crates (NFR-MNT-002/004; IFX-004 holds because fetching is a separate, consented step). Background work via std::thread and a channel polled per frame, as in persistence/autosave.rs. TLS backend: rustls brings ring (Apache-2.0 AND ISC) and, with webpki-roots, a CDLA-Permissive-2.0 or (older versions) MPL-2.0 licence; technology choices allow MPL only after review, so prefer the platform verifier or native-tls and record the choice. Plain http:// imports and redirects to http are refused and reported as unresolved. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:92-130 (ArchiCraftApp::new), 152-180 (open_path), 238-290 (guard, proceed), 548-632 (prompts), crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/mod.rs (DataDirs), crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/autosave.rs (thread pattern), resolve.rs (02), deny.toml, docs/technology-choices.md:257.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest with a counting fetcher: opening a file with a remote import shows the consent dialog and the fetcher has been called 0 times; 'Open without them' opens the file with an unresolved-import warning and still 0 calls; 'Download and open' calls it once per URI, caches the result, and reopening the file does not prompt (IFX-081, IFX-066).
- No test performs a real HTTP request; the suite passes without network (IFX-004).
- http:// URIs and redirects to http are refused and reported as unresolved; a download above the D.9 size cap is aborted and reported.
- The headless crates still have no HTTP client (task 02's test stays green); cargo deny check licenses sources bans passes with ureq; docs/technology-choices.md lists ureq with its licence and health check.
notes:
SRS: IFX-081 IFX-004 IFX-066
D-12: no other network access exists. Appendix D.9: the 2 GB file limit applies to downloaded imports.

title: Add fillet and chamfer of solid edges and segmentation changes
description:
WHY: SOL-005 (S) includes fillet and chamfer of edges and changing the segmentation of curved edges and faces; SOL-006 (S) makes the segmentation of curved input user-controllable with a default no coarser than IFX-034 (2 mm, 10°).

WHAT: SolidEdit::Chamfer { edges, distance } replaces each selected edge by a planar face at the given distance along both adjacent faces; corners where three chamfered edges meet get a corner face; v1 supports edges whose end vertices have degree 3. SolidEdit::Fillet { edges, radius, segments: Option<u32> } does the same with planar strips approximating the arc, strip edges smooth and hidden, segments = segments_for(radius, π − dihedral angle, project tessellation) unless given, recorded as CurvedFeature::Fillet. SolidEdit::Resegment { feature, segments } regenerates the faces of a CurvedFeature (extruded circles from task 01's cylinder builder used by task 05's Circle mode, revolves from task 11, fillets, edge chains from task 09; polyline sweeps are faceted and have no feature) while the feature's faces are unchanged since creation (stored face-id set plus a geometric hash); otherwise it is refused with 'The curved surface was edited; its segmentation can no longer be changed.' UI: 'Fillet…' and 'Chamfer…' dialogs (radius or distance with units, segments 'Auto (n)') and 'Change segmentation…' for a face or edge belonging to a feature, all through ui/dialogs.rs as Command::EditSolid. Radii or distances larger than the adjacent faces allow are rejected. Out of scope: variable-radius fillets and vertices of degree above 3 (rejected with a message).
design: Chamfer/fillet: offset the two adjacent face planes inward by the distance (chamfer) or construct the rolling-ball centre line at radius r from both planes (fillet), intersect with the neighbouring faces at the end vertices, and replace the edge by the new face or strips; restricting v1 to degree-3 end vertices keeps the vertex blend to one corner polygon. Strip vertices lie on the exact arc, so the volume formula is exact for the polygonal fillet. Feature regeneration replaces exactly the feature's face set and reconnects to the unchanged boundary loop, so ids outside the feature stay stable. Pointers: solid/ops.rs, solid/segments.rs (task 01), CurvedFeature records (tasks 01, 09, 11), ui/dialogs.rs and widgets.rs (length fields).
acceptance_criteria:
- Chamfer of one unit-cube edge by 0.1 gives 7 faces and volume 0.995 within 1e-9; chamfering the three edges at one corner adds a corner face and validates.
- Fillet of one unit-cube edge with r = 0.2 and the default tessellation uses 9 strips (10° rule) and the volume equals 1 − (r² − ½·r²·n·sin(90°/n)) within 1e-9.
- Resegment of the golden sample's cylinder from 36 to 72 gives 72 side faces, the matching polygon volume and unchanged cap face ids; after a push/pull of one side face the command is refused with the message.
- Resegment of a 360° revolve of task 11 from 36 to 18 segments gives 18 segment faces and the volume h·(n/2)·sin(2π/n)·(r2² − r1²) for n = 18 within 1e-9.
- A fillet radius of 0.6 on the unit cube is rejected with an explanation.
- kittest: the Fillet dialog on a selected edge shows 'Auto (9)' and creates the fillet in one undo step.
- Satisfies the fillet, chamfer and segmentation clauses of SOL-005 and the user-control clause of SOL-006.
notes: SRS: SOL-005 SOL-006

title: Add radial grid systems within a one-day time box
description:
WHY: GRD-007 (C) says radial grid systems may be provided. The epic risk states that radial grids are time-boxed, and the acceptance puts them last, so they can never delay the Must and Should scope or AS-02. The gap analysis rates GRD-007 missing ('polar axes: radii and angular axes').

WHAT: kinds/grid.rs: `GridLayout::Radial { rings: AxisSet (offset = radius), rays: AxisSet (offset = angle from rotation), sweep: Option<(f64, f64)>, ray_extension: [f64; 2] }` with validation (radii > 0 and increasing, angles in [0, 2 pi) and increasing, sweep within a turn), intersections ray x ring and the centre. Geometry: rings tessellated with the project tessellation settings (IFX-034 defaults: 2 mm chordal deviation, at most 10 degrees per segment), rays as segments, both in GridPlan and as NamedCurves; IFCX: layout 'radial' in archicraft::grid and one Axis_<label> basiscurve per ring and per ray; snapping to rays, ring segments, exact ray-ring intersections and the centre (3D follows through the shared source of grids-08 and grids-13); the grid tool gains a Radial mode (centre click, start-angle click); the settings dialog shows ring and ray tables; PlaceOnGrid places columns at ray-ring intersections and straight beams along rays. Time-box cut line: when one day is used up, ship model, geometry, plan drawing and IFCX and file a follow-up bead for snapping, PlaceOnGrid and dialog support. Out of scope: beams along rings (curved members, members-profiles-adv), angular dimension chains beyond a text list of angles.
design: Approach: reuse the shared arc type and its tessellation from drafting-trim-split or curved-geometry when present (same IFX-034 settings, bit-identical vertices across producers); otherwise a local tessellate_arc(centre, r, a0, a1, settings) in archicraft-geometry that those epics can replace. The enum added in grids-01 makes every call site from grids-02..11 a compile error until Radial is handled, which is the checklist. Pitfalls: angular offsets wrap at 2 pi; label series per family (rings lettered, rays numbered by default); a ray-ring intersection set must exclude the centre for columns unless asked. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:27-43 (tessellation settings, stored but unused until now), kinds/grid.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/grid.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: series per family, validation errors with explanations, the intersection of ray 30 degrees with ring r = 5 m at centre + 5 (cos 30, sin 30) within 1e-12.
- Geometry: a full ring of radius 10 m tessellates into at least 36 segments with chordal deviation <= 2 mm, and plan and IFCX use the same tessellation function (identical points).
- tests/roundtrip.rs: a radial sample round-trips equal and passes conformance with one curve per ring and ray.
- If inside the time box: a snap test hits a ray-ring intersection exactly and PlaceOnGrid on a 6-ray x 3-ring grid creates 18 columns per storey.
- GRD-007 satisfied, or partially satisfied with the follow-up bead linked if the cut line was used.
notes: SRS: GRD-007. Could requirement; keep the time box strict.

title: Detect divergent stored geometry on open; offer regenerate or keep
description:
WHY: IFX-065 (S): on opening, if stored evaluated geometry deviates from regenerated geometry (for example because another tool edited the file), the system lists the affected elements; per element the user chooses to regenerate from the parameters or to keep the external geometry, in which case the element becomes an imported (non-parametric) element. IFX-064 sets 0.1 mm as the round-trip tolerance. Gap: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:592-734 reads only archicraft:: attributes and never looks at an element's stored usd::usdgeom::mesh (gap row IFX-065, effort L, depending on the imported kind).

WHAT: The ArchiCraft reader collects the stored body meshes of every parametric element by part key (Body, Body_n, Skin_n, compound part children) into ReadOutcome.stored: StoredGeometry, kept outside the Project. New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/compare.rs: `compare_bodies(stored: &[(String, TriMesh)], regenerated: &ElementGeometry, tolerance) -> Option<Deviation { reason, max_distance }>` (same part keys; fast path: equal after 1e-6 rounding; otherwise symmetric vertex-to-surface distance with an rstar index and a volume check). archicraft-ifcx `divergences(&Project, &ModelGeometry, &StoredGeometry) -> Vec<Divergence>` runs in the app after the first evaluation of an opened document. Command::ConvertToImported { id, parts } (command.rs) replaces the element by an Imported element with the same id, name, layer, storey, class and foreign data, identity placement and parts from the stored meshes; undoable. App: a 'Changed geometry' section of the load report (restructured by task 17) lists the elements with reason and distance and a per-row choice Regenerate (default) or Keep external geometry; Apply executes ConvertToImported for each kept element. PRJ-008's load report exists (crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:589-600) and is extended, not replaced. Out of scope: diffing attributes other than meshes.
design: Use the rstar 0.12 dependency introduced by point-input-snapping-02 (the version geo pins) for an AABB tree of triangles. Vertex-to-surface distance in both directions tolerates re-triangulation; add |volume difference| <= tolerance x surface area. Only parametric kinds are compared (imported elements have no regeneration). Drop StoredGeometry once the dialog is closed to free memory. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:592-734, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:361-417 (part keys), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:22-48, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs, kinds/imported.rs (04), crates/archicraft-app/src/app.rs:589-600 (load report).
acceptance_criteria:
- Test: a golden whose wall Body points are moved by 5 mm (edit helper of roundtrip.rs) reports exactly that wall with a maximum distance of about 5 mm; unchanged goldens and a re-triangulated but identical surface report nothing at 0.1 mm; a missing or extra part key is reported.
- Command test: ConvertToImported keeps id, name, layer, storey and class, the evaluated geometry equals the stored mesh, undo restores the wall; saving then writes the stored mesh and archicraft::imported instead of archicraft::wall.
- kittest: opening the modified file lists the wall; Keep converts it (properties show 'Imported element'); Regenerate followed by save writes the regenerated mesh.
- Elements whose regeneration failed (fallback of NFR-REL-006) are listed as 'cannot regenerate' with Keep preselected.
- The comparison over the 1,000-element stand-in finishes within 1 s (timed test), thanks to the fast path for unchanged elements.
notes:
SRS: IFX-065
Tolerance 0.1 mm (IFX-064, IFX-031).

title: Fetch R2 examples at test time and compare composition to compose3
description:
WHY: NFR-LEG-003 (S): buildingSMART example files used as test inputs are fetched at test time from R2 rather than redistributed, because R2 asks users not to create derivatives. AS-06 (S) and the epic acceptance require Hello Wall, PCERT Building-Architecture and Tekla House to compose with the same tree and mesh counts as the reference compose3. The epic risk names drift of the examples: the commit stays pinned and the test skips with a warning offline. Gap: conformance/run.sh:11-16 already clones R2 at 1a63082 but uses only its code; no test consumes the examples. conformance/.gitignore already ignores node_modules/, .build/ and .ifc5/ (git check-ignore conformance/.ifc5/x confirms it; the technical-debt entry at docs/implementation-status.md:151 is a false positive from checking directories that did not exist yet), but nothing stops an example copied elsewhere from being committed. Proving IFX-081 composition against compose3 now, right after task 01, is the point of the risk slice.
