WHAT: conformance/fetch-r2.sh (called by run.sh) performs a sparse, blob-filtered checkout of R2 at the one pinned commit constant including the examples; conformance/r2-examples.txt lists the example paths used, verified against that checkout: Hello Wall, PCERT Building-Architecture and Tekla House (AS-06) plus the ACCA building of SRS 7.3 (RX-1…n) for the composition comparison only. conformance/.gitignore stays as it is, and the CI conformance job fails if any file named in the manifest, or any tracked file with the content hash of a manifest example, is in git ls-files. conformance/check.ts gains a `--summary` mode that runs compose3 per example and prints JSON (roots, node count, nodes per class code, mesh count, total mesh points); crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/compose_summary.rs prints the same JSON from compose::compose (task 01) with the resolver of task 02. crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/r2_examples.rs finds the checkout through ARCHICRAFT_R2_DIR (default conformance/.ifc5), prints a skip warning when it is absent, and composes each example without Error problems. The CI conformance job (.github/workflows/ci.yml) fetches, runs both summaries, diffs them and runs the Rust test with ARCHICRAFT_R2_DIR set. Out of scope: opening examples into a project (07), the AS-06 edit-and-save run (15).
design: Make the summary order-independent where compose3's order is unspecified: sort the class histogram and compare a sorted list of (depth, class code) pairs instead of raw child order. compose3 flattens object attributes into `<attribute>::<field>` keys (check.ts classOf reads `bsi::ifc::class::code`), so the Rust side counts meshes on `usd::usdgeom::mesh` and classes on `bsi::ifc::class.code`; document the mapping next to flattened_view(). The check.ts fetch override serves bundled schemas; in summary mode log any URI it fetches over the network so task 09's cache can be seeded in CI. Use `git sparse-checkout set src schema examples` with `--filter=blob:none` to keep the download small. Keep the job on the ubuntu runner (sh). The synthetic fixtures of tasks 07 and later are authored from scratch, never adapted from R2 files. Pointers: conformance/run.sh:11-16, conformance/check.ts:18-56 and 105-130, .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-69, .gitignore, crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs (example pattern).
acceptance_criteria:
- The compose3 summary and the compose_summary example produce identical JSON for every manifest example (the three AS-06 files and the ACCA building) at the pinned commit; the CI conformance job diffs them and fails on any difference (IFX-081 against the reference).
- r2_examples passes with the checkout and skips with a printed warning (not a failure) without it, so offline `cargo test` stays green.
- No R2 example is in git: conformance/.gitignore still covers the checkout and build directories, and the CI guard (`git ls-files` against the manifest names and content hashes) passes (NFR-LEG-003).
- The pinned commit is defined once and shared by run.sh, fetch-r2.sh and the manifest; a missing example at that commit fails loudly instead of skipping.
- Imports the examples need are resolved from bundled or local copies or reported per IFX-083; composition proceeds either way.
notes:
SRS: NFR-LEG-003 IFX-081
NFR-LEG-003 partial: run.sh already clones R2 at test time (keep, extend to the examples). Open: the exact example paths at commit 1a63082 are confirmed from the checkout (the SRS names Hello Wall, PCERT Building-Architecture and Tekla House; SRS 7.3 adds the ACCA building).

title: Draw grids in plan and add the grid creation tool
description:
WHY: GRD-001 (M) is a user-facing capability: a user creates an orthogonal grid with origin and rotation and sees its axes, labels and bubbles at one or both ends with the extension lengths; GRD-004 (M) makes it visible on every storey of the chosen range. The gap analysis lists 'its drawing in plan, a creation tool' as missing; the toolbox has only Select, Wall and Slab (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:13-17).

WHAT: archicraft-app: paint every GridPlan of the current plan (grids-03) beneath the elements through a pure grid_shapes(&GridPlan, bubble_radius: f64) -> Vec<GridShape { Line | Circle | Text }> builder in model coordinates and a thin egui painter that maps them to the screen - axis lines in a dash-dot centre-line style, bubbles as circles of bubble_diameter paper millimetres with the label centred and upright, at the configured ends; the selected grid is highlighted. Add crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/grid.rs (in the tools module that point-input-snapping-01 moved out of views/tools.rs) as an InputConsumer of the PointInput service: step 1 origin point, step 2 optional direction (click or typed angle) for the rotation, Enter after step 1 accepts rotation 0; axis counts, spacing, series, bubbles, extensions and storey range come from the grid defaults slot shown in the properties strip; commit = Command::AddElements with Project::new_grid. Wire Action::ToolGrid (toolbox button, Design menu, a free single-key shortcut checked by shortcuts_are_unique), properties.rs gather() mapping ToolKind::Grid -> KindTag::Grid, and workspace.rs select_all. Out of scope: the settings dialog with the axis table (grids-06), axis editing (grids-07), snapping (grids-08), 3D display and 3D snapping (grids-13), dimension chains (grids-09), radial mode (grids-12).
design: Approach: draw through whichever plan path exists when this lands - the egui painter in views/plan.rs draw_plan today, or the lyon/wgpu stroke path of plan-renderer (increment 1) - and emit axis lines as strokes with a dedicated 'grid' role so plan-attributes pens and line types can style them later; text (labels) through the egui painter as an overlay, the approach sections-elevations-dims also plans for annotation text. Paper millimetres resolve against the per-view DrawingScale (crates/archicraft-model/src/drawing.rs from plan-renderer-01); if that has not landed yet, a single paper_mm_to_model(view, mm) helper with a 1:100 constant keeps the switch a one-line change. Dash-dot via egui Shape::dashed_line in screen space; label font height 0.5 x bubble diameter. The tool's preview shows the axes as rubber band through Preview outlines. Pitfalls: labels stay upright at any rotation; the INP-013 drafting grid (draw_grid) is a different feature and stays untouched; the grid tool must not offer body-related defaults (material, layer structure). Pointers: views/plan.rs:150-201 (draw_grid, drafting grid), :237-320 (draw_plan), crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/mod.rs (ToolKind, moved from views/tools.rs:13-17 by point-input-snapping-01), the 'Add a drawing tool' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs toolbox, ui/properties.rs:47-131, workspace.rs:204 (select_all).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool state-machine test without egui (in the style of wall_chain_closes_into_joined_walls): origin click (2, 3) then typed angle 30 degrees yields one AddElements with a grid at (2, 3), rotation 30 degrees and the default 5 + 4 axes at 6.00 m; Esc after the first click cancels without a command; Enter after the first click creates rotation 0.
- Headless grid_shapes test: BubbleEnds Start gives one circle and one label per axis at the start end, Both gives two, None gives none; circles use the paper-size radius and sit centred on the BubbleAnchor plus radius along the outward direction; labels are centred in their bubble and upright (text angle in (-90, 90] degrees) at rotation 0, 30 and 170 degrees; axis lines carry the dash-dot centre-line pattern and run to the extended ends.
- Paper-size helper test: bubble radius in model units = diameter / 2 x scale denominator / 1000 (8 mm at 1:100 -> 0.40 m), independent of the zoom factor.
- kittest: the 'Grid' toolbox button exists, clicking it sets ws.tool.kind to Grid, and after the two input steps the document contains one grid and the plan data of the active storey contains its GridPlan.
- Switching to a storey outside a bounded range shows no grid; switching back shows it (plan data asserted in the kittest).
- Prompt strings are StepSpec prompts with generated key hints (the NFR-USE-003 check of point-input-snapping passes for the new tool).
- GRD-001 creation and plan display and GRD-004 plan visibility satisfied from the user's point of view.
notes: SRS: GRD-001 GRD-004. No D.8 shortcut is mandated for grids (Appendix D.8 lists element tools wall to free-form solid). Soft ordering: DrawingScale (plan-renderer) and the tools module (point-input-snapping) are increment-1 work. Hard ordering: depends on grids-04 so that a grid drawn in the app saves and reopens without loss.

title: Select, inspect, hide, transform and re-layer imported elements
description:
WHY: IFX-082 (S): imported elements can be selected, inspected, hidden, moved, copied, deleted and assigned to layers and storeys, but cannot be edited parametrically. EDT-007 (M): imported elements rotate about any 3D axis, so the Rotate-about-axis dialog of selection-transforms-12 must accept tilted axes for this kind while still refusing them for walls and slabs. AS-06 hides, moves and deletes imported elements in the application.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app: imported elements are pickable in plan (generic body slices) and 3D (id buffer of selection-transforms-06); the properties panel shows Name, IFC class (D.5 combo; an original class outside D.5 is shown read-only until changed), Layer and Home storey (rehome keeps the world position) plus read-only rows Source file, Source path, Parts, Triangles and Closed, with no parameter fields; the reshape palette and edit mode offer nothing for the kind (no PartRefs); the Rotate-about-axis dialog enables options from KindDescriptor.transforms, Mirror shows the hook's refusal naming the kind and Resize shows the position-only note (EDT-006). The project browser lists imported elements under their storeys with the 'Imported element' label. Hiding works through layer visibility (Layer.visible, crates/archicraft-model/src/layer.rs, exists) without kind-specific code; the per-view Hide selection of 3D views (VIEW-040) belongs to 3d-view-restrictions (increment 1, not a prerequisite edge of this epic) and needs no kind-specific code either. Out of scope: editing meshes, reference models (14, 18).
design: Mostly verification that registry-driven UI (properties Fields getters that auto-hide, KindDescriptor.transforms, browser grouping) covers the kind; add only the read-only source rows. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs (Rotate about axis, selection-transforms-12), crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/browser.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs, crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs (selection).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest on the task 07 fixture (crates/archicraft-app/tests/imported.rs): clicking an imported element selects it; the properties show 'Imported element', its class and source and no thickness or height fields.
- kittest: move by a typed vector, copy, and rotate about the axis (1, 0, 1) by 15 degrees succeed; mirror shows the refusal naming the kind (EDT-007); Resize by factor 2 moves it and lists the 'geometry kept' note.
- kittest: delete removes the element and its contained windows; undo restores them.
- kittest: moving it to another layer and hiding that layer hides it in plan and 3D (once 3d-view-restrictions has landed, Hide selection in a 3D view hides it too, without kind-specific code); changing the home storey keeps its world bounds within 0.1 mm (assigned to storeys).
- Entering edit mode on the kind does nothing and no reshape palette appears (never edited parametrically).
notes:
SRS: IFX-082
EDT-007 any-axis clause asserted in the UI for imported elements.

title: Show grids in 3D views and snap to their axes there
description:
WHY: GRD-003 (M) requires grid axes and their intersections to be snap targets in all views (INP-008), and the epic acceptance requires that axes snap in plan and 3D; GRD-004 (M) makes a grid visible on all storeys of its range, which in a 3D view means one set of axis lines per range storey at that storey's elevation. The gap analysis rates GRD-003 missing and notes that the 3D view has no snapping at all (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs); build_scene draws meshes and feature edges only (views/render3d.rs:77-180), and feature edges are drawn only in edge display modes (render3d.rs:570-571). 3d-input-navigation (increment 1, not a declared prerequisite) adds the WorkingPlane and the Camera3d ViewSurface (task 07) and point input in 3D views (task 08), which resolves horizontal working planes against the storey SnapIndex of point-input-snapping-02; grids-08 registers grids in that index. Split from grids-08 so that the plan half does not wait for the 3D input work.

WHAT: 3D snapping: on a horizontal working plane while the active storey lies in the grid's StoreyRange, the grid SnapSource of grids-08 provides axis edges and exact intersections lifted to z = plane elevation through SurfaceFrame.to_model, with the same precedence, MODEL_TOLERANCE deduplication and Tab cycling as in plan; fill any gap the 3D path leaves (range check against the active storey, lift of Intersection-level targets) rather than writing a second source. 3D display: draw every visible grid's axes as dash-dot lines on every storey of its range at the storey elevation, with bubbles and screen-aligned labels at the axis ends, through the Overlay3d painter (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/overlay3d.rs, profiles-columns-beams-12), independent of DisplayMode and hidden with the grid's layer; a View menu checkbox 'Grids in 3D' (Action::ToggleGrids3d next to Action::ToggleReferenceLines, ui/shell.rs:89-93) toggles a preference show_grids_3d (#[serde(default)], outside the project like prefs.show_reference_lines at persistence/prefs.rs:48). Out of scope: grid targets on vertical, three-point or face working planes (3d-input-navigation-08 limits those to drafting-grid and body targets), face snapping and axis guides (3d-input-navigation-10/-11), sections and elevations (sections-elevations-dims-04/-07).
design: Approach: no new snap geometry - the 3D path reuses the grids-08 source through the storey SnapIndex, because plane coordinates equal plan coordinates on horizontal planes (3d-input-navigation-07); this task proves it and closes gaps. Drawing through Overlay3d (egui painter over the 3D image) instead of a GPU line buffer keeps dashes and label text in one place and avoids SceneKey/FrameKey churn; reference lines are drawn on top without depth occlusion, as profiles-columns-beams-12 does for wall and beam axes. Soft dependency: if 3d-input-navigation-07/-08 have not merged, land the overlay and the toggle, keep the snap test against the ViewSurface trait with a stub horizontal surface, and note the gap in the bead. Pitfalls: open-ended ranges and storeys inserted later (reuse StoreyRange::storeys of grids-01); storey elevations change, so key the overlay on the project revision; labels stay screen-aligned. Pointers: views/view3d.rs:102 (ui), views/render3d.rs:77-180 (SceneData, build_scene) and :570-571 (edges only in edge modes), workspace.rs:44 (SceneKey), persistence/prefs.rs:48 and ui/shell.rs:89-93 (the show_reference_lines pattern), 3d-input-navigation-07/-08 designs, profiles-columns-beams-12 (views/overlay3d.rs).
acceptance_criteria:
- Through the ViewSurface trait without a GPU: with a horizontal working plane at storey 1's elevation (3.00 m) and storey 1 in range, a cursor ray through the projected Axis_C x Axis_3 crossing resolves to the exact intersection with z = 3.00 within 1e-9 and kind Intersection, even when a wall edge passes closer; a ray near Axis_B away from crossings snaps on the edge; with storey 1 outside a bounded range no grid candidate appears.
- Tab cycling in 3D reaches the grid intersection among overlapping candidates, and a column axis point on the same intersection collapses into one candidate within MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- Headless overlay test: the 3D grid line list of a 5 x 4-axis grid with a three-storey range holds 27 segments (9 axes x 3 storeys) at the storey elevations within 1e-9; after SetStoreyElevation the segments follow; the list is empty when the grid's layer is hidden or 'Grids in 3D' is off; segments crossing the near plane are clipped at it (project() returns None behind it).
- The grid lines show in every DisplayMode, not only the edge modes, and toggling the preference repaints without rebuilding the GPU scene.
- kittest: the View menu item 'Grids in 3D' toggles ws.prefs.show_grids_3d, and the value survives the preferences save and load round trip.
- The 3D half of the AS-02 step 'axes snap in plan and 3D' is covered; GRD-003 satisfied for 3D views and GRD-004 visibility extended to 3D.
notes: SRS: GRD-003 GRD-004. Related, owned elsewhere: INP-015, INP-016, VIEW-025 (3d-input-navigation).

title: Edit grid axes in plan: pick, drag, add, delete and rename
description:
WHY: GRD-002 (M) requires axes to be addable, deletable, movable and renamable; in plan the expected interaction is direct manipulation of single axes (KB 303962). selection-transforms introduced the part-selection infrastructure of SEL-008 (Selection holds (ElementId, Option<PartRef>), kind-registered PartRef, EditMode) and names grid axes explicitly as a future PartRef with stable addressing; the epic design asks for an axis edit palette reusing it. GRD-005 (grids-10) also needs a selection of axes.

WHAT: archicraft-model kinds/grid.rs: register `GridPart::{ Axis { axis: AxisId }, Intersection { a: AxisId, b: AxisId } }` as the grid's KindPart (PartRef::Kind in crates/archicraft-model/src/selection.rs, selection-transforms-01) through the kinds! entry and implement the part hooks of that task: part_refs, part_label ('axis C', 'intersection C/3'), part_anchor (the start bubble or the crossing point), part_outline (the axis segment) and validate_part (the axis ids still exist). archicraft-app: in edit mode on a grid, hover highlights and click selects an axis (Shift adds, intersections hit-tested as small circles); a palette offers Move (drag, or PointInput with a typed distance -> EditGridAxes::Move with the perpendicular offset), Add parallel axis (click a point -> Add at the projected offset), Delete (Del key, deletes the selected axes, not the grid) and Rename (F2 or double-click on a bubble -> inline text field); the drag previews the moved axis and its two changed spacings and excludes the moved axis from the grid snap source of grids-08 for the duration of the drag; Selection::retain_valid drops deleted axes. Out of scope: rotating single axes (axes stay orthogonal), editing several grids at once, radial families (grids-12).
design: Approach: offset delta = (p - origin) . n_set with n_set the rotated normal of the axis set; the Move command carries the absolute new offset, so typed distances and drags share one path. Hit testing of axes uses GridPlan segments (grids-03) with the snap radius; intersections use GridPlan.intersections. Soft dependency: PartRef and EditMode come from selection-transforms-01 and -08 (increment 1, scheduled before this increment-2 epic but not one of its declared prerequisites); if they are not merged, keep a grid-local axis selection in PlanViewState behind the same palette API and port it when they land. The per-axis snap exclusion is the part-level exclusion grids-08 provides on top of the owner exclusions of point-input-snapping-12 (INP-017). Pitfalls: Del in edit mode must not delete the whole grid; double-click must not start a new tool; excluded snap owners must be restored after the drag. Pointers: selection-transforms-01 design (KindPart macro, stable addressing), crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:54 (selection), views/plan.rs:638 (handle_keys), :728 (context_menu).
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: GridPart::Axis round-trips through Selection; retain_valid drops an axis removed by EditGridAxes::Delete; the module-layout test confirms the variants live only in kinds/grid.rs plus the kinds! line.
- Headless palette test: picking Axis_C of a default grid and typing a move distance of 1.20 yields one EditGridAxes::Move with offset +1.20 along the set normal; with rotation 30 degrees the offset is computed with the rotated normal exactly (1e-12).
- kittest: enter edit mode on a grid, click Axis_B, press Del -> axis count drops by one and the grid remains; one undo restores it; double-click the B bubble, type B' and Enter -> renamed; Esc leaves edit mode.
- While dragging, the moved axis is excluded from the grid snap source of grids-08 (it does not snap to itself or its own intersections) while the other axes still snap, the exclusion is cleared after commit or Esc, and the preview shows the two affected spacings.
- GRD-002 graphical move, add, delete and rename satisfied.
notes: SRS: GRD-002 GRD-005 (axis and intersection selection consumed by grids-10).

title: Add the imported element kind with pass-through mesh geometry
description:
WHY: IFX-082 (S): elements from third-party files become imported elements that keep their geometry, class, name, material and hierarchy position; they can be selected, inspected, hidden, moved, copied, deleted and assigned to layers and storeys, but not edited parametrically. EDT-007 (M, owned by selection-transforms) states that imported elements rotate about any 3D axis and leaves that positive case to this epic through the registry transform hook. IFX-065 needs the kind for 'keep the external geometry'. Gap: no imported or mesh-based kind exists (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:190-194) and the reader skips such nodes (reader.rs:860-870).

WHAT: Model: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/imported.rs, one kinds! line: `Imported { class: ClassCode (a D.5 IfcClass or the preserved original code), placement: DAffine3 in home-storey coordinates, parts: Vec<ImportedPart { key, path, mesh: Arc<ImportedMesh { points: Vec<DVec3>, indices: Vec<u32> }>, material: MaterialId, writes_material: bool, visible: bool, origin: Own | Inherited(type path) }>, source: ImportSource { node_path, file_name } }`; descriptor label 'Imported element', code 'imported', prefix 'IMP', default class IfcBuildingElementProxy, the D.5 class list, no tool. Hooks: validate (finite points, indices in range, triangle list), material/set_material, transform: Move, Rotate, vertical Move and RotateAxis about any axis compose into the placement, Scale moves only the placement origin about the reference point and keeps the mesh, returning TransformNote::NotScaled { parameter: "geometry" } (the EDT-006 position-only rule of selection-transforms-02); Mirror returns TransformError::Unsupported naming the kind (a mirrored third-party mesh needs either a negative determinant, which IFX-051 forbids, or a mirrored type the file does not have); KindDescriptor.transforms declares Move, Rotate, vertical Move, RotateAxis about any axis and Scale; rehome keeps the world position; vertical_extent and plan_bounds from the transformed bounds. Relations: `Relation::Contained { child, parent }` in relations.rs (element-kind-framework-08) for nested imported elements, validated like Host (one parent per child, no cycle) and persisted through archicraft::relations, with Transform and DeleteElements expanded to contained descendants in command.rs and remapped by Project::duplicate. Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/imported.rs turns parts into BodyParts (placement applied, name = key, closed flag from mesh.rs check_closed); invisible parts are not drawn. IFCX: codec crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/imported.rs writes archicraft::imported { class, sourcePath, file, parts: [{ key, path, origin }] } (declared only when present) and the parts as standard mesh children with their stored paths; the reader restores them from those children. FORMAT_VERSION bump with a no-op step in alpha/migrate.rs. A sample in samples.rs gives a new golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/imported-element.ifcx. Out of scope: third-party reading (07) and writing (08), foreign attributes (05, 16), UI (11), conversion from parametric elements (10).
design: Keep mesh points in element-local coordinates exactly as read and change only the placement on transforms, so moving never rewrites third-party geometry. Placement in home-storey coordinates (not parent-relative) means evaluation needs no parent chain; the writer derives parent-relative transforms (task 08). RotateAxis: new placement = Transform::affine() * placement. Share meshes through Arc so ReplaceElement undo snapshots and copies do not duplicate large meshes; serde needs the `rc` feature (workspace serde has only `derive`) or a newtype with manual impls, and PartialEq should try Arc::ptr_eq first. Parts without a material node get a per-colour synthesized material for display and plan fills with writes_material = false, so the writer keeps the original direct colour attributes and writes no material reference. ClassCode keeps classes outside D.5 (for example distribution elements) until the user changes them (ELM-011). Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-02), crates/archicraft-model/src/transform.rs (selection-transforms-02), crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs (element-kind-framework-08), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-15), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:122 (check_closed), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-06), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework-12), crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs and the FixtureBuilder (element-kind-framework-03).
acceptance_criteria:
- commands.rs tests (and the registry-iterating transform test of selection-transforms): Move, Rotate, vertical Move and RotateAxis about the axis (1, 1, 0) by 30 degrees succeed and undo; Mirror returns CommandError::Unsupported whose message names 'Imported element'; Scale x2 about a point doubles the placement offset from that point, keeps the mesh bit-identical and returns the NotScaled note (EDT-007 any-axis clause asserted for this kind, EDT-006 position-only rule).
- Copy gives a new ElementId and new part paths (v5 from the new owner and the part key, IFX-011); deleting a parent removes its Contained children and undo restores both.
- Geometry test: evaluated bodies equal placement times mesh within 1e-9 m; an open mesh is flagged not closed, gets no cut fill and appears as projected lines in the plan output.
- Round trip: a project with an imported element saves and reopens equal (assert_eq on Project); the golden imported-element.ifcx is reproduced and passes conformance/run.sh; FORMAT_VERSION is bumped, the migration chain test passes and the frozen format fixtures still load.
- Module-layout test: only the three kinds/imported.rs modules and one registry line per crate were added.
- kittest: the properties strip shows no parametric fields (thickness, height) for the kind.
notes:
SRS: IFX-082
Appendix D.5: selectable classes for imported elements (IfcBuildingElementProxy default). EDT-007 any-axis rotation of imported elements is asserted here; the requirement belongs to selection-transforms. EDT-006: imported elements are scaled in position only, with the note.

title: Read third-party IFCX files into a project with imported elements
description:
WHY: IFX-081 (S): the system opens third-party IFCX files and composes them according to R2. IFX-082 (S): their elements become imported elements that keep geometry, class, name, material and hierarchy position. IFX-083 (S, done): composition and validation problems are reported with the node path and the file opens as far as possible. MAT-006 (S) needs materials read from other IFCX files. Gap: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:735-745 rejects files without archicraft::project ('not supported yet'), reader.rs:860-870 skips storey children without archicraft::element, and roundtrip.rs:358 third_party_files_are_reported_as_unsupported asserts the refusal.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/third_party.rs maps the composition of task 01 (with provenance) to a Project: the IfcProject root (synthesized with a problem when missing or when there are several roots) gives the project id (path UUID, else v5 from the path) and name; the first IfcSite and IfcBuilding give site and building (further ones are merged with a Warning); each IfcBuildingStorey becomes a Storey whose elevation is the z translation of its accumulated usd::xformop (other components are folded into element placements with an Info); every non-spatial node with bsi::ifc::class below a storey becomes an Imported element (task 04) with its placement in storey coordinates, parts from its class-less mesh descendants (key, path, mesh, material from `inherits.material`, visibility, Own or Inherited origin) and nested classed descendants as their own imported elements linked by Relation::Contained; classed nodes directly below the site become site-level elements (element-kind-framework-07); classed nodes below the building or project without a storey go to a storey 'Imported' at elevation 0 with an Info. Material nodes become project materials (name from bsi::ifc::prop::Name or the path, colour, opacity, category by reverse lookup of bsi::ifc::material in the CategoryTable of task 06; a classification that is not in the table gives category OTHER with Classification::Preserved { code, uri }, so it is written back verbatim, and a material without one gives OTHER with Classification::Unclassified (task 06), so ArchiCraft never replaces or invents a third-party classification; cut fill and priority from the category defaults of plan-attributes). Imported elements go on a new layer 'Imported – <file name>'. Unmapped attributes and nodes, their schemas and the imports are captured as foreign data (task 05). In ArchiCraft files, storey children without archicraft::element become imported elements the same way instead of being skipped. crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/lib.rs load_with dispatches on the presence of archicraft::project. Problems use the existing Report pattern (reader.rs:41-66) and validate::Problem node paths (IFX-083 done: keep, extend to third-party nodes). Out of scope: writing them back (08), consent (09), divergence (10), UI (11).
design: Read from compose::compose rather than validate::flatten so that parts arriving through inherits are marked Inherited(type path); task 08 writes them back through the preserved inherits instead of duplicating them. Split rule: classed non-spatial node = element; class-less descendants with usd::usdgeom::mesh = parts; curves and invisible meshes (usd::usdgeom::visibility invisible, such as Void children) are kept as invisible parts; classed descendants = nested elements. Element ids: Uuid::parse_str(path) or Uuid::new_v5(project namespace, path), with source.node_path keeping the original path for writing (IFX-010 governs ArchiCraft-created nodes; third-party identities are preserved and reported as Info when not UUIDs). One matrix helper converts usd::xformop (4x4, row-major, row-vector convention, translation in the fourth row, IFX-031) and is shared with the writer. Log load time for Tekla House; rely on the memoisation of task 01 and the Arc meshes of task 04. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/lib.rs:43-51, crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:735-889, compose.rs (01), resolve.rs (02), kinds/imported.rs (04), foreign.rs (05), material.rs CategoryTable (06), crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs:358-368.
acceptance_criteria:
- Synthetic fixture crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/third-party/wall-with-windows.ifcx (authored for the test, not derived from R2): project, site, building, storey, a wall whose body inherits a material, a window type inherited by two window occurrences nested under the wall, a foreign attribute with an in-file schema; it opens with one storey, three imported elements (the windows Contained in the wall), materials with colours and table categories, captured foreign data and no Error problems.
- Placement test: storey elevation, element and child transforms compose so that world mesh positions match a hand-computed reference within 0.1 mm.
- A missing site, building or storey, several roots, non-UUID paths, classed nodes without geometry and unknown classes open with Warning or Info problems carrying node paths; nothing is dropped silently (IFX-083).
- With the task 03 checkout present, the three R2 examples open without Error problems and their imported element and mesh part counts equal the classed-node and mesh counts of the compose3 summary; without it the test skips with a warning.
- third_party_files_are_reported_as_unsupported is replaced by third_party_files_open_as_imported_elements; an ArchiCraft file with an extra third-party element under a storey loads it as an imported element.
- All existing roundtrip and golden tests stay green.
- Kept properties (IFX-082): names come from bsi::ifc::prop::Name, classes from bsi::ifc::class with original codes outside D.5 kept, materials from inherits.material; a fixture material classified with a dictionary outside the table reads as OTHER/Preserved and one without classification as OTHER/Unclassified.
notes:
SRS: IFX-081 IFX-082 IFX-083 MAT-006
IFX-083 done: extended to third-party nodes (keep the Report pattern). Open: the model has one site and one building (D-3); additional spatial nodes are merged and reported. O-7: R2's Hello Wall uses a MIDAS material dictionary, hence Classification::Preserved.

title: Snap to grid axes and intersections in plan views
description:
WHY: GRD-003 (M) requires grid axes and their intersections to be snap targets in all views (INP-008). The gap analysis rates it missing: SnapTargets::from_plan collected only plan outlines and wall reference lines (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:164-187) and the 3D view had no snapping. point-input-snapping replaced this with an indexed snap-source API with owner fingerprints and the fixed precedence node > intersection > division > guide intersection > edge > guide > grid (INP-009), and reserves grids as a later target and context-distance provider (INP-021 names grid axes). NFR-ACC-003 treats points closer than 0.01 mm as identical in snapping, so a grid intersection and a column axis point on it must collapse into one candidate.

WHAT: Implement the SnapSource trait of point-input-snapping-02 for grids (crates/archicraft-app/src/input/, next to the plan element source): for every GridPlan on the active storey (range-aware through grids-03) emit each axis segment as an Edge target (on-edge, division and perpendicular points then derive from it) and each intersection as an exact Intersection-level target owned by the grid; bubbles produce no targets; fingerprints from the grid payload keep the rstar index incremental; element and layer exclusions (INP-017, point-input-snapping-12) apply, plus a part-level exclusion of single axes that grids-07 uses while dragging. Implement the ContextProvider trait (input/context.rs, point-input-snapping-13) so live distances to the nearest grid axes show while placing elements (INP-021 names grid axes). Targets are produced in storey plane coordinates, independent of the plan camera, so the same source serves the 3D working plane (grids-13) and section and elevation views (sections-elevations-dims-07 registers grid axes as section edges after grids-done); these three together cover GRD-003's 'all views'. Out of scope: 3D display and 3D snapping (grids-13), section and elevation views (sections-elevations-dims-04/-07, GRD-009), face snapping and axis guides in 3D (3d-input-navigation).
design: Approach: implement the snap-source trait of point-input-snapping for grids, reading PlanDrawing.grids; intersections are precomputed exact points from the model math, not found by intersecting nearby edge pairs (which misses crossings outside the near set and adds rounding). Pitfalls: open-ended ranges and storeys inserted later; a grid's own axes must be excludable while it is being moved (grids-07); keep target deduplication at MODEL_TOLERANCE from the framework's tolerance module, not a new epsilon. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/input/snap.rs (SnapKind, Snap, snap(); moved from views/tools.rs:120-267 by point-input-snapping-01, today's SnapTargets::from_plan at views/tools.rs:164-187 shows the pre-refactor target set), input/context.rs (point-input-snapping-13), point-input-snapping-02/-03/-12/-13 designs.
acceptance_criteria:
- PointInput unit tests: a cursor within the radius of the Axis_C x Axis_3 crossing snaps to the exact intersection (kind Intersection) even when a wall edge passes closer; near an axis away from crossings it snaps on the edge; the midpoint between two intersections is a division snap; a column axis point coinciding with a grid intersection within MODEL_TOLERANCE yields one candidate at the higher level.
- Targets exist on storey 2 only when 2 is in the grid's range; moving an axis (EditGridAxes::Move) updates only the grid's index entries (fingerprint test extended from point-input-snapping-02).
- Excluding one axis (grid id + AxisId) removes that axis's edge and its intersections from the candidates while the other axes still snap; clearing the exclusion restores them (consumed by grids-07).
- The grid SnapSource is built without a plan camera or screen transform (constructed from the project, the storey and PlanDrawing.grids only), so grids-13 and sections-elevations-dims-07 can reuse it.
- Context-distance provider test: placing a column shows the distance to the nearest parallel grid axis and a typed distance places it exactly.
- Tab cycling (INP-009) reaches the grid intersection among overlapping candidates.
- The plan half of the AS-02 step 'axes snap in plan and 3D' is covered; GRD-003 satisfied for plan views (3D in grids-13, sections and elevations in sections-elevations-dims-07).
notes: SRS: GRD-003. Related, owned elsewhere: INP-008, INP-009, INP-017, INP-021 (point-input-snapping, 3d-input-navigation); NFR-ACC-003 (element-kind-framework tolerance module).

title: Generate object geometry and write objects as shared IFCX types
description:
WHY: OBJ-001 (M) needs the generic box and cylinder as parametric 3D geometry with a plan symbol (OBJ-002 through the generator key), and OBJ-003 (M) needs a placed object to appear at its insertion point, rotation, mirroring and storey-relative elevation in plan, 3D and the file. EDT-025 (S): a Free object rotated about a horizontal axis must render and export correctly. Table 5-1 writes free-standing objects as children of their storey; IFX-050/IFX-051 make identical instances occurrences of one type and mirrored ones occurrences of a mirrored type, never with a negative-determinant transform; Appendix D.5 lists IfcFurniture and IfcBuildingElementProxy (default) for objects. Epic design note: objects do not cut.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/components/objects.rs, registered in the generator table of components/registry.rs (components-dw-catalogue-04): generators object.box@1 (closed box, unit-local origin at the centre of the base) and object.cylinder@1 (closed cylinder whose segment count follows the project tessellation settings through the circle-anchored tessellator of curved-geometry-03), each with a plan symbol per detail level (Simplified: outline; Detailed: outline plus centre mark) and the declared key points (base corners, top centre). crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/object.rs replaces the task-01 stub: transform = translation(insertion, home elevation + elevation) x Rz(yaw) x tilt, mirroring folded into the mirrored type (TypeKey.mirrored), evaluated through components::evaluate_instance (components-dw-catalogue-07), so identical objects share one Arc<TypeGeometry>. Plan (plan.rs): Upright objects draw their parametric symbol placed by insertion, yaw and mirror instead of the sliced body; objects whose effective orientation (definition trait or the per-instance override of task 01) is Free and whose tilt is not the identity fall back to the generic slice and projection of their bodies; both stay pickable through world_parts. Objects register no cut source and no void, so walls and slabs are never cut by them. IFCX: objects are written as children of their storey with bsi::ifc::class from the element class, inherits.type to the type node of components-dw-catalogue-09 and a usd::xformop of the proper rotation (row-major, translation in the fourth row, IFX-031). Sample samples::objects() built with the seeded builder: two identical boxes, a mirrored box, a box tilted about the x axis, a cylinder at elevation 0.75 m and one box on the upper storey; registered in crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and in samples() of tests/roundtrip.rs, golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/objects.ifcx. Out of scope: furniture content (03, 04), GPU instancing (perf-tuning-rm-m-l).
design: Reuse the shared-type machinery instead of a second path: TypeKey, TypeCache and world_parts (components-dw-catalogue-07) and the type writer of components-dw-catalogue-09 already work for every element with InstanceGeometry, so this task adds generators, the carrier transform, plan placement and a sample. The box origin at the base centre keeps rotation about the insertion point intuitive; furniture definitions declare their own origins (task 03). Tessellate the cylinder with the single tessellate() of drafting-trim-split/curved-geometry so its facets match arcs elsewhere. The tilted plan fallback uses slice.rs and the cut/projected/overhead classification already applied to bodies. Pitfalls: keep the det > 0 assertion of InstanceGeometry (mirror only through the type); the tilt must enter TypeKey only through the transform, not the type, so tilted and upright boxes share geometry; the element class override (ELM-011) changes the type node because TypeKey includes the class. Pointers: evaluate.rs:20-62, plan.rs:21-60 and :117-160, mesh.rs check_closed, extrude.rs, alpha/types.rs (components-dw-catalogue-09), conformance/check.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: box meshes are closed and outward (check_closed, positive signed volume) with volume w x d x h within 1e-9; the cylinder volume differs from pi r^2 h by no more than the chord-error bound of the tessellation settings.
- An object at insertion (2, 3), elevation 0.75 m on a storey at 3.00 m with yaw 90 degrees has its world bounds exactly where computed by hand; a mirrored object uses a separate TypeGeometry whose meshes still have positive signed volume; two identical objects share one Arc<TypeGeometry>.
- A box tilted by 30 degrees about the x axis renders with the expected bounds, and its plan comes from the body slice instead of the symbol; an untilted box keeps its parametric symbol.
- No wall or slab body changes when an object overlaps it (objects do not cut; geometry test comparing volumes).
- objects.ifcx round-trips equal; conformance/run.sh is green on it; the two identical boxes reference one type node; the mirrored box references a mirrored type; no usd::xformop has a non-positive determinant; the viewer-tree check finds every occurrence mesh through inheritance.
- Satisfies OBJ-001 (generic parametric box and cylinder) and the geometric and file side of OBJ-003 and EDT-025.
notes:
SRS: OBJ-001 OBJ-003 EDT-025
Also: OBJ-002, OBJ-011, IFX-031, IFX-050, IFX-051, Table 5-1, Appendix D.5.

title: Third-party IFCX composition, imported elements, foreign-data preservation and material categories
description:
Goal: Open any IFCX file: composition per R2 (later entries win attribute by attribute, null removes, inherits order) with local schema resolution and consented remote fetch, imported elements with mesh geometry that can be selected, hidden, moved, copied, deleted and re-layered, divergence detection between stored and regenerated geometry, preservation of unknown attributes, nodes and schemas with a local import cache (so the imports actually written are derived from the attributes present), material import from other files, the material category mapping table with bSDD codes and URIs written on material nodes, optional base quantities, drag-and-drop opening and read-only reference models. Pulled from increment 3 to 2 as a risk slice: proving the composition semantics against compose3 is cheapest right after the reader generalisation of element-kind-framework; the AS-06 end-to-end run is re-run at the increment-3 exit.

Risks: R2 examples may drift; the commit stays pinned and the test skips with a warning offline, never a redistributed copy. Preservation ordering must stay deterministic (IFX-007). The O-7 dictionary choice is pending; the mapping table is data, not code.
design: archicraft-ifcx composition engine in validate.rs (flatten, inherits expansion, roots) producing ImportedElement entries and a Foreign side table per node written back verbatim; schema and import cache under DataDirs; ureq for consented fetches (planned in technology-choices); IFX-041 mapping table in template.rs; archicraft-model kinds/imported.rs (pass-through mesh parts, class, name, material, placement); archicraft-app load-report dialog upgrade, consent dialog (D-12) and drag-and-drop via eframe file-hover events; conformance/run.sh gains the R2 sparse checkout.
acceptance_criteria: AS-06 automated: Hello Wall, PCERT Building-Architecture and Tekla House are fetched at test time at the pinned commit (never committed, NFR-LEG-003), compose with the same tree and mesh counts as the reference compose3 in the conformance job, some elements are hidden, moved and deleted, and the saved file preserves unknown attributes and in-file schemas, keeps non-Table-5-2 imports through the local cache and passes IFX-006; a remote import URI opens a consent dialog and no network call happens before consent (test with a blocked resolver); an imported element is selected, hidden, moved, copied, rotated about an arbitrary 3D axis (EDT-007 clause through the registry transform hook), deleted and re-layered, never edited parametrically; a file whose stored geometry deviates from the regenerated one lists the elements with a regenerate-or-keep choice; material nodes carry bsi::ifc::material code and uri from the template's mapping table and pass conformance; NetVolume/NetArea appear as prop@v5a quantities when the option is on; a material library .ifcx imports into the project with category grouping; dropping a file opens it.
notes: SRS: IFX-003 IFX-004 IFX-023 IFX-040 IFX-041 IFX-065 IFX-066 IFX-081 IFX-082 IFX-083 IFX-084 MAT-006 MAT-007 SW-002 NFR-LEG-003

title: Add the revolve and sweep modes to the solid tool
description:
WHY: SOL-010 (S): free-form solids are creatable by revolving a profile around an axis and by sweeping a profile along a 2D or 3D path; task 11 provides the generators, this task the user input. SOL-006 (S): the segmentation of revolved input is user-controllable with the IFX-034 default. SOL-007 (S): the swept result keeps a continuous orientation, which the tool must preserve by passing the path points unchanged.

WHAT: New SolidTool modes in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/solid.rs (task 05). Revolve: profile polygon on the working plane, axis by two points on that plane, angle typed (default 360°), segments 'Auto (n)' from segments_for or a number. Sweep: profile polygon on the working plane, then the path as a polyline through the point-input service: points on one working plane give a 2D path; points on several working planes, typed relative coordinates with ΔZ and snaps to existing 3D points (3d-input-navigation-10) give a 3D path; 'Pick path' instead chooses a chain of connected solid edges with the edit-mode picking of task 07 restricted to edges; Enter finishes; a wire preview shows the path and the profile at both ends, computed from the input points only (no generator run per frame, NFR-PERF-005). Commit: Command::AddElements with the solid from revolve() or sweep(); generator errors (180° reversal, corner too tight) are shown in the step prompt and keep the input. Out of scope: merge (18), subtract and intersect between solids (associative solid operations of solid-kernel-ops), arc path segments (curved-geometry), 2D drafting polylines as paths (drafting-trim-split).
design: Profiles reuse the outline input of the Polygon mode (task 05). Path points are collected in world coordinates and converted to the home storey frame before calling sweep(); the input order is kept exactly so the frames of task 11 are reproduced. 'Pick path' orders the picked edges into a chain by shared vertices and rejects branches. Pointers: tools/solid.rs (task 05), views/solid_edit.rs (task 07), solid/build.rs and solid/sweep.rs (task 11), input/consumer.rs (point-input-snapping-01), views/surface3d.rs and input/snap3d.rs (3d-input-navigation-07/10).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool unit tests: the revolve tool with a 1..2 m rectangle profile about the Y axis and 360° creates the solid whose volume matches task 11's formula, and with 18 typed segments uses 18; the sweep tool with the task 11 path typed as relative coordinates (ΔX, ΔY, ΔZ) produces the same frame-continuous solid (vertex sets within MODEL_TOLERANCE).
- A sweep path drawn on the horizontal working plane (2D path) gives the same solid as task 11's planar L-shaped path test.
- 'Pick path' on a chain of three connected box edges sweeps along them; a selection of unconnected edges is refused with a prompt.
- A path with a 180° reversal shows the generator's message and creates nothing.
- kittest: the sweep tool prompts for the profile and then for path points with Enter to finish; the revolve tool prompts for the axis and the angle.
- The golden sample gains a revolved and a swept solid; conformance/run.sh stays green.
- Satisfies the revolve and sweep creation paths of SOL-010, the revolve segmentation control of SOL-006 and SOL-007 through the tool.
notes:
SRS: SOL-006 SOL-007 SOL-010
Picking 2D polylines or arcs as sweep paths arrives once drafting-trim-split elements exist (path source adapter, no change to sweep()).

title: Automate AS-06 end to end on the fetched R2 examples
description:
WHY: AS-06 (S): open the R2 examples Hello Wall, PCERT Building-Architecture and Tekla House, hide, move and delete some imported elements, then save; the files compose as in the reference viewer, unknown attributes are preserved and the saved file passes IFX-006. It exercises third-party composition (IFX-081) and imported elements (IFX-082) on real files; the epic acceptance adds the same tree and mesh counts as compose3 in the conformance job, preserved in-file schemas, non-Table-5-2 imports kept through the local cache (IFX-066, IFX-003, IFX-004), and examples fetched at test time and never committed (NFR-LEG-003).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/as06.rs (skips with a warning without the task 03 checkout): for each manifest example, load through load_with with a temporary import cache (remote imports from a cache seeded by the conformance job, otherwise reported), assert imported element and part counts against the compose3 summary (read via ARCHICRAFT_R2_SUMMARY), put two deterministically chosen elements on a hidden layer, move one (Transform::Move) and rotate one about a tilted axis, delete one, save to target/as06/<name>.ifcx, and assert that foreign attributes and in-file schemas of untouched nodes are value-equal per path, non-Table-5-2 imports are written with their cache entries present and validate() is clean. The CI conformance job runs conformance/run.sh --cache on the saved files (IFX-006 a and b) and compares the compose3 summaries of source and saved files, allowing only the deleted element's nodes to differ. A kittest smoke test opens Hello Wall by drop (task 17) when the checkout exists and hides an element by moving it to a hidden layer (and with Hide selection once 3d-view-restrictions has landed). Out of scope: the manual visual check in the hosted viewer R4 (once per release).
design: Choose edited elements deterministically (first classed elements per storey in path order) so the run is stable across machines. Summary comparison through a small node script (conformance/compare-summary.mjs) or jq. Pointers: tests and harness of tasks 03, 07, 08, 09 and 17; conformance/run.sh; conformance/check.ts; .github/workflows/ci.yml (conformance job).
acceptance_criteria:
- as06 passes in the CI conformance job with the R2 checkout and skips with a warning offline.
- CI: compose3 summaries of the three saved files equal those of the sources minus the deleted elements; run.sh with the import cache passes on them (IFX-006).
- Per example the test prints preserved attributes, schemas and imports; non-Table-5-2 imports survive through the cache.
- No R2 file is written into the repository (outputs under target/, guard of task 03 green).
notes:
SRS: NFR-LEG-003 IFX-081 IFX-082 IFX-066 IFX-003 IFX-004
The AS-06 run is repeated at the increment-3 exit (roadmap).

title: Transform solid parts with numeric input and edit face and edge attributes
description:
WHY: SOL-002 (M): the vertices, edges and faces of a free-form solid shall be movable, rotatable and scalable in 3D with numeric input, including push/pull of a face along its normal or a chosen axis by a typed distance; task 07 delivers picking, moves along the axis handles and push/pull along the normal, this task rotation, scaling, plane mirroring and push/pull along a chosen axis. SOL-003 (M) needs a UI to assign face materials and edge flags. selection-transforms-10 disables whole-element transforms in edit mode and leaves part transforms to this epic, and the dialogs of selection-transforms-12 and the plane mirror of 3d-input-navigation-13 do the same.

WHAT: In edit mode on a solid, the transform tool (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/transform.rs, selection-transforms-10: Move, Rotate, Mirror, Vertical), the 'Rotate about axis…' and 'Resize…' dialogs (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs, selection-transforms-12; Resize gains a Z factor in edit mode) and the plane mirror (tools/mirror3d.rs, 3d-input-navigation-13) build a PartTransform (task 06) from their inputs and execute Command::EditSolid with SolidEdit::TransformParts on the selected parts instead of showing 'Leave edit mode to transform whole elements.'; centres, axes and reference points come from the point-input service on Camera3dSurface with typed values; 'Keep original (copy)' is disabled for parts. 'Push/pull along axis…' for one selected face takes the axis from an axis arrow (X, Y, Z), a selected edge's direction or two picked points and a typed distance (PushDirection::Axis). Properties strip in edit mode (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs): faces show a material combo (SetFaceMaterial, 'Mixed' for several materials), edges Smooth/Hard and Visible/Hidden toggles (SetEdgeFlags), a single vertex X/Y/Z fields in working units parsed by crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs (TransformParts Move by the difference); element-level fields stay read-only while parts are selected (selection-transforms-08 rule). Failures show the SolidIssue text in the status line and change nothing. Out of scope: picking and handles (07), refinement commands (09, 10).
design: The existing tools keep their step machines; only the commit differs: when the Selection is in edit mode on a solid they lower their Transform (or Plane3) into PartTransform and emit EditSolid, so no transform UI is duplicated. Rotation uses Transform::RotateAxis; Resize in edit mode builds PartTransform::Scale3 with X, Y and Z factors about the chosen reference point. Each strip field change is one command, so undo granularity matches the model tests. Pointers: tools/transform.rs (selection-transforms-10), ui/dialogs.rs Resize and 'Rotate about axis…' (selection-transforms-12), tools/mirror3d.rs (3d-input-navigation-13), solid/ops.rs (task 06), views/solid_edit.rs (task 07), ui/properties.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/units.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest rotate_face_by_typed_angle: in edit mode select the top face of the unit box, 'Rotate about axis…' with axis X through the face centroid and 10° → one EditSolid, the solid validates with 6 faces, and one undo step restores it.
- kittest: 'Resize…' with factor 0.5 about the face centroid on the selected top face gives a frustum of volume 7/12 within 1e-9; a side face scaled by (1, 1, 0.5) validates; 'Mirror about plane' with the top face selected and the horizontal plane at z = 1.25 gives volume 1.5.
- 'Push/pull along axis…' on the top face with the axis through (0, 0, 0) and (1, 0, 1) and the typed distance 0.70711 m gives volume 1.500 within 1e-4 in one undo step; an axis lying in the face plane is refused with a message.
- kittest: selecting an edge and toggling Hidden removes it from ElementGeometry.edges; two selected faces get a new material in one undo step, and the combo shows 'Mixed' for faces of different materials.
- Typing '1.2 m' into a vertex's Z field moves it to z = 1.2 (the top is split by task 06's repair); a value that would self-intersect shows the SolidIssue text in the status line without changing the model.
- Satisfies the rotate, scale and plane-mirror with numeric input and the axis push/pull clauses of SOL-002 and the UI side of SOL-003.
notes:
SRS: SOL-002 SOL-003
Split from task 07 to keep both within three days.

title: Commit AS-02 sample structural_frame with alignment test and golden
description:
WHY: AS-02 (SRS 7.2) is the structural frame scenario: grid 4 x 3 bays of 6.00 m, columns at grid intersections on three storeys, beams on grid lines, slabs and pad footings; it passes when all members sit on grid lines and storey levels within the model tolerance (NFR-ACC-003, 0.01 mm) and the IFC classes are IfcColumn, IfcBeam, IfcSlab and IfcFooting. Appendix F makes AS-02 an exit criterion of increment 2 and the roadmap makes it a committed asset of this epic exercising GRD-005 and GRD-006 end to end; the verification-asset map rates AS-02 not-yet-possible.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs: `structural_frame()` built with the framework's FixtureBuilder (v5 ids from 'structural_frame/...', axis ids included) and commands only: storeys 00 (0.00), 01 (3.00), 02 (6.00) and Roof (9.00), each 3.00 m high; one grid on 00 with 5 numbered and 4 lettered axes at 6.00 m and the default all-storey range; Command::PlaceOnGrid for columns on 00..02 (60) and for beams on 00..02 with start and end elevation = storey height - slab thickness, so the top-centre anchored beam tops meet the underside of the slab above (93); a ground slab on 00 and slabs on 01, 02 and Roof with their top at the storey elevation covering the grid extent plus half a column width; 20 pad footings as slabs with the IfcFooting class and predefined type PAD_FOOTING, 1.20 x 1.20 x 0.50 m centred under each ground-floor column with their top at 00's elevation. Register it in samples::catalogue() so the reference_models example, tests/roundtrip.rs and the CI conformance job include the golden structural-frame.ifcx. Add an expectations sidecar (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/structural-frame.expect.json) that conformance/check.ts reads when present: class counts IfcColumn 60, IfcBeam 93, IfcSlab 4, IfcFooting 20, IfcGrid 1 and one basiscurve per axis (9). Add the alignment test crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/as02.rs. Out of scope: priority clean-up between beams, columns and slabs (cleanup-and-trims; overlapping volumes are acceptable output in v1), AS-01 and the reference models (reference-models epic).
design: Approach: build through Commands only (the FixtureBuilder executes them), so the sample doubles as an integration test of GRD-005 and of journal replay. The footing is a class override of a slab (Table 5-1) with the framework's IfcClass and PredefinedType (element-kind-framework IFX-024 task). The beam level uses PlaceOnGrid's beam elevation override (Beam start_elevation/end_elevation relative to the home storey, D.2 top-centre anchor), computed from the storey list in the fixture. Column tops are storey-linked (D.2: home storey + 1), so the test also proves the link resolves to the next storey's elevation. The sidecar keeps check.ts generic for files without one. Pitfalls: golden size with about 180 elements - keep the pretty golden if it stays below roughly 5 MB, otherwise write this golden compact (IFX-008) and document why; v5 ids for axes must come from the fixture name so renames in later edits of the sample keep stable ids. Pointers: crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs, tests/roundtrip.rs samples(), conformance/check.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-69 (conformance job), the 'Add a sample/golden model' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- as02.rs: every column axis point equals a grid intersection within MODEL_TOLERANCE, and its base and top equal its storey's and the next storey's elevations within MODEL_TOLERANCE; every beam axis lies on one grid axis line (distance <= MODEL_TOLERANCE) between consecutive intersections with its top at the next storey elevation minus the slab thickness; every slab top equals its storey elevation; every footing is centred on an intersection with its top at 00's elevation - checked on parameters and on the evaluated axes and bounds (ElementGeometry).
- Counts and health: 1 grid, 60 columns, 93 beams, 4 slabs and 20 footings; integrity_problems() empty; evaluate reports no problems; every body passes check_closed and stays under 65,535 points.
- tests/roundtrip.rs: structural_frame loads back equal, re-saves byte-identically, and two builds produce identical projects and files (seeded ids).
- conformance/run.sh green on structural-frame.ifcx with the sidecar; a sidecar mismatch (edited count) fails with a message naming the class; the CI conformance job runs it without workflow changes.
- The NFR-ACC-003 alignment part of AS-02 and the IFC-class part are automated; GRD-005 and GRD-006 are exercised end to end.
notes: SRS: GRD-005 GRD-006. Interpretation to confirm in review: 'sit on storey levels' is checked as column base and top at storey elevations, slab tops at storey elevations, beam tops at the underside of the slab above and footing tops at the ground-storey elevation.

title: Add commands to add, delete, move, rename and respace grid axes
description:
WHY: GRD-002 (M) requires individual grid axes to be addable, deletable, movable and renamable, with their spacings editable numerically. The gap analysis rates it missing ('Add/delete/move/rename individual axes with numeric spacing edits; commands and UI'). Every model change must be one undoable Command planned into primitive Edits (the increment-0 command core, crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs) with a precise label, so that Edit > Undo reads 'Rename axis B to B1' instead of a generic update. The grid settings dialog (grids-06), the plan axis palette (grids-07) and the GRD-005 placement all edit axes through these commands.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs gains `Command::EditGridAxes { grid: ElementId, edit: AxisEdit }` with `AxisEdit::{ Add { set, offset, label: Option<String> }, Delete { axis }, Move { axis, offset }, Rename { axis, label }, SetSpacing { axis, spacing, mode: SpacingMode }, Relabel { set, series } }` and `SpacingMode::{ ShiftFollowing, KeepOthers }`, planned into a single ReplaceElement (no new Edit primitive), with label() arms naming the grid and the axis. Add without a label takes the next free label of the set's series; Move re-sorts the set by offset and keeps the axis id and label; SetSpacing sets the distance to the previous axis and either shifts all following axes (default, keeps their spacings) or moves only this axis (the next spacing absorbs the change); Relabel re-applies a series in offset order. Out of scope: UI (grids-06, grids-07), radial families (grids-12), edits spanning several grids.
design: Approach: plan() clones the grid payload, applies the edit, runs the kind validation from grids-01 and emits ReplaceElement, following the 'Add a command' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md (Extension points). Next free label: series.label(k) for the smallest k above the highest series index in use that is not taken; labels outside the series are ignored when computing k. Moves that change the order are allowed (the axis travels past its neighbour) because the user intent is a position; spacings are always recomputed from the sorted offsets. Pitfalls: Command must stay Clone + Serialize + Deserialize; columns and beams placed on the grid earlier (grids-10) are not moved by axis edits because the SRS defines no grid relation - say so in the command docs. Pointers: command.rs Command enum, label() and plan(), edit_lock_reason in project.rs:212, crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs patterns.
acceptance_criteria:
- commands.rs tests for every AxisEdit variant: execute then undo restores the project exactly (revision normalised), redo re-applies, and an unchanged value (rename to the same label, move to the same offset) returns CommandError::NoChange.
- Add inserts at the sorted position; on A, B, C an Add without label yields D; Add keeps every existing axis id; Delete removes exactly one id.
- Rejected with CommandError::Invalid and an explanation, project unchanged: deleting the last axis of a set, a duplicate label, a label containing '/', a Move onto another axis within MODEL_TOLERANCE, a spacing <= MODEL_TOLERANCE, SetSpacing on the first axis of a set ('the first axis has no spacing; move it instead').
- SetSpacing on axis 3 of axes 1..5 at 6.00 m to 7.50 m: ShiftFollowing moves axes 3, 4, 5 by +1.50 m; KeepOthers moves only axis 3 (spacing 3-4 becomes 4.50 m); both exact to 1e-12.
- Relabel of set 0 with Numbers start 10 renames 1..5 to 10..14 in offset order without changing ids.
- A grid that is locked, or on a locked layer, rejects every edit with CommandError::Locked (edit_lock_reason path, ELM-013).
- Commands serialise and replay from the journal (serde round trip of every variant).
- GRD-002 satisfied at the model level (add, delete, move, rename, numeric spacing).
notes: SRS: GRD-002. A grid-to-member relation (members following axis moves) is not required by the SRS and stays out of v1; record it as a follow-up idea only if users ask.

title: Write imported elements back after moves, copies and deletions
description:
WHY: IFX-082 (S): imported elements keep geometry, class, name, material and hierarchy position while being moved, copied, deleted and assigned to layers and storeys. IFX-066 (S): their foreign attributes and nodes survive as long as the owning node exists. IFX-003 (M): the written imports follow from what is written (task 16). IFX-040 (M): every material used by a part is written with diffuseColor and opacity and referenced through inherits.material. AS-06: after hiding, moving and deleting imported elements, the saved file composes as in the reference viewer, preserves unknown attributes and passes IFX-006. Gap: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:361-417 (write_element) regenerates Body children from evaluated geometry with v5 paths, which would duplicate inherited type geometry and lose third-party structure.

WHAT: Writer path for the imported kind (alpha/kinds/imported.rs and writer.rs): the element node keeps its source path (copies get a new UUID path and v5 part paths from the new owner and the part key, IFX-011), its class and Name, its foreign attributes (tasks 05 and 16), its preserved inherits (type references) and a usd::xformop relative to its written parent (storey, site or Contained parent), written when not the identity or when the source had one; own parts are written with their original keys and paths, mesh values, material reference (only if writes_material) and foreign part attributes; inherited parts are not written because the preserved inherits and the reachable type node bring them back. Contained children are nested under their parent node by generalising element-kind-framework-07's hosted-child nesting (write_element nests the hosted end of a Relation::Host under its host through RelationStore::host_of) to a parent_node_of query that also follows Relation::Contained; a child whose parent was deleted goes under its storey with an Info. archicraft::element { kind 'imported', layer, locked, position } and archicraft::imported keep layer and storey assignments; type and material nodes that nothing references any more are garbage-collected (reachability rule of task 16). Material nodes of imported parts keep their source path, foreign attributes (tasks 05 and 16) and classification (task 06: Preserved written verbatim, Unclassified none); diffuseColor and opacity are added from the material's colour only when the source lacked them, so every material used by a part carries them (IFX-040), with an Info on open. Reopening an ArchiCraft-saved file reads imported elements through the ArchiCraft reader with meshes from their standard children. conformance/check.ts gets a third-party mode in which elements that had no body in the source are not required to have one. Out of scope: UI (11), the AS-06 run (15).
design: Parent-relative transform: local = parent_world.inverse() * child_storey_placement, converted with the shared matrix helper of task 07. Never take imported parts from ModelGeometry (it holds transformed copies); take them from the model. Coordinate rounding (round_coordinate, IFX-007) changes values by at most 0.5 micrometre, far below the 0.1 mm tolerance; document it as the one deviation from verbatim preservation. Keep the strict body-and-colour check of check.ts:67-103 for ArchiCraft elements. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:243-424, kinds/imported.rs (04), foreign.rs (05), the preservation writer (16), third_party.rs (07), the hosted-child nesting of write_element and RelationStore::host_of (element-kind-framework-07 and -08), conformance/check.ts:67-103.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round trip on the task 07 fixture: open, move the wall, rotate one window about a tilted axis, copy the other window, delete one window, put the wall on a hidden layer, save and reopen: positions match within 0.1 mm, the copy has new paths, the deleted window and its unused type node are gone, foreign attributes and in-file schemas survive, the layer assignment persists.
- compose::compose of the saved file gives the source's mesh count minus the deleted parts; validate() reports no errors and one root; conformance/run.sh with --cache and the third-party mode passes on the saved fixture (IFX-006).
- Saving twice gives byte-identical files apart from timestamp and dataVersion (IFX-007).
- No transform with a negative determinant is written (IFX-051 assertion).
- An untouched imported element is written with its original attributes and mesh values, the only change being coordinate rounding to 1e-6 m; imports are those of task 16's derivation (IFX-003).
- IFX-040 on imported data: every material referenced by a written imported part is written once with diffuseColor and opacity; a fixture material with a classification outside the table is written with that code and uri unchanged.
notes: SRS: IFX-082 IFX-066 IFX-003 IFX-040

title: Write optional prop@v5a base quantities from evaluated geometry
description:
WHY: IFX-023 (C): elements may carry basic geometric quantities from prop@v5a where they are well defined: Height, Width, Length, Depth, NetVolume, NetArea, NetSideArea and CrossSectionArea, computed from the evaluated geometry. Gap: NetVolume (all kinds), Length (walls) and NetArea (slabs, net of holes) are computed for the properties panel (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:542-572, derived) but nothing is written; the bundled prop@v5a.ifcx, imported by every written file, already declares all eight keys.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/quantities.rs: `BaseQuantities { height, width, length, depth, net_volume, net_area, net_side_area, cross_section_area: Option<f64> }` and a GeometryKind hook `quantities(&Element, &ElementGeometry)` with a default (NetVolume from closed parts only, Height from bounds); walls give Length, Width, Height, NetSideArea (area of triangles facing the reference side) and NetVolume; slabs give Depth, NetArea (up-facing area) and NetVolume; imported elements give Height and NetVolume when every part is closed; the test-kinds Dummy returns Width and CrossSectionArea from its footprint so the write path of every key is exercised, and columns and beams of profiles-columns-beams (increment 1) add Length and CrossSectionArea in their own geometry kind modules; quantities that are not well defined are omitted, never written as 0. ProjectSettings.write_base_quantities (default false, optional member of archicraft::project settings) with a checkbox in the Project settings dialog; when on, the writer adds bsi::ifc::prop::<Quantity> attributes in SI units to element nodes, imported elements through the writer path of task 08, and a computed key replaces a preserved foreign value of the same key (task 16 rule). properties.rs derived() uses the same function. Out of scope: quantity take-off UI (MEA requirements), quantity sets that ifcx_alpha does not define.
design: Round quantities to 1e-9 before writing so output stays deterministic (IFX-007). With the option on, a computed key replaces a preserved foreign value of the same key (task 16 rule); with it off, a foreign value is preserved. Pointers: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:542-572, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:46-48 (volume), crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:105 (signed_volume), crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:396-413, crates/archicraft-ifcx/schemas/prop@v5a.ifcx, crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs (ProjectSettings), crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs (Project settings).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: a 5 m x 0.25 m x 3 m wall gives Length 5, Width 0.25, Height 3, NetVolume 3.75 and NetSideArea 15 (within 1e-9); a slab with a hole gives NetArea = outline minus hole and Depth = thickness; an open imported mesh gives no NetVolume.
- With the option on, written files carry the quantities as prop@v5a attributes, validate() reports no errors and conformance passes on a new golden quantities.ifcx; with the option off every existing golden is byte-identical.
- The derived rows in the properties panel equal the written values.
- The option round-trips; files without it default to off.
- The Dummy (test-kinds) writes Width and CrossSectionArea; with profiles-columns-beams landed, a 0.3 m x 0.3 m column 3 m long writes Length 3 and CrossSectionArea 0.09 (all eight IFX-023 keys exercised).
- An imported element with closed parts writes Height and NetVolume; with an open part it writes Height only.
notes:
SRS: IFX-023
IFX-023 partial: NetVolume, wall Length and slab NetArea are computed for the properties panel (keep, unify through quantities.rs); writing them is new.

title: Verify exit criterion: Free-form solids with sub-element editing
description:
WHY: The epic is complete only when its acceptance holds end to end on the merged code: SOL-001 (box, extrusion, conversion), SOL-002 (sub-element selection, 3D transforms, push/pull with typed distance), SOL-003 (face materials, edge flags), SOL-004 (conversion keeping geometry and face materials), SOL-005 (refinement commands), SOL-006 (segmentation control), SOL-007 (twist-free sweeps), SOL-008 (closed manifold guarantee), SOL-009 (selectable IFC class), SOL-010 (revolve, sweep, merge), SOL-011 (open auxiliary sheets) and SOL-033 (non-associative crop), plus the positive EDT-007/EDT-022 cases for solids.

WHAT: Run the epic acceptance as one checklist against the merged tasks, run the workspace quality gates and the conformance job, update docs/implementation-status.md (rows of all twelve SOL IDs with evidence paths, the 4.22 section counts, readiness of increment 2, the architecture summary of archicraft-model/archicraft-geometry for solids, and remove the 'no arbitrary-plane slicing' remark), and close the epic in beads. No new features; defects found become beads issues under this epic.
design: Map each acceptance clause to its test: SOL-002 cube test (crates/archicraft-model/tests/solids.rs, task 06), layered-wall conversion kittest (task 17) on the conversion engine (task 08), rejection tests (tasks 01, 06), frame-continuity test (crates/archicraft-model/tests/sweep.rs, task 11; tool in task 12), 3D edit-mode kittest (task 07) and part transforms with numeric input (task 16), D.5 class kittest (task 05), EDT-007/EDT-022 kittests (task 05) and model tests (task 02), merge tests (task 18), crop permanence tests (tasks 14, 15). Re-run the golden bless only if a task left it stale and review the diff.
acceptance_criteria:
- Raising the top face of a 1 m cube by 1.000 m gives a 1×1×2 m body (SOL-002 acceptance); converting a layered wall keeps the evaluated geometry and face materials after one confirmation; operations that would open the volume are rejected; a profile swept along a non-coplanar 3D path shows no twist (frame-continuity test); the edit mode selects faces, edges and vertices in 3D with handles (kittest); the IFC class is selectable from the D.5 list. Rotating a solid about an arbitrary 3D axis and mirroring it about a 3D plane succeed where walls refuse (EDT-007/EDT-022 positive cases). Cropping a wall below a picked face converts it into a closed free-form solid cut at that plane, and moving or deleting the reference afterwards changes nothing (SOL-033).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files, including free-form-solids.ifcx with its converted, revolved, swept, merged and cropped solids.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (SOL-001 … SOL-011, SOL-033) with evidence paths, and the per-merge status check of regression-and-status passes.
- The epic free-form-solids is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: SOL-001 SOL-002 SOL-003 SOL-004 SOL-005 SOL-006 SOL-007 SOL-008 SOL-009 SOL-010 SOL-011 SOL-033

title: Add inclined wall faces with lofted bodies, IFCX and fields
description:
WHY: WAL-010 (S): 'Inclined walls shall have one face inclined, or both faces inclined independently, by an angle from vertical.' Gap row WAL-010: 'bodies are vertical extrusions only (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18, evaluate.rs:167)'; it needs inclined faces and non-prismatic bodies. Epic risk: 'Inclined walls interact with openings and junctions: fixtures first' (junctions in task 23, openings in task 16).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/wall.rs: `inclination: Inclination { exterior_deg, interior_deg }` (0 = vertical; equal values give a slanted wall with parallel faces; each face independently settable), validated: finite, below a maximum angle, faces not crossing within the wall height (top thickness at least MIN_THICKNESS), non-zero only on straight axis walls ('Inclined faces are available on straight walls only.'); layered walls keep skin thicknesses when the faces are parallel and interpolate skin boundaries proportionally when the angles differ.
