Geometry (wall GeometryKind, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs): for an unjoined wall, build each skin's ring at the base and at the top elevation from the face offsets at those heights (offset + (z - base) * tan(angle) per face) and loft between the two rings (identical vertex topology; planar quads split into two triangles with hard edges; caps by CDT). Until task 23, an inclined wall at a junction node keeps square ends and reports 'Junctions with inclined walls are not resolved yet.'. Plan cuts slice the lofted bodies; projected lines come from the cap outlines. IFCX: optional `inclination` in archicraft::wall (FORMAT_VERSION bump shared with tasks 06 and 13). App: two angle fields (exterior and interior inclination) in the properties strip (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs) and, if properties-and-dialogs has landed, the wall settings dialog. Out of scope: junction resolution (23), openings and units in inclined walls (16), inclined arc walls (conical faces) and inclined polygonal walls.
design: Two-level construction: for straight walls with planar faces, every face is linear in z, so the rings at the base and top elevations plus a loft are exact. Sign convention to document: a positive angle tilts the top of that face towards the wall's interior side, so equal positive values lean the whole wall inwards. Pitfall: slice.rs assumes nothing about verticality, but up_facing_outline and down_facing_outline (mesh.rs:196-201) now see sloped faces; projected lines of inclined faces must come from the cap outlines, not from the sloped faces. The loft generator is shared with task 23, which feeds it junction-resolved rings instead of square ones.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: validation of ranges and the crossing rule; arc and polygonal walls refuse inclination; command tests with undo.
- Geometry: a 0.30 m wall, 3.00 m high, exterior face inclined 10 degrees and interior vertical: closed body, volume = L x h x (0.30 +/- h tan(10 degrees)/2) within 1e-9 by the sign convention, plan cut width at 1.10 m equals 0.30 +/- 1.10 tan(10 degrees) within 1e-9.
- Independent faces: exterior 10 degrees and interior 4 degrees give a closed body whose cut widths at 0, 1.10 and 3.00 m match the two independent face lines within 1e-9; a slanted wall (both 10 degrees) has constant horizontal thickness.
- An F2-structured wall with exterior 10 and interior 0 degrees: six closed skins whose boundaries interpolate proportionally; disjoint skin interiors.
- An inclined wall touching another wall at a node shows square ends and exactly one problem message; no mesh fails check_closed.
- IFCX round trip with inclination bit-identical; curved_walls() gains an inclined wall; golden re-blessed and conformance green.
- kittest: the properties strip shows both inclination fields for a straight wall and none for an arc wall.
- Satisfies the inclined-face clause of WAL-010 for unjoined walls (junctions in task 23).
notes:
SRS: WAL-010
Appendix D.1 model tolerance; D.2 wall defaults; D.7 F2.
Open question: the maximum inclination (proposed 60 degrees from vertical) is not in the SRS; confirm in the inspection checklist.

title: Add polygonal walls with straight and arc edges
description:
WHY: WAL-009 (S): 'Single-material polygonal walls shall have an arbitrary closed plan outline (straight and arc edges) extruded between base and top.' Gap row WAL-009: missing; it needs a polygonal wall kind with junctions with line walls (task 22), a tool and IFCX. NFR-USE-002: polygonal walls get the same outline editing (palette, union/difference of task 19, fillet of task 10) as slabs.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/wall.rs: add `WallShape::Polygonal(Outline)` beside the `Axis(Segment)` variant of task 02; for polygonal walls the reference-line fields (reference-line location, flip, the thickness of `Structure::Thickness`) do not apply and their getters return None, the material of `Structure::Thickness { material, .. }` (layer-structures-02) is used, and base offset and top (ELM-006, fixed height or storey link) apply unchanged; validation through the Outline pipeline of task 01; the outline reshape hook makes the palette, union/difference and fillet/chamfer work. Geometry: the wall GeometryKind extrudes the tessellated outline (task 03) between the wall's base and top elevations with smooth arc faces. IFCX: archicraft::wall gains `shape` with 'polygonal' plus outline/holes and the edge arrays through the alpha/kinds/common.rs outline helper of task 06 (FORMAT_VERSION bump shared with task 06). App: WallMode::Polygonal in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/wall.rs using the shared polygon input with arc segments and the circle mode of task 08; contour detection with the wall tool in Polygonal mode creates a polygonal wall from a region; the door and window tool and the opening tool refuse polygonal hosts with 'Doors and windows need a wall with a reference line.' Every consumer of Wall that assumes an axis (snap sources, plan reference line, insert host frame, properties, junction inputs) matches on WallShape; until task 22 a polygonal wall takes no part in junctions. Out of scope: junctions (22), layer structures (14), inclination (15), hosting units in polygonal walls.
design: Keep polygonal walls inside the wall kind (same IFC class IfcWall, name prefix W, defaults, layers, top link, join group) rather than a new kind: the SRS treats them as a wall geometry method, and wall-wide features (top linking, join groups, priority) then apply unchanged; task 02 already introduced WallShape so this is one new variant. The selection-transforms PartRef for polygonal walls is the outline's (nodes, edges, rings), like slabs. Pitfalls: Wall::same_settings (drafting-trim-split-12) and the split/trim planners must refuse polygonal walls with a message rather than panicking on a missing axis; the plan reference-line drawing skips them; the properties strip hides the reference-line and thickness rows for them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: create, validate, translate/rotate/mirror and reshape (offset edge, union with a rectangle, FilletAll r = 0.2 of task 10) a polygonal wall with an arc edge, each with undo; the kind-coverage test of task 10 now includes polygonal walls.
- Geometry: closed body from base to top, smooth arc faces, plan cut equals the outline polygon at the cut height; with the top linked to the upper storey, raising that storey by 0.5 m raises the body top by 0.5 m, and a base offset of -0.10 m lowers its bottom (WAL-009 'extruded between base and top').
- IFCX: curved_walls() gains a polygonal wall; round trip bit-identical; golden re-blessed and conformance green.
- kittest: the Wall tool shows a 'Polygonal' mode that creates one polygonal wall (polygon with an arc segment, and circle); the window tool over it shows the refusal message.
- All existing wall tests pass unchanged.
- Satisfies WAL-009 except its junctions with line walls (task 22).
notes:
SRS: WAL-009
Appendix D.2 wall defaults apply (0.25 m masonry material; thickness unused).
Coordinate the FORMAT_VERSION bump with tasks 06 and 15.

title: Add sub-element transforms and push/pull as validated solid edits
description:
WHY: SOL-002 (M): vertices, edges and faces of a free-form solid are selectable individually or in any combination and movable, rotatable and scalable in 3D with numeric input, including push/pull of a face along its normal or a chosen axis by a typed distance; acceptance: raising the top face of a 1 m cube by 1.000 m yields a 1 × 1 × 2 m box. SOL-008 (M): operations that would open the volume are rejected or repaired (NFR-REL-005). SOL-003 (M): face materials and edge flags must be editable by command. The gap rows rate SOL-002 XL and missing: only the element-level 2D translate exists.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/solid/ops.rs: enum SolidEdit (not SolidOp, which relations.rs already defines for solid-kernel-ops-04) { TransformParts { parts: Vec<SolidPart>, transform: PartTransform }, PushPull { face: FaceId, direction: PushDirection { Normal, Axis(DVec3) }, distance: f64 }, SetFaceMaterial { faces, material }, SetEdgeFlags { edges, smooth: Option<bool>, visible: Option<bool> } } with PartTransform::{Affine(Transform), MirrorPlane(Plane3), Scale3 { center: DVec3, factor: DVec3 }} lowered to a DAffine3 (Transform of selection-transforms-02, Plane3 of 3d-input-navigation-13). TransformParts applies the affine to the vertices of the selected parts (face: its loop vertices; edge: its two ends) and repairs: faces that became non-planar are split into planar triangles (ear clipping in the best-fit plane; the original FaceId stays on the first piece, new edges hard and visible), an edge shorter than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH is collapsed when the result stays manifold; anything else is rejected. PushPull extrudes the face along the direction (new side faces in the face's material) and then merges each new side face into its old neighbour when both are coplanar with equal material and flags, so a raised cube top keeps six faces; a negative distance pushes inward. Command::EditSolid { element, edit: SolidEdit } in crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs with labels ('Push/pull face', 'Move vertices', 'Set face material', 'Set edge flags'), planned as ReplaceElement after solid::validate; failures return CommandError::Invalid with the SolidIssue text ('Push/pull by −1.20 m would turn the solid inside out.') and leave the project untouched; locked elements are refused (ELM-013). Out of scope: the UI (07, 16) and the refinement commands (09, 10).
design: Operations run on a clone and only a validated result becomes a ReplaceElement edit, so undo is the existing primitive. Transform and its affine come from selection-transforms-02. archicraft-model has no triangulation library: ear clipping is enough for repairing simple loops; a holed face that becomes non-planar is rejected in v1 with a message. Coplanarity for the seam merge: plane distance within MODEL_TOLERANCE and normals parallel within 1e-9 rad. Push/pull of a holed face also extrudes the hole loops (inner side faces). Side faces created by push/pull get hard, visible seam edges. Pitfalls: a push/pull direction parallel to the face makes zero-area side faces (refuse); repeated pulls must not accumulate collinear seam vertices (the merge removes them). Pointers: solid/ (task 01), kinds/solid.rs (task 02), command.rs plan()/ReplaceElement, docs/implementation-status.md 'Add a command'.
acceptance_criteria:
- SOL-002 acceptance (crates/archicraft-model/tests/solids.rs): PushPull of the unit cube's top face along its normal by 1.000 gives bounds 1 × 1 × 2 within MODEL_TOLERANCE, exactly 6 faces, 8 vertices and volume 2.000.
- PushPull of the top face along Axis(1, 0, 1) by √2 m yields volume 2.000 and validates; PushPull along a direction lying in the face plane is refused.
- PushPull of the top face by −1.000 and by −1.200 is rejected with explanatory messages and the revision is unchanged.
- TransformParts: moving vertex (1, 1, 1) by +0.2 in z keeps both side faces planar, splits the top into two triangles (7 faces) and validates; moving an edge, rotating a face by 10° about an axis through its centroid and scaling a face by 0.5 about its centroid all validate; scaling a face by 0 is rejected; moving the top face down by 1.5 m is rejected because the solid would turn inside out; MirrorPlane of the top face about z = 1.25 gives volume 1.5 and validates; Scale3 of a side face by (1, 1, 0.5) about its centroid validates.
- SetFaceMaterial and SetEdgeFlags (hidden) execute, undo and redo exactly; an unknown material is rejected.
- Untouched vertices and faces keep their ids after every op (a selected part survives Selection::retain_valid).
- A journal replay of a recorded EditSolid sequence reproduces the identical PolyMesh.
- Satisfies the model side of SOL-002 (part transforms, push/pull with typed distance), SOL-008 (rejection of opening or inverting edits) and the command side of SOL-003.
notes:
SRS: SOL-002 SOL-003 SOL-008
Two semantics on purpose: TransformParts stretches neighbouring faces, PushPull adds faces (then merges coplanar seams).

title: Verify exit criterion: Arc walls, curved slab edges, fillet, units in arc walls, polygonal and inclined walls
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its acceptance holds end to end on the integrated workspace, not task by task: F8 coincidence in plan and export, the D-10 circle in plan, 3D and the viewer, the IFX-034 settings, arc junctions in the NFR-MNT-005 suite, fillet on every polygon-based kind, chord-aligned units in arc walls, openings in inclined walls and polygonal walls joining straight walls. It covers WAL-002, WAL-009, WAL-010, WAL-032, WAL-035, SLB-001, SLB-004, IFX-034, DW-019 and EDT-014.

WHAT: Run the full verification: cargo test, clippy and fmt on the workspace, conformance/run.sh on every golden file including curved-walls.ifcx and the re-blessed drafting.ifcx, the headless viewer run, and a manual inspection pass of the arc, circle, slab, fillet, polygonal, inclined and combine tools in the app. Update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence with file paths and test names, remaining gaps such as DW-020 curved units or conical inclined faces) and for the deferred clauses this epic closes for other owners (EDT-008 curve/straighten, WAL-033 curve/straighten/radius, INP-018 arcs preserved, WAL-031 same-circle merge). File follow-up beads for deferred clauses (edge angles on arc edges, inclined arc walls, separating combined walls, the circle-wall seam check in section and elevation views) and close the epic in beads.
design: Verification only; no new features. Use the CI jobs of .github/workflows/ci.yml on the three platforms as the source of truth for test, clippy, fmt and conformance. Re-run F8 and the circle case with non-default tessellation settings once more on the integrated build. For the status document, follow the format of the existing requirement table (status, evidence, gap) and remove or correct the technical-debt entry 'Tessellation settings ... unused because no curved geometry exists' if drafting-trim-split has not already done so.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture F8: a slab traced from an arc wall's reference line and then from its core face shows zero gaps and identical tessellation in plan and export (vertex lists compared bit for bit).
- A full circle entered in one operation is one IfcWall node with a closed mesh and no seam in plan, 3D and the viewer (D-10).
- Tessellation obeys the 2 mm / 10 degree project settings and both are editable in the project dialog.
- Arc-to-straight L and T junctions pass the junction suite.
- Fillet of a slab corner with r = 0.5 m stores an arc edge exactly and 'fillet all corners' works on every polygon-based kind.
- A window in an arc wall is placed on the chord and its void cuts all skins through the full curved thickness (radial void prism, geometry test with conformance).
- Openings in inclined walls follow the inclination.
- A polygonal wall joins straight walls in plan.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx).
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for WAL-002, WAL-009, WAL-010, WAL-032, WAL-035, SLB-001, SLB-004, IFX-034, DW-019 and EDT-014 with evidence.
- The epic curved-geometry is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for every deferred clause.
notes: SRS: WAL-002 WAL-009 WAL-010 WAL-032 WAL-035 SLB-001 SLB-004 IFX-034 DW-019 EDT-014

title: Fillet and chamfer one or all corners of outlines
description:
WHY: EDT-014 (S): 'Fillet (radius) and chamfer (distance) shall be applicable to one corner or all corners of a polyline or polygon-based element, with per-corner values and without exploding the element.' Gap row EDT-014: 'No fillet/chamfer; slab outlines cannot hold arcs (element.rs:179-180), so fillet needs a polycurve outline type first.' edit-reshape-palette-03 delivered `ReshapeOp::Chamfer { distance }` on one corner of straight outlines and edit-reshape-palette-07 a 'Fillet corner' palette stub; NFR-USE-002 asks for the same commands on every polygon-based kind. The epic acceptance: fillet of a slab corner with r = 0.5 m stores an arc edge exactly and 'fillet all corners' works on every polygon-based kind.

WHAT: One corner routine on curve.rs Segments (previous and next edge of a vertex), used by Outline (crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/edit.rs) and by DraftPolyline's PolyCurve: `ReshapeOp::Fillet { radius }` on a node, `FilletAll { radius }` and `ChamferAll { distance }` on a ring or the whole outline (holes included), and `Corners { values: Vec<(PartRef, CornerOp)> }` with CornerOp::{Fillet(r), Chamfer(d)} so per-corner values change in one undo step; the existing single-corner Chamfer is kept and extended to corners next to arc edges. Fillets between line/line, line/arc and arc/arc edges from offset-curve intersections (task 18's concentric offsets) and tangent points; corners where the value does not fit (tangent points beyond the available edge length, counting neighbouring fillets) are skipped and named in the result ('Corner 3: the radius does not fit.'), and a command where nothing fits is Invalid; open polylines skip their end vertices. Hook it into every kind with an outline or polycurve reshape: slabs, DraftFill (Outline) and DraftPolyline (PolyCurve, open or closed) of drafting-trim-split, and polygonal walls once task 13 lands. App: replace the 'Fillet corner' stub in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/palette.rs, add 'Fillet all corners' and 'Chamfer all corners' on rings, ReshapeTool steps (tools/reshape.rs) with typed radius or distance and a live preview; with several nodes selected in edit mode (selection-transforms PartRef) the typed value applies to those corners. Out of scope: corners between joined walls (not polygon-based), roofs (they inherit it through Outline in the roofs epic).
design: Fillet construction: offset both adjacent edge curves by r towards the inside of the corner (for lines a parallel line, for arcs a concentric circle with r added or subtracted according to the side), intersect them (line-line, line-circle, circle-circle; nearest root to the corner) to get the centre, project the centre onto both curves for the tangent points, replace the corner vertex by the two tangent vertices and insert a curve.rs Arc { centre, radius: r, start_angle, sweep } whose sweep sign follows the turn direction. Store the typed radius value itself, not |centre - tangent|, so 'stores an arc edge exactly' holds. Inside/outside per corner from the ring orientation (outer CCW, holes CW): a reflex corner gets a concave fillet. Fit check: the tangent distance r / tan(alpha/2) for line pairs, and the angular span for arcs, against the edge length minus the neighbour's consumption. Per-edge data (EdgeData::split/merge) of the trimmed neighbours is kept; the new arc gets EdgeData::default(). Preview calls the same Outline method on a clone and runs the repair pipeline of edit-reshape-palette-02, so preview equals result.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fillet r = 0.5 at corner (4,3) of the rectangle (0,0)-(4,3): one new arc edge with centre exactly (3.5, 2.5) and radius exactly 0.5 (bits), tangent vertices (4, 2.5) and (3.5, 3), area 12 - 0.25(1 - pi/4) = 11.94635 within 1e-12.
- FilletAll r = 0.5 on the rectangle gives four arcs and four lines; ChamferAll d = 0.3 gives an octagon; a Corners command with fillet 0.5, fillet 1.0 and chamfer 0.2 on three corners changes all three in one undo step; undo restores the outline bit for bit.
- A fillet between a line and an arc edge is tangent to both within 1e-12; a radius that does not fit is reported for that corner and leaves it unchanged; FilletAll on a ring with an arc edge does not touch the arc's interior; Chamfer on a corner next to an arc measures the distance along the arc.
- Not exploded: after every fillet and chamfer command the element keeps its id, kind, name and all non-outline properties, and the element count of the project is unchanged.
- A coverage test iterates the kind registry and applies FilletAll to every kind exposing an outline or polycurve reshape hook (slab, DraftFill, DraftPolyline open and closed; polygonal wall added by task 13).
- kittest: on a selected slab node the palette's 'Fillet corner' entry is enabled; typing 0.5 and Enter creates the arc edge; a ring offers 'Fillet all corners' and 'Chamfer all corners'; the filleted slab saves and reopens with the arc (task 06 codec).
- Satisfies EDT-014.
notes:
SRS: EDT-014
Appendix D.8 lists offset and trim but no fillet shortcut; a provisional binding is left to commands-and-l10n.
Open question: Archicad applies 'fillet all' with one value; per-corner values are delivered through the multi-node selection and the Corners op.

title: Add the PolyMesh solid representation with stable ids and validation
description:
WHY: SOL-001 (M) creates free-form solids as a box, as an extruded polygon, rectangle or circle with a height, or by conversion; SOL-003 (M) needs a material per face and, per edge, a smooth/hard shading flag and a visible/hidden display flag; SOL-008 (M) requires closed, manifold volumes and the rejection or repair of operations that would open the volume (NFR-REL-005); SOL-006 (S) wants curved input segmented by default no coarser than the IFX-034 tessellation (2 mm chord deviation, at most 10° per segment). The gap rows rate all of them missing: TriMesh has no face or edge identity (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:9-13) and check_closed (mesh.rs:122-177) only judges triangle soups and serves IFCX export validation; it stays the check for evaluated bodies (task 03). docs/technology-choices.md:157 prescribes our own half-edge structure with planar faces, per-face materials and per-edge flags instead of a B-rep kernel, and selection-transforms requires solid parts to be addressed by stable ids, never by mesh indices.

WHAT: New headless module crates/archicraft-model/src/solid/ (mod.rs, polymesh.rs, topology.rs, validate.rs, build.rs, segments.rs), re-exported from lib.rs. PolyMesh { vertices: IndexMap<VertexId, DVec3>, faces: IndexMap<FaceId, Face { loops: Vec<Vec<VertexId>> (outer loop counter-clockwise seen from outside, then hole loops), material: MaterialId }>, edge_flags: BTreeMap<EdgeKey, EdgeFlags { smooth, visible }> (absent = hard and visible), features: Vec<CurvedFeature>, next_id: u32 } with VertexId/FaceId newtypes over u32 and EdgeKey as the ordered vertex pair. topology.rs derives half-edges on demand (origin, twin, next, face) with queries for the faces of an edge, the edges of a face, vertex stars and boundary edges. validate(&PolyMesh, ValidateOptions { allow_open }) -> Result<(), SolidIssue> checks: closed (every half-edge has an opposite twin), 2-manifold edges and single-fan vertex links, consistent orientation, every face planar within MODEL_TOLERANCE, no edge shorter than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, no zero-area face, holes inside their outer loop, no intersection between non-adjacent faces, positive volume per shell (several disjoint shells are allowed, each closed and outward-oriented, for merges and conversions of separate parts) and coordinates within MAX_COORDINATE (validate.rs:17); SolidIssue carries user-facing messages ('The solid would be open at the edge between vertices 4 and 7.'). build.rs: box(min, max, material), prism(outer, holes, z0, z1, material) from rings accepted by validate_ring, cylinder(centre, radius, z0, z1, segments, material) whose side edges are smooth and hidden and which records CurvedFeature::ExtrudedCircle. segments.rs: segments_for(radius, sweep, &Tessellation) reading the existing Tessellation settings (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:27-43, IFX-034 defaults 2 mm and 10°, kept unchanged). PolyMesh::transformed(&DAffine3) reverses every loop when the determinant is negative. Out of scope: the element kind (02), tessellation into triangles (03), edit operations (06), building solids from triangle meshes (08).
design: Placement: the roadmap names archicraft-geometry halfedge.rs, but Element must store the solid and archicraft-geometry depends on archicraft-model (crates/archicraft-geometry/Cargo.toml), and validate.rs is the single validity gate used by Command::plan. Storage, topology, validation and the edit operations therefore live in archicraft-model/src/solid/, so SOL-008 rejections happen inside the command and stay journal-replayable; archicraft-geometry keeps triangulation (spade), the SolidKernel-backed operations (conversion, merge, crop) and evaluation. Canonical form is face-vertex loops; half-edges are derived on demand, which keeps edits simple (no twin pointers to repair) and serde trivial. Ids are allocated monotonically and never reused within one solid; operations keep the ids of untouched entities so the selection survives edits (Selection::retain_valid). Faces with holes are first-class because converted walls have faces with openings. Geometry: face normal by Newell's method, planarity as the largest distance of loop vertices from the plane through the loop centroid; volume = 1/3 Σ (centroid · area vector) over faces, exact for planar faces without triangulating; the self-intersection test is segment-against-face-polygon with an AABB prefilter, O(F·E), acceptable for v1 sizes (a BVH is a later optimisation). segments_for = max(ceil(sweep / max_angle), ceil(sweep / (2·acos(1 − chord / r)))), at least 3. Use MODEL_TOLERANCE from crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs (element-kind-framework-01; today validate.rs:10) and MIN_EDGE_LENGTH and MAX_COORDINATE from validate.rs:12 and :17. archicraft-geometry's extrude.rs (vertical prisms as triangle soups, the reuse candidate the gap row names) is not reused here because a PolyMesh keeps polygon faces; triangulation happens only in task 03. Pitfalls: collinear vertices on an edge (T-vertices after splits) are allowed, zero-length edges are not; hole loops run clockwise seen from outside.
acceptance_criteria:
- solid/build.rs tests: box(0..1) has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 faces (V − E + F = 2), volume 1.000 within 1e-9 and validates.
- An L-shaped prism with a square hole validates and its volume equals ring area × height.
- cylinder(r = 0.5 m, h = 1 m) with the default Tessellation has 36 segments, smooth and hidden side edges, hard and visible cap edges, and validates.
- Negative tests, each returning its specific SolidIssue: a removed face (open), a third face on one edge (non-manifold), one flipped face (orientation), a quad made non-planar by 1 mm, a zero-length edge, two crossing non-adjacent faces (self-intersection), an inside-out box (negative volume).
- Two disjoint unit boxes in one PolyMesh validate as two shells with volume 2.000.
- segments_for: full circle r = 0.5 m gives 36 and r = 5 m gives 112 with the defaults (2 mm, 10°); never fewer than 3.
- transformed() with a mirror affine keeps validate Ok and a positive volume.
- PolyMesh and its parts derive Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize and Deserialize (serde round-trip test); crates/archicraft-model/Cargo.toml gains no new dependency.
- Satisfies the data and validity clauses of SOL-001 (box, prism, circle builders), SOL-003 (per-face material, per-edge flags), SOL-006 (segment rule) and SOL-008 (closed-manifold check).
notes:
SRS: SOL-001 SOL-003 SOL-006 SOL-008
Open: planarity tolerance MODEL_TOLERANCE (0.01 mm, chosen) versus 0.1 mm for converted or imported meshes; task 06 splits faces that become non-planar instead of loosening the tolerance.

title: Make outline node and edge commands arc-aware with curve and straighten
description:
WHY: EDT-008 (M, owned by edit-reshape-palette) lists 'curve edge (make an arc), straighten edge' among the edge commands; edit-reshape-palette-03 shipped `ReshapeOp::CurveEdge { through }` as a stub ('Curved edges arrive with arc geometry.') and Straighten as NoChange. SLB-008 and NFR-USE-002 require insert node, delete node and offset on every polygon-based kind, which now includes arc edges. SLB-004 (M): an edited arc must keep its exact circle, otherwise a slab traced from a wall face stops coinciding with it after the first edit. Fillet (EDT-014, task 10) reuses the offset and intersection routines.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/edit.rs (edit-reshape-palette-03): InsertNode on an arc splits it with curve.rs Segment::split_at into two arcs with bit-identical centre and radius; DeleteNode between two arcs with bit-identical centre and radius merges them into one arc, otherwise the joined edge becomes straight; OffsetEdge on an arc moves it concentrically (radius changed by d, centre bits kept) and re-intersects the neighbours with curve.rs intersect() on carriers (line-circle, circle-circle); offset_ring and OffsetAll handle arc edges the same way (the geo Buffer fallback gains arcs in task 19); MoveEdge on an arc translates it when keep_directions is false and offsets it concentrically when true. Implement `ReshapeOp::CurveEdge { through }` (Arc::through of the edge's end vertices and the through point, sharing the code drafting-trim-split-07 wrote for DraftPolyline edges) and `ReshapeOp::Straighten` (arc to line, NoChange on lines), replacing the stub. EdgeData::split/merge is called for arcs so per-edge data stays aligned. The same routines serve DraftPolyline's PolyCurve where drafting-trim-split-07 has not already implemented them (verify first, do not duplicate). Out of scope: palette and handles (task 11), Booleans (19), fillet and chamfer (10).
design: Concentric offsets: an arc's supporting carrier is its circle, so OffsetEdge replaces the radius by r + s*d (s = +1 when the outward normal points away from the centre, -1 otherwise) computed once and stored; never rebuild the arc from offset end points. Neighbour intersection: intersect the offset carrier with the neighbours' carriers (Extent::Carriers) and take the root nearest to the old vertex; if there is none (a line parallel to and outside the offset circle), insert a connecting straight edge as edit-reshape-palette-03 does for parallel neighbours. Merge rule for DeleteNode: identical circle bits only, because a tolerance-based merge would silently change a traced edge. CurveEdge stores the circumcircle of the edge's two vertices and the through point; the sweep sign follows the side of the through point. Pitfalls: the follow-up part returned for selection retargeting must be recomputed after repair; split points from Segment::split_at are the stored vertex, so the derived end of the first arc and the start of the second agree bitwise with the new vertex only through the vertex itself.
acceptance_criteria:
- CurveEdge on a straight edge with a through point yields the circumcircle (centre within 1e-12) while the ring's vertices stay bit-identical; a collinear through point gives CommandError::Invalid('The three points are collinear.'); Straighten returns the original line; undo restores the outline bit for bit (crates/archicraft-model/tests/reshape.rs).
- InsertNode on an arc edge gives two arcs whose centre and radius are bit-identical to the original (f64::to_bits); DeleteNode of their shared vertex restores one arc with the original sweep within 1e-12.
- OffsetEdge by 0.1 on an outward arc edge keeps the centre bits and increases the radius by exactly 0.1; the neighbouring straight edges meet it at the analytic line-circle intersections within 1e-12; OffsetAll of a slab with rounded corners keeps every arc concentric.
- An offset that would make a radius zero or negative is rejected with a message instead of being repaired silently.
- The stub message 'Curved edges arrive with arc geometry.' no longer appears in the workspace; all existing reshape tests of edit-reshape-palette pass unchanged, also on Outline<TestEdge>.
- Keeps the SLB-004 exactness under node and edge editing; completes the model half of the deferred EDT-008 'curve edge' and 'straighten edge' clauses.
notes:
SRS: SLB-004
Also completes the deferred EDT-008 clauses 'curve edge (make an arc)' and 'straighten edge' at model level (UI in task 11); EDT-008, SLB-008 and EDT-010 are owned by edit-reshape-palette.
Decision proposed here: DeleteNode between arcs of different circles yields a straight edge.

title: Shade curved faces smoothly in 3D and edit the maximum segment angle
description:
WHY: IFX-034 (M): 'The values are user-adjustable per project.' Gap row IFX-034: 'Max segment angle has no UI field (only chord deviation is in the dialog)' (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:593-604). WAL-002 (M) and D-10: a full circle has 'no seam artefact in any view'; the 3D view computes flat per-triangle normals (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:152-168), so the smooth strips of tasks 03 and 04 would still shade faceted. The epic acceptance: the 2 mm / 10 degree settings are 'both editable in the project dialog'.

WHAT: render3d.rs: average normals over shared vertex indices within a part (the smooth strips) and keep the flat triangle normal for unshared vertices, so planar faces render exactly as before; edges keep coming from mesh.feature_edges, which task 03 taught to skip smooth edges. dialogs.rs: a 'Maximum segment angle' widgets::angle field next to 'Curve chord deviation', built like the true-north field (dialogs.rs:580-592); the range check of check_settings (command.rs:599-603) stays the single gate and OK commits one SetSettings. Keep: the IFCX persistence of both values (writer.rs:163-164, reader.rs:347-356) gets a regression test with non-default values. Out of scope: tessellation rules (03), wall bodies (04).
design: Normal averaging: accumulate area-weighted face normals per point index and normalise; because add_face gives every planar face its own vertices (IFX-038, mesh.rs:81-89), only smooth strips share indices, so no crease angle threshold is needed and the shading equals the reference viewer's (which averages over shared vertices). The scene cache key (SceneKey, workspace.rs) already changes with the geometry revision. The dialog edits a draft copy of the settings, so Cancel leaves the project untouched (existing pattern). Use the kittest harness of crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- render3d scene test: a full circle wall (task 04) produces averaged vertex normals on its curved faces and no vertical line in the scene's edge list; a box keeps flat normals and 12 feature edges.
- kittest: the Project settings dialog shows 'Maximum segment angle'; entering 5 and OK changes the setting in one undo step and doubles the segment count of a 0.5 m radius slab arc; undo restores both.
- Entering 0 or 120 degrees is rejected with 'The tessellation tolerances are out of range.' and the setting keeps its old value.
- IFCX round trip of chordDeviation 0.001 and maxSegmentAngle 5 is bit-identical (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs).
- Satisfies the per-project adjustability clause of IFX-034 and the 3D no-seam clause of WAL-002 and D-10 in the application.
notes:
SRS: IFX-034 WAL-002
Appendix D.1 tessellation defaults; IFX-038 vertex sharing; D-10 no seams in 3D.

title: Allow layer structures on polygonal walls
description:
WHY: WAL-035 (C): 'Polygonal walls may use layer structures.' Gap row WAL-035: missing, depending on WAL-009 (tasks 13 and 22) and PRF-001 (layer-structures). Layered walls elsewhere export one Skin_n part per skin (IFX-017, layer-structures) and resolve junctions per skin by priority (WAL-023, junction-engine-05).

WHAT: Polygonal walls accept `Structure::Layered(LayerStructureId)` (layer-structures-02). Rule: skins are laid inward from the outline boundary in structure order: every skin except the last is a band of constant thickness along the whole boundary (offset_ring of edit-reshape-palette-03 made arc-aware in task 18, arcs offset concentrically), and the last skin fills the remaining interior; outlines whose offset collapses are rejected ('The layer structure is thicker than this polygonal wall allows.'). Geometry: one closed body per skin, skin rings sharing their boundary vertices; junction.rs resolves the skins against other walls by priority like any layered wall (task 22's contact); plan regions per skin; core faces exposed for snapping and tracing as closed rings. IFCX: Skin_n parts with materials; the structure reference written in archicraft::wall as for other layered walls. Properties: the structure choice is offered for polygonal walls. Out of scope: per-edge exterior sides or skins following only some edges (a follow-up if users need it).
design: Offsets with arcs: offset_ring handles line/line, line/arc and arc/arc corners; arc edges map to concentric arcs of radius r -/+ d with the same centre bits, so the band stays exact and tessellates with task 03's grid. When an offset makes an edge vanish (short edges next to concave corners), offset_ring falls back to geo Buffer with mitre joins and the arc recovery of task 19; if the result is multi-part or empty, reject. The last skin filling the interior means a structure whose total thickness exceeds the outline's inradius still works as long as the shell skins fit; the core is usually the last skin. Pitfall: the core faces of a polygonal wall are closed rings, not lines; PlanElement.core_faces and PlanElement.curves must accept them.
acceptance_criteria:
- A two-skin structure (20 mm render, then concrete) on an L-shaped polygonal wall with one arc edge yields two closed skins; the render band is 20 mm wide everywhere, including along the arc (concentric radius minus 0.02 exactly), and the shared boundary vertices are bit-identical in both skins.
- An outline too small for the structure is rejected with the message; undo leaves the wall single-material.
- A junction-suite row: a straight F2 wall ending on the layered polygonal wall resolves skins by priority (D.4) with closed bodies and permutation independence.
- IFCX round trip and conformance on curved-walls.ifcx with Skin_1 and Skin_2 parts naming their materials.
- kittest: the properties strip offers the structure selector for a polygonal wall.
- Satisfies WAL-035.
notes:
SRS: WAL-035
Appendix D.4 priorities; IFX-017 Skin_n parts (layer-structures).
Decision proposed here: shell skins along the whole boundary with the last skin filling the interior; recorded in docs/ for review because the SRS gives no rule.

title: Tessellate solids into bodies with smooth and hard edges
description:
WHY: SOL-003 (M) requires per-edge smooth/hard shading and visible/hidden display flags; IFX-038 (M) states that vertices are shared only across smooth edges, explicitly naming free-form solids with soft edges, that each planar face region otherwise gets its own vertices and that no mesh exceeds 65,535 points. Today the 3D view shades every triangle flat (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:150-160) and draws edges from an angle threshold (render3d.rs:164 calling mesh.rs:239 feature_edges), so neither flag could show. SOL-001 solids must appear in 3D, plan and export, and SOL-008 requires every evaluated body to pass the closed-mesh check. members-profiles-adv expects 3D picks on solid faces to resolve to FaceIds through this task's face provenance.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/solid.rs: tessellate(&PolyMesh) -> SolidBodies { body: TriMesh (closed; triangles grouped by face material in order of first appearance; used for plan slicing, the kernel and picking), face_materials: Vec<FaceMaterialRun> (the run type solid-kernel-ops-07 adds to BodyPart for SOL-026; empty for one material), face_ids: Vec<u32> (the source FaceId of every triangle), edges: Vec<[DVec3; 2]> (visible edges only) }. Each face is projected into its own plane frame and triangulated with triangulate() (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/triangulate.rs:41) including holes; faces joined by smooth edges form smooth regions that share vertex indices, hard edges duplicate vertices. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/solid.rs registers the GeometryKind (element-kind-framework-07) returning ElementGeometry with one closed Body part in the dominant material that carries face_materials (render3d.rs build_scene colours triangles per run after solid-kernel-ops-07) and a new BodyPart.face_ids: Vec<u32> (empty for other kinds); bodies above MAX_MESH_POINTS (mesh.rs:49) are partitioned into Body_n by the Normalize stage (normalize_parts, solid-kernel-ops-03), which carries runs and face_ids with their triangles. ElementGeometry gains edges: Option<Vec<[DVec3; 2]>> (None for other kinds). crates/archicraft-geometry/src/pick.rs (3d-input-navigation-06): Hit gains source_face: Option<u32> taken from BodyPart.face_ids, so 3D picks resolve to solid FaceIds. views/render3d.rs: per-vertex normals averaged over the triangles that share a vertex index inside a part (identical output for walls and slabs, whose faces never share vertices, and the same rule as the reference viewer), and ElementGeometry.edges used instead of feature_edges when Some. Plan views slice the closed body generically and fill the cut with the dominant material. Out of scope: IFCX writing (04), hidden-edge handling in plan projection lines, per-face fills in plan.
design: Face frame: u = any unit vector perpendicular to the Newell normal, v = n × u; outer loops stay counter-clockwise in the frame and holes clockwise, as triangulate() expects. Smooth regions: union-find over faces joined by smooth edges; inside a region a VertexId maps to one output index. Normal averaging uses the sum of unnormalised triangle normals (area weighting), which matches the reference viewer's averaging over shared vertices and keeps flat faces flat. Hidden edges are dropped from the edge list but still bound smooth regions only when smooth. Adding an Option field to ElementGeometry and an empty-by-default face_ids to BodyPart keeps existing constructors working through ..Default; face_ids is derived data like the material runs. Pitfall: triangulating a face whose loop has collinear T-vertices is fine with spade's constrained Delaunay triangulation as long as constraint edges do not overlap; validated loops guarantee that. Pointers: evaluate.rs:23-49 (BodyPart, ElementGeometry), mesh.rs:83-89 (add_face), render3d.rs:100-170 (build_scene), plan.rs (generic slicing), normalize_parts (solid-kernel-ops-03, IFX-038 splitting), FaceMaterialRun (solid-kernel-ops-07), pick.rs (3d-input-navigation-06).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/solids.rs: the unit box gives 24 points, 12 triangles, check_closed Ok and 12 visible edges.
- The 36-segment cylinder with smooth side edges shares vertices across the side (72 side points, not 144) and its edge list contains only the two cap rings (72 segments, no side seams).
- The L-prism with a hole triangulates to its exact face areas and a closed body.
- A two-material box yields one closed Body whose two FaceMaterialRuns cover all 12 triangles, with a volume equal to the PolyMesh volume within 1e-9; the 3D scene colours the faces per run.
- face_ids has one entry per triangle and the top face's two triangles map to the top FaceId; a PickIndex ray onto the top face returns that FaceId as source_face.
- A solid above 65,535 points is partitioned by normalize_parts into Body_n parts that each pass check_closed and keep their runs and face_ids.
- The plan slice of the unit box at z = 0.5 is one 1 × 1 loop (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs slice_loops).
- render3d unit tests: the smooth cylinder gets differing vertex normals within one side triangle; a wall produces the same vertex buffer as before; existing render tests stay green.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/transforms.rs (selection-transforms-02) iterates the solid kind: the body of a transformed solid equals the transformed body.
- Satisfies the display side of SOL-003, the IFX-038 vertex-sharing rule for solids, SOL-001 visibility in all views and SOL-008 for evaluated bodies.
notes:
SRS: SOL-001 SOL-003 SOL-008
Open: hidden edges have no effect on plan projected and overhead lines in v1 (plan lines come from slices and up-facing outlines); revisit with 3d-display-styles.

title: Keep arc edges through outline union, difference and buffer
description:
WHY: EDT-015 (S, edit-reshape-palette-04) unions and subtracts drawn polygons on polygon-based elements with geo BooleanOps (i_overlay), which only knows polylines. Without arc recovery the first union turns every arc edge into chords, which breaks SLB-004 (M, exact coincidence with curved walls) and SLB-001 (arc edges) and removes fillets (EDT-014). Contour tracing with arcs preserved (INP-018 clause, task 08), the buffer fallback of OffsetAll and the skins of layered polygonal walls (task 14) need the same recovery.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/recover.rs: flatten arc edges with a fixed fine tolerance (0.1 mm chord, independent of the project tessellation and of archicraft-geometry, NFR-MNT-002), tag every flattened vertex with the (ring, edge) of its source, run the geo operation, then rebuild: maximal runs of consecutive result vertices lying on one source circle within MODEL_TOLERANCE become one curve.rs Arc with the source's exact centre and radius, the run ends projected onto the circle and snapped to the analytic intersection point where two sources meet; a run covering a whole source circle becomes a one-vertex ring at the source's start vertex. Use it in the Union, Difference and AddHole commands of edit-reshape-palette-04 and in offset_ring's geo Buffer fallback (edit-reshape-palette-03), re-mapping EdgeData per recovered edge from its source edge. Expose `recover_arcs(points, sources: &[Arc]) -> Ring` for contour detection (task 08). Out of scope: tracing (08), polygonal walls (13).
design: Flatten finely and recover rather than writing curved Booleans: i_overlay stays the only polygon kernel (technology-choices), and recovery is exact because the result vertices are only used to find runs and run ends, never to re-derive circles. Tag propagation: i_overlay does not carry tags, so membership is decided geometrically (distance to the source circle within MODEL_TOLERANCE and angle inside the source sweep extended by one flattening step); a vertex on two sources (an intersection) ends both runs. Run ends: intersect the two adjacent sources analytically (curve.rs intersect, nearest root) so a recovered arc ends exactly where the straight neighbour begins. Pitfalls: i_overlay returns rings with arbitrary start vertices and collinear points, so normalise first; a run of only two vertices on a circle is ambiguous (a chord or a tiny arc): keep it straight unless the source edge was an arc spanning the same interval.
acceptance_criteria:
- Union of a 4 x 3 rectangle and a full circle of r = 1 centred on a corner keeps one arc edge whose centre and radius equal the circle's bits and whose ends lie on the analytic line-circle intersections within 1e-9; difference of a circle inside the rectangle gives a hole that is a one-vertex circle ring.
- Union of two slabs whose arc edges lie on the same circle returns no vertex off the circle by more than MODEL_TOLERANCE and no extra vertices along the arc.
- An OffsetAll that collapses an edge next to an arc goes through the buffer fallback and returns arcs concentric with the originals.
- EdgeData of a recovered arc equals its source edge's data (Outline<TestEdge> test); undo restores the original outline bit for bit.
- The existing union, difference and hole tests of edit-reshape-palette-04 pass unchanged.
- Keeps the arc edges of SLB-001 and the exactness of SLB-004 through EDT-015 edits.
notes:
SRS: SLB-001 SLB-004
EDT-015 and the OffsetAll fallback are owned by edit-reshape-palette; INP-018's arc-preserving clause is completed in task 08.
Appendix D.1 model tolerance 0.01 mm.

title: Free-form solids with sub-element editing
description:
Free-form solids as box, extrusion or conversion, sub-element (vertex, edge, face) selection and 3D transforms with push/pull, per-face materials and edge flags, segmentation control, the closed-manifold guarantee, a selectable IFC class, refinement commands, revolve, sweep and merge, open auxiliary sheets, and the non-associative crop by a plane (a single-plane roof's plane, a picked face or three points) that permanently rewrites the cropped element as a free-form solid (SOL-033); uses the PartRef edit mode of selection-transforms and the kernel's validity checks.

Risks: Manifold editing operations are intricate; v1 keeps planar faces only (technology-choices) and validates with kernel checks after every edit.
design: archicraft-geometry halfedge.rs PolyMesh structure with face materials and edge flags, tessellated to TriMesh with IFX-038 splitting, rotation-minimising frames for sweeps (SOL-007); archicraft-model kinds/solid.rs storing the PolyMesh and class; PartRef::{Vertex, Edge, Face} registered through the selection model; archicraft-app tools/solid.rs on 3D input with handles projected into 3D.
acceptance_criteria: Raising the top face of a 1 m cube by 1.000 m gives a 1×1×2 m body (SOL-002 acceptance); converting a layered wall keeps the evaluated geometry and face materials after one confirmation; operations that would open the volume are rejected; a profile swept along a non-coplanar 3D path shows no twist (frame-continuity test); the edit mode selects faces, edges and vertices in 3D with handles (kittest); the IFC class is selectable from the D.5 list. Rotating a solid about an arbitrary 3D axis and mirroring it about a 3D plane succeed where walls refuse (EDT-007/EDT-022 positive cases). Cropping a wall below a picked face converts it into a closed free-form solid cut at that plane, and moving or deleting the reference afterwards changes nothing (SOL-033).
notes: SRS: SOL-001 SOL-002 SOL-003 SOL-004 SOL-005 SOL-006 SOL-007 SOL-008 SOL-009 SOL-010 SOL-011 SOL-033

title: Convert any element into a free-form solid with its face materials
description:
WHY: SOL-004 (M): any selected model element, including elements modified by solid operations and imported elements, shall be convertible into free-form solids; conversion keeps the evaluated geometry and face materials (the confirmation notice is task 17). SOL-001 (M) lists conversion as the third way to create a solid. SOL-006 (S): converting a curved element keeps the segmentation user-controllable, by default no coarser than IFX-034. SOL-008 (M): the result is a closed manifold. The gap row names the evaluated geometry per element in ModelGeometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:52-60) as the input; crop (14) and merge (18) reuse this path.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/solid_convert.rs: solid_from_parts(&[BodyPart]) -> Result<PolyMesh, ConvertError> welds points within MODEL_TOLERANCE, unions several parts through SolidKernel::union_all (solid-kernel-ops-02) with face provenance from KernelMesh.sources (internal faces between skins disappear, every remaining triangle keeps its part material, or the material of its FaceMaterialRun where solid-kernel-ops-07 set one), groups edge-connected coplanar triangles of equal material into planar faces with hole loops, drops collinear interior vertices, flags edges hard and visible except between strips of one tessellated curved surface (smooth and hidden), and validates (several shells allowed, task 01). convert_element(project, geometry, id, tessellation: Option<Tessellation>) re-evaluates the element with a finer tessellation when one is given: EvalContext (element-kind-framework-07) gains tessellation: Option<Tessellation>, passed by evaluate_element (evaluate.rs:150), and GeometryKind gains is_curved(&Element) -> bool (default false) for the segmentation field of task 17. The test-kinds Dummy gains round: bool (a cylinder from the EvalContext tessellation, is_curved true) as the curved stand-in until curved-geometry's arc walls exist. Model: Command::ReplaceWithSolids { replacements: Vec<(ElementId, Solid)>, remove: Vec<ElementId>, hosted: HostedPolicy::{ConvertOwn, Delete} } in crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs (reused by crop and merge) keeps id, name, home storey, layer and position, keeps the IFC class when it is in D.5 (IfcWall stays IfcWall) and otherwise uses the proxy, removes relations in which a converted element is the target of a solid operation or trim (their effect is baked in), clears its half-space clips (Element.clips of solid-kernel-ops-15, baked in), keeps relations in which it is an operator, deletes hosted openings (kinds/opening.rs of host-openings-01; their voids are baked in), converts other hosted elements with a body of their own (doors and windows once doors-windows-core lands) into their own solids or deletes them per HostedPolicy, and deletes the elements listed in remove; one undo step restores everything; locked elements are refused (ELM-013). Out of scope: the action and notice (17), imported elements themselves (ifcx-interop re-asserts conversion with its ImportedElement kind; their evaluated parts convert unchanged), per-part stair conversion STA-048 (stair-body-plan calls ReplaceWithSolids with one solid per part).
design: Face provenance: the SolidKernel trait of solid-kernel-ops (Manifold run/face original ids, used there for SOL-026); if unavailable, remove coincident opposite triangle pairs between parts (exact when parts come from the same footprints) and report inexact cases as ConvertError instead of guessing. Planar grouping: flood fill over welded triangle adjacency with plane tolerance MODEL_TOLERANCE; boundary loops ordered counter-clockwise about the face normal; holes classified by signed area in the face frame. Curved-strip detection uses the dihedral angle (below the tessellation max angle plus epsilon) and a per-part curved flag from the source kind. Pitfalls: T-vertices between coplanar triangles of different sizes (keep them, they validate), relations must be removed before the old kind disappears so integrity checks of element-kind-framework-08 stay clean. Pointers: evaluate.rs:150 (evaluate_element), kinds/ and EvalContext (element-kind-framework-07), kernel/ (solid-kernel-ops-02), relations.rs (element-kind-framework-08), kinds/opening.rs (host-openings-01), Element.clips (solid-kernel-ops-15), docs/implementation-status.md 'Add a command'.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/convert.rs: a single-material wall converts to 6 faces with volume and bounds equal within 0.1 mm; a wall with a hosted opening converts to a solid whose faces carry hole loops and which validates; the F2 layered wall (layer-structures, six skins, 680 mm) converts to one solid whose volume equals the sum of the skin volumes within 1e-6 m³ and whose exposed face area per material equals that skin's exposed area; a wall cut by a subtract operation converts to the cut shape, the relation is removed and the operator keeps cutting its other targets; a wall with a half-space clip converts to the clipped shape and the solid has no clips.
- Registry-driven test: every kind whose KindDescriptor.solid is true converts and keeps its evaluated volume within 1e-6 m³, including the test-kinds Dummy with compound parts (the stand-in for compound and imported elements, whose bodies arrive as given closed meshes).
- Curved stand-in: a round Dummy converts with 36 side faces by default (project tessellation, smooth and hidden side edges) and with 72 when convert_element gets a tessellation giving 72 segments.
- Command tests (crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs): ReplaceWithSolids keeps id, name, layer and storey, keeps IfcWall and deletes the hosted opening, and undo restores the wall, its opening and its relations exactly; remove deletes the listed elements in the same undo step; a locked element is refused.
- The golden sample gains a converted F2 wall; conformance/run.sh stays green.
- Satisfies SOL-004 (conversion keeping geometry and face materials), the conversion clause of SOL-001, the conversion side of SOL-006 and SOL-008 for conversion results.
notes:
SRS: SOL-001 SOL-004 SOL-006 SOL-008
Open: hosted doors and windows default to 'convert into their own solids' (chosen) or 'delete'.

title: Make openings, doors and windows follow inclined walls
description:
WHY: WAL-010 (S): 'Openings in inclined walls follow the inclination.' DW-009 (doors and windows cut all skins), IFX-036 (closed Void child) and IFX-033 (host bodies already cut) apply to inclined hosts too. The epic acceptance: 'openings in inclined walls follow the inclination'. host-openings-05's wall_cut.rs cuts openings in a vertical wall plane with extrude_layers (frame: &DAffine3) and doors-windows-core-01's InsertFrame::resolve places units by unit_to_storey; both assume a vertical wall plane.

WHAT: For inclined hosts (tasks 15 and 23), the wall-plane frame becomes (s, v) with v along the reference face's inclined up direction (for independently inclined faces, the bisector plane of the two faces). Cut sections are defined in that plane, so sill and head lie in planes perpendicular to it and the jambs contain the inclined direction. wall_cut.rs: for a slanted wall (parallel faces) pass extrude_layers a sheared DAffine3 frame whose local z is the inclined direction; for independently inclined faces project each hole along the bisector-plane normal onto each face and generate the lofted span with holes; the Void part is the tilted prism extended beyond both faces by VOID_MARGIN. InsertFrame::resolve for inclined hosts: unit_to_storey gains the rotation about the reference-line direction by the inclination; width and height are measured in the inclined plane, and the pinned edge's elevation (DW-007) is measured where that edge meets the reference face. Plan symbols come from the frame at the cut height; IFCX occurrences carry the tilted transform and Void. Extend curved_walls() with a window in the inclined wall and re-bless. Out of scope: openings in inclined arc or polygonal walls (not modelled).
design: Reuse the host-openings cut machinery in a tilted frame instead of a 3D Boolean (solid-kernel-ops is not a prerequisite of this epic): for a slanted wall both faces are parallel to the reference plane, so the mapping is affine and extrude_layers takes it as its frame; for independently inclined faces, projecting the hole along the bisector-plane normal onto each face keeps jamb faces planar. Keep unit_to_storey a proper transform (determinant > 0, IFX-051) and the reflection handling unchanged. The DW-007 elevation rule makes a sill pinned at 0.90 m stay at 0.90 m above the storey at the reference face regardless of inclination; document it in the inspector help text. Pitfall: the reveal (DW-008) is measured perpendicular to the inclined face, not horizontally.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a 1.20 x 1.40 m window in a wall with both faces inclined 15 degrees: every skin closed; the void's sill and head faces are perpendicular to the wall plane and its jambs contain the inclined direction (normals within 1e-9); each skin's volume decreases by width x height x the skin's perpendicular thickness within 1e-9.
- An opening in a wall with only the exterior face inclined cuts through both faces; the Void encloses the removed volume.
- The unit's transform rotation equals the inclination about the reference-line direction within 1e-12; the pinned sill stays at its elevation when the height changes.
- Deleting the window restores the host body bit for bit (undo).
- Golden curved-walls.ifcx with the inclined wall and its window passes conformance/run.sh; the plan shows the opening at the cut height.
- Satisfies the opening clause of WAL-010.
notes:
SRS: WAL-010
Appendix D.2: window 1.20 x 1.40 m, sill 0.90 m.
Open question: whether height should be measured vertically instead of in the inclined plane; the SRS is silent, the choice here follows the unit's own geometry.

title: Add the solid tool: box and extruded polygon, rectangle and circle
description:
WHY: SOL-001 (M): free-form solids as a box and as an extruded polygon, rectangle or circle with a height. SOL-006 (S): curved input is segmented by default no coarser than the IFX-034 export tessellation and the segmentation is user-controllable. SOL-009 (M): the class is selectable, through the generic class combo driven by the kind's ifc_classes (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:478-492). Appendix D.8 requires a default shortcut for the free-form solid tool. The epic acceptance also needs the positive EDT-007/EDT-022 cases at the UI level: rotating a solid about an arbitrary axis and mirroring it about a 3D plane succeed where walls refuse.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/solid.rs: SolidTool implementing the InputConsumer of point-input-snapping-01 with modes Box (two corners on the working plane, then the height typed or picked), Rectangle and Polygon extrusion (outline on the active working plane: the storey plane in plan, any working plane in 3D through Camera3dSurface (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/surface3d.rs, 3d-input-navigation-07) with StepSpec.needs_horizontal = false so the outline stays on tilted planes (3d-input-navigation-08), then a height along the plane normal) and Circle (centre, radius, height) with segments = the override or segments_for(radius, 2π, project tessellation). Outlines on tilted working planes are built with PolyMesh::prism in the plane frame and mapped to the world with the frame's affine. Commit: Command::AddElements(vec![project.new_solid(...)]). Action ToolSolid with a single-key shortcut (D.8, uniqueness test), toolbox button and Design menu entry, properties strip for the solid defaults through Subject::Defaults of element-kind-framework-04 (material, layer, IFC class combo with the 20 D.5 classes, height, segments 'Auto (36)' or a number stored as Solid.segments in the prototype), and properties of a selected solid (class, material for all faces, name, layer, read-only volume and bounds). Out of scope: revolve and sweep (12), sheets (13), sub-element editing (07), the max-segment-angle field of the project dialog (curved-geometry).
design: The plane frame comes from the WorkingPlane of 3d-input-navigation; the height step uses Expect::Distance measured along the plane normal. Preview: outline plus the prism's edges computed by PolyMesh::prism and drawn as lines, never a geometry evaluation per frame (NFR-PERF-005). The segment label shows the computed default so the user sees what Auto means. Follow the 'Add a drawing tool' extension point of docs/implementation-status.md (ToolKind, actions.rs, shell.rs toolbox, properties.rs gather/prototype, workspace.rs select_all). Pointers: tools/mod.rs (point-input-snapping-01), input/consumer.rs, input/surface.rs, ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs, ui/properties.rs:478-492.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool unit tests without egui: a box from (0, 0) to (1, 1) with typed height 1 creates one solid of volume 1.000; a rectangle extruded on the vertical working plane x = 0 by 0.3 m extends along +X; a circle of r = 0.5 m has 36 segments with the default tessellation and 12 with the override 12; a zero or negative height is refused with a prompt message.
- kittest: the toolbox shows 'Free-form solid', the shortcut activates it and drawing a box in the plan creates FS-001; the IFC class combo lists the 20 D.5 classes and switching to IfcSlab changes Element::ifc_class in one undo step.
- kittest (positive EDT-007/EDT-022 cases): 'Rotate about axis…' (selection-transforms-12) with axis X and 90° on the box succeeds and changes vertex z while on a wall it shows the refusal naming the kind; 'Mirror about plane' (3d-input-navigation-13, tools/mirror3d.rs) about an inclined three-point plane succeeds on the box and is refused for a wall.
- Save and reopen in the app keep the solid (task 04).
- Satisfies SOL-001 (box and extrusions), SOL-006 (default and override segmentation for circles) and the UI clause of SOL-009.
notes:
SRS: SOL-001 SOL-006 SOL-009
Shortcut letter to be confirmed by commands-and-l10n.

title: Add refinement commands: merge faces, merge edges and stretch
description:
WHY: SOL-005 (S): the system shall provide refinement commands for free-form solids: merge coplanar faces, smooth-merge faces, curve-merge edges, change the segmentation of curved edges and faces, fillet and chamfer edges, and stretch by face, edge or vertex. The gap row rates it XL and missing. This task delivers the merge commands and stretch; task 10 adds fillet, chamfer and segmentation changes.

WHAT: New SolidEdit variants in crates/archicraft-model/src/solid/ops.rs (task 06). MergeCoplanarFaces { faces: Option<Vec<FaceId>> } merges adjacent coplanar faces of equal material (all, or within the selection), removes shared edges and collinear vertices and may create hole loops. SmoothMergeFaces { faces } marks every edge between the selected faces smooth and hidden, so they shade and display as one surface (non-destructive; SetEdgeFlags reverses it). CurveMergeEdges { edges } treats a connected chain of edges as one curved edge: the side edges at its interior vertices become smooth and hidden and the chain is recorded as CurvedFeature::EdgeChain for later segmentation changes. Stretch { parts, direction, distance } moves the selected vertices, edges or faces along a direction while connecting faces stretch, without new faces (non-planar results repaired as in task 06). UI: the edit-mode context menu (selection-transforms-08) and an Edit > Free-form solid submenu (ui/shell.rs) offer 'Merge coplanar faces', 'Smooth and merge faces', 'Curve and merge edges' and 'Stretch…' (direction from a handle axis or two points, typed distance through the point-input service), each as one Command::EditSolid. Out of scope: fillet, chamfer, segmentation (10).
design: Coplanar merge: union-find over faces sharing an edge with equal plane (MODEL_TOLERANCE) and material, then rebuild loops by walking boundary half-edges of the merged region (outer loop = largest positive area in the face frame). SmoothMergeFaces stays a flag operation so it never changes topology or volume. CurveMergeEdges stores the chain's vertex ids so task 10 can regenerate it. Stretch reuses TransformParts with a pure translation and the same repair path. Pointers: solid/ops.rs and topology.rs (tasks 01, 06), views/solid_edit.rs (task 07), ui/shell.rs menus.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: a 2 × 1 × 1 solid whose top consists of two coplanar faces merges to one top face (7 → 6 faces) and validates; faces of different materials are not merged; merging the faces around a square hole produces one face with a hole loop.
- SmoothMergeFaces on the 36 hard-edged side faces of a converted cylinder sets all 36 side edges smooth and hidden; task 03's tessellation then shares the side vertices and draws no side seams.
- CurveMergeEdges on the top ring of an arc-approximating prism records one EdgeChain feature and makes its interior side edges smooth and hidden; the chain is listed as one curved edge in edit mode.
- Stretch of the unit cube's top face by 0.5 along +Z gives 1 × 1 × 1.5 with 6 faces; stretching one top edge by 0.3 along +Z gives a valid wedge with planar faces; stretching one top vertex by 0.3 along +Z splits the top into planar triangles and validates; a stretch that self-intersects is rejected with the SolidIssue text.
- kittest: the edit-mode context menu shows the four commands for a face and an edge selection and 'Merge coplanar faces' is one undo step.
- Satisfies the merge and stretch clauses of SOL-005.
notes:
SRS: SOL-005
Naming follows the reference product's morph commands; labels to be confirmed by commands-and-l10n.

title: Curve, straighten and set radius of walls and edges in the palette
description:
WHY: WAL-002 (M) arc walls must stay exact under editing, and WAL-033 (M, partial, owned by edit-reshape-palette) requires direct manipulation to 'curve or straighten it; change its arc radius', with numeric input; EDT-008 lists 'curve edge (make an arc), straighten edge' among the edge commands. edit-reshape-palette-07/09 shipped these palette entries as stubs that point at this epic ('Curve wall' stub, 'Straighten wall' disabled), and the epic design names a radius handle in the reshape palette. The properties strip (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:220-226 wall getters) shows no arc parameters.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/handles.rs: handles for arc walls (both ends, the arc midpoint as radius handle, the centre, face midpoints) and for arc edges of outlines (edge midpoint as radius handle); a closed circle offers no end handles. tools/palette.rs: 'Curve wall' and 'Curve edge' (pick a point the arc passes through), 'Straighten wall' and 'Straighten edge' (enabled only on arcs, disabled with a reason on a full circle), 'Set radius' (typed radius, end points fixed), and an end-point stretch that slides along the circle by default and moves freely with a modifier; all through the ReshapeOps of tasks 02 and 18 on the ReshapeTool consumer. properties.rs and, if properties-and-dialogs has landed, the wall settings dialog: Radius and Sweep angle fields (editable), Centre (read-only) and Arc length (derived), hidden for straight walls because the getters return None. Out of scope: polygonal-wall properties (13), inclination fields (15).
design: Hit precedence of edit-reshape-palette-07 (node > wall end > edge > face > body) is kept; the radius handle ranks with edges. Sliding an end point along the circle changes the sweep only: compute the new sweep from the projected cursor angle and keep start_angle for the start handle's counterpart, so centre and radius bits survive. Typed values go straight into the ReshapeOp (never via a constructed point) for the same exactness reason as task 07. Sweep edits on a full circle are refused (the circle is defined as closed); changing a partial arc's sweep to 360 degrees makes it closed only through an explicit 'Close circle' action, which is out of scope here. Pitfall: the palette remembers the last command per (kind, part class): arc and straight wall edges are the same class, so a remembered 'Straighten' must fall back when disabled.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: selecting an arc wall shows Radius, Sweep angle and Arc length in the properties strip; typing 6 in Radius changes the wall in one undo step and keeps both end points bit-identical; a straight wall shows none of these fields.
- Palette on a straight wall: 'Curve wall' then a click at a point creates an arc through it with the end points unchanged; 'Straighten wall' restores the line; on a full circle 'Straighten wall' is disabled with a reason.
- Dragging the radius handle with a typed radius 4.5 sets radius exactly 4.5; dragging an arc wall end point slides along the circle and keeps centre and radius bits.
- On a slab, 'Curve edge' is enabled on straight edges and 'Straighten edge' only on arc edges; no palette entry shows the old stub message any more.
- Satisfies the editing part of WAL-002 (the exact arc is stored after every edit) and closes the deferred curve/straighten/radius clauses.
notes:
SRS: WAL-002
Closes the deferred WAL-033 and EDT-008 curve/straighten/radius clauses at UI level.

title: Combine parallel touching walls into one layered wall
description:
WHY: WAL-032 (C): 'Parallel, touching walls may be combined into one wall with a combined cross-section, so that one opening cuts through all of them.' Gap row WAL-032: missing, depending on PRF-001 (layer structures) and openings. Decision D-7: an explicit command with a preview. Hosted openings, doors and windows (host-openings, doors-windows-core, task 12 for arcs) must end up in the combined wall so that one void cuts every skin (DW-009). WAL-031 (merge collinear end-to-end walls, drafting-trim-split-12) is a different command.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs: `Command::CombineWalls { walls }`. Preconditions, each with its own message: at least two walls; all straight with parallel reference lines, or all arcs with the same centre and sweep; same home storey and identical vertical extent; identical extent along the axis (end projections within MODEL_TOLERANCE); faces pairwise touching within MODEL_TOLERANCE (no gap, no overlap); none polygonal (task 13) or inclined (task 15). Result in one undo step: the exterior-most wall is kept and receives `Structure::Layered` of a new layer structure added with Command::AddLayerStructure (layer-structures-01) and named after the parts ('Concrete 200 + Insulation 100'), whose skins concatenate the walls' skins from exterior to interior (single-material walls become one skin; walls drawn in the opposite direction contribute their skins reversed); its reference line becomes a Custom offset so the body does not move; the other walls are deleted; their hosted elements are re-hosted to the kept wall with reveals recomputed, and their junction edges re-pointed (relation store). App: 'Combine walls' in the Edit menu and the context menu, enabled with two or more walls selected and disabled with the failing reason otherwise. IFCX: nothing new beyond the layer structure resource. Out of scope: separating a combined wall again, combining walls of different heights or lengths.
design: Order the walls by the signed offset of their exterior faces along the common left normal (for arcs: by radius, respecting the sweep sign) and check adjacency pairwise on that order. Reuse the layer-structures resource commands so the new structure appears in the structures dialog and can be edited later (PRF editing updates all users). Keep the exterior-most wall's id so references from views or schedules survive; record deleted ids in the inverse edits for undo. Re-hosting: recompute each insert's reveal from the new exterior face (doors-windows-core reveal rule) and keep its along-wall position; for arcs compare angles. Junction edges of the removed walls move to the kept wall when the contact still exists, otherwise they are dropped. Pitfall: priority-based plan merging (WAL-023) already shows touching same-material skins without a line; combining must not change the plan appearance except for the boundary between different materials.
acceptance_criteria:
- Command tests: two touching straight walls (0.20 m concrete and 0.10 m insulation, same length and height) combine into one wall with a two-skin structure; the skin bodies equal the previous two bodies (same rings bit for bit) and the volume is the sum; undo restores both walls, their ids and hosted relations.
- A door previously hosted by the concrete wall is hosted by the combined wall and its void cuts both skins; a window placed on the combined wall afterwards also cuts both skins with one void (geometry tests).
- Two concentric arc walls with the same centre and sweep combine; a 1 mm gap, a 1 mm overlap, different heights, different lengths, a polygonal wall and an inclined wall are each rejected with their own message.
- The combined wall round-trips through IFCX with its new layer structure (roundtrip test).
- kittest: 'Combine walls' is disabled with one wall selected and enabled with two touching walls, and executes one undo step.
- Satisfies WAL-032.
notes:
SRS: WAL-032
Related: WAL-031 (merge collinear walls, drafting-trim-split) is a different command; PRF-001 resource handling from layer-structures.

title: Edit solids in 3D: pick vertices, edges and faces with handles
description:
WHY: SOL-002 (M): vertices, edges and faces are selectable individually or in any combination and movable in 3D with numeric input, including push/pull of a face by a typed distance. SEL-008's edit mode comes from selection-transforms-08, but its 3D id buffer has only 8-bit part slots (selection-transforms-06), which leaves kinds with more than 255 parts to CPU picking, and solids need it. The epic acceptance requires a kittest in which the edit mode selects faces, edges and vertices in 3D with handles.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/solid_edit.rs with hooks in views/view3d.rs: when the edit-mode element (Selection::enter_edit, selection-transforms-01) is a solid, picking runs on its PolyMesh on pointer move only (vertex within 8 px > edge within 5 px > face by ray hit), Tab cycles candidates, Shift-click toggles, and a screen-space rectangle collects the parts of the active part filter fully inside it (vertices by default, edges or faces through the filter), producing SelItem { element, part: Some(PartRef::Kind(..)) }. Overlays through Overlay3d (3d-input-navigation-07): vertex dots, edge lines (hidden edges dashed while editing), hover and selection colours, other elements dimmed through the uniform of selection-transforms-08. Handles at the selection centroid projected into 3D (Kind::part_anchor_3d, task 02): three axis arrows (move along X, Y, Z) and, for a single face, a push/pull arrow along its normal; dragging starts the point-input service with Expect::Distance along the handle axis on Camera3dSurface (typed values, snapping to 3D points of 3d-input-navigation-10), and the commit executes Command::EditSolid (TransformParts Move or PushPull Normal, task 06). Handles are ghosted and inactive for locked solids (ELM-013, as in selection-transforms-09). Plan edit mode picks solid vertices and edges through the kind's part hooks (generic, selection-transforms-08). Out of scope: rotate, scale and mirror of parts, axis push/pull and the edit-mode properties strip (16), the refinement commands (09, 10).
design: CPU picking is O(F + E) for the one element being edited: project its vertices once per pointer move with Camera3d (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/camera.rs), test edges as screen segments clipped at the near plane, faces by ray against face polygons in their planes. Handles are painted with the egui painter over the 3D image, like the existing overlays, and hit-tested in screen space. The drag distance is the signed projection of the pointer ray's closest point onto the handle axis; typed values override it. Pointers: views/view3d.rs:166-215 (current picking), views/render3d.rs (dimming uniform after selection-transforms-06/08), views/surface3d.rs and input/snap3d.rs (3d-input-navigation-07/10), input/consumer.rs (point-input-snapping-01).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest edit_solid_selects_parts_in_3d (CPU fallback path): select a box in the 3D pane, press Enter, click a face centre → [(solid, Face)]; Shift-click an edge → two items; Shift-click a vertex → three items; Esc leaves edit mode with [(solid, None)].
- kittest push_pull_top_face_by_typed_distance: select the top face, drag the push/pull handle, type 1 and press Enter → bounds 1 × 1 × 2 in one undo step; undo restores the cube.
- kittest: select the vertex (1, 1, 1), drag the Z arrow and type 0.2 → the top splits into two planar triangles (7 faces) and the solid validates (task 06 repair); typing −1.5 on the top face's Z arrow shows the SolidIssue text in the status line without changing the model.
- Unit tests: at a cube corner the vertex wins over edges and faces; Tab cycles vertex, edges and faces; a rectangle around the top selects its 4 vertices, with the face filter its top face; handles are not offered for a locked solid (ghosted, ELM-013).
- Hover in edit mode causes no scene upload (upload counter as in selection-transforms-06).
- Satisfies the selection clause of SOL-002 (individually or in any combination, in 3D) and its move and push/pull-along-normal clauses with typed distances.
notes:
SRS: SOL-002
Plane handles (move in a plane) are optional if time allows; D.1 snap radius 8 px reused for vertex picking.

title: Resolve junctions of inclined walls at base and top
