description:
WHY: WAL-010 (S) inclined walls must join like any wall: WAL-020 (M) trims or extends bodies and skins at L, T and X junctions, WAL-023 resolves skins by priority, WAL-026 requires order independence, and NFR-MNT-005 requires regression rows. Epic risk: 'Inclined walls interact with openings and junctions: fixtures first.' Task 15 leaves inclined walls square-ended at nodes.

WHAT: Fixtures first: add the rows to crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs before the implementation and see them fail: inclined/vertical L, vertical branch T onto an inclined face, double-inclined L (independent angles), layered F2 wall inclined at an L, and a topology-mismatch row. Then crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs resolves each node at the base and at the top elevation of the participating walls, feeding a WallInput per level with the face offsets at that elevation and the same junction edges, keys corners by (node, face pair) so both levels list them in the same order, and hands the two resolved rings per skin to task 15's loft; if the two levels differ in topology, the node falls back to square ends and reports a problem. Plan merging (junction-engine-07) slices the lofted bodies. Add the rows to docs/junctions.md. Out of scope: openings (16), inclined arc walls.
design: Every face and every face intersection line of straight walls with planar faces is linear in z, so resolving the 2D junction at a wall's own base and top elevations and lofting between them is exact; the only failure is a change of topology between the two levels (a corner that exists at the base but not at the top), which falls back. Walls of different heights at one node: resolve at each participant's own base and top and use the vertical-coverage rule of junction-engine-06 unchanged. Per-node resolution stays deterministic because both levels use the same canonical node order. Golden rings store both levels.
acceptance_criteria:
- The new junction-suite rows are added first and fail against task 15's square-end fallback (recorded in the task notes); after the implementation they pass closedness, volume conservation, disjoint skins and permutation independence.
- Vertical branch T onto a face inclined 10 degrees: the branch end follows the slope, its end face lies in the inclined face plane within 1e-9.
- Double-inclined L (exterior 10 / interior 4 degrees on one wall, vertical other wall): the corner lines are straight in 3D and equal the intersection of the face planes within 1e-9.
- Layered F2 wall inclined at an L resolves skins by priority (D.4) at both levels with closed bodies.
- The topology-mismatch row asserts the fallback problem and square ends; the task-15 problem 'Junctions with inclined walls are not resolved yet.' is gone.
- docs/junctions.md lists the inclined rows as covered; the catalogue test passes.
- Satisfies WAL-010 at junctions (WAL-020, WAL-023, WAL-026 for inclined walls).
notes:
SRS: WAL-010
Covers WAL-020, WAL-023, WAL-026 and NFR-MNT-005 for inclined walls (owned by junction-engine for vertical walls).
Appendix D.4 priorities; D.7 F2.

title: Join polygonal walls with straight and arc walls
description:
WHY: The epic acceptance requires that 'a polygonal wall joins straight walls in plan'; gap row WAL-009 lists 'junctions with line walls'. WAL-020, WAL-023 and WAL-026 (junction-engine) and NFR-MNT-005 regression rows apply to the new geometry. D-6 defines junctions by reference-line contact, which a polygonal wall does not have.

WHAT: Model (crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs, arc-aware since task 21): a straight or arc wall whose reference-line end lies on a polygonal wall's outline boundary, or inside it within the snap tolerance, gets a Member contact against the polygonal wall (contact kind `Outline { ring, edge, t }`); auto_join projects such an end onto the boundary along its own axis. Geometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs): the polygonal wall is a through participant; the other wall is trimmed at the first crossing of its reference curve with the outline (analytic for arc edges via curve.rs intersect()); the priority stage (junction-engine-05/06) decides which material wins, and same material and priority merge into one plan region (junction-engine-07). Write the interpretation into docs/junctions.md and add the rows to crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs. Out of scope: polygonal/polygonal contact (they overlap as drawn and the priority rule decides the plan cut), layered polygonal walls (14).
design: For a polygonal wall, contact is defined as the other wall's reference-line end touching the outline; this extends D-6 without inventing a reference line. The trim point is the first intersection of the other wall's reference curve with the outline boundary; the other wall's skins are clipped by the polygon after priority resolution, so a lower-priority straight wall stops at the boundary and a higher-priority one cuts into the polygonal wall. Golden rings pin the default Tessellation like the arc rows of task 05. Pitfall: an end exactly on an outline vertex belongs to both adjacent edges; pick the lower edge index so the result is deterministic.
acceptance_criteria:
- Junction suite rows: a straight wall ending on a polygonal edge is trimmed to the boundary; an arc wall ending on a polygonal arc edge is trimmed at the analytic circle-circle intersection within 1e-9; an L-shaped polygonal wall with two straight walls; same material and priority merges into one plan region without a boundary line; a higher-priority straight wall cuts the polygonal wall; every row passes closedness, volume conservation and permutation independence.
- Model: a straight wall end placed 3 mm inside a polygonal outline auto-joins and ends on the boundary; moving it away unjoins (command tests with undo).
- docs/junctions.md documents the polygonal-contact rule and lists the new rows as covered; the catalogue test passes.
- Satisfies the 'polygonal wall joins straight walls in plan' clause of the epic acceptance and the junction part of WAL-009.
notes:
SRS: WAL-009
Covers WAL-020, WAL-023, WAL-026 and NFR-MNT-005 for polygonal walls (owned by junction-engine for line walls); D-6 interpreted for outlines.
Appendix D.4 priorities.

title: Persist free-form solids in IFCX with per-face materials
description:
WHY: IFX-060 (M) requires everything needed to restore the editable model in archicraft:: attributes and IFX-064 (M) a round trip in which regenerated geometry equals the stored geometry within 0.1 mm, so SOL-001 solids, the SOL-003 face materials and edge flags and the SOL-009 class must survive save and open. Generic consumers must see the face materials too (IFX-040 materials are referenced per node through inherits; IFX-017 writes one child per material part) and the class as bsi::ifc::class with the D.5 code (Table 5-1 default IfcBuildingElementProxy); the reader currently downgrades unknown classes (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/reader.rs:625-637). SOL-008 and NFR-REL-005: the writer never writes a corrupt body.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/solid.rs implements the KindCodec of element-kind-framework-06: archicraft::solid { vertices: [[x, y, z], …] in id order, faces: [{ loops: [[index, …], …], material: reference }], edges: [{ a, b, smooth, visible }] for non-default flags only, features: [...], open: bool }, declared with a complete value description (IFX-061), plus a FORMAT_VERSION bump with a no-op migration entry in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework-12; older versions would otherwise drop solids silently). Bodies: one material writes a closed Body child; several materials (the Body's FaceMaterialRuns, task 03) write one non-volumetric child per material, Surface_1 … Surface_n in order of first appearance, each inheriting its material node; the strict per-part write check that solid-kernel-ops-03 adds to write_element checks the union of an element's Surface_n children with check_closed instead of each child. The reader rebuilds the PolyMesh with fresh ids and validates it; an invalid solid is skipped with an error naming the node path (lenient reading, strict writing); every class of IfcClass::SELECTABLE_D5 is accepted, and an unknown code falls back to the kind's default class with a warning (the rule of reader.rs:625-637, generalised by element-kind-framework). conformance/check.ts (whose per-mesh closedness check comes from solid-kernel-ops-03) and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs check the Surface_n parts of an element together as one closed mesh. Sample: crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs free_form_solids() built with the FixtureBuilder (box, L-prism with a hole, smooth cylinder, two-material box with one hidden edge, box with class IfcSlab), registered in catalogue(), golden file crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/free-form-solids.ifcx. Out of scope: excluding open sheets from the standard content (13).
design: Vertices are written in IndexMap order and loops refer to positions, so ids need not be persisted (selections are never saved). Parameters are written at full precision; round_coordinate applies only to meshes (writer conventions in docs/implementation-status.md 'Add an IFCX attribute'). Surface_n sub-node ids come from sub_node_id(owner, role) (writer.rs write_element), so they are v5 and stable while the material order is unchanged (IFX-010 allows regenerated sub-nodes to be renamed by role). Edge flags keyed by vertex position pairs. Pointers: writer.rs:361-416 (write_element), schema.rs (declarations), reader.rs:592-734 (read_element), conformance/check.ts:67-103, samples.rs FixtureBuilder (element-kind-framework-03), ARCHICRAFT_BLESS workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: every solid of free_form_solids reopens with the same PolyMesh up to id renumbering (coordinates exact at full parameter precision; faces, materials, flags and features equal) and regenerated geometry equals the stored meshes within 0.1 mm (IFX-064).
- The golden file is byte-identical on re-save apart from timestamp and dataVersion (IFX-007) and conformance/run.sh passes on it, including the new closed-union check for Surface_n parts; the two-material box shows two colours in the reference viewer (manual release check).
- Reader tests: a solid with a missing face loop is skipped with an error naming its path; an unknown class code falls back to IfcBuildingElementProxy with a warning; IfcSlab is preserved.
- archicraft::solid is declared only when the project contains a solid (content-derived declarations), so walls-and-slab.ifcx and two-storey-shell.ifcx change only in the format version written by the bump (re-blessed once, reviewed diff).
- A solid whose evaluated body fails check_closed is written without a body plus a warning (existing writer behaviour, writer.rs:390-393), never as a corrupt mesh.
- Satisfies persistence of SOL-001, SOL-003 and SOL-009 and the writer clause of SOL-008.
notes:
SRS: SOL-001 SOL-003 SOL-008 SOL-009
Open question for the SRS owner: IFX-032 requires every volumetric part to be closed; the per-material Surface_n parts of one solid are non-volumetric and closed only together. The alternative (a closed Body in the dominant material plus coloured overlay surfaces) duplicates geometry and z-fights in viewers. Chosen: Surface_n parts plus the union check; align with whatever solid-kernel-ops writes for SOL-026 faces in operator materials.

title: Place doors and windows in arc walls with radial voids
description:
WHY: DW-019 (M): 'Doors and windows shall be placeable in arc walls as straight units aligned to the chord, with the void cutting the full curved wall thickness. Curved units are covered by DW-020.' Gap row DW-019: 'Needs arc walls, chord-aligned placement, and a void that cuts the full curved thickness (not a planar 2D cut; needs a radial prism or 3D Boolean).' DW-009 (all skins cut, host restored on delete), IFX-036 (closed Void child enclosing the removed volume) and IFX-033 (exported host bodies already have the volume removed) apply. Exists: host-openings-05's crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall_cut.rs cuts the VoidPrisms collected in EvalContext::cutters per skin band with extrude_layers (host-openings-04) along the face normal of a straight span, explicitly leaving 'arc and inclined walls (curved-geometry)' out; doors-windows-core-03 feeds insert voids into it through insert_void() in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/insert.rs, and doors-windows-core-01's InsertFrame::resolve (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/insert.rs) yields [s0, s1], sill, head, reveal and unit_to_storey for straight hosts; task 02 makes it refuse arc hosts and task 04 reports openings in arc walls as unsupported.

WHAT: wall_cut.rs gains an arc path: the (s, z) cut sections map to angular intervals theta(s) = start_angle + sign(sweep) * s / r_ref on the reference arc, so each jamb is a radial plane through the centre ('radial void prism'). Per skin band, the curved faces are triangulated in (theta, z) parameter space with the hole rectangles as constraints (task 03 stations plus the jamb angles, triangulate.rs), jamb faces are radial quads, sill and head faces are annular strips; the Void part is the annular-sector prism extended beyond both faces by VOID_MARGIN (host-openings-03). InsertFrame::resolve for arc hosts: the along-wall interval [s0, s1] on the reference arc, the unit's local x along the chord through the jamb points at the reveal face, origin and rotation of unit_to_storey from that chord, so the straight unit sits on the chord; the void's angular span is widened when needed so the straight unit fits between the radial jambs; a problem is reported when the unit cannot fit inside the curved thickness at its reveal ('The window is too wide for this curved wall at this reveal.'). Remove task 02's refusal and task 04's 'not supported' problem. Plan symbols are placed by the frame; IFCX occurrences carry the chord transform and the radial Void. Generic openings of host-openings use the same path. Extend curved_walls() with a window and a door in the arc wall and re-bless the golden. Out of scope: curved units (DW-020, C), units in polygonal walls (refused, task 13).
design: Cutting in the developed (s, z) plane keeps one code path for straight and arc walls: host-openings computes cut sections in wall-local coordinates; for arcs the mapping from s to angle uses the reference radius, and every skin is swept radially between its two band radii, so a constant s is a radial plane through all skins: no 3D Boolean (solid-kernel-ops is not a prerequisite). Triangulate each curved face with spade CDT in (theta, z), then map to 3D; vertices along the curved face stay shared (smooth), the jamb columns are hard edges. The straight unit and the radial jambs: compute the unit's four plan corners at the reveal depth and the frame depth, take the extreme angles, and use [min, max] as the void span if larger than the nominal [s0, s1]; document that the reveal is measured at the unit's centre. Seam case: a full circle has no start column, so an interval crossing start_angle is split at 2 pi in parameter space before triangulation. Pitfall: the clear-length check of doors-windows-core-03 compares s against skin end projections; for arcs compare angles. unit_to_storey must stay a proper transform (determinant > 0, IFX-051).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a 1.20 x 1.40 m window (Appendix D.2) in an F2-structured arc wall of reference radius 5 m: every skin body stays closed, each skin's volume decreases by its annular-sector void volume within the chord-loss bound, and rays along the radius at both jamb angles pass through all six skins without hitting material inside the opening.
- A 0.90 x 2.10 m door (Appendix D.2) in the same wall: the void reaches from the storey elevation to 2.10 m through all skins and the unit sits on the chord.
- Jamb faces are radial: their normals are perpendicular to the radial direction within 1e-9.
- The unit lies on the chord: its local x equals the chord direction within 1e-12 and it is centred at the opening's mid-angle; its frame does not intersect the wall's faces at the default reveal.
- An opening straddling the start angle of a full circle wall cuts correctly and the wall stays one closed body.
- Deleting the window restores the host body bit for bit (command test with undo).
- Golden curved-walls.ifcx with the IfcWindow and IfcDoor occurrences and their radial Voids passes conformance/run.sh; the plan cut shows the openings (cut fill masked) in an arc wall.
- The door and window tool previews a chord-aligned unit while hovering an arc wall and a click places it (state-machine test).
- Satisfies DW-019.
notes:
SRS: DW-019
Appendix D.2: window 1.20 x 1.40 m, sill 0.90 m above the storey, centred in the core; door 0.90 x 2.10 m.
DW-020 (curved units, C) stays with a later epic.

title: Detect junction contact and auto-join on arc reference lines
description:
WHY: WAL-020 (M): walls are joined where their reference lines touch (L, T, X), decision D-6: junctions come from reference-line contact; WAL-021 (M): a wall end auto-joins when it comes within snap tolerance of another reference line; WAL-022 (S): join and unjoin commands. junction-engine-02 moved detection into crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs (JunctionGraph, detect, detect_around, `Member { wall, contact: Start | End | Body { t } }`), junction-engine-09 added JoinWalls/UnjoinWalls and junction-engine-10 auto_join, all on straight reference lines. Gap row WAL-002 names 'arc junctions'.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs: contact detection on the axis Segments of task 02 with curve.rs: end-end contact (L) including tangent continuation, end-on-body contact via Segment::param_of (T, `Body { t }` with t the arc parameter), and crossings via intersect() with Extent::Bounded (X, both line-circle or circle-circle roots inside the sweeps); a closed circle has no ends and appears only as a Body member; the grid index uses the exact arc bounding boxes. auto_join: project a free end onto the nearest point of an arc reference line within the snap tolerance, moving the end along its own axis (a straight end along its line, an arc end along its circle with centre and radius bits kept). JoinWalls on an arc wall extends or trims its sweep along its circle to the other carrier; UnjoinWalls records the Separated relation as for straight walls. The incremental dirty-set expansion keeps working with arc members. Out of scope: geometric resolution (05), polygonal walls (22), inclined walls (23).
design: Detection stays reference-curve based (D-6) and uses axis geometry only, never bodies. Use JOIN_TOLERANCE of tolerance.rs for contact and the carrier root nearest to the end for joins. Moving an arc end along its circle changes only the sweep (start end: start_angle and sweep), which keeps the exact-arc invariant of task 02; moving it onto the projection of the other wall's end instead would change centre or radius. Pitfall: a full circle's start() == end() must not be reported as an L with itself; tangent end-end contact is an L whose geometric resolution (05) degenerates to a flush joint.
acceptance_criteria:
- Detection table: arc end on straight end (L); arc end on straight body (T); straight end on arc body (T, with t equal to the analytic parameter within 1e-12); arc/arc end contact with tangency; arc/line crossing (X at each root inside the sweep); straight end on a full circle (T); a full circle never contacts itself; results are canonically sorted and independent of input order.
- auto_join: an arc wall end placed 3 mm from a straight reference line joins and keeps its centre and radius bits; a straight end 3 mm off an arc reference line ends exactly on the circle (|p - c| = r within 1e-12); moving it away unjoins (command tests with undo).
- JoinWalls on an arc wall and a straight wall whose carriers intersect changes only the arc's sweep so that its end lies on the intersection within 1e-12; UnjoinWalls separates them.
- Existing junction-engine model tests pass unchanged.
- Satisfies the detection, auto-join and join/unjoin parts of WAL-020, WAL-021 and WAL-022 for arc walls (owned by junction-engine for straight walls); prerequisite of the arc junction rows of task 05.
notes:
SRS: WAL-002
Covers WAL-020, WAL-021 and WAL-022 for arc walls (owned by junction-engine for straight walls); D-6 reference-line contact.
Appendix D.1 snapping radius 8 px for the auto-join tolerance.

title: Register the free-form solid kind with any-axis transforms and parts
description:
WHY: SOL-001 needs a free-form solid element kind. SOL-009 (M): the IFC class of a free-form solid shall be user-selectable (ELM-011) from the Appendix D.5 list with IfcBuildingElementProxy as the default (Table 5-1); the gap row says no free-form kind exists and the class list was incomplete (element-kind-framework-05 adds IfcClass::SELECTABLE_D5). EDT-007 (M) makes free-form solids rotatable about any axis in 3D and EDT-022 (S) adds mirroring about a 3D plane; selection-transforms-02 refuses tilted rotations and 3d-input-navigation-13 inclined-plane mirrors for walls and slabs, and both leave the positive case to this epic. SEL-008's edit mode needs the solid's faces, edges and vertices registered as parts with stable addressing (selection-transforms-01). SOL-008: the kind's validate hook makes solid::validate the gate for every command touching a solid.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/solid.rs: Solid { mesh: PolyMesh, open: bool (false until task 13), segments: Option<u32> (creation override for curved input, None = Auto, remembered in the defaults prototype) } in storey coordinates (x, y as in the model, z relative to the home storey elevation, like evaluated bodies); one kinds! line solid => Solid (element-kind-framework-02) with type Part = SolidPart, from which the macro of selection-transforms-01 generates PartRef::Kind(KindPart::Solid(..)). DESCRIPTOR: KindDescriptor { label 'Free-form solid', code 'solid', name_prefix 'FS', default_class IfcClass::BuildingElementProxy, ifc_classes IfcClass::SELECTABLE_D5, has_tool true, transforms TransformSupport::ALL (selection-transforms-02), part_roles &[] (no IFC child parts, so Kind::parts() stays empty), solid true (the closed-body flag of solid-kernel-ops-04, so solids can be targets and operators of solid operations), template_defaults returning a DefaultsSlot (element-kind-framework-04) whose prototype is a 1 × 1 × 1 m box in the template's default material, i.e. a default height of 1.00 m, with segments None }. Hooks: material() returns the dominant face material and set_material() sets every face; validate runs solid::validate and checks that every face material exists; vertical_extent from the mesh z bounds; rehome/relink shift z by the elevation difference so the absolute position is kept (ELM-005); storey_links() is empty; transform(&Transform, &TransformContext) -> Result<Transformed<Solid>, TransformError> applies Move, Rotate, Mirror, non-uniform Scale and RotateAxis as Transform::affine() through PolyMesh::transformed, never returns Unsupported and never adds a NotScaled note; the plane mirror of 3d-input-navigation-13 (ElementKind::mirrored(&Plane3, elevation)) reflects the mesh about any plane; plan_bounds from the mesh. Part hooks of selection-transforms-01: SolidPart { Vertex(VertexId), Edge(EdgeKey), Face(FaceId) }; part_refs() lists faces, edges and vertices in stable id order; part_label ('face 3', 'edge 2–5', 'vertex 7'); part_anchor/part_outline as plan projections; validate_part rejects stale ids. The Kind trait gains part_anchor_3d(&PartRef) -> Option<DVec3> and part_polyline_3d(&PartRef) -> Option<Vec<DVec3>> with None defaults (one change in kinds/mod.rs) for the 3D edit mode. Project::new_solid(storey, mesh) is a thin wrapper over Project::new_element (element-kind-framework-04). Out of scope: geometry evaluation (03), IFCX (04), tools (05), sub-element edits (06).
design: Transforms reuse Transform::affine() (selection-transforms-02, crates/archicraft-model/src/transform.rs); because the solid stores explicit vertices, every affine map is representable, so the hook only rejects non-finite input (already filtered upstream). The dominant material (largest total face area, ties by first face) feeds the plan cut fill and the properties strip. Storey coordinates match crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:1-7 ('Bodies are generated in the coordinates of the element's home storey'). Part addressing by VertexId/FaceId/EdgeKey follows selection-transforms-01's rule (stable ids, never tessellation indices); Selection::retain_valid drops parts whose ids vanished after an edit. The extra 3D part hooks belong to the Kind trait so stairs and curtain walls can reuse them in 3D later. Pointers: kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-02), selection.rs (selection-transforms-01), transform.rs Transform and TransformSupport (selection-transforms-02), Plane3 and ElementKind::mirrored (3d-input-navigation-13), element.rs IfcClass (element-kind-framework-05), validate.rs:256-261 (allowed-class check), command.rs:567-571 (check_tool_defaults), project.rs ToolDefaults (a DefaultsSlot map after element-kind-framework-04).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements of a box solid executes, undoes and redoes; the name is FS-001; an open mesh is rejected with CommandError::Invalid carrying the SolidIssue message and the project is unchanged.

The name prefix FS and the default height 1.00 m are proposals (Appendix D gives no values).

title: Add Trim and RoofJoin relations, trimming volumes and commands
description:
WHY: SOL-030 (M): selected walls, columns, beams and free-form solids are trimmable associatively to one or more roofs, shells or slabs, and the user picks the part to keep (or, with a modifier, the part to remove). SOL-032 (S): each roof and shell defines its trimming volume - downward (footprint from the roof outline or from the pivot line), upward, or a finite, user-editable volume. ROF-010 (S): two roofs are joinable so that both are trimmed associatively to their line of intersection. SRS 3.3 lists Trim as a stored relation that survives save and open and is re-evaluated when a participant changes. The gap analysis rates all three missing. What exists after the prerequisites: the relation store of element-kind-framework-08 (crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs) already declares `Relation::Trim { target, by }` with its ends only, dependents_of (target depends on by), Edit::InsertRelation/RemoveRelation, the delete cascade and the archicraft::relations codec; the roof kind (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/roof.rs, roofs-01) has no trimming volume and nothing joins two roofs.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs extend the framework's `Relation::Trim { target, by }` with `side: TrimSide::{Inside, Outside}` (one relation per target and tool, so the v5 RelationId and dependents_of of element-kind-framework-08 apply unchanged) and add `Relation::RoofJoin { a, b }` with a canonical pair order as junction-engine-02 did for Junction, dependents in both directions, integrity checks and delete cascade; KindDescriptor flags trim_target (wall, column, beam, and the test-kinds Dummy so the generic path is tested) and trim_tool (roof, slab) plus an `inclined(&ElementKind) -> bool` hook for SOL-031 (beams with a non-zero pitch; walls and columns answer false until WAL-010 and COL-004 land); `TrimmingVolume::{Downward { footprint }, Upward, Finite { footprint, bottom }}` with `TrimFootprint::{Outline, PivotLine, Custom(Outline)}` as a `trimming_volume` field of `Roof` (default Downward from the outline); commands TrimElements { targets, tools, side }, UntrimElements { targets, tools: Option<Vec<ElementId>> }, JoinRoofs { a, b } and UnjoinRoofs { a, b } with labels as message keys in locales/en/model.ftl (commands-and-l10n-02). In archicraft-ifcx add the side member of the trim record and the roofJoin kind to the archicraft::relations codec and an optional trimmingVolume to archicraft::roof (roofs-06), following the alpha/mod.rs version rule of element-kind-framework-12. Start docs/trims.md. If free-form-solids has landed, set trim_target on its solid kind here; otherwise the done task files that one-line follow-up against free-form-solids. Out of scope: geometry (06-08), UI (09, 10), shells (ROF-013, Could: could-scope-polish sets trim_tool) and curtain walls (CW-008: curtain-walls-13 sets trim_target).
design: Relation edits go through Edit::InsertRelation/RemoveRelation of element-kind-framework-08; changing the side of an existing pair is a RemoveRelation plus InsertRelation inside one command. Semantics recorded in docs/trims.md: the kept part of a target is the part inside the union of its Inside tools' volumes (the whole target when it has none) minus the union of its Outside tools' volumes, so trims with several tools commute and the order of relations never matters; a gable wall trimmed Inside to a main roof and a dormer roof keeps the part under either roof. TrimSide is stored relative to the trimming volume, not as a pick point, so the trim stays meaningful after edits; it is called TrimSide rather than KeepSide because free-form-solids-14 uses KeepSide { Above, Below } for the non-associative crop. Deviation from the epic design note (Relation::Trim{element, by, keep_side, volume}, also quoted by curtain-walls-13): SOL-032 makes the volume a property of each roof and the framework stores one relation per end pair, so the stored shape is Trim { target, by, side }; docs/trims.md records this, the volume kinds, the fixed slab volume (downward from the outline, under the top surface) and later the rules of tasks 06-08. dependents_of already re-evaluates a target when a tool changes; add RoofJoin to its per-variant direction table in both directions. Every new model field gets #[serde(default)]; the codec writes trimmingVolume only when it differs from the default and writes relations sorted by kind and ids (IFX-007 determinism); the reader drops relations that reference missing elements with a warning (lenient reading of element-kind-framework-08). The JoinRoofs bounds check is deliberately coarse because the model has no roof geometry; task 08 reports 'roofs do not intersect' exactly.
acceptance_criteria:
- TrimElements on two walls with two roofs creates four Trim relations with the given side; repeating it with the other side replaces their side; an identical repeat is NoChange; locked targets give CommandError::Locked; a slab is accepted as tool and the test-kinds Dummy flagged trim_target as target; a roof as target, a door as tool or a target among its own tools give CommandError::Invalid.
- UntrimElements removes all tools or only the named ones; execute plus undo restores the project exactly (crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs).
- Deleting a tool roof removes its Trim relations, restoring the target; DeleteStorey cascades; integrity_problems is empty after every step; dependents_of(tool) contains its targets and dependents_of of either joined roof contains the other.
- JoinRoofs(A, B) and JoinRoofs(B, A) create the same RoofJoin (same RelationId); JoinRoofs rejects one roof twice, non-roofs, an existing pair (NoChange) and roofs whose plan bounds (Kind::plan_bounds) do not overlap; UnjoinRoofs and undo restore.
- TrimmingVolume validation: a Finite bottom must lie below the roof's lowest eave and a Custom footprint must pass validate_ring and overlap the roof's plan bounds; PivotLine means the pivot polygon of a multi-plane roof and, for a single-plane roof, the part of the outline on the uphill side of the pivot line (documented in docs/trims.md).
- A file with Trim and RoofJoin relations and a non-default trimming volume round-trips with assert_eq; every new key is declared in the schemas section (IFX-005, IFX-061); a trim record without side reads as Inside and a roof without trimmingVolume as Downward from the outline; existing golden files stay byte-identical, or, if the relation-kind declaration forces a FORMAT_VERSION bump, differ only in the version with a no-op entry in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs (reviewed diff).
- Command journals with the four new commands serialise and replay.
notes: SRS: SOL-030 SOL-032 ROF-010. Context: SRS 3.3 relations, SOL-022 persistence clause, ELM-014 (auxiliary tools keep trimming, re-asserted in 07), IFX-060/061/062. Kind flags are set later by curtain-walls-13 (CW-008 target), could-scope-polish-12 (ROF-013 shell tool), free-form-solids (solid target) if it lands after this task, curved-geometry-15 (inclined walls) and members-profiles-adv-04 (inclined columns).

title: Store arc and full-circle reference curves on walls
description:
WHY: WAL-002 (M): 'Arc walls shall be created by centre, radius and sweep; by three points on the arc; or by tangent continuation of the previous segment. The exact arc shall be stored. A full circle entered in one operation shall be one closed circular wall'. Decision D-10: a full circle wall is one closed element, not two halves. WAL-003 and WAL-004 (both partial: reference-line locations and faces, thickness changes keep the reference line in place) must hold for arcs too, and the curve/straighten/radius clause of WAL-033 was deferred to this epic by edit-reshape-palette-09. Gap row WAL-002: 'Wall is a straight segment start/end only (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:130-139); no arc/curve type anywhere'.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/wall.rs (element-kind-framework) replace `start`/`end` by `shape: WallShape` whose only variant for now is `Axis(Segment)`, Segment being curve.rs's `Line { a, b }` or `Arc(Arc)` (drafting-trim-split-01; |sweep| = 2 pi means a closed circle), so polygonal walls (task 13) add a variant instead of a second refactor. Accessors `start()`, `end()`, `is_closed()`, `length()` (arc length), `point_at(s)`, `tangent_at(s)`, `left_normal_at(s)` and one `face_curve(offset) -> Segment` that returns the concentric arc of radius r - sign(sweep) * offset for every face, core face and skin boundary (offsets from ReferenceLine::face_offsets, element.rs:96-107, and the SkinBands of layer-structures-04). Constructors reuse curve.rs: Arc::centre_radius, Arc::through, Arc::circle and Arc::tangent_continuation; add `Project::new_arc_wall` and `Project::new_circle_wall` beside new_wall (project.rs:281). Validation through the wall descriptor (validate.rs:199 today): finite values, radius and arc length at least MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, |sweep| at least MIN_CORNER_ANGLE_DEG, smallest skin radius at least MIN_THICKNESS. Transform hooks (translate, rotate, mirror negating the sweep). Wall ReshapeOps (edit-reshape-palette-05) gain `CurveWall { through }`, `StraightenWall` and `SetArcRadius { radius }` (keeps both end points and the bulge side). Replace every read of `wall.start`/`wall.end` in all crates by the accessors (junction inputs, plan reference line, snap sources, tools, properties, IFCX codec). Existing wall commands keep working on arc axes: drafting-trim-split-10/11's split, trim and extend planners operate on the axis Segment (split_at, sub), and drafting-trim-split-12's merge planner switches on its same-circle branch (same_carrier). Until tasks 04, 06 and 12 land: the wall GeometryKind reports 'Arc wall geometry is not available yet.' as a problem, the IFCX wall codec refuses arc walls with an error, and InsertFrame::resolve (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/insert.rs, doors-windows-core-01) returns an error for arc hosts; none of this is reachable from the UI. Out of scope: bodies (04), junction detection (21) and resolution (05), IFCX (06), tools (07), properties and palette (11), inclined and polygonal walls (13, 15).
design: Store centre, radius, start angle and sweep (the exact parameters of curve.rs) and derive the end points with one function, so every consumer computes start() and end() with the same bits; a full circle has start() == end() by construction, which is what makes it one closed element without a seam vertex pair. Sign convention: the exterior is on the right of the start-to-end direction (element.rs:80-85); for a counter-clockwise arc (sweep > 0) the left-hand normal points to the centre, so an offset d along the left normal has radius r - d; for sweep < 0 it is r + d. face_curve() is the single source of face circles: geometry (04), snapping (07), tracing (08) and IFCX (06) must call it rather than recompute radii, otherwise SLB-004 fails on rounding. SetArcRadius keeps the chord end points and the side of the bulge and rejects radii smaller than half the chord; for a full circle it keeps the centre. Pitfalls: junction-engine-02's detector reads end points: a full circle has no free ends (task 21 makes it a body-only member); layer-structures' SkinBand offsets are along the left normal, so arc band radii follow from face_curve with the same offsets; the PartRef enumeration of selection-transforms must not offer wall ends for a closed wall; Wall::same_settings (drafting-trim-split-12) masks the axis, so arc and straight walls never merge with each other.
acceptance_criteria:
- Constructor tests: centre (0,0), start (5,0), sweep +90 degrees gives end (0,5) within 1e-12 and stores radius 5.0 exactly; three points (5,0), (5 cos 45, 5 sin 45), (0,5) give centre (0,0) within 1e-12; tangent continuation from the segment (0,0)-(5,0) to end (8,3) is tangent at (5,0) (dot product with (1,0) equals 1 within 1e-12).
- A full circle: is_closed() is true, start() and end() are bit-identical, length() = 2 pi r within 1e-12; translate, rotate and mirror keep it closed, and after mirror the exterior face is still on the right of the axis direction (face_curve(exterior) radius unchanged).
- face_curve() for Outside, Center, Inside, Custom(0.1) and the two core faces of an F2-structured arc wall returns the expected radii, and two calls return identical bits.
- Validation messages: inner skin radius below MIN_THICKNESS ('The wall is thicker than its inner radius allows.'), sweep below 0.1 degrees, NaN radius.
- Command tests with undo for CurveWall, StraightenWall and SetArcRadius (end points bit-identical after each); StraightenWall on a full circle gives CommandError::Invalid; changing the thickness of an arc wall leaves the axis bit-identical (WAL-004).
- Splitting an arc wall at a point gives two arc walls with the original centre and radius bits; merging two end-to-end arc walls of the same circle with identical settings gives one arc wall whose sweep is the sum (WAL-031 same-circle branch of drafting-trim-split-12).
- All existing workspace tests pass after the accessor refactor; golden files are byte-identical; the command journal round-trips arc walls through serde.
- Satisfies the exact-storage and one-closed-element clauses of WAL-002 and D-10 at model level.
notes:
SRS: WAL-002
Also completes the deferred WAL-033 clause 'curve or straighten it; change its arc radius' at model level (UI in task 11).
D-10: a full circle wall is one closed element (not two halves).
Appendix D.2 wall defaults (0.25 m masonry, reference line on the exterior face) apply unchanged to arc walls.

title: Show trimming volumes and add roof join and member unjoin controls
description:
WHY: SOL-032 (S): the trimming volume of each roof is selectable (downward from outline or pivot line, upward, finite and user-editable) and displayable on demand. ROF-010 (S): two roofs are joinable. For the cleanup of BEA-004, COL-006 and SLB-007 users need to separate a beam or column pair that should not clean up; junction-engine-11 already shows the join group of every construction element and the join and unjoin actions for walls.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs add the roof property 'Trimming volume' (Downward from outline, Downward from pivot line, Upward, Finite with a unit-aware bottom elevation, Custom footprint), the custom footprint being edited with the polygon reshape commands through a PartRef on the volume outline; add the per-view option 'Show trimming volumes' (a CommandRegistry command with a View menu item) drawing the selected roofs' volumes (06) translucent in 3D through Renderer3d::draw_overlay (host-openings-10) and as dashed outlines in plan; add the commands 'Join roofs' and 'Unjoin roofs' for two selected roofs (JoinRoofs, UnjoinRoofs; strings in locales/en/commands.ftl) and let the unjoin action accept beam and column pairs (task 01). Out of scope: the trim tool (09).
design: PartRef gains a TrimFootprint { roof } variant handled by Command::Reshape of edit-reshape-palette with the Outline operations, so no second polygon editor appears. Plan display follows the 'Add a plan-view overlay' recipe (a new collection on PlanDrawing drawn in views/plan.rs); 3D display uses Renderer3d::draw_overlay of host-openings-10 with a translucent PreviewStyle beside the trim styles of task 09. Volume meshes are requested from the cache of task 06 only while the option is on. The option is view state (plan-views-browser view definition or the per-view state), never project data. Property rows use the Fields pattern of properties.rs (a getter returning None hides the row for slabs, which have a fixed volume).
acceptance_criteria:
- Selecting a roof shows 'Trimming volume'; switching to Upward issues one UpdateElements (one undo step) and walls trimmed by that roof change in the same revision.
- The Finite bottom accepts typed lengths with units and rejects a value above the lowest eave with the validation message (ELM-017 style).
- 'Show trimming volumes' toggles a translucent volume in 3D and a dashed outline in plan for the selected roof; the saved IFCX is byte-identical with the option on and off (IFX-068).
- 'Join roofs' with two roofs selected creates the RoofJoin and 'Unjoin roofs' removes it; both are disabled for any other selection.
- Unjoin on a selected beam and column adds the Separated relation and the beam keeps its full length after re-evaluation.
- kittests cover each item; the existing UI tests stay green.
notes: SRS: SOL-032 ROF-010 BEA-004 COL-006 SLB-007. Context: WAL-025 join groups, IFX-068.

title: Anchor arc tessellation to the circle and build smooth curved slab faces
description:
WHY: IFX-034 (M): 'Curved geometry shall be tessellated. Defaults: maximum chordal deviation 2 mm and at most 10 degrees per segment (hence at least 36 segments per full circle). The values are user-adjustable per project.' SLB-004 (M): 'coincident curves shall be tessellated identically for display and export'. IFX-038: vertices are shared only across smooth edges, because the reference viewer averages normals over shared vertices; the no-seam clause of WAL-002/D-10 depends on that. IFX-034 is partial. Exists: Tessellation (chord_deviation 0.002 m, max_angle_deg 10) in crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:27-43, validated (command.rs:599-603), saved (writer.rs:163-164, reader.rs:347-356), chord deviation editable (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:593-604); drafting-trim-split-02 added crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs with segment_count() and tessellate(), and drafting-trim-split-04 the ElementGeometry.curves list with CurveKey and ModelGeometry::curve(key), so 2D arcs already use the settings. Missing: no wall or slab tessellates (gap row IFX-034), the max-angle field (task 20), and arc stations that let partly coincident arcs share vertices.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs: change drafting-trim-split-02's arc station rule from 'n equal steps from the canonical start' to the circle-anchored grid theta_k = k * (TAU / n) with n = segment_count(r, TAU, settings), keeping the grid stations strictly inside the arc's angular interval (a station closer than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH of arc length to an end is dropped) plus the arc's own end points, all evaluated by one point_on(centre, radius, theta); update drafting-trim-split-02's tests that assumed equal steps and re-bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/drafting.ifcx, whose IfcAnnotation Curve points move. Add `tessellate_outline(&Outline<E>, &Tessellation) -> TessellatedOutline` (rings of points with per-segment provenance: source edge index and a smooth flag for runs within one arc and across tangent-continuous joints detected with is_parallel() of crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs). Register every slab arc edge in ElementGeometry.curves under a CurveKey (drafting-trim-split-04), so plan, snapping and the writer read ModelGeometry::curve(key), and extend drafting-trim-split-04's dirty rule so a tessellation change re-evaluates slabs with arcs. Slab bodies with arc edges (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/slab.rs; evaluate.rs:177-186 and extrude.rs:18-58 in the increment-0 code): side faces along one smooth run are emitted as a strip with shared vertex columns (`TriMesh::add_smooth_strip` beside add_face, mesh.rs:83-89; both extrude() and host-openings-04's extrude_layers() accept the smooth flags, the latter used by arc walls in task 04); caps and other side faces keep their own vertices (IFX-038). mesh.rs feature_edges (mesh.rs:239-258) skips edges whose two triangles share both vertex indices. Out of scope: 3D shading and the dialog field (task 20), wall bodies (04), IFCX (06).
design: Why circle-anchored: tessellating each curve independently from its own start angle gives different interior vertices for two curves that coincide only partly (a slab edge along part of a wall face, or a wall face trimmed at a junction corner) or that run in opposite directions, and the chords then deviate by up to 2 mm from each other: exactly the gap F8 forbids. Anchoring the grid to the circle (centre, radius, settings) and adding only the curve's own end points makes the vertex set a function of the circle and the end points. The remaining rule, enforced by tracing (08) and F8 (09), is that coincident spans must end at shared vertices. Compute theta_k = (k as f64) * (TAU / n as f64) the same way everywhere and never accumulate angles by repeated addition; the end-drop rule uses the arc-length distance r * |theta_k - theta_end| so it is identical for coincident arcs. Smooth strips: emit the side quads of consecutive segments of one smooth run with shared vertex indices; a full circle closes the strip onto its first column, so there is no seam column. check_closed (mesh.rs:122) already merges coincident points, so closedness tests are unaffected. MAX_MESH_POINTS (mesh.rs:49) is far away: 497 segments for r = 100 m. One producer: only evaluate.rs and the kind generators call tessellate(); everything else reads ModelGeometry::curve(key) (drafting-trim-split-04 contract).
acceptance_criteria:
- n via segment_count(r, TAU, defaults): r = 0.5 m gives 36, r = 1 m 50, r = 6 m 122, r = 10 m 158; with max angle 5 degrees r = 0.5 m gives 72; a property test over radii 0.05-100 m and random sub-arcs asserts every segment's chordal deviation <= chord_deviation + 1e-12 and angle <= max_angle_deg + 1e-12.
- Coincidence: for an arc from 0 to 90 degrees, its sub-arc from 30 to 60 degrees and its reverse, every interior station of the sub-arc is bit-identical to a station of the full arc and the reverse yields the reversed list; a station 1e-5 m from an end is dropped in both, deterministically.
- A slab whose outline is a 2 x 1 rectangle with a semicircular end: closed body (check_closed), volume within the chord-loss bound of the exact value, the curved strip shares vertices, caps share none with the sides (an IFX-038 helper test), and feature_edges returns no vertical line at the tangent joints but one at a non-tangent arc/line joint; the box test mesh.rs:333-336 (12 feature edges) is unchanged.
- Curve-id test: the points of ModelGeometry::curve(key) for the slab's arc edge equal the corresponding body vertices and plan-cut vertices bit for bit; after SetSettings with chord deviation 0.001 the slab is re-evaluated and unrelated straight elements are not (dirty-set assertion).
- drafting-trim-split's tessellation tests are updated and green; drafting.ifcx is re-blessed with a reviewed diff; conformance/run.sh is green.
- Satisfies the 'curved geometry shall be tessellated' and defaults clauses of IFX-034 for slabs and the 'tessellated identically' clause of SLB-004 for the tessellator.
notes:
SRS: IFX-034 SLB-004
Appendix D.1: curve tessellation 2 mm chord deviation, at most 10 degrees per segment, hence at least 36 segments per circle.
IFX-038 governs vertex sharing; the reference viewer uses 16-bit indices (65,535 points per mesh).
Decision proposed here: n is computed per circle from its radius, so concentric faces of a thick wall may have different segment counts; caps are triangulated by CDT, so no radial alignment is needed. This changes the station rule of drafting-trim-split-02 deliberately.

title: Add arc, tangent and circle wall input with arc snapping
description:
WHY: WAL-002 (M): arc walls by centre, radius and sweep; by three points; by tangent continuation of the previous segment; a full circle entered in one operation is one closed wall. INP-001 requires every point to pass through the shared point-input service with previews and prompts; WAL-007 cycling of the reference-line location while drawing applies to arc walls. WAL-001 (M, done) has the straight Single, Chain, Rectangle and RotatedRectangle modes (views/tools.rs:41-64 today, crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/wall.rs after point-input-snapping-01), which must keep working. point-input-snapping left 'producers of arcs' to this epic: its SnapSource understands circles and arcs (point-input-snapping-03), drafting-trim-split-04 added circle targets with an angular range in crates/archicraft-app/src/input/targets.rs, and point-input-snapping-09 tests tangent and centre-line guides 'against synthetic circles until ... arc walls (curved-geometry) exist'.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/wall.rs: new WallMode::ArcCentre (centre, then start point fixing the radius, then end point fixing the sweep, direction from the cursor side), WallMode::ArcThreePoints (start, end, point on the arc) and WallMode::Circle (centre, then radius point: one Command::AddElements with Project::new_circle_wall), plus a key in the existing Chain mode that toggles the next segment between straight and tangent arc (tangent to the previous segment at its end). StepSpecs with prompts and typed fields (radius, sweep angle, arc length), previews of the tessellated reference curve and faces (task 03), the Esc ladder and Backspace of point-input-snapping. Chains commit joined walls (contact detected by task 21). Snapping: a SnapSource for PlanElement.curves (task 04) in input/targets.rs reusing the existing circle targets with angular range (nearest point on the true arc, centre, end points, midpoint, tangent points, intersections with lines and arcs); activate point-input-snapping-09's tangent and centre-line inference guides on arc walls; extend the Snap result with `source: Option<CurveKey>` so slab input (08) can adopt exact circles. Mode buttons in the properties strip (tool_modes, crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:745). Out of scope: editing existing arc walls (11), slab arcs (08), 3D input of arcs (3d-input-navigation).
design: Implement the modes as ToolState steps on the InputConsumer API (point-input-snapping-01), reusing the arc constructors of curve.rs and, where drafting-trim-split-06 built them, the 2D arc tool's step specs, so drafting arcs and arc walls behave identically (NFR-USE-002). Typed values: when the user types the radius or the sweep, construct the Arc from those numbers directly; deriving them back from a constructed end point loses bits and breaks 'the exact arc shall be stored'. Direction of an ArcCentre sweep: the side of the cursor relative to the centre-start line, with a modifier for the major arc. Circle mode starts the circle at the radius point (start_angle = atan2 of it) and sweeps +2 pi, so the exterior face is outside with the default exterior-face reference line. Tangent continuation from an arc segment uses the arc's end tangent. Snap index: arc targets come from the exact CurveSource list, never from tessellated plan segments; nearest-on-arc is the projection of the cursor through the centre, clamped to the sweep. Do not add a second arc snap implementation beside input/targets.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- State-machine tests without egui: ArcCentre with centre (0,0), typed radius 5 and typed sweep 90 creates one wall whose stored radius is exactly 5.0 and sweep exactly pi/2 (typed values are stored, not cursor-derived points); ArcThreePoints through three exact points reproduces their circumcircle within 1e-12; Chain line, tangent arc, line creates three walls joined end to end with tangency within 1e-12; Circle mode creates exactly one element whose axis is closed.
- Esc cancels one step and Backspace one point in each arc mode; the reference-line key cycles Outside/Center/Inside and the preview shows the faces at the right radii.
- Snapping: a cursor near an arc wall face snaps to a point whose distance to the centre equals the face radius within 1e-12; the centre snap exists; a tangent point from the previous point to an arc wall face is offered; the intersection of an arc reference line and a straight reference line is offered; Snap.source names the wall's CurveKey.
- The existing Single, Chain, Rectangle and RotatedRectangle wall tool tests pass unchanged (WAL-001 regression).
- kittest: the Wall tool shows 'Arc (centre)', 'Arc (3 points)' and 'Circle' mode buttons; two clicks in Circle mode add one wall to the document and one element to the 3D scene; saving the document succeeds (task 06 codec).
- Satisfies the three creation methods and the one-operation full circle of WAL-002.
notes:
SRS: WAL-002
Appendix D.1 snapping: radius 8 px, reference dwell 1.0 s, angle increment 45 degrees; D.8 lists the wall tool shortcut (no new shortcut needed).
Open question: Archicad's three-point arc takes start, end, then a point on the arc; the order is a UI decision recorded in the tool prompt.

title: Trim joined roofs to their common ridge or valley line
description:
WHY: ROF-010 (S): two roofs are joinable so that both are trimmed associatively to their line of intersection (ridge or valley), for example a dormer roof meeting the main roof. The epic acceptance requires a dormer roof joined to the main roof along the valley that follows a pitch change. The gap analysis rates ROF-010 missing. The roofs epic already clips the planes of one multi-plane roof against their neighbours (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/body.rs); a join applies the same joint rule across two roofs.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/join.rs evaluates every RoofJoin of task 05 per plane pair (P of roof A, Q of roof B) with overlapping plan regions: L is the intersection line of the top surfaces and S its part inside both regions; a plane is split when S runs from boundary to boundary of its region. Both split: both planes are clipped by the joint plane through the top- and bottom-surface intersection lines, each keeping the side with its own pivot (eaves) line. One split: that plane is cut by the other plane's facing surface and the other stays whole (the main roof under a dormer keeps its body; the hole belongs to the dormer opening). None split: unchanged; a join without any split reports 'roofs do not intersect'. The stage runs in Stage::Junction of solid-kernel-ops-05, before Stage::Openings, so roof openings and roof windows (roofs-11, roofs-12) cut the joined planes, with dirty propagation in both directions through dependents_of of the RoofJoin relation (task 05). Out of scope: UI (10), dormer walls and openings, shells.
design: Per plane the roofs epic provides the top and bottom plane equations, the plan region polygon and the eave edge. L from the cross product of the two normals; S by clipping L against both regions with geo; a component of S splits a region when both its endpoints lie on the region boundary within JOIN_TOLERANCE. Kept side: the side of L that contains the eave midpoint in plan; if the eave straddles L keep the larger part and report. Joint plane: the plane through the parallel top and bottom intersection lines (the bisector for equal thicknesses), shared with roof/body.rs by extracting a `joint_plane(p, q)` helper there. Facing surface: top when a sample point on the kept side near S lies above the other plane's top surface, else bottom. Rebuild a clipped plane with plane_body of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/body.rs (roofs-02) from the clipped region and the joint plane as the side plane of the new edge, which is exact and needs no Boolean; SolidKernel::split of solid-kernel-ops-02 is the fallback for a region the builder rejects. Each roof uses the other's unjoined planes, so mutual joins cannot loop and results do not depend on order; process pairs in (roof id, plane index) order. Pitfalls: nearly parallel planes (|n_p x n_q| < 1e-9) form no joint; mansard break levels produce extra plane pairs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two single-plane roofs facing each other with overlapping outlines are both trimmed at the ridge at the analytic height (0.1 mm); the bodies are interior-disjoint and touch on the joint plane; JoinRoofs(A, B) and JoinRoofs(B, A) give identical meshes.
- Two gable roofs forming an L: the valley line equals the valley of the ROF-003 L-shaped fixture with the same pitches within 0.1 mm, and the wing planes end on the main roof.
- A gable dormer roof joined to the main roof ends on the main roof's top surface along both analytic valley lines while the main roof is unchanged; one UpdateElements on the main roof pitch moves both valleys in the same revision and undo restores bit for bit.
- A shed dormer flatter than the main roof ends on it along a horizontal valley.
- Roofs that do not intersect: one problem on the join and unchanged bodies; UnjoinRoofs restores the unjoined planes exactly.
- All results are closed; the Plane_<k> children of IfcRoof (IfcSlab parts of roofs-06) carry the joined bodies; the incremental-versus-full property test is extended with joins; trimming volumes of task 06 are unaffected.
notes: SRS: ROF-010. The split rule is ArchiCraft's interpretation of 'both are trimmed to their line of intersection'; document it in docs/trims.md and validate it in early user tests together with O-9.

title: Build trimming volume solids for roofs and slabs
description:
WHY: SOL-032 (S): each roof defines its trimming volume - downward with the footprint from the roof outline or from the pivot line, upward, or finite - and the volumes are displayable on demand. SOL-031 (M): trimming an inclined element cuts only where the element passes through the roof surface, never where it leaves the roof's plan footprint, which needs a volume whose side faces never touch the element. SOL-030 names roofs and slabs as tools. These solids are the operators of the trim stage (07) and the display meshes of task 10.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/trim/volume.rs: `trimming_volume(project, tool, extent) -> Result<TriMesh>` builds one closed mesh directly, without a Boolean union: the roof's top-surface facets over the footprint (Downward, Finite) or its underside facets (Upward), vertical faces along the footprint boundary and a flat cap at z_far or at the Finite bottom; the footprint is the roof outline (the single-plane outline, or the eaves outline formed by the plane regions of a multi-plane roof), the pivot footprint (the pivot polygon, or for a single-plane roof the outline part on the uphill side of the pivot line) or the custom polygon, partitioned by the per-plane regions of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/regions.rs (roofs-05) and lifted onto the offset surfaces of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/plane.rs (roofs-02); slabs give the volume under their top surface, sloped slabs included. `surface_only_volume(project, tool, target_bounds)` builds the same with the footprint offset beyond the target's plan bounds and every edge's eave lowered by offset x tan(pitch), so the planes inside are unchanged; single-plane roofs extend their plane; multi-plane roofs rerun weighted_skeleton of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/skeleton.rs (roofs-03) on the offset pivot polygon. Volumes are cached per tool revision and extent. Out of scope: applying them (07), display (10), shells.
design: Top facets: triangulate each plane region of the footprint (triangulate.rs) and lift the vertices onto the plane's top surface; with layer structures measured perpendicular to the plane (ROF-007) the vertical offset of the top surface is thickness / cos(pitch). Compute every vertex shared by two regions (hip, valley, ridge points) once from the skeleton nodes so neighbouring facets are bit-identical. Side faces: one vertical strip per footprint edge from z_far to the surface polyline above that edge; insert a vertex wherever a plane region boundary meets the edge, otherwise T-junctions break manifoldness. Footprint partition: geo BooleanOps of the footprint with each plane region. z_far: the extent AABB (target plus tools) minus or plus 1 m, never infinity, to keep coordinates small for the kernel. Surface-only offset d = distance from the footprint to the target's plan bounds + 0.5 m; lowering each eave by d x tan(pitch_i) keeps each edge plane identical, gable edges (vertical) are translated without lowering, and the skeleton of the roofs epic is rerun on the offset pivot polygon. Trimming volumes use the roof's own planes, never the joined ones (operators act with unmodified bodies, as SOL-024 requires for solid operations), so joins (08) cannot feed back into trims. Pitfall: an outward offset can make short edges at reflex vertices vanish; limit d and validate the offset polygon with validate_ring.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every volume for the roofs fixture corpus (gable rectangle, hip, L with valley, single plane, mansard with one break level) and for a flat and a sloped slab passes check_closed (closed, 2-manifold, outward-oriented).
- Volumes match analytic values within 1e-9 relative: for a single-plane roof over a rectangle the Downward volume is the integral of (top surface - z_far) over the footprint; Outline and PivotLine footprints differ exactly by the overhang band (multi-plane) or by the downhill part of the outline (single-plane); Upward lies above the underside; Finite lies between the top surface and its bottom.
- The surface-only volume coincides with the standard volume inside the original footprint (vertex distance below MODEL_TOLERANCE), its side faces lie outside the target bounds, and on a hip roof the extended hip lines continue the original hips.
- An offset footprint that fails validation (an edge collapsing at a reflex vertex) falls back to the standard volume with a reported problem; no panic and no open mesh.
- Two evaluations give bit-identical meshes; trimming volumes ignore roof joins (they come from the roof's own planes).
notes: SRS: SOL-032 SOL-031 SOL-030. Appendix D.2 roof defaults: pitch 35 degrees, 0.30 m thick, eaves overhang 0.50 m.

title: Add fixture F8 and the coincidence and seam regression tests
description:
WHY: Appendix D.7 F8: 'Curved wall with a slab traced from its reference line, then from its core face: zero gaps' (KB 669891). SLB-004 (M): coincident curves tessellated identically for display and export. WAL-002 and D-10: a full circle has no seam in any view or in the export. The epic acceptance compares vertex lists bit for bit in plan and export and demands the circle check in plan, 3D and the viewer; NFR-MNT-005 needs these as permanent regression cases, and junction-engine-12 registered F8 as a pending row owned by this epic.

WHAT: Add `fixtures::f8_curved_wall_slab()` to crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (the D7 table of regression-and-status-02) and its assertions to the registry test crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs: an F2-structured arc wall (centre (0,0), reference radius 6 m, sweep 120 degrees) closed by two straight F2 walls to a sector, slab A traced from the reference-line region and slab B from the core-face region, both through the headless tracing API of task 08. Add crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curved.rs: plan (slab B's arc vertices equal the core-face boundary vertices of the wall's plan cut bit for bit; symmetric difference of slab B and the region enclosed by the core faces has zero area), 3D (slab mesh vertices along the arc equal the wall skin mesh vertices), export (the written IFCX point strings agree for the coincident vertices), a D-10 circle case (one polygon with one hole in plan, no vertical feature edge, shared vertex indices at the start angle) and a settings case (chord 5 mm, angle 5 degrees keeps all of the above). Extend conformance/check.ts so the headless reference-viewer run asserts, for the circle wall of curved-walls.ifcx, one composed IfcWall with closed meshes and no duplicated seam vertices. Flip F8 and add the circle case as covered rows of the NFR-MNT-005 catalogue in docs/junctions.md. regression-and-status (increment 1) is not a declared prerequisite of this epic: if its registry or headless viewer step is missing, keep F8 in curved.rs, keep the viewer assertion in the Node-based check.ts composition run, and file a bead to move them. Section and elevation views do not exist yet (sections-elevations-dims, increment 3): file a bead to add the circle wall to their seam checks. Out of scope: performance of large curved models (perf epics).
design: Compare bits, not tolerances, for coincident vertices: the purpose is to prove that one tessellator and one face_curve() feed all producers; a tolerance would hide a second code path. Compute 'zero gap' as an area test in addition (it catches topological gaps the vertex test cannot). The export comparison parses the written JSON and compares the coordinate strings after round_coordinate (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/json.rs:153), since IFX-007 rounding of identical f64 inputs is deterministic. In check.ts, detect seam duplicates as two points with identical coordinates and different indices referenced by adjacent triangles of the curved face; the reference viewer averages normals over shared indices, so duplicates are exactly what would shade as a seam. Fixture coordinates are proposals; F2 is the 680 mm structure of D.7 with a 300 mm concrete core.
acceptance_criteria:
- F8 is listed by the fixture registry under its D.7 id and builds from seeded ids.
- curved.rs passes: slab A and slab B each show zero gap to the wall (symmetric difference area < 1e-12 m^2 against the respective boundary), and the arc vertices of each slab are bit-identical to the corresponding wall vertices in the plan cut and in the 3D meshes.
- The exported curved-walls.ifcx (re-blessed with F8 added to the sample) has identical coordinate strings for every coincident vertex; conformance/run.sh green.
- The circle case: one IfcWall node, closed meshes, no seam vertex pair, plan polygon with one hole and no radial segment, no vertical feature edge; the viewer assertion in conformance/check.ts passes in CI.
- Changing the project tessellation to 5 mm / 5 degrees and re-evaluating keeps all assertions true.
- docs/junctions.md lists F8 and the circle case as covered rows; the catalogue test passes; the follow-up beads for sections/elevations (and for the registry, if it was missing) are filed.
- Satisfies SLB-004 (display and export) and the plan/3D/viewer no-seam clauses of WAL-002 and D-10.
notes:
SRS: SLB-004 WAL-002
Appendix D.7 F8 (KB 669891) and F2; D.1 tessellation defaults.
The viewer run and fixture registry come from regression-and-status (increment 1).

title: Resolve junction geometry between arc and straight walls
description:
WHY: WAL-020 (M): bodies and all skins trimmed or extended at L, T and X junctions; WAL-023 skins by material priority; WAL-026 order independence; NFR-MNT-005 requires regression tests for all junction cases, and junction-engine-12 left the arc rows of docs/junctions.md as pending(curved-geometry). Gap row WAL-002 names 'arc junctions'. Epic risk: 'Arc junction maths with skins fall back to square ends plus a reported problem rather than invalid geometry.'

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs (junction-engine-04..07) consumes the arc contact graph of task 21: an arc end is extended along its end tangent by the node reach for the overlap computation; corner points where a face arc meets another face (line or arc) are computed analytically (curve.rs intersect) and inserted into both walls' tessellated rings so the shared corner is the same DVec2 in both; the existing per-node geo Boolean and priority resolution (junction-engine-05/06) then runs on the tessellated rings, the arc wall's result is clipped back to its own sector plus its assigned overlap, and arc segments that survive keep their CurveKey. A full circle is resolved as a through wall. Unresolvable nodes fall back to radial square ends plus the junction-engine problem message. Plan merging by material and priority (junction-engine-07) works unchanged on the resulting rings. Add the arc rows to crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs and resolve the pending(curved-geometry) junction entries of docs/junctions.md (F8 itself is activated by task 09). Out of scope: contact detection (21), polygonal walls (22), inclined walls (23), openings at arc-wall ends (task 12's tests).
design: Analytic intersections: line-circle by projecting the centre on the line; circle-circle by the radical line; choose the root nearest to the node. Corner insertion: compute every corner once per node and push the same DVec2 into both rings (the junction-engine rule for shared corners); the tessellation stations of an arc trimmed at a corner are then the circle grid inside the remaining interval plus the corner, which keeps task 03's coincidence property for traced slabs. The tangent extension of an arc end is a straight strip of the wall's thickness; after Boolean resolution, clip the arc wall's result back to its own sector plus the assigned overlap, otherwise the extension leaks. Priority cutting (junction-engine-05/06) and the 3+-wall rule work unchanged on rings. The acute-angle limit of the straight case (spike beyond 10x thickness) applies to the tangent-at-corner angle. Golden ring files store tessellated points, so they depend on the default Tessellation; pin the settings in the suite's builder.
acceptance_criteria:
- The table-driven suite gains at least ten arc rows: arc/straight L for each reference-line location, straight branch T onto an arc, arc branch T onto a straight wall, straight T onto a full circle, arc/arc L, tangent chain line-arc-line, arc/line X, F2-structured arc at an L with equal priorities and with the F7 priorities swapped, an acute arc/line fallback; every row passes closedness, volume conservation, disjoint skin interiors, golden rings and permutation independence.
- The mitre corner of an arc/straight L equals the analytic line-circle intersection within 1e-9 and is bit-identical in both walls' rings.
- A straight wall ending on a full circle stops at the circle's near face; the trimmed end lies on the true arc within 1e-9 and the circle stays one closed body.
- A tangent continuation gives flush ends without a spike, and the joint is smooth in plan (no extra corner beyond the shared end vertex).
- The fallback row reports exactly one problem per affected wall and produces radial square ends; no mesh fails check_closed.
- Two concrete arc walls at an L show one plan cut region without a seam line (junction-engine-07 merge).
- docs/junctions.md has no remaining pending(curved-geometry) junction entry other than F8; the catalogue test passes.
- Satisfies the arc-to-straight L and T clause of the epic acceptance and the geometric part of WAL-020, WAL-023 and WAL-026 for arc walls.
notes:
SRS: WAL-002
Covers WAL-020, WAL-023, WAL-026 and NFR-MNT-005 geometry for arc walls (owned by junction-engine for straight walls).
Appendix D.4 priorities and D.7 F2/F7 are reused; D.1 model tolerance 0.01 mm.

title: Write and read arc walls and arc slab edges in IFCX
description:
WHY: D-1 makes IFCX the native format, so arc walls and arc outline edges must round-trip with their exact parameters (WAL-002 'the exact arc shall be stored'; NFR-ACC-002 bit-for-bit parameters via serde_json float_roundtrip). IFX-034: curved geometry is written tessellated; IFX-035 (partial): wall reference lines as usd::usdgeom::basiscurves in an Axis child (writer.rs:229-235, 382-389); SLB-004: coincident curves tessellated identically for export; D-10: no seam in IFCX. Today the wall schema has start/end only (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs:232-244) and slabs outline/holes as point arrays (schema.rs:246-255), mapped directly by writer.rs:192-217 and reader.rs:660-712 in the increment-0 code; after element-kind-framework these live in the wall and slab KindCodecs (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/wall.rs, kinds/slab.rs) with the outline helper of alpha/kinds/common.rs (edit-reshape-palette-10).

WHAT: schema.rs: optional `arc` object in archicraft::wall { centre, radius, startAngle, sweep } (the encoding of drafting-trim-split-05's archicraft::arc); optional `outlineEdges` and `holeEdges` arrays aligned with the vertex order (edge i starts at vertex i), each entry {type: 'straight'} or {type: 'arc', centre, radius, startAngle, sweep} (the edge encoding of drafting-trim-split-05's archicraft::polyline), written through the alpha/kinds/common.rs outline helper only when a ring has an arc, so slabs, 2D fills (archicraft::fill of drafting-trim-split-09) and later polygonal walls (13) share it; one-vertex rings allowed when their edge is an arc. FORMAT_VERSION (schema.rs:15) is raised through MIGRATIONS in alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework-12), reusing a bump of the same release if one already happened, because an older reader would silently draw straight walls. Wall codec: writes `arc` plus the derived start and end; the Axis child carries ElementGeometry.axis of task 04 (closed curves repeat the first point); bodies are already tessellated. Reader: `arc` wins over start/end (a mismatch is a warning); edge arrays restored; missing or invalid entries fall back leniently through report.or. Samples: add `curved_walls()` to crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs (an arc wall joined L and T to straight walls, a full circle wall, a slab with an arc edge built from face_curve()), register it in crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and in samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs, bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/curved-walls.ifcx; extend drafting_sample() with a fill that has an arc edge and re-bless drafting.ifcx. Out of scope: polygonal and inclined wall attributes (13, 15), insert occurrences in arc walls (12).
design: Parameters at full precision with json! (float_roundtrip is enabled per technology-choices), coordinates in meshes and curves through round_coordinate (json.rs:153, used by curve_attribute). Write start/end even for arc walls: generic consumers and older tooling see a sensible chord, and the reader uses them only as a consistency check. The Axis polyline must come from the evaluated geometry, not from a second tessellation in the writer, so plan, 3D and export share one source (drafting-trim-split-05 rule: the writer never calls tessellate()). Reusing drafting's edge encoding keeps one JSON shape for every arc in the file and one reader function. Declare new enumerations from model ALL arrays (schema.rs pattern). Pitfalls: one-vertex rings must pass the reader's ring validation, so run validate_element on read as today; build the sample through commands (samples.rs execute helper, samples.rs:24) so it also exercises undo journal serialisation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round trip: load(write(p)) equals p for curved_walls(), with every arc parameter bit-identical (f64::to_bits) and the full circle still closed; the DraftFill with an arc edge in drafting_sample() round-trips likewise.
- Golden curved-walls.ifcx blessed with ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 and conformance/run.sh green on all golden files; the circle wall is one IfcWall node whose Axis basiscurves is closed and whose Body/Skin meshes are closed (IFX-032).
- In the written file, the points of the slab mesh along the arc edge are identical strings to the corresponding wall face points (IFX-007 rounding applied to identical inputs), and the Axis points equal ModelGeometry's reference-line curve rounded to 10^-6.
- A file without `arc` reads as a straight wall and a file without edge arrays as straight-edged outlines (backward compatibility); a file of the previous FORMAT_VERSION loads through the migration table; a file declaring a newer version is flagged newer_format; an `arc` that disagrees with the start/end keys loads with a warning.
- The existing goldens two-storey-shell.ifcx and walls-and-slab.ifcx change only in the declared format version, if at all.
- Satisfies the export clauses of WAL-002 (exact arc, one closed node), IFX-034 (tessellated output) and SLB-004 (identical tessellation in export).
notes:
SRS: WAL-002 IFX-034 SLB-004
IFX-035 (Axis basiscurves) and IFX-007 (10^-6 m plain decimals) govern the output; NFR-ACC-002 governs parameters.
Coordinate the FORMAT_VERSION bump with tasks 13 and 15 so the release raises it once.

title: Add the Trim tool with keep-side preview and Untrim
description:
WHY: SOL-030 (M) ends with the interaction: the user picks the part to keep (or, with a modifier, the part to remove), and a preview highlights the part that will remain. Decision D-7 requires an explicit command for every operation, with modifier gestures only as accelerators. ELM-014: auxiliary roofs still act as trim tools, so they must be pickable as tools. What exists after the increment-1 epics and is reused: the InputConsumer step/preview API (crates/archicraft-app/src/input/consumer.rs) and the tools module crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/ (point-input-snapping), point input and element tools in 3D views (3d-input-navigation-08), the BVH PickIndex (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/pick.rs, 3d-input-navigation-06) and the Camera3dSurface ray (3d-input-navigation-07), transient PreviewMesh overlays drawn by Renderer3d::draw_overlay in 3D and by views/plan.rs (host-openings-10), id-buffer hover in 3D (selection-transforms-06, which also removes the dead HOVER_TINT path), the CommandRegistry in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs (commands-and-l10n-03), the auxiliary pick toggle and modifier (solid-kernel-ops-11) and the relation inspector in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs (solid-kernel-ops-12). No trim command exists and UI coverage is thin (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs has four tests today).

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/trim.rs: a TrimTool InputConsumer on the current selection (kinds with trim_target), usable in plan and 3D views. Step 1 picks the tools (kinds with trim_tool; auxiliary ones with the pick toggle or modifier of solid-kernel-ops-11), Enter confirms, and the tool computes both candidate results once through trim::apply_trims (07) with TrimSide::Inside and Outside.
