Step 2 finds the piece under the cursor (3D: TriMesh::ray_hit of the candidate meshes along the Camera3dSurface ray; plan: point-in-polygon on each candidate's slice at the cut plane) and previews the part that will remain tinted and the part that will go ghosted, as PreviewMeshes with new PreviewStyle::{TrimKeep, TrimRemove} variants (host-openings-10); a click issues TrimElements with the side of the clicked piece, or of the other piece in Remove mode, which is a prompt-bar toggle with the modifier as accelerator (D-7); in plan, where a pick cannot tell vertical parts apart, the default is Inside with a 'Swap side' button. Register the commands 'Trim to Roof/Slab' and 'Untrim' in the CommandRegistry (Design menu) with strings in locales/en/commands.ftl and prompts in locales/en/tools.ftl; Untrim issues UntrimElements for all or picked tools; extend the relation inspector of solid-kernel-ops-12 with 'Trimmed by' and 'Trims' lists (click to select, remove). Out of scope: trimming-volume properties and display, roof joins (10).
design: Candidates: apply_trims with TrimSide::Inside and Outside on the selected targets. Kernel calls can exceed one frame: compute the candidates when the tool set is confirmed, show progress in the status bar and drop the result on Escape. Preview meshes are transient (draw_overlay uploads a small buffer per frame after the scene, depth test on, depth writes off), so the tool needs no SceneKey change and no scene rebuild; hovering a candidate piece is a CPU ray test on two meshes per target, run on pointer move only. Tool picks in 3D go through PickIndex::ray with a filter on trim_tool kinds; in plan through PlanDrawing::pick. Locked or invalid targets surface through Workspace::execute messages. Follow the 'Add a drawing tool' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md as reshaped by point-input-snapping (InputConsumer, StepSpec, Preview) and commands-and-l10n-12 (prompts generated from the keys each step handles).
acceptance_criteria:
- State-machine unit tests without egui: select targets, Trim, pick a roof, pick a piece gives TrimElements with Inside or Outside according to the piece; Remove mode inverts; Escape cancels without a command; picking a door as tool is refused with a prompt message; an auxiliary roof is pickable as tool only with the pick toggle or modifier.
- Preview (SOL-030 'a preview highlights the part that will remain'): in Keep mode the hovered piece is emitted as TrimKeep and the other as TrimRemove; in Remove mode the hovered piece is TrimRemove and the other, which will remain, TrimKeep; the plan preview outlines the remaining part.
- The two candidate results are computed once per tool set (call counter in a test) and equal the evaluated result for the chosen side bit for bit after the command; moving the cursor never rebuilds or uploads the scene (upload counter of selection-transforms-06 constant).
- kittest: Design > Trim to Roof/Slab with a selected wall and a roof, simulated picks, then 'Undo Trim' in the Edit menu restores the wall; Untrim from the menu removes the relation; the inspector lists the roof under 'Trimmed by' for the selected wall.
- shortcuts_are_unique passes and the literal-string lint of commands-and-l10n is clean.
notes: SRS: SOL-030. Context: D-7; ELM-014 (auxiliary tools pickable); relation inspector of solid-kernel-ops-12 (SOL-023). The 3D hover technical-debt item is removed by selection-transforms-06, not by this task.

title: Generate arc and full-circle wall bodies, skins and plan lines
description:
WHY: WAL-002 (M) requires the exact arc and 'no seam artefact in any view or in the export' for a full circle; D-10 makes the circle one closed element. WAL-003 (reference-line locations, faces) and layer-structures' skins (one body per skin, Skin_n parts, F2) must work on arcs. Today the footprint is built from start and end (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:137-176 in the increment-0 code); after the prerequisites it is junction-engine-03's WallOutline (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs) per SkinBand (layer-structures-04), resolved per node into `ResolvedWall { outline: MultiPolygon<f64> }` (junction.rs, junction-engine-04) and cut by wall_cut.rs (host-openings-05) in the wall GeometryKind (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs). PlanElement.reference_line is a single segment (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:23-33).

WHAT: archicraft-geometry: WallInput carries the wall's axis Segment (task 02). WallOutline gains an arc form: per SkinBand an annular sector (outer arc, radial end edge, inner arc reversed, radial end edge) with arc points from the circle-anchored tessellator of task 03; a full circle yields an annulus (outer ring CCW, hole CW), which ResolvedWall's MultiPolygon already carries. Extrude per skin with extrude_layers (host-openings-04) using task 03's smooth-run option (curved faces smooth, radial end faces and caps hard). Register every face circle (reference line, exterior and interior face, core faces, skin boundaries, all from face_curve()) in ElementGeometry.curves under a CurveKey with a fixed index per role (drafting-trim-split-04) and keep the exact circle beside it: `ElementGeometry.curve_sources: Vec<CurveSource { key: CurveKey, role: CurveRole, arc: Arc }>` with CurveRole::{ReferenceLine, ExteriorFace, InteriorFace, CoreExterior, CoreInterior, SkinBoundary(u16), OutlineEdge { ring, edge }}; slab arc edges (task 03) register with OutlineEdge. (The name avoids tessellate.rs's `CurveRef<'a>`.) ElementGeometry.axis becomes the tessellated reference curve (closed curves repeat the first point). Plan: PlanElement.reference_line becomes a polyline with a closed flag, drawn by crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs (or views/plan_gpu.rs if plan-renderer has landed) with the WAL-007 direction marker; PlanElement gains `curves: Vec<CurveSource>` for walls and slabs, which snapping (07, 08) and tracing (08) consume; layer-structures' PlanElement.core_faces carries the tessellated core-face chords of arc walls, the exact circles being in curves. Arc walls bypass wall_cut.rs: a hosted opening or insert on an arc wall is reported as 'Openings in arc walls are not supported yet.' until task 12. Verify slice.rs loops_to_polygons (slice.rs:151) returns the annulus as one polygon with one hole. Out of scope: junctions (05; arc walls are square-ended until then), wall-plane holes (12), IFCX (06), tools (07), 3D shading (20).
design: Build the arc footprint in polar terms and convert once: stations from task 03 for each face circle (the two face circles have their own n), radial ends at the exact start and end angles. Holes: junction-engine resolves per node with geo Booleans, which already support polygons with holes, and extrude_layers takes MultiPolygon sections, so only WallOutline needs the annulus form. A closed wall participates in junctions only as a through wall (task 21). Provenance per curve, not per vertex: ElementGeometry.curve_sources holds the exact circles and ModelGeometry::curve(key) their points, so the plan slicer needs no tags; tracing (08) matches plan segments against these exact curves geometrically. The reference-line polyline comes from the same curve entry (display = export, SLB-004). Pitfalls: BodyPart.name uniqueness per element (writer.rs child_key) holds for Skin_n parts; the view-cache key (SceneKey) changes with the geometry revision only; wall_cut.rs assumes a straight span between split planes, which is why arc walls must not enter it before task 12.
acceptance_criteria:
- An arc wall r = 5 m, sweep 90 degrees, thickness 0.3 m, reference line Outside: closed body; plan area of the footprint equals (pi/4)(5^2 - 4.7^2) = 2.2855 m^2 minus the chord loss (bound: arc length x 2 mm); every footprint point on a face is bit-identical to ModelGeometry::curve(key) of that face's CurveKey.
- A full circle r = 3 m, thickness 0.25 m: one body per skin, closed and 2-manifold; no two vertices with distinct indices coincide on the curved faces (no seam column); the plan cut at 1.10 m above the storey is one polygon with one hole and no radial segment; feature_edges has no vertical edge; the reference-line polyline is closed.
- An F2-structured arc wall: six concentric skin bodies, each closed; the boundary arc between two adjacent skins is bit-identical in both skins; plan cut regions per skin match the skin bands.
- PlanElement.curves of an arc wall lists the reference line, both faces and both core faces with radii equal to face_curve() bits; a slab with an arc edge lists it with CurveRole::OutlineEdge.
- An opening hosted by an arc wall yields the problem message and leaves the wall body uncut and closed.
- Straight walls produce identical footprints and meshes to before (existing tests, golden files unchanged byte for byte).
- Satisfies the body, plan and mesh no-seam clauses of WAL-002 and D-10 for unjoined arc walls.
notes:
SRS: WAL-002
D-10 (one closed element, no seams in plan, 3D or IFCX).
Appendix D.7 F2 (680 mm layered wall) is reused as an arc-wall structure in the tests.

title: Enable exact arc edges in Outline with analytic queries and validation
description:
WHY: SLB-001 (M): 'Slabs shall be created from a closed outline of straight and arc edges.' SLB-004 (M): a slab edge traced from or snapped to a curved wall 'shall coincide with it exactly', which is only possible if an arc edge stores the exact circle it was copied from. EDT-014 (S, task 10) stores fillets as arc edges, and DraftFill (drafting-trim-split-09) and polygonal walls (task 13) share the same Outline. SLB-001 is partial. Exists: edit-reshape-palette-01's Outline<E>/Ring<E>/Vertex<E>/Edge<E> in crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/ (straight edges, per-edge EdgeData), the repair pipeline of edit-reshape-palette-02, and drafting-trim-split-01's shared `Curve { Straight, Arc(Arc) }` of crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs re-exported as the outline edge shape, with slab and fill validation still rejecting arcs ('Arc edges arrive with curved geometry'). Missing (gap row SLB-001): 'No arc edges (outline is Vec<DVec2>; validate_ring, extrude, triangulate, SnapTargets, IFCX schema outline=array(point2) all assume polylines).'

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/ allow `Curve::Arc(Arc)` edges, Arc being the curve.rs type (centre, radius, start_angle, sweep): edge i runs from vertex i to vertex i+1 along the arc, whose derived start() and end() lie within MODEL_TOLERANCE of those vertices, and joints always use the vertex, never the derived point. A ring with exactly one vertex and one arc edge of |sweep| = 2 pi is a full circle. If the edge shape is still edit-reshape-palette-01's `#[non_exhaustive] EdgeShape`, add `EdgeShape::Arc(Arc)` holding the same curve.rs type: there is no second arc type. Make every Ring query arc-aware analytically: signed area with circular-segment terms, area with holes, contains, bounding box (the exact Segment bbox of curve.rs), perimeter, segments() yielding curve.rs Segments, point and tangent at a parameter, nearest point. Extend the validation and repair pipeline (validate.rs, edit-reshape-palette-02, Appendix D.1 thresholds) to arcs: arc ends on their vertices, radius and arc length at least MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, |sweep| at least MIN_CORNER_ANGLE_DEG, self-intersection of line/arc and arc/arc pairs through curve.rs intersect(), holes with arcs inside the outline. Remove the 'Arc edges arrive with curved geometry' rejection for slabs and DraftFill. Whole-element transforms through the Kind transform hook of selection-transforms (translate, rotate, mirror with curve.rs Placement2: mirror negates the sweep). MoveNode (edit-reshape-palette-03) on a vertex next to an arc re-fits that arc through its moved end points with the same signed sweep. SetEdgeAngle (SLB-005, edit-reshape-palette-10) on an arc edge is rejected with 'Edge angles on curved edges are not supported yet.'. Out of scope: InsertNode, DeleteNode, offsets, CurveEdge and Straighten on arcs (task 18); union, difference and buffer with arcs (task 19); tessellation and bodies (03); IFCX (06); UI (08, 11); fillet (10); wall axes (02).
design: Store the circle, not a bulge: with only end points plus a bulge, centre and radius are re-derived with rounding, so a slab edge traced from a wall face would not carry the wall face's circle bits and the shared tessellation (task 03) would produce different interior vertices. The curve.rs Arc keeps centre and radius exactly as copied; the end points are the ring's vertices (shared with the neighbouring edges), so the invariant is 'both end vertices lie on the arc within MODEL_TOLERANCE' (crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs of element-kind-framework-01; validate.rs:10 in the increment-0 code), checked on every edit. One-vertex rings are the only representation of a full circle: two semicircles would introduce a vertex that a coincident wall circle does not have (task 09). Analytic predicates: area = polygon area of the vertices + the sum of signed circular-segment areas (r^2/2)(phi - sin phi); containment by crossing count against chords plus the segment regions; bounding box from Segment::bbox. Self-intersection uses curve.rs intersect() with MODEL_TOLERANCE and the existing MIN_CORNER_ANGLE_DEG sliver rule. MoveNode re-fit: keep the signed sweep phi and put the centre on the perpendicular bisector of the new chord c at distance (c/2)/tan(phi/2); keeping the radius instead would fail when the chord grows beyond 2r. Pitfalls: plan_update_elements detects 'no change' by equality (command.rs:372-395), so Arc must derive PartialEq; EdgeData::split/merge of edit-reshape-palette-01 stays aligned because an arc is still one Edge; keep archicraft-model free of archicraft-geometry (NFR-MNT-002).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in outline/: a 2 x 1 rectangle whose short side is replaced by an outward semicircle of r = 0.5 has area 2 + pi/8 within 1e-12; a one-vertex full-circle ring of r = 3 has area 9 pi, perimeter 6 pi and a bounding box of exactly centre +/- 3; contains() is correct for points between an arc and its chord and inside a hole with arc edges.
- Validation: an arc whose end vertex lies 1 mm off the arc is rejected with a message; an arc crossing another edge is rejected as self-intersecting; an arc chord below the D.1 short-edge threshold is repaired and reported; a hole with arc edges inside the outline is accepted; a slab and a DraftFill with arc edges now validate and the old rejection message is gone from the workspace.
- MoveNode on a vertex between a line and an arc keeps the arc's signed sweep bit-identical (f64::to_bits) with both ends on the moved vertices; undo restores the outline bit for bit (crates/archicraft-model/tests/reshape.rs).
- Translate, rotate and mirror of a slab with an arc edge preserve its area within 1e-12; mirror negates the sweep; mirroring twice restores the outline within 1e-12.
- SetEdgeAngle on an arc edge returns 'Edge angles on curved edges are not supported yet.'; edit-reshape-palette-10's edge-angle tests on straight edges pass unchanged.
- A serde round trip of a command journal containing arc edges is bit-identical; all existing outline, reshape, slab and fill tests pass unchanged.
- Satisfies the straight-and-arc-edge data-model clause of SLB-001 and the exact-storage precondition of SLB-004.
notes:
SRS: SLB-001 SLB-004
Appendix D.1: model tolerance 0.01 mm; repair thresholds 0.1 mm edges and 0.1 degree slivers.
Decision proposed here: non-vertical slab edge angles (SLB-005) on arc edges would need conical faces; they are rejected and a follow-up bead is filed. MoveNode keeps the sweep of an adjacent arc (open question for the inspection checklist).

title: Verify exit criterion: Cross-kind priority cleanup and associative trims to roofs and slabs
description:
WHY: This closes the cleanup-and-trims epic and supplies the trim part of the increment-2 exit criterion of Appendix F ('AS-01 without railings and AS-02 pass'): the AS-01 gable walls trimmed to the roof and clean junctions between the structural members of AS-02. It confirms on a clean main build, not only task by task, that COL-006 (columns join walls, beams and slabs by priority), BEA-004 (beams join by axis contact L/T/X and priority), SLB-007 (priority cleanup in 3D, sections and plan cuts), SOL-030 (associative trims with keep-side preview), SOL-031 (inclined-element rule), SOL-032 (trimming volumes, displayable on demand) and ROF-010 (roof joins at ridge or valley) are met together.

WHAT: Run the full verification on the merged state of tasks 01-11: workspace tests, clippy and fmt, the conformance job on all golden files, the NFR-MNT-005 suite, the IFX-033 test and the agreement tests; map each clause of the epic acceptance to a named test; update docs/implementation-status.md (requirement rows, readiness per increment, technical debt) and close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new functionality; any defect found is fixed in the owning task or filed as a bead before closing.
design: Checklist: (1) cargo build, test, clippy and fmt exactly as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs them; (2) cargo run --locked -p archicraft-ifcx --example reference_models -- target/reference-models, then conformance/run.sh target/reference-models/*.ifcx crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx; (3) map the clauses to tests, including the ELM-014 trim clause (07): column in wall and slab band (02), beam to column face and beam L/T/X (03), order independence and plan/vertical/export agreement (02, 03, 07), AS-01 gable and pitch follow (07, 11), SOL-031 (07), trimming volumes and display (06, 10), dormer join (08, 11), suite rows (04, 11); record the mapping in the closing comment; (4) update the seven requirement rows and the IFX-033 and NFR-MNT-005 evidence in docs/implementation-status.md and the increment-2 readiness line; (5) bd close cleanup-and-trims with the summary and file follow-ups (beam join and auto-join commands, three-beam mitres, the equal-priority precedence check against KB 364093, the WAL-010, COL-004 and free-form-solid pending rows and their kind flags or inclined hooks if those epics have not set them, and the reference-models hand-off for the AS-01 and AS-02 automation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Cleanup tests: a concrete column inside a masonry wall cuts the wall skins.
- a steel beam meeting a concrete column is trimmed to its face.
- a slab of priority 900 cuts a wall of 800 at the slab band.
- beams at L/T/X axis contact with walls and columns clean up.
- results are order-independent and identical in the plan slice, in a vertical slice and in the exported mesh (IFX-033 extended).
- the AS-01 gable walls are trimmed to the roof and follow a pitch change in one revision.
- a wall inclined 15 degrees outward under a hip roof keeps its full base (SOL-031).
- trimming volumes (downward from outline or pivot line, upward, finite) are selectable and displayable on demand.
- a dormer roof is joined to the main roof along the valley and follows a pitch change.
- every case joins the NFR-MNT-005 suite.
- cargo test --workspace --locked, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green on the workspace.
- conformance/run.sh is green on the golden files, including crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/structural-cleanup.ifcx and trims-and-joins.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (COL-006, BEA-004, SLB-007, SOL-030, SOL-031, SOL-032, ROF-010) with status and evidence paths, the evidence of IFX-033, NFR-MNT-005 and the trim clause of ELM-014 is extended, and the increment-2 readiness line is updated.
- The epic cleanup-and-trims is closed in beads; follow-up work found on the way is filed as beads issues.
notes: SRS: COL-006 BEA-004 SLB-007 SOL-030 SOL-031 SOL-032 ROF-010. Appendix F increment 2 exit: 'AS-01 without railings and AS-02 pass' (the scenario automation itself belongs to reference-models).

title: Draw and trace slab outlines with arc edges and a circle mode
description:
WHY: SLB-001 (M): the slab outline of straight and arc edges 'is drawn (polygon, rectangle, rotated rectangle, circle) by snapping to existing wall faces, wall reference lines, wall core faces, 2D shapes or other elements' outlines, or, with contour detection (INP-018, S), traced from them in one pick'. SLB-004 (M): a slab edge traced from or snapped to a curved wall's reference line or face coincides with it exactly. SLB-001 is partial. Exists: SlabMode Polygon/Rectangle/RotatedRectangle (views/tools.rs:66-84 today, crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/slab.rs after point-input-snapping-01); snapping to cut faces and wall reference lines (input/targets.rs, point-input-snapping-02/03); core-face snapping (PlanElement.core_faces, layer-structures-04); 2D shapes as snap and contour sources (drafting-trim-split-04); contour detection in the slab tool (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/contour.rs of edit-reshape-palette-06, tool hook of edit-reshape-palette-12), whose graph edges carry `source` (set by drafting-trim-split-04 for drafting arcs only). Missing: arc segments in polygon input, a circle mode, exact adoption of snapped circles, and arc-preserving tracing of walls and slabs.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/slab.rs: SlabMode::Circle (centre, radius point: a one-vertex full-circle ring starting at the radius point) and, in Polygon mode, a key that switches the next segment between line, arc through a point and tangent arc. Curve adoption: when an arc segment's end points and through point snap to the same Snap.source (task 07), the arc edge copies that source's exact Arc (centre and radius bits) instead of recomputing them; this works for wall reference lines, wall faces, core faces, 2D arcs and circles and other elements' arc edges (all in PlanElement.curves or the drafting SnapSource). Contour detection: fill each graph edge's `source` for walls and slabs by matching it against PlanElement.curves (both ends on the exact circle within MODEL_TOLERANCE and sagitta within chord deviation plus tolerance); when a region or chain becomes an Outline, recover_arcs of task 19 turns maximal runs of one source into one arc with the source circle, with run ends snapped to the exact stations; add a ContourOptions flag for core faces next to reference_lines. Traced holes and the wall tool's contour detection use the same conversion, so walls traced along an arc chain become arc walls. Out of scope: fillet (10), polygonal walls (13), contour detection in 3D views.
design: Matching rather than threading provenance: the contour graph is built from unioned plan polygons (geo unary_union over i_overlay), which can move vertices by rounding and loses tags, so recover sources geometrically against the exact CurveSource list of task 04; end points are then snapped back to exact stations (wall ends, junction corners or the circle-anchored grid), which is what makes the vertex sets of slab edge and wall face identical (task 03, F8 in task 09). Full circles: a closed run covering a whole source circle becomes a one-vertex ring at the source curve's start point (for a circle wall, its start angle), never two semicircles, because the extra vertex would not exist on the wall face. Arc segments in polygon input reuse the arc constructors of curve.rs; tangent arcs start from the previous segment's direction. Keep slab and wall tools on one shared polygon-input helper (edit-reshape-palette-08 introduced it for reshape polygons), so union/difference polygons gain arcs for free. Pitfall: an arc run whose ends are not stations of the source (a partial overlap) must end exactly where the region boundary turns, which are intersection points computed analytically; document the limitation if a run ends at a tessellated chord point.
acceptance_criteria:
- State-machine tests: Circle mode with typed radius 2 creates a slab with one ring of one vertex and an arc edge of radius exactly 2.0; Polygon mode with one three-point arc segment and one tangent arc segment creates the expected arc edges (tangency within 1e-12).
- Snapping the three points of an arc segment onto an arc wall's exterior face, its reference line and its core face each produces an arc edge whose centre and radius equal the corresponding face_curve() bits; onto a 2D circle and onto another slab's arc edge, the arc edge copies that source's bits.
- Contour detection inside three straight walls and one arc wall gives a slab outline with exactly one arc edge (circle bits equal to the arc wall's interior face) and three straight edges; with the core-face option it follows the core face; with the reference-line option it follows the reference line; tracing the inner face of a full circle wall gives a one-vertex circle ring whose vertex is the wall's start station.
- Tracing a closed chain of 2D arcs and lines keeps the arcs; a traced hole with an arc edge subtracts exactly.
- The wall tool's contour detection along an arc slab edge creates an arc wall with the slab edge's circle.
- The existing Polygon, Rectangle and RotatedRectangle slab tests and edit-reshape-palette-12's contour tests pass unchanged.
- kittest: the Slab tool shows a 'Circle' mode button; two clicks create one slab.
- Satisfies SLB-001 (circle mode, arc edges, snapping to every listed source and tracing) and the snapped/traced coincidence clause of SLB-004.
notes:
SRS: SLB-001 SLB-004
INP-018 (contour detection, owned by edit-reshape-palette) gains its arc-preserving clause here.
Appendix D.2 slab default 0.20 m reinforced concrete, top at the storey elevation.

title: Add the trims-and-joins sample, golden file and suite rows
description:
WHY: AS-01 requires a gable roof with the gable walls trimmed to the roof and a file that passes IFX-006; AS-03 requires the roof and its dependants to follow changes with unchanged UUIDs; NFR-MNT-005 requires regression tests for every intersection case, and the epic acceptance lists the SOL-030, SOL-031, SOL-032 and ROF-010 cases explicitly. IFX-033 requires the trims in the exported geometry and IFX-064 round-trip fidelity.

WHAT: Add samples::trims_and_joins() built through commands with the seeded fixture builder: an AS-01-like attic (four exterior walls, a gable roof generated from them, both gable walls trimmed), a gable dormer roof joined to the main roof, a column trimmed below a single-plane roof, a pitched beam under a hip roof, a wall trimmed by a sloped slab, and roofs with PivotLine and Finite trimming volumes. Register it with one line in samples::catalogue() (element-kind-framework-03), which feeds crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs, the round-trip samples() and the consistency test, bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/trims-and-joins.ifcx and run conformance; add an AS-03-style test. In crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs switch the pending ROF-010 row of junction-engine-12 to active, add active rows for SOL-030, SOL-031 and SOL-032, and add pending rows owned by curved-geometry (WAL-010 inclined wall), members-profiles-adv (COL-004 inclined column), free-form-solids (solid target) and could-scope-polish (shell tool). Out of scope: RM-S and the full AS-01 automation (reference-models).
design: Same recipe as task 04. The AS-03 test reuses the spatial-tree and identity checks of roundtrip.rs:142-191. Pending rows use Status::Pending { owner, requires_kind } from junction-engine-12, so they switch on automatically when the kind registers. Keep the sample to about 15 elements; a pitch-change fixture generator shared with task 07's tests avoids two definitions of the AS-01 attic.
acceptance_criteria:
- samples::trims_and_joins round-trips with assert_eq, regenerated geometry equals the stored geometry within 0.1 mm and save-load-save is byte-identical.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/trims-and-joins.ifcx is blessed, reviewed and green in conformance/run.sh; the trimmed gable walls and the joined roof planes appear as closed bodies.
- AS-03-style test in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: reopen, change the main roof pitch and the upper storey height (so the storey-linked gable walls grow), re-save; the file validates, element UUIDs and the v5 ids of Body, Skin_n and Plane_<k> children are unchanged, the gable walls still end on the roof underside and the dormer follows the pitch.
- Active NFR-MNT-005 rows with golden outlines: trim Inside and Outside, several tools, slab tool, pitch follow, SOL-031 at body level and with a pitched beam, PivotLine and Finite volumes, ridge join, L valley join, gable and shed dormer joins, non-intersecting join problem; pending rows name their owner and required kind.
- The generic IFX-033 hash test of junction-engine-08 and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/consistency.rs cover the new sample through catalogue().
notes: SRS: SOL-030 SOL-031 SOL-032 ROF-010. Context: AS-01, AS-03, NFR-MNT-005, IFX-006, IFX-033, IFX-064.

title: Arc walls, curved slab edges, fillet, units in arc walls, polygonal and inclined walls
description:
Apply the shared arc type of drafting-trim-split to walls and slabs: arc walls (centre and radius, three points, tangent, a full circle as one element per D-10), slab outlines with arc edges coinciding exactly with curved walls (fixture F8), the circle mode and contour tracing with arcs preserved, fillet and chamfer on polygon outlines (EDT-014, which needs the arc edge), doors and windows as chord-aligned units in arc walls whose void cuts the full curved thickness (DW-019), polygonal and inclined walls and combined parallel walls. WAL-002 (Must) sits in increment 2 because Appendix F's increment 1 does not name it, AS-01 and F2/F6/F7 need no arcs, and the junction engine must be general-polygon first.

Risks: WAL-002 is extra large; coincident slab and wall tessellation needs the one shared tessellator, enforced by F8. Arc junction maths with skins fall back to square ends plus a reported problem rather than invalid geometry. Inclined walls interact with openings and junctions: fixtures first.
design: archicraft-model Edge::{Line, Arc} in Outline and in the wall reference curve (exact storage from curve.rs); archicraft-geometry: footprints as general polygons from junction.rs with arc contact, the single tessellate() for wall footprints, slab rings, plan cuts and the writer, radial void prisms for DW-019 cut per skin band in the curved wall plane, extrude.rs with per-edge angles and inclined faces; archicraft-app arc input modes in the point-input service, radius handle in the reshape palette, fillet/chamfer palette commands; archicraft-ifcx exact arc parameters in archicraft::wall and tessellated Axis basiscurves.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture F8: a slab traced from an arc wall's reference line and then from its core face shows zero gaps and identical tessellation in plan and export (vertex lists compared bit for bit); a full circle entered in one operation is one IfcWall node with a closed mesh and no seam in plan, 3D and the viewer (D-10); tessellation obeys the 2 mm / 10 degree project settings and both are editable in the project dialog; arc-to-straight L and T junctions pass the junction suite; fillet of a slab corner with r = 0.5 m stores an arc edge exactly and 'fillet all corners' works on every polygon-based kind; a window in an arc wall is placed on the chord and its void cuts all skins through the full curved thickness (radial void prism, geometry test with conformance); openings in inclined walls follow the inclination; a polygonal wall joins straight walls in plan.
notes: SRS: WAL-002 WAL-009 WAL-010 WAL-032 WAL-035 SLB-001 SLB-004 IFX-034 DW-019 EDT-014

title: Evaluate associative trims in the pipeline with the inclined rule
description:
WHY: SOL-030 (M): walls, columns, beams and free-form solids are trimmed associatively to one or more roofs, shells or slabs, keeping the chosen part. SOL-031 (M): an inclined element is cut only where it passes through the roof surface; acceptance: a wall inclined 15 degrees outward under a hip roof keeps its full base. AS-01 requires a gable roof with the gable walls trimmed to the roof, AS-03 that the roof follows changes, and IFX-033 that trims to roofs and slabs are part of the exported geometry. NFR-REL-005 forbids silent corruption when a Boolean fails. ELM-014: auxiliary elements still act as operators of trims; solid-kernel-ops-09 leaves that clause to this epic.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/trim/apply.rs: `apply_trims(kernel, parts, inside, outside)` where inside and outside are the volumes (task 06) of the target's Inside and Outside tools, the surface-only variant when KindDescriptor::inclined is true; every part keeps part intersect union(inside) (the whole part when there is no Inside tool) minus union(outside), then minus the tools' own bodies (ModelGeometry.own_bodies of solid-kernel-ops-05, extended to trim tools) so a kept part never overlaps the roof or slab; the result does not depend on relation order; an element trimmed away completely is valid without visible parts and gets an informational problem, as solid-kernel-ops-05 does for solid operations. Fill the empty Stage::Trims hook of solid-kernel-ops-05 (after SolidOperations, before Normalize), with dirty propagation from tools to targets through dependents_of in the same revision and the last-valid-body fallback. Complete docs/trims.md. Out of scope: UI (09), the golden sample (11), free-form solids and shells (pending suite rows).
design: For Inside with several tools build the kernel union of the volumes first (sorted tool order); for Outside subtract the volumes one by one. Subtract the tools' own bodies (ModelGeometry.own_bodies: generator output without junction resolution, so a roof join of task 08 or the tool's own cleanup never feeds back) only when the AABBs overlap with positive extent, which also avoids coplanar kernel input for a gable wall under a gable without overhang. Trim per part so Skin_n and Region_n names and materials stay; new faces take the part's material (single-material parts), so the SOL-026 material choice is not needed for trims. The extent passed to task 06 is the AABB of target and tools. Volumes and tool bodies are moved into the target's storey frame (bodies are storey-local; an attic roof on another storey than the gable wall is the AS-01 case). The stage reads Relation::Trim through the relation store; the framework expands the dirty set along these edges (dependents_of of element-kind-framework-08: target on by). Keep inclined detection in the kind registry so free-form solids and inclined walls opt in without touching this module.
acceptance_criteria:
- AS-01 gable: on a 10.00 x 8.00 m house with the D.2 roof (35 degrees, 0.30 m, overhang 0.50 m) generated from the walls, two gable walls of fixed height above the ridge trimmed with Downward/Inside end on the roof underside: apex and eave heights equal the analytic values within 0.1 mm, every skin is trimmed, all bodies are closed and the kernel intersection with the roof is below 1e-12 m3.
- One UpdateElements setting the pitch to 45 degrees re-evaluates the roof and both gable walls in the same revision (incremental dirty set) and the new apex matches the analytic value; undo restores the 35-degree bodies bit for bit.
- Outside keeps the part above the roof; a column trimmed below a single-plane roof, a beam trimmed below a sloped slab (SLB-006) and a wall trimmed Inside by a main roof and a dormer roof together (kept under either roof, union of volumes) give the analytic results.
- ELM-014 trim clause: marking the roof auxiliary, hiding it or showing it as wireframe leaves the trimmed gable wall bit-identical.
- Generic target path: the test-kinds Dummy flagged trim_target is trimmed like a wall; a pending NFR-MNT-005 row for a free-form solid target (owner free-form-solids) switches on when the solid kind registers with the flag.
- SOL-031 body-level test through apply_trims: a sheared-prism wall inclined 15 degrees outward under a hip roof keeps its bottom face unchanged (area and vertices), every new face lies on an extended roof plane within MODEL_TOLERANCE and none on the footprint's vertical boundary; in the variant whose pivot-line footprint lies inside the wall base a naive intersection loses base area while the trim keeps it.
- Model-level SOL-031: a beam pitched 20 degrees crossing the eaves is cut only at the roof surface and its part outside the footprint is kept; a pending NFR-MNT-005 row for a WAL-010 inclined wall switches on when curved-geometry registers inclined walls.
- Deleting the roof or UntrimElements restores the untrimmed body exactly; several trims in shuffled relation order give bit-identical meshes; the incremental-versus-full property test is extended with trims; a trim case joins the single-edit benchmark of regression-and-status (NFR-PERF-006).
- Plan slice, slice_plane and IFCX read-back of trimmed walls agree (slice_plane and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/consistency.rs of solid-kernel-ops-17); the IFX-033 hash test passes.
- An injected kernel failure keeps the last valid body and lists the target and its tools as a problem.
notes: SRS: SOL-030 SOL-031. Context: AS-01, AS-03, IFX-033, NFR-REL-005, ELM-014 (trim clause re-asserted here, left open by solid-kernel-ops-09). WAL-010 inclined walls come from curved-geometry, which this epic does not depend on; until then the inclined-wall acceptance runs at body level and the model-level row is pending.

title: Add high-quality lighting reduced during navigation and editing
description:
WHY: VIEW-053 (S): higher-quality lighting (ambient occlusion, soft shadows, sky light) shall be selectable, and these effects are reduced automatically during navigation and editing so the performance targets are met (NFR-PERF-003: at least 30 frames/s on RM-M, 20 on RM-L and 30 on RM-S on minimum hardware). Gap row VIEW-053: missing. The shader has a fixed key + fill + sky term (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/shader.wgsl fs_fill) and a view re-renders only when FrameKey changes (render3d.rs:501-517).

WHAT: render3d.rs and a new views/lighting.rs: (1) sky light - hemispherical ambient from the style's sky and ground colours (gradient of 06, a neutral pair for solid backgrounds) replacing the fixed sky term; (2) soft shadows - a blocker search plus Poisson-disc PCF whose penumbra scales with the sun's angular diameter (PCSS), replacing 3x3 PCF; (3) ambient occlusion - a single-sample depth-and-normal prepass, an SSAO pass (16-sample hemisphere kernel, 4x4 rotation noise) and a bilateral blur at half resolution, sampled in fs_fill. A QualityGovernor {Interactive, Full} per view: Interactive while the camera moved within the last 250 ms, a drag or wheel gesture is active, a tool shows a preview or an edit is in progress, or the last Full frame exceeded 33 ms; after 300 ms idle one Full refinement render is requested via request_repaint_after. Interactive keeps sky light, uses 3x3 PCF and skips SSAO; Lighting::Standard never runs the extra passes. Quality is part of FrameKey. Out of scope: global illumination, reflections and image rendering (Section 8).
design: The 4x MSAA target (SAMPLE_COUNT, render3d.rs:19) cannot be sampled for SSAO, hence the separate single-sample half-resolution prepass (Rgba16Float view-space normal + Depth32Float) and a depth-aware upsample to avoid halos at silhouettes. PCSS: 16 blocker-search taps, penumbra = (d_receiver - d_blocker) x tan(0.27 degrees) in light-space units, 16-25 Poisson filter taps on the shadow map of 07 (no second map). Sky light: irradiance = mix(ground, sky, 0.5 + 0.5 n.z) in linear space, multiplied by AO. The governor is plain Rust without egui so it is unit-testable; view3d.rs feeds it camera-changed, drag, tool-preview (ws.tool) and edit-in-progress flags. Pitfalls: request_repaint_after must fire once per idle period, never keep the app busy; extra targets live per Viewport and are recreated on resize (render3d.rs:438-500).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of QualityGovernor with an injected clock: camera motion, a tool preview and an edit switch to Interactive immediately; 300 ms idle switches to Full exactly once; a slow Full frame keeps the next navigation Interactive.
- Headless goldens of the 'White model with shadows' preset at Full quality (AO darkens the inner corner of an L junction against the wall middle by a probe threshold; the penumbra widens with distance from the occluder) and at Interactive quality (equal to the hard-shadow image of 07 apart from sky light).
- With Lighting::Standard no prepass, SSAO or blur pass is encoded (draw counter).
- Interactive and Full frame times on the largest available sample are recorded on reference hardware; Interactive meets the NFR-PERF-003 frame rate, Full may take longer because it renders only when idle.
- Satisfies VIEW-053.
notes: SRS: VIEW-053

title: Add the structural-cleanup sample, golden file and suite rows

title: Join beams at L, T and X contacts with beams, walls and columns
description:
WHY: BEA-004 (M): beams join each other, walls and columns by axis contact (L, T, X) and material priority, as walls do (WAL-020, WAL-023). COL-006 (M) includes columns joining beams. The epic acceptance names a steel beam meeting a concrete column trimmed to its face and beams at L/T/X axis contact with walls and columns. Priority subtraction (02) handles overlaps but cannot fill the outer corner where two beam ends meet at one point, nor run a higher-priority ending beam through a lower through-beam. Beam ends are planar cuts made by sweep.rs (profiles-columns-beams-05) from the BeamCut parameters (profiles-columns-beams-07), so extensions belong before the sweep and need no Boolean.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/cleanup/beams.rs computes per beam end an optional replacement CutPlane from the contacts of task 01: L with equal effective priority gives a mitre through the meeting point; L with different priorities gives a butt joint in which the higher-priority beam runs to the other's outer face and the lower keeps its end for 02 to trim; T with a higher-priority ending beam extends it to the far face of the through beam, T with a lower one leaves it for 02 to trim to the near face; X needs no extension and 02 decides continuity by priority with the wall tie rule; beam-wall and beam-column contacts need no extension, 02 cuts them by priority. Pass the planes into the beam generator (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/beam.rs) as replacements for the user's end cuts; the stored BeamCut stays and applies again when the contact disappears. Validate that the planes do not cross inside the section, otherwise keep the user cuts and report a problem. Out of scope: the join command extending beams to meet and auto-join for beams (WAL-021, WAL-022 beam parts), three-beam mitres, segmented and curved beams (BEA-005, BEA-009).
design: Use CutPlane { point, normal } of sweep.rs. Mitre: a and b are unit 3D directions pointing away from the meeting point P along each anchor line, the plane passes through P with normal normalize(a - b), so pitched beams mitre correctly. Butt and T far face: the extension distance is the largest projection of the other beam's rolled section bounding-box corners onto the extending beam's direction, measured from P. Compute per (pair, end) in ElementId order. When one beam end has several beam-beam contacts (a node of three or more beams) no plane is replaced and 02 alone resolves the overlap; record this limitation in docs/junctions.md. Validation reuses the 'end cuts cross' check of sweep.rs (section corner lengths between the two planes above MIN_HEIGHT). The replacement planes bypass the model validation of BeamCut (profiles-columns-beams-07 rejects a Horizontal cut on a level beam) but must pass the geometric check. Pitfalls: P lies on the anchor lines, not the centroid lines; roll changes the section extents; changing a contact partner must re-evaluate the beam (task 01 dirty set).
acceptance_criteria:
- A steel IPE 300 (860) whose axis ends on the axis of a 0.30 x 0.30 m reinforced-concrete column (900) ends exactly at the column face: its length shrinks by 0.15 m, its volume equals section area x remaining length (1e-9 m3) and its kernel intersection with the column is below 1e-12 m3.
- L of two D.2 reinforced-concrete beams (equal priority) at 90 and 60 degrees: mitred, outer corners filled, bodies interior-disjoint and touching on the mitre plane; L of a steel and a glulam beam (860 / 760): butt joint with the steel beam running to the glulam beam's outer face.
- T: a secondary beam ending on a primary beam's axis is trimmed to the primary's near face; with the higher priority it runs to the far face and notches the primary, which may become two closed pieces.
- X at one elevation: the higher-priority beam stays continuous and the other is cut into two closed pieces; equal priorities follow the documented tie rule (section area, canonical direction angle, ElementId).
- Beam-wall: a steel beam whose axis ends on a masonry wall's reference line (T) cuts the wall skins it overlaps; a softwood beam (740) in the same position is trimmed at the wall face; a beam ending at an end point of the wall's reference line (L) and a beam crossing the wall (X) resolve by priority in the same way, without end-plane extension.
- Moving a beam out of contact restores its user end cuts exactly; a Separated pair keeps its own cuts.
- Permutation tests over beam scenes are bit-identical; the plan, vertical-slice and IFCX agreement tests of 02 run on every beam case; the incremental-versus-full property test is extended with beam moves.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/columns-and-beams.ifcx (profiles-columns-beams-09) is re-blessed with a reviewed diff in which beams end at column faces; conformance/run.sh green.
notes: SRS: BEA-004 COL-006. Context: D-6, WAL-020, WAL-023, WAL-026. File follow-up beads for join and auto-join of beams (WAL-021, WAL-022 beam parts) and for three-beam mitres.

description:
Finish the 3D display modes (hidden line, wireframe, edge thickness, transparency switch), named display styles as project resources with the shipped presets, a directional sun with shadows and solar position from location, date and time, higher-quality lighting reduced during navigation, backgrounds, display override rules, per-face material overrides including opening reveals, roughness with PBR export, canvas background and contrast rules, and WCAG-conformant light and dark themes.

title: Cut lower-priority parts in a 3D cleanup stage through the kernel
description:
WHY: SLB-007 (M): slabs, walls, columns and beams that meet are cleaned up by material priority in 3D, sections and plan cuts. COL-006 (M): columns join walls, beams and slabs by material priority. WAL-023 defines the rule: a higher-priority skin cuts through the lower-priority skins of the other element, and touching skins with the same material and priority merge into one region without a boundary line; WAL-025 excludes pairs in different join groups or in 'never join'; WAL-027 requires cleanup and cut fills to come from the same 3D geometry; IFX-033 requires the exported mesh to be the evaluated result. What exists: Material.priority with the D.4 values (crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:153-154), and after junction-engine the per-skin effective priority SectionSkin.priority (junction-engine-01), BodyPart.priority and ModelGeometry.clusters (junction-engine-07), all consumed only by the 2D wall engine; slabs are independent extrusions (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:177-187 today, Skin_i parts after layer-structures-05) that nothing cleans up, so the gap analysis rates SLB-007 and COL-006 missing. A slab band or a column inside a wall over part of its height cannot be expressed by the 2D per-skin footprints of junction-engine; the SolidKernel of solid-kernel-ops turns it into one generic Boolean stage.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/cleanup/priority.rs: for every ContactPair of task 01, at part level (Skin_n of walls and slabs, Body or Region_n of columns and beams), the part with the higher effective priority cuts the overlapping part of the other element; result(part) = input(part) minus the input bodies of all winning parts in contact, where input is the body after Stage::Openings and before this stage, so every cutter acts with its own uncut body (a slab's stair hole is respected) and the result does not depend on evaluation order. Equal priorities are settled by a documented precedence. Register the stage as Stage::PriorityCleanup directly after Stage::Openings, in the slot that solid-kernel-ops-05 reserves between Openings and SolidOperations (so explicit solid operations still prevail, SOL-027), with the incremental cache; on a kernel error keep the last valid body, or the uncleaned body on a full evaluation, and list both elements as a GeometryProblem (NFR-REL-005). Extend ModelGeometry.clusters (junction-engine-07) with the cross-kind contact pairs so plan regions merge only same material and priority in contact. Reuse, do not re-add, slice_plane and mesh_hash (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs, mesh.rs) and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/consistency.rs of solid-kernel-ops-17 and the agreement tests of junction-engine-07 (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/agreement.rs, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/agreement.rs) for the plan, vertical-slice and IFCX legs. Out of scope: beam end planes (03), the golden sample (04), drawing region boundaries (plan-renderer), section views (sections-elevations-dims), stepped wall-wall bodies at partial vertical overlap (see notes).
design: Priorities come only from BodyPart.priority (junction-engine-07): SectionSkin.priority of Project::cross_section (junction-engine-01, per-skin overrides included) for wall and slab skins, the region material's priority for column and beam regions. Fetch every cutter body through one function so members-profiles-adv-18 can substitute its Kind::cleanup_hull() for holed sections without touching this stage. Precedence as a RankKey with derived Ord: (effective priority desc, kind rank column > beam > slab > wall, ElementId), documented in docs/junctions.md next to the wall rule. Algorithm per lower part: collect the winning parts of all contact partners whose AABB overlaps it with positive extent, subtract them one by one in RankKey order (deterministic, avoids building a large union), never between parts of the same element. Run check_closed before each kernel call as solid-kernel-ops does, and memoise results in the incremental cache by (part hash, cutter hashes). Bodies are storey-local: move the cutter into the lower element's storey frame by the elevation difference and back. Clusters: ClusterId = smallest ElementId of the connected component over the junction graph plus contact pairs. Pitfalls: flush faces (a column face in a wall face plane) are coplanar kernel input, covered by a dedicated fixture; slivers below MIN_EDGE_LENGTH from Boolean output go through the kernel repair and are reported; parts above 65,535 points are split by the writer (IFX-038, solid-kernel-ops).
acceptance_criteria:
- Column in wall: a 0.30 x 0.30 m reinforced-concrete column (900) centred in a wall 'plaster 15 / brick 240 / plaster 15' (300 / 800 / 300) leaves a 0.30 m gap in every skin over the column height; each skin volume drops by exactly its overlap volume (1e-9 m3), the column body is unchanged and every mesh passes check_closed.
- Slab band: a 0.20 m reinforced-concrete slab (900) with its top at +3.00 m over brick walls (800) running to +3.00 m removes the band from +2.80 to +3.00 m wherever the slab covers the walls; with a single-skin layered slab whose skin priority is overridden to 700 (WAL-024 override of junction-engine-01) the walls cut the slab instead.
- Column and slab: a D.2 reinforced-concrete column (900) through a 0.20 m concrete slab (880) stays continuous and the slab gets a hole of the column section over its full thickness; a steel column (860) through a reinforced-concrete slab (900) is cut into two closed pieces at the slab band.
- Slab and beam: a glulam beam (760) whose top is flush with the top of a reinforced-concrete slab (900) loses the slab band; a D.2 reinforced-concrete downstand beam under a reinforced-concrete slab is interior-disjoint from it by the precedence and forms one plan and vertical-slice region with the slab (same material and priority, no boundary).
- Slab and slab: of two overlapping slabs of 900 and 600 (screed) the screed slab loses the overlap volume exactly.
- Equal priorities follow the documented precedence; a reinforced-concrete column inside a reinforced-concrete wall yields one plan cut region without a boundary, while a column in a masonry wall keeps its own region (WAL-023 merge clause).
- A slab with a stair opening over a brick wall leaves the wall band intact under the opening (cutters are taken after Stage::Openings).
- Pairs in different join groups, in JoinGroup::NEVER or with a Separated relation are not cleaned up and keep their overlapping bodies (WAL-025).
- Order independence: a permutation property test over scenes of three to five elements (column, two walls, slab, beam) gives bit-identical meshes.
- Agreement for every case: plan cut regions equal the horizontal slice of the evaluated meshes, slice_plane (solid-kernel-ops-17) of the evaluated meshes equals slice_plane of the meshes read back from a saved IFCX file (symmetric difference below 1e-8 m2, crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/consistency.rs), and the IFX-033 hash test of junction-engine-08 passes.
- An injected kernel failure keeps the last valid body (uncleaned body on a full evaluation), adds one problem naming both elements and never yields an open mesh.
- Every catalogue golden whose elements now clean up (two-storey-shell.ifcx with its upper slab over the ground-floor walls, columns-and-beams.ifcx, and roofs.ifcx or solid-operations.ifcx where their elements overlap) is re-blessed with a reviewed diff limited to the cleaned elements; conformance/run.sh stays green.
- The dirty set after moving one column holds only that column and its contact neighbours; a cleanup case is added to the performance harness of regression-and-status for the single-edit budget of NFR-PERF-006.
notes: SRS: SLB-007 COL-006. Context: WAL-023, WAL-024, WAL-027, IFX-033, NFR-REL-005. Appendix D.4: reinforced concrete 900, concrete 880, structural steel 860, masonry 800, CLT/glulam 760, softwood 740, plaster 300. Hand-off: junction-engine-06 names this epic for stepped wall bodies at partial vertical overlap; that case belongs to WAL-020/WAL-026, not to COL-006/BEA-004/SLB-007, and stays the follow-up bead filed by junction-engine-done (the pair table can host it later with one wall-wall row limited to the uncovered height band). Open question: the equal-priority precedence (column > beam > slab > wall) is ArchiCraft's choice; verify against KB 364093 before closing.

title: Detect cross-kind contacts for beams, columns and slabs
description:
WHY: COL-006 (M) requires columns to join walls, beams and slabs by material priority (WAL-023); BEA-004 (M) requires beams to join each other, walls and columns by axis contact (L, T, X) and material priority, as walls do (WAL-020, WAL-023); SLB-007 (M) requires slabs, walls, columns and beams that meet to be cleaned up by material priority in 3D, sections and plan cuts. Decision D-6 detects wall and beam junctions from reference-line contact only and demands order-independent results. After junction-engine the contact graph (`JunctionGraph`, `detect`/`detect_around` in crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs, junction-engine-02) knows walls only, and the gap analysis notes that SLB-007 needs an element-pair detection beyond wall reference lines and that BEA-004 needs the junction code generalised from the wall footprint (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:102) to 3D bodies. The priority stage (02), the beam end adjustments (03) and the framework's incremental dirty set all need one canonical list of contacting pairs.

WHAT: (a) archicraft-model: extend the JunctionGraph of junction-engine-02 from walls to linear members, `Member { element, role: MemberRole::{Wall, Beam, Column}, contact: Start | End | Body { t } }` (renaming its `wall` field; the 2D node engine in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs keeps only role Wall members, so wall results stay bit-identical); beam anchor lines (the stored axis, IFX-035) take part as 3D segments, columns as vertical axes with their section outline; add `junction_role: JunctionRole::{None, Axis, AxisWithSection, Body}` to the KindDescriptor in crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs (walls and beams Axis, columns AxisWithSection, slabs Body). (b) Generalise `Relation::Junction { a, b, mode: JunctionMode::Separated }` (junction-engine-02) from wall pairs to any pair of elements with a junction role, with the relation-store validation, delete cascade and the archicraft::relations codec of junction-engine-08 accepting such pairs, and let the unjoin planner of junction-engine-09 accept them (its join planner already takes any kind that implements the reference_axis hook). (c) archicraft-geometry: new module root crates/archicraft-geometry/src/cleanup.rs (the path members-profiles-adv-18 and reference-models refer to) with the submodule crates/archicraft-geometry/src/cleanup/contacts.rs holding `ContactIndex` (rstar R-tree of base-body AABBs in absolute coordinates) and `contact_pairs(project, geometry, graph) -> Vec<ContactPair { a, b, kind: Axis(L | T | X) | Body }>` that merges the axis contacts (beam-beam, beam-wall, beam-column) with body contacts from a pair table (slab-wall, slab-column, slab-beam, slab-slab, column-wall, column-column), filtered by JoinGroup::joins and Separated relations and sorted canonically; wall-wall pairs stay with the 2D junction engine. (d) Expose `ContactIndex::neighbours(id, old_bounds, new_bounds)` to the framework's dirty-set expansion. Out of scope: cutting (02), beam end planes (03), UI controls (10).
design: Axis contacts reuse the uniform grid and segment helpers that junction-engine-02 moved into junction.rs, with a clamped 3D segment-segment distance for beam-beam contacts and plan contact plus an elevation check for beam-wall contacts; beam-column contact is a point-in-section test in plan (section outline rotated by the column rotation and offset by its anchor) at the contact elevation, so the grid case of AS-02 (beam ends on column centres) and beams drawn to a point inside the column both join. Classification as in junction-engine-02: L end-end, T end-body (t inside (0, 1) by more than tolerance/length), X proper crossing. The graph stays derived and is never stored. ContactIndex: `rstar::RTree<GeomWithData<AABB<[f64; 3]>, ElementId>>`, bulk-loaded on full evaluation and updated by remove/insert in evaluate_incremental; boxes inflated by MODEL_TOLERANCE; a Body contact needs a common extent above MODEL_TOLERANCE on all three axes, which removes the coplanar 'wall on slab' case before any kernel call (solid-kernel-ops lists coplanar faces as its main robustness risk). Use rstar 0.12, the version geo 0.33 pins (docs/technology-choices.md), as a direct dependency of archicraft-geometry so only one copy is compiled. The pair table is a const array keyed by kind code, so curtain walls or free-form solids opt in with one row. Pitfalls: bodies are in storey-local coordinates (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:1-7), so translate bounds by the home-storey elevation before indexing; the beam anchor line is not the centroid line (default top-centre anchor, D.2); rename the unjoin command variant only with #[serde(alias = ...)] so autosave journals still deserialise.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/junction.rs: beam L (end to end), T (end on another beam's axis) and X (crossing at the same elevation) are detected with the right contact kind; beams crossing in plan with a vertical axis distance above JOIN_TOLERANCE are not joined.
- A beam whose axis ends at an end point of a wall's reference line forms an L, one whose axis ends on the reference line inside the wall's vertical extent forms a T, a beam crossing the reference line forms an X (BEA-004 'as walls do'), and a beam inside a wall body that does not touch its reference line stays unjoined (D-6); the rule is written in docs/junctions.md.
- A beam whose axis ends on a column axis (the grid case) or inside the column's section in plan, at an elevation within the column's extent, is in contact with the column; a beam passing above the column top is not.
- Geometry tests in cleanup/contacts.rs: a slab overlapping a wall band, a column inside a wall and a slab crossing a column are reported as Body contacts; a wall standing on a slab (overlap thinner than MODEL_TOLERANCE on any axis) is not.
- Pairs in different join groups or with JoinGroup::NEVER are excluded; a Separated pair of a beam and a column is excluded, comes back on undo, and its relation disappears when either element is deleted (integrity_problems empty).
- A project with a Separated beam-column pair saves and loads equal through the relation codec of junction-engine-08 (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs); files with only wall junctions are read and written byte-identically.
- Shuffling Project.elements yields the identical pair list (permutation helper from junction-engine-06).
- Moving a column out of a wall puts exactly the column and the wall into the dirty set; the framework's incremental-versus-full property test, extended with column, beam and slab scenes, stays bit-identical.
- A command journal containing the previous unjoin variant replays; cargo test --workspace is green and all golden files are unchanged (no geometry change in this task).
notes: SRS: COL-006 BEA-004 SLB-007. Decision D-6; Appendix D.1 model tolerance 0.01 mm. Open question for docs/junctions.md and early user tests: with D-6 applied literally, a beam drawn into the middle of a wall whose reference line lies on the exterior face (D.2 default) stays unjoined.

title: Build the Display Overrides rule editor
description:
WHY: DSP-016 (C): a view applies display overrides from an ordered rule list with criteria element kind, storey, layer and material and effects pen, line type, fill and 3D colour, the top-most matching rule winning; users must be able to build and reorder such lists, not only use the presets. UI-017 (M): every command reachable from a menu or the command palette. Task 15 provides the commands, 16 the per-view application; today there is no override UI.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs: a 'Display Overrides' window with the project's override sets (new, duplicate, rename, delete with a replacement-or-none modal when a view uses the set) and, for the selected set, its ordered rules (add, duplicate, delete, move up and down, enable toggle, name), criteria multi-selects (kinds from the kind registry, storeys, layers, materials) and effect pickers (pen, line type and fill from the attribute lists filtered by role, 3D colour none, fixed or by storey); every edit issues one UpdateOverrideSet (15). Action::DisplayOverrides in the View menu and the command palette; strings through the externalisation of commands-and-l10n. Out of scope: applying the effects (16), criteria beyond DSP-016.
design: Follow the 'Add a dialog' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md and the list-and-editor pattern of materials_window (dialogs.rs:376); reuse the attribute pickers of plan-attributes-08/09 (ui/attributes.rs) and widgets::choice. Edit a draft of the selected set and commit each field change as one UpdateOverrideSet so undo granularity matches the field. Pitfall: rule order is the semantics, so move up and down must be keyboard-reachable (NFR-A11Y-001).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: creating the rule 'layer Structure -> pen 5', moving it above another rule and toggling it updates the plan of the view using the set and not of another view.
- Each edit is one undo step; deleting a set used by a view opens the replacement modal and re-points or clears the view in the same step.
- The effect pickers offer only fills that may serve as cut fills and the project's pens and line types; an empty criterion list is shown as 'any'.
- The action appears in the View menu and in the command palette (UI-017), and every control has an AccessKit label (NFR-A11Y-002).
- Satisfies the rule-list editing of DSP-016.
notes: SRS: DSP-016

title: Sort transparent faces and add the transparency switch
description:
WHY: VIEW-050 (M): transparent materials render see-through, and transparency can be switched off for performance; the epic acceptance asks that sorted transparent faces render overlapping glass correctly. Gap row VIEW-050 (partial) and the technical-debt list. Existing, kept and regressed: materials with opacity below 1 already go to an alpha-blended pipeline drawn after the opaque faces (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:146-150, 353-359, 573-575; Glass at opacity 0.3 in template.rs). Missing: that buffer is drawn unsorted with depth writes off and without culling (render3d.rs:311), so overlapping glass blends in arbitrary order, and there is no switch.

WHAT: render3d.rs: SceneData keeps transparent geometry per part as TransparentBatch {centroid, range} in one vertex buffer; whenever the camera or scene changes, the batches are sorted back to front by view-space depth of their centroid into a persistent u32 index buffer, and each batch is drawn back faces first (cull Front) then front faces (cull Back) with premultiplied alpha blending and depth test without writes. ResolvedStyle.transparency = false routes transparent parts through the opaque pipeline at alpha 1 (no sorting, no blending); hidden line keeps glass invisible as today. Shadow casting of transparent parts is decided in 07. Out of scope: order-independent transparency (fallback only, see design).
design: Per-batch sorting with back-then-front faces is exact for convex, non-intersecting batches (glazing panes, glass blocks), the common case for windows and doors; intersecting faces inside one batch stay approximate, which is documented. If curtain walls later show artefacts, weighted blended order-independent transparency (McGuire and Bavoil 2013: accumulation and revealage targets plus a composite pass) is the drop-in fallback, recorded as a decision, not implemented now. Write the index buffer with queue.write_buffer into a buffer sized to capacity. Batches keep the element slot used for picking and the per-view flag buffer of 3d-view-restrictions-04 if present. FrameKey carries the transparency flag through ResolvedStyle. Pointers: render3d.rs:102-175 (opacity split in build_scene), 353-359 (transparent pipeline), 560-575 (draw order).
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure unit test of sort_batches: three parallel panes at different depths come out far to near for a camera in front and reversed for a camera behind.
- Headless golden 'overlapping_glass': two crossing glass panes of different tint (opacity 0.3 like Glass in template.rs) in front of an opaque wall match the reference from two opposite camera positions within tolerance, and a pixel behind both panes shows both tints in the reference order.
- With transparency off the same scene renders the panes opaque, the transparent draw count is 0 and camera moves rebuild no index buffer.
- Camera moves re-sort only the index buffer (vertex upload counter unchanged); sorting 10,000 batches takes under 2 ms (unit benchmark recorded in the pull request).
- Regression: a single glass pane in front of a wall still renders see-through in shaded mode with transparency on, as today.
- Satisfies the transparency clauses of VIEW-050 (see-through rendering and the performance switch).
notes: SRS: VIEW-050

title: Pick, edit and save display styles and the sun per view
description:
WHY: VIEW-051 (S): display styles are applied per view and maintained as project resources; VIEW-052 (S): the sun is set by azimuth and altitude or from date and time, with shadows updating live while date and time change; VIEW-056 (S) and VIEW-053 (S) need their settings exposed; VIEW-004 (M, plan-views-browser) stores display style and sun settings in saved views; UI-017 (M): every command reachable from a menu or the command palette. Gap: the view-control bar offers only a DisplayMode combo (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:199-205); there is no style or sun UI.

WHAT: shell.rs: the view-control bar of a 3D view shows a 'Display style' combo with the project's styles and 'Edit display styles...', replacing the mode combo. ui/dialogs.rs: a 'Display Styles' window (list with incremental search per UI-014; new, duplicate, rename, delete with a replacement modal when in use; fields for mode, edge thickness and colour, silhouette thickness, transparency, monochrome, background kind and colours, shadows, lighting quality and its three effects) issuing the commands of 01, one undo step per edit; a 'Sun' window for the active 3D view: Manual (azimuth and altitude with typed angle input in project units) or Solar (date, time slider with live update, UTC offset, latitude and longitude shown read-only from the location) and 'Use project default'. views/state.rs (plan-views-browser-09) capture and apply include the style id and the sun settings. Actions DisplayStyles and SunSettings in the View menu and the command palette. Out of scope: display-override UI (16), canvas preference (17).
design: Follow the 'Add a dialog' extension point (Dialogs state, window function, Action, menu item, kittest by label). The style choice of a view is pane state (View3dState.style: Option<DisplayStyleId>) persisted only through capture and apply into ViewDefinition, so switching styles is not an undoable model change (consistent with VIEW-047); editing a style resource is. Use widgets::angle for azimuth and altitude so units follow the project settings (NFR-L10N-003). Live update: the slider changes SunSettings in pane state, and the shadow map of 07 is cached per sun direction, so each slider step costs one shadow pass. Strings go through the externalisation of commands-and-l10n (NFR-L10N-001). Pointers: shell.rs:190-245; dialogs.rs materials_window (:376) as the list-and-editor pattern; workspace.rs; views/view3d.rs:15-33.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: the combo lists the seven presets; choosing 'Hidden line' changes the active view's resolved style (FrameKey) without a command, and another 3D view keeps its style.
- kittest: editing a style's edge thickness in the dialog issues one UpdateDisplayStyle (one undo step) and every view using that style re-renders; deleting an in-use style opens the replacement modal and re-points the views; the search field filters the list.
- Dragging the time slider updates the view's sun vector on every change (pure state test) without undo steps; typed azimuth 135 degrees in Manual mode gives the expected vector; without latitude and longitude the Solar option shows the fallback notice.
- Save as view, change style and sun, open the view again: the stored style id and sun are re-applied (VIEW-004 test extended).
- Both actions appear in the View menu and in the command palette with labels (UI-017).
- Satisfies the UI parts of VIEW-051, VIEW-052, VIEW-053 and VIEW-056.
notes: SRS: VIEW-051 VIEW-052 VIEW-053 VIEW-056

title: Tune light and dark themes to WCAG 2.2 AA and CVD-safe highlights
description:
WHY: NFR-A11Y-003 (S): UI chrome shall meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast; selection and highlight colours shall remain distinguishable for common colour-vision deficiencies; light and dark UI themes shall be provided. Epic acceptance: a contrast check passes on both themes. Gap row NFR-A11Y-003: partial - themes exist, but egui's default Visuals and the custom colours are unaudited (weak small status text in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:170, 239-241), and the plan's selection, hover, reference, snap and preview colours (views/plan.rs:116-120, 130-134) are hue-coded (red reference against green snap, blue selection against light-blue hover) without a colour-vision check. Existing, kept and regressed: the light, dark and follow-system themes (prefs.rs:9-15, app.rs:527-534). After plan-attributes the plan's selection, pre-selection, guide and snap colours are screen-only pens of the default attribute set (DSP-005, template.rs default_attributes, with DARK pen-table entries, plan-attributes-02/10), so their defaults are tuned here too. The theme clause of UI-010 is covered with this task.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/theme.rs: visuals(dark) -> egui::Visuals derived from egui's light and dark visuals with adjusted text, weak text, widget foreground and border strokes, selection and hyperlink colours, installed for both themes in app.rs so follow-system switching stays correct; a shared HighlightPalette per theme (selection, pre-selection and hover, reference line, snap, preview, warning) with lightness separation in addition to hue, used for the app-owned colours (reference line, preview, warning, 3D selection and hover: SELECTION_COLOR and HOVER_TINT, render3d.rs:91-92) and copied into the template's screen-only pens and DARK pen-table entries, so plan feedback drawn from screen-only pens matches (affected goldens re-blessed). Tests: an audit enumerating every text/background pair of the installed Visuals (normal and weak text on panel, window, extreme and faint backgrounds, every widget state, selected text) for 4.5:1 and every component boundary and focus indicator for 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11), and a colour-vision check simulating protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia (Machado et al. 2009, severity 1.0) that asserts a minimum OKLab distance between all highlight colours and contrast against both canvases. Out of scope: screen-reader work (NFR-A11Y-002), keyboard operability (NFR-A11Y-001).
design: Simulation in linear RGB with the Machado 3x3 matrices, distances in OKLab, contrast from color.rs (17). Start from a CVD-robust set (for example #0072B2 selection, #56B4E9 pre-selection with a lightness gap, #D55E00 reference, #009E73 snap with its distinct glyph, #E69F00 preview) and let the test, not the eye, decide; snap markers already differ by shape (plan.rs draw_snap_marker :321). Check egui widget states inactive, hovered, active and open; weak text is used for the small status text, so it must reach 4.5:1 as well. Pointers: app.rs:520-535; prefs.rs:9-15; shell.rs:160-245; plan.rs:91-139; render3d.rs:91-92.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo test -p archicraft-app theme_contrast: every audited pair meets 4.5:1 (text) or 3:1 (non-text) in the light and the dark theme; the test reports the weakest pair.
- cvd_highlights: under the three simulations every pair of highlight colours differs by an OKLab distance of at least 0.10 and every highlight colour has at least 3:1 against the default canvas of its theme.
- kittest renders the app in light and dark and runs the audit on the installed ctx.style() visuals, including the status-line text.
- cvd_highlights also runs over the template's screen-only pens in the COLOUR and DARK pen tables.
- kittest: ThemeChoice Light, Dark and System (the system theme simulated through egui's RawInput.system_theme) install the matching audited visuals (regression of the theme clause of UI-010 and NFR-A11Y-003).
- plan.rs, plan_style.rs and render3d.rs take highlight colours only from the screen-only pens or HighlightPalette (no remaining literal highlight colours; checked in review and by a grep test).
- Satisfies NFR-A11Y-003 and the theme clause of UI-010.
notes: SRS: NFR-A11Y-003 UI-010

title: Make canvas backgrounds preferences and keep drawing colours at 3:1
description:
WHY: UI-010 (S): light, dark and follow-system themes; the 2D and 3D canvas background is configurable, and drawing colours whose contrast ratio against the canvas background is below 3:1 are adjusted automatically. Epic acceptance: the canvas background is a preference. Gap row UI-010 is partial. Existing, kept and regressed: light, dark and follow-system themes (ThemeChoice, crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs:9-15; Preferences rows ui/dialogs.rs:701-710; ctx.set_theme in app.rs:527-534). Missing: the canvas is hard-coded per theme - today the plan Palette (views/plan.rs:91-139), after plan-attributes-07/10 the background of the view's pen table resolved by PlanPens::resolve (views/plan_style.rs, automatic = DARK or COLOUR by theme) and drawn by plan_gpu.rs (plan-renderer-06), and the 3D background (views/view3d.rs:93-99); pen and fill colours are drawn as stored (plan.rs:264-282, later the pen buffer of plan-renderer-08). PRJ-007 keeps personal settings such as these outside the project file. VIEW-056's Background::Canvas (06) consumes the 3D value.

WHAT: prefs.rs: plan_canvas and model_canvas: CanvasColor {Auto, Custom(Rgb)} with serde defaults and sanitizing (Auto = the pen table background in plans, the theme colour in 3D); dialogs.rs preferences_window: two colour rows with 'Automatic'; PlanPens::resolve(project, table, canvas) takes the effective canvas (a Custom colour overrides the pen table's background) and derives the grid colours from it; Background::Canvas in 3D resolves to model_canvas. New crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/color.rs: relative_luminance and contrast_ratio per WCAG 2.2 and ensure_contrast(colour, background, 3.0), which moves OKLab lightness away from the background by bisection, reduces chroma to stay in gamut and falls back to black or white; applied inside PlanPens::resolve to every pen colour (so the GPU pen buffer of plan-renderer-08, hatches of -09 and dashes of -13 inherit it) and at draw time to egui line and hatch strokes, plan feedback colours (reference, selection, hover, preview, snap), 3D edge colours and overlay text, cached per (colour, canvas). Out of scope: UI chrome contrast (18); solid area fills keep their colour (see notes).
design: WCAG relative luminance from sRGB (linearised channels weighted 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722), ratio (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05). Adjust in OKLab (Ottosson) to keep perceived hue; choose the lightness direction from the background luminance. Cache in a small HashMap keyed by packed u32 pairs, cleared when the canvas changes, so nothing is recomputed per frame. Pen colours are resolved in one place, PlanPens::resolve (views/plan_style.rs, plan-attributes-07/10), which also fills the GPU pen buffer (plan_gpu.rs, plan-renderer-08) - apply there; egui overlays in plan.rs take adjusted colours from the same resolution. Display overrides (16) are resolved before this step. Follow the 'Add a preference' extension point. Pointers: prefs.rs:28-77 and sanitized() :100; dialogs.rs:679-760; plan.rs:91-145 and 264-282 (today), views/plan_style.rs and plan_gpu.rs (after plan-attributes and plan-renderer); view3d.rs:93-99.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of color.rs: contrast_ratio(black, white) is 21; colours already at 3:1 or more are unchanged; #FFFF00 on white and #303030 on #1E1E1E become colours with ratio at least 3.0 and a hue shift under 10 degrees; ensure_contrast is idempotent.
- Property test over random colour pairs: the result always reaches 3.0 against the background.
- kittest: a custom plan canvas set in Preferences changes the plan paper colour, survives a preferences reload and is not changed by opening a project (PRJ-007).
- Plan golden: a pale-yellow pen on a white canvas is drawn at 3:1 or more (probe), and black cut lines are lightened on a dark custom canvas.
- Headless 3D golden: Background::Canvas follows a custom model_canvas.
