- Regression: with plan_canvas Automatic a view's pen table background still applies (DSP-007), and switching ThemeChoice still switches the UI theme and the automatic canvases.
- Satisfies UI-010 (configurable 2D and 3D canvas background and automatic 3:1 adjustment) together with the existing themes.
notes:
SRS: UI-010
Decision proposed for product-owner confirmation: the 3:1 rule applies to lines, hatch strokes, markers and text; solid area fills keep their tone (their outline pen is adjusted), because lightening a fill changes its meaning.

title: Add the directional sun with a shadow-map pass, switchable per style
description:
WHY: VIEW-052 (S): a directional sun, defined by azimuth and altitude, shall cast real-time shadows, switchable per style, with shadows updating live while date and time change. Epic acceptance: the shadow pass toggles per style. Gap row VIEW-052: missing - the light direction is fixed at crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:521 and there is no shadow pass. Task 02 resolves the sun vector, task 01 carries the per-style shadows flag; the epic design names a shadow-map pass in render3d.rs.

WHAT: render3d.rs: a depth-only shadow pipeline (Depth32Float, 4096 squared, 2048 on downlevel adapters) rendering opaque geometry from the sun with an orthographic projection fitted to the scene bounds in light space, slope-scaled depth bias and front-face culling; a comparison sampler and 3x3 PCF in fs_fill attenuate the sun term; the sun direction and colour replace light_dir; the map is cached per (scene generation, sun direction, restrictions generation) and re-rendered only when one changes, so camera moves cost no shadow pass; a sun below the horizon switches the sun term and shadows off. View3dState carries the view's SunSettings (ProjectSettings.default_sun when the view has none) and resolves the vector with solar.rs only when the settings change. Parts with opacity below 0.5 cast no shadow. Out of scope: soft shadows and ambient occlusion (08), sun UI (09).
design: Light space: view matrix looking along -sun from the scene centre; the ortho box encloses the 8 scene AABB corners, independent of the camera, which is what makes caching possible (RM-S with terrain of about 100 m gives about 2.5 cm texels at 4096; cascades only if measurements require them). Bias: DepthBiasState constant 2, slope 2.0, plus a normal offset at the receiver; front-face culling is valid because bodies are closed (IFX-032), terrain tiles included. With 3d-view-restrictions clip planes active the shadow vertex stage applies the same planes so cut-away parts cast no shadow (hence the restrictions generation in the key). The bind group gains the shadow texture and comparison sampler; keep group numbers consistent with the cap passes of 3d-view-restrictions-07. Sun colour: warm white dimmed near the horizon by a simple air-mass factor, documented. Pointers: render3d.rs:66-73 (Uniforms), 270-380 (pipelines), 501-580 (render); shader.wgsl fs_fill; view3d.rs:15-33.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless goldens: two_storey_shell with a manual sun (azimuth 225, altitude 35 degrees) casts the upper storey's shadow on the ground slab (probe inside the shadow darker than outside by the sun term) with shadows on; with the style's shadows off the shadow pass is skipped and the probe is lit.
- Draw counters: 0 shadow passes with shadows off, exactly 1 per sun or scene change with shadows on, none while orbiting the camera.
- Live update: stepping a solar sun by 10 minutes re-renders the map once and changes FrameKey; on a pole fixture the shadow points away from the azimuth computed by 02 (probe).
- No shadow acne on a flat slab at sun altitude 10 degrees and no visible gap at wall bases (probes); the bias values are documented.
- The orbit frame time with shadows on RM-S (or the largest available sample) is measured on reference hardware and recorded against NFR-PERF-003 (30 frames/s for RM-S on minimum hardware).
- Satisfies VIEW-052 (real-time shadows switchable per style, live update with date and time).
notes: SRS: VIEW-052

title: Shade 3D views with material roughness and metalness
description:
WHY: MAT-008 (S): materials have a roughness, and SRS 3.4 makes roughness part of the 3D appearance next to colour and opacity; the gap row MAT-008 lists its use in 3D shading as missing. Task 10 adds the values; the shader (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/shader.wgsl fs_fill) has a fixed diffuse key + fill + sky term and the Vertex (render3d.rs:59-64) carries no appearance data beyond colour. The sun of 07 and the sky light of 08 are the light sources.

WHAT: render3d.rs: the Vertex gains packed roughness and metalness (unorm16x2), filled by build_scene from the material (and the resolved face material of 12); shader.wgsl: a Cook-Torrance specular term (GGX distribution, Smith-Schlick geometry, Schlick Fresnel with F0 = mix(0.04, base, metalness)) for the sun, or the default key light when the style has no sun, diffuse scaled by (1 - metalness), plus the sky light of 08 and a small constant ambient specular; monochrome styles keep the material's roughness; hidden line and wireframe are unaffected. Out of scope: environment maps, reflections and image rendering (Section 8).
design: Without an environment map metals look dark, so the constant ambient specular is deliberate and documented. Evaluate specular for the sun only; the sky light of 08 stays diffuse. Pack roughness and metalness into 4 bytes so the vertex grows from today's 40 bytes (plus the element slot of 3d-view-restrictions-04) by 4 only. Pointers: render3d.rs:59-64 (Vertex), 102-175 (build_scene), 501-580 (render); shader.wgsl fs_fill; views/lighting.rs (08).
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless golden: a curved sample with roughness 0.1 shows a tighter and brighter highlight than roughness 0.9 (probe peak intensity and highlight width); a metal is tinted by its base colour.
- Editing a material's roughness in the editor re-renders every element using it (MAT-002) without re-evaluating geometry (evaluation counter).
- The Vertex size is asserted in a test (4 bytes more than before) and the memory effect on the RM-M and RM-L budgets is noted in the pull request.
- The goldens of 04 to 08 change only where specular light appears; their diffs are reviewed and re-blessed.
- Satisfies the 3D appearance part of MAT-008.
notes: SRS: MAT-008

title: Compute the sun from location, date and time with an own routine
description:
WHY: VIEW-052 (S): a directional sun, defined by azimuth and altitude; its position can also be computed from the project location and true north (STR-012) for a date and time, with shadows updating live while date and time change. Epic acceptance: the sun computed for a given location, date and time matches an astronomical reference within 0.5 degrees. Gap row VIEW-052: missing, the light direction is fixed at crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:521. Location holds altitude, survey point and true north (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:64-73); terrain-and-site adds latitude, longitude and the EPSG code. plan-views-browser-07 defines SunSettings (date, time, shadows) as plain data in ViewDefinition.sun and allows optional fields only. The epic design asks for an own solar-position routine.

WHAT: Extend SunSettings with optional fields: source: SunSource {Manual {azimuth, altitude} (radians, azimuth clockwise from project north) | Solar} and utc_offset_minutes; ProjectSettings.default_sun used by views without their own sun. New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/solar.rs: civil date and time to Julian day (proleptic Gregorian, own code, no new dependency), solar_position(latitude, longitude, utc) -> SolarPosition {azimuth_true, altitude} after the NOAA/Meeus equations with refraction correction, and sun_direction(&Location, &SunSettings) -> SunVector {direction: DVec3 towards the sun in project coordinates (+Y project north, +Z up), above_horizon} applying true north. Validation in validate.rs: years 1901-2099, time 00:00-24:00, offset -12:00 to +14:00, manual altitude -90..90 degrees. Out of scope: shadows and rendering (07), UI (09), IFCX (03), daylight-saving rules (the offset is explicit).
design: Algorithm: NOAA solar calculator equations (after Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms): Julian century, geometric mean longitude and anomaly, equation of centre, apparent longitude, corrected obliquity, declination, equation of time, true solar time, hour angle, zenith and azimuth, plus NOAA's refraction approximation; accuracy about 0.01 degrees for 1901-2099, far inside 0.5. No chrono or time crate: date as y/m/d, time as seconds since local midnight plus the UTC offset, converted to UTC in the routine. Convention: azimuth clockwise from north. With Location.true_north the angle from project north to true north (sign as documented in project.rs and as IFX-070's second reference point uses it), project azimuth = true azimuth - true_north for a counter-clockwise positive angle; pin it with the 90-degree test, because a sign slip mirrors every shadow. The routine lives in archicraft-geometry so archicraft-model stays free of numerics and the renderer and later sun studies reuse it. Pitfalls: normalise the hour angle to (-180, 180]; clamp acos arguments; at the poles the azimuth is undefined (return 0 with above_horizon set correctly).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/solar.rs: the NREL SPA reference case (Reda and Andreas 2004: 2003-10-17 12:30:30 at UTC-7, 39.742476 N, 105.1786 W) yields zenith 50.11162 and azimuth 194.34024 degrees within 0.5 degrees (expected well under 0.1).
- Two further reference cases from the NOAA Solar Calculator, recorded in the test with their source (a southern-hemisphere winter morning and a high-latitude summer evening), agree within 0.5 degrees.
- Invariants: at 0 N 0 E on an equinox the noon altitude is within 0.5 degrees of 90 minus the declination; at 80 N on 21 December above_horizon is false all day; in the northern hemisphere the azimuth increases monotonically from morning to evening.
- sun_direction: with true north 0, Manual {azimuth 180, altitude 45} gives (0, -0.7071, 0.7071); rotating true north by 90 degrees rotates the horizontal component by exactly 90 degrees in the documented sense.
- A Solar sun on a location without latitude and longitude resolves to the manual fallback plus one ViewIssue instead of failing.
- Validation rejects out-of-range dates, times, offsets and altitudes; existing goldens stay unchanged (new fields optional).
- Satisfies the solar-position clause of VIEW-052 and the 0.5-degree clause of the epic acceptance.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-052
Appendix D has no sun values. Proposed defaults: Solar on 21 June 12:00 local time with utc_offset = round(longitude / 15) hours when latitude and longitude are set, otherwise Manual with azimuth 225 and altitude 40 degrees. Open question: should the UTC offset belong to the project location (one per project) instead of each view's sun settings?

title: Add override rule sets with poché and colour-by-storey presets
description:
WHY: DSP-016 (C): a view may apply simple, non-destructive display overrides from an ordered rule list; criteria element kind, storey, layer, material; effects pen, line type, fill, 3D colour; the top-most matching rule wins; presets include 'all cut fills solid (poché)' and 'colour by storey'; overrides never change model data. Gap row DSP-016: missing; it depends on the attribute system (DSP-001: pens, line types and fills as resources with ids, plan-attributes) and on view definitions (VIEW-004). The epic design: a DisplayOverrideRule list referenced by saved views.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/display.rs: DisplayOverrideSet {id, name, rules: Vec<DisplayOverrideRule>}; DisplayOverrideRule {name, enabled, criteria: OverrideCriteria {kinds, storeys, layers, materials} (an empty list means any; every non-empty list must match), effects: OverrideEffects {pen: Option<PenId>, line_type: Option<LineTypeId>, fill: Option<FillId>, color3d: Option<ColorEffect {Fixed(Rgb), ByStorey}>}}; Project.override_sets; ViewStyle.overrides: Option<DisplayOverrideSetId>; pure resolver first_match(set, project, element, part_material) -> Option<&OverrideEffects>; a storey palette for ByStorey; commands AddOverrideSet, UpdateOverrideSet and DeleteOverrideSet (views re-pointed to a replacement or none in the same undo step) on an Edit snapshot; template presets 'Poché' (any element: the template's solid fill in the structural cut-line pen colour) and 'Colour by storey' (any element: ByStorey). IFCX: overrideSets in archicraft::project and the view reference, presets added to older files on load, goldens re-blessed. Out of scope: applying effects and the editor (16).
design: Effects come whole from the winning rule (no merging across rules), as 'top-most wins' implies. The resolver takes the part material so a rule can restyle only the insulation skin. The ByStorey palette is defined in the model so plan and 3D agree: eight colour-vision-deficiency-safe colours (Okabe-Ito order), cycling. Pens, line types and fills reference the attribute ids of plan-attributes (crates/archicraft-model/src/attributes.rs); the Poché preset looks up the template's solid fill and structural cut-line pen by role, never by name. Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point; share the FORMAT_VERSION bump with 03, 10 and 13 within one release. ELM-012 and ELM-020 name position and structural function as later criteria - keep OverrideCriteria extensible with optional fields. Pointers: views.rs ViewStyle (plan-views-browser-07), template.rs, schema.rs, writer.rs project_attribute.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: rules are evaluated top-down and the first enabled match wins even if a later rule is more specific; disabled rules never match; criteria combine with AND across kinds, storeys, layers and materials and OR within one list; the material criterion matches per skin material.
- ByStorey gives each storey of samples::two_storey_shell a distinct palette colour by storey order, unchanged by renaming and deterministic when storeys are added.
- Commands are one undo step each; deleting a set used by a view requires a replacement or explicit none; validation rejects dangling pen, line-type, fill, storey, layer or material references and unknown kinds.
- Round trip of both presets and a custom set; with archicraft:: stripped the file is byte-identical with and without override sets; older files get the presets with an info Problem.
- Applying a set is view data only: Project equality of elements, materials and attributes before and after.
- Provides the data model, presets and persistence of DSP-016.
notes:
SRS: DSP-016
Appendix D has no override defaults. Proposed storey palette (Okabe-Ito): #E69F00, #56B4E9, #009E73, #F0E442, #0072B2, #D55E00, #CC79A7, #999999. Open question: should 'colour by storey' also tint remote-storey elements in plans? Proposed: 3D colour only.

title: Apply display overrides in plan and 3D views and choose a set per view
description:
WHY: DSP-016 (C): a view may apply simple, non-destructive display overrides from an ordered rule list; effects pen, line type and fill in 2D and colour in 3D; the top-most matching rule wins; presets 'all cut fills solid (poché)' and 'colour by storey'; overrides never change model data. Epic acceptance: the 'colour by storey' and 'poché' override presets. Task 15 provides the data, presets and persistence. Today the GPU plan renderer of plan-renderer (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan_gpu.rs, pen buffer of plan-renderer-08, fills of -06, dashes of -13), the painter fallback in views/plan.rs draw_plan and build_scene (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:102-175) draw only attribute and material values.

WHAT: Plan: when plan_gpu.rs builds PlanBuffers from the cached PlanDrawing, it resolves per element and per cut region the winning rule of the view's override set (ViewStyle.overrides) and substitutes the stroke pen index, line-type index and cut-fill index; the PlanBuffers key gains an override generation, the painter fallback substitutes the same way, and archicraft-geometry's PlanDrawing and its cache stay untouched. 3D: build_scene applies color3d with the precedence selection > override colour > style monochrome > face material (12) > part material, keeping material opacity; the scene key gains the override generation. The contrast adjustment of 17 runs on the final, substituted colours. UI: an 'Overrides' combo (none or a set) in the view-control bar of plan and 3D panes, stored in the pane state (PlanViewState and View3dState) and captured into and applied from ViewDefinition by views/state.rs (plan-views-browser-09); choosing a set is pane state, not an undoable model change. Out of scope: the rule editor (21), criteria beyond kind, storey, layer and material (Section 8: rule-based graphic overrides beyond DSP-016).
design: Substituting while building GPU buffers keeps archicraft-geometry's plan cache valid; only the PlanBuffers of storeys shown with a set are rebuilt when the set or the override generation changes. For cut regions the material criterion uses the region's material (same-material regions are merged, archicraft-geometry plan.rs:153-160). Order: resolve the override first, then the contrast adjustment of 17 on the final colour. Precompute per rule sorted id sets so resolution is O(rules) per element. Pointers: views/plan_gpu.rs (plan-renderer-06/08/13), views/plan.rs draw_plan, render3d.rs build_scene, ui/shell.rs:190-245 (view-control bar), views/state.rs (plan-views-browser-09).
acceptance_criteria:
- Plan golden (plan-renderer harness): the F2 wall plan with the Poché set draws every cut region solid in the cut-line pen colour; the same view without a set matches the existing golden.
- 3D golden: two_storey_shell with Colour by storey shows each storey in its palette colour; the selection colour still wins.
- A set built through the commands of 15 with 'layer Structure -> pen 5' above 'kind Slab -> line type DASH' draws matching outlines in pen 5's colour and weight and slab outlines dashed (plan probes), only in the view using the set.
- Precedence unit test: selection > override colour > monochrome > face override (12) > part material, with opacity kept.
- After applying and removing both presets the project equals its previous state, history gained no step from applying, and the saved file is byte-identical (overrides never change model data).
- Choosing a set in the view-control bar, saving the view and reopening it restores the set; a pen-only edit still rebuilds no geometry buffer.
- An override pen that is too pale for a dark custom canvas is adjusted to 3:1 by 17 (probe).
- Satisfies DSP-016 in plan and 3D views, including both presets.
notes: SRS: DSP-016

title: Cross-kind priority cleanup and associative trims to roofs and slabs
description:
Generalise the junction engine from 2D wall footprints to 3D bodies with the Boolean kernel: columns and beams join walls, slabs and each other by material priority with axis-contact detection (L/T/X), slabs clean up against walls, columns and beams in 3D, sections and plan cuts; and add the associative Trim relation: trim walls, columns, beams and solids to roofs, shells and slabs with keep-side preview, the inclined-element rule, per-roof trimming volumes and roof-to-roof joins. Delivers the AS-01 gable walls trimmed to the roof. The pipeline-order rule (SOL-027) is solid-kernel-ops and the non-associative crop (SOL-033) is free-form-solids, so this epic holds only the relation-driven cleanup and trim stages.

Risks: The gap analysis sizes SLB-007, COL-006 and BEA-004 as extra large because each estimate includes a Boolean engine; with the kernel and the junction node graph in place they share one contact-detection and priority stage, which is why they fit one epic, and the scope is bounded by the AS-02 and D.7 cases (everything else falls back to no cleanup plus a reported problem). The beads split is cleanup first, trims second; if the cleanup wave overruns, the trims become the first bead of reference-models' lead time rather than a new epic. Boolean failures on coplanar or tangent cases keep the last valid body and list the element (NFR-REL-005).
design: archicraft-geometry cleanup.rs: contact detection on an rstar index of body bounds (axis/face overlap), one generic pairwise priority-cutting stage through the SolidKernel shared by the column, beam and slab cases, ordered before explicit operations in the evaluation pipeline fixed by solid-kernel-ops; Relation::Trim{element, by, keep_side, volume} evaluated through the kernel with downward/upward/finite trimming volumes from the roof outline or pivot line; archicraft-app selection-based commands with keep-side preview (decision D-7).
acceptance_criteria: Cleanup tests: a concrete column inside a masonry wall cuts the wall skins, a steel beam meeting a concrete column is trimmed to its face, a slab of priority 900 cuts a wall of 800 at the slab band, beams at L/T/X axis contact with walls and columns clean up, results are order-independent and identical in the plan slice, in a vertical slice and in the exported mesh (IFX-033 extended); the AS-01 gable walls are trimmed to the roof and follow a pitch change in one revision; a wall inclined 15 degrees outward under a hip roof keeps its full base (SOL-031); trimming volumes (downward from outline or pivot line, upward, finite) are selectable and displayable on demand; a dormer roof is joined to the main roof along the valley and follows a pitch change; every case joins the NFR-MNT-005 suite.
notes: SRS: COL-006 BEA-004 SLB-007 SOL-030 SOL-031 SOL-032 ROF-010

title: Tag wall, slab and opening faces by role and colour them by face material
description:
WHY: MAT-004 (S) and OPN-008 (S) need, for every triangle of a body, the face it belongs to: reference side, opposite side, ends, top, bottom, edges, or a reveal or end face created by a specific opening, including a niche whose end face lies exactly on a skin boundary (OPN-008: overrides shall also work when an opening face coincides with a skin boundary). The epic design: archicraft-geometry per-face parts for overrides, reveal materials as separate parts. Today parts carry one material and no face information (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:21-28); walls are Skin_n parts (layer-structures-04), wall openings are cut by extrude_layers and wall_cut.rs (host-openings-04/05) with the VoidPrisms of EvalContext::cutters, which doors and windows feed too (doors-windows-core-03), and slab openings are outline holes (host-openings-06). Existing and extended, not duplicated: solid-kernel-ops-07 adds BodyPart.face_materials (FaceMaterialRun, SOL-026) and per-run colouring in build_scene.

WHAT: archicraft-geometry: BodyPart gains faces: Vec<FaceRun {role: FaceRole, owner: Option<ElementId>, triangles: Range<u32>}> covering every triangle of a visible part; Void parts (PartRole::Void, host-openings-03) carry none. extrude.rs (extrude and extrude_layers) emits runs for caps, side faces per ring and exposed interface faces; hole rings carry HoleSource {Own, Cutter(ElementId)} for every hosted cutter (opening, door or window); exposed interface faces inside a void's section become OpeningEnd owned by that cutter, so a niche ending on a skin interface is tagged on the deeper skin. The wall and slab generators (kinds/wall.rs, kinds/slab.rs of element-kind-framework-15) pass the tags through. Wall classification: a side face whose centroid offset from the reference line (radius for arc walls) equals the envelope's exterior or interior face offset within MODEL_TOLERANCE is ReferenceSide or OppositeSide per the ReferenceLine side convention, other skin side faces are internal, remaining vertical faces Ends, horizontal faces Top and Bottom; slabs Top, Bottom, Edges. resolve_face_materials(project, element, part) -> Vec<(Range<u32>, MaterialId)> applies the precedence of 11 and merges the SOL-026 runs of solid-kernel-ops-07 (operation-created triangles keep their run material). crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs build_scene extends its per-run colouring (solid-kernel-ops-07) to the resolved ranges (opacity per material) and SceneKey (workspace.rs:44-47) gains an appearance generation. Out of scope: roofs, columns, beams and faces cut through the solid kernel (20), IFCX splitting (13), UI (14).
design: Tags are produced where faces are created, not inferred afterwards, so they survive junctions and cuts: extrude_layers knows which rings are voids and which interface faces are exposed, and the wall side classification uses offsets because junction-engine and curved-geometry reshape footprints (more than four edges, arcs). Owner tagging of exposed interface faces: test the triangle centroid against each void section (few voids per wall), once per evaluation. Runs are contiguous because generators emit faces in order; Range<u32> keeps memory at a few entries per part. Appearance is resolved at render and write time from project data, which is why an override is appearance-only and never invalidates geometry; plan slicing, picking and closedness checks keep using the unsplit parts. Pointers: extrude.rs:18-58 and extrude_layers (host-openings-04), wall_cut.rs (host-openings-05), slab opening holes (host-openings-06), evaluate.rs:21-50 and 150-189, render3d.rs:102-175, workspace.rs:44-47 (SceneKey).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/faces.rs: every part's runs cover all triangles exactly once; a free single-skin wall has one ReferenceSide and one OppositeSide face, two Ends, Top and Bottom with the expected areas; for the F2 six-skin wall only the outer face of skin 1 and the inner face of skin 6 are sides and skin interfaces are internal.
- A 1.0 x 1.0 m through opening in the F2 wall yields Reveal runs owned by the opening in all six skins with a total area of 4 x 1.0 x 0.68 m within tolerance.
- A niche ending exactly on a skin boundary of the F2 wall yields one OpeningEnd run of 1.0 m2 on the next skin and no sliver triangles; 0.4 mm off the boundary the snap of host-openings-05 gives the same result.
- A slab opening's hole sides are Reveal runs owned by the opening, the slab's own polygon holes are Edges.
- resolve_face_materials: a wall Ends override recolours only End triangles; an opening's Reveal override beats the host's; meshes and signed volumes are bit-identical with and without overrides and SetFaceOverride triggers no re-evaluation (evaluation counter).
- Scene test: build_scene colours exactly the overridden triangle ranges (vertex colours), and the scene is rebuilt after SetFaceOverride although geometry is unchanged.
- A door in the F2 wall yields Reveal runs owned by the door in all six skins; Void parts carry no runs; operation-created faces (solid-kernel-ops-07) keep their SOL-026 material and are not changed by role overrides.
- Satisfies the geometry and display parts of MAT-004 and OPN-008.
notes: SRS: MAT-004 OPN-008

title: Add roughness and metalness to materials, the editor and gltf::material
description:
WHY: MAT-008 (S): materials shall also have a roughness (SRS 3.4: appearance is colour, opacity and roughness; D-5 one material concept). IFX-042 (C): physically based appearance (roughness, metalness) may be written as a gltf::material attribute declared in-file, as in R2's Domestic Hot Water example; textures are not part of v1 (D-11) and the registry's mesh schema has no texture coordinates. MAT-007 (M) writes materials per IFX-040 and IFX-043; MAT-002 (M) propagates material edits to every element. Gap rows: MAT-008 missing (no roughness in crates/archicraft-model/src/material.rs:142-157, the writer, the reader or the shader); IFX-042 missing (no gltf::material in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs). Existing and kept: the material command path (UpdateMaterial, command.rs) and the materials editor (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs materials_window :376, Opacity slider :800).

WHAT: material.rs: Material.roughness and metalness (0..1, serde defaults 0.5 and 0.0) with range checks in Material::validate; template.rs: values for all 25 template materials (MATERIALS table); dialogs.rs materials_window: Roughness and Metalness sliders beside Opacity with a swatch preview, issuing the existing material command. IFCX: the archicraft::project materials record gains roughness and metalness (optional on read, defaults 0.5 and 0); every written material node gains gltf::material in exactly the shape of R2's Domestic Hot Water example in the pinned IFC5-development checkout (conformance/run.sh, commit 1a63082), declared in the file's schemas section; the reader prefers the archicraft record and falls back to gltf::material. Goldens re-blessed. Out of scope: shading with roughness and metalness (22), textures and texture coordinates (D-11), environment reflections.
design: Keep the existing material command path so MAT-002 propagation is automatic. gltf::material: copy the attribute name, value structure (glTF 2.0 pbrMetallicRoughness with metallicFactor and roughnessFactor as used there) and the schema declaration verbatim; where the example and the glTF specification differ, follow the example. Write gltf::material on every material node (not only non-default values) so consumers see a consistent shape; the archicraft record stays authoritative for ArchiCraft. Share the FORMAT_VERSION bump with 03, 13 and 15 within one release (migration table of element-kind-framework-12). Pointers: material.rs:140-178; template.rs:31 (MATERIALS) and 274-300; writer.rs:72 (rgb), 122-140 and 325-338; schema.rs:172-185; dialogs.rs:376 and :800.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: all template materials validate with roughness and metalness in range; glass, steel and aluminium carry the proposed values; out-of-range or non-finite values are rejected and leave the project untouched.
- Round trip (crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs): roughness and metalness survive bit-exactly; an older golden reads with the defaults and no error; a hand-edited file whose material node carries only gltf::material restores those values.
- The written attribute and its in-file declaration match the R2 example's key paths (test against a snippet copied to crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures/); no texture reference and no texture coordinate is written (D-11); the offline validator, conformance/run.sh and the reference viewer accept the re-blessed goldens.
- kittest: the material editor shows Roughness and Metalness, and an edit issues one material command (one undo step) that reaches every element using the material (MAT-002).
- Satisfies the data, editing and persistence of MAT-008 and all of IFX-042.
notes:
SRS: MAT-008 IFX-042
Proposed roughness/metalness for product-owner confirmation: glass 0.05/0, steel 0.35/1, aluminium 0.3/1, tiles 0.2/0, natural stone 0.5/0, membrane 0.6/0, timber products 0.7/0, concrete, masonry, render, plaster, gypsum board, screed, insulation, soil and gravel 0.85-0.95/0. Open question: should metalness (not required by MAT-008) be user-visible or only set by the template?

title: Draw solid and gradient sky and ground backgrounds in 3D views
description:
WHY: VIEW-056 (S): backgrounds shall be solid or gradient sky and ground colours; VIEW-051 (S) bundles background colours in a display style. Gap row VIEW-056: missing - a clear colour picked by theme (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/view3d.rs:93-99) is used only as clear colour and hidden-line fill (render3d.rs:501-545), not visible or changeable anywhere, and the shader has no gradient path.

WHAT: render3d.rs and shader.wgsl: a background pipeline drawing one full-screen triangle before the opaque pass (depth compare Always, no depth writes); Background::Solid fills one colour; Background::Gradient blends sky zenith to sky horizon above and ground horizon to ground nadir below the horizon, from the per-pixel view-ray elevation in perspective and from a screen-space gradient whose horizon row follows the camera pitch in parallel projection; Background::Canvas resolves to the model canvas colour handed in by the view (the theme constant today, the preference after 17). Hidden-line faces use the solid colour or the gradient's horizon colour. Uniforms gain the four background colours, the inverse view-projection and the kind. Out of scope: canvas preference (17), sky lighting (08), background images (VIEW-062 withdrawn by D-11).
design: Full-screen triangle from vertex_index (no buffer). Ray direction = inverse(view_proj) x (ndc.xy, 1, 1) minus the camera position; elevation = asin(dir.z / |dir|). Parallel projection has no common horizon, so the decision is a screen-space gradient with horizon_row = centre - pitch / (pi / 2) x half height, clamped: top views show ground, elevations show sky over ground; record it in docs/testing.md and the pull request. Blend in linear space and write sRGB as shader.wgsl does today. The MSAA colour attachment still clears for robustness, but the background pass overwrites it. Pointers: view3d.rs:93-99, 227; render3d.rs:501-545.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless goldens: a gradient style looking slightly upwards shows sky above and ground below a horizon row that moves with the pitch; a parallel top view shows only ground; a solid style fills one colour; probes match the configured colours within tolerance.
- Hidden line on a gradient background draws faces in the horizon colour; wireframe shows the gradient through the model.
- Background::Canvas follows the colour passed by the view (light and dark constants in a test).
- FrameKey changes with every background field; the clear-colour-only path of view3d.rs:93-99 is removed.
- Satisfies VIEW-056 and the background part of VIEW-051.
notes:
SRS: VIEW-056 VIEW-051
Proposed gradient for the Shaded preset (product-owner confirmation): sky zenith #6E9BD1, sky horizon #DCE6F0, ground horizon #CFC8BC, ground nadir #8C8478.

title: Persist display styles, sun settings and view style links in IFCX
description:
WHY: Display styles are project resources (VIEW-051) and a saved view stores display style and sun settings (VIEW-004), so styles, the per-view style reference, the extended sun settings (VIEW-052) and backgrounds (VIEW-056) must survive save and reopen in the archicraft:: namespace, declared in the file (IFX-061) and versioned (IFX-062). Today project_attribute in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs has no style record, and plan-views-browser-08 writes ViewDefinition with style {mode} and sun {date, time, shadows} only.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: displayStyles array in archicraft::project (id, name, description, mode, edges {thickness, silhouetteThickness, color}, transparency, monochrome {color, keepGlass}, background {kind canvas|solid|gradient, colours}, shadows, lighting {kind standard|high, ambientOcclusion, softShadows, skyLight}), defaultStyle, settings.defaultSun, and inside views style.style (reference), sun.source {kind manual|solar, azimuth, altitude} and sun.utcOffset; writer.rs and reader.rs accordingly, read leniently with defaults; a file without displayStyles gets the seven presets on load with an info Problem; a view pointing to a missing style keeps its mode with a warning. FORMAT_VERSION bump through the migration table of element-kind-framework unless already bumped since the last release. samples.rs: the saved 3D view of plan-views-browser-08 references 'White model with shadows' with a solar sun; goldens re-blessed and reviewed. Out of scope: app behaviour.
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md: declare with optional(...) in schema.rs, write with json! in writer.rs project_attribute, read with report.or(...) in reader.rs. Enumerations from the model ALL arrays via .map(code); colours as [r, g, b] like material colours (writer.rs rgb). Reuse the archicraft::-stripping comparison helper of plan-views-browser-08 and 3d-view-restrictions-02 (move it into a shared test module if it is local). One FORMAT_VERSION bump per release: if 10, 13 or 15 of this epic land in the same release they share it (check the migration table). Pitfalls: deterministic key order (json.rs) keeps golden diffs reviewable; preset ids in goldens come from the seeded fixture builder (v5 ids).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs display_styles_round_trip: the seven presets plus a custom style with gradient background, monochrome and high lighting survive write and read with Project equality (bit-exact floats).
- sun_settings_round_trip: manual and solar sources, UTC offsets and the project default sun survive.
- old_file_gets_presets: the previous golden loads with the seven presets and one info Problem; a hand-edited view with a dangling style id loads with one warning and keeps its mode.
- With all archicraft:: attributes stripped, the file is byte-identical with and without styles and sun settings (display data never changes the model).
- The offline validator accepts the declarations (IFX-061); conformance/run.sh is green on the re-blessed goldens; the golden diff touches only archicraft::project.
- Satisfies the persistence of VIEW-051, VIEW-052 and VIEW-056.
notes: SRS: VIEW-051 VIEW-052 VIEW-056

title: Tag roof, column and beam faces and reveals cut through the solid kernel
description:
WHY: MAT-004 (S) names 'a roof's top, bottom and edges' among the faces that accept an appearance override, and OPN-008 (S) requires the faces an opening creates to default to the materials of the cut elements (plural) and to be overridable separately. Task 12 tags only the extrusion paths of walls, slabs and host cuts. Roofs (increment 2) build their skins with plane_body (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/body.rs, roofs-02/05) as Plane_k children and host openings through hole rings (roofs-11); columns and beams are swept by sweep.rs (profiles-columns-beams-05) in kinds/column.rs and kinds/beam.rs; openings cut further elements through the Manifold kernel in the FurtherCuts stage (solid-kernel-ops-13/14), which explicitly leaves 'reveal materials on further cuts (OPN-008)' to this epic; solid operations recombine faces through the kernel (solid-kernel-ops-02/05) and give operation faces SOL-026 runs (solid-kernel-ops-07). Gap rows MAT-004 and OPN-008: missing.

WHAT: Roofs: plane_body emits FaceRuns for the upper offset surface (Top), the lower one (Bottom) and the side planes at eaves, verges, hips, valleys and ridges (Edges); exposed skin interfaces are internal; the hole sides of roof openings are Reveal owned by the opening; each Plane_k child part (ElementGeometry.children, element-kind-framework-15) carries its own runs. Columns and beams: sweep.rs tags the end faces Ends and the lateral strips Sides. Kernel: the SolidKernel of solid-kernel-ops-02 gives every input FaceRun its own Manifold face id, so surviving triangles keep role and owner; triangles that the FurtherCuts stage takes from an opening's void prism become Reveal (prism sides) or OpeningEnd (prism ends) owned by that opening in the cut element's part, so they default to that element's skin material and take the opening's Reveal override; triangles from solid-operation operators keep their SOL-026 runs; Body_n partitioning (solid-kernel-ops-03) splits runs with their triangles. resolve_face_materials (12) needs no change. Out of scope: IFCX splitting (13), UI (14), free-form solid faces (free-form-solids), curtain-wall panels.
design: Tags are produced where faces are created (as in 12), and only the kernel path needs provenance: Manifold keeps a face id per input region and merges coplanar triangles only within one id, so distinct ids per run keep runs apart; map output groups back by (input, face id) exactly as solid-kernel-ops-02 already groups triangles for IFX-038. Give each void prism of the FurtherCuts stage its own original id so prism-sourced triangles are recognisable without geometric tests. Roof plane frames already distinguish upper and lower offset surfaces (roofs-02 plane.rs), so no normal-based guess is needed. Pitfall: the canonical output order of the kernel must keep each run contiguous; if not, split it into several FaceRuns with the same role and owner. Pointers: roof/body.rs and roof/plane.rs (roofs-02/05), roofs-11 hole rings, sweep.rs and kinds/column.rs, kinds/beam.rs (profiles-columns-beams-05/06/07), kernel/mod.rs and the FurtherCuts stage (solid-kernel-ops-02/05/14), evaluate.rs BodyPart.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/faces.rs: a single-plane roof with a three-skin structure has Top on the upper surface, Bottom on the soffit and Edges on every eaves and verge face with the expected areas; a hip roof's Plane_k parts carry Edges at hips and the ridge; runs cover every triangle of each part exactly once.
- A perpendicular roof opening (roofs-11) yields Reveal runs owned by the opening in all skins.
- A column and a beam with angled end cuts each have two Ends runs on the cut faces and Sides runs covering every lateral face.
- An opening whose cut list (solid-kernel-ops-13/14) includes a second wall: the further cut wall gets Reveal runs owned by the opening, coloured with that wall's skin materials by default and with the opening's Reveal override when set; the host's runs are unchanged.
- A wall cut by a solid operation keeps ReferenceSide, OppositeSide and Ends runs on its surviving faces, and operator-created faces keep their SOL-026 material.
- Meshes and signed volumes are bit-identical with and without overrides, and Body_n partitioning keeps full run coverage.
- Satisfies the roof clause of MAT-004 and the 'cut elements' clause of OPN-008 for further cut elements.
notes: SRS: MAT-004 OPN-008

title: Render display styles: thick edges, silhouettes, modes and monochrome
description:
WHY: VIEW-050 (M): 3D views provide shaded, shaded with edges, hidden line and wireframe with adjustable edge thickness. VIEW-051 (S): a style's mode, monochrome override and edge settings must reach the renderer. Gap row VIEW-050 is partial. Existing, kept and regressed: the four modes (DisplayMode, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:25-57, drawn at :566-575, hidden-line faces take the background colour in shader.wgsl fs_fill) and the face depth bias (render3d.rs:341-345). Missing: edges are a 1-pixel LineList (render3d.rs:362-368) because wgpu has no wide lines; build_scene draws every edge above 1 degree (render3d.rs:164 calls TriMesh::feature_edges(1.0), mesh.rs:239), so tessellated curves show every facet and only smooth terrain parts are special-cased by terrain-and-site-14 (BodyPart.smooth, TriMesh::vertex_normals, a 60-degree threshold); the mode is the only style input to FrameKey (render3d.rs:235-240). The epic design names an edge-extraction pass and style uniforms.

WHAT: archicraft-geometry mesh.rs: edge_records(min_angle) -> Vec<EdgeRecord {a, b, n1, n2, kind: Crease | Smooth | Border}>, Smooth when both triangles share the edge's vertex indices (IFX-038 shares vertices only across smooth edges); this also classifies smooth terrain parts (BodyPart.smooth of terrain-and-site-14), replacing its 60-degree special case while its smooth/faceted switch keeps working. render3d.rs: edges become an instance buffer of EdgeInstance {a, b, n1, n2, color, kind}; a new edge pipeline expands each instance into a screen-space quad of thickness_pt x pixels_per_point in vs_edge (near-plane clipping in clip space before the divide), draws creases and borders always and smooth edges only on silhouettes (n1 and n2 facing opposite ways relative to the eye, or the view direction in parallel projection) with the silhouette thickness of the style; Uniforms gain a StyleBlock (mode flags, edge colour and thicknesses, monochrome colour and flag, viewport size) built from ResolvedStyle (01); View3dState and FrameKey carry ResolvedStyle instead of DisplayMode (the status-bar combo keeps working through mode-synthesised styles until 09); back-face culling of opaque closed bodies when no clip plane is active. Goldens of the four modes through the headless render harness. Out of scope: transparency sorting (05), backgrounds (06), sun and shadows (07), style UI (09).
design: Wide lines: wgpu exposes no line width, so each edge is an instanced quad (6 vertices from vertex_index, no index buffer) expanded in screen space: project both endpoints, clip the segment against w > epsilon in clip space, offset by the screen-space normal x half thickness / viewport size x 2, keep the endpoints' depth and rely on the existing face bias (render3d.rs:341-345) so edges win against their own faces. Silhouette test in vs_edge: s1 = dot(n1, eye - a), s2 = dot(n2, eye - a) (constant view direction in parallel projection); visible if kind != Smooth or s1 * s2 < 0, otherwise a degenerate quad. Instance size about 56 bytes, below today's 2 x 40 bytes per edge. Hidden line keeps faces in the style's face colour (the solid background, or the horizon colour of a gradient after 06). Back-face culling only while 3d-view-restrictions adds no clip plane (its stencil parity pass needs both faces). Uniform layout: 16-byte aligned, bytemuck Pod, size asserted in a test. Harness: reuse crates/archicraft-app/tests/support/render3d.rs and kittest.toml (3d-view-restrictions-03, plan-renderer-07); if absent, add exactly that minimal subset here. Pointers: render3d.rs:25-57, 59-75, 102-175, 270-380, 501-580; shader.wgsl; view3d.rs:15-33, 227, 248-262.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in mesh.rs: a box yields 12 crease edges and no smooth edge; a 36-segment cylinder yields smooth edges along the mantle and crease edges at the caps; coplanar triangulation diagonals are never edges.
- Headless goldens in crates/archicraft-app/tests/render3d_golden.rs of samples::two_storey_shell plus a smooth cylinder body in shaded, shaded with edges, hidden line and wireframe pass on the three CI platforms within the documented tolerance.
- Edge thickness: at 1 pt and 3 pt the measured stroke width of a vertical wall edge in the readback is 1 and 3 device pixels (+-1) at pixels_per_point 1, and twice that at 2.
- Silhouettes: orbiting around the cylinder moves its outline and never draws mantle facet edges (pixel probes); the technical drawing preset draws silhouettes heavier than creases.
- Monochrome white renders every non-glass face in the monochrome colour, shaded; the selection colour still wins.
- Any style field change alters FrameKey; camera moves do not rebuild the edge buffer (upload counter).
- Regression: the existing render3d.rs unit tests (build_scene vertex counts, selection colour) stay green; smooth terrain (terrain-and-site-14) shows boundary, skirt and silhouette edges but no TIN creases, and the faceted setting still shows every TIN edge.
- Satisfies VIEW-050 (four modes with adjustable edge thickness) and the rendering of the mode, edge and monochrome bundle of VIEW-051.
notes: SRS: VIEW-050 VIEW-051

title: Write face overrides as per-part materials and read them back
description:
WHY: Epic acceptance: a face override on a wall end changes appearance only and exports per-part materials. The MAT-004 and OPN-008 overrides are parametric data that must round-trip, and other IFC5 tools must show their colours: IFX-040 (M) lets parts reference materials via inherits.material; IFX-043 (M) requires every part of a layered element to reference a named material; IFX-014 and IFX-010 require unique child keys and stable v5 ids; IFX-032 (M) requires closed volumetric parts.

WHAT: schema.rs: optional faceOverrides object (role code to material reference) in archicraft::element or in the per-kind codec of element-kind-framework, role codes from FaceRole::ALL; writer.rs write_element splits each BodyPart, including the parts of compound children such as roof Plane_k children (element-kind-framework-07), by resolve_face_materials (12, 20): triangles with the part's own material stay in the part (Body or Skin_n), each override material becomes a sibling part named <Part>_<role code> (suffix _2, _3 for further materials of one role, ordered by role then material id) with sub_node_id ids, inherits.material and per-face vertices; projects without overrides write byte-identical output. reader.rs reads faceOverrides leniently (a dangling material is a warning and the entry is dropped). conformance/check.ts and the closedness test treat a part plus its <Part>_* siblings as one body group for IFX-032 and require every face part's material to resolve to a colour. samples.rs face_overrides_showcase(): the F2 wall with an Ends override, a slab with an Edges override, a single-plane roof with a Top override, an opening with a Reveal override and a niche ending on a skin boundary with an OpeningEnd override, registered in examples/reference_models.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs, golden blessed. Out of scope: UI (14).
design: IFX-032 asks every volumetric part to be closed; a face part split from a skin is a surface, so this task treats the body group (base part plus its face parts) as the volumetric unit, documents that in the IFCX notes under docs/ and raises the wording as an SRS clarification (see notes). Child names keep the base part name first so consumers grouping by prefix keep skins together. Splitting preserves the original triangle order per face, so output stays deterministic (json.rs) and IFX-038 per-face vertices hold. used_materials (writer.rs:325-338) picks up override materials automatically. Share the FORMAT_VERSION bump with 03, 10 and 15 within one release. Pointers: writer.rs:356-406; schema.rs:240-257; reader.rs element reading; conformance/check.ts:82-100; the 'Add a sample/golden model' extension point. Consistency with solid-kernel-ops-07: that task keeps writing each closed part with its part material because of IFX-032; this task changes the rule for user face overrides only, and SOL-026 runs follow only if the product owner accepts the body-group reading for them too (follow-up bead). Fallback if the body-group reading is rejected: keep closed single-material parts, persist faceOverrides in archicraft:: only, and ask the product owner to waive the 'exports per-part materials' clause of the epic acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs face_overrides_round_trip: overrides on walls, slabs and openings survive with Project equality; the existing goldens stay byte-identical.
- In the showcase golden the F2 wall has Skin_1..Skin_6 plus the end-face parts of skins 1-6 referencing the override material, the skin parts still reference the skin materials, and every material node carries Name, diffuseColor and opacity (IFX-040, IFX-043).
- Every body group is closed and 2-manifold after merging coincident points; conformance/run.sh passes and the reference viewer shows the override colours (Playwright step of regression-and-status where present).
- A hand-edited file with a dangling override material loads with one warning and the element keeps its other overrides.
- In the showcase golden the roof's Plane child carries Skin_1 plus Skin_1_top referencing the Top override material; solid-operation runs (SOL-026) are not written as face parts (they stay derived, as solid-kernel-ops-07 decided).
- Satisfies the IFCX parts of MAT-004 and OPN-008 and the 'exports per-part materials' clause of the epic acceptance.
notes:
SRS: MAT-004 OPN-008
Open question for the product owner: confirm the body-group reading of IFX-032 for face-override parts (proposed SRS wording: 'the union of a part and its face-override parts shall be closed'); a single closed part per material region is impossible without changing geometry.

title: Add DisplayStyle resources with the seven shipped presets
description:
WHY: VIEW-051 (S): named display styles shall be project resources that bundle the display mode, transparency, an optional monochrome override, background colours, edge settings and shadows, applied per view; shipped presets: shaded, simple shaded, white model (with and without shadows), hidden line, wireframe and technical drawing. VIEW-050 (M) asks for adjustable edge thickness and a switch that turns transparency off for performance; VIEW-056 (S) for solid or gradient sky and ground backgrounds; VIEW-052 (S) makes shadows switchable per style; VIEW-053 (S) makes higher-quality lighting selectable. Gap rows: VIEW-051 missing (DisplayMode is a transient per-view enum in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:25-57, chosen in the status bar ui/shell.rs:199-205, no presets, no persistence); VIEW-056 missing (one of two constants in views/view3d.rs:93-99); VIEW-050 partial (no edge thickness, no transparency switch). plan-views-browser-07 defines ViewDefinition.style: Option<ViewStyle {mode: RenderMode}> in crates/archicraft-model/src/views.rs and allows this epic to add optional fields only.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/display.rs: DisplayStyle {id: DisplayStyleId, name, description, mode: RenderMode (the model enum of plan-views-browser-07), edges: EdgeSettings {thickness_pt, silhouette_thickness_pt: Option<f32>, color: Option<Rgb> (None = theme edge colour)}, transparency: bool, monochrome: Option<Monochrome {color: Rgb, keep_glass: bool}>, background: Background {Canvas | Solid(Rgb) | Gradient {sky_zenith, sky_horizon, ground_horizon, ground_nadir}}, shadows: bool, lighting: Lighting {Standard | High {ambient_occlusion, soft_shadows, sky_light}}}; DisplayStyleId through id_type! in ids.rs; Project.display_styles: Vec<DisplayStyle> plus default_style for new 3D viewpoints. ViewStyle gains style: Option<DisplayStyleId>; ViewStyle::resolve(&Project) -> (ResolvedStyle, Option<ViewIssue>) falls back to a style synthesised from mode when the id is absent or dangling. Commands AddDisplayStyle, UpdateDisplayStyle, DuplicateDisplayStyle and DeleteDisplayStyle {id, replacement} (an in-use style needs a replacement as DSP-003 asks for attributes; referencing views are re-pointed in the same undo step; the last style cannot be deleted) on an Edit::SetDisplayStyles snapshot; ranges in validate.rs. crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs creates the seven presets. Out of scope: IFCX (03), rendering (04-08), UI (09), sun settings (02), display overrides (15).
design: Plain serde data without UI dependency (NFR-MNT-002); Rgb from material.rs. RenderMode stays the single source of mode names; the app maps it to DisplayMode (render3d.rs:25) until 04 replaces that enum. Background::Canvas means 'use the user's model canvas preference' (UI-010, task 17), so presets do not hard-code a theme colour and a project looks right in light and dark themes. ResolvedStyle is a flat Copy + Hash struct (floats hashed by bits) that the renderer puts into FrameKey (render3d.rs:233-240). Edit::SetDisplayStyles {styles, default_style, views} keeps delete-with-replacement atomic; follow the 'Add a command' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md and the replacement pattern of plan_delete_material in command.rs. Pitfalls: keep presets ordered as in VIEW-051 so pickers and goldens are stable; never index styles by position in views, only by id.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/display.rs: the default template contains exactly the seven presets in VIEW-051 order with unique names (Shaded, Simple shaded, White model, White model with shadows, Hidden line, Wireframe, Technical drawing), each valid; the two white models differ only in shadows and lighting.
- Add, update, duplicate and delete are one undo step each and execute + undo restores the project (pattern of crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs); an identical update is NoChange; edge thickness outside 0.25-8 pt, colour components outside 0..1 and empty or duplicate names are rejected and leave the project untouched.
- Deleting a style referenced by a ViewDefinition without a replacement fails with an 'in use' error; with a replacement every referencing view points to it after the command and back after undo; deleting the last remaining style fails.
- ViewStyle::resolve returns the referenced style; a dangling id yields the mode-synthesised style plus one ViewIssue and never panics; a view without a style id behaves as today (mode only).
- New projects get fresh preset ids (every_project_gets_new_identities pattern, template.rs:405); existing round-trip tests and goldens stay green because the writer ignores the new fields until 03.
- Provides the data model of VIEW-051 and the style-level switches of VIEW-050 (edge thickness, transparency), VIEW-052 (shadows), VIEW-053 (lighting quality) and VIEW-056 (background).
notes:
SRS: VIEW-051 VIEW-050 VIEW-052 VIEW-053 VIEW-056
Appendix D has no display-style values. Proposed preset definitions for product-owner confirmation: Shaded = mode shaded with edges 1 pt, transparency on, shadows on, standard lighting, gradient sky background; Simple shaded = mode shaded without edges, no shadows, canvas background; White model = monochrome white with glass kept transparent, edges 1 pt, no shadows, canvas; White model with shadows = the same with shadows and high lighting (ambient occlusion, soft shadows, sky light); Hidden line = edges 1 pt black on canvas; Wireframe = edges 1 pt; Technical drawing = hidden line with crease edges 1 pt and silhouettes 2 pt, transparency off. Default style for new 3D viewpoints: Shaded.

title: Model per-face material overrides with face roles and commands
description:
WHY: MAT-004 (S): faces of construction elements shall accept a material override for appearance only, without changing the skin material - a wall's reference side, opposite side and end faces; a slab's top, bottom and edges; a roof's top, bottom and edges; opening reveals. OPN-008 (S): the faces an opening creates (reveal and end faces) default to the materials of the cut elements and are overridable separately, also when an opening face coincides with a skin boundary. Decision D-5 relies on per-face overrides instead of split materials. Gap rows: MAT-004 and OPN-008 missing - geometry has one single-material part per element or skin (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:21-28) and no element carries face materials.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model: FaceRole {ReferenceSide, OppositeSide, Ends, Top, Bottom, Edges, Sides, Reveal, OpeningEnd} with code() and ALL; the Element envelope (element-kind-framework) gains face_overrides: BTreeMap<FaceRole, MaterialId> (serde default empty); each kind declares its supported roles through the kind registry: walls ReferenceSide, OppositeSide, Ends, Top, Bottom, Reveal; slabs Top, Bottom, Edges, Reveal; openings Reveal and OpeningEnd, applying to the faces they create in every cut element; doors and windows (doors-windows-core) Reveal, applying to the reveal faces their void cuts; columns and beams Ends and Sides; roofs (kinds/roof.rs of the roofs epic, increment 2) Top, Bottom, Edges, Reveal. Command SetFaceOverride {ids, role, material: Option<MaterialId>} as one undo step (ReplaceElement edits, applied to the selected elements that support the role, Invalid if none does, NoChange if equal); wall and slab tool defaults carry face overrides too (UI-003 edits defaults with the same fields). Material deletion counts face overrides as uses and replaces them (DSP-003). Pure precedence function face_material(project, element, part_material, role, owner) -> MaterialId: the creating opening's (or door's or window's) override, then the element's own override, then the part (skin) material; the owner may be an opening that cuts the element as a further cut element (OPN-002, solid-kernel-ops-13), so its override reaches every element it cuts. Out of scope: geometry tagging (12), IFCX (13), UI (14).
design: A BTreeMap gives deterministic order for IFCX and equality. Keeping overrides on the element and the opening, not in geometry, means an override never invalidates the geometry cache: the incremental evaluator of element-kind-framework must not mark elements dirty for SetFaceOverride (asserted with the evaluation counter in 12). FaceRole::Reveal on a host means all reveal faces in that element, on an opening the reveals that opening creates; OpeningEnd is the back face of a limited opening (niche) or a recess floor. Follow the 'Add a command' extension point and reuse the in-use counting of plan_delete_material (command.rs). Pitfall: copy, paste and parameter transfer (templates-presets) must carry face_overrides - they live on the envelope, so cloning covers them; the copy test guards it.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: SetFaceOverride on a wall's Ends is one undo step and execute + undo restores the project; layer structure, skin materials and every geometric parameter are unchanged (appearance only).
- A wall-plus-slab selection with role Top applies to both; with Ends it applies to the wall only; Ends on slabs only is Invalid; an unchanged value is NoChange; locked elements follow the Locked semantics of the command extension point.
- Deleting a material used only by a face override requires a replacement and re-points the override; undo restores it.
- face_material precedence: an opening's Reveal override beats the host's Reveal override, which beats the skin material; without overrides the skin material is returned (OPN-008 default); copying an element keeps its overrides.
- Validation rejects an unsupported role for a kind and a dangling material; existing goldens unchanged (empty maps are not written until 13).
- Role table test over the kind registry: walls, slabs, roofs, columns, beams, openings, doors and windows declare exactly the documented roles; Top on a roof is accepted, Edges on a wall is Invalid; the opening's Reveal override also wins on a further cut element listed in its cut list.
- Provides the data model of MAT-004 and OPN-008.
notes:
SRS: MAT-004 OPN-008
Decision proposed: one 'Ends' role covers both wall ends (MAT-004 names end faces collectively); per-end overrides can follow on request.

title: Verify exit criterion: Display styles, sun, lighting, backgrounds, face materials and themes
description:
WHY: Closes the epic by verifying its exit criterion on the merged state: Snapshot tests for the four display modes and every shipped style on RM-S; the shadow pass toggles per style and the sun computed for a given location, date and time matches an astronomical reference within 0.5°; sorted transparent faces render overlapping glass correctly; a face override on a wall end changes appearance only and exports per-part materials; the 'colour by storey' and 'poché' override presets; a contrast check passes on both themes; the canvas background is a preference. It covers VIEW-050, VIEW-051, VIEW-052, VIEW-053, VIEW-056, DSP-016, MAT-004, MAT-008, OPN-008, IFX-042, UI-010 and NFR-A11Y-003.

WHAT: Run the full acceptance end to end (RM-S goldens of 19, shadow toggle counters and solar reference tests of 02/07, overlapping-glass golden of 05, face tagging of 12 and 20 (walls, slabs, roofs, columns, beams, reveals of host and further cuts), face-override round trip and conformance of 13, roughness shading of 22, the Poché and Colour-by-storey goldens of 16 and the rule editor of 21, the theme audits of 17/18, the canvas preference test); run the workspace quality gates and conformance on every golden file; update docs/implementation-status.md for all twelve requirement IDs with status, file:line evidence and any remaining gap; file beads for leftovers (for example roof face roles if the roof kind arrived late, the order-independent transparency fallback, per-end wall overrides, picking faces in 3D to assign materials); close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new features.
design: Verification only. Use the per-merge status check of regression-and-status (srs_ids against changed rows of docs/implementation-status.md) and scripts/status.py if present to regenerate the table from gap-analysis data. Record measured frame times (07, 08) and platform tolerance observations (19) in the status evidence. Follow the session-completion protocol of the repository's CLAUDE.md: conservative profile - report changed files, validation and proposed git commands, commit or push only with explicit authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- Snapshot tests for the four display modes and every shipped style on RM-S pass on all three CI platforms within tolerance.
- The shadow pass toggles per style (draw counters) and the sun computed for a given location, date and time matches an astronomical reference within 0.5° (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/solar.rs).
- Sorted transparent faces render overlapping glass correctly (overlapping_glass golden from two opposite cameras).
- A face override on a wall end changes appearance only (geometry, skin materials and plan output unchanged) and exports per-part materials (face_overrides_showcase golden).
- The 'colour by storey' and 'poché' override presets render as specified in 3D and plan goldens and leave the saved file byte-identical.
- A contrast check passes on both themes (theme_contrast and cvd_highlights); the canvas background is a preference (kittest).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden (including the re-blessed goldens and face-overrides-showcase).
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (VIEW-050 VIEW-051 VIEW-052 VIEW-053 VIEW-056 DSP-016 MAT-004 MAT-008 OPN-008 IFX-042 UI-010 NFR-A11Y-003) and the status check of regression-and-status passes.
- The epic 3d-display-styles is closed in beads with follow-up beads filed for remaining work.
notes: SRS: VIEW-050 VIEW-051 VIEW-052 VIEW-053 VIEW-056 DSP-016 MAT-004 MAT-008 OPN-008 IFX-042 UI-010 NFR-A11Y-003

title: Edit face materials in the properties panel and settings dialogs
description:
WHY: MAT-004 (S) and OPN-008 (S) need a way to set per-face materials on walls, slabs (and roofs, columns and beams where present) and on openings (reveal and end faces). UI-002 (M): the properties panel edits all editable selected elements and marks differing values; UI-003 (M): the settings dialog's model and appearance section edits tool defaults and selections with the same fields. Today appearance_fields (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:466, section at :714) offers only the element material.

WHAT: properties.rs: a 'Face materials' group in the Model and appearance section listing the roles supported by every selected kind (the intersection for mixed selections), each with a material picker whose first entry is 'Skin material' (no override), mixed values marked; roofs show Top, Bottom, Edges and Reveals; doors and windows show 'Reveal material'; openings show 'Reveal material' and 'End face material' with the hint 'default: material of the cut element'; edits issue SetFaceOverride, one undo step per field; the same group in the settings dialog for wall and slab tool defaults. The 3D view updates immediately without geometry re-evaluation. Out of scope: assigning a material by picking a face in 3D (possible follow-up bead).
design: Follow the Fields getter/setter pattern of properties.rs (a field hides when its getter returns None) with the role list from the kind registry; the material picker reuses widgets::choice with colour swatches (the MAT-006 browser style if available). The appearance generation added to SceneKey in 12 makes build_scene rerun although geometry is unchanged. Pointers: properties.rs:466-520 and 700-745; dialogs.rs settings_window (:628); workspace.rs:44-47.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: selecting a wall shows Reference side, Opposite side, End faces, Top, Bottom and Reveals pickers; choosing Brick for End faces issues one SetFaceOverride, the geometry evaluation counter is unchanged and the 3D scene is rebuilt.
- kittest: a wall-plus-slab selection shows only the shared roles; differing values show the mixed marker; setting a value applies to both.
- kittest: an opening shows Reveal material and End face material with the default hint; setting the reveal recolours the reveal faces in all cut skins (scene vertex colours).
- The settings dialog edits the wall tool defaults' face overrides and a newly drawn wall carries them.
- All labels are externalised strings and exposed to AccessKit (NFR-A11Y-002).
- kittest: selecting a roof shows Top, Bottom, Edges and Reveals pickers, and an Edges material recolours the eaves and verge faces only (scene vertex colours); a window shows the Reveal material picker.
- Satisfies the UI parts of MAT-004 and OPN-008.
notes: SRS: MAT-004 OPN-008

title: Initialise GitHub repo with CC BY 4.0 license and minimal README
description: Add LICENSE (CC BY 4.0) and a minimal README.md, push history to github.com/Graficraft/ArchiCraft main.

title: Sum selection quantities per kind, union area and opening voids
description:
WHY: MEA-002 (S): for the current selection the system shall show length, area, height and volume where applicable, summed over the selected elements of one kind, including the length of a selected polyline or spline. MEA-004 (C): the plan-projected union area of a selection may be measurable (roof coverage without double-counting overlaps). OPN-011 (C): the net void volume of an opening within the elements it cuts may be reported, for example the excavation volume of an opening in terrain (MEA-002). Gap rows: MEA-002 partial - exists and is kept: derived() in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/properties.rs:541-575 shows wall Length, slab Area and Volume for exactly one selected element (`let [id] = ids.as_slice()` at :543-546), which properties-and-dialogs-08 turns into ElementGeometry.quantities rendered through ui/fields.rs; missing: height, sums over several elements of one kind, curve lengths of polylines and splines; MEA-004 missing (geo::unary_union is already used at crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:156), OPN-011 missing (TriMesh::signed_volume at mesh.rs:105 can measure once the void inside each cut element is known). The epic acceptance requires selection quantities summed per kind.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/quantities.rs (introduced by properties-and-dialogs-08) gains `selection_quantities(project, geometry, ids) -> Vec<KindQuantities { kind, count, length, area, height: Option<HeightSummary { min, max }>, volume }>`: length from the per-element Quantity keys (wall reference-line length, column and beam axis length) and exact curve lengths of 2D elements (lines, arcs and polylines from the curve.rs parameters, splines from their tessellation), area from slab top areas, roof plane areas and drafting fill areas, height per element (walls, columns, openings) summarised as a min-max range, volume as net body volume; `union_area(project, geometry, ids) -> f64` projecting every non-vertical triangle of the selected bodies (Void parts excluded) and 2D fills to plan and uniting them with geo BooleanOps; `opening_void_volume(project, geometry, opening) -> Result<VoidVolume { per_element: Vec<(ElementId, f64)>, total }>` computed as the volume difference of each cut element evaluated with and without the opening (DeleteElements planned and applied to a scratch clone through Edit::apply_all, then evaluation of the cut elements only), so it holds for 2D-cut and kernel-cut openings alike. App: extend the derived-values section of the properties panel instead of adding a parallel one: single selections keep their existing per-element rows and gain a Height row (walls, columns, openings), selections of two or more elements show a 'Selection quantities' block, one row per kind such as 'Walls (3): length 12.000 m, height 2.800-3.000 m, volume 9.000 m3', a 'Plan union area' row computed on demand for large selections and cached by (revision, selection), and 'Net void volume' with a per-element tooltip among an opening's derived values, formatted with format_length, format_area and format_volume. Out of scope: quantity take-off and schedules (Section 8), base quantities in IFCX (ifcx-interop).
design: Sums come from the cached per-element quantities of the incremental evaluator, so the panel costs one pass over the selection; union area and void volume are on demand because they can be expensive for large selections. Computing the void by difference avoids a Boolean kernel and stays correct when solid-kernel-ops lets openings cut further elements (OPN-002) and when terrain hosts openings (OPN-012 in members-profiles-adv). Summing heights is meaningless, so heights are shown as a range, recorded as the interpretation of 'height where applicable'. Pitfalls: Void parts never count into body volumes; layered walls sum all skins; the scratch clone must not touch History or the open document; height summaries use vertical_extent, not mesh bounds. Pointers: quantities.rs and ElementGeometry.quantities (properties-and-dialogs-08), properties.rs:542-575 (today's derived()), mesh.rs:105 (signed_volume), plan.rs:150-163 (unary_union), curve.rs lengths (drafting-trim-split-01), kinds/opening.rs (host-openings-01), units.rs format_area and format_volume.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: three walls of 5.00, 4.00 and 3.00 m plus two slabs give Walls count 3, length 12.000 and the sum of their body volumes, and Slabs count 2 with the summed top area; a polyline with straight edges of 2.00 and 3.00 m and a quarter-arc edge of radius 1.00 has length 5 + pi/2 within 1e-12; a spline's length is within the tessellation tolerance.
- union_area: two 10 x 10 m slabs overlapping by 5 x 10 m give 150.000 m2 while their summed area is 200.000 m2; a single slab equals its plan area.
- opening_void_volume: a 1.00 x 1.00 m through-opening in a 0.25 m wall gives 0.250 m3; a limited niche 0..0.40 m in a 0.50 m wall gives 0.400 m3; an opening partly beyond the wall end counts only the part inside; a shaft through two slabs lists both slabs with their shares.
- Regression: a single selected wall keeps its existing derived rows (Length, Volume and the rows of properties-and-dialogs-08) and gains Height 3.000 m.
- kittest (epic acceptance): selecting three walls of heights 2.80 and 3.00 m shows the Walls row with count 3, summed length and 'height 2.800-3.000 m'; selecting a polyline and a spline shows their summed curve length; adding a slab adds a Slabs row; reducing the selection to one element shows its single-element derived rows.
- MEA-002, MEA-004 and OPN-011 satisfied.
notes: SRS: MEA-002 MEA-004 OPN-011. Interpretation: heights are summarised as a range, not summed. Relies on the Quantity list of properties-and-dialogs-08 (increment 1, outside this fragment's declared prerequisites); if it is missing, add the per-kind quantities here.

title: Add element labels with dynamic name, material, structure and elevation fields
description:
WHY: ANN-008 (C): element labels may show an element's name, material, layer structure or elevation as dynamic fields that update with the model. SRS 3.3: an annotation binding references element geometry or a datum, so labels are associative like dimensions; Section 8 keeps property labels and keynotes out of v1, so labels stay limited to these fields. ANN-009 (S): a label copied with its element refers to the copy, copied alone it keeps the original. Gap row ANN-008 (M, missing): no label exists; the binding (task 13), the text styles and layout (task 16) and the copy remap (task 17) are in place when this task starts.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/label.rs registered with one kinds! line: Label (code 'label', prefix 'LB') { view: DraftingView, target: DimPoint::Bound (FeatureKey::Centre or a picked feature), offset: DVec2 (paper mm from the target's view position), leader: bool, fields: Vec<LabelField { Name, Material, LayerStructure, Elevation { surface: SurfaceRole, origin: LevelOrigin }, Literal(String) }>, style: TextStyleId }, has_body = false and ifcx_node = false, its codec in archicraft::annotations (task 02); it derives AnnotationBinding through Kind::bindings() (task 13) and implements the remap_ids hook of task 17. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/annotation.rs evaluates label text in the annotation pass from the current model (Name: element name; Material: the material name, the core skin's material for layered elements; LayerStructure: the structure name or 'Single material'; Elevation: z of the Surface feature (slabs, task 12) or of the base or top from Project::vertical_extent (walls, columns) relative to the origin, formatted in the app with format_elevation) and flags a lost target like a dimension (Unresolved, problems-panel entry, '?' at the fallback position). App: a Label tool in plan and section views (pick an element, place the text box; the leader runs from the target to the box), drawn with the text layout of task 16 through views/annotation_draw.rs, and a field-list editor in the properties (add, remove, reorder, literal text). Out of scope: property labels, keynotes and schedules (Section 8), labels in 3D views.
design: Labels evaluate in the same annotation pass as dimensions and so share dirty propagation (dependents_of via AnnotationBinding), flagging and fallback positions; field values are recomputed, never stored, which is what makes them dynamic. The offset is in paper mm so the label keeps its distance from the element at any drawing scale. Pitfalls: attribute edits (material or structure renames) must mark label dependents dirty through the in-use queries of plan-attributes and layer-structures; never format values in the model or geometry crate; a label in a section resolves 3D features and projects them with the marker frame. Pointers: kinds/dimension.rs and annotation.rs (task 13), features.rs (task 12), text.rs and the layout helper (task 16), remap_ids (task 17), layer-structures-01 (structure names, core skin), attributes.rs in-use queries (plan-attributes).
acceptance_criteria:
- Label dynamics (model plus annotation.rs tests): a label on a wall shows its name and updates after a rename; the material field follows a material change; the layer-structure field shows the structure name and follows a structure swap; an elevation field on a slab top follows an offset change and the chosen origin (project zero, storey, sea level and user reference level with the values of the task 13 fixture); a literal field is kept verbatim.
- Renaming a material or a layer structure re-evaluates the labels that show it although no element geometry changed.
- Deleting the wall flags the label (problems-panel entry, '?' text) instead of showing stale values; undo resolves it again.
- Copy semantics (task 17 rule): a label copied with its wall shows the copy's name; copied alone it keeps showing the original's name.
- kittest: the Label tool places a label on a wall in plan and on a wall in a section; the label uses its text style and follows a style edit in the Text styles dialog.
- IFCX round trip of resolved and unresolved labels; golden annotations.ifcx extended; the standard content is unchanged.
- ANN-008 satisfied (ANN-009 asserted for labels).
notes: SRS: ANN-008 (also asserts ANN-009 for labels). Split from sections-elevations-dims-16. Proposals: prefix LB; default fields Name only; leader on.

title: Project bodies beyond the section plane with depth clipping and painter order
description:
WHY: VIEW-030 (S): section and elevation views use the same cut and projection rules as plans (VIEW-010: elements beyond the cut are drawn projected with uncut lines), the marker's depth limits how far the view looks and its optional horizontal limits clip it; an elevation is a view line that only projects.
