Gap row VIEW-030 (XL, missing): mesh.rs offers only plan-facing outlines (up_facing_outline and down_facing_outline, mesh.rs:196-205) and feature_edges (mesh.rs:239, used by the 3D view at crates/archicraft-app/src/views/render3d.rs:164); there is no projection onto a vertical plane, no depth clipping and no hidden-line handling. Epic risk: VIEW-030 is extra large and hidden-line removal stays simple (depth-ordered painting) in v1. Task 03 delivers the cut half and the SectionDrawing structure; this task fills its projected parts and painter list.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/section.rs: section_element fills `projected: Vec<ProjectedPart { material, depth_near, fills: Vec<[DVec2; 3]>, edges: Vec<[DVec2; 2]> }>` for every body part (Void parts excluded) beyond the plane: triangles are clipped to the slab 0 <= d <= depth (unlimited depth = no far plane) and to the two horizontal limit planes (Sutherland-Hodgman), back faces culled, and projected to (u, v); the part's feature edges (mesh.rs feature_edges with the 1 degree crease angle of the 3D view) are clipped the same way. Parts crossing the plane contribute only their side beyond the plane when cut = true and project whole when cut = false (elevations); parts entirely beyond the depth limit are skipped. assemble() builds the painter list `faces`: parts sorted far to near by depth_near (ties by element order, then part index), each part's fills in the background tone followed by its edges, cut regions last; bounds and content_hash include projected geometry; pick() falls back to projected parts nearest first after the cut parts. A criterion bench section_drawing on RM-S (or the synthetic stand-in of element-kind-framework-03) joins the regression harness. Out of scope: exact hidden-line removal (follow-up bead for an edge-versus-depth visibility test), level lines and grid axes (04), on-screen drawing (06).
design: Projection per triangle uses Sutherland-Hodgman against the near plane d = 0 (so parts crossing the plane keep only their far side), the far plane d = depth and the two limit planes; points are mapped with the same MarkerFrame convention as the cut (u.(p - O), p.z), so cut and projected geometry line up exactly. Painter granularity is the body part (all its fills, then its edges), because per-triangle painting cuts crease edges in half; fills carry the background tone so nearer parts hide farther edges without a depth buffer, and the GPU upload of task 06 keeps the order. Known v1 limitation, accepted by the epic risk: hidden edges of a non-convex part can show through its own faces and parts interleaved in depth can paint in the wrong order. Pitfalls: drop degenerate triangles after clipping (area below MODEL_TOLERANCE squared); triangles exactly in the plane belong to the cut, not the projection; back-face test with the outward normal (normal.n >= 0 culled); keep section_element pure so Document can cache it. Pointers: mesh.rs:196-260 (facing outlines, feature_edges), views/render3d.rs:164 (crease angle), section.rs and drawing.rs (task 03), plan-renderer-06 (ordered fill batches), element-kind-framework-03 (synthetic stand-in).
acceptance_criteria:
- On two_storey_shell, a section perpendicular to the exterior walls: walls beyond the plane appear only as projected parts with their visible faces and feature edges, the wall crossing the plane contributes its cut region and only its far side as projected geometry, and walls behind the plane are absent.
- A depth limit excludes an element entirely beyond it and clips one straddling it at exactly that depth (clipped edge ends at d = depth within 1e-9); unlimited depth keeps everything beyond the plane.
- Custom limits clip projected fills and edges to the u-interval; an elevation (cut = false) projects the walls crossing its line as whole parts and has no cut regions.
- Back faces never appear: a closed box beyond the plane and facing it yields exactly its front face (two fill triangles) and its four outline edges.
- Painter order: parts are ordered far to near with stable ties and cut regions come last; two evaluations give identical faces lists and hashes.
- Moving a wall that is only projected changes content_hash(); crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/golden/section-hashes.txt is re-blessed (ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1) with a reviewed diff for the projected content of the task 03 RM-S cases.
- The section_drawing bench runs on RM-S; re-slicing one element plus assemble stays within the NFR-PERF-006 200 ms budget on the reference machine (recorded; provisional for sections).
- VIEW-030 'same projection rules as plans', the depth and the optional horizontal limits satisfied in geometry.
notes: SRS: VIEW-030 (geometry: projection, depth and horizontal limits). Split from sections-elevations-dims-03. RM-S comes from reference-models (increment 2), outside this fragment; the bench falls back to the synthetic stand-in when it is missing.

title: Bind level dimensions to roof and terrain surfaces
description:
WHY: ANN-005 (S): level dimensions 'on slabs, roofs and terrain' are associative and can measure the top, the bottom or the top of the core. Tasks 12-14 deliver the slab case and the generic Surface feature path; roofs (roofs-01: RoofReference { Bottom, Top, CoreTop }, plane bodies of roofs-02/05) and terrain (terrain-and-site-03/04: the TIN surface and TerrainBottom) are increment-2 kinds that register their surfaces through the same hooks. Gap row ANN-005 (M, missing) lists TER-001 and the PRF layer structures among its dependencies.

WHAT: Roof features: the roof geometry generator publishes, per roof plane, `FeatureKey::Kind(RoofSurface { plane: usize, role: SurfaceRole })` as FeatureGeom::Plane for Top, Bottom and CoreTop (the core skin's top of the roof's layer structure, measured perpendicular to the plane as in ROF-007), with remap_feature mapping plane indices through roof edits and reporting Lost when a plane disappears. Terrain features: `FeatureKey::Surface { role: Top }` resolves at the annotation's plan position through the TIN (FeatureGeom::Plane of the triangle under the point, so the value follows terrain edits), `Surface { role: Bottom }` from TerrainBottom; CoreTop on terrain is refused with a message. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/annotation.rs evaluates a plane feature at the level dimension's anchor (z of the plane at the anchor's plan position). Tool: the LevelDimension surface cycling of task 14 (Top, Bottom, CoreTop) offers the roof and terrain roles in plan and section views. Out of scope: curved roofs, terrain features for linear dimensions.
design: Roof planes are numbered in the roof's own plane order (single-plane roofs: plane 0), which derives from the pivot polygon's edges and survives regeneration, never from mesh faces; terrain surfaces resolve on demand at the anchor because a TIN has no single plane. Reusing the hooks of task 12 keeps annotation.rs unchanged apart from evaluating plane features at an anchor. Pitfalls: perpendicular thickness versus vertical offset on pitched planes (use the plane geometry, not thickness arithmetic); keep the plane order stable through roofs-10 edits; terrain re-tiling (terrain-and-site-05) must not change resolved values. Pointers: features.rs (task 12), annotation.rs and kinds/dimension.rs (task 13), tools/dimension.rs (task 14), roofs-01/02/05 (RoofShape, RoofReference, plane bodies), terrain-and-site-03/04 (Terrain payload, TIN).
acceptance_criteria:
- A single-plane roof with pitch 35 degrees, pivot elevation +5.80 and 0.30 m thickness: a level dimension bound to its Top at a point 2.00 m upslope of the pivot line reads the analytic plane height (within 1e-9 before display rounding), Bottom reads the underside plane at the same plan point, and CoreTop on a layered roof reads the top plane of its core skin.
- Changing the roof pitch or pivot elevation updates the bound value; splitting the roof so that the bound plane disappears (roofs-13) flags the dimension as lost.
- On a sloped terrain, a level dimension bound to Top reads the interpolated TIN height at its point; moving a terrain point updates it; Bottom reads the terrain bottom; CoreTop is refused at placement with the message; a point outside the terrain boundary is Unresolved, never extrapolated.
- The four origins of task 13 apply unchanged to roof and terrain values.
- kittest: the level-dimension tool cycles Top, Bottom and CoreTop on a roof in plan and shows the fixture values.
- The roof and terrain clause of ANN-005 satisfied.
notes: SRS: ANN-005 (roof and terrain surfaces). Dependency note: roofs and terrain-and-site are increment-2 epics, completed before this increment-3 epic but not declared prerequisites of it, so this fragment cannot reference roofs-done or terrain-and-site-done; confirm both are closed before starting, otherwise leave this task open and ANN-005 partial in the status report.

title: Copy associative annotations with or without their elements
description:
WHY: ANN-009 (S): when an associative annotation is copied together with its element, the copy shall refer to the copied element; when the annotation is copied alone, it shall keep referring to the original element. Gap row ANN-009 (M, missing): Project::duplicate (selection-transforms-03) drops relations whose ends are not both in the copied set, which would make a dimension copied alone lose its reference, and nothing remaps payload references for annotations.

WHAT: A kind hook `remap_ids(&mut self, map: &IdRemap)` over the IdRemap of selection-transforms-03 (crates/archicraft-model/src/ids.rs), called from the copy path that host-openings-13 built (copy::duplicate in crates/archicraft-model/src/copy.rs, which re-points hosted copies through Kind::carry) after the map holds every copied element, implemented by the linear and level dimension kinds of task 13 (tasks 15 and 21 implement it for angle dimensions and labels): Bound targets present in the map are replaced by the copy's id, targets outside the map stay unchanged. Every copy path routes through it: Command::Transform with copy and multiple copy, arrays and path distribution (drafting-trim-split-14), and paste (selection-transforms-13) in the same project, including paste onto another storey. A dimension copied alone with a transform moves its free points, offset and fallbacks while its bound points keep resolving on the original element. Cross-project paste (the SW-003 clipboard payload): bindings to elements absent from the destination become free points at their fallback positions, reported once ('3 dimension points lost their reference'). Out of scope: the multi-window paste UI (library-dw-exchange), implicitly copying annotations that are not selected (they are not copied).
design: Because bindings live in the payload (task 13), copy semantics reduce to remapping ids during duplicate; no relation edits and no special case in the transform command. The rule is the default for annotation kinds and documented on the hook. Pitfalls: the IdRemap must contain every element of the copied set before remapping (hosts, hosted openings and annotations in one pass); arrays create one map per copy; fallbacks are transformed with the copy so a later flag is drawn where the copy is. Pointers: Project::duplicate and Command::Transform (selection-transforms-03), clipboard.rs (selection-transforms-13), host-openings-13 copy::duplicate (copy.rs), selection-transforms-03 IdRemap (ids.rs), drafting-trim-split-14 array planners, kinds/dimension.rs (task 13).
acceptance_criteria:
- Command tests: copying a wall and its dimension by (0, 5.00) creates a dimension bound to the copied wall (moving the copied wall changes only the copy's value); copying the dimension alone keeps it bound to the original wall (moving the original updates both dimensions); multiple copy x3 and a linear array of wall plus dimension each bind their own wall; undo removes the copies.
- Level dimensions follow the same rules on slabs.
- Paste in the same project and onto another storey follows the rules; paste into a fresh project converts the bindings to free points and reports their count.
- Copying a dimension whose target was deleted earlier keeps the copy unresolved (flagged).
- ANN-009 satisfied (angle dimensions and labels assert it again in tasks 15 and 21).
notes: SRS: ANN-009.

title: Add the geometry clean-up check for duplicates and overlaps
description:
WHY: MEA-005 (S): a geometry clean-up check shall find duplicate and overlapping elements of the same kind (for example two walls on top of each other) and elements with failed geometry, list them, navigate to each, and drop entries once they are fixed. Gap row MEA-005 partial - exists and is kept: problems_panel (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:847-873) lists ModelGeometry.problems with click-to-select-and-zoom (Request::ZoomTo), and entries drop because Document::geometry re-evaluates per revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-100), extended by element-kind-framework-13/14 (fallback boxes, navigation across storeys); missing: duplicate and overlap detection, an explicit check command and a navigable list with a resolved counter. The epic acceptance: the clean-up check finds two overlapping walls and drops the entry once fixed.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/cleanup.rs: `cleanup_check(project, geometry) -> CleanupReport { entries: Vec<CleanupEntry { key, category: Duplicate | Overlap | Failed, elements, message, location: (StoreyId, DVec2) }> }`. Broad phase on absolute AABBs per kind with sort-and-sweep along x; narrow phase: Duplicate when two elements of one kind on one storey have equal parameters within MODEL_TOLERANCE (kind hook `same_geometry(&self, other, tol)` with a default comparing body bounds, volume and plan footprint), Overlap when their bodies share more than 1 cm3 (exact for vertical prisms via the intersection area of their plan slices at the middle of the common vertical interval times its height; three slices for non-prismatic bodies, documented as approximate), excluding parts of one element, host and hosted pairs, body-less kinds and pairs touching only at a junction; Failed from ModelGeometry.problems (fallback boxes included). Stable keys (category plus sorted ids) let the UI keep its cursor. App: Action 'Geometry clean-up check' in the Design menu opens a 'Clean-up' tab of the problems panel listing category, element names and message; clicking an entry selects its elements and zooms to them across storeys (the request of element-kind-framework-14), Next and Previous buttons step through entries; while the tab is open the check re-runs when the revision changes (debounced, off the UI thread when it exceeds a frame budget) so fixed entries disappear and a counter shows how many were resolved; 'All clear' when empty. Out of scope: automatic repair, cross-kind clash detection (model checking is out of v1, Section 8).
design: Detection lives headless in the geometry crate so it is testable and reusable by a future model check; the UI only formats and navigates. Plan slices over the common height interval reuse slice.rs and geo intersections and are exact for walls, slabs, columns and beams, the cases users meet; roofs and stairs are covered approximately by three slices. MODEL_TOLERANCE governs parameter equality and a 1 cm3 floor keeps faces touching at junctions out of the list. Pitfalls: junction-trimmed walls touch along faces with zero volume and must not be reported; layered walls are compared as whole elements, not skins; the re-check must not block the UI on large models (debounce plus the incremental geometry cache). Pointers: dialogs.rs:847-873 (problems panel), document.rs:97-121, slice.rs, plan.rs:150-163 (geo union and intersections), evaluate.rs problems map, element-kind-framework-14 (clickable problems across storeys), relations.rs Host and Junction queries.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: two identical walls give one Duplicate entry; a wall shifted 0.10 m across its thickness over another gives Overlap; walls joined at an L or T junction give no entry; a wall and an overlapping slab (different kinds) give no entry; an opening and its host give no entry; a failed element (panicking test kind) gives a Failed entry.
- After moving one overlapping wall away or deleting a duplicate, a re-run has no entry for that pair while the remaining entries keep their keys.
- kittest (epic acceptance): the action opens the Clean-up tab listing the overlap of two walls; clicking it selects both walls and zooms to them; moving one wall away by a typed distance drops the entry and shows the resolved counter.
- Regression: the existing failed-geometry list of the problems panel and its click-to-zoom keep working, and main_window_has_the_parts_of_ui_001 in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs ('No problems') stays green.
- A criterion bench of cleanup_check on RM-S (or the 5,000-element stand-in) joins the regression harness; the re-check after one edit stays interactive (recorded).
- MEA-005 satisfied.
notes: SRS: MEA-005. Proposal: overlap volume floor 1 cm3.

title: Verify exit criterion: Section and elevation views, dimensions, labels and quantities
description:
WHY: The epic closes only when its exit criterion holds as a whole: live section and elevation views driven by markers with storey lines and grid axes, selection and stretching in sections, the four default elevations, associative linear, level and angle dimensions that survive regeneration and are flagged when their reference disappears, copy semantics, text and labels, selection quantities, union area, void volume and the clean-up check. VIEW-030, VIEW-031, VIEW-032, VIEW-058, VIEW-059, GRD-009, OPN-013, WAL-011, ANN-004, ANN-005, ANN-006, ANN-007, ANN-008, ANN-009, ANN-012, MEA-002, MEA-004, MEA-005 and OPN-011 must each be verified and recorded in the status report so the increment-3 readiness is current.

WHAT: Run the full workspace quality gates and the conformance job on every golden file, walk through the epic acceptance with the tests that now exist, update docs/implementation-status.md (the requirement rows of all nineteen IDs (ANN-005 including the roof and terrain clause of task 22) with evidence paths and tests, the 4.4, 4.10, 4.11, 4.17, 4.26 and 4.29 per-section counts, the increment-3 readiness line, and the served clauses of VIEW-003, VIEW-013, SLB-008, ANN-002 and ANN-010), file follow-up beads for anything cut (for example exact hidden-line removal in sections (the task 20 limitation), openings drawn in sections for roofs and beams, and task 22 if roofs or terrain were not yet available), and close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new functionality.
design: Checklist run, no new code: execute the gates, run the reference_models example twice to confirm byte-identical output, re-run the section hash test on RM-S, open a new project and RM-S in the app to confirm the four elevations, a live section with storey lines and grid axes, stretching a wall height with typed input, a flagged dimension after deleting its wall and the clean-up entry dropping after a fix (the automated tests are the evidence; the walk-through is inspection), then edit the status report rows from the tests that now exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- Moving a marker updates its section (slice hash test on RM-S); the section shows labelled storey lines and grid axes; a wall height is stretched in a section with numeric input; a new project has four elevations in the browser; a dimension picked on a wall node follows the wall and is flagged when its reference disappears; level dimensions relative to project zero, storey, sea level and user origin; selection quantities summed per kind; the clean-up check finds two overlapping walls and drops the entry once fixed. Dimension bindings reference element id plus a semantic feature key (face role, node index), never mesh indices, so a regenerated wall keeps its dimensions (test).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on all golden files, including the template-based goldens with the four elevation markers, outline-walls.ifcx and annotations.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (VIEW-030 VIEW-031 VIEW-032 VIEW-058 VIEW-059 GRD-009 OPN-013 WAL-011 ANN-004 ANN-005 ANN-006 ANN-007 ANN-008 ANN-009 ANN-012 MEA-002 MEA-004 MEA-005 OPN-011) with evidence paths and tests.
- Follow-up beads exist for every deferred part and the sections-elevations-dims epic is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: VIEW-030 VIEW-031 VIEW-032 VIEW-058 VIEW-059 GRD-009 OPN-013 WAL-011 ANN-004 ANN-005 ANN-006 ANN-007 ANN-008 ANN-009 ANN-012 MEA-002 MEA-004 MEA-005 OPN-011. Size note: the honest task sum of this epic is well above the roadmap's 15-day cap (gap sizes XL/XL/L x5); the order lets sections (01-08, 20) ship before annotations (12-17, 21, 22) if a second wave is needed; tasks 03 and 16 were split into 03/20 and 16/21 to stay within the 3-day task cap. RM-S comes from reference-models (increment 2), outside this fragment.

title: Add linear and level dimensions with associative bindings
description:
WHY: ANN-004 (S): linear dimensions (horizontal, vertical, aligned, chained) are placed by picking points or an edge and then an offset; the value equals the exact distance in the project unit and precision; points on element nodes or edges are associative and update with the element; a dimension whose reference disappears is flagged instead of showing a stale value. ANN-005 (S): level dimensions show the elevation of a picked point or element surface relative to a selectable origin (project zero, storey elevation, sea level or user origin), and on slabs, roofs and terrain they are associative and measure top, bottom or top of core. SRS 3.3: annotation bindings are stored with the model, kept across save and open and re-evaluated automatically; ANN-010: dimensions are stored in the ArchiCraft namespace only; NFR-ACC-005: values are rounded only for display. Gap rows ANN-004 (L) and ANN-005 (M): no dimension kind, no binding relation; Location.altitude (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:63-72) is the only datum, extended to reference levels by properties-and-dialogs-03.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/dimension.rs with LinearDimension (code 'dimension', prefix 'DM') { view: DraftingView, direction: DimDirection { Fixed(angle), Aligned }, points: Vec<DimPoint> (two or more; more = chain), offset, style: DimStyle { pen, text_size_mm, tick: Tick { Slash, Arrow, Dot }, gap_mm, overshoot_mm } } and LevelDimension (code 'level', prefix 'LV') { view, at: DimPoint, origin: LevelOrigin { Level(LevelRef), Storey(StoreyId) }, symbol } reusing LevelRef { ProjectZero, SeaLevel, User(LevelId) } of properties-and-dialogs-03 (levels.rs), where `DimPoint { Free(DVec3), Bound { target: ElementId, feature: FeatureKey, fallback: DVec3 } }`; both kinds have has_body = false and ifcx_node = false. Bindings are derived from the payload (Kind::bindings()) and indexed by the relation store as AnnotationBinding { annotation, target, feature } through the derived-index pattern used for storey links (element-kind-framework-08), so dependents_of(target) finds dimensions and incremental evaluation re-evaluates them; deleting a target never deletes a dimension; Command::Reshape on a target applies remap_feature (task 12) to its dependents in the same command. Geometry: new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/annotation.rs evaluates annotations after their targets: points resolved through ModelGeometry::feature and projected into the view frame (plan or section uv), values as exact f64 distances along the direction, dimension line, extension lines, ticks and text anchors; status Unresolved { lost: Vec<usize> } when a target or feature is missing, listed in ModelGeometry.problems ('DM-003: reference to W-007 lost') and drawn at the fallback positions; level values = z(point) minus Project::level_elevation(LevelRef) (0, -vertical_datum() or the user level's elevation, properties-and-dialogs-03) or minus the storey elevation. IFCX: codecs in archicraft::annotations (task 02) with a stable FeatureKey encoding; dangling targets are kept as unresolved and reported, never dropped. samples::annotation_sample() with chained, aligned and level dimensions, its golden and conformance. Out of scope: tools and display (14), roof and terrain surfaces (22), angle dimensions (15), text styles (16 moves DimStyle text to a style reference), copy semantics (17).
design: The payload is the single source of truth (like TopLink for storey links) and the relation index is derived, so copying, undo and IFCX need no relation edits; this is what reduces ANN-009 to an id remap in task 17. Distances are computed from resolved 3D points projected into the view frame and onto the direction, never from screen coordinates or rounded values (NFR-ACC-005). Fallback positions are refreshed whenever a binding resolves, so a flagged dimension stays where it was. ANN-005's 'user origin' is realised as a named reference level (STR-007, LevelOrigin::Level(LevelRef::User)) because the INP-014 user origin is session-only and planar (point-input-snapping-07); recorded as a decision. Pitfalls: evaluation order (annotations after their targets, dirty propagation along AnnotationBinding via dependents_of); dimensions in sections resolve 3D features and project them with the marker frame; never store screen- or paper-space positions except the paper-mm style values. Pointers: relations.rs (element-kind-framework-08), evaluate_incremental (element-kind-framework-10), levels.rs and format_elevation (properties-and-dialogs-03), features.rs (task 12), alpha/kinds/annotations.rs (task 02), units.rs:281-308 (format_length), samples.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model command tests: add, update and delete dimensions with undo; dependents_of(wall) lists the bound dimensions; deleting the wall keeps the dimension and undo restores its resolution.
- Geometry tests: a horizontal dimension between two wall nodes 5.00 m apart reads exactly 5.0 (f64 equality for typed coordinates); a chained dimension over four points returns three consecutive values that sum to the overall distance; for free points (0,0) and (3,4) a horizontal dimension reads 3.0, a vertical one 4.0 and an aligned one 5.0; a dimension in a section frame measures in (u, z).
- Associativity (epic acceptance): moving the bound wall by (1.00, 0) updates the value and lines on re-evaluation; deleting it yields Unresolved with a problems-panel entry and no value; undo resolves it again.
- Regeneration (epic acceptance): changing the wall thickness 0.25 -> 0.365 or its layer structure keeps every bound dimension resolved, and a dimension on a face corner follows the new face exactly.
- Level dimensions on a slab top (offset 0 on storey 01 at +3.00, datum altitude 412.000, a user reference level at +1.20): ProjectZero +3.000, Storey(01) +-0.000, SeaLevel +415.000, User(level) +1.800; Bottom of a 0.20 m slab gives +2.800; CoreTop of a layered slab gives its core top.
- Edge points: a point bound to EdgePoint { t = 0.5 } on a slab outline edge stays at the edge midpoint after one end node of that edge is moved, and the value follows.
- Reshape remap: inserting a node before a bound slab node keeps the dimension on the same physical node.
- IFCX: resolved and unresolved dimensions round-trip exactly; the standard content is identical with and without dimensions; golden annotations.ifcx passes conformance/run.sh.
- ANN-004 and ANN-005 satisfied in model, geometry and IFCX (tools and display in 14).
notes: SRS: ANN-004 ANN-005. Decision: ANN-005 'user origin' = user reference level (LevelOrigin::Level(LevelRef::User)); open question for the product owner. Proposals: prefixes DM/LV, default text 2.5 paper mm, slash ticks. Reference levels come from properties-and-dialogs (increment 1, not a declared prerequisite of this epic).

title: Add storey level lines and filtered grid axes to section drawings
description:
WHY: VIEW-031 (S): section and elevation views shall show storey level lines labelled with storey name and elevation, and grid axes (GRD-004). GRD-009 (S): grid systems shall also be visible in section and elevation views, with filters by axis name and storey. Gap rows VIEW-031 (M) and GRD-009 (M): no section views exist, and grids are drawn in plan only (kinds/grid.rs axis math from grids-01, plan evaluation from grids-03). The epic acceptance requires that the section shows labelled storey lines and grid axes.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/section.rs gains `levels: Vec<LevelLine { storey, z }>` (every storey whose elevation lies within the drawing's vertical extent plus the storeys bounding it; u-range from the content bounds; labels are formatted in the app so a unit or datum change needs no re-evaluation) and `axes: Vec<SectionAxis { grid, axis: AxisId, label, u, z0, z1, bubble_ends }>` computed with the model-side axis_line() of grids-01: an axis is shown when it is not parallel to the section line (angle above 0.1 degree) and its extended segment intersects the depth slab within the horizontal limits; it is drawn at the u where its infinite line crosses the section line and spans from the lowest storey elevation to the top of the highest storey of the grid's storey range intersected with the view's storey filter. GridFilter of SectionViewSettings (task 01): axis_names (empty = all; entries matched case-insensitively, '*' as wildcard) and storeys (limits which grids appear and their vertical extent); show_levels and show_grids switch either part off. Filters are view settings, never stored on the grid. Out of scope: drawing (06), editing grids in sections, grid dimension chains in sections.
design: Grid math stays in the model crate (grids-01 axis_line and intersections); geometry only intersects lines with the marker frame, so the grid geometry has one implementation. Bubbles are paper-sized: geometry stores anchor and direction, the radius is resolved at draw time (grids-03 convention). For elevations the view line lies outside the building, so 'intersects the depth slab' (not 'crosses the drawn line segment') is the rule that makes perpendicular axes appear. Pitfalls: open-ended StoreyRanges, negative storey indices and storeys inserted later; labels must not be formatted here because datum and units are display concerns (properties-and-dialogs-03 format_elevation). Pointers: kinds/grid.rs (grids-01), grids-03 plan module, storey.rs:88-130 (index_of, relative_elevation, storey_at_elevation), section.rs (task 03).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests on samples::structural_frame (grids-11): a section perpendicular to the lettered axes shows exactly the lettered axes, 6.00 m apart in u (within 1e-9), labelled A..D; an elevation looking north shows the numbered axes 1..5 at their x positions and no lettered axis.
- Axis filter 'A, C' keeps two axes and 'A*' keeps the axes starting with A; the storey filter 0..1 limits the axes' z-extent to the top of storey 1 and hides a grid whose range lies entirely outside it.
- Level lines for two_storey_shell: one per storey at its elevation in elevation order with the storey id attached; show_levels = false yields none and show_grids = false no axes.
- Axes parallel to the section line are skipped; a grid rotated by 30 degrees gives the analytic crossing u.
- content_hash changes with the axis filter and after an axis move (grids-02 command) followed by re-evaluation.
- VIEW-031 and GRD-009 satisfied in geometry (display in task 06).
notes: SRS: VIEW-031 GRD-009. Interpretation: oblique axes are drawn at their crossing with the section line, as the reference product does for grid elements in sections.

title: Select, snap and move elements in section and elevation views
description:
WHY: VIEW-032 (S): in section and elevation views, elements shall be selectable, movable and stretchable (heights, elevations, node positions). INP-001 (M): every point passes through the shared point-input service in every view, and the picking rules of SEL-001..004 and VIEW-045 (selection kept when switching views) apply. Gap row VIEW-032 (L, missing): the ViewSurface trait (point-input-snapping-01) is implemented for plan views and the 3D working plane (3d-input-navigation-07) only. This task delivers selection and moving; stretching is task 08.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/section_surface.rs: SectionSurface implementing input::ViewSurface with SurfaceFrame { origin: (O.x, O.y, 0), x: (u, 0), y: +Z }, so plane coordinates are (u, absolute z); snap targets from the SectionDrawing's segments and nodes (cut outline corners, projected edge ends, level lines as guides, grid axes as edges) through a per-view SnapSource (point-input-snapping-02/03), rebuilt per drawing revision. Picking: SectionDrawing::pick returns cut parts first, then projected parts nearest first (reverse painter order), with Tab cycling and hover highlighting; marquee and containment modes of selection-transforms-07 in section coordinates; the shared Selection keeps the selection when switching to plan or 3D (VIEW-045). Moving: the transform tool of selection-transforms-10 runs on the section surface; a vector (du, dv) becomes Transform::Move { delta: du*u + dv*Z } with copy and multiple-copy variants, and after a vertical move the re-association offer of selection-transforms-14 appears. Locked elements show ghosted handles and the hover reason. Out of scope: stretch handles (08), rotate and mirror in sections (refused with a message because they need a plan axis), drawing tools (10, 11).
design: The frame keeps u horizontal and v vertical in absolute z, so consumers that take full 3D points (move, measure, dimensions) use frame.to_model and need no section special case, matching the 3d-input-navigation-08 contract (consumers without needs_horizontal receive 3D points). Picking order mirrors painting order; cut parts are nearest by definition. Snap kinds: cut corner and projected end as Node, level line as guide, grid axis as edge, with point-input-snapping-03's precedence. Pitfalls: compute du*u exactly so a section move never drifts perpendicular to the plane; the pick tolerance uses the section camera's model_per_pixel; cancel an active move step if the marker changes underneath. Pointers: input/surface.rs (point-input-snapping-01), views/surface3d.rs (3d-input-navigation-07) as the pattern, tools/transform.rs (selection-transforms-10), selection.rs (selection-transforms-01), selection-transforms-07 area selection, views/section.rs (task 06).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: SectionSurface to_plane/to_screen round-trip; a typed relative point (2.00, 0.50) in a section along +X maps to model (O.x + 2.00, O.y, 0.50) exactly.
- kittest: clicking a cut wall in an open section selects it, the plan view highlights the same wall, and switching tabs keeps the selection; Tab cycles between a cut slab and a projected wall behind it.
- Moving a selected slab in a section by a typed vertical 0.50 m executes one Transform Move with delta (0, 0, 0.50): the slab offset grows by 0.50 and undo restores it; a horizontal 1.00 m move moves it along u in plan.
- A vertical move of a wall across the storey boundary offers re-association (selection-transforms-14); declining keeps the home storey.
- Rotate and mirror in a section are refused with a status message; a locked element cannot be moved and the message names the element or layer.
- SnapSource unit test: cut corners, projected edge ends, level lines and grid axes of a section are snap targets with the point-input precedence.
- VIEW-032 'selectable, movable' satisfied.
notes: SRS: VIEW-032 (select and move).

title: Open section and elevation views in tabs and list them in the browser
description:
WHY: VIEW-030 (S): the view can be opened from its marker and updates when the marker moves; VIEW-031 (S): it shows storey level lines labelled with name and elevation, and grid axes; GRD-009 (S): grids are visible with filters by axis name and storey; VIEW-059 (S): section and elevation view types exist and a new project shows four elevations. VIEW-003 (M): the browser lists sections and elevations, double-click opens, the context menu offers rename, delete, settings and save as view, and new sections appear automatically; VIEW-001 (M): edits in any view appear in all views; VIEW-013 (S): every 2D view has its own drawing scale. Gap: no pane shows a section (workspace.rs:18-21; Pane::View(ViewId) after plan-views-browser-09), pane_ui (app.rs:728-733) knows only plan and 3D, and the browser (ui/browser.rs, rebuilt by plan-views-browser-10) has no section group. The epic acceptance requires a new project to have four elevations in the browser.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/section.rs: `SectionViewState { camera: Camera2d in (u, z), zoom_history, scale: DrawingScale, fitted, last_rect }` and ui(ui, ws, view) for Pane::View of kind Section or Elevation with the plan view's navigation (pan, zoom about the cursor, fit, previous and next zoom), the status-bar drawing-scale combo, hover highlighting and drawing of the SectionDrawing through the plan renderer: views/plan_gpu.rs (plan-renderer-06/08) gains an ordered batch list so projected part fills and edges (the painter list of task 20) are painted far to near, then cut fills, cut outlines (cut pens), level lines and grid axes; storey labels ('name +3.000' via format_elevation with the active reference level), axis bubbles and labels through the egui overlay at paper size. Document::section(view) caches per-element contributions keyed by (element geometry Arc, frame key) and the assembled drawing by (revision, marker, settings). Browser: Sections and Elevations groups (ViewKind grouping of plan-views-browser-10) with double-click open, rename, delete (deletes the marker through DeleteElements, so task 01's cascade applies), settings (a dialog for SectionViewSettings: storey lines, grids, axis-name and storey filters, projected parts) and save as view; capture/apply in views/state.rs (plan-views-browser-09) learns the section camera. Open from marker: the marker's double-click and context-menu item (task 05) push Request::OpenView. Pane pruning closes tabs of deleted markers; tab titles are view names; a GPU-less fallback text as in view3d.rs. Out of scope: selecting and editing in sections (07, 08), drawing tools in sections (10, 11), annotations (13-16).
design: Reuse the plan pane architecture instead of a second renderer: SectionDrawing implements Drawing2d (task 03), the GPU upload takes an ordered list of fill and stroke batches so painter order holds without a depth buffer, and overlays (labels, snap glyphs) stay in egui as plan-renderer planned for plans. Camera2d works in (u, v) unchanged with v up on screen. Caching: per-element contributions survive edits elsewhere (NFR-PERF-006 spirit), the assembled drawing is rebuilt per revision, a marker edit invalidates all contributions of its view. Labels: storey labels at the drawing's left end, axis bubbles at the top end, resolved in paper mm and kept upright. Pitfalls: the Pane serialisation of plan-views-browser-14 must accept the new view kinds; tabs go into the tracked active Tabs container (plan-views-browser-09), never the HashMap-order heuristic (technical debt, app.rs:302-305); kittest without wgpu needs the fallback path. Pointers: app.rs:291-307 (open_pane), :709-733 (handle_requests, pane_ui), :774-780 (retain_pane), document.rs:97-121 (caches), views/plan.rs:21-90 (PlanViewState, fit, zoom history), views/camera.rs:1-95, ui/browser.rs, views/state.rs (plan-views-browser-09), views/plan_gpu.rs (plan-renderer-06).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: a new project lists 'North elevation', 'East elevation', 'South elevation' and 'West elevation' under Elevations, and double-clicking one opens a tab with that title (epic acceptance).
- kittest: a section drawn in plan appears under Sections automatically; double-clicking its marker in plan opens its tab; deleting it from the browser closes the tab and removes the marker, and undo brings both back.
- VIEW-001 test: with a section open, moving a wall in the plan changes the section's content hash in the next frame and re-slices only that wall's contribution (cache counters); moving the marker updates the open section without closing it.
- Storey lines with 'name +-elevation' labels and grid axes with bubbles are drawn, and the settings dialog's axis-name and storey filters hide axes and storey lines (kittest on labels plus a golden image).
- Golden image (plan-renderer-07 infrastructure on the CI software adapters) of a two_storey_shell section with cut fills, projected parts and level lines passes on all three platforms within the documented tolerance.
- The drawing scale is per section view, zooming never changes it, and save as view / open restores camera and scale.
- VIEW-030 (open from marker, live update), VIEW-031 and GRD-009 (display), VIEW-059 (browser) and the section clauses of VIEW-003 and VIEW-013 satisfied.
notes: SRS: VIEW-030 VIEW-031 VIEW-059 GRD-009 (UI). Also serves the section and elevation clauses of VIEW-003 (browser) and VIEW-013 (drawing scale per 2D view).

title: Add angle dimensions between two edges and for arcs
description:
WHY: ANN-006 (C): angle dimensions between two edges (inner or outer angle) and for arcs may be provided. Gap row ANN-006 (M, missing). The binding, evaluation, drawing and copy infrastructure of tasks 12-14 and 17 makes it a small addition.

WHAT: kinds/dimension.rs gains AngleDimension (code 'angle', prefix 'AN') { view, a: [DimPoint; 2], b: [DimPoint; 2], side: AngleSide { Inner, Outer }, radius, style: DimStyle } and ArcDimension (code 'arcangle', prefix 'AA') { view, arc: DimPoint::Bound to an arc feature (FeatureGeom::Arc of drafting arcs and, once curved-geometry provides them, arc slab edges and arc walls) or free centre, start and end, radius, style: DimStyle } (DimStyle shared with task 13, so task 16's move of its text to a TextStyleId covers angles too); evaluation in annotation.rs (inner angle theta in [0, pi] between the edge directions at their intersection, outer 2 pi - theta; the arc's sweep), the dimension arc and its ticks, Unresolved handling as for linear dimensions; IFCX codecs in archicraft::annotations; the remap_ids hook of task 17 for both kinds; tool modes 'Angle' (pick edge 1, edge 2, then the placement whose side selects inner or outer, Tab toggles) and 'Arc angle' in tools/dimension.rs; values formatted with format_angle in the project angle unit. Out of scope: arc-length dimensions, angles between non-coplanar edges.
design: Edges are pairs of DimPoints so both ends can be bound (Corner or Node features) and the angle follows either element; the vertex is the intersection of the two lines, never a stored point. Orient each edge direction away from the intersection towards the edge's far end so inner and outer stay stable when edges are picked in reverse. Pitfalls: arc features used in sections must lie in the view plane (refuse others); angle formatting must use the project's angle unit and precision (STR-009). Pointers: annotation.rs and tools/dimension.rs (tasks 13, 14), curve.rs Arc (drafting-trim-split-01), units.rs format_angle, features.rs FeatureGeom::Arc (task 12).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: edges at 0 and 30 degrees give 30.00 degrees inner and 330.00 degrees outer; parallel edges are rejected with a message; the three-point arc (0,0)/(1,1)/(2,0) gives 180.00 degrees; a quarter circle gives 90.00 degrees exactly in degrees and 100.00 in grads.
- Associativity: rotating a bound wall by 15 degrees updates the angle; deleting it flags the dimension; copying the dimension alone keeps the original binding (task 17 rule).
- kittest: an angle dimension between two wall edges in plan shows the expected value, and the placement side switches inner and outer.
- IFCX round trip; golden annotations.ifcx extended and conformance green.
- ANN-006 satisfied.
notes: SRS: ANN-006. Proposals: prefixes AN/AA.

title: Publish semantic feature keys for associative annotation points
description:
WHY: ANN-004 (S): dimension points picked on element nodes or edges are associative and update with the element, and a dimension whose reference disappears is flagged. ANN-005 (S): level dimensions on slabs, roofs and terrain are associative and can measure the top, the bottom or the top of the core. SRS 3.3: an annotation binding references element geometry or a datum. The epic acceptance demands that bindings reference the element id plus a semantic feature key (face role, node index), never mesh indices, so a regenerated wall keeps its dimensions. Gap row ANN-004 (L): there is no annotation-binding relation and nothing names element features; ElementGeometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:30-36) holds only meshes and an axis.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/features.rs: `FeatureKey { Node { ring, index } (the PartRef::Node addressing), EdgePoint { ring, index, t }, Corner { face: FaceRole, end: End, level: CornerLevel { Base, Top } }, Face { role: FaceRole }, Surface { role: SurfaceRole { Top, Bottom, CoreTop } }, Axis { axis: AxisId }, Centre, Kind(KindFeature) }` with FaceRole { Exterior, Interior, CoreExterior, CoreInterior, Start, End } and `FeatureGeom { Point(DVec3), Line(DVec3, DVec3), Plane { origin, normal }, Arc { centre, radius, start, sweep, normal } }`, all in absolute coordinates. Kind hooks: `feature(&self, key, &StoreyList) -> Option<FeatureGeom>` for parametric features (reference-line ends, slab outline nodes, grid axes, drafting nodes and centres, opening profile corners) and `remap_feature(&self, key, op: &ReshapeOp) -> FeatureRemap { Same, Moved(FeatureKey), Lost }` so node insertion and deletion keep bindings on the same physical node. Geometry: ElementGeometry gains `features: Vec<(FeatureKey, FeatureGeom)>` published by the generators for resolved features: wall face corners after junction resolution (per end, base and top, per skin-boundary role from layer structures), slab Top, Bottom and CoreTop planes and outline corners at those levels, opening corners, column and beam axis ends; `ModelGeometry::feature(id, key)` prefers the published value and falls back to the kind hook; `feature_at(project, geometry, frame, point, radius)` finds the nearest feature point or edge point of the shown elements in a plan frame or a section frame (MarkerFrame of task 01). The point-input Snap gains `source: Option<FeatureRef { element, key }>`, set by node, edge and face snaps so tools know what was picked. Out of scope: dimension kinds (13; task 13 applies remap_feature in commands), roof and terrain surface features (task 22 registers them through the same hooks).
design: Two sources are deliberate: parametric features come from the model (cheap, available without evaluation, usable in commands), resolved features from evaluation (junction-trimmed corners only exist there); ModelGeometry::feature merges them so consumers ask one place. Keys use roles and parametric indices, which survive regeneration by construction; EdgePoint keeps a parameter t on the parametric edge so 'a point on this edge' follows stretching proportionally. Published features live in the per-element Arc<ElementGeometry> of the incremental evaluator, so they are cached and invalidated with the element for free. Pitfalls: lift storey-local values to absolute z once, here, not in every consumer; CoreTop needs the layer-structure core skin (layer-structures); keep FeatureKey extensible (Kind(KindFeature) generated per kind like KindPart) so stairs, roofs and curtain walls add features without touching this module. Pointers: selection.rs PartRef (selection-transforms-01), wall.rs Footprint (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs:102) and the per-skin polygons of junction-engine, evaluate.rs:20-48, kinds/grid.rs AxisId (grids-01), curve.rs (drafting-trim-split-01), input/snap.rs (point-input-snapping-03).
acceptance_criteria:
- Wall: Node{0,0} and Node{0,1} resolve to the reference-line ends; after a thickness change from 0.25 to 0.365 (WAL-004) Corner{Exterior, Start, Base} moves by the face-offset change while the keys stay the same; at an L junction the exterior corner equals the junction-resolved footprint corner (compared with the wall footprint output).
- Slab: Surface{Top} is the plane at storey elevation + offset; CoreTop of a layered slab equals the top of its core skin; outline and hole nodes resolve; remap_feature after InsertNode at index 2 maps Node{0,3} to Node{0,4} and after DeleteNode 3 reports Lost for Node{0,3}.
- A grid Axis{id} resolves to the axis line after a rename; a drafting arc's Centre resolves exactly.
- Regeneration (basis of the epic acceptance): re-evaluating a wall after any parameter edit publishes features under identical keys; FeatureKey's serde form is pinned by a snapshot test and contains no mesh, triangle or buffer index.
- feature_at returns the nearest corner within the radius in a plan frame and in a section frame; node, edge and face snaps carry their FeatureRef.
- Associativity infrastructure of ANN-004 and ANN-005 satisfied.
notes: SRS: ANN-004 ANN-005 (associativity infrastructure). Roof and terrain surfaces are registered in task 22 through the same hooks. Wall face corners use the existing footprints() of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/wall.rs plus the per-skin polygons of junction-engine (increment 1, not a declared prerequisite of this epic). Depends on task 01 for the section frame used by feature_at.

title: Add text blocks and one text style editor with presets
description:
WHY: ANN-007 (C): text blocks may be provided, with font, size in paper units, bold, italic and underline, alignment, pen colour, line spacing and an anchor point that stays fixed when the text grows; one text style editor and style presets serve all text-bearing annotations. SRS 3.2: text is a reference element that is not written as an IFCX element (ANN-010: text and dimensions are stored in the ArchiCraft namespace only). Gap row ANN-007 (L, missing): no text element exists, the hard-coded 'Scale 1:100' label (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:241, replaced by plan-renderer-01) was the only text concept, and ProjectSettings (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:47-52) has no text attributes. Element labels (ANN-008) build on this in task 21.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/text.rs: a TextStyle project attribute { id: TextStyleId, name, font: FontFamily { Sans, Serif, Mono }, size_mm, bold, italic, underline, align: TextAlign { Left, Center, Right }, pen: PenId, line_spacing } with Add/Update/DeleteTextStyle commands (deleting a style in use requires a replacement, the DSP-003 rule of plan-attributes) and template presets; the text part of DimStyle (task 13, shared by the linear, level and angle dimensions of tasks 13 and 15) moves to a TextStyleId reference so one editor serves all text-bearing annotations (ANN-007), with the format migration of element-kind-framework-12 for files written before. Kind Text (code 'text', prefix 'TX') { view: DraftingView, anchor: DVec2, anchor_pos: AnchorPos (nine positions), angle, content, style: TextStyleId, overrides: TextOverrides (optional per-property deltas) }, has_body = false and ifcx_node = false, with its codec in archicraft::annotations (task 02) and the styles in archicraft::project. App: bundled font faces (regular, bold, italic and bold-italic per family) registered at startup in egui FontDefinitions from files under crates/archicraft-app/assets/fonts; text layout through egui LayoutJob (underline via TextFormat, colour from the resolved pen, line spacing, alignment) at paper size times the drawing scale with the anchor fixed, through the overlay helper of views/annotation_draw.rs (task 14) in plan and section panes; a Text tool (click the anchor, type in an inline multi-line editor, Ctrl+Enter commits); a 'Text styles' dialog (presets, preview, add, rename, edit, delete with in-use replacement) opened from the Design menu and from the text properties; properties fields for Text through ui/fields.rs. Out of scope: element labels (21), rich-text runs inside one block, property labels, keynotes and schedules (Section 8).
design: Text styles are project attributes like pens (plan-attributes pattern: stable ids, in-use queries, replacement on delete) referenced by every text-bearing annotation; per-element overrides are optional deltas so a style change updates all non-overridden properties. egui's default font has no bold face, so bundling faces is required for 'bold', and italic faces avoid synthetic slanting. Text height: paper mm x drawing scale gives the model height and the overlay converts to pixels each frame, so zoom and scale behave like dimension text (task 14 helper). Pitfalls: font licence and binary size (one family with four faces is enough if size matters); the inline editor must not trigger single-key tool shortcuts (UI-008, works_while_typing); text in rotated plan views stays upright relative to the view unless an explicit angle is set; the DimStyle migration must keep task 13 files readable. Pointers: attributes.rs (plan-attributes), template.rs, kinds/dimension.rs and annotation.rs (task 13), views/annotation_draw.rs (task 14), ui/dialogs.rs (dialog pattern), egui FontDefinitions and LayoutJob, deny.toml (NFR-LEG-001 inventory), element-kind-framework-12 (format migration).
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: text style create, update and delete with undo; deleting an in-use style requires a replacement and reassigns every text and dimension using it; validation rejects size_mm <= 0, line_spacing <= 0 and an empty or duplicate name with explanations; the template contains the presets (template test).
- Style properties (headless tests on the LayoutJob builder plus a kittest galley check): the font family selects the bundled face; bold and italic select the bold, italic and bold-italic faces (no synthetic slanting); underline sets the TextFormat underline stroke; the text colour equals the resolved pen colour; the line height equals size x line_spacing; Left, Center and Right place each line relative to the anchor as specified.
- Size in paper units: at 1:100 a 2.5 mm text is 0.25 m tall in model units and at 1:50 0.125 m; zooming changes only its pixel size, never its paper size (VIEW-013, DSP-019).
- Anchor test: for each of the nine anchor positions, growing the content from one to three lines keeps the anchor's model position fixed.
- kittest: the Text tool creates a text with the default style; changing font, size, bold, italic, underline, alignment, pen and line spacing in the Text styles dialog updates every text using the style while a text with a size override keeps its size; dimension values use the dimension preset and follow its edits (one editor for all text-bearing annotations).
- IFCX round trip of styles and texts (task 13 files migrate to style references); golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/annotations.ifcx extended; the standard content is unchanged (IFX-068) and texts are not IFCX nodes (ANN-010).
- The bundled font files and their licence texts are inventoried per NFR-LEG-001 (licence admitted by the R8 list of docs/technology-choices.md; cargo deny stays green).
- ANN-007 satisfied.
notes: SRS: ANN-007. Proposals: presets 'Standard 2.5 mm', 'Dimension 2.5 mm', 'Small 1.8 mm', 'Heading 5.0 mm'; prefix TX; font families limited to the bundled ones. Open question: which font family to bundle and whether its licence (for example OFL-1.1) needs adding to the R8 list (licence review with release-candidate). Split: element labels (ANN-008) moved to sections-elevations-dims-21.

title: Slice bodies on vertical marker planes into section cut regions
description:
WHY: VIEW-030 (S): section and elevation views are derived live from the model with the same cut and projection rules as plans (VIEW-010): elements intersected by the plane are drawn cut (cut outline and cut fill); moving the marker updates the view. Gap row VIEW-030 (XL, missing): crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs:35-63 (slice_loops) slices only at a horizontal z and plan.rs:111-170 (plan_drawing) classifies only for horizontal plans; nothing cuts a body with a vertical plane. The epic acceptance requires a slice hash test on RM-S showing that moving a marker updates its section; technology-choices and the epic note say arbitrary-plane slicing is a generalisation of slice.rs, not a Boolean, so no kernel is needed. This task delivers the cut half of the section drawing and its data structure; the projected half (parts beyond the plane, depth clipping, painter order) is task 20, split off because VIEW-030 is the epic's extra-large risk.

WHAT: slice.rs gains `slice_loops_on(mesh, plane: &SectionPlane) -> Vec<Vec<DVec2>>` returning oriented loops in the plane's (u, v) frame, while slice_loops(mesh, z) stays untouched as the horizontal fast path and loops_to_polygons (slice.rs:151) is reused for hole assignment. New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/section.rs: SectionPlane built from the model's MarkerFrame (task 01) with v = absolute z; `section_element(project, geometry, element, frame, options) -> Option<SectionElement>` (cut polygons per material, plus a `projected` field that stays empty until task 20) and `assemble(frame, Vec<SectionElement>) -> SectionDrawing` so the app can cache per element; SectionDrawing { marker, frame, elements, cut_regions, faces (painter list, filled by task 20), bounds } with pick(), hit(), segments(), bounds() and content_hash(). New crates/archicraft-geometry/src/drawing.rs factors the per-material union and fill triangulation out of plan.rs (fill_mesh at plan.rs:90-105 and the merge at plan.rs:150-163; CutRegion and FillMesh move with re-exports so plan callers do not change) and defines a Drawing2d trait (segments, hit, pick, bounds) implemented by PlanDrawing and SectionDrawing for picking and snapping. Cut rules: storey-local bodies are lifted by their home storey elevation; elements on every storey take part; elements entirely in front of the plane are skipped; parts crossing the plane are cut when the marker's cut flag is set (an elevation, cut = false, yields no cut regions and task 20 projects those parts); horizontal limits clip cut polygons to the u-interval; Void parts (host-openings PartRole::Void) never appear; the shown predicate (layers, view filters) is honoured as in plan_drawing. Out of scope: projected parts and depth clipping (20), level lines and grid axes (04), on-screen drawing (06), 2D elements and annotations in sections (11, 13), exact hidden-line removal.
design: Generic crossing: signed distance d(p) = (p - O).n with the edge endpoints ordered lexicographically as in slice.rs:16-29 (bit-identical points for neighbouring triangles), t = -d(a) / (d(b) - d(a)), the point mapped to (u.(p - O), p.z); keep slice.rs's 1e-9 key quantisation for chaining and the 'material on the left' orientation so loops_to_polygons and hole assignment are reused. The horizontal fast path must remain byte-for-byte because plan goldens and plan-renderer images depend on it; equivalence is asserted to 1e-9, not bit identity. content_hash: FNV-1a 64 over coordinates quantised to 1 micrometre (round_coordinate semantics) in canonical order (element order, then polygon and edge order), not std's DefaultHasher, so blessed values survive toolchain updates. The per-element entry point lets Document cache contributions by (element geometry Arc, frame key) so a single edit re-slices one element while a marker move re-slices all. SectionElement carries the projected field from the start so task 20 adds content without changing the API that tasks 04 and 06 use. Pitfalls: no elements_on(storey) shortcut; negative storey elevations; faces exactly in the plane (treat d == 0 consistently with slice.rs's p.z >= z rule); never translate meshes in place (map points on the fly). Pointers: slice.rs:10-160, plan.rs:59-170 (ViewRange, classification, merge), evaluate.rs:20-48 (ElementGeometry, storey-local z), plan-views-browser-03 design (z-extent index, shown predicate), host-openings-03 (PartRole::Void).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/section.rs: for every part of two_storey_shell, slice_loops_on with a horizontal plane equals slice_loops within 1e-9 (plus a property test on random boxes); plan.rs tests and plan goldens stay unchanged after the drawing.rs extraction.
- A section perpendicular to an exterior wall of two_storey_shell: the wall's cut polygon is thickness x wall height at the right absolute elevation (within 1e-9), both slabs are cut 0.20 m thick at their elevations, the stair hole appears as a gap, and walls behind the plane are absent.
- Custom limits clip cut polygons to the u-interval; an elevation (cut = false) has no cut regions.
- Void parts never appear (host-openings sample), a layered wall yields one cut region per skin material, and same-material cut regions of joined walls merge without a seam through the shared drawing.rs merge code.
- Slice hash on RM-S (samples::rm_s from reference-models): moving the marker 0.50 m along n changes content_hash(), moving it back restores the identical hash, the hash equals a fresh assemble() of freshly evaluated elements, and the blessed file crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/golden/section-hashes.txt (ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1) pins the values (epic acceptance; task 20 extends the hashed content to projected parts).
- Determinism: two evaluations give identical SectionDrawing values and hashes; pick() and hit() find a cut wall at a point inside its cut polygon and nothing outside the drawing.
- VIEW-030 'derived live from the model with the same cut rules as plans' satisfied in geometry for the cut part (projection, depth and horizontal limits of projected parts in task 20).
notes: SRS: VIEW-030 (geometry: cut). Dependency note: RM-S is built by the reference-models epic (increment 2), which this fragment cannot reference; if it is missing when this task starts, run the hash test on two_storey_shell and samples::structural_frame and add the RM-S case when it lands. Split: the projected half of the former 1,440-minute task is sections-elevations-dims-20.

title: Stretch heights, elevations and nodes in sections with numeric input
description:
WHY: VIEW-032 (S): elements shall be stretchable in section and elevation views: heights, elevations, node positions. EDT-009 (M): nodes and edges are stretchable by dragging, with numeric input, and the stretch clause of INP-002 makes the tracker show the resulting total length by default and the change on demand. SLB-008 (M): the slab elevation can be changed by dragging in section, elevation or 3D views (the 3D part is edit-reshape-palette-11). The epic acceptance requires that a wall height is stretched in a section with numeric input. Gap row VIEW-032 (L).

WHAT: Kind hooks in crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/mod.rs: `section_handles(&self, ctx: &SectionHandleContext) -> Vec<SectionHandle { key: HandleKey, anchor: DVec3, axis: HandleAxis { Vertical, Along(DVec2) } }>` and `apply_section_handle(&self, key, target: f64, ctx) -> Result<Self, String>` with empty defaults, implemented for walls (Top: fixed height or link offset; Base: base offset, keeping the absolute top of fixed-height walls; Start/End nodes along the reference line when |dir.u| >= cos 80 degrees), slabs (the handle on the face named by SlabReference moves the slab through its offset, the opposite face changes the thickness while the reference face stays; with the default SlabReference::Top that is Top = elevation, Bottom = thickness), openings of host-openings (Sill, Head: placement elevation and height) and columns and beams of profiles-columns-beams (top, base, beam elevation). App: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/section_stretch.rs, an InputConsumer on the SectionSurface: handles drawn for the selection, press-drag-release or click-click (point-input-snapping-14), the tracker in TrackerMode::TotalLength (resulting height, thickness or length) by default and LengthChange on demand, typed values committing; a live preview of the moved edge; one UpdateElements per stretch, validated through validate_element; locked elements refused. Out of scope: polygon node editing of slab outlines in sections (plan only), roof handles (the roofs kinds can register later through the same hooks), 3D handles.
design: Handles come from parameters (vertical_extent, plan positions) in the model crate and are projected with the marker frame of task 01, so no geometry evaluation is needed and every registered kind can opt in. Typed TotalLength values are relative to the handle's opposite edge (the base for Top, the top for Base) and need no datum; absolute elevations shown in the tracker use the active reference level (properties-and-dialogs-04). Pitfalls: top links keep their type and only change the offset, otherwise storey changes stop propagating (ELM-006); node handles on oblique walls move along the wall direction by du/(dir.u) and are refused beyond 80 degrees to avoid huge jumps; walls with an elevation outline (task 09) get outline editing instead of Top/Base handles, wired in task 10. Pointers: kinds/wall.rs and kinds/slab.rs (element-kind-framework-02), kinds/opening.rs (host-openings-01), TopLink (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:60-90 before the framework), Project::vertical_extent (project.rs:245-260), edit-reshape-palette-08 (tracker usage), TrackerMode (point-input-snapping).
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests per kind: a wall Top handle with fixed height 3.00 and target top 3.50 above the base gives height 3.50; with TopLink::Storey offset 0 it gives offset 0.50 and keeps the link; the Base handle raises the base offset and keeps the absolute top of a fixed-height wall; slab Top changes the offset and Bottom the thickness for SlabReference::Top and the roles swap for SlabReference::Bottom, rejecting a thickness below MIN_THICKNESS with a message; a column Top handle with a storey-linked top changes only the link offset and a beam Elevation handle changes start_elevation and end_elevation together by the typed amount; opening Sill/Head change elevation and height and refuse to leave the host.
- kittest (epic acceptance): in a section through a wall, dragging its top handle and typing 3.50 sets the wall height to 3.50 (the tracker shows the total height while dragging; in change mode typing 0.50 gives the same result); undo restores 3.00.
- Dragging a slab's top edge in a section by -0.10 m changes its offset by -0.10 (section clause of SLB-008).
- A wall parallel to the plane gets end-node handles; moving one by a typed 1.00 m lengthens the wall by exactly 1.00; a wall perpendicular to the plane offers no node handle.
- A locked element shows ghost handles and refuses the stretch naming the lock; a validation failure leaves the model unchanged and shows the explanation.
- VIEW-032 'stretchable (heights, elevations, node positions)' satisfied.
notes: SRS: VIEW-032 (stretch). Also serves the section and elevation clause of SLB-008 (owned by edit-reshape-palette).

title: Add the wall elevation outline to the model, body and IFCX
description:
WHY: WAL-011 (S): a wall shall have an optional elevation outline, a polygon of straight and arc edges drawn in the wall's elevation plane (gable, arched top, stepped base), stored as an editable property of the wall with no helper elements. Gap row WAL-011 (L, missing): the wall (kinds/wall.rs, formerly crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:129-147) has only a base offset and a top link, and its body is a vertical extrusion between them. host-openings-05 already builds wall bodies in the wall's own elevation plane (a trace minus opening voids per skin band before extrusion) and drafting-trim-split-01 provides the exact PolyCurve with straight and arc edges, so the outline fits both without a Boolean kernel.

WHAT: Model: Wall gains `elevation_outline: Option<PolyCurve>` (closed, in wall-local coordinates: x along the reference line from its start, z relative to the home storey elevation), validated as closed, simple and counter-clockwise, spanning x from 0 to the reference-line length within MODEL_TOLERANCE and at least MIN_HEIGHT tall; vertical_extent returns the outline's z-range while it is set (top link and base offset are kept but inactive, and the properties show 'defined by elevation outline'). `Command::SetWallElevationOutline { walls, outline: Option<PolyCurve> }` (labels 'Set elevation outline' / 'Remove elevation outline'); kind hooks: transform (move and rotate keep the local outline, mirror maps x to L - x and restores the orientation, vertical move shifts z), end stretching (edit-reshape-palette-05 endpoint operations and task 08 node handles) moves the outline nodes lying on the moved end and re-bases x when the start moves. Geometry: the wall-plane layering of host-openings-05 uses the tessellated outline (the one tessellate() function with the project settings) as the trace instead of the base-top rectangle, minus the opening voids; end pieces outside the split planes are subdivided at the outline's vertex x-positions so each slab is a planar-faced hexahedron bounded by the end polygon's y-range and the outline's z-range; every skin band receives the same trace so layered walls stay stitched. IFCX: archicraft::wall gains elevationOutline with the curve encoding of the drafting codec (points plus edges, full precision), FORMAT_VERSION bump through the migration table; samples::outline_walls() with a gable wall, an arched-top wall and a stepped-base wall carrying an opening, registered in tests/roundtrip.rs and examples/reference_models.rs with its golden. Out of scope: drawing and editing the outline in views (10), outlines on polygonal, inclined or arc walls (their kinds may opt in later).
design: Wall-local coordinates make the outline independent of the wall's position and direction (moves and rotations are free), while z relative to the home storey makes it follow storey elevation changes; replacing the vertical extent instead of intersecting with it is the only way a gable can rise above the nominal top, which matches the reference product's custom elevation profiles. Exact end pieces: on an x-interval where the end polygon's y-bounds and the outline's z-bounds are both linear in x, the solid is a hexahedron with planar faces, so subdividing at outline vertices gives exact bodies for straight edges and the arc's tessellation for curved ones; stitching uses the identical trace on both sides of every split plane (host-openings-05 rule). Pitfalls: arcs only through tessellate() (bit-identity contract of drafting-trim-split-02); an outline narrower than the wall would leave the junction ends empty, hence the coverage validation; MAX_MESH_POINTS with many arc segments (report, do not split); WAL-004 (thickness changes keep the reference line) is unaffected because the outline lives in the elevation plane. Pointers: kinds/wall.rs, curve.rs (drafting-trim-split-01), tessellate (drafting-trim-split-02), host-openings-05 design (wall-local frame, split planes, skin bands), wall.rs:102 Footprint, evaluate.rs:150-189, alpha/kinds/drafting.rs curve encoding (drafting-trim-split-05).
acceptance_criteria:
- Validation tests: open or self-intersecting outlines, outlines that do not cover [0, L] and degenerate heights are rejected with explanations and leave the model unchanged.
- Geometry tests (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/outline.rs): a gable wall 6.00 m long and 0.25 m thick with 3.00 m eaves and a 5.00 m ridge has volume 0.25 x 24.00 = 6.00 m3 within 1e-9 and a closed, outward-oriented mesh (check_closed); an arched top (semicircle of radius 1.00 over a 2.00 m wall with 2.50 m sides) matches the analytic volume within the IFX-034 chord tolerance; a stepped base is exact; an opening through the gable removes exactly its volume; a layered wall yields closed bodies per skin whose summed volume equals the single-skin case.
- The plan cut at 1.10 m of a stepped-base wall shows material only where the outline reaches the cut height; the wall's 3D bounds equal the outline's z-range.
- No helper elements: setting an outline adds no element and no relation (element and relation counts unchanged); the outline is a field of the wall payload and the properties show 'defined by elevation outline'.
- Command tests: set and remove with undo; mirror maps the outline; stretching the wall end by 1.00 m moves the end nodes so the outline still spans the wall.
- IFCX: exact round trip of the PolyCurve parameters, golden outline-walls.ifcx blessed, conformance/run.sh green, an older reader flags the newer format.
- WAL-011 satisfied in model, geometry and IFCX (view editing in task 10).
notes: SRS: WAL-011. Decision recorded: while an outline is set it replaces base offset and top link for the body; removing it restores them unchanged.

title: Add section and elevation markers with their views to the model
description:
WHY: VIEW-030 (S): section and elevation views shall be defined by a marker in a plan view (cut or view line, direction, depth and optional horizontal limits); they are derived live from the model with the same cut and projection rules as plans (VIEW-010); moving the marker updates the view, and the view can be opened from its marker. VIEW-059 (S): section and elevation view types shall be provided and a new project shall contain four elevations. SRS 3.2 groups such aids with the reference elements that support reading the model, and decision D-8 makes sections S for viewing and basic editing. ANN-002 (M) and ANN-012 (C) bind 2D elements to "a section/elevation view". Gap rows VIEW-030 and VIEW-059 (XL, missing): there is no marker element, the ViewKind of plan-views-browser-07 knows only Plan and Model3d, Pane (crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:18-21, Pane::View(ViewId) after plan-views-browser-09) cannot show a section, and drafting-trim-split-03's DraftingView only has Plan { storey }. Every later task of this epic (slicer, marker tool, section pane, drawing and annotating in sections) builds on this payload.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/marker.rs with the shared payload `ViewMarker { line: [DVec2; 2], side: ViewSide { Left, Right }, depth: Option<f64> (None = unlimited), limits: MarkerLimits { Unlimited, Line, Custom { start: f64, end: f64 } } (u-interval along the line), cut: bool, shown_on: StoreyRange, tag: String }` and two kinds, each registered with one kinds! line: SectionMarker (code 'section', prefix 'SE', default cut = true) and ElevationMarker (code 'elevation', prefix 'EL', default cut = false), both with descriptor flags has_body = false (drafting-trim-split-03) and a new ifcx_node = false (consumed by task 02). Pure frame math in the same module: `ViewMarker::frame() -> MarkerFrame { origin, u, n }` (u along start->end, n the viewing direction chosen by side), `MarkerFrame::to_view(DVec3) -> (DVec2 /*u, absolute z*/, f64 /*depth*/)` and `to_model(uv, depth) -> DVec3`, so model commands, geometry and app share one convention. ViewKind gains Section { marker: ElementId } and Elevation { marker } and ViewDefinition an optional `section: Option<SectionViewSettings { show_levels, show_grids, grid_filter: GridFilter { axis_names: Vec<String>, storeys: Option<StoreyRange> }, show_projected }>`. Commands: `Command::AddViewMarker { element, view_name }` (InsertElement + SetCounters + SetViews with one plain view, one undo step, labels 'Add section' / 'Add elevation'); `Command::FitElevationMarkers { ids, margin }` (moves elevation markers outside the plan bounds of all body elements, keeping each viewing direction); the delete planner cascades a marker's plain view and every element bound to DraftingView::Section { marker } (2D elements now, annotations from task 13) into the same command, while saved views that reference the marker stay and report on open (the tolerant resolve rule of plan-views-browser-07). DraftingView gains Section { marker } with validation (the marker exists and is a marker kind; the bound element's home storey equals the marker's). Kind hooks: transform (move, rotate; mirror swaps side; vertical move and tilted rotation return Unsupported naming the kind), validate, storey links of shown_on with unlink_storey (grids-01 pattern) and the visible_on(&self, storeys, home, storey) hook of grids-03 (grids-03 design) returning shown_on.contains(storey). A placeholder IFCX codec that writes nothing keeps goldens unchanged until task 02 (host-openings-01 pattern). Out of scope: IFCX and the template's default elevations (02), geometry (03, 04), all UI (05, 06).
design: Two kinds over one payload because ELM-019 counters, tool defaults (sections get a finite default depth, elevations an unlimited one) and the browser groups differ while geometry and UI are identical; one module generates both so the frame logic exists once. The marker is the single source of the view's geometry (it is what the user moves in plan); the ViewDefinition carries only display state (scale, camera, layer states, section settings), so moving the marker updates the view without any view edit, and saved views reuse plan-views-browser's capture/apply. Coordinates: u horizontal along the line, v = absolute z above project zero, depth along n; storey-local meshes are lifted by their home storey elevation in geometry, never stored lifted. Cascade: use the closure helper host-openings-02 introduced for hosted elements (dependents found by scanning DraftingView bindings now, by the relation index once annotation bindings exist in task 13), deterministic order for journal replay. Pitfalls: SectionViewSettings must be optional so plan-views-browser files stay valid; the marker's home storey matters only for storey deletion (rehome like other elements, shown_on narrowed through unlink_storey); ViewSide must flip on Mirror or a mirrored section looks the wrong way; validate before normalising the line direction. Pointers: kinds/mod.rs kinds! macro and Kind trait (element-kind-framework-02), views.rs ViewDefinition/ViewKind (plan-views-browser-07), kinds/grid.rs StoreyRange (grids-01), grids-03 visible_on hook, kinds/drafting.rs DraftingView (drafting-trim-split-03), transform.rs (selection-transforms-02), command.rs plan_delete_elements (command.rs:344-360 before the framework), Project::plan_bounds (selection-transforms-03).
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in kinds/marker.rs: the frame of line (0,0)-(10,0) with side Left has u = (1,0) and n = (0,1), side Right n = (0,-1); to_view/to_model round-trip random points within 1e-12; Custom limits map to the stated u-interval; Mirror swaps the side so the mirrored frame's n is the mirrored n.
- Validation rejects with CommandError::Invalid and an explanation, leaving the project unchanged (NFR-REL-005): a line shorter than MIN_EDGE_LENGTH, depth <= 0 or non-finite, Custom start >= end, shown_on ends missing from the StoreyList, an empty tag.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddViewMarker creates the element and exactly one plain ViewDefinition of kind Section or Elevation in one undo step; Transform Move moves the marker and undo restores it; DeleteElements on a marker removes its plain view and a 2D line bound to it in one step and undo restores all three exactly; a saved view of the marker survives the delete and resolve() reports the missing marker.
