- FitElevationMarkers on two_storey_shell with four elevation markers places every line outside the plan bounds by the margin with unchanged direction (exact coordinates asserted), as one undo step; NoChange when the markers are already fitted.
- A 2D line with DraftingView::Section { marker } validates; one whose home storey differs from the marker's is rejected.
- Registry and module-layout tests pass: codes 'section' and 'elevation' and prefixes SE and EL are unique, has_body is false; existing golden files are byte-identical.
- Model parts of VIEW-030 (marker definition: line, direction, depth, horizontal limits) and VIEW-059 (section and elevation view types) satisfied; the section-view binding of ANN-002 is prepared.
notes: SRS: VIEW-030 VIEW-059 (model). Proposals without an Appendix D value: prefixes SE/EL, default section depth 10.00 m, elevation depth unlimited, fit margin 3.00 m. Interpretation: 'optional horizontal limits' = a u-interval along the marker line (Unlimited by default; Line = the drawn endpoints).

title: Draw 2D geometry and new elements in section and elevation views
description:
WHY: ANN-012 (C): 2D construction geometry may also be drawn in section and elevation views, and ANN-002 (M) binds 2D elements to a view, which may be a section or elevation. VIEW-058 (C): new elements may be drawn directly in section and elevation views, beyond the cases of OPN-013 and WAL-011; decision D-8 keeps drawing in sections at C. Gap rows ANN-012 (M) and VIEW-058 (L): drafting kinds bind only to plan views (DraftingView::Plan of drafting-trim-split-03, extended with Section in task 01) and element tools run only on plan and 3D surfaces.

WHAT: 2D in sections: the drafting tool group (drafting-trim-split-06: lines, chains, polylines, arcs, circles, rectangles, splines, fills) runs on the SectionSurface; created elements store their points in the view's (u, v) coordinates with DraftingView::Section { marker } and the marker's home storey; section assembly adds them in view coordinates after the cut regions, with picking, hover and snapping; trim, extend and split (drafting-trim-split-11/13) use 2D elements of the same view and the section's cut outlines as boundaries; drafting fills can be traced by contour detection (contour.rs of edit-reshape-palette-06) from the section's segments. Elements in sections: following the vertical-plane rules of 3d-input-navigation-08, consumers without needs_horizontal (a beam from two 3D points when the beam kind accepts the inclination, the measure tool) receive 3D points; dedicated section adapters exist for walls (a rectangle in the view gives a wall whose reference line lies on the section line from u0 to u1, base and fixed top from z0 and z1, home storey from storey_at_elevation(z0)) and columns (a point gives a column at that u with its base at z and the default height); every other kind shows 'Draw <kind> in plan or 3D' and creates nothing. Out of scope: slabs, roofs and stairs drawn in sections, annotation planes in 3D, dimensions (13, 14).
design: View coordinates for section 2D elements follow ANN-002 (they belong to the view) and make them move with the marker like drawings in the reference product's sections; their plan-related hooks (rehome, plan_bounds) treat them as non-plan elements. Element adapters translate view input into plan parameters plus elevations, so the created elements are ordinary parametric elements and no new kind is needed. Pitfalls: consumers flagged needs_horizontal must not silently fall back to the horizontal plane in sections as they do in 3D, because the section plane is edge-on to plan; report instead; snapping between section 2D elements and section geometry uses the task 07 SnapSource. Pointers: kinds/drafting.rs (drafting-trim-split-03), tools/drafting.rs and tools/linear_edit.rs (drafting-trim-split-06/13), geometry contour.rs (edit-reshape-palette-06), 3d-input-navigation-08 design (needs_horizontal), section.rs (task 03), Project::new_wall (project.rs:281), storey.rs:124 storey_at_elevation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A line drawn in a section is bound to its marker, appears only in that section (not in plan or other sections), keeps its view coordinates when the marker moves (it moves with the view) and is deleted with the marker through task 01's cascade (undo restores it).
- Trimming a 2D line at a section cut outline and splitting it by another 2D line of the same section keep the chosen part (drafting tests in section coordinates).
- A drafting fill traced from a closed region of section segments has the region's area (exact for straight edges).
- A wall drawn by rectangle u 1.00..5.00, z 0.00..2.80 in a section along +X at y = 3.00 yields start (O.x + 1, 3.00), end (O.x + 5, 3.00), base offset 0 and fixed height 2.80 on the ground storey; a column placed at z = 3.00 lands on storey 01 with base offset 0; a beam drawn from (u 1.00, z 2.80) to (u 5.00, z 3.20) gets its start and end on the section line with start_elevation 2.80 and end_elevation 3.20 on the ground storey.
- Unsupported kinds show the refusal message and create nothing; section-bound 2D elements round-trip through IFCX (codec of task 02).
- ANN-012 and VIEW-058 satisfied for the listed kinds.
notes: SRS: ANN-012 VIEW-058.

title: Draw opening profiles and wall elevation outlines in section views
description:
WHY: OPN-013 (S): an opening's profile shall also be drawable in a section or elevation view. WAL-011 (S): the wall's elevation outline is drawn in the wall's elevation plane and is an editable property. Gap rows OPN-013 (M) and WAL-011 (L): the opening tool (host-openings-11) works in plan and 3D only, and no editor for elevation outlines exists. Both need the same step: picking a host whose face is parallel to the view plane and mapping view coordinates to the host's face coordinates.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/host_face.rs: host candidates under the pointer in a section or elevation (SectionDrawing pick of task 07) whose face frame is parallel to the view plane within 0.5 degree, with the affine map view (u, z) <-> host face (along, elevation) derived from the wall-local frame of the WallFace placement (host-openings-01) and the marker frame; other hosts show a refusal hint ('Openings in slabs are drawn in plan or 3D', 'This wall is not parallel to the view'). Opening tool in sections: the host-openings-11 consumer on the SectionSurface with the same cross-section methods (rectangle, circle, polygon) drawn directly in the view, creating an opening with WallFace placement, perpendicular orientation and the tool's depth default, previewed in the section and as a void in 3D. Wall outline tool (ToolKind::WallOutline, enabled in section and elevation views): pick a parallel wall, draw the outline with the chain input of the 2D tools (straight and arc segments, drafting-trim-split-06) or as a rectangle, executing SetWallElevationOutline; 'Edit elevation outline' enters edit mode with outline nodes and edges registered as WallPart::OutlineNode/OutlineEdge parts (PartRef registration of selection-transforms-01), so the reshape palette (move, insert and delete node, offset edge, curve edge where curved-geometry provides it) edits the outline through Command::Reshape; 'Remove elevation outline' in the context menu and properties. The Top/Base section handles of task 08 are suppressed for outlined walls in favour of outline nodes. Out of scope: openings in roofs or beams drawn from sections (their kinds can expose host face frames later), drawing outlines in plan.
design: One host-face abstraction for both tools keeps NFR-USE-002 (same input, same edit commands): the outline is an Outline/PolyCurve edited by the generic reshape commands, never a dedicated editor. A 0.5 degree parallelism threshold tolerates tiny drafting rotations but refuses oblique walls whose profile would be distorted. The sign of 'along' depends on which side the view looks from (n against the wall's exterior normal); both sides are tested. Pitfalls: the outline stores z relative to the home storey and a WallFace opening stores its elevation above the host base (storey elevation plus base offset), while the view works in absolute z (convert once, in the map); the WallFace anchor is the profile's bottom-centre, not its lower-left corner; openings drawn near the wall end must stay inside the host (host-openings validation reports otherwise); new PartRef variants are appended so existing WallPart indices are not renumbered. Pointers: tools/opening.rs (host-openings-11), kinds/opening.rs WallFace (host-openings-01), tools/drafting.rs chain input (drafting-trim-split-06), tools/reshape.rs (edit-reshape-palette-08), selection.rs PartRef (selection-transforms-01), views/section_surface.rs (task 07), Command::SetWallElevationOutline (task 09).
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure mapping tests: in an elevation looking at the exterior face of a 6.00 m wall whose start lies at u = 0, a rectangle with lower-left (2.00, 0.90) and size 1.00 x 1.20 in view coordinates yields Section::Rectangle { width 1.00, height 1.20 } with the WallFace anchor (bottom-centre, host-openings-01) at along 2.50 and elevation 0.90 above the host base (base offset 0; with base offset 0.20 the elevation is 0.70), face Exterior, exactly; viewed from the interior side, where u runs against the reference line, a rectangle whose u-interval starts 2.00 from the wall's end gives along L - 2.50 and face Interior; circle and polygon profiles map the same way (polygon rings relative to the anchor, counter-clockwise).
- kittest: drawing a rectangular opening in an elevation creates one opening hosted by the wall, visible in plan with its symbol and as a void in 3D (volume check through ModelGeometry); undo removes it.
- Pointing at a slab or at a wall perpendicular to the view shows the refusal hint and creates nothing (the 'clear feedback, create nothing' rule of OPN-007 and DW-001).
- The outline tool creates a gable outline from typed points (0,0), (6,0), (6,3), (3,5), (0,3) on a 6.00 m wall; dragging the ridge node to 5.50 with numeric input updates the body volume; remove restores the rectangular body; every step is undoable; an arched top drawn as a chain with one three-point arc segment stores a PolyCurve with exactly that arc edge and the body follows it.
- An outlined wall shows outline node handles instead of Top/Base handles in sections.
- OPN-013 and the drawing and editing part of WAL-011 satisfied.
notes: SRS: OPN-013 WAL-011 (editing). Proposal: parallelism tolerance 0.5 degree.

title: Draw section markers in plan and add the section and elevation tools
description:
WHY: VIEW-030 (S): sections and elevations are defined by a marker in a plan view and moving the marker updates the view; VIEW-059 (S) adds four default elevations that users must see and be able to move. EDT-009 (M) direct manipulation applies to the marker like to any element, and every point goes through the shared point-input service (INP-001, point-input-snapping-01). Gap row VIEW-030: no marker symbol and no tool exist.

WHAT: Geometry: markers contribute to plans through the visible_on path of grids-03 (body-less reference kinds bypass the z-extent index): PlanElement gains `marker: Option<MarkerPlan { line, arrows, depth_line, limit_ticks, tag_anchors }>`, stroked with the annotation-line pen (DSP-005) and a dash-dot line type and pickable through segments()/hit(). App: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/marker.rs consumers for ToolKind::Section and ToolKind::Elevation in the 2D/annotation group of the toolbox (shortcuts checked by the actions uniqueness test): first point, second point, then a side click (Tab flips) with the depth typed or clicked (Enter keeps the tool default), executing Command::AddViewMarker with the next tag (A, B, C... for sections). Selection handles: line endpoints (stretch through the node handles of edit-reshape-palette-07), a depth handle dragged along n, limit handles; 'Flip direction' and 'Fit elevations to model' (FitElevationMarkers) in the context menu and the Design menu; tags drawn by the egui overlay at paper size (DrawingScale of plan-renderer-01); properties fields (tag, depth, unlimited depth, limits, cut, shown_on) through the FieldSpecs of ui/fields.rs. Out of scope: opening the view and drawing the section (06), saved views of sections.
design: Reuse every generic path: moving and rotating through Command::Transform (selection-transforms), endpoint stretch through PartRef::Node ring 0 index 0/1 like wall ends, so markers need no special editing code; only the depth and limit handles are marker-specific and execute UpdateElements. The side step uses the sign of (p - a).perp(u). Tags are egui overlay text, never baked into lyon geometry, matching grids-05 and the annotation text helper of task 14. Pitfalls: marker segments must not disturb wall drawing, so register them as an 'annotation' snap group that point-input-snapping-12 exclusions can switch off; the default elevations live on the ground storey but are shown on all storeys, so selection and deletion must work from every storey (shown_on decides visibility, not the home storey); single-key shortcuts must not collide. Pointers: views/plan.rs draw_plan (plan.rs:237-320) or views/plan_gpu.rs (plan-renderer-06/08), tools/ module (point-input-snapping-01), ui/actions.rs, ui/shell.rs toolbox, grids-05 (tool and paper-size text pattern), edit-reshape-palette-07 (part handles), ui/fields.rs (properties-and-dialogs-05).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool state-machine tests without egui: typed points (0,0) and (10,0), a side click above the line and typed depth 8.00 produce AddViewMarker with that line, side Left and depth 8.00 exactly; Esc after the second point cancels one step; Backspace removes the last point.
- Plan geometry test: a marker contributes its line, two arrows, the depth line and tag anchors on every storey of shown_on and on no other storey; hit() picks it within the snap radius.
- Limit handles: dragging the start limit handle of an unlimited marker by a typed 2.00 sets MarkerLimits::Custom { start: 2.00, end: line length } in one undo step; a depth handle drag with typed 6.00 sets depth 6.00.
- kittest: the Section and Elevation tool buttons exist; drawing a section creates one SectionMarker element and exactly one plain view of kind Section (model assertion; the browser group arrives in task 06); dragging its endpoint handle with typed length 12.00 updates the line; 'Flip direction' swaps the side and undo restores it; 'Fit elevations to model' moves the four default elevations outside two_storey_shell.
- Markers use the annotation-line pen resolved at the drawing scale (DSP-019) with at least one device pixel, and tags use the paper size of the template text preset and are never upside down.
- VIEW-030 'defined by a marker in a plan view' and 'moving the marker' satisfied on the plan side; VIEW-059's default elevations are visible and editable.
notes: SRS: VIEW-030 VIEW-059 (plan side). Proposed shortcuts and the tool group are to be confirmed against Appendix D.8 by the uniqueness test; tags A, B, C... for sections.

title: Persist markers and section views and add four default elevations
description:
WHY: IFX-060 (M) requires every datum needed to restore the editable model, views included, in archicraft:: attributes. SRS 3.2 states that text, dimensions and guide lines are not written as IFCX elements; markers are view definitions rather than building elements, so they must not appear as nodes that change the standard content (IFX-063; IFX-068: the standard content never depends on view state). VIEW-059 (S): a new project shall contain four elevations. VIEW-030 (S) derives every section from its marker, so markers and their views must survive save and open with all their parameters. VIEW-003 (M) requires new sections and elevations to appear in the browser, which only holds across save and open if they persist. Gap row VIEW-059: the template (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs:367-376) creates only the two 3D views. The storage mechanism built here is reused by dimensions, angles, texts and labels in tasks 13, 15, 16 and 21.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/annotations.rs: elements of kinds with ifcx_node = false are collected per home storey into one `archicraft::annotations` attribute on the storey node, an array of { id, kind, name, layer, locked, data } in model order, declared in the in-file schema only when used (element-kind-framework-06 rule); per-kind codecs write `data` at full precision (marker: markerKind, line, side, depth or null, limits, cut, shownOn, tag). The reader restores annotation entries in a second pass after all element nodes and relations (later bindings need their targets), skipping and reporting malformed entries (PRJ-008: no silent drops). The ViewDefinition codec of plan-views-browser-08 gains the section and elevation kinds with SectionViewSettings; the drafting codec of drafting-trim-split-05 gains view { type: 'section', marker }. A marker without a plain view gets one recreated with a warning; a view whose marker is missing is kept and reported. Template: default_metric_project() adds four ElevationMarkers tagged N, E, S and W on the ground storey, 30.00 m lines on a square of +/-15.00 m around the origin looking inward, depth unlimited, limits Unlimited, shown_on all storeys, each with a plain view named 'North elevation', 'East elevation', 'South elevation' and 'West elevation'. FORMAT_VERSION bump through the framework's migration table (an older reader would drop markers silently). Re-bless every golden built from the template with a reviewed diff. Out of scope: section drawings (03), UI (05, 06), dimension, text and label codecs (13, 15, 16, 21), adding elevations to files written before this change.
design: One attribute per storey keeps the composed tree's standard content identical (IFX-063) and avoids hundreds of nodes once dimensions exist; each entry carries the element envelope, so the model needs no special case (annotations stay ordinary elements in Project.elements with a home storey). Declaring only when used keeps test-kind and release goldens identical (element-kind-framework-06 pitfall). The default elevations are fixed, not fitted, because element evaluation must not depend on other elements; users fit them with FitElevationMarkers (task 01, exposed in task 05). Pitfalls: deterministic order (model order) and full-precision numbers (json.rs format_f64), no round_coordinate on parameters; entries are not nodes, so no v5 sub-node ids; keep the annotation pass after the relation restoration of element-kind-framework-08 so bindings can be validated against restored elements. Pointers: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs (declarations), writer.rs:243-417 (storey and element nodes), reader.rs:735-880 (element pass), template.rs:347-376, examples/reference_models.rs, tests/roundtrip.rs, the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round trip: a project with sections and elevations (Custom limits, finite depth, both sides, Unlimited) saves and reopens equal (Project PartialEq), and its views keep kind and SectionViewSettings; a 2D line bound to a section round-trips.
- IFX-068 test: for two_storey_shell the files written with and without markers are byte-identical after stripping every archicraft:: attribute and its schema declaration.
- Template test: default_metric_project() holds four elevation markers tagged N/E/S/W with inward directions, unlimited depth and exactly one plain view of kind Elevation each.
- Lenient reading: a malformed annotation entry is skipped with a warning naming its id; a marker without view gets a recreated plain view and a warning; a view with a missing marker loads and is reported.
- A FORMAT_VERSION n-1 fixture migrates without gaining markers, and the version bump makes an older reader stub flag the file as newer.
- Tests that count the elements of template-based projects (samples_are_valid in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs expects 12 for two_storey_shell, plus element counts in tests/commands.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs) are updated for the four markers, never by leaving markers out of Project.elements.
- Goldens re-blessed (ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx) with a reviewed diff limited to archicraft::annotations, views and schema declarations; conformance/run.sh is green on every golden.
- VIEW-059 'a new project shall contain four elevations' satisfied at model and file level; IFX-060 holds for markers and section views.
notes: SRS: VIEW-059 VIEW-030 (persistence). Proposal without an Appendix D value: +/-15.00 m square and 30.00 m lines. Open question: whether markers should also be visible to third-party viewers as IfcAnnotation; this task keeps them in the archicraft namespace only, following SRS 3.2 for text and dimensions.

title: Add dimension tools and draw dimensions in plan and section views
description:
WHY: ANN-004 (S): linear dimensions are placeable by picking points or an edge and then an offset, and a lost reference is flagged; ANN-005 (S): level dimensions show elevations relative to a selectable origin. INP-001 (M) names dimensioning among the steps of the shared point-input service. VIEW-013 and DSP-019 (S): annotation sizes are in paper units at the view's drawing scale; DSP-005 provides the annotation-line and annotation-text pens. The epic acceptance: a dimension picked on a wall node follows the wall and is flagged when its reference disappears; level dimensions relative to project zero, storey, sea level and user origin.

WHAT: New crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/dimension.rs: consumers on PointInput for ToolKind::Dimension with modes Horizontal, Vertical, Aligned and Chained (pick points, where snaps carrying a FeatureRef create Bound points and others Free points, or click an element edge to take both edge ends; then the offset by click or typed distance; Chained keeps adding points until Enter or double-click) and ToolKind::LevelDimension (pick a point or, on slabs, roofs and terrain, a surface with a key cycling Top, Bottom and CoreTop; the origin comes from the tool defaults and is switchable in the info bar), in plan views and in section views (SectionSurface of task 07). New crates/archicraft-app/src/views/annotation_draw.rs shared by plan and section panes: dimension lines, extension lines and ticks as strokes through the plan renderer with the annotation-line pen at the drawing scale; values through the egui overlay at text_size_mm x scale, rotated along the dimension line and kept upright, formatted with format_length (project unit and precision) and level values with format_elevation; unresolved dimensions drawn dashed in the warning colour with '?' and a tooltip naming the lost reference. Dimensions are pickable and selectable (segments in Drawing2d), the offset handle is draggable with numeric input, and properties fields cover direction, origin, style and the point list (read-only 'free' / 'bound to W-003 node 1'). Out of scope: angle dimensions (15), text styles (16), roof and terrain surfaces (22, which reuse this tool's surface cycling), automatic dimensioning (Section 8).
design: Tools stay thin: the step logic turns Resolved snaps into DimPoints (FeatureRef present -> Bound with fallback = the snapped point); everything else is the model of task 13. Text goes through the egui overlay (a galley at the resolved pixel size) because lyon would need a font tessellator; the same helper renders level values, angles (15), texts (16) and labels (21), grid bubbles and storey labels (06). Upright rule: flip when the text direction points into the screen's left half-plane. Pitfalls: snapping must prefer element features over plain plan segments so bindings are actually created; collinear chain points need no duplicate extension lines; unresolved dimensions are drawn at their fallback positions, never at the origin. Pointers: input/ (point-input-snapping-01/03), tools/ module, views/plan_gpu.rs strokes (plan-renderer-08), plan_style.rs pen resolution (plan-renderer-02), units.rs format_length and format_elevation, ui/fields.rs (properties-and-dialogs-05), views/section.rs and section_surface.rs (tasks 06, 07).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool tests without egui: picking two wall nodes (snaps with FeatureRef) and then an offset creates a LinearDimension with two Bound points and that offset; clicking an edge binds both ends; Chained with four clicks and Enter creates one dimension with four points; a typed offset of 1.00 is exact.
- kittest (epic acceptance): a dimension placed on two wall nodes in plan shows '5.000'; moving the wall end by a typed 1.00 updates it to '6.000'; deleting that wall shows '?' and adds a problems-panel entry; undo restores '6.000'.
- Project unit and precision: with the unit switched to millimetres with 0 decimals the same dimension shows '6000', with centimetres and 1 decimal '600.0', and the stored value is unchanged (NFR-ACC-005, values rounded for display only).
- Level dimension tool on a slab top in plan and on a free point in a section: switching the origin between project zero, storey, sea level and the user reference level shows the values of the task 13 fixture (+3.000, +-0.000, +415.000, +1.800).
- Display: on-screen text height equals text_size_mm at the view's scale (zoom scales it, a scale change changes it), lines use the annotation pen with at least one device pixel, text is never upside down; a golden image of a dimensioned plan passes on CI.
- Dimensions can be selected, deleted and re-offset with numeric input in plan and in sections.
- ANN-004 and ANN-005 satisfied end to end.
notes: SRS: ANN-004 ANN-005 (tools and display).

title: Section and elevation views, dimensions, labels and quantities
description:
Section and elevation markers as reference elements driving live views from arbitrary-plane slices with the plan rules, storey level lines and grid axes, selection and stretching in sections, drawing openings, elevation outlines and 2D geometry there, four default elevations; linear, level and angle dimensions with associative bindings and copy semantics, text and labels, selection quantities, union area, net void volume and the geometry clean-up check. Arbitrary-plane slicing is a generalisation of slice.rs, not a Boolean, so no kernel dependency.

Risks: VIEW-030 is extra large; projection depth and hidden-line removal stay simple (depth-ordered painting) in v1.
design: archicraft-geometry slice.rs generalised to arbitrary planes with projection and depth clipping, reusing plan.rs classification; archicraft-model kinds/marker.rs and kinds/dimension.rs with the annotation-binding relation keyed by (ElementId, feature key); archicraft-app Pane::Section in egui_tiles drawn by the plan renderer; dimensions and text in paper units at the view scale (decision D-8: viewing and basic editing); text drawn by egui as an overlay layer at the resolved paper size.
acceptance_criteria: Moving a marker updates its section (slice hash test on RM-S); the section shows labelled storey lines and grid axes; a wall height is stretched in a section with numeric input; a new project has four elevations in the browser; a dimension picked on a wall node follows the wall and is flagged when its reference disappears; level dimensions relative to project zero, storey, sea level and user origin; selection quantities summed per kind; the clean-up check finds two overlapping walls and drops the entry once fixed. Dimension bindings reference element id plus a semantic feature key (face role, node index), never mesh indices, so a regenerated wall keeps its dimensions (test).
notes: SRS: VIEW-030 VIEW-031 VIEW-032 VIEW-058 VIEW-059 GRD-009 OPN-013 WAL-011 ANN-004 ANN-005 ANN-006 ANN-007 ANN-008 ANN-009 ANN-012 MEA-002 MEA-004 MEA-005 OPN-011

title: Add the AS-01 railing to RM-S, its conformance check and procedure step
description:
WHY: AS-01 (SRS 7.2) contains a U-shaped stair with railing, and its railing is the only Should part of the scenario; the epic acceptance requires that the AS-01 railing on the U-stair exports IfcRailing with parts and passes conformance. reference-models left the railing variant of RM-S, the railing step of the scripted AS-01 procedure (reference-models-07) and the railing clause of the NFR-USE-006 template-only demonstration (reference-models-08) to this epic. RAI-002 (attachment and continuation), RAI-007 (presets) and RAI-010 (IfcRailing with parts) are exercised together on the real reference model; NFR-USE-006 requires that the railing needs no attribute beyond the template.

WHAT: Extend samples::rm_s() (crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs, reference-models-01/02) with the AS-01 railing: the vertical-bars preset (task 09) on the template layer 'Stairs and railings', added with Command::AddAttachedRailing to the U-stair's inner edge and continued along the upper slab's stair-opening edge, using only template materials (Steel) and presets; re-bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/rm-s.ifcx after reviewing the diff; extend the AS-01 assertions of conformance/check.ts (reference-models-05) with the IfcRailing under the stair's storey and its IfcMember children; add the railing step to the scripted AS-01 procedure and its kittest (reference-models-07): railing tool, pick the stair edge, accept the proposed slab edge, Enter; extend the template-only test of reference-models-08 to the railing. Explicitly out of scope: three-OS execution (release-candidate), RM-M and RM-L (perf-tuning-rm-m-l).
design: rm_s() comes from reference-models (increment 2): extend it rather than building a parallel AS-01 model. Build the railing through commands with seeded v5 ids so the golden stays deterministic. Pitfall: bless rm-s.ifcx only after reviewing the diff; the railing adds many small part nodes, so check the file-size and timing budgets of the regression harness.
acceptance_criteria:
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green with the updated rm-s.ifcx; check.ts verifies the AS-01 railing on the U-stair as IfcRailing with IfcMember children (posts, rails, balusters), each with a class, a name and a closed mesh (the epic acceptance).
- roundtrip.rs: rm_s() loads back equal including the attachment; save-load-save is byte-identical; the AS-03 automation (reference-models-06, storey height change) re-solves the stair, the railing follows and its UUID is unchanged.
- The AS-01 procedure kittest draws the railing with picking and continuation in one undo step.
- The reference-models-08 template-only test passes with the railing: no material, layer structure or other attribute is created.
- Satisfies the AS-01 railing part through RAI-002, RAI-007 and RAI-010.
notes:
SRS: RAI-002 RAI-007 RAI-010
If rm_s() is not yet merged when this starts, attach the railing to samples::u_stair() and move it into rm_s() when it lands (reference-models is increment 2, so ordering normally guarantees it).

title: Sweep railing rails along 3D polylines with ends and corners
description:
WHY: RAI-003 rails (top rail, handrail, intermediate rails) each carry their own profile shape, size, material and vertical position; RAI-001 places the railing on the left, centre or right of its 3D reference line with an offset and gives each segment a height; RAI-006 requires rail end extensions (0 allowed) with an end shape and corners that are mitred or disconnected. technology-choices.md builds 3D bodies with our own mesh generation; profiles-columns-beams-05 delivered sweep.rs (a section swept along a straight axis with planar end cuts) and section.rs (parametric and profile sections), which this task reuses. Every body must be closed, 2-manifold and outward oriented, share vertices only across smooth edges and stay below 65,535 points (IFX-038).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/railing/{mod.rs, rails.rs} and the railing entry in the geometry kind registry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/railing.rs, element-kind-framework-15): `rail_path(railing, rail) -> Vec<DVec3>` offsets the reference line in plan by side and offset with mitred joints (Arc segments offset exactly and tessellated with tessellate() of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs, drafting-trim-split-02, elevations interpolated along the arc length), keeps each node's elevation and lifts it by the rail's vertical position (measured vertically, to the top of the section; the top rail and handrail take the effective segment height of task 02, so a segment with its own height lifts them on that segment only); `rail_bodies(path, spec, closed, tessellation) -> Result<Vec<BodyPart>, GeometryError>` sweeps the section along every segment with sweep(): the frame keeps the profile upright (v = world Z made perpendicular to the axis), interior nodes are cut by the bisector plane (normal = normalize(d_i + d_i+1)) for Mitred, or by perpendicular planes pulled back to the corner post faces for Disconnected; open ends are extended along the end tangent by the extension and finished as Square (perpendicular cut), Plumb (vertical cut) or a Return piece (down, or horizontally towards the railing side, of the given length, joined with a mitre); closed railings mitre the last node with the first; where two neighbouring segments have different effective heights the joint between them is Disconnected (a vertical step between two perpendicular end faces) whatever the corner setting. The registry entry emits PartGeometry children TopRail_<run>, Handrail_<run> and Rail_<k>_<run> with the roles of Kind::parts(). Explicitly out of scope: posts, balusters and panels (task 04), host-derived paths (task 05), plan symbol (task 07), IFCX parts (task 06).
design: Reuse sweep() and CutPlane from crates/archicraft-geometry/src/sweep.rs: mitre planes are exact for prisms, so volumes stay exact and the two bodies at a joint meet face to face. frame_for_beam rejects vertical axes, so a ReturnDown piece takes the previous segment's u axis as its frame hint. Upright frames (not rotation-minimising ones) keep a handrail's top face horizontal; where a plan turn coincides with a slope change the two sections differ slightly on the mitre plane, which is accepted for symmetric profiles and documented (Archicad behaves alike). Joints sharper than about 15 degrees make the mitre plane almost parallel to the axis: fall back to Disconnected for that joint and report it instead of omitting geometry (the STA-044 principle). Use profile_section for Profile sections and parametric_section for inline rectangles and circles (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/section.rs); one section triangulation per rail is reused for all caps. The plan offset of straight runs uses offset_polyline(points, closed, distances) next to offset_ring in crates/archicraft-model/src/outline/edit.rs (edit-reshape-palette-05) instead of a second offset implementation; arc segments use Segment::offset of crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs (drafting-trim-split-01) before tessellation.
acceptance_criteria:
- New crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/railing.rs: a straight 4.300 m railing with a 50 x 50 mm top rail at 1.00 m gives one closed body (TriMesh::check_closed) with volume 0.05 x 0.05 x 4.3 m3 (1e-9 relative) and its top at z = 1.000 m.
- A 90-degree L railing with Mitred corners gives two closed bodies whose mitre faces lie in the bisector plane, whose volumes sum to area x centreline length and do not overlap; with Disconnected both bodies end in perpendicular faces separated by the corner post width.
- A 3D polyline (2 m flat, 3 m rising 1.5 m, 1 m flat) keeps the section upright on every segment (|u.z| < 1e-12) and every body closed across the slope changes.
- Extension 0.30 m adds 0.30 m along the end tangent at each end; ReturnDown 0.10 m adds a closed vertical piece; a Plumb end face has a horizontal normal; no degenerate triangles.
- Side Left, Centre and Right with offset 0.05 m put the rail axis at the expected perpendicular distance from the reference line (1e-9).
- A circular 42 mm handrail tessellated per IFX-034 shares vertices only around its circumference (smooth strip) and a 30-segment railing stays below MAX_MESH_POINTS.
- A 180-degree back-tracking node or a self-overlapping extension returns GeometryError and is listed as a problem; nothing panics.
- Segment height: on a three-segment railing with 1.10 m on segment 2 the top rail of segment 2 has its top at 1.10 m and those of segments 1 and 3 at 1.00 m; both joints are Disconnected steps and every body is closed.
- Section shapes: a handrail with a Profile(ProfileId) section of a custom profile (profiles-columns-beams-15) sweeps to a closed body of profile area x length (1e-9 relative); an extension of 0.000 m adds no length; a ReturnToSide end adds a closed horizontal piece towards the railing side.
- Intermediate rails: InnerRails { count: 3, bottom: 0.10, top: 0.70 } gives three closed rail bodies with their tops at 0.10, 0.40 and 0.70 m; disabling the top rail removes only TopRail parts.
- Satisfies the rail geometry of RAI-003, the side, offset and segment-height clauses of RAI-001 and RAI-006 (end extension and shape, mitred or disconnected corners).
notes:
SRS: RAI-001 RAI-003 RAI-006
Vertical positions are measured to the top of the rail section because handrail heights are specified to the top.

title: Add a ramp mode to the stair with fixed or limited pitch
description:
WHY: STA-050 (C): a ramp mode may provide a step-less flight with fixed or limited pitch, width and landings, and a plan symbol with walking line and up/down label but without step lines. Test: a pitch fixed at 5 degrees and a rise of 0.500 m give a horizontal length of about 5.715 m. Simple ramps remain possible as sloped slabs (SLB-006). Gap STA-050: missing (M).

WHAT: `StairParams.mode: StairMode::{Steps, Ramp(RampSpec { pitch: PitchRule::{Fixed(f64), Limited { max: f64 }} })}` in crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/config.rs. Solver (crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/solve.rs): ramps skip the riser rules; Fixed gives the total horizontal flight length L = rise / tan(pitch) (flights lengthen with lock baseline off; with it on, a mismatch beyond tolerance is a conflict offering Limited or unlocking); Limited computes pitch = atan(rise / available flight length) and reports a conflict above max; landings stay flat with the STA-022 minimum length; the rise is shared by the flights in proportion to their length (one pitch); arc baselines (task 13) give curved ramps. Geometry (new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/ramp.rs): straight flights as sloped bodies through extrude_profile of the side profile across the width, arc flights through the helicoidal strip builder of task 14, with a planar walking surface and the STA-041 structure thickness, landings flat, all closed. Plan (stair/symbol.rs): outline, walking line with arrow, up/down label and break line, no step lines. IFCX: mode in archicraft::stair (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs); in ramp mode the stair's default class becomes IfcRamp (D.5 list, element-kind-framework-05) with IfcRampFlight and IfcSlab landing parts, adding IfcRampFlight to IfcClass and the predefined-type registry (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/registry.rs). UI: mode switch and pitch fields in the stair settings (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs); the read-out shows pitch and length instead of R and G. Explicitly out of scope: ramp gradient standards and automatic handrails.
design: Ramp mode reuses baseline, width, side, segments and landings of the stair so editing, display range and the plan break line come for free; only the solver branch, the flight generator and the plan step lines differ. Flights are generated with extrude_profile and the task 14 strip builder (no Boolean). Use exact trigonometry with angles in radians internally (SRS 3.5) and format in degrees.
acceptance_criteria:
- Solver test: Fixed(5 degrees) with a 0.500 m rise gives a horizontal length of 5.715 m (0.5 / tan 5 degrees = 5.71503 m, 1e-4), the STA-050 test.
- Limited(6 degrees) with a drawn 4.0 m flight and 0.5 m rise (7.125 degrees) is a conflict naming the pitch rule with alternatives; a 6.0 m flight (4.764 degrees) is accepted.
- A ramp with one landing has two flights at the same pitch and a flat landing of at least 1.00 m (D.3 automatic landing length).
- Bodies closed; the plan symbol contains a walking line, arrow and up/down label and no step lines.
- IFCX: IfcRamp with IfcRampFlight children round-trips and passes conformance.
- kittest: switching an existing stair to Ramp mode makes the read-out show the pitch.
- Width and landings: a 1.20 m wide ramp gives 1.20 m wide flight and landing bodies; inserting a baseline node creates a flat automatic landing as for stairs (STA-022).
- Satisfies STA-050.
notes:
SRS: STA-050
Open question: Table 5-1 lists no ramp; chosen mapping IfcRamp with IfcRampFlight parts (alternative: keep IfcStair with archicraft::stair.mode = ramp).

title: Verify exit criterion: Railings, winders, spiral stairs and stair extras
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its exit criterion is demonstrated on the integrated workspace: railings (RAI-001 to RAI-010), winders (STA-025, STA-026), curved and spiral flights with chord or arc goings (STA-027, STA-028), stringers (STA-042), numbering (STA-047), conversion to free-form solids (STA-048), stairs in solid operations (STA-049) and the ramp mode (STA-050) must work together, AS-01 must pass including its railing, and the status document must say so.

WHAT: Run the workspace quality gates and the conformance job on all golden files; walk through the exit scenario in the app (draw a railing as a 3D polyline, attach one to the AS-01 U-stair and continue it onto the upper slab, change the riser count and watch it follow, apply the three presets, drape a railing on terrain, set a winder corner and a winder segment, draw a curved flight and a spiral, switch chord and arc measures, add stringers, enable numbering, switch a stair to ramp mode, convert a stair to free-form solids and cut a stair into terrain); update docs/implementation-status.md rows RAI-001 to RAI-010, STA-025 to STA-028, STA-042, STA-047, STA-048, STA-049 and STA-050 with evidence paths and remaining gaps, the AS-01 row (railing part) and the increment-3 readiness; close the epic in beads and file follow-up beads for anything left (for example per-bar baluster members, handrail brackets, further winder constructions of Section 8).
design: Verification only; no new features. Use the integrated main branch after all tasks have merged. Evidence comes from the tests named in tasks 01-23: distribution.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/railing.rs and railing_plan.rs, railing/path.rs, railing/presets.rs, stair/winders.rs, stair_advanced.rs, the round-trip suite and golden files (railings.ifcx, rm-s.ifcx, stairs-advanced.ifcx, stair-solid-ops.ifcx), the tools tests and kittests. If a gate fails, reopen the owning task rather than patching here.
acceptance_criteria:
- RAI-004: 4.300 m with a 1.200 m maximum gives 4 bays of 1.075 m.
- RAI-005: one tread with 3 divisions puts balusters at 1/3 and 2/3.
- A railing follows its stair when the riser count changes.
- The AS-01 railing on the U-stair exports IfcRailing with parts (conformance).
- Winder count rules and the arc versus chord measures (r·θ versus 2r·sin(θ/2)) are covered by unit tests.
- A ramp at 5° with 0.500 m rise is about 5.715 m long.
- A stair converts to one free-form solid per part after one notice.
- A stair cut into terrain through a solid operation follows when the stair re-solves (STA-049).
- The scripted AS-01 procedure includes the railing step (reference-models-07) and the NFR-USE-006 template-only test covers the railing (reference-models-08).
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green on every golden file, including railings.ifcx, rm-s.ifcx with the railing, stairs-advanced.ifcx and stair-solid-ops.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (RAI-001 to RAI-010, STA-025, STA-026, STA-027, STA-028, STA-042, STA-047, STA-048, STA-049, STA-050) with evidence and remaining gaps.
- The epic is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for every remaining gap.
notes:
SRS: RAI-001 RAI-002 RAI-003 RAI-004 RAI-005 RAI-006 RAI-007 RAI-008 RAI-009 RAI-010 STA-025 STA-026 STA-027 STA-028 STA-042 STA-047 STA-048 STA-050 STA-049
The task breakdown sums to about 30 engineer-days (14,460 minutes) against the roadmap's 15-day epic size; the difference reflects the L/XL gap ratings (RAI-001, RAI-002, RAI-003, STA-025, STA-027, STA-042) and the AS-01 railing fixture work that reference-models handed to this epic.

title: Add the railing distribution engine as pure functions
description:
WHY: RAI-004 (S) distributes railing components along each segment by one of three modes, with start, centre or end alignment: a fixed number of divisions, a fixed pattern length, or equal distribution with a maximum length where bays = ⌈length / max⌉ and bay length = length / bays; its test is 4.300 m with a 1.200 m maximum giving 4 bays of 1.075 m. RAI-005 (S) lets the pattern on stairs repeat every n treads with a post on each riser line and a chosen number of balusters per tread; its test is a pattern length of 1 tread with 3 divisions giving balusters at 1/3 and 2/3 of each tread between the posts. Appendix D.2 fixes the railing defaults: inner posts at most 1.20 m apart and vertical bars with at most 0.12 m clear spacing. Gap rows RAI-004 and RAI-005 are missing (M each): nothing in the codebase distributes anything along a path. Writing the engine first as pure functions pins both numeric acceptances before any geometry exists, and the same engine later places posts, balusters, panels and the draped posts of RAI-008.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/distribution.rs (re-exported from lib.rs, no geometry or UI dependency): `Distribution::{Divisions { count: u32 }, PatternLength { length: f64 }, MaxLength { max: f64 }}`, `Alignment::{Start, Centre, End}`, `fn stations(length: f64, d: &Distribution, a: Alignment) -> Result<Vec<f64>, DistributionError>` returning the bay boundary stations including 0 and length; `Infill::{Count(u32), MaxClearSpacing { max_clear: f64, bar_width: f64 }}` with `fn fill_bay(start: f64, end: f64, post_widths: (f64, f64), infill: &Infill) -> Vec<f64>` for baluster centres inside a bay (the D.2 0.12 m rule chooses the smallest bar count whose clear gaps stay within max_clear); `TreadPattern { every_treads: u32, divisions_per_tread: u32 }` with `fn tread_stations(riser_stations: &[f64], p: &TreadPattern) -> TreadLayout { posts: Vec<f64>, balusters: Vec<f64> }`, where riser stations are the plan arc-length positions of the riser lines along a railing path, posts sit on the first and last riser line (end posts) and on every n-th riser line, and balusters sit at the interior division points of each tread and on riser lines that carry no post. Typed DistributionError for count 0, non-positive or non-finite lengths. Explicitly out of scope: the railing data model (task 02), 3D placement of components (task 04), extraction of riser stations from a stair (task 05) and any UI.
design: Compute stations as i·L/bays (never by cumulative addition) so the last station is exactly L and no drift accumulates; bays = max(1, ceil((L - MODEL_TOLERANCE) / max)) so 3.600 / 1.200 stays 3. PatternLength: whole = floor((L + tol) / p), remainder r = L - whole·p; Start places whole patterns from 0 and the remainder at the end, End mirrors it, Centre splits the remainder equally at both ends. Use MODEL_TOLERANCE from crates/archicraft-model/src/tolerance.rs (element-kind-framework-01) only. The module is generic on purpose (a length and parameters in, stations out): railings use plan arc length, draping (task 10) uses 3D arc length, and curtain-wall grids may reuse it. drafting-trim-split-14 adds crates/archicraft-model/src/array.rs (ArrayMethod::{CountSpacing, CountBetween, SpacingToExtent, CountToExtent}, ArraySpec::placements) for copies, not bays with alignment: reuse its count and spacing arithmetic where it matches and keep only the railing-specific modes, alignment, infill and tread pattern here, so there is one station implementation per concept. Pitfall: keep TreadPattern independent of stair types so the model crate's stair modules do not become a dependency of this file.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in distribution.rs: MaxLength { max: 1.200 } on 4.300 m gives stations [0, 1.075, 2.150, 3.225, 4.300] within 1e-12 (the RAI-004 test); 3.600 m gives exactly 3 bays (no sliver bay from floating error); a length below the maximum gives one bay.
- Divisions { count: 5 } on 4.000 m gives 0.800 m bays; PatternLength { length: 1.200 } on 4.300 m gives [0, 1.2, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3] with Start, [0, 0.7, 1.9, 3.1, 4.3] with End and [0, 0.35, 1.55, 2.75, 3.95, 4.3] with Centre; a remainder below MODEL_TOLERANCE adds no station.
- fill_bay with MaxClearSpacing { max_clear: 0.12, bar_width: 0.02 } in a 1.075 m bay between 0.05 m posts yields 7 bars with a clear gap of 0.110625 m, and every gap is <= 0.12 m.
- tread_stations with riser stations [0, 0.28, 0.56, 0.84], every_treads 1, divisions_per_tread 3 puts posts on all four riser lines and balusters at 1/3 and 2/3 of each tread (0.0933.., 0.1866.., ...; 1e-12) (the RAI-005 test); every_treads 2 keeps the end posts, puts a post on riser 2 and a baluster on riser 1.
- A seeded randomized loop (the workspace has no proptest dependency) asserts stations start at 0, end at length, increase strictly and keep every bay <= max in MaxLength mode.
- Invalid parameters return DistributionError; nothing panics.
- Satisfies the distribution modes and alignment of RAI-004 and the per-tread pattern arithmetic of RAI-005 (applied to real railings in tasks 04 and 22).
notes:
SRS: RAI-004 RAI-005
Appendix D.2: inner posts at most 1.20 m apart; vertical bars with <= 0.12 m clear spacing (typical European requirement, to be verified per jurisdiction).

title: Attach railings to stair and slab edges and follow the host
description:
WHY: RAI-002 (S): a railing shall be attachable to stair edges and slab edges by picking them, shall follow the host when the host changes unless set to static, and can continue from a stair edge onto the slab the stair arrives at as one continuous element. The epic acceptance requires that a railing follows its stair when the riser count changes. SRS 3.3 stores relations with the model and re-evaluates them automatically. Gap RAI-002: missing (L): no edge picking, no host relation or associativity (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:64-91 evaluates elements independently), no static mode, no continuation. What the prerequisites provide and this task builds on: the relation store with dependents_of, Edit::InsertRelation/RemoveRelation and the relation codec (crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs, element-kind-framework-08), incremental evaluation from a dirty set (element-kind-framework-10), the mesh-free stair layout StairLayout { outline, flights, landings, risers: Vec<RiserLine { a, b, z, station }> } of crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/layout.rs (stair-body-plan-02) with the stored StairSolution, and arc slab edges as exact curve.rs arcs (curved-geometry-01/08).

WHAT: Model: a `Relation::RailingAttachment { railing, host, edge: HostEdge, seq: u16 }` variant in relations.rs with `HostEdge::{Stair { side: Left|Right, from: Option<u32>, to: Option<u32> } (riser index range), SlabEdge { ring: u16, start: (u32, f64), end: (u32, f64) } (start and end edge index with parameter on one outline ring, so one attachment may span several consecutive edges, for example around a stair opening)}`; because a RelationId is the v5 of the variant and its ends, a railing has at most one attachment per host, which the spanning SlabEdge makes sufficient. dependents_of(host) returns the railing. Railing gains `fixed: bool` (static) and keeps `reference` with its RailSegment shapes (task 02) as the last resolved path. Pure resolution in crates/archicraft-model/src/railing/path.rs (no geometry dependency, NFR-MNT-002): `resolve(project, railing) -> Result<RailPath { nodes, segments, riser_stations, floor_z: [f64; 2] }, PathError>` takes a stair edge from StairLayout (left or right boundary at the nosing line, elevations from the riser z values, landings flat) and a slab edge at the slab top as exact segments (arc edges stay Curve::Arc; the geometry tessellates them with the shared tessellate() so posts land on the slab body's edge), orders the pieces by seq, orients each by its nearest end and joins them; a gap above the join tolerance is bridged by a straight connector and reported. riser_stations (plan arc-length position of every riser line along the path) and floor_z (bottom floor or landing, arrival slab top) are produced here for task 22. Commands in crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs: `Command::AttachRailing { railing, hosts: Vec<(ElementId, HostEdge)> }` for an existing railing and `Command::AddAttachedRailing { element, hosts }`, which plans InsertElement and the InsertRelation edits in one command (one undo step; Command::Batch only arrives with could-scope-polish-18), both validating host kinds and edges; `Command::SetRailingStatic { railing, fixed }` snapshots the resolved path into reference when fixing and re-resolves when releasing; plan_delete_elements, which already removes the relations of deleted elements (element-kind-framework-08), also turns railings attached to a deleted host static with their snapshot in the same undo step. Geometry: the railing GeometryKind (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/railing.rs, task 03) evaluates the resolve() path while attached and the stored reference while static; components keep the segment distribution of task 04 on every piece until task 22 adds the per-tread pattern. Explicitly out of scope: the per-tread stair pattern and floor-reaching end posts (task 22), the picking UI (task 08), the plan break line (task 07), IFCX persistence (task 06), terrain draping (task 10).
design: A relation in the store instead of host ids inside the railing gives dependency queries, integrity checks, dangling-end repair, undo and IFCX persistence from element-kind-framework-08; seq orders the continuation chain. Resolution is a pure model function so commands can snapshot without the geometry crate (NFR-MNT-002); it calls layout() with the stored StairSolution and never re-solves, as the stair GeometryKind does (stair-body-plan-04). Height on stair pieces is measured vertically above the nosing (pitch) line, on landings and slabs above the walking surface. Deleting a host makes the railing static rather than deleting it: a railing is not a hosted element in the IFX-015 sense and stays a storey child, unlike the ELM-016 cascade of openings. Pitfalls: the arrival slab edge may run opposite to the stair edge, so orient by nearest end points; arc slab edges stay exact in the model and are tessellated only by the geometry's tessellate() (fixture F8 rule), never in path.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AttachRailing and AddAttachedRailing then undo and redo restore identical projects (AddAttachedRailing is one undo step); attaching to a wall or to a missing edge returns CommandError::Invalid; SetRailingStatic stores exactly the resolve() nodes and segments; deleting the stair leaves the railing static with its last path and one undo restores stair and attachment.
- railing/path.rs tests: a straight stair (3.000 m rise, 18 risers) right edge resolves to the nosing line with one riser station per riser line; the inner edge of samples::u_stair() (stair-body-plan-02) gives a flat landing piece; a stair edge continued onto the arrival slab edge yields one path whose consecutive nodes coincide within MODEL_TOLERANCE; a SlabEdge spanning the three edges of a stair opening resolves to one piece with two corners; an arc slab edge resolves to an exact Arc segment.
- Follow test (epic acceptance): an attached railing's path gains one riser station and its top end follows the moved top nosing when the riser count changes from 18 to 19, and it follows a storey height change from 3.000 to 3.300 m that re-solves the stair to 22 risers; a static railing does not change.
- Incremental evaluation: editing the stair or the slab puts the railing into the dirty set (element-kind-framework-10 dirty-set test extended); after delete and undo Project::integrity_problems() is empty.
- Satisfies RAI-002 at the model and geometry level (attachment, following, static, continuation); picking is task 08.
notes:
SRS: RAI-002
Open question: Archicad deletes stair railings with the stair; ArchiCraft keeps them static (undoable, reported). Join tolerance assumed 0.10 m.

title: Convert stairs to free-form solids, one per part
description:
WHY: STA-048 (S): a whole stair shall be convertible into plain free-form solids, one per part (SOL-004: conversion keeps the evaluated geometry and face materials after confirmation that the parametric definition is lost); NFR-USE-004 allows one notice with a 'do not show again' option. The epic acceptance requires one free-form solid per part after one notice. Gap STA-048: missing (M): no free-form solid element and no conversion. free-form-solids-08 now provides solid_from_parts(&[BodyPart]) -> Result<PolyMesh, ConvertError> and convert_element in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/solid_convert.rs, Command::ReplaceWithSolids { replacements: Vec<(ElementId, Solid)>, hosted } (one solid per element, keeping id, name, storey, layer and position, baking relations in which the element is a target and keeping those in which it is an operator) and the conversion notice with 'Do not show again' in Preferences (crates/archicraft-app/src/persistence/prefs.rs); it explicitly leaves the per-part stair conversion to this epic.

WHAT: Extend ReplaceWithSolids so one source element can be replaced by several solids: the stair's Kind::parts() order (Flight_n, Landing_n, Stringer_..., as in IFCX) gives one solid per part, each built by solid_from_parts from that part's bodies (tread, riser, finish and structure bodies united through the SolidKernel with per-face materials kept; when a union fails, one solid per body and a report, never a failed conversion); the first part keeps the stair's ElementId as single conversions do and the further parts get new ids; names '<stair name> <part label>', same storey and layer, class by part from the D.5 list (landing IfcSlab, stringer IfcMember, flight IfcStair, because IfcStairFlight is not selectable for free-form solids). Relations, planned inside the same command (one undo step): railings attached to the stair become static with their snapshot (task 05), solid operations using the stair as operator are copied to every new solid (task 20), operations targeting the stair are baked into the converted geometry and removed (free-form-solids-08 rule). App: the existing 'Convert to free-form solid' action accepts stairs and shows the same notice once, listing the parts. Explicitly out of scope: converting the attached railings (they stay elements, made static), new Boolean features.
design: One solid per part, not per body, matches 'one per part' and the IFCX part structure; uniting the touching tread, riser and structure bodies needs the kernel, and the fallback keeps conversion from failing on coplanar contacts (a known Manifold sensitivity covered by solid-kernel-ops fixtures). Extending ReplaceWithSolids instead of adding a stair-specific command keeps one conversion path for undo, relation baking and hosted elements. Relation handling follows SOL-004: what the stair suffered is baked, what it did to others continues through the new solids.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests: converting samples::u_stair() with stringers (task 16) yields exactly one closed free-form solid per part with the source face materials and the same total volume (1e-9 relative); one undo restores the stair, its railing attachment and its relations; an attached railing becomes static with an unchanged path.
- A stair that operates on terrain (task 20) leaves every converted part as an operator of that terrain, and the terrain cut volume is unchanged (1e-6 relative).
- A forced union failure (failing kernel injected) produces one solid per body plus a report, and the conversion still succeeds.
- kittest: 'Convert to free-form solid' on a stair shows the notice once; with 'Do not show again' ticked the next conversion runs without it and the preference persists.
- IFCX round trip of the converted solids with their classes; conformance green.
- Satisfies STA-048.
notes:
SRS: STA-048
IfcStairFlight is not in the D.5 list, hence IfcStair for converted flights (open question). Keeping the stair's ElementId on the first part is an assumption consistent with free-form-solids-08.

title: Add stringer and beam supports to stairs
description:
WHY: STA-042 (C): stringer and beam supports may be provided — closed or open stringers left and right, with profile, offset and end cuts. STA-051 writes stringers as IfcMember children of IfcStair; STA-044 requires a reported simple joint when a part such as a stringer corner piece cannot be built. Gap STA-042: missing (L), no stringers and no profile resource at the time; profiles-columns-beams has since delivered profiles, section.rs and sweep.rs.

WHAT: Model (crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/config.rs, embedded in StairParams): `StairParams.supports: Vec<StairSupport { position: SupportPosition::{Left, Right, Offset(f64)}, kind: SupportKind::{Closed, Open}, section: ComponentSection, material, vertical_offset, lateral_offset, end_cuts: [EndCut; 2] }>` with `EndCut::{Plumb, Horizontal, Perpendicular, Angle(f64)}`; Offset positions a beam support under the treads at a lateral distance from the baseline; validation in StairParams::validate_config (open stringers need a rectangular section, profiles need ProfileUsage.beams of profiles-columns-beams-01). Geometry (new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/supports.rs, reusing sweep() and CutPlane of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/sweep.rs and the sections of section.rs, profiles-columns-beams-03/05): closed stringers and beams are sweep()s along the support path — parallel to the pitch line on flights, horizontal on landings, tessellated and mitred along winder and arc edges — with mitred corner pieces between flight and landing, or a butt joint plus an STA-044 report when the mitre degenerates; open (cut) stringers are sawtooth plates (top following treads and risers, bottom parallel to the pitch line) extruded by the thickness, one plate per step on curved edges; end cuts as CutPlanes at the floor and at the arrival slab. Parts Stringer_L_n, Stringer_R_n and Beam_n as IfcMember with predefined type STRINGER; supports in archicraft::stair (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs, optional); the stairs-advanced golden of task 21 gains stringers. UI: a support list in the stair settings dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs: add, remove, fields, the profiles dialog picker of profiles-columns-beams-14). Explicitly out of scope: cantilever, plate and pan structures (Section 8).
design: The support path is derived from the stair layout (boundary polylines and nosing elevations), the same data railings use in task 05, so stringers and railings stay aligned. Closed stringers reuse sweep() with mitre planes exactly like rails (task 03); open stringers are 2D polygons in the edge's vertical plane extruded with extrude() in a local frame. Beam supports are IfcMember (Table 5-1 lists only IfcMember for stair supports). Pitfall: open stringers on arc edges cannot be one planar plate; one plate per step keeps every body planar and closed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: a straight 18-riser stair with closed UPE 200 stringers on both sides gives two closed bodies parallel to the pitch line (1e-9), a plumb cut at the floor and the configured cut at the slab, volume = area x length between the cuts (1e-6 relative).
- An open 40 x 250 mm stringer is one closed sawtooth plate whose top vertices coincide with the tread and riser corners (1e-9).
- A centred HEA 140 beam support (Offset 0) lies under the treads at the configured offset.
- A U-stair's landing corner pieces are mitred and closed; a degenerate corner reports per STA-044 and uses a butt joint.
- A spiral with a closed outer stringer is closed and follows the helix within the IFX-034 tolerance.
- IFCX round trip; conformance shows IfcMember STRINGER children; kittest: adding a right stringer in the settings dialog makes the Stringer_R_1 part appear.
- Offsets and end cuts: a lateral offset of 0.05 m and a vertical offset of -0.02 m move the stringer axis by exactly those amounts relative to the stair edge and the nosing line (1e-9); each EndCut variant (Plumb, Horizontal, Perpendicular, Angle 30 degrees) gives an end face with the expected normal (1e-12).
- Satisfies STA-042.
notes: SRS: STA-042

title: Edit winders and draw curved and spiral stairs in the stair tool
description:
WHY: Users must be able to choose winders as a corner turning type or a segment type with their count rule (STA-025, STA-026), enter arc baselines with a centre point for curved and spiral flights (STA-027) and choose the chord or arc going measure per stair (STA-028); STA-002 previews the live riser count during input and STA-009 shows R, G, 2R+G, N and the pitch while placing and editing; STA-011's conflict dialog must name winder conflicts. The stair tool of stair-solver-tool draws straight baseline segments only.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/stair.rs: baseline input gains arc segments modelled on curved-geometry-07's WallMode::ArcCentre (centre, start, end) and WallMode::ArcThreePoints in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/wall.rs (their StepSpecs factored into a shared arc-input helper in crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/ rather than copied), a Spiral mode (centre, start point fixing the radius, sweep by cursor or typed, 360 degrees for a full turn) and the Chain-mode key that toggles the next segment between straight and tangent arc; the live preview shows the riser count and the read-out with the selected measure. Edit mode: selecting an interior baseline node (PartRef::Node) shows its turning type (Landing or Winder) with construction, offsets and count mode; selecting a segment shows its type (Flight, Landing or Winder); the stair properties and the settings dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs, stair-solver-tool-10 and stair-body-plan-13) show the going measure and update dependent values live (ELM-017). The conflict dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs, stair-solver-tool-11) lists winder conflicts with their alternatives. Explicitly out of scope: stringer, numbering and ramp fields (tasks 16-18).
design: Arc input reuses the StepSpecs and previews of curved-geometry-07 (wall arc modes) so snapping, typed radius and sweep and the Esc ladder behave identically. Turning-type fields are FieldSpecs registered by the stair kind for PartRef::Node, so the properties panel needs no stair-specific code paths. The preview re-runs the pure solver per mouse move on a temporary stair; keep it allocation-light (the 50 ms latency budget of point-input-snapping applies).
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless tool tests: ArcCentre input of a 90-degree curved flight creates a stair whose baseline segment is an exact Arc with the snapped centre bit for bit; Spiral mode with a typed 360-degree sweep creates a full-turn spiral; Backspace removes the last segment.
- kittest: setting corner 1 of an L-stair to Winder with Fixed(3) and offsets 0.5/0.3 goings updates the riser read-out and the plan shows winder step lines; switching the measure to Chord changes the going read-out; choosing SinglePoint shows before/after fields.
- kittest: Fixed(6) on a narrow corner opens the conflict dialog naming 'winder risers cross'.
- Satisfies the user-facing clauses of STA-025, STA-026, STA-027 and STA-028.
notes: SRS: STA-025 STA-026 STA-027 STA-028

title: Add the railing kind with a 3D reference line and component set
description:
WHY: RAI-001 (S) defines a railing by a 3D polyline reference line whose nodes carry independent elevations, with a segment height, a side of the reference line (left, centre, right) and an offset. RAI-003 (S) requires a top rail, a handrail, intermediate rails, end and corner posts, inner posts, balusters and infill panels (glass or solid), each switchable and with its own profile shape, size, material and vertical position. RAI-006 (S) gives rail ends an extension length (0 allowed) and an end shape, and lets rails at corners connect mitred or stay disconnected. Appendix D.2 sets the railing defaults (height 1.00 m, inner posts at most 1.20 m apart, top rail 50 x 50 mm, vertical bars with at most 0.12 m clear spacing) and Table 5-1 maps a railing to IfcRailing with IfcMember and IfcPlate parts. Gap: there is no railing element at all (RAI-001 L, RAI-003 XL, RAI-006 M) and plan tool points are 2D only (`points: Vec<DVec2>` in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:289, which point-input-snapping-01 moves to crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/railing.rs (payload and Kind impl) registered with one line in the kinds! macro of kinds/mod.rs (element-kind-framework-02), plus a new domain module crates/archicraft-model/src/railing/mod.rs for the component and section types (the layout stair-solver-tool chose with stair/ next to kinds/stair.rs; tasks 05 and 09 add railing/path.rs and railing/presets.rs): `Railing { reference: Vec<RailNode { position: DVec2, z: f64 }>, closed: bool, side: RailSide::{Left, Centre, Right}, offset: f64, height: f64, segments: Vec<RailSegment { shape: Curve, height: Option<f64>, posts: Option<(Distribution, Alignment)> }>, components: RailingComponents, tread_pattern: Option<TreadPattern> }` with node z relative to the home storey. One RailSegment per reference segment: shape is Curve::{Straight, Arc(Arc)} of crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs (drafting-trim-split-01), Straight by default and Arc only where a railing follows an arc slab edge (task 05), so the reference stays a 3D polyline in the RAI-001 sense; the effective segment height (RAI-001) is the segment's height or else the railing height, and the top rail, handrail and posts follow it while the other components keep their own vertical positions. `RailingComponents { top_rail, handrail: Toggle<RailSpec>, inner_rails: Toggle<InnerRails { count, bottom, top, rail: RailSpec }>, end_posts, corner_posts: Toggle<PostSpec>, inner_posts: Toggle<InnerPosts { post: PostSpec, distribution: Distribution, alignment: Alignment }>, balusters: Toggle<Balusters { bar: BarSpec, infill: Infill, bottom, top }>, panels: Toggle<Panels { kind: Glass|Solid, thickness, bottom, top, gap, material }> }` where `Toggle<T> { enabled, spec }` keeps the settings while switched off; `ComponentSection::{Profile(ProfileId), Rectangle { width, depth }, Circle { diameter }}` plus material; `RailSpec { section, material, height (vertical position to the top of the rail), ends: [RailEnd; 2], corner: CornerJoint::{Mitred, Disconnected} }`, `RailEnd { extension, shape: EndShape::{Square, Plumb, ReturnDown { length }, ReturnToSide { length }} }`. Kind hooks: validate (>= 2 nodes, no segment shorter than MODEL_TOLERANCE, finite z, height > 0, one RailSegment per segment with height > 0 and arc ends on their nodes within MODEL_TOLERANCE, sizes > 0, extension >= 0, profile references existing and flagged ProfileUsage.railings from profiles-columns-beams-01), transform (mirror flips side and ReturnToSide), vertical_extent (min z to max z plus height), material, profiles() so DeleteProfile re-points users, parts() with roles TopRail, Handrail, Rail, Post, Balusters, Panel and classes IfcMember/IfcPlate, edit-mode parts RailingPart::{Node { index }, Segment { index }} through PartRef (selection-transforms-01). RailingDefaults in the per-kind tool-defaults slot (element-kind-framework-04) filled from D.2 in template.rs; IfcClass::Railing as default class (element-kind-framework-05). Explicitly out of scope: bodies (tasks 03, 04), host attachment (task 05), IFCX codec (task 06), tool and dialogs (tasks 08, 09).
design: Store the reference line itself and apply side and offset in geometry, as walls do with their reference line, so attachment (task 05) can replace the path without touching the component settings. Node z relative to the home storey keeps railings following storey edits like wall base offsets. Inline Rectangle and Circle sections avoid forcing a Profile resource for plain bars; geometry maps them to profiles-columns-beams' ParametricShape so section.rs stays the single section generator. Part roles are derived from the parametric definition (component, segment, index), never from tessellation, so IFX-010 v5 ids stay stable. Keep KindDescriptor.has_tool false until task 08 so registry-iterating tests do not expect a tool before it exists; until task 06 the writer's wildcard arm saves railings without the kind attribute and warns (element-kind-framework-02), and until task 03 the geometry registry falls back to the framework's fallback box (element-kind-framework-13). Pointers: kinds/mod.rs and kinds/wall.rs, crates/archicraft-model/src/profile.rs, selection.rs, template.rs, validate.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- validate tests: a two-node railing with nodes at z 0.000 and 1.500 m is valid; a zero-length segment, a NaN elevation, a negative extension and a profile without the railings usage flag are rejected with explanatory messages; a disabled component keeps its settings through validation.
- Segment height: a three-segment railing with 1.10 m on segment 2 reports effective heights 1.00, 1.10 and 1.00 m; a segment height <= 0 and an Arc segment whose ends miss its nodes are rejected; an end extension of 0.000 m is valid (RAI-006 '0 allowed').
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements, UpdateElements, MoveElements, the Transform mirror (side Left becomes Right) and DeleteElements on a railing, each undone and redone to the identical project; DeleteProfile with a replacement re-points railing component sections.
- vertical_extent of a railing with node elevations 0 and 1.5 m and height 1.00 m spans 0 to 2.5 m above the home storey and follows a storey elevation change.
- template test asserts the D.2 values: height 1.00 m, top rail 0.050 x 0.050 m, inner posts MaxLength 1.20 m, balusters MaxClearSpacing 0.12 m.
- The framework's module-layout test still passes (only kinds/railing.rs plus one macro line added).
- Satisfies the data clauses of RAI-001 (3D nodes, segment height, side, offset), RAI-003 (component set, each switchable with section, size, material and position) and RAI-006 (end extension and shape, corner joint).
notes:
SRS: RAI-001 RAI-003 RAI-006
Appendix D.2 railing: height 1.00 m; inner posts at most 1.20 m apart; top rail 50 x 50 mm; vertical bars <= 0.12 m clear. Post and bar sizes are not in D.2: assume 50 x 50 mm posts and 20 x 20 mm bars and document them in template.rs.

title: Add single-point equal-going winders
description:
WHY: STA-026 (C): equal-going winders with the single-point construction, where risers fan from one centre point, with counts before and after the middle step. Other equal-going constructions are out of v1 (Section 8, deferred element depth). Gap STA-026: missing (M), depends on STA-025 (task 11).

WHAT: `WinderSpec.construction: WinderConstruction::{EqualAngle, SinglePoint { centre: CentreRef (inner corner by default, or an offset from it), before: u32, after: u32 }}` in crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/config.rs; in crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/winders.rs (task 11) the walking line of the winder zone is divided into before + 1 + after equal goings (measured with the stair's going measure) and every winder riser is the line from the centre point through its walking-line station, clipped to the stair boundary; the middle step straddles the corner bisector. Validation: before and after >= 1; the centre must lie on the inner side outside the walking zone so no riser crosses the walking line twice; rule evaluation and conflicts as in task 11. Explicitly out of scope: every other equal-going construction (Section 8), bodies, plan and IFCX (tasks 14, 21), UI (task 15).
design: Share the walking-line station machinery of task 11; only the riser direction differs (through the centre instead of equal angles). With the centre on the inner corner, steps touching the corner have zero inner going, which is inherent to the construction; the walking-line minimum distance rule still applies.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: a 90-degree L-turn with before 2 and after 2 gives 5 winder goings of equal walking-line length (1e-9), every riser passes through the centre point (collinearity 1e-12) and the middle step is symmetric about the bisector.
- before 3 and after 1 shifts the middle step and differs from the equal-angle result; mirroring the turn direction mirrors the layout exactly.
- A centre inside the walking zone is rejected with a message; rule violations are listed per step.
- Satisfies STA-026 at the layout level.
notes: SRS: STA-026

title: Generate railing posts, balusters and infill panels
description:
WHY: RAI-003 (S) requires end and corner posts, inner posts, balusters and infill panels (glass or solid), each switchable and with its own profile, size, material and vertical position; RAI-004 (S) distributes components along each segment by divisions, pattern length or maximum length with start, centre or end alignment (4.300 m with a 1.200 m maximum gives 4 bays of 1.075 m). Appendix D.2 limits inner posts to 1.20 m apart and the clear spacing of vertical bars to 0.12 m. The epic design notes build posts as prisms; task 01 provides the station arithmetic and task 03 the railing geometry module.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/railing/components.rs: per segment, inner-post stations from distribution::stations (segment override or railing setting), end posts at open path ends and corner posts at interior nodes when enabled (a corner post replaces any inner post within MODEL_TOLERANCE of the node; with corner posts off, stations restart per segment); posts are vertical sweeps (frame_for_column) of their section from the reference-line elevation at the station to their vertical position (end, corner and inner posts reach the effective segment height of task 02 unless their own position is set); balusters are placed inside each bay between the post faces with distribution::fill_bay and cut horizontally at their bottom and top positions relative to the local reference-line elevation; panels are one plate per bay in the vertical plane of the segment (a parallelogram on sloped segments: vertical edges at the bay ends minus the gap, top and bottom parallel to the reference line) built with extrude() in a local frame and moved into place; glass panels take the panel material (the template's Glass, transparent through its appearance) and solid panels their own material; every part carries the material of its component. Parts: Post_<n> (IfcMember, predefined POST), Balusters_<bay> (IfcMember, one Body_n per bar), Panel_<bay> (IfcPlate), numbered deterministically by segment and station.
