Explicitly out of scope: per-tread stair patterns and floor-reaching end posts (task 22), plan symbol (task 07), IFCX (task 06).
design: Bars and posts of one section share one cap triangulation and are emitted as translated copies, which keeps hundreds of balusters cheap. Grouping balusters per bay into one IfcMember part with Body_n per bar bounds the IFCX node count while keeping each bar a closed body; per-bar members are an open question for the IFCX reviewers (notes). Panels in local (s, z) coordinates: build the outline in the segment plane, extrude along the local normal with extrude() (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/extrude.rs:18) and apply a rigid transform; assert a positive signed volume because a mirrored frame flips orientation. Station lookups along the plan polyline use plan arc length with the node elevations interpolated, so posts are vertical and bays measured in plan. Pitfall: a corner post and the rail mitre must agree on the corner position after side and offset are applied, so both use rail_path's offset polyline from task 03.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/railing.rs: a straight 4.300 m railing with inner posts MaxLength 1.200 m has 5 posts centred at stations 0, 1.075, 2.150, 3.225 and 4.300 m (1e-9), the RAI-004 case at the geometry level; Divisions and PatternLength with each alignment place posts at the task 01 stations.
- With the D.2 defaults every clear gap between neighbouring bars or between a bar and a post is <= 0.12 m, measured on the generated bodies' bounds.
- An L railing with corner posts has exactly one post at the corner node and no duplicate inner post there.
- Glass panels of 10 mm with a 0.02 m gap give one closed plate per bay; on a sloped segment the plate's end edges are vertical and its top and bottom faces are parallel to the slope (normal check 1e-12).
- Switching a component off removes only its parts, switching it on again restores the same part roles and therefore the same v5 sub-node ids.
- All bodies are closed, outward and below MAX_MESH_POINTS; a 50 m vertical-bar railing evaluates without per-bar triangulation (shared section triangulation, timing recorded in the regression harness).
- End posts sit at both open ends of an open railing and none on a closed loop; switching end posts off removes exactly those two Post parts.
- Solid panels (0.04 m, a template material) give one closed plate per bay like glass; every Post, Balusters and Panel part carries its component's material (checked per part).
- On a segment with its own 1.10 m height the posts reach 1.10 m, on the other segments 1.00 m.
- Satisfies the post, baluster and panel clauses of RAI-003 (each switchable, with its own section, size, material and vertical position) and all three distribution modes with alignment of RAI-004.
notes:
SRS: RAI-003 RAI-004
Open question: balusters as one IfcMember per bay (chosen) or one per bar. D.2: inner posts <= 1.20 m, bars <= 0.12 m clear.

title: Add the railing tool: 3D polylines, edge picking and continuation
description:
WHY: RAI-001 (S) needs reference-line nodes with independent elevations, which users enter in plan with typed elevations or directly in 3D; RAI-002 (S) attaches a railing to stair and slab edges by picking them and continues from a stair edge onto the arrival slab as one element. UND-003 lets Backspace remove the last point of a railing during input; INP-015 provides the 3D working plane (3d-input-navigation). Gap RAI-001: tool points are 2D only (`points: Vec<DVec2>`, crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs:289); point-input-snapping and 3d-input-navigation now deliver the PointInput service with full 3D points through the ViewSurface trait.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/railing.rs: ToolKind::Railing (tools/mod.rs of point-input-snapping-01) implementing InputConsumer with two modes. Polyline: click nodes in plan or a 3D view; a node takes the elevation of the snapped 3D point or the working plane, or a typed Z field added to the tracker; Backspace removes the last node, Enter or a double-click finishes, a key cycles the side. PickEdge: hovering highlights stair boundary edges and slab outline edges (PartRef::Edge) in plan and 3D with a live preview of the resolved railing; a click attaches; after a stair edge the tool proposes the arrival slab edge nearest the top nosing and Enter or Shift-click appends it; the result is one Command::AddAttachedRailing (task 05: the new railing and its attachments in one command, one undo step). Edit mode: selecting a railing node shows its elevation in the properties panel and typing a value updates it. Action::ToolRailing with a free single-key shortcut, toolbox button, Design menu item, the properties strip showing railing defaults; KindDescriptor.has_tool becomes true. Explicitly out of scope: the settings dialog and presets (task 09), terrain draping (task 10), reshape palette commands for railing nodes beyond elevation editing.
design: The consumer leaves needs_horizontal unset so 3D views deliver full 3D points (3d-input-navigation-08). Edge hover in plan uses Kind::part_outline hit tests for slab edges and the stair's boundary polylines; in 3D the GPU id buffer returns the element and the nearest boundary segment in screen space selects the edge. The preview evaluates a temporary railing off the document so no undo step or revision bump happens per mouse move. Follow the tool-extension recipe in docs/implementation-status.md (ToolKind, actions.rs, shell.rs, properties.rs gather mapping, workspace select_all). Pitfall: the typed Z field must not swallow the single-key shortcuts while the tracker is unfocused (ws.input.captures_keys()).
acceptance_criteria:
- Headless tool tests: a four-node polyline with typed Z values creates one railing with exactly those elevations; Backspace removes the last node; Esc follows the point-input Esc ladder.
- PickEdge test: picking the right edge of a sample stair and then the proposed arrival slab edge creates one railing with two attachments in one undo step, and one undo removes both.
- Drawing the same polyline in a 3D view on the storey working plane yields an element equal to the one drawn in plan (ViewSurface test).
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: the Railing toolbox button activates the tool; in edit mode selecting node 2 shows its elevation field and typing 0.500 m updates the railing.
- The Appendix D.8 shortcut uniqueness test (shortcuts_are_unique in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs) passes.
- Satisfies the input clauses of RAI-001 and the picking and continuation clauses of RAI-002 (behaviour from task 05).
notes:
SRS: RAI-001 RAI-002
UND-003 (Backspace during multi-step railing input) is exercised here; its requirement row belongs to another epic.

title: Drape railings on terrain with equally spaced posts
description:
WHY: RAI-008 (C): a railing may be draped on terrain, with posts at equal distances along the path (KB 304213). The terrain kind with its TIN top surface comes from terrain-and-site (increment 2); task 05 provides the attachment and follow mechanism and task 08 the picking tool; terrain-and-site-04 provides the TIN (Tin with elevation_at in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/terrain.rs). Gap RAI-008 (M): no terrain element and no draping existed.

WHAT: A third attachment edge `HostEdge::TerrainSurface { offset: f64 }` in crates/archicraft-model/src/relations.rs (task 05). Because the TIN lives in archicraft-geometry and the model crate must not depend on it (NFR-MNT-002), draping is a geometry step: new crates/archicraft-geometry/src/railing/drape.rs projects the railing's own plan polyline onto the terrain top with Tin::elevation_at, adding a node at every crossing with a TIN edge so the path follows the surface between nodes, lifted by the offset and converted from absolute to home-storey-relative elevations, then merges consecutive pieces whose direction changes by less than 0.5 degrees; inner posts of a draped railing are distributed along the 3D path length (distribution::stations on the 3D arc length, mapped back to plan positions) so posts are equally spaced along the path, stand vertically and start at the surface. Static: Command::SetRailingStatic (task 05) gains `snapshot: Option<Vec<RailNode>>`, which the app fills from the evaluated draped path of a terrain-attached railing; deleting the terrain keeps the railing's own nodes and reports it. The tool's PickEdge mode accepts a terrain after a polyline is drawn (or a Drape toggle); the relation codec writes kind terrainSurface; railings.ifcx gains a draped railing on a small terrain fixture built with terrain-and-site's builder. Explicitly out of scope: draping on slabs or roofs, terrain editing.
design: Sample z with Tin::elevation_at (locate plus barycentric interpolation, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/terrain.rs of terrain-and-site-04); find TIN edge crossings by intersecting the plan polyline with the triangle edges using geo's robust predicates. Merging nearly collinear pieces keeps the rail sweep (task 03) to few segments on smooth terrain. Measuring bays along the 3D path is the point of RAI-008; normal railings keep plan measure.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/railing.rs drape tests: on a planar terrain z = 0.1·x a straight 10 m plan polyline drapes to one straight 3D segment after merging, and MaxLength 1.20 m gives 9 equal bays of 1.1166 m along the 3D length; on a TIN with a ridge the path gains a node at the ridge crossing and every post base lies on the TIN within MODEL_TOLERANCE.
- Moving a terrain point re-evaluates the draped railing through dirty propagation; a static railing keeps its elevations.
- A path leaving the terrain boundary is reported and keeps the node's own elevation outside it.
- Round trip of the draped railing and the updated railings.ifcx golden; conformance green.
- SetRailingStatic with the evaluated snapshot stores the draped 3D nodes; one undo releases the railing to follow the terrain again.
- Satisfies RAI-008.
notes:
SRS: RAI-008
Needs the terrain kind of terrain-and-site (increment 2); it is not a listed prerequisite epic, but increment ordering guarantees it.

title: Add railing settings, component editor and whole-railing presets
description:
WHY: RAI-003 makes every railing component switchable with its own profile, size, material and vertical position; RAI-004 and RAI-005 let users choose the distribution mode, alignment and stair pattern; RAI-006 sets rail end extensions, end shapes and corner joints; RAI-007 (S) requires whole-railing presets, at least glass balustrade, vertical bars and horizontal rails/cables (ELM-002). UI-003 gives every kind a settings dialog with live preview (properties-and-dialogs-09). Gap RAI-007 (M): no presets and no D.2 railing defaults in the UI.

WHAT: A railing settings dialog on the settings-dialog framework (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs and ui/fields.rs FieldSpecs from properties-and-dialogs-05): general fields (height, side, offset, static, segment overrides); a component list with an enable checkbox per component and a detail panel (section from the profiles dialog picker of profiles-columns-beams-14 or an inline rectangle/circle, size, material, vertical position, rail ends with extension and shape, corner joint); distribution (mode, value, alignment, infill count or maximum clear spacing, stair pattern every n treads and balusters per tread); a live 3D preview of a 3 m sample. Presets in crates/archicraft-model/src/railing/presets.rs: `RailingPreset::{GlassBalustrade, VerticalBars, HorizontalRails}` building RailingComponents, `Command::ApplyRailingPreset { targets, preset }`, and a preset choice for new railings in the tool strip; when templates-presets' ELM-002 tool-preset resource (templates-presets-03) is merged, the same builders register the three as template presets of the railing tool on the template layer 'Stairs and railings' (crates/archicraft-model/src/template.rs:267) instead of a hard-coded list. The properties panel shows height, side, offset, static and the preset selector. Explicitly out of scope: a pattern editor and user-authored components (Section 8), cable hardware.
design: Presets are code-defined builders keyed by an enum, testable headlessly, and the single source for the ELM-002 template entries, so values are never duplicated. The component list uses one FieldSpec set per spec type so the properties panel, the dialog and multi-selection editing stay consistent. The live preview evaluates a temporary element off the document (no undo step). Preset values (assumptions to verify per jurisdiction): glass balustrade = no posts, 10 mm glass panels in bays of at most 1.20 m with 0.01 m gaps, 42 mm round handrail on top; vertical bars = 50 x 50 mm end, corner and inner posts at most 1.20 m apart, 50 x 50 mm top rail, 40 x 40 mm bottom rail at 0.10 m, 20 x 20 mm bars at <= 0.12 m clear; horizontal rails/cables = the same posts and top rail with 8 round 6 mm rails from 0.10 to 0.90 m (0.114 m spacing). Preset materials come from the template (Glass, Steel), so NFR-USE-006 holds for railings.
acceptance_criteria:
- presets.rs tests: each preset validates, has height 1.00 m and meets the D.2 clear spacing <= 0.12 m on a 4.300 m segment, checked on generated geometry.
- commands.rs: ApplyRailingPreset on two railings and one undo restores both; applying keeps the reference line and attachments.
- kittest: opening the settings dialog from a selected railing, disabling Balusters and enabling glass Panels changes the railing's part roles after OK; choosing 'Horizontal rails/cables' in the strip makes the next drawn railing use it.
- Inline range checks reject a negative extension with a message before OK (ELM-017).
- Satisfies RAI-007 and the user-facing settings clauses of RAI-003, RAI-004, RAI-005 and RAI-006.
notes:
SRS: RAI-003 RAI-004 RAI-005 RAI-006 RAI-007
templates-presets (ELM-002) runs in the same increment and is not a prerequisite; the hook keeps both orders of merging working.

title: Railings, winders, spiral stairs and stair extras
description:
Railings with 3D polyline reference lines, attachment to stair and slab edges, the component set (rails, posts, balusters, panels) with profiles and distribution modes, stair patterns, rail ends, presets, terrain draping, plan representation and IfcRailing export; plus winders, curved and spiral flights with chord or arc measures, stringers, step numbering, conversion to solids and ramps. Also stairs as solid-operation targets and operators (STA-049).

Risks: RAI-003 is extra large; the component kit is limited to the SRS list with no pattern editor (Section 8).
design: archicraft-model kinds/railing.rs with a host relation to stair and slab edges and a pattern engine as pure functions; archicraft-geometry profile sweeps along 3D polylines (shared with beams) and posts as prisms; stair solver extensions for winders and arc baselines; archicraft-ifcx compound parts.
acceptance_criteria: RAI-004: 4.300 m with a 1.200 m maximum gives 4 bays of 1.075 m; RAI-005: one tread with 3 divisions puts balusters at 1/3 and 2/3; a railing follows its stair when the riser count changes; the AS-01 railing on the U-stair exports IfcRailing with parts (conformance); winder count rules and the arc versus chord measures (r·θ versus 2r·sin(θ/2)) as unit tests; a ramp at 5° with 0.500 m rise is about 5.715 m long; a stair converts to one free-form solid per part after one notice. A stair cut into terrain through a solid operation follows when the stair re-solves (STA-049).
notes: SRS: RAI-001 RAI-002 RAI-003 RAI-004 RAI-005 RAI-006 RAI-007 RAI-008 RAI-009 RAI-010 STA-025 STA-026 STA-027 STA-028 STA-042 STA-047 STA-048 STA-050 STA-049

title: Write railings as IfcRailing with component parts and a railing fixture
description:
WHY: RAI-010 (S): railings shall be written to IFCX as IfcRailing with their components as parts; Table 5-1 makes posts and rails IfcMember and infill panels IfcPlate children of the railing node. IFX-016 requires compound parts as child nodes with their own class, IFX-010 gives regenerated parts v5 ids from the owner and role, IFX-060 stores authoring data and relations in the archicraft namespace. The epic acceptance requires the AS-01 railing on the U-stair to export IfcRailing with parts and pass conformance; this task provides the codec, the writer and a railing fixture, and task 23 adds the AS-01 railing to RM-S on top of it. Gap RAI-010: the IfcClass enum was closed (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:10-32) and parts were unclassed (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:361-385); the framework has since added the D.5 class list and the compound-part codec.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/railing.rs: an `archicraft::railing` codec in the per-kind registry (element-kind-framework-06), declared in crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: reference nodes (x, y, z), closed, side, offset, height, per-segment shape (straight or arc), height and distribution overrides, every component with enabled flag, section (profile id or inline shape), material, vertical position, ends, corner joint, distribution, infill and tread pattern, plus the static flag; RailingAttachment entries in archicraft::relations (kind railingAttachment, host, edge, seq) through the relation codec. Writer: an IfcRailing node (predefined type GUARDRAIL by default, selectable HANDRAIL/BALUSTRADE through the predefined-type mechanism of element-kind-framework-05) with the part children of tasks 03, 04 and 22: TopRail_n, Handrail_n, Rail_n, Post_n and Balusters_n as IfcMember, Panel_n as IfcPlate. Reader: parameters and attachments restored after all elements are read, part nodes ignored, dangling hosts make the railing static with a report entry. Fixture: samples::railings() in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs through the FixtureBuilder (element-kind-framework-03): straight, mitred L, glass panels, solid panels, sloped 3D polyline, closed loop, a segment with its own height, and a railing added with AddAttachedRailing to the inner edge of samples::u_stair() (stair-body-plan-02) with a 1-tread pattern and continued onto a slab edge; registered in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs samples() and crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs; golden railings.ifcx blessed with a reviewed diff; conformance/check.ts asserts that every IfcRailing has IfcMember children and that every part has a class, a name and a mesh. Explicitly out of scope: the AS-01 railing in RM-S (task 23), draping attributes (task 10), presets (task 09).
design: Part roles come from Kind::parts() and the geometry children of tasks 03, 04 and 22, so writer and geometry cannot disagree; the writer's generic compound helper writes Body_n per part. Parameters are written at full precision; all railing fields are optional with defaults so tasks 09 and 10 add fields without a format bump. A new kind would be dropped silently by older readers, so bump FORMAT_VERSION through the framework migration table (no-op migration) and let older versions flag newer_format. Pitfall: bless the golden file only after reviewing the diff; balusters add many small part nodes, so keep the fixture railings short.
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs: railings() loads back to an equal Project (parameters, attachments, static flag, segment shapes); save-load-save is byte-identical; part node ids are v5 of (railing UUID, role) and unchanged by an unrelated edit; a riser-count change of the attached stair alters the railing's parts but not its UUID.
- A file whose attachment host is missing loads with the railing static and a report entry; files written before the FORMAT_VERSION bump load unchanged and an older reader flags newer_format.
- validate.rs (IFX-006 offline) passes and every mesh is a closed sub-solid with <= 65,535 points (IFX-038).
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green including railings.ifcx; check.ts verifies every IfcRailing with IfcMember children (and IfcPlate children for the panel samples), each part with a class, a name and a mesh.
- Satisfies RAI-010 and re-asserts IFX-016 for railings.
notes:
SRS: RAI-010
Predefined type GUARDRAIL as default is an assumption; HANDRAIL and BALUSTRADE stay selectable.

title: Build winder and curved stair bodies in 3D
description:
WHY: Winders (STA-025, STA-026) and curved and spiral flights (STA-027, with STA-028 goings) must exist as closed stair bodies: STA-040 gives treads, risers and finishes, STA-041 the monolithic structure with smooth or stepped underside, STA-043 seamless same-material steps, STA-044 a reported simple fallback for parts that cannot be built; IFX-034 tessellates curves (2 mm, 10 degrees) and IFX-038 shares vertices only across smooth edges. stair-body-plan built these generators for straight, L and U stairs only (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/mod.rs, finish.rs and structure.rs of stair-body-plan-04/05/06/07), and tasks 11-13 now deliver winder and arc step layouts.

WHAT: Extend crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/mod.rs and finish.rs: treads, risers and finishes (STA-040) from general step outlines — winder quadrilaterals with non-parallel risers and annular sectors with arc edges tessellated by tessellate() (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs, circle-anchored stations, so shared edges of neighbouring steps coincide bit for bit) — through the existing extrude(), extrude_profile and TriMesh::append_disjoint (stair-solver-tool-06, stair-body-plan-04). Extend stair/structure.rs: a monolithic structure (STA-041) with a smooth underside under winders and curved flights built as a triangulated ruled (helicoidal) strip between the inner and outer underside lines with smooth vertices along curved directions, and the stepped underside per step; a part that cannot be closed is reported through stair-body-plan-07's mechanism (STA-044) and falls back to the stepped underside; stair-body-plan-06's seam suppression treats the helicoid strip as smooth. Fixture samples::stairs_advanced() in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs through the FixtureBuilder (element-kind-framework-03): L with corner winders, U with a winder segment, single-point winder, curved flight, full-turn spiral; it joins samples::catalogue() with its golden in task 21. Explicitly out of scope: plan symbol and IFCX (task 21), tool and properties UI (task 15), stringers (task 16), numbering (task 17).
design: Reuse stair-body-plan's builders (extrude_profile, TriMesh::append_disjoint); the only new inputs are general step polygons and curved edges. Helicoid underside: for each tessellation station compute inner and outer underside points (z = nosing-line elevation minus the structure thickness measured perpendicular to the walking-line pitch), triangulate the quad strip and close it with side faces sharing those station points, which makes closedness exact. Winder undersides are not developable: triangulated facets with the walking-line pitch are accepted. Point budget: a two-turn spiral at 36 segments per turn per edge stays far below 65,535. Pitfall: stair-body-plan's seam suppression (STA-043) must treat the smooth helicoid strip edges as smooth, not as feature edges.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/stair_advanced.rs: every part of the five fixture stairs is closed and outward with positive volume; tread tops lie at i·R (1e-9); winder tread outlines equal the task 11/12 layout polygons (1e-9); arc edges shared by neighbouring spiral treads have bit-identical vertices and vertices are shared only along curved strips (IFX-038).
- Same-material treads and risers of winder and spiral steps produce no seam edges in the feature-edge output (STA-043).
- A spiral with inner radius 0 and a thick smooth structure reports the structure part and falls back to the stepped underside without omitting geometry (STA-044).
- A two-turn spiral stays below MAX_MESH_POINTS per part.
- All stair-body-plan geometry tests stay green (straight, L and U bodies unchanged).
- Satisfies the 3D geometry clauses of STA-025, STA-026 and STA-027 (STA-028 takes effect through the layout).
notes: SRS: STA-025 STA-026 STA-027 STA-028

title: Draw railings in plan with cut, projected and break-line parts
description:
WHY: RAI-009 (S): in plan, railings shall be drawn with their components cut or projected, and a railing attached to a stair uses the stair's break line (STA-045: break line at a configurable height, the part below drawn solid and the part above dashed). STA-046 shows a stair on the storey above with only the part above the break line, and its railing must match. Gap RAI-009 (M): the generic cut/projected machinery (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:111-170) could apply, but nothing couples a railing to the stair's break line.

WHAT: The railing implements GeometryKind::plan_symbol(&PlanSymbolContext) (stair-body-plan-08) in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/railing/symbol.rs, consumed by crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs and drawn by crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs with plan-attributes pens through plan-renderer; PlanSymbol, which has lines, arrows, markers and labels only, gains filled regions (SymbolRegion { ring, class }) and the line classes Cut and Projected so cut posts can be filled: posts and balusters as section outlines at their plan positions, cut (filled) where the view's cut plane passes through them and projected otherwise; rails as their plan outline per path piece, classified by whether the cut plane intersects the rail there; panels as thin rectangles. For a stair-attached railing the path is split at the station where the stair's break line crosses it, computed by one helper break_line(stair, layout, &PlanSymbolContext) extracted from crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/symbol.rs (stair-body-plan-08) so stair and railing never disagree: on the home storey the part below is drawn normally and the part above with the stair's above-break style (dashed or hidden); on the storey above only the part above the break line appears, drawn solid, following the stair's display range (ELM-008, relation Above(n) of PlanSymbolContext as in stair-body-plan-09). Slab-attached and free railings use the view range only. The railing's reference line and post centres become snap and pick targets. Explicitly out of scope: sections and elevations (sections-elevations-dims), 3D display.
design: Emit the symbol from parametric data (stations, sections, rail paths) instead of slicing hundreds of slender bars, which would create tiny loops and cost per frame; use the component z ranges against the view's cut plane to choose cut versus projected. Intersect the railing's plan path with the break-line segment geometrically rather than by riser index, because side and offset move the railing off the stair edge. Cache the symbol per element revision like other plan elements (element-kind-framework-11). Pitfall: a railing continuing onto the arrival slab is partly outside the stair's display range; the slab piece follows the railing's own range, only the stair piece follows the break line.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/railing_plan.rs: a free 1.00 m railing with the cut plane at 1.10 m is entirely projected; with the cut plane at 0.50 m its posts and balusters are cut and its rails projected.
- The stair-attached railing of samples::railings() on samples::u_stair(): on the home storey the pieces before the break-line station are drawn normally and those after it in the above-break style; on the storey above only the part above the break line appears, solid; the split station equals the break-line intersection within MODEL_TOLERANCE and moves when the stair's break-line height changes.
- A golden plan image of the U-stair with railing is committed through the plan-renderer golden harness (crates/archicraft-app/tests/plan_golden.rs, plan-renderer-07).
- Snap test: the reference line and post centres are snap targets in plan.
- A railing with a tread pattern (task 22) shows a post outline at every post station and its balusters per tread in plan.
- Satisfies RAI-009.
notes: SRS: RAI-009

title: Lay out equal-angle winders at corners and as baseline segments
description:
WHY: STA-025 (S): the system shall provide equal-angle winders as a corner turning type and as a baseline segment type; the first and last winder risers are perpendicular to the walking line at the configured offsets, intermediate risers have equal angular spacing, and the count is set by a fixed number, a maximum number or an optimum going width (at least 2 winder steps). Test: a 90-degree L-turn with 3 winder goings and offsets of 0.5 and 0.3 goings gives risers every 30 degrees between the first and the last winder riser. STA-011 forbids silently outputting a rule-violating stair. Gap STA-025: missing (L); it depends on STA-020/021 (segment types, corner turning types, riser offsets), which stair-body-plan delivered.

WHAT: In crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/: config.rs gets `TurningType::Winder(WinderSpec)` beside Landing (TurningType is #[non_exhaustive] for exactly this, stair-body-plan-01) and `SegmentKind::Winder(WinderSpec)` beside Flight and Landing; `WinderSpec { offsets: [RiserOffset; 2], count: WinderCount::{Fixed(u32), Max(u32), OptimumGoing(f64)} }` reusing STA-021's RiserOffset (length or multiples of the going). New crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/winders.rs, called from stair/layout.rs (StairLayout.risers gains the winder RiserLines) and stair/solve.rs: in a turn of angle Δ the walking line follows an arc of radius w (walking-line distance from the inner edge) around the inner corner, tangent to both flights' walking lines (the walking line of stair/walking.rs, with its point_at/tangent_at arc-length parametrisation, becomes a PolyCurve of crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs lines and arcs); the first winder riser is perpendicular to the incoming walking line at offset o1 before the turn zone's incoming edge, the last perpendicular to the outgoing walking line at o2 after its outgoing edge (offset 0 is flush, as for landing corners); for k winder steps, riser i (0..k) is rotated by i·Δ/k and crosses the walking line at the station s_first + i·L_w/k. A Winder segment distributes the turns at both of its ends over the segment. Count resolution: Fixed(k >= 2); Max(kmax) = the largest k in [2, kmax] whose winder goings satisfy the enabled going and step-formula rules; OptimumGoing(g) = round(L_w / g) clamped to >= 2. Winder steps count towards N; flights adapt (lock baseline off) or only the step distribution adapts (STA-029 on). Checks: winder risers clipped to the stair boundary must not cross, else a RuleConflict (stair/conflict.rs) 'winder risers cross' with alternatives (fewer winders, larger offsets); every winder step is evaluated against the enabled rules and violations listed as for STA-008. Explicitly out of scope: single-point winders (task 12), arc baselines and the chord measure (task 13), bodies (task 14), plan and IFCX (task 21), UI (task 15).
design: Pure functions over baseline, width, side, walking-line distance and rules, tested with seeded randomized turns (the workspace has no proptest dependency) (risers monotone in angle, non-crossing when admissible, end points on the boundary). Offsets are interpreted by analogy with STA-021 landing-corner riser offsets measured from the edges of the turn zone; isolate this in one function and confirm against KB 303759. The arc walking line around the inner corner is the rounded offset of the inner edge, which is what makes winder goings depend on the going measure of task 13 (arc until then). Pitfalls: the inner side depends on the turn direction; for a centred baseline compute the boundaries first; keep riser lines as exact 2D lines, never tessellated.
acceptance_criteria:
- winders.rs unit tests: the SRS case (90-degree L-turn, Fixed(3), offsets 0.5 and 0.3 goings) gives winder riser directions at 0, 30, 60 and 90 degrees from the first winder riser (1e-12 rad), the first and last perpendicular to the walking line (|dot| < 1e-12) at the configured offsets (1e-9 m).
- A 180-degree Winder segment of a U-stair with Fixed(6) gives 30-degree steps; a right-hand turn mirrors the left-hand result exactly.
- Count modes: Max(5) picks 4 where 5 would violate the 0.25 m minimum going; OptimumGoing(0.28) picks round(L_w / 0.28); Fixed(1) is rejected.
- Crossing risers (tiny offsets, Fixed(6), narrow stair) produce a conflict naming 'winder risers cross' with alternatives, and the last valid stair is kept (STA-011).
- Each winder step reports R, its walking-line going and 2R+G; the risers still sum exactly to the total rise.
- All stair-solver-tool and stair-body-plan tests stay green (straight, L and U stairs unchanged).
- Satisfies STA-025 at the layout level (geometry in task 14, plan and export in task 21).
notes:
SRS: STA-025
Appendix D.3 rules apply (going 250 to 350 mm, 2R+G 600 to 650 mm, walking-line distance >= 300 mm); walking line at half the width by default (STA-010).

title: Place railing posts and balusters per tread on stair pieces
description:
WHY: RAI-005 (S): on stairs the railing pattern shall be settable to repeat every n treads, with a post on each riser line and a chosen number of balusters per tread; end posts reach the floor. Test: a pattern length of 1 tread with 3 divisions gives balusters at 1/3 and 2/3 of each tread between the posts. The epic acceptance repeats the RAI-005 test and requires that a railing follows its stair when the riser count changes. Gap RAI-005: missing (M): no per-tread pattern, riser-line posts, balusters per tread or floor-reaching end posts; it depends on RAI-002 (task 05 delivers RailPath.riser_stations and floor_z), RAI-004 (task 01 delivers distribution::tread_stations, task 04 the post and baluster bodies) and STA-040 (the stair finish of stair-body-plan-01/04 gives the tread top surface).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/railing/stair_pattern.rs, called by the railing GeometryKind (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/railing.rs) for the stair pieces of a railing whose Railing.tread_pattern (task 02) is set: post and baluster stations from distribution::tread_stations over the piece's riser stations (a post on every n-th riser line plus the end posts, the chosen number of balusters per tread at the interior division points and on riser lines without a post); posts and balusters stand on the finished tread surface under them (tread top from StairLayout and the flight's FinishSettings), and their tops follow the pitch line plus the effective height; the end posts of a stair piece extend down to RailPath.floor_z (the bottom floor or landing, the arrival slab top), so they reach the floor. Landing and slab pieces of the same railing keep the segment distribution of task 04. Part names stay deterministic per riser index (Post_<riser>, Balusters_<tread>), so an unchanged tread keeps its v5 sub-node ids when the riser count changes. A static railing with a tread pattern uses the riser stations of its snapshot. Explicitly out of scope: the settings UI (task 09), IFCX (task 06).
design: tread_stations stays a pure function of the model crate (task 01), so the same arithmetic serves the geometry, the plan symbol (task 07) and tests; this module only maps stations to 3D. Tread heights come from the StairLayout riser z values plus the finish thickness, never from slicing stair bodies. Posts on riser lines sit on the nosing line offset by the railing side and offset; with a nosing projection the post is set back by the projection so it does not clash with the tread nosing (document the rule). Pitfall: winder and curved flights (tasks 11-13) have non-parallel riser lines; use the riser/path intersection stations of task 05, never equal spacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/railing.rs: the RAI-005 test at geometry level: every 1 tread with 3 divisions puts posts on every riser line and balusters at 1/3 and 2/3 of each tread's plan going between them (1e-9).
- Every 2 treads with 2 divisions: posts on every second riser line plus both end posts, balusters at the tread midpoints and on the riser lines without a post.
- The end posts' bottoms lie at the bottom floor and at the arrival slab top (1e-9); every other post and baluster starts on the finished tread top surface.
- Follow (epic acceptance): changing the stair from 18 to 19 risers adds exactly one post and two balusters to the attached railing with every 1 tread and 3 divisions; the parts of unchanged treads keep their roles.
- On the samples::u_stair() inner railing both flights use the tread pattern and the landing piece the segment distribution; all bodies are closed, outward and below MAX_MESH_POINTS.
- Satisfies RAI-005.
notes: SRS: RAI-005

title: Number risers or treads in the stair plan symbol
description:
WHY: STA-047 (C): riser or tread numbering in plan may be shown, with a start index, every n-th step and a stop step. Gap STA-047: missing (M), depending on the STA-045 plan symbol (stair-body-plan) and on plan text, which the app draws with the egui painter at paper sizes as for grid labels.

WHAT: `StairParams.numbering: Option<StepNumbering { target: Risers|Treads, start_index: i32 (default 1), every: u32 (>= 1), stop_step: Option<u32>, text_size_mm: f64 }>` in crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/config.rs next to BreakLine; the stair plan symbol (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/symbol.rs) emits them as PlanSymbol labels (stair-body-plan-08's SymbolLabel { anchor, direction, text, height_mm }) with a new SymbolText::StepNumber(i32) and a below/above-break class — tread labels at the tread's walking-line midpoint, riser labels at the riser/walking-line intersection — counted from the bottom, filtered by every-n and the stop step, including winder and curved steps; the storey above shows the labels of its visible part only. crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draws upright text sized in paper millimetres at the view's drawing scale (plan-renderer DrawingScale) in the stair's pen, with the above-break style where flagged (extending stair-body-plan-10's SymbolLabel drawing). IFCX: numbering in archicraft::stair (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs, optional). UI: fields in the plan section of the stair settings dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/stair.rs, stair-body-plan-13). Explicitly out of scope: text styles (ANN-007).
design: Labels are renderer-agnostic primitives in the plan drawing, like the stair's other plan primitives, so the plan renderer and future sections can draw them; text size is in paper units so it scales with the drawing scale. Anchors use the walking-line stations of the layout (tasks 11-13), which keeps winder numbering on the walking line. Pitfall: keep text upright when the plan view is rotated (plan-views-browser-12).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: 18 risers with tread numbering start 1 and every 1 give 17 labels '1'..'17' at the tread walking-line midpoints; every 2 gives '1', '3', ...; stop step 10 gives no label after 10; start index 5 gives '5'..'21'; riser numbering anchors on the riser lines; winder and spiral fixture stairs label every step on their curved walking line.
- Labels above the break line are flagged; the storey above shows only labels of its visible steps.
- IFCX round trip of the numbering settings; kittest: enabling numbering in the stair dialog makes the plan drawing contain 17 StepNumber labels.
- Satisfies STA-047.
notes: SRS: STA-047

title: Add arc baselines for curved and spiral flights, chord or arc goings
description:
WHY: STA-027 (S): curved and spiral flights shall be defined by an arc baseline with a centre point; the radius is measured at the baseline and the steps are divided at equal angles. STA-028 (S): on curved walking lines, goings shall be measurable along the chord or along the arc, selectable per stair, and the rules are evaluated with the selected measure; for radius r and sweep θ the arc measure is r·θ and the chord measure 2r·sin(θ/2). Gap STA-027: missing (L), no arc baseline and no arc input in any tool; STA-028: missing (S). The exact Arc type exists in crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs (drafting-trim-split-01) and arc walls and slab edges use it (curved-geometry).

WHAT: StairSegment (crates/archicraft-model/src/stair/config.rs) gains `shape: Curve` with curve.rs's `Curve::{Straight, Arc(Arc)}` (drafting-trim-split-01; centre, radius, start angle, signed sweep with 0 < |sweep| <= 2π; a spiral is a full-turn arc or several co-centric arcs); validation: arc ends on their nodes within MODEL_TOLERANCE, inner edge radius >= 0 for the chosen side and width. StairParams (stair/mod.rs) gains `going_measure: GoingMeasure::{Arc, Chord}` (default Arc). The radius is the baseline's radius (STA-027): the inner and outer boundary radii follow from side and width, the walking-line radius from the walking-line distance. Layout: on an arc flight risers are radial and treads span equal angles; the walking line is the concentric arc at the walking-line distance from the inner edge; the going between consecutive risers is the walking-line arc length (Arc) or the straight distance between the riser/walking-line intersections (Chord), the same function serving the winder arcs of tasks 11 and 12. Solver (stair/solver.rs of stair-solver-tool-02 and stair/solve.rs): the admissible riser counts (STA-006), the going range (STA-007), fixed-going violations (STA-008) and the read-out (STA-009) use the selected measure; for mixed straight and arc flights the angular step on each arc is solved so its going equals the stair going (θ = g/r_w for Arc, θ = 2·asin(g / 2r_w) for Chord). Explicitly out of scope: bodies (task 14), plan symbol and IFCX (task 21), tool input (task 15), headroom checks (no SRS requirement).
design: Station arithmetic on the PolyCurve walking line (arc-length parameter per segment) keeps lines, winder arcs and arc flights in one model; chord goings use consecutive intersection points so straight parts give identical results in both measures. Chord requires g <= 2r_w: report a conflict instead of NaN. Spirals beyond one turn chain co-centric arcs because curve.rs limits |sweep| to 2π. Keep riser lines exact (centre plus angle); tessellation happens only in geometry (task 14) through tessellate().
acceptance_criteria:
- Measure unit tests: r = 1.2 m and θ = 20 degrees give an arc going of 0.418879 m (r·θ) and a chord going of 0.416756 m (2r·sin(θ/2)) within 1e-6, and the two converge for small angles.
- An arc flight of 270 degrees divides its treads at equal angles (1e-12 rad) with radial risers; a full-turn spiral (sweep 360 degrees) and a two-arc 450-degree spiral solve without error.
- A tight spiral where the arc measure meets the 250 mm minimum going but the chord measure does not: the violation is reported only with Chord selected, and the admissible riser-count set differs between the two measures (values computed in the test).
- Switching the measure changes the winder goings of a task 11 stair accordingly.
- A negative inner radius and arc ends off their nodes are rejected with messages.
- All straight-stair solver tests stay green.
- Radius at the baseline: for a 1.00 m wide stair with a 2.00 m baseline radius the boundary radii are 2.00/3.00 m, 1.50/2.50 m and 1.00/2.00 m for the baseline on the inner edge, the centre and the outer edge (1e-12).
- Satisfies STA-027 at the layout level and STA-028.
notes:
SRS: STA-027 STA-028
Default measure Arc is an assumption; national rule presets (STA-052, templates-presets) may set Chord.

title: Draw winders and curved flights in plan and write them to IFCX
description:
WHY: STA-045 (M) draws step lines, a walking line with arrow and up/down label and a break line; STA-046 (S) shows the part above the break line on the storey above; STA-051 (M) writes IfcStair with IfcStairFlight and IfcSlab children and stores the solver inputs in the ArchiCraft namespace. Winders (STA-025, STA-026) and curved and spiral flights (STA-027, STA-028) must appear in plan and survive a round trip. stair-body-plan built the plan symbol (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/stair/symbol.rs, stair-body-plan-08/09) and the archicraft::stair codec (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/stair.rs, stair-solver-tool-07 and stair-body-plan-11) for straight, L and U stairs only.

WHAT: Plan symbol in stair/symbol.rs: winder and radial step lines from the StairLayout riser lines, the walking line as a PolyCurve with arcs in winder zones and on curved flights (arc pieces tessellated by tessellate() into SymbolLines) with its arrow, a radial break line on curved flights at the break station, the up/down label; the storey above shows only the part above the break line (stair-body-plan-09); crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs draws the symbol unchanged. IFCX: archicraft::stair gains segment shapes (centre, radius, start angle, sweep), winder specs (construction, offsets, count mode) and the going measure, all optional so files from before this task load as straight segments with the Arc measure; IfcStairFlight predefined types WINDER, CURVED and SPIRAL and IfcStair types QUARTER_WINDING_STAIR, HALF_WINDING_STAIR, CURVED_RUN_STAIR and SPIRAL_STAIR where they fit, through the predefined-type mechanism of element-kind-framework-05; a Winder segment becomes its own Flight_n part. samples::stairs_advanced() (task 14) is registered in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs samples(), samples::catalogue() and crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs, with golden stairs-advanced.ifcx blessed after a reviewed diff. Explicitly out of scope: tool and properties UI (task 15), stringers (task 16), numbering (task 17).
design: The plan symbol stays parametric: step lines are the riser lines of the layout, never slices of bodies, so winder lines are exact. Tessellate walking-line arcs with the same tessellate() and Tessellation as the bodies so plan and 3D agree. The new codec fields are optional with defaults so old files load; bump FORMAT_VERSION through the migration table (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/migrate.rs) because older readers would drop winders and arcs silently. Pitfall: the IfcStair predefined type follows the turn types (one 90-degree winder corner is QUARTER_WINDING_STAIR, 180 degrees HALF_WINDING_STAIR); anything else stays NOTDEFINED rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Plan: the number of step lines equals the number of risers for each fixture stair; the walking line contains arc pieces in winder zones and on curved flights; the spiral's break line is radial with the part above it drawn in the above-break style, and the storey above shows only that part (STA-046).
- Golden plan images of the spiral and the winder L-stair through crates/archicraft-app/tests/plan_golden.rs.
- IFCX: all five fixture stairs round-trip to equal Projects and save-load-save is byte-identical; IfcStairFlight predefined types WINDER, CURVED and SPIRAL appear; a stairs.ifcx written before this task loads as straight segments.
- conformance/run.sh is green on stairs-advanced.ifcx and validate.rs reports no problem.
- Satisfies the plan and export clauses of STA-025, STA-026 and STA-027 and the persistence of the STA-028 measure.
notes: SRS: STA-025 STA-026 STA-027 STA-028

title: Use stairs as targets and operators of solid operations
description:
WHY: STA-049 (S): stairs shall be usable as targets and operators of solid operations (SOL-020), for example to cut a stair into terrain. The epic acceptance requires that a stair cut into terrain through a solid operation follows when the stair re-solves. Gap STA-049: missing (S): no solid operations and no relation store at increment 0. solid-kernel-ops now provides Relation::SolidOperation with SolidOp and Command::AddSolidOperations, gated by the KindDescriptor flag solid: bool (solid-kernel-ops-04), the operator's own body and the SolidOperations stage with one-hop dirty propagation (solid-kernel-ops-05), apply_operations over the target's parts (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kernel/ops.rs, solid-kernel-ops-18), Extrusion::Up (solid-kernel-ops-06) and the solid operations palette (solid-kernel-ops-12); terrain-and-site-11 makes terrain a target tile by tile; stair-solver-tool-04/05 re-solve the stair on commit and on storey edits.

WHAT: Set solid: true on the stair KindDescriptor (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/stair.rs), so AddSolidOperations accepts stairs and the palette lists them; check that the stair GeometryKind (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/stair.rs) yields its own body for operators (all part bodies, no junctions) and that apply_operations keeps the part roles and classes when a stair is the target, so a cut stair is still IfcStair with IfcStairFlight, IfcSlab and IfcMember children; fix whatever the existing pipeline does not cover for compound kinds instead of adding a second path. Re-solve propagation: a re-solve bumps the stair's revision, so its targets (the terrain) re-evaluate through the dirty set; add the regression. Fixture samples::stair_solid_ops() in crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs (a basement stair subtracting terrain with Extrusion::Up, a stair cut by a free-form block) registered in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs and crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs with golden stair-solid-ops.ifcx. Explicitly out of scope: railings as operators (they can use the same flag later), new Boolean features.
design: Operators act with their own unmodified bodies (SOL-024), so a compound operator is the union of its unmodified parts, computed once per evaluation and cached by revision as solid-kernel-ops-05 does for every operator. Targets are cut per part so the IFCX part structure survives (IFX-016). Pitfall: the terrain must be a closed body (TER-001) for the subtract; the test builds it with terrain-and-site's builder.
acceptance_criteria:
- STA-049: a basement stair as operator subtracting the terrain with Extrusion::Up removes the stair volume and the soil above it (volume check, 1e-6 relative); changing the riser count or the storey height re-solves the stair and the cut follows with no further action (the epic acceptance).
- A stair as target cut by a free-form block keeps its parts, each cut, with roles and classes unchanged in IFCX.
- Random operator orderings give identical meshes with stair participants (SOL-024); a failing kernel keeps the last valid bodies and lists the stair (NFR-REL-005).
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddSolidOperations with a stair as target or operator undoes and redoes to the identical project; kittest: the solid operations palette accepts a stair selection.
- conformance/run.sh green on stair-solid-ops.ifcx.
- Satisfies STA-049.
notes:
SRS: STA-049
Terrain comes from terrain-and-site (increment 2), not a listed prerequisite; increment ordering guarantees it.

title: Add column inclination across model, geometry, IFCX and properties
description:
WHY: COL-004 (S): columns shall support an inclination (angle from vertical and direction). Status missing (gap: inclination parameters, sheared or rotated body generation, plan projection of the inclined body, UI and schema; M). profiles-columns-beams-06 builds columns with frame_for_column(position, rotation) (axis +Z) and cut planes through the anchor axis at base and top; COL-003 cuts are horizontal or tilted about the local x axis.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/column.rs: `Column.inclination: Inclination { angle: f64, direction: f64 }` (radians; angle from vertical, 0 = vertical; direction = plan azimuth of the lean, counter-clockwise from the storey x axis), serde default zero; validation 0 <= angle <= 60 degrees, direction normalised to [0, 2pi); the transform hook rotates direction with the plan and reflects it on mirror; plan_bounds include the top section. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/sweep.rs: `frame_for_inclined_column(position, rotation, inclination)` = the vertical frame of frame_for_column rotated by angle about k = Z x (cos d, sin d, 0); kinds/column.rs keeps base and top cut planes horizontal through the axis points at base and top elevation (COL-003 custom angles relative to horizontal about the frame's u axis) and returns axis = [base anchor, top anchor]. IFCX: optional `inclination { angle, direction }` in archicraft::column, written only when non-zero (shared bump rule of 03); the columns-and-beams sample of profiles-columns-beams-09 gains an inclined column. App: ui/properties.rs 'Inclination' and 'Lean direction' angle fields (widgets::angle) in the strip and the column settings dialog; the plan draws the projected axis from base to top anchor. Cross-epic hooks of cleanup-and-trims (increment 2, not a declared prerequisite; if it has not merged, file a bead there instead): the column's `inclined(&ElementKind)` answer of cleanup-and-trims-05 becomes true for a non-zero inclination, so SOL-031 trims cut an inclined column only where it passes through the roof; the beam-column contact test of cleanup-and-trims-01 (point-in-section in plan at the contact elevation) places the section through a new `Column::axis_point_at(z)`, shifted by the lean at that elevation; the pending 'COL-004 inclined column' row that cleanup-and-trims-11 added to crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs is switched to active with blessed golden outlines and listed as covered in docs/junctions.md. Out of scope: an inclination handle, segments on inclined columns (07 handles the frame generically), new join rules for inclined columns (the existing cleanup stages apply through the hooks above).
design: Rotating the whole vertical frame about the horizontal axis perpendicular to the lean keeps rotation meaningful (about the column's own axis) and makes a zero lean exactly the existing frame, so there is no special case and the regression is bit-identical. Horizontal end planes through the axis points keep the storey-linked top meaning (ELM-006) and let a slanted column stand flat on a slab; the axis length H / cos(angle) comes from the plane intersection in the sweep, never stored. Horizontal cuts of a sheared prism keep the volume section area x height, which is the geometry oracle. The sweep rejects planes within 1 degree of the axis, so 60 degrees leaves margin. Pitfalls: plan_bounds must include the top section for culling and picking; cleanup-and-trims-01 assumed vertical column axes, so every place that puts a column section at an elevation uses axis_point_at(z); the stored position is the base anchor, so the top anchor moves when the lean changes (field tooltip). Pointers: kinds/column.rs and sweep.rs (profiles-columns-beams-05/06), ui/properties.rs field getters, samples.rs columns_and_beams (profiles-columns-beams-09).
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: an inclination of 61 degrees is rejected with a message; rotating an inclined column by 90 degrees adds 90 degrees to its direction and mirroring reflects it; UpdateElements with a new inclination executes and undoes exactly.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs: a 0.30 x 0.30 m column, 3.00 m high, inclined 10 degrees towards +x is closed and outward, has volume 0.09 x 3.00 m3 within 1e-9, its top section centroid is offset by 3.00 x tan(10 deg) in +x, and its plan slice at 1.10 m is a (0.30 / cos(10 deg)) x 0.30 m rectangle shifted by 1.10 x tan(10 deg).
- An inclined column with a 15-degree top cut stays closed; inclination 0 reproduces the previous column meshes bit for bit (regression).
- IFCX: the inclined column round-trips with assert_eq, its Axis basiscurves run from base to top anchor, conformance passes.
- egui_kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): selecting the inclined column shows 'Inclination' with the formatted angle; editing it issues one undoable command.
- Cleanup hooks: inclined() is true for a 10-degree column and false at 0 degrees; a 10-degree column trimmed to a hip roof keeps its full base (SOL-031 rule), as the now active COL-004 row of tests/junctions.rs asserts; a beam resting on top of an inclined column is found as a contact at the shifted section.
- Satisfies COL-004.
notes:
SRS: COL-004
Open question: the SRS gives no maximum inclination; 60 degrees is an assumption. Direction is an absolute plan azimuth, not relative to the column rotation.

title: Model chimneys and flues with holed profiles and vertical openings
description:
WHY: WAL-034 (S): vertical elements with internal voids (chimneys, flues, shafts) shall be modellable with profiles containing holes or with vertical openings (OPN-006); they appear hollow in 3D, sections and plan cuts and join cleanly with the surrounding walls. Epic acceptance: a chimney from a holed profile is hollow in plan, section and 3D and joins the surrounding walls. Status missing (L). Columns with custom holed profiles exist (profiles-columns-beams-15), slicing keeps holes (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/slice.rs loops_to_polygons), storey-spanning vertical openings exist (host-openings-06) and, after task 15, can be hosted by columns. Missing is the join: a priority cleanup that subtracts a holed body from a wall leaves wall material inside the flue.

WHAT: Geometry: a `Kind::cleanup_hull()` hook (default None) that returns, for columns whose resolved sections have holes, the hull body (each region's outer ring swept with the holes filled), and for columns and free-form solids that host a vertical flue opening, their body before the Openings stage (solid-kernel-ops-05); the cross-kind contact-and-priority stage (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/cleanup.rs of cleanup-and-trims) uses the hull instead of the body when the member is the cutting element, so walls running into the chimney are cut back to its outer faces by material priority and never enter the flue; slabs meeting the chimney follow the same rule. Flue route: a vertical opening with Storeys depth hosted by a chimney column that is top-linked several storeys up, or by one storey's chimney with the other storeys' chimneys in its cut list (OPN-002, solid-kernel-ops-13), so one flue follows storey elevation changes (OPN-006). Section check: the vertical cut used by section views (the arbitrary-plane slice of sections-elevations-dims if merged, otherwise the kernel split by a vertical plane of solid-kernel-ops-15) shows the flue as a gap. NFR-MNT-005: switch the Pending("members-profiles-adv") chimney rows that junction-engine-12 created in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs to active (chimney at a wall corner, chimney within a straight wall run, chimney with a flue through two storeys) and list them as covered in docs/junctions.md. members_advanced gains a holed-profile chimney column (class IfcColumn: Section 4 allows columns only IfcColumn or IfcMember) and, for the vertical-opening route, a free-form solid chimney classed IfcChimney (D.5 allows that class for free-form solids) with a vertical flue opening hosted through the Plan placement in solids of task 15; golden re-blessed. Out of scope: flue liners, caps and smoke-pipe objects.
design: The hull rule is the one new piece of logic: priority cleanup subtracts the cutting body from the lower-priority element, and a holed cutting body would leave the flue filled with wall material, so members with holed sections cut with their hull. Both WAL-034 routes otherwise reuse existing machinery (holed custom profiles, vertical openings), so the task is mostly integration and regression. Chimneys are columns because a column's profile plane is horizontal; a profiled wall's profile is its vertical section, where a hole would be a horizontal tunnel. Pitfalls: build the hull from the same resolved section as the body so faces coincide; keep the flue off the chimney's top and base planes (VOID_MARGIN); keep cleanup order-independent (sorted pairs). Pointers: cleanup.rs (cleanup-and-trims), slice.rs:149-169, kinds/opening.rs, geometry opening.rs, tests/junctions.rs (junction-engine-12), samples.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: a 0.60 x 0.60 m chimney column with a 0.20 x 0.20 m flue hole between two 0.25 m masonry walls: the plan slice at 1.10 m shows one region with a hole, the wall cut regions do not intersect the hull and no wall area lies inside the flue; the 3D body has inner flue faces and volume (0.36 - 0.04) x height; a vertical split through the flue gives two closed halves whose cut faces exclude the flue rectangle (area check).
- A masonry chimney joined to masonry walls of equal priority merges into one plan region without a boundary line (WAL-023 rule through the cleanup stage).
- Flue route: a solid 0.60 x 0.60 m chimney spanning storeys 0 to 2 with a Storeys flue opening is hollow on every storey, follows a storey-elevation change in one revision, and the storey-1 slab is cut by the chimney hull rather than left inside the flue.
- The three chimney rows run active in the NFR-MNT-005 suite with golden outlines; members_advanced with the chimney round-trips and passes conformance.
- The free-form solid chimney (IfcChimney) with a vertical flue opening is hollow in plan and 3D, walls joined to it leave no area inside the flue (pre-opening hull), its Void child is written under it, and it passes conformance.
- Satisfies WAL-034.
notes:
SRS: WAL-034
Roadmap gap: cleanup-and-trims (increment 2, owner of the COL-006/SLB-007 stage in cleanup.rs) is not a declared prerequisite of this epic; increment order normally guarantees it has merged. If it has not, implement a minimal wall-and-slab-versus-hull stage in cleanup.rs with the API cleanup-and-trims plans and file a bead to fold it in there.

title: Add profiled walls that follow storey-linked heights through stretch zones
description:
WHY: PRF-010 (S): profiles shall also be usable by walls and railings and allow per-edge material overrides. PRF-007: a profiled wall can follow a storey-linked height while its footing keeps its dimensions (epic acceptance: a profiled wall following a storey-linked height scales only its stretch zone). layer-structures-02 left `Structure::{Thickness, Layered}` closed with the note that the PRF-010 epic adds `Profile(ProfileId)`. Status missing (L). Junctions of profiled walls and the railing hookup follow in task 20.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model (kinds/wall.rs, layer-structures-02's Structure): `Structure::Profile { profile: ProfileId, instance: ProfileInstance }` (the width can follow a horizontal zone; the height always follows the wall's resolved height); Project::cross_section returns the envelope (profile width as total, one Core band) so reference positions, face offsets and junction inputs keep working; validation: the walls flag, a vertical zone whenever the resolved height differs from the nominal height ('Profile Footing wall has no vertical stretch zone and cannot follow the storey height'), straight reference lines only; profile_uses reports Wall, so profile edits dirty profiled walls and UpdateProfile re-validates them (01); the storey-edit rejection of element-kind-framework-09 also rejects a storey change that a zone-less profiled wall cannot follow. crates/archicraft-geometry: the wall generator (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/wall.rs) sweeps the resolved section (02; profile x to the right of the reference line seen from its start, that is towards the exterior face; y up from the wall base; origin on the reference line) along the reference line with sweep(), with square ends until task 20 adds junction cuts; one part per profile region ('Body' or 'Region_n') with the region material; edge material runs come from 02. IFCX: archicraft::wall structure kind 'profile' with profile and instance (shared bump rule of 03); members_advanced gains a profiled wall with a footing whose top is storey-linked; golden re-blessed. Out of scope: junctions and railings (20), arc and polygonal profiled walls (rejected with a message), openings, doors and windows in profiled walls, priority resolution between profile regions, the picker UI (12).
design: Height: the stretch map receives the resolved wall height as the actual vertical size, so storey links (ELM-006) drive it with no new code. The envelope keeps every cross_section consumer (reference positions, face offsets, plan-renderer, junction inputs) working without a profile branch; profile regions are not skins, so priority resolution inside the profile stays out of scope and is documented. Square ends keep this task independent of the junction engine; task 20 adds the cuts. Pitfalls: the side convention (exterior on the right, ReferenceLine docs in element.rs) must match the profile x axis, so test both drawing directions; profiled walls report no Skin_n parts, so plan-renderer skin separators skip them; profile edits must dirty profiled walls through profile_uses. Pointers: kinds/wall.rs (model and geometry), Project::cross_section (layer-structures, junction-engine-01), sweep.rs and section.rs (02), the wall codec (alpha/kinds/wall.rs), samples.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test (crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/walls_profiled.rs): a straight profiled wall with a 0.60 x 0.30 m footing, a 0.25 m stem and a vertical zone in the stem, top linked to the next storey at 3.00 m: after the storey is raised to 3.40 m the footing vertices are bit-identical, the stem top moved by +0.40 m, the body is closed and outward, and the plan slice at 1.10 m equals the stem band; the change arrives in one revision through incremental evaluation, equal to a full evaluation.
- Both drawing directions put the footing on the exterior side (vertex check); a profile with one edge material override shows the run on that face and keeps one closed part.
- Model tests: a profile without the walls flag, a zone-less profile on a wall whose resolved height differs from the nominal height and an arc wall with a profile structure are rejected with messages; a storey change that a zone-less profiled wall cannot follow is rejected and leaves the project unchanged; UpdateElements to Structure::Profile and back executes and undoes exactly.
- IFCX round trip of members_advanced with the profiled wall (assert_eq, byte-identical second save) and conformance green.
- Satisfies PRF-010 for walls (usage, per-edge materials) and the storey-linked example of PRF-007.
notes: SRS: PRF-010 PRF-007

title: Generate lofted tapered segments with joint planes and kernel merge
description:
WHY: COL-005 and BEA-005 need bodies for segmented members: each segment with its own section and uniform or tapered size, each joint with its own cut plane, and the member as one clean body per material in plan, 3D and IFCX (WAL-027 agreement, IFX-032 closed bodies, IFX-038 hard edges never shared). Epic risk: tapered lofts keep planar faces only. Status missing; after task 06 uniform segments are separate prisms and tapered ones are reported.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/loft.rs: `loft(start: &Section, end: &Section, frame: &MemberFrame, s0, s1, start_plane: &CutPlane, end_plane: &CutPlane) -> Result<Vec<SweptRegion>, GeometryError>`: corresponding vertices (resolve_pair of 02, or parametric sections generated with identical tessellation counts) define ruled lines from station s0 to s1; each line meets each cut plane in one line-plane intersection; caps are the intersection polygons, validated with validate_ring ('the cut plane folds the segment' otherwise) and triangulated in the plane frame with triangulate.rs including holes; a lateral quad is one face when planar within MODEL_TOLERANCE, otherwise two triangles split along the shorter diagonal with their own vertices (hard edge). Uniform segments keep sweep() (exact prisms). crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/member.rs (shared by column.rs and beam.rs): stations from 06, each segment between its joint planes (cut_plane of 05; Square = perpendicular at the station), the member's end cuts on the first and last segment, the inclined column frame of 04; consecutive segments of equal material are merged with the SolidKernel union_all (solid-kernel-ops-02) into parts 'Body' (single run) or 'Segment_<i>' per run (sub_node_id(owner, role), IFX-010); a KernelError or the NullKernel keeps the unmerged closed segment parts and lists a GeometryProblem (NFR-REL-005). Beam joins keep working: the replacement end planes that cleanup-and-trims-03 (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/cleanup/beams.rs) passes into the beam generator replace the end cuts of the first and last segment, so one-segment beams join exactly as before and segmented beams join the same way (cleanup-and-trims-03 left segmented beams out of scope). Plan classification and slicing stay generic. Out of scope: IFCX (08), operations and UI (09, 10, 21), curved beams (17), openings (15).
design: A loft between topologically identical sections is a ruled surface whose quads are planar only where corresponding edges stay parallel; splitting the others into two planar triangles meets the epic's planar-faces-only rule without a curved-surface representation. Clipping a ruled line by a plane is one intersection, as in sweep.rs, so caps stay exact for perpendicular joints and remain valid polygons for moderate tilts; an invalid cap becomes a reported problem, never folded geometry. The kernel union removes the internal joint faces where a narrow segment meets a wide one (corbel) and its canonical output keeps hard edges separate (solid-kernel-ops-02). Pitfalls: compute each joint plane once and use it for both neighbouring segments so their caps coincide bit for bit before the union; parametric circles taper with the segment count of the larger end; parts above MAX_MESH_POINTS go through the Normalize stage (solid-kernel-ops-03); cache per element revision through the framework. Pointers: sweep.rs, section.rs (02), kernel/mod.rs, evaluate.rs stage order (solid-kernel-ops-05), tests/common helpers of junction-engine.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs: a 0.30 m segment tapering from 1.40 to 0.60 m in width at 0.40 m depth has volume 0.30 x 0.40 x (1.40 + 0.60) / 2 within 1e-9 and is closed and outward; a tee whose web stretches from 0.60 to 0.90 m over 4.50 m has volume 4.50 x (A(0.60) + A(0.90)) / 2 within 1e-9 (area linear in height).
- Property test over random tapers, profiles and joint angles: every face is planar within MODEL_TOLERANCE, every body is closed and outward, and no vertex is shared across a hard edge (IFX-038).
- A four-segment beam of one material yields exactly one closed 'Body' part; a column whose corbel has another material yields two closed parts; with the NullKernel the segments stay separate closed parts and one problem is listed.
- A joint plane tilted 20 degrees between two uniform segments keeps the union watertight (union volume = sum of volumes).
- The plan slice of an F5-type column inside the corbel is the 1.40 x 0.40 m rectangle, and plan slice, 3D body and exported mesh agree (agreement helper of junction-engine-07 / IFX-033).
- One-segment members keep bit-identical meshes (regression), and the beam L, T and X rows of the structural-cleanup sample (cleanup-and-trims-04) stay green after the generator switch; an equal-priority L of two four-segment beams mitres through the meeting point with closed bodies.
- Satisfies the geometry clauses of COL-005 and BEA-005 (segments, tapered sizes, per-joint cut planes).
notes: SRS: COL-005 BEA-005

title: Verify exit criterion: Segmented and inclined members, advanced profiles and more opening hosts
description:
WHY: Close the epic against its exit criterion for COL-004, COL-005, BEA-003, BEA-005, BEA-006, BEA-007, BEA-009, OPN-012, OPN-010, PRF-006, PRF-007, PRF-008, PRF-010 and WAL-034: fixtures F4 and F5 with the COL-005 and BEA-005 acceptance values, segment operations with undo, a storey-linked profiled wall that scales only its stretch zone, a hollow chimney joined to its walls, and a notch in a beam through an opening.

WHAT: On the integrated main branch after tasks 01 to 21 have merged, run the workspace quality gates (cargo test, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo fmt --check) and conformance/run.sh on every golden file; walk through the exit scenario in the app (incline a column; mitre two beams in plan; model F4 and F5 with the segment palette and the Segments table and stretch both; insert, remove, reorder and split a segment, change a joint cut and undo each; draw a profiled wall with a footing, raise its storey and join two profiled walls at an L; capture a profile from selected and from pasted 2D shapes, from a wall and from a beam; place two openings sharing a profile and edit the profile; notch a beam, drill a column, open a solid face and dig a terrain pit; build a chimney from a holed profile between walls and check plan, vertical section and 3D; draw a curved beam); update the rows of all fourteen requirement IDs in docs/implementation-status.md with evidence paths, the D.7 fixture lines for F4 and F5 and the increment-3 readiness row; close the epic in beads and file follow-up beads for anything left (for example region priorities inside profiled walls, segmented curved beams, joins of curved beams (BEA-004, left out by cleanup-and-trims-03 and task 17), the cleanup-and-trims hooks of task 04 if that epic was missing, the railing hookup if railings-stairs-adv was missing, the cleanup.rs hull stage if it had to be built here). Out of scope: new features.
design: Verification only; no new features. Evidence comes from the tests named in tasks 01 to 21 (profile.rs and validate.rs tests, tests/commands.rs segment and profile commands, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs, walls_profiled.rs, openings_kernel.rs, profile_capture.rs and junctions.rs rows for F4, F5, the inclined column, profiled walls and chimneys, the D7 fixture registry tests, the round-trip suite with members-advanced.ifcx, the kittest UI tests). If a gate fails, reopen the owning task instead of patching here.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixtures F4 (9.80 m double-pitch beam with four segments) and F5 (6.00 m corbel column with a 5.10 m flexible body) as geometry tests added to the NFR-MNT-005 suite together with the COL-005 and BEA-005 acceptance values; segment insert, remove, reorder and split with undo; a profiled wall following a storey-linked height scales only its stretch zone; a chimney from a holed profile is hollow in plan, section and 3D and joins the surrounding walls; a notch in a beam through an opening. F4 and F5 are registered in the fixture registry.
- cargo test, cargo clippy (-D warnings) and cargo fmt --check are green on the whole workspace.
- conformance/run.sh is green on every golden file, including members-advanced.ifcx and the re-blessed columns-and-beams golden.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (COL-004 COL-005 BEA-003 BEA-005 BEA-006 BEA-007 BEA-009 OPN-012 OPN-010 PRF-006 PRF-007 PRF-008 PRF-010 WAL-034) with evidence paths, and the per-merge status check of regression-and-status passes.
- The epic is closed in beads and follow-up beads exist for every deferred item.

title: Add beams curved in plan with arc sweeps, IFCX and arc input
description:
WHY: BEA-009 (C): beams curved in plan may be supported. Status missing; gap: arc axis, sweep geometry along an arc, tessellation (IFX-034: at most 2 mm chord deviation and 10 degrees per segment), plan projection; XL. The shared arc type (curve.rs, drafting-trim-split-01), the circle-anchored tessellator with smooth strips (curved-geometry-03) and arc input modes (curved-geometry-07) exist.

WHAT: Model (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/beam.rs): `Beam.curve: Curve` (Straight by default; an Arc between start and end stored exactly as for arc walls in curved-geometry-02); elevations interpolate linearly with arc length (a helical rise when they differ); validation: |sweep| < 360 degrees, radius greater than half the section width plus the lateral offset plus MIN_THICKNESS, one segment only ('Segments are available on straight beams only'), compound end cuts relative to the end tangent frames. Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/sweep.rs `sweep_arc(section, arc, elevations, roll, start_plane, end_plane)`: stations from the shared tessellate() of crates/archicraft-geometry/src/tessellate.rs (the circle-anchored grid of curved-geometry-03), the section placed perpendicular to the tangent at each station (tangent, Z made perpendicular, roll), lateral strips sharing vertices along the arc within one smooth run and hard at profile corners (IFX-038), caps as in sweep(); the Vertical end cut is the plumb plane perpendicular to the end tangent; axis = the tessellated anchor arc; openings hosted by curved beams (15) use the tangent frame at their station. IFCX: optional `curve` in archicraft::beam with exact arc parameters (shared bump rule of 03), tessellated Axis basiscurves; members_advanced gains a curved beam. App: the beam tool (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/beam.rs, profiles-columns-beams-11) gains the arc modes of curved-geometry-07 (three points, centre and radius, tangent) through the point-input service; the properties strip shows radius and arc length. Cleanup: cleanup-and-trims-01 treats beam anchor lines as straight 3D segments, so curved beams are excluded from axis contacts (no L, T or X joins; the body-based priority cleanup of cleanup-and-trims-02 still cuts them) and a follow-up bead covers BEA-004 for curved beams. Out of scope: segmented curved beams, curved columns, free 3D axes, joins of curved beams.
design: Sweeping along the circle-anchored tessellation makes plan cuts, slab edges and walls on the same circle coincide vertex for vertex (curved-geometry-03). For a level arc every lateral quad is planar: a profile edge lies in a radial plane and either meets the circle's vertical axis or is parallel to it, and so does its rotated copy at the next station, so the two edges are coplanar; roll or a helical rise breaks this and those quads are split into two planar triangles as in the loft of task 07. Pitfalls: roll rotates about the tangent at every station; the lateral offset is concentric (a radius change), not a translation; vertical_extent and plan_bounds must use the arc's extreme points (curve.rs bbox); stations come only from the shared tessellator. Pointers: curve.rs, the shared tessellate(), sweep.rs, kinds/beam.rs, the beam codec, the arc modes of curved-geometry-07, geometry opening.rs (15).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a 0.25 x 0.50 m beam on a 90-degree arc of r = 5.00 m at constant elevation is closed and outward, its volume equals the analytic value for the inscribed station polygon within 1e-9, no chord deviates more than 2 mm and no step exceeds 10 degrees (IFX-034), side faces of one run share vertices and profile corners do not.
- The plan slice at mid-height equals the annular sector built from the same tessellation (vertex lists bit-identical with tessellate(), the coincidence rule of curved-geometry); projected and overhead classification work for it (BEA-008 regression row).
- A rising curved beam (2.80 to 3.30 m) is closed and its axis rises linearly with arc length; its non-planar quads are split into planar triangles.
- Validation rejects a radius below half the width, a full circle and a second segment with messages.
- A notch hosted at along = 1.00 m sits on the tangent frame there (within 1e-9).
- A curved beam crossing a wall creates no axis contact (contact-list test) while the priority cleanup still trims the lower-priority body.
- IFCX round trip and conformance; egui_kittest: the beam tool's 'Arc' mode creates a curved beam from three clicks.
- Satisfies BEA-009.
notes: SRS: BEA-009
