title: Add the Segments table to the column and beam settings dialog
description:
WHY: COL-005 and BEA-005 give every segment its own cross-section, material, uniform or tapered size (start and end width and height) and fixed or flexible length (flexible = percentage share of the length not taken by fixed segments), and every joint its own cut plane; PRF-008 lets elements override offset parameters per instance and per end of a tapered segment. The palette of task 10 edits one selected part at a time; the settings dialog needs the whole list so members such as F4 and F5 can be set up numerically in one place. Status missing (COL-005 XL, BEA-005 XL, PRF-008 L). The settings dialog is ui/properties.rs settings_dialog (properties-and-dialogs-09) rendering FieldSpecs through ui/fields.rs (properties-and-dialogs-05), with the column and beam fields of profiles-columns-beams-10/11 (member_fields helper).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/segments_table.rs, shown as a 'Segments' section of the column and beam settings dialog through a per-kind custom-section hook next to ui/fields.rs (a table does not fit the static FieldSpec list; whichever of 12 and 21 lands first adds the hook): one row per segment from start to end (index, Fixed or Flexible, length or share in percent with the resolved length read-only, section kind with width and height or a profile combo filtered by the Column or Beam usage flag, material, 'Tapered' toggle with end width and height or end profile size, start and end offset overrides with one field per offset parameter of the segment's profile, empty = profile default, the end fields only while tapered) and, between rows, the joint cut (Square, or Plane with mitre and tilt angles). For a selection, row edits issue SegmentOp::Set, joint edits SegmentOp::SetJoint and the row buttons Insert, Remove, Move up and Move down the operations of 09, each one undo step; for tool defaults the table edits the prototype's Segments with the pure functions of 09 through SetToolDefaults. Validation messages from validate_element appear under the table. Action 'Edit segments' (column and beam context menus and the properties strip) enters edit mode on the selected member (task 10). One-segment members show a single row, so the profiles-columns-beams fields stay unchanged. Out of scope: the palette and handles (10), profile editing (12).
design: Rows edit whole segments through SegmentOp::Set, so the table needs no new command and stays consistent with the palette; joint cuts sit between rows because joints belong to positions, not segments (06). Resolved lengths come from Segments::resolve_lengths at the member's current total, the function the geometry uses, so the table never disagrees with the body. Reuse widgets::length and widgets::angle and the profile combo of profiles-columns-beams-10/11. Pitfalls: offset override fields depend on the segment's profile, so changing the profile drops overrides the new profile does not declare (with a note); keep the dialog draft-free like the other settings dialog sections; long tables scroll inside the section; mixed selections of members with different segment counts show the table read-only with an explanation. Pointers: ui/properties.rs settings_dialog, ui/fields.rs, ui/widgets.rs, views/segments.rs (10), kinds/member.rs (06, 09).
acceptance_criteria:
- egui_kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): the settings dialog of a three-segment beam shows three rows with resolved lengths; editing a flexible share issues one EditSegments command and bumps the document revision; undo restores the share.
- Toggling 'Tapered' on a profile segment shows end size and end offset fields; typing an end height of 0.90 m and an end override 'lip' = 0.03 m issues one SegmentOp::Set whose end_instance carries both (state test without egui).
- The profile combo of a column segment lists only profiles with the Column flag; a joint row set to Plane with a 20-degree mitre issues SegmentOp::SetJoint; in the beam tool-defaults dialog a second segment added in the table appears on the next beam drawn.
- 'Edit segments' on a selected column enters edit mode with its segments selectable.
- Satisfies the numeric editing of COL-005 and BEA-005 (per-segment section, material, taper, fixed or flexible length, per-joint cut plane) and the per-end override clause of PRF-008 in the UI.
notes: SRS: COL-005 BEA-005 PRF-008

title: Let openings use a shared profile as their cross-section
description:
WHY: OPN-010 (C): an opening whose cross-section is a shared profile (PRF) may update everywhere when the profile changes. Status missing (M; gap: no profile reference on openings and no re-evaluation on profile change). host-openings-01 offers Section::{Rectangle, Circle, Polygon}; profiles-columns-beams-06 made the dirty set follow Kind::profiles(), and task 01 added the openings usage flag.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/opening.rs: `Section::Profile { profile: ProfileId, instance: ProfileInstance }`; profile_uses reports Opening; validation through validate_instance. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/opening.rs: section_ring for Profile = the outer rings of the resolved section's regions (holes ignored, documented: a void has no core), placed at the anchor with the profile origin; VoidPrism and void_mesh are unchanged, so wall in-plane cuts, slab holes, kernel cuts and the Void child all follow. IFCX: archicraft::opening section kind 'profile' with profile and instance (shared bump rule of 03); members_advanced gains two openings sharing the arched opening profile of 03. App: the opening tool's shape modes (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/opening.rs) gain 'Profile' with a picker filtered by the openings flag; the opening properties show profile and instance size. Out of scope: voids with a core, reveal materials (OPN-008).
design: Using the outer rings keeps the void a prism and every cut path unchanged; multi-region profiles (twin windows) give several rings and the union rule of host-openings-05 applies. Update-everywhere comes from the framework's dirty set over profile_uses, so this task only adds the variant, the ring and persistence. Pitfalls: the profile origin becomes the opening anchor (bottom-centre for wall-face placements, host-openings-01), so document that opening profiles should have their origin at the bottom centre; instance sizes stretch only inside zones (02). Pointers: kinds/opening.rs, geometry opening.rs (host-openings-03), the opening codec (host-openings-08), crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/opening.rs (host-openings-11).
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: two wall openings reference one custom arched profile; an UpdateProfile raising the arch by 0.10 m changes both voids and both host bodies in one revision through incremental evaluation, identical to a full evaluation (property-test helper of element-kind-framework-10).
- DeleteProfile of a profile used by an opening is rejected without a replacement and re-points the opening with a replacement that has the openings flag (command test with undo).
- IFCX round trip with assert_eq; Void children regenerate identically after reading (hash comparison); conformance green.
- egui_kittest: the opening tool offers 'Profile' and a placed opening references the selected profile.
- Satisfies OPN-010.
notes: SRS: OPN-010

title: Add fixtures F4 and F5 to the registry and the regression suite
description:
WHY: The epic acceptance requires fixtures F4 (precast double-pitch beam, 9.80 m, anchor bottom-centre, four segments: 400 mm fixed rectangular 600 x 200 mm; a flexible tee profile tapered from 600 to 900 mm high; that tee mirrored; 400 mm fixed) and F5 (precast column 6.00 m with corbel: fixed segments of 200, 400 (1400 mm wide) and 300 mm (taper 1400 to 600 mm) plus a flexible body; stretching resizes only the body) as geometry tests in the NFR-MNT-005 suite with the COL-005 and BEA-005 acceptance values, registered in the D.7 fixture registry. BEA-005 acceptance: F4 can be modelled and stretched. COL-005 acceptance: the 5.10 m flexible segment becomes 6.10 m when the column is stretched to 7.00 m. BEA-006 operations must undo cleanly on the fixture.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs (the D.7 registry of regression-and-status-02): `pub fn f4_double_pitch_beam() -> Project` and `pub fn f5_corbel_column() -> Project` built through commands with the FixtureBuilder (v5 ids from the fixture names), and the D7 entries F4 and F5 (owner members-profiles-adv, increment 3) set to `build: Some(..)` and `seeded: true`, so the generic checks of crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/fixtures.rs and crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/fixtures.rs (integrity, closed bodies, IFCX round trip within 0.1 mm) run on them. F4: a custom tee profile with a vertical stretch zone in the web (see notes for the dimensions), segments [Fixed 0.40 Rectangular 0.20 x 0.60, Flexible 50 % tee 0.60 to 0.90, Flexible 50 % tee 0.90 to 0.60, Fixed 0.40 Rectangular 0.20 x 0.60], anchor BottomCentre. F5: segments from the base [Flexible body 0.60 x 0.40, Fixed 0.30 taper 0.60 to 1.40 x 0.40, Fixed 0.40 corbel 1.40 x 0.40, Fixed 0.20 0.60 x 0.40], top linked to give 6.00 m. crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs: switch the Pending("members-profiles-adv") F4 and F5 rows of junction-engine-12 to active ('F4 segmented beam' and 'F5 corbel column', srs BEA-005 and COL-005) with golden outlines at defined stations, plus stretch rows (F4 at 11.80 m by moving the end point, F5 at 7.00 m by a storey-height change), and list them as covered in docs/junctions.md. The sample catalogue gains f4 and f5 (in members_advanced or as their own entries) so the golden IFCX and conformance cover them. Out of scope: precast connections and reinforcement, raising REQUIRED_INCREMENT (the increment-3 exit verification does that).
design: Fixtures are built only through commands and the seeded builder so ids, golden outlines and IFCX stay stable (element-kind-framework-03). A custom tee with a stretch zone in the web makes F4 exercise PRF-007 and the loft topology rule of tasks 02 and 07 together, which is the knowledge-base workflow (KB 303950); a parametric TShape variant is a one-line alternative if the product owner prefers it. Golden outlines follow junction-engine-12 (rounded to 1e-9 m, counter-clockwise, smallest vertex first). Pitfalls: segments run from the base in code while D.7 describes F5 top-down; comment that. Keep the rows fast (two members, a few stations). regression-and-status (increment 1) is not a declared prerequisite: if its D7 table is missing, add f4 and f5 to crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs in the shape junction-engine used for f1, f6 and f7 and file a bead to register them.
acceptance_criteria:
- F4: resolved segment lengths 0.40/4.50/4.50/0.40 m at 9.80 m and 0.40/5.50/5.50/0.40 m after moving the end point to 11.80 m (one command, undo restores); the bottom is flat at the anchor elevation; the top is 0.90 m above the bottom at mid-span and 0.60 m at the tee ends; one closed outward Body part; volume equals the analytic sum (prisms plus lofts with area linear in web height) within 1e-9.
- F5: the flexible body is 5.10 m at 6.00 m and 6.10 m after a storey-height change to 7.00 m (COL-005 values asserted literally); the corbel top is 5.80 m above the base before and 6.80 m after; vertices of the fixed segments keep their positions relative to the column top; the plan slice inside the corbel is 1.40 x 0.40 m; closed body; analytic volume within 1e-9.
- F4 and F5 are built, seeded entries of the D7 table in crates/archicraft-model/src/fixtures.rs: the registry test crates/archicraft-model/tests/fixtures.rs pins their owner and increment and passes check() on both; they pass the generic geometry and IFCX fixture checks, run as active NFR-MNT-005 rows with blessed golden outlines, appear as covered rows in docs/junctions.md, and round-trip through IFCX with conformance green.
- On F4, inserting a copy of segment 2, removing it, swapping segments 2 and 3 and splitting segment 2 at 1.50 m each undo to a project equal to f4().
- Satisfies the acceptance clauses of BEA-005 and COL-005, exercises BEA-006 on a real fixture, and registers F4 and F5 (Appendix D.7).
notes:
SRS: BEA-005 COL-005 BEA-006
Assumptions (D.7 gives no full dimensions), to be confirmed by the product owner: '600 x 200 mm' read as height x width so the end block meets the tee's 600 mm start height; tee flange 400 x 150 mm and web 200 mm; F5 body 0.60 x 0.40 m with a symmetric corbel 1.40 m wide and 0.40 m deep.

title: Add segment lists with flexible lengths to columns and beams
description:
WHY: COL-005 (S): columns shall support multiple segments along their axis, each with its own cross-section, material, uniform or tapered size and fixed or flexible length; acceptance: a 6.00 m column with fixed segments of 0.20 m, 0.40 m (corbel 1.40 m wide) and 0.30 m (taper from 1.40 m to 0.60 m) has a 5.10 m flexible segment, which becomes 6.10 m when the column is stretched to 7.00 m. BEA-005 (S): the same for beams; tapered size = start and end width and height; flexible lengths are percentage shares of the length not taken by fixed segments; each joint has its own cut plane. PRF-008: offset overrides per end of a tapered segment. Status: both missing, XL. Column and Beam (profiles-columns-beams-06/07) hold one `section: CrossSection` and one `material`.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/member.rs: `Segments { items: Vec<MemberSegment>, joints: Vec<CutSpec> }` (joints.len() == items.len() - 1, CutSpec from task 05) and `MemberSegment { section: CrossSection, material: MaterialId, end_size: Option<SectionSize { width, height }>, length: SegmentLength::{Fixed(f64), Flexible(f64)}, start_instance: ProfileInstance, end_instance: Option<ProfileInstance> }` (start size = the section's own size or the profile instance size; end_size or end_instance = tapered); `Segments::resolve_lengths(total) -> Result<Vec<f64>, SegmentError>` (fixed lengths kept, the remainder shared by the flexible shares normalised to 100 %), `stations(total)`, `segment_at(station)`, `Segments::single(section, material)`. Column and Beam replace section and material by `segments: Segments`, keeping `section()`/`material()` accessors for one-segment members so tools, properties and tests of profiles-columns-beams compile unchanged; serde accepts the legacy fields as one flexible 100 % segment. Validation: 1 to 32 segments, at least one flexible segment, positive shares, fixed sum leaving at least MIN_EDGE_LENGTH per flexible segment at the current total ('The fixed segments (0.90 m) leave no room for the flexible segment of this 0.80 m column'), valid sizes and instances (01), profile uses Column or Beam per segment. Total = axis length between the end planes (columns: height / cos(inclination); beams: anchor-line length). Compile-preserving adaptions: geometry sweeps each uniform segment between perpendicular joint planes with the existing sweep and reports 'Tapered segments are not generated yet' until 07; the IFCX codecs write the first segment as section and material plus a writer warning when there are more (until 08); properties edit the single segment. Out of scope: lofts and kernel merge (07), IFCX (08), segment operations (09), UI (10, 21).
design: Flexible lengths are never stored; they are resolved from the current total at every evaluation, which makes stretching (moving a beam end, changing a storey height) work without any extra command (ELM-006). Items run from the member start (beam start point, column base) to its end; documented because F5 is usually described top-down. Joints belong to positions between segments, not to segments, so reordering (09) keeps the joint list. One shared type serves both kinds, so the codec, the operations and the UI of 08 to 10 are written once. Pitfalls: plan_update_elements detects no-change by equality, so derive PartialEq; profiles() and profile_uses() of members now iterate all segments, so DeleteProfile replacement and dirty propagation cover every segment; top-linked columns change their total silently, which is why the storey-edit rejection must include the fixed-sum rule. Pointers: kinds/member.rs, kinds/column.rs, kinds/beam.rs, validate.rs, kinds/mod.rs Kind trait, element-kind-framework-09.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test with the COL-005 acceptance values: fixed 0.20, 0.40 and 0.30 m plus one flexible segment resolve to 5.10 m at 6.00 m and to 6.10 m at 7.00 m (1e-12); a storey-height change that stretches a top-linked column re-resolves the flexible length with no edit of the column (command test with undo).
- BEA-005 shares: two fixed 0.40 m and two flexible 50/50 segments on a 9.80 m beam resolve to 4.50/4.50 m and to 5.50/5.50 m at 11.80 m; shares 30/90 are normalised to 25/75 %.
- Validation tests: no flexible segment, a joints-count mismatch, a fixed sum longer than the member, a profile segment whose profile lacks the Beam flag and an end instance on a non-profile segment are rejected with messages.
- Legacy serde: a Column JSON with section and material deserialises to one flexible 100 % segment; one-segment members keep their meshes and golden files bit for bit (regression).
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: UpdateElements with a three-segment beam executes and undoes exactly; the storey-edit rejection of element-kind-framework-09 also rejects a storey change that leaves no room for the flexible segments.
- Satisfies the model clauses of COL-005 and BEA-005 and the per-end override clause of PRF-008.
notes:
SRS: COL-005 BEA-005 PRF-008
The limit of 32 segments is an assumption; the SRS gives none.

title: Join profiled walls at L and T and hook profiles into railings
description:
WHY: A profiled wall (task 11) must take part in wall junctions like any other wall (WAL-020 L, T and X; WAL-026 order independence), otherwise PRF-010's profiled walls cannot be used in real plans, and NFR-MNT-005 requires every junction case of Section 4 in the regression suite. PRF-010 (S) also names railings: profiles shall be usable by railings, with per-edge material overrides. Status missing (PRF-010 L). Task 11 sweeps profiled walls with square ends; railings-stairs-adv (increment 3, not a prerequisite of this epic) adds the railing kind whose component sections can reference profiles (railings-stairs-adv-02 validates ProfileUsage.railings) and sweeps rails with sweep() (railings-stairs-adv-03).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry: the junction engine (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/junction.rs, junction-engine-04) takes part with the profile's bounding envelope from Project::cross_section (11), and the profiled body is clipped by vertical CutPlanes through the resolved envelope end edges (mitre at L, butt at T); a basic wall whose end meets a profiled wall is extended to the profiled wall's reference line and the profiled body is subtracted from it through the SolidKernel (solid-kernel-ops-02), so a non-vertical profile face leaves no gap; the subtraction follows the stage order of solid-kernel-ops-05 (junctions first, Booleans later) and a KernelError keeps the butt end and lists a GeometryProblem. NFR-MNT-005: rows 'profiled wall L', 'profiled wall T with a basic wall' and 'profiled wall X' in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/junctions.rs with golden outlines, listed as covered in docs/junctions.md. Railings: Kind::profile_uses (01) of the railing kind (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/railing.rs) reports ProfileUse::Railing for every component section that references a profile, so UpdateProfile refuses to drop the railings flag while a railing uses the profile and profile edits dirty the railing; rails swept with sweep() inherit the edge-material runs of 02 with no railing-specific geometry code. If railings-stairs-adv has not merged when this task runs, cover the rule with the test-kinds Dummy as a railing user and file a bead in railings-stairs-adv for the railing hookup. Out of scope: priority resolution between profile regions, arc profiled walls (rejected in 11), posts and balusters with per-edge materials beyond what sweep() gives.
design: The envelope approach reuses the node graph, determinism and order independence of the junction engine (WAL-026) without priority resolution inside the profile: profile regions are not skins, so that stays out of scope and is documented. Vertical planar end cuts through the resolved envelope corners are exact for walls with the same profile (mitre) and for butts against plane faces; the one case they cannot handle, a branch ending at a non-vertical profile face, is solved by the kernel subtraction of the profiled body. Railings get per-edge materials without railing-specific geometry because profile_section fills the edge materials and sweep() emits the runs (02). Pitfalls: test both drawing directions; profiled walls report no Skin_n parts, so skin separators skip them; keep the subtraction order-independent (sorted pairs). Pointers: junction.rs (junction-engine-04), tests/junctions.rs (junction-engine-12), docs/junctions.md, kernel/mod.rs, evaluate.rs stage order (solid-kernel-ops-05), kinds/railing.rs and railing/rails.rs (railings-stairs-adv-02/03).
acceptance_criteria:
- L junction of two equal profiled walls: end caps coincide in the bisector plane (vertex check) and the union volume equals the sum; the result is identical for both creation orders (permutation check of junction-engine-06).
- T junction of a basic 0.20 m wall onto the profiled wall: zero intersection volume with the profiled body (kernel) and the branch end volume equals the analytic value against stem and footing (no gap); with a failing test kernel the branch keeps its butt end and one problem names both walls.
- The three profiled-wall rows run active in cargo test -p archicraft-geometry --test junctions with blessed golden outlines and appear as covered rows in docs/junctions.md.
- Railings: UpdateProfile removing the railings flag from a profile used by a railing (or by the Dummy railing user) is rejected naming the element and leaves the project unchanged; when railings-stairs-adv has merged, an overridden profile edge colours the corresponding rail face (face_materials run test in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/railing.rs), otherwise the bead exists.
- Satisfies the junction behaviour of PRF-010 profiled walls and the railing clause of PRF-010 (usage enforcement and per-edge materials through the shared sweep).
notes:
SRS: PRF-010
Roadmap gap: railings-stairs-adv (increment 3) is not a prerequisite of this epic, so the railing hookup is conditional; file a bead there if the railing kind is missing when this task runs.

title: Edit stretch zones, offsets and edge materials in the profile dialog
description:
WHY: PRF-007, PRF-008 and PRF-010 are user features: stretch zones, offset parameters, edge materials and usage flags must be editable in the profile editor, and elements must expose their instance size and offset overrides. Profiled walls (11) need a profile choice in the wall properties. profiles-columns-beams-14/15 built crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/profiles.rs (parametric shapes, catalogue, custom canvas with regions, holes and origin) and listed these features as out of scope.

WHAT: ui/profiles.rs: 'Nominal size' fields with a 'Fit to geometry' button; stretch zones drawn as translucent bands on the canvas with draggable boundaries and numeric min and max per axis, plus a preview size (width, height) showing the resolved section of task 02 live; an 'Offset parameters' list (add, rename, default value, delete) whose edges are bound by clicking edges on the canvas (Shift adds; an edge already bound elsewhere is refused with a message); an edge selection mode with a material combo ('By region' or a material) for per-edge overrides; usage checkboxes for columns, beams, walls, railings and openings. Each completed operation issues one UpdateProfile; rejections (including users named by the re-validation of 01) appear in the dialog and the status line. ui/properties.rs and the settings dialog (settings_dialog, properties-and-dialogs-09): for one-segment columns and beams with a profile (editing segment 0's start instance of tasks 06 and 08) and for profiled walls, size fields per stretch-zone axis (disabled with a tooltip when the axis has no zone) and one field per offset parameter (empty = profile default), rendered through a per-kind custom-section hook next to ui/fields.rs because their number depends on the profile and does not fit the static FieldSpec list of properties-and-dialogs-05 (whichever of 12 and 21 lands first adds the hook); the wall 'Structure' choice gains 'Profile' with a picker filtered by the walls flag; every profile picker filters by the usage flag of the target kind. Out of scope: segment-level overrides (in the Segments table of 21), profile capture (13).
design: Reuse the canvas ViewSurface and polygon consumer of profiles-columns-beams-15; zones and edges are extra hit-test layers on the same canvas, computed by pure functions in a sibling module. The preview calls archicraft-geometry resolve_instance, the code the elements use, so the preview equals the swept result. Keep the dialog draft-free (one command per completed operation) like the existing profile dialog. Pitfalls: UpdateProfile re-validates users (01), so a zone edit that would break an element is refused with the element named; show that in the dialog. Pointers: ui/profiles.rs, ui/properties.rs, ui/dialogs.rs, ui/widgets.rs length and angle fields.
acceptance_criteria:
- egui_kittest: the profile dialog on a custom profile shows 'Stretch zones'; typing a vertical zone issues one UpdateProfile and the preview at a larger height changes only inside the band (checked through the resolved section); adding an offset parameter 'lip' and binding one edge issues one command; choosing a material for a selected edge stores an edge override.
- Pure-function tests without egui: canvas edge picking returns (region, ring, index) per the PartRef convention; dragging a zone boundary snaps to profile vertices within the snap radius (8 px, D.1).
- Properties: a profiled wall shows 'Profile' and the picker lists only profiles with the walls flag; a column with a zone-less axis shows that size field disabled; editing an offset override issues one UpdateElements that undo reverts.
- Satisfies the user-facing parts of PRF-007, PRF-008 and PRF-010.
notes: SRS: PRF-007 PRF-008 PRF-010

title: Resolve profile instances: offsets, stretch zones, edge materials
description:
WHY: PRF-007: when an element's size differs from the nominal size, only the geometry inside the stretch zones scales. PRF-008: offset parameters move their bound edges per instance and per end of a tapered segment, so start and end sections of a segment must have the same topology for lofting (BEA-005, COL-005). PRF-010: per-edge material overrides colour the faces swept from those edges. Status missing. profiles-columns-beams-03 produces `Section { regions: Vec<SectionRegion { outer: SectionLoop, holes, material, role }> }` through profile_section(&Profile, &Tessellation) and -05 sweeps it with sweep(); neither knows instances.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/section.rs: `resolve_instance(&Profile, &ProfileInstance, &Tessellation) -> Result<Section, GeometryError>` = profile_section, then offsets (each bound edge moved along its outward normal by the override or default, end points recomputed by intersecting with the adjacent edge lines, reusing the line-offset routine of edit-reshape-palette's offset_ring restricted to a subset of edges), then a split of every loop edge that crosses a zone boundary (x = zone.min or max, y = zone.min or max, in nominal coordinates), then the piecewise-linear map per axis: below min unchanged, inside min + (v - min) * k with k = (max - min + delta) / (max - min), above v + delta (delta = actual - nominal). SectionLoop gains `edge_materials: Vec<Option<MaterialId>>` (one per edge, None = region material), filled by profile_section itself from ProfileRegion.edge_materials so every caller receives them (the railing rails of railings-stairs-adv-03 included), and carried through offsets and splits. `resolve_pair(profile, start, end, tess) -> (Section, Section)` guarantees identical loop topology for both ends (split vertices from the union of zone crossings, tessellation counts from the larger end) for the loft of task 07. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/sweep.rs: lateral strips from overridden edges are recorded as FaceMaterialRun entries (BodyPart.face_materials of solid-kernel-ops-07) inside sweep() itself, so every caller (members, the profiled walls of 11, rails of railings-stairs-adv-03) inherits them; caps keep the region material. The column and beam generators (kinds/column.rs, kinds/beam.rs) resolve the element's instance (the default instance until segments arrive in 06). Out of scope: tapered lofts (07), wall sweeps (11), UI (12).
design: Split before mapping: the stretch map is piecewise linear per axis, so an edge crossing a zone boundary needs a vertex on that boundary or it would bend; inserting those vertices in nominal coordinates makes the inserted set independent of the actual size and therefore topology-stable across sizes, which the loft (07) needs. Order: offsets first (defined on nominal geometry), then stretch; documented in the module. A zone boundary on an existing vertex inserts nothing (MODEL_TOLERANCE from the tolerance module). Inserted vertices on an arc run stay smooth; stretching turns arcs into elliptical arcs, acceptable and documented. Circle tessellation depends on the radius, so resolve_pair takes the counts from the larger end. Edge materials ride on edges so the loop stays the single source; per-face runs avoid splitting closed parts (IFX-032; solid-kernel-ops-07 explains why the writer keeps one material per part). Pointers: section.rs and sweep.rs (profiles-columns-beams-03/05), offset_ring in outline/edit.rs (edit-reshape-palette-03), FaceMaterialRun in evaluate.rs (solid-kernel-ops-07), triangulate.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- section.rs unit tests: a wall profile with a 0.60 x 0.30 m footing, a 0.25 m stem and a vertical zone from 0.40 to 2.90 m at nominal height 3.00 m, resolved at 3.40 m, keeps every vertex below 0.40 m bit-identical, moves every vertex above 2.90 m by exactly +0.40 m and grows the area by 0.25 x 0.40 m2.
- Both zones together scale a custom rectangular hollow profile in both axes while the wall thickness outside the zones stays unchanged (vertex comparison).
- An offset parameter 'lip' bound to one edge of a custom L moves that edge by 0.02 m along its outward normal and keeps all other edges on their lines; an offset that makes the loop self-intersect returns GeometryError naming the parameter.
- resolve_pair of a tee with a vertical web zone at heights 0.60 and 0.90 m returns sections with equal vertex counts and smooth flags per loop (property test over random sizes inside the valid range).
- sweep.rs: a prism swept from a profile with one edge override is closed (check_closed) and its face_materials runs cover exactly the triangles of that lateral face; render3d shows them in the override colour through the existing run support.
- profile_section of a custom profile with one edge material returns the override on exactly that edge (unit test), so callers that never resolve an instance still receive it.
- Satisfies the geometry clauses of PRF-007 and PRF-008 and the per-edge material clause of PRF-010 for columns and beams.
notes:
SRS: PRF-007 PRF-008 PRF-010
Arcs inside a stretched zone become elliptical; the SRS does not require exact arcs there.

title: Add stretch zones, offset parameters and edge materials to profiles
description:
WHY: PRF-007 (S): profiles shall have a nominal width and height and horizontal and vertical stretch zones; when an element's size differs from the nominal size, only the geometry inside the stretch zones scales (a profiled wall follows a storey-linked height while its footing keeps its dimensions). PRF-008 (C): profiles may have named offset parameters bound to one or more edges, which elements override per instance and per end of a tapered segment. PRF-010 (S): profiles shall also be usable by walls and railings and allow per-edge material overrides. OPN-010 (C) adds openings as a further profile user. Status: all missing (gap rows PRF-007 L, PRF-008 L, PRF-010 L). profiles-columns-beams-01 stores ProfileUsage { columns, beams, walls, railings } but enforces only columns and beams and has no size, zone, offset or edge data. Every later task of this epic (instance resolution, segments, profiled walls, the dialog, profile openings) reads these fields.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/profile.rs: `Profile.nominal: Option<DVec2>` (None = bounds size, resolved by `Profile::nominal_size()`), `Profile.stretch: StretchZones { x: Option<Interval>, y: Option<Interval> }` with `Interval { min, max }` in profile coordinates, `Profile.offsets: Vec<OffsetParameter { name: String, edges: Vec<ProfileEdge { region: u16, ring: u16, index: u32 }>, default: f64 }>`, `ProfileRegion.edge_materials: Vec<EdgeMaterial { ring: u16, index: u32, material: MaterialId }>` (sparse, sorted; custom regions only) and `ProfileUsage.openings: bool` (serde default false). Add `ProfileInstance { size: Option<DVec2>, offsets: BTreeMap<String, f64> }`, the per-element instance used by members, segment ends, walls and openings, with `effective_size(&Profile)` and the rule 'an axis without a stretch zone keeps the nominal size'. validate.rs: validate_profile checks zones inside the bounds with min < max, nominal equal to the bounds extent in an axis without a zone, unique non-empty identifier names, existing edge references, each edge bound by at most one parameter, finite defaults within +-1 m, existing edge materials on existing edges, and no offsets or edge materials on parametric shapes ('Convert to custom first'); `validate_instance(&Profile, &ProfileInstance)` checks positive sizes, sizes that keep each zone at least MIN_EDGE_LENGTH long, overrides only for declared names, values within +-1 m. Usage enforcement: `Kind::profile_uses() -> Vec<(ProfileId, ProfileUse)>` with ProfileUse::{Column, Beam, Wall, Railing, Opening} (default derived from Kind::profiles() and the descriptor) so UpdateProfile rejects removing a flag in use, DeleteProfile's replacement must carry every needed flag, and UpdateProfile re-validates every user instance (a zone shrunk below a user's size is rejected naming the element); plan_delete_material also reassigns edge materials. Out of scope: geometry (02), persistence (03), UI (12), the users themselves (06, 11, 14, 20).
design: Keep the model geometry-free (archicraft-model depends only on glam, indexmap, serde, thiserror and uuid): zones and offsets are data, the piecewise mapping lives in archicraft-geometry (02). Edge addressing (region, ring, index) follows the PartRef ring convention of selection-transforms-01 (ring 0 = outer, 1.. = holes, edge i from vertex i to i+1) so the editor (12) can reuse its hit tests. Parametric profiles get offsets and edge materials only after 'Convert to custom' (profiles-columns-beams-15) because their polygon is generated. Store `nominal` explicitly once a zone exists, so editing a region does not silently resize every user (PRF-004 'editing updates users' must not change their sizes). Users: Column and Beam through segments (06), Wall (11), Opening (14), Railing (20); the default profile_uses keeps existing kinds compiling. Pitfalls: BTreeMap keeps offset overrides deterministic in files (IFX-007); the user re-validation loop must stay kind-agnostic through Kind::profile_uses (no kind-specific code in command.rs, framework module-layout test); messages name profile and element, for example 'Profile Footing wall: the vertical stretch zone is too short for wall W-012'. Pointers: profile.rs and validate_profile (profiles-columns-beams-01), command.rs plan_delete_profile and plan_delete_material, kinds/mod.rs Kind trait.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in crates/archicraft-model/src/profile.rs and validate.rs: a zone outside the bounds, an empty zone, a duplicate offset name, an offset bound to a missing edge, an edge bound twice and an offset on a parametric profile are rejected with user-facing messages; a valid custom profile with both zones, two offset parameters and an edge material passes and its edge materials come back sorted.
- effective_size: with only a vertical zone, an instance height of 3.40 m on a 3.00 m nominal profile is accepted and the width stays nominal; a size that would shrink the zone below MIN_EDGE_LENGTH is rejected.
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: UpdateProfile that shrinks a zone below a user's size, removes the walls flag while a test-kind user needs it, or drops an offset parameter a user overrides is rejected and leaves the project unchanged; DeleteProfile with a replacement lacking the openings flag is rejected; DeleteMaterial reassigns edge materials; execute plus undo restores the project on every new path.
- A profile serialised without the new fields deserialises with defaults (serde test).
- Satisfies the model clauses of PRF-007 (nominal size, zones), PRF-008 (named offsets bound to edges, per-instance overrides) and PRF-010 (walls and railings usage enforced, per-edge material overrides); geometry follows in task 02.
notes:
SRS: PRF-007 PRF-008 PRF-010 OPN-010
Open questions: the SRS gives no limit for offset values (+-1 m assumed) and does not say whether an axis without a stretch zone scales uniformly; this plan keeps the nominal size in that axis (complex-profile behaviour in the knowledge base) and documents it.

title: Persist segments and joints in IFCX with legacy single-section reading
description:
WHY: Segmented members (COL-005, BEA-005) must round-trip: IFX-060 keeps authoring data in archicraft:: attributes, IFX-061 declares it, IFX-062 versions it and IFX-011 keeps identities stable; exported parts must be the evaluated merged bodies (IFX-033). Status missing; after task 06 the codecs write only the first segment and warn.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/column.rs and beam.rs (codecs of profiles-columns-beams-06/07) and schema.rs: `segments: array(object { section { kind, width, height, diameter, profile }, material, endSize: optional object { width, height }, length: object { kind: enumeration(fixed, flexible), value }, startInstance: optional object { size, offsets }, endInstance: optional object { size, offsets } })` and `joints: array(cut)` sharing the cut schema of task 05. The writer always writes segments and no longer writes section and material; the reader accepts both shapes (legacy section/material become one flexible 100 % segment, silently for files older than the epic's bump and with a warning otherwise), validates through validate_element and repairs a joints-count mismatch with Square joints and a warning. Parts 'Body' or 'Segment_<i>' with v5 sub-node ids, each inheriting its material node (IFX-043); Axis basiscurves unchanged. samples.rs members_advanced gains a four-segment beam with tapered profile segments, a corbel column with a different corbel material and a one-segment column that uses the hollow profile of 03 at a non-nominal size with an offset override (the first element instance in the golden); golden re-blessed. The epic's migration entry (03) gets the description 'segments on columns and beams'. Out of scope: curved beams (17), fixture registration (19).
design: Follow the per-kind codec registration of element-kind-framework-06 and 'Add an IFCX attribute'. Accepting the legacy shape in the reader, instead of a migration that rewrites JSON, keeps intermediate development files loadable and costs one branch; the shared bump still makes older releases flag new files (IFX-062). Length kinds use an enumeration derived from a model ALL array. Pitfalls: segment order is model order (start to end), never sorted; part names come from segment indices, never from kernel output order; stable member order (IFX-007). Pointers: alpha/kinds/column.rs and beam.rs, schema.rs, reader.rs lenient helpers (report.or), samples.rs, tests/roundtrip.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs: members_advanced round-trips with assert_eq (segments, joints, tapered sizes, instances with offsets) and two saves are byte-identical; the columns-and-beams golden loads into one-segment members and its re-save differs only in the segments shape and format version (reviewed diff).
- Hand-edited files: a beam with three segments and one joint loads with a warning and gains a Square joint; a segment with an unknown section kind is skipped with an error naming the element and the beam stays valid.
- The exported Body and Segment_n meshes equal the evaluated parts (hash test, IFX-033); conformance/run.sh passes and the composed viewer tree shows the merged beam as one body.
- Satisfies persistence of COL-005 and BEA-005.
notes: SRS: COL-005 BEA-005

title: Persist profile extensions in IFCX and add the members-advanced golden
description:
WHY: The PRF-007, PRF-008 and PRF-010 data of task 01 must survive save and open: PRJ-007 stores profiles in the project, IFX-060 keeps authoring data in archicraft:: attributes, IFX-061 declares them in the file's schemas and IFX-062 versions the schema so older releases flag newer files. profiles-columns-beams-02 declared the profiles array in archicraft::project (dimensions object, regions, usage) without zones, offsets, edge materials or the openings flag. The epic also needs one golden reference model that grows with each feature.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/schema.rs: optional `nominal: point2`, `stretch: object { x, y: optional object { min, max } }`, `offsets: array(object { name: string, default: length, edges: array(object { region, ring, index }) })`, per-region `edgeMaterials: array(object { ring, index, material })` and usage `openings: boolean` in the profile record. writer.rs profile_record writes them only when present (byte-identical output for profiles without them); reader.rs read_profiles reads leniently (an invalid zone or offset is dropped with a warning naming the profile, a missing edge material is repaired to the region material with a warning) and then runs validate_profile. FORMAT_VERSION rule for this epic: its reader-visible additions (03 profiles, 04 inclination, 05 compound cuts, 08 segments, 11 wall profiles, 14 opening profiles, 16 opening placements, 17 curved beams) share one bump with one entry in alpha/migrate.rs (element-kind-framework-12); whichever lands first bumps and creates the entry, the others extend its description, unless a release was cut in between (then bump again per the rule in alpha/mod.rs). crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs: `members_advanced()` built with the FixtureBuilder (a wall-and-footing profile with a vertical zone, a hollow column profile with both zones, one offset parameter and one edge material used by a profiles-columns-beams column at its nominal size, and an arched opening profile with the openings flag; elements store their own instances only from task 06 on, so non-nominal users arrive with 08, 11 and 14), registered in catalogue(); golden crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/members-advanced.ifcx blessed. Out of scope: element instances and their records (segments 08, wall structures 11, opening sections 14).
design: Follow 'Add an IFCX attribute' in docs/implementation-status.md and keep profiles inside archicraft::project as profiles-columns-beams-02 decided (authoring data without an ifc@v5a counterpart). All new members are optional, so files of the previous version validate after migration. Parameters at full precision (round_coordinate only for meshes, NFR-ACC-002), stable member order (IFX-007), edge references positional because regions are written in order. Pitfalls: bless only after reviewing the diff (ARCHICRAFT_BLESS=1 cargo test -p archicraft-ifcx --test roundtrip); derive enumeration options from model ALL arrays; samples are built through commands only.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: members_advanced round-trips with assert_eq on the Project (zones, offsets, edge materials, openings flag) and two saves are byte-identical; the golden diff is reviewed.
- The columns-and-beams golden of profiles-columns-beams still loads without warnings and re-saves byte-identically except for the format version.
- Lenient reading: a hand-edited file with a zone outside the bounds and an edge material pointing to a missing material loads with two warnings and a valid profile.
- conformance/run.sh passes on members-advanced.ifcx (IFX-006 a) and every new member is declared in the file's schemas (IFX-061).
- A reader pinned to the previous FORMAT_VERSION reports newer_format for the new file (unit test with the constant patched).
- Satisfies persistence of PRF-007, PRF-008 and PRF-010 data.
notes:
SRS: PRF-007 PRF-008 PRF-010
Also touches PRJ-007, IFX-060, IFX-061 and IFX-062 (owned elsewhere, kept green).

title: Segmented and inclined members, advanced profiles and more opening hosts
description:
Column inclination and segments, beam end cuts as arbitrary planes, segments with tapered sizes and segment operations, notches and holes in beams, curved beams, openings hosted by beams, columns, free-form solids and terrain, profiles from existing geometry, stretch zones, offset parameters, profiled walls and railings with per-edge materials, vertical voids and shared-profile openings.

Risks: BEA-005 and COL-005 are extra large; tapered lofts keep planar faces only.
design: archicraft-model segment lists on Column and Beam, profile stretch zones and offset parameters; archicraft-geometry lofted (tapered) segment sweeps merged with the kernel; archicraft-app segment palette on PartRef. Openings in beams, columns, solids and terrain subtract through the SolidKernel.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures F4 (9.80 m double-pitch beam with four segments) and F5 (6.00 m corbel column with a 5.10 m flexible body) as geometry tests added to the NFR-MNT-005 suite together with the COL-005 and BEA-005 acceptance values; segment insert, remove, reorder and split with undo; a profiled wall following a storey-linked height scales only its stretch zone; a chimney from a holed profile is hollow in plan, section and 3D and joins the surrounding walls; a notch in a beam through an opening. F4 and F5 are registered in the fixture registry.
notes: SRS: COL-004 COL-005 BEA-003 BEA-005 BEA-006 BEA-007 BEA-009 OPN-012 OPN-010 PRF-006 PRF-007 PRF-008 PRF-010 WAL-034

title: Build segment parts, the segment palette and joint handles
description:
WHY: BEA-006 (S) asks for insert, remove, reorder, copy and paste segment settings (also between elements), swap start and end sizes, split at a picked point and drag a joint with numeric input; BEA-005 gives each joint its own cut plane; COL-005 and BEA-005 segments must be selectable and editable in plan and 3D. Status missing (BEA-006 L). The epic design notes place a segment palette on PartRef in archicraft-app: selection-transforms-01 built PartRef with the selection-part hooks of the Kind trait (part_refs(), part_ref_for_role(), part_label(), part_anchor(), part_outline(), validate_part(), KindDescriptor.part_roles) and anticipated segmented beams and columns, selection-transforms-08 provides edit mode, and free-form-solids-02 added part_anchor_3d and part_polyline_3d. Task 09 provides the commands; the settings-dialog table follows in 21.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/member.rs: `MemberPart::{Segment { index }, Joint { index }}` as the associated `type Part` of Column and Beam (the kinds! macro generates the KindPart variants), with part_refs() (segments then joints, stable order; selection-transforms-01 notes that 'parts()' for selectable parts means part_refs(), while Kind::parts() stays the IFC PartSpec list), part_ref_for_role ('Segment_<i>' of task 07 maps to Segment { i }, 'Body' to None), part_label ('segment 2', 'joint 1'), part_anchor (plan point of a joint or segment midpoint on the axis), part_outline (beam segment footprints in plan, column segments as their section outline), part_anchor_3d and part_polyline_3d (section outlines at both stations plus corner lines), validate_part (index in range) and part_roles on both descriptors. crates/archicraft-app/src/views/segments.rs: a contextual palette in edit mode for selected segment or joint parts (Insert, Remove, Move earlier, Move later, Copy settings, Paste settings, Swap sizes, Split, plus a length or share field) issuing Command::EditSegments; with a joint selected it shows the joint cut (Square, or Plane with 'Mitre angle' about_v and 'Tilt angle' about_u through widgets::angle, the field labels of task 05) and issues SegmentOp::SetJoint; `Workspace.segment_clipboard: Option<SegmentSettings>` works across elements and kinds; Split starts a point-input step constrained to the member axis (typed distance from the segment start); joint handles in plan (beams) and 3D (columns and beams) through crates/archicraft-app/src/views/handles.rs (profiles-columns-beams-13), dragged along the axis with live preview from the pure functions of 09 and typed values (Enter commits, Esc cancels); 3D picks map the hit point to a station and so to a segment. Out of scope: the Segments table of the settings dialog (21), openings on segments (15), curved beams (17).
design: Segment picking uses stations on the analytic axis instead of per-segment meshes, because equal-material segments are merged into one body by task 07; part_polyline_3d supplies the highlight. Interaction geometry (station from a ray or plan point, drag clamping between neighbouring joints) lives in pure functions over model values, tested without egui as in views/handles.rs. Reuse the HandleDrag consumer and the input-mode preference (press-drag-release or click-click) of profiles-columns-beams-13, or the shared handle registry if edit-reshape-palette-07 has absorbed it. The joint-cut fields reuse the compound-cut field helper of task 05, so beam end cuts and joint cuts edit identically. Pitfalls: Selection::retain_valid after remove and reorder drops stale Segment parts; the palette stays disabled for locked elements and shows the lock reason; single-key shortcuts must not fire while typing (UI-008).
acceptance_criteria:
- egui_kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): with a beam in edit mode and segment 1 selected the palette shows; Insert creates a second segment and the Edit menu offers 'Undo Insert segment'; Remove, Move later and Swap sizes each issue one command.
- State-machine tests without egui in views/segments.rs: a joint drag from station 0.40 m with typed 0.55 m emits MoveJoint { station: 0.55 }; Esc emits nothing; Split with typed 1.50 m emits Split { at: 1.50 }; a typed mitre angle of 20 degrees on a selected joint emits SetJoint { cut: Plane { about_u: 0, about_v: 20 degrees } }.
- Copy settings on a beam segment then Paste settings on a column segment issues PasteSettings with the clipboard content; Paste is disabled with an explanation while the clipboard is empty.
- Model unit tests: part_refs of a four-segment beam lists four segments and three joints; part_ref_for_role('Segment_2') returns Segment { 2 }; validate_part rejects index 4; Selection::retain_valid drops a Segment part after Remove.
- Hovering a segment in 3D tints its part_polyline_3d outline; the properties strip shows the segment part label.
- Satisfies the interaction clauses of BEA-006 (insert, remove, reorder, copy and paste including between elements, swap, split at a picked point, drag a joint with numeric input), the per-joint cut-plane edit of BEA-005 and makes COL-005 and BEA-005 segments selectable and editable in plan and 3D.
notes: SRS: BEA-006 BEA-005 COL-005

title: Host openings in beams, columns, solids and terrain via the kernel
description:
WHY: OPN-012 (S): beams, columns, free-form solids and terrain shall also be able to host openings. BEA-007 (S): beams shall accept notches and holes as openings (OPN-001). Epic acceptance: a notch in a beam through an opening. host-openings-01 left the HostCapability of these hosts to this epic; walls and slabs are cut in their own plane (host-openings-05/06), which does not work for swept, lofted, faceted or TIN bodies, so these hosts subtract voids through the SolidKernel (epic design notes). Status: OPN-012 missing (L), BEA-007 missing (M). The flue route of WAL-034 (task 18) builds on this.

WHAT: Model (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/opening.rs): `HostPlacement::Member { along, across, side: MemberSide::{Right, Left, Top, Bottom} }` (along the anchor axis from the beam start or column base; across = offset on that face from the axis line; sides in the section frame) and `HostPlacement::Face { face: FaceId, origin: DVec2, rotation }` (free-form solid face frame: Newell normal, u along the face's first edge); HostCapability on the column and beam descriptors (Member placements perpendicular, vertical Plan placements for columns), the solid descriptor (Face perpendicular, Plan vertical) and the terrain descriptor (Plan, vertical only; the opening's container follows the host's site container); KindDescriptor gains `cut: CutMode::{InPlane, Kernel}`. Validation: along within the resolved axis length, face present, the section intersects the host face (a notch may overhang an edge). Geometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/opening.rs): void_prism for the new placements: member frame at the station, Through = section bounds at that station plus VOID_MARGIN on both sides, Limited from the face; solid faces: Through = the solid's extent along the face normal plus margin; terrain: void top VOID_MARGIN above the highest TIN point inside the section, Through down to the terrain bottom (D.2: 5.00 m below the lowest point), Limited measured down from the surface at the anchor. Evaluation: Kernel-cut hosts subtract the union of their hosted voids (sorted by ElementId) from every visible part in the Openings stage with kernel::boolean, through the void-subtraction helper that solid-kernel-ops-14 wrote for the FurtherCuts stage (moved into geometry opening.rs if it is private there), so hosted cuts and further cuts share one Boolean path; terrain subtracts only from tiles whose bounds meet a void; a KernelError keeps the previous body and lists a problem (solid-kernel-ops-05 rule); a void that misses its host is reported. Out of scope: IFCX and tools (16), curved-beam frames (17), reveal materials (OPN-008), excavation volume (OPN-011).
design: Kernel subtraction is the one cut path that works for every one of these bodies; it runs in the existing Openings stage, before FurtherCuts and SolidOperations (solid-kernel-ops-05), so explicit operations still prevail. Placements stay host-relative (Member, Face), so 'positioned relative to that host and moves with it' holds without cascades, as host-openings-01 decided for WallFace; Plan placements in solids and terrain use the carry rule of host-openings-02. FaceId stability comes from free-form-solids-01 (ids never reused); if an edit removes a hosting face, the opening is reported ('host face 7 no longer exists') and left uncut rather than deleted silently. Terrain depth measured from the surface at the anchor keeps a pit on the ground when points are edited. Pitfalls: no void face coplanar with a host face (VOID_MARGIN, host-openings-03); union the voids before subtracting to keep one Boolean per part; cut large terrains per touched tile (terrain-and-site risk). Pointers: kinds/opening.rs, geometry opening.rs, kernel/mod.rs, evaluate.rs stages, kinds/solid.rs (free-form-solids-02), terrain.rs (terrain-and-site).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/openings_kernel.rs: a 0.20 x 0.15 m notch at the top of a beam end through its 0.25 m width removes exactly 0.20 x 0.15 x 0.25 m3 (1e-9) and the body stays closed and outward; a 0.10 m round hole through an IPE 300 web removes the tessellated circle area times the web thickness; a hole across a joint of a merged segmented beam (07) cuts both segments.
- A 0.20 x 0.20 m vertical opening through a 0.50 x 0.50 m column gives a body whose plan slice has one hole; a perpendicular opening on a free-form solid face cuts through the solid and survives a push/pull of another face; a 2 x 3 m pit 1.50 m deep in terrain removes the expected volume from the touched tiles only.
- Moving or rotating the host beam moves the void with no cascade (Member placements are host-relative); deleting the host deletes the opening (host-openings cascade); incremental evaluation equals full evaluation for these hosts.
- With a failing test kernel the previous body is kept and one problem names host and opening.
- Satisfies OPN-012 and BEA-007 (notches and holes) at model and geometry level.
notes:
SRS: OPN-012 BEA-007
Open question: whether terrain openings should use an absolute bottom elevation instead of a surface-relative depth (excavation practice).

title: Create profiles from 2D shapes, wall sections and member sections
description:
WHY: PRF-006 (S): a profile shall be creatable from existing geometry: 2D shapes copied from any view, the cross-section of a selected wall, beam or column, or a set of selected adjacent walls. Status missing (L; gap: needs ANN-001 2D shapes, selection of several walls, columns and beams). 2D elements exist from drafting-trim-split-03 (DraftLine, DraftArc, DraftPolyline bound to a DraftingView), contour regions from edit-reshape-palette-06, layered walls from layer-structures, segmented members from task 06.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/profile_capture.rs: `from_shapes(project, ids, origin: Option<DVec2>, tess) -> Result<Profile, CaptureError>`: the selected 2D elements (closed polylines, circles, chains of lines, arcs and open polylines) feed contour.rs's planar graph; minimal regions at even nesting depth become regions and those at odd depth holes; arcs are flattened with the project tessellation; view-local coordinates are translated to the origin (default bounding-box centre); one default material per region. `from_clipboard(payload: &ClipboardPayload, origin, tess)` runs the same capture on the 2D elements of a clipboard payload (crates/archicraft-model/src/clipboard.rs, selection-transforms-13), so shapes copied in any view (plan and drafting views, and section or elevation views once sections-elevations-dims exists) become profile regions. `from_wall(project, wall, station: Option<f64>)`: the vertical section perpendicular to the reference line at the station (default mid-length) from model data, one rectangle per skin (trapezoid for inclined faces) with the skin material, x to the right of the reference line seen from its start, y from the wall base; usage walls. `from_member(project, element, segment)`: rectangular and circular sections become parametric Rectangle and Circle profiles, profile sections are duplicated with their resolved instance baked into the regions; usage columns and beams. `from_adjacent_walls(project, ids)`: walls that are parallel and touch side by side (the adjacency test of the WAL-032 combine in curved-geometry-17) are placed at their offsets from the first wall's reference line and their base elevations, one region per skin; otherwise 'The selected walls are not parallel and touching'. Results are named after the source ('Section of W-004', numeric suffix on clashes), validated with validate_profile and added with AddProfile (one undo step). App: action 'Create profile from selection' (Design menu, plan and 3D context menus) picks the capture by selection content and opens the profile dialog on the new profile; the profile dialog's canvas (ui/profiles.rs) gains 'Paste shapes' (Ctrl+V), which adds the clipboard's 2D shapes as regions and holes to the selected custom profile in one UpdateProfile, or creates a new profile when none is selected. Out of scope: exact arcs in custom profiles; section and elevation views work unchanged once sections-elevations-dims adds their DraftingView, because capture reads view-local coordinates.
design: Model data instead of mesh slices keeps captured wall and member sections exact and independent of junction trimming; the station parameter keeps tapered walls meaningful. Shape capture reuses contour.rs so region and hole rules match contour detection elsewhere (INP-018). The profile convention of profiles-columns-beams-01 (seen from the member start, x right, y up) is the same as the profiled-wall convention of task 11, so a captured wall section applied as a wall profile reproduces the wall. Capture lives in archicraft-geometry because it needs tessellation and contour detection; the model stays geometry-free (NFR-MNT-002). The clipboard route reuses the payload of selection-transforms-13 instead of a second copy format. Pitfalls: flattened arcs lose smooth flags (tooltip, as for 'Convert to custom'); 2D elements from several views in one selection are refused; duplicate names get a suffix. Pointers: contour.rs (edit-reshape-palette-06), kinds/drafting.rs (drafting-trim-split-03), the shared tessellate(), layer-structures CrossSection, kinds/member.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/profile_capture.rs: two nested closed polylines give one region with one hole; a circle of r = 0.10 m gives a ring of at least 36 segments; a closed chain of four lines and one arc gives one region; three nested rectangles give a region, a hole and an island region; an open chain is refused with the gap position.
- from_wall on the F2 wall gives six regions 120, 60, 180, 10, 300 and 10 mm wide and 3.00 m high with the F2 materials in exterior-to-interior order; on the F1 trapezoidal wall at mid-length the single region is 400 mm wide.
- from_member on an IPE 300 beam gives a profile whose section area equals the beam's within 1e-12; on a column with a stretched custom profile the captured regions equal the resolved instance section.
- from_adjacent_walls on a 0.25 m wall and a touching parallel 0.10 m wall gives two side-by-side regions; on non-touching walls it returns the message.
- egui_kittest: with a wall selected, 'Create profile from selection' adds one profile (undo removes it) and opens the profile dialog on it.
- Copying a closed polyline and a circle inside it in a plan view and pasting them on the profile canvas adds one region with one hole in one UpdateProfile (egui_kittest); a clipboard without 2D shapes leaves 'Paste shapes' disabled with an explanation.
- Satisfies PRF-006 (2D shapes copied from any view, by selection and by clipboard; wall, beam and column sections; adjacent walls).
notes: SRS: PRF-006

title: Write member, solid and terrain openings and place them in plan and 3D
description:
WHY: OPN-012 and BEA-007 openings must round-trip and be placeable: OPN-007 (live preview over the host under the pointer in plan and 3D views), IFX-015 (hosted elements as children of their host) and IFX-036 (an invisible Void child). host-openings-08 restricts conformance to parents of class IfcWall, IfcSlab or IfcRoof, and host-openings-10 finds only walls and slabs as host candidates.

WHAT: IFCX: archicraft::opening placement kinds 'member' (along, across, side) and 'face' (face position in the solid record of free-form-solids-04, origin, rotation; remapped to FaceId on read) under the shared bump rule of 03; the writer emits openings as hosted children of beams, columns, solids and terrain through the framework's contained_children hook (terrain openings under the terrain node at site level); conformance/check.ts accepts parents of class IfcBeam, IfcColumn, IfcMember, IfcFooting, every D.5 class and IfcGeographicElement; the reader's orphan repair covers the new hosts. members_advanced gains a notched beam, a column with a round hole, a solid with a face opening and a small terrain with a pit; golden re-blessed. App: crates/archicraft-app/src/input/host.rs: candidates_in_plan returns beams and columns (plan slice or projection footprint), solids and terrain (outline containment), filtered by HostCapability; candidate_in_3d classifies member side faces by comparing the hit normal with the member frame (HostHit::Member { along, across, side }), solid faces by FaceId (BVH pick of 3d-input-navigation-06 with the face provenance of free-form-solids-03) and terrain tops (Plan). The opening tool's (crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/opening.rs, host-openings-11) automatic orientation becomes perpendicular on member sides and solid faces and vertical on terrain and column tops; previews use the same void_prism path. Out of scope: curved beams (17).
design: One codec and one tool: the new placements are variants, not kinds, so the host-openings writer, reader, tool state machine and preview stay single paths. Face references are positional in files and stable ids in memory, the split free-form-solids-04 uses for vertices. Pitfalls: terrain is site-level, so its openings must not land in a storey; the 3D side classification uses the member frame at the hit station; refresh the BVH after solid edits before picking faces. Pointers: alpha/schema.rs and the opening codec (host-openings-08/09), conformance/check.ts, input/host.rs (host-openings-10), crates/archicraft-app/src/tools/opening.rs (host-openings-11).
acceptance_criteria:
- roundtrip.rs: members_advanced with the four new host cases round-trips with assert_eq; every Void child is an invisible closed mesh of at most 65,535 points; conformance/run.sh passes with the extended parent-class check.
- A file whose face reference points past the solid's face count loads with that opening removed and reported (orphan repair test).
- Unit tests in input/host.rs: a pointer over a beam in plan yields a Member candidate on the Top side; a 3D ray hitting the beam's right face yields side Right with along and across equal to the hit point within 1e-9; a ray on a solid face yields its FaceId.
- egui_kittest: the opening tool over a beam in plan shows the preview and a click creates an opening hosted by the beam in one undo step; with no host under the pointer nothing is created and the status line explains why.
- Satisfies OPN-012 and BEA-007 for persistence and placement (OPN-007 behaviour extended to the new hosts).
notes: SRS: OPN-012 BEA-007

title: Add compound end-cut planes to beams with plan mitre handles
description:
WHY: BEA-003 (S): end cuts shall be definable as arbitrary planes (angles about both cross-section axes), so that a mitre visible in plan needs no 90-degree roll. Status missing (M). profiles-columns-beams-07 offers BeamCut::{Vertical, Horizontal, Angle(f64)} (angle in the vertical plane through the axis), its sweep accepts any CutPlane normal, and -13 maps plan drags to that one angle. BEA-005 joints ('each joint has its own cut plane') reuse the same plane type in tasks 06 and 07.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/member.rs: `CutSpec::{Square, Plane { about_u: f64, about_v: f64 }}` (angles in the member frame after roll: about_v turns the cut about the section's vertical axis, which is the plan mitre of an unrolled beam; about_u tilts it in the vertical plane through the axis), and BeamCut gains `Compound { about_u, about_v }`; validation: each angle within (-85, 85) degrees, the plane at least 5 degrees from parallel to the axis, end planes not crossing at any corner of the rolled section bounds. crates/archicraft-geometry/src/sweep.rs: `cut_plane(frame, &CutSpec, point)` with normal = R_v(about_v) R_u(about_u) d (d = axis direction, mirrored at the start), shared with joints; kinds/beam.rs maps Compound through it. IFCX: startCut/endCut kind 'compound' with aboutU and aboutV (shared bump rule of 03); the columns-and-beams sample gains a mitred beam pair. App: properties fields 'Mitre angle' (about_v) and 'Tilt angle' (about_u) for compound ends; the plan end handle of views/handles.rs (profiles-columns-beams-13) gains a mitre mode (cursor offset perpendicular to the axis at the far section edge gives about_v) with snaps at 0 and +-45 degrees and typed angles; a 'Mitre beams' command sets both ends of two selected beams whose axes meet in plan to the bisector plane in one undo step. Out of scope: segment joints (06, 07), curved beams (17), priority joins (BEA-004, cleanup-and-trims).
design: Angles about the section axes (u right, v up after roll) are what the SRS names; for a level unrolled beam about_v is exactly the plan mitre, so no roll is needed (the BEA-003 rationale). The composition order R_v after R_u is fixed and documented because rotations do not commute. Square (perpendicular to the axis) is the default joint cut for segments; Vertical stays the plumb cut of BEA-002, so existing files are unchanged. The handle mapping is a pure function next to beam_cut_from_plan in views/handles.rs, tested without egui. Pitfalls: on rolled beams about_v is no longer a plan angle (tooltip); the crossing check must use all rolled corners at both ends; the mitre command needs a defined meeting point. Pointers: kinds/member.rs, kinds/beam.rs, sweep.rs, views/handles.rs, ui/properties.rs, samples.rs columns_and_beams.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: two level 0.25 x 0.50 m beams meeting at 90 degrees in plan with Compound { about_u: 0, about_v: +-45 deg } and roll 0 have all end-cap vertices within MODEL_TOLERANCE of the common bisector plane; the kernel intersection volume of the two bodies is 0 and the union volume equals the sum.
- A compound cut with both angles at 20 degrees gives a closed outward body whose cap normal equals R_v R_u d within 1e-12; Vertical, Horizontal and Angle keep their previous meshes bit for bit (regression).
- Validation: 86 degrees and crossing end planes on a short beam are rejected with messages.
- 'Mitre beams' on two beams meeting at 120 degrees in plan sets about_v to +-30 degrees in one undo step; parallel beams are rejected.
- IFCX round trip of the mitred pair (columns-and-beams golden) and conformance green.
- egui_kittest: the properties strip shows 'Mitre angle' for a compound end; editing it issues one command; a pure-function test maps a plan drag to about_v.
- Satisfies BEA-003.
notes: SRS: BEA-003

title: Add segment operations as single undoable commands
description:
WHY: BEA-006 (S): segment operations shall include insert (a copy of the selected segment), remove, reorder, copy and paste segment settings (also between elements), swap start and end sizes, split at a picked point and drag a joint with numeric input. COL-005 refers to the same operations for columns. Status missing (L). The epic acceptance requires segment insert, remove, reorder and split with undo.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs: `Command::EditSegments { element: ElementId, op: SegmentOp }` with `SegmentOp::{Insert { index }, Remove { index }, Move { from, to }, PasteSettings { index, settings: SegmentSettings, with_length: bool }, SwapSizes { index }, Split { index, at }, MoveJoint { joint, station }, Set { index, segment }, SetJoint { joint, cut: CutSpec }}` and labels ('Insert segment', 'Split segment', 'Change joint cut' and so on); plan() builds the new Segments with pure functions in kinds/member.rs (insert_copy, remove, reorder, paste, swap, split, move_joint), validates through validate_element and emits one ReplaceElement (exact undo). Rules: Insert puts a copy after the segment with a Square joint (a fixed copy adds its length, a flexible copy takes the same share); Remove rejects the last segment and the last flexible one; Move keeps joints by position; SegmentSettings = section, material, end size and instances (length only with with_length), and pasting checks the target kind's profile use; SwapSizes swaps start and end size and instances (NoChange for uniform); Split at distance at from the segment start interpolates sizes and offset overrides linearly, splits Fixed L into Fixed at and Fixed L - at and Flexible p into proportional shares so all resolved lengths stay equal at the current total; MoveJoint changes the adjacent lengths (fixed and fixed: both; fixed and flexible: the fixed one; flexible and flexible: shares redistributed); SetJoint replaces the cut plane of one joint (CutSpec of task 05: Square or Plane { about_u, about_v }), the BEA-005 'each joint has its own cut plane' edit, rejected when the new plane crosses a neighbouring joint or end plane inside either adjacent segment. `SegmentSettings::from(&MemberSegment)` feeds the app clipboard. Out of scope: UI (10, 21).
design: One command with an operation enum keeps the Edit set unchanged (ReplaceElement only) and makes every operation one undo step with an exact inverse, following 'Add a command' in docs/implementation-status.md. The pure functions are shared by the command and the app previews (10), so previews equal results. Stations refer to the resolved axis length at command time and are converted into fixed lengths or shares, so later stretching keeps flexible behaviour. Pitfalls: Split and MoveJoint must use the current total, which depends on storey elevations for top-linked columns (resolve through Project::vertical_extent); interpolating instances needs the same offset names at both ends (validated in 01).
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: every SegmentOp executes, undoes to the exact previous project and redoes; invalid indices, removing the last flexible segment and a joint moved beyond its neighbours return Invalid with messages and leave the project unchanged.
- Split of a 4.50 m flexible tapered segment at 1.50 m gives segments resolving to 1.50 and 3.00 m whose joint size equals the original taper at 1.50 m (1e-12); the evaluated body volume is unchanged within 1e-9 (assertion in crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/members.rs).
- MoveJoint between a fixed 0.40 m and a flexible segment to station 0.55 m makes the fixed segment 0.55 m; between two flexible segments it redistributes shares so the joint lands on the requested station.
- PasteSettings of a beam segment with an IPE profile onto a column segment is rejected when the profile lacks the Column flag and accepted otherwise; with_length false keeps the target's length.
- SetJoint with Plane { about_u: 0, about_v: 20 degrees } on joint 1 executes and undoes exactly and the evaluated joint caps of both neighbouring segments lie in that plane; a joint plane that would cross the next joint inside a 0.20 m segment is rejected with a message.
- Satisfies BEA-006 at command level (insert, remove, reorder, copy/paste settings including between elements, swap, split, joint move), the per-joint cut-plane edit of BEA-005 and the operation clause of COL-005.
notes: SRS: BEA-006 COL-005

title: Add the curtain wall tool and properties with the grid editor
description:
WHY: Users must be able to create curtain walls and edit what CW-001 (path, base elevation, height or storey-linked top, boundary placement), CW-002 (distribution mode per axis, individual sizes, locks with at least one flexible column and row) and CW-003/CW-004 (the default frame and panel class assignment chosen from the project's classes) define; the classes themselves are edited in the dialog of task 17. NFR-USE-002 asks for the same input and edit behaviour across element tools, which the point-input service of point-input-snapping provides (the field framework of properties-and-dialogs is used where it has landed; that epic is not a prerequisite, so the existing ui/properties.rs and ui/widgets.rs helpers are the fallback). Gap rows: no curtain wall UI of any kind; the wall tool (views/tools.rs, wall_chain_closes_into_joined_walls) and the wall fields of ui/properties.rs are the templates.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs (or the tool module after point-input-snapping): ToolKind::CurtainWall as a chain tool on the PointInput service: each click adds a path vertex with a rubber-band preview of the path and its boundary frames, Backspace removes the last vertex, double-click or Enter finishes into one Command::AddElements(project.new_curtain_wall(...)) when at least two vertices exist, Esc cancels; Action::ToolCurtainWall in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs (or the command registry of commands-and-l10n where it has landed; that epic is not a prerequisite) without a default key (D.8 does not list curtain walls), with toolbox and Design menu entries in ui/shell.rs. ui/properties.rs: curtain wall fields (base offset, top link, boundary placement, exterior side, default class assignments as choices over the class lists) and derived rows (path length, height, number of frames and panels); a Grid section per axis with the distribution choice, the divisions count and an items table (size, lock, add, remove) whose edits execute EditCurtainGrid ops so overrides are remapped (task 07); the lock of the last flexible item is disabled with the reason. An 'Edit classes...' button in the curtain wall section opens the classes window of task 17. All strings through the string tables of commands-and-l10n where present. Out of scope: the classes dialog (17), edit mode (10), the crossing-order controls (11), panel kind editors (12, 16), arc segment input (15).
design: Follow the 'Add a drawing tool' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md; the chain logic reuses the wall chain's state machine shape (tools.rs wall_chain_closes_into_joined_walls) on the PointInput step/preview API. The preview builds a temporary CurtainWall and its layout (task 04) to draw boundary and division frame positions, not meshes, so it stays within the 50 ms input feedback budget. Grid edits must go through EditCurtainGrid, never a generic element replacement, or overrides would only be pruned instead of remapped. Pitfalls: the items table must not trigger single-key tool shortcuts while typing (UI-008, works_while_typing); class choices must handle a class deleted in the classes window while the properties are shown (re-read the element after every command); widgets::length keeps unit-aware input.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools.rs unit tests without egui: three clicks and Enter create one curtain wall with three vertices and the D.2 defaults; Backspace removes the last vertex; Esc creates nothing; one click and Enter creates nothing.
- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): the toolbox button exists and selects ToolKind::CurtainWall; the Design menu entry does the same.
- kittest: switching the column distribution to Divisions 4 executes one EditCurtainGrid command that undo reverts; the last flexible row's lock is disabled and shows the reason.
- kittest: the 'Edit classes...' button opens the 'Curtain wall classes' window; choosing another default mullion class in properties executes one UpdateElements that undo reverts.
- kittest: editing the base offset and switching the top link to home + 2 executes one UpdateElements each; boundary placement Outside is stored and the derived frame and panel counts update.
- Satisfies the user-interface clauses of CW-001 (path input, base offset, top link, boundary placement) and CW-002 (distribution per axis, individual sizes, locks with one flexible item), and the class-assignment UI of CW-003 and CW-004.

title: Curtain walls
description:
Curtain walls from a base path with grid patterns and distribution modes, frame and panel classes as project resources, an edit mode for per-cell overrides, crossing rules and priorities, symbolic or projected plan display, roof trims, insert and layered panels, and IfcCurtainWall export with IfcMember and IfcPlate children.
