Risks: Override stability across grid edits; cell ids derive from column and row indices with a remap on insert and delete.
design: archicraft-model kinds/curtain_wall.rs with FrameClass and PanelClass resources and a cell override map keyed by stable cell ids; archicraft-geometry frames as profile sweeps along grid lines, panels as thin slabs; PartRef::{Frame, Panel} through the edit mode of selection-transforms; archicraft-ifcx compound children through the parts codec; CW-008 (roof trims, Could) is implemented last through the Trim relation of cleanup-and-trims, applied to frames and panels individually (hence that dependency).
acceptance_criteria: Best-fit distribution ends exactly at each segment end and locked columns keep their size (tests); deleting a division frame merges panels and the override survives a grid edit where the cell still exists; mullions run through and transoms are trimmed by default; the RM-M entrance curtain wall exports IfcCurtainWall with IfcMember and IfcPlate parts (conformance and viewer); a curtain wall trimmed by a roof keeps frames and panels on the trimmed outline.

title: Verify exit criterion: Curtain walls
description:
WHY: The epic is finished only when its exit criterion holds on the integrated workspace: curtain walls with paths, grids and classes (CW-001..CW-004), per-instance overrides in edit mode (CW-005), crossing rules and class priorities (CW-006, CW-011), symbolic and projected plans (CW-007, CW-012), roof trims (CW-008), IFCX export (CW-009) and the Could panel kinds (CW-010) must work together, and the status document must say so.

WHAT: Run the workspace quality gates and the conformance job on all golden files; walk through the exit scenario in the app (draw a three-segment curtain wall, change distribution modes and locks, edit frame and panel classes, enter edit mode, reassign a panel class, delete a division frame, insert a column into the pattern and confirm the override moved with its cell, switch a plan view between symbolic and projected, set class-order crossings, add a layered and a door insert panel, draw a curtain wall with an arc segment, trim a curtain wall by a roof); confirm the RM-M entrance and gable fixtures in the conformance and viewer runs; update docs/implementation-status.md rows CW-001..CW-012 with evidence (file paths and test names), plus the readiness table for increment 3; close the epic in beads and file follow-up beads (path reshaping with override remap, curved glass panels on arc segments, typed insert panels via IFX-050, dragging grid lines in edit mode). No new features.
design: Verification only; no new features. Use the integrated main branch after tasks 01-17 have merged. Evidence comes from the tests named in those tasks (grid.rs property tests, tests/curtain_layout.rs, tests/curtain_overrides.rs, crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_wall.rs and curtain_trim.rs, the round-trip suite and golden files, tools.rs unit tests and the kittests). If a gate fails, reopen the owning task rather than patching here.
acceptance_criteria:
- Best-fit distribution ends exactly at each segment end and locked columns keep their size (tests).
- Deleting a division frame merges panels and the override survives a grid edit where the cell still exists.
- Mullions run through and transoms are trimmed by default.
- The RM-M entrance curtain wall exports IfcCurtainWall with IfcMember and IfcPlate parts (conformance and viewer).
- A curtain wall trimmed by a roof keeps frames and panels on the trimmed outline.
- cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are green.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx is green on every golden file, including curtain-walls.ifcx, rm-m-entrance.ifcx and curtain-wall-gable.ifcx.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (CW-001, CW-002, CW-003, CW-004, CW-005, CW-006, CW-007, CW-008, CW-009, CW-010, CW-011, CW-012) with evidence; any remaining gap has a follow-up bead.
- The epic is closed in beads, with follow-up beads filed for every remaining gap.

title: Trim curtain walls by roofs with frames and panels on the outline
description:
WHY: CW-008 (C): a curtain wall may be trimmed by roofs like other elements (SOL-030), with frames and panels following the trimmed outline. SOL-030 (M) makes selected elements associatively trimmable to roofs, shells or slabs with a keep-side preview; cleanup-and-trims implements it as Relation::Trim { target, tools, keep: KeepSide::{Inside, Outside} } with KindDescriptor flags trim_target and trim_tool (cleanup-and-trims-05), the roof's TrimmingVolume::{Downward, Upward, Finite} solids (SOL-032, cleanup-and-trims-06) and the trims stage trim::apply_trims evaluated through the SolidKernel (cleanup-and-trims-07). Gap row CW-008: no trim relation and no Booleans at gap-analysis time, and the trim must apply to frames and panels individually. The epic acceptance requires that a curtain wall trimmed by a roof keeps frames and panels on the trimmed outline; the epic design notes put this task last.

WHAT: Set KindDescriptor.trim_target for the curtain wall (cleanup-and-trims-05; inclined() stays false), so TrimElements, UntrimElements, the Trim tool with its keep-side preview (cleanup-and-trims-09) and the relation's persistence apply unchanged. Curtain-wall specific trim application in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/curtain/trim.rs: per segment (per straight facet for the arc segments of task 15) transform each trim's keep volume into the SegmentFrame so the glazing plane is z = 0, slice it with slice.rs slice_loops at 0, intersect the loops with the segment's u x v rectangle (geo) to get the trimmed outline; re-run the layout with this clip outline: cells are clipped to it (panels become clipped polygons, cells outside or below a minimum area are dropped), division frame pieces are clipped to it, and new boundary pieces (FrameAxis::Outline keys per outline edge with the role 'Frame_<s>_O<edge>', added to keys.rs and its parser of task 04 so part_ref_for_role and the IFCX part paths stay stable; Boundary class) follow every outline edge that is not part of the original rectangle, swept with mitre cut planes where they meet vertical pieces; finally the generic trims stage (trim::apply_trims, cleanup-and-trims-07) intersects every child part body with the keep volume through the SolidKernel, per part, so sloped roofs leave no frame depth above the roof; because the clipping happens in the generator before that stage, the curtain-wall generator reads the element's Trim relations and the tools' volumes through the EvalContext (extend its neighbour-data slot of element-kind-framework-15 if needed). Kernel failure keeps the last valid body and lists the element (NFR-REL-005). Plan symbols (task 08) and parts follow the clipped layout; overrides of cells that still exist keep applying; insert and component panels in clipped cells are dropped with a reported problem. Out of scope: trims by slabs and shells beyond what the generic stage provides, crop (SOL-033).
design: Two stages on purpose: clipping the layout in the glazing plane is what makes frames and panels follow the outline (new boundary frames along the rake, clipped panels with stable cell keys), while the per-part kernel intersection only removes depth-wise protrusion; trimming the whole compound body with one Boolean would cut through frames and leave no boundary frame along the rake. slice.rs works on any TriMesh, so slicing the transformed keep volume needs no new kernel API. Pitfalls: inclined roofs over segments at an angle give non-axis-aligned outline edges, so outline boundary pieces must accept arbitrary in-plane directions (the sweep frame handles it); a keep volume that misses a segment entirely removes that segment's parts and should report it; the rake boundary pieces need stable keys (outline edge index) or v5 ids churn on every pitch change.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_trim.rs: a curtain wall under the D.2 35-degree gable roof, trimmed downward, has every panel vertex at or below the roof's lower plane within MODEL_TOLERANCE, boundary frame pieces along both rake edges, no vertex of any part above the trim surface, and closed bodies.
- Changing the roof pitch regenerates the trimmed frames and panels in one revision (dirty propagation along the Trim relation); deleting the relation restores the rectangular outline.
- An override on a cell that still exists after trimming keeps applying; a cell removed by the trim drops out of parts() without errors; a clipped insert panel is reported, not generated.
- The plan symbol of the trimmed curtain wall at a cut height above the eaves omits the trimmed-away frames; a test-local trimmed project round-trips with its Trim relation and passes conformance (the golden fixture follows in task 14).
- A forced kernel failure keeps the last valid body and lists the element in the problems panel.
- The Trim tool accepts a selected curtain wall (SOL-030 'like other elements'): a tool-level test issues one TrimElements with the picked roof and keep side Inside, the preview shows the kept part, and UntrimElements restores the rectangular outline in one undo step.
- An arc segment (task 15) under the roof is trimmed facet by facet with closed bodies and boundary pieces along the rake on every facet.
- Satisfies CW-008 (roof trims with frames and panels following the trimmed outline).
notes: SRS: CW-008

title: Add frame and panel class resources with commands and persistence
description:
WHY: CW-003 (S): frame classes shall be named, project-wide definitions with a rectangular section (width, depth, offset to the glazing plane) and a material; the defaults are boundary, corner, mullion and transom, and the boundary and corner classes cannot be removed. CW-004 (S): panel classes shall be named, project-wide definitions of type glass or solid, each with thickness and material. Appendix D.2 sets the curtain wall defaults: frames 0.05 x 0.15 m aluminium, glass panels 0.03 m. SRS 3.4 makes such definitions project resources referenced by stable ID; IFX-060 (M) requires the authoring data to be stored in archicraft:: attributes, IFX-061 declared in the file and IFX-062 versioned. Gap rows CW-003 and CW-004: missing; the Material resource pattern is the template (Command::AddMaterial/UpdateMaterial/DeleteMaterial in crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:78-82 and :234-252, plan_delete_material at :520-552, Edit::InsertMaterial/RemoveMaterial/ReplaceMaterial at :624-626 and :686-709, material records in alpha/writer.rs and alpha/reader.rs), already repeated for profiles by profiles-columns-beams-01/02. Every later task of this epic references the classes by id, so they come first.

WHAT: Add crates/archicraft-model/src/curtain_classes.rs (exported from lib.rs) with FrameClassId and PanelClassId (one id_type! line each in ids.rs). `FrameClass { id, name, fixed: Option<FixedFrameRole>, width, depth, glazing_offset, material }` with `FixedFrameRole { Boundary, Corner }`; `PanelClass { id, name, kind: PanelKind, thickness, material }` with `PanelKind { Glass, Solid }` (#[non_exhaustive], code/from_code/label/ALL; tasks 12 and 16 add the Could kinds). `Project.frame_classes` and `Project.panel_classes` (#[serde(default)]) with frame_class(id)/panel_class(id). validate.rs: validate_frame_class and validate_panel_class (width 0.01-1.00 m, depth 0.01-2.00 m, glazing_offset within [0, depth], thickness 0.001-0.50 m, material exists, names non-empty and unique per list). command.rs: Command::{AddFrameClass, UpdateFrameClass, DeleteFrameClass { class, replacement: Option<FrameClassId> }, AddPanelClass, UpdatePanelClass, DeletePanelClass { class, replacement: Option<PanelClassId> }} with labels, and Edit::{InsertFrameClass, RemoveFrameClass, ReplaceFrameClass, InsertPanelClass, RemovePanelClass, ReplacePanelClass} with exact inverses. Deleting a class with a fixed role is CommandError::Invalid ('The boundary frame class cannot be removed.'); UpdateFrameClass cannot set, clear or change `fixed`; deleting the last panel class is refused; deleting a class in use needs a replacement (users are found and re-pointed through two new Kind hooks that mirror profiles-columns-beams-01's Kind::profiles()/replace_profile(): `curtain_classes() -> CurtainClassRefs { frames, panels }` with an empty default and `replace_curtain_class(from: CurtainClassRef, to: CurtainClassRef) -> bool` with a no-op default, CurtainClassRef::{Frame(FrameClassId), Panel(PanelClassId)}, so the kind of task 03 plugs in without kind code in command.rs) and re-points them with ReplaceElement edits in the same undo step; Edit::apply records the frame- and panel-class edits as changed resource ids in Project.changes (the ChangeLog of element-kind-framework-10), which task 05 turns into dirty curtain walls; plan_delete_material also reassigns class materials with Replace edits; integrity_problems reports dangling class materials and a missing fixed Boundary or Corner class. template.rs: frame classes Boundary (fixed), Corner (fixed), Mullion and Transom, each 0.05 x 0.15 m aluminium with glazing_offset 0.075 m, and panel classes 'Glass panel' (glass, 0.03 m) and 'Solid panel' (aluminium, 0.03 m), with deterministic template ids that New remaps (IFX-011). IFCX: frameClasses and panelClasses arrays in archicraft::project (schema.rs declaration from the model's ALL arrays, writer.rs project_attribute after the profiles array, always present; reader.rs read_curtain_classes: an invalid record is skipped with an error, an unknown material repaired to the first material with a warning, a missing fixed Boundary or Corner class recreated from the D.2 values with a warning); bump FORMAT_VERSION with a no-op step in the framework's migration table ('adds curtain wall classes'); re-bless the golden files. Out of scope: the curtain wall kind (03), crossing order (11), layered panels (12), insert and component panels (16), every UI (the classes dialog is task 17).
design: Follow the 'Add a command' and 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipes in docs/implementation-status.md (Extension points) and mirror Material and Profile: Vec storage, Insert/Remove/Replace edits returning exact inverses via std::mem::replace, delete-with-replacement planning like plan_delete_material. Protection is a stored role, not a name match, so renaming 'Boundary' keeps it undeletable and a duplicated boundary class is an ordinary, deletable class. Section conventions documented on FrameClass: width is the face width measured in the glazing plane along the curtain wall surface, depth is measured perpendicular to the glazing plane, glazing_offset is the distance from the frame's exterior face to the glazing plane (0.075 m centres the glazing in a 0.15 m frame). Classes live inside archicraft::project like profiles (authoring data without a counterpart in the pinned ifc@v5a schema), with ids as UUID strings and parameters at full precision (float_roundtrip). Pitfalls: Project derives PartialEq, so keep both vectors in model order and compare in round-trip tests; member order must stay stable for byte-identical output (IFX-007); the FORMAT_VERSION bump follows the rule documented in alpha/mod.rs (whichever epic lands second rebases its number and adds its own step); the reader repair of fixed classes must run before any curtain wall is read, because task 03's codec resolves class references; keep kind-specific code out of command.rs so the framework's module-layout test stays green.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs (or a new tests/curtain_classes.rs): add, update and delete of frame and panel classes followed by undo restore the starting project exactly; an invalid command leaves the project untouched.
- Deleting the Boundary or Corner class is refused with CommandError::Invalid and the user-facing message; deleting Mullion without a replacement while a user exists (test-kinds dummy implementing curtain_classes()) is refused naming the user count, and with a replacement re-points the user in one undo step; deleting the last panel class is refused.
- Deleting the Aluminium material with Steel as replacement reassigns the four default frame classes and 'Solid panel'; integrity_problems reports a class with a dangling material.
- Validation rejects width 0, depth 3 m, a glazing offset larger than the depth, thickness 0 and duplicate names, each with a message.
- Template test: a new project has exactly the four D.2 frame classes (0.05 x 0.15 m aluminium, Boundary and Corner fixed) and the two panel classes of 0.03 m, with fresh UUIDs after New.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: round_trip_restores_the_editable_model and golden_files_are_reproduced pass with the classes; a FORMAT_VERSION n-1 file migrates and receives the fixed classes with a warning; a reader test drops an invalid class and repairs an unknown material; conformance/run.sh passes on all re-blessed golden files.
- Satisfies the data and persistence clauses of CW-003 (named sections with material, four defaults, boundary and corner not removable) and CW-004 (glass or solid with thickness and material); the dialog follows in task 17.
notes:
SRS: CW-003 CW-004
Appendix D.2: frames 0.05 x 0.15 m aluminium; glass panels 0.03 m. Assumptions to confirm: glazing offset 0.075 m (centred) and a 'Solid panel' default (aluminium, 0.03 m) are not stated in the SRS.

title: Derive the curtain wall layout, stable part keys and crossing rule
description:
WHY: CW-006 (S): where frames cross, mullions shall run through and transoms shall be trimmed by default. CW-005 (S) needs individually selectable frames and panels whose overrides survive later grid edits where the cell still exists; the epic risk states that cell ids derive from column and row indices with a remap on insert and delete. SEL-008 (M) gives compound elements an edit mode with selectable frames and panels through the kind-registered PartRef of selection-transforms-01, which reserved Frame and Panel variants for this kind. IFX-016 and IFX-010 write each part as a child node with a v5 id derived from its owner and role, so roles must be stable strings built from the same keys. CW-001 decides where boundary frames sit (inside, centred on or outside the outline). Gap rows: CW-005 needs part addressing stable across grid edits, CW-006 'belongs in the frame generator'; putting the topology in the headless model lets parts(), selection, plan symbols and geometry share one layout.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/curtain_wall/{keys.rs,layout.rs} (pure, no geometry dependency). Keys: `CellId { segment: u16, col: u32, row: u32 }` and `FrameKey { segment: u16, axis: FrameAxis { Vertical, Horizontal }, line: u32, span: u32 }` with role() strings 'Panel_<s>_<c>_<r>' and 'Frame_<s>_V<line>_<span>' / 'Frame_<s>_H<line>_<span>' and a parser back. `CurtainWall::layout(&self, height) -> Result<CurtainLayout, LayoutError>`: per segment the column cells from columns.distribute(segment length) and the row cells from rows.distribute(height); `FramePiece { key, role: FrameRole { Boundary, Corner, Mullion, Transom }, class, from_uv, to_uv, start: PieceEnd, end: PieceEnd }` with `PieceEnd { Node, Face(f64), Mitre(DVec2) }`: one vertical piece per (line, row span) and one horizontal piece per (line, column span); vertical lines at the path ends are Boundary, at interior path vertices one Corner line keyed on the segment that ends there (the next segment's line 0 is omitted), horizontal lines 0 and m are Boundary, all others Mullion or Transom. Crossing resolution at every grid node through rank(role, axis): Corner > Boundary > Mullion > Transom, ties to the vertical piece; the winner's pieces meet at the node centre (continuous through it), the loser's pieces end at the winner's face (PieceEnd::Face with half the winner's class width), horizontal pieces at path vertices end with a Mitre against the corner frame. Boundary placement offsets boundary axes towards the inside of the outline by +w/2 (Inside), 0 (Centred) or -w/2 (Outside). `PanelPiece { key: CellId, cells: Vec<CellId>, class }`, one per cell (groups arrive with overrides in task 07). Kind hooks: parts() returns PartSpec { role, class IfcMember for frames and IfcPlate for panels, label 'Mullion 2, row 1' / 'Panel C3-R2' } in a stable order (segment, frames by key, panels by key), extended with the framework's part context (home elevation and &StoreyList) if parts() lacks it; the associated `type Part = CurtainWallPart { Frame(FrameKey), Panel(CellId) }` (folded into KindPart by the kinds! macro, selection-transforms-01); part_refs() (every frame and panel key in parts() order, so selection-transforms-08's edit mode can be entered), part_ref_for_role(role) (parses 'Frame_...' and 'Panel_...' roles back to CurtainWallPart for the 3D id buffer of selection-transforms-06), part_label, part_anchor, part_outline (the frame piece's plan rectangle at its glazing-plane offset, the panel's glazing-plane line) and validate_part (key present in the current layout). Out of scope: bodies (05), overrides and merged panels (07), the class-order option (11), edit-mode UI (10).
design: The layout is the single source for parts(), plan symbols (08), bodies (05) and selection, so it lives in the model and stays pure f64 with no geo dependency. Pieces are split at every crossing so each span is individually selectable (CW-005 deletes one span of a division frame and merges exactly two panels); 'runs through' means the winner owns the crossing node, which keeps keys stable regardless of the rule and lets task 11 swap the rank function. Part counts stay bounded: a 20 m two-storey entrance with 14 columns and 3 rows has about 100 parts; add LayoutError::TooManyParts above 10,000 parts per element to protect IFCX size. Corner keys are canonical on the segment that ends at the vertex, so inserting a segment later only shifts segment indices (path reshaping is out of scope; note it in a follow-up bead). Pitfalls: u16 segment indices cap paths at 65,535 segments (validate far below); horizontal pieces at a path vertex must use the mitre so the two segments' frames meet without overlap; the rank function must be total and deterministic (ties to vertical) or the property tests of later tasks flake.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/curtain_layout.rs: a 4.50 x 3.00 m single segment with columns [1.50] BestFit and rows [1.00 locked, flexible] yields 3 x 2 cells, 2 boundary vertical lines x 2 spans, 2 mullion lines x 2 spans, 2 boundary horizontal lines x 3 spans and 1 transom line x 3 spans.
- CW-006 topology: the lower mullion piece's to_uv equals the upper piece's from_uv at the transom node, transom pieces end with PieceEnd::Face(0.025) at the mullion faces, and boundary pieces win over mullions and transoms at the outline.
- An L-shaped path produces one Corner piece per row span at the interior vertex, mitred horizontal pieces on both sides and no duplicated vertical line.
- Boundary placement Inside, Centred and Outside shift the boundary axes by +0.025, 0 and -0.025 m for the D.2 class.
- Every key's role string parses back to the same key; keys are unchanged after a size-only edit (a longer path in BestFit with the same column count).
- parts() is deterministic across evaluations and its count matches the layout; selection-transforms' module-layout test shows the CurtainWallPart variants were added without touching selection code; Selection::retain_valid drops a part whose key vanished after a grid edit; part_ref_for_role maps every PartSpec role back to its CurtainWallPart and part_refs() lists exactly the parts() roles.
- Per-segment best fit (epic acceptance): a three-segment path of 4.20, 6.00 and 2.70 m with columns [1.50 flexible, 0.30 locked] BestFit has the last vertical line of every segment exactly at u = segment length (assert_eq on f64) and every locked column exactly 0.30 m wide on every segment.
- Satisfies the default crossing rule of CW-006 at topology level and the stable addressing required by CW-005 and SEL-008 for curtain walls.
notes: SRS: CW-006 CW-005 CW-001

title: Register the curtain wall kind with path, height and grid
description:
WHY: CW-001 (S): the system shall provide a curtain wall defined by a base path in plan (straight segments; arcs C), a base elevation and a height or storey-linked top (ELM-006); boundary frames are placed inside, centred on or outside the path. CW-002 (S) attaches a column and a row pattern to each curtain wall. ELM-006 (M): the top of curtain walls is a fixed height or linked to a storey plus an offset, and linked elements follow storey changes; ELM-011 (M) defaults the IFC class from the kind (Table 5-1: IfcCurtainWall); IFX-060 (M) stores the parameters in archicraft:: attributes. Gap row CW-001: missing (no curtain wall kind; TopLink exists at crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:71, BodyPart lists per element at crates/archicraft-geometry/src/evaluate.rs:22-28). The element-kind-framework registry requires a geometry generator and an IFCX codec for every kind, so the kind lands in all three crates at once; real bodies follow in task 05.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/curtain_wall/mod.rs: `CurtainWall { path: Vec<DVec2>, link: VerticalLink, boundary: BoundaryPlacement, exterior: Side, columns: GridAxis, rows: GridAxis, classes: ClassAssignment }` with `BoundaryPlacement { Inside, Centred, Outside }`, `Side { Right, Left }` (Right = the wall convention of ReferenceLine::face_offsets, element.rs:94-106) and `ClassAssignment { boundary, corner, mullion, transom: FrameClassId, panel: PanelClassId }`; VerticalLink is element-kind-framework-02's shared base offset plus TopLink. Kind impl through one kinds! line: descriptor { label 'Curtain wall', code 'curtain_wall', prefix 'CW', default IfcCurtainWall, classes [IfcCurtainWall], has_tool, part_roles ['Frame', 'Panel'], default display range Intersecting where plan-views-browser-01's descriptor fields exist }; validate (at least two path points, each segment longer than twice the widest boundary or corner class width plus MIN_CELL, no self-intersection, vertex angles between 10 and 350 degrees, height >= 0.10 m, both grids valid and distributable on every segment length and on the resolved height, all class references existing); vertical_extent, storey_links, rehome and relink through VerticalLink; transform hook (selection-transforms-02): Move and Rotate act on the path and base offset, Mirror reflects the path keeping the vertex order and toggles `exterior`, Scale scales the path and keeps class sections with a NotScaled note, tilted rotation is Unsupported ('Curtain walls can only be rotated about a vertical axis.'), declared in KindDescriptor.transforms (TransformSupport of selection-transforms-02) so the UI pre-check and the agreement test cover it; curtain_classes() returns the assigned ids (task 01's replacement and the dirty set). material() has no element material (frames and panels take class materials). Per-kind defaults slot (element-kind-framework-04) CurtainWallDefaults filled in template.rs: columns [1.50 flexible] BestFit, rows [3.00 flexible] BestFit, boundary Inside, exterior Right, top linked to home + 1 with offset 0, the four default frame classes and 'Glass panel'; Project::new_curtain_wall(storey, path). Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/curtain_wall.rs registered with an interim generator, the path's envelope prism (deepest assigned frame class x height) as one closed Body, replaced in task 05. IFCX: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/kinds/curtain_wall.rs codec `archicraft::curtainWall` { path: array(point2), baseOffset, top, boundary, exterior, columns and rows: { distribution, divisions, items: array({ size, locked }) }, classes: { boundary, corner, mullion, transom, panel } } plus the defaults slot; lenient reading: an unknown class id falls back to the class with the same fixed role or the first class with a warning, an undistributable grid to the D.2 grid with a warning, fewer than two path points skip the element with an error. Rides on task 01's FORMAT_VERSION bump. Out of scope: layout and part keys (04), bodies (05), parts in IFCX (06), overrides (07), arc segments (the C clause of CW-001, task 15, which adds a sparse per-segment arc map without changing `path`) and path reshaping.
design: The path's vertex order defines the u direction of every segment and therefore where each column pattern starts; Mirror must keep that order (reversing it would move the pattern origin and scramble cell ids), so the reflection's orientation change is absorbed by toggling `exterior`. Height comes from VerticalLink resolved against &StoreyList, which is why validate needs the storey context of the framework's validate hook; the 'distributable' check calls grid.rs distribute() on every segment length and the resolved height. Defaults mirror the wall row of D.2 for the top because D.2 gives no curtain-wall top. The codec writes parameters at full precision and enumerations from the model ALL arrays; member order is fixed for byte-identical output. Pitfalls: the framework's material() hook may require a MaterialId — if so, change it to Option (stairs and railings need the same) rather than inventing a curtain wall material; the counters map gains the 'CW' key only when a curtain wall exists (codec rule of element-kind-framework-06), so existing golden files stay byte-identical; prefix 'CW' must not collide with other kinds' prefixes (registry test). Pointers: kinds/mod.rs and kinds/wall.rs after element-kind-framework, validate.rs:243, template.rs, alpha/kinds/wall.rs.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: AddElements with a three-segment curtain wall, undo and redo restore the project; the registry-iterating transform test of selection-transforms covers Move, Rotate, Mirror, Scale and copies for the curtain wall; Mirror keeps the vertex order and toggles exterior; a tilted rotation is refused with the kind-named message.
- Validation tests reject a zero-length segment, a self-intersecting path, a 5-degree vertex, a height of 0.05 m, an all-locked row pattern and an unknown class id, each with a user-facing message.
- ELM-006: a curtain wall linked to home + 1 follows a storey elevation change (vertical_extent test); a storey edit that would invert it (top below base) is rejected by element-kind-framework-09's validate_storey_change naming the curtain wall, while an edit that only makes its locked rows exceed the new height is accepted and leaves the curtain wall to the fallback and problems path of task 05.
- Template test: the curtain wall defaults slot holds the D.2 grid 1.50 x 3.00 m, boundary Inside and the default classes.
- crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs: a test-local project with a three-segment curtain wall round-trips equal (written_files_validate_without_problems, round_trip_restores_the_editable_model); reader tests cover the unknown-class, bad-grid and short-path repairs.
- The framework module-layout test confirms that only the kind modules and one registry line per crate changed; the interim body passes check_closed.
- Satisfies CW-001 (straight-segment path, base elevation, height or storey-linked top, boundary placement stored) and the per-element storage of CW-002.
notes:
SRS: CW-001 CW-002
D.2: grid 1.50 x 3.00 m. Open question: default top (home + 1, as for walls) and boundary placement Inside are assumptions.

title: Draw curtain walls symbolically or projected in plan per view
description:
WHY: CW-007 (S): in plan, curtain walls shall be drawn symbolically by default (frames as rectangles, panels as lines). CW-012 (C): curtain walls may be drawn projected in plan. Gap rows: CW-007 missing (PlanElement had no symbol layer, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs:23-33; host-openings-07 adds PlanElement.symbols with symbol and line classes); CW-012 missing although projected drawing of bodies exists generically (up_facing_outline, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:196; classification at plan.rs:143) because no per-view switch exists. VIEW-010 (M) classifies cut, projected and overhead parts within the view range and ELM-018 (M) gives each kind plan display options. Symbolic output must stay pickable and snappable like other plan geometry.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/plan.rs: SymbolClass gains CurtainFrame and CurtainPanel. For a curtain wall whose vertical extent contains the effective cut height: every vertical frame piece (boundary, corner, mullion) whose v range contains the cut contributes its plan rectangle (the mitred polygon for corners) as a closed segment loop in the Cut line class; every panel piece whose v range contains the cut contributes one segment on the glazing plane between the adjacent frame faces (merged panels one segment); a horizontal piece within half its width of the cut height contributes its rectangle. Curtain walls outside the cut contribute the outer outline of their frames in the Projected or Overhead class according to the view range (VIEW-010) and the element's plan display option (ELM-018). Symbol segments are part of PlanElement::segments(), so they are pickable and snappable; cut regions stay empty in symbolic mode. Mode: `CurtainWallPlanMode { Symbolic, Projected }` in PlanOptions (the plan cache key of plan-views-browser-03; extend the plan function's options if that type is absent); Projected bypasses the symbol path and uses the generic slicing of the child bodies (cut regions by material, projected and overhead lines). App: PlanViewState.curtain_walls (default Symbolic), a View menu item and a plan context-menu entry 'Curtain walls: symbolic / projected' for the active plan view, drawn in draw_plan (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/plan.rs) with the existing line weights; Document::plan includes the mode in its cache key; where plan-views-browser-07 exists the mode is an optional field of the plan section of ViewDefinition and of its IFCX record, so saved views keep it. Out of scope: pens and line weights (plan-renderer), insert-panel symbols (16), arc facets (15), trimmed outlines (13).
design: Follow the 'Add a plan-view overlay or line class' extension point: data in geometry plan.rs, painting in the app's draw_plan. The symbol generator reads the model layout (task 04) plus the frame footprints already computed for the bodies, not the meshes, so symbols are exact and cheap; the projected mode is the generic pipeline and needs no curtain-wall code. Panel lines sit on the glazing plane, not on the panel faces, which is what 'panels as lines' asks for. The cut height is relative to the curtain wall's home storey elevation when the element is drawn on another storey (where plan-views-browser-03's remote-storey drawing exists it shifts by dz; meshes are storey-local; plan-views-browser is not a prerequisite of this epic). Pitfalls: PlanOptions must stay Copy + Eq + Hash (enum, no floats); remote-storey drawing applies the remote style to symbols too; do not merge curtain-wall symbol rectangles into the same-material cut regions, or the symbolic look is lost.
acceptance_criteria:
- Plan tests in crates/archicraft-geometry: the symbolic plan of the D.2 4.50 m wall cut at 1.10 m has four 0.05 x 0.15 m frame rectangles (two boundary, two mullions) and three panel segments on the glazing plane.
- With the mullion span between C0-R0 and C1-R0 removed (task 07) the plan has three rectangles and two panel segments; the L-shaped sample shows a mitred corner polygon.
- A curtain wall entirely below the cut plane is drawn as a projected outline and one entirely above as overhead; CutOnly suppresses both.
- Projected mode yields aluminium and glass cut regions and no curtain-wall symbols.
- Picking a panel segment in plan selects the curtain wall; snapping finds the frame rectangle corners.
- kittest: the View menu entry toggles PlanViewState.curtain_walls and the document's plan cache key changes; if saved views exist, the mode survives save and reopen of a saved plan view.
- Default (CW-007 'by default'): a fresh PlanViewState and a newly opened plan view draw curtain walls symbolically without any setting.
- Satisfies CW-007 (symbolic default) and CW-012 (projected per view).
notes: SRS: CW-007 CW-012

title: Add the grid pattern solver with distribution modes and locks
description:
WHY: CW-002 (S): the grid pattern shall consist of columns and rows with individual sizes and a distribution mode per axis: fixed sizes, best fit (the pattern ends exactly at the segment end) or number of divisions; in the flexible modes each column and row has a lock, and at least one column and one row must remain flexible. The epic acceptance requires tests that best-fit distribution ends exactly at each segment end and that locked columns keep their size. Gap row CW-002: missing, no grid model; validation is expected in Command::plan through validate_element (crates/archicraft-model/src/validate.rs:243). The epic risk (overrides surviving grid edits, cell ids derived from column and row indices with a remap on insert and delete) depends on the solver telling which pattern repeat and item every cell came from. A pure solver without geometry or UI dependencies is the base for the kind (03), the layout (04), the override remap (07) and the grid editor (09), and it can start in parallel with task 01.

WHAT: New module crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/curtain_wall/grid.rs (the directory module is created here; the kind itself follows in task 03): `GridItem { size: f64, locked: bool }`; `Distribution { Fixed, BestFit, Divisions { count: u16 } }` with code/from_code/label/ALL; `GridAxis { distribution, items: Vec<GridItem> }` with validate(axis_label) (at least one item, sizes within [MIN_CELL, 100 m], count 1-999, at least one unlocked item in BestFit and Divisions: 'At least one column must stay flexible.' / '... row ...'); `distribute(&self, length) -> Result<Vec<GridCell>, GridError>` with `GridCell { start, size, repeat: u32, item: u32 }` and `GridError::{LockedExceedLength, CellTooSmall, Invalid}` with user-facing Display. Fixed: the pattern repeats from 0 and the last cell is the remainder; a remainder below MIN_CELL is added to the previous cell so no sliver panel appears; locks are stored but ignored. BestFit: n = max(1, round(length / pattern length)) repeats, flexible sizes scaled by s = (length - n*locked) / (n*flexible); if any scaled flexible cell falls below MIN_CELL, n is reduced towards 1, otherwise LockedExceedLength or CellTooSmall. Divisions: n = count with the same scaling and errors. `GridOp { SetDistribution(Distribution), SetItem { index, item }, InsertItem { index, item }, RemoveItem { index } }` with `GridAxis::apply(&GridOp) -> Result<GridAxis, GridError>`, and `remap_cells(old: &[GridCell], new: &[GridCell], op: &GridOp) -> Vec<Option<u32>>` mapping each old flat cell index to its new flat index through (repeat, item): items before an insertion keep their item index, later ones shift by one, the removed item maps to None, and cells whose repeat no longer exists map to None. Out of scope: the curtain wall kind and per-segment application (03, 04), override storage (07), UI (09).
design: Pure f64 arithmetic: starts are accumulated by summation and the final boundary is assigned `length` exactly; the rounding residue of the scaling goes to the last flexible cell, so locked sizes are copied, never recomputed (bit-identical). Rounding of n uses f64::round on length / pattern length with ties away from zero; document it, because users see the column count jump at half-pattern lengths. Keeping (repeat, item) per cell is what makes the remap deterministic: flat indices (used in keys, task 04) are recomputed from the new cell list, while identity is carried by (repeat, item). Columns are distributed per straight segment from the segment start (task 04), rows over the curtain wall height; the same type serves both. Pitfalls: guard against NaN and infinite lengths (reject before solving); cap the number of cells per axis (e.g. 2,000) with GridError::Invalid so a 1 mm pattern on a 60 m path cannot create millions of parts; the error messages take the axis label so properties (09) can show them verbatim.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit and property tests in grid.rs (proptest added as a dev-dependency of archicraft-model if not yet present; MIT/Apache-2.0 per deny.toml): for lengths 0.30-60.00 m and random patterns of 1-5 items with random locks and at least one flexible item, BestFit and Divisions return cells whose last end equals `length` exactly (assert_eq on f64), starts strictly increasing and every size >= MIN_CELL, or a GridError.
- locked_items_keep_their_size: in BestFit and Divisions every locked cell's size is bit-identical to its item size.
- Fixed mode: 7.00 m with [1.50] gives 4 x 1.50 + 1.00; 6.02 m gives 3 x 1.50 + 1.52 (sliver merged into the previous cell).
- Divisions 4 over 6.00 m with [1.00 locked, 1.00 flexible] gives repeats of 1.00 + 0.50; a pattern whose locked total exceeds the length returns LockedExceedLength.
- validate() rejects an all-locked BestFit axis with 'At least one column must stay flexible.' (and the row variant), size 0, count 0 and an empty pattern.
- remap_cells: InsertItem at index 1 into [a, b] maps (r, 0) to (r, 0) and (r, 1) to (r, 2); RemoveItem 0 maps (r, 0) to None; a shorter BestFit length that drops a repeat maps that repeat's cells to None; SetItem and SetDistribution keep (repeat, item).
- cargo test -p archicraft-model is green and archicraft-model gains no geometry or UI dependency.
- Satisfies the distribution-mode and lock clauses of CW-002 at model level (per-segment use in 04, editor in 09).
notes:
SRS: CW-002
Open question: MIN_CELL proposed as 0.05 m (one D.2 frame width); not stated in the SRS.

title: Follow arc segments in curtain wall paths with facetted panels
description:
WHY: CW-001 (S) defines the base path as 'straight segments; arcs C', so arc segments are a Could clause of a Should requirement; tasks 03-09 deliver straight segments only. Gap row CW-001: missing. curved-geometry (increment 2) adds exact arcs for walls and outlines (curved-geometry-01: EdgeShape::Arc(ArcEdge { centre, radius, ccw }); curved-geometry-03: the circle-anchored tessellate()), but it is not a prerequisite of this epic and has nothing for curtain walls. The epic acceptance requires best-fit columns to end exactly at each segment end, which must hold along an arc as well; overrides (task 07) must keep working.

WHAT: Model (crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/curtain_wall/path.rs, new): CurtainWall gains `arcs: BTreeMap<u16, SegmentArc>` (#[serde(default)], sparse, keyed by segment index, so straight curtain walls and their files are unchanged) with `SegmentArc { sagitta: f64 }` (signed, positive bulging to the left of the segment direction, 0 < |sagitta| <= half the chord, at most a semicircle) and helpers arc_length, point_at(s), tangent_at(s) and centre/radius; conversions to and from curved-geometry-01's ArcEdge where that type exists. validate: sagitta range, radius at least the deepest assigned frame depth, every column cell's chord at least MIN_CELL plus the widest frame width, the 10-350 degree vertex rule measured on the adjacent facet chords. Layout (layout.rs): an arc segment distributes its columns over the arc length with grid.rs distribute(), so BestFit ends exactly at the segment end; every column grid point lies on the arc; vertical frame pieces stand at the grid points with their depth along the bisector of the adjacent chords; horizontal frame pieces and panels are straight facets on the chords between adjacent grid points (flat panels, the usual construction for curved unitised façades) and meet at the mullions with PieceEnd::Mitre; keys and roles are unchanged ((segment, col, row) and line/span). Transforms (selection-transforms-02 hook of task 03): Move and Rotate keep the sagitta, Mirror negates it (the vertex order stays as in task 03), uniform Scale scales it, non-uniform Scale of a curtain wall with arcs is Unsupported ('Curtain walls with arc segments can only be scaled uniformly.'). Geometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/curtain/): one SegmentFrame per facet so frame.rs and panel.rs of task 05 run unchanged per facet; corner frames at a vertex between an arc and a straight segment mitre against the adjacent facet chord. Plan (task 08): mullion rectangles rotated to the bisector and one panel line per facet in symbolic mode; projected mode is generic. IFCX: optional `arcs: array({ segment, sagitta })` in archicraft::curtainWall, absent for straight walls (optional addition, no format bump); the reader straightens an invalid arc with a warning. App: the curtain wall tool of task 09 gains an 'Arc segment' toggle in its prompt bar: with it on, the next segment takes a point on the arc before its end vertex, with a rubber-band preview of the arc and its facets; properties list each segment with its length and a 'Sagitta' length field (0 = straight) executing UpdateElements (overrides of cells that disappear are pruned by task 07's normalising validate). Out of scope: curved (bent) glass panels and curved horizontal frames (follow-up bead), full circles, trims (task 13 handles arc segments facet by facet).
design: A sparse arc map keyed by segment index keeps `path` and every straight-wall code path untouched, needs no format bump and makes arcs opt-in per segment; the signed sagitta is transform-friendly (only Mirror and Scale change it) and has no centre point that could drift from the vertices. Facets reuse the straight-segment machinery: the layout produces chord-aligned pieces, so sweep(), extrude(), the panel subtraction, plan symbols and IFCX parts need no arc code, and mitre ends at mullions already exist for path vertices. Distributing over the arc length (not the chord) is what the SRS best-fit clause means on a curved segment. Pitfalls: point_at must be computed from the segment start angle with one formula for all grid points so the end point is assigned exactly (no accumulated drift); a bisector at the first and last grid point of an arc next to a straight segment is the corner frame's mitre plane; the vertex-angle rule must use facet chords, otherwise a tight arc next to a straight segment slips through validation; reuse curved-geometry's helpers where they have landed instead of a second arc implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/curtain_layout.rs: a single 90-degree arc segment of radius 6.00 m with columns [1.50 flexible] BestFit has 6 columns over the 9.42 m arc length, the last grid point exactly at the end vertex and every grid point on the arc within MODEL_TOLERANCE; a straight-arc-straight path keeps every key's role parseable and unchanged after a sagitta edit that keeps the column count.
- Validation rejects a sagitta larger than half the chord and a radius smaller than the deepest frame depth, each with a user-facing message.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_wall.rs: the arc wall and the straight-arc-straight path produce closed bodies with positive volume, planar panels on the facet chords ending at the frame faces, and no overlap between adjacent facets' horizontal frames at the mitres.
- Plan: the symbolic plan of the arc wall at 1.10 m shows rotated mullion rectangles and one panel line per facet.
- Transforms: Mirror negates the sagitta and keeps the vertex order; uniform Scale scales it; non-uniform Scale is refused with the kind-named message.
- Round trip: an arc curtain wall round-trips equal; the existing golden files, including curtain-walls.ifcx, are reproduced byte-identically; an invalid arc is straightened with a warning.
- tools.rs unit test: with the arc toggle on, start, arc point and end clicks create one arc segment with the expected sagitta; kittest: editing a segment's sagitta in properties executes one UpdateElements that undo reverts.
- Satisfies the arc clause (C) of CW-001.
notes:
SRS: CW-001
Arc clause (C) of CW-001. Decision to confirm: flat panels on the facet chords (no bent glass).

title: Add the curtain wall classes dialog for frame and panel classes
description:
WHY: CW-003 (S): frame classes are named, project-wide definitions with a rectangular section (width, depth, offset to the glazing plane) and a material, the defaults are boundary, corner, mullion and transom, and the boundary and corner classes cannot be removed. CW-004 (S): panel classes are named, project-wide definitions of type glass or solid with thickness and material. Task 01 delivers the resources, commands and persistence; users need a place to edit them. Gap rows CW-003 and CW-004: missing; the materials dialog (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs:376 materials_window and material_editor at :765) is the template for a resource dialog. Split out of task 09 so the dialog can be built as soon as the kind exists (task 03) and so tasks 11, 12 and 16 extend one dialog.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/dialogs.rs: Dialogs gains a `curtain_classes` flag and `fn curtain_classes_window(&mut self, ctx, ws)` following materials_window: a frame class table (name, width, depth, glazing offset through widgets::length, material choice) and a panel class table (name, type choice from PanelKind::ALL, thickness, material), each field edit executing exactly one UpdateFrameClass or UpdatePanelClass; Add (D.2 values), Duplicate and Delete; Delete of a class in use (counted through Kind::curtain_classes of task 01) opens a replacement picker and executes DeleteFrameClass or DeletePanelClass with the replacement; Delete is disabled for classes with a fixed role, with the tooltip 'The boundary frame class cannot be removed.' or 'The corner frame class cannot be removed.', and for the last panel class with its reason; validation messages of task 01 are shown inline and the project stays unchanged. Action::CurtainWallClasses in crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/actions.rs (label, no shortcut) handled in ArchiCraftApp::run (app.rs:377) by setting the flag, and a 'Curtain wall classes...' item in the Project menu of ui/shell.rs; strings through the string tables of commands-and-l10n where present. Out of scope: the button in curtain wall properties (09), Move up/Move down for class order (11), layered, insert and component panel editors (12, 16).
design: Follow the 'Add a dialog' extension point in docs/implementation-status.md (Dialogs flag, window function, Action and menu item, kittest by label) and mirror materials_window/material_editor so the resource dialogs look and behave alike. Protection follows the stored fixed role of task 01, never the name. Pitfalls: field edits must commit once per change (on focus loss or Enter), not every frame, or the undo history fills with partial values; widgets::length keeps unit-aware input; the replacement picker must not offer the class being deleted; a class deleted by undo while the window shows it must not panic (re-read the project every frame).
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest (crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs): the Project menu item opens the 'Curtain wall classes' window; Add frame class executes one AddFrameClass that undo removes.
- kittest: editing a frame class width executes exactly one UpdateFrameClass; entering width 0 shows the validation message and leaves the project unchanged.
- kittest: deleting the Mullion class while a curtain wall uses it asks for a replacement and, with Transom chosen, re-points the curtain wall in one undo step; the Delete buttons of Boundary and Corner are disabled and show the tooltip; renaming 'Boundary' keeps its Delete disabled.
- kittest: the panel class table changes a class's type from glass to solid and its thickness, one UpdatePanelClass each; Delete of the last panel class is disabled with its reason.
- Satisfies the user-interface clauses of CW-003 (named sections with material, boundary and corner not removable) and CW-004 (glass or solid with thickness and material).
notes:
SRS: CW-003 CW-004
User-interface clauses; the resources, commands and persistence are task 01.

title: Generate frame and panel bodies as curtain wall parts
description:
WHY: CW-001 (S) requires the curtain wall body along its path; CW-003 (S) gives every frame a rectangular section (width, depth, offset to the glazing plane) and a material, CW-004 (S) every panel a thickness and a material; CW-006 (S) must be visible in 3D: mullions run through, transoms are trimmed. IFX-032 and IFX-038 require closed, consistently oriented 2-manifold bodies with at most 65,535 points; IFX-017 one single-material Body per part; element-kind-framework-15 provides the per-kind geometry registry and ElementGeometry.children (PartGeometry { role, parts, axis }) keyed by PartSpec roles, which element-kind-framework-07 writes as part nodes. The epic design notes make frames profile sweeps along grid lines and panels thin slabs; profiles-columns-beams-05 supplies sweep() with planar end cuts and no Boolean kernel. Gap row CW-001: no frame or panel body generation.

WHAT: Replace the interim generator in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/curtain_wall.rs with crates/archicraft-geometry/src/curtain/{mod.rs,frame.rs,panel.rs}. Per segment a right-handed SegmentFrame: origin at the segment start at the base elevation, e_u along the segment, e_v = +Z, e_w = e_u x e_v (the right-hand side; offsets change sign for exterior Left, the basis never does). Frames: every FramePiece of the layout is swept with sweep() using a rectangular Section (width in the glazing plane, depth along e_w, positioned so the glazing plane lies glazing_offset from the frame's exterior face) and a MemberFrame along the piece; end CutPlanes are perpendicular at PieceEnd::Node and PieceEnd::Face (at the face distance) and the bisector plane for PieceEnd::Mitre; corner pieces are vertical prisms of the mitred plan polygon (both segments' offset strips intersected at the vertex) built with extrude.rs. Panels: for every PanelPiece the union of its cell rectangles in (u, v) minus the union of all frame footprints in the glazing plane (geo BooleanOps), each resulting polygon extruded by the class thickness centred on the glazing plane in local coordinates with extrude.rs and mapped by a positive-determinant DAffine3. ElementGeometry.children gets one PartGeometry per PartSpec role with a single 'Body' BodyPart in the class material and no direct parts; axis stays empty (Table 5-1 lists only member and plate children). LayoutError, degenerate polygons or a frame wider than its cell become a GeometryError, so the framework shows the fallback box and lists the element (NFR-REL-006); curtain_classes() makes UpdateFrameClass and UpdatePanelClass re-evaluate exactly the users through the dirty set. Out of scope: overrides (07; the union code already handles multi-cell pieces), plan symbols (08), trims (13), layered panels (12), insert and component panels (16), arc segments (15).
design: Reuse rather than new primitives: sweep.rs (profiles-columns-beams-05) for all straight frame pieces, extrude.rs for corner prisms and panels, geo for the panel outline subtraction (panel = cells minus frame footprints handles boundary placement, merged cells and, later, trimmed outlines with one code path). Map local (u, v, w) to storey coordinates with DAffine3::from_cols(e_u, e_v, e_w, origin); assert a positive determinant in debug builds so IFX-051's rule (no mirrored transforms) holds. Pitfalls: frames and panels touch at faces but are separate meshes, so check_closed's point merging (mesh.rs:122) never sees shared vertices; drop subtraction slivers with area below MODEL_TOLERANCE x 1 m and report them instead of emitting degenerate triangles; sweep() rejects end planes within 1 degree of parallel, which validation already prevents through the 10-350 degree vertex rule; glass is translucent (opacity 0.3 in template.rs) and the renderer's unsorted transparency (technical debt, render3d.rs:311) shows here first, which is not this task's fix. Pointers: evaluate.rs:22-48, extrude.rs:18, mesh.rs:49/105/122, sweep.rs after profiles-columns-beams-05, crates/archicraft-geometry/src/kinds/ registry after element-kind-framework-15.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_wall.rs: every child mesh of the D.2 sample walls passes check_closed, has positive signed_volume and at most MAX_MESH_POINTS points.
- A 4.50 x 3.00 m single-segment D.2 wall has three 0.03 m glass panels and a total frame volume equal to the analytic value within 1e-9 m3.
- CW-006 in 3D: the lower and upper mullion bodies meet in the transom plane, transom bodies end at the mullion faces (u extents checked), and panel bodies end at the frame faces without overlapping any frame body.
- An L-shaped wall has a closed mitred corner frame and no overlap between the two segments' horizontal frames; exterior Left mirrors all w offsets.
- A curtain wall whose locked rows no longer fit after a storey change evaluates to the fallback and appears in the problems list with a message naming the rows.
- Dirty-set test: UpdateFrameClass re-evaluates only the curtain walls using that class; the incremental-versus-full property test of element-kind-framework stays green with curtain walls in the stand-in model.
- Generic plan slicing of the children at 1.10 m yields aluminium and glass cut regions (sanity check for task 08).
- Satisfies the 3D body of CW-001, the section, thickness and material clauses of CW-003 and CW-004, and CW-006 in the generated bodies.

title: Edit curtain wall frames and panels in edit mode
description:
WHY: CW-005 (S): in an edit mode the user shall be able to select individual frames and panels, reassign their class and delete a division frame (merging the adjacent panels). SEL-008 (M) requires that edit mode for curtain walls; selection-transforms-08 provides the generic edit mode (enter, part highlighting, Tab cycling, Esc), and task 04 registered the CurtainWallPart addressing and part outlines, task 07 the commands. The epic acceptance demonstrates deleting a division frame and the merged panel; without this task the overrides are only reachable through tests.

WHAT: Plan and 3D: entering edit mode on a curtain wall (context menu, Enter or double-click, selection-transforms-08) shows its parts from part_outline: frame rectangles and panel lines in plan, child bodies in 3D picked through the id buffer's part slot (selection-transforms-06), mapped from the part role to CurtainWallPart through Kind::part_ref_for_role (task 04); removed frames are drawn as dashed ghosts in edit mode only, so they can be picked and restored; Tab cycles frame and panel candidates at the pointer. Properties strip in edit mode: the part label and size, a class choice for selected frames (default plus frame classes) executing AssignCurtainFrameClass and for selected panels executing AssignCurtainPanelClass, and 'Reset to default class'. Delete key and the context-menu entry 'Delete frame' on selected division frames execute RemoveCurtainFrames; a selection containing boundary or corner frames shows the refusal in the status line and changes nothing; 'Restore frame' on ghosts executes RestoreCurtainFrames. Selection::retain_valid after each command; after a merge the merged panel is selected. Out of scope: dragging grid lines or part transforms (follow-up bead), path reshaping, panel kinds of task 12.
design: No selection-code changes are expected: the kind registered its part hooks in task 04, so this task wires curtain-wall specific actions (class choice, delete, restore) into the edit-mode panels and draws ghosts. Ghosts come from layout pieces whose override says removed; they are not parts of the evaluated geometry, so picking uses part_outline in model coordinates (plan) and is plan-only for restore. Pitfalls: the id buffer of selection-transforms-06 has an 8-bit part slot (255 parts per element) while long curtain walls have more parts: while an element is in edit mode, encode that element's parts with a full-width part index in the id pass (only one element is in edit mode) or fall back to the CPU ray pick over its child bodies, never truncate; Delete in edit mode must not fall through to deleting the whole element; the Esc ladder of selection-transforms-08 stays (step input, then edit mode, then selection); the properties strip keeps element fields read-only while parts are selected.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: entering edit mode on the curtain_walls sample, selecting panel C2-R0 and choosing 'Solid panel' executes one AssignCurtainPanelClass, the panel's class changes and undo restores it.
- kittest: selecting a mullion span and pressing Delete reduces the panel count by one and selects the merged panel; 'Restore frame' on its ghost brings the frame back.
- kittest: Delete on a selected boundary frame leaves the model unchanged and shows 'Boundary and corner frames cannot be deleted.' in the status line.
- Unit test on view3d::pick: a ray through a panel body in edit mode returns the curtain wall and the CurtainWallPart::Panel key; Esc leaves edit mode with the curtain wall still selected.
- A 60 m two-storey curtain wall with more than 255 parts still picks the correct frame and panel in 3D edit mode (unit test on the pick mapping).
- Satisfies the user-facing clauses of CW-005 and SEL-008 for curtain walls.
notes: SRS: CW-005

title: Let the frame class order decide frame crossings
description:
WHY: CW-011 (C): per-class intersection priorities may decide which frames run through. CW-006 (S) keeps mullions running through and transoms trimmed by default. Section 8 defers the reference system's numeric curtain-wall priorities ('curtain-wall junction hardware, numeric priorities and full frame/panel catalogues'), so the Could requirement is met with an ordinal priority: the order of the frame classes. Gap row CW-011: missing; a priority per frame class used in the CW-006 trimming. The crossing logic of task 04 already isolates the decision in one rank function.

WHAT: Model: `CurtainWall.crossing: CrossingRule { Position, ClassOrder }` (default Position, the CW-006 rule of task 04); with ClassOrder the piece whose class stands earlier in Project.frame_classes runs through and equal classes fall back to the position rule. Command::MoveFrameClass { class, to_index } with an Edit that snapshots the class order (exact inverse); the template order Corner, Boundary, Mullion, Transom reproduces the default behaviour for default assignments. layout.rs rank(role, axis) gains the class-order branch; validation unchanged. IFCX: the frameClasses array order already carries the ranking (writer keeps model order); archicraft::curtainWall gains an optional crossing member ('position' or 'classOrder'), absent meaning position; FORMAT_VERSION per the framework's bump rule. App: the classes dialog of task 17 gains Move up/Move down for frame classes with the hint 'Classes higher in the list run through where frames cross (curtain walls set to class order)'; the curtain wall properties of task 09 get a 'Frame crossings' choice. Out of scope: numeric priorities, junction hardware (Section 8).
design: An ordinal class order instead of a numeric field honours Section 8's deferral of numeric priorities and needs no new data per class; making it opt-in per curtain wall keeps CW-006 ('by default') literally true even when a user assigns the Transom class to a vertical line. Ties (same class on both pieces) use the position rule, so the rank function stays total. Pitfalls: the class order is project-wide, so reordering re-evaluates every curtain wall with ClassOrder (dirty set through curtain_classes()); plan symbols (task 08) and parts follow automatically because both read the layout.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/curtain_layout.rs: with ClassOrder and Transom moved above Mullion, transom pieces own the crossing nodes and mullion pieces end at the transom faces; Boundary and Corner still win over both; with Position the same project keeps CW-006 behaviour.
- MoveFrameClass and its undo restore the order exactly; the order and the crossing member survive a round trip; a file without the crossing member reads as Position.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_wall.rs: the swapped rule produces closed bodies and transom bodies continuous through the mullion line.
- kittest: Move up in the classes dialog executes one MoveFrameClass.
- Satisfies CW-011 (class priorities decide crossings) while keeping the CW-006 default.
notes:
SRS: CW-011 CW-006
Section 8 defers numeric curtain-wall priorities; the class order is the ordinal reading of CW-011.

title: Add door/window insert and custom component panels
description:
WHY: CW-010 (C): layered panels (ordered skins), door/window insert panels and custom component panels may be added; task 12 delivers the layered panels, this task the insert and component panels. Gap row CW-010: missing; needs CW-004 plus the door and window generators (DW-011). components-dw-catalogue supplies component definitions with parameter schemas and opening-size bindings (components-dw-catalogue-01: Definition, DefinitionRef, InstanceParameters, Binding::{OpeningWidth, OpeningHeight}), definition embedding and relinking (-02: ComponentStore as Project.components, InsertDefinition, RelinkDefinition, missing_definitions()), the built-in catalogue (-03: door.hinged.single, window.tilt-turn, ...), unit generators producing UnitGeometry in a unit-local frame (-04, -05), plan SymbolPrimitives (-06), IFCX persistence of embedded definitions (-08), the schema-driven parameter fields (-11) and the definition picker (-12). Task 12 extends PanelKind first, task 08 provides the symbolic plan path, task 17 the panel class editor. IFX-017 names unit parts by role (Frame, Leaf, Glazing).

WHAT: Model (crates/archicraft-model/src/curtain_classes.rs): PanelKind gains `Insert { definition: DefinitionRef, parameters: InstanceParameters }` (definitions of category door or window) and `Component { definition, parameters }` (any category); validation requires a definition with OpeningWidth and OpeningHeight bindings ('<name> cannot adapt to a panel size.'), parameters valid against ParameterSchema::validate, and a rectangular panel: assigning an Insert or Component class to an L-shaped merged group (task 07) is refused with a message; the class thickness is the definition's frame depth (read-only). The AddPanelClass and UpdatePanelClass plans append components-dw-catalogue-02's InsertDefinition edit so a referenced built-in definition is embedded in the same undo step; RelinkDefinition re-points panel classes; Project::missing_definitions() counts panel classes as users. Geometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/curtain/panel.rs): Insert and Component panels call the generator registry of components-dw-catalogue-04 with the panel's clear opening (cell minus frame faces) bound to the opening parameters and map UnitGeometry from the unit-local frame (x along the wall from the left outer frame edge seen from the exterior, y through the wall from the exterior face, z up from the bottom) into the cell with a positive-determinant DAffine3, one BodyPart per UnitPart named by its PartRole; a missing definition yields the components placeholder box inside the panel (OBJ-005). PartSpec class per panel: the definition's default_class (IfcDoor, IfcWindow, ...) for Insert and Component panels, IfcPlate otherwise. Plan: symbolic mode (task 08) places the definition's SymbolPrimitives at the panel, transformed from unit-local plan coordinates, instead of the panel line, so an insert door shows its leaf and swing. IFCX: panelClasses records gain the kind codes 'insert' and 'component' with optional definition ({ id, version }) and parameters members; the definition itself is written through components-dw-catalogue-08's embedded-definitions record; conformance/check.ts accepts IfcDoor, IfcWindow and the definition classes as curtain-wall children besides IfcMember and IfcPlate. App: the panel class table of task 17 offers Insert and Component with components-dw-catalogue-12's definition_picker (filtered to door and window categories for Insert) and components-dw-catalogue-11's parameter_fields for the instance parameters. Out of scope: shared type nodes for insert panels (IFX-050; follow-up bead), handedness labels beyond what the symbols carry, layered panels (12).
design: Reuse over new generators: inserts and components use the unit generators and symbols of components-dw-catalogue in their unit-local frame (layout.rs of components-dw-catalogue-04), placed by a positive-determinant mapping local to panel.rs (doors-windows-core uses the same idea in walls but is not a prerequisite). The panel's clear opening (cell minus frame faces) drives the opening bindings, so a grid edit resizes inserts automatically. Pitfalls: insert units must not intersect the surrounding frames (clear opening, not cell size); unit parts carry their own materials and must not be recoloured by the panel class; IFC part classes other than IfcPlate are a deliberate extension of Table 5-1 for inserts and are documented in docs/components.md; a relink or a definition change re-evaluates every curtain wall using the class through the ChangeLog.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_wall.rs: an Insert panel with the built-in door.hinged.single fills a 1.45 x 2.35 m cell: every unit part is closed and lies inside the cell's clear opening without overlapping a frame body; a window.tilt-turn insert does the same; a Component panel with the test-kinds probe definition is generated through the registry; a missing definition yields the placeholder box inside the panel.
- crates/archicraft-model tests with undo: assigning an Insert class to an L-shaped merged panel and creating a class from a definition without opening bindings are refused with messages; AddPanelClass with a built-in door embeds the definition in the same undo step; RelinkDefinition re-points the class.
- The symbolic plan of a curtain wall with a door insert shows the door's leaf and swing arc primitives at the panel position.
- Round trip: insert and component panel classes survive save and open with their definitions embedded; the IfcDoor part appears as a curtain-wall child; conformance/run.sh passes with the widened check.ts.
- kittest: the panel class table creates an insert class from the catalogue picker and edits one of its parameters.
- Satisfies the door/window insert and custom component clauses of CW-010.
notes:
SRS: CW-010
Door/window insert and custom component clauses; layered panels in task 12.

title: Add per-instance frame and panel overrides with grid-edit remap
description:
WHY: CW-005 (S): in an edit mode the user shall be able to select individual frames and panels, reassign their class and delete a division frame (merging the adjacent panels); overrides apply to that instance only and survive later edits of the grid where the cell still exists. The epic acceptance requires that deleting a division frame merges panels and that the override survives a grid edit where the cell still exists; the epic risk names the mechanism (cell ids from column and row indices with a remap on insert and delete). Gap row CW-005: needs per-instance override storage and the delete-division-frame merge on top of the part addressing (task 04). This task delivers the model, geometry and persistence half; the edit-mode UI is task 10.

WHAT: Model: `CurtainOverrides { frames: BTreeMap<FrameKey, FrameOverride { class: Option<FrameClassId>, removed: bool }>, panels: BTreeMap<CellId, PanelClassId> }` as CurtainWall.overrides (#[serde(default)]). layout.rs applies them: class overrides on frame pieces; removed Mullion and Transom pieces disappear and a union-find over cells joined across removed pieces builds PanelPiece groups keyed by the representative cell (lowest row, then lowest column) whose class is the representative's override or the default; crossings are recomputed so a transom crossing a removed mullion span runs through that node. Commands, planned in kinds/curtain_wall/commands.rs with one variant, label and plan arm each in command.rs: AssignCurtainFrameClass { element, frames, class: Option<FrameClassId> }, AssignCurtainPanelClass { element, panels, class: Option<PanelClassId> } (None resets to the default), RemoveCurtainFrames { element, frames } (Boundary and Corner pieces refused: 'Boundary and corner frames cannot be deleted.'), RestoreCurtainFrames { element, frames }, and EditCurtainGrid { element, axis: GridAxisKind { Columns, Rows }, op: GridOp } which applies the op (task 02), recomputes the layout and remaps every override key through remap_cells for each segment (columns) or for the height (rows), dropping keys of cells and lines that no longer exist; each plans a single ReplaceElement. The kind's normalising validate hook prunes keys outside the current layout (shortened path, lowered top), so only existing cells keep overrides. curtain_classes() and replace_curtain_class() (task 01) include the override classes, so DeleteFrameClass and DeletePanelClass re-point overrides to the replacement and the dirty set also covers curtain walls that use a class only through an override. Geometry: merged multi-cell panels and removed frames through task 05's union path; verify, no new generator code. IFCX: optional frameOverrides [{ key, class, removed }] and panelOverrides [{ key, class }] in archicraft::curtainWall with keys as role strings, read leniently (unknown key or class dropped with a warning; FORMAT_VERSION per the framework's bump rule); samples::curtain_walls() gains one removed mullion span and one 'Solid panel' override; golden re-blessed. Out of scope: edit-mode UI (10), class order (11).
design: Overrides are keyed by the stable keys of task 04 and stored sparsely, so an untouched curtain wall writes nothing new. Remap is explicit in EditCurtainGrid because only the command knows the op; generic element replacements (properties edits of height or path) rely on pruning by the validate hook, which matches the SRS clause 'where the cell still exists'. Union-find over at most a few thousand cells per element is trivial; the representative rule (lowest row, then column) is deterministic and documented, and overrides on non-representative cells of a group are kept but inactive, so restoring the frame revives them. Pitfalls: keys in BTreeMap give deterministic serialisation order for the journal, autosave and IFCX; pruning must run in validate (normalising) so files never accumulate dangling keys; a removed frame's own class override stays dormant; Selection::retain_valid after these commands drops selected parts that merged away.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-model/tests/curtain_overrides.rs: removing the mullion span between C0-R0 and C1-R0 yields one fewer panel, a merged PanelPiece of two cells keyed C0-R0 and no piece with that frame key; restoring it brings the original layout back; undo of every command restores the project exactly.
- Assigning 'Solid panel' to C2-R1 changes that panel's class only; resetting with None removes the override entry.
- Grid-edit survival: after EditCurtainGrid InsertItem at column item 0 the override formerly on C2-R1 sits on the remapped cell and still applies; after RemoveItem of the item containing the overridden cell the override is gone; a size-only edit (SetItem changing a size, or a longer path in BestFit with the same column count) keeps every key; lowering the top so row R1 disappears prunes its overrides.
- Removing a Boundary or Corner piece is refused with CommandError::Invalid and the message; an L-shaped merge (one mullion span and one transom span removed around a cell) produces one L-shaped panel.
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_wall.rs: the merged panel body spans both cells between the boundary frames and is closed; the removed frame role is absent from ElementGeometry.children.
- Round trip with overrides is equal; the re-blessed curtain-walls.ifcx shows the merged IfcPlate and the solid panel's material; conformance/run.sh green.
- Frame overrides: assigning the Transom class to one mullion span changes only that piece (the other spans of the line keep Mullion); after EditCurtainGrid InsertItem the frame override sits on the remapped line and span; deleting a panel class that is used only by an override, with a replacement, re-points the override in one undo step.
- Satisfies CW-005 at model, geometry and file level: per-instance class reassignment, delete division frame with merge, and overrides that survive grid edits where the cell still exists.
notes: SRS: CW-005

title: Write IfcCurtainWall with IfcMember and IfcPlate parts and a golden
description:
WHY: CW-009 (S): curtain walls shall be written to IFCX as IfcCurtainWall with IfcMember (frames) and IfcPlate (panels) children (Table 5-1). IFX-016 (M) makes compound parts child nodes with their own class, IFX-010 gives regenerated parts v5 ids from the owner's UUID and role, IFX-020 requires class code and bSDD uri on every part, IFX-017 and IFX-043 a Body with a named material, IFX-006 conformance on reference models. Gap row CW-009: IfcClass lacked the classes (element.rs:10-14; element-kind-framework-05 adds the D.5 list), the writer had no compound children (writer.rs:361-406; element-kind-framework-07 generalises it) and the reader ignored non-storey children (reader.rs:854-858). What remains is the curtain wall's use of that codec, a reference sample, a golden file and conformance rules that would catch a regression.

WHAT: Wire and verify the framework's parts codec for the curtain wall: part nodes with bsi::ifc::class IfcMember or IfcPlate (code and uri), bsi::ifc::prop::Name '<element name> <part label>', path sub_node_id(owner, role), one Body child per part with the class material reference, no archicraft:: attributes on parts and no Body directly under the IfcCurtainWall node; the reader regenerates parts from archicraft::curtainWall and ignores part nodes without warnings. crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs: samples::curtain_walls() built with the framework's seeded FixtureBuilder: one storey with a straight 4.50 m D.2 curtain wall, an L-shaped wall (3.00 + 4.00 m) with Fixed columns [1.20] and rows [0.90 locked, flexible] linked to home + 1, and a 6.00 m wall with Outside boundary placement and Divisions 5; add it to samples::catalogue() (element-kind-framework-03), the single list that feeds crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs; bless crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/curtain-walls.ifcx and review the diff. conformance/check.ts: every IfcCurtainWall has at least one IfcMember and one IfcPlate child, every part has a class, a name and a mesh with colour, no mesh sits directly under an IfcCurtainWall, and the summary counts parts. If regression-and-status has landed its fixture registry and headless viewer run, register the sample there and assert that members and plates appear in the viewer tree. Out of scope: overrides in the sample (07 extends it), the RM-M entrance (14), IsExternal (IFX-022, owned with ELM-012).
design: Follow the 'Add a sample/golden model' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md. check.ts walks the composed tree like checkViewerTree (conformance/check.ts:67-103), extended by element-kind-framework-07 to recurse into parts; the curtain-wall rule only adds class expectations for children of IfcCurtainWall (task 16 widens it to IfcDoor, IfcWindow and component classes).
