Keep the sample small enough for a reviewable golden diff (three walls, about 120 parts) and use the fixed author and timestamp of the other goldens. Pitfalls: part names include the element name, so renaming an element changes names but never paths (IFX-014); the reader must not report part nodes as unknown elements; MAX_MESH_POINTS is checked per Body, which a single frame piece never approaches.
acceptance_criteria:
- The round-trip suite passes on samples::curtain_walls(): written_files_validate_without_problems, round_trip_restores_the_editable_model, regenerated_geometry_matches_the_stored_geometry, output_is_deterministic_and_plain, written_meshes_are_closed_bodies and golden_files_are_reproduced.
- spatial_tree_and_identities: every part path equals v5(owner, role); paths are unchanged after a size-only grid edit and after a save/load/save cycle.
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx passes on every golden file including curtain-walls.ifcx; a scratch copy with a Body moved directly under the IfcCurtainWall, or with all IfcPlate children removed, fails check.ts (verified once and recorded in the PR description).
- The golden file shows IfcCurtainWall nodes under the storey with IfcMember and IfcPlate children named after their labels and Body meshes referencing the Aluminium and Glass material nodes.
- Satisfies CW-009 and re-asserts IFX-016, IFX-010 and IFX-020 with a real compound kind.
notes: SRS: CW-009

title: Add the RM-M entrance curtain wall and trimmed-wall fixtures
description:
WHY: The epic acceptance requires that the RM-M entrance curtain wall exports IfcCurtainWall with IfcMember and IfcPlate parts (conformance and viewer) and that a roof-trimmed curtain wall keeps frames and panels on the trimmed outline. RM-M (SRS 7.3: five-storey residential building with a curtain-wall entrance) is generated by perf-tuning-rm-m-l in increment 4, which depends on this epic, so the entrance must exist here as a reusable builder; SRS 7.1 makes the curtain-wall entrance of RM-M part of v1 acceptance when curtain walls are in the release. CW-009 (S) is verified end to end on a realistic element that also exercises CW-001, CW-002, CW-005, CW-010 and CW-008.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/samples.rs, built through commands with the seeded FixtureBuilder: `rm_m_entrance_into(builder, storey, origin)` adds a two-storey entrance curtain wall on a three-segment path (1.80 m return, 6.00 m front, 1.80 m return, 90-degree corners), top linked to home + 2, columns [1.50 flexible] BestFit, rows [2.40 locked, 0.60 locked, flexible], a layered spandrel panel class on the 0.60 m row, a single-leaf door insert panel in the front segment, one removed mullion span merging two upper panels and a frame class override on the door mullions; `rm_m_entrance()` wraps it in a project with two 3.00 m storeys for its own golden. `curtain_wall_gable()` builds a gable end where a curtain wall replaces the gable wall under the D.2 35-degree roof with a Trim relation. Add both to samples::catalogue() (element-kind-framework-03), which feeds crates/archicraft-ifcx/examples/reference_models.rs and samples() of crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/roundtrip.rs, bless rm-m-entrance.ifcx and curtain-wall-gable.ifcx, and register them in the regression-and-status fixture registry and headless viewer run where present. Document rm_m_entrance_into for perf-tuning-rm-m-l. Out of scope: RM-M itself and performance measurement (perf-tuning-rm-m-l).
design: Follow the 'Add a sample/golden model' recipe in docs/implementation-status.md. Builder functions, not files: perf-tuning-rm-m-l generates RM-M in-process and must place the entrance without copying data, so the fixture takes the builder, storey and origin; v5 ids derive from the fixture name, keeping goldens deterministic. Keep the entrance realistic but bounded (about 150 parts) so the golden diff stays reviewable. Pitfalls: the gable fixture depends on roofs and cleanup-and-trims kinds being registered in release builds (not test-kinds); bless only after reviewing the diff; the door insert needs the built-in catalogue definition embedded in the file.
acceptance_criteria:
- The round-trip suite (validation, editable round trip, regenerated geometry within 0.1 mm, determinism, closed meshes, identities, golden reproduction) passes on rm_m_entrance() and curtain_wall_gable().
- conformance/run.sh crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden/*.ifcx passes; rm-m-entrance.ifcx contains one IfcCurtainWall with IfcMember and IfcPlate children, an IfcDoor insert part and Skin_n bodies on the spandrel plates; the headless viewer run (if present) lists the members and plates.
- curtain-wall-gable.ifcx shows boundary members along both rakes and no part above the roof plane (asserted in a test on the evaluated geometry, not only by inspection).
- A test asserts that rm_m_entrance_into places the same element set at another origin (used by perf-tuning-rm-m-l).
- Satisfies the RM-M entrance clause of the epic acceptance for CW-009 and provides the regression fixtures for CW-001, CW-002, CW-005, CW-010 and CW-008.

title: Add layered panel classes built from layer structures
description:
WHY: CW-010 (C): layered panels (ordered skins), door/window insert panels and custom component panels may be added; this task delivers the layered panels, task 16 the insert and component panels (the original single task was about three days of work across four crates and was split). Gap row CW-010: missing; needs CW-004 plus skins (layer structures, PRF-001) and the door and window generators (DW-011). layer-structures supplies the LayerStructure resource (layer-structures-01: LayerStructure { id, name, skins }, total_thickness(), Command::DeleteLayerStructure { structure, replacement: Option<LayerStructureId> }) and the Skin_n body convention (layer-structures-04); task 01 supplies the panel classes, task 07 per-panel class assignment, task 17 the class editor. IFX-017 names multi-material parts by role (Skin_n).

WHAT: Model (crates/archicraft-model/src/curtain_classes.rs): PanelKind gains `Layered { structure: LayerStructureId }`; the thickness of a layered class is derived from LayerStructure::total_thickness() (validate rejects a stored thickness that differs, the editor shows it read-only) and must stay within the 0.001-0.50 m panel range; the DeleteLayerStructure plan of layer-structures-01/02 treats layered panel classes as users and re-points them to the replacement with ReplacePanelClass edits in the same undo step, or refuses without one ('<structure> is used by panel class <name>.'); UpdateLayerStructure re-evaluates the curtain walls using such classes through the ChangeLog (element-kind-framework-10); integrity_problems reports a panel class with a dangling structure. Geometry (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/curtain/panel.rs): a layered panel extrudes the same clipped panel polygon of task 05 once per skin, stacked along e_w from the exterior face and centred on the glazing plane, one BodyPart per skin named Skin_1..Skin_n (IFX-017) in the skin material; the PartSpec class stays IfcPlate. Plan: symbolic mode keeps the panel line (CW-007); projected mode slices the skins generically. IFCX: panelClasses records gain the kind code 'layered' and an optional `structure` member (optional addition under the framework's bump rule); the reader turns a class with an unknown structure into a solid panel of the same thickness with a warning. App: the panel class table of task 17 offers the Layered type with a layer-structure choice over Project.layer_structures and the derived thickness read-only. Out of scope: insert and component panels (16), core reference positions (layer-structures-03 applies to walls and slabs).
design: Reuse layer-structures' skin order and Skin_n naming so walls and panels export alike; panel polygons come from task 05 (cells minus frame footprints), so merged and trimmed panels get their layers without new code. Pitfalls: skins are ordered from the curtain wall's exterior side (task 03's `exterior`), so exterior Left reverses the w direction, never the skin order; a structure thicker than the frame depth makes panels protrude, which is allowed but shown as a warning in properties; Glass and Solid classes keep their single Body (no Skin_n for single-material panels), so existing goldens stay byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- crates/archicraft-geometry/tests/curtain_wall.rs: a Layered panel class with a three-skin structure produces Skin_1..Skin_3 bodies whose total thickness equals the structure, centred on the glazing plane, each closed with positive volume and in its skin material; exterior Left reverses the stacking direction in w, not the skin order.
- crates/archicraft-model tests: DeleteLayerStructure of a structure used by a panel class is refused without a replacement and re-points the class with one, both undoable; UpdateLayerStructure changing a skin thickness re-evaluates exactly the curtain walls using that class (dirty-set test); validation rejects a layered class whose structure is thicker than 0.50 m.
- Round trip: a project with a layered panel class assigned through a panel override round-trips equal; the reader repair of an unknown structure warns; the written IfcPlate part carries Skin_n bodies and conformance/run.sh passes.
- kittest: the panel class table creates a layered class from a structure and shows its derived thickness read-only.
- Satisfies the layered-panel clause of CW-010 (ordered skins).
notes:
SRS: CW-010
Layered-panel clause; the door/window insert and custom component clauses follow in task 16.

Check them like the rest (latest version, release date, downloads per month on lib.rs or npm, licence, maintainers) and add them to the Health check table.

title: Manage several buildings in the browser, storey dialog and properties
description:
WHY: STR-014 (C) in the UI: the project browser lists storeys highest first (VIEW-003, M), storeys are inserted, renamed and deleted in a storey dialog and in the browser's context menu (STR-003, M), context menus offer the relevant commands (UI-005, M) and building names are editable (STR-013, M). The epic design asks for per-building grouping in the project browser of plan-views-browser.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/browser.rs: with more than one building the Storeys group nests one collapsible node per building (storeys highest first within each); with one building the tree is unchanged. Building context menu: Rename, New storey, Delete (dialog with the element count and the delete or move-to-building choice of DeleteBuilding, task 20) and Settings. Command project.new-building (Project menu, palette) with a dialog: name, copy levels from an existing building or from the template, elevation offset (the copy option of AddBuilding, task 20). The Storeys dialog gets a building selector; plan tab titles read '<building> - <storey>' when several buildings exist; the home-storey picker in properties is grouped by building; switching the active storey across buildings keeps tool defaults valid. Out of scope: building properties beyond the name, per-building site plans.
design: Group by building only when buildings().len() > 1, so single-building projects and the existing kittests see no change. Dialogs follow the 'Add a dialog' recipe with unit-aware widgets; new commands are registered in the command registry (commands-and-l10n-03) so the palette reaches them (UI-017). Pitfalls: Workspace.plan_views is keyed by StoreyId, which stays unique project-wide; saved views referencing storeys of a deleted building are removed by DeleteBuilding's plan (ViewDefinition of plan-views-browser), not left dangling.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: project.new-building copying the first building's levels: the browser shows two building nodes with their storeys; a one-building project shows the flat storey list as before.
- kittest: double-clicking a storey of the second building opens its plan with the building name in the tab title, and a wall drawn there is homed on that storey.
- kittest: deleting the second building with elements and choosing 'Move to building 1' moves them, and one undo step restores everything; the last building's Delete entry is disabled with a reason tooltip.
- The UI clauses of STR-014 are satisfied (with tasks 15, 20 and 16 the whole of STR-014).
notes: SRS: STR-014

title: Support 6-DoF 3D mice in 3D views after a HID crate health check
description:
WHY: HW-004 (C): 3D mouse (6-DoF navigation device) support in 3D views. The technology choices require permissive licences, maturity, active maintenance and pure Rust where possible, and the epic design allows HW-004 only with a permissive-licence HID crate after a health check. UND-005 (M): navigation creates no undo steps. Gap row HW-004: missing - no HID or 6-DoF handling anywhere.

WHAT: Health check of the candidates (a pure-Rust HID crate such as async-hid, and the hidapi bindings with their C library) against the selection criteria, recorded in docs/technology-choices.md; if none passes, the bead is closed as deferred with that reason. Implementation: crates/archicraft-app/src/input/spacemouse.rs, a device thread enumerating HID devices of the 3Dconnexion vendor ids (0x046D legacy, 0x256F) and the multi-axis usage, parsing translation, rotation and button reports (separate report ids 1/2/3 and the combined 12-byte report) into SixDof { t: DVec3, r: DVec3, buttons } and posting them over a channel with ctx.request_repaint(); an egui-free mapping in views/navigation.rs with dead zone, per-axis sensitivity and inversion (translation pans and dollies, rotation orbits about the pivot), applied to the active 3D pane only; Preferences rows (enable, sensitivity, dead zone, inversion). An absent device or one held exclusively by a vendor driver leaves the feature idle with a status note. Out of scope: the proprietary vendor SDK, device buttons beyond Fit and Menu, plan navigation with the device, driving walk mode.
design: Device I/O runs on its own thread so a blocking read never stalls the UI; egui's Context is Send + Sync for request_repaint. Normalise axes to [-1, 1] by the device's logical maximum (350 for most devices) and scale by frame dt so motion is frame-rate independent. On macOS and Windows the vendor driver may hold the device exclusively; report that instead of failing, because the vendor SDK is proprietary and outside the licence policy. Linux needs udev permissions for hidraw - document the rule in the procedure and never install it (no installer, D-12). Pitfall: selection criterion 4 (pure Rust where possible) - a C library adds a toolchain step on three CI runners.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision record with the health-check data (licence, monthly downloads, last release, maintainers, toolchain) in docs/technology-choices.md; cargo deny check licenses passes with the chosen crate.
- Unit tests of the report parser with byte fixtures for the separate-report and combined-report formats, and of the mapping: input inside the dead zone gives no intent, inversion flips the sign, and a table-driven test drives each of the six axes alone (tx and ty pan, tz dollies, rx orbits in pitch, rz orbits in yaw, ry is ignored because the orbit camera has no roll) and checks that no other motion results.
- Integration test: SixDof events fed through the channel into a 3D pane move the camera; project revision and undo length stay unchanged (UND-005).
- Manual procedure docs/test-plan/hw-004-3d-mouse.md with results on every OS for which a device is available.
- HW-004 is satisfied and its row in docs/implementation-status.md cites the tests and the procedure.
notes: SRS: HW-004

title: Serve the script interface on a local socket with docs and a client
description:
WHY: SW-004 (C): the command interface is out-of-process, documented and versioned. NFR-SEC-001 (M) requires offline operation and NFR-SEC-004 (M) allows network access only to fetch import URIs, so the transport must be local IPC, never a network service. The epic acceptance requires that a scripted client creates a wall through the command interface with explicit units and the same Command objects.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/script/server.rs: a local-socket listener (Unix domain socket in the data directory with user-only permissions on macOS and Linux, a named pipe restricted to the current user on Windows) through the interprocess crate after a health and licence check (fallback: std TCP bound to 127.0.0.1 with a random token in a user-only discovery file); off by default and enabled in Preferences with the endpoint shown; discovery file <data dir>/script-endpoint.json { protocol, endpoint, pid }; line-delimited JSON-RPC per connection on a reader thread, requests forwarded to the UI thread over a channel and executed between frames in ArchiCraftApp::update through the dispatcher of task 18 (status line 'Script: Create wall'), replies through a per-request channel, ctx.request_repaint() on arrival; shutdown removes socket and discovery file. docs/scripting.md: protocol, methods, units and dims patterns per command, errors, limits, versioning and deprecation policy, security notes, examples. crates/archicraft-app/examples/script_client.rs: std + serde_json client doing the version handshake, creating a wall in millimetres on the ground storey and querying it back in feet. Out of scope: remote access, authentication beyond OS permissions, scripting languages and plugins (Section 8).
design: The UI thread stays the only writer of the Workspace (egui is single-threaded), so the listener never touches the model; a per-frame drain limit (for example 64 requests) keeps the UI responsive, and bulk work comes as one batch request. Local sockets keep NFR-SEC-004 intact and avoid firewall prompts that a TCP listener can trigger; OS permissions are the access control. Pitfalls: the macOS sun_path limit of 104 bytes - keep the socket name short or place it in the per-user temporary directory when the data path is long; Windows pipe names must be unique per session (include the pid); a script command arriving during a tool's multi-step input must not corrupt tool state, so tools re-validate their element references after any revision change.
acceptance_criteria:
- Integration test crates/archicraft-app/tests/script.rs: the server on a temporary endpoint with a headless Workspace pumped by the test thread; the example client's library function connects over the real local socket, creates a 5000 mm wall and reads it back as 16.404 ft; the project has one new wall and one undo step labelled as in the UI.
- Malformed JSON returns -32700 and the connection stays usable; a second concurrent client is served; with the preference off neither socket nor discovery file exists.
- On shutdown socket and discovery file are removed; a stale discovery file from a crashed run is replaced at start.
- cargo deny check licenses passes with the chosen IPC crate and the health-check data is recorded in docs/technology-choices.md.
- docs/scripting.md documents every method and error code with an example request and response; the example builds in CI (cargo build --examples).
- The documented, versioned and out-of-process clauses of SW-004 are satisfied (with task 18 the whole of SW-004).
notes: SRS: SW-004

title: Verify exit criterion: Could scope by user feedback: spaces, buildings, shells, gravity, walk mode, devices, toolbars, history, scripting
description:
WHY: The epic's exit criterion must be verified as a whole: every Could item taken into the release (INP-019, SPC-001, SPC-002, STR-014, SW-004, UI-013, UND-004, ROF-013, ROF-014, HW-004, HW-005, VIEW-024) has its model or geometry test and round trip, and every item not taken is recorded as deferred with the feedback that decided it, so that docs/implementation-status.md and beads tell the same story.

WHAT: Run the quality gates on the whole workspace, run conformance/run.sh on all golden files, walk the epic acceptance item by item against the tests of tasks 01-22, update docs/implementation-status.md for every covered requirement ID (status, evidence with test names) and list each untaken item as deferred with its feedback rationale, close the beads of cut items with reason 'deferred: <rationale>', and close the epic in beads. Out of scope: new feature work.
design: Items are independent beads, so a cut item's bead is closed as deferred rather than left open, which lets this task close; the per-merge status check of regression-and-status compares the epic's srs_ids with the changed rows of docs/implementation-status.md. Verify the acceptance on the integrated build, not per branch: spaces with detection and auto-update together, shells together with the facet conversion, buildings with the browser and the headless viewer tree, scripting through the real socket with the example client.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each item taken into the release has its own model/geometry test and round-trip: a space detected inside a wall-bounded region shows name, number and area, is written as IfcSpace and its boundary follows a bounding wall; a second building has its own storeys and IfcBuilding node and the file passes IFX-006; a vault shell is modelled and converted into planar roofs per face; gravity drops a column onto the highest slab under the pointer; walk mode moves at eye height; a scripted client creates a wall through the command interface with explicit units and the same Command objects; untaken items are listed as deferred in docs/implementation-status.md with the feedback rationale.
- cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test --workspace are green.
- conformance/run.sh is green on every file in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden, including the new space, shell and two-building goldens of the items taken.
- docs/implementation-status.md is updated for every covered requirement ID (INP-019 SPC-001 SPC-002 STR-014 SW-004 UI-013 UND-004 ROF-013 ROF-014 HW-004 HW-005 VIEW-024), with deferred items and their feedback rationale listed.
- The epic could-scope-polish is closed in beads.
notes: SRS: INP-019 SPC-001 SPC-002 STR-014 SW-004 UI-013 UND-004 ROF-013 ROF-014 HW-004 HW-005 VIEW-024

title: Add the space kind with boundary, height link, area and plan stamp
description:
WHY: SPC-001 (C): a space element may be provided with a name, a number, a boundary polygon (drawn, or detected by clicking inside a region bounded by walls, INP-018), a storey-linked height and a plan stamp showing name, number and area; it is exported as IfcSpace. Section 4.25 limits v1 to this simple element because rooms and zones with area calculation are BIM information management, and Section 8 excludes zones with calculation rules. Gap row SPC-001: missing - no space kind, and IfcClass lacked IfcSpace (crates/archicraft-model/src/element.rs:10-15) until element-kind-framework-05 completed the Appendix D.5 class list.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/space.rs registered through the kind registry: Space { long_name, number, boundary: Outline, base_offset, top: TopLink (default Relative { storeys: 1, offset: 0 }), source: BoundarySource::Drawn | Detected { seed: DVec2, auto_update: bool }, stamp_offset: DVec2 }, name prefix 'SP', IfcClass::Space fixed, SpaceDefaults in the per-kind defaults slot, descriptor flags marking it as no construction element (no junctions, hosts, trims or solid operations) and excluding it from the contour-detection sources; Space::net_area() from the Outline; number suggestion '<storey number>.<two-digit counter>'; validation through the Outline rules of edit-reshape-palette-02 plus a positive resolved height. Geometry: a geometry generator registered for the kind (element-kind-framework-15) producing one closed BodyPart by extruding the boundary between base and top; PlanDrawing.stamps: Vec<PlanStamp { element, anchor, name, number, area }> with the anchor at the boundary's interior point plus stamp_offset and the area formatted with units::format_area in the project area unit and locale; views/plan.rs draws the boundary thinly with a light tint below construction elements and the stamp as three text lines at paper size; spaces pick by stamp or boundary. Out of scope: IFCX (task 07), tool and detection (task 08), automatic update (task 09), area rules, deductions, schedules, room volumes and finishes (Section 8).
design: Follow the 'Add an element kind' recipe of docs/implementation-status.md as reshaped by element-kind-framework (one kinds/ module plus one registry line, codecs and defaults slots). Element.name keeps the ELM-019 ID (SP-001); long_name is the room name and number the room number, both free text without uniqueness checks (numbering schemes belong to the excluded calculation rules). geo's InteriorPoint (geo 0.33) yields a point inside concave polygons, so no new dependency is needed. Spaces are not sliced into CutRegions (no cut fill); in 3D they render translucent through the transparency path and can be hidden with the kind filter of 3d-view-restrictions. Pitfalls: keep stamp_offset zero by default for deterministic files; format the area through the area-unit setting of commands-and-l10n-09, never a literal 'm²'; keep spaces out of the junction candidate index of element-kind-framework-10.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: adding a space and undo/redo restore the project; a self-intersecting and a zero-area boundary are rejected with CommandError::Invalid and leave the project unchanged; an L-shaped 6 x 4 m boundary minus a 2 x 2 m notch has net_area 20.000 m2, with a 1 x 1 m hole 19.000 m2; changing the storey height changes the resolved top (STR-006).
- Geometry tests: the body is closed and outward-oriented with volume = net area x resolved height (relative 1e-9); the stamp anchor lies inside the L-shaped boundary; for long name 'Kitchen' and number '0.01' the stamp reads 'Kitchen', '0.01', '20.00 m²' in the default metric template.
- Contour detection ignores spaces: a space drawn inside a room does not split the room's region.
- The model, geometry and plan-stamp clauses of SPC-001 are satisfied.
notes: No Appendix D value: proposed stamp text height 2.5 mm on paper; default height link storey + 1, offset 0 as for walls in D.2. Translucent 3D display uses the sorted transparent batch of 3d-display-styles and hiding by kind the filter of 3d-view-restrictions (both increment 3, complete by increment 4). SRS: SPC-001

title: Add user-customizable toolbars built from the command registry
description:
WHY: UI-013 (C): toolbars may be user-customizable. UI-017 (M) still holds: every command stays reachable from a menu or the command palette and bindable without first adding it to a toolbar; UI-004 (S) persists the layout per user and UI-011 (S) gives tools tooltips with their shortcut. Gap row UI-013: the toolbox is a fixed list (crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/shell.rs:120-162) and nothing can be customised.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/toolbars.rs: ToolbarSet { toolbars: Vec<Toolbar { id, name, visible, dock: Top | Left | Right, items: Vec<ToolbarItem::Command(CommandId) | Separator> }> } with a default derived from the ToolGroup grouping of commands-and-l10n-15 (selection, modelling, 2D/annotation, view tools). Rendering replaces the ToolGroup-generated toolbox in ui/shell.rs (today the fixed toolbox() at shell.rs:120-162): each visible toolbar draws its items through tool_button of ui/command_widgets.rs (commands-and-l10n-13), so a click calls ArchiCraftApp::invoke(id, Target::active(), Origin::Toolbar) and the checked state, the disabled reason from Enabled::No and the 'description (shortcut)' tooltip of UI-011 come from the registry. A 'Customize toolbars' dialog (command view.customize-toolbars in the View menu and the palette): toolbar list with new, rename, delete, show/hide, dock side and reset to defaults, and an item editor with a searchable list of all registry commands (palette-only ones included), add, remove, separator and reordering by drag and drop plus Up/Down buttons. Persistence in Preferences.toolbars (serde default, versioned and exported with commands-and-l10n-07). Out of scope: icon design (technology-choices risk 5), floating toolbars outside the main window, per-project toolbars.
design: Toolbars store command ids, never handlers, so they are plain data that survive new commands; the ids are the public contract defined by commands-and-l10n-03. Docked toolbars are egui panels inside the main window, laid out before the egui_tiles area in ui/shell.rs. Drag and drop uses egui's Ui::dnd_drag_source and dnd_drop_zone with the item index as payload; keep Up/Down buttons for keyboard users (commands-and-l10n-16). Pitfalls: the old toolbox mixed tools and actions (Fit, Orbit, Plan/3D) - after the registry both are commands; hiding a toolbar must not disable shortcuts, which belong to the registry; keep egui ids derived from the toolbar id so drag state does not jump between frames.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of ToolbarSet (egui-free): the default holds every command of the former fixed toolbox; unknown command ids from a newer preferences file are dropped with one log line and the rest kept; serde round trip.
- kittest: in the dialog, create toolbar 'My tools', add 'Slab tool' and a separator, close: the button appears, and clicking it records an invocation of the slab tool command (test recorder of commands-and-l10n-03) and makes the slab tool active.
- kittest: after removing every item from every toolbar, the wall tool is still reachable through the command palette and the Design menu (UI-017).
- Saving and reloading Preferences in a test keeps the custom toolbar; 'Reset to defaults' restores the default set.
- UI-013 is satisfied and its row in docs/implementation-status.md cites these tests.
notes: No Appendix D value; default toolbar contents follow the palette grouping of UI-001. SRS: UI-013

title: Verify pen-tablet input as mouse input and drop touch-only gestures
description:
WHY: HW-005 (C): pen-tablet input, treated as a mouse. Gap row HW-005: nothing explicit; pen input reaches the views only through winit/egui pointer events (views/plan.rs:365 and views/view3d.rs:103 allocate a plain Sense::click_and_drag), it was never verified with a tablet, and pressure, eraser and hover semantics are unaddressed. Depending on the platform a pen arrives as mouse events (macOS tablet events, X11) or as touch events (Windows Ink through winit Touch, Wayland pointer emulation); egui then synthesises pointer events for the first touch, which is the 'treated as a mouse' path, but touch-only behaviour such as egui's long-touch context menu can fire during a slow pen click.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/pointer.rs: canvas pointer normalisation used by views/plan.rs and views/view3d.rs: a tap is a primary click, a drag is a drag, the barrel button as delivered by the driver is a secondary click, long-touch context menus are suppressed on plan and 3D canvases (touch-first UI is out of scope by Section 8), pressure and tilt are ignored, and in-range hover drives highlight and snap preview where the platform reports it; review the click distance threshold (egui InputOptions) for pen jitter. Manual procedure docs/test-plan/hw-005-pen-tablet.md for macOS, Windows (Windows Ink on and off) and Linux (X11 and Wayland) with a results table. Out of scope: pressure-sensitive drawing, eraser semantics beyond 'pointer', multi-touch gestures on touch screens, Wayland tablet-v2 support in winit.
design: egui 0.36 does not tell a pen from a finger, so the code must not depend on that distinction; remove only touch-specific behaviour on canvases: show canvas context menus on secondary_clicked() and ignore long_touched() there, and avoid any branch on i.any_touches(). Keep the threshold change local to canvases if it would affect widgets elsewhere. The headless crates are untouched. Pitfall: Windows Ink can turn a press-and-hold into a right click itself; the procedure must record whether that happens with Windows Ink on and off.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest with injected egui::Event::Touch sequences on a plan view with the wall tool: two taps place a wall; holding a touch still for 1.5 s on the canvas opens no context menu, while a secondary PointerButton event still opens it.
- kittest: an injected pointer hover without press shows the snap marker (the mouse-emulating pen path is unchanged).
- kittest: a pen click whose down and up positions differ by 4 points still counts as a click in click-click input (INP-020 default).
- docs/test-plan/hw-005-pen-tablet.md lists the steps (wall chain, select, area select, context menu by barrel button, orbit in 3D) with the observed result and driver version per platform; any platform without hover reporting is named as a known limitation.
- HW-005 is satisfied and its row in docs/implementation-status.md cites the tests and the procedure.
notes: Hardware: one Wacom-class tablet; record driver versions in the procedure. SRS: HW-005

title: Add gravity placement onto the highest slab, roof or terrain surface
description:
WHY: INP-019 (C): with gravity enabled, newly placed columns, walls, objects and stairs may take the elevation of the highest slab, roof or terrain surface under the pointer. Decision D-3: every element keeps exactly one home storey, so gravity changes the base offset, never the home storey. The epic acceptance requires that gravity drops a column onto the highest slab under the pointer. Gap row INP-019: missing entirely; it depends on slab, roof and terrain surfaces, the column, object and stair elements and the base-offset semantics of ELM.

WHAT: Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/gravity.rs surface_below(index: &PickIndex, xy: DVec2, accept) -> Option<SurfaceHit { element, part, z, normal }>, a downward vertical ray from above the model bounds through the PickIndex of 3d-input-navigation-06; accepted parts belong to kinds whose KindDescriptor sets a new gravity_surface flag (slab, roof including the IfcSlab planes of multi-plane roofs, the terrain TopSurface part), upward-facing only. Model: a KindDescriptor hook set_base_elevation(&mut self, relative_to_home_storey), implemented once on VerticalLink.base_offset for walls, columns and stairs (element-kind-framework-02, profiles-columns-beams-06, stair-solver-tool-04) and on the storey-relative elevation of objects (library-dw-exchange-01). App: command input.gravity (checked toggle, view-control bar button and status indicator, remembered in Preferences), applied in the creation tools' point-input step at the placement point (columns and objects: the point; walls: each segment's first point; stairs: the first baseline point) before preview and commit; the prompt shows 'Gravity: <element> at +3.200' or 'Gravity: no surface'; a typed Z or elevation overrides gravity. Out of scope: gravity for slabs, roofs and beams, sloping wall bases, re-applying gravity to existing elements.
design: Highest surface = first accepted hit of a downward ray from z_top = model bounds max z + 1 m; reject faces with normal.z < sin(1 degree) and downward faces so a roof underside never wins over its top. PickIndex coordinates are absolute: base_offset = hit.z - home storey elevation, where the home storey stays the active storey even if the surface belongs to another storey (D-3). Plan tools use the same lazily built index (no GPU needed); in 3D views with a horizontal working plane gravity samples at the working-plane point's XY. Accept terrain by part role (TopSurface) so skirt faces never count; at shared edges take the highest hit within MODEL_TOLERANCE. Walls with TopLink::Fixed keep their height above the new base; storey-linked tops do not move.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests on a fixture with a ground slab (top +/-0.000), a mezzanine slab (top +1.500) over half the footprint, a single-plane roof over part of it and a terrain patch outside: surface_below returns the roof top where it is highest, the mezzanine top under it, the ground slab elsewhere, the terrain outside the building and None beyond everything; roof soffits, slab bottoms and vertical faces are never returned.
- Tool test (egui-free, views/tools.rs): the column tool with gravity on, clicked over the mezzanine, creates a column with base_offset 1.500 on the active storey; with gravity off 0.000; over terrain at +0.850 it gets 0.850; each creation is one undo step.
- Wall tool test: a chain started over the mezzanine gives the first wall base_offset 1.500; a wall whose storey-linked top would fall below its gravity base is rejected with the validation message and the tool keeps its input.
- Object and stair tool tests: an object placed with gravity on over the roof gets the roof-top elevation at its insertion point as storey-relative elevation; a stair whose first baseline point lies over the mezzanine gets base_offset 1.500 while its top stays storey-linked, so its resolved total rise shrinks by 1.500; with gravity off both keep 0.000.
- kittest: input.gravity toggles the indicator and the checked menu state, and the setting persists in Preferences.
- INP-019 is satisfied for columns, walls, objects and stairs; its row in docs/implementation-status.md cites these tests.
notes: No Appendix D value. Columns come from profiles-columns-beams (increment 1), stairs from stair-solver-tool (increment 2) and objects from library-dw-exchange (increment 3); all are present in increment 4, so no edge to those epics is drawn. SRS: INP-019

title: Could scope by user feedback: spaces, buildings, shells, gravity, walk mode, devices, toolbars, history, scripting
description:
The Could requirements without a natural home in a feature slice, taken up by user feedback within a capped budget: spaces with drawn or detected boundaries and IfcSpace, several buildings per site, shells and faceted-surface-to-roof conversion, gravity placement, walk mode, 3D mouse and pen tablet support, configurable toolbars, a history panel and the out-of-process command interface. Each item is its own bead, scheduled only after feedback and cut first.

Risks: STR-014 and SW-004 are extra-large Could items: explicitly optional, scheduled last and cut first. Spaces must not grow into the out-of-scope zones with calculation rules (Section 8). Budget: the beads below add up to about 37 engineer-days, about two and a half times the 15-day cap; the cap is spent on the items users ask for, in the default order history panel, pen tablet, toolbars, walk mode, gravity, spaces, faceted-surface conversion, shells, 3D mouse, buildings, scripting, and a bead that is not taken is closed as deferred with the feedback rationale. Epics of increments 1 to 3 that are not listed as prerequisites (profiles-columns-beams, cleanup-and-trims, ifcx-interop, regression-and-status, 3d-view-restrictions, 3d-display-styles, templates-presets, stair-solver-tool, library-dw-exchange, curtain-walls) are complete by increment 4; the tasks that use them say so in their notes. element-kind-framework, point-input-snapping, selection-transforms, junction-engine, drafting-trim-split and solid-kernel-ops are reached transitively through the listed prerequisites.
design: Space kind on the contour detection of edit-reshape-palette; StoreyList moved under Building with several IfcBuilding children and per-building grouping in the project browser of plan-views-browser (STR-014); gravity samples the evaluated slab, roof and terrain bodies under the pointer (INP-019); Shell kind on the half-edge and sweep machinery; toolbar model in ui/shell.rs; history panel over History's journal; SW-004 as a JSON-RPC over a local socket speaking serde-serialised Command values (NFR-MNT-001); HW-004 only with a permissive-licence HID crate after a health check.
acceptance_criteria: Each item taken into the release has its own model/geometry test and round-trip: a space detected inside a wall-bounded region shows name, number and area, is written as IfcSpace and its boundary follows a bounding wall; a second building has its own storeys and IfcBuilding node and the file passes IFX-006; a vault shell is modelled and converted into planar roofs per face; gravity drops a column onto the highest slab under the pointer; walk mode moves at eye height; a scripted client creates a wall through the command interface with explicit units and the same Command objects; untaken items are listed as deferred in docs/implementation-status.md with the feedback rationale.
notes: SRS: INP-019 SPC-001 SPC-002 STR-014 SW-004 UI-013 UND-004 ROF-013 ROF-014 HW-004 HW-005 VIEW-024

title: Add the shell kind: extruded, revolved and ruled forms with validation
description:
WHY: ROF-013 (C): the system may provide a shell element - an extruded, revolved or ruled membrane of constant thickness, with side flip, contour editing and holes; until shells exist, vaults are modelled as free-form solids (SOL-001). Section 3.2 lists the shell among the construction elements (closed 3D body, junctions, openings, trims and solid operations, drawn cut or projected in plan); SOL-030/SOL-032 name shells as trim tools. ELM-011 (M) gives every element a default IFC class from Table 5-1, user-selectable from Appendix D.5. D-9 makes shells C and Section 8 lists them under deferred element depth. Gap row ROF-013: missing, size XL, nothing exists. This task is the model half; bodies follow in task 21.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-model/src/kinds/shell.rs registered through the KindDescriptor registry (element-kind-framework-02, name prefix 'SH', ShellDefaults in the per-kind defaults slot of element-kind-framework-04): Shell { form, thickness, side: Outside | Inside | Centred, placement (origin and rotation about Z relative to the home storey), base_offset, contour: Option<Outline> and holes in the parameter domain (validated and used from task 12), material } with ShellForm::Extruded { profile: PolyCurve (open, local XZ plane, arcs through the shared Arc/PolyCurve type of drafting-trim-split, crates/archicraft-model/src/curve.rs), length, direction }, Revolved { profile, axis origin and direction in the profile plane, start angle, sweep up to 360 degrees } and Ruled { a, b: open 3D polylines }; validation in the kind's validator (profile not self-intersecting, 0 < thickness < minimum radius of curvature on the side the thickness grows into, axis not crossing the profile, sweep in (0, 360], non-degenerate ruled curves with at least two distinct points each); transform hook (move, rotate about Z, mirror) acting on placement and profile; vertical-extent hook for the z-extent index of plan-views-browser-03; IfcClass default IfcRoof, user-selectable from Appendix D.5 (ELM-011, element-kind-framework-05); Command::label message key 'Create shell'. Out of scope: body generation (task 21), contour and holes (task 12), tool and editing (tasks 13 and 22), layer structures for shells, double-curved free-form shells.
design: Parameters stay in the model and generation in the geometry crate (task 21), as for roofs and terrain. Profiles use the exact Arc/PolyCurve of drafting-trim-split so arcs stay exact in the file and offsets can be exact later. The minimum radius of curvature of a PolyCurve profile is its smallest arc radius on the side the thickness grows into (straight segments are unbounded; Centred uses half the thickness). Ruled curves are stored as given and resampled only in geometry. Pitfalls: placement rotates about Z only, so mirroring maps to a mirrored profile plus placement; keep contour and holes None by default so files stay small and deterministic; the vertical extent comes from the bounding box of the profile swept by the form, not from evaluated geometry, so the z-extent index stays model-only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: a barrel vault (extruded half-circle, span 6 m, length 10 m, thickness 0.20 m), a dome (revolved quarter circle, sweep 360 degrees) and a ruled surface between two skew lines are created via AddElements, undone and redone, and survive a serde round trip.
- Model tests: thickness >= the profile's curvature radius, a zero sweep, an axis crossing the profile, a self-intersecting profile and a ruled curve of coincident points are rejected with CommandError::Invalid and leave the project unchanged.
- Model tests: MoveElements and a rotation about Z change only the placement; mirroring gives a profile whose sampled points are the mirror images; the IFC class defaults to IfcRoof and accepts the Appendix D.5 classes.
- The extruded, revolved and ruled membrane clause of ROF-013 is satisfied at model level (geometry with task 21).
notes: Table 5-1 has no Shell row: proposed default IfcRoof (vaults), selectable per ELM-011; add the row to the SRS. No Appendix D value: proposed default thickness 0.20 m and side Outside. ROF-013's fallback (vaults as free-form solids, SOL-001) is delivered by free-form-solids and stays the documented route if the shell beads are cut. SRS: ROF-013

title: Add building commands with per-building numbering and storey links
description:
WHY: STR-014 (C): a project may contain several buildings on one site, each with its own storey set. STR-013 (M) keeps one site and one building with editable names as the default, STR-001 (M) numbers storeys per storey set with the ground storey 0, STR-002 (M) shifts upper storeys on height changes, STR-004 (M) rehomes or deletes the elements of a deleted storey, STR-006 (M) makes storey-linked elements follow, ELM-006 (M) puts the default top link into every vertical kind's defaults and D-3 keeps exactly one home storey per element. After task 15 the model holds a list of buildings but nothing can add a second one.

WHAT: Model: Edit::InsertBuilding and Edit::RemoveBuilding with exact inverses; commands AddBuilding { name, storeys, copy_from: Option<(BuildingId, elevation offset)> } (fresh StoreyIds for copied levels), RenameBuilding and DeleteBuilding { id, elements: Delete | MoveTo(storey map) } (refused for the last building; MoveTo keeps absolute positions as StoreyElements::MoveTo does for STR-004); storey numbers per building; validation (validate.rs): TopLink::Storey must target a storey of the home storey's building and TopLink::Relative resolves within it; tool defaults with absolute storey links (the defaults slots of element-kind-framework-04) are re-targeted as relative links of the same height when placing in another building; element name counters (ELM-019) stay project-wide; Command::label message keys for the new commands (commands-and-l10n-02). Out of scope: IFCX for several buildings (task 16), building UI (task 17).
design: The building is an ordered list entry, so InsertBuilding carries its index and RemoveBuilding's inverse restores it at the same place (IFX-007 order). DeleteBuilding plans the element moves first and the building removal last, so apply_all's rollback covers a failure halfway. Pitfalls: copied levels need fresh StoreyIds and keep names and heights; saved views and plan panes referencing storeys of a removed building are cleaned up by the plan of DeleteBuilding (ViewDefinition of plan-views-browser), not left dangling; numbering is per building, so the same storey number may appear in two buildings and lookups must never go by number.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests: AddBuilding with storeys -1..2 numbers them -1, 0, 1, 2 independently of the first building's 0..1, and undo/redo restore; AddBuilding copying the first building's levels with +0.450 m offset gives fresh StoreyIds at shifted elevations.
- Model tests: DeleteBuilding refuses the last building; with MoveTo it rehomes the elements keeping their absolute positions (as STR-004) and with Delete it removes them, each in one undo step; RenameBuilding changes only the name.
- Model tests: a TopLink::Storey to a storey of another building is rejected with CommandError::Invalid; a relative top link resolves within the home building; changing a storey height in building B shifts only B's upper storeys (STR-002) and B's linked elements (STR-006).
- Model test: a wall placed on a storey of building B with wall defaults linked absolutely to a storey of building A gets a relative top link of the same resolved height.
- The model clauses of STR-014 are satisfied (with task 15).
notes: Scheduled last and cut first together with SW-004 (both XL). SRS: STR-014

title: Generate closed shell bodies with exact offsets and side flip
description:
WHY: ROF-013 (C): a shell is a membrane of constant thickness with side flip. Section 3.2: the shell is a construction element with a closed 3D body, drawn cut or projected in plan. IFX-032 (M) requires closed bodies (check_closed), IFX-038 (M) caps meshes at MAX_MESH_POINTS (crates/archicraft-geometry/src/mesh.rs:49) and Appendix D.1 sets the tessellation tolerance (2 mm chord). The shell kind and its validation exist after task 11; nothing generates its geometry.

WHAT: Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/shell.rs registered as the shell kind's geometry generator (element-kind-framework-15): samples the reference sheet on a (u, v) grid with the shared tessellate(curve, settings) of drafting-trim-split and segments_for of free-form-solids-01, offsets exactly for extruded and revolved forms (2D offset of the profile with mitred joints, then sweep, reusing the revolution frames of free-form-solids-11) and by averaged vertex normals for ruled forms, applies the side (Outside, Inside, Centred) and closes the sheet with rim faces into one closed, outward-oriented BodyPart built with mesh.rs add_face and the smooth-edge tessellation of free-form-solids-03 (smooth inside curved strips, hard rims); plan display through the generic slice (slice.rs) as cut regions. Out of scope: contour and holes (task 12), tool and editing (tasks 13 and 22), layer structures for shells, double-curved free-form shells.
design: Exact constant thickness for extruded and revolved forms comes from offsetting the 2D profile (arcs become concentric arcs, segments parallel segments with mitre joins); only ruled forms approximate by vertex normals, with the deviation bounded by thickness x (1 - cos(theta/2)) documented. Parameters stay in the model (task 11) and generation here, as for roofs and terrain. Pitfalls: a profile touching the revolution axis creates a pole - collapse it to a vertex fan; 360-degree sweeps must weld the seam; ruled curves with different point counts are resampled by normalised arc length to the larger count; the side changes the volume of curved shells (inside offsets shrink radii), so tests compare against the analytic value per side.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry tests: the bodies of the barrel vault, the dome and the ruled sample of task 11 pass check_closed; the vault volume equals pi/2 x (Ro^2 - Ri^2) x L within the D.1 tessellation tolerance (2 mm chord) for Ri = R, Ro = R + t (Outside) and for Ri = R - t, Ro = R (Inside); Centred straddles the reference sheet by t/2 on each side.
- Geometry tests: a 360-degree dome has a welded seam (no boundary edges) and stays below MAX_MESH_POINTS; a profile touching the axis yields a vertex fan without degenerate triangles; the ruled body's thickness deviates from t by no more than the documented bound.
- Plan test: the vault cut at 1.10 m yields two cut regions (the two vault legs).
- The constant-thickness and side-flip clauses of ROF-013 are satisfied at geometry level.
notes: No Appendix D value beyond D.1 tessellation. Revolution frames come from free-form-solids-11 and the shared curve type from drafting-trim-split (increment 1). SRS: ROF-013

title: Update detected space boundaries when the bounding walls change
description:
WHY: SPC-002 (C): a space boundary detected from walls may update automatically when the bounding walls move. Section 3.3: relations are re-evaluated automatically when a participating element changes. The epic acceptance requires that the detected space's boundary follows a bounding wall. Gap row SPC-002: missing, no relation model, depends on SPC-001 and INP-018.

WHAT: Geometry: ModelGeometry::evaluate gets a pass after the construction elements in which every space with source Detected { auto_update: true } takes its effective boundary from space_region(seed) (task 08) on the current footprints; body, stamp and area use it, and ElementGeometry carries effective_boundary. If the seed is no longer in a closed region, the stored boundary is kept and the problems panel lists 'Space boundary could not be updated: the region is open' (UI-012). Incremental evaluation (element-kind-framework-10): a change of a footprint source on the same storey whose old or new footprint box meets a detected space's box (stored union effective, grown by the thickest wall) dirties that space. Model: Command::SetSpaceSource { id, source, boundary } behind 'Detach boundary' (freezes the effective boundary as Drawn) and 'Re-detect' (Detected with a new seed). IFCX: NetArea and the body come from the effective geometry while archicraft::space keeps the stored boundary. App: properties checkbox 'Update with walls' and context-menu entries Detach and Re-detect. Out of scope: virtual boundaries; editing nodes of an attached boundary detaches it with a status note.
design: Deriving the boundary during evaluation (like junctions, D-6) instead of rewriting the model keeps undo exact, needs no follow-up commands inside History and keeps replay (NFR-MNT-001) and the script interface consistent; the stored boundary is only the fallback and the source for Detach. A spatial dependency instead of a stored relation is needed because a newly added wall that splits the room must update the space too. If the seed ends up inside a wall after a move, retry from the stored boundary's interior point before failing. Keep the order deterministic (walls, then spaces in model order) so files stay byte-identical (IFX-007). Pitfalls: the dirty rule needs old and new footprints (ModelGeometry keeps the previous inputs, element-kind-framework-10 design); spaces are never footprint sources; problems of clean elements are carried forward.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: moving a bounding wall of a detected room 0.5 m outward increases the evaluated area by 0.5 m x the room depth, and undo restores the previous area.
- Geometry test: a new wall across the room shrinks the space to the side containing the seed; deleting a bounding wall keeps the stored boundary and adds one problem entry naming the space.
- Equivalence test: incremental and full evaluation give identical space bodies after a random sequence of wall moves (extends element-kind-framework's property test).
- Model test: Detach freezes the boundary so later wall moves leave the area unchanged, is one undo step and is undoable; Re-detect resumes following.
- Round trip: a project with a moved wall saves and reopens with the same evaluated area, and the IfcSpace NetArea in the file equals the effective area.
- SPC-002 and the epic clause 'its boundary follows a bounding wall' are satisfied.
notes: SRS: SPC-002

title: Add shell contours and holes, IFCX persistence and trimming to shells
description:
WHY: ROF-013 (C): shells support contour editing and holes. IFX-060 (M) stores the parametric definition in the archicraft namespace, IFX-017 (M) the evaluated body as a Body child, IFX-006 (M) requires conformance and IFX-007 (S) determinism. SOL-030 (M) lets walls, columns, beams and free-form solids be trimmed to roofs, shells or slabs, and SOL-032 (S) gives every roof and shell a trimming volume.

WHAT: Geometry: clip the reference sheet in its (u, v) parameter domain (u along the path, or angle x maximum radius; v along the profile arc length; ruled: along and across the rulings) by the contour and holes with geo BooleanOps, triangulate the clipped domain with a spade CDT constrained by the segmentation grid lines, map vertices exactly through the analytic form P(u, v) and its offset surface, and close the body with side faces along the contour and every hole. Model: validation that contour and holes lie inside the domain, plus a helper that turns a plan polygon into a domain polygon by projecting its densified edges vertically onto the sheet. IFCX: archicraft::shell codec (form, profile curves, thickness, side, placement, contour and holes) through the codec registry, an IfcRoof node (or the chosen class) with a Body child; sample samples::vaulted_hall (vault with a clipped contour and two holes) with a blessed golden. Trim: the shell kind sets the trim-tool capability of cleanup-and-trims with a downward trimming volume from the reference sheet (SOL-032). Out of scope: tool and editor UI (tasks 13 and 22).
design: Clipping in the parameter domain gives one code path for all three forms and keeps holes and contours independent of the 3D shape; the analytic map keeps vertices exact. Arc length in v and path length or angle x r_max in u keep the domain roughly isometric, so polygon edits in the unrolled editor of task 22 feel natural. CDT: insert the grid lines clipped to the domain polygon as constraints, then contour and holes, and drop outside triangles with the Outline contains of edit-reshape-palette-01 (no new point_in_ring copy, technical debt). Side faces: one quad per domain boundary edge between the reference and offset surfaces. Pitfalls: merge holes that touch the contour first (geo difference does it); 360-degree revolutions have a periodic u - split the domain at the seam and weld; respect IFX-038 for large domes by splitting into Body_n parts as terrain tiles do.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a vault (reference radius R, side Outside) with a 1 x 2 m rectangular domain hole stays closed and its volume equals the full volume minus hole area x thickness x (1 + thickness / (2R)), the exact volume of the removed curved strip, within the tessellation tolerance; a trapezoidal domain contour gives a closed body whose rim follows the contour.
- Geometry test: a plan rectangle projected onto the vault gives a domain polygon whose mapped boundary lies vertically above the plan rectangle within 1 mm.
- Round trip: samples::vaulted_hall saves and reopens to an equal project; the golden passes conformance/run.sh (IFX-006 a) and is byte-stable apart from the header (IFX-007).
- Trim test: a wall under the vault trimmed to the shell (SOL-030) keeps only the part below the inner sheet.
- The contour-editing (model side) and holes clauses of ROF-013 are satisfied.
notes: cleanup-and-trims (increment 2) provides the trim-tool hook; it is present in increment 4. SRS: ROF-013

title: Write and read spaces as IfcSpace with a Body and NetArea
description:
WHY: SPC-001 (C): the space is exported as IfcSpace; Table 5-1 maps Space to IfcSpace with the storey as parent and a Body child. IFX-012 (M) places it in the spatial tree under its home storey, IFX-017 (M) stores the geometry in a Body child, IFX-020 (M) writes the class code with its bSDD URI, IFX-005 (M) allows only declared attributes, IFX-023 (C) names NetArea and Height as basic quantities, IFX-060 (M) keeps authoring data in the archicraft namespace and IFX-006 (M) requires every written file to pass the reference implementation.

WHAT: crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha: an archicraft::space codec through the per-kind codec registry of element-kind-framework-06 (long name, number, boundary as ring arrays like the slab codec, base offset, top link, source with seed and auto_update, stamp offset) declared in schema.rs; writer: an IfcSpace node under its storey with bsi::ifc::prop::Name = long name (the number when empty), NetArea and Height through the IFX-023 quantity mechanism from evaluated geometry, and a Body child whose mesh carries its own bsi::ifc::presentation::diffuseColor and opacity (light blue, 0.25) instead of a project material; reader: the read_element arm with missing values as warnings. New sample samples::two_storey_shell_with_spaces (two drawn spaces, one with a hole) registered in examples/reference_models.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs with a blessed golden. Out of scope: LongName (not declared in the pinned prop@v5a schema), IfcRelSpaceBoundary (no IFCX equivalent), detected boundaries (task 09 decides what is written for them).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe: parameters at full precision, only mesh coordinates rounded. Presentation on the Body keeps the material list untouched and lets viewers show spaces translucent; verify that the reference viewer composes presentation attributes on a body node (R2 puts them on material nodes) - if not, write one shared 'Space presentation' node that space bodies inherit, kept outside the project's material list. IFC convention puts the number in Name and the room name in LongName; without LongName in prop@v5a, Name carries the room name for a readable viewer tree and the number stays in archicraft::space, to be revisited as with IFX-024 once a standard attribute exists. Bump FORMAT_VERSION only if the codec registry would let an older reader misread a new kind.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round-trip test: samples::two_storey_shell_with_spaces saves and reopens to an equal project (revision normalised), source and seed included.
- Golden test: the blessed file has one IfcSpace node per space under its storey with a closed Body child and NetArea equal to the model net area within 1e-6 m2; saving twice is byte-identical apart from the header (IFX-007).
- conformance/run.sh passes on the new golden (IFX-006 a) and the headless viewer tree check of regression-and-status lists the spaces under their storeys.
- A file with an IfcSpace body but no archicraft::space data opens without error, the space read as an imported element.
- The IfcSpace export clause of SPC-001 is satisfied; with task 06 and task 08 the whole of SPC-001.
notes: Open question: IfcSpace Name/LongName convention once the registry declares LongName. IFX-023's quantity mechanism comes from ifcx-interop (increment 2); the viewer tree check from regression-and-status (increment 1). SRS: SPC-001

title: Add a history panel that steps back to any executed command
description:
WHY: UND-004 (C): a history panel may list the executed commands by name and allow stepping back to any of them. It must respect UND-001 (at least 100 steps, history not cleared by saving), UND-002 (no operation clears the history) and UND-005 (navigation creates no steps). Gap row UND-004 is partial: History already keeps a bounded undo deque, a redo stack and a journal and exposes journal(), applied_commands(), undo_label() and redo_label() (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:766-891), and Command::label() names every command (command.rs:111-144), but no panel lists them and there is no multi-step jump; the Edit menu only shows 'Undo <label>' (ui/shell.rs:59-71).

WHAT: Model: History::entries() -> Vec<HistoryEntry { serial, label, applied }> (undo deque oldest first, then the redo stack in redo order), History::undo_to(project, Option<serial>) and redo_to(project, serial), implemented as repeated single undo/redo through the existing path so each step is journalled, stopping at the first step whose inverse fails and returning a StepError that names it. Workspace::step_to(serial) wraps it with the status line ('Undone 3 steps: back to Create wall'). App: crates/archicraft-app/src/ui/history.rs, a dockable History pane (egui_tiles) opened by the registered command view.history (View menu, command palette) with an 'Opened project' origin row, applied entries, the current-state marker and undone entries greyed; a click (or Up/Down plus Enter) steps to the row; long lists use ScrollArea::show_rows. Out of scope: persisting the history across sessions (UND-002 ends it at close), a branching history tree, editing past commands, and fixing the silent stack clear of History::undo (command.rs:827-833) beyond reporting the failure in undo_to.
design: The panel is a view over History; stepping back is undo, not a model change, so no new Command is introduced (NFR-MNT-001 keeps undo outside the command set) and Document::is_dirty stays correct because it compares state_id. Rebuild the entry snapshot only when state_id or the undo/redo lengths change, not every frame. Labels come from Command::label, which commands-and-l10n-02 turned into message keys, so the panel shows translated names. When the undo limit (DEFAULT_UNDO_LIMIT 200, prefs.undo_steps) has trimmed old steps, the origin row reads 'Earlier steps discarded' and is not clickable. Pointers: command.rs:766-891 (History), workspace.rs:138-152 (undo/redo status), commands/edit.rs and commands/view.rs of the registry (commands-and-l10n-03), app.rs pane handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test in crates/archicraft-model/tests/commands.rs: after five commands, undo_to(serial of the second) leaves the project equal (revision normalised) to the state after the second command, entries() reports 2 applied and 3 undone and the journal gains three Undone lines; redo_to(fifth serial) restores the final state; undo_to(None) returns to the opened state; a new command after undo_to drops the undone entries.
- Unit test: a step whose inverse fails stops undo_to there, returns StepError with that step's label and leaves the earlier steps applied.
- kittest in crates/archicraft-app/tests/ui.rs: view.history opens the panel; after three walls it lists 'Create wall' three times; clicking the first row undoes two steps (two walls fewer, the Edit menu offers 'Redo Create wall'); clicking the last greyed row redoes them.
- Saving the project leaves the panel's entries unchanged (UND-001).
- UND-004 is satisfied and its row in docs/implementation-status.md cites these tests.
notes: No Appendix D value. SRS: UND-004

title: Move storey sets under buildings behind project-wide storey lookups
description:
WHY: STR-014 (C): a project may contain several buildings on one site, each with its own storey set; Section 3.1 makes one building the v1 rule and several the Could. STR-013 (M) stays the default (one site and one building with editable names), STR-001 (M) numbers storeys per storey set, STR-002..006 (M) keep storey operations undoable with linked elements following, and D-3 keeps one home storey per element. Gap row STR-014: missing, size XL - one building: Building { id, name } and one storeys: StoreyList on Project (crates/archicraft-model/src/project.rs:164-182), the writer assumes one building (crates/archicraft-ifcx/src/alpha/writer.rs:282-296) and the reader takes the first IfcBuilding (reader.rs:769). This task is the behaviour-preserving restructure that the building commands (task 20), IFCX (task 16) and UI (task 17) build on; every epic since increment 0 has added call sites that read project.storeys directly.

WHAT: Model: Project.buildings: Vec<Building { id, name, storeys: StoreyList }> replaces building and storeys, with project-wide unique StoreyIds and lookups Project::storey(id), storey_list_of(storey), building_of(storey), buildings() and primary_building(); Edit::SetStoreys { building, storeys } replaces Edit::SetStoreys(list) (command.rs:179, 317, 478) with an exact inverse; the storey commands (InsertStorey, DeleteStorey, RenameStorey, SetStoreyElevation, SetStoreyHeight, SetStoreyCutPlane) find their building from the storey id; SetSpatialNames renames the site and the primary building; integrity_problems and reidentify_all (selection-transforms) walk every building. Mechanical call-site migration in archicraft-geometry (plan.rs ViewRange::for_storey, the per-kind generators, the z-extent index of plan-views-browser-03), archicraft-ifcx (writer.rs and reader.rs still write and read exactly one building through primary_building()) and archicraft-app (active storey, browser, storey dialog, properties, plan panes keyed by StoreyId in workspace.rs). Out of scope: a second building with its commands and storey-link rules (task 20), IFCX for several buildings (task 16), building UI (task 17).
design: StoreyList keeps its logic (sorted storeys, ground storey, STR-002 rules) and simply moves inside Building. A project-wide index StoreyId -> building (serde skip, excluded from PartialEq like the relation index of element-kind-framework-08) keeps lookups O(1). Migrate call sites to storey_list_of(home) where a home storey is known and to primary_building() only in single-building paths that tasks 16 and 17 replace. The SetStoreys snapshot changes the serialised Command form, which only affects in-memory journals and the not yet published script protocol. Pitfalls: template.rs builds one building; saved views that reference storeys keep working because StoreyIds stay unique; keep the serde form of a single-building Project stable where it reaches files (it does not: IFCX is written node by node), so goldens stay byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria:
- All existing tests pass and every existing golden file in crates/archicraft-ifcx/tests/golden is byte-identical (single-building projects unchanged).
- Model tests: storey(), storey_list_of() and building_of() resolve every storey of samples::two_storey_shell to the primary building; a storey command naming an unknown storey id is rejected with CommandError::NotFound; InsertStorey and DeleteStorey through Edit::SetStoreys { building, storeys } undo and redo exactly (existing storey tests extended).
- No direct access to a project-level storeys or building field remains outside project.rs (grep check in review).
- The model restructure for STR-014 is in place (the model clauses complete with task 20).
notes: Scheduled last and cut first together with SW-004 (both XL). reidentify_all comes from selection-transforms (increment 1). SRS: STR-014

title: Define the versioned script protocol with explicit units and batches
description:
WHY: SW-004 (C): a documented, versioned, out-of-process command interface may allow scripts to query, create and modify elements with explicit units; it batches bulk operations with deferred regeneration, rejects degenerate input and uses the same command objects as the UI (NFR-MNT-001). NFR-SEC-003 (M) treats external input as untrusted with the Appendix D.9 limits, and Section 8 excludes a scripting language. Gap row SW-004: partial. Existing and kept: commands are serialisable and replayable (crates/archicraft-model/src/command.rs:35-92 derive Serialize/Deserialize, replay() at 900-910) and run through the same History::execute path as the UI (Workspace::execute, crates/archicraft-app/src/workspace.rs:123-136, and Document::execute); validate.rs is the single validity gate that rejects degenerate input with CommandError::Invalid; the Vec-payload commands (AddElements, UpdateElements, MoveElements, DeleteElements) already apply atomically with rollback (apply_all, command.rs:728-746) and Document::geometry re-evaluates lazily by revision (crates/archicraft-app/src/document.rs:97-103); Project accessors and its Serialize form are an in-process query surface. Missing: an out-of-process transport (main.rs only takes a file path), a versioned and documented schema, explicit units (commands take metres; units.rs affects only display and input), one transaction across commands of different types, and a query API reachable from outside the process.

WHAT: Model: archicraft_model::units::Dim { Length, Angle, Area, Volume, Ratio, Count } and a Dimensioned trait implemented for Command and every payload (element kinds through their KindDescriptor) returning the JSON-pointer patterns of their dimensioned fields; Command::Batch { label, commands }, planned on a scratch clone and applied as one transaction (one undo step, geometry evaluated once afterwards). App, headless part: crates/archicraft-app/src/script/ with protocol.rs (JSON-RPC 2.0 messages), dims.rs (SI conversion in and out through the patterns) and dispatch.rs; methods api.version, project.describe (buildings, storeys, layers, materials, units), elements.query (filters kind, storey, layer, ids), commands.execute, commands.batch, history.undo and history.redo; every request carries a mandatory units object ({length, angle}); Command values run through the same Document/Workspace execute path as the UI; errors -32700, -32600, -32601, -32602 (missing units, unmapped or non-finite numbers) and 1001 Invalid, 1002 Locked, 1003 NotFound, 1004 NoChange; limits: JSON nesting below 128 (D.9), request size and batch length caps. Out of scope: the socket transport, documentation and sample client (task 19), any scripting language (Section 8).
design: Units at request level keep payloads identical to the serde form of Command (the 'same command objects' clause) while making the unit explicit; the dims patterns are the one place that knows which numbers are lengths, and the coverage test keeps them complete as kinds are added. Batch: plan each inner command against the clone and apply its edits there, collect the forward edits, then let History apply them atomically with the rollback of apply_all (command.rs:728-746). Deferred regeneration follows from lazy evaluation by revision (document.rs:97-103) and the ChangeLog of element-kind-framework-10. The protocol version (1.0) is independent of the app version and is reported by api.version together with the IFCX FORMAT_VERSION. Pitfalls: reject non-finite numbers after conversion; the serde enum representation defines the patterns, so document it; TopLink offsets and outline points are Length, opacity is Ratio and storey offsets are Count.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit test: each Command of a sample set covering every variant, serialised in metres, converted to millimetres through the dims patterns and back, equals the original; a coverage test fails if any f64 leaf of the serialised samples is not covered by a Dim pattern (catches fields added later).
- Dispatcher tests on a headless Document: commands.execute with units {length: mm} creating a 5000 mm wall gives a 5.0 m wall and one undo step with the UI's label; elements.query in feet returns 16.404 ft; a request without units is rejected with -32602; a zero-length wall and a self-intersecting slab are rejected with 1001 and leave the project unchanged.
- Dispatcher test (modify): commands.execute with UpdateElements setting that wall's thickness to 300 in {length: mm} gives 0.300 m, MoveElements by (1000, 0) mm moves it 1.0 m, and history.undo reverts the move with the UI's label.
- Batch test: 100 walls in one commands.batch give one undo step and one geometry evaluation (evaluation counter); an invalid 57th command rolls the whole batch back.
- Golden JSON of the serialised sample commands guards the protocol contract: changing Command serde fails the test until the protocol version is bumped.
- The explicit-units, query, create, modify, batching, degenerate-input and same-command-objects clauses of SW-004 are satisfied.
notes: Scheduled last and cut first together with STR-014 (both XL). SRS: SW-004

title: Add the shell tool with presets, settings, properties and side flip
description:
WHY: ROF-013 (C): shells are extruded, revolved or ruled membranes with side flip. NFR-USE-002 (M) requires the common geometry methods, numeric input and snapping, NFR-USE-003 (M) a prompt for every input step, UI-002/UI-003 (M) a properties panel and a settings dialog, VIEW-025 (M) element tools on the 3D working plane and UI-017 (M) menu and palette reach. The epic acceptance requires that a vault shell is modelled; the kind and its bodies exist after tasks 11, 21 and 12.

WHAT: App: ToolKind::Shell in crates/archicraft-app/src/views/tools.rs with modes Extruded, Revolved and Ruled plus a 'Barrel vault' preset (span, rise, length and thickness typed in a small dialog, placed by two clicks in plan); profiles are drawn on a vertical working plane in 3D (3d-input-navigation-07), extrusion length or sweep angle by a further point or typed value, ruled shells by two polylines; command tool.shell (Design menu, toolbox modelling group, palette); settings dialog section Shell (thickness, side, class, material); properties panel (ui/properties.rs): thickness, side, a side-flip button running the command shell.flip-side (also in the context menu), derived area and volume. Out of scope: contour and hole editing and the conversion to roofs (task 22), dragging profile nodes in 3D, shell junctions with walls.
design: The preset is the main entry for the acceptance and for users without practice in 3D profile drawing; it builds an Extruded form with a half-circle (rise = span / 2) or segmental-arc profile (rise < span / 2) of the shared Arc type. Side flip is an UpdateElements that swaps Outside and Inside (Centred stays), so it is one undo step and replays. Pitfalls: prompts per step come from the keys each state handles (commands-and-l10n-12); profile input needs a vertical working plane - show a hint otherwise; for curved shells the side changes the volume (inside offsets shrink radii), so derived values are re-read after the flip, never kept.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool test (egui-free): the barrel-vault preset with span 6 m, rise 3 m, length 10 m creates a shell with the matching bounding box; revolved mode with a typed 180-degree sweep creates a half dome; ruled mode creates a shell from two typed polylines; Esc cancels (INP-001); each creation is one undo step.
- kittest: create a vault with the preset (reference radius R = 3 m, thickness t = 0.20 m, length L = 10 m) and flip its side from the properties panel: the reference sheet becomes the outer surface and the derived volume changes from pi/2 x ((R + t)^2 - R^2) x L to pi/2 x (R^2 - (R - t)^2) x L within the tessellation tolerance; one undo restores it.
- kittest: tool.shell is reachable from the Design menu and the command palette, and every input step of the extruded mode shows a prompt (NFR-USE-003).
- The side-flip clause of ROF-013 is satisfied in the UI.
notes: SRS: ROF-013

title: Add first-person walk mode with eye height to perspective 3D views
description:
WHY: VIEW-024 (C): a first-person walk mode for perspective views may be provided, with configurable eye height and mouse-look plus keyboard movement. UND-005 (M): navigation creates no undo steps. UI-008 (M): single-key tool shortcuts must not fire while another input owns the keys. The epic acceptance requires that walk mode moves at eye height. Gap row VIEW-024: missing; it depends on the editable eye and target of VIEW-020 (3d-input-navigation-01).

WHAT: crates/archicraft-app/src/views/walk.rs (egui-free): WalkSettings { eye_height, speed, run_factor, look_sensitivity } and WalkController { position: DVec2, storey: StoreyId, yaw, pitch } with enter(camera, project, storey), step(WalkInput { forward, strafe, look_delta, run, dt }), storey_up() and storey_down(); it drives Camera3d through the eye/target setters of 3d-input-navigation-01 with eye.z = storey elevation + eye height. Integration in views/view3d.rs and views/navigation.rs (walk as a navigation state with its own input mapping): command view.walk (View menu, 3D context menu) enters walk mode on the active 3D view (a parallel view switches to perspective with a status note), Esc or the command leaves it with the camera in place; W/A/S/D and the arrow keys move, Shift runs, primary-button drag looks (optional confined pointer through ViewportCommand::CursorGrab), PageUp/PageDown change the storey; a small HUD shows storey, eye height (unit-aware editable field) and speed; settings in Preferences with rows in the Preferences dialog. Out of scope: collision with walls, following stairs and slopes, recorded walkthroughs (Section 8), driving walk mode with a 3D mouse.
