design: Movement is time-based (i.stable_dt clamped to 0.1 s) with ctx.request_repaint() while a movement key is down, so the frame rate does not change the speed. Forward follows the horizontal heading, independent of pitch, as in architectural walkthroughs. Consume the walk keys with i.consume_key while walk mode is active and the 3D pane has focus, and register them as a 'Walk' scope in the command registry so the shortcut list shows them and conflicts are detected (UI-009). On exit set the orbit target to eye + forward x the previous orbit distance so orbiting continues naturally. Pitfalls: Camera3d is orbit-parametrised (3d-input-navigation-01 design) - set the view through look_along to avoid the orbit pitch clamp; CursorGrab is unreliable on Wayland, so drag-to-look stays the default; vertical correction (VIEW-023) keeps working as configured.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests of WalkController: entering on '01 First floor' (+3.000 m) puts eye.z at 4.600 m with the default 1.60 m eye height (1e-9); one second forward at 1.4 m/s with pitch 30 degrees moves the eye 1.4 m horizontally along the heading with z unchanged; strafe moves perpendicular to the heading; storey_up from the ground floor puts eye.z at the next storey elevation + eye height; pitch clamps at +/-85 degrees.
- kittest: view.walk on a 3D pane and W held for ten frames moves the camera eye while the project revision, the undo length and the dirty flag stay unchanged (UND-005); W does not select the wall tool while walking and does after Esc.
- kittest: a primary-button drag of 100 points to the right in walk mode turns the heading by 100 x look_sensitivity and leaves the eye position unchanged; a vertical drag changes only the pitch (mouse-look).
- kittest: view.walk on a parallel-projection 3D pane switches it to perspective with the status note; Esc leaves walk mode with the camera in place and orbiting continues about eye + forward x the previous orbit distance.
- kittest: setting the eye height to 1.75 m in the HUD moves the eye at once and the value persists in Preferences.
- With the frame-time metrics of regression-and-status-17 (perf feature), a scripted 10 s walk through the largest available reference model is recorded next to the orbit measurement and stays within 10 % of it (NFR-PERF-003 names walk among the navigation modes).
- VIEW-024 is satisfied and its row in docs/implementation-status.md cites these tests.
notes: No Appendix D value: proposed eye height 1.60 m, speed 1.4 m/s (walking pace), run factor 3, look sensitivity 0.2 degrees per point; confirm with users. The frame-time metrics come from regression-and-status-17 (increment 1). SRS: VIEW-024

title: Convert faceted surfaces into a group of planar single-plane roofs
description:
WHY: ROF-014 (C): the system may convert a faceted surface (a set of free-form solid faces, or terrain) into a group of planar roofs, one per planar face. ROF-013 (C) notes that until shells exist vaults are modelled as free-form solids (SOL-001); ROF-001 (M) defines the single-plane roof by outline, pivot line, slope side, pitch, pivot elevation and structure, and ROF-007 (M) the reference surface the pivot elevation refers to. Gap row ROF-014: missing; it depends on SOL-001, SOL-002 face selection, ROF-001, terrain and ELM-015 groups.

WHAT: Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/roof/from_faces.rs faces_to_roofs(project, geometry, source, options) -> Result<FacetConversion> with source: FacetSource::SolidFaces { solid, faces } (stable face ids of free-form-solids-01/07) or FacetSource::Terrain { terrain, region: Option<Outline> } (TIN triangles merged into planar faces); per planar face one single-plane roof: outline = face boundary with holes projected to plan, pitch from the face normal, slope side towards rising z, pivot line = the lowest horizontal face edge or the horizontal line through the lowest vertex clipped to the outline, pivot elevation relative to the home storey (the solid's home storey, or the active storey for site-level terrain, D-3), structure from the roof defaults with the face on the chosen reference surface (top or bottom, ROF-007), Custom bisector eaves cuts on edges shared between converted faces and plumb cuts elsewhere; skipped faces (vertical within 1 degree, downward-facing, slivers) are reported. Model: Command::ConvertFacetsToRoofs { roofs, group_name, remove_source } as one undo step that adds the roofs together with one new ELM-015 Group (templates-presets-15: crates/archicraft-model/src/group.rs, Element.group) holding exactly them, which is the 'group of planar roofs' of ROF-014. App: 'Convert to planar roofs' in the solid face edit-mode context menu and the terrain context menu with an options dialog (reference surface, keep or remove source) and a result note. Out of scope: shells as source (task 22), curved faces (each terrain triangle is planar, so a curved terrain gives many roofs).
design: With the unit normal n (n.z > 0): pitch = atan(|n_xy| / n.z), the roof rises opposite to n_xy, and a horizontal face (|n_xy| < 1e-9) becomes a flat roof with its pivot line on the longest edge. Placing the face on the roof's top or bottom uses the ROF-007 reference surface so the body lies on the chosen side, offset perpendicular to the plane as in roofs-02. Shared edges reuse EdgeCut::Custom (angle to the roof plane) from roofs-01, which roofs-13 uses for exact bisector planes. Terrain merging: union-find over triangles sharing an edge whose normals differ by less than 0.01 degree and whose vertices lie within MODEL_TOLERANCE of the plane. Pitfalls: roofs must validate (minimum edge length and repair thresholds of edit-reshape-palette-02), so collapse sub-0.1 mm edges first; face holes stay holes in the outline; the home storey is the solid's storey, or the active storey for terrain, which is site-level and has none.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test: a free-form barrel-vault solid with 8 planar top faces converts into 8 single-plane roofs whose reference surfaces coincide with the faces within 0.1 mm at every face vertex and whose shared edges meet without gaps or overlaps (0.1 mm, as in ROF-003).
- Geometry test: a terrain of two coplanar triangles and one tilted triangle gives two roofs; a vertical and a downward-facing solid face are skipped and listed in the report.
- Model test: the conversion is one undo step; with remove_source the solid is deleted and undo restores it; an empty face set is rejected with CommandError::Invalid.
- Model test: the new roofs share one new GroupId whose members are exactly the created roofs, so clicking one selects the group (templates-presets-16); undo removes roofs and group together.
- Model test: a terrain conversion limited to a region Outline creates roofs only for the merged faces inside the region, homed on the active storey, with reference surfaces matching the TIN within 0.1 mm.
- kittest: faces selected in a solid's edit mode, 'Convert to planar roofs': the roofs appear as one selected group; the same entry in the terrain context menu shows the options dialog and a result note with the created and skipped face counts.
- ROF-014 is satisfied and its row in docs/implementation-status.md cites these tests.
notes: ELM-015 groups come from templates-presets-15/16 (increment 3) and terrain from terrain-and-site; both are complete by increment 4, so the result is always a group. SRS: ROF-014

title: Write and read several IfcBuilding nodes with their storey sets
description:
WHY: STR-014 (C) in the file: IFX-012 (M) expresses the spatial tree IfcProject -> IfcSite -> IfcBuilding -> IfcBuildingStorey, Table 5-1 gives the site Building(s) children, IFX-010/011/014 (M) fix identities and child keys, IFX-006 (M) requires conformance, IFX-007 (S) determinism, PRJ-008 forbids silent drops and IFX-090 makes older versions flag newer formats. The epic acceptance requires that a second building has its own storeys and IfcBuilding node and that the file passes IFX-006. Builds on the restructure of task 15 and the building commands of task 20.

WHAT: writer.rs: one IfcBuilding child of the site per building (child key Building_<8 hex>, IFX-014), each with its storeys; building order and ground storey per building in an archicraft::building attribute declared in schema.rs. reader.rs: every IfcBuilding child of the site with its storeys, ground storey per building, elements homed by storey id, storey id collisions repaired with a report. Files with several buildings carry FORMAT_VERSION + 1 while single-building files keep the current version, so goldens stay unchanged and older ArchiCraft versions flag newer_format instead of reading only the first building. Sample samples::two_buildings built with AddBuilding (main building at +/-0.000 with storeys 0..1, an annex with storeys -1..0 at other elevations, walls and slabs in both) registered in examples/reference_models.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs with a blessed golden. Out of scope: composing third-party multi-building files beyond reading every building (ifcx-interop owns composition).
design: Follow the 'Add an IFCX attribute' recipe. The format version is computed from the features a project uses (several buildings -> N + 1), so older readers refuse instead of silently reading the first building as increment 0 did. Node order follows the spatial tree with buildings in their stored order (IFX-007). Pitfalls: child keys must be unique within the site (child_key in writer.rs already resolves collisions); RefElevation stays on the site (STR-011, one vertical datum); do not add NumberOfStoreys unless IFX-023 is extended to it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round trip: samples::two_buildings saves and reopens to an equal project with per-building storey numbering, home storeys and unchanged UUIDs (IFX-011).
- Golden: the file has one IfcSite with two IfcBuilding children, each with its own IfcBuildingStorey children; conformance/run.sh passes (IFX-006 a) and the headless viewer tree check shows project, site, two buildings and their storeys (IFX-006 b spatial tree).
- All single-building goldens stay byte-identical.
- Reader tests: a file whose second building lacks archicraft data still reads both buildings with warnings (PRJ-008); a reader limited to the current FORMAT_VERSION flags the two-building file as newer_format.
- The IFCX clauses of STR-014 are satisfied.
notes: The headless viewer tree check comes from regression-and-status (increment 1). SRS: STR-014

title: Add the space tool with drawn and wall-detected boundaries
description:
WHY: SPC-001 (C): the boundary is drawn, or detected by clicking inside a region bounded by walls, reusing the contour detection of INP-018 delivered by edit-reshape-palette. NFR-USE-002 (M) requires the same geometry methods, numeric input and snapping as other element tools, NFR-USE-003 (M) a prompt for every step, and UI-002/UI-003 (M) properties and a settings dialog. The epic acceptance requires that a space detected inside a wall-bounded region shows name, number and area.

WHAT: Geometry: crates/archicraft-geometry/src/space.rs space_region(project, geometry, storey, seed) -> Result<Outline, RegionError> (new RegionError { Unbounded when region_at finds no bounded face around the seed, SeedInFootprint when the seed lies inside a footprint }) building a ContourGraph (edit-reshape-palette-06) from the evaluated footprints of the storey's walls, columns, curtain walls and free-form solids - not from the plan cut polygons - and returning region_at(seed) with islands as holes. App: ToolKind::Space in views/tools.rs with the polygon and rectangle methods of the slab tool and a detection mode (the contour-detection key and toggle of edit-reshape-palette-12) that previews the region under the cursor and creates a space with source Detected { seed, auto_update: true }; properties.rs fields long name, number, height link and base offset plus a read-only derived 'Area' row; settings dialog section 'Space'; command tool.space with a free single-key shortcut, toolbox entry in the modelling group and Design menu item. Out of scope: automatic update when walls move (task 09), dragging the stamp, virtual space separators.
design: Wall footprints instead of cut polygons keep the region from leaking through door and window openings, which are cut at the cut plane; columns standing inside a room become holes, which matches a net area. Footprints come from the junction engine's per-skin footprints (union of skins per wall), so L and T junctions close the region. Cache the graph per storey and geometry revision as edit-reshape-palette-12 does. The polygon and rectangle steps are the slab tool's StepSpecs on the shared InputConsumer (point-input-snapping), keeping NFR-USE-002. Pitfalls: gaps smaller than MODEL_TOLERANCE close the region, larger ones leak - show 'Region is open' in the prompt instead of creating anything; numbers increment per storey from the defaults slot.
acceptance_criteria:
- Geometry test on samples::two_storey_shell_with_shaft (edit-reshape-palette-06): space_region inside the ground-floor room returns the inner wall faces as boundary with the analytic inner area (1e-6 m2); a seed in the shaft returns the shaft; a seed outside the building returns RegionError::Unbounded.
- Geometry test: a room with a door opening in one wall still yields the closed room (footprints ignore openings).
- Tool test (egui-free): a detection click creates one space with source Detected and that boundary; the polygon method with typed lengths creates the drawn boundary; Esc cancels (INP-001); each creation is one undo step.
- kittest: select the space tool, enable detection, click inside the room: the plan shows the stamp with name, number and area, and the properties panel shows the same area.
- The drawn and detected boundary clauses of SPC-001 are satisfied.
notes: INP-018 is owned by edit-reshape-palette and only reused here. Curtain-wall footprints come from curtain-walls (increment 3) and free-form solid footprints from free-form-solids; both are complete by increment 4. SRS: SPC-001

title: Edit shell contours and holes in an unrolled editor and convert shells to roofs
description:
WHY: ROF-013 (C): shells support contour editing and holes; ROF-014 (C) converts a faceted surface into a group of planar roofs, one per planar face, which here includes the shell's facets. SEL-008 (M) provides the edit mode for parts and NFR-USE-002 (M) the same editing methods as for other elements. The epic acceptance requires that a vault shell is modelled and converted into planar roofs per face. The domain clipping and the plan-to-domain projection helper exist after task 12, the shell tool after task 13 and the converter after task 10.

WHAT: App: 'Edit contour and holes' in the shell's edit mode opens an unrolled-domain editor pane (crates/archicraft-app/src/views/shell_domain.rs) in which the contour and holes are edited with the reshape commands of edit-reshape-palette on the shell's domain Outline, issuing UpdateElements; 'Add hole from plan polygon' uses the projection helper of task 12. Geometry: shell_facets(shell, geometry) -> Vec<PlanarFacet> in crates/archicraft-geometry/src/shell.rs (planar strips of the reference sheet for extruded and revolved forms, triangles for ruled forms) and a FacetSource::Shell for faces_to_roofs of task 10; command shell.convert-to-roofs ('Convert to planar roofs' in the shell context menu) with the options dialog of task 10. Out of scope: dragging profile nodes in 3D, shell junctions with walls.
design: The unrolled editor is a plan-like pane on a Camera2d whose world is the (u, v) domain, reusing the plan input pipeline (InputConsumer of point-input-snapping) and the edit palette so node and edge operations behave as on slabs (NFR-USE-002). Facets for conversion: extruded and revolved forms give planar quads per strip (planarity checked within MODEL_TOLERANCE, falling back to triangles), ruled forms give triangles; facets come from the reference sheet so the roofs' reference surfaces coincide with it. Pitfalls: the domain of a 360-degree revolution is periodic - the editor shows one period with the seam marked and rejects contours that cross it; the domain uses arc length in v, so typed lengths in the editor are lengths on the sheet, which the prompt says.
acceptance_criteria:
- kittest: on a vault created with the preset, 'Edit contour and holes' opens the editor; moving a contour node shrinks the domain and the evaluated body (part area reduced accordingly); drawing a rectangular hole shows the opening in the 3D scene; each edit is one undo step.
- Tool test (egui-free): 'Add hole from plan polygon' with a 1 x 2 m plan rectangle creates a hole whose mapped boundary lies vertically above the rectangle within 1 mm.
- Integration test: 'Convert to planar roofs' on a vault with 8 segments creates 8 single-plane roofs coinciding with the reference-sheet facets within 0.1 mm, held in one ELM-015 group, as one undo step, with or without removing the shell (epic acceptance).
- The contour-editing and holes clauses of ROF-013 are satisfied in the UI (with tasks 11, 21, 12 and 13 the whole of ROF-013), and ROF-014 covers shells.
notes: SRS: ROF-013 ROF-014

title: Trademark check of the product name ArchiCraft (SRS O-17)
description: SRS O-17: 'ArchiCraft' resembles 'ArchiCAD', Graphisoft's earlier spelling of Archicad, in the same market (NFR-LEG-002). Check trademarks before any public release; keep the name during development.

value: ArchiCraft SRS v0.2 (docs/SRS.md, 2026-10-16) is aligned with docs/technology-choices.md (R8). Decisions: IFCX is the ONLY file format (D-11: no DXF/DWG/PDF/images/survey CSV/glTF/OBJ/STL/IFC4 import or export, no material textures); no installer, updater or online service, .ifcx association at first start with consent, crash reports stay local (D-12); Windows, macOS and Linux all Must (D-2); solid operations/trims/terrain cuts stay Must and Manifold is planned for v1 at the latest in SRS increment 2. Counts: 567 = 314 M / 199 S / 54 C; withdrawn reqs keep IDs as '· *withdrawn by D-1x (was X)*'. IFCX writer rules: evaluated meshes, every attribute schema-declared, per-face vertices, <=65,535 points per mesh, voids on occurrences, bundled schemas, mesh coords rounded to 1e-6 m in plain decimal (serde_json prints 2e-6 in exponent form, so use a custom formatter), JSON nesting <128 (serde_json limit). Conformance: buildingSMART ifcx-core + viewer under Node/Playwright in CI. Perf: RM-M >=30 fps orbit, edit-to-update <=200 ms. Every model change is an undoable command.

bd create --graph <plan.json> (bd 1.3.1) format: {"nodes":[{"key":"k","title","type":"epic|task|feature|bug","priority":0-4,"description","acceptance_criteria","design","notes","labels":[..],"estimate":<min>,"parent":"<key>"}],"edges":[{"from_key":"a","to_key":"b","type":"blocks"}]}. EDGE DIRECTION: from_key DEPENDS ON to_key (from_key is the blocked issue, to_key its prerequisite) — verified 2026-10-17. Always --dry-run first; unknown fields are silently dropped with a warning (use acceptance_criteria, not acceptance). Output maps key -> issue id. bd delete <ids> --force removes probes.

Parallel Rust builds in several git worktrees: clone the warm cargo cache with `cp -Rc <main-worktree>/target <new-worktree>/target` (APFS clonefile, ~7 s for 3.4 GB, copy-on-write). Third-party deps keep their fingerprints; only the workspace crates rebuild. sccache is not installed; never share one CARGO_TARGET_DIR between concurrent builds (they serialize on the lock).

ifccad evaluated 2026-10-16: NOT suitable as archicraft foundation - 2D CAD drawing profile only (no BIM/3D), single author (216/218 commits since 2026-08-10, ~100k LOC), provisional 0.1.0 contracts, not on crates.io. Candidate later for 2D drawing/sheet export. DWG/DXF candidate: opencadcodec (github HakanSeven12/opencadcodec, fork of acadrust, pure Rust, MPL-2.0, claims DWG+DXF R12-2018 read/write) - corrects earlier claim that no permissive DWG lib exists; needs real-world DWG corpus testing.

IFCX library landscape (checked 2026-10-16): IfcOpenShell has NO IFCX/IFC5 support - maintainer aothms said 'nothing planned' in issue #8989 (2026-07-31); IfcOpenShell's IFCJSON is the old IFC4 JSON format, not IFCX. Rust IFCX option: openbimrs/ifcx v0.1.0 (read/compose/validate ifcx_alpha draft, very young). ifc-lite (MPL-2.0) has an IFC5 exporter in TypeScript. Use IfcOpenShell only for legacy IFC2x3/IFC4 STEP import.

OpenAEC Foundation (open-aec.com, checked 2026-10-16) uses NO shared IFCX library: each tool hand-rolls IFCX. Open Calculations Studio = TS generator packages/core/src/ifc-generator.ts (JSON-LD 'ifcx:0.1' draft + IFC4x3 STEP). ifccad repo (Rust, MPL-2.0) = IFCCAD 2D drawing profile on IFCX with own composition code (src/ifccad/source/composition.rs, targets ifcx_alpha) - useful reference for plan/section drawings in IFCX. Open CAD Studio (Rust, wgpu/iced) has no IFC support.

Gap analysis 2026-10-17 (docs/implementation-status.md, 567 reqs): done 62 / partial 160 / missing 345; Must 58/118/138. Increment 0 delivered; inc 1 scope 2/37/117, inc 2-4 essentially untouched. Gating structural work before new element kinds: ElementKind/IfcClass/tool-default enums are closed and matched in ~15 places across all crates; IFCX schema kind enum is [wall, slab] and FORMAT_VERSION has no migration hook (IFX-062); no relation store (host/solid-op/annotation binding) in Project. Biggest Must hole: EDT (all 25 rows), Command::MoveElements has no UI caller, no hit-testing/handle framework, point input inlined in plan.rs. Junctions: wall::footprints handles 2-wall L/T only, ignores Material.priority, no layer structures (PRF). Perf: full re-evaluation + full GPU re-upload per revision, no spatial index, no RM-M/RM-L/benchmarks. Known small bugs: STR-002 height default inverted, storey moves can orphan linked walls (NFR-REL-005), Esc discards whole op (INP-003), LAY-001 adds to locked layers, IFX-007 unrounded storey elevations, bundled IFCx.dev schema files lack a licence (NFR-LEG-001).
